note: Web sweep of trading strategies and asset patterns that use the learning program's variables or adjacent ones (user request 2026-10-20). Per cluster: research (web candidates with sources), cross (against Mandel's registry, the children, the signal map and the ML results), verify (adversarial check of sources, duplicates, data and look-ahead; final registration text) and knowledge (the signal-map file). Dropped rows are kept with reasons.

candidates.name: VIX-build-up conditioned pre-announcement drift (FOMC, NFP, ISM, GDP)
candidates.summary: Hu, Pan, Wang and Zhu explain the pre-FOMC drift (Lucca-Moench) as a premium for 'heightened uncertainty'. Before scheduled releases VIX builds up over days -3..-1, and that uncertainty resolves before the announcement. Their test that matters here: announcements with a larger prior VIX build-up have a larger pre-announcement return, and lagged VIX changes do not predict returns on non-event days. Mandel already tested the unconditional drift (T-341, T-215, T-343), which failed after 2015. The VIX-conditioned version is untested.
candidates.mechanism: Investors who hold the market into a known uncertainty event want to be paid for it. Hedgers and de-riskers sell or buy protection in the days before (VIX rises, prices dip). Holders who carry the risk collect the premium as the uncertainty resolves in the hours before the release. The input is implied vol, not price.
variables: calendars: FOMC statement days, Employment Situation, ISM, GDP (CPI as secondary)
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY, ES futures; QQQ/IWM secondary)
candidates.horizon: intraday to 1 day (close t-1 to just before the release)
candidates.claimed_effect: Sep 1994 to May 2018, S&P 500 futures, 4 pm t-1 to 5 min before the release. FOMC +27.14 bps (t 5.95), NFP +10.10 (t 3.63), ISM +9.14 (t 2.10), GDP +7.46 (t 2.08). A one-sd larger VIX change over days -3..-1 adds +9.15 bps to the pre-FOMC return. For the high-return FOMC group, VIX rises 1.88 pts and the market falls 81.8 bps in the accumulation period. No costs stated.
candidates.replication: Lucca-Moench is the original (NY Fed SR 512, JF 2015). Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert (FRL 2021) find the drift 'essentially disappeared after 2015', both with and without press conferences. Hu et al. themselves note smaller pre-FOMC returns after 2011. Mandel's own record: T-341 statement-day excess +17.4 bps over 1994-2026 but -5.3 bps over 2016-2026 (not supported); T-215 and T-343 not supported. This is a duplicate-adjacent conditional successor of T-341/T-215/T-343. It adds the VIX-accumulation input and the NFP/ISM/GDP families. I did not search for any post-2018 test of the conditional version (the shared web-search budget ran out mid-sweep). Child learning: these are risk or flow premia, not reference-price leads (the Kelly/Brier CLAUDE.md), so judge them as cost-charged expected-return tilts.

sources.title: Premium for Heightened Uncertainty: Explaining Pre-Announcement Market Returns (Hu, Pan, Wang, Zhu), NBER WP 25817
The disappearing pre-FOMC announcement drift (Kurov, Wolfe, Gilbert), Finance Research Letters 40
The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift (Lucca, Moench), NY Fed Staff Report 512

candidates.proposed_test: Register as a conditional successor of T-341. Events: scheduled FOMC statement days (fomc-meetings) and Employment Situation days (macro-release-employment-situation); CPI is a pre-registered secondary. Signal: z = VIX change from close t-4 to close t-1 (cboe-VIX-history), standardized by the trailing 250-day sd of 3-day VIX changes, so it is point-in-time. Outcome windows: FOMC, SPY close t-1 to close t (daily, 1994-2026), plus close t-1 to 13:30 ET on 60-min bars where they exist (2024-2026). NFP, SPY close t-1 to open t. Statistics: (1) HAC slope of the event return on z; (2) top-tercile-z minus bottom-tercile-z mean; (3) placebo, the same regression on non-event days, which must be about zero. Train 1994-2009; holdouts 2010-2026 and 2016-2026 reported separately. Cost 2 bps round trip. Deflate over 2 event families x 2 windows.

candidates.name: Post-VIX-spike next-day premium (HVIX days)
candidates.summary: Hu et al.'s out-of-sample test of the same theory: on the day after an unexpected VIX spike-up (cutoff fixed so there are about 8 per year), the S&P 500 earns about 57 bps, more than the pre-FOMC drift. The signal comes from implied vol, not price, which fits the program. No Mandel theory tests next-day equity returns conditioned on a VIX jump.
candidates.mechanism: Uncertainty that arrives unexpectedly mostly resolves the next day. Forced de-riskers (vol targeting, risk parity, margin calls, put buyers) pay a premium to liquidity providers who absorb the selling. The other side is mechanical deleveraging flow.
variables: implied volatility (VIX daily change, VIX level)
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY/ES; QQQ, IWM secondary)
candidates.claimed_effect: Sep 1994 to May 2018: next-day close-to-close S&P 500 return 57.22 bps (t 3.24) over 202 HVIX days; 54.73 bps (t 3.73) after trimming the top and bottom 1%. About 8 events a year by construction. No costs stated.
candidates.replication: In-paper only; I found no independent replication (the search budget ran out). Related Mandel results: T-332 (SPY IBS < 0.2 next-day reversal, price-based) supported; T-535 (VIX > 30 in backwardation, VIX lower 21 days later) supported. The risk is overlap: VIX spikes coincide with large down days, so the test must separate the VIX input from plain short-term price reversal.

sources.title: Premium for Heightened Uncertainty (Hu, Pan, Wang, Zhu), NBER WP 25817, HVIX section and Table 1

candidates.proposed_test: SPY, 1994-2026 daily. Event: the VIX daily change exceeds the expanding-window 96.8th percentile of all prior daily changes (about 8 a year). Timing caveat: VIX closes at 16:15 ET, after SPY's 16:00 close, so the primary trade enters at the t+1 open and exits at the t+1 close. A secondary uses the 15:55 VIX from IDX_VIX 5-min bars for a close-to-close trade over the recent period. Control: days with the same SPY-return decile but no VIX spike. HVIX minus control isolates the VIX input from price reversal and must be > 0. Holdout 2018-06 to 2026-10 (after the paper's sample). Cost 2 bps. Block bootstrap; both halves positive; also report the joint result with the T-332 IBS signal.

candidates.name: Announcement-day beta premium (Savor-Wilson 'tale of two days')
candidates.summary: CAPM beta is strongly and positively related to average returns on scheduled CPI, jobs and FOMC days. On all other days the beta-return line is flat. Rotating into high beta only on announcement days, and into low beta otherwise, is a calendar-conditioned factor timing rule. It uses non-price inputs (the release calendar and beta as a risk loading).
candidates.mechanism: The macro risk premium is realised when scheduled news resolves. High-beta assets carry more exposure to it. On non-announcement days, leverage-constrained investors bid up high beta (the BAB logic), which flattens the slope.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (901-symbol archive); beta-sorted ETFs (SPHB/SPLV)
candidates.horizon: 1 day, on about 30-35 announcement days a year
candidates.claimed_effect: 1964-2011 (JFE 2014): nearly all of the annual excess returns of diverse US assets are earned on announcement days, which are about 10% of trading days. The beta-return slope is strongly positive on announcement days and about zero on other days, for stocks, test portfolios, bonds and currencies. Wachter-Zhu reproduce the slope pattern on beta-sorted portfolios from 1961-01 to 2016-09. No costs stated.
candidates.replication: Wachter and Zhu (NBER w24432) replicate it to 2016-09. I found no post-2016 out-of-sample test (the search budget ran out). Mandel's record points to decay: T-343 found the SPY announcement-day premium was +12.7 bps over 1993-2009 but failed over the full span. T-387 (BAB via ETFs) and T-347 (SPHB-SPLV day of week) were not supported. This is new as a cross-sectional test; it is adjacent to T-343.

sources.title: Asset pricing: A tale of two days (Savor, Wilson), JFE 113(2)
The Macroeconomic Announcement Premium (Wachter, Zhu), NBER WP 24432 (replication to 2016-09)
Asset Pricing: A Tale of Two Days (draft, full text)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 901 archived daily histories (current constituents, so flag the survivorship bias). Beta: rolling 252-day beta to SPY at t-1. Announcement days: union of macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation and FOMC statement days. Statistic: the daily Fama-MacBeth slope of return on beta (decile portfolios, value-weighted by sec-companyfacts shares x price). Test the announcement-day mean minus the other-day mean, with a block bootstrap by month. Holdout 2012-2026; both halves positive. Tradeable version: long SPHB minus SPLV (2011 onward) from close t-1 to close t on announcement days only, flat otherwise, at 4 bps round trip per leg. Deflate jointly with T-343.

candidates.name: FOMC-day short-dollar carry (Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi, Vedolin)
candidates.summary: A short-USD basket long other G10 currencies earns much higher returns on scheduled FOMC days, especially in high-yielding currencies, when monetary-policy uncertainty is high, and in easing cycles. The move arrives after the 2:15 pm release: it is significant when sampled at 4 pm ET but not at 2:15 pm. It is executable on OANDA. The inputs are the FOMC calendar and rate differentials.
candidates.mechanism: Constrained financiers intermediate global currency demand and need compensation for bearing monetary-policy uncertainty. When the uncertainty resolves at the announcement, high-yield currencies against USD pay off. The other side is USD hedgers and dollar demanders.
candidates.assets: G10 FX spot (OANDA)
candidates.claimed_effect: 1994-2010, sampled at 4 pm ET. High-interest-rate portfolio +16.83 bps on FOMC days vs +1.67 bps on other days (difference 15.17 bps, t 2.43). Low-rate portfolio +5.71 vs -0.55. AUD +21.76 vs +0.98. No currency is significant when sampled at 2:15 pm ET. The result survives bid-ask costs, with annualized Sharpe ratios 'up to 0.5'. The effect is larger in easing cycles and when uncertainty is high.
candidates.replication: In-paper only for 1994-2010 (JF 2017); I did not find a post-2010 replication (the search budget ran out), so 2011-2026 is a clean holdout. Mandel: T-368 and T-431 (G10 and EM carry) not supported over 2013-2026; T-575 (USD weakness at month end) not supported. Calendar-conditioned FX carry is untested.

sources.title: Exchange Rates and Monetary Policy Uncertainty (Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi, Vedolin), FMG Discussion Paper 54
Exchange rates and monetary policy uncertainty, LSE Research Online

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: 9 G10 currencies vs USD (fx-spot-g10). These are FRED H.10 noon-New-York rates, so the window is noon t to noon t+1 on statement days (it contains the 14:00 release) against the same window on other days. EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD 5-min and 60-min bars cross-check the 14:00-16:00 move in recent years. Portfolios: the top-3 by one-month-lagged OECD 3m rate (fx-rates-3m) minus USD, and the equal-weight DOL basket. Statistics: FOMC minus non-FOMC mean, a date-permutation null, and both halves of 2011-2026 positive. Cost: about 1.5 bps per currency per side, an assumption to be checked against OANDA spreads. Pre-registered secondaries: interaction with easing (a target cut in the prior 6 months, from FRED target series) and with the VXTLT level.

candidates.name: Post-FOMC announcement drift in Treasury yields (Brooks, Katz, Lustig)
candidates.summary: After federal funds target changes, longer Treasury yields keep drifting in the direction of the change for weeks. The authors link this to bond-fund outflows that follow rate increases. It is a calendar-plus-policy-surprise signal for Treasury futures and ETFs. Mandel tested only the equity analogue (T-361).
candidates.mechanism: Fund investors react to salient target increases by slowly redeeming short- and intermediate-duration bond funds. That gradually raises the supply arbitrageurs must absorb, so yields drift. The other side is extrapolative, slow-moving fund investors.
variables: policy surprise (2-year yield change on the day; target change)
candidates.assets: Treasury ETFs (IEF, TLT) / CME Treasury futures (ZN, ZB)
candidates.claimed_effect: A search result quoting an earlier abstract version (not the current NBER abstract) says a 10 bp fed funds surprise moves the 10-year yield about 1.7 bps on the day but about 14 bps after 50 days. I did not read the PDF, so the sample period and costs are unverified.
candidates.replication: NBER WP (2018, revised 2019); no independent replication found. Mandel T-361 (SPY momentum after DGS2 surprises) failed its minimum n (85 classified meetings) and was not supported. The bond version is untested. The zero-lower-bound years (2009-2015, 2020-2022) have no target changes, which limits n.

sources.title: Post-FOMC Announcement Drift in U.S. Bond Markets (Brooks, Katz, Lustig), NBER WP 25127
IDEAS/RePEc listing of the Stanford version

candidates.proposed_test: Events: scheduled FOMC statement days 1994-2026 (fomc-meetings). Surprise s = DGS2(t) - DGS2(t-1) from FRED closes; secondary: the sign of the target change from FRED target series. Outcome: the DGS10 change from close t+1 to close t+k for k = 10, 20, 50, and the synthetic 10-year total return (T-574 method). Trade: short (long) duration-scaled IEF from the t+1 close for 20 days after s > +5 bps (< -5 bps). Statistic: slope of the cumulative yield change on s at meeting level, HAC with overlap-consistent lags; holdout 2019-2026 (after the paper). Cost 2 bps per round trip. Require at least 60 classified meetings or report inconclusive.

candidates.name: Dash-for-cash month-end cycle with the settlement-cycle shift as a natural experiment
candidates.summary: Month-end cash needs (pensions, dividends, salaries) force institutions to sell before payment dates, so stocks fall on T-8..T-4 and rebound on T-3..T-1 and the first days of the month. Treasuries feel the pressure later because they settle T+1. US equity settlement moved from T+3 to T+2 (2017-09-05) and to T+1 (2024-05-28); both dates are from my memory. So the selling window should move one day closer to month end in each regime. That is a falsifiable, point-in-time prediction that tests the mechanism, not just the calendar.
candidates.mechanism: Payments due on day T require selling that settles by T, so the selling day is set by the settlement lag. Liquidity providers earn the reversal. The other side is pension funds and mutual funds raising cash, at an estimated cost of about US$30.6bn a year.
candidates.assets: US equity ETFs (SPY, IWM); Treasury ETFs (IEF/TLT) as control
candidates.claimed_effect: Jul 1995 to Dec 2013 (T+3 era): returns low on T-8..T-4 and high on T-3..T+3. Over 2003-2013 the reversal windows earned a cumulative 103% excess return (73% of the market's excess return), against -31% in the selling windows. corr(T-3..T-1, T-8..T-4) = -0.54. Fund-flow selling predicts more than 40% of the variation in T-3..T-1 returns. Institutional cost about US$30.6bn a year (ANcerno, 1999-2013).
candidates.replication: Mandel: T-59 (SPY turn of month) supported; T-344/T-443 (5-asset replication) not supported (2 of 5 pass); T-547 (country ETFs) not supported; T-574 (Treasury last-day-of-month) supported, consistent with the paper's later Treasury timing; T-345 (month-end rebalancing) supported. Crypto: T-344 found turn of month on BTC (+13.5 bps, p 0.041) and Hurst's forward test H-btc-tom is proposed. Quantpedia's in-sample BTC 21:00-23:00 UTC hour pattern (2015-2022) is the kind of pattern Hurst's 549-trial null already rejected, so I did not register it. I found no paper testing the T+2/T+1 shift (the search budget ran out).

sources.title: Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs (Etula, Rinne, Suominen, Vaittinen), RFS 33(1), open access
Dash for Cash, RFS article page

candidates.proposed_test: SPY and IWM daily, 1995-07 to 2026-10, split by settlement regime: T+3 to 2017-09-01, T+2 from 2017-09-05 to 2024-05-24, T+1 from 2024-05-28. Pre-registered prediction: the last selling-pressure day is T-4 / T-3 / T-2 in the three regimes, and the reversal is the next three sessions. Statistics: per regime, mean(reversal) - mean(selling) net of 2 bps; a permutation test on the location of the minimum-return day. Key comparison: the regime-shifted window must beat the fixed T+3 window out of sample in the T+2 era. The T+1 era is only about 29 months, so it is a forward-tracked read. Controls: IEF (always T+1, so no shift predicted); dividend pay dates and FOMC days. Secondary conditioning on the FRED SOFR month-end spike (2018 onward).

candidates.name: Threshold (drift-band) rebalancing signal for stocks vs bonds
candidates.summary: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone simulate a 60/40 portfolio and measure how far equities drift from target. The 'threshold' signal (average over bands delta = 0 to 2.5%) and the 'calendar' signal (month end) both predict lower next-day stock-minus-bond returns when equities are overweight. Mandel tested only month-end versions (T-345 supported, T-450 not). The intra-month threshold signal is new.
candidates.mechanism: Pensions, sovereign funds and target-date funds rebalance mechanically when weights breach bands, or at month and quarter end. Their predictable orders move prices for about a day. Front-runners profit; the other side is the rebalancers, at an estimated cost of about US$16bn a year.
variables: cross-asset leaders: S&P 500 and 10-year Treasury returns
adjacent_variables: CFTC COT asset-manager positions in ES/ZN
candidates.assets: S&P 500 (SPY/ES) vs 10-year Treasury (IEF/ZN)
candidates.claimed_effect: 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17, daily futures. The threshold (calendar) signal predicts about 16 bps (17 bps) lower next-day equity returns and about 4 bps (2 bps) higher bond returns, in the paper's units. The threshold signal's predictive |t| exceeds 4. Calendar predictability peaks in the last four days of the month and rises toward quarter end. A front-running ES-vs-ZN portfolio has a Sharpe ratio above 1 over 1997-2023. A first-half-only recalibration gives qualitatively similar results.
candidates.replication: Mandel: T-345 (SPY beat TLT month-to-date by more than 2 pp, last two days) supported at -45.6 bps net; T-450 (SPY-AGG, last 3 days plus day 1) not supported. The threshold variant is untested; this is a duplicate-adjacent extension. Caveat for the price-isolated ML program: the signal is a deterministic transform of past SPY and bond returns, so it belongs in a 'flow' family that gets the leakage review.

sources.title: The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing (Harvey, Mazzoleni, Melone), NBER WP 33554
NBER WP 33554 full text (signal construction, eq. 1-3, Fig. 2-3)

candidates.proposed_test: Build the signal as in the paper. Simulate a daily 60/40 SPY / synthetic 10-year portfolio (DGS10 total return as in T-574; IEF as a check). For each delta in 0..2.5% in 0.1% steps, reset when |w - 0.6| >= delta, then average the 26 deviation series. Trade SPY minus duration-scaled IEF from close t to close t+1, signed by -signal, when |signal| exceeds its trailing-252-day 80th percentile. Holdout 2023-04 to 2026-10 (after the paper); full 2002-2026 also reported. Cost 2 bps per leg per trade. Statistics: HAC predictive slope; net Sharpe; placebo bands of 4-6% must be weaker; the signal must add over T-345's calendar signal and turn-of-month dummies.

candidates.name: Dividend payment-day price pressure (market level)
candidates.summary: On days when large aggregate dividends are paid, value-weighted market returns are higher, because predictable reinvestment creates uninformed buying. The amounts and dates are announced weeks ahead, so the signal is point-in-time and not price-based. It is distinct from T-374, which tested single-stock returns before ex-dates.
candidates.mechanism: Fund and DRIP reinvestment of dividend cash is uninformed, predictable buying that meets inelastic demand. The authors estimate price multipliers of 1.5-2.3. The other side is liquidity providers who do not fully pre-position. The effect is absent in Q4, when asset managers hold cash for their own distributions.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY/VTI/ES)
candidates.claimed_effect: CRSP 1926-2018. A one-sd higher daily payout means +3.2 bps VW market return (unconditional mean 4.1 bps). Top-quintile payout days return about 4x the bottom quintile. The past year's top-10 payout days earn +11.6 bps and the top quarter +7.1 bps. Above-average days account for about 70% of the equity premium. Strongest in Q1 (+6.4 bps per sd), none in Q4. Holds across 58 countries and survives controls for turn of month, FOMC, macro days and weekday.
candidates.replication: The related dividend-month premium (DivSeason, Hartzmark-Solomon 2013) is a 'clear' predictor in Chen-Zimmermann (t 16.19, 1927-2011). Mandel T-374 (single-stock dividend capture, 2010-2026) not supported, but that is a different channel. Pay dates cluster at the turn of the month (Etula et al., Fig. 1B), so T-59's turn-of-month effect is a confound that must be controlled.

sources.title: Predictable Price Pressure (Hartzmark, Solomon), NBER WP 30688
Chen-Zimmermann Open Source Asset Pricing signal documentation (DivSeason row)

candidates.proposed_test: Payout(t) = sum over stocks of amount_i x shares_i on pay date t, divided by the sum of market caps at t-1, for the 901-stock universe (daily-events dividends; sec-companyfacts shares). Pay dates come from a free history (Nasdaq dividend API, unverified). Fallback, pre-registered: estimated pay date = ex-date + the firm's median ex-to-pay lag over its prior 8 dividends, which is point-in-time. Regress SPY close t-1 to close t on payout quintile, controlling for turn-of-month, FOMC/CPI/NFP and weekday dummies. Holdout 2019-2026 (after the paper). Tradeable version: long SPY only on top-quintile days (about 50 a year), 2 bps round trip. Statistic: top-minus-bottom quintile mean with a block bootstrap; pre-registered secondary: the Q1-vs-Q4 interaction.

candidates.name: Option-expiration-week premium in high option-activity stocks (Stivers-Sun)
candidates.summary: Stocks with a high option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) earn abnormally high returns during the monthly options-expiration week. The comparison is against other stocks and against the same stocks' other weeks. It is attributed to market-maker delta-hedge rebalancing as options decay into expiry, and to falling implied vol. Mandel tested only the index-level OPEX week (T-353/T-438), which was not supported. The O/S-conditioned cross-section is untested.
candidates.mechanism: As expiry approaches, dealer hedges unwind through charm and vanna flows, and implied vol falls. Hedgers' stock purchases and sales create predictable pressure in option-heavy names. The other side is option end-users and the hedging dealers.
variables: options volume and open interest (O/S ratio)
candidates.assets: US large-cap stocks with listed options
candidates.claimed_effect: High-O/S strategy (28 stocks, 1996-2008): OPEX-week spread +67.9 and +70.7 bps in the two subperiods. Quantpedia's backtest of long S&P 100 only in OPEX weeks, 1988-2010: about 9.3% a year (about 6.3% of it from the 12 OPEX weeks), vol 8.7%, Sharpe 0.61, max drawdown -15.1%. No costs.
candidates.replication: The journal (Journal of Banking & Finance, 2013) is from my memory; Quantpedia cites SSRN 1571786. Cao, Chordia and Zhan (cited on the Quantpedia page) report third-Friday selling pressure that cuts the monthly IVOL effect by at least 40%. Mandel: T-353/T-438 (SPY OPEX week, -1.2 bps excess, halves disagree) not supported; T-216 (OPEX Friday short straddle, model-priced) supported. Expect decay as weekly and 0DTE expiries dilute monthly concentration.

sources.title: Quantpedia: Option-Expiration Week Effect (Stivers and Sun, SSRN 1571786)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 901 stocks. O/S needs per-stock option volume history, which Mandel does not have (chain snapshots exist only from 2026-10-14 onward). So run it either (a) forward from the capture box, ranking on prior-month O/S, or (b) historically, with a pre-registered proxy for option-active names from a free OCC/Cboe volume ranking, with the look-ahead flagged. Holding: from the Friday close before the third Friday to the third-Friday close. Statistic: difference-in-difference, (high-O/S OPEX week minus the same stocks' non-OPEX weeks) minus the same for low-O/S stocks. Block bootstrap by month, holdout 2011-2026, cost 10 bps round trip. Pre-registered secondary: reversal in the week after OPEX.

candidates.name: Gamma-conditioned market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)
candidates.summary: The return from the previous close to 15:30 predicts the last half-hour return. In S&P 500 futures it does so only when option dealers are net short gamma (NGE < 0), and the effect also scales with leveraged-ETF market share. Mandel's unconditional SPY test (T-427, 2023-11 to 2026-10) failed. A free daily GEX series exists, so the conditional version is testable.
candidates.mechanism: Short-gamma hedgers (option market makers, leveraged-ETF rebalancing) must buy into rallies and sell into declines near the close. That creates momentum into the bell, which reverts over the next days. The other side is liquidity providers and mean-reverters. When dealers are long gamma, their hedging dampens moves instead.
adjacent_variables: leveraged-ETF daily rebalancing demand (L^2-L) x AUM x return
candidates.assets: SPY/ES; QQQ/NQ, IWM/RTY secondary
candidates.claimed_effect: S&P 500 futures, Jan 1996 to May 2020. Slope of the last-half-hour return on the rest-of-day return is 6.63 (t 4.78, R^2 3.58%) when NGE(t-1) < 0 and 0.82 (t 1.03) when NGE >= 0 (coefficients x100). Over 60+ futures from 1974-2020, intraday momentum appears everywhere. Positive net Sharpe for S&P futures at a one-tick cost; no full cost study.
candidates.replication: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018) is the earlier first-half-hour version. In the cross-section of single stocks, Baltussen, Da and Soebhag's 'End-of-Day Reversal' WP (2025) finds the opposite: a last-30-minute reversal of 3.78 bps a day VW (1993-2019) that gamma does not explain. Mandel: T-427 (unconditional SPY) and T-428 (closing reversal) not supported. The gamma-conditioned test is untested; 0DTE growth since 2022 changes intraday dealer gamma.

sources.title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens), JFE 142
End-of-Day Reversal (Baltussen, Da, Soebhag), working paper
SqueezeMetrics DIX/GEX daily history (free CSV)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: SqueezeMetrics GEX daily from 2011-05, published after the close, so use GEX(t-1). Bars: SPY/ES_F 5-min (last 60 days) and 30-/60-min (2 years). Signal: the sign of the return from close t-1 to 15:30 (15:00 on 60-min bars), traded only when GEX(t-1) < 0. The threshold is fixed at 0 and the bottom tercile is a pre-registered secondary. Hold 15:30 to 16:00. Statistics: HAC interaction slope; mean net per trade at 2 bps round trip; negative-GEX minus positive-GEX difference. All of Mandel's bar history is after May 2020, so it is out of sample for the paper. Deflate jointly with T-427.

candidates.name: Treasury pre-auction concession, scaled by auction size
candidates.summary: Secondary-market Treasury prices drop in the few days before auctions and recover shortly after, even though auction size and timing are announced in advance. The authors link this to dealers' limited risk-bearing capacity. Mandel's T-442 tested only the post-auction leg on TLT and failed. The pre-auction leg and the size conditioning are untested, and the free Fiscal Data API now gives point-in-time announcement dates and sizes.
candidates.mechanism: Dealers must absorb lumpy new supply, so they cheapen the issue beforehand. End investors' capital moves slowly and arrives after the auction. The other side is the Treasury, which bears a hidden issuance cost, and the dealers.
variables: calendars: Treasury auction announcement and auction dates
candidates.assets: Treasury ETFs (IEF, TLT) / CME Treasury futures
candidates.horizon: days (about t-5 to t+2 around the auction)
candidates.claimed_effect: Prices drop significantly in the days before auctions and recover shortly after. The implied hidden issuance cost is 9-18 bps of the auction size, over half a billion dollars at 2007 issuance. The sample period is not verified; my memory says roughly the 1980s to 2008.
candidates.replication: Mandel T-442 (TLT from the close of a 10/30-year auction day to 3 days later, 2002-2026) not supported. That tested only the recovery leg, so this is a duplicate-adjacent successor. Post-publication decay is unknown (the search budget ran out). Quantpedia's BTC seasonality page cites this paper as a canonical calendar anomaly.

sources.title: Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets (Lou, Yan, Zhang), RFS 26(8)
US Treasury Fiscal Data: Treasury Securities Auctions Data API

candidates.proposed_test: Auctions: nominal 2-, 5-, 7-, 10-, 20- and 30-year coupons from the Fiscal Data API (announcemt_date, auction_date, offering_amt, primary_dealer_accepted), clustered by ISO week as in T-442. Outcome: the synthetic same-tenor total return from FRED DGS2/5/10/30 (T-574 method) and IEF/TLT. Windows: close t-5 to close t-1 (concession; predicted negative) and close t-1 to close t+2 (recovery). Size signal: offering amount z-score vs the trailing 12-month same-tenor mean, known at announcement. Statistics: mean concession vs matched non-auction weeks; slope of the concession on size z; holdout 2014-2026 (after publication); both halves; cost 2 bps per round trip.

candidates.name: Payday (16th-of-month) anomaly
candidates.summary: Ma and Pratt report that the S&P 500 return on the 16th of the month is significantly above other days, which they tie to semi-monthly paychecks and retirement-plan contributions. They also say it became less prominent as bi-weekly pay spread. Mandel has a supported turn-of-month effect (T-59) but no mid-month test. The ML F0 features include day of month, but not this pre-specified contrast.
candidates.mechanism: Semi-monthly paydays (15th and last day) deliver 401(k) and brokerage contributions that are invested mechanically the next day. The other side is liquidity providers. The effect weakens as pay schedules diversify.
variables: calendars: day of month, payday schedule
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY; IWM, QQQ secondary)
candidates.claimed_effect: S&P 500: the mean return on the 16th is 0.214% (t 3.07) over the 1980s-2010s and t 2.62 over the 1950s-2010s. Quantpedia (1980-2010): about 2.57% a year, vol 4.31%, Sharpe 0.6 for one day a month. The 16th's decade rank fell in the 2010s. No costs.
candidates.replication: Seen only through the Quantpedia summary of SSRN 3257064. The authors report the effect weakening in the 2010s; I found no independent replication (the search budget ran out). Mandel T-59 (turn of month) supported; T-344/T-547 (turn-of-month replications) not supported.

sources.title: Quantpedia: Payday Anomaly (Ma and Pratt, SSRN 3257064)

candidates.proposed_test: SPY, IWM and QQQ, 1993-2026. Hold from the close of the last trading day before the 16th to the close of the first trading day on or after the 16th. Compare with all other days outside the turn-of-month window (T-59's -4..+3 excluded). The contrast is one pre-specified day: no day-of-month search, and a Bonferroni correction if other days are inspected. Holdout 2011-2026 (after the paper's 1980-2010 sample). Cost 2 bps round trip. Statistic: block-bootstrap difference; both halves positive; SPY primary, others Holm-adjusted.

candidates.name: Informative pre-FOMC price pressure (Arif, Da, Lin)
candidates.summary: Informed investors hedge their market exposure on the day before FOMC meetings, so the average market return on that day reveals their positioning with a minus sign. The return is reversed the next day. The trailing 24-month average of these pre-meeting returns negatively predicts market returns 1 to 24 months ahead, with positive out-of-sample R^2. It is a calendar-selected flow signal at the day-to-month horizon. The input is price on specific calendar days, so it is price-derived and needs the leakage review.
candidates.mechanism: Hedging trades placed when informed-trading intensity is low (and VIX is higher) leave detectable price pressure. Aggregated over meetings it reveals informed investors' net long or short view. The other side is liquidity providers absorbing the hedge.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY)
candidates.claimed_effect: SPY 1994-2023: a one-sd lower trailing-24-month 'FOMC Day -1' return (0.43%) predicts a market return 11.78% higher over the next two years. Adjusted R^2 is 0.34, vs < 0.03 for other FOMC-window days. Out-of-sample R^2 is 7-30% for forecast start dates 2005-2013 (Clark-West significant). Predictability rises with horizon; not significant in 1964-1981.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. The effective sample is small: overlapping 24-month returns over about 30 years give only about 15 independent windows. Mandel T-341 tested statement-day returns, not this predictor. It is new.

sources.title: Informative Price Pressure (Arif, Da, Lin), working paper

candidates.proposed_test: Monthly, 1996-2026. Predictor: the mean SPY close-to-close return on the trading day before each scheduled FOMC meeting's first day (fomc-meetings 'start'), over the trailing 24 months, known at month end. Pre-register which day counts as 'Day -1'. Targets: SPY excess return over the next 1, 3 and 6 months; non-overlapping quarterly sampling is primary. Statistics: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with an expanding window from 2005, Clark-West test, Newey-West lags equal to the horizon. Timing strategy: SPY vs DTB3, 2 bps per switch. Deflate across horizons; expect the 1-month horizon to be weak.

candidates.name: Nontrading-period (weekend/holiday) option mispricing, measured on Cboe put-write indices
candidates.summary: Option returns are significantly lower over nontrading periods, mostly weekends. Delta-hedged index options lose overnight and gain intraday. Two independent top-journal papers attribute this to option prices mis-handling variance while markets are closed. Mandel's quoted-straddle test (T-526) is blocked for lack of quotes. But Mandel already archives Cboe's real option-marked PUT, WPUT, BXM and BXMW daily indices, which allows a direct test with no model pricing.
candidates.mechanism: Option prices decay by calendar time while variance accrues in trading time. Sellers who hold over the weekend collect decay the market fails to charge for. The other side is option buyers (hedgers, retail) paying for the closed period.
variables: options pricing (index put-write and buy-write levels)
calendars: weekends, holidays, time of day
candidates.assets: SPX/SPY options (via Cboe strategy indices; executable as weekly SPY put sales on Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Jones-Shemesh (JF 2018): option returns are significantly lower over nontrading periods, not explained by risk. Muravyev-Ni (JFE 2020): delta-hedged S&P 500 index option returns average -0.7% a day, made up of -1% close-to-open and +0.3% open-to-close, across all maturities and moneyness. Da et al. (WP 2026): intraday straddle returns about +8 bps a day.
candidates.replication: Two independent papers agree on the sign (JF 2018, JFE 2020), and the 2026 Da et al. WP corroborates it. Mandel: T-511 (SPY weekend variance under 1.5x a weeknight) not supported, i.e. weekend realised variance is not small, so a premium would come from mispricing, not low realised moves. T-526 (quoted straddles Friday to Monday) blocked; T-515 (BTC weekend variance lower) supported; T-216 (OPEX short straddle, model-priced) supported. This is a duplicate-adjacent unblock of T-526 using archived data.

sources.title: Option Mispricing around Nontrading Periods (Jones, Shemesh), JF 73(2)
Why do option returns change sign from day to night? (Muravyev, Ni), JFE 136(1)
Intraday Option Return Predictability (Da, Filippou, Goyenko, Zhang, Zhou, Zhou)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: cboe-PUT-history, cboe-WPUT-history, cboe-BXM-history, cboe-BXMW-history daily closes (2006-2026 where available), SPY total return and DTB3. Residual: each index's excess return minus a rolling 60-day beta x SPY excess return, with beta estimated on the prior window. Pre-registered claim: the mean residual over Friday close to Monday close (and pre-holiday to post-holiday) exceeds the mean residual over single weekday intervals. Exclude each index's roll dates, and check Cboe's marking convention (closing mid vs last) before running. Statistics: block bootstrap by week; both halves; 2016-2026 subsample. Tradeable shadow: sell 1-week SPY puts at Friday close and buy back at Monday close, charging captured half-spreads from the capture box.

candidates.name: Quarter-end marking-up in hedge-fund-held stocks (13F cross-section)
candidates.summary: Stocks heavily held by hedge funds earn abnormal returns on the last trading day of a quarter and reverse the next day, much of it in the final minutes. That is consistent with marking up portfolios for reporting. Mandel's index-level versions on IWM (T-346/T-439) failed. The cross-sectional version conditioned on 13F ownership is untested, and the SEC's free 13F data sets cover 2013 onward, after the paper's sample.
candidates.mechanism: Managers with ranking or fee incentives push up the closing prices of their holdings on reporting dates. The prices revert when the pressure stops. The other side is closing-auction liquidity providers and the funds' investors.
variables: calendars: quarter-end, last minutes of the session
candidates.assets: US single stocks
candidates.claimed_effect: Top-quartile hedge-fund-held stocks earn +0.30% abnormal return on the last trading day of the quarter and reverse -0.25% the next day. A substantial share comes in the final minutes; effects are stronger for funds with more incentive to improve their peer ranking. The sample period is from my memory (roughly 2000-2010) and was not verified.
candidates.replication: 'Leaning for the tape' (Carhart, Kaniel, Musto, Reed, 2002, from memory) is the mutual-fund precedent. Mandel T-346/T-439 (IWM quarter-end minus next day, -21 bps net) not supported, with a placebo month-end showing the same sign. After publication and regulatory attention the effect has probably decayed; 2013-2026 is a clean post-publication test.

sources.title: Do Hedge Funds Manipulate Stock Prices? (Ben-David, Franzoni, Landier, Moussawi), JF 68(6)
SEC Form 13F data sets (2013Q2 onward)

candidates.proposed_test: From the SEC 13F data sets, compute each stock's share held by filers classified as hedge funds under a pre-registered rule (a public hedge-fund filer list, or high-turnover concentrated filers). Make it point-in-time by filing acceptance date: at quarter q's end, use the latest holdings filed before that day. Universe: 901 stocks, 2013Q3 to 2026Q3 (about 53 quarters). Returns: last trading day of the quarter (close t-1 to close t) minus SPY, and the next day. Long-short top vs bottom ownership quartile. Statistic: mean (quarter-end minus next-day) spread, bootstrap by quarter, a placebo on non-quarter month ends, both halves. Cost 10 bps round trip.

candidates.name: Same-weekday momentum (Da-Zhang)
candidates.summary: About 70% of stock momentum is continuation on the same weekday (Monday to Monday, and so on), linked to weekly seasonality in institutional trading and fund flows. A strategy that ranks stocks on past same-weekday returns and holds them only on that weekday nearly doubles standard momentum. The inputs are price-derived plus the weekday calendar. It also maps directly to an ML feature (same-weekday mean return) for the T-578 swing program.
candidates.mechanism: Funds with seasonal (same-weekday) flows trade persistently on fixed weekdays, so price pressure repeats on those days. The other side is liquidity providers who do not anticipate the weekly cycle.
candidates.assets: US single stocks
candidates.horizon: days to months (daily rebalanced, monthly formation)
candidates.claimed_effect: US stocks 1963-2021. Daily-rebalanced same-weekday momentum earns 2.05% a month (t 10.94; FF5 alpha 2.18%), vs standard momentum 1.28% (t 5.19) and other-weekday momentum 0.28% (not significant). The same-weekday share of momentum was 39% before 1963, 62% in 1963-1992 and 18% in 1993-2021. No costs, and turnover is very high.
candidates.replication: Related Heston-Sadka seasonality signals are 'clear' in Chen-Zimmermann (MomSeasonShort t 7.6, 1965-2002). Mandel: T-476 (same-calendar-month on 14 ETFs) not supported; T-347 (weekday speculative spread) not supported. The falling share after 1993 and the daily turnover suggest little survives costs. I found no post-publication evidence (the search budget ran out).

sources.title: Same-Weekday Momentum (Da, Zhang), working paper
Chen-Zimmermann signal documentation (MomSeason family)

candidates.proposed_test: 901 stocks, daily, 2000-2026. For weekday k, the formation score is the sum of log returns on weekday-k sessions over months t-12 to t-2. Long the top decile and short the bottom, held only on weekday-k sessions, so the book changes daily. Cost 5 bps per side. Placebo: the other-weekday score, which must be weaker. Statistics: net mean monthly return, block bootstrap, holdout 2010-2026, both halves. Also register 'same-weekday mean return' as an F0-adjacent ML feature, scored by IC in T-578 and deflated with that program's cell count.

rows.name: VIX-build-up conditioned pre-announcement drift (FOMC, NFP, ISM, GDP)

overlaps.note: Unconditional statement-day drift. +17.4 bps net over 1994-2026, but -5.3 bps over 2016-2026, so it failed. The candidate conditions the same window on a VIX build-up.
FOMC close-to-close over 2012-2026: +4.4 bps (CI -15.1 to +23.3). 1994-2011: +31.4 bps.
CPI/NFP/FOMC release-day premium: 2010-2026 -2.7 bps. Per type: CPI +0.6, NFP +4.6.

The mechanism tested with an adjacent ex-ante uncertainty measure (Kalshi/Polymarket p(1-p) three sessions before). It did not predict the 2-session pre-event SPY return: slope p 0.553 over 143 event dates, 2021-2026.
VIX-implied move vs realised move on FOMC days: no out-of-sample signal.
The FOMC-cycle even-week effect also decayed (2017-2026 -5.2 bps).
Confound. Low-IBS next-day reversal (+12 bps). A VIX build-up coincides with falling prices, so the test must separate it from price reversal.

learnings.finding: The unconditional pre-FOMC / statement-day drift is gone after 2015, matching Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert.
Ex-ante event uncertainty from event-contract prices does not scale pre-event SPY returns (2021-2026).
Next-day reversal after weak closes is real on SPY/QQQ/IWM. Any VIX-change slope can be plain price reversal, so a non-event placebo and a reversal control are required.

learnings.source: ML T-578 swing_dev (F0 includes fomc_days, cpi_days)
learnings.finding: Calendar distance features: 306 cells, 0 pass.
Surviving edges are reference-price leads or structural premia. An uncertainty premium is a risk premium, so judge it as a cost-charged expected-return tilt. Published anomalies decay.

rows.missing_data: No ISM release calendar is archived. The rule is the first business day of the month at 10:00 ET; it can be built and checked against the ISM archive, which is free, or ISM can be dropped. There are no pre-release intraday windows before 2024 (ES 5-min bars cover only 60 days). The FOMC window is therefore close-to-close and includes the post-statement move, which costs power.

registration.claim: Over 2010-2026, pooled across scheduled FOMC statement days (window SPY close t-1 to close t) and Employment Situation days (close t-1 to open t), the event-window return rises with the standardized VIX build-up z = (VIX close t-2 minus VIX close t-5) / trailing-250-session sd of 3-session VIX changes, by more than the same z predicts same-type windows on non-event days, net of 2 bps a round trip.
registration.statistic: Interaction coefficient (event slope minus non-event slope) from a pooled OLS of the window return on z, an event dummy and z x event, with Newey-West SE (lag 5). Secondary: top-tercile-z minus bottom-tercile-z mean event return, net.
registration.null: Interaction <= 0: the lagged VIX build-up predicts event-window returns no better than it predicts ordinary next-session returns.
registration.procedure: Events: scheduled decision_day from fomc-meetings (unscheduled excluded) and release days from macro-release-employment-situation. Point in time: Cboe VIX closes at 16:15 ET, after SPY's 16:00 close, so z ends at the t-2 close for a close t-1 entry. A secondary arm uses z through t-1 with an entry at the t open. Terciles are expanding. Controls in the regression: SPY return t-4..t-1 and an IBS<0.2 flag at t-1; these are price-derived controls, never model inputs. Studentized circular block bootstrap of the paired daily series (21-session blocks, 5 seeds) alongside HAC. Halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026; 2016-2026 subsample; FOMC-only and NFP-only subsets; 1994-2009 reported as an in-paper replication.
registration.data: cboe-VIX-history, fomc-meetings, macro-release-employment-situation, macro-release-cpi (secondary), macro-release-gdp (secondary), daily-history-SPY
registration.pass: Interaction > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 under both HAC and block bootstrap; same sign in both halves and in the FOMC-only and NFP-only subsets; top-minus-bottom tercile net of 2 bps > 0; Holm over 2 families x 2 windows, deflated jointly with T-341/T-215/T-343.
registration.controls: One continuous signal, with no threshold and no grid. Costs 2 bps a round trip. CPI and GDP are pre-registered secondaries (Holm). ISM is excluded unless its rule calendar is verified first. 2020-03 and the ZLB years are flagged. Overlap of statement days with CPI sessions is flagged. The non-event placebo slope is reported separately.

rows.notes: Testable now, but power is weak: about 133 FOMC and 200 NFP events in 2010-2026, and the claimed 9 bps per sd is about one SE on FOMC days alone. Expect inconclusive or not_supported. The interaction design matters because a plain VIX-change slope will pick up T-332's reversal. Do not use the t-1 VIX close for a close t-1 entry; that is a 15-minute look-ahead.

rows.name: Post-VIX-spike next-day premium (HVIX days)

overlaps.note: Confound. SPY IBS<0.2 next-day +12 bps. HVIX days are mostly big down days.
IBS reversal on QQQ/IWM/DIA.
IBS reversal is stronger at low Hurst.
After a VIX spike above 30 in backwardation, VIX reverts faster than the curve prices. The same unwinding of uncertainty.
VIX falls after backwardation.
A liquidity-shock signal, controlling for the same-day VIX change, did not predict 20-day returns.
The calendar sleeve's IBS slot would overlap an HVIX rule.

learnings.finding: SPY next-day reversal after weak closes survives costs. The raw HVIX premium is probably largely this.
Vol spikes mean-revert faster than the VIX curve implies, consistent with fast resolution of unexpected uncertainty.
Shock conditioning beyond the VIX change added no forward-return information.
baseline_reversal has positive IC (+0.0487 swing, +0.0256 intraday) but no cell passes after costs.
Price-only rules start from a negative base rate. Only the VIX increment beyond price counts as a non-price input.

rows.missing_data: The 15:55 VIX snapshot exists only on local bars: 60-min for 2 years, 5-min for 60 days. A long-history close-to-close version cannot be made point-in-time. The overnight leg after the 16:15 VIX print would need SPY after-hours prices, which are not archived; Alpaca extended hours could trade it forward.

registration.claim: Over the holdout 2018-06..2026-10 (2000-2026 reported), on days when VIX's close-to-close log change exceeds the expanding 96.8th percentile of all prior daily log changes since 1990, SPY's return from the t+1 open to the t+1 close exceeds the same-window return on control days in the same expanding SPY close-to-close return decile without a spike, by more than 2 bps a round trip.
registration.statistic: Mean HVIX next-session open-to-close return minus the mean of decile-matched non-HVIX control days (bps). Secondary: raw HVIX mean minus unconditional; HVIX with IBS<0.2 vs IBS<0.2 alone.
registration.null: Difference <= 2 bps: the VIX spike adds nothing beyond the day's price move.
registration.procedure: Thresholds and deciles are expanding with no look-ahead. VIX closes at 16:15 ET, so entry is the t+1 official open (daily-history; opens before 2000 are unreliable). Exit is the t+1 close. Events within 5 sessions of a prior event count once (de-clustered) as a robustness arm. Studentized stationary bootstrap with month-clustered event blocks (5 seeds). Holdout halves 2018-06..2022-08 and 2022-09..2026-10. QQQ and IWM are Holm secondaries. The close-to-open leg is reported, not traded. The 15:55-VIX close-to-close arm runs only on the local-bar window and is descriptive.
registration.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM
registration.pass: Holdout difference > 2 bps with one-sided p < 0.05, both holdout halves positive, raw HVIX mean above the unconditional mean; QQQ/IWM Holm-adjusted same sign.
registration.controls: One threshold (96.8th percentile, log change), no grid; costs 2 bps a round trip; 2008/2020 flagged; joint report with T-332 so the sleeve does not double count; DSR over the 3 tickers.

rows.notes: Cheap and fully archived. The real question is incremental: does the implied-vol jump add to price reversal? At about 8 events a year the holdout gives about 66 events with a high daily sd, so power is modest. A pass would add a VIX-gated slot or filter to the T-559 calendar sleeve. A fail still informs it: the IBS slot already captures this.

rows.name: Announcement-day beta premium (Savor-Wilson 'tale of two days')

overlaps.note: The SPY announcement-day premium is +12.7 bps over 1993-2009 but -2.7 bps over 2010-2026. With no announcement-day market premium after 2010, the announcement-day beta slope has nothing to load on.
The FOMC component decayed after 2015.
BAB via SPLV/SPHB ETFs: no positive excess.
SPLV-SPHB -3.23 bps/day over 2011-2026, so high beta outran low beta on ordinary days.
SPHB-SPLV calendar (weekday) contrast failed.

learnings.finding: No announcement-day market premium after 2010. For diversified beta-sorted portfolios, a day's realised cross-sectional beta slope is approximately that day's market excess return. The tradeable SPHB-SPLV version is therefore close to a levered rerun of T-343.
The low-beta anomaly did not survive in ETF form after 2011. The non-announcement-day slope was positive, not flat.
A long-history BAB series allows a 1964-2026 check: BAB announcement-day minus other-day returns should be negative if Savor-Wilson holds.
Published anomalies decay; risk-premium tilts must be cost-charged.

rows.missing_data: The cross-sectional secondary is survivorship-biased: delisted-stock prices are not archived and no free point-in-time source exists here (see the T-392 triage). The ETF primary is complete.

registration.claim: Over 2011-05..2026-10, the SPHB-minus-SPLV close-to-close return on scheduled CPI, Employment Situation and FOMC statement days exceeds its mean on all other days by at least 4 bps (two legs at 2 bps), with both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean SPHB-SPLV return on announcement days minus other days (bps). Secondaries: the daily slope of return on trailing-252-day beta across value-weighted beta deciles, announcement minus other days; and the BAB factor, announcement minus other days, from 1964.
registration.procedure: Announcement set: the union of release days, one flag per day, all dates scheduled in advance. Window close t-1 to close t. Studentized circular block bootstrap of the day-flagged series (21-session blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2011-05..2018-12 and 2019-2026. Per type, Holm over 3. Cross-sectional secondary: betas from 252 sessions to t-1 against SPY; point-in-time S&P 500 members from fja-sp500-components; weights from SEC shares at filing acceptance times the prior close; names without archived prices are counted and flagged.
registration.data: daily-history-SPHB, daily-history-SPLV, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation, fomc-meetings, aqr-bab-daily, sec-companyfacts, fja-sp500-components
registration.pass: Difference > 4 bps with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive; the cross-sectional secondary has the same sign. Deflated jointly with T-343 (Holm over 2).
registration.controls: Turn-of-month and pre-holiday overlaps reported; FOMC-only, CPI-only and NFP-only splits; costs 2 bps per leg per switch; survivorship flagged on the secondary; no grid.

rows.notes: Low prior. T-343's 2010-2026 result already settles most of it mechanically. Worth running only as a cheap confirmation, because every input is archived. The BAB long history (1964-) gives an in-paper replication without the ETF window.

overlaps.note: Unconditional monthly G10 carry over 2013-2026: net Sharpe -0.30.
G10+EM carry failed.
A calendar-conditioned G10-vs-USD basket (last two days of the month): +3.82 bps, positive in 9 of 9 currencies, but p 0.196.
Currency momentum failed.

Calendar FX flows have the expected sign in every G10 currency but are too small for daily FX noise.

The Cboe PUT index beats BXM on Sharpe on real index marks.

The SPX variance risk premium is positive.
Calendar-conditioned short-vol premium (OPEX Friday).

Short-vol forms carry catastrophic months (BTC straddle -88% in a month). Size so a tail event changes nothing, and use defined-risk spreads for any trade.

Residual = index return minus DTB3 accrual minus a trailing 60-interval beta times the ^GSPC excess return.

registration.null: Difference <= 0: option marks are not cheaper to hold short over nontrading days.
registration.procedure: Index closes are dated by Cboe publication after 16:15 ET. Beta comes from the prior 60 intervals of the same index (point in time). Excluded: WPUT Thu-Fri intervals (expiry and roll) and PUT intervals spanning the third-Friday roll. Fri-Mon for WPUT is the first weekend of each weekly put, so the same contract is held. Studentized circular block bootstrap by week (4-week blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2007-2016 and 2017-2026. Launch-onward subsample. Weeks with Monday macro releases reported.
registration.data: cboe-WPUT-history, cboe-PUT-history, daily-history--GSPC, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: WPUT difference > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, launch-onward subsample same sign; PUT same sign (Holm over 2).
registration.controls: One beta window, no grid. Back-tested values flagged. Tradeable shadow (forward, not in the pass): sell 1-week SPY puts or defined-risk put spreads at the Friday close and buy back at the Monday close, charging captured half-spreads from the capture box. Index marks carry no costs, so a pass is a premium estimate, not a net trade.

rows.notes: Model-free and archived. It unblocks T-526 and completes the leg T-511 left open. Two independent top-journal papers agree on the sign. Risk: Friday option prices may already embed the weekend decay, which is the null. A pass leads to a defined-risk weekend put-spread shadow on the capture box before any money, because short-vol tails are the known hazard.

rows.name: Quarter-end marking-up in hedge-fund-held stocks (13F cross-section)

overlaps.note: IWM quarter-end minus next day was -17.1 bps (the wrong sign); placebo month ends -26.7.
Same claim net of costs: -21.1 bps.
13F data sets plus missing delisted-stock prices block any 13F cross-section.
Month-end flows exist, but they are rebalancing flows, not mark-ups.

learnings.finding: No index-level quarter-end mark-up and reversal in 2000-2026; the sign is reversed.
Delisted prices are unavailable free, so 13F-conditioned cross-sections are survivorship-biased.
Published anomalies decay, and this one drew regulatory attention after 2013.

rows.missing_data: SEC Form 13F data sets (2013Q2 onward; free from sec.gov, not archived). A pre-registered hedge-fund filer classification rule (no free canonical list). Delisted-stock prices (no free source here).

registration.claim: Over 2013Q3-2026Q3, the top-minus-bottom quartile of hedge-fund 13F ownership share (latest holdings filed before quarter end) earns a positive SPY-adjusted return on the last trading day of the quarter minus the next day, net of 10 bps a round trip, with both halves positive and no effect at non-quarter month ends.
registration.statistic: Mean (quarter-end minus next-day) long-short spread (bps), bootstrap by quarter.
registration.procedure: 13F holdings aligned by filing acceptance date. Hedge-fund classification by a rule fixed before any return is read. Studentized bootstrap by quarter. Placebo at non-quarter month ends. Halves 2013-2019 and 2020-2026.
registration.data: SEC 13F data sets (to fetch), sec-submissions, daily-history (901)
registration.pass: Spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, placebo not significant (two-sided p > 0.1).
registration.controls: Costs 10 bps; survivorship flagged; classification rule frozen; one quartile cut.

rows.notes: Not worth the 13F ingest now. The index-level tests already have the wrong sign, and the effect probably decayed after publication and regulatory scrutiny.

rows.name: Same-weekday momentum (Da-Zhang)

overlaps.note: Same-calendar-month return seasonality on 14 ETFs failed.
No weekday effect in SPY.
SPHB-SPLV weekday contrast failed.
Sector residual momentum failed.

learnings.finding: Return-seasonality rules (calendar month, weekday) do not survive in Mandel's ETF data.
Weekday features: 0 of 306 cells pass.
The same-weekday share of momentum fell to 18% in 1993-2021, and daily rebalancing turnover is extreme.
Price-only strategies start from a negative base rate; costs decide.

rows.missing_data: Delisted-stock prices: the 901 histories are mostly current names and include only a few delisted ones, and no free point-in-time source exists here (the T-392 triage). A decile long-short momentum book is biased by missing losers. The F0-adjacent ML feature (same-weekday mean return) is testable on the local 123-symbol daily bars inside T-578.

registration.claim: Over 2010-2026, on point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, a long-top-decile / short-bottom-decile book on the past same-weekday return score (sum of log returns on weekday-k sessions over months t-12..t-2), held only on weekday-k sessions, earns a positive mean monthly return net of 5 bps per side, and more than the other-weekday placebo score.
registration.statistic: Net mean monthly return of the same-weekday book. Its difference from the other-weekday placebo book.
registration.procedure: Monthly formation from scores known at month end. Daily book changes. Studentized block bootstrap by month (block 3). Halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026. Membership-weighted, with absent names counted. Separately, register a 'same-weekday mean return' feature for T-578, scored by IC and deflated with that program's cell count.
registration.data: daily-history (901), fja-sp500-components
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, placebo weaker.
registration.controls: Costs 5 bps per side on actual turnover; survivorship flagged; one formation window; no grid.

rows.notes: The strategy is blocked by survivorship and very likely dead after costs. The only cheap use is as one more F0-adjacent feature in the T-578 swing program, deflated with its 306 cells.

rows.name: VIX-build-up conditioned pre-announcement drift (FOMC, NFP, ISM, GDP)
rows.source_notes: I opened NBER w25817 (rev. March 2020, Hu, Pan, Wang, Zhu) as PDF text. Confirmed: Sep 1994 to May 2018, S&P 500 futures, window 4 pm t-1 to 5 min before the release. FOMC +27.14 bps (t 5.95, 190 statements), NFP +10.10 (t 3.63), ISM +9.14 (t 2.10), GDP +7.46 (t 2.08). Table 4: FOMC slope on dVIX[-3,-1] is 3.66 (t 2.20); times the sd of 2.50 that gives 9.15 bps. The 6-day window gives 2.48 (t 1.39). Non-event placebo slope -0.85 (t -0.52). Two corrections to the candidate. (1) For the pooled macro releases (718 events) the 3-day VIX change does NOT predict (0.43, t 0.32). Only the 6-day window does (3.63, t 2.50). So a pooled FOMC+NFP design on one 3-day signal contradicts the paper. (2) The paper's accumulation window is days -6..-1, not -3..-1; the 1.88-point / -81.8 bps figures refer to -6..-1. Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert (FRL 40, 2021) confirmed on IDEAS: the drift 'essentially disappeared after 2015', with and without press conferences.
rows.replication_concerns: The shared web-search budget was used up before this row. I could not search for a post-2018 test of the conditional version; only direct fetches were possible. Mandel's record: the unconditional drift is gone (T-341 2016-2026 -5.3 bps; T-215 2012-2026 +4.4 bps, CI -15 to +23). T-358 found that ex-ante event-contract uncertainty did not scale the pre-event SPY return (p 0.553). The paper's FOMC slope is t 2.2 on 190 events. The roughly 67 post-paper FOMC events (2018-06..2026-10) imply an expected t of about 1.3 at full size. The macro arm carries a forking risk: the authors moved to a 6-day window after the 3-day one failed. A VIX build-up coincides with falling prices, so T-332's reversal must be controlled.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX-history: 1990-01-02..2026-10-14, 9,294 rows, close stamped 21:15 UTC (16:15 ET). fomc-meetings: 276 rows, 1994-02..2027-12, with start/decision_day and a scheduled flag (271 scheduled, 5 unscheduled). macro-release-employment-situation: 860 releases 1955-05..2026-10-02, stamped 12:30 UTC. daily-history-SPY: 1993-01-29..2026-10-14. Local 60m SPY bars start 2023-11-21 and cover only about 20 FOMC days, so the intraday pre-statement window is descriptive only. No ISM calendar is archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: VIX closes at 16:15 ET (16:00 before 2003, per the paper), after SPY's 16:00 close. So z must end at the t-2 close for a t-1 close entry. The paper's own dVIX[t-3,t-1] includes the t-1 close and cannot be traded at 16:00. The daily FOMC window (close t-1 to close t) includes the post-statement move. The NFP window (close t-1 to open t) includes the 8:30 reaction. Terciles must be expanding. Unscheduled meetings are excluded because they were not known in advance.
rows.missing_data: ISM release calendar (not archived; ISM is dropped). Intraday pre-release SPY/ES windows before 2023-11.

final.claim: Over 2010-01..2026-10, on scheduled FOMC statement days, SPY's close(t-1)-to-close(t) return rises with the lagged VIX build-up z = (VIX close t-2 minus VIX close t-5) / trailing-250-session sd of 3-session VIX changes. This is the paper's 3-day accumulation change shifted one session so it is known at the t-1 close. The rise must exceed what the same z predicts for the next-session SPY return on non-event days.
final.statistic: Interaction b3 from an OLS over all sessions: r(close t-1 -> close t) = a + b1 z + b2 D + b3 z*D + c1 r(close t-5 -> close t-2) + c2 1{IBS(t-1) < 0.2}, with D = 1 on scheduled FOMC statement days; Newey-West lag 5. Secondary arm: Employment Situation days with the paper's 6-day macro window, z6 = (VIX t-2 minus VIX t-8) / trailing sd of 6-session changes, window close t-1 -> open t. Reported: the top-minus-bottom expanding-tercile mean event return net of 2 bps.
final.null: b3 <= 0: the lagged VIX build-up predicts statement-day returns no better than it predicts ordinary next-session returns.
final.procedure: z uses closes through t-2 only; its sd comes from the trailing 250 sessions ending at t-2. Events are the decision_day of scheduled rows in fomc-meetings; unscheduled meetings are excluded. Primary sample 2010-01..2026-10. Halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026. The post-paper subsample 2018-06..2026-10 is reported. The 1994-2009 run is reported as an in-paper replication and is not in the pass. Inference: HAC plus a studentized circular block bootstrap of the paired daily series (21-session blocks, 5 seeds). The price terms are controls only, never model inputs.
final.data: cboe-VIX-history, fomc-meetings, macro-release-employment-situation, daily-history-SPY
final.pass: b3 > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 under both HAC and the block bootstrap. b3 > 0 in both halves and in 2018-06..2026-10. Top-minus-bottom tercile mean net of 2 bps > 0. Holm over the 2 arms (FOMC primary, NFP secondary), deflated jointly with T-341/T-215/T-343.
final.controls: One continuous signal per arm. Window lengths are fixed from the paper (3 sessions for FOMC, 6 for macro); no grid. Cost 2 bps a round trip. CPI, GDP and ISM are not added as arms. Statement days that share a session with a CPI or NFP release are flagged. 2020-03 and the ZLB years are flagged. The non-event placebo slope b1 is reported separately and should be near zero.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the conditional version is not registered. But the candidate's pooled FOMC+NFP 3-day design contradicts the paper, where the 3-day change fails for macro releases, and its t-1 VIX timing is a 15-minute look-ahead. The fix uses the paper's own window per family, shifted one session, and tests the event-versus-non-event interaction. Power is about 1 SE at full size.

rows.name: Post-VIX-spike next-day premium (HVIX days)
rows.source_notes: Same NBER w25817 PDF. Confirmed: an HVIX day is the session after a day when VIX_t minus its EWMA through t-1 (eq. 6-7, decay 0.3) is at least 3.0 vol points. It is not a percentile of daily changes. Baseline next-day close-to-close S&P 500 return 57.22 bps (t 3.24), trimmed 54.73 (t 3.73), Sep 1994 to May 2018. Table 6: with the 3:45 pm intraday VIX there are about 6.5 events a year and the return is 46.94 bps, so in the paper the effect survives the 16:15 timing problem. Section 5.2: the authors concede that large price drops 'capture the same information'. They argue only that VIX is less noisy, which is the overlap with T-332.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication found. The web-search budget was used up, so post-2018 decay could not be searched. The authors' own Section 5.2 implies that the VIX input adds little beyond the price drop. Mandel T-332/T-570 (IBS reversal) are supported. T-421 found that shock conditioning added no forward information beyond the VIX change. At about 6.5 events a year the 2018-06..2026-10 holdout holds about 55 events, clustered in 2020-03, 2022 and 2025-04.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX-history: daily OHLC 1990-01-02..2026-10-14. daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29.., QQQ 1999-03-10.., IWM 2000-05-26.., all to 2026-10-14, with official opens and closes. Local 60m IDX_VIX bars start in 2024-01 and 60m SPY bars in 2023-11. That is too short for a 3:45 pm VIX history, so it is descriptive only.
rows.lookahead_risks: The VIX close is at 16:15 ET (16:00 before 2003) and SPY closes at 16:00. A close(t)-to-close(t+1) trade keyed on the VIX close is therefore a 15-minute look-ahead, so the primary trade runs from the t+1 open to the t+1 close. The EWMA and the decile cutoffs must be computed from past data only. Yahoo opens before about 2000 are unreliable; the holdout starts 2018-06. Event de-clustering may use only past events.
rows.missing_data: Intraday VIX history before 2024, needed to run the paper's 3:45 pm close-to-close variant point in time. SPY after-hours prices for the overnight leg.

final.claim: Over 2018-06..2026-10 (after Hu et al.'s sample), on sessions t+1 that follow a day t on which the VIX close exceeds its EWMA through t-1 (decay 0.3, as in the paper) by at least 3.0 vol points, SPY's t+1 open-to-close return exceeds the mean t+1 open-to-close return of non-spike days in the same expanding decile of the day-t SPY close-to-close return by more than 2 bps.
final.statistic: Mean HVIX t+1 open-to-close return minus the mean over decile-matched non-HVIX control days (bps). Reported secondaries: the raw HVIX mean minus the unconditional open-to-close mean; HVIX days with IBS < 0.2 vs IBS < 0.2 days alone; the close(t)-to-open(t+1) leg, which is not tradeable.
final.null: Difference <= 2 bps: the VIX spike adds nothing beyond the day's price move.
final.procedure: EWMA mu(t-1) = (1-0.3) * sum_k 0.3^k VIX(t-1-k), as in eq. 7, computed from 1990. The rule is fixed at 3.0 points, with no grid. Decile cutoffs of SPY close-to-close returns are expanding from 1993. Entry at the t+1 official open, exit at the t+1 official close. In a de-clustered robustness arm, events within 5 sessions of a prior event count once. Studentized stationary bootstrap with month-clustered event blocks (5 seeds). Holdout halves 2018-06..2022-08 and 2022-09..2026-10. 2000-2018 reported as in-paper. QQQ and IWM are Holm secondaries.
final.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM
final.pass: Holdout difference > 2 bps with one-sided p < 0.05. Both holdout halves positive. Raw HVIX mean above the unconditional open-to-close mean. QQQ and IWM the same sign after Holm.
final.controls: One threshold, taken from the paper (3.0 points over an EWMA with decay 0.3). Cost 2 bps a round trip. 2020-03 and 2022 flagged. Reported jointly with T-332 so the calendar sleeve does not double count. DSR over the 3 tickers. With fewer than 40 holdout events the verdict is inconclusive.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the candidate's spike rule (the 96.8th percentile of daily changes) is not the paper's rule and would add an unregistered threshold. The fix uses the paper's EWMA rule, a point-in-time open entry, and a decile-matched control that separates the VIX input from T-332's price reversal.

rows.name: Announcement-day beta premium (Savor-Wilson 'tale of two days')
rows.source_notes: The IDEAS page of JFE 113(2), 2014, 171-201 confirms the authors, title and abstract. Average returns of risky assets are significantly higher on announcement days, and beta is strongly related to average returns on those days, for stocks, test portfolios, bonds and currencies. The 1964-2011 sample and the 'flat slope on other days' are not on the page (full text paywalled). Wachter-Zhu NBER w24432 (March 2018) confirmed: the beta-return relation is 'much stronger' on announcement days. Its replication window (to 2016-09) is not on the page.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2016 out-of-sample test was found; the search budget was used up. Mandel: T-343 found the SPY announcement-day premium at -2.7 bps over 2010-2026. T-384 found SPLV-SPHB at -3.23 bps/day over 2011-2026: high beta outran low beta on ordinary days, which contradicts a flat non-announcement slope. T-387, the beta-neutral SPLV/SPHB BAB, failed. For diversified beta-sorted portfolios, a day's realised slope is about that day's market excess return times the beta spread.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPHB and daily-history-SPLV: 2011-05-05..2026-10-14, 3,884 rows each. aqr-bab-daily: 1930-12-01..2026-07-31, 25,369 rows; AQR revises history and keeps no vintages. macro-release-cpi (1972..2026-10-14), macro-release-employment-situation and fomc-meetings are present. A cross-section on the 901 symbols would be survivor-biased: they are current constituents with few delisted names.
rows.lookahead_risks: Rolling betas must end at t-1. AQR BAB is revised monthly, so it is a research series, not a point-in-time signal. The 901-symbol universe is today's survivors. SEC share counts need alignment to filing acceptance dates.
rows.missing_data: Delisted-stock prices for an unbiased cross-section.

final.claim: Over 2012-01..2026-07 (after Savor-Wilson's 1964-2011 sample), the AQR BAB-USA daily return is lower on scheduled CPI, Employment Situation and FOMC statement days than on all other days, so the low-beta premium is earned on non-announcement days.
final.statistic: Mean BAB return on other days minus the mean on announcement days (bps). Tradeable check: the ex-ante beta-neutral SPLV-levered / SPHB-delevered spread (T-387 construction), split the same way over 2011-05..2026-10.
final.procedure: One flag per day for the union of scheduled releases; window close t-1 to close t. Studentized circular block bootstrap (21-session blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2012-2018 and 2019-2026. 1964-2011 reported as an in-paper replication.
final.data: aqr-bab-daily, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation, fomc-meetings, daily-history-SPHB, daily-history-SPLV, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Difference > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, and the ETF spread the same sign net of 2 bps per leg per switch. Holm jointly with T-343.
final.controls: No grid. Turn-of-month and pre-holiday overlaps reported. Per-release splits Holm over 3. Back-revisions of the AQR series flagged.

rows.reason: Drop as T-343 in substance. The tradeable SPHB-minus-SPLV announcement contrast is about 0.9 times the market's own announcement-day contrast, which T-343 already put at -2.7 bps over 2010-2026. The only non-mechanical implication, that low-beta alpha is concentrated on non-announcement days, is a calendar split of T-387/T-384, both of which went the wrong way after 2011. It would add a test with a near-zero prior and about 1 SE of power. The final registration above is kept for the record only.

rows.name: FOMC-day short-dollar carry (Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi, Vedolin)
rows.source_notes: I opened the FMG/SRC Discussion Paper 54 (January 2016) as PDF text; it was published in JF 2017, and I did not open the journal page. Confirmed: tick data 1994-01-01..2010-12-31 sampled at 4 pm ET. pf3, the three highest-rate currencies, earns 16.83 bps on announcement days vs 1.67 on other days (difference 15.17, t 2.43). pf1: 5.71 vs -0.55 (t 1.17). DOL: difference 12.10 (t 2.34). AUD: 21.76 vs 0.98 (t 2.72). Sharpe ratios reach 0.5 after bid-ask costs. Correction: the candidate says the move 'arrives after the 2:15 pm release'. The paper says the opposite: about 75% of the 4 pm-to-4 pm return is earned between 4 pm t-1 and 2:15 pm, and pre-announcement returns are significant while post-announcement returns are not. What loses significance is a misaligned window, sampled 2:15-to-2:15 or at the 4 pm London fix.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2010 replication was found (the search budget was used up), so 2011-2026 is a clean holdout that no one has tested. Mandel: T-368/T-431 (carry) failed over 2013-2026. T-575 (month-end USD weakness) had the expected sign in 9 of 9 currencies but p 0.196: calendar FX effects tend to be small next to daily FX noise. The Kelly child notes that FOMC decisions were telegraphed in 2024-25, which predicts a small premium. Because the paper shows that misaligned sampling kills significance, the candidate's noon(t)-to-noon(t+1) window, which misses the 4 pm t-1 to noon t pre-announcement leg, is set up to fail.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10: FRED H.10 noon New York rates, observed_at 17:00 UTC. EUR from 1999-01-04; GBP, AUD, NZD, JPY, CHF, CAD, NOK and SEK from 1971; all to 2026-10-09 (MXN and ZAR are also present but are not G10). fx-rates-3m: monthly OECD 3-month rates. EUR and GBP end at 2026-01 (stale), JPY starts 2002-04, CHF 1999-07, the others run to 2026-07/08. fred-DFF 1954..2026-10-13. cboe-VXTLT-history 2004-01-02..2026-10-14. Local 60m bars cover about 2 years for EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD and USDCHF.
rows.lookahead_risks: The Fed releases H.10 noon rates weekly, so the bundle's same-day available_at is optimistic. These rates only measure the outcome, though: the signal (the FOMC calendar and month-end rate ranks) is known in advance. Ranks must use month m-1 rates available at the end of month m, because OECD monthly prints are lagged. EUR/GBP rates forward-filled after 2026-01 must be flagged. The statement time was 14:15 ET before 2013 and 14:00 after; both fall inside a noon-to-noon window.
rows.missing_data: A 4 pm ET daily FX history (only H.10 noon rates are archived; 4 pm sampling exists only on the 2-year local bars). OANDA spread history for NOK and SEK.

final.claim: Over 2011-01..2026-10 (after the paper's 1994-2010 sample), an equal-weight basket long the three highest-yielding non-USD G10 currencies against USD earns more over the two-day noon(t-1)-to-noon(t+1) window around each scheduled FOMC statement day t than twice its mean noon-to-noon daily return on non-FOMC days, by more than 3 bps. The basket is re-ranked at each month end on one-month-lagged OECD 3-month rates.
final.statistic: Mean basket log return over FOMC windows noon(t-1)->noon(t+1), minus 2 x the mean noon-to-noon daily basket return on days outside any FOMC window (bps). Secondary: the equal-weight 9-currency DOL basket.
final.procedure: The two-day noon window is the shortest window in the H.10 data that contains the paper's whole 4 pm(t-1)->4 pm(t) announcement-day span. Only windows in which every basket currency prints are used. The top 3 are re-ranked at each month end on rates known then. Two nulls must both pass: a date permutation that moves FOMC windows to random non-FOMC weeks at the same position in the month (10,000 draws), and a studentized circular block bootstrap (21-day blocks). Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. Timing check on local 60m bars, 2024-2026: the 16:00(t-1)->14:00 and 14:00->16:00 legs are reported but are not in the pass.
final.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fomc-meetings, fred-DFF, cboe-VXTLT-history
final.pass: Difference > 3 bps with one-sided p < 0.05 under both nulls, and both halves positive. DOL the same sign after Holm over 2.
final.controls: Costs of 1.5 bps a side per major currency and 4 bps a side for NOK and SEK, to be checked against OANDA before any trade. Windows that overlap the last two trading days of a month (T-575) and CPI release days are dummied and reported. The ZLB years 2011-2015 are flagged. Pre-registered secondaries, Holm over 2: an easing interaction (the fred-DFF 30-day mean down more than 20 bps over the prior 6 months) and a VXTLT-level interaction. No other thresholds.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the candidate misreads the paper's timing. Its noon-to-noon window would miss most of the pre-announcement return, which the paper says carries the premium. The fix uses the two-day noon window that contains the paper's 4 pm-to-4 pm span and adds a month-end control for T-575.

rows.name: Post-FOMC announcement drift in Treasury yields (Brooks, Katz, Lustig)
rows.source_notes: I opened NBER w25127 (October 2018, revised April 2019), both the abstract page and the PDF text. Confirmed: 157 regularly scheduled FOMC meetings, 1989-06-05..2008-10-29. The surprise is Kuttner's (2001) current-month fed funds futures surprise. A 10 bp surprise moves the 10-year yield 1.7 bps on the day and 14 bps after 50 days, then partly reverts. The effect comes mostly from positive surprises. The proposed mechanism is bond-fund outflows after salient target increases. Correction: the candidate's holdout '2019-2026 (after the paper)' is wrong. The paper's sample ends 2008-10, so all of 2008-11..2026-10 is out of sample, much of it at the ZLB.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication was found (search budget used up). Mandel T-361 (SPY after DGS2 surprises) had only 85 classified meetings and failed its min_n.
