T-484 found no slow trend in Treasuries. T-574 shows that Treasury flow effects exist but have decayed since 2022. The fed funds futures surprise is not archived; dDTB3 and dDGS2 are noisier proxies that mix in path news and bill-supply noise. ZLB meetings (2008-12..2015-12 and 2020-03..2022-03) carry almost no surprise variance, so the effective holdout is about 60-70 meetings.
rows.data_notes: fomc-meetings covers 1994-2027 with a scheduled flag; the paper's 1989-1993 meetings are not archived. fred-DTB3 1954..2026-10-13. fred-DGS2 1976-06..2026-10-13. fred-DGS10 1962..2026-10-13. fred-DFF present. daily-history-IEF 2002-07-30..2026-10-14. The FRED H.15 rows carry an available_at of 20:00 UTC on the same day, which is optimistic: H.15 posts the next business day.
rows.lookahead_risks: FRED H.15 values post the next business day, so a signal built from FRED closes cannot be traded at the t+1 close; entry is at the t+2 close. 50-session windows overlap the next meeting, which HAC handles. ETF entries use official closes.
rows.missing_data: Kuttner fed funds futures surprises (CME ZQ history, not free). The FRED target-rate series (free but not archived).

final.claim: Over 2008-11..2026-10 (after Brooks-Katz-Lustig's 1989-2008 sample), across scheduled FOMC meetings, the DGS10 change from the t+2 close to the t+22 close has a positive slope on the statement-day 3-month bill surprise s = DTB3(t) - DTB3(t-1). A duration-scaled IEF position sized in proportion to -s, capped at +/-2 sd, entered at the t+2 close and held 20 sessions, earns a positive mean net of 2 bps a round trip.
final.statistic: OLS slope of dDGS10(t+2 -> t+22) on s across all scheduled meetings in the holdout (Newey-West, lag of 1 meeting). Mean net return per meeting of the proportional IEF trade. Reported: 10- and 50-session horizons, DGS2 as the surprise (T-361's measure), and a 1994-2008 in-paper replication.
final.procedure: s comes from FRED closes on t and t-1. Entry is at the t+2 close because H.15 posts the next business day. Inference: a studentized bootstrap over meetings plus a permutation of s across meetings (10,000 draws). Holdout halves 2008-11..2017-12 and 2018-01..2026-10. Unscheduled meetings are excluded. ZLB meetings are kept (they carry little leverage) and flagged. Positive and negative s are reported separately, since the paper finds the drift mostly after positive surprises.
final.data: fomc-meetings, fred-DTB3, fred-DGS2, fred-DGS10, fred-DFF, daily-history-IEF
final.pass: Slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 under both the bootstrap and the permutation, positive in both holdout halves, and a trade mean net > 0, with at least 60 scheduled holdout meetings outside the ZLB (DFF above 0.25%). With fewer, the verdict is inconclusive.
final.controls: No threshold: sizing is proportional, with one cap. Costs 2 bps a round trip. Month-end sessions (T-574) and CPI days inside the window are reported. A 20-session window cannot overlap the next meeting; at 50 sessions the overlap is HAC-handled.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the bond version is untested. But the candidate's post-paper holdout date is wrong, and its DGS2 surprise mixes in path news. The fix moves the holdout to 2008-11 onward, uses the closest archived proxy for the near-term target surprise, and replaces the trading threshold with proportional sizing.

rows.name: Dash-for-cash month-end cycle with the settlement-cycle shift as a natural experiment
rows.source_notes: I opened the open-access RFS 33(1) 2020 PDF (Etula, Rinne, Suominen, Vaittinen). Confirmed: T is the last trading day of the month. The T+3 sample runs July 1995 to December 2013. Pensions must sell by the close of T-4 to have cash on the morning of T; Treasuries (T+1) can be sold until the close of T-2. Over 2003-2013 the reversal windows earned +103% cumulative (73% of the market's excess return) against -31% in the selling windows, and corr(T-3..T-1, T-8..T-4) = -0.54. A footnote notes the US move to T+2 in September 2017. The paper already ran this natural experiment on Europe's T+3->T+2 switch of 2014-10-06 (Table 3): the autocorrelation at T-2, i.e. corr(r(T-3), r(T-2)), fell by 0.777 (t -3.20), treated countries against controls that include the US, one year on either side. So the US 2017 and 2024 shifts are an out-of-sample replication of the paper's own causal test. The US T+1 date (2024-05-28) was not checked against an SEC release in this run.
rows.replication_concerns: The search budget was used up, so I found no post-2017 US evidence. Mandel: T-59 (turn of month) supported; the T-344/T-443 replications were mixed; T-574 (Treasury month end) supported but decayed since 2022. A mean-return contrast between windows that differ by one edge day has an SE of about 12-15 bps on 81 months, which is too weak. The paper's autocorrelation statistic has more power: the SE of the correlation difference is about 0.13 with 266 vs 81 months. The T+1 era (about 29 months) can only be forward-tracked.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..2026-10-14; IWM from 2000-05-26; IEF from 2002-07-30, so the IEF control has only 2002-2017 in the T+3 era. fomc-meetings present. The daily-events family includes SPY ex-dividend dates. Month positions must come from the trading days in the price files.
rows.lookahead_risks: Month position T comes from the realised NYSE calendar. Holidays are scheduled in advance, but unscheduled closures (2012-10-29/30, 2018-12-05, 2025-01-09) must be treated as known only when they were announced. The settlement-regime dates were fixed in advance. Adjusted closes include dividends, so ex-dividend days near month end are flagged.
rows.missing_data: SOFR (free on FRED, not archived) for the secondary conditioning. ICI fund flows.

final.claim: In the US T+2 settlement regime (2017-09-05..2024-05-24), the cross-month correlation between SPY's returns on day T-3 and day T-2 (T = last trading day of the month) is lower than in the T+3 regime (1995-07..2017-09-01). Etula et al.'s European 2014 natural experiment predicts this when the last selling day moves from T-4 to T-3.
final.statistic: rho(T+2 era) - rho(T+3 era), the Pearson correlation of r(T-3) and r(T-2) across months (the paper's 'autocorrelation at T-2'). Secondary: mean r(T-3) in the T+2 era minus in the T+3 era (bps). Forward-tracked: in the T+1 era (2024-05-28 on), rho of r(T-2) and r(T-1) against the T+2 era.
final.procedure: Month positions come from the trading days in daily-history-SPY. The regimes split at the SEC compliance dates; verify 2017-09-05 and 2024-05-28 against SEC releases before the run. Inference: a month-level bootstrap (months resampled within regime, 10,000 draws) and a permutation of regime labels across months. A Spearman version is reported. IWM gets the same statistic as a Holm secondary. IEF, whose underlying Treasuries settle T+1 throughout, is the no-shift control. T+3-era months 1995-2013 are in-paper; 2014-2017 are reported separately.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history-IWM, daily-history-IEF, daily-events-SPY, fomc-meetings
final.pass: rho difference < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 under both nulls on SPY. IWM the same sign. The IEF difference not significant (two-sided p > 0.1). The T-3 mean-return secondary negative.
final.controls: One statistic, fixed by the paper; no window search. Months with an FOMC statement, a CPI release or an SPY ex-dividend date on T-3 or T-2 are flagged and dropped in a robustness arm. 2020-03 flagged (the Spearman version is the robustness check). Costs do not apply to the statistic; any trading version needs its own registration.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the mechanism test is new for the US, but the candidate's window-shift contrast is underpowered. The fix adopts the paper's own natural-experiment statistic (the autocorrelation at T-2), so the US settlement shifts become a clean out-of-sample replication of a test fixed in advance.

rows.name: Threshold (drift-band) rebalancing signal for stocks vs bonds
rows.source_notes: I opened NBER w33554 (issued March 2025, revised January 2026), both the abstract page and the PDF text. Confirmed: daily futures, 1997-09-10..2023-03-17. The signals are simulated 60/40 equity-weight deviations at the previous close; the threshold signal averages bands of 0-2.5%. Next-day equity returns are about 16 bps lower on the threshold signal and 17 bps on the calendar signal, bonds about +4 / +2 bps. The threshold signal's |t| exceeds 4. The front-running portfolio has a Sharpe ratio above 1 over 1997-2023. A first-half recalibration gives qualitatively similar results. Estimated cost about $16bn a year. The 0-2.5% band range was chosen in-sample, after predictability was seen to vanish above 2.5%, and only partly checked on the first half.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-paper evidence was found (search budget used up). The holdout 2023-03-18..2026-10 is about 3.6 years. Scaling the paper's |t| > 4 over 25.5 years gives an expected holdout t of about 1.5, so inconclusive is the likely verdict. Mandel T-345 (calendar form, supported) and T-450 (continuous month-to-date slope, not supported) bracket it. The signal is price-derived, so it belongs in the flow family with a leakage review.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY from 1993; daily-history-IEF and daily-history-TLT 2002-07-30..2026-10-14; fred-DGS10 1962..2026-10-13 (for the synthetic 10-year as in T-574). The paper used S&P 500 and 10-year note futures; the ETFs and the synthetic return are close proxies.
rows.lookahead_risks: The paper uses the signal at close t to predict close t -> t+1, which needs the t close before the MOC cutoff; reading (b), with the t-1 signal, is the honest version. FRED DGS10 posts the next business day, so for point-in-time use the signal should run on IEF returns (or lag the synthetic leg one day). Percentile triggers must be trailing.
rows.missing_data: None for the test.

final.claim: Over 2023-03-18..2026-10 (after Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone's sample), the threshold rebalancing signal negatively predicts the close(t)-to-close(t+1) return of SPY minus beta-matched IEF, and the prediction survives controls for T-345's calendar signal and turn-of-month dummies. The signal is the mean, over bands 0-2.5% in 0.1% steps, of the simulated 60/40 SPY/IEF equity-weight deviation at the close of t-1.
final.statistic: HAC predictive slope of the next-day SPY - k*IEF return on the standardized signal, where k is the trailing 252-day beta-neutral ratio. Secondary: the mean of -sign(signal) x spread on days when |signal| exceeds its trailing 252-day 80th percentile, net of 2 bps per leg.
final.procedure: Simulate the 26 banded portfolios from SPY and IEF closes (IEF for point-in-time use, with the DGS10 synthetic return as a check). Reset each when |w - 0.6| >= delta and average the deviations. Rule 12, both readings: (a) signal at close t, position close t -> t+1, with MOC optimism flagged; (b) signal at close t-1, position close t -> t+1. Reading (b) is primary. Stationary bootstrap (block 10). The incremental regression adds the T-345 dummy and the T-59 turn-of-month dummies. Placebo bands of 4-6% must be weaker. 2003-2023 reported as in-paper.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history-IEF, fred-DGS10
final.pass: Holdout slope < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 under reading (b) and the same sign under (a). The partial coefficient over T-345 and turn of month negative with p < 0.05. Placebo bands weaker. The secondary trigger's mean net > 0.
final.controls: The band range is taken from the paper and the secondary uses one percentile (the 80th); no grid. Costs 2 bps per leg per trade. 2020-03 and 2022 flagged. Leakage review: the signal is a deterministic transform of past SPY and bond returns.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the threshold signal is not registered (T-345 and T-450 are the calendar and month-to-date forms). But the candidate relied on a percentile trigger and same-close timing. The fix makes the paper's continuous slope on the t-1 signal primary over the post-paper window and requires it to add to T-345.

rows.name: Dividend payment-day price pressure (market level)
rows.source_notes: I opened NBER w30688 (November 2022), both the abstract page and the PDF text. Confirmed: CRSP 1926-2018. A one-sd higher payout yield over days t and t-1 predicts a +3.2 bps value-weighted market return on day t (the unconditional mean is 4.1 bps). Top-quintile payout days return four times the lowest quintile. The past year's top-10 days earn +11.6 bps and the top quarter +7.1 bps (t 4.27). Price multipliers are 1.5-2.3. Asset managers make their largest payouts in Q4, which explains the weak Q4. The paper's main predictor is the payout on t AND t-1, not on t alone, and a robustness check proxies payments by the same calendar day in prior years. I did not re-check the 58-country result or Chen-Zimmermann's DivSeason row.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2018 replication was found (search budget used up). Power is weak: about 3 bps per sd against a daily sd of about 110 bps over about 1,950 holdout days gives t of about 1.3 at full size. Pay dates cluster at the turn of the month and mid-month, so they overlap T-59 and this cluster's 16th-of-month (payday) row.
rows.data_notes: The daily-events-<symbol> bundles (857 of them) hold Yahoo ex-dates and amounts only, with amounts adjusted for later splits; the AAPL file confirms there are no pay or declaration dates. SEC company facts exist only as 36 shard bundles (sec-companyfacts-b000 ...), not under the name 'sec-companyfacts'. fja-sp500-components covers point-in-time members 1996-01-02..2026-08-18. daily-history-SPY present. The pay-date source the registration depends on is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Pay dates must have been declared before t-1. Yahoo amounts are split-adjusted to today, so multiplying them by as-reported SEC shares overstates pre-split payouts unless the split factors are undone. SEC shares must be taken at filing acceptance. A current-snapshot ex-to-pay lag is a look-ahead. Delisted members' dividends are missing, but that affects only the predictor, because the outcome is SPY.
rows.missing_data: Historical dividend pay and declaration dates for S&P 500 members (for example the Nasdaq dividend-history API, unverified, or CRSP). Without them neither the paper's predictor nor its prior-year same-calendar-day proxy can be built.

final.claim: Over 2019-01..2026-10 (after Hartzmark-Solomon's 1926-2018 sample), SPY's close(t-1)-to-close(t) return increases with the aggregate dividend payout yield of point-in-time S&P 500 members paid on days t and t-1 (the sum of declared amount x shares, over total member market cap at t-2). The regression controls for the T-59 turn-of-month window, FOMC/CPI/NFP days and weekday dummies.
final.statistic: Slope of the daily SPY return on the standardized payout yield (HAC). Secondary: the top-minus-bottom expanding-quintile mean (bps), and the net mean of holding SPY long on top-quintile days at 2 bps a round trip.
final.procedure: Only dividends whose pay date was declared before t-1 count. Amounts x shares must be split-consistent: undo Yahoo's split adjustment, or use split-adjusted shares. Quintiles are expanding from 2010. Studentized block bootstrap (21-session blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2019-2022 and 2023-2026. Secondary: the Q1-vs-Q4 interaction. Members without dividend records are counted and flagged.
final.data: daily-events-* (amounts and splits), sec-companyfacts-b* shards (shares), fja-sp500-components, daily-history-SPY, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation, fomc-meetings, plus a pay/declaration-date source (to fetch)
final.pass: Slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, and the top-quintile rule's net mean > 0.
final.controls: Turn-of-month, FOMC/CPI/NFP and weekday dummies, plus a 16th-of-month dummy for the payday row. Cost 2 bps. The quintile cut is fixed. Q4 is expected to be null (a pre-registered secondary).

rows.reason: The source is verified and the market-level channel is new to Mandel, but the test cannot be built yet. Archived dividends carry ex-dates only, so the paper's predictor (payments on t and t-1) needs a pay-date fetch first. The fix also corrects the predictor to the paper's two-day payout and flags the split-adjustment trap.

rows.name: Option-expiration-week premium in high option-activity stocks (Stivers-Sun)
rows.source_notes: I opened the Quantpedia page. The source is Stivers and Sun, 'Returns and Option Activity over the Option-Expiration Week for S&P 100 Stocks' (SSRN 1571786; the page gives no year). The high-O/S strategy uses 28 stocks over 1996-2008, with OPEX-week spreads of 67.9 and 70.7 bps in the two subperiods. The backtest figures (9.3% a year, vol 8.7%, Sharpe 0.61, max drawdown -15.14%) are Quantpedia's, not the paper's. The page confirms Cao-Chordia-Zhan (SSRN 3659479) on third-Friday selling pressure. The SSRN abstract returned 403, so the paper itself and the 'Journal of Banking & Finance 2013' attribution are unverified.
rows.replication_concerns: The paper's universe is S&P 100 stocks, not a 901-stock cross-section. Index-level T-353/T-438 failed (-1.2 bps, halves disagree), and T-192/T-502 found no strike pinning. Weekly and 0DTE expiries dilute the monthly OPEX concentration. ML days_to_opex: 0 of 306 cells pass. Search budget used up, so post-2008 decay could not be searched.
rows.data_notes: The capture box records chains for only 14 underlyings (SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD, SLV, USO, IBIT, ETHA, TSLA, NVDA, AAPL, SPX, VIX), so the proposed forward O/S ranking of 901 stocks cannot be formed. Only the 2026-10-14/15 chain snapshots are archived, and no per-stock option-volume history exists in the archive.
rows.lookahead_risks: Applying today's ranking of 'option-active names' to history is a look-ahead. S&P 100 membership must be point in time. The 901-symbol set is survivor-biased.
rows.missing_data: Per-stock daily option-volume history (OCC or Cboe; a free bulk history is unverified).

final.claim: Over 2011-2026, among the 100 largest point-in-time S&P 500 members by prior-month market cap, the top quintile by prior-month option-to-stock volume ratio earns a larger OPEX-week return (from the Friday close before the third Friday to the third-Friday close) minus its own non-OPEX-week mean than the bottom quintile does, net of 10 bps a round trip.
final.statistic: Difference-in-differences: (high-O/S OPEX week minus the same stocks' non-OPEX weeks) minus the same quantity for low-O/S stocks (bps).
final.procedure: O/S is ranked on the prior calendar month's volumes. Block bootstrap by month. Halves. Secondary: the reversal in the week after OPEX.
final.data: daily-history (901), fja-sp500-components, plus an OCC/Cboe per-stock option-volume history (not available)
final.pass: Difference-in-differences > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive.
final.controls: Costs 10 bps a round trip. The quintile cut is fixed. Earnings weeks excluded. Survivorship flagged. No grid.

rows.reason: Drop: there is no data path. The capture box covers 14 underlyings, not a cross-section, and no option-volume history is archived or verified free. The paper itself could not be opened, and the index-level OPEX-week tests have already failed.

rows.name: Gamma-conditioned market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)
rows.source_notes: I opened the JFE 142 (2021) PDF (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens). Confirmed: futures from December 1974 to May 2020. The last-30-minute return is predicted by the rest-of-day return, from the previous close to the last half hour. For the S&P 500, NGE comes from OptionMetrics for 1996-2017 and is extended with SqueezeMetrics to May 2020. Momentum is present when NGE < 0 and absent when NGE > 0. NGE was negative on 2,930 days and positive on 3,158, i.e. about 48% negative. I did not find the exact coefficients 6.63 (t 4.78) and 0.82 (t 1.03) in the extracted text. I did not open Baltussen-Da-Soebhag's 'End-of-Day Reversal'.
rows.replication_concerns: I fetched SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (2011-05-02..2026-10-20; columns date, price, dix, gex) to inspect it. GEX was negative on only 19 of the 734 sessions since 2023-11-15: 1 in 2024, 9 in 2025 and 9 in 2026. So the candidate's GEX(t-1) < 0 rule has n of about 19 on the local bar window, far below min_n. The published GEX is also negative on only 2-23% of days a year, against 48% for the paper's NGE, so 'GEX < 0' is not the paper's condition. T-427 (first-half-hour predictor) failed at -2.09 bps net with a slope of -0.004, and ML T-577 shows negative continuation at bar scale. 0DTE growth since 2022 has changed intraday dealer gamma. Search budget used up: I found no post-2020 replication.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m SPY bars: 2023-11-21..2026-10, 5,081 rows, about 726 sessions of 7 bars each, stamped at the bar open from 09:30 to 15:30 ET, so the 15:30 bar open exists. 60m QQQ and IWM bars are present. 30m, 15m and 5m bars cover only about 60 days. daily-history-SPY supplies the official close. DIX.csv is not archived; I fetched it only to inspect it.
rows.lookahead_risks: GEX(t) is published after the t close, so the rule must use GEX(t-1). DIX.csv has no vintages and SqueezeMetrics' method is proprietary and may be restated, so the history is not provably point in time; record the fetch date and hash. Yahoo bars are stamped by open time: the entry is the 15:30 bar's open and the exit is the official daily close, not the bar's last trade. The trailing-median split must use prior sessions only.
rows.missing_data: SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (free; archive it with a capture date). An OptionMetrics-style NGE (not free). Leveraged-ETF AUM history.

final.claim: On SPY 60-minute bars 2023-11..2026-10, on sessions after SqueezeMetrics GEX(t-1) is below its trailing 252-session median, holding SPY from the 15:30 bar open to the official close in the direction of the close(t-1)-to-15:30 return earns a positive mean net of 2 bps a round trip, and more than the same rule earns on above-median sessions.
final.statistic: Mean net per trade on below-median-GEX sessions. The below-minus-above difference. The HAC slope of the last-half-hour return on r_ROD x 1{GEX(t-1) below its trailing median}.
final.procedure: GEX(t-1) is taken as archived at fetch, with the date and hash recorded; the trailing median uses the 252 prior sessions. r_ROD runs from the official close of t-1 to the 15:30 bar open. The exit is the official daily close. Early closes are excluded. Block bootstrap by week. QQQ and IWM are Holm secondaries. Deflated jointly with T-427's 60 cells. GEX < 0 is reported descriptively (about 19 sessions).
final.data: local 60m bars SPY/QQQ/IWM (mandel/ml_data), daily-history-SPY, SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (to archive)
final.pass: Below-median mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation, difference > 0, and the same sign on QQQ and IWM.
final.controls: One threshold, the trailing median, chosen because the paper's NGE split is about half the days. Costs 2 bps. FOMC, CPI and OPEX sessions flagged. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the rest-of-day predictor with gamma conditioning is untested. But the candidate's GEX < 0 cutoff leaves about 19 sessions in the bar window and does not match the paper's roughly 50/50 NGE split. The fix uses a trailing-median split and needs DIX.csv archived with a capture date first.

rows.name: Treasury pre-auction concession, scaled by auction size
rows.source_notes: The IDEAS page of RFS 26(8), 1891-1912 (2013) confirms Lou, Yan and Zhang. Secondary-market Treasury prices fall significantly in the few days before auctions and recover shortly after, even though timing and size are announced in advance. The paper attributes this to dealers' limited risk-bearing capacity and end investors' imperfect capital mobility. It puts the hidden issuance cost at 9-18 bps of the auction size, over half a billion dollars at 2007 issuance. Not confirmed: the sample period and the size of the pre-auction drop, which are not on the page (I did not open the full text).
rows.replication_concerns: Search budget used up, so post-publication decay is unknown. Mandel's own T-442 secondary V2 has already been seen: TLT from close t-5 to t-1 averaged -21.1 bps against +6.5 unconditional, an excess of -27.6 bps over 264 10/30-year clusters 2002-2026 (flags-fixed p 0.0022, placement p 0.0005; halves not reported). 121 of those 264 clusters fall in CPI weeks. Because V2 was seen, the TLT and 10/30-year weeks of 2014-2026 are not fresh. The replication must come from the 2-, 5-, 7- and 20-year auction weeks, which fall in other weeks of the month. T-574 shows Treasury flow effects decayed after 2022.
rows.data_notes: treasury-auctions 1979-10-31..2026-10-22: 5,584 rows, made of 2,793 auction-announcement and 2,791 auction-result records, so each auction appears twice. Fields include announcemt_date, offering_amt, reopening, inflation_index_security and floating_rate. The '2-Year' term also covers FRNs (floating_rate = Yes) and the '5-Year' term covers TIPS; both must be filtered out. Reopenings appear under terms such as '9-Year 11-Month', '29-Year 11-Month' and '19-Year 10/11-Month'. The median lag from announcement to auction since 2014 is 5-7 calendar days. fred-DGS2/3/5/7/10/20 run to 2026-10-13/14. There is no fred-DGS30 bundle, so 30-year weeks use DGS20 or TLT. daily-history-IEF/TLT/SHY 2002-07-30..2026-10-14.
rows.lookahead_risks: Auction dates come from the quarterly tentative schedule, known well in advance, but offering amounts only from the announcement about 2-5 sessions before the auction, so the size secondary's window must start after the announcement. FRED H.15 yields post the next business day; that is fine for synthetic returns used as outcomes, but not for a yield-based signal. Announcement and result rows must be deduplicated, and FRNs and TIPS removed.
rows.missing_data: None for the primary. IEI (the 5-7 year ETF) is not archived. Primary-dealer positions and ZN/ZB COT are adjacent only.

final.claim: Over 2014-01..2026-10 (after Lou-Yan-Zhang 2013), consider ISO weeks with a nominal 2-, 5-, 7- or 20-year coupon auction and no 10- or 30-year auction; T-442's V2 never examined these weeks. In those weeks, the 10-year-DV01-equivalent synthetic total return of the auctioned tenors from the close of t-5 to the close of t-1 (t = the week's first auction) is below its unconditional mean over all 4-session windows by more than 2 bps.
final.statistic: Mean excess per cluster (bps): each tenor's window return scaled by D10/Dn and averaged over the cluster's auctioned tenors, minus the same tenors' unconditional mean 4-session return. Secondaries: the same on the 10/30-year weeks (disclosed as already seen), and the slope of the concession on the offering-amount z-score against the trailing 12-month same-tenor mean, measured from the close of the announcement day to t-1.
final.procedure: Deduplicate to one row per CUSIP auction from the announcement records. Keep nominal fixed-coupon notes and bonds; drop FRNs and TIPS; keep reopenings and report them. Synthetic daily return per tenor = y(t-1)/252 - D dy from FRED DGSn (the T-574 method; the 30-year uses DGS20). IEF and SHY are the tradeable checks. Two nulls must both pass: a flags-fixed studentized circular block bootstrap (block 10) and a placement null that moves clusters to random weeks without a coupon auction. Halves 2014-2019 and 2020-2026. An ex-CPI version drops clusters whose window contains a CPI release. Month-end sessions (T-574) are excluded from the windows.
final.data: treasury-auctions, fred-DGS2, fred-DGS5, fred-DGS7, fred-DGS10, fred-DGS20, daily-history-IEF, daily-history-SHY, daily-history-TLT, macro-release-cpi, fomc-meetings
final.pass: Excess < -2 bps with one-sided p < 0.05 under both nulls on the unseen-week clusters, both halves negative, and the ex-CPI version negative with p < 0.1. The 10/30-year-week secondary the same sign. The size slope negative as a Holm secondary (over 2).
final.controls: One window (t-5..t-1, as in the paper and T-442 V2), one cost (2 bps a round trip), no grid. FOMC weeks flagged; 2020-03 and 2022 flagged. Tradeable form: short IEF/SHY or micro Treasury futures over the window, or skip duration in a bond sleeve.

rows.reason: This is the strongest prior in the cluster and the source is verified. But the candidate's pooled 2014-2026 test reuses the 10/30-year TLT weeks Mandel already saw in T-442 V2. The fix makes the unseen 2/5/7/20-year weeks the primary evidence, deduplicates the doubled auction records and removes FRNs and TIPS.

rows.name: Payday (16th-of-month) anomaly
rows.source_notes: I opened the Quantpedia page for Ma and Pratt, 'Payday Anomaly' (SSRN 3257064). Confirmed: t 2.62 (1950s-2010s) and t 3.07 (1980s-2010s). The 0.214% mean is labelled 'annualized' on the page, but 0.214% x 12 = 2.57% matches the 'indicative performance' figure, so it is a per-event mean. Quantpedia's backtest covers 1980-2010 (vol 4.31%, Sharpe 0.6). The 16th's prominence fell in the 2010s, which the abstract attributes to bi-weekly pay. I could not open the SSRN paper (403), so its exact day definition and sample end are unverified. Its tables include the 2010s, so the paper's data overlaps 2011-2017.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication, and the authors themselves report decay. Search budget used up. Mandel: T-59 (turn of month) supported; the T-344/T-443 replications were mixed; ML T-578 day-of-month features pass in 0 of 306 cells. With about 190 events over 2011-2026 the SE is about 8 bps, against an effect the authors say decayed. The 16th often falls in OPEX week (the third Friday is the 15th-21st), and mid-month CPI releases fall near it.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..2026-10-14, QQQ from 1999-03-10, IWM from 2000-05-26; macro-release-cpi and fomc-meetings present.
rows.lookahead_risks: Nothing material: the calendar is known in advance. Use official adjusted closes. Keep to the one pre-specified day; no day-of-month search.
rows.missing_data: None.

final.claim: Over 2011-01..2026-10, SPY's return from the close of the last session before the 16th to the close of the first session on or after the 16th exceeds its mean daily return on sessions outside the T-59 turn-of-month window (-4..+3) by more than 2 bps. Both halves and the post-publication subsample (2018-10 on) must be positive.
final.statistic: Mean 16th-session return minus the mean return of the other sessions (bps).
final.procedure: One pre-specified session per month; no day-of-month search. Studentized circular block bootstrap (21-session blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. The 2018-10..2026-10 post-SSRN subsample is reported. IWM and QQQ are Holm secondaries.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history-IWM, daily-history-QQQ, macro-release-cpi, fomc-meetings
final.pass: Difference > 2 bps with one-sided p < 0.05; both halves positive; the 2018-10..2026-10 mean difference > 0; IWM and QQQ the same sign after Holm.
final.controls: The T-59 window is excluded from both groups. Overlaps with OPEX Fridays, CPI days and FOMC days are dummied and reported. Costs 2 bps a round trip. Bonferroni if any other day is inspected.

rows.reason: It is testable in minutes and not registered, though the source was seen only through Quantpedia. The fix adds a post-publication subsample requirement, since the paper's own data runs into the 2010s, and controls for OPEX and CPI overlaps. Low prior, because the authors report decay.

rows.name: Informative pre-FOMC price pressure (Arif, Da, Lin)
rows.source_notes: I opened the 2025-02-12 working paper PDF (Arif, Da, Lin). Confirmed: SPY 1994-2023, with a monthly sample of 1996-01..2021-12 (312 observations). 'FOMC Day (-1)' is the trading day before the meeting's first day (example: 2017-03-13 for the March 14-15 meeting), and Day 0 covers both meeting days. A one-sd (0.43%) lower trailing-24-month Day -1 return predicts a next-two-year return 11.78% higher. Adjusted R2 is up to about 0.34. Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 runs from 7% to over 30% for forecast starts shifted monthly from 2005-01 to 2013-12, Clark-West significant. The registration's Day -1 definition matches the paper's.
rows.replication_concerns: The paper's out-of-sample forecasts already cover origins from 2005 to 2021 on the same SPY data. A Mandel run over 2005-2026 would therefore reproduce the paper rather than test it. The only unseen targets come from forecast origins after 2021-12: about 4 non-overlapping one-year windows up to 2026-10. In the paper, overlapping 24-month targets give only about 15 independent windows. No independent replication found (search budget used up). Mandel T-341/T-342 show FOMC-calendar patterns weakened after 2016.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..2026-10-14; fomc-meetings with start dates for 1994-2027 (scheduled flag); fred-DTB3; cboe-VIX-history.
rows.lookahead_risks: The predictor is known at each month end. Overlapping horizon targets need a HAC lag equal to the horizon. The specification (a 24-month window, Day -1) was chosen by the authors after they had seen 1994-2023, which is why only post-2021 origins count.
rows.missing_data: Time: the decisive post-2021 forecast origins mostly do not have complete targets yet. ITI series (not available).

final.claim: For forecast origins from 2022-01 onward (after Arif-Da-Lin's last monthly observation), the trailing-24-month mean SPY return on FOMC Day -1 (the session before each scheduled meeting's first day) negatively predicts SPY's excess return over the next 12 months. The regression is estimated on all data from 1996 to each origin, and the Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R2 against the expanding historical mean must be > 0.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 on non-overlapping annual forecasts from origins 2022-01, 2023-01, and so on. Clark-West statistic on monthly origins, Newey-West lag 12. Slope sign. Reported: a reproduction over the 2005-2021 origins (in-paper) and the quarterly horizon.
final.procedure: Day -1 is fixed as the trading session before the 'start' date of scheduled rows in fomc-meetings. The predictor is computed at each month end from closes known then. Expanding OLS from 1996. Forward-tracked: the verdict stays inconclusive until 48 post-2021 monthly origins have complete 12-month targets. A timing strategy, SPY vs DTB3 at 2 bps per switch, is reported.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, fomc-meetings, fred-DTB3, cboe-VIX-history
final.pass: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over at least 48 post-2021 monthly origins (HAC lag 12). Negative slope in the expanding estimate at every year end. OOS R2 > 0 on the non-overlapping annual forecasts. Timing-strategy Sharpe above buy-and-hold net of costs.
final.controls: One Day -1 definition, one 24-month window and one horizon, all the paper's; no grid. 2008 and 2020 flagged. Leakage review: the predictor is price on calendar-selected days.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the predictor is new to Mandel. But the paper's own out-of-sample forecasts already cover 2005-2021 on the same SPY data, so only origins after 2021 are evidence. The fix registers it as a forward-tracked test on those origins at the paper's 12-month horizon.

rows.name: Nontrading-period (weekend/holiday) option mispricing, measured on Cboe put-write indices
rows.source_notes: IDEAS pages confirm both papers. Jones-Shemesh (JF 73(2), 2018, 861-900): option returns are significantly lower over nontrading periods, mostly weekends; risk does not explain it; they attribute it to option prices treating return variance incorrectly while markets are closed. Muravyev-Ni (JFE 136(1), 2020): delta-hedged S&P 500 index option returns average about -0.7% a day, -1% close-to-open and +0.3% open-to-close, across maturities and moneyness. I did not open Da et al. (2026 WP). The Cboe PutWrite methodology PDF (cdn-api.cboe.com governance) covers PUTY, PUTR, WPUT, WPTR and PTLT, but not PUT. It confirms that daily marks are the average of the last bid and ask before 4:00 pm ET. WPUT rolls every Friday (the preceding business day on a holiday) and sells the new put at the last bid before 4 pm on PM-settled roll days, or at the first bid after 9:30 am on AM-settled days. The T-bill account accrues at the 4-week bank discount rate by calendar days (exponent (t - (t-1))/28), with no interest on roll days.
rows.replication_concerns: Two independent top-journal papers agree on the sign, so the effect is well replicated in-sample. Their samples end before about 2014, and post-2014 decay was not searched (budget used up). The candidate's null, 'weekend residual exceeds weekday residual', is wrong: a correctly priced short option still earns more over a weekend. Fri-Mon carries about 1.27 weeknights of variance (T-511, CI 1.01-1.53). And for a weekly put, theta per day rises toward expiry, so WPUT's weekday intervals are not comparable to its first weekend. Index marks carry no costs. Short-vol tails (T-561: putwrite drawdown -70%) mean any trade starts as a defined-risk shadow.
rows.data_notes: cboe-PUT-history: daily from 2007-01-03 (plus 7 scattered back-test prints 1991-2004), back-tested to 2007-06-19, live from 2007-06-20, to 2026-10-14. cboe-WPUT-history: daily 2006-01-31..2026-10-14, back-tested through 2015-07-31, live from 2015-08-03. cboe-PUTY-history: daily from 1986-06-30, back-tested through 2019-02-14. daily-history--GSPC 1927..2026-10-14. fred-DTB3. No 4-week bill series is archived; DTB3 differs from it by a few bps a year, under 0.1 bp a weekend.
rows.lookahead_risks: Index closes use 4:00 pm quote mids, matched by ^GSPC's 4:00 pm close. Back-tested values (PUT before 2007-06-20, WPUT before 2015-08-03) were not published at the time, and Cboe chose the designs after the fact. Betas must use prior intervals only. Intervals next to holidays (Good Friday, Monday holidays) must be excluded using the realised calendar. The T-bill accrual must follow the index's calendar-day rule; otherwise weekends carry a mechanical extra accrual.
rows.missing_data: PUT's own methodology document must be read before the run, for PUT's marking and T-bill rules, which the PutWrite family PDF does not cover. Quoted SPY weekly put spreads exist only from the capture box (2026-10-14 on).

final.claim: Over 2007-06-20..2026-10, using live PUT marks, the Cboe PUT index's mean residual return over Friday-close-to-Monday-close intervals exceeds 1.5 times its mean residual over single-weekday intervals (Mon-Tue, Tue-Wed, Wed-Thu, Thu-Fri). The residual is the index return minus the T-bill accrual for the interval's calendar days, minus a trailing 60-interval beta times the ^GSPC excess return. The 1.5 multiplier bounds T-511's measured weekend-to-weeknight variance ratio (1.27, CI up to 1.53), so a correctly priced option should not clear it.
final.statistic: D = mean weekend residual - 1.5 x mean single-weekday residual (bps of index level). Secondaries: the same on WPUT live marks (2015-08-03 on), where Fri-Mon is the first weekend of each weekly put, reported with the theta-acceleration caveat; PUTY live marks (from 2019-02-15); and pre-holiday-to-post-holiday intervals.
final.null: D <= 0: option marks decay over nontrading days no faster than the variance that accrues over them.
final.procedure: Intervals run between consecutive Cboe closes. Excluded: intervals that span a roll (the Thu-Fri into a third-Friday roll, and the roll day), intervals in which the held put has fewer than 10 calendar days to expiry, and intervals next to exchange holidays. T-bill accrual follows the index's calendar-day rule, with DTB3 as the proxy rate. Beta comes from the prior 60 intervals of the same index. Studentized circular block bootstrap by week (4-week blocks, 5 seeds). Halves 2007-06..2016-12 and 2017-01..2026-10. Weeks with Monday macro releases are reported.
final.data: cboe-PUT-history, cboe-WPUT-history, cboe-PUTY-history, daily-history--GSPC, fred-DTB3, macro-release-employment-situation
final.pass: D > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 on PUT, both halves positive, and D the same sign on WPUT's live period. Holm over the 2 indices (PUT primary, WPUT secondary).
final.controls: One multiplier (1.5, from T-511) and one beta window; no grid. Back-tested rows are excluded from the pass. Index marks carry no costs, so a pass is a premium estimate, not a net trade. The tradeable shadow is a separate forward test: sell defined-risk SPY put spreads at the Friday close and buy them back at the Monday close, charging the half-spreads captured by the capture box.

rows.reason: Two independent top-journal sources are verified, and the design unblocks T-526 on archived marks. But the candidate's null would pass even a correctly priced option, because weekend variance is about 1.27 weeknights and WPUT's theta accelerates toward the Friday expiry. The fix uses PUT's live monthly marks, a 1.5x variance-ratio null taken from T-511, and calendar-day T-bill accrual.

rows.name: Quarter-end marking-up in hedge-fund-held stocks (13F cross-section)
rows.source_notes: The IDEAS page of JF 68(6), 2013, 2383-2434 confirms Ben-David, Franzoni, Landier and Moussawi. Stocks in the top quartile of hedge-fund holdings earn abnormal returns on the last trading day of each quarter and partly reverse the next day. Much of the gain comes in the final minutes, and the effect is strongest for funds with ranking incentives. The +0.30% / -0.25% magnitudes and the sample period are not on the page and remain unverified. The SEC page confirms the Form 13F data sets: July 2013 to August 2026, earliest file 2013Q2, quarterly ZIPs, flattened as filed.
rows.replication_concerns: Search budget used up, so I found no post-2013 evidence. The paper drew regulatory attention to marking the close. Mandel T-346/T-439 found IWM quarter-end minus next day at -17 to -21 bps, the wrong sign, with the same sign at placebo month ends; that points to a turn-of-month effect, not mark-up. There is no canonical free list of hedge-fund filers, so the classification is a large researcher degree of freedom. 13F holdings are reported with up to a 45-day lag.
rows.data_notes: The 13F data sets are not archived. sec-submissions exists only as 36 shard bundles (sec-submissions-b000 ...). fja-sp500-components covers 1996-01-02..2026-08-18. daily-history covers the 901 current symbols and is survivor-biased.
rows.lookahead_risks: 13F holdings become public at filing acceptance, up to 45 days after quarter end. The ownership rank for quarter q must therefore use the latest filing accepted before q's last trading day, usually holdings as of the end of q-1. Amendments are dated by their own acceptance. The hedge-fund classification must be frozen before any return is read. Survivorship in the 901-symbol set.
rows.missing_data: The SEC 13F data sets (free, not archived). A frozen hedge-fund filer rule, for example SEC Form ADV filers that report hedge funds as most of their private-fund assets (not verified as a bulk source). Delisted-stock prices.

final.claim: Over 2013Q3-2026Q3, among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, the top-minus-bottom quartile of hedge-fund 13F ownership share (from the latest filings accepted before the quarter's last trading day) earns a positive SPY-adjusted return on the quarter's last trading day minus the next day, net of 10 bps a round trip. Both halves must be positive, with no effect at non-quarter month ends.
final.statistic: Mean (quarter-end minus next-day) long-short spread (bps), bootstrapped by quarter.
final.procedure: 13F holdings are aligned by filing acceptance date, and amendments by their own acceptance. A hedge-fund classification rule is frozen and hashed before any return is read. Studentized bootstrap by quarter. Placebo at non-quarter month ends. Halves 2013-2019 and 2020-2026. Members without prices are counted and flagged.
final.data: SEC 13F data sets (to fetch), sec-submissions-b* shards, fja-sp500-components, daily-history (901)
final.pass: Spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, and the month-end placebo not significant (two-sided p > 0.1).
final.controls: Costs 10 bps a round trip. Survivorship flagged. Classification rule frozen. One quartile cut. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the cross-section is not registered, but nothing it needs is archived and the classification rule is a free parameter. It is registered as blocked, with a frozen-rule requirement and point-in-time filing alignment, and its prior is low after T-346/T-439's wrong-sign results.

rows.name: Same-weekday momentum (Da-Zhang)
rows.source_notes: I opened the 2025-10-30 draft PDF (Da and Zhang; first draft March 2024). Confirmed: 1963-2021, with 70% of momentum being same-weekday continuation. The same-weekday strategy earns 2.05% a month (t 10.94), with FF3/FF5 alphas of 2.18%. Standard momentum earns 1.28% (t 5.19) and other-weekday momentum 0.28% (not significant). The net same-weekday share was 39% in 1927-1962, 62% in 1963-1992 and 18% in 1993-2021. Stocks below the NYSE 10% breakpoint are excluded.
rows.replication_concerns: Chen-Zimmermann's MomSeasonShort is related but was not re-checked (search budget used up). The post-1993 share fell to 18%. The cost arithmetic: the five weekday books are formed on disjoint daily-return sums, so consecutive books overlap little. Replacing about three-quarters of each leg every day at 5 bps a side costs about 15 bps a day on a $1-long/$1-short book, against about 10 bps a day gross (2.05% a month / 21). Mandel T-476 (same calendar month, ETFs), T-60 and the ML T-578 weekday features (0 of 306 cells) all failed.
rows.data_notes: daily-history covers the 901 current symbols, with only a few delisted names. fja-sp500-components provides point-in-time members 1996-2026, but most delisted members have no archived prices (see the T-392 triage). The local 123-symbol daily bars could carry a feature-level test inside T-578.
rows.lookahead_risks: Survivorship: a decile long-short on today's survivors drops the delisted losers. Formation scores must use months t-12..t-2 only. Membership must be point in time.
rows.missing_data: Delisted-stock prices for point-in-time members.

final.claim: Over 2010-2026, on point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, a book long the top decile and short the bottom decile of the past same-weekday return score (the sum of log returns on weekday-k sessions over months t-12..t-2), held only on weekday-k sessions, earns a positive mean monthly return net of 5 bps per side on actual turnover, and more than the other-weekday placebo score.
final.statistic: Net mean monthly return of the same-weekday book, and its difference from the other-weekday placebo book.
final.procedure: Monthly formation from scores known at month end; the book changes daily. Studentized block bootstrap by month (block 3). Halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026. Membership-weighted, with members that lack prices counted.
final.data: daily-history (901), fja-sp500-components
final.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, and the placebo weaker.
final.controls: Costs of 5 bps per side on actual turnover. Survivorship flagged. One formation window. No grid.

rows.reason: Drop. The source is verified, but the strategy is dead after costs by construction: replacing the book daily costs more than the gross premium. The cross-section on today's 901 survivors is also biased. The one cheap use, a same-weekday mean-return feature, belongs inside T-578's deflated feature set rather than in a new theory.

knowledge.title: Calendar and macro-event patterns: uncertainty premia, FOMC-window carry and bond drift, month-end flows, auction concessions and weekend option decay
knowledge.markdown:
# Calendar and macro-event patterns: uncertainty premia, FOMC-window carry and bond drift, month-end flows, auction concessions and weekend option decay

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 15 sweep candidates: ten peer-reviewed papers (JF, JFE, RFS, FRL), six working papers and two Quantpedia practitioner summaries.
- **Links:** https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w25817/revisions/w25817.rev2.pdf · https://acris.aalto.fi/ws/portalfiles/portal/40965155/hhz054.pdf · https://www.fmg.ac.uk/sites/default/files/publications/dp-54.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.65 (26 works and data documents, weighted full text 1, abstract 0.5, summary 0.25: 13 full, 7 abstracts, 2 summaries, 4 not opened).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full text for nine papers and Cboe's PutWrite methodology, every data claim checked against the archive; abstracts only for Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert, Savor-Wilson, Wachter-Zhu, Lou-Yan-Zhang, Jones-Shemesh, Muravyev-Ni and Ben-David et al.; SSRN returned 403 for Stivers-Sun and Ma-Pratt. No post-2018 replication of a conditional version was searched (the web-search budget ran out).
- **Selected because:** calendar inputs (FOMC, CPI, payrolls, month-end, OPEX, holidays, time of day) are the registry's most-tested, most-decayed family; the question is whether an effect survives conditioning on a non-price input (implied volatility, dealer gamma, auction size, settlement regime, rate differentials) and whether its mechanism predicts where it moves.

## What it says

- **Uncertainty build-up before releases (Hu-Pan-Wang-Zhu).** Holders of known event risk are paid as it resolves; VIX builds beforehand. 1994-2018, close t-1 to just before: FOMC +27.1 bps (t 5.95, 190 statements), payrolls +10.1, ISM +9.1, GDP +7.5. The FOMC slope on the 3-day VIX change has t 2.20; the non-event placebo is flat. For pooled macro releases the 3-day change fails (t 0.32) and only a 6-day window works. Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert: the unconditional drift "essentially disappeared after 2015".
- **VIX-spike next-day premium (same paper).** 1994-2018: after VIX closes 3 points above its EWMA, the S&P earns +57.2 bps the next day (t 3.24, about 8 events a year; +46.9 with the 3:45 pm VIX). The authors concede large price drops carry the same information.
- **Announcement-day beta (Savor-Wilson; Wachter-Zhu).** Macro risk resolves on release days, so beta is priced on CPI, jobs and FOMC days and much less otherwise. No post-2016 test.
- **FOMC-day short-dollar carry (Mueller-Tahbaz-Salehi-Vedolin).** 1994-2010: the three highest-rate currencies against USD earn 16.83 bps on FOMC days vs 1.67 otherwise (t 2.43); Sharpe up to 0.5 after bid-ask. About 75% arrives before the statement, more when policy uncertainty is high.
- **Post-FOMC Treasury drift (Brooks-Katz-Lustig).** 157 meetings 1989-2008: a 10 bp fed funds surprise moves the 10-year yield 1.7 bps on the day and 14 bps after 50 days, mostly after positive surprises; slow bond fund flows.
- **Dash for cash (Etula et al.).** Month-end payments force selling that settles by T, so returns are low on T-8..T-4 and high on T-3..T+3 in the T+3 era (2003-2013 reversal windows +103% cumulative against -31%). Europe's 2014 move to T+2 cut the autocorrelation at T-2 by 0.777 (t -3.20).
- **Threshold rebalancing (Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone).** A simulated 60/40 drift signal over bands of 0-2.5% predicts lower next-day equity returns (1997-2023, |t| > 4, front-running Sharpe > 1).
- **Dividend payment-day pressure (Hartzmark-Solomon).** 1926-2018: +3.2 bps market return per sd of payout on t and t-1; multipliers 1.5-2.3; nothing in Q4.
- **Gamma-conditioned intraday momentum (Baltussen et al.).** The rest-of-day return predicts the last half hour (futures 1974-2020); on the S&P only when dealer gamma is negative (48% of days). Free SqueezeMetrics GEX is negative on only 19 of 734 sessions since 2023-11: not the paper's condition.
- **Treasury pre-auction concession (Lou-Yan-Zhang).** Prices fall before auctions and recover after; hidden cost 9-18 bps of size.
- **Payday (Ma-Pratt).** Paycheck flows: the 16th earns +0.214% per event (t 3.07), decayed in the 2010s.
- **Informative pre-FOMC pressure (Arif-Da-Lin).** Informed hedging the session before meetings: a one-sd lower trailing-24-month mean predicts +11.78% over two years; out-of-sample R2 7-30% (origins 2005-2013), about 15 independent windows.
- **Weekend option decay (Jones-Shemesh; Muravyev-Ni).** Option prices mis-handle variance while markets are closed, so returns are lower over weekends; delta-hedged index options lose 1% overnight and gain 0.3% intraday.
- **Quarter-end mark-up (Ben-David et al.).** Marking up for reporting, hedge-fund-held stocks rise on the last quarter day, mostly in the final minutes, then partly reverse.
- **Same-weekday momentum (Da-Zhang).** Fixed-weekday fund flows: 2.05% a month (t 10.94, 1963-2021), but its share of momentum fell to 18% after 1993.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** Nine of fifteen claims rest on JF, JFE, RFS or FRL papers; Hu et al. and Etula et al. test mechanisms with a placebo or natural experiment. Not a tradable edge: samples end 2008-2018, transaction costs are absent or bid-ask only, several windows were chosen after looking (Hu's 6-day window, the 0-2.5% bands, Arif-Da-Lin's 24 months), and the only post-publication evidence (Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert; T-341, T-343) shows decay.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Nine conditional successors are testable now, pre-registered as successors, not discoveries.** `vix-buildup-pre-fomc-drift` (T-341/T-215/T-343) ends the VIX change at t-2 so it is point-in-time, and tests an event-versus-non-event interaction controlling for T-332's reversal; power is about 1 SE. `hvix-next-session-premium` enters at the t+1 open and must beat decile-matched price drops; T-535 and T-580's VIX-level IC (+0.11 at 1 day on equity ETFs) agree in sign, while T-421 found a spread shock added nothing beyond the VIX change.
- **`treasury-pre-auction-concession` has the strongest prior.** T-442's secondary already saw -27.6 bps over t-5..t-1 in 10/30-year weeks (p 0.0022), so the primary evidence is the unseen 2-, 5-, 7- and 20-year weeks of 2014-2026, deduplicated, FRNs and TIPS removed.
- **Mechanism tests.** `dash-for-cash-settlement-shift` uses the paper's T-2 autocorrelation on the US 2017 T+2 switch, IEF as the no-shift control, agreeing with T-59, T-345 and T-574. `fomc-window-short-dollar-carry` (OANDA) uses a two-day noon window containing the pre-announcement leg, with a T-575 month-end control. `post-fomc-treasury-yield-drift` holds out 2008-11 on and needs 60 non-ZLB meetings.
- **`threshold-rebalancing-signal` must add to T-345 and turn-of-month dummies; `payday-16th-anomaly` is one pre-specified day.**
- **`putwrite-weekend-decay-excess` unblocks T-526 on archived PUT marks** with a 1.5x variance-ratio null from T-511 (weekend variance 1.27 weeknights), net of the variance risk premium PUT always carries. It agrees with T-216 and T-170; any trade starts as a defined-risk shadow (T-561: drawdown -70%).
- **Forward or blocked:** `pre-fomc-day-minus-1-predictor` counts only origins after 2021-12; dealer-gamma `gex-conditioned-intraday-momentum` (after T-427) needs DIX.csv archived; dividend payday needs pay dates; quarter-end mark-up needs 13F data and a frozen classification rule.
- **The children set the expectation.** The event-contract children's learnings class these as risk or flow premia, not reference-price leads, judged as cost-charged return tilts; their Fed bucket rule shows a telegraphed regime (2024-25) shrinks event premia.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Decayed:** the unconditional pre-FOMC drift (T-341 -5.3 bps over 2016-2026; T-215 +4.4, CI -15 to +23), the announcement-day premium (T-343: +12.7 bps 1993-2009, fails over the full span), FOMC-cycle weeks (T-342 -5.2 over 2017-2026), payday seasonality.
- **Contradicted by Mandel:** Savor-Wilson is dropped as T-343 in substance; T-384 found high beta beating low beta on ordinary days and T-387 failed. Quarter-end mark-up starts from T-346/T-439, wrong sign, same sign at placebo month-ends. T-358: event-contract uncertainty did not scale pre-event SPY returns (p 0.553).
- **Dead after costs:** same-weekday momentum (replacing the book daily costs about 15 bps against 10 gross); T-60, T-347 and T-476 agree.
- **No data path:** the Stivers-Sun OPEX-week cross-section (paper unopened; the capture box covers 14 underlyings; T-353/T-438 failed and T-192/T-502 found no pinning).
- **Not registered:** crypto hour-of-day seasonality, which the desk child's 549-trial null rejects. Everything here trades on US-legal venues (Alpaca, CME, OANDA).

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Features:** event dummies (FOMC, CPI, payrolls, auction week by tenor, OPEX, pre-holiday, month position T-k by settlement regime); VIX build-up z ending t-2; VIX-minus-EWMA spike; auction-size z; the rebalancing deviation (flow family, leakage review); same-weekday mean return as one deflated F0 feature in T-578. No T-578 cell with calendar features passed (0 of 306), so they enter as interactions with implied volatility, gamma or flows.
- **Data to add:** DIX.csv with fetch hash, dividend pay dates, per-stock option volume history, SEC 13F data sets, FRED SOFR and target series, an ISM calendar, intraday VIX history.
- **A shared calendar utility against the look-ahead traps found here:** the realised NYSE calendar with unscheduled closures dated at announcement, SEC-verified settlement dates, and release timestamps (VIX 16:15 ET, H.10 noon FX, H.15 yields next day, split-adjusted dividends, DIX.csv without vintages).
- **Gate:** matched non-event placebos, joint deflation with each predecessor family, declared power. Nothing joins T-559's calendar sleeve or T-567 before a pass and an independent refutation.

candidates.name: Supplier/customer industry cross-momentum (Menzly-Ozbas 2010)
candidates.summary: The past-month returns of an industry's linked supplier and customer industries, weighted by input-output links, predict that industry's next-month return. The paper finds the effect weaker where analyst coverage and institutional ownership are high. Not in Mandel's registry: no supplier, customer or input-output theory exists.
candidates.mechanism: Investors specialise and markets are segmented, so holders of industry A do not process news that first shows up in A's suppliers or customers. That news reaches A's price over weeks. The other side is A's own specialist holders, who update slowly, plus liquidity traders. Arbitrage is limited because exploiting the effect means covering many linked industries at once.
candidates.assets: US equities: Fama-French 49 industry portfolios (archived french-industry49-daily) as the research proxy; tradable as industry stock baskets or sector ETFs on Alpaca
candidates.horizon: months (signal on month-t returns, hold month t+1)
candidates.claimed_effect: Journal of Finance 2010. Chen-Zimmermann's SignalDoc lists the original-paper t-statistics as customer-industry momentum (iomom_cust) t = 4.11 and supplier-industry momentum (iomom_supp) t = 5.03, sample 1986-2005, and grades the replication '2_likely'. The doc gives no return magnitude. A 2010 Financial Analysts Journal study that appeared in my search results reports up to 15% a year abnormal return from lagged customer-industry returns; I did not open it. No costs are stated.
candidates.replication: Likely replicated in Chen-Zimmermann Open Source Asset Pricing (graded 2_likely, not 1_clear). Schlag and Zeng (JEF 2019) extend the effect to horizontal links between competitor and substitute industries. I found no figure after 2005. The paper's own mechanism predicts decay as coverage and institutional ownership rise, so 2006-2026 is a real out-of-sample test. The OSAP long-short series to 2025 would give the decay curve directly, but its Google Drive download hit a quota limit today.

Chen & Zimmermann, Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (iomom_cust, iomom_supp)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 49 FF industries, using daily returns compounded to months, 1990-2026. Links: BEA benchmark Use tables mapped to FF49 by SIC. At each month-end t, use only the latest table published before t; BEA benchmark tables appear about 5 years after their reference year, so hard-code the publication dates. Signal: the link-weighted mean month-t return of each industry's customers, and separately of its suppliers, excluding the industry itself. Rank into quintiles and go long Q5, short Q1 at the t close, holding through t+1. Controls: own month-t return, own 12-1 momentum, and FF5+UMD alpha, with Fama-MacBeth slopes on the linked return net of own lags. Select variants (customer or supplier, 1- or 3-month formation) on 1990-2005; the test window is 2006-01 to 2026-09. Cost: 10 bps per leg per rebalance on turnover. Statistics: HAC t of the long-short mean, a one-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound above 0, and DSR over 4 variants. Tradability check: rerun on the 11 SPDR sector ETFs with BEA weights; small N, reported only.

candidates.name: Customer momentum, firm-level economic links (Cohen-Frazzini 2008)
candidates.summary: A firm's next-month return follows the past-month return of its major customers. The effect is documented and replicated, but has roughly halved and lost value-weighted significance since 2005. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Limited attention: investors do not update a supplier's price when news reaches its principal customer's price. The other side is the supplier's holders, who ignore customer news. Arbitrageurs need the link data, which is costly (Compustat segments).
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: months (1-month hold); weekly variants reported to be stronger
candidates.claimed_effect: Chen-Zimmermann's SignalDoc lists CustomerMomentum at 1.578% a month, t = 3.79, sample 1980-2004. Pinchuk's replication (arXiv 2023, Table 8): equal-weighted long-short decile 1.52% a month (t 4.74) and value-weighted 1.30% (t 3.03) over 1978-2004. Over 2005-2018 the same portfolios earn equal-weighted 0.62% (t 2.12) and value-weighted 0.62% (t 1.54, not significant). Gross of costs.
candidates.replication: Replicated in-sample by OSAP (graded 1_clear) and by Pinchuk 2023. Post-discovery it has decayed: about 60% smaller, and the value-weighted version is insignificant after 2005. Pinchuk also finds it partly driven by the small-to-large lead-lag. Ferment et al. (2013), cited in an Erasmus thesis, find weak evidence of decline and a stronger weekly version. The effect is contested at large caps.

sources.title: Cohen & Frazzini (2008), Economic Links and Predictable Returns, JF (AQR page)
Pinchuk (2023), Customer Momentum (replication incl. post-discovery 2005-2018)
Chen & Zimmermann, OSAP SignalDoc (CustomerMomentum)

candidates.proposed_test: Blocked on data: Compustat segment links are not free. Free proxy: from EDGAR full-text search (10-K Item 1 or the segment note, 2001+), extract customers named as 10% or more of sales, keeping only pairs where both firms are in the 901-symbol daily-history archive. A link becomes valid at the 10-K 'filed' date from sec-submissions and lasts 12 months. Signal: the value-weighted month-t return of each supplier's customers. Hold a long-short of the supplier tercile in month t+1, value-weighted. Test 2010-01 to 2026-09 with a monthly and a weekly variant (Monday-open entry). Cost: 10 bps per side. Statistics: HAC t, bootstrap lower bound, and DSR over 2 variants. Expect too few pairs among large caps: pre-register min_n of 60 months with at least 30 linked suppliers, else inconclusive. Low priority given the documented decay.

candidates.name: Big / high-volume stocks lead small / low-volume stocks within an industry (Hou 2007; Chordia-Swaminathan 2000)
candidates.summary: Within an industry, last week's return of the big, high-dollar-volume firms predicts this week's return of the small, low-volume firms. The effect is mostly intra-industry and driven by slow reaction to bad news. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Industry information diffuses slowly to neglected, thinly traded firms. Chordia-Swaminathan find that daily and weekly returns of high-volume portfolios lead low-volume portfolios after controlling for size, and that nonsynchronous trading does not explain it. The other side is holders of low-attention stocks who update late; market makers in illiquid names quote stale prices.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Chen-Zimmermann's SignalDoc lists IndRetBig (Hou 2007) at t = 11.0 and EarnSupBig at t = 8.91, sample 1972-2001; returns are not listed. Chordia-Swaminathan (JF 2000): daily and weekly high-volume returns lead low-volume returns. I opened no effect-size table. Costs not stated, and they would be large in small caps.
candidates.replication: OSAP replicates IndRetBig (1_clear). Other markets are mixed: Taiwan supports the volume and size lead (1986-2006), New Zealand is partial, and Vietnam 2006-2012 finds no volume effect. Medhat-Schmeling note that the reversal component has tapered since about 2011 with rising liquidity. I found no US post-2001 decay figure; the web-search budget ran out before I could look further. Mandel's archive holds mostly large caps, so the small-firm leg that carries most of the effect is largely absent. Expect a weak or null result.

Chordia & Swaminathan (2000), Trading volume and cross-autocorrelations in stock returns, JF
Chen & Zimmermann, OSAP SignalDoc (IndRetBig, EarnSupBig)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 901-symbol daily-history stocks, which is a survivor list, so state the bias. Industry is the 2-digit SIC from sec-submissions. Weekly, at Friday close t: within each industry with at least 6 names, split into the top and bottom dollar-volume terciles using the trailing 60-day mean. Leader signal: the cap-weighted week-t return of the top tercile. Position: long the bottom tercile of industries whose leaders rose most, short the bottom tercile of industries whose leaders fell most (cross-industry quintiles). Enter at Monday open to skip the bounce and hold to Friday close. Control: regress follower returns on leader week-t return plus the follower's own week-t return. Cost: 5 bps per side plus 0.5 x the Corwin-Schultz spread for low-volume names. Train 2005-2014, test 2015-2026. Statistics: HAC t of the leader slope in Fama-MacBeth, net long-short mean, and DSR over 4 variants (day or week, volume or size split). Reported only: the same test on the 5-minute local bars with ETF leaders (sector SPDR leads member stocks).

candidates.name: Industry returns lead the stock market (Hong-Torous-Valkanov 2007), contested
candidates.summary: Lagged returns of certain industries (retail, services, commercial real estate, metals, petroleum, financials) forecast next-month and two-month US market returns. A reexamination with longer data finds little left. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Gradual information diffusion: the broad market is slow to absorb fundamentals news that shows up first in specific industries. The other side is index investors who do not track industry signals. Petroleum and metals carry a contrarian (negative) sign, which links to the oil and metals candidates below.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES futures)
candidates.claimed_effect: HTV (JFE 2007), 1946-2002: a significant number of the 34 industries forecast the market by up to two months, the strongest being financial, retail, print and commercial real estate. Industry-based market timing had a lower mean than buy-and-hold and a slightly higher Sharpe before costs, and the authors call it not economically significant for traders (CXO summary of the 2004 draft).
candidates.replication: Contested and largely gone. Tse (JEF 2015) reexamines 1946-2013 with 48 industries and finds only 1 to 7 industries with significant predictive power, depending on model and significance level. Even the original 34-industry 1946-2002 sample is less significant after CRSP data revisions. Tse concludes the results are consistent with market efficiency.

sources.title: Hong, Torous & Valkanov (2007), Do industries lead stock markets?, JFE 83
CXO Advisory summary of HTV (trading-rule results)
Tse (2015), Do industries lead stock markets? A reexamination, JEF 34

candidates.proposed_test: Cheap refutation run. Data: french-industry49-daily compounded to months, ^GSPC/SPY total return, DTB3. Pre-register HTV's named industries ex ante: financial, retail, real estate, metals (FF49 Steel + Mines), petroleum (Oil), services. Predictor: each industry's month-t return, entered separately and as a PCA composite. Target: SPY month t+1 excess return. Out-of-sample period 2003-01 to 2026-09, after HTV's sample, with expanding-window OLS from 1963. Statistics: Campbell-Thompson R2_OS, Clark-West p, and the Bonferroni/DSR count of 49 single-industry trials plus the composite. Trading rule: long SPY when the forecast exceeds DTB3, else bills; 2 bps per switch; compare against the historical-mean rule. Expected result: not_supported. Recording the failure protects the substrate from the claim.

candidates.name: Oil price changes predict lower equity returns (Driesprong-Jacobsen-Maat 2008)
candidates.summary: Rises in crude oil prices predict lower stock market returns over the following month or quarter, in the US and most developed markets. Investors underreact to the earnings and discount-rate news in oil. Not in the registry. Oil is not among the T-578/T-579 F1 leaders (SPY, QQQ, VIX, DXY, TNX, BTC, TLT, GLD).
candidates.mechanism: Underreaction or slow diffusion of oil-shock information into equity prices. The predictability also forecasts negative excess returns, which the authors argue rules out a time-varying risk premium. The other side is equity investors who do not map energy-price shocks into future earnings and costs.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY, ES futures); also sector ETFs
candidates.claimed_effect: DJM (JFE 2008): using about 30 years of monthly data, oil changes significantly predict returns in 12 of 18 developed markets plus the world index. A trade-press summary reports about 4% a year outperformance from a simple strategy, but on in-sample predictability. Casassus-Higuera (2011 WP), 1983Q2-2009Q4: short-term oil futures returns are the best out-of-sample predictor among those compared, with R2_OS of about 1.2% at one quarter.
candidates.replication: Supported out of sample through 2009 by Casassus-Higuera. The 2004 coverage says out-of-sample emerging-market evidence is weaker than in-sample. I found no post-2010 replication; the web-search budget ran out before a decay source could be looked for. The 2010-2026 shale era and 2020 negative WTI are untested by me, and the sign may have flipped when oil became a demand-driven risk-on asset (an unverified hypothesis).

sources.title: Driesprong, Jacobsen & Maat (2008), Striking oil: Another puzzle?, JFE (ERIM version)
Casassus & Higuera (2011), Stock Return Predictability and Oil Prices (PUC WP 406)
Advisor.ca: Study confirms oil's impact on equities

candidates.proposed_test: Data: CL-F daily-history (Yahoo continuous front month; also FRED DCOILWTICO spot to avoid roll gaps), SPY adjclose, DTB3. Signal: the log change in WTI spot over month t, measured at the month-end close; for April 2020 use spot, not CL=F. Target: SPY month t+1 excess return. A weekly variant uses the week-t oil change to predict week t+1 (DJM mention lagged reaction). Train 1990-2009; test 2010-01 to 2026-09. Statistics: R2_OS against the historical mean, Clark-West p, and HAC t of the slope with the pre-registered sign negative. Trading rule: long SPY or bills, switched on the forecast, 2 bps per side. DSR over 4 variants (monthly or weekly, spot or futures). Split-sample sign check pre- and post-2015. Separately, add CL_F and HG_F r1/r5/r20 to the T-579 F1 leader list so the IC scan covers them.

candidates.name: Industrial metal (copper) returns predict equity returns with a business-cycle-dependent sign (Jacobsen-Marshall-Visaltanachoti 2019)
candidates.summary: Rising industrial-metal prices predict lower stock returns in expansions, as an overheating and discount-rate signal, and higher returns in recessions, as an earnings-recovery signal. Pooling the two regimes hides the effect. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: The same news means different things in different states, and investors process it slowly. In expansions metal rallies signal inflation and tighter policy; in contractions they signal demand recovery. The other side is investors who read metal moves with a fixed sign.
adjacent_variables: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (real-time vintages)
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES futures)
candidates.claimed_effect: Management Science 2019 abstract: a one-standard-deviation rise in metal returns is associated with about 1.5% lower monthly stock returns in expansions and about 0.5% higher in recessions. The 2010 draft (CXO summary), 1977-2010: the sign holds for all five metals, copper and aluminium are strongest, and similar results appear in most EU markets. A simulated real-time switching rule over the five years to June 2010 earned up to 0.73% a month and beat buy-and-hold. Costs ignored.
candidates.replication: Published in Management Science after a long working-paper history. The only out-of-sample evidence is the authors' own five-year window. I found no independent replication or post-2010 test. Look-ahead landmine: NBER recession dates are announced months late, so any test must classify the state with real-time CFNAI vintages.

sources.title: Jacobsen, Marshall & Visaltanachoti (2019), Stock Market Predictability and Industrial Metal Returns, Management Science 65(7)
CXO Advisory: Industrial metals as asymmetric equity return predictors (2010 draft summary)
Abstract mirror (SUFE academic newsletter)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: HG-F daily-history (2000+), plus CPER from 2011 as the tradable check, SPY, DTB3, and ALFRED CFNAI-MA3 vintages (to fetch). State at month-end t: expansion if the CFNAI-MA3 value in the vintage available on that date exceeds -0.7, else contraction. Model: SPY excess(t+1) = a + b1*copper(t)*expansion + b2*copper(t)*contraction. Pre-registered signs: b1 < 0, b2 > 0. Out-of-sample 2010-07 to 2026-09, expanding window from 1990 (use FRED PCOPPUSDM before 2000 if needed). Statistics: R2_OS, Clark-West, HAC t of b1 (b2 has few recession months: report it, but do not gate on it). Rule: long SPY or bills, 2 bps per switch. DSR over 2 metals x 2 state definitions. A rule that uses ex-post NBER dates must be reported as a look-ahead placebo, never as the result.

candidates.name: Gold-to-platinum price ratio predicts the equity premium (Huang-Kilic 2019)
candidates.summary: A high gold/platinum ratio, where gold holds up relative to the industrial metal, predicts higher future US equity excess returns. The ratio proxies a slow-moving tail-risk state variable and is reported robust out of sample and across sub-samples. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Risk-based: gold and platinum have similar consumption uses, so their ratio isolates time-varying disaster or tail risk. When tail risk is high, gold outperforms platinum and the equity premium demanded is high. The other side is investors who reduce equity exposure in high-risk states.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES futures); metals via GLD/PPLT or CME GC/PL
candidates.claimed_effect: Huang (2015 NBER conference draft, opened): 1975-2013 monthly. The 1-month R2 is just above 1% (slope t 2.82) and the 1-year R2 is 16.57% (10.89% with the Hodrick VAR). A one-s.d. rise in log GP predicts +6.4% excess return over the next year. GP is significant at every horizon from 1 month to 5 years and outperforms nearly all standard predictors. Out-of-sample R2 is 'large, positive, significant' and similar to in-sample. Published JFE 132(3), June 2019, with Kilic.
candidates.replication: Mixed. A study from Otago confirms the US result but finds GP unreliable for China. Xu, Li and Singh (IJMF 2023) find that the first difference of GP, not the level, carries the predictive power internationally. Hulbert's commentary (chart-based, not a test) says it did 'creditably' after 2014. I found no formal post-2013 out-of-sample test. From memory and unverified: platinum collapsed relative to gold after about 2014, so the level sits far outside its 1975-2013 range. That is a structural-break risk for the level version.

sources.title: Huang (2015), Gold, Platinum, and Expected Stock Returns (NBER conference draft)
JFE June 2019 issue listing (Huang & Kilic, vol 132 issue 3)
