candidates.proposed_test: Data: GC-F and PL-F daily-history (archived) as the monthly average of daily closes, matching the paper's monthly-average fixings, with PPLT/GLD as a tradable cross-check; SPY total return; DTB3. Predictors: log GP level and its 1-month change (2 trials, both declared). Targets: SPY excess returns over 1 month (primary, for power) and over 12 months with non-overlapping annual observations (reported). Out-of-sample 2014-01 to 2026-09, expanding window from the start of PL-F; the paper's sample ends in 2013. Statistics: R2_OS against the historical mean, Clark-West, an IVX or bootstrap correction for persistence (Stambaugh bias), and DSR over 2 predictors x 2 horizons. Rule: monthly long SPY or bills when the forecast exceeds DTB3, 2 bps per switch. Pre-register a structural-break check: GP's 2014-2026 range against its 1975-2013 range. If out of range, the level version is inconclusive, not supported.

candidates.name: Equity returns lead corporate-bond (HY/IG) ETF returns (Downing-Underwood-Xing 2009; Jiang-Li-Xiao 2024)
candidates.summary: Stock returns lead junk and BBB bond returns at hourly frequency. A 2024 SSRN paper finds that returns of bond issuers' stocks predict corporate-bond ETF returns, but not the reverse. Mandel's T-578 F0F1 already uses SPY as a leader for bond ETFs: the bond_etf h = 1 ridge cell had IC +0.10 but net -0.1 bps per trade and DSR 0.014. The direction is consistent; the trade is not yet profitable after costs.
candidates.mechanism: The bond market is less informationally efficient: firm news is priced first in equity. High-yield bonds behave like equity claims on distressed issuers. The bond ETF's NAV, and to a lesser extent its price, update late. The other side is slower bond-market participants and ETF arbitrage that runs on stale NAVs.
candidates.assets: HYG, LQD (Alpaca); the reverse-direction claim is excluded
candidates.horizon: intraday (hours) to 1-2 days; equity-to-bond monthly lag also reported
candidates.claimed_effect: DUX (JFQA 2009): hourly stock returns lead nonconvertible junk and BBB bond returns, and convertible bonds of all ratings, mostly at distressed issuers; no trading P&L stated. Jiang-Li-Xiao (SSRN 2024): adaptive-LASSO issuer-equity portfolios predict bond ETF returns and random stock portfolios do not; magnitude not in the abstract. Chordia, Goyal, Nozawa, Subrahmanyam and Tong: equity returns predict bond returns with a one-month lag, but this is not profitable after costs. Practitioner (CSS Analytics 2014): timing HYG with SPY's 20-day SMA beat HYG's own SMA since 1995, with no cost-adjusted figures given.
candidates.replication: Equity-leads-bonds is consistent across several studies at intraday and monthly horizons. Whether it is exploitable is contested: Chordia et al. say not after costs. Child learning (VENUE_LEAD_LAG): lead-lag measured from last-trade prints is suspect until fresh quotes confirm it. Mandel's T-577 and T-578 F1 cells for bond ETFs show positive IC but no net edge.

candidates.proposed_test: Two cells, registered as a successor to the T-578 bond_etf F0F1 reading, not a new discovery. (a) Intraday, on the local 60-minute bars (2 years) and 15-minute bars (60 days): SPY's bar-h return, and an issuer-equity basket of the 901-universe stocks most represented in HYG's holdings, predict HYG's bar h+1 return. Execute at HYG's next-bar open; charge a 1 bp half-spread plus 1 bp slippage; trade only when |SPY bar return| exceeds 1 trailing s.d. Placebo: a random 30-stock basket, as Jiang-Li-Xiao do. (b) Daily: SPY's 15:00-16:00 return predicts HYG's next open-to-close, so the leader is known before the entry. Train 2024-10 to 2025-09; test 2025-10 onward, with the lockbox rule. Statistics: HAC t of beta, net mean per trade, one-sided bootstrap p, DSR over 2 ETFs x 2 horizons x 2 leaders. Use quote-based mids where available to address the stale-print caveat.

candidates.name: Corporate-bond market information predicts the equity premium (Li-Yuan-Zhou; excess bond premium)
candidates.summary: Bond-to-stock direction: the cross-sectional mean and skewness of corporate bond returns predict future stock market returns in and out of sample. The Gilchrist-Zakrajsek excess bond premium (EBP), a gauge of credit-market risk appetite, predicts recessions. This candidate uses changes and skewness, not the spread level Mandel tested in T-430 (credit-carry timing, not_supported).
candidates.mechanism: Informed trading in bonds, especially in distressed names, and gradual diffusion from the bond market to equity. Rising EBP signals intermediaries pulling back from risk. The other side is equity investors who lag credit-market information.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES futures)
candidates.claimed_effect: The seminar abstract (Yuan; SSRN 4374753 by Li, Yuan and Zhou) reports that the mean and skewness of corporate bond returns predict market returns both in and out of sample. Skewness is the stronger predictor and is uncorrelated with known predictors. No R2, sample period or economic gains were given on the pages I could open. Fed notes: EBP predicts NBER recessions over the next 12 months; its equity-return predictability was not confirmed by my search.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found, and the web-search budget ran out before more could be searched. Mandel cross-check: T-430 found BAA10Y level-based credit timing not supported over 2003-2026. The bond-mean proxy available here (HYG minus duration-matched IEF) is a crude stand-in for the paper's TRACE cross-section, so treat a null as weak evidence against the paper.

Renmin University seminar abstract: Can asymmetric information in corporate bonds predict equity market return?

candidates.proposed_test: Data: fred-BAA10Y (archived), HYG, LQD and IEF adjclose (archived), and EBP from the Fed's monthly CSV (to fetch). EBP is revised as balance-sheet data arrive, so use the value as first published, stamped available on the release date (month t+1), or skip EBP before vintages were kept. Predictors at month-end t, each a separate declared trial: (1) the 1-month change in BAA10Y; (2) the credit excess return HYG minus beta times IEF, with beta from a trailing 36-month duration match; (3) the change in EBP; (4) cross-sectional skewness of monthly returns across the 901 stocks' bonds. (4) is not available, so it is listed and blocked. Target: SPY month t+1 excess return. Out-of-sample 2010-01 to 2026-09 (HYG from 2007). Statistics: R2_OS, Clark-West, sign pre-registered (credit up predicts equity up), DSR over 3 testable predictors. Rule: long or bills, 2 bps per switch.

candidates.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover large caps (Medhat-Schmeling 2022)
candidates.summary: Double-sort stocks on last month's return and last month's share turnover. Low-turnover stocks reverse, but high-turnover stocks continue: short-term momentum. The continuation is strongest in the largest, most liquid stocks, and the authors report it survives costs. This is distinct from Mandel's ETF tests (T-420, 6-month momentum conditioned on low turnover; T-319 and T-462 reversal), all not_supported. Uses volume and shares outstanding as non-price inputs.
candidates.mechanism: Some traders underappreciate the information carried by a high-volume price move, which is likely informed, so it continues. Low-volume moves are liquidity shocks that revert. The other side of the momentum leg is contrarian liquidity providers who fade informed moves.
adjacent_variables: VIX (only small-cap reversal is VIX-predictable per the paper)
candidates.assets: US single stocks, large caps (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: months (1-month formation, 1-month hold; returns persist about 12 months after formation)
candidates.claimed_effect: From the accepted version (opened), July 1963 to December 2018, value-weighted. Within the highest-turnover decile, winners minus losers earn +1.37% a month (t 4.74). Within the lowest-turnover decile, reversal is -1.41% a month (t -7.13). Largest-500 2x2 STMOM earns 0.42% a month (t 4.91) while largest-500 reversal earns -2 bps. Megacap STMOM earns 0.53% a month (t 2.53). STMOM rises across sub-samples to 2.03% a month (t 4.80) in 1991-2018. The authors report it survives the Novy-Marx-Velikov cost estimates. The reversal leg has 'tapered off' since 2011.
candidates.replication: RFS 2022, with an international extension to 23 developed markets in the paper itself. I found no independent post-2018 replication. Unlike most anomalies the effect grew rather than decayed through 2018, but 2019-2026 is unmeasured.

sources.title: Medhat & Schmeling (2022), Short-term Momentum, RFS 35(3), accepted version
Medhat & Schmeling, CEPR DP15857

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 901-symbol daily-history stocks (a survivor list: report the bias, and drop each name before its first bar). Turnover in month t = sum of daily volume / shares outstanding, where shares come from sec-companyfacts dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding as last filed before t (point-in-time). At month-end t, run independent median 2x2 sorts on the month-t return and the month-t turnover, the paper's largest-500 construction. STMOM = high-turnover winners minus high-turnover losers, value-weighted, entered at the next close and held one month. Report STREV* too. Cost: 5 bps per side on actual turnover. Pre-period 2010-2018 overlaps the paper, so report it only. Test window 2019-01 to 2026-09 (post-sample, 93 months). Statistics: HAC t of the net mean, FF5+UMD alpha from the archived factors, and DSR over 4 variants (2x2 or tercile, value- or equal-weighted). Pre-register min_n of 90 months. Refutation: placebo turnover from a shuffled-month panel.

candidates.name: VIX-conditioned short-term reversal as liquidity provision (Nagel 2012); partial duplicate of T-462
candidates.summary: Short-term (1-5 day) reversal returns proxy the return to providing liquidity. They are strongly time-varying and forecast by the VIX level. Even industry-portfolio reversal, which earns little unconditionally, pays when VIX is high. T-462 tested a weekly quintile version on 68 ETFs (not_supported). The web evidence adds the daily stock-level construction, the industry version, and a counterpoint from Medhat-Schmeling.
candidates.mechanism: Financially constrained intermediaries withdraw liquidity when volatility spikes. Prices then overshoot more on order-flow shocks, and the expected return to taking the other side rises. The counterparty is liquidity demanders who must trade in stress: forced sellers, deleveraging funds.
candidates.assets: US single stocks and industry portfolios (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Nagel (RFS 2012, NBER WP opened), 1998-2010. Daily reversal returns were close to 1% a day in the 1998 LTCM crisis and the 2000-01 Nasdaq decline, fell to under 0.2% a day by 2007, then exploded in 2008. The strategy never lost money in any 3-month period from 1998 to 2010. These are gross returns from transaction prices; returns on quote midpoints are smaller but still VIX-predictable. Medhat-Schmeling (1990-2018, monthly): only the small-cap reversal is VIX-predictable, at -9 bps more a month per VIX point (t -2.13); large-cap reversal is not.
candidates.replication: Partly reproduced (Honarvar offers an alternative explanation for the same VIX link). Monthly large-cap evidence says the VIX link sits in small caps. Mandel's T-462 on ETFs failed out of sample. Transaction-price reversal includes bid-ask bounce, so on close prices it overstates what can be captured. Expect the large-cap daily version to be weak after costs.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the 901 daily-history stocks and, as a costless diagnostic, the 49 FF industries (french-industry49-daily). Daily, at close t-1: weights w_i proportional to -(r_i(t-5..t-1) - mean r). Enter at the open of day t, skipping the close to remove the bid-ask bounce from close prices, and exit at the close of day t. Regress daily strategy returns on VIX at close t-2, known before formation. Train 2000-2012; test 2013-2026. Cost: 3 bps per side on large caps, charged on gross turnover. Statistics: HAC t of the VIX slope (pre-registered positive), net Sharpe in the top VIX tercile against the others, and DSR over 2 universes x 2 formation lengths, counting T-462 as a prior trial in the deflation. A close-to-close variant is reported as a bounce-inflated upper bound only.

candidates.name: Dollar carry trade: long/short the dollar on the average forward discount (Lustig-Roussanov-Verdelhan 2014)
candidates.summary: Go long a basket of developed currencies against USD when the basket's average interest rate (average forward discount) exceeds the US rate, and short the basket otherwise. This is a time-series dollar bet, largely uncorrelated with the cross-sectional carry trade. Not in the registry; T-368 tested the cross-sectional G10 carry, not this.
candidates.mechanism: Compensation for aggregate US business-cycle risk: the strategy is short the dollar in bad times, when the US price of risk is high, and the forward discount tracks that. The other side is investors paying for dollar safety, such as hedgers and reserve managers.
candidates.assets: G10 FX via CME currency futures (6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S, 6N) or OANDA
candidates.claimed_effect: Quantpedia summary of Table I Panel A (opened), developed basket, Nov 1983 to Jun 2010, net of spot and forward bid-ask: 5.60% a year, volatility 8.53%, Sharpe 0.66, maximum drawdown -31.72%. All-countries basket: 3.80% a year, Sharpe 0.54. The average forward discount plus US IP growth forecast up to 25% of one-year dollar return variation (NBER WP abstract). The NBER WP adds that the plain carry-sorted basket version delivers only a Sharpe of about 0.3.
candidates.replication: Published in JFE 2014 (AQR Insight honourable mention). I found no post-2010 performance figures; the search budget ran out. The 2009-2015 near-zero US rates (signal short USD) and the 2016-2019 and 2022-2024 positive US differential (signal long USD) make 2011-2026 a strong out-of-sample regime test. From memory and unverified: the dollar rallied in 2014-15 and 2021-22.

sources.title: Lustig, Roussanov & Verdelhan, Countercyclical Currency Risk Premia (NBER WP 16427; JFE 2014)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: fx-spot-g10 (FRED DEX*, archived) and fx-rates-3m (OECD IR3TIB monthly, archived). Lag the rates one month for publication, the same convention as T-368. At month-end t: AFD = the equal-weight mean of 9 foreign 3m rates minus the US 3m rate. Long the basket against USD if AFD > 0, else short, filled at the next day's FRED fix. Monthly return = basket spot change + sign x AFD/12, the carry accrual a futures position earns. Cost: 2 bps per leg per rebalance plus 1 bp a month roll. Test window 2011-01 to 2026-09, post-publication (189 months); 1999-2010 is reported only. Statistics: HAC t of the mean, annualised Sharpe against the pre-registered 0.3 bar, bootstrap lower bound, and DSR over 2 universes (G10, G10 + MXN/ZAR) x 2 signals (AFD sign; AFD + IP-growth regression with ALFRED INDPRO vintages). Report correlation with SPY and with the T-368 cross-sectional carry.

candidates.name: COT speculative / hedging pressure across futures (Fan-Fernandez-Perez-Fuertes-Miffre 2018; Basu-Miffre 2013)
candidates.summary: Rank futures by large speculators' net position relative to its own one-year average, from the CFTC Commitments of Traders report. Go long contracts with positive speculative pressure and short those with negative. The signal captures the hedging-pressure (normal backwardation) premium and is reported to add information beyond momentum and carry. Mandel tested only gold COT extremes (T-405 parked, T-456 blocked).
candidates.mechanism: Keynesian normal backwardation: commercial hedgers pay a premium to speculators who take the other side of their hedges. Shifts in net positioning reveal where that premium is high. The other side is hedgers, producers and consumers, paying for insurance.
adjacent_variables: COT positioning (legacy commercial/non-commercial; disaggregated managed money)
candidates.assets: CME/ICE US futures: commodities, currencies, equity indexes (rates excluded per evidence)
candidates.claimed_effect: Fan, Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes and Miffre, 'Speculative Pressure' (2018; CXO summary opened). 84 futures, 1992-09 to 2018-05, gross annualised: commodities 4.1% (Sharpe 0.61); currencies 2.5% (0.47); equity indexes 4.0% (0.50); interest rates -0.7% (-0.28). The authors say it is robust to reasonable frictions given low turnover, with episodic multi-year losses. Basu, Oomen and Stremme (2000-2006 test): commercial hedging-pressure timing on gold and silver gave alphas of about 11% and 19% a year against the S&P 500, ignoring frictions.
candidates.replication: Several papers from the same research group (Miffre and co-authors). I found no independent post-2018 test. Time-series momentum, the obvious competitor, duplicates T-300/T-310/T-58, all not_supported. Huang-Li-Wang-Zhou (JFE 2020, 55 contracts 1985-2015) show TSMOM is matched by a historical-mean strategy, and Mandel already uses that as its null. Speculative pressure must therefore be judged against both TSMOM and the historical-mean rule. Data blocker shared with T-371: Mandel lacks per-contract futures histories, and continuous front-month series carry roll gaps.

Long positive, short negative, equal risk at 10% annualised volatility per asset using trailing 60-day volatility. candidates.name: Factor momentum across a broad factor set (Ehsani-Linnainmaa 2022); duplicate of T-388
candidates.summary: Most equity factors are positively autocorrelated, so holding factors after positive trailing returns times them, and this factor momentum subsumes individual-stock momentum. Duplicates T-388, which failed on 6 factors over 1964-2026: Sharpe difference -0.04 [-0.24, +0.17], DSR 0.08. It is kept only because the published claim rests on breadth, 20 factors and up to 212 OSAP long-short series, which T-388 did not test.
candidates.mechanism: Factor returns drift because of slow-moving risk premia or underreaction at the factor level. Stock momentum is the aggregate of those factor autocorrelations. The other side is investors and arbitrageurs who rebalance factor exposures slowly.
candidates.assets: US equity factor portfolios; tradable only through factor ETFs (MTUM, QUAL, VLUE, USMV, SIZE), whose holdings are not the paper factors
candidates.claimed_effect: Ehsani-Linnainmaa (NBER WP 25551, opened), factors from July 1963 to December 2015: the average factor earns 1 bp a month after a year of losses and 53 bps a month after a positive year; factor momentum explains all forms of stock momentum. Paper factors are gross of costs.
candidates.replication: Contested. Fan et al. (Financial Review) find factor momentum does not outperform long-only factor holdings in either of their samples, possibly specific to a subset of factors. Mandel's T-388 is not supported on 6 factors, with a post-2019 difference of +0.06 reported. Post-publication decay of the underlying anomalies (the McLean-Pontiff pattern) lowers the base. Low priority.

candidates.name: BTC's overnight/weekend move into crypto-linked US equities (COIN, MSTR, IBIT) at the open
candidates.summary: BTC trades 24/7 while COIN, MSTR and IBIT trade only in US hours. Test whether BTC's move between the equity close and the next open is fully priced at the open, or whether the equity keeps drifting toward it during the session. The closest registry entry is T-424 (BTC leads alts, hourly), which failed: the lagged BTC coefficient was negative (-0.035, HAC t -2.76) out of sample. Child learning: Kalshi's hourly crypto ladders are not slow to spot.
candidates.mechanism: Hypothesised only. Equity investors and opening auctions may under-incorporate news that arrived while the equity market was closed. Crypto-equity linkage strengthened after 2020, so BTC information matters more for these names. The other side is opening-auction participants.
adjacent_variables: MSTR mNAV (market cap vs BTC holdings)
candidates.assets: COIN, MSTR, IBIT, FBTC (Alpaca); BTC reference from Coinbase
candidates.claimed_effect: No direct predictability claim was found. IMF (2022, opened): the BTC-S&P 500 correlation rose from 0.01 in 2017-19 to 0.36 in 2020-21. During the pandemic, BTC volatility explained about one-sixth of S&P 500 volatility and about one-tenth of the variation in its returns, with spillovers rising in stress. That is co-movement, not lead-lag.
candidates.replication: None. Mandel's T-424 and the children's crypto results point to efficient cross-venue pricing at hourly horizons. Expected not_supported; recording it closes off a commonly suggested idea. The web-search budget ran out before an academic source on crypto-equity open-gap efficiency could be searched.

candidates.proposed_test: Data: local 5-minute bars (60 days) and 60-minute bars (2 years) for COIN, MSTR and IBIT; Coinbase BTC-USD 1-minute (archived). Signal: BTC log return from the 16:00 ET equity close to 09:30 ET, including weekends for Monday. Control: the equity's own open gap. Test whether the residual mispricing, BTC move x trailing beta minus the gap, predicts the 09:35 to 16:00 return. Entry at 09:35, after the auction, to avoid the opening print. overlaps.note: Industry-level OWN 12-1 momentum on the 9 sector SPDRs: alpha +17.3 bps/month 1999-2026, CI -5.9 to +41.0, under the random-pick 95th percentile. Linked-industry momentum is a different signal, but this failure lowers the base rate.
Re-registration of T-306 (CAPM alpha). Same failure.
Residual momentum on sector SPDRs also fails.
Momentum at the factor level fails. Same family of slow-diffusion stories.
Other-asset leaders (F0F1) raise mean IC (+0.030 vs F0 +0.011) but not net Sharpe. A cross-asset lead shows up as correlation and does not survive as a trade.
Precedent for the french-industry49-daily data path only.

learnings.finding: Price momentum at the industry level does not pass after costs and the permutation null on 1999-2026.

The edges that exist are reference prices: a sharper source that LEADS a thinner crowd. Here the linked industry is a candidate leading source only if the follower's holders really do not read it. A consensus the crowd already reads does not lead.
Cross-asset leads found by search sit at the noise level. The best of 48 macro relations (2s10s -> XLF, t +2.6) is undeflated; nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close.
Cross-asset leaders add a little IC but no net edge. 0 of 306 cells pass DSR.
Most published anomalies decay. The paper's own mechanism predicts weakening as analyst coverage and 13F ownership rose after 2005, so 2006-2026 is a hard out-of-sample test.

registration.claim: Over 2006-01 to 2026-08, across the 49 Fama-French industries, a monthly portfolio long the top and short the bottom quintile of the input-output-weighted month-t return of each industry's linked industries earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps per leg on turnover, with a positive FF5+UMD alpha. The links come from the latest BEA Use table published before month-end t, the own industry is excluded, and the portfolio is formed at the t close and held through t+1. The variant (customer or supplier links, 1- or 3-month formation) is chosen on 1990-2005 only.
registration.statistic: Test-window mean monthly net long-short return with Newey-West (lag 6) t; FF5+UMD alpha and its NW t; Fama-MacBeth slope of the month t+1 industry return on the linked return, controlling for the own month-t return and own 12-1 momentum; DSR over the 4 variants.
registration.null: Mean net long-short return <= 0 over 2006-01..2026-08: linked-industry returns carry no information beyond own-industry returns.
registration.procedure: Compound the daily FF49 returns to calendar months. Map each BEA benchmark Use table to FF49 by SIC ranges (NAICS tables via the Census concordance). Customer weight w_ij = share of industry i's intermediate output sold to j; supplier weight = share of j's inputs bought from i; final demand and the diagonal are excluded. Each table enters at its hard-coded BEA release date, never its reference year. At each month-end t compute L_i = sum_j w_ij r_j(t) (or over t-2..t), sort into quintiles (9-10 industries a leg), equal weight, enter at the t close, hold month t+1, and charge 10 bps per leg on turnover. Choose the variant on 1990-01..2005-12 net Sharpe and freeze it. Inference: studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks, 10,000 draws, one-sided. Report the halves 2006-2015 and 2016-2026, a 5-year rolling decay curve, and the 11 SPDR sector ETFs with BEA weights (2000 on; XLRE/XLC from inception) as a tradability check, reported only.
registration.data: french-industry49-daily, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3, daily-history sector SPDRs; to fetch: BEA Use tables + concordance (free)
registration.pass: Test-window net mean > 0 with one-sided bootstrap p < 0.05, both halves positive, FF5+UMD alpha NW t > 1.65, beats the 95th percentile of the permuted-link placebo, and DSR > 0.95 over 4 variants.
registration.controls: Own month-t return and own 12-1 momentum (Fama-MacBeth and a double sort). Placebo: IO weights permuted across industries with row sums kept, 1,000 draws. One variant, fixed before 2006; no grid. 10 bps per leg. No BEA table used before its release date.

rows.notes: This is the strongest-evidenced candidate in the cluster (peer reviewed, OSAP t 4.1-5.0), and 2006-2026 is genuinely out of sample. It needs one free fetch: the BEA tables plus a concordance, or the OSAP series once the quota resets. The permuted-link placebo is the key refutation: industries co-move, so the IO weights must beat random links. Horizontal (competitor) links (Schlag-Zeng) would be a separate later registration, not an extra variant here.

registration.procedure: Search EDGAR full text for 10-K phrases ('accounted for 10%', 'major customer', 'largest customer'). Resolve the names through sec-cik-lookup and sec-company-tickers; a link enters at the 10-K acceptance time from sec-submissions and lapses after 12 months. Customer signal = value-weighted month-t return of the linked customers, using market cap from close x dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding last filed before t. Supplier terciles, value-weighted, entered at the t close (weekly variant: Monday open) and held one month (one week). Months with fewer than 30 linked suppliers are dropped. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month (13-week) blocks, one-sided.
registration.data: daily-history-*, sec-submissions-b*, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-cik-lookup, sec-company-tickers; to fetch: EDGAR full-text search hits and 10-K text
registration.pass: At least 60 months with >= 30 linked suppliers (else inconclusive). Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, DSR > 0.95 over 2 variants.
registration.controls: The supplier's own month-t return and its FF49 industry return (via SIC), and size. Placebo: random customers drawn from the same industry. 10 bps per side. The survivor-tilted universe is stated.

rows.notes: Low priority: the effect is documented as decayed (value-weighted insignificant after 2005), the data needs text extraction, and the archive lacks the small suppliers that carry the effect. Park until the industry-level IO test (io-linked-industry-momentum) reports; run this only if that one passes.

rows.name: Big / high-volume stocks lead small / low-volume stocks within an industry (Hou 2007; Chordia-Swaminathan 2000)

overlaps.note: The closest Mandel lead-lag test (big leader BTC to small followers, the alts) has a negative lagged coefficient out of sample (-0.035, HAC t -2.76).
Volume information (high-volume return premium) failed on ETFs.
Volume-conditioned momentum failed on ETFs.
Sector-ETF-residual stat-arb on S&P 500 survivors fails: within-industry relative pricing is not tradable at large caps.
Lead-lag of the same asset across venues (NYSE/TSX) does not cover costs.
Intraday SPY/QQQ leaders (F1) for single stocks: no cell passes.

learnings.finding: crypto-proxy-crossref (43 trials): the leader's move shows up as beta, not a tradable lead.
The lagging book does follow the leader (23% of the gap in 90 s), but hitting the lagging ask marks out at -1.9 to -2.2 points. A real lead is not a taker trade once the spread is paid.
The archive is large-cap heavy, so the small, neglected follower leg that carries the published effect is mostly absent. The expected result is weak or null.

rows.missing_data: Nothing blocking. SIC in sec-submissions is the current profile, not point-in-time; it is slow-moving and flagged. The universe is survivor-tilted.

registration.claim: Over 2015-01 to 2026-09, within 2-digit-SIC industries of the daily-history archive with at least 6 names, the low-dollar-volume tercile's week t+1 return (Monday open to Friday close) loads positively on the cap-weighted week-t return of the industry's high-dollar-volume tercile, controlling for the followers' own week-t return and SPY's week-t return (Fama-MacBeth slope > 0). A cross-industry quintile long-short of followers built on that signal also earns a positive mean net return after 5 bps per side plus half the Corwin-Schultz spread.
registration.statistic: Fama-MacBeth slope with NW t over weeks; net weekly long-short mean with HAC t; DSR over 4 variants (week or day horizon; dollar-volume or size split).
registration.procedure: Dollar volume = trailing 60-session mean of close x volume, known at the Friday close. Market cap = close x the last dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding filed before t. A name enters at its first bar and leaves at its last. Leader return: Friday close to Friday close; followers are entered at the Monday open, which skips the nonsynchronous bounce, and exited at the Friday close. Corwin-Schultz spread from the trailing 20 days of daily highs and lows. Choose the variant on 2005-2014, test on 2015-2026. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 8-week blocks. Reported only: sector SPDR leaders vs member stocks on the 5-minute bars (60 days).
registration.data: daily-history-*, sec-submissions-b*, sec-companyfacts-b*, daily-history-SPY
registration.pass: FM slope one-sided p < 0.05 AND net long-short mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both test halves positive, DSR > 0.95 over 4 variants.
registration.controls: Followers' own week-t return, SPY week-t return (market lead-lag), and a random-other-industry leader placebo (intra- vs inter-industry). Monday-open entry removes stale-close bounce. Costs include a spread term for illiquid names. The survivorship direction is stated.

rows.notes: Cheap to run on archived data, but the universe lacks the small caps where the effect lives, and Mandel's lead-lag record (T-424, Hurst's 43 crypto-proxy trials) is uniformly negative. Run it to record the null. Do not widen the universe by scanning thresholds.

rows.name: Industry returns lead the stock market (Hong-Torous-Valkanov 2007), contested

overlaps.note: The template market-timing predictor test (orthogonalised sentiment -> size premium) gives R2_OS -8.6% (CW t +1.67, Holm p 0.48). Monthly predictors fail out of sample in Mandel's hands.
A bond-momentum cross-asset signal timing SPY is significantly worse than SPY's own TSMOM (Sharpe difference -0.216, CI -0.412 to -0.029).
Industry-return-based rules on sector SPDRs fail.
Daily ML with cross-asset leaders for the equity_etf class: no cell passes.

learnings.finding: On 1946-2013 with 48 industries, only 1 to 7 industries are significant, consistent with chance and with market efficiency.
macro-relations: the best of 48 (2s10s -> XLF, t +2.6) is undeflated. Picking the best of many lead candidates produces exactly this kind of claim.
Liquid markets are calibrated within noise, and price-only signals start from a negative base rate.

rows.missing_data: None. french-industry49 ends 2026-08 (revised monthly; research proxy for real-time industry returns).

registration.claim: Over 2003-01 to 2026-08, expanding-window OLS forecasts of the month t+1 market excess return from the month-t returns of six pre-named FF49 industry groups (financial = EW Banks/Insur/Fin, Rtail, RlEst, metals = EW Steel/Mines, Oil, services = EW PerSv/BusSv), each alone and as a first-principal-component composite, achieve Campbell-Thompson R2_OS > 0 against the expanding historical mean with Holm-adjusted Clark-West p < 0.05 over the 7 trials. The long-SPY-or-bills rule switched on the winning forecast beats the historical-mean rule after 2 bps per switch.
registration.statistic: R2_OS (Campbell-Thompson) vs the expanding historical mean; Clark-West MSPE-adjusted HAC t; Holm over 7 trials; Sharpe difference of the switching rule vs the historical-mean rule.
registration.null: R2_OS <= 0: the industry forecasts are no better than the historical mean.
registration.procedure: Industry returns compounded to calendar months from the daily FF49 file. Target for estimation: FF Mkt-RF month t+1 (1963-07 on). The month t+1 forecast uses OLS fitted on 1963-07..t, so the first OOS forecast is for 2003-01, after HTV's sample. The PC1 composite is estimated inside the same expanding window. Pre-registered signs: metals and Oil negative, others positive; sign-restricted forecasts are reported. Rule: at the next session's close after month-end t, hold SPY (adjclose) if forecast > DTB3/12, else bills; 2 bps per switch. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks, for the Sharpe difference.
registration.data: french-industry49-daily, french-ff5-daily, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: At least one of the 7 trials has R2_OS > 0 with Holm-adjusted CW p < 0.05, R2_OS > 0 in both halves (2003-2014, 2015-2026), and a switching-rule Sharpe above the historical-mean rule with paired bootstrap lower bound > 0.
registration.controls: Historical-mean benchmark (Goyal-Welch). Only the 6 pre-named groups plus the composite are trials; the other 43 industries are reported only as a placebo distribution. 2 bps per switch. Deflate jointly with the other equity-premium predictors in this cluster (oil, copper, gold/platinum, credit).

rows.notes: A cheap refutation run, expected not_supported. Recording it protects the substrate from a famous claim. Build one shared equity-premium-predictor harness (Campbell-Thompson R2_OS + Clark-West + switching rule, reusing T-458's code) for this candidate and the oil, copper, gold/platinum and credit candidates. Count all their trials (about 22) as one deflation family.

rows.name: Oil price changes predict lower equity returns (Driesprong-Jacobsen-Maat 2008)

overlaps.note: Precedent for oil data handling: CL=F roll windows and April 2020 are masked.
Oil's measured structural premium is in volatility (crude VRP positive, CI excludes 0), not in direction.
OVX VRP supported.
Template monthly predictor fails out of sample (R2_OS negative).
Oil is not among the F1 leaders (SPY, QQQ, VIX, DXY, TNX, BTC, TLT, GLD), so no ML evidence either way.

learnings.finding: A reference must lead the book on the identical event. Oil does not price equity earnings; it is at best an indirect fundamentals input, the class Mandel and the children keep finding already in the price.
In Hurst's 48 macro-to-ETF relations no oil lead survived; the best was 2s10s -> XLF.
Oil-related premia Mandel has confirmed are volatility premia (T-63, T-512), not directional predictability.

rows.missing_data: Primary trial testable now on CL-F. The spot variants need fred-DCOILWTICO (free; 1986 on), which would lengthen training from about 112 to about 280 months and avoid roll gaps.

registration.claim: Over 2010-01 to 2026-09, the log change in the WTI front-month (CL-F) close over calendar month t predicts SPY's month t+1 excess return with a negative expanding-window OLS slope, a Campbell-Thompson R2_OS > 0 vs the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05), and a long-SPY-or-bills switching rule that beats the historical-mean rule after 2 bps per switch.
registration.statistic: R2_OS vs the expanding historical mean; Clark-West HAC t; NW t of the slope (pre-registered negative); switching-rule Sharpe minus the historical-mean rule's.
registration.procedure: CL-F month-end closes (CME settlement-time bar, known by 17:00 ET; acted on at the next SPY session's close, the T-430 convention). Log change over the month; non-positive prints are masked (T-468's April 2020 rule). Target: SPY adjclose excess return from that fill close to the next month's fill close (DTB3 accrual). Expanding OLS from 2000-09, first forecast 2010-01. Declared trials: monthly CL-F (primary), weekly CL-F (Friday-close change -> next week's Monday open to Friday close), monthly and weekly WTI spot (fred-DCOILWTICO, once fetched). SPY's own month-t return is reported as an extra regressor. Split-sample sign check 2010-2015 vs 2016-2026. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
registration.data: daily-history-CL-F, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3; to fetch: fred-DCOILWTICO (spot variants)
registration.pass: Primary trial: R2_OS > 0 with CW one-sided p < 0.05, slope NW t < -1.65, R2_OS > 0 in both 2010-2015 and 2016-2026, switching-rule Sharpe above the historical-mean rule with paired lower bound > 0, and DSR > 0.95 over the 4 declared trials.
registration.controls: Historical-mean benchmark. Sign fixed in advance. No threshold on the oil move. 2 bps per switch. Deflate jointly with the cluster's equity-premium predictors (HTV industries, copper, gold/platinum, credit).

rows.notes: Cheap and testable now. The shale era and oil's turn into a demand-driven risk-on asset after 2008 make a sign flip plausible, which is why the split-sample check is gated. Also add CL_F and HG_F r1/r5/r20 to the ML leader list, but as a NEW pre-registered IC family (T-579 is already registered and must not be widened after the fact).

rows.name: Industrial metal (copper) returns predict equity returns with a business-cycle-dependent sign (Jacobsen-Marshall-Visaltanachoti 2019)

overlaps.note: Metals trend timing fails against the historical-mean strategy.
Same, re-registered with DSR.
Its copper variant (HG=F vs CPER) was not archived then; HG-F and CPER are archived now.
Precedent for using first-release ALFRED vintages in a macro-conditioned predictor; that predictor failed out of sample.

learnings.finding: A value enters only once published. fred-USREC (NBER dates) is announced months late, so it can serve only as a look-ahead placebo.
2010-2026 has very few contraction months (essentially 2020). The recession slope b2 cannot be identified, and b1 is close to the unconditional copper slope.
In Hurst's 48 macro-to-ETF relations no metals lead survived.

rows.missing_data: ALFRED vintages of CFNAI-MA3 (free; alfred.stlouisfed.org), which are essential for the real-time state. Also FRED PCOPPUSDM (pre-2000 copper) and PALUMUSDM (aluminium) for the second metal, both free.

registration.claim: Over 2010-07 to 2026-09, in months classed as expansion by the CFNAI-MA3 vintage available at month-end t (value > -0.7), the month-t HG-F log return has a negative expanding-window slope for SPY's month t+1 excess return. The state-interacted model achieves R2_OS > 0 vs the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05) and adds R2_OS over the pooled copper model.
registration.statistic: HAC t of b1 (expansion slope); R2_OS and Clark-West t of the interacted model; R2_OS gain over the pooled (state-free) copper model; switching-rule Sharpe vs the historical-mean rule.
registration.procedure: State at t is the latest CFNAI-MA3 vintage with realtime_start <= t (the release about 3-4 weeks after the reference month, so it refers to t-1 or t-2). Copper return from HG-F month-end closes (before 2000-08, PCOPPUSDM monthly averages as available). Model: excess(t+1) = a + b1 x copper(t) x expansion + b2 x copper(t) x contraction, expanding OLS from 1990. b2 is reported, not gated. Rule: long SPY or bills at the next session's close, 2 bps per switch. Trials: {copper, aluminium} x {CFNAI-MA3 > -0.7, > 0}. The ex-post USREC version is reported as a look-ahead placebo only. Studentised block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
registration.data: daily-history-HG-F, daily-history-CPER, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3; to fetch: alfred-CFNAIMA3, fred-PCOPPUSDM, fred-PALUMUSDM
registration.pass: b1 HAC t < -1.65, R2_OS > 0 with CW p < 0.05, R2_OS > 0 in both halves, positive gain over the pooled model, rule beats the historical mean (paired lower bound > 0), and DSR > 0.95 over 4 trials.
registration.controls: Pooled copper model as the nested baseline (the state split must add value). Historical mean. NBER ex-post placebo reported, never decisive. 2 bps. Joint deflation with the cluster's equity-premium predictors.

rows.notes: Needs one free fetch (ALFRED CFNAI-MA3). The test period is almost all expansion, so this is in effect a test of 'copper up -> lower SPY next month' in expansions. Pre-register that limitation; do not relax the state threshold to manufacture contraction months.

rows.name: Gold-to-platinum price ratio predicts the equity premium (Huang-Kilic 2019)

overlaps.note: A metal price ratio (gold/silver) as a signal fails.
Gold/silver ratio extremes fail.
Gold/silver ratio reversion fails.
A tail-risk state variable (SKEW) does not predict SPY drawdowns.
SKEW does not raise -2 sigma frequency.
Template monthly predictor fails out of sample.

learnings.source: Mandel archive check (predictor only, no outcomes read)
learnings.finding: Monthly-average GC-F/PL-F ratio: 0.43-1.13 over 2000-08..2013-12 and 0.87-3.40 over 2014-2026; 88% of post-2014 months lie above the pre-2014 maximum. The level predictor is far outside its estimation range, so the level trial is inconclusive under the pre-registered structural-break rule.
The option-implied tail-risk state variable available to Mandel (SKEW) failed to predict equity tails.
Internationally the first difference of GP, not the level, carries the predictive power. That supports using the change as the primary trial.

rows.missing_data: None for the 2000-2026 design. The paper's 1975-1999 history (LBMA fixings) is not archived; it is not needed for an out-of-sample test from 2014.

registration.claim: Over 2014-01 to 2026-09, the 1-month change in the log gold/platinum ratio (monthly averages of GC-F and PL-F daily closes) predicts SPY's month t+1 excess return positively, with Campbell-Thompson R2_OS > 0 vs the expanding historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05). The long-SPY-or-bills rule switched on that forecast beats the historical-mean rule after 2 bps per switch.
registration.statistic: R2_OS vs the historical mean; Clark-West HAC t; NW t of the slope (pre-registered positive); switching-rule Sharpe minus the historical-mean rule's; IVX or residual-bootstrap persistence correction for the level trial.
registration.procedure: Log GP = log of the mean GC-F close over calendar month t minus log of the mean PL-F close (both CME 17:00 ET bars, complete at the month-end close; acted on at the next SPY session's close). Expanding OLS from 2000-09 (first forecast 2014-01, 160 training months). Declared trials: Delta-logGP at 1 month (primary), log GP level at 1 month, and both at 12 months on non-overlapping annual observations (reported). Structural-break rule, outcome-free: if more than 50% of 2014-2026 level values lie outside the 2000-2013 range, the level trials are inconclusive. The archive check gives 88%, so the level trials are pre-declared inconclusive. GLD/PPLT ratio cross-check from 2010. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
registration.data: daily-history-GC-F, daily-history-PL-F, daily-history-GLD, daily-history-PPLT, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Primary trial: R2_OS > 0 with CW one-sided p < 0.05, slope NW t > 1.65, R2_OS > 0 in both halves (2014-2019, 2020-2026), switching rule beats the historical mean (paired lower bound > 0), and DSR > 0.95 over the 4 declared trials.
registration.controls: Historical-mean benchmark. Persistence (Stambaugh) correction. Pre-declared range rule for the level. GLD/PPLT tradable cross-check. 2 bps. Joint deflation with the cluster's equity-premium predictors.

rows.notes: Testable now. The level version the paper rests on is already disqualified out of sample by its own range, an outcome-free finding worth recording. Only the change version is a live test. Prior is low: tail-risk proxies have failed in Mandel, and gold's 2024-26 central-bank-driven rally is a non-risk reason for GP to rise.

rows.name: Equity returns lead corporate-bond (HY/IG) ETF returns (Downing-Underwood-Xing 2009; Jiang-Li-Xiao 2024)

overlaps.note: The bond_etf h=1 F0F1 ridge cell shows the lead as correlation and no edge: IC +0.102, net -0.05 bp per trade, DSR 0.014 (560 trades). h=5 ridge: +3.8 bp, DSR 0.004.
Intraday bond_etf F0F1 at 1 bp per side. 15m ridge: IC +0.066, net -1.96 bp (1,074 trades). 30m ridge: IC +0.098, net -2.47 bp. 45m gbm: IC +0.37 on only 65 trades, +2.4 bp, DSR 0.016.
Credit ETF timing (LQD-IEF on BAA10Y) fails.
Cross-asset bond/equity timing fails.

learnings.finding: SPY-to-bond-ETF lead shows up as positive IC at 15m-1d horizons, but net per trade is <= 0 at 1 bp per side. Per-bar HYG moves are too small for the IC to pay the spread.
A lead-lag read from last-trade prints is suspect until fresh quotes confirm it. A real follow (Polymarket follows Kalshi) still loses as a taker.
Equity predicts bonds with a one-month lag, but not profitably after costs.

rows.missing_data: The issuer-equity basket needs point-in-time HYG holdings (iShares publishes only current holdings); it is replaced by IWM as the second leader. Quote midpoints are not archived, so the stale-print caveat cannot be addressed and is stated.

registration.claim: From 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 on Yahoo 60-minute bars, with every parameter fixed on 2023-11 to 2025-09, holding HYG in SPY's direction from the next bar's open to its close whenever SPY's bar-h return exceeds one trailing 20-session standard deviation in absolute value earns a positive mean net return per trade after 2 bps per side.
registration.statistic: Net mean per trade with session-block bootstrap one-sided p; HAC t of b in HYG(h+1) = a + b SPY(h) + c HYG(h); DSR over 8 cells (HYG or LQD x 60-minute or daily last-hour x SPY or IWM leader).
registration.procedure: Bars are stamped at the open; a bar's return is known at its close. Entry at the next bar's open, exit at its close. The 15:30 bar's signal maps to the daily cell instead: SPY's 15:30-16:00 return -> HYG next-day open-to-close. Threshold: 1 sd of the leader's bar returns over the trailing 20 sessions, no other threshold. Cost: 1 bp half-spread + 1 bp slippage per side. Lockbox 2026-10-01 onward stays sealed. Bootstrap: circular blocks of 5 sessions, 10,000 draws. Placebo: a random 30-stock basket from the 60-minute stock bars as leader.
registration.data: mandel/ml_data/bars/60m (SPY, IWM, HYG, LQD, IEF), daily-history-HYG, daily-history-LQD
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves of the test year positive, beats the random-basket placebo, DSR > 0.95 over the 8 cells plus the T-577/T-578 bond_etf F0F1 cells counted as prior trials.
registration.controls: HYG's own lagged bar return. Random-basket leader placebo. Yahoo-open-vs-print check as in T-549. Costs stated per side. Registered as a successor to the T-578 bond_etf reading, not a new discovery.

rows.notes: Mandel already holds the answer in outline: the direction is right and the edge is absent after even 1 bp a side. Run only to close the question with the stricter design. Do not tune the threshold. A maker-only variant (resting HYG bids) cannot be measured from bars and would need its own forward record.

rows.name: Corporate-bond market information predicts the equity premium (Li-Yuan-Zhou; excess bond premium)

overlaps.note: Same variable (BAA10Y), different design: level-based timing of LQD-IEF. Sharpe 0.23 in 2013-2026, CI -0.29 to +0.53, DSR 0.43.
A bond-market signal used to time SPY was significantly worse than SPY's own TSMOM (Sharpe difference -0.216, CI -0.412 to -0.029).
Template predictor with R2_OS negative.
Another aggregate predictor of the SPY excess return (short interest), blocked.

learnings.finding: Credit-spread state does not time credit itself well after costs over 2003-2026.
Using a bond-market signal for equity timing hurt Sharpe significantly.
EBP is revised as balance-sheet data arrive. Only a first-published vintage stamped at its release can enter, and the Fed's CSV gives only the current vintage.

rows.missing_data: The EBP change trial needs EBP vintages (the Fed CSV is current-vintage only, so it is blocked unless vintages are reconstructed). The cross-sectional bond-return skewness trial needs TRACE bond returns (not free at scale) and is blocked. Three trials are testable now.

registration.claim: Over 2010-01 to 2026-09, each of three pre-signed credit predictors of the month t+1 market excess return achieves Campbell-Thompson R2_OS > 0 vs the expanding historical mean with Holm-adjusted Clark-West p < 0.05: the month-t change in BAA10Y (negative), the duration-hedged LQD excess return (positive) and the duration-hedged HYG excess return (positive). The long-SPY-or-bills rule switched on the passing forecast beats the historical-mean rule after 2 bps per switch.
registration.statistic: R2_OS; Clark-West HAC t with Holm over 3 trials; NW t of the slope with the pre-registered sign; switching-rule Sharpe minus the historical-mean rule's.
registration.procedure: BAA10Y daily month-end print (available 20:00 UTC; traded at the next session's close, as in T-430). Credit excess return = r_HYG(t) - beta x r_IEF(t), with beta from the trailing 36 monthly returns known at t; LQD the same. Estimation target: FF Mkt-RF (from 1986 for BAA10Y; from the first 60-month window for the ETF trials, so the HYG trial forecasts from 2012-05). Trading-rule target: SPY adjclose excess. Expanding OLS. EBP and skewness trials are listed and blocked. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
registration.data: fred-BAA10Y, daily-history-HYG, daily-history-LQD, daily-history-IEF, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: At least one testable trial has R2_OS > 0 with Holm-adjusted CW p < 0.05 and the pre-registered sign, R2_OS > 0 in both halves, and a switching rule that beats the historical mean (paired lower bound > 0).
registration.controls: Historical-mean benchmark. SPY's own month-t return as a control regressor (reported). T-430 and T-481 counted as prior trials. 2 bps per switch. Joint deflation with the cluster's equity-premium predictors.

rows.notes: The available proxies are crude stand-ins for the paper's TRACE cross-section, so a null is weak evidence against the paper. The skewness predictor, which the paper calls strongest, is untestable here. Run it inside the shared predictor harness; do not fund a separate build.

rows.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover large caps (Medhat-Schmeling 2022)

overlaps.note: ETF 6-month momentum conditioned on LOW turnover. Out of sample -0.62%/quarter (HAC t -1.61). Different horizon, universe and direction of conditioning.
High-volume return premium on ETFs fails. Volume information alone does not pay.
Plain weekly cross-sectional reversal on ETFs fails.
Reversal as liquidity provision on ETFs fails.
28-stock 20-day cells with r20 and relative-volume features: ALL ridge sign +381 bp/trade (IC +0.333, DSR 0.365), F2 gbm xs +441 bp (DSR 0.126), on only 9 periods. Suggestive, not a pass.

learnings.finding: Price-only strategies start from a negative base rate. STMOM conditions on turnover, a non-price input, which is the kind of variable that could break that prior.
Daily stock models combining own returns with relative volume found the strongest (still undeflated) 20-day signals in the grid.
Published anomalies decay, and PnL over about 93 months has low power. At the paper's largest-500 size (0.42%/month, sd about 2.2%), 93 months give t of about 1.8 gross and about 1.2 net.

rows.missing_data: None blocking. The universe is survivor-tilted, mostly current large caps with some delisted names. That biases the loser leg upward, so against STMOM; state it.

registration.claim: Over 2019-01 to 2026-09, among the 500 largest daily-history US common stocks by month-end market cap, a value-weighted portfolio long high-turnover month-t winners and short high-turnover month-t losers, entered at the next session's close and held one month, earns a positive mean net return after 5 bps per side on actual turnover. Winners, losers and high turnover come from independent median 2x2 sorts on the month-t return and month-t turnover, where turnover = month-t volume / shares outstanding last filed before t.
registration.statistic: Monthly net mean with NW (lag 3) t; FF5+UMD alpha with NW t; DSR over 4 variants (2x2 or tercile sorts x value or equal weight).
registration.procedure: Universe: names with a bar at month-end t and shares outstanding filed before t and under 400 days old (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, else us-gaap CommonStockSharesOutstanding); ETFs, indices, futures and crypto excluded. Shares are put on Yahoo's split-adjusted basis using daily-events splits between the fact's end date and t. Market cap = close x shares; keep the largest 500. Turnover = sum of daily volume over month t / shares. Independent median sorts; value weights at t; filled at the next session's close; 5 bps per side on weight changes. STREV* (low-turnover losers minus winners) reported. 2010-2018 overlaps the paper and is reported only. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 6-month blocks, one-sided. Refutation: turnover permuted across months within each stock, 1,000 draws.
registration.data: daily-history-*, daily-events-*, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, sec-company-tickers, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves (2019-01..2022-10, 2022-11..2026-09) positive, FF5+UMD alpha > 0, above the 95th percentile of the shuffled-turnover placebo, and DSR > 0.95 over 4 variants.
registration.controls: Plain 1-month return sort (STREV) and UMD as baselines. Shuffled-turnover placebo. 5 bps per side on actual turnover. Survivorship direction stated. Power reported (expected t about 1.2 net at the paper's effect size).

rows.notes: The best candidate in the cluster to test now. Turnover is a non-price input, the paper reports the effect growing to 2018 and surviving costs at large caps, and Mandel's own daily ML hints in the same direction. Its weakness is power: if it fails on t alone with a positive point estimate, the verdict should be 'inconclusive (power)', not a refutation, and it moves to a forward paper record.

rows.name: VIX-conditioned short-term reversal as liquidity provision (Nagel 2012); partial duplicate of T-462

overlaps.note: Same claim on 68 ETFs, weekly. Out of sample -0.35%/week (HAC t -2.58); the VIX high-minus-low difference is -0.06%/week (t -0.34). This candidate changes the universe (stocks), horizon (daily) and execution (open entry).
Weekly ETF reversal fails net.
A daily reversal premium exists on the SPY index: IBS < 0.2 next day +12 bps above unconditional, DSR 0.976.
IBS reversal is stronger in anti-persistent regimes. The conditioning idea has worked once in Mandel.
SPY gap-reversal at the open fails.

learnings.finding: The reversal baseline has positive IC daily (+0.049, annual SR +0.28) but loses intraday after costs (IC +0.026, SR -29.5). Gross reversal exists and costs decide.
VIX predicts only small-cap reversal (t -2.13); large-cap reversal is not VIX-predictable. Mandel's universe is large caps.
Liquidity-provision returns are real only at the front of the queue. Strict fills earn about zero, so a close-price reversal overstates the capturable return.

rows.missing_data: None. Quote midpoints are not archived, so the open-print entry is a trade print and is flagged.

registration.claim: Over 2013-01 to 2026-09, a daily dollar-neutral reversal portfolio on the top-500 daily-history stocks by trailing dollar volume, with weights proportional to minus the demeaned return from close t-6 to close t-1 and held from the open to the close of day t, has a net daily return that rises with VIX at close t-2 (positive slope). Its mean net return in the top trailing-252-day VIX tercile is also positive, after 3 bps per side on gross turnover.
registration.statistic: HAC (lag 10) t of the slope of the net daily return on VIX(t-2); top-VIX-tercile net mean with one-sided bootstrap p; DSR over 4 variants (stocks or FF49 industries x 1- or 5-day formation) plus T-462's 18 cells as prior trials.
registration.null: VIX slope <= 0, and top-tercile net mean <= 0.
registration.procedure: Membership: top 500 by trailing 20-session dollar volume with price >= $5, known at close t-1. Weights scaled to $1 long and $1 short. Entry at the day-t open (skips the close-print bounce), exit at the day-t close. VIX close from cboe-VIX-history (available 21:30 UTC) at t-2. VIX terciles from the trailing 252 sessions. Formation length chosen on 2000-2012, tested on 2013-2026. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 20-day blocks. The FF49-industry version is reported gross as a costless diagnostic. The close-to-close version is reported only as a bounce-inflated upper bound.
registration.data: daily-history-*, cboe-VIX-history, french-industry49-daily, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: VIX slope HAC t > 1.65 AND top-tercile net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive, DSR > 0.95 with T-462's cells counted.
registration.controls: Unconditional reversal net as baseline. Portfolio beta reported (dollar neutral). Open entry removes the bid-ask bounce. 3 bps per side on gross turnover. One VIX conditioning (terciles), no grid.

rows.notes: T-462 already failed both the reversal and its VIX conditioning on ETFs, and the published VIX link sits in small caps that the archive lacks. Daily large-cap reversal with full daily turnover is very likely cost-dominated. Run it only if the harness from the STMOM test makes it nearly free.

rows.name: Dollar carry trade: long/short the dollar on the average forward discount (Lustig-Roussanov-Verdelhan 2014)

overlaps.note: Same variables, cross-sectional G10 carry: net Sharpe -0.30 in 2013-2026, CI -0.66 to +0.10, gross 0.01. The dollar-carry design is time-series and largely uncorrelated with it.
G10 + MXN + ZAR carry fails.
Multi-sleeve carry composite fails 2013-2026.
CIP basis / dollar lending.

learnings.finding: Carry is one of the premium classes where real edges are expected.
Every carry sleeve Mandel has tested failed out of sample since 2013, after financing and spreads.
Carry is short crash risk with fat left tails. Drawdown and skew must be reported, not just Sharpe.

data: fx-spot-g10 (FRED DEX*, incl. MXN and ZAR)
fx-rates-3m (OECD IR3TIB incl. MX and ZA)
rows.missing_data: Main trial: none. EUR and GBP 3-month rates are stale after 2026-01 (forward-filled and flagged, as in T-368). The AFD + IP-growth variant needs ALFRED INDPRO vintages (free).

registration.claim: Over 2011-01 to 2026-09, going long an equal-weight basket of the 9 non-USD G10 currencies against USD when the one-month-lagged average 3-month rate differential (foreign mean minus US) is positive, and short otherwise, rebalanced monthly at the FRED noon fix, earns an annualised net Sharpe above 0.3 with a stationary-bootstrap lower bound above 0. Costs: 2 bps per leg per rebalance plus 1 bp a month roll.
registration.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe; HAC t of the mean; stationary-bootstrap 95% interval; skew and maximum drawdown; DSR over 4 trials.
registration.null: Uncovered interest parity for the dollar: net Sharpe <= 0.
registration.procedure: AFD_t = mean of 9 foreign IR3TIB minus US IR3TIB, OECD monthly averages lagged one month (T-368 convention). The sign is decided at month-end t and filled at the next business day's noon fix (DEX* are published the next business day). Monthly return = sign x mean basket spot change + sign x AFD/12 (the carry a futures position accrues); costs as stated. 1999-2010 reported only. Stationary bootstrap, mean block 12 months, 5,000 draws. Declared trials: {G10, G10+MXN+ZAR} x {sign of AFD, AFD + US IP-growth regression with ALFRED INDPRO vintages}. Correlation with SPY and with T-368 reported.
registration.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3, daily-history-SPY; to fetch (variant only): alfred-INDPRO
registration.pass: Primary trial (G10, AFD sign): net Sharpe > 0.3 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, both halves (2011-2018, 2019-2026) positive, and DSR > 0.95 over the 4 trials with T-368 and T-431 counted in the family.
registration.controls: Always-short-USD and always-long-USD baselines. Cross-sectional carry (T-368) correlation. Financing and roll costs. Stale-rate splice flagged. No threshold on AFD beyond its sign.

rows.notes: Testable now on archived data with an existing harness (mandel/experiments/carry.py), 189 out-of-sample months, and a structural-premium mechanism. The 2011-2026 regimes (ZIRP short-USD, then long-USD in 2017-19 and 2022-24) make it a real test. Executable via CME FX futures or OANDA. Prior is held down by Mandel's run of carry failures since 2013.

rows.name: COT speculative / hedging pressure across futures (Fan-Fernandez-Perez-Fuertes-Miffre 2018; Basu-Miffre 2013)

overlaps.note: Gold COT positioning extremes: insufficient extremes (20/62 weeks), difference +0.04% (CI -2.90 to +2.70), slope t +0.55. Same variable, single contract.
Gold COT percentile, blocked.
12-1 TSMOM does not beat the historical-mean strategy. That is the baseline this candidate must beat.
Trend rules fail after deflation.
Shares the blocker: no per-contract futures histories for about 15 commodities.

learnings.finding: Point-in-time COT handling is solved (release_rule stamps, backcast rows dropped), but positioning showed no return information on gold.
Hedging pressure is an insurance premium paid by hedgers. That is the structural-premium class where real edges are expected.
Mandel's null for futures timing is the historical-mean strategy. Momentum-like signals have not beaten it.

rows.missing_data: COT for about 22 more contract codes (free; the existing Socrata fetcher, legacy futures-only 6dca-aqww). Continuous front-month histories for NG, HO, RB, ZC, ZS, ZW, KC, SB, CT, LE, HE, NQ, RTY, YM and the FX futures (Yahoo =F, free, roll-masked). Synthetic FX futures can come from fx-spot-g10 + fx-rates-3m.

registration.claim: Over 2018-06 to 2026-09, a monthly portfolio across about 25 liquid US futures (commodities, currencies, equity indices; rates excluded) earns a positive net Sharpe after 5 bps per side plus 2 bps per roll, with positive alpha against 12-1 TSMOM and the historical-mean strategy. It goes long contracts whose large-speculator net position / open interest exceeds its trailing 52-week mean and short those below, each scaled to 10% annualised volatility. COT data enters at the Friday 15:30 ET release and is traded at the next session's open after the last release of the month.
registration.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe with stationary-bootstrap interval; alpha vs the TSMOM 12-1 and historical-mean strategies with NW t; DSR over 6 trials (3 sleeves x non-commercial or reversed commercial pressure).
registration.null: Net Sharpe <= 0, or no alpha over TSMOM and the historical-mean strategy.
registration.procedure: Socrata legacy futures-only rows per contract code, available_at = the release_rule time (holiday shifts honoured; backcast and superseded rows handled as in T-405). Signal = (non-commercial long - short)/OI minus its trailing 52-report mean, read at the last release of each month. Positions: sign of the signal, scaled to 10% vol on trailing 60-session volatility. Returns: roll-masked continuous futures where archived (T-370/T-468 masks), else ETF proxies (flagged), FX from spot + rate differentials. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
registration.data: cftc-cot-legacy-f-*, daily-history futures and ETF proxies, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m; to fetch: COT for the remaining codes and Yahoo continuous futures
registration.pass: Pooled net Sharpe > 0 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, alpha NW t > 1.65 against both baselines, both halves positive, DSR > 0.95 over 6 trials.
registration.controls: TSMOM 12-1 and historical-mean baselines. Equal-risk long-only control. Proxy returns flagged. Publication timing enforced. 5 bps per side + 2 bps per roll. One lookback (52 weeks), no grid.

rows.notes: Worth fetching: low turnover, a structural (insurance) mechanism, and the paper's sample ends 2018-05, so 2018-2026 is clean out of sample. Two free fetches (COT codes, Yahoo continuous futures) also unblock part of T-371. Expect a modest Sharpe; the 2018-2026 sample is about 100 months, so power is limited.

overlaps.note: Same rule on 6 factors, 1964-2026: Sharpe difference -0.04 (CI -0.24 to +0.17), DSR 0.08. Post-2019 +0.06 reported.
The opposite (contrarian factor timing) also fails.
Post-publication RMW mean not significant: factor-level decay.

Factor momentum does not beat long-only factor holdings in independent samples.

Monthly signal = sign of the trailing 12-month factor return, with a 1-month embargo as in T-388. Equal weight across held factors, cash otherwise. Window 2006-01 to the OSAP end. Paper factors are gross of costs: report a 5 bps per switch charge on factor ETFs (MTUM, QUAL, VLUE, USMV, SIZE) 2014-2026 as the investability check.
