Run only when the OSAP file can be fetched cheaply, and treat it as the breadth test of T-388, not a new idea. A pass would still need to be shown on investable factor ETFs before it counts.

rows.name: BTC's overnight/weekend move into crypto-linked US equities (COIN, MSTR, IBIT) at the open

overlaps.note: BTC as a lagged leader fails: the out-of-sample coefficient is negative (HAC t -2.76).
IBIT premium/discount fading vs Coinbase spot: not supported. The ETF tracks BTC closely at its own close.
Overnight drift in QQQ/IWM is positive and intraday drift about zero. The intraday baseline must be controlled.
SPY open-gap reversal fails. Gap handling precedent.
BTC Monday effect. The weekend-to-Monday BTC move is a calendar control.

learnings.finding: crypto-proxy-crossref, 43 trials: BTC's proxies' overnight move is beta, not a lead. Nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close. This is the same question, already answered negatively.
H-btc-us500-lead (BTC perp leads US500 perp off-session) is recording, read on 2026-11-05. It is the cleaner forward version of this idea.
Kalshi's hourly BTC/ETH ladders are not slow to Coinbase spot. Crypto-linked prices absorb BTC quickly.

rows.missing_data: None for the open-entry design. IBIT has no 60-minute bars (5/15/30-minute only, 60 days), so its 10:30 entry is not testable. MSTR mNAV and CME basis are not archived (reported-only controls).

registration.claim: Over 2022-01 to 2026-09, for COIN, MSTR and IBIT (IBIT from 2024-01-11), the stock's same-day open-to-close return loads positively on the residual R = beta_60 x (BTC log return from the prior 16:00 ET close to 09:30 ET) minus the stock's own open gap (pooled HAC t > 1.65). Trading the residual's sign at the official open when |R| exceeds one trailing 60-session sd earns a positive mean net return per trade after 2 bps plus half the trailing Corwin-Schultz spread per side.
registration.statistic: Pooled and per-ticker HAC t of the residual coefficient; net mean per trade with session-block bootstrap one-sided p; DSR over 6 cells (3 tickers x official-open or 10:30 entry) with Hurst's 43 crypto-proxy trials counted as prior trials.
registration.null: Residual coefficient <= 0 and net mean per trade <= 0.
registration.procedure: BTC from Coinbase 1-minute bars: the close of the minute ending 16:00 ET on the prior session (13:00 ET on early closes) to the minute ending 09:30 ET; weekends and holidays included for Monday and post-holiday sessions. Beta is the trailing 60-session regression of the stock's close-to-close return on BTC over the same windows, known at the prior close. Entry at the official open (market-on-open via Alpaca), exit at the close. 10:30 entry from the 60-minute bars for COIN/MSTR from 2023-11. Chronological split: train on the first 60% of sessions (thresholds and betas only), test on the last 40%. Circular bootstrap, 5-session blocks.
registration.data: daily-history-COIN, daily-history-MSTR, daily-history-IBIT, daily-history-FBTC, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD-*, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, mandel/ml_data/bars/60m
registration.pass: In the test 40%: pooled residual coefficient HAC t > 1.65, net mean per trade > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive on at least 2 of 3 tickers, DSR > 0.95 over the 6 cells plus Hurst's 43 prior trials.
registration.controls: The stock's own gap (T-333 gap behaviour). Unconditional intraday drift (T-549). Contemporaneous in-session BTC move reported, never used. IBIT as the mechanical placebo: an ETF holding BTC should show a residual of about zero. Monday/BTC weekend effect (T-436) as a calendar control. Costs stated.

rows.notes: Expected not_supported, and Hurst's 43-trial crossref already answers it in outline. Record it only to close a commonly suggested idea. Better still, wait for Hurst's H-btc-us500-lead forward read (2026-11-05) and register this as its equity-side companion only if that passes.

rows.name: Supplier/customer industry cross-momentum (Menzly-Ozbas 2010)
rows.source_notes: I opened ideas.repec, which confirms Menzly and Ozbas, JF 65(4) 1555-1580 (2010): supplier and customer industries cross-predict, and the effect shrinks as analyst coverage and institutional ownership rise. I also downloaded OSAP SignalDoc.csv. It gives iomom_cust t 4.11 and iomom_supp t 5.03 over 1986-2005, equal-weighted, from Fama-MacBeth regressions ('t=4/5 in mv reg'). Predictability is graded '2_likely' and replication quality '2_fair'. No return magnitude is listed. I did not open the FAJ 15%/yr figure or Schlag-Zeng. The web-search budget ran out before I could search for post-2005 decay, and I found none.
rows.replication_concerns: The original evidence is firm-level Fama-MacBeth slopes, not an FF49 quintile sort, so the test is an adaptation. OSAP rates its own replication only 'fair'. The paper's mechanism predicts decay after 2005. Industries co-move, so an IO-weighted average of other industries partly carries generic cross-industry momentum and beta. Only a permuted-link placebo can isolate the information in the links. Mandel's industry-momentum tests (T-306, T-475, T-308) all failed. FF49 legs are not directly tradable, and BEA links across the 11 SPDR sectors are coarse.
rows.data_notes: Verified in the archive: french-industry49-daily 1926-07-01..2026-08-31 (value-weighted first block), french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily to 2026-08-31, fred-DTB3 to 2026-10-13, and the sector SPDRs (XLRE from 2015-10, XLC from 2018-06). The window must end 2026-08 because the industry and factor files end there. The BEA tables are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: BEA benchmark Use tables come out years after their reference year, so each must enter at a hard-coded release date. The SIC/NAICS-to-FF49 concordance must be written and hashed before any return is read. French revises the FF49 history, and Tse 2015 showed that data revisions moved HTV's significance, so the 2026 vintage is not what traders saw in real time. Month-t returns are known only at the t close, so fill at the next session's close, not the t close. Variant selection must use 1990-2005 only.
rows.missing_data: BEA benchmark Use tables (1987, 1992, 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017) with their release dates, plus a SIC/NAICS-to-FF49 concordance (all free). Or the OSAP iomom_cust/iomom_supp series, blocked today by a Google Drive quota.

final.claim: Over 2006-01 to 2026-08, across the 49 Fama-French industries, an equal-weight portfolio long the top and short the bottom quintile of each industry's input-output-linked return earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps per leg on turnover, a positive FF5+UMD alpha, and a mean above the 95th percentile of a permuted-link placebo. The linked return is the BEA-weighted month-t return of the industry's customer or supplier industries, own industry excluded. The link type and the 1- or 3-month formation are chosen on 1990-01..2005-12 and frozen. The portfolio is formed from month-t data, entered at the first session close of month t+1 and held one month.
final.statistic: Test-window mean monthly net long-short return with Newey-West (lag 6) t and a studentised circular-block-bootstrap one-sided p. Also: FF5+UMD alpha with NW t; the Fama-MacBeth slope of the t+1 industry return on the linked return, controlling for own month-t return and own 12-1 momentum; the permuted-link placebo percentile; and DSR over the 4 variants examined on 1990-2005.
final.null: Mean net long-short return <= 0 over 2006-01..2026-08: linked-industry returns carry no information beyond own-industry returns and generic cross-industry co-movement.
final.procedure: Compound the daily FF49 value-weighted returns to calendar months. Map each BEA benchmark Use table to FF49 with a concordance frozen and hashed before any return is read. Each table enters at its hard-coded BEA release date, and each month-end uses the latest released table. Customer weight w_ij is the share of i's intermediate output bought by j; supplier weight v_ij is the share of i's intermediate inputs bought from j. Exclude the diagonal and final demand, and renormalise the rows. L_i(t) = sum_j w_ij r_j(t), or the same over t-2..t. Sort into quintiles (9-10 industries a leg), equal weight, fill at the first session close of t+1, hold to the first session close of t+2, and charge 10 bps per leg on turnover. Choose the variant on 1990-2005 net Sharpe and freeze it. Bootstrap: 12-month blocks, 10,000 draws. Placebo: IO matrices permuted across industries with row sums kept, 1,000 draws, same variant. Report the halves 2006-2015 and 2016-2026-08, a 60-month rolling decay curve, and the 11 SPDR sectors with BEA weights (reported only).
final.data: french-industry49-daily, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3, daily-history sector SPDRs. To fetch: BEA benchmark Use tables with release dates and a SIC/NAICS-to-FF49 concordance (free).
final.pass: Test-window net mean > 0 with one-sided bootstrap p < 0.05, both halves positive, FF5+UMD alpha NW t > 1.65, mean above the 95th percentile of the permuted-link placebo, and DSR > 0.95 over the 4 variants.
final.controls: Own month-t return and own 12-1 momentum, in Fama-MacBeth and a double sort. Permuted-link placebo, which separates IO information from co-movement. One variant, frozen before 2006. Quintiles only, no grid. BEA tables used only after release. The FF49 vintage is stated as a revised research proxy. T-306, T-475 and T-308 are cited as prior industry-momentum failures.

rows.reason: The source checks out and 2006-2026 is a real out-of-sample period, but the test needs a free BEA fetch. The fixes: fill at the next session's close instead of the signal close, freeze the concordance before reading returns, and gate on the permuted-link placebo so generic industry co-movement cannot pass.

rows.name: Customer momentum, firm-level economic links (Cohen-Frazzini 2008)
rows.source_notes: The AQR page confirms Cohen and Frazzini, JF 2008, the customer momentum strategy, and that a typical customer is about 20% of a supplier's sales. OSAP SignalDoc gives CustomerMomentum 1.578%/month, t 3.79, 1980-2004, value-weighted quintiles, graded 1_clear / 1_good. Pinchuk (arXiv 2301.11394) Table 8 matches exactly: 1978-2004 EW 1.52 (t 4.74) and VW 1.30 (t 3.03); 2005-2018 EW 0.62 (t 2.12) and VW 0.62 (t 1.54). Pinchuk finds the effect at least partly driven by the small-to-large lead-lag.
rows.replication_concerns: Value-weighted returns have been insignificant since 2005, and the effect is roughly 60% smaller. Part of it is Hou's big-leads-small effect: Pinchuk reports that an interaction with relative customer size flips the sign. Large-cap suppliers with named 10% customers are few, and many 10-K disclosures say 'Customer A' or name the US government.
rows.data_notes: Customer-supplier links are not archived; Compustat segments cost money. EDGAR full-text search starts in 2001. dei shares-outstanding facts in sec-companyfacts start in 2009 and reach full coverage in 2011 (I checked bundle b000), so value weights are point-in-time only from 2011. sec-company-tickers is a current map, so tickers of delisted companies are absent. T-473 found 247 of 903 S&P tickers without a Yahoo series and 30 reused-ticker mismatches.
rows.lookahead_risks: A link enters only at the 10-K acceptance time, never at the fiscal year. The name-to-CIK-to-ticker map is survivor-biased (current tickers) and has reused-ticker traps. Shares must come from the 'filed' date. The hand audit of pairs must be frozen before any return is read. Do not use the t close as the fill.
rows.missing_data: EDGAR full-text-search hits and 10-K text for major-customer disclosures, 2009 on (free; needs a fetch, text extraction and a frozen hand audit).

final.claim: Over 2011-01 to 2026-09, a value-weighted portfolio long the top and short the bottom tercile of suppliers, sorted on the value-weighted month-t return of their linked customers, entered at the first session close of month t+1 and held one month, earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps per side. Suppliers are point-in-time S&P 500 members (fja-sp500-components) whose 10-K, accepted within the prior 12 months, names a non-government customer at 10% or more of sales, and that customer must be in the archive. The customer-return slope must stay positive after controlling for the supplier's own FF49 industry return.
final.statistic: Monthly net long-short mean with NW (lag 6) t and a one-sided block-bootstrap p. The Fama-MacBeth slope of supplier t+1 return on customer month-t return, with controls. DSR over 2 declared trials: monthly, and weekly with Monday-open entry.
final.null: Mean net long-short return <= 0, or the customer slope <= 0 once the supplier's industry return is controlled.
final.procedure: Search EDGAR full text of 10-Ks (2009 on) for major-customer phrases. Resolve names to CIKs (sec-cik-lookup) and to archived tickers (sec-submissions), and hand-audit the pairs into a frozen list written before any return is opened. Drop anonymous ('Customer A') and government customers. A link starts at the 10-K acceptance time and lapses after 12 months or at the next 10-K. Market cap = close x dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding filed before t, put on Yahoo's present split basis. Sort suppliers into terciles and drop months with fewer than 30 linked suppliers. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month (13-week) blocks.
final.data: daily-history-* stocks, fja-sp500-components, sec-submissions-b*, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-cik-lookup, sec-company-tickers, french-industry49-daily. To fetch: EDGAR full-text hits and 10-K text.
final.pass: At least 60 months with >= 30 linked suppliers, else inconclusive. Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves (2011-2018, 2019-2026) positive, FM slope t > 1.65 with controls, and DSR > 0.95 over the 2 trials.
final.controls: The supplier's own month-t return, its FF49 industry month-t return, its industry's big-firm return (the Hou lead-lag), and customer/supplier relative size (Pinchuk's confound). Placebo: a random customer from the same industry. 10 bps per side. Survivorship of the current ticker map and the T-473 reused-ticker filters stated. Run only after io-linked-industry-momentum reports.

rows.reason: The source is verified but the effect is documented as decayed and partly Hou's lead-lag. The fixes add Pinchuk's relative-size and industry controls, start at 2011 when shares are point-in-time, and use point-in-time S&P membership. Low priority: blocked on text extraction.

rows.name: Big / high-volume stocks lead small / low-volume stocks within an industry (Hou 2007; Chordia-Swaminathan 2000)
rows.source_notes: ideas.repec confirms Hou, RFS 20(4) 1113-1138 (2007): the effect is 'predominantly an intra-industry phenomenon', driven by slow reaction to negative news and stronger in neglected industries. ideas.repec also confirms Chordia and Swaminathan, JF 55(2) 913-935 (2000): daily and weekly high-volume portfolio returns lead low-volume ones after controlling for size, and nonsynchronous trading does not explain it. OSAP: IndRetBig t 11.0 and EarnSupBig t 8.91, 1972-2001, both 1_clear. I did not open the Vietnam negative replication. No decay search was possible this run (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: The effect lives in small, neglected followers. A point-in-time S&P 500 universe has none, so the 'low-volume' leg here is large caps. Mandel's lead-lag record is uniformly negative: T-424's BTC lead had the wrong sign, T-467 did not cover costs, and in VENUE_LEAD_LAG a real follow still lost as a taker. Weekly long-short turnover is high.
rows.data_notes: daily-history (901 symbols, mostly current large caps, with some delisted and some reused tickers such as BBBY with 63 rows and EMC with 858). fja-sp500-components gives point-in-time membership from 1996-01-02, last change 2026-08-18. sec-submissions SIC is the current profile only. dei shares-outstanding facts start in 2009 (full from 2011), so cap weights and size splits cannot be point-in-time before 2011; the leader weights use dollar volume instead.

rows.name: Oil price changes predict lower equity returns (Driesprong-Jacobsen-Maat 2008)
rows.source_notes: The ERIM page (Driesprong, Jacobsen, Maat; ERS-2003-082, the 2003 version of JFE 2008) confirms predictability in 12 of 18 developed markets plus the world index on about 30 years of monthly data. The page states no sign; the title and the cross-check imply negative. I opened the Casassus-Higuera PUC WP 406 text: 1983Q2-2009Q4, oil measured as short-term futures returns, out-of-sample R2 'close to 1.2% at one quarter', and no variable significant at longer horizons. Its abstract says oil changes are 'the only variable with forecasting power'. It also notes that DJM-type underreaction 'should tend to disappear' at quarterly horizons. I did not verify the trade-press 4%/yr figure. No post-2010 search was possible (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: There is no independent post-2010 evidence. The oil-equity correlation turned positive after 2008 as oil became a demand signal, so the sign may have flipped. Mandel's confirmed oil premia are volatility premia (T-63, T-512), not directional ones. Hurst's 48 macro relations found no oil lead.

rows.name: Gold-to-platinum price ratio predicts the equity premium (Huang-Kilic 2019)
rows.source_notes: I extracted the Huang 2015 NBER draft text and every claimed number matches: monthly averages of daily LBMA/LPPM a.m. fixings, 1975-2013; 1-month R2 'just above 1%' with slope t 2.82; 1-year R2 16.57%; one s.d. of log GP is +6.4% over the next year; out-of-sample R2 'large, positive, and significant' except the 1-month rolling 10-year case. The change version is a different predictor from the paper's. I could not verify Xu-Li-Singh's sign for ΔGP. Tail-risk proxies failed in Mandel (T-52, T-227), and gold's 2024-26 central-bank rally is a non-risk reason for GP to rise.

Raw (unhedged) LQD and HYG returns are reported only. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
final.data: fred-BAA10Y, daily-history-HYG, daily-history-LQD, daily-history-IEF, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
final.pass: At least one trial has R2_OS > 0 with Holm-adjusted CW p < 0.05 and the pre-registered sign, R2_OS > 0 in both halves of its own window, and a switching rule that beats the historical mean with paired lower bound > 0. Joint-family DSR > 0.95.
final.controls: Historical-mean benchmark. SPY's own month-t return as a reported control regressor. T-430 and T-481 counted as prior trials. 2 bps per switch. Joint deflation with the cluster's equity-premium predictors. The proxy caveat (not the paper's TRACE moments) is stated in the verdict.

rows.reason: The claim is verified only via the seminar abstract, and the testable trials are proxies, so the run is a weak cheap check inside the shared predictor harness. The fixes: per-trial forecast start dates (the cross-check's single 2010-01 start was impossible for HYG), the SPY target, and joint deflation.

rows.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover large caps (Medhat-Schmeling 2022)
rows.source_notes: I extracted the accepted-version text (RFS 35(3) 1480-1526) and every number matches. July 1963 to December 2018, value-weighted, financials excluded. In the top turnover decile, winners minus losers earn +1.37%/month (t 4.74); in the bottom decile, -1.41% (t -7.13). The largest-500 construction is 2x2 independent sorts at the 250th rank: STMOM 0.42% (t 4.91), STREV* -0.02. Megacaps 0.53% (t 2.53). 1991/07-2018/12: 2.03% (t 4.80). Net of half-spreads the benchmark earns 1.00% (t 3.47). Skipping the last 3 trading days of the formation month gives large caps and megacaps about 0.60% net with t above 3. Turnover is month-t volume / shares outstanding. Only the small-cap STREV* is VIX-predictable.
rows.replication_concerns: I found no independent post-2018 replication; 2019-2026 is unmeasured. Power is low: at 0.42%/month with s.d. about 2.21%, 93 months give a gross t of about 1.8. The 901 list is survivor-heavy. The cross-check's split adjustment had a bug: it took splits between the fact's end date and t, but Yahoo volume and closes are on today's split basis, so splits after t must also be applied. The paper excludes financials, which the cross-check omitted.
rows.data_notes: daily-history (901), with daily-events present for every stock (the 46 names without one are ETFs, futures and indices). sec-companyfacts dei shares-outstanding facts start in 2009 and are full from 2011 (checked in bundle b000), so the 2019+ test is covered. fja-sp500-components gives point-in-time membership 1996..2026-08-18. sec-submissions SIC is current. french-ff5 and momentum run to 2026-08.
rows.lookahead_risks: Today's 901-name list is a look-ahead selection: use fja point-in-time S&P 500 members and report the missing-price share. Shares must be filed before t. Split basis: shares x the split factor from the fact's end date to the fetch date (not to t). Watch for multi-class dei counts. For the full-month trial, the month-t signal is known only at the month-end close, so fill at the next session's close. The skip-3-days trial may fill at the month-end close.
rows.missing_data: None blocking. S&P changes after 2026-08-18 are not in fja (minor).

final.claim: Over 2019-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 non-financial members (fja-sp500-components; SIC 6000-6999 excluded as in the paper) with usable prices and point-in-time shares outstanding, a value-weighted portfolio long high-turnover month-t winners and short high-turnover month-t losers earns a positive mean net return after 5 bps per side on actual weight changes. Winners, losers and high turnover come from independent 2x2 sorts at the cross-sectional medians of month-t return and month-t share turnover (Medhat-Schmeling's largest-500 construction). The portfolio is entered at the first session close after month-end and held one month.
final.statistic: Monthly net mean with NW (lag 3) t and a one-sided studentised block-bootstrap p; FF5+UMD alpha with NW t (to 2026-08); the shuffled-turnover placebo percentile; DSR over 2 declared trials.
final.procedure: Shares = dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, else us-gaap CommonStockSharesOutstanding, filed before t and under 400 days old, multiplied by the cumulative daily-events split factor from the fact's end date to the fetch date (Yahoo's present basis). Sum the class counts for multi-class issuers when dei reports per class, else drop the name (flagged). Turnover = sum of Yahoo daily volume over month t / adjusted shares. Market cap = close x adjusted shares. Apply T-473's reused-ticker filters and report coverage. Trial (a): full-month formation, filled at the first session close of t+1. Trial (b): formation skipping the month's last 3 trading days (the paper's implementation-lag version), filled at the month-end close. STREV* is reported. 2010-2018 overlaps the paper and is reported only. Bootstrap with 6-month blocks. Placebo: turnover permuted across months within each stock, 1,000 draws.
final.data: daily-history-* stocks, daily-events-*, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves (2019-01..2022-10, 2022-11..2026-09) positive, FF5+UMD alpha > 0, above the 95th percentile of the shuffled-turnover placebo, and DSR > 0.95 over the 2 trials. Pre-registered verdict map: a positive net mean with p >= 0.05 is inconclusive (power; expected net t about 1.2-1.8), moving to a forward paper record; a net mean <= 0 is not_supported.
final.controls: Plain 1-month reversal (STREV) and UMD as baselines. Shuffled-turnover placebo. 5 bps per side on actual turnover. Financials excluded. Point-in-time membership with coverage reported; the survivorship direction is unknown and stated. Power stated in advance.

rows.reason: The best-evidenced candidate in the cluster, with every number verified. The fixes: point-in-time S&P membership replaces the survivor list, the split-basis bug is corrected, financials are excluded as in the paper, the 4-variant grid becomes the paper's 2 constructions, and the low-power verdict is mapped in advance.

rows.name: VIX-conditioned short-term reversal as liquidity provision (Nagel 2012); partial duplicate of T-462
rows.source_notes: The NBER WP 17653 page confirms Nagel's 'Evaporating Liquidity' (RFS 2012). Reversal returns proxy liquidity-provision returns and are 'highly predictable with the VIX'. Industry-portfolio reversal pays when VIX is high. I verified the counterpoint in the Medhat-Schmeling text: over 1990-2018 only the small-cap STREV* is VIX-predictable, by 9 bps per VIX point (t -2.13, R2 2.3%). Nagel's 1998-2010 sample, the never-lost-a-quarter claim and the quote-midpoint results were not on the page I opened.
rows.replication_concerns: T-462 failed on 68 ETFs weekly, with a VIX high-minus-low difference of -0.06%/week (t -0.34). Large-cap reversal is not VIX-predictable (Medhat-Schmeling). Daily full turnover is costly. In child maker-fill evidence, liquidity-provision returns exist mainly at the front of the queue, so open-print fills overstate what a taker captures.
rows.data_notes: daily-history open/close for the stocks, cboe-VIX-history 1990-01-02..2026-10-14 (available 21:15 UTC), french-industry49-daily to 2026-08, and fja point-in-time membership.
rows.lookahead_risks: Selecting the 'top 500 by dollar volume' from today's survivors is a look-ahead; use fja point-in-time membership. VIX(t-1) closes at 16:15 ET and is known before the day-t open, so the cross-check's t-2 lag is needlessly stale but harmless. Close-to-close returns carry bid-ask bounce, so enter at the open. The open print is a trade, not a quote.
rows.missing_data: None. Quote midpoints are not archived (flagged).

final.claim: Over 2013-01 to 2026-09, the net daily return of a dollar-neutral reversal portfolio rises with VIX at the close of t-1, and its mean net return in the top trailing-252-session VIX tercile is positive, after 3 bps per side on gross turnover. The portfolio holds point-in-time S&P 500 members priced at $5 or more, weighted by minus the cross-sectionally demeaned formation-window return, from the day-t open to the day-t close.
final.statistic: HAC (lag 10) t of the slope of daily net return on VIX(t-1); top-tercile net mean with one-sided bootstrap p; DSR over 2 formation lengths plus T-462's cells as prior trials.
final.null: VIX slope <= 0 and top-tercile net mean <= 0.
final.procedure: Membership from fja-sp500-components at close t-1, with T-473's usable-series filters. Weights are proportional to -(r_i - mean r) over the formation window ending at close t-1, scaled to $1 long and $1 short. Enter at the day-t official open, exit at the day-t close. VIX close at t-1; terciles from the trailing 252 sessions. Formation (1 day or 5 days) is chosen on 2000-2012 net Sharpe and frozen. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 20-day blocks. The FF49 industry version is reported gross as a costless diagnostic. The close-to-close version is reported only as a bounce-inflated upper bound.
final.data: daily-history-* stocks, fja-sp500-components, cboe-VIX-history, french-industry49-daily, fred-DTB3
final.pass: VIX slope HAC t > 1.65 AND top-tercile net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves (2013-2019, 2020-2026) positive, and DSR > 0.95 with T-462's cells counted.
final.controls: Unconditional reversal as baseline. Portfolio beta reported. Open entry removes the close bounce. 3 bps per side on gross turnover. One VIX conditioning (terciles), no grid. T-462 counted in the deflation.

rows.reason: Registered in substance as T-462, but the design differs materially: single stocks rather than ETFs, a daily rather than weekly horizon, and open entry. That keeps it as a fix. The fixes: point-in-time membership instead of survivor dollar-volume ranks, VIX at t-1, and T-462 counted in the deflation.

rows.name: Dollar carry trade: long/short the dollar on the average forward discount (Lustig-Roussanov-Verdelhan 2014)
rows.source_notes: The NBER WP 16427 page confirms Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan, published in JFE 2014. The dollar carry trade's returns are uncorrelated with standard carry, and the average forward discount plus US IP growth forecast 'up to 25%' of one-year dollar-return variation. The Quantpedia page confirms the rule (10 developed currencies including DKK, AFD vs the 3-month T-bill, monthly) and the figures: net of spot and forward bid-ask, 5.60%/yr, volatility 8.53%, Sharpe 0.66, maximum drawdown -31.72%; all countries 3.80%, Sharpe 0.54; 11/1983-6/2010. No post-2010 figures were found (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: The rule makes about one bet a month on a sign that switches rarely: roughly short USD in 2011-15 and long USD in 2016-19 and 2022-24. The effective sample is a handful of regimes, and a secular dollar rally can make it look good by luck. Every Mandel carry sleeve since 2013 failed (T-368, T-431, T-381). IR3TIB differentials are not the futures-implied forward discount after 2008: the CIP basis means carry accrual is approximate.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10 1999-01-04..2026-10-09 (FRED noon buying rates, inc. MXN and ZAR). fx-rates-3m (OECD IR3TIB monthly averages) to 2026-08, with available_at stamped at the same month's end. That stamp is not OECD's publication date, so the one-month lag is required. DKK is not archived (pegged to EUR). EUR and GBP rates are stale after 2026-01 (forward-filled, as in T-368).
rows.lookahead_risks: OECD monthly averages are published weeks after month-end, so use month t-1 values at end-t (T-368 convention); the bundle's same-month available_at must not be trusted. DEX rates are published the next business day; filling at the noon fix after the decision is fine. Stale EUR/GBP rates after 2026-01 must be flagged. ALFRED INDPRO vintages would be needed for the IP variant (dropped).
rows.missing_data: None for the registered trials. DKK not archived. The CIP basis / futures-implied carry is unobserved (approximated by IR3TIB).

final.claim: Over 2011-01 to 2026-09, going long an equal-weight basket of the 9 archived non-USD G10 currencies against USD when the one-month-lagged average 3-month rate differential (foreign mean minus US) is positive, and short otherwise, rebalanced monthly at the FRED noon fix, earns an annualised net Sharpe above 0.3. The stationary-bootstrap lower bound must be above 0, and the mean must beat a regime-preserving shuffled-sign placebo. Costs: 2 bps per leg per rebalance plus 1 bp a month roll.
final.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe with a stationary-bootstrap 95% interval; HAC t of the mean; shuffled-sign placebo percentile; skew and maximum drawdown; DSR over 2 trials.
final.null: Uncovered interest parity for the dollar: net Sharpe <= 0.
final.procedure: AFD_t = mean of the 9 foreign IR3TIB values minus US IR3TIB, using month t-1 averages at end of month t. Decide the sign at month-end t and fill at the first business day's noon fix of t+1. Monthly return = sign x (mean basket spot change + AFD/12); the carry share of the return is reported. Primary trial: G10. Second trial: G10 + MXN + ZAR. The IP-growth regression is dropped (needs ALFRED vintages; adds a model). 1999-2010 is reported only. Stationary bootstrap, mean block 12 months, 5,000 draws. Placebo: the rule's sign series cut into its own regime spells, spells shuffled in time, 1,000 draws. The number of sign regimes is reported.
final.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3, daily-history-SPY
final.pass: Primary trial: net Sharpe > 0.3 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, both halves (2011-2018, 2019-2026) positive, above the 95th percentile of the shuffled-sign placebo, and DSR > 0.95 over the 2 trials with T-368 (6) and T-431 (4) counted in the family.
final.controls: Always-long-USD and always-short-USD baselines. Shuffled-regime placebo against a secular-dollar-trend fluke. Correlation with SPY and with T-368. Financing and roll costs. Stale-rate splice flagged, with Sharpe through 2026-01 reported. CIP-basis caveat on carry accrual. No threshold beyond the AFD sign.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the time-series design differs materially from T-368's cross-section. The fixes: a regime-preserving placebo, because one sign bet with few switches can ride a dollar trend; the IP-regression grid is dropped; and the OECD timestamp and CIP caveats are stated.

rows.name: COT speculative / hedging pressure across futures (Fan-Fernandez-Perez-Fuertes-Miffre 2018; Basu-Miffre 2013)
rows.source_notes: The CXO summary, which I opened, confirms the paper ('Speculative Pressure', Fan, Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes, Miffre; SSRN November 2018): 84 futures (43 commodities, 11 currencies, 19 equity indexes, 11 rates), legacy COT 1992-09..2018-05, signal = month-end non-commercial net position relative to its past-year weekly average. Gross results: commodities 4.1% (Sharpe 0.61), currencies 2.5% (0.47), equity 4.0% (0.50), rates -0.7% (-0.28). The authors say it is robust to reasonable frictions, with episodic multi-year losses. I did not verify a journal publication or open the Basu-Miffre manuscript.
rows.replication_concerns: The evidence is from one research group, all gross; I found no independent post-2018 test. Mandel's gold COT test (T-405) found no information, and TSMOM-like signals have not beaten the historical-mean null (T-300). About 25 contracts over about 100 months gives limited power. 'Reversed commercial pressure' is nearly the mirror of non-commercial pressure, so it is not an independent trial.
rows.data_notes: Archived COT covers only gold 088691 and silver 084691 (legacy, disaggregated) and CME bitcoin 133741 (TFF); 133741 is bitcoin, not an equity index. Continuous futures are archived for GC, SI, HG, CL, ES, PL and BTC only. The other COT codes and futures histories need fetches.
rows.lookahead_risks: The report is as of Tuesday and released Friday at 15:30 ET (holiday shifts), so use the T-405 release_rule stamps and drop backcast or superseded rows. Yahoo continuous futures carry roll jumps: mask roll days rather than substitute ETF proxies, whose contango drag is a different return. Rebalance at the next session's open after the month's last release.
rows.missing_data: Legacy futures-only COT for about 22 more contract codes (free, existing Socrata fetcher). Yahoo continuous futures for NG, HO, RB, ZC, ZS, ZW, KC, SB, CT, LE, HE, NQ, RTY, YM and the FX futures (free, roll-masked); synthetic FX from fx-spot-g10 + fx-rates-3m.

final.claim: Over 2018-06 to 2026-09, an equal-risk monthly portfolio across about 25 liquid US futures (commodities, currencies, equity indices; rates excluded per the evidence) earns a positive net Sharpe after 5 bps per side plus 2 bps per roll, with positive alpha against 12-1 TSMOM and the historical-mean strategy. It goes long contracts whose legacy non-commercial net position / open interest is above its trailing 52-report mean and short those below, each scaled to 10% annualised volatility. COT enters at its Friday release and positions change at the next session's open after the month's last release.
final.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe with a stationary-bootstrap interval; alpha against the TSMOM 12-1 and historical-mean strategies with NW t; sleeve Sharpes reported.
final.null: Net Sharpe <= 0, or no alpha over both TSMOM and the historical-mean strategy.
final.procedure: Socrata legacy futures-only rows per contract code, with available_at from the release rule (holiday shifts honoured; backcast and superseded rows handled as in T-405). Signal = (non-commercial long - short) / OI minus its trailing 52-report mean, read at the month's last release. Positions take the sign, scaled to 10% vol on trailing 60-session volatility. Returns come from roll-masked continuous futures. FX can be synthetic from spot plus rate differentials. A contract without a usable futures series is excluded, not ETF-proxied. One pooled trial; the 3 sleeves are reported only. The commercial-mirror variant is dropped as redundant. Studentised circular block bootstrap, 12-month blocks.
final.data: cftc-cot-legacy-f-* (to extend), daily-history continuous futures (to extend), fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m. To fetch: COT for the remaining codes and Yahoo continuous futures.
final.pass: Pooled net Sharpe > 0 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, alpha NW t > 1.65 against both baselines, both halves (2018-06..2022-07, 2022-08..2026-09) positive, and DSR > 0.95 with T-405's cells counted.
final.controls: TSMOM 12-1 and historical-mean baselines. Equal-risk long-only control. Publication timing enforced. Roll masking with no ETF substitution. 5 bps per side plus 2 bps per roll. One lookback (52 reports), no grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified via CXO, and 2018-2026 is clean out of sample, but it is blocked on two free fetches. The fixes: one pooled trial instead of 6, the redundant commercial mirror dropped, roll-masked futures instead of contango-dragged ETF proxies, and the archived COT inventory corrected (133741 is CME bitcoin).

rows.name: Factor momentum across a broad factor set (Ehsani-Linnainmaa 2022); duplicate of T-388
rows.source_notes: The NBER WP 25551 page confirms Ehsani and Linnainmaa (JF 2022): about 1 bp/month after a losing year vs 53 bps after a positive year, and factor momentum 'explains all forms of individual stock momentum'. The sample and factor count are not on the page. I did not open Fan et al.'s contrary evidence (the Alpha Architect page).
rows.replication_concerns: T-388 already failed cleanly on 6 core factors over 1964-2026: Sharpe difference -0.04 (CI -0.24 to +0.17), DSR 0.08. Contrarian timing (T-389) also failed. Post-publication anomaly decay lowers the base rate. Paper factors are gross long-short portfolios.
rows.data_notes: The OSAP long-short file is not archived (Drive quota). Archived: french-ff5, momentum, aqr-bab, accruals and net-issuance portfolios.
rows.lookahead_risks: Selecting factors by publication date needs OSAP metadata. A 1-month embargo is needed as in T-388. The long-short paper factors cannot be traded.
rows.missing_data: OSAP predictor long-short returns (free; blocked by the Google Drive quota).

final.claim: Over 2006-01 to the OSAP end date, holding each OSAP long-short predictor whose original sample ended before 2005 only after a positive trailing 12-month return gives a higher Sharpe ratio than static equal weight across the same factors, with the studentised block-bootstrap lower bound of the difference above 0.
final.statistic: Sharpe difference (timed minus static) with a studentised block-bootstrap CI (12-month blocks); DSR counting T-388's 5 variants plus this one; PBO via CSCV.
final.procedure: Fix the predictor list from OSAP metadata (original sample end before 2005). Signal = sign of the trailing 12-month factor return, with a 1-month embargo. Equal weight across held factors, cash otherwise. Investability check on factor ETFs (MTUM, QUAL, VLUE, USMV, SIZE), 2014-2026, 5 bps per switch.
final.data: To fetch: OSAP predictor long-short returns. Archived: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, aqr-bab-daily.
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the Sharpe difference > 0, DSR > 0.95, PBO < 0.5, and a positive point estimate on the factor-ETF check.
final.controls: Static equal-weight baseline. Embargo month. Post-publication universe only. Gross-vs-investable gap reported.

rows.reason: T-388 has already registered and cleanly failed this claim. The only material difference is breadth (200+ OSAP long-short factors), which cannot be traded on a US retail venue, and the tradable form (5 factor ETFs) is no broader than T-388.

rows.name: BTC's overnight/weekend move into crypto-linked US equities (COIN, MSTR, IBIT) at the open
rows.source_notes: No source makes this claim. The IMF blog (January 2022), which I opened, confirms BTC-S&P 500 correlations of 0.01 (2017-19) and 0.36 (2020-21), with BTC explaining about one-sixth of S&P volatility and one-tenth of return variation. It makes no lead-lag claim and says spillovers run both ways. That is co-movement, not predictability. The idea is Mandel's own, with no published evidence; the academic search could not be run (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: The neighbouring questions are already answered negatively. T-424 (BTC lagged into alts, out of sample) had the wrong sign, t -2.76. Hurst's crypto-proxy-crossref (43 trials) found that BTC proxies' overnight move is beta, not a lead. Kalshi's hourly BTC ladders are not slow to spot. IBIT and COIN/MSTR pre-market and opening auctions are quoted off live BTC, so the residual is near zero by construction. Hurst's H-btc-us500-lead forward test reads on 2026-11-05.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-COIN 2021-04-14.., MSTR 1998-06.., IBIT and FBTC 2024-01-11.., coinbase-1m-BTC-USD monthly bundles from 2022-01. Local 60m bars exist for COIN and MSTR but not IBIT (5/15/30m only, 60 days).
rows.lookahead_risks: A beta estimated with the day-t close leaks; it must be trailing. Yahoo's official open vs the first print. Early closes (13:00 ET). Weekend and holiday BTC windows.
rows.missing_data: None for the open-entry design. MSTR mNAV and the CME basis are not archived.

final.claim: Over 2022-01 to 2026-09, for COIN and MSTR (IBIT from 2024-01-11 as a mechanical placebo), the stock's open-to-close return loads positively on the residual R = beta_60 x (BTC log return from the prior 16:00 ET close to 09:30 ET) minus the stock's own open gap, and trading R's sign at the official open when |R| exceeds one trailing 60-session s.d. earns a positive mean net return per trade after 2 bps plus half the trailing Corwin-Schultz spread per side.
final.statistic: Pooled HAC t of the residual coefficient; net mean per trade with a session-block bootstrap one-sided p; DSR counting Hurst's 43 crypto-proxy trials and T-424.
final.null: Residual coefficient <= 0 and net mean per trade <= 0.
final.procedure: BTC from Coinbase 1-minute bars, prior 16:00 ET (13:00 ET on early closes) to 09:30 ET, weekends included. Beta is the trailing 60-session regression on the same windows, known at the prior close. Market-on-open entry, exit at the close. Train on the first 60% of sessions (beta only), test on the last 40%. Circular bootstrap, 5-session blocks.
final.data: daily-history-COIN, daily-history-MSTR, daily-history-IBIT, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD-*
final.pass: In the test 40%: pooled HAC t > 1.65, net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive for both COIN and MSTR, IBIT residual about zero, and DSR > 0.95 with the prior trials counted.
final.controls: Own open gap (T-333), unconditional intraday drift (T-549), IBIT placebo, BTC Monday effect (T-436). Costs stated.

rows.reason: No source asserts this effect (the IMF piece is co-movement only), and Mandel's and Hurst's records already answer the neighbouring questions negatively. Defer to Hurst's H-btc-us500-lead read on 2026-11-05, and re-propose this only as its equity-side companion if that passes.

knowledge.title: Cross-asset lead-lag, momentum and carry: economic links, commodity and credit leaders, turnover momentum, VIX-conditioned reversal, dollar carry and COT pressure
knowledge.markdown:
# Cross-asset lead-lag, momentum and carry: economic links, commodity and credit leaders, turnover momentum, VIX-conditioned reversal, dollar carry and COT pressure

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 15 sweep candidates: 13 peer-reviewed papers (JF, RFS, JFE, JFQA, Management Science; 2000-2022), two working papers (Li-Yuan-Zhou; Fan et al. 2018), replications (OSAP, Pinchuk 2023, Tse 2015, Xu-Li-Singh 2023) and practitioner summaries (CXO, Quantpedia).
- **Links:** https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/31278/ · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/master/SignalDoc.csv · https://www.nber.org/papers/w17653 · https://www.nber.org/papers/w16427
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.56 (23 of 41 distinct sources opened and checked against the claim; four returned 403, several were read as abstracts or summaries only).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full text for Medhat-Schmeling, the Huang 2015 draft, Pinchuk and Casassus-Higuera, plus the downloaded OSAP SignalDoc. The rest were abstracts, with CXO/Quantpedia summaries standing in for Jacobsen et al., Fan et al. and LRV's tables. No search for decay after 2010 was possible.
- **Selected because:** it covers the program's cross-asset leaders (SPY, dollar, 10-year yield, gold, oil, BTC, credit) and their neighbours (economic links, turnover, COT positioning, rate differentials), and every claim is old enough for 2006-2026 to be out-of-sample.

## What it says

- **Industry economic links (Menzly-Ozbas).** Segmented investors miss news that first moves an industry's suppliers and customers, so the input-output-weighted return of linked industries predicts next month's industry return. It is weaker where analyst coverage is high. OSAP: customer t 4.11, supplier t 5.03 (1986-2005), graded "likely". No magnitude or post-2005 figure was found.
- **Customer momentum (Cohen-Frazzini).** Suppliers follow their major customers' past-month return (investor inattention). 1978-2004: 1.30%/month value-weighted (t 3.03). 2005-2018: 0.62% (t 1.54, not significant). It has roughly halved, and is partly Hou's big-leads-small effect (Pinchuk).
- **Big, high-volume firms lead within an industry (Hou; Chordia-Swaminathan).** High-dollar-volume leaders' weekly returns predict low-volume followers', mostly on bad news, and nonsynchronous trading does not explain it. IndRetBig t 11.0 (1972-2001). The follower leg is neglected small caps, which the archive mostly lacks.
- **Industries lead the market (HTV).** Financial, retail, print and real-estate returns forecast the market by up to two months (1946-2002); gross Sharpe barely beats buy-and-hold. Tse: 1 to 7 of 48 industries significant to 2013. Contested.
- **Oil leads equities negatively (DJM).** Oil rises predict lower stock returns in 12 of 18 markets. Out-of-sample R2 is about 1.2% at one quarter through 2009 (Casassus-Higuera). Untested after 2010, and the sign may have flipped.
- **Copper, sign set by the business cycle (JMV).** Metal rises predict lower returns in expansions and higher in contractions (CFNAI state). Verified only from the 2010 draft: gross, five out-of-sample years of the authors' own. 2010-2026 has almost no contraction months.
- **Gold/platinum ratio (Huang-Kilic).** A tail-risk proxy predicting the equity premium: 1-month R2 just above 1% (t 2.82), 1-year 16.6% (1975-2013). Xu-Li-Singh: the level fails internationally to 2019; only the change predicts. 87.7% of post-2014 levels exceed the 2000-2013 maximum.
- **Equities lead corporate bonds (DUX).** Hourly stock returns lead junk and BBB bond prices; HYG, an ETF, is tied to equities within the hour, and net-of-cost profit is disputed.
- **Bond-return moments predict the equity premium (Li-Yuan-Zhou).** Mean and skewness of corporate bond returns predict the market; abstract only, no numbers.
- **Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks (Medhat-Schmeling).** Turnover is monthly volume over shares outstanding. High-turnover winners minus losers earn +1.37%/month (t 4.74) and low-turnover stocks reverse (-1.41%, t -7.13), 1963-2018. The largest-500 2x2 earns 0.42% (t 4.91). It survives half-spreads and grew rather than decayed through 2018; 2019-2026 is unmeasured.
- **VIX-conditioned reversal (Nagel).** Reversal returns are the price of liquidity provision and rise with VIX; they are gross, on transaction prices that include bid-ask bounce. Medhat-Schmeling find the VIX link only in small caps.
- **Dollar carry (LRV).** Long developed currencies against USD when the average forward discount is positive, short otherwise: Sharpe 0.66 net of bid-ask, drawdown -31.7% (1983-2010), uncorrelated with cross-sectional carry. Few sign switches, and no figure after 2010.
- **COT speculative pressure (Fan et al.).** Net non-commercial positions relative to their one-year mean capture the hedging-pressure (backwardation) premium. Gross Sharpe: commodities 0.61, currencies 0.47, equity indices 0.50; rates negative (1992-2018). The evidence comes from one research group.
- **Factor momentum (Ehsani-Linnainmaa).** 53 bps/month after a positive year against 1 bp after a losing one. Contested (Fan et al.).

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** Thirteen of fifteen claims are in JF, RFS, JFE, JFQA or Management Science, and OSAP replicates four in sample. That is not a tradable edge today: nearly every figure is gross, samples end 2004-2013, and the only post-publication numbers found (Cohen-Frazzini, HTV, the gold/platinum level) show decay or failure.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks is the best-evidenced test now.** `short-term-momentum-high-turnover` runs on point-in-time S&P 500 members over 93 post-sample months. Low power is declared in advance: a positive mean with p >= 0.05 is inconclusive and goes to a forward record. It differs from T-420 and T-319, both on ETFs.
- **Three more tests are runnable now, registered as successors rather than discoveries.** `industry-leader-lead-lag-weekly` and `vix-conditioned-daily-reversal-stocks` (T-462 counted in its deflation) need no new data. So does `dollar-carry-afd-timing`, a time-series bet distinct from T-368's cross-section.
- **`spy-leads-hyg-60m` is the one intraday test, a successor to the T-577/T-578 bond_etf cells.** Those cells had IC +0.10, net -0.05 bp and DSR 0.014. The new test asks whether a thresholded 60-minute rule turns that IC into net return.
- **One shared monthly harness tests five SPY-timing predictors:** oil, gold/platinum change, HTV industries, credit change and, after the ALFRED fetch, copper-by-state. It uses expanding OLS, R2_OS against the historical mean, Clark-West with Holm for multiple comparisons, a 2 bps switching rule, and one joint DSR family that also counts T-458 and T-481.
- **Three tests are kept, blocked on free fetches.** `io-linked-industry-momentum` must beat a permuted-link placebo, so generic co-movement (which sank T-306, T-475, T-308) cannot pass. `cot-speculative-pressure-futures` faces both TSMOM and the historical mean. `customer-momentum-edgar-links` is low priority.
- **The children's reference-price rule sets the expectation.** An edge exists where a source leads the market (fed-funds futures), not where the crowd already reads it; oil, copper, credit and gold are watched, so equities probably absorb them.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Decayed:** customer momentum (value-weighted insignificant after 2005) and the Hou follower leg (small caps). Expect nulls; record them.
- **Contested:** HTV gets a cheap refutation run, expected to be not_supported. The gold/platinum level is pre-declared inconclusive by a range rule that reads no outcomes. Tail-risk proxies have failed before: SKEW in T-52 and T-227.
- **Lead-lag has failed every time costs were charged.** T-424 (BTC into alts) had the wrong sign, t -2.76, and T-467 failed. In VENUE_LEAD_LAG, Polymarket follows Kalshi but a taker loses about 2 points. LAG_2026-10-05's 3-second lead was not tradable. The desk child's 48 macro relations gave one candidate (2s10s -> XLF, t +2.6).
- **A positive IC is not a net return.** T-577 (276 cells) and T-578 (306 cells) passed none. T-579's strongest cross-asset rows are inverse: SPY's 20-day return has IC -0.11 to -0.20 against stocks and ETFs over the next 1-20 days. That is market-level reversal, not a lead.
- **Carry on US venues has failed:** T-368, T-431, T-381 and T-430, and the desk child finds funding rate carry dead on US venues (Hyperliquid's is closed to US persons; not pursued). Dollar carry needs a regime-preserving placebo, since one sign bet can ride a dollar trend.
- **Dropped:** factor momentum duplicates T-388 (Sharpe difference -0.04, DSR 0.08). BTC's overnight move into COIN, MSTR and IBIT has no source, and the desk child's crypto-proxy-crossref (43 trials) calls it beta, not a lead; it defers to H-btc-us500-lead (read 2026-11-05).
- **Not directly tradable:** FF49 legs, paper factors and TRACE moments are proxies; stocks, ETFs, CME futures and OANDA FX execute.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **New F1 leader features for T-579:** roll-masked CL_F and HG_F r1/r5/r20, the change in log gold/platinum, the change in BAA10Y, and duration-hedged HYG and LQD excess returns.
- **New F0 features:** turnover × month-t return, the within-industry high-dollar-volume leader return, and reversal × VIX(t-1). T-580's VIX-level IC is positive, which agrees with Nagel in direction but has not been tested as an interaction.
- **Data to fetch:** BEA Use tables with release dates (concordance hashed before any return is read), ALFRED CFNAI-MA3 vintages, fred-DCOILWTICO, COT for ~22 more contracts with continuous futures, EDGAR major-customer text, OSAP.
- **Shared utilities:** a futures roll-mask (T-468 windows), point-in-time S&P membership with T-473's filters (survivorship reported), and placebos as gates.
- **Monthly signals fill at the next session after month-end.** A fill at the signal's own close is a look-ahead.

candidates.name: Perp-spot premium convergence (random-maturity arbitrage bound), positive leg only
candidates.summary: Short the perpetual and hold spot when the perp's price deviation from spot (the premium, annualised as rho) exceeds a cost bound. Close when rho returns to zero. This is not the trailing-funding threshold that T-363 tested. He, Manela, Ross and von Wachter find that most of the return comes from price convergence, with funding the smaller share.
candidates.mechanism: Retail trend-chasers want leveraged long exposure, and arbitrage capital is scarce and margin-constrained, so perps trade rich (BIS 'crypto carry'). The arbitrageur is paid for supplying the short side and for carrying liquidation and margin risk. The other side is leveraged longs paying a convenience yield.
adjacent_variables: Coinbase Derivatives / Kalshi perp mark vs Coinbase spot
candidates.assets: BTC, ETH: Kalshi perps or Coinbase Derivatives perp-style nano futures short, Coinbase spot long (US-legal). The negative-rho leg needs short spot, which is not executable retail except by IBIT borrow in US hours, so only the positive leg is tested.
candidates.claimed_effect: Binance hourly data from 2020-01 to 2024-03-11, BTC/ETH/BNB/DOGE/ADA. With zero costs the BTC Sharpe is 11.65 (52.55%/yr). With high retail costs it is 3.35, and 3.27 after effective spreads. Mean BTC rho fell from 0.69 before 2022 to 0.17 after; the paper says deviations shrink about 22 points a year. BTC return split: price convergence 37.61% vs funding 14.94%. Borri-Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (2025) report the Schmeling et al. carry trade at Sharpe 6.45 over 2020-2025, 4.06 from 2024, and negative in 2025.
candidates.replication: Decayed and contested. He et al. themselves document decay. The Borri et al. survey (independent authors) finds carry Sharpe falling from 2024 and negative in 2025. Mandel's own T-363 (funding-threshold carry, test 2023-2026: Sharpe -0.64 central) and T-198/T-258 failed. BitMEX data via Coincub show BTC funding pinned at the 0.01%/8h baseline for 78.19% of Q3-2025, so funding is a censored signal; use the premium, not funding.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: BTC and ETH perps. Back-test on Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL (archived funding history with index_price; premium recovered from interest_1h) and on Binance premiumIndexKlines 1h (public, from 2020-01), read for the signal only. Forward test on Kalshi perps and Coinbase Derivatives vs Coinbase spot. Signal at each hourly close: annualised rho above an entry bound. The bound is fixed on 2020-2023 at Mandel's retail costs: Coinbase spot taker or maker plus perp fee, both legs, round trip. Enter at the next hour, exit when rho <= 0 or after 30 days. Funding is accrued and margin is financed at DTB3 + 1.5%. Statistic: Sharpe of daily excess return over DTB3 in the 2024-01..2026-09 test window, studentized block bootstrap (blocks of 30 days), DSR counting T-363/T-198/T-258/T-553 as prior trials. Report the price-convergence and funding shares separately. Pass: one-sided 95% lower bound of Sharpe > 0 and DSR > 0.95. The prior is strongly against.

candidates.name: Crypto size factor (CSIZE), long-only small-cap tilt on a liquid US-listed universe
candidates.summary: Small-cap coins earn more than large ones (the Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu C-3 model). Test whether a long-only smallest-quintile portfolio of Coinbase-listed coins beats BTC after costs. It uses market cap and supply, not price, as the sort.
candidates.mechanism: Illiquidity and risk premium on small networks, or a lottery-like retail preference. Fieberg, Liedtke and Zaremba find the premium lives in micro-caps that are uneconomic to trade.
variables: market cap and shares outstanding (circulating supply)
candidates.assets: Coinbase USD spot altcoins (long-only; executable).
candidates.claimed_effect: Borri et al. (2025), weekly value-weighted quintiles. CSIZE 5-1 is -2.3%/week (t -2.66) from 2014-01 to 2025-09, but only -0.9%/week (t -1.69) after 2020; the smallest quintile alone earns +2.1%/week (t 2.53) post-2020. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (JF 2022) is the primary paper.
candidates.replication: Partly decayed. The post-2020 long-short is significant only at 10%. Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba (IRFA 2024): size and volume anomalies come from micro-caps of little economic importance, and anomaly returns concentrate in bull markets and fade over time. Fieberg-Guenther-Poddig-Zaremba (IRFA 2024, 20,736 designs): size is robust across designs, but non-standard errors exceed standard errors. Mandel has not tested crypto size; T-546 found high-volume altcoin events earn -1.8%/10d, a hostile prior for altcoins.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time Coinbase USD products (the 492 coinbase-daily bundles) with market cap from cmc-daily-listings. Exclude stablecoins and wrapped or staked tokens as T-546 did, and require trailing 30-day Coinbase dollar volume >= $1m. Sort each Sunday 00:00 UTC on the prior day's CMC market cap, which is published by then. Hold the smallest quintile value-weighted (and, as a variant, equal-weighted) for one week. Benchmarks: BTC and the largest quintile. Cost: 50 bp per side on turnover, plus 50% haircut on delisted names at their last price. Test window 2019-2026, halves split 2022-11. Statistic: mean weekly net excess over BTC, date-clustered bootstrap CI, DSR over the declared variants. Pass: lower 95% bound > 0 in both halves. The prior is to expect failure on a liquid universe.

candidates.name: Crypto 2-week momentum: test the short leg (losers) on Kalshi-perp coins
candidates.summary: Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu CMOM sorts coins on their past 1-4 week return. Fieberg et al. find that momentum survives in larger coins mostly through the short leg. Mandel's T-314 tested only the long top-tertile leg and failed. This candidate tests whether 2-week losers underperform BTC, executed short on Kalshi perps.
candidates.mechanism: Slow diffusion of bad news and network-adoption shocks, plus retail extrapolation. Losers keep losing because shorting alts is costly and limited (limits to arbitrage on the short side).
variables: crypto funding/basis (perp funding cost of the short)
candidates.assets: Kalshi-perp-listed coins (BTC, ETH, SOL, DOGE, SHIB, ... per Hurst's universe); Coinbase spot top-30 as long-only 'avoid losers' variant.
candidates.claimed_effect: Borri et al. (2025): CMOM 5-1 is +2.6%/week (t 3.89) over the full sample and +2.1%/week (t 3.70) post-2020, value-weighted weekly. Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba (2024): momentum persists among larger coins but carries heavy trading costs and comes mostly from short positions. Their numbers were not readable (the page returned 403).
candidates.replication: Replicated post-2020 by Borri et al. Robust across the 20,736 designs of Fieberg et al. Implementability is contested (costs, short leg). Duplicates T-314 (long leg, not supported) and relates to T-556 (DOGE/SHIB bounce-short, supported) and T-477 (CTREND, blocked).

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the point-in-time top-30 Coinbase USD coins by trailing 30-day dollar volume (T-424's construction). Signal: 14-day return to Sunday 00:00 UTC. Short the bottom tercile, equal-weighted against a BTC long (beta-neutral by trailing 60-day beta), for one week. Primary arm: the coins with Kalshi perps, where the short is executable. Secondary arm, long-only and executable on all coins: hold BTC and exclude losers. Costs: Kalshi perp taker fee both legs plus the realised funding paid or received; Coinbase 50 bp per side in the long-only arm. Window 2019-2026, halves split 2022-11. Statistic: mean weekly net return of the (BTC - losers) spread, block bootstrap (8 weeks), DSR counting T-314's trials. Pass: lower bound > 0 in both halves.

candidates.name: Crypto network value (price-to-active-addresses, CVALUE)
candidates.summary: Coins whose market cap is high relative to network adoption (addresses) underperform. This is the value factor of the C-4 model and uses a non-price fundamental.
candidates.mechanism: Network-effect valuation (Metcalfe-style). Price runs ahead of adoption on hype and mean-reverts toward fundamental usage. Buyers of hyped low-usage tokens are on the other side.
candidates.assets: Coinbase USD spot coins that have CoinMetrics community address data (138 assets carry AdrActCnt). Long-only high-value quintile, or a short via Kalshi perps where listed.
candidates.claimed_effect: Borri et al. (2025): CVALUE (price-to-new-address ratio) 5-1 is -3.5%/week (t -3.50) over the full sample and -2.3%/week (t -2.32) post-2020, value-weighted weekly. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (2021, C-4 model) is the primary source as cited by Borri et al.; I did not open that paper.
candidates.replication: Post-2020 replication by Borri et al. comes from the same author group, so it is not independent. No independent replication was found before the web-search budget ran out. Untested in Mandel; no network or address theory exists.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: coins with CoinMetrics community AdrActCnt ∩ point-in-time Coinbase USD listings, volume >= $1m/day. Signal: CMC market cap / trailing 28-day mean AdrActCnt (new addresses are not in the free API; active addresses are the adjacent proxy). Lag it 2 days because CoinMetrics publishes 'flash' values that are later revised. Store first-seen values going forward and treat the backfill as revised data, reported separately. Sort weekly. Hold the cheapest (low ratio) quintile vs BTC, long-only. Cost 50 bp per side. Window 2019-2026, halves split 2022-11. Statistic: mean weekly net excess, date-clustered bootstrap, DSR across ratio definitions (active addresses; MVRV as an alternative 'value'). Pass: lower bound > 0 and the same sign in both halves.

candidates.name: Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum (first half-hour predicts last half-hour)
candidates.summary: Shen, Urquhart and Wang (2022) use a volume-defined session clock and find the first half-hour return of BTC's session positively predicts the last half-hour return, most strongly in high-volume or high-volatility sessions.
candidates.mechanism: The authors attribute it to liquidity provision rather than late-informed trading, as in FX: intermediaries' inventory is unwound late in the session in the direction of the early flow.
candidates.assets: BTC on Coinbase spot, CDE nano futures or Kalshi perps (US-legal)
candidates.claimed_effect: Positive first-to-last half-hour predictability with meaningful market-timing gains, especially in BTC downturns (Financial Review 57(2), 2022). The sample period and coefficients were not on the accessible page; I have not verified them.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Mandel's SPY analogue (T-427, half-hour momentum 2023-2026) failed, and the T-577 intraday ML program has 0 passing cells, both hostile priors. Retail crypto costs (about 0.4-0.6% per side on Coinbase) likely dominate a half-hour move.

candidates.proposed_test: Data: Coinbase BTC-USD 1-minute bundles 2022-01..2026-10. Two pre-registered session clocks: (a) the UTC day; (b) the NYSE session, 13:30-20:00 UTC adjusted for DST, when IBIT and CME volume peak. Signal: sign of the first-30-minute return. Trade the last 30 minutes in that direction, entering at the bar close 30 minutes before session end. Conditional arm: first-half-hour volume in its top tercile (trailing 60 sessions). Fit nothing; fixed rule. Test 2024-01..2026-10 with 2022-2023 reported. Costs: Coinbase maker 0.40% and taker 0.60% per side for small accounts (from memory; recheck current schedule), and the CDE nano futures fee schedule. Statistic: HAC slope of last-half-hour on first-half-hour return, mean net per trade, block bootstrap by week, Bonferroni over 2 clocks × 2 arms. Pass: net mean lower bound > 0. Expect a gross effect below cost.

candidates.name: Spot bitcoin ETF net flows predict next-day BTC returns (timestamp-aligned)
candidates.summary: Daily net creations or redemptions of US spot BTC ETFs, led by IBIT, are a non-price flow input. After aligning ETF trading hours with 24/7 BTC, same-day flows are reported to predict next-day BTC returns, with strong reverse feedback (returns predict flows).
candidates.mechanism: Authorised participants buy or sell BTC to create or redeem shares, so flows are real spot demand. Persistent flows plus slow-moving advisor and RIA allocations produce price pressure. The other side is crypto-native holders supplying coins.
candidates.assets: BTC (Coinbase spot), IBIT, CME BTC/MBT, Kalshi perps
candidates.claimed_effect: Fabus et al. (SSRN 7545019, Sep 2026), from the ML-Quant summary: +1.67 percentage points of next-day BTC return per $1bn of same-day net inflow after timestamp correction, with prior returns significantly predicting flows. Lim (SSRN 6592830, 2026; search abstract only, not opened): a $100m inflow corresponds to about 53 bp same-day return, and flow persistence makes temporary impact look permanent. Mazur-Polyzos report R^2 of 95% on price levels, which is spurious for returns.
candidates.replication: Contested. Several 2024-2026 working papers disagree on direction and size depending on timestamp handling; none is peer-reviewed. Untested in Mandel (no BTC ETF-flow theory; T-404 GLD holdings flows was parked).

candidates.proposed_test: Data: daily net flow by fund from Farside (new bundle). Cross-check against IBIT daily shares outstanding × NAV from iShares, which is published the next morning. Window 2024-01-11..2026-09. Point in time: day-t flow is treated as known only from 13:30 UTC on t+1 (the next US open), not at 00:00 UTC, because Farside posts estimates in the evening and issuers confirm the next morning. Target: BTC (Coinbase) return 13:30 UTC t+1 → 13:30 UTC t+2, and IBIT open-to-close on t+1. Regression of target on flow ($bn) with controls for the BTC return over day t and the 5-day lagged return (the reverse-feedback confound). HAC t-stat. Out-of-sample: fit the sign and threshold on 2024-01..2025-06, test 2025-07..2026-09. Rule: long IBIT for the day when flow > +$500m, flat otherwise, at 5 bp round trip. Pass: OOS slope > 0 with HAC t >= 2, and rule net Sharpe > buy-and-hold over the same days.

candidates.name: CME bitcoin COT: follow leveraged-funds position changes
candidates.summary: In the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report for CME bitcoin, leveraged-money traders hold the largest, net-short positions and are reported to show market-timing ability, mainly by adjusting their shorts. Strategies built on changes in their positions are reported to be profitable.
candidates.mechanism: Informed hedge funds and CTAs adjust shorts ahead of moves, and other trader types follow them later. A competing explanation: since 2024 the leveraged-fund shorts are largely cash-and-carry hedges against ETF longs, so position changes track the basis, not views.
candidates.assets: BTC via IBIT or CME MBT (US-legal)
candidates.claimed_effect: Baur & Smales (J. Futures Markets 2022): leveraged money traders display market timing, and profitable strategies can be built on variations in leveraged-money positions. The magnitudes were not readable (the publisher page returned 403); only the abstract was seen, via Crossref.
candidates.replication: No replication found. The regime has likely changed since the spot ETFs (2024-01), when basis-trade shorts grew; practitioner commentary reads leveraged-fund shorts as basis hedges. Untested in Mandel for bitcoin; the gold analogue T-405 was parked (not supported).

candidates.proposed_test: Data: archived bundles cftc-cot-tff-f-133741 / -fo-133741 (CME Bitcoin, about 444 weekly reports), release-time stamped (Friday 15:30 ET for Tuesday positions). Signal: weekly change in leveraged-funds net position divided by open interest. A secondary arm uses a z-score of its level over the trailing 52 reports. Pre-registered sign: an increase in LF net (short covering) is bullish. Entry at the first tradable price after release (BTC Coinbase at Friday 20:00/21:00 UTC; IBIT at Monday open from 2024). Hold 7 days. Controls: the synchronous CME annualised basis and its change, because LF shorts are basis hedges, plus the prior-week BTC return. Window 2018-2026, split at 2024-01.
