candidates.name: Crypto weekend returns predict Monday US equity returns (negative-side asymmetry)
candidates.summary: BTC trades through the weekend while US stocks do not. Negative weekend crypto returns are reported to predict Monday equity declines, positive ones have no effect, and the link strengthened after the May 2022 LUNA collapse. BTC is the input and SPY/QQQ/IWM the target, so the target's own price stays isolated.
candidates.mechanism: Weekend crypto prices aggregate news and risk appetite while equity markets are closed. Investors are loss-averse and crypto is now a systemic-risk transmitter, so the bad news is not fully priced at the Monday open. Monday-morning equity buyers who ignore the weekend signal are on the other side.
candidates.assets: SPY, QQQ, IWM (Alpaca), and COIN as a crypto-beta stock; signal from Coinbase BTC
candidates.claimed_effect: Mourey, Shahrour and Soiman (Finance Research Letters 86, 2025), Bayesian/Kalman framework on 20 large coins (about 85% of market cap). Negative weekend returns significantly predict Monday declines in the Nasdaq, Russell 2000, S&P sectors and the S&P Crypto Index, and the effect is stronger after May 2022. Coefficients and sample dates were not available on the accessible page.
candidates.replication: No replication found. Not tested in Mandel; weekend tests so far (T-62, T-264, T-515, T-436) concern BTC's own returns and variance. Related to Hurst's forward test H-btc-us500-lead (BTC perp leads US500 perp off-session, read 2026-11-05). Part of the information is already in ES futures from Sunday 18:00 ET, so only the open-to-close piece is tradable in ETFs.

sources.title: A crypto-stock weekend effect: Predicting Monday stock returns using weekend cryptocurrency returns (Mourey, Shahrour, Soiman), FRL 86
SSRN version

candidates.proposed_test: Signal: Coinbase BTC log return from the Friday NYSE close (20:00/21:00 UTC, DST-aware) to Monday 13:00 UTC (30 minutes before the open), known before the trade. Holiday Mondays use the first session after. Targets: SPY, QQQ, IWM Monday open-to-close (tradable). The Friday-close-to-Monday-open gap is reported only, since it is not tradable in ETFs. Primary contrast: mean open-to-close return after bottom-tercile weekend BTC returns (terciles from the trailing 104 weekends) minus after other weekends. Secondary: an ES-adjusted version that conditions on the BTC weekend return net of its regression on the SPY gap, to test information beyond the futures. Window 2018-2026, split 2022-05. Bonferroni over 3 ETFs. Block bootstrap by month. Rule: short or flat SPY Monday after a bottom-tercile weekend, 2 bp round trip. Pass: contrast < 0 with p < 0.05 after Bonferroni in both halves, and a positive net rule return vs always-long Monday.

candidates.name: Deribit expiry return reversal conditioned on dealer gamma (GEX)
candidates.summary: Around Deribit BTC option expiry (Fridays 08:00 UTC) there is a significant return reversal, largest when cumulative dealer gamma exposure is negative. Activity rises in Deribit perps and in the spot venues that feed the settlement index.
candidates.mechanism: Market makers net short gamma hedge in the direction of the move into the settlement TWAP, pushing price, and the move reverses after expiry once hedges are unwound. Option writers and holders transfer wealth through the settlement window.
adjacent_variables: IBIT OPEX (Fri 16:00 ET) as US analogue
candidates.assets: BTC via Coinbase spot, CDE nano futures, Kalshi perps; IBIT options expiry as a forward US analogue
candidates.claimed_effect: Weiss, Gaudiosi, Zhou and Webb (Finance Research Letters, 2026; doi 10.1016/j.frl.2026.110340): a statistically and economically significant reversal around expiry, largest with negative cumulative GEX, implying about USD 50 million a year in wealth transfers. Per the search abstract; the full text was not opened (403).
candidates.replication: No replication found, and one press check could not confirm the condition for a specific expiry. Related Mandel tests: T-223 (pin short straddle on expiry Fridays, not supported), T-513 (max-pain pin, blocked), T-216 (SPY opex pin, supported). This candidate is directional and gamma-conditioned, which differs from those.

sources.title: Bitcoin option expiration, gamma exposure, and intraday price reversals (FRL)
DOI record (Crossref)

candidates.proposed_test: Stage 1 (archived data, unconditional): Coinbase BTC 1-minute bars 2022-2026, with Deribit expiry Fridays taken from deribit-delivery-prices-btc. Regress the 08:00-16:00 UTC return on the 00:00-08:00 UTC return separately for monthly or quarterly expiry Fridays, weekly-expiry Fridays, and non-expiry weekdays at the same clock. Statistic: difference in slopes (expiry minus control), bootstrap by week. Pre-registered sign: more negative on expiry. Stage 2 (gamma conditioning): GEX needs strike-level OI history, which Mandel lacks. Option A: Tardis.dev historical Deribit option book (paid; free monthly samples from memory). Option B: forward capture of deribit-book snapshots (already running) each Thursday 20:00 UTC, giving sign(GEX) under the standard dealers-short-customer-calls/long-puts convention. Trade: fade the pre-expiry move at 08:05 UTC, exit 16:00 UTC, maker cost on CDE nano futures, taker on Coinbase as stress. Pass: slope difference < 0 (p < 0.05) and net mean per trade > 0 in the negative-GEX bucket out of sample.

candidates.name: BTC 25-delta risk reversal (skew) predicts returns
candidates.summary: The 30-day 25-delta risk reversal (call IV minus put IV) from Deribit is tested as a forward predictor of BTC returns, with controls. It uses the options-pricing input (skew) for the BTC price target.
candidates.mechanism: Skew reflects option-market positioning and informed demand for upside or downside protection. If option traders are better informed, or if skew captures crash-insurance pricing that mean-reverts, it predicts spot. A confound: skew mostly reflects recent returns.
candidates.assets: BTC via IBIT, Coinbase spot, CME MBT
candidates.claimed_effect: Neo (SMU thesis, 2026; search abstract only, not opened), daily Deribit data 2021-04 to 2025-12: the RR t-stat rises from 1.91 univariate to 3.73 with full controls, weakens to the 5% level after 2024, and the butterfly becomes insignificant. Independent GitHub backtest: T-30 sign accuracy 58.9% (33/56), p about 0.18; T-90 77.4% on 31 expiries; RR-vs-move correlation r = 0.076. A ScienceDirect paper on BTC implied-vol slopes reports left and right slopes have no return-predictive capability, only weekly realised-vol forecasting.
candidates.replication: Contested and decaying after 2024. All Mandel SPX skew-predicts-returns tests failed (T-52, T-138, T-227). T-257 tested RR P&L, not return predictability (inconclusive).

sources.title: Bitcoin options risk-reversal predictability (Neo, SMU thesis)
deribit-rr: BTC option Risk Reversal backtest
Implied volatility slopes and jumps in bitcoin options market
Bitcoin Options: Finding edge in four years of volatility regimes (Deribit Insights)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: daily BTC smiles from deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC (07:00-09:00 UTC trade sample, as built for T-257/T-262), 2022-01..2026-10. RR25 is interpolated to 30 DTE. Signal: RR25 z-score vs its trailing 90 days, known at 09:00 UTC. Targets: BTC log return 09:00 UTC → +7d and +30d (Coinbase), sampled weekly to avoid overlap. Controls: trailing 7d and 30d return, DVOL, 7-day mean funding. Statistic: Newey-West and Hansen-Hodrick t on RR25 with controls. Out-of-sample R^2 vs the expanding historical mean (Campbell-Thompson) on 2025-01..2026-10 after a 2022-2024 fit. Rule: long IBIT/BTC when z > +1, flat otherwise, 10 bp IBIT or 50 bp Coinbase per switch. Pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with the pre-registered sign and controlled t >= 2.

candidates.name: BTC variance risk premium and vol-of-vol as return predictors
candidates.summary: Mandel already established that the BTC variance risk premium exists (T-49, T-246 supported). The open question is the equity-style result that the VRP, or option-implied vol-of-vol, forecasts subsequent BTC returns, which would make DVOL a non-price input for the price target.
candidates.mechanism: VRP compensates for bearing variance and jump risk. When it is high, the price of risk is high and expected returns are high, as in the Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou equity result (recalled from memory, not re-checked).
candidates.assets: BTC via IBIT, Coinbase spot, CME
candidates.claimed_effect: Atanasova, Miao, Segarra and Willeboordse (SSRN 6771170; search abstract only, page 403): option-implied factors, particularly vol-of-vol, predict BTC excess returns. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov and Wang (arXiv 2410.15195): BVRP is high in low-volatility regimes and lower in high-volatility regimes. That result is contemporaneous, not a forecasting test. No effect sizes were verified.
candidates.replication: No out-of-sample replication found. Untested in Mandel as a return predictor. The VRP existence results (T-49, T-246, T-255) are supported. The ETH VRP (T-67) is not.

sources.title: Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market (Almeida, Grith, Miftachov, Wang)
What Do Crypto Options Tell Us? Risk Premia Implied by BTC Option Prices (Atanasova et al.)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: deribit-dvol-BTC-history (2021-03..), Coinbase daily BTC. Signals at 00:00 UTC: VRP_t = (DVOL/100)^2 − trailing 30-day realised variance (365-day annualisation, both known at t), and vol-of-vol = 30-day realised vol of daily log DVOL changes. Target: BTC log return over the next 30 days (weekly non-overlapping) and 7 days. Statistic: predictive slope with Newey-West and Hansen-Hodrick t. Out-of-sample R^2 vs the expanding mean, fit 2021-2023, test 2024-2026. Report all 7 weekday phases per house rule 10. Rule: long when VRP is in its top tercile (trailing 365 days), flat otherwise, 10 bp IBIT per switch. Deflate over 2 signals × 2 horizons. Pass: OOS R^2 > 0 and t >= 2 on the pre-registered positive sign.

candidates.name: Stablecoin issuance after BTC drawdowns, and exchange net flows (conditional, not unconditional)
candidates.summary: Griffin and Shams find Tether purchases were timed after market downturns and produced sizeable BTC price gains. Mandel's T-402 tested unconditional 30-day supply growth and failed. This candidate tests the conditional version (issuance following a drawdown) plus the adjacent on-chain exchange net-inflow signal.
candidates.mechanism: Fresh stablecoin issuance is new buying power, possibly deployed to support prices after dips; Griffin-Shams attribute it to one entity. Exchange inflows signal intent to sell, outflows accumulation. Sellers into dips are on the other side.
candidates.assets: BTC via Coinbase spot, IBIT, CME
candidates.claimed_effect: Griffin & Shams (J. Finance 2020; 2017-2018 era): flow attributable to one entity, issuance timed after downturns, sizeable price increases. Counter-evidence: Kristoufek (FRL 2021, VAR spillovers) finds no evidence that stablecoins lift other crypto prices. Wei (2018) reports issuance does not affect BTC returns (via citation, not opened). Effect sizes were not verified.
candidates.replication: Contested and likely decayed (manipulation-era sample). Duplicates T-402 (unconditional supply growth, not supported: pooled NW t +0.33) and T-464 (weekly >1 sigma growth, blocked). The netflow arm overlaps T-401 (SOPR + netflows, blocked). Kept only because the drawdown-conditional design and the free CoinMetrics flow data are new. The base rate to beat is T-320 (BTC bottom-decile next-day +8.9 bp gross, no tradable reversal).

sources.title: Is Bitcoin Really Un-Tethered? (Griffin, Shams), J. Finance 75 (2020)
Tethered, or Untethered? On the interplay between stablecoins and major cryptoassets (Kristoufek), FRL 43

candidates.proposed_test: Data: DefiLlama stablecoin supply (daily from 2017-11, free) and CoinMetrics community SplyCur for USDT and USDC. CoinMetrics FlowInExUSD and FlowOutExUSD for BTC, free but marked 'flash' and later revised. Use values lagged 2 days and record first-seen values forward. Events: days with combined USDT+USDC supply increase > 2 sigma (trailing 180 days) within 2 days after a BTC 3-day return in the bottom decile (trailing 365 days). Control events: bottom-decile drawdowns with no issuance spike. Target: BTC return from the next 00:00 UTC over +1 to +3 days. Statistic: event minus control mean, clustered by week, halves 2019-2021 / 2022-2026. Netflow arm: z-score of net inflow (in − out) vs the next-day return, HAC t, pre-registered negative sign. Costs: 50 bp Coinbase round trip. Pass: event-control difference > cost with lower bound > 0 in both halves.

candidates.name: Coinbase premium (US vs offshore BTC price gap) as a US-demand signal
candidates.summary: The Coinbase BTC-USD price minus the Binance BTC-USDT price (in percent) is widely read as a gauge of US institutional or ETF-era demand. Practitioners claim shifts in the premium precede broader moves. No academic test was found.
candidates.mechanism: Segmented venues: US buyers (ETF APs, advisors, Coinbase Prime) lift Coinbase offers before cross-venue arbitrage closes the gap. The premium is persistent because of capital frictions. Borri et al. find cross-exchange discounts have a half-life of about 1.1 weeks and are compensation for risk, not free money.
candidates.assets: BTC via Coinbase spot, IBIT, CME. Binance data is read only as a public signal.
candidates.claimed_effect: Practitioner only: the index is defined as (coinbase − binance)/binance × 100. In Feb 2024 commentary it reached 0.12, the highest since May 2023, during the ETF-driven rally; 2026 reports describe extended negative stretches. Borri et al. (2025): 10th/90th percentile BTC discounts across 510 BTC-fiat pairs are −1.8%/+3.7% (2014-2025), with a half-life of about 1.1 weeks.
candidates.replication: No rigorous test found. The gap is probably contaminated by the USDT/USD basis, which must be removed. Untested in Mandel; T-331 (Coinbase vs Kraken, both USD venues, untested) is a different variable.

candidates.proposed_test: Data: Coinbase BTC-USD 1-minute bundles (2022-01..2026-10) and Binance spot BTCUSDT 1-minute klines (public data.binance.vision, a new bundle read as a signal only). USDT/USD from the coinbase-daily-USDT-USD bundle; a Kraken USDTUSD minute series is preferable. Premium_t = Coinbase close / (Binance close × USDTUSD) − 1 at synchronous minute closes, averaged over the trailing 24h at 00:00 UTC, then z-scored vs the trailing 90 days. Target: next 24h Coinbase BTC return; secondary target IBIT next open-to-close. Statistic: HAC slope and tercile contrast, split pre-ETF (2022-2023) / post-ETF (2024-2026), Bonferroni over 2 targets. Rule: long when z > 1, else flat, at 50 bp round trip on Coinbase and 5 bp on IBIT. Pass: same positive sign in both halves, t >= 2 post-ETF, rule net > buy-and-hold on the same days.

candidates.name: CME bitcoin weekend gap 'fill' vs a random-walk first-passage null
candidates.summary: Folklore says BTC almost always revisits the CME Friday close after the weekend. Test whether the fill rate exceeds what a random walk with the same volatility implies, and whether fading toward the gap pays after costs.
candidates.mechanism: The claimed mechanism is CME-spot arbitrage and basis convergence. Statistically, most small gaps 'fill' under any random walk, so the claim is suspect until benchmarked.
candidates.assets: BTC via CME MBT, Coinbase spot, Kalshi perps
candidates.claimed_effect: An unverified TradingView post claims about 90-95% of CME gaps fill, with no sample or method given. Another indicator page notes large gaps in trends can stay open for weeks.
candidates.replication: No study found. Likely a first-passage artifact. If CME moved crypto futures to 24/7 trading in 2026 as announced (recalled from memory, verify the date), new gaps stop at the switch and the sample ends there. Untested in Mandel.

sources.title: What is CME gap: do they always fill? (TradingView ideas)
BTC CME Weekend Gap Tracker (TradingView open-source script)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: daily-history-BTC=F for the Friday CME close, and Coinbase BTC 1-minute bars for spot at the Friday CME close minute and at the Sunday reopen (DST-aware CME hours). Window 2019-05..min(2026-09, CME 24/7 switch). Gap_t = Sunday-reopen spot vs Friday-close spot, |gap| > 1%. Fill = spot trades through the Friday level within 5 days. Null: per-event first-passage probability 2·Φ(−|gap|/(σ√T)), with σ the trailing 30-day realised vol. Placebo: the same computation from Wednesday-close pseudo-gaps. Statistic: observed fill rate minus mean null probability, Wilson/bootstrap CI by month. Trade arm: at reopen + 5 min, enter toward the Friday level, target the fill, stop at 2×|gap|, exit after 5 days; MBT fees plus 1 tick slippage. Pass: fill-rate excess > 0 with the CI excluding 0 vs both null and placebo, and net trade mean > 0.

candidates.name: Open-interest flush / liquidation-cascade reversal
candidates.summary: Large one-day drops in perp open interest during sharp price falls mark forced deleveraging (liquidations). The claim is that the price overshoots and partly reverses over the next days, beyond the plain short-term reversal that Mandel found too small to trade.
candidates.mechanism: Forced sellers (liquidated longs) are price-insensitive. Liquidity providers who absorb the cascade earn a premium as prices recover once leverage is cleared. Reflexive leverage-liquidity-volatility loops drive the overshoot.
candidates.assets: BTC, ETH via Coinbase spot, CDE nano futures, Kalshi perps. Offshore OI is read only as a public signal.
candidates.claimed_effect: Case-study level only. Ali (SSRN 5611392): the Oct 10-11 2025 cascade erased $19bn of OI in 36 hours through reflexive leverage-liquidity-volatility loops. A secondary write-up of a 2026 preprint (not verified) says 87.8% of post-onset forced selling came within 30 minutes and no pre-event measure ranked cascade severity. MDPI Forecasting (2026; page 403) links liquidation-tail risk to delayed marks and funding memory. No return-predictability estimate was found.
candidates.replication: No systematic study found before the search budget ran out. The base rate is hostile: T-320 and T-469 found BTC bottom-decile next-day reversal at +8.9 to +11 bp gross, below cost. The OI-flush condition is the new information. Untested in Mandel; no OI or liquidation theory exists.

sources.title: Anatomy of the Oct 10-11, 2025 Crypto Liquidation Cascade (Ali), SSRN
Delayed Marks, Funding Memory, and Forecasting Liquidation-Tail Risk in Crypto Perpetual Futures (MDPI Forecasting 8(5):76)
Crypto carry (BIS WP 1087): margins spike and liquidations occur in drawdowns

candidates.proposed_test: Data: Binance USD-M futures daily 'metrics' files for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT (5-minute sum_open_interest, taker long/short volume ratio; public archive from 2020-09-01, verified), a new bundle read as signal only. Coinbase daily and 1-minute BTC/ETH for the target. Event: UTC day with a 24h OI change in the bottom 5% of its trailing 365 days AND a 24h return below −2 trailing sigma. Control: days with the same price-drop condition but OI change above its median (no flush). Enter at the next 00:00 UTC (Coinbase), hold 1 and 3 days. Statistic: event minus control mean return, week-clustered bootstrap, fit-free. Out-of-sample: report 2020-09..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-10 separately. Costs: 50 bp Coinbase round trip; CDE nano maker as an alternative. Pass: event-control difference > cost with lower bound > 0 in both halves and a minimum of 30 non-overlapping events.

rows.name: Perp-spot premium convergence (random-maturity arbitrage bound), positive leg only

overlaps.note: Long BTC / short Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL, entered on trailing 7-day funding above DTB3 + 4%. The Sharpe already includes the perp-spot spread marked to market, i.e. the convergence leg. Test 2023-01..2026-09: central Sharpe -0.64 (pessimistic -1.35, optimistic 0.40), DSR 0.001, 118 switches. The premium was rebuilt from funding, with |u| <= 0.05% unobservable inside the dampener band. This candidate swaps in an hourly premium-level entry and a premium-based exit.

Salvage successor of T-363 on ETH with a hysteresis exit. On BTC the hysteresis control gave central Sharpe 1.13, but that was already seen, so BTC cannot be the test. Any new BTC premium rule must count it as a prior trial.
Perp funding beat the quarterly basis in only 43.8% of 90-day windows. The mean difference is -0.14 pp.
Option-hedged funding carry: +0.91%/month net, CI [-0.03, +3.16]%. Sharpe over DTB3 is 0.44.
The Deribit quarterly basis does not exceed bills + 100 bp at the median (2019-2026).
CME cash-and-carry above DTB3 + 3%: excess +0.14%/yr, lower bound -0.57%.
Convergence after a CME basis z > 2 nets +0.178% per 5-day trade. Pre-2024 it is +0.229% (n 22), post-2024 +0.039% (n 8). Convergence profits shrank after the ETFs.
Top-decile funding does not predict 7-day spot returns. Rich perps are not a timing signal for spot.
IBIT-hedged BTC funding carry on Kalshi perps is already the US-executable form of this trade. Any Mandel premium rule should be read alongside it, not run as a duplicate live record.

learnings.finding: Funding carry is dead on US venues. Funding there averages about zero, and a 14-day hedged hold at > 8%/yr funding nets -0.15%. Hyperliquid carry is 'alive' (+3.8 to +12.2%/yr) but closed to US users.
No killed model becomes profitable at 2-10x on Kalshi perps. Funding and rollover exceed the edges.

learnings.source: deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL (archived interest_1h, read for this check)
learnings.finding: Mean annualised funding by year: 2024 +10.3%, 2025 +5.4%, 2026 YTD +2.2%, against DTB3 of about 4-5%. Funding sits at zero (inside the dampener) in 18% of hours overall and 31% in 2026. The premium is censored exactly where the post-2024 signal lives.
Carry is a structural premium, but published crypto carry has decayed (Borri et al.: negative in 2025), consistent with T-363's test-window failure.
Deribit get_tradingview_chart_data bars are stamped by their open time. A BTC-PERPETUAL hourly candle used for an exact premium must be keyed by its close.

rows.missing_data: No US-venue premium or funding history: Coinbase Derivatives perp-style nano futures only since 2025-07, Kalshi perps only in 2026, and Hurst records them forward. An exact Deribit premium needs BTC-PERPETUAL 1h candles (free, reachable via get_tradingview_chart_data, not archived). Binance premiumIndexKlines 1h are free on data.binance.vision, as a signal only. Without these, the premium is known only to within the funding dampener band, as in T-363.

registration.claim: From 2024-01 to 2026-09 (entry bound fixed on 2020-01..2023-12), a long BTC spot / short BTC-PERPETUAL position earns a positive Sharpe of daily excess return over DTB3. It enters at the next hourly close after the perp premium reconstructed from Deribit interest_1h exceeds a cost-clearing bound, and exits when funding returns to zero (premium inside the dampener band) or after 30 days. US-retail costs are charged on both legs and margin is financed at DTB3 + 1.5%.
registration.statistic: Annualised Sharpe of daily excess return over DTB3 in the test window: funding accrued + premium mark-to-market + spot P&L - costs - financing. Reported separately: price-convergence share vs funding share, in-position days, trade count, max drawdown.
registration.procedure: Hourly premium p = 8 x interest_1h plus or minus the dampener (T-363 reconstruction), available at the funding record timestamp. Premium inside the band is unobservable, so every statistic is computed under pessimistic, central and optimistic bounds. One entry bound is chosen on 2020-2023: the smallest annualised premium whose expected convergence clears the round-trip cost of both legs. Costs: Coinbase spot 0.60% taker / 0.40% maker per side plus a 4 bp per side perp taker; a reported variant uses IBIT as the spot leg at 5 bp round trip, US hours only. The bound is then frozen. Inverse-contract P&L is converted to USD at each hourly mark, and liquidation at 2x is checked on hourly marks. Studentized circular block bootstrap, 30-day blocks, 5,000 draws. DSR counts T-363's 12 trials plus T-198, T-258, T-553, H-ibit-carry and this rule (17). If Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL hourly candles are fetched, key them by close time and use them to replace the bounded premium as a robustness arm.
registration.data: deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3; optional new deribit-perp-candles-BTC-1h
registration.pass: Test-window Sharpe with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0 under the PESSIMISTIC premium bound, and DSR > 0.95. A pass licenses only a forward record on Kalshi BTC perp or CDE nano vs Coinbase spot/IBIT, read jointly with H-ibit-carry.
registration.controls: Baselines on the same window: the T-363 funding-threshold rule and always-in carry. One bound, no grid. Funding and premium enter only after each hour. Costs per leg on both legs, plus the DTB3 hurdle on total capital. Regimes reported: 2024 ETF era, 2025, 2026. Venue-transfer risk recorded, since Deribit is not US-accessible and Hurst measures US-venue funding at about 0, so the back-test is an upper bound.

rows.notes: A variant of T-363, which already marked the perp-spot spread, so the 'convergence share' is not new information. The only new elements are a premium-level entry and a premium-based exit. On Deribit the premium below about 5 bp is censored by the funding dampener, so the claimed rho <= 0 exit cannot be observed. Recast it as 'funding back to zero'. At retail Coinbase spot costs (about 1% round trip on both legs) almost no post-2022 premium clears the bound. The IBIT spot leg is the only cheap US form, and it is Hurst's H-ibit-carry forward test. Prior strongly against. Run only as a cheap archived-data check after higher-priority items. Signal-map addition suggested: 'perp premium / funding' and 'carry decay' as market-variable concepts (the map currently has none).

rows.name: Crypto size factor (CSIZE), long-only small-cap tilt on a liquid US-listed universe

overlaps.note: Built the survivorship-aware point-in-time CMC weekly universe (cmc-historical-listings) that this test needs. Today's-top-30 inflated returns by +1.14%/week, so survivorship dominates crypto cross-sections.

On the same Coinbase top-50 universe, high-volume altcoin events earned -1.80% net per 10 days market-adjusted, negative every year 2020-2026 (raw 10-day -1.29%). Alts as a class drifted down against BTC through the test window.
Universe construction (top-N by trailing 30-day Coinbase dollar volume, exclusion lists for stablecoins, wrapped/staked and fx_stablecoin ids) is reusable.
The equity size-adjacent factor (net issuance) also failed post-publication. Anomaly decay is the house prior.

learnings.finding: Liquid Coinbase altcoins underperformed BTC by year in 2022-2026, which is exactly the second half of this test. A long-only small-cap alt book must beat that drift.
Cross-sectional lift over the same-day basket is +0.002%/trade. Hurst's edge is basket timing, not coin selection.

learnings.source: T-578 swing ML (306 cells, 0 pass dev)
learnings.finding: Daily-horizon feature models, including volume and price-free families, produced no passing cell.

learnings.source: Mandel-wide lesson (published anomalies decay; micro-cap concentration)
learnings.finding: The candidate's own replication puts the post-2020 premium in micro-caps (Fieberg et al.). A $1m/day volume filter removes most of them.
89 delisted USD products carry daily bundles, alongside 403 online ones. Delisted names can be held to their last price, so the Coinbase-side survivorship is partly covered.

rows.missing_data: None for the test. Caveats: CMC weekly snapshots keep only the top 500 by rank, so liquid Coinbase coins ranked below 500 have no market cap and are excluded and counted. The 2020-11-30 snapshot is corrupt (T-314) and treated as missing. Only Sunday and Monday snapshots exist, not the 'prior day' the candidate names.

registration.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, on the point-in-time Coinbase USD universe (stablecoins, wrapped/staked and fx_stablecoin ids excluded; trailing 30-day Coinbase dollar volume >= $1m), the value-weighted smallest market-cap quintile earns a mean weekly return above BTC after 50 bp per side on turnover, with both halves positive. Coins are sorted on the CMC Sunday snapshot (available Monday 00:00 UTC) and held from Monday 00:00 to the next Monday 00:00 UTC.
registration.statistic: Mean weekly net excess return, Q1 (smallest) minus BTC. Reported: Q1 - Q5 and Q1 - equal-weight universe (gross and net), turnover, names per quintile.
registration.procedure: Universe rebuilt weekly with the T-424/T-546 exclusion lists plus CMC snapshot flags. Market cap = marketCap of the Sunday snapshot, available Monday 00:00 UTC. Coins missing from the top 500 are dropped and their count reported. Entry and exit at Coinbase daily opens (Monday 00:00 UTC bar). A name that stops trading is held to its last Coinbase price minus a 50% haircut. Weekly date-clustered bootstrap and an 8-week circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. DSR over 2 declared variants (value- and equal-weighted) plus T-314's 24 crypto cross-section trials.
registration.data: cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, coinbase-products-2026-10-15, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD
registration.pass: Lower 95% bound of mean weekly net excess > 0, both halves (split 2022-11-17) positive, DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: BTC, Q5 and equal-weight-universe benchmarks, to separate size from the alt-vs-BTC drift. 50 bp per side on drift-adjusted turnover. Survivorship stress (delisted -50%). One sort, one rebalance day, no grid. Snapshots older than 8 days are never used. Bull/bear regime split reported (Fieberg: anomalies concentrate in bull markets).

rows.notes: Novel to Mandel (no crypto size theory exists), but every adjacent learning is hostile. Alts lost to BTC in every year of the second half (T-546), selection lift is about zero (Hurst), and the claimed premium sits in micro-caps a liquid filter removes. Fix to the proposed timing: sort on the Sunday snapshot, available Monday 00:00 UTC, and trade at the Monday open. The archive has no Saturday snapshot. Cheap to run on the T-314/T-424 machinery, so run it as a decisive negative rather than a hopeful test. Signal-map addition: 'market cap / circulating supply (crypto)' and 'survivorship inflation' as concepts.

rows.name: Crypto 2-week momentum: test the short leg (losers) on Kalshi-perp coins

overlaps.note: Long top-tertile 3-week momentum of the point-in-time top 30 vs BTC: -0.479%/week net (gross -0.074%), CI -1.25..+0.37, DSR 0. The permutation p was 0.035, with the null 95th percentile at -0.522%. Momentum ranks beat random tertile picks even though every alt book lost to BTC, which points to losers doing worse than random.
The DOGE/SHIB bounce-short (a short-side, loser-continuation-adjacent rule) is supported at +2.55%/trade after refutation. That is a time-series rule on two coins, not a cross-section.
CTREND long-only top quintile, blocked.
BTC/ETH 1-week time-series momentum minus historical mean: -41.3 bps/week.
Same, pooled over 7 weekday phases: -50.0 bps/week, CI excludes 0.
Source of the top-N dollar-volume universe construction.
Alt-vs-BTC drift confound: any 'BTC minus losers' spread inherits it.

learnings.finding: Momentum ranks are informative relative to random tertiles (p 0.035) although the long leg loses to BTC net. That is consistent with Fieberg's finding that the effect lives in the short leg.
The bounce-short's edge is basket timing. The cross-sectional lift over the same-day basket is +0.002%/trade.

Kalshi perp round trip is about 16-18 bp on DOGE/SHIB (4 bp taker plus 4-5 bp from mid per side), and BTC's spread is about 0.2 bp. Funding on US venues averages about zero. A weekly short leg is cheap if the coin is listed.
The Kalshi-listed coin set is hindsight-selected (DOGE/SHIB because Kalshi lists them). A Kalshi-only primary arm tests a universe chosen after the fact.
0 of 306 daily swing cells pass dev, including the cross-sectional long-short rule.

rows.missing_data: No Kalshi perp price or funding history before 2026; Hurst collects it forward. The Kalshi short arm can only be priced on Coinbase spot with assumed Kalshi costs, at funding 0 plus or minus a stress band.

registration.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, among the point-in-time top-30 Coinbase USD coins by trailing 30-day dollar volume, the bottom tercile by 14-day return to Monday 00:00 UTC underperforms the equal-weight top-30 basket over the following Monday-to-Monday week. The executable long-only book (equal-weight top 30 excluding that tercile) therefore beats the equal-weight top 30 after 50 bp per side on its extra turnover, with both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean weekly net return of EW(top-30 ex-losers) - EW(top-30). Secondary, reported: EW(top-30) - EW(losers) gross; (BTC - losers) beta-neutral by trailing 60-day beta, net of Kalshi perp costs (18 bp round trip, funding 0 with a plus/minus 10%/yr stress) on the Kalshi-listed subset.
registration.procedure: Universe each Monday 00:00 UTC by the T-424 construction (stablecoin, wrapped/staked and fx_stablecoin exclusions; CMC flags as a cross-check). Signal = Coinbase close-to-close 14-day return through the daily bar ending Monday 00:00 UTC. Entry at the Monday 00:00 UTC open, exit at the next Monday open. Delisted names are held to their last price minus 50%. 8-week circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Random-tercile placebo, 1,000 permutations of the tercile labels within each week. DSR counts T-314's 24 trials plus the 3 arms here. Halves split 2022-11-17.
registration.data: coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, coinbase-products-2026-10-15, cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, coinbase-hourly-<SYM>-USD
registration.pass: Primary mean weekly net with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, both halves positive, DSR > 0.95, and above the placebo 95th percentile. The Kalshi arm is reported only (hindsight universe). A primary pass licenses a forward paper record of the short leg on Kalshi perps.
registration.controls: The equal-weight basket benchmark and the random-tercile placebo separate momentum from the alt-vs-BTC drift (T-546). Fixed 14-day lookback and weekly hold, no grid. 50 bp per side on Coinbase. Survivorship haircut. Regime split by year reported.

rows.notes: The strongest candidate in the cluster. The T-314 permutation result is an unexploited hint that losers carry the signal. The proposed 'BTC minus losers' spread is confounded by the alt-vs-BTC drift that T-546 measured. Its 'hold BTC and exclude losers' long-only arm is literally holding BTC. So the registration isolates losers against the equal-weight basket and makes the executable long-only form 'top 30 excluding losers'. The Kalshi-perp short arm covers only a handful of hindsight-selected coins. Keep it as a reported secondary and a forward record, not the verdict. Signal-map addition: 'cross-sectional momentum (crypto), short leg'.

rows.name: Crypto network value (price-to-active-addresses, CVALUE)

overlaps.note: The BTC time-series MVRV regime ran the wrong way: 90-day forward return was +0.206 when MVRV < 1 vs +0.412 when MVRV > 3, CI spans 0. The MVRV 'value' alternative named here has already failed in its time-series form.
SOPR and exchange netflows (on-chain holder behaviour) are blocked on paid data.
Long-alt books face the measured alt-vs-BTC drift.
Point-in-time CMC universe; survivorship inflation +1.14%/week.

learnings.finding: An on-chain 'value' ratio (MVRV) did not predict BTC returns in the expected direction over 2011-2026.

Coin Metrics community data in the archive is current vintage, not point-in-time: realised cap and hash rate are recomputed without vintages. A backfilled address ratio carries revision bias by construction.

learnings.source: Mandel rule: nothing is built on a result that has not survived independent refutation
learnings.finding: The only post-2020 replication of CVALUE comes from the original author group (Borri, Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu), so it is not independent evidence.
Long-only cross-sectional alt selection has shown no lift on liquid US-listed coins.

rows.missing_data: Per-asset active addresses (Coin Metrics community AdrActCnt) for altcoins. The archive holds only BTC/ETH Coin Metrics metrics, and not AdrActCnt. Free from community-api.coinmetrics.io (CC BY-NC 4.0, current vintage). New-address counts, the paper's actual signal, are not in the free tier. Start a daily first-seen capture now so a revision-free forward record accumulates.

registration.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, on Coinbase USD coins with Coin Metrics AdrActCnt and trailing 30-day dollar volume >= $1m, the value-weighted quintile with the lowest CMC market cap / trailing 28-day mean active addresses earns a higher mean weekly return than BTC after 50 bp per side, with both halves positive. The ratio is lagged 2 days and coins are sorted weekly at Monday 00:00 UTC.
registration.statistic: Mean weekly net excess return, cheap quintile minus BTC. Reported: cheap minus rich quintile, and cheap quintile minus a size-matched portfolio.
registration.procedure: Market cap from the CMC Sunday snapshot (available Monday 00:00 UTC). AdrActCnt is lagged 2 days to clear flash revisions. The backfill is current vintage and labelled 'revised-data result'; a forward first-seen capture is the confirmatory test. Entry at the Monday 00:00 UTC Coinbase open. Delisted names are held to their last price minus 50%. Weekly date-clustered and 8-week block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. DSR over 2 ratio definitions (active addresses; MVRV where Coin Metrics publishes it) plus T-400.
registration.data: cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, new coinmetrics-adractcnt-<asset>-daily
registration.pass: Lower 95% bound > 0 and both halves (split 2022-11-17) positive, DSR > 0.95, and the forward first-seen record agrees in sign after 52 weeks.
registration.controls: Size-matched benchmark (the low ratio can be a small-cap proxy), equal-weight universe and BTC. 2-day lag. Revision-bias disclosure. At least 20 eligible coins per week, otherwise the week is dropped. 50 bp per side. No grid over the 28-day window.

rows.notes: Untested in Mandel. It needs a new fetch, and its data is revised, which conflicts with the point-in-time rule, so a historical pass would be weak evidence. The MVRV alternative is contradicted by T-400. Worth starting the free daily capture now (cheap) so that a clean forward record exists, but do not spend a harness on the backfill before the higher-priority items. Signal-map addition: 'on-chain adoption (active addresses, MVRV)' as a concept, with the vintage caveat.

rows.name: Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum (first half-hour predicts last half-hour)

overlaps.note: SPY half-hour momentum (previous close to 10:30 predicting 15:30-16:00), 2023-11..2026-10: mean net -2.09 bps (gross -0.09). The last-half-hour slope on the early return is -0.004 (t -0.22). QQQ and IWM are also negative.
Closing-auction reversal on SPY, not supported.
QQQ opening-range breakout; Hurst runs a paper pilot of the same idea.
Intraday ML on crypto 5-minute bars: 50 cells, 0 net > 0. Best mean net -7.75 bp per trade.

learnings.finding: Hourly reversal, momentum and hour-of-day rules on 20 Kalshi perps carry under 6 bp of predictable follow-through against a 16-18 bp round trip. The walk-forward loses -45 bp/trade. No hour of day or weekday gives direction.
Crypto 5-minute cells: F0 price-free mean IC -0.0068, F2 own-price IC +0.0040. No cell nets a positive return.
The equity analogue of the first-to-last half-hour effect is absent 2023-2026 even before costs.
A pre-registered 5-minute opening-range breakout on QQQ is 'alive' in backtest (+32.6%/yr, Sharpe 1.05) and in paper pilot. Early-session momentum can exist in equities at 1 c/share costs.

rows.missing_data: None for the test; 1-minute history starts 2022-01, so there is no 2019-2021 sample. The Coinbase Derivatives nano fee schedule and current Coinbase retail tiers must be rechecked (the candidate quotes them from memory).

registration.claim: From 2024-01 to 2026-10 (2022-2023 reported), trading the last 30 minutes of the session on Coinbase BTC-USD 1-minute bars in the direction of the session's first-30-minute return earns a positive mean net return per trade after a 10 bp round trip (Kalshi BTC perp) in at least one of 4 pre-declared cells after Bonferroni. The cells cross two clocks (UTC day; NYSE session) with all days vs days whose first-half-hour volume is in the top tercile of the trailing 60 sessions.
registration.statistic: Mean net return per trade per cell. Reported: the HAC slope of the last-half-hour return on the first-half-hour return.
registration.procedure: Bars are stamped by start (close = start + 60 s); a missing minute is stale, carried forward and counted. NYSE clock: DST-aware 13:30-20:00 or 14:30-21:00 UTC, with early-close and holiday sessions excluded. Signal = sign of the open-to-+30-minute return. Entry at the close of the bar 30 minutes before session end, exit at the session-end bar close. Volume terciles use only the trailing 60 sessions. No fitting. Weekly circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Stress at the Coinbase retail taker (0.60% per side) and the CDE nano schedule.
registration.data: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi
registration.pass: In at least one cell: one-sided 95% lower bound of net mean > 0 after Bonferroni (4 cells), and the same sign in 2022-2023.
registration.controls: Random-sign placebo (1,000 draws), FOMC/CPI days reported separately, T-427 SPY analogue and T-577 as priors. Cost stress at the retail taker. One fixed rule per cell, no grid.

rows.notes: Every adjacent Mandel and child result is negative: T-427 (SPY), Hurst's 26 hourly rules on perps, and T-577's crypto 5-minute cells. Even at the cheapest US cost (Kalshi BTC perp, about 10 bp round trip) a half-hour BTC move needs > 10 bp of predictable drift. The source paper's coefficients were not verified. Lowest priority: run only if the harness is a by-product of other 1-minute work.

rows.name: Spot bitcoin ETF net flows predict next-day BTC returns (timestamp-aligned)

overlaps.note: Fading IBIT premium/discount: net -0.67% per trade. Premium AR(1) is 0.36 (half-life 0.68 sessions). The ETF-BTC price link is arbitraged within a session.
The gold analogue (GLD holdings flow predicting GLD) is parked, not supported.
The mutual-fund flow 'dumb money' predictor failed on US equities.
Abnormal volume on ETFs and BTC/ETH carried no forward premium.

learnings.finding: Nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close: same-day comovement is already priced by 16:00 ET, and the overnight move of BTC proxies is beta, not a lead.
IBIT's premium to NAV mean-reverts within about one session. Creations and redemptions keep the ETF tied to spot, so a flow is mostly the trace of same-day demand already in the price.

A predictor beats a liquid market only when it is a deeper or earlier source of the same information. Flows published after the close are an aggregate the market has already traded through, which fits the reverse-feedback finding.

learnings.source: Mandel-wide lesson (flows are a structural premium class)
learnings.finding: Flow-driven effects (month-end, T-574 supported) can survive, but Mandel has no supported daily-flow return predictor.

rows.missing_data: Daily net flow by fund, plus IBIT daily shares outstanding and NAV. Farside publishes per-fund daily flows as a free public HTML table, possibly behind bot protection. iShares' IBIT fund page has a free 'data download' with a historical tab of daily NAV and shares outstanding. Neither is archived. First-seen timestamps must be recorded going forward, because Farside revises evening estimates.

registration.claim: From 2024-01-11 to 2026-09 (sign and threshold fixed on 2024-01..2025-06, tested on 2025-07..2026-09), US spot BTC ETF net flow for day t, treated as known at 13:30 UTC on t+1, predicts the Coinbase BTC return from 13:30 UTC t+1 to 13:30 UTC t+2 with a positive slope, after controlling for the day-t and trailing 5-day BTC returns. A rule that holds IBIT from open to close on t+1 when flow > +$500m beats buy-and-hold on the same days at a 5 bp round trip.
registration.statistic: Out-of-sample HAC t of the flow slope (in $bn) with the return controls. Rule net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold Sharpe on the same days. Reported: IBIT open-to-close target, and the reverse regression of flow on lagged returns.
registration.null: OOS slope <= 0, and the rule does not beat buy-and-hold
registration.procedure: Flow_t = sum over funds of Farside day-t flows. Cross-check with IBIT dShares(t) x NAV(t) from iShares, dated by its publication morning. Available at 13:30 UTC t+1, never earlier. Coinbase hourly bars keyed by close time. Controls: BTC return 00:00 UTC t to 13:30 UTC t+1, trailing 5-day return, and the change in the CME annualised basis (basis-trade demand). Newey-West lag 5. Fit the sign and the $500m threshold on 2024-01..2025-06 (one threshold, no grid), test on 2025-07..2026-09. Paired stationary bootstrap (mean block 10 days) for the Sharpe difference.
registration.data: new farside-btc-etf-flows, new ishares-ibit-history (daily NAV and shares outstanding), coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT, daily-history-BTC-F, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: OOS slope > 0 with HAC t >= 2, and the rule's net Sharpe exceeds buy-and-hold with a paired one-sided 95% lower bound > 0.
registration.controls: Lagged returns (reverse feedback), basis change, and IBIT-only flows vs all-fund flows. Revision check: first-seen vs final Farside values on the forward capture. 5 bp round trip on IBIT. Days with US holidays dropped. FOMC/CPI days reported.

rows.notes: A genuinely new non-price flow input for the BTC target, and a US-executable vehicle (IBIT) at low cost. The point-in-time rule (known at the t+1 open) removes most of the published contemporaneous effect, and child learnings say same-day comovement is priced by the close, so expect little. Worth a cheap data capture: iShares history gives a clean, first-party flow series back to 2024-01, and a forward Farside capture fixes the revision problem. Signal-map addition: 'ETF creations/redemptions (flows)' as an adjacent variable.

rows.name: CME bitcoin COT: follow leveraged-funds position changes

overlaps.note: Gold managed-money positioning extremes (z over 156 reports, release-time entry) did not predict 4-week GLD returns.
Gold COT percentile extremes, blocked.
A top-decile CME basis (the variable that drives leveraged-fund shorts after 2024) does not predict deeper 30-day drawdowns: gap -3.6 pp, permutation p 0.96.
Basis z > 2 convergence: post-2024 +0.039% on n 8. The basis trade is crowded.

learnings.finding: Speculator positioning in COT did not predict returns in the one market Mandel tested, despite the same release-time alignment.
Informed traders are a pointer to a source, not a signal to follow. Copying them loses the fee at any delay. A COT print, already 3 days stale at release, is a delayed copy.
444 weekly CME Bitcoin TFF reports, release-time stamped. Each row carries a pit class (live / schedule / bound / backcast / not_realtime), so a point-in-time test is possible now.
After 2024 the leveraged-fund shorts are mostly cash-and-carry hedges (T-362/T-329 basis), so a change in them is more likely a basis signal than a view.

rows.missing_data: None. The CME basis control is built from Yahoo BTC=F daily closes against Coinbase hourly spot at the same hour, which is approximate (settlement vs last trade).

registration.claim: From 2018 to 2026-09, the weekly change in leveraged-funds net position in CME Bitcoin futures, divided by open interest, predicts a positive BTC return over the 7 days from the first Coinbase hourly bar after release, after controlling for the synchronous CME annualised basis, its weekly change and the prior-week BTC return. The sign is the same in both regimes (split at 2024-01-11), and a long/flat rule beats buy-and-hold at 10 bp per switch.
registration.statistic: HAC (Newey-West lag 4) t of the slope on dLF/OI with the controls. Reported: the long/flat rule's net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold, and the per-regime slope.
registration.procedure: LF net = lev_money_positions_long_all - lev_money_positions_short_all, divided by open_interest_all, from the futures-only TFF report (the F&O report as a robustness arm). Rows with pit = not_realtime are excluded. available_at = the bundle's release time, never before Friday 15:30 ET. Entry at the open of the first Coinbase hourly bar starting at or after available_at; exit 7 days later. IBIT arm from 2024-01-11: Monday open to the next Monday open. Basis = ln(BTC=F close / Coinbase spot at the matching hour) x 365/days to expiry, measured at the Tuesday as-of date. A secondary arm uses the z-score of the LF level over the trailing 52 reports. Block-permutation null for the rule (8-week blocks, 2,000 draws).
registration.data: cftc-cot-tff-f-133741, cftc-cot-tff-fo-133741, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-F, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Pooled slope > 0 with HAC t >= 2 after the basis controls, a positive slope in both regimes, and the rule's net Sharpe above buy-and-hold with block-permutation p < 0.05.
registration.controls: Basis level and change, prior-week return, and the asset-manager net change as a competing regressor. 10 bp per switch on IBIT, 50 bp on Coinbase as stress. One pre-registered sign (an increase in LF net is bullish). The z-score arm is counted in the deflation (2 trials plus T-405).

rows.notes: Cheap and fully testable on archived, release-time-stamped data, and novel for bitcoin. Priors are hostile: T-405's gold failure, the stale-copy lesson, and the post-ETF reading of LF shorts as basis hedges, which makes the basis control decisive. A negative result is still useful. It would close the 'smart money' COT idea for crypto and stop it being re-proposed. Signal-map addition: 'COT positioning (TFF leveraged funds / asset managers)'.

rows.name: Crypto weekend returns predict Monday US equity returns (negative-side asymmetry)

overlaps.note: BTC weekend vs weekday returns do not differ.
BTC's own Monday return exceeds other days by +36.5 bps (halves +52.9 / +20.2). The weekend-to-Monday window carries information about BTC itself.
BTC weekend squared returns are 0.47x weekday. Weekend moves are quieter, so a bottom tercile is a smaller move than it looks.
Fading SPY opening gaps loses -6.25 bps net (CI excludes 0), so SPY gaps tend to continue intraday. Any BTC signal must add to the gap itself.
QQQ/IWM close-to-open drift nets +3.4 to +3.6 bp a night. The Monday baseline has its own overnight structure.
BTC perp leading the US500 perp off-session is the same mechanism measured forward on Kalshi perps. Do not read Mandel's test as confirmation of it, or the reverse.

learnings.finding: The overnight move of BTC proxies is beta, not a lead. Nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close, which is the reverse direction but the same 'already priced' finding.
SPY opening gaps continue into the session (fading loses). This fits Monday-open prices not fully absorbing weekend news, but the information may already be in the gap.

BTC trades through the weekend while equities are closed, so it is a candidate leading reference for the Monday open. ES/NQ futures from Sunday 18:00 ET already absorb most of it, so only information beyond the gap is new.

learnings.source: T-579 correlation / inverse-relationship scan (ML program, in progress)
learnings.finding: Cross-asset lead structure is being scanned by the ML program. Its cells must be counted as trials if they include BTC to equity leads.

rows.missing_data: Coinbase hourly history starts 2019-01, so the claimed 2018 start is not possible. With a 52-weekend burn-in for the terciles, signals start in 2020-01. ES Sunday-evening futures intraday history is not archived; the SPY opening gap stands in for it.

registration.claim: From 2020-01 to 2026-09, the Monday (first post-weekend session) open-to-close return of SPY, QQQ and IWM is lower after weekends whose Coinbase BTC return from the Friday NYSE close to 30 minutes before the Monday open falls in the bottom tercile (expanding window, at least 52 weekends) than after other weekends. The difference is significant after Bonferroni over the 3 ETFs, negative in both halves (split 2022-05-09), and a flat-on-signal Monday rule beats always-long Monday after 2 bp round trip.
registration.statistic: Contrast: mean Monday open-to-close return after bottom-tercile weekends minus after other weekends, per ETF. Rule net mean vs always-long Monday.
registration.procedure: BTC Friday mark = close of the Coinbase hourly bar ending at the NYSE close (20:00 UTC in EDT, 21:00 UTC in EST; 1-minute bars from 2022 as a check). Monday mark = close of the bar ending 30 minutes before the open (13:00 or 14:00 UTC). Holiday Mondays roll to the first session after. Bars are keyed by close time. Terciles are expanding, using only past weekends. Targets: Yahoo daily open to close (same-day ratio, unaffected by adjustment). The Friday-close-to-Monday-open gap is reported, not traded. Secondary: the residual of the BTC weekend return on the SPY gap (fitted on past weekends only) tests information beyond the gap. Monthly block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Bonferroni over 3 ETFs; COIN reported.
registration.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM, daily-history-COIN
registration.pass: Pooled contrast < 0 with Bonferroni-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 for at least one ETF, negative in both halves for that ETF, and the rule's net mean Monday return above always-long Monday.
registration.controls: Gap-residualised secondary arm (information beyond the futures), FOMC/CPI Mondays reported, 2 bp round trip, T-549 overnight drift as baseline context, and a placebo using Wednesday 'pseudo-weekends' (BTC Tuesday close to Wednesday 30 minutes before the open). One tercile cut, no grid.

rows.notes: Novel, cheap, executable on Alpaca ETFs at low cost, and it keeps the target's price isolated from the input, as the user's program wants. The archive covers 2019-2026 only through Coinbase hourly bars. Mechanism risk: the ES/NQ Sunday session and the SPY opening gap probably absorb the weekend BTC information, so the gap-residualised arm is the real test. Coordinate with Hurst's H-btc-us500-lead (read 2026-11-05). It is the same idea measured forward, so record both and do not double-count. Signal-map addition: '24/7 market as leading reference for closed markets'.

rows.name: Deribit expiry return reversal conditioned on dealer gamma (GEX)

overlaps.note: Same window (Friday 00:00-08:00 UTC into the Deribit 08:00 delivery TWAP). Monthly-expiry minus other Fridays: model-priced 8-hour straddle P&L +15.7 bp, CI [-15, +45]. The mean |00-08 return| is not larger on expiry (diff -15.5 bp, p 0.82), so there is no measured push into the fixing.
Max-pain pin vs the delivery price, blocked on strike-level open-interest history.
SPY monthly opex Friday short straddle (model-priced) +9.1 bp vs other Fridays, CI excludes 0. Dampening on equity opex exists.
SPY closes are not pinned to strikes on expiry days.
The SPX GEX-conditioned 0DTE test is blocked for the same reason: no gamma-exposure history.
The opex-week return effect is absent on SPY.

learnings.finding: Deribit monthly-expiry Fridays show no larger 00-08 UTC move and no straddle-P&L difference over 2021-2026.
Equity monthly opex shows measurable vol dampening (model-priced), so expiry-related dealer hedging leaves a footprint somewhere.
Only 2 Deribit book snapshots (2026-10-14/15) carry open interest. Historical GEX cannot be built from the archive.
No hour-of-day or weekday gives BTC direction across 549 trials.
Coinbase and Deribit candles are stamped by bar open. The 08:00 boundary must use bars ending at 08:00, not starting at it.

rows.missing_data: Strike-level option open-interest history, needed for the gamma conditioning that is the paper's actual claim. Not archived. Tardis.dev Deribit history is paid (free monthly samples only). Deribit's public history API has trades but not open interest. Forward capture of Deribit book summaries (bid/ask/OI per strike) each Thursday 20:00 UTC would give sign(GEX) going forward, at about 52 Fridays a year.

registration.claim: On Coinbase BTC-USD from 2019-05 to 2026-10, the slope of the 08:00-16:00 UTC return on the 00:00-08:00 UTC return is more negative on Deribit monthly and quarterly expiry Fridays (last Friday of the month) than on Monday-Thursday at the same clock. Fading the pre-expiry move from 08:05 to 16:00 UTC on those Fridays earns a positive net mean per trade at a 10 bp round trip.
registration.statistic: Slope difference (monthly/quarterly expiry Fridays minus Mon-Thu controls). Net mean per fade trade. Reported: weekly-expiry Fridays minus controls, and quarterly minus non-quarterly monthly.
registration.procedure: Returns from Coinbase hourly closes keyed by bar end (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC); 1-minute bars from 2022 for the 08:05 entry. Expiry calendar from the Deribit rule (last Friday monthly; Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec quarterly), cross-checked against delivery dates in deribit-delivery-prices-btc. Every Friday is a weekly expiry and Deribit lists dailies, so the controls are Mon-Thu, not 'non-expiry' days. OLS by group, with the slope difference bootstrapped in 4-week circular blocks (5,000 draws). Trade: at 08:05 UTC take the side opposite the sign of the 00:00-08:00 return, exit at the 16:00 bar close. Costs: 10 bp round trip (Kalshi BTC perp / CDE nano maker), with Coinbase taker 1.2% round trip as stress. Halves split at 2023-01-01. Stage 2, forward and not part of this verdict: condition on sign(GEX) from captured Thursday books.
registration.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, deribit-delivery-prices-btc, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL
registration.pass: Slope difference < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, negative in both halves, and the net mean per trade on monthly/quarterly Fridays with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0.
registration.controls: Mon-Thu same-clock controls and the weekly-Friday group. FOMC/CPI-coincident Fridays dropped as a robustness check. The 08:00 Deribit index print vs the Coinbase price reported. One window, no grid over hours. T-223 as the prior trial (counted in deflation).

rows.notes: The candidate's real claim is gamma-conditioned and cannot be tested historically: open-interest history is missing, which is what blocked T-513/T-217. The unconditional stage 1 is cheap on archived hourly data from 2019 and is registered here as the claim. If the unconditional slope difference is absent, the GEX version has little chance and the forward capture can be deprioritised. T-223 already found no larger move into the fixing, which argues against the 'push then reverse' mechanism. Only about 90 monthly expiries exist, so power is limited. testable_now = true refers to stage 1 only. Signal-map addition: 'dealer gamma / expiry fixing (crypto)'.

rows.name: Stablecoin issuance after BTC drawdowns, and exchange net flows (conditional, not unconditional)

overlaps.note: Unconditional 30-day aggregate stablecoin supply growth vs the next-30-day BTC return: pooled NW t +0.33, 0 of 7 weekday grids at t >= 2, 2022-2026 half negative, OOS R2 mostly <= 0.
Weeks with > 1 sigma supply growth vs the next-week BTC return. Blocked, though the same Coin Metrics series now exist.
SOPR and exchange netflows, blocked on paid Glassnode/CryptoQuant data.
Stablecoin peg reversion: 11 episodes, not supported.
After bottom-decile BTC days the next-day excess is +8.9 bp gross, -51 bp net of 0.6%. The drawdown condition alone gives no tradable reversal.
Trailing-percentile reversal: +11.3 bp, CI -23.6 to +47.2.

learnings.finding: Stablecoin supply growth carries no unconditional information about BTC returns over 2018-2026, and the post-2022 half has the wrong sign.
The reversal after BTC drawdowns is about 9-11 bp gross, so the issuance condition must add more than the 50 bp round trip on its own.
Supply series are current vintage, not point-in-time. Supply is rarely restated, but the 2-day lag and a first-seen forward capture are still required.
Griffin-Shams' 2017-2018 sample predates the regulated stablecoin era, so decay is the default expectation.

rows.missing_data: The issuance arm is testable now. The netflow arm needs Coin Metrics FlowInExUSD/FlowOutExUSD for BTC: the free community tier may carry them as revised 'flash' values, verify. UST supply (DefiLlama, free) would cover the survivorship gap noted in T-402.

registration.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, BTC's return from the next 00:00 UTC open over +1 to +3 days after a combined USDT+USDC daily supply increase above 2 sigma (trailing 180 days, value lagged 2 days) that comes within 2 days after a bottom-decile BTC 3-day return (trailing 365 days) exceeds the return after bottom-decile drawdowns with no issuance spike by more than the 50 bp Coinbase round trip, with a lower bound > 0 in both halves.
registration.statistic: Event minus control mean BTC log return at +1 and +3 days (+3 primary), clustered by week.
registration.procedure: Daily supply change from Coin Metrics SplyCur (USDT + USDC; DAI, BUSD and TUSD in a reported aggregate). The day-d value counts as known at d+2 00:00 UTC (lag for revisions). Drawdown days use Coinbase daily closes; deciles use only the trailing 365 days. Events are de-overlapped with a 5-day refractory period. Entry at the first 00:00 UTC open after both conditions are known. Week-clustered bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Halves 2019-2021 / 2022-2026. Netflow arm (when data exists): z-score of (in - out) USD vs the next-day return, HAC t, pre-registered negative sign.
registration.data: coinmetrics-usdt-daily, coinmetrics-usdc-daily, coinmetrics-dai-daily, coinmetrics-busd-daily, coinmetrics-tusd-daily, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD
registration.pass: At least 30 non-overlapping events, event - control > 0.50% at +3 days with a week-clustered one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, and positive in both halves.
registration.controls: Drawdown-only control events (the T-320 base rate), unconditional issuance-spike events (the T-402/T-464 base rate), a 2-day lag, a 50 bp round trip, fixed thresholds with no grid, and T-402 and T-464 counted as prior trials.

rows.notes: A narrow conditional salvage of a failed family (T-402). Both component signals are individually dead: unconditional issuance and drawdown reversal. The event count is likely near the 30 minimum and clustered in 2020-2022. Testable now on archived Coin Metrics supply (issuance arm only). Cheap to compute with the T-402 harness, but expect a decisive or inconclusive negative.

rows.name: BTC 25-delta risk reversal (skew) predicts returns

overlaps.note: Built the daily 30-DTE RR25 series from the 07:00-09:00 UTC Deribit trade sample (1,748 smile days, 2022-2026) that this test needs. It tested RR P&L, not return predictability. Note 257 of 262 |RR| > 5 days were put-rich.
Top-quintile CBOE SKEW does not raise the probability of an SPY 21-day drop (it lowered it).
Top-quintile SKEW months do not improve a bullish SPY risk reversal.
High SKEW does not raise the frequency of 2-sigma S&P drops.
SKEW-implied tail probability far exceeds the realised one: skew prices insurance, which is a premium, not a forecast.
The options-implied swing features include the market-wide SKEW but no BTC skew. A BTC RR25 feature would be new, and its trials must be counted.

learnings.finding: Every Mandel test of SPX skew as a return or crash predictor failed.

Option skew overprices the tail (risk-neutral 8.5% vs realised 1.05%). Skew level reflects an insurance premium, consistent with mean-reverting crash-insurance pricing but not with a directional forecast.
A Deribit-implied lognormal does not lead Polymarket or Kalshi BTC digitals. The option market's distribution is already in the crypto prices at 1h-24h.
A point-in-time daily smile (known by 09:00 UTC) exists for 2022-01..2026-10, so the test is runnable now.

rows.missing_data: None for 2022-2026. Earlier years need more Deribit trade pulls (the history API is free), so the sample is about 4.8 years and power is limited at the 30-day horizon.

registration.claim: From 2022-01 to 2026-10 (fit 2022-2024, out-of-sample 2025-01..2026-10), the z-score of BTC's 30-day 25-delta risk reversal against its trailing 90 days, known at 09:00 UTC, predicts the Coinbase BTC log return from 09:00 UTC over +7 and +30 days with a positive sign. The controls are trailing 7- and 30-day returns, DVOL and 7-day mean funding. Out-of-sample R2 is above 0 vs the expanding mean, and a long-when-z > +1 rule beats buy-and-hold net of 10 bp IBIT per switch.
registration.statistic: Newey-West (7-day horizon) and Hansen-Hodrick (30-day) t on RR25 z with controls. Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 vs the expanding historical mean. Rule net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold.
registration.procedure: RR25 from the T-257 smile fits (quadratic in ln(K/S)/sqrt(T) per expiry, interpolated to 30 DTE), available at 09:00 UTC each day. Days without a fit are skipped, never filled forward beyond 1 day. Targets keyed by Coinbase hourly bar close at 09:00 UTC. Sampled weekly (all 7 weekday phases reported, pooled per house rule 10). DVOL taken from the previous day's candle (stamped by open, so available a day after its stamp). Funding = mean interest_8h over the trailing 7 days. Fit on 2022-01..2024-12 and freeze the sign; test on 2025-01..2026-10. Deflate over 2 horizons x 2 statistics.
registration.data: deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC, deribit-dvol-BTC-history, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT
registration.pass: OOS R2 > 0 on the pre-registered sign, controlled t >= 2 at either horizon after deflation, and the rule's net Sharpe above buy-and-hold.
registration.controls: Trailing-return controls (skew mostly follows recent returns), DVOL and funding. The butterfly reported as a placebo regressor. 10 bp IBIT or 50 bp Coinbase per switch. One z threshold. T-257 trial count and the SPX skew failures in the deflation.

rows.notes: Runnable now on the T-257 smile series. Mandel's SPX skew predictors all failed, the source is a thesis abstract with the effect weakening after 2024, and the practitioner backtest is p 0.18. The confound that skew follows past returns is handled by controls. Medium priority only because the data is ready and the harness is small. Signal-map addition: 'option skew (risk reversal) as a predictor vs as a premium'.

rows.name: BTC variance risk premium and vol-of-vol as return predictors

overlaps.note: The BTC DVOL VRP exists: +0.094 variance 2021-2026, halves +0.154 / +0.034 (the second half much smaller).
Implied 62.9 vs realised 54.9 vol points, positive on 71% of days.
Delta-hedged short BTC straddle (model-priced) positive: the premium is harvestable as volatility.
No significant ETH VRP.
Low-DVOL straddles: only 18 non-overlapping entries, which shows how little independent BTC vol history exists.
Scaling SPX short variance by the implied-minus-forecast z did not raise the Sharpe. VRP timing failed on equities.

The options-implied swing family already feeds own_iv_rv (DVOL over 20-day realised) and BTC funding into 1/5/20-day crypto models. Same variable, ML design. Its cells must be counted in this test's deflation, and its F3 IC rows should be read first.

learnings.finding: The BTC VRP is real (about +5 vol points at Hurst's gate, t 2.8) but shrank in the second half. The structural premium is harvestable as short vol, not obviously as a spot-return forecast.
Conditioning on the size of the equity variance premium did not improve even the variance trade itself.

learnings.source: T-578 swing ML (306 cells, 0 pass) / T-580 pending
learnings.finding: Daily-horizon models have no passing cell yet. The F3 options-implied family, which contains this variable, is still running.

learnings.source: Mandel-wide lesson (PnL from hundreds of bets cannot settle an edge)
learnings.finding: DVOL starts 2021-03, giving about 290 weekly or 66 monthly non-overlapping observations, too few to estimate a 30-day predictive slope with power.

rows.missing_data: None. DVOL history starts 2021-03-24, which caps the sample. The BTCDVOL futures basis (deribit-dvol-futures-trades, 38 expiries) is too sparse for a predictor arm.

registration.claim: From 2021-03 to 2026-10 (fit through 2023-12, test 2024-01..2026-10), the BTC variance risk premium at 00:00 UTC, VRP = (DVOL/100)^2 minus trailing 30-day realised variance (365-day annualisation), predicts the Coinbase BTC log return over the next 7 and 30 days with a positive slope and positive out-of-sample R2. A long-when-VRP-in-its-trailing-365-day-top-tercile rule beats buy-and-hold net of 10 bp IBIT per switch.
registration.statistic: Predictive slope with Newey-West (7-day) and Hansen-Hodrick (30-day) t. Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 vs the expanding mean. Rule net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold. Second signal: vol-of-vol = 30-day realised vol of daily log DVOL changes.
registration.procedure: DVOL from the daily candle stamped day t-1 (open-time stamp; it closes at 23:59 and is available at day t 00:00 UTC). Realised variance from Coinbase daily closes through day t-1. Target from the day-t 00:00 UTC open. Weekly sampling with all 7 weekday phases reported and pooled (house rule 10). The 30-day horizon is overlapping in weekly samples, so Hansen-Hodrick lag 4. Fit 2021-03..2023-12, frozen sign, test 2024-01..2026-10. Deflate over 2 signals x 2 horizons plus T-580's BTC F3 cells. Stationary bootstrap (mean block 8 weeks) for the rule's Sharpe difference.
registration.data: deribit-dvol-BTC-history, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: OOS R2 > 0 on the pre-registered positive sign, t >= 2 after deflation at either horizon, both halves of the test window positive, and the rule's net Sharpe above buy-and-hold.
registration.controls: Trailing 30-day return and DVOL level as controls (VRP is mechanically low after crashes). Weekday phases. One tercile cut. 10 bp per switch. ETH replication reported (T-67 says the ETH VRP itself is weak). T-580 trials in the deflation.

rows.notes: Uses a premium Mandel has confirmed (T-246) as a non-price input for the BTC target. Low power: the test window holds about 140 weekly and about 33 monthly independent observations. Check T-580's F3 IC rows for own_iv_rv on BTC/ETH first. If the ML program already shows IC around 0 at 5/20 days, this is a near-duplicate and the prior falls further. Signal-map addition: 'variance risk premium as a return predictor (vs as a harvestable premium)'.

rows.name: Coinbase premium (US vs offshore BTC price gap) as a US-demand signal

overlaps.note: Coinbase-vs-Kraken gap (two USD venues, no USDT basis) above the 0.70% maker cost. A different variable, but the same aligner and 60-second staleness null apply.
Inventory-neutral Coinbase-Kraken arbitrage at 1-minute resolution.
The IBIT premium to synthetic NAV is gone within a session, and fading it nets -0.67%.
Hourly lead-lag inside crypto (BTC leading alts) fails after 50 bp costs.
Cross-venue convergence on Polymarket-Kalshi pairs.

learnings.finding: Cross-venue gaps above a few points are suspect matches, not edges. A reference leads only when it is a deep market pricing the identical event against a thin crowd. Binance is the deeper BTC venue, so the 'US demand' reading is a segmentation story, not a reference-price lead.
Followers close about 93% of cross-venue gaps within 20 s in play. Venue gaps are arbitraged fast, which leaves only slow segmentation as a possible signal.
Cross-asset features added no out-of-sample IC to crypto 5-minute models.

Borri et al. read cross-exchange discounts as risk compensation with a 1.1-week half-life. That is consistent with a slow-moving demand variable rather than free money, so a daily horizon is the right test.

rows.missing_data: Full Binance spot BTCUSDT 1-minute klines for 2022-2026. The archived binance-1m bundle covers only the windows around Polymarket 'Bitcoin above' resolutions. Free on data.binance.vision, read as a public signal only. USDT/USD at minute resolution (Kraken USDTUSD trades, free), since the archived Coinbase USDT-USD series is daily only.

registration.claim: From 2022-01 to 2026-10, the trailing-24h mean Coinbase BTC premium over Binance BTCUSDT converted at USDT/USD, z-scored against its trailing 90 days at 00:00 UTC, predicts the next-24h Coinbase BTC return with the same positive sign before and after the ETF launch (split 2024-01-11), with HAC t >= 2 after the ETF launch. A long-when-z > 1 rule beats buy-and-hold on the same days net of 50 bp round trip on Coinbase and 5 bp on IBIT.
registration.statistic: HAC slope (Newey-West lag 5) and the top-minus-bottom tercile contrast of the next-24h return. Rule net excess vs buy-and-hold. Bonferroni over 2 targets (Coinbase 24h; IBIT next open-to-close).
registration.procedure: Premium_m = Coinbase close / (Binance close x USDTUSD) - 1 at synchronous minute closes. Bars keyed by close, and a minute missing on either venue is dropped, not filled. Averaged over the 24h ending at 00:00 UTC, then z-scored against the trailing 90 days. The USDT basis is removed by the conversion. As a control, the Coinbase-Kraken USD gap (no USDT) is run as the same regression to separate venue demand from stablecoin basis. A 60-second staleness null as in T-331. Targets keyed by Coinbase hourly bar close. Pre-ETF and post-ETF halves.
registration.data: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-daily-USDT-USD, kraken-trades-1m-XBTUSD, daily-history-IBIT, new binance-1m-BTCUSDT-full, new kraken-1m-USDTUSD
registration.pass: Positive slope in both halves, HAC t >= 2 post-ETF after Bonferroni, and the rule's net return above buy-and-hold on the same days for at least one target.
registration.controls: USDT-basis removal and the Coinbase-Kraken USD-only placebo, the staleness null, trailing-24h return control (momentum confound), one z cut, 50 bp / 5 bp costs, and FTX (2022-11) and 2023-03 (USDC depeg) windows reported separately.

rows.notes: Widely quoted, untested, and the free Binance data makes it cheap to unblock. The child learnings on cross-venue gaps argue it is arbitrage noise plus stablecoin basis. A daily-horizon demand reading with a USD-only placebo can separate the two. It shares the minute-alignment machinery with T-331/T-425, so build them together. A Binance read is signal-only and fits the house rule on public data.

rows.name: CME bitcoin weekend gap 'fill' vs a random-walk first-passage null

overlaps.note: Fading SPY overnight gaps loses -6.25 bps net. Gap-fill folklore failed on equities.
BTC weekend variance is 0.47x weekday. A null sigma from all-day realised vol misstates the weekday fill window, so sigma must come from weekdays.
BTC short-term reversal is real but below cost (+8.9 bp gross), the base rate for any fill-toward-level trade.
BTC Monday return is +36.5 bp above other days. The post-gap window has its own drift, which the null must allow.
Weekend vs weekday return levels do not differ.

learnings.source: mandel/ml_data/bars/60m/BTC_F.csv.gz (local CME BTC hourly bars, read for this check)
learnings.finding: CME BTC futures bars appear on Saturdays from 2026-05-30 and Sunday bars jump from about 8 to 36-75 a month after 2026-05. CME weekend trading began around 2026-05-29, so the weekend-gap sample ends with the 2026-05-22 weekend.
Weekend realised variance is about half of weekday, so a first-passage null with a blended sigma understates weekday fills and would manufacture 'excess fills'.

learnings.source: Mandel-wide lesson (price-only strategies start from a negative base rate)
learnings.finding: A gap-fill rule is price-only, and its mechanism claim (CME-spot arbitrage) concerns the futures basis, not a spot level.
Next-day reversal after large BTC moves is about 9-11 bp gross against costs of 50 bp or more.

rows.missing_data: None for spot-defined gaps. CME's own Sunday-reopen futures price before 2024 needs intraday futures bars, which are not archived, so gaps are defined on Coinbase spot at the CME close and reopen times, as the candidate proposes. Confirm the exact 24/7 switch date from a CME notice. The local bars put it at about 2026-05-29.

registration.claim: From 2019-05 to 2026-05-22 (before CME BTC futures traded through weekends), for weekends where Coinbase BTC at the Sunday 17:00 CT CME reopen differs from its level at the Friday 16:00 CT CME close by more than 1%, the share of gaps whose Friday level is revisited within 5 days exceeds a driftless first-passage null 2*Phi(-|gap|/(sigma*sqrt(T))), where sigma is the trailing 30-weekday realised vol. It also exceeds the same statistic for Tuesday-to-Thursday pseudo-gaps. A fill-targeting MBT trade earns a positive net mean.
registration.statistic: Observed fill rate minus mean null probability (and minus the placebo excess). Net mean per trade of the fill-targeting arm.
registration.null: Fill-rate excess <= 0 relative to both the null and the placebo
registration.procedure: Friday mark = Coinbase price at the CME close (21:00 UTC CDT / 22:00 UTC CST). Reopen mark = price at the Sunday reopen (22:00 / 23:00 UTC). Hourly bars before 2022, 1-minute from 2022, all keyed by bar end. Fill = any later high/low through the Friday level within 120 hours. Sigma from weekday-only daily log returns over the trailing 30 weekdays (T-515), with T = fill-window days. Placebo pseudo-gaps: Tuesday 21:00 to Thursday 22:00 UTC (49 hours, matching the weekend span), same fill window. Month-clustered bootstrap and Wilson intervals. Trade: enter at reopen + 5 minutes (next hourly open before 2022) toward the Friday level on CME MBT, target the Friday level, stop at 2 x |gap| beyond entry, time exit at 5 days. Costs: exchange plus broker fees of about 5 bp round trip plus 1 tick, with stop-first ordering within a bar.
registration.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-F, local 60m BTC_F bars (switch-date check)
registration.pass: Fill-rate excess > 0 with the month-clustered 95% CI excluding 0 against both the first-passage null and the placebo excess, and the trade arm's net mean with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0.
registration.controls: First-passage null with weekday sigma. A null variant that allows drift via the trailing 30-day mean, reported. Wednesday/Tuesday placebo. Gap-size buckets reported (1-2%, 2-4%, > 4%) but judged pooled. Stop-first fills. One gap threshold. Sample cut at the CME 24/7 switch.

rows.notes: Folklore with no study. The registration's main value is closing it with the proper null. The archive shows CME BTC futures trading through weekends from about 2026-05-29, so the phenomenon has ended and the sample is about 360 weekends, of which perhaps 150-200 have gaps above 1%. Any 'edge' would only be historical, so the trade arm cannot become a live strategy on CME. Run it only if a cheap harness is free. A decisive negative is the expected and useful outcome.
