rows.name: Open-interest flush / liquidation-cascade reversal

overlaps.note: BTC bottom-decile next-day excess is +8.9 bp gross, -51 bp net. The unconditioned version is below cost.
Trailing 10th-percentile reversal: +11.3 bp, CI -23.6 to +47.2.
Perp funding extremes (a leverage-crowding proxy) do not predict 7-day returns.
Top-decile CME basis (leverage) does not predict drawdowns.
The memecoin bounce-short trades the opposite side of short-term bounces inside declines, on DOGE/SHIB.

learnings.finding: Plain BTC reversal after large down days is about 9-11 bp gross. The OI-flush condition must add about 40 bp or more on its own to clear a 50 bp round trip.
Taker order flow over 5 and 30 minutes predicts nothing worth trading on Kalshi perps (|t| <= 2.5). The taker long/short ratio named as an adjacent variable has no measured footprint on US venues.

learnings.source: BIS WP 1087 (as summarised in the candidate) / Mandel-wide lesson (structural premia)
learnings.finding: Liquidity providers absorbing forced selling is a structural premium mechanism, the class Mandel finds survives. That makes the condition plausible in principle.

learnings.source: Mandel-wide lesson (PnL from hundreds of bets cannot settle an edge)
learnings.finding: A bottom-5% OI and -2 sigma joint condition gives perhaps 30-60 events over 6 years, too few to bound a sub-1% effect tightly.

rows.missing_data: Perp open-interest history. Binance USD-M daily 'metrics' files (5-minute sum_open_interest, taker long/short ratio) are free on data.binance.vision, read as a signal only; verify the first available date (the candidate says 2020-09). Deribit open-interest history is not archived and the public API has no history. CME weekly OI from COT (archived) is too coarse for a daily flush.

registration.claim: From 2020-09 to 2026-10, on UTC days when the 24h change in Binance USD-M BTCUSDT (ETHUSDT) open interest is in the bottom 5% of its trailing 365 days and the 24h Coinbase return is below -2 trailing sigma, the Coinbase return from the next 00:00 UTC open over 1 and 3 days exceeds that after equal price drops without an OI flush (OI change above its trailing median). The difference exceeds the 50 bp round trip, with a lower bound > 0 in both halves.
registration.statistic: Event minus control mean return at +1 and +3 days (+3 primary), week-clustered.
registration.procedure: OI from the 5-minute sum_open_interest. The 24h change is measured at 00:00 UTC, known once the last 5-minute file row of the day is published (enter at the next 00:00 UTC open only if the file is available by then, else the following day). Return sigma from the trailing 60 days of Coinbase daily returns. Events are de-overlapped with a 3-day refractory period. Fit-free. Week-clustered bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Halves 2020-09..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-10. Costs: 50 bp Coinbase round trip; CDE nano / Kalshi perp at 10-18 bp as an alternative, reported.
registration.data: coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, coinbase-daily-ETH-USD, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-hourly-ETH-USD, new binance-um-metrics-BTCUSDT, new binance-um-metrics-ETHUSDT
registration.pass: At least 30 non-overlapping events, event - control > 0.50% at +3 days with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, and positive in both halves.
registration.controls: Price-drop-only controls (the T-320 base rate), funding level at the event as a reported covariate (T-423), BTC and ETH judged separately and pooled. Taker-ratio arm reported only. One OI cut (5%), one return cut (-2 sigma), no grid.

rows.notes: The OI condition is the only new information over the failed plain reversal (T-320/T-469). It needs a free Binance fetch (signal only, which fits the house rule). Event counts will be small and concentrated in 2021-2022 and October 2025, so even a true effect may come out inconclusive. Worth registering as blocked-on-fetch. Prioritise below the archived-data candidates. Signal-map addition: 'open interest / forced deleveraging' as a concept.

rows.name: Perp-spot premium convergence (random-maturity arbitrage bound), positive leg only
rows.source_notes: Opened arXiv 2212.06888v7 (He, Manela, Ross, von Wachter; v1 2022-12-13, v7 2026-09-17). Confirmed: Binance hourly perp and spot, BTC 2020-01-08..2024-03-11 (36,578 obs), coins BTC/ETH/BNB/DOGE/ADA; BTC random-maturity Sharpe 11.65 at zero cost (Table 5), 3.35 at high retail cost, 3.27 with effective spreads; 52.55%/yr; mean rho 0.69 before 2022 vs 0.17 after (Table 4B, decimals); 'deviations decline on average about 22 percentage points a year'; BTC return split 37.61% price convergence vs 14.94% funding (Table 7). Borri-Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu PDF text extracted and confirmed: carry Sharpe 6.45 over 2020-2025, 4.06 from 2024, negative in 2025, with profit mostly from funding (about 8%/yr mean). The Coincub piece and BIS WP 1087 were not opened. The web-search budget was exhausted, so no further decay search was possible; WebFetch only.
rows.replication_concerns: Decay is documented by the authors and by Borri et al. If rho is the annualised premium, as the candidate says, the post-2022 mean of 0.17 is a raw premium of about 1.5 bp per 8-hour interval. That sits inside Deribit's +/-5 bp funding dampener and inside Binance's interest clamp (funding pinned for premiums of -4 to +6 bp), so neither venue's funding reveals it, and the 'rho back to zero' exit cannot be observed on Deribit. The paper's P&L is on Binance; Binance and Deribit are barred to US persons. Hurst measured US-venue funding at about zero, with a 14-day hedged hold at > 8%/yr funding netting -0.15%. Mandel's ML F3 scan has already used BTC funding as a crypto feature (fund_btc 5d/20d discovery IC -0.12/-0.21, t -5.4/-6.8, not confirmed). The 'convergence share' is already inside T-363's marked perp-spot spread.
rows.data_notes: deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL: 65,382 hourly rows from 2019-05 {timestamp, index_price, prev_index_price, interest_1h, interest_8h}. coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD 2019-01-01..2026-10-15 (bar-start stamps). daily-history-IBIT 692 rows (2024-01-11..). fred-DTB3. No perp mark/candle bundle, no Binance premium index, and no Coinbase Derivatives or Kalshi perp funding/mark history (Hurst captures those forward). Signal-map: add 'perp premium / funding' and 'carry decay' as market-variable concepts; the map currently has no market-variable concepts at all.
rows.lookahead_risks: An entry bound fixed on 2020-2023 is not clean: T-363's 2023-2026 result and T-553's BTC hysteresis control (central Sharpe 1.13) have both been seen. interest_1h is a trailing-hour average, known only at its record timestamp. Deribit candles are open-stamped. Inverse-contract P&L must be marked hourly in USD. The premium inside the dampener is unobservable, so any historical Sharpe is a bound, not a measurement.
rows.missing_data: US-venue perp mark/index and funding history (CDE nano perp-style futures from 2025-07, Kalshi perps from 2026) exists only in Hurst's forward captures. Exact Deribit premiums would need BTC-PERPETUAL 1h candles keyed by close, but that is still a non-US venue.

final.claim: On US venues, from the first day of captured mark and funding history, a short Kalshi BTC perp (or CDE nano perp-style future) / long Coinbase spot (or IBIT in US hours) position earns a positive Sharpe of daily excess return over DTB3. It enters when the observed perp premium (mark / spot - 1) exceeds the both-leg round-trip cost, and exits when the premium returns to <= 0 or after 30 days.
final.statistic: Annualised Sharpe of daily excess return over DTB3: funding accrued + premium convergence + spot leg - costs - margin financing at DTB3 + 1.5%. Reported: convergence share, funding share, trade count, in-position days, max drawdown.
final.procedure: Forward only, on Hurst's Kalshi perp and CDE captures. Hourly premium from synchronous perp mark and Coinbase spot (IBIT-implied BTC in US hours). One bound: c = perp taker round trip + spot-leg round trip (about 15 bp with IBIT), with nothing fitted. Funding is accrued as captured. Studentized circular block bootstrap, 30-day blocks, 5,000 draws. No Deribit or Binance P&L enters.
final.data: Hurst forward captures (Kalshi perp books and funding, CDE funding), coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3
final.pass: One-sided 95% lower bound of Sharpe > 0 and DSR > 0.95, counting T-363's 12 trials, T-198, T-258, T-553 and H-ibit-carry. Read jointly with H-ibit-carry, never as a separate live record.
final.controls: Always-in carry and the T-363 rule on the same days. One bound, no grid. Costs on both legs. Venue funding about 0 per Hurst is recorded as the prior.

rows.reason: In substance this duplicates T-363/T-553: outside the dampener, Deribit funding is a deterministic function of the premium, and inside it the premium is unobservable. The back-test venue is barred to US persons, and the US-executable form is already Hurst's H-ibit-carry forward test, so read that on 2027-02-12 instead of adding a trial.

rows.name: Crypto size factor (CSIZE), long-only small-cap tilt on a liquid US-listed universe
rows.source_notes: Extracted Table 2 from the Borri et al. PDF (arXiv 2510.14435 v4). It reports weekly value-weighted quintile excess returns with Newey-West t. CSIZE 5-1 is -0.023 (t -2.66) over the full sample and -0.009 (t -1.69) post-2020 (since 2020-01-01). The smallest quintile earns +0.021 (t 2.53) post-2020 and the largest +0.012 (t 2.11). These are excess returns over the risk-free rate, not over BTC, so post-2020 smallest-minus-largest is only about +0.9%/week. The NBER page confirms Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu, Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency, NBER w25882 (2019), JF 77(2):1133-1177 (2022), with a three-factor model (market, size, momentum). RePEc confirms Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba, IRFA 94 (2024): size and volume anomalies come from micro-caps of little economic importance, and abnormal returns appear mainly in bull markets and fade over time. The non-standard-errors paper was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The post-2020 long-short is significant only at 10%. The paper's sorting universe (CMC coins above about $1m cap) is mostly not on Coinbase, and Fieberg places the premium in micro-caps that a $1m/day Coinbase volume filter removes. On the same Coinbase universe, T-546 measured alts losing to BTC in every year 2020-2026, and Hurst's cross-sectional selection lift is +0.002%/trade, so a Q1-minus-BTC result would mostly be an alt-vs-BTC timing bet. Q1-minus-Q5 and Q1-minus-EW-universe must therefore be reported. Mandel's ML daily crypto scan has no size feature, so the variable is unseen. Its own-return features do show 5-20-day reversal (r20 1d confirmed IC -0.097), a regime small coins may load on.
rows.data_notes: cmc-historical-listings: 463,917 rows of Sunday and Monday snapshots from 2017-12, top 500 by rank, with marketCap and circulatingSupply as of each snapshot. The 2020-11-30 snapshot is corrupt (T-314). cmc-daily-listings holds only about 8 rows a day, too few for a sort. There are 493 coinbase-daily bundles covering 2015-07..2026-10-14; they include non-USD quotes such as CBETH-ETH and 89 delisted USD products. coinbase-products 2026-10-15/16 carries online/delisted status. Signal-map: 'crypto market cap / circulating supply' and 'survivorship inflation (+1.14%/week in T-314)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: The CMC snapshot's time of day is uncertain (T-314 used snapshot date + 1 day), so trade at the close of the Monday Coinbase daily bar (Tuesday 00:00 UTC), not at the Monday open. Coinbase bars are start-stamped. The product list is a 2026 download, so products purged from the API entirely are missing; count known-listed CMC coins with no bundle. The 30-day volume filter must use bars ending before the snapshot. Delisted coins are held to their last price minus 50%.
rows.missing_data: None for the test.

final.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, the value-weighted smallest market-cap quintile of Coinbase USD spot coins earns a mean weekly return above BTC after 50 bp per side on turnover, with both halves positive. Eligible coins exclude stablecoins and wrapped/staked/fx_stablecoin ids (T-424/T-546 lists), have trailing 30-day Coinbase dollar volume >= $1m, and appear in the CMC Sunday top-500 snapshot. The quintile is sorted on the Sunday snapshot and held from Tuesday 00:00 UTC to the next Tuesday 00:00 UTC.
final.statistic: Mean weekly net return of value-weighted Q1 minus BTC over the same Tuesday-to-Tuesday weeks. Reported: equal-weighted Q1, Q1 - Q5, Q1 - equal-weight universe (gross and net), turnover, names per quintile, coins dropped for missing CMC cap.
final.procedure: Universe rebuilt weekly. Market cap = marketCap in the Sunday snapshot; snapshots older than 8 days are never used, and 2020-11-30 is treated as missing. Weeks with fewer than 15 eligible coins are dropped and counted. Cap weights within Q1 are fixed at entry and drift through the week. Entry and exit at the Coinbase close of the Monday daily bar (Tuesday 00:00 UTC). Turnover is charged at 50 bp per side; a coin that stops trading exits at its last Coinbase close minus 50%. 8-week circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. DSR counts T-314's 24 crypto cross-section trials, T-546 and the 2 weighting variants. Halves: 2019-01..2022-11-16 and 2022-11-17..2026-09.
final.data: cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, coinbase-products-2026-10-15, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD
final.pass: Value-weighted Q1 - BTC mean weekly net has a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, both halves are positive, and DSR > 0.95. The equal-weighted variant is reported, not judged.
final.controls: BTC, Q5 and equal-weight-universe benchmarks separate size from the alt-vs-BTC drift (T-546). One sort, one rebalance day, one volume floor, no grid. Survivorship stress (delisted -50%) and a count of uncovered coins. Bull/bear split reported (BTC above/below its 200-day average at entry), per Fieberg.

rows.reason: Novel to Mandel, with the effect sizes confirmed in Borri Table 2 and the data archived. The timing must move to one day after the CMC snapshot, and the Coinbase universe differs from the paper's. Every adjacent learning is hostile, so expect a decisive negative.

rows.name: Crypto 2-week momentum: test the short leg (losers) on Kalshi-perp coins
rows.source_notes: From the Borri et al. Table 2 text: CMOM sorts on the past two-week return. Value-weighted weekly 5-1 is +0.026 (t 3.89) over the full sample and +0.021 (t 3.70) post-2020. Post-2020 the loser quintile earns +0.001 (t 0.08) against +0.016/+0.021 for Q4/Q5, so the spread uses both legs. Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba, IRFA 94 (2024), via RePEc: momentum persists among larger coins, carries substantial trading costs, and most of its alpha comes from short positions; they advise that tradable anomalies should focus on long positions. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu's original CMOM, used by T-314, has a three-week lookback; the two-week lookback here follows Borri.
rows.replication_concerns: T-314 already tested the three-week version on a point-in-time top-30 universe over the same years. Its permutation p of 0.035 comes from that same sample, so it motivates this test but is not evidence for it. Switching from 21 to 14 days after T-314 failed is a forking path that the DSR must count. The long-only exclusion arm captures only a third of the rest-minus-losers spread, since EW(ex-losers) - EW(all) = (R - L)/3, and incremental turnover at 50 bp per side may consume it. Mandel's ML daily crypto IC scan finds own 5- and 20-day returns negatively related to the next 1-5 days (r20 1d confirmed IC -0.097, t -5.8). That is a time-series reversal on a survivor universe, hostile unless cross-sectional demeaning removes it. Hurst's selection lift is +0.002%/trade, and the Kalshi-listed coin set is hindsight-selected (G-bde6c8d0a8).
rows.data_notes: 493 coinbase-daily bundles (2015-07..2026-10-14, including 89 delisted USD products) and 109 coinbase-hourly bundles (for example SOL and DOGE from 2021-06). coinbase-products-2026-10-15 and cmc-historical-listings serve as a stablecoin/peg cross-check. Coinbase listed fewer than 30 USD coins in 2019, so early terciles are thin. Signal-map: 'cross-sectional momentum (crypto), loser leg' and 'short-horizon reversal (ML ic_scan)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: The signal uses closes through the daily bar ending Monday 00:00 UTC (bars are start-stamped). Trailing dollar volume runs through Sunday. The trailing 60-day beta for the Kalshi arm uses pre-entry data only. Product-list survivorship as in T-546. The Kalshi listing set is 2026 knowledge.
rows.missing_data: No Kalshi perp price or funding history before 2026 (Hurst records it forward), so the Kalshi short arm can be priced only from Coinbase spot with assumed costs.

final.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, an equal-weighted book of the point-in-time top-30 Coinbase USD coins by trailing 30-day dollar volume (T-424 construction), excluding the bottom tercile by 14-day return to Monday 00:00 UTC and held Monday to Monday, beats the equal-weighted top-30 basket after 50 bp per side on each book's own turnover. Both halves must be positive.
final.statistic: Mean weekly net return of EW(top-N ex losers) minus EW(top-N), each net of its own turnover cost. Reported: gross EW(rest) - EW(losers); T-314's 21-day lookback as a robustness row, not judged; on the Kalshi-listed subset, BTC minus losers (beta-neutral by trailing 60-day beta) net of an 18 bp round trip with funding 0 +/- 10%/yr.
final.procedure: Universe rebuilt each Monday 00:00 UTC, with stablecoin, wrapped/staked and fx_stablecoin exclusions and CMC flags as a cross-check. Weeks with fewer than 15 eligible coins are dropped and counted. Signal = Coinbase close-to-close 14-day return through the daily bar ending Monday 00:00 UTC; bottom tercile = the floor(n/3) lowest. Entry at the Monday daily open, exit at the next Monday open, weights reset weekly. Delisted names are held to their last price minus 50%. 8-week circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Random-tercile placebo: 1,000 within-week permutations of the tercile labels. DSR counts T-314's 24 trials, T-546 and the 3 arms here. Halves split at 2022-11-17.
final.data: coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, coinbase-products-2026-10-15, cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, coinbase-hourly-<SYM>-USD (Kalshi-arm betas)
final.pass: Primary mean weekly net has a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, both halves are positive, it exceeds the placebo's 95th percentile, and DSR > 0.95. The Kalshi arm is reported only (hindsight universe). A primary pass licenses only a forward paper record of the short leg on Kalshi perps.
final.controls: The equal-weight basket benchmark and the placebo separate the loser effect from the alt-vs-BTC drift. One lookback, one hold, no grid. Turnover is charged on both books. Survivorship haircut. Per-year results and the BTC-trend regime are reported.

rows.reason: Not a duplicate: T-314 tested the winner leg on a three-week lookback, while this tests the loser leg, which Fieberg et al. identify as the source of momentum alpha, in a form executable long-only on Coinbase. The T-314 hint is in-sample and the 14-day lookback is a fork, so the DSR must count both.

rows.name: Crypto network value (price-to-active-addresses, CVALUE)
rows.source_notes: Borri et al. Table 2 confirmed: CVALUE sorts weekly on the price-to-new-address ratio, value-weighted. 5-1 is -0.035 (t -3.50) over the full sample and -0.023 (t -2.32) post-2020, and the cheap (high-value) quintile earns +0.030/week post-2020 (t 2.35). The candidate's cited RFS paper is mis-attributed: Liu and Tsyvinski (2021), Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency (confirmed on RePEc), is about exposure to network factors, time-series momentum and attention, not the CVALUE sort. Borri's CVALUE cites a different Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (2021) paper, which was not opened. The Coin Metrics community catalog confirms 138 assets with daily AdrActCnt (ada from 2017-09, doge 2013-12, link 2017-09; sol absent). New-address counts are not in the free tier.
rows.replication_concerns: The only post-2020 evidence comes from the original author group, so it is not independent. The free proxy (active addresses) is a different variable from new addresses, and for ERC-20 tokens AdrActCnt counts token-transfer addresses, which are not comparable with L1 chains. T-400's MVRV regime test went the wrong way. A low price-to-activity ratio may proxy small size, so a size-matched benchmark is needed. Coin Metrics data are current vintage, so a backfill is revised data under Mandel's point-in-time rule.
rows.data_notes: cmc-historical-listings and the coinbase-daily bundles exist. coinmetrics-btc-daily and -eth-daily carry only PriceUSD, CapMVRVCur, HashRate, CapMrktCurUSD and SplyCur, not AdrActCnt, and there is no altcoin Coin Metrics bundle. Signal-map: 'on-chain adoption (active addresses, MVRV), current vintage'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Current-vintage on-chain metrics (methodology restatements, flash values): lag them 2 days and capture first-seen values forward. CMC snapshot timing: trade one day after the snapshot. Token vs native address definitions. Survivorship of Coinbase products.
rows.missing_data: Daily AdrActCnt for the eligible altcoins: free from community-api.coinmetrics.io (CC BY-NC 4.0, current vintage), backfilled once and then captured daily as first-seen values.

final.claim: On Coinbase USD coins with Coin Metrics AdrActCnt and trailing 30-day Coinbase dollar volume >= $1m, the value-weighted quintile with the lowest ratio of CMC market cap to trailing 28-day mean AdrActCnt (lagged 2 days) earns a higher mean weekly return than BTC after 50 bp per side. Coins are sorted weekly on the Sunday snapshot and held from Tuesday 00:00 to Tuesday 00:00 UTC. The result must hold in the revised-data backfill 2019-01..2026-09, with both halves positive, and in a first-seen forward record of at least 52 weeks.
final.statistic: Mean weekly net return, cheap quintile minus BTC. Reported: cheap minus rich quintile, cheap minus a size-matched portfolio, and the native-L1 vs token split.
final.procedure: Ratio = CMC marketCap (Sunday snapshot) / mean AdrActCnt over the 28 days ending 2 days before the snapshot. Weekly sort; value-weighted cheap quintile. Entry and exit at the Coinbase close of the Monday bar (Tuesday 00:00 UTC). Delisted names are held to their last price minus 50%. The backfill is labelled 'revised-data result'; a daily first-seen capture from registration is the confirmatory record. Weekly date-clustered and 8-week block bootstraps, 5,000 draws. DSR over this ratio plus MVRV (reported) and T-400.
final.data: cmc-historical-listings, coinbase-daily-<SYM>-USD, coinbase-products-2026-10-15, new coinmetrics-adractcnt-<asset>-daily (backfill plus first-seen daily capture)
final.pass: Backfill: one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, both halves (split 2022-11-17) positive, DSR > 0.95. Forward first-seen record (>= 52 weeks): mean > 0. Supported only if both hold.
final.controls: Size-matched benchmark, equal-weight universe and BTC. At least 20 eligible coins a week, or the week is dropped. One ratio window (28 days), no grid. MVRV is a reported alternative only. 50 bp per side. Revision disclosure.

rows.reason: Untested, and the effect is confirmed in Borri Table 2, but the replication is not independent, the free proxy differs from the paper's variable, and the data are revised. Register it as blocked on the fetch, start the first-seen capture now, and spend no harness on the backfill ahead of the archived-data candidates.

rows.name: Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum (first half-hour predicts last half-hour)
rows.source_notes: The Birmingham research portal confirms Shen, Urquhart and Wang, Bitcoin intraday time series momentum, Financial Review 57(2):319-344 (May 2022; online 2021-10-26), doi 10.1111/fire.12290. The first half-hour return positively predicts the last half-hour return, with trading time defined by volume because BTC trades 24/7. Predictability is strongest in high-volume or high-volatility sessions, timing gains are largest in downturns, and the authors attribute the effect to liquidity provision. The sample period and coefficients are not on the page.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication. The paper's session is volume-defined: a UTC-day clock is arbitrary for a 24/7 asset, and the NYSE session is only the nearest analogue. Every adjacent result is negative: T-427 (SPY half-hour momentum, slope -0.004, t -0.22), T-577's crypto 5-minute cells (0 of 50 net > 0), and Hurst's hourly rules on 20 Kalshi perps (< 6 bp follow-through against 16-18 bp). A half-hour BTC move needs > 10 bp of predictable drift to clear even the cheapest US cost.
rows.data_notes: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD: 58 monthly bundles 2022-01..2026-10, one row per minute with trades, stamped by bar start (a missing minute had no trade). fomc-meetings and macro-release-cpi exist. There is no 1-minute history before 2022. Signal-map: 'intraday session momentum (24/7 asset)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Bars are start-stamped, so the 14:00:00 price is the close of the bar starting 13:59. Entering at a minute's close is a fill at the last trade: use the next bar's open, or charge the taker cost. Volume terciles come from the trailing 60 sessions only. DST transitions and early-close days must be handled explicitly. Fee tiers quoted from memory must be rechecked.
rows.missing_data: None for the test; the current Coinbase Advanced and CDE nano fee tiers need rechecking.

final.claim: From 2024-01 to 2026-10, with 2022-2023 required to agree in sign, positioning Coinbase BTC-USD over the last 30 minutes of the NYSE session in the direction of the session's first-30-minute return earns a positive mean net return per trade after a 10 bp round trip. The session is DST-aware (13:30-20:00 or 14:30-21:00 UTC), full sessions only. The effect must appear in at least one of two cells: all sessions, or sessions whose first-half-hour volume is in the top tercile of the trailing 60 sessions.
final.statistic: Mean net return per trade per cell. Reported: the HAC slope of the last-half-hour return on the first-half-hour return, and the UTC-day clock (00:00-00:30 predicting 23:30-24:00) as a reported row.
final.procedure: Signal = sign of the session-open-to-+30-minute return from 1-minute bar closes. Entry at the open of the bar starting 30 minutes before session end; exit at the close of the last session bar. Missing minutes are carried forward and counted. Nothing is fitted. Weekly circular block bootstrap, 5,000 draws; random-sign placebo, 1,000 draws. Cost: a 10 bp round trip (Kalshi BTC perp, about 4 bp taker each side plus spread), with a stress run at the Coinbase retail taker. Bonferroni over 2 cells.
final.data: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi
final.pass: In at least one cell: one-sided 95% lower bound of the net mean > 0 after Bonferroni over 2 cells, the 2022-2023 mean of the same sign, and the result above the placebo's 95th percentile.
final.controls: Random-sign placebo. FOMC/CPI days reported separately. T-427, T-577 and Hurst's hourly rules as priors. One rule per cell, no grid. Cost stress at the retail taker.

rows.reason: The peer-reviewed source is verified, the test runs on archived 1-minute bars, and it is not a duplicate (T-427 is SPY). Every adjacent Mandel and child result is negative, so register it at the lowest priority, with two cells instead of four.

rows.name: Spot bitcoin ETF net flows predict next-day BTC returns (timestamp-aligned)
rows.source_notes: SSRN 7545019 and 6592830 returned 403. The secondary ML-Quant summary confirms the paper, Spot Bitcoin ETF Flows and Bitcoin Returns: Timestamp Alignment and Asymmetric Feedback, by Juraj Fabus et al., posted 2026-09-30. It reports same-day flows predicting next-day BTC returns at 1.67 pp per $1bn after timestamp correction, and prior returns predicting flows. The sample, the alignment method and any out-of-sample test are not stated. Lim (6592830) and Mazur-Polyzos were not opened. So the claim is confirmed only at abstract level, through a secondary source.
rows.replication_concerns: 1.67 pp per $1bn is large against BTC's daily sd of about 2.5-3% and typical daily flows of a few hundred million dollars. That suggests the paper's 'next day' window overlaps the after-close hours before flows are public. The paper is three weeks old and unreplicated, and 2024-2026 working papers disagree. T-328 (IBIT premium half-life 0.68 sessions), Hurst ('nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close') and T-404 (GLD flows, parked) are hostile. Creations for day t partly reflect AP orders that settle T+1, so dating is ambiguous.
rows.data_notes: Archived: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT (692 rows, 2024-01-11..), daily-history-BTC-F, fred-DTB3, ishares-ibit-premium-discount (480 daily rows; NAV derivable as close / (1 + pct/100)) and ishares-ibit-snapshots (a single row with shares outstanding). Not archived: per-fund daily flows (Farside) and IBIT daily shares-outstanding history. Signal-map: 'ETF creations/redemptions (flows)' as an adjacent variable.
rows.lookahead_risks: Farside's evening estimates are revised, and IBIT's figure is often posted the next morning. Issuer shares outstanding lag creation orders by a settlement day. Yahoo IBIT daily bars are tradable open-to-close only from the open. Day-t flow is treated as known at 13:30 UTC t+1, and first-seen values must be recorded forward.
rows.missing_data: Farside per-fund daily flows (free HTML, possibly bot-protected), iShares IBIT daily NAV and shares-outstanding history (fund-page download), and a forward first-seen capture of both.

final.claim: From 2025-07 to 2026-09, with 2024-01-11..2025-06 reported as in-sample replication, US spot BTC ETF net flow for day t, treated as known only at 13:30 UTC on t+1, predicts IBIT's t+1 open-to-close return with a positive slope. This holds after controlling for the BTC return from 20:00 UTC t to 13:30 UTC t+1 and the trailing 5-day BTC return. A rule that holds IBIT open-to-close on t+1 when flow > +$500m beats holding IBIT open-to-close every day at a 5 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Out-of-sample HAC t of the flow slope ($bn) with controls, and the rule's net Sharpe minus the always-long Sharpe on the same days. Reported: the in-sample slope, the reverse regression of flow on lagged returns, IBIT-only vs all-fund flows, and a BTC 13:30 UTC t+1 to 13:30 UTC t+2 target.
final.null: Slope <= 0, or the rule's Sharpe does not exceed always-long
final.procedure: Flow_t = sum of Farside per-fund flows for day t; IBIT dShares x NAV from iShares, dated by its publication morning, as a cross-check. Available at 13:30 UTC t+1, never earlier. Target: IBIT open-to-close on t+1 from Yahoo daily bars. Controls: the BTC return 20:00 UTC t to 13:30 UTC t+1, the trailing 5-day BTC return, and the change in the CME annualised basis. Newey-West lag 5. The $500m threshold is fixed now, not fitted. Paired stationary bootstrap (mean block 10 days, 5,000 draws) for the Sharpe difference. Forward first-seen capture of Farside and iShares values from registration, with revision sizes reported.
final.data: new farside-btc-etf-flows, new ishares-ibit-history (daily NAV and shares outstanding), daily-history-IBIT, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-F, ishares-ibit-premium-discount, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Out-of-sample slope > 0 with HAC t >= 2, and the rule's net Sharpe exceeds always-long with a paired one-sided 95% lower bound > 0.
final.controls: Lagged-return controls for reverse feedback, the basis change, IBIT-only vs all-fund flows, a revision check on the forward capture, a 5 bp round trip, US holidays dropped, FOMC/CPI days reported.

rows.reason: A genuine non-price flow input with a cheap US vehicle. But the source is an unreplicated, three-week-old working paper confirmed only at abstract level through a secondary summary, and the data are not archived. Register it as blocked on the iShares/Farside fetch, with the threshold fixed now instead of fitted.

rows.name: CME bitcoin COT: follow leveraged-funds position changes
rows.source_notes: Crossref record: Baur and Smales, Trading behavior in bitcoin futures: Following the 'smart money', Journal of Futures Markets 42(7):1304-1323, online 2022-04-27. The abstract says leveraged-money traders hold the largest, typically net-short positions; they show market timing mainly by adjusting shorts; other trader groups follow later; and strategies based on changes in leveraged-money positions can be profitable. Magnitudes and sample dates were not visible (the publisher page returned 403).
rows.replication_concerns: No replication. The paper's sample, from the CME launch to about 2021, overlaps this candidate's 2018-2022 window, so only post-publication data (2022-05 on) is out of sample. Since 2024-01, leveraged-fund shorts are largely basis hedges against ETF and cash longs (T-362, T-329), so their changes may track the basis rather than views. T-405 (gold COT) failed. Result 18's lesson applies: informed traders are a pointer, not a signal, and this print is 3 days stale at release.
rows.data_notes: cftc-cot-tff-f-133741 and -fo-133741 hold 444 weekly reports from 2018-04-10 (not 2017-12) to 2026-10-06, with fields lev_money_positions_long/_short, asset_mgr_positions_long/_short and open_interest_all. available_at is Socrata created_at for the 221 live rows (2022-07 on) and the CFTC release schedule for the 223 bulk-loaded rows; no rows are not_realtime. daily-history-BTC-F starts 2017-12. coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD starts only 2019-01, so 2018 entries need coinbase-daily bars. Signal-map: 'COT positioning (TFF leveraged funds / asset managers)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Releases are Friday 15:30 ET for Tuesday positions, but they slip on holidays and in shutdowns (the 2025 backlog), so use the stored available_at, never the report date. The basis compares Yahoo's BTC=F daily close (settlement vs last trade) with a Coinbase hourly bar, keyed to the Tuesday as-of hour. Hourly bars are start-stamped, so enter at the open of the first bar starting at or after available_at.
rows.missing_data: None. The basis control is approximate: Yahoo daily futures close vs Coinbase spot at the matching hour.

final.claim: From 2022-05 to 2026-09 (after the source's publication; 2018-04..2022-04 reported as in-sample replication), the weekly change in CME Bitcoin leveraged-funds net position divided by open interest, known at release, predicts a positive BTC return over the 7 days from the first Coinbase price after release. This holds after controlling for the synchronous CME annualised basis, its weekly change and the prior-week BTC return. The slope must be positive in both 2022-05..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-09, and a long/flat rule (long when the change is > 0) must beat buy-and-hold at 10 bp per switch.
final.statistic: Newey-West (lag 4) t of the slope on dLF/OI with the controls, post-publication window. Reported: per-period slopes, the rule's net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold, the asset-manager net change as a competing regressor, the F&O report as a robustness check, and the z-score of the LF level over the trailing 52 reports as a secondary arm.
final.procedure: LF net = lev_money_positions_long - lev_money_positions_short from the futures-only TFF report, divided by open_interest_all, and differenced against the previous report; available_at from the bundle. Entry at the open of the first Coinbase hourly bar starting at or after available_at (the daily bar before 2019); exit 7 x 24 hours later. Basis = ln(BTC=F close / Coinbase spot at the matching hour) x 365 / days to the front expiry, at the Tuesday as-of date. Block-permutation null for the rule (8-week blocks, 2,000 draws). DSR counts the 2 arms here and T-405.
final.data: cftc-cot-tff-f-133741, cftc-cot-tff-fo-133741, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-F, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Post-publication slope > 0 with HAC t >= 2 after the basis controls, positive in both post-publication sub-periods, and the rule's net Sharpe above buy-and-hold with block-permutation p < 0.05. A 50 bp per-switch Coinbase stress is reported.
final.controls: Basis level and change, prior-week return, asset-manager change. One pre-registered sign and one rule threshold (zero). 10 bp per switch (CME MBT) with Coinbase stress. Regimes reported.

rows.reason: Novel for bitcoin, with the peer-reviewed source verified at abstract level and the test fully runnable on release-time-stamped archived data. The fix moves the verdict to post-publication data and makes the basis control decisive, because 2018-2022 overlaps the paper's own sample.

rows.name: Crypto weekend returns predict Monday US equity returns (negative-side asymmetry)
rows.source_notes: RePEc confirms Mourey, Shahrour and Şoiman, A crypto-stock weekend effect: Predicting Monday stock returns using weekend cryptocurrency returns, Finance Research Letters 86 (PE), 2025, doi 10.1016/j.frl.2025.108661. It uses 20 large coins (about 85% of market cap) in a Bayesian/Kalman framework. Negative weekend returns significantly predict Monday declines in the Nasdaq, Russell 2000, S&P sectors and the S&P Crypto Index; positive ones have no effect; and the link strengthens markedly after the May 2022 LUNA collapse. Sample dates and coefficients are not on the page. 'Monday returns' are almost certainly index close-to-close, which includes the Friday-close-to-Monday-open gap.
rows.replication_concerns: No replication. If the effect lives in the gap, ES/NQ price it from Sunday 18:00 ET, and only the open-to-close remainder is tradable in ETFs. Mandel's ML daily scan finds no next-day IC from BTC's 1-day return to equity ETFs (+0.007, t 0.5), and a confirmed negative IC from BTC's 5-day return (-0.037), the opposite sign. Hurst finds overnight moves of BTC proxies are beta, not a lead. Bottom-tercile weekends are smaller moves than they look (T-515: weekend variance 0.47x weekday). A Kalman/Bayesian design with a post-LUNA break is flexible, a forking-path risk.
rows.data_notes: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD 2019-01-01..2026-10-15 (start-stamped), coinbase-1m 2022-01.., daily-history-SPY/QQQ/IWM/COIN. Local 60m ES_F and NQ_F bars cover only about the last two years. With a 52-weekend burn-in, signals start 2020-01. Signal-map: '24/7 market as leading reference for closed markets'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Hourly bars are start-stamped. The Friday mark is the close of the bar starting 19:00 UTC (EDT) or 20:00 UTC (EST); the Monday mark is the close of the bar starting 12:00 or 13:00 UTC. Yahoo's daily open is the official opening print, executable with a market-on-open order. Holiday Mondays roll to the next session. Terciles and the gap-residual fit use past weekends only.
rows.missing_data: ES/NQ intraday history before about 2024, so an ES Sunday-reopen arm covers only the last two years.

final.claim: From 2020-01 to 2026-09, the open-to-close return of SPY, QQQ or IWM on the first session after a weekend is lower after weekends whose Coinbase BTC log return, from the Friday NYSE close to 30 minutes before the Monday open, falls in the bottom tercile of all prior weekends (expanding, at least 52). For at least one ETF the contrast must survive Bonferroni over the 3 ETFs and be negative in both halves (split 2022-05-09). A rule that stays flat on signal weekends must beat always-long Monday after a 2 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Per ETF: mean Monday open-to-close return after bottom-tercile weekends minus that after other weekends. Rule net mean vs always-long Monday.
final.procedure: BTC Friday mark = close of the Coinbase hourly bar ending at the NYSE close; Monday mark = close of the bar ending 30 minutes before the open. Holiday Mondays roll to the first session after; early-close Fridays use their actual close. Terciles are expanding from 2019-01 with at least 52 prior weekends. Target: the Yahoo daily open-to-close ratio of the first post-weekend session. Monthly block bootstrap, 5,000 draws; Bonferroni over 3 ETFs. Reported: the Friday-close-to-Monday-open gap (not traded); a gap-residualised arm (residual of the BTC weekend return on the SPY gap, fitted on past weekends only); COIN; an ES Sunday-reopen-to-Monday-close arm on local 60m ES_F bars for the last two years.
final.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM, daily-history-COIN, local 60m ES_F bars (reported arm)
final.pass: For at least one ETF: contrast < 0 with Bonferroni-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05, negative in both halves, and the flat-on-signal rule's net mean Monday return above always-long Monday after a 2 bp round trip.
final.controls: Wednesday pseudo-weekend placebo (BTC from the Tuesday NYSE close to 30 minutes before Wednesday's open, predicting Wednesday open-to-close). FOMC/CPI Mondays reported. T-549 overnight drift as context. One tercile cut, no grid. Hurst's H-btc-us500-lead is not counted as confirmation, nor the reverse.

rows.reason: Novel, with a verified peer-reviewed source; it is cheap, executable on Alpaca ETFs, and keeps the target's price isolated from the input. The fix adds the gap-residual and ES arms and flags that the paper's close-to-close effect probably sits in the untradable gap.

rows.name: Deribit expiry return reversal conditioned on dealer gamma (GEX)
rows.source_notes: Crossref confirms Weiss, Gaudiosi, Zhou and Webb, Bitcoin option expiration, gamma exposure, and intraday price reversals, Finance Research Letters vol. 107 (September 2026), doi 10.1016/j.frl.2026.110340. Crossref carries no abstract and ScienceDirect returned 403, so the reversal, the negative-GEX condition and the USD 50m figure are confirmed only as far as the title goes.
rows.replication_concerns: No replication. T-223 found the |00-08 UTC| move no larger on monthly-expiry Fridays (difference -15.5 bp, p 0.82), which argues against a hedging push into the fixing. Hurst found no hour or weekday direction over 549 trials. Deribit lists daily 08:00 expiries, so every day is an expiry day and the contrast is monthly/quarterly vs ordinary days. About 90 monthly expiries 2019-2026 give low power. The paper's own claim is GEX-conditioned and cannot be tested historically.
rows.data_notes: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD 2019-01.. (start-stamped); coinbase-1m 2022-01..; deribit-delivery-prices-btc (2,639 daily deliveries, 30-minute TWAP to 08:00 UTC); deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL index_price from 2019-05. deribit-book-BTC has only the 2026-10-14/15 snapshots, so there is no historical OI or GEX. Signal-map: 'dealer gamma / expiry fixing (crypto)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Take the 08:00 mark from the close of the bar starting 07:00, not the bar starting 08:00. Enter at the open of the bar starting 08:00 (the first trade after the fixing), never at a close. The expiry calendar comes from the rule (last Friday; Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec quarterly), because the daily delivery-price series cannot identify monthly expiries by itself.
rows.missing_data: Strike-level option OI history for the GEX condition (Tardis, paid; or a forward capture of book summaries each Thursday 20:00 UTC). testable_now applies to stage 1 only.

final.claim: On Coinbase BTC-USD hourly bars from 2019-05 to 2026-10, the slope of the 08:00-16:00 UTC return on the 00:00-08:00 UTC return is more negative on Deribit monthly and quarterly expiry Fridays (last Friday of the month) than on Monday-Thursday at the same clock. Fading the 00:00-08:00 move from the 08:00 open to the 16:00 close on those Fridays earns a positive net mean per trade at a 10 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Slope difference (expiry Fridays minus Mon-Thu) and net mean per fade trade. Reported: the weekly-Friday group minus Mon-Thu, and quarterly minus non-quarterly monthly expiries.
final.procedure: Marks from Coinbase hourly bars keyed by bar end: 00:00 = close of the bar starting 23:00; 08:00 = close of the bar starting 07:00; 16:00 = close of the bar starting 15:00. Groups: monthly/quarterly expiry Fridays, other Fridays, and Monday-Thursday controls. OLS of the 08-16 return on the 00-08 return by group; the slope difference is bootstrapped with 4-week circular blocks over the calendar (5,000 draws). Trade: at the open of the bar starting 08:00, take the side opposite the sign of the 00-08 return; exit at the close of the bar starting 15:00. Cost: a 10 bp round trip (CDE nano maker or Kalshi BTC perp), with a Coinbase retail-taker stress. Halves split at 2023-01-01. Stage 2, sign(GEX) from Thursday 20:00 UTC captures, is forward only and not part of this verdict.
final.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, deribit-delivery-prices-btc, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL
final.pass: Slope difference < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, negative in both halves, and the net mean per fade trade on expiry Fridays with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0.
final.controls: Mon-Thu same-clock controls and the other-Friday group. FOMC/CPI-coincident Fridays dropped as a robustness check. The Deribit 08:00 index vs the Coinbase price reported. T-223 counted as a prior trial. One window, no hour grid.

rows.reason: Only the paper's title could be confirmed, and its gamma-conditioned claim cannot be tested without OI history. The cheap unconditional stage 1 on archived hourly bars is still worth registering: if the reversal is absent, the forward GEX capture can be deprioritised.

rows.name: Stablecoin issuance after BTC drawdowns, and exchange net flows (conditional, not unconditional)
rows.source_notes: RePEc confirms Griffin and Shams, Is Bitcoin Really Untethered?, Journal of Finance 75(4):1913-1964 (2020): in the 2017 boom, Tether purchases were timed after market downturns and followed by sizable BTC price increases, with the flow attributed to one entity. The abstract gives no magnitudes. Kristoufek (FRL 2021) returned 503, so that counter-evidence is unverified.
rows.replication_concerns: The source's sample is from the manipulation era and predates the 2019-2026 window. T-402 (unconditional supply growth, NW t +0.33, negative 2022-2026 half) and T-320/T-469 (drawdown reversal +9-11 bp gross) mean the conditional event must add more than 50 bp by itself. Griffin and Shams traced transfers from the Tether treasury to exchanges, not mints, whereas SplyCur jumps when Tether mints into its own treasury (authorised but not issued). A supply spike is therefore a noisy proxy for the purchases they measured. The event count is likely near 30 and clustered in 2020-2022.
rows.data_notes: coinmetrics-usdt-daily (4,393 rows), -usdc (2,996), -dai, -busd and -tusd carry daily SplyCur, current vintage, with available_at = day + 1. coinbase-daily-BTC-USD covers 2015-07..2026-10-14. Before running, verify that Coin Metrics 'usdt' aggregates every chain (Tron, Ethereum, Omni) against DefiLlama circulating totals. Signal-map: 'stablecoin issuance (dry powder)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Current vintage: lag supply 2 days and record first-seen values forward. Treasury mints vs circulating supply. Drawdown deciles from the trailing 365 days only. Entry at the first 00:00 UTC open after both conditions are known.
rows.missing_data: The netflow arm needs Coin Metrics FlowInExUSD/FlowOutExUSD (free-tier availability unverified); UST supply would make the aggregate complete.

final.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-09, BTC outperforms after a stablecoin issuance spike that follows a drawdown. The event: a combined USDT+USDC daily SplyCur increase above 2 sigma of its trailing 180 days, counted as known 2 days after the day it covers, within 2 days after a BTC 3-day return in the bottom decile of its trailing 365 days. The Coinbase BTC return from the next 00:00 UTC open over 3 days exceeds the return after bottom-decile drawdowns with no issuance spike by more than 0.50%, with a lower bound > 0 in both halves.
final.statistic: Event minus control mean BTC log return at +3 days (primary) and +1 day (reported), week-clustered.
final.procedure: Daily supply change from Coin Metrics SplyCur (USDT + USDC; DAI, BUSD and TUSD in a reported aggregate), checked against DefiLlama circulating totals for chain coverage. Day-d supply counts as known at d+2 00:00 UTC. Drawdown days come from Coinbase daily closes, with deciles over the trailing 365 days only. Events are de-overlapped with a 5-day refractory period; controls are drawdown days without a spike. Entry at the first 00:00 UTC open after both conditions are known. Week-clustered bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Halves 2019-2021 / 2022-2026.
final.data: coinmetrics-usdt-daily, coinmetrics-usdc-daily, coinmetrics-dai-daily, coinmetrics-busd-daily, coinmetrics-tusd-daily, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD
final.pass: At least 30 non-overlapping events, event - control > 0.50% at +3 days with a week-clustered one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, and positive in both halves. Fewer than 30 events gives inconclusive.
final.controls: Drawdown-only controls (the T-320 base rate) and unconditional spike events (the T-402/T-464 base rate). 2-day lag, 50 bp round trip, fixed thresholds. T-402 and T-464 counted as prior trials. The netflow arm runs only once the data exist, with a pre-registered negative sign.

rows.reason: A narrow conditional salvage of a dead family (T-402, T-464, T-320), not a duplicate, and the issuance arm is testable now. The source predates the window and supply mints are a noisy proxy for the purchases Griffin-Shams traced, so expect an inconclusive or negative result.

rows.name: BTC 25-delta risk reversal (skew) predicts returns
rows.source_notes: The SMU INK thesis page returned no content, so Neo's numbers (t 1.91 univariate rising to 3.73 with controls, weaker after 2024) are unconfirmed. The GitHub practitioner backtest (JERONIMODIFRANCO/deribit-rr) was opened: about 4.5 years of data; T-30 sign accuracy 33/56 = 58.9% (p about 0.18, called not significant); T-90 24/31 = 77.4% with no p-value; RR-vs-move r = 0.076 (R2 0.006). Its author calls the signal effectively noise. Deribit Insights and the ScienceDirect counter-evidence paper were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Every Mandel SPX skew predictor failed (T-52, T-138, T-227), and T-228 says skew prices insurance. The Brier/Shannon learnings say the Deribit-implied distribution is already in crypto prices at 1-24 h. RR mostly follows recent returns, and Mandel's ML crypto scan shows recent returns reversing at 1-20 days, so the controls are decisive. The ML F3 iv_skew feature is CBOE SKEW, not BTC's RR, so this variable is unseen. The out-of-sample window 2025-01..2026-10 holds only about 95 weekly observations.
rows.data_notes: deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC: 2,465,638 trades from the 07:00-09:00 UTC window each day, 2022-01..2026-10 (T-257 built 1,748 smile days from them). deribit-dvol-BTC-history: 2,032 daily rows from 2021-03-24, open-stamped. deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD and daily-history-IBIT are present. Signal-map: 'option skew (risk reversal): predictor vs premium'.
rows.lookahead_risks: The smile is known only after 09:00 UTC. DVOL daily candles are open-stamped, so use the candle stamped t-1. The 30-day target overlaps in weekly samples (Hansen-Hodrick). Missing smiles are never filled beyond 1 day.
rows.missing_data: None for 2022-2026; earlier years would need a further Deribit history pull.

final.claim: From 2022-01 to 2026-10, with the sign fixed on 2022-01..2024-12 and out of sample on 2025-01..2026-10, the z-score of BTC's 30-day 25-delta risk reversal against its trailing 90 days, known at 09:00 UTC, predicts the Coinbase BTC log return from 09:00 UTC over the next 7 days with a positive slope. The controls are trailing 7- and 30-day returns, DVOL and 7-day mean funding. Out-of-sample R2 vs the expanding mean is above 0, and a long-when-z > +1 rule beats buy-and-hold net of 10 bp per switch.
final.statistic: Newey-West t of the RR25-z slope with controls (full window); Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R2 (2025-01..2026-10); the rule's net Sharpe minus buy-and-hold in the out-of-sample window. Reported: the 30-day horizon with Hansen-Hodrick t, and the butterfly as a placebo regressor.
final.procedure: RR25 from the T-257 smile fits (quadratic in ln(K/F)/sqrt(T) per expiry, interpolated to 30 DTE), available at 09:00 UTC. Days without a fit are skipped, never filled beyond 1 day. Target: from the Coinbase hourly close at 09:00 UTC (the bar starting 08:00) to the same hour 7 days later. Weekly sampling with all 7 weekday phases reported and pooled (house rule 10). DVOL from the candle stamped t-1; funding = mean interest_8h over the trailing 7 days. The sign is fixed on 2022-2024. Rule: long BTC (IBIT in US hours) when z > +1, flat otherwise, 10 bp per switch, with a 50 bp Coinbase stress. Deflate over 2 horizons x 2 statistics plus T-257's trials.
final.data: deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC, deribit-dvol-BTC-history, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT
final.pass: Fitted sign positive, full-window controlled NW t >= 2 after deflation, out-of-sample R2 > 0, and the rule's net Sharpe above buy-and-hold in the out-of-sample window.
final.controls: Trailing-return controls, DVOL and funding. Butterfly as a placebo regressor. One z threshold. Cost stress. The SPX skew failures (T-52, T-138, T-227) set the prior.

rows.reason: Testable now on T-257's smile series, and new as a return predictor. But the thesis source could not be opened and the one checkable replication calls the signal noise. Register with one primary horizon (7 days) and controls that separate skew from recent returns.

rows.name: BTC variance risk premium and vol-of-vol as return predictors
rows.source_notes: Opened arXiv 2410.15195 (Almeida, Grith, Miftachov, Wang; v1 2024-10-19, v2 2025-08-01). It decomposes BTC premia by return region and finds BVRP high in a low-volatility regime and lower in a high-volatility one; it makes no forecasting claim. The source of the predictability claim (Atanasova, Miao, Segarra, Willeboordse, SSRN 6771170) returned 403 and is unverified. The Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou analogy is from memory.
rows.replication_concerns: Mandel's own ML F3 scan (T-580, state/ml/ic_scan_f3.json) has already covered this variable for crypto over the whole DVOL history: 58 discovery months (2021-03..2025-12) plus 9 confirmation months. own_iv_rv (DVOL over realised vol) shows 1d IC +0.018 (t 2.3) in discovery and +0.054 (t 2.3) in confirmation; 5d confirmation +0.091 (t 2.6); 20d +0.059 (t 2.0) in discovery and +0.10 (t 1.6) in confirmation. own_iv level is also confirmed positive at 1d and 5d. The proposed 2024-2026 test window is therefore not out of sample. T-235 (SPX VRP timing) failed, T-246's second-half VRP is much smaller, and the VRP is mechanically low after crashes, which a 30-day return control must absorb.
rows.data_notes: deribit-dvol-BTC-history (2021-03-24..2026-10, 2,032 daily rows, open-stamped), coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT and fred-DTB3 exist and span the claim, but that window is contaminated by T-580. An unseen sample needs Deribit option trades for 2019-04..2021-03 (free history API, not archived) to rebuild a 30-day ATM IV with the T-257 smile method. Signal-map: 'variance risk premium as a return predictor vs a harvestable premium'.
rows.lookahead_risks: The DVOL candle stamped t-1 closes at 23:59, so use it at t 00:00. Realised variance runs through t-1. T-580 has seen 2021-2026, so any rerun on that window is in-sample. The rebuilt pre-2021 ATM IV differs in method from the VIX-style DVOL, which must be stated.
rows.missing_data: Deribit BTC option trades for 2019-04..2021-03 for the holdout IV, and a forward window from 2026-11.

final.claim: On data no Mandel scan has seen, the BTC variance risk premium at 00:00 UTC, VRP = IV30^2 minus trailing 30-day realised variance (365-day annualisation), predicts the Coinbase BTC log return over the next 7 days with a positive slope and positive out-of-sample R2. IV30 is a 30-day ATM implied vol rebuilt from Deribit trades for the 2019-04..2021-03 holdout, and DVOL for the forward window 2026-11-01..2027-10-31. The slope must be positive in both samples.
final.statistic: Predictive slope with Newey-West t, pooled over holdout and forward, and Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R2 vs the expanding mean in each sample. Reported: the 30-day horizon (Hansen-Hodrick), vol-of-vol, the 2021-03..2026-10 in-sample slope labelled 'seen by T-580', and the top-tercile long/flat rule at 10 bp per switch.
final.procedure: Holdout IV30: Deribit BTC option trades 2019-04..2021-03, ATM 30-day IV from per-expiry smile fits (T-257 method) interpolated to 30 days, using trades up to 00:00 UTC. Forward IV30 = the DVOL candle stamped t-1. Realised variance from Coinbase daily closes through t-1. Target: the Coinbase BTC log return from the day-t 00:00 open over 7 days, sampled weekly with all 7 weekday phases reported and pooled. Expanding-mean benchmark within each sample. The 2021-03..2026-10 DVOL window is reported, not judged.
final.data: new deribit-option-trades-BTC-2019-2021 (holdout), deribit-dvol-BTC-history, coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, daily-history-IBIT, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Pooled slope > 0 with NW t >= 2 after deflation (2 signals x 2 horizons plus T-580's crypto F3 cells), and a positive slope with out-of-sample R2 > 0 in each sample.
final.controls: Trailing 30-day return and IV level as controls. Weekday phases. One tercile cut for the rule. ETH replication reported (T-67: the ETH VRP itself is weak). The method difference between rebuilt ATM IV and DVOL is disclosed.

rows.reason: The variable looks promising, since Mandel's own F3 scan shows positive IC, but that scan already used the whole DVOL history, so the proposed 2024-2026 out-of-sample window is not clean. Register it only on an unseen pre-DVOL holdout plus a forward window.

rows.name: Coinbase premium (US vs offshore BTC price gap) as a US-demand signal
rows.source_notes: Opened the bgeometrics page: index = (Coinbase BTC-USD - Binance BTC-USDT) / Binance x 100, with no USDT/USD conversion and no predictive claim, plus an explicit not-advice disclaimer. The 2024-02 CoinDesk commentary was not opened. Borri et al. (PDF text) confirmed: 510 BTC-fiat pairs on 165 exchanges vs Kraken, with 10th/90th-percentile discounts of -1.8%/+3.7% (2014-2025), -2.1%/+3.5% post-2020, and a half-life of about 1.1 weeks, attributed to capital controls. That is a cross-country segmentation result, not evidence about Coinbase vs Binance. Only the definition is verified; no predictive claim exists to verify.
rows.replication_concerns: No test exists, only practitioner readings. The raw index mixes US demand with the USDT/USD basis. Cross-venue gap learnings (Brier, Kelly: gaps close within seconds, and large gaps are mismatches) and T-577's null cross-asset features are hostile. Binance is the deeper BTC venue, so 'Coinbase leads' is a segmentation claim, not a reference-price lead.
rows.data_notes: Archived: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD (2022-01..), coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD (2019-01..), coinbase-daily-USDT-USD (1,990 daily rows, from about 2021-05), kraken-trades-1m-XBTUSD (48 monthly bundles 2022-01..2025-12, so no 2026). binance-1m-BTCUSDT-btc-above covers only windows around Polymarket resolutions. Signal-map: 'cross-venue premium (Coinbase vs offshore)'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Binance klines are stamped by open time and Coinbase candles by bar start, so key both by close and use only synchronous closes. Drop, rather than fill, missing hours. USDT/USD before 2021-05 needs Kraken.
rows.missing_data: Binance spot BTCUSDT 1h klines 2019-01..2026-10 (data.binance.vision, signal only); hourly USDT/USD (Coinbase USDT-USD hourly from 2021-05, Kraken USDTUSD before); Kraken XBTUSD for 2026 for the placebo.

final.claim: From 2019-01 to 2026-10, the Coinbase BTC premium over Binance BTCUSDT predicts the next-24h Coinbase BTC return with a positive slope, before and after the ETF launch (split 2024-01-11), with HAC t >= 2 after it. The signal is the mean of the 24 hourly synchronous premiums ending at 00:00 UTC, converted at USDT/USD and z-scored against the trailing 90 days. A long-when-z > 1 rule beats buy-and-hold on the same days net of a 50 bp round trip.
final.statistic: HAC (Newey-West lag 5) slope of the next-24h return on the premium z, and the top-minus-bottom tercile contrast. Rule net excess vs buy-and-hold. Bonferroni over 2 targets (Coinbase 24h; IBIT next open-to-close at 5 bp).
final.procedure: Premium_h = Coinbase hourly close / (Binance BTCUSDT 1h close x USDT/USD hourly close) - 1, at synchronous hour ends (Binance klines keyed by open time + 1h, Coinbase candles by start + 1h). An hour missing on any series is dropped. The daily signal is the mean of the 24 premiums ending at 00:00 UTC, z-scored against the trailing 90 days. Target: the Coinbase BTC 00:00-to-00:00 UTC return. Placebo: the same regression on the Coinbase-Kraken USD gap (2022-01..2025-12). Pre-ETF and post-ETF halves.
final.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-daily-USDT-USD, kraken-trades-1m-XBTUSD, daily-history-IBIT, new binance-1h-BTCUSDT, new coinbase-hourly-USDT-USD, new kraken-1h-USDTUSD (pre-2021-05)
final.pass: Positive slope in both halves, HAC t >= 2 post-ETF after Bonferroni, the rule's net return above buy-and-hold on the same days for at least one target, and the Coinbase-Kraken placebo not showing the same effect.
final.controls: USDT basis removed by the conversion. Coinbase-Kraken placebo. Trailing 24h return control. One z cut. 50 bp / 5 bp costs. The FTX (2022-11) and USDC-depeg (2023-03) windows are reported separately.

rows.reason: Widely quoted but untested, and the only verified source is a definition page that makes no predictive claim. Free hourly Binance data unblock it cheaply; the fix uses hourly synchronous closes with the USDT basis removed and a Coinbase-Kraken placebo.

rows.name: CME bitcoin weekend gap 'fill' vs a random-walk first-passage null
rows.source_notes: Opened the TradingView ideas page. Two ideas assert that '±90% of CME gaps are filled sooner or later' and another that they 'almost always get backfilled', with no sample, window or method; the 95% figure does not appear. The verified source is anecdotal. The gap-tracker script page was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: No study exists. Most small gaps 'fill' under any random walk (first passage), and T-333 found that gap-fading loses on SPY. The CME weekend gap itself has ended. Local CME BTC_F hourly bars show Friday trading continuing to 03:00 UTC Saturday and Sunday trading from 04:00 UTC from the 2026-05-29 weekend on, after none in either window before. The last old-schedule weekend was Memorial Day weekend, 2026-05-22. So a result could license no live strategy.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-BTC-F from 2017-12; coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD 2019-01..; coinbase-1m 2022-01..; the local 60m BTC_F bars (2024-05-29..2026-10) confirm the schedule change. Signal-map: only the 'first-passage null for folklore claims' idea under Monte Carlo / bootstrap.
rows.lookahead_risks: CME close and reopen times are in CT with DST. Spot stands in for the futures (basis ignored). Sigma must be weekday-only (T-515). Stop-first ordering within bars.
rows.missing_data: CME intraday futures bars before 2024, so gaps would be defined on spot.

final.claim: From 2019-05 to the 2026-05-22 weekend (before CME BTC futures traded through weekends), take the weekends where Coinbase BTC at the Sunday 17:00 CT CME reopen differs from its level at the Friday 16:00 CT close by more than 1%. The share whose Friday level is revisited within 120 hours exceeds a driftless first-passage null 2*Phi(-|gap|/(sigma*sqrt(T))) with weekday-only sigma, and also exceeds the same excess for Tuesday-to-Thursday pseudo-gaps.
final.statistic: Observed fill rate minus the mean null probability, and minus the placebo excess. Reported: the net mean per trade of a fill-targeting MBT arm.
final.null: Excess <= 0 against the null or the placebo
final.procedure: Marks from Coinbase bars keyed by bar end (hourly before 2022, 1-minute after). Fill = a later high/low through the Friday level within 120 hours. Sigma = the weekday-only daily log-return sd over the trailing 30 weekdays (T-515). Placebo: Tuesday CME close to Thursday 22:00/23:00 UTC (49 hours). Month-clustered bootstrap and Wilson intervals. Holiday weekends use the actual reopen.
final.data: coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-F, local 60m BTC_F bars (switch date)
final.pass: Excess > 0 with the month-clustered 95% CI excluding 0 against both the null and the placebo. Even a pass licenses no strategy, because the gap no longer exists.
final.controls: Weekday sigma, a drift-allowing null variant, gap-size buckets reported, one threshold, and the sample cut at the switch.

rows.reason: Anecdotal folklore whose phenomenon no longer exists after CME's 2026-05 switch to weekend trading, so even a pass would license nothing tradable; not worth a harness. If a first-passage harness is built for another test, run this as a by-product to close the folklore.

rows.name: Open-interest flush / liquidation-cascade reversal
rows.source_notes: SSRN 5611392 (Ali) returned 403. The MDPI paper and the write-up of the 2026 preprint were not opened, and BIS WP 1087 was not re-opened. No source makes the return-reversal claim; it is Mandel's own hypothesis built on a case study. The Binance public archive was checked: data/futures/um/daily/metrics/BTCUSDT/ starts with BTCUSDT-metrics-2020-09-01.zip, as the candidate says.
rows.replication_concerns: No systematic study exists. T-320/T-469 put plain BTC reversal after large down days at +9-11 bp gross, so the OI condition must add about 40 bp or more. Hurst finds taker flow on Kalshi perps predicts nothing worth trading. Events combining the bottom 5% of OI change with a -2 sigma day will number about 5-8 a year, concentrated in 2021-2022 and October 2025. USD-denominated OI falls mechanically when price falls, so the condition must use coin-denominated OI.
rows.data_notes: Archived target data: coinbase-daily and -hourly bars for BTC and ETH, and deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL for the funding covariate. Not archived: Binance USD-M daily metrics (5-minute sum_open_interest in coin, sum_open_interest_value in USD, taker long/short ratio), available from 2020-09-01. No Deribit OI history is archived. Signal-map: 'open interest / forced deleveraging'.
rows.lookahead_risks: Daily metrics files are published after the UTC day closes, so the historical test assumes a live implementation that polls Binance's public OI endpoint at 00:00 UTC; historical file values are as recorded, not revised. Use coin-denominated OI. Coinbase hourly bars are start-stamped, so enter at the open of the 00:00 bar.
rows.missing_data: Binance USD-M daily metrics for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT, 2020-09..2026-10 (free, signal only).

final.claim: From 2020-09 to 2026-10, an open-interest flush during a sharp drop predicts a larger rebound than the drop alone. A flush day is a UTC day when the 24h change in Binance USD-M BTCUSDT open interest (coin-denominated sum_open_interest) is in the bottom 5% of its trailing 365 days and the 24h Coinbase BTC return is below -2 trailing 60-day sigma. The Coinbase BTC return from the next 00:00 UTC open over 3 days exceeds that after equal price drops without a flush (OI change above its trailing median) by more than 0.50%, with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, positive in both halves.
final.statistic: Event minus control mean Coinbase return at +3 days (primary) and +1 day (reported), week-clustered.
final.procedure: OI = the 5-minute coin-unit sum_open_interest from Binance USD-M daily metrics; the 24h change runs 00:00 to 00:00 UTC and is treated as known at 00:00 UTC (a live rule polls the public endpoint). Return sigma from the trailing 60 Coinbase daily returns; OI percentile from the trailing 365 days. Events are de-overlapped with a 3-day refractory period; controls have the same price condition and an OI change above its trailing median. Entry at the open of the Coinbase 00:00 UTC hourly bar after the event day; exits at +1 and +3 days. Nothing is fitted. Week-clustered bootstrap, 5,000 draws. Halves 2020-09..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-10. ETH runs identically as a replication.
final.data: coinbase-daily-BTC-USD, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, coinbase-daily-ETH-USD, coinbase-hourly-ETH-USD, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, new binance-um-metrics-BTCUSDT, new binance-um-metrics-ETHUSDT
final.pass: At least 30 non-overlapping BTC events, event - control > 0.50% at +3 days with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, positive in both halves, and ETH of the same sign.
final.controls: Price-drop-only controls (T-320). Funding at the event reported (T-423, Deribit funding). USD-value OI as a reported variant. Taker-ratio arm reported only. One OI cut and one return cut, no grid. Kalshi perp / CDE nano costs (10-18 bp) reported as an alternative to the 50 bp Coinbase round trip.

rows.reason: Not a duplicate, and the structural mechanism is plausible, but no source makes the return claim and the plain reversal it conditions on is below cost (T-320). Register it as blocked on the free Binance metrics fetch, with BTC primary, ETH as replication, and coin-denominated OI to avoid a mechanical link to the price drop.

knowledge.title: Crypto derivatives, flows and on-chain-adjacent variables: what the 2020-2026 literature claims and what survives
knowledge.markdown:
# Crypto derivatives, flows and on-chain-adjacent variables: what the 2020-2026 literature claims and what survives

- **Authors / kind:** Survey of 14 strategies or patterns from about 31 sources: peer-reviewed papers (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu, J. Finance 2022; Griffin-Shams, J. Finance 2020; Baur-Smales, JFM 2022; Shen-Urquhart-Wang, Financial Review 2022; Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba, IRFA 2024; Mourey-Shahrour-Şoiman, FRL 2025; Weiss et al., FRL 2026), working papers (He-Manela-Ross-von Wachter; Borri-Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu 2025; Fabus et al. 2026; Almeida et al. 2024), a thesis, a GitHub replication and practitioner pages.
- **Links:** https://arxiv.org/html/2212.06888v7 · https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.14435 · https://www.nber.org/papers/w25882 · https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2024.103218 · https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/fut.22332 · https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finlet/v86y2025ipes1544612325019154.html
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.35 (7 of about 31 sources read in full, including the two that carry most of the effect sizes; 8 checked at abstract or metadata level only; the rest unopened or 403).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** text was extracted from He et al. (v7) and Borri et al. (Table 2) and their numbers checked. Almeida et al., the deribit-rr backtest, the ML-Quant summary of Fabus et al., and the bgeometrics and TradingView pages were opened. Seven peer-reviewed papers were confirmed from the abstract only, and Weiss et al. from the title only. Every data claim was checked against Mandel's bundles.
- **Selected because:** the learning program's inputs include funding rate, basis, open interest, implied volatility, skew, the variance risk premium, ETF flows, COT positioning and market cap, and Mandel's crypto record (T-363, T-314, T-402, T-546) has tested only price and funding versions of them. This cluster covers the variables one step away.

## What it says

- **Perp premium convergence (He et al.).** Short the perp and hold spot when the perp trades rich. The premium exists because leveraged retail longs pay for exposure and margin-constrained arbitrage capital is scarce. On Binance hourly BTC, 2020-01..2024-03: Sharpe 11.65 at zero cost and 3.35 at high retail fees; 37.6% of the return comes from convergence and 14.9% from funding. The effect has decayed: the mean premium was 0.69 before 2022 and 0.17 after, and Borri puts the carry Sharpe at 4.06 from 2024 and negative in 2025. Only the positive leg can be executed from the US. The negative leg needs short spot, which means paying an IBIT borrow cost in US hours.
- **Size (CSIZE).** Coins with small market caps earn more. Borri Table 2, weekly value-weighted: 5-1 is -2.3%/week (t -2.66), and -0.9% (t -1.69) post-2020; smallest minus largest is about +0.9%/week post-2020. Fieberg et al.: the premium sits in micro-caps too small to trade economically, appears mainly in bull markets, and decays.
- **Two-week momentum, loser leg.** 5-1 is +2.6%/week (t 3.89), and +2.1% (t 3.70) post-2020. Fieberg et al.: most of the alpha comes from the short leg, and trading costs are heavy.
- **Network value (CVALUE).** Market cap relative to new addresses: 5-1 is -3.5%/week (t -3.50), and -2.3% post-2020. Only the same author group has replicated it, and the free data carry active addresses, not new ones.
- **Intraday half-hour momentum (Shen et al.).** In a session defined by volume, the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour, most strongly in high-volume sessions. The authors attribute it to liquidity provision. Coefficients unseen; no replication.
- **Spot BTC ETF flows (Fabus et al., via a secondary summary).** After timestamp alignment, each $1bn of net inflow is followed by +1.67 pp of next-day BTC return, and returns also predict flows. Unreplicated, and other papers disagree.
- **CME Commitments of Traders (Baur-Smales).** Leveraged funds time the market by adjusting their net shorts, and following their changes is profitable. Magnitudes unseen. Since 2024 those shorts are largely basis hedges.
- **Weekend crypto predicts Monday equities (Mourey et al.).** Negative weekend crypto returns predict Monday declines in the Nasdaq and Russell 2000, more strongly after May 2022; positive weekends predict nothing. It is a day-of-week effect, and most of it probably sits in the opening gap, which ES futures already price on Sunday.
- **Deribit expiry reversal with dealer gamma (Weiss et al.).** Returns reverse around the Friday 08:00 UTC expiry, most when dealer gamma exposure is negative. Confirmed from the title only.
- **25-delta risk reversal (skew).** The thesis claim (controlled t 3.73, weaker after 2024) could not be opened. The one replication that could be opened gets 58.9% sign accuracy (p about 0.18) and calls the signal noise.
- **Variance risk premium as a predictor.** The vol-of-vol forecasting paper returned 403. Almeida et al. show only that the BTC VRP (implied variance minus trailing realised volatility squared) is high in low-volatility regimes. That is a same-period relationship, not a forecast.
- **Stablecoin issuance after drawdowns (Griffin-Shams).** In 2017-2018, Tether purchases followed downturns and came before price rises. The sample is from the manipulation era.
- **Coinbase premium.** An index with a definition but no predictive claim anywhere.
- **CME weekend gap fill.** The claim of "±90% fill" comes with no method, and most small gaps fill under any random walk.
- **Open-interest flush and liquidations.** Only case studies exist ($19bn of open interest gone in 36 hours, Oct 2025), and none makes a return claim.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: practitioner.** The rigorous core (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu, Fieberg et al., and the checked numbers in He et al. and Borri et al.) documents effects that have decayed, sit in micro-caps Coinbase does not list, or were earned on Binance, which US persons cannot use. The claims Mandel could trade rest on short papers read only at abstract level, an unreplicated working paper, a thesis that could not be opened, and anecdote. A Sharpe of 11.65 against a liquid market should be treated as a cost or leak artefact until shown otherwise.

## What Mandel adopts

- Testable now on archived bundles, each pre-registered with a DSR that counts prior trials:
  - `cme-btc-leveraged-funds-change`: COT positioning stamped by release time, judged on post-publication data only (from 2022-05), with the CME basis as the decisive control.
  - `btc-weekend-drop-monday-equity-session`: BTC as a cross-asset leader for SPY/QQQ/IWM open-to-close, with the target's own price kept out of the inputs. It has the reference-price shape the children require (a market that trades while the book is closed), but it must beat ES futures. T-549 (overnight drift, supported) is context.
  - `crypto-two-week-losers-exclusion`: the loser leg, long-only on Coinbase, consistent with T-556 (DOGE/SHIB bounce-short, supported). T-314's failed winner leg enters the DSR.
  - `crypto-small-cap-quintile-vs-btc`, traded a day after the CMC snapshot. T-546 predicts a negative result.
  - `deribit-monthly-expiry-reversal-unconditional` (stage 1). T-216 (SPY OPEX gamma pin, supported) shows that gamma effects exist; T-223 found no larger BTC move into the fixing.
  - `btc-rr25-z-predicts-weekly-return` on T-257's smiles; `stablecoin-mint-after-btc-drawdown`, which must add 50 bp over the T-320 base rate; and `btc-us-session-first-half-hour-momentum` at lowest priority. Each reports FOMC and CPI days separately.
- Blocked, with first-seen capture starting now: `spot-btc-etf-flow-next-session` (the $500m threshold is fixed, not fitted), `perp-oi-flush-reversal-btc` (coin-denominated open interest), `coinbase-binance-premium-next-day` (with a Coinbase-Kraken placebo), `crypto-active-address-value-quintile`, and `btc-vrp-predicts-returns-holdout`. For the last one, T-580's F3 scan has already seen own_iv_rv with positive IC over the whole DVOL history, so only a 2019-2021 holdout plus a forward window counts as out-of-sample.
- Perp premium carry survives only as Hurst's H-ibit-carry forward test, read on 2027-02-12.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- Funding-rate carry: the effect has decayed, and T-363 (Sharpe -0.64), T-198, T-258 and T-423 are not supported. Funding is a censored signal: a practitioner count (not opened) puts BitMEX BTC funding at its 0.01%/8h baseline for 78% of Q3-2025, and Deribit's ±5 bp dampener hides small premiums. So funding data cannot show the post-2022 premium. Hurst measures US-venue funding near zero. P&L earned on Binance or Deribit is not US-legal, so their data are used as signals only.
- CME weekend gaps: dropped, because CME BTC futures have traded through weekends since 2026-05-29.
- ETF flow magnitude: too large relative to daily volatility, which suggests look-ahead. T-328 and T-404 are parked.
- Skew and the VRP as predictors: T-52, T-138, T-227 and T-235 failed on SPX, and the child crypto study found Deribit's implied distribution already priced into Polymarket BTC/ETH contracts. T-49 and T-246 show that the VRP exists, not that it forecasts.
- Intraday momentum: T-427 failed, T-577 has 0 of 50 crypto 5-minute cells net positive, and Hurst's hourly rules show under 6 bp of follow-through against 16-18 bp of fees.
- Cross-venue premiums: Brier and Kelly find that gaps close fast and that large gaps are mismatched questions, and Kalshi's hourly BTC/ETH ladders do not lag Coinbase spot.
- On-chain value: the replication is not independent, the data are current-vintage, and T-400 (MVRV) is not supported.
- Smart-money COT: Result 18 (informed traders are a pointer, not a signal) and T-405 (parked) are hostile.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- New bundles, with offshore venues used as signals only: binance-1h-BTCUSDT, binance-um-metrics, farside-btc-etf-flows, ishares-ibit-history, coinbase-hourly-USDT-USD, coinmetrics-adractcnt, deribit-option-trades-BTC-2019-2021, and a Thursday Deribit book capture for sign(GEX).
