- First-seen capture for every series that gets revised; backfills are labelled as revised data.
- Point-in-time rules: Coinbase bars are stamped at the start, Binance and Deribit candles at the open. CMC snapshots become tradable a day later. COT uses available_at. Day-t ETF flows enter at 13:30 UTC on t+1. On-chain data lag 2 days. Delisted coins get a survivorship haircut.
- Candidate features: dLF/OI, the percentile of the change in coin open interest, stablecoin-mint z, Coinbase premium z, RR25 z, the weekend BTC return, CMC market cap rank, and ETF flow. Funding is used only as a control.
- Never condition on USD-denominated open interest during a price drop, because it falls mechanically with price.
- Default placebos: Wednesday pseudo-weekends, random-tercile labels and first-passage nulls.

## Cross-links

- A4: liquidation cascades and vol-of-vol are bursts of trading time. A5: its retrieval-date leakage control is the same idea as the t+1 flow rule.
- 12, 13, 14: their indicator and HMM-regime pipelines should be scored on these features under the same gate.
- venues/US-LEVERAGE-VENUES-2026-10-20.md (Kalshi perps, CDE nano futures, IBIT).
- T-363, T-553, T-198, T-258, T-423, T-314, T-546, T-556, T-402, T-464, T-320, T-223, T-216, T-257, T-49, T-246, T-580, T-405, T-404, T-328, T-427, T-549, T-400; H-ibit-carry, H-btc-us500-lead.

## Sources used

- He et al., Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures: https://arxiv.org/html/2212.06888v7
- Borri et al. (2025): https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.14435
- Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu: https://www.nber.org/papers/w25882
- Fieberg-Liedtke-Zaremba: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2024.103218
- Shen-Urquhart-Wang: https://research.birmingham.ac.uk/en/publications/bitcoin-intraday-time-series-momentum/
- Fabus et al. summary: https://www.ml-quant.com/papers/ssrn/7545019/
- Baur-Smales: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/fut.22332
- Mourey et al.: https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finlet/v86y2025ipes1544612325019154.html
- Weiss et al. (title only): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.frl.2026.110340
- deribit-rr: https://github.com/JERONIMODIFRANCO/deribit-rr/tree/main
- Almeida et al.: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.15195
- Griffin-Shams: https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=3195066
- Coinbase Premium Index: https://charts.bgeometrics.com/coinbase_premium.html
- TradingView CME gaps: https://www.tradingview.com/ideas/cmegaps/

candidates.name: Post-earnings announcement drift (SUE / announcement-return sort), large-cap vs microcap split
candidates.summary: Buy the top and short the bottom decile of earnings surprise (SUE, or the CAR(-1,+1) announcement return) after the announcement and hold about 60 trading days. Modern evidence says the drift is gone outside microcaps. This DUPLICATES T-338 and T-452 (both blocked by survivorship and the lack of a point-in-time consensus). The web evidence adds a pre-registrable null for Mandel's investable large-cap universe and a 2025-26 dispute over whether the drift is dead.
candidates.mechanism: Investors underreact to earnings news (limited attention, conservatism), and arbitrage is limited by costs in small names. The counterparty is the slow or inattentive holder. Two explanations for the decline compete: faster price discovery after decimalisation and Reg NMS (Martineau), and earnings that carry less information, especially for small firms (Griffin-McInnis-Zhao 2026).
adjacent_variables: earnings surprise SUE from XBRL EPS
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca equities); long-short needs borrow
candidates.claimed_effect: Original: Bernard-Thomas (1989) extreme-SUE spread of roughly 4% over 60 days (from memory, not re-verified). OSAP records Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok's announcement-return signal at t=9.25 (1977-1992, EW). Recent: Martineau (CFR 2022) finds no drift in non-microcaps since about 2006, and it has only recently disappeared in microcaps. Subrahmanyam (2025 WP), 2001-2024: t=2.18 for all stocks and t=1.43 excluding microcaps, which are about 3% of market value. Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang (RFS 2025) report drift with t of about 14. Costs are not netted in these figures.
candidates.replication: Widely replicated before 2006. It has decayed to about zero in non-microcaps (Martineau), and survival is contested in 2025-26 (UCLA Anderson review). Subrahmanyam attributes the disagreement to research design and microcap inclusion. Chordia et al. (2014, cited in the Columbia PEAD paper) find a significant downward trend for PEAD over 1976-2011. Mandel's tradable universe is large caps, where the best evidence predicts a null.

sources.title: Martineau - Rest in Peace Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (Critical Finance Review 2022)
UCLA Anderson Review - Is post-earnings announcement drift a thing again? (Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang 2025, Dickerson-Julliard-Mueller, Subrahmanyam 2025)
Griffin, McInnis, Zhao - Explaining the Decline of PEAD: More Arbitrage or Less News? (JAAF 2026)
Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (EarningsSurprise, AnnouncementReturn, EarnSupBig, RevenueSurprise)

candidates.proposed_test: Refutation-first, as a diagnostic only, because the universe is survivor-only. Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members (the fja05680 + Wikipedia membership already built for T-394/T-334), plus the 901-symbol archive as a second arm. Events: earnings release dates from SEC 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance times. This needs the submissions 'items' field re-fetched, because the archive kept only XBRL filings, and 10-Q dates lag the release. Signals: (a) SUE = seasonal difference in diluted EPS from XBRL companyfacts, as filed in that accession, scaled by the std of the prior 8 differences (no price input); (b) CAR(-1,+1) against SPY. Enter at the close of day +2, which avoids look-ahead on after-close releases. Hold 60 sessions. Decile breakpoints come from the trailing 63 days of events. Costs: 10 bp per side plus 1%/yr borrow. Statistics: calendar-time daily long-short mean with a block bootstrap, FF5+UMD Newey-West alpha, both halves (2011-2018 and 2019-2026), and a placebo that shifts announcement dates by 20-120 sessions. Pre-register a null for the top 500. Any pass still needs a delisted-inclusive universe before funding.

candidates.name: Earnings-day unexplained volume predicts post-announcement returns (opinion-divergence / high-volume premium at earnings)
candidates.summary: Stocks whose turnover around the announcement is far above what their own prior trading predicts earn higher returns over the next 60 days, separately from the sign of the surprise. The input is pure volume and turnover, not price. It is NEW to the registry. Its non-earnings cousins failed in Mandel (T-419 ETF high-volume premium, T-546 crypto alts), so the earnings-event version is the untested piece.
candidates.mechanism: Volume beyond the expected level signals opinion divergence and greater visibility. Under short-sale constraints and a broader investor base (Merton), the stock earns higher subsequent returns. The other side is short-term liquidity providers and the pessimists who are constrained from shorting.
adjacent_variables: short-sale constraint proxies (borrow fee, short interest)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Garfinkel-Sokobin (JAR 2006): 45,187 NYSE/AMEX announcements, 1985-1998. The top unexpected-turnover group earns a mean 60-day size-adjusted return of +1.386% against -0.070% for the bottom (t=9.49). By SUV, high +1.415% vs low -0.220%. The effect holds in regressions with the earnings surprise. Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin (2001) give the general high-volume premium (from memory). No costs stated.
candidates.replication: This sweep found no post-2000 replication; the search budget ran out. Its mechanism sits next to PEAD, which decayed. Mandel's general high-volume premium tests on ETFs (T-419) and crypto alts (T-546) were not_supported, so expect weakness. Still untested on single-stock earnings events.

sources.title: Garfinkel & Sokobin - Volume, Opinion Divergence, and Returns: A Study of Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (JAR 2006)
The High-Volume Return Premium and Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (NYU working paper)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members, with the 901-symbol archive as a survivor-only diagnostic. Events: 8-K Item 2.02 dates, with BMO/AMC known from the acceptance time. SUV = turnover summed over days -1..0 minus the prediction from a turnover market model fitted on days -55..-6, divided by the residual std. It uses Yahoo volume and XBRL shares outstanding as of the prior filing, with no price input. Each quarter, sort events into SUV deciles using breakpoints from the previous quarter. Enter at the close of day +2. Hold 60 sessions. Benchmark: size-matched ETF (SPY/MDY/IJR). Costs: 10 bp per side. Statistic: high-minus-low mean abnormal return with an event-date clustered bootstrap, plus a regression that controls for CAR(-1,+1), SUE sign and pre-event momentum. Halves: 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. Deflated Sharpe over 4 trials (SUV vs raw turnover x 20/60-day holds).

candidates.name: Earnings announcement premium (expected announcers outperform), US decay after the 2004 8-K rule
candidates.summary: Stocks expected to announce earnings in a month, judged from the month they announced a year earlier, earn more that month. This DUPLICATES T-339 (blocked: survivorship). The web adds strong evidence that the US premium disappeared after 2004, while it survives abroad and mostly arrives before the release.
candidates.mechanism: Risk: announcements carry systematic news that investors use to update on other firms, so announcers are riskier (Savor-Wilson). Attention: announcement-driven buying by attention-constrained investors (Frazzini-Lamont). Disappearance: more frequent 8-K filings after 2004 pre-empt the information, so the premium moved to 8-K dates (Heitz et al.).
adjacent_variables: expected announcement month from last year's 8-K/10-Q dates
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); an aggregate arm on SPY/sector ETFs
candidates.horizon: monthly (announcement month) or 10-21 days around the event
candidates.claimed_effect: Savor-Wilson (JF 2016): 9.9% annualised abnormal return for firms scheduled to report. Frazzini-Lamont (2007) give an earlier estimate of the same premium (from memory, magnitude not re-verified). Heitz-Narayanamoorthy-Zekhnini find the US premium has disappeared since the 2004 Form 8-K disclosure rule but persists in nine non-US markets. A 1983-2016 study finds the premium lowest in 2006-2016. Gao-Hu-Zhang: about 71% of the premium is earned before the release.
candidates.replication: Barber et al. (2013) replicate it in nine non-US markets. The US premium is reported to have disappeared after 2004 (Heitz et al. working paper) and was weakest in 2006-2016 (Pacific-Basin Finance Journal 2023). Treat the US premium as decayed until shown otherwise.

sources.title: Savor & Wilson - Earnings Announcements and Systematic Risk (JF 2016), draft
Heitz, Narayanamoorthy, Zekhnini - The Disappearing Earnings Announcement Premium
Earnings announcement premium and return volatility (Pacific-Basin Finance Journal 2023)

candidates.proposed_test: Expected-announcer flag: the firm filed an 8-K Item 2.02 (or a 10-Q/10-K as a fallback) in the same calendar month 11-13 months earlier. This uses only information at least 11 months old. Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members (T-394 machinery). Report the share of unpriced delisted members and the return they would need to flip the verdict. Portfolios: monthly announcers minus non-announcers, equal- and value-weighted, 10 bp round trip at about 100% monthly turnover. Window: 2005-2026, with 2005-2015 and 2016-2026 halves. Second arm: a 10-day pre-release window (T-10 to T-1 close) against SPY, following Gao-Hu-Zhang. Statistics: Newey-West t and deflated Sharpe over 5 variants. Pre-register the Heitz et al. prediction of about zero after 2004 as the null being tested.

candidates.name: Pre-announcement run-up conditional on option-implied uncertainty (uncertainty resolution before earnings)
candidates.summary: Stocks with high implied volatility about 11 trading days before earnings earn positive market-adjusted returns over the next 10 days as their uncertainty falls. Low-IV stocks do not. The input is implied vol, not price. NEW to the registry, though related to T-339.
candidates.mechanism: Investors acquire information, and analysts and managers supply it, before the release, so uncertainty resolves early and the risk premium for bearing it is paid in the pre-release window. The effect is larger when aggregate uncertainty is high. The counterparty is the holder who demands compensation for event uncertainty.
adjacent_variables: change in IV over the pre-announcement window
analyst forecast activity before the release
candidates.assets: US single stocks with listed options (Alpaca); only the stock leg is traded
candidates.horizon: days (10 trading days before the announcement)
candidates.claimed_effect: Gao, Hu, Zhang (SSRN 3595953): 71-72% of the earnings announcement premium is earned before the release. The 21-day window centred on the announcement averages 0.42% excess, of which 0.31% falls in the 10 pre-release days. The high-IV group (sorted at T-11) earns +1.52% market-adjusted over 10 days while its IV falls 1.8%; the low-IV group shows no significant return. An interquartile IV increase means +0.65% higher return. The sample period was not stated on the pages read, and no costs are given.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found; searches ran out. It inherits the decay risk of the earnings announcement premium (see the disappearing-premium evidence).

sources.title: Quantpedia - Pre-Announcement Returns (Gao, Hu, Zhang: Uncertainty Resolution Before Earnings Announcements)
Gao, Hu, Zhang working paper (Tsinghua PBCSF host)

candidates.proposed_test: Historical pilot, testable now and small: AAPL, GOOGL and AMZN with Cboe VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN (archived since about 2010; about 190 events in all). Earnings dates come from 8-K Item 2.02. At the T-11 close, rank the name's VX level against its own trailing 504-session distribution (point-in-time). Buy at the T-11 close and exit at the T-1 close, before the event, measured against QQQ. Costs: 2 bp per side. Statistic: top-tercile minus bottom-tercile mean with an event-clustered bootstrap, also split by VIX tercile (the paper says the effect is stronger when aggregate uncertainty is high). This is underpowered. The children's power lesson applies: a few hundred events cannot settle a 1% effect. So the deciding test is a forward one: the capture box's options-surface atm_iv on the roughly 30 single stocks in the ML universe, with a read date fixed in advance after at least 300 events and pre-registered thresholds.

candidates.name: Pre-earnings long straddle: buy the implied-vol ramp, exit before the release
candidates.summary: Buy an ATM straddle in the first post-event expiry about 3 days before earnings and sell it at the last close before the release. This captures the rise of implied vol into the event, not the event itself. DUPLICATES T-204 (blocked: no historical chains). Mandel's archived single-stock vol indices make a model-priced pilot possible now. An index-level check of the same ramp is possible through COR1M (relevant to T-521 and T-538).
candidates.mechanism: Event variance is fixed while time to expiry shrinks, so the implied vol of the expiry containing the event rises mechanically as the event nears (sigma_imp^2 = sigma_diffusive^2 + sigma_jump^2/tau). Investors who price the event too cheaply early, or premium sellers who sell too soon, are on the other side. At the index level, rising component IVs in earnings season lower implied correlation (Cboe COR uses top-50 ATM component IVs).
candidates.assets: US single-stock options (Alpaca options); index-level proxy via COR1M/DSPX (data only)
candidates.claimed_effect: Gao, Xing, Zhang (JFQA 2018): ATM straddles held from three days before the announcement to the announcement average a 3.34% return, while single-stock straddles generally lose money. An earlier version reported 2.3% from T-1. Costs as stated in the paper were not captured.
candidates.replication: This sweep found no independent replication. Practitioner guides (TradeStation, OptionsTradingIQ) describe the ramp but warn that buying in the final days overpays. Mandel's T-57 lesson applies: flat-IV model pricing overstated quoted prices by 20-79%, so a model-priced pilot can only check the sign of the ramp.

sources.title: Gao, Xing, Zhang - Anticipating Uncertainty: Straddles around Earnings Announcements (JFQA 2018)
Cboe Implied Correlation indices (methodology: top-50 SPX components' ATM IVs)

candidates.proposed_test: Arm A (pilot, sign check only): AAPL, GOOGL and AMZN events 2010-2026. Model-price the ATM straddle with the VX index as a flat IV, entering at the T-3 close and exiting at the T-1 close, using the time to the first post-event monthly expiry. P&L = BS(VX_T-1, tau-2d) - BS(VX_T-3, tau) on the realised T-3 to T-1 spot path, minus a 1 vol-point round trip. Statistic: mean P&L per debit with an event-clustered bootstrap. Arm B (index level, testable now, all archived): COR1M mean level and daily change in earnings-season weeks (weeks 2-6 after quarter-end) against other weeks, 2007-2026. Use a block bootstrap and a placebo with shifted calendar weeks. Pre-register COR1M as lower in season. This tests the component-IV ramp without chains and feeds T-521/T-538. Arm C (deciding, forward): market-quoted straddles from the capture box on about 30 names at half-spread costs. Read date fixed after at least 200 events.

candidates.name: Earnings IV crush: implied event move exceeds realised move (short straddle held through the release)
candidates.summary: Implied announcement-day volatility is systematically above the volatility that follows. Straddles held over the announcement lose about 8% per event in the academic sample, which makes a short straddle or iron condor through earnings the mirror trade, with tail risk. DUPLICATES T-205, T-206, T-207 and T-248 (blocked: no chains). It is testable now as an implied-vs-realised measurement on VXAPL/VXGOG/VXAZN.
candidates.mechanism: Holders pay a jump or variance risk premium for event risk: intermediaries are capital-constrained, and retail demands lottery-like event exposure. The short-vol seller earns it but carries fat right-tail losses. This is the opposite of Mandel's FOMC/CPI finding (T-214, T-224), where a flat 30-day vol under-prices event-day variance; single-stock IV is event-aware.
candidates.assets: US single-stock options (Alpaca options; defined-risk structures for a small account)
candidates.horizon: overnight to 1-2 days (T-1 close to T+1 open)
candidates.claimed_effect: Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck, Seeger (RFS 2019; NYU 2017 slides): uniform evidence that implied announcement-day jump vol exceeds subsequent return vol; announcement-day straddle returns are highly significant at -8% per announcement. Announcement-day variance is more than 5x normal days (Dubinsky-Johannes 2006 working paper, quoted secondhand). Vendor beat-rate data vary widely: NVDA about 25% and UNH about 88% of moves exceed the implied move (July 2026). A vendor claims 70-75% of moves stay within the implied move (unverified).
candidates.replication: The direction is consistent across academic and vendor sources, but heterogeneity by name is large and losses cluster in tail events. This sweep found no study netting quoted spreads in 2015-2026. Mandel has no chain history yet (capture started 2026-10-14).

sources.title: Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck, Seeger - Option Pricing of Earnings Announcement Risks (NYU Derivatives conference slides 2017)
Option Pricing of Earnings Announcement Risks (RFS 2019, IDEAS listing)
EarningsWatcher - Who beats the implied move? (beat rates by stock, July 2026)

candidates.proposed_test: Testable now: AAPL, GOOGL and AMZN events 2010-2026 (about 190) from Cboe VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN. Implied event variance = (VX_pre^2 - VX_base^2) x tau, where VX_pre is the T-1 close, tau is 30/365, and VX_base is the name's VX level 10 sessions after its previous event. That is point-in-time. Do not use the post-event IV, which would leak. Realised = ln(close at T+1 / close at T-1)^2. Statistics: mean ln(realised/implied) with an event-clustered bootstrap, the share of events with |move| < implied move, and a model-priced 1-day short straddle P&L (T-1 close to T+1 open) net of half the median quoted spread from the capture box. Pre-register implied > realised. Report the worst 5% of events and the max-loss-on-margin path (Reg-T), because small-account survival matters. Deciding arm, forward: T-248's design on about 30 capture-box names with quoted mids.

candidates.name: Earnings seasonality: firms announcing their seasonally strong quarter earn higher returns
candidates.summary: Firms whose earnings are reliably highest in a given fiscal quarter earn abnormal returns when that quarter is announced, because investors and analysts anchor on the weaker recent quarters. The input is an accounting calendar, not price. NEW to the registry. The closest Mandel test (T-476, ETF return seasonality) was a different, price-based claim and failed.
candidates.mechanism: Recency bias: investors overweight the recent low-earnings quarters and forecast the coming seasonal peak too pessimistically. Analysts' errors are more positive in those quarters. The counterparty is the anchored forecaster. The authors rule out risk, volume and idiosyncratic-volatility explanations.
adjacent_variables: seasonal rank of the upcoming quarter
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon, Soltes (RFS 2017): the highest earnings-seasonality quintile earns about 65 bps/month four-factor alpha against about 31 bps for the lowest in announcement months, a difference significant at 1%. The value-weighted figure of 55 bps/month is reported as 'stronger'. The full sample period was not captured from the summary. No costs stated.
candidates.replication: No post-publication replication found; searches ran out. The related return-seasonality family (Heston-Sadka) replicates strongly in OSAP (MomSeason t of about 5-7 in-sample). Mandel's ETF version, T-476, was not_supported.

sources.title: Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon, Soltes - Being Surprised by the Unsurprising (Harvard Law School Forum summary)
Being Surprised by the Unsurprising: Earnings Seasonality and Stock Returns (RFS 2017, IDEAS)

candidates.proposed_test: Seasonality score: the average rank, among the four fiscal quarters, of the upcoming quarter's EPS (or net income per share) over the prior 3-5 fiscal years. Use XBRL companyfacts values as filed, which needs the us-gaap EarningsPerShareDiluted and NetIncomeLoss tags fetched; the archive kept only share tags. Signals therefore start around 2013-2014, so the whole test is out-of-sample after publication. Form the score at month start for expected announcers, using last year's announcement dates. Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members, with the 901-symbol archive as a diagnostic. Portfolio: top minus bottom quintile among that month's announcers, held for the month. Costs: 10 bp round trip. Statistics: mean spread with a month block bootstrap, FF5+UMD alpha with Newey-West t, both halves, and deflated Sharpe over 3 lookbacks.

candidates.name: Earnings-date timing: late or delayed announcers (and Friday announcers) carry bad news the market prices late
candidates.summary: Firms that announce later than their usual schedule tend to report worse news, and equity prices do not reflect the scheduling signal until the release. Friday announcers also report worse news, and more of the reaction is delayed. This uses the 'days until earnings' variable directly. NEW to the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Managers delay bad news and schedule it for low-attention days. Investors ignore schedule changes that are visible weeks ahead, though option markets price the volatility-timing information (Johnson-So). The counterparty is the inattentive equity holder.
variables: calendars (day of week, time of day)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); short side needs borrow
candidates.horizon: days to weeks (expected date to announcement, plus 1 month after)
candidates.claimed_effect: Johnson & So (JFQA 2018): later-than-expected schedulers report worse news, and equities do not reflect the timing disclosures until the announcement. A Wall Street Horizon summary of the working paper (about 19,000 companies, 8+ years) says advancers outperform delayers by 260 bps the following month (vendor figure, not checked against the JFQA text). DellaVigna & Pollet (NBER 11683, JF 2009): Friday announcements have a 45% higher probability of a negative surprise and a 50 bp lower abnormal return. 60% of their total response is delayed, against 40% for other weekdays, and announcement volume is 10% lower.
candidates.replication: This sweep found no out-of-sample or 2015-2026 replication. Historical date-revision data are proprietary (Wall Street Horizon). A free point-in-time proxy, 'not yet announced by the expected date', has not been tested.

sources.title: Johnson & So - Time Will Tell: Information in the Timing of Scheduled Earnings News (JFQA 2018)
Wall Street Horizon - Earnings dates can predict stock performance (summary of So's paper)
DellaVigna & Pollet - Investor Inattention, Firm Reaction, and Friday Earnings Announcements (NBER w11683)

candidates.proposed_test: A point-in-time rule that needs only free EDGAR data. Expected date E = the same fiscal quarter's 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance one year earlier plus 364 days. At the E+3 session close, a firm with no 2.02 filing yet is 'late'. Short it, or underweight it against its sector SPDR, from the E+3 close to the close after its release. Compare with on-time announcers in the same week. Second arm: NT 10-Q/NT 10-K (Form 12b-25) notices, entered at the first open after acceptance. Third arm: Friday or pre-holiday after-close announcers, long or short by CAR(0,+1) sign, held 20 sessions. Window 2012-2026 with halves. Costs: 10 bp per side plus 1%/yr borrow. Statistic: mean abnormal return per event with a date-clustered bootstrap. Deflated Sharpe over 3 lateness thresholds x 3 arms. Survivorship: late filers delist more often. EDGAR covers delisted CIKs but Yahoo prices do not, so report the unpriced share and the return it would need to flip the verdict, as T-394 does.

candidates.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) predicts returns and earnings news
candidates.summary: Stocks with high option volume relative to stock volume underperform, because informed traders with negative private information prefer options when shorting is costly. O/S also predicts the next earnings surprise. It uses derivative volume, which is on the variable list. NEW to the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Under short-sale costs, negative private information flows into options (puts, synthetic shorts), so high O/S signals bad news. Positive information is traded in the stock. The counterparty is the option market maker who hedges in the stock, and the uninformed holders. The effect is stronger when short-sale costs are high or option leverage is low.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); signal from listed options
candidates.horizon: weekly (1-week hold); event variant around earnings
candidates.claimed_effect: Johnson & So (JFE 2012): the lowest O/S decile beats the highest by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualised), 1996-2010. OSAP records OptionVolume1 at 0.916 (monthly, EW, t=3.45) and OptionVolume2 at t=2.45. O/S predicts firm-specific earnings news. No transaction costs netted.
candidates.replication: OSAP replicates it as a clear predictor in-sample. Ge-Lin-Pearson (JFE 2016) argue that signed volume is needed to reconcile mixed results. This sweep found no 2015-2026 evidence; weekly turnover costs are likely to eat much of it.

sources.title: Johnson & So - The option to stock volume ratio and future returns (JFE 2012, IDEAS)
Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (OptionVolume1/2)

candidates.proposed_test: Data gap: no historical per-underlying option volume; chain snapshots exist only from 2026-10-14. Forward test from the capture box: each Friday, O/S = 5-day sum of option volume (options-surface oi/vol by side) / 5-day share volume, ranked within the roughly 30 single stocks in the ML universe and sorted into terciles. Hold the low-minus-high tercile 1 week. Costs: 5 bp per side. Event arm: O/S over days -5..-1 before each earnings release, regressed on CAR(0,+1) and SUE sign. Pre-register a read date after at least 52 weekly formations and at least 150 earnings events. Statistic: mean weekly spread with Newey-West t, deflated Sharpe over 2 variants. If OCC historical volume per symbol is obtainable, run 2015-2026 historically first, with point-in-time S&P 500 members.

candidates.name: Pre-earnings abnormal short volume (FINRA Reg SHO) and long-window shorting flows
candidates.summary: The classic claim: abnormal short selling in the days before earnings predicts negative surprises and announcement returns. With FINRA's public daily data (2010-2015), however, abnormal short-term shorting does NOT predict bad news; only persistent, longer-window shorting predicts returns. Testable now on archived FINRA data. Mandel's T-394 (abnormal short-volume z > 2, not conditioned on earnings) already came out null, consistent with Wang-Yan-Zheng.
candidates.mechanism: Informed short sellers trade on private information before releases (Christophe-Ferri-Angel), or they trade on slowly incorporated public information and anomalies (Wang-Yan-Zheng). Only the second appears in the public-data era. The counterparty is buyers who ignore the published shorting flow.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); short side needs borrow
candidates.horizon: days (pre-event 5 days, post-event 1-20 days); 20-day to 1-year for the level effect
candidates.claimed_effect: Christophe-Ferri-Angel (JF 2004; about 900 Nasdaq firms, Sept-Dec 2000): abnormal shorting in the 5 days before announcements precedes negative surprises (via secondary summaries). Wang, Yan, Zheng (JFE 2020; 2010-2015 FINRA daily short volume): heavily shorted stocks (prior 5 days, quintiles, skip 1 day, hold 20) underperform by 12.6%/yr EW (t=6.0) and 6.0%/yr VW (t=4.0). No evidence of abnormally high shorting in the 5 days before negative earnings surprises, downgrades or large insider sales. Predictability decays slowly and lasts about a year.
candidates.replication: Contested. Daske-Richardson-Tuna (2005) find short sellers do not anticipate negative shocks. Wang-Yan-Zheng find no anticipation in the public-data era. Mandel T-394 (S&P 500, 2019-2026, z > 2 abnormal short-volume ratio): survivor subset +0.7 bp gross 5-day abnormal, inconclusive or null.

sources.title: Wang, Yan, Zheng - Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency (JFE 2020)
Boehmer, Jones, Zhang - (NY Fed 2010 conference paper summarising Christophe-Ferri-Angel 2004)

candidates.proposed_test: Two arms on finra-regsho-cnms, 2018-08 to 2026-10, with point-in-time S&P 500 members (T-394 machinery). Arm A (event; pre-registered expectation null, per Wang-Yan-Zheng): abnormal short-volume ratio over days -5..-1 before each earnings release, as a z-score against days -65..-6. Regress CAR(0,+1) and CAR(+2,+20) on it, controlling for size and momentum. Short the top-decile abnormal names at the T-1 close and cover at the T+1 close, 10 bp per side plus borrow. Arm B (the level effect Wang-Yan-Zheng found persistent, an untested sibling of T-394): each month-end, sort by the 60-day average short-volume ratio into quintiles. Hold heavy minus light for 1 month, net of 10 bp round trip and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. Statistics: date-clustered slope t, quintile spread with a block bootstrap, halves, deflated Sharpe over 4 trials. Report the survivorship gap as T-394 does.

candidates.name: Analyst earnings-forecast revision momentum
candidates.summary: Stocks with upward revisions to the consensus FY1 EPS forecast outperform those with downward revisions over the next 1-6 months. This DUPLICATES T-396 (blocked: no free point-in-time consensus history). The web adds decay context and a forward-capture route.
candidates.mechanism: Analysts and investors underreact to revisions, and revisions cluster as analysts herd and adjust slowly. Prices drift with the revision. The counterparty is investors who anchor on stale estimates. The effect is stronger for low-dispersion stocks (Dische).
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: OSAP SignalDoc: AnalystRevision (Hawkins-Chamberlin-Daniel 1984) 0.46%/month long-short, t=3.17 (1975-1980, EW). REV6 (Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok 1996) t=4.07 (1977-1992). ChangeInRecommendation (Jegadeesh et al. 2004) 0.225, and ForecastDispersion t=2.88. McLean-Pontiff (JF 2016): across 97 predictors, returns are 26% lower out-of-sample and 58% lower after publication.
candidates.replication: OSAP replicates the in-sample results. This sweep found no peer-reviewed 2010-2023 performance figure; practitioner claims of decay by month 6-8 are unsourced. Expect substantial post-publication decay (McLean-Pontiff).

sources.title: Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (AnalystRevision, REV6, ChangeInRecommendation)
McLean & Pontiff - Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability? (JF 2016)
Dische - Dispersion in Analyst Forecasts and the Profitability of Earnings Momentum Strategies

candidates.proposed_test: There is no free point-in-time history, so start a forward capture now. Each day, snapshot Yahoo's earnings-trend consensus for point-in-time S&P 500 members: current FY1 EPS, its value 7/30/60/90 days ago, and up/down revision counts over the last 7/30 days. The module and field names are from memory and must be verified before registration. Each month-end, sort on the 30-day % change in FY1 consensus (top minus bottom decile, sector-neutral), hold 1 month, 10 bp round trip. Pre-register a read date after 24 monthly formations. Statistics: mean spread with Newey-West t, FF5+UMD alpha, deflated Sharpe over 3 variants (30-day, 90-day, net up-minus-down count). The snapshots are point-in-time by construction, so no look-ahead.

candidates.name: Size premium conditional on quality ('size matters if you control your junk')
candidates.summary: The raw small-minus-big premium is weak and has decayed, but Asness et al. argue it reappears, stable and not concentrated in microcaps, once quality (profitability, growth, safety, payout) is controlled. PARTIAL DUPLICATE: raw size T-385 (IJR-IWM) is not_supported, and the January small-cap tests T-351 and T-444 are not_supported. The conditional claim is not registered; T-385's notes anticipate a separate conditional trial.
candidates.mechanism: Small firms are on average junky (unprofitable, risky), and junk earns low returns. That masks a genuine size premium, which may reflect illiquidity or risk. The counterparty is investors who overpay for large, safe, liquid firms.
candidates.assets: US equity ETFs (IJR, IWM, SPY, QUAL) and factor portfolios; Alpaca
candidates.claimed_effect: Banz (1981), per OSAP: Size 1.01%/month, t=3.07 (1926-1975). Asness, Frazzini, Israel, Moskowitz, Pedersen (JFE 2018): controlling for junk, a significant size premium appears that is stable over time, robust, not concentrated in microcaps, and present in 30 industries and 24 countries. Hou-Xue-Zhang (NBER w23394): with NYSE breakpoints and value weighting, 64% of 447 anomalies are insignificant at 5% (85% at t<3).
candidates.replication: Raw SMB is widely documented to have decayed. The conditional result is AQR's own and was not independently verified in this sweep (searches ran out). Mandel T-385: IJR-IWM +0.22%/yr (CI -1.21 to +1.71), RMW loading t 4.68.

sources.title: Asness et al. - Size Matters, if You Control Your Junk (draft; JFE 2018)
Hou, Xue, Zhang - Replicating Anomalies (NBER w23394)
Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (Size, Banz 1981)

candidates.proposed_test: Factor level first, with no survivorship issue. Regress monthly French SMB on MKT, HML, UMD and AQR's QMJ (free download; also the FF5 RMW/CMA variant) over 1993-2014 in-sample and 2015-2026 out-of-sample (post-publication). Pass only if the out-of-sample SMB alpha's 95% lower bound is above 0 and the deflated Sharpe over the size family (35 trials with T-385's 34) exceeds 0.95. If it passes, test an executable ETF sleeve over 2006-2026: long IJR (profitability-screened S&P 600), short SPY, and short QUAL-minus-SPY sized by the in-sample QMJ beta. Costs: 5 bp per monthly reset and 0.3% borrow. Report alpha against FF5+UMD.

candidates.name: Net share issuance and buybacks from point-in-time SEC shares outstanding
candidates.summary: Firms that shrink their share count (net repurchasers) outperform firms that issue. The long-run drift after buyback announcements (and underperformance after equity offerings) was a classic anomaly. PARTIAL DUPLICATE: T-449 (French net-issuance portfolios after 2008) is not_supported and T-395 (buyback announcements) is blocked. The web adds evidence that both effects disappeared after 2003, and Mandel already archives the point-in-time share counts needed for an investable large-cap version.
candidates.mechanism: Managers time the market, buying back undervalued and issuing overvalued equity, and investors underreact to the signal. The decline is attributed to market timing becoming a less important motive and to institutional ownership rising (repurchasers with more than 50% institutional ownership went from 34% to 70%).
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); ETF proxy PKW (buyback) vs SPY
candidates.claimed_effect: OSAP SignalDoc: ShareIss1Y (Pontiff-Woodgate 2008) t=7.08 (1970-2003); CompEquIss (Daniel-Titman 2006) t=4.39; ShareRepurchase (Ikenberry-Lakonishok-Vermaelen 1995) only 'likely' at t=1.85. Fu & Huang (Management Science 2016): about +10% (repurchases) and -12% (SEOs) 3-year gross abnormal returns through 2002, falling to about 0% in 2003-2008 at 24, 36 and 48-month horizons.
candidates.replication: Decayed. Fu-Huang show it gone after 2003. Mandel T-449: French net-issuance repurchaser-minus-high-issuer +0.30%/month over 2008-2026 (CI -0.18 to +0.86), FF5 alpha t 1.35, versus +0.55%/month before 2008.

sources.title: CXO Advisory - Extinction of the buyback/secondary offering effect (Fu, Huang, Lin)
Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (ShareIss1Y, ShareIss5Y, CompEquIss, ShareRepurchase)

candidates.proposed_test: Use the archived sec-companyfacts dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding and us-gaap CommonStockSharesOutstanding with their filed dates, which are point-in-time. Adjust for splits with Yahoo daily-events. Signal: 12-month log change in shares outstanding, available from the 10-Q/10-K filed date. Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members 2011-2026, plus the 901-symbol archive as a diagnostic. Portfolio: each month-end, bottom decile (net repurchasers) minus top decile (issuers), held 1 month. Costs: 10 bp round trip plus 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. Statistics: mean spread with a month block bootstrap, and FF5+UMD alpha reported both raw and against FF5 (CMA absorbs issuance). Pre-register a null given T-449 and Fu-Huang. Its value over T-449 is an executable large-cap version with the shares data Mandel already holds.

candidates.name: S&P 500 additions: direct additions vs MidCap migrations
candidates.summary: The S&P 500 inclusion effect has nearly vanished on average. Greenwood-Sammon show that the average hides a split: direct additions (from outside the S&P MidCap) still earned about +5.4% in the 2010s, while migrations from the S&P 400 earned about -1.8%, because MidCap funds sell what S&P 500 funds buy. DUPLICATES T-340 and T-453 (blocked), with T-334 (post-effective reversal) inconclusive and T-213 the options version. The migration flag is new conditioning information.
candidates.mechanism: Index funds create forced demand at inclusion, against limited arbitrage and downward-sloping demand curves. For migrations, S&P 500 trackers' buying is matched by S&P 400 trackers' selling, so the net demand shock is small. The counterparty is the index-tracking flow and the liquidity providers who absorb it.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: days (announcement to effective date, typically 3-10 sessions)
candidates.claimed_effect: Greenwood & Sammon (HBS WP 23-025, revised Nov 2023): the S&P 500 addition abnormal return fell from 7.4% (1990s) to 0.3% (past decade). Deletions went from -16.1% (1990s) to -0.6% (2010-2020). Direct additions returned 5.4% against -1.8% for migrations in the 2010s. Migrations rose from about 50% to over 70% of additions. The 20 days before announcement show little change, so the decline is not front-running. The decline for Russell additions is not statistically significant.
candidates.replication: Bennett-Stulz-Wang (2020) independently document the decline over 1997-2017. Russell evidence (2000-2005) also shows a weakening effect. Mandel T-334 (post-effective reversal, 327 additions 2010-2026, 83% priced) was inconclusive.

sources.title: Greenwood & Sammon - The Disappearing Index Effect (HBS Working Paper 23-025)
CXO Advisory - Strategies for exploiting index rebalancing (Russell reconstitution summaries)

candidates.proposed_test: Reuse T-334's event set (fja05680 + Wikipedia, additions 2010-2026). Add a migration flag: the added firm is removed from the S&P 400 (Wikipedia S&P 400 changes table, or S&P DJI press releases) with the same effective date. Enter at the close of the first session after the announcement (press releases come after the close) and exit at the effective-date close, measured against SPY. Costs: 10 bp round trip. Claims: (i) direct additions' mean is above 0, and (ii) direct minus migration is above 0. Statistics: event bootstrap, halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026, and a placebo with dates shifted by plus or minus 30 sessions. Report the unpriced share (delisted or renamed) and the return absent names would need to flip the verdict. Expect small n for direct additions (perhaps 80-120).

candidates.name: Insider open-market purchases (Form 4): opportunistic and cluster buys, and where the return actually sits
candidates.summary: Following insider purchases, especially opportunistic (non-routine) ones, earned large abnormal returns historically. Recent evidence (2018-2025) says the reaction is concentrated on the first day, often in an overnight gap an outsider cannot capture, and that there is no timing premium beyond which firms insiders buy. DUPLICATES T-391 (blocked: survivorship). The web adds a decay verdict and a sharper entry rule.
candidates.mechanism: Insiders have private information about firm value and trade on it when they are not following a routine schedule. The counterparty is the uninformed seller. Speed of dissemination (2-business-day Form 4 filing since SOX 2002, EDGAR feeds, algorithmic monitoring) now moves most of the value into the first session.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Cohen, Malloy, Pomorski (NBER 16454; JF 2012; 1986-2007): following only opportunistic trades earns about 82 bps/month value-weighted (180 bps/month equal-weighted), with routine trades near zero. Equibles (47,458 purchases, 2020-2025): the median beats the median listed stock by +0.12% (1 month) to +2.56% (1 year). Against the S&P 500 it trails by -1.54% to -12.95%. A 180-session placebo shift shows no timing premium, and the routine/opportunistic split is not reproduced. arXiv 2602.06198 (2018-2024 microcaps, 13,534 purchase lines): day-1 abnormal return 4.13% for stocks far below their 52-week high vs 0.86% near it; days 2-30 show no significant calendar-time alpha.
candidates.replication: Decayed or contested after 2010. An Aalto thesis (2008-2024) finds returns about halved. Equibles finds no timing premium. arXiv finds the tradable part concentrated on day 1, including the overnight gap after after-close filings. Survivorship (delisted microcaps) biases recent vendor studies upward.

sources.title: Cohen, Malloy, Pomorski - Decoding Inside Information (NBER w16454)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (2006q1 onward; access verified in T-391's notes) with acceptance datetimes. Entry: the first regular-session open strictly after acceptance, never the filing-day close. Arms: all code-P purchases, clusters (3+ insiders in 30 days), and opportunistic purchases (Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski rule: the insider has not traded in the same calendar month in each of the prior 3 years). Horizons: 1, 5, 21 and 126 sessions. Benchmark: size-matched ETF. Placebo: entry shifted 180 sessions, as in Equibles. Restrict to point-in-time S&P 1500 names to limit delisting bias, and report the unpriced share. Costs: 10/20/30 bp per side by size bucket. Statistic: mean abnormal return with a date-clustered bootstrap. Deflated Sharpe over 3 arms x 4 horizons. Pre-register that days 2-126 add nothing beyond the day-1 open.

candidates.name: Dividend initiations and omissions (plus the dividend-month premium)
candidates.summary: Firms that start paying dividends drift up and firms that omit them drift down for months after the event. Separately, stocks earn more in the months they are predicted to pay. The dividend-month premium DUPLICATES T-374 (not_supported for S&P 500 payers 2010-2026). Initiation and omission drift is NEW to the registry and testable with Yahoo dividend events.
candidates.mechanism: Dividend changes signal management's private view of persistent earnings, and investors underreact. The month premium is price pressure from dividend-seeking clienteles buying before the ex-date, which reverses after it. The counterparty is investors who ignore payout signals and the liquidity providers absorbing clientele demand.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); dividend ETFs for the month-premium arm
candidates.horizon: months (12-month drift); days to weeks for the month premium
candidates.claimed_effect: Michaely-Thaler-Womack (JF 1995), as recorded in OSAP SignalDoc: DivInit 0.625 (t=3.37) and DivOmit 0.92 (t=6.33), 1964-1988, equal-weighted. Hartzmark-Solomon (JFE 2013, CRSP 1927-2011): predicted dividend months beat all other firms by 53 bps/month and dividend payers' non-dividend months by 37 bps/month. Daily returns rise into the ex-date and turn negative after.
candidates.replication: The month premium did not replicate in Japan (1991-2014). Mandel T-374 (S&P 500 payers 2010-2026): run-up difference +10.6 bp gross / +5.6 bp net, p 0.16, not_supported; ETF arm -0.4 bp. This sweep found no post-1995 replication of initiation/omission drift (searches ran out).

sources.title: Alpha Architect - The Dividend Month Premium (Hartzmark & Solomon)

candidates.proposed_test: Initiation = the first cash dividend in Yahoo daily-events after at least 24 months without one. Omission = an expected regular payment missing for more than 1.5 of the firm's usual cycles, detected point-in-time at the expected ex-date plus 45 days. Yahoo gives ex-dates, not declaration dates, so entry (next close after the ex-date or detection) is later than in the paper. Label it a conservative variant, or add Nasdaq dividend-history declaration dates if verified. Hold 12 months: long initiators and short omitters against a size-matched ETF. Statistic: calendar-time monthly mean with a block bootstrap, FF5+UMD alpha, halves 2005-2015 and 2016-2026. Expect only a few hundred events, so state the minimum detectable effect before running.

XBRL SUE decile with a 60-day hold, 2011-2026. Its notes already predict a large-cap null (Martineau); blocked on acceptance datetimes and a delisted-inclusive universe.
PEAD expressed as a call debit spread; blocked on chains.

learnings.finding: A placebo entry 25 sessions after the report earned +1.77%/month, more than the real entry's +1.32%. A placebo 25 sessions early earned -1.10%. So the sort picks names by their price path, not by the news: survivorship plus a low-price selection in a current-listings panel.
Pre-registered %-surprise sort, top decile minus all announcers: -0.65%/month at <= $5B, with 2022-26 at -36.9%. The long-short Sharpe was negative in every variant.
Mandel already expects a large-cap null (Martineau), and no free point-in-time delisted universe exists for the cross-section.
Published anomalies decay after publication. A sort on the announcement return is a price-based signal, and price-only strategies start from a negative base rate.
Survivor-only universes give inconclusive verdicts: 38-91% of the cross-sectional universes were unpriced. A point-in-time S&P 500 universe was 82-93% priced in T-334/T-394.

rows.missing_data: Earnings release dates. The sec-submissions archive keeps XBRL filings only and drops the 'items' field. 8-Ks exist in it mostly from 2019-06, with no way to tell Item 2.02. The SUE arm also needs quarterly diluted EPS or NetIncomeLoss from 10-Q facts, which is also free: the archived companyfacts kept share tags from every form but F-score concepts from annual forms only.

registration.claim: Over 2011-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, a dollar-neutral portfolio long the top and short the bottom decile of the SPY-adjusted announcement return CAR(D-1..D+1) is formed around each 8-K Item 2.02 release. D is the first regular session whose open follows the release's available_at. The portfolio enters at the D+2 close, takes breakpoints from the trailing 63 sessions of releases, and holds 60 sessions. The claim is that it earns a positive calendar-time mean daily return net of 10 bp per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. The registered expectation is a null (Martineau 2022).
registration.statistic: Mean calendar-time daily long-short return, equal weight across open cohorts, in bp/day and annualised; FF5+UMD alpha with Newey-West t (lag 60).
registration.null: Mean <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily series (block 126 sessions, at least twice the 60-session overlap, 5,000 draws). Placebo: each firm's release dates shifted by a uniform random 20-120 sessions, 1,000 shifts.
registration.procedure: Releases are 8-Ks whose data.sec.gov 'items' include 2.02, with available_at = min(acceptance, filing date 22:00 ET) as in sec-submissions. CIKs map to point-in-time members through the fja05680 spells and the SEC CIK tables (T-393/T-451 machinery). CAR comes from adjusted Yahoo closes minus SPY. Entry is at the D+2 close. Deciles need at least 50 releases in the trailing 63 sessions. Halves are 2011-2018 and 2019-2026, with 2020-03..06 reported separately. Survivorship (rule 9): report the share of member releases without prices and the mean 60-session return they would need to flip the bootstrap lower bound. If a plausible value (|x| < 500 bp) flips it, the verdict is inconclusive. A SUE arm (seasonal difference in as-filed quarterly diluted EPS over the s.d. of the prior 8 differences) runs only after the quarterly XBRL fetch and counts as a second trial.
registration.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, wikipedia-sp500-changes, sec-submissions-b*, sec-cik-lookup, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily; to fetch: data.sec.gov submissions with 'items'
registration.pass: All of: mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; both halves positive; real-date mean above the placebo's 95th percentile; survivorship unable to flip the lower bound. Otherwise not_supported, or inconclusive if survivorship decides.
registration.controls: One surprise definition (CAR), one horizon (60 sessions), one threshold (deciles). The placebo-shifted dates are the baseline. The D+2 close entry removes after-close look-ahead. Costs: 10 bp/side plus 1%/yr borrow, with a 20 bp/side sensitivity. Counted in the PEAD family with T-338 and T-452 for the deflated Sharpe.

rows.notes: Do not spend a harness on this ahead of the others. Hurst has already shown, on a 2015-2026 panel, that the surviving small-cap 'drift' is survivorship (killed by its own placebo), and the large-cap version is predicted null. Its only value is as a cheap refutation once the 8-K items fetch exists, because that fetch is shared with rows 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 (event arm). Web evidence that Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang (2025) find t of about 14 is not in investable large caps after costs; treat it as a design dispute, not a lead. The signal map has no market-variable concepts yet (earnings, volume, implied vol, short interest, shares outstanding), so this cluster maps only onto method concepts.

registration.claim: Over 2011-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members' 8-K Item 2.02 releases, events in the top decile of standardized unexpected turnover beat bottom-decile events in calendar time from the D+2 close over 60 sessions, SPY-adjusted and net of 10 bp per side. Unexpected turnover is measured over sessions D-1..D as residuals from a log-turnover market model fitted on D-55..D-6, with deciles from the previous calendar quarter's releases. The SUV slope must also stay positive after controlling for CAR(D-1..D+1) and 60-session pre-release momentum.
registration.statistic: Mean calendar-time daily high-minus-low SUV-decile return in bp/day. Secondary: the pooled event-level slope of the 60-session SPY-adjusted return on SUV decile rank, controlling for CAR, momentum and log market cap, with t clustered by release week.
registration.null: Spread <= 0 and slope <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily spread (block 126 sessions). Placebo: release dates shifted by 20-120 sessions.
registration.procedure: Turnover = Yahoo share volume / split-adjusted SEC cover shares known before the session (dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding at its acceptance). Market turnover = summed member volume / summed member shares. SUV = (residual on D-1 + residual on D) / (residual s.d. x sqrt 2). The estimation window ends at D-6, which keeps the pre-release run-up out. Release dates are as in the PEAD row. Entry at the D+2 close, 60-session hold, SPY-adjusted. Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. Survivorship is reported as in T-394.

registration.pass: All of: spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; both halves positive; controlled slope > 0 with t >= 2; DSR > 0.95 over 4 trials (SUV or raw abnormal turnover, x a 20- or 60-session hold); real-date spread above the placebo's 95th percentile.

From 2019-06 on, the earnings 8-K can be identified in the archive as the XBRL 8-K accepted at most 1 day before each 10-Q/10-K (verified for AAPL, AMZN and GOOGL), but that gives only about 87 events. registration.claim: For AAPL, GOOGL and AMZN earnings releases 2011-2026 (8-K Item 2.02), a long stock position held from the close 11 sessions before the reaction session D to the close of D-1 (the last close before the after-close release) earns a higher QQQ-adjusted mean return when the name's Cboe VX index (VXAPL, VXGOG or VXAZN) at the entry close is in the top tercile of its own trailing 504-session distribution than when it is in the bottom tercile, net of 2 bp per side.
registration.statistic: Top-minus-bottom tercile mean of the 10-session QQQ-adjusted return in pp. Secondary: the pooled mean of all events and the slope on the VX percentile.
registration.null: Difference <= 0, tested with a bootstrap that resamples calendar quarters (all three names report in the same weeks), 10,000 draws, percentile-t.
registration.procedure: VX closes enter at 21:30 UTC. Terciles come from each name's own trailing 504 sessions ending at the entry close. Release dates come from data.sec.gov 8-K items, and from 2019-06 they are cross-checked against the archived XBRL 8-K accepted at most 1 day before each 10-Q/10-K. The realised date is treated as known at D-11; once confirmation dates are collected, any event whose date confirmation (company IR release) came after the entry close is dropped. Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. The VIX-tercile split is reported but is not a criterion. MDE stated before the run: about 1.4 pp at 80% power for about 63 events per tercile at a 4% per-event s.d.
registration.data: cboe-VXAPL-history, cboe-VXGOG-history, cboe-VXAZN-history, cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-AAPL, daily-history-GOOG, daily-history-AMZN, daily-history-QQQ, sec-submissions-b006/b020/b025/b033; to fetch: 8-K items for 4 CIKs
registration.pass: All of: difference > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; top-tercile mean > 0 after costs; both halves positive; placebo (the same rule on windows ending 30 sessions before each release) below the event difference. A pass on 3 names is a pilot, not a verdict on the cross-section.
registration.controls: Placebo windows with no release. One tercile threshold, one window. Costs 2 bp/side. QQQ adjustment. The deciding version runs on S&P 500 names with DoltHub iv_current histories (2019-2026), or forward on the capture box.

rows.notes: Three mega-caps are a thin, hindsight-selected sample, and the claim inherits the decay of the announcement premium. Run it only as a by-product of the IV-crush row (same data and dates). The cross-sectional test that could decide it depends on verifying DoltHub's single-stock volatility_history coverage. That is the cheaper unlock compared with waiting for the capture box.

rows.name: Pre-earnings long straddle: buy the implied-vol ramp, exit before the release

overlaps.note: Same T-3 to last-pre-release-close ATM straddle; blocked on historical chains.
Pre-earnings calendar that trades the same ramp.
Event calendar on implied/realised move.
Earnings-season dispersion; the COR1M arm of this candidate feeds it.
COR1M vs realised correlation; the sector-ETF proxy was biased.
Model-priced premia are not verdicts: flat VIX overstated quoted SPY premia by 17-79%.

learnings.finding: Model pricing at a flat vol index overstated quoted premia by 17-79%. Model-priced options results can only check a sign.

VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN are 30-day constant-maturity variance indices. The event sits inside the 30-day window throughout T-3..T-1, so the fixed-expiry ramp the trade earns is not observable in them. A model-priced ramp built from VX would be produced by the jump-variance model, not by data. The candidate's Arm A is therefore not a test of the claim.

DoltHub chain snapshots run at about 145 dates a year in 2020-23 and 175-244 a year in 2024-26, with bid, ask and IV. The same keyless source likely carries single-stock chains, which would make T-204's family historically testable on quoted prices for 2019-2026.
Half-spread costs (2.5%) and the structure of the position decide small-account options results; costs are not a footnote.
An event-blind 30-day IV under-prices event-day variance on gold, so how the event is priced matters. Single-stock IV is event-aware, which is why a ramp exists at all.

rows.missing_data: Quoted single-stock chains around past releases are missing; only 2026-10-14/15 are archived, for AAPL, NVDA and TSLA. Release dates (8-K items) are also missing. Free route: DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain for S&P 500 names 2019-2026 (verify single-name coverage first). Forward route: extend the capture box's CHAIN_SYMBOLS from 3 single stocks to the ML universe's ~30.

registration.claim: Over 2019-02 to 2026-10, for point-in-time S&P 500 members with DoltHub option-chain snapshots on both sessions, an ATM straddle in the first standard monthly expiry after an 8-K Item 2.02 release has a positive mean return on debit when bought at the snapshot ask on session D-3 (three sessions before the reaction session) and sold at the snapshot bid on the last session before the release.
registration.statistic: Mean per-event return on debit: (exit bid - entry ask) / entry ask. Secondary: the mean change in the expiry's ATM IV against theta, as % of debit.
registration.null: Mean <= 0, tested with a studentized bootstrap clustered by release week, 10,000 draws.
registration.procedure: Fetch DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain for the members. First verify single-stock coverage and the snapshot calendar, and drop rows flagged stale or backfilled after the next open. Before any return is computed, check Dolt quotes against the archived Cboe chains for AAPL, NVDA and TSLA on 2026-10-14/15 (provenance). Strike = the listed strike nearest the D-3 close, kept at exit. Events need snapshots on exactly D-3 and the last pre-release session. Snapshot gaps are calendar-driven, so the selection is independent of returns; report the share of events kept. Halves 2019-02..2022-12 and 2023-01..2026-10.
registration.data: fja-sp500-components, sec-submissions-b*, daily-history-<members>, cboe-VIX-history, options-chain-AAPL/NVDA/TSLA (provenance check); to fetch: DoltHub single-stock chains, 8-K items
registration.pass: All of: lower 95% bound of the mean net return > 0 with a point estimate > 1% of debit; both halves positive; placebo (same names, 2-session windows ending 15 sessions before a release, same expiry rule) below the event mean; no single release week contributing > 20% of total P&L.
registration.controls: Placebo non-event windows. Windows with a VIX change > 10% reported separately. One entry day (D-3); T-204's D-7 and D-10 variants count as trials if run. The cost is the quoted spread itself. The release date must be public at entry: S&P 500 dates are confirmed weeks ahead, and unconfirmed cases are flagged.

rows.notes: Drop Arm A (VX model-priced ramp): it is circular, for the constant-maturity reason above. Arm B (COR1M lower and falling in weeks 2-6 after quarter-end, 2007-2026) is testable now from cboe-COR1M-history alone. It is only a mechanism diagnostic for T-521/T-538, though: a pass makes no money, so it should not displace a real test. The higher-value action here is data, not this claim. A DoltHub single-stock chain fetch would unblock about ten blocked options theories (T-158, T-204-T-210, T-226, T-248, T-519, T-520) on quoted prices. GXZ's 3.34% per event is gross. Quoted ATM straddle spreads on S&P 500 names (often 1-3% of mid per side) can absorb most of it, hence the low prior.

rows.name: Earnings IV crush: implied event move exceeds realised move (short straddle held through the release)

overlaps.note: Realised/implied move ratio < 0.85 on captured chains.
Hold-through long straddle filtered on IM/HM, which is the mirror trade.
Short strangle through the release.
Iron condor through the release; the defined-risk form.
Reverse calendar through the release.
Covered-call overwrite through the release.
An event-blind flat VIX under-prices FOMC days; that claim, about the opposite sign of mispricing, was not supported over the full window.
An event-blind GVZ under-prices FOMC/CPI days on GLD. Single-stock VX is event-aware, so the sign can differ.
Model-priced structural option premia are measurable from archived vol indices.
Model-priced, so results must report sensitivity to the IV scale (rule 8).

learnings.finding: The volatility premium is real (DVOL above realised by about 5 vol points, t 2.8, positive every year 2021-2026), but the one-straddle form had a -88% month. Only a ladder tames it.
Defined risk at small size: the credit is kept 71% of the time, and wipes about one month in five erase 27 months of credit. Sharpe 0.37, not tradeable on $1,000.
The SPY variance premium appears in model-priced form: +0.24%/month at IV x 0.81, and the realised distribution is narrower than risk-neutral (T-135 supported).
The edges that survive are structural premia (variance risk premium, carry) and reference-price edges. An earnings event variance premium is in the first class.

The candidate's 'mean ln(realised/implied)' is biased toward 'implied > realised' even with no premium (E ln chi2_1 = -1.27). 'Share of |move| < implied move' has a null of about 0.68, not 0.5. So vendor claims that 70-75% of moves stay inside the implied move are consistent with no premium. Use variance sums instead.

learnings.source: signal map: Multifractal time / fat tails
learnings.finding: Earnings jumps are fat-tailed and cluster by name, so short-vol P&L is dominated by a few events; worst-case and concentration criteria are required.

rows.missing_data: Release dates before 2019-06 are missing. 2019-06 onward can be derived from archived XBRL 8-K/10-Q pairs: about 87 events, below min_n 150. Free fix: data.sec.gov submissions with 'items' for 4 CIKs (AAPL 320193, Google Inc. 1288776, Alphabet 1652044, AMZN 1018724), a handful of keyless calls. The deciding quoted arm needs DoltHub single-stock chains 2019-2026 or an extended capture-box CHAIN_SYMBOLS.

registration.claim: For AAPL, GOOGL and AMZN earnings releases 2011-2026 (8-K Item 2.02), the implied event-session variance at the last close before the release exceeds the realised squared log return from that close to the reaction-session close. IEV = (VX_pre^2 - VX_base^2) x 30/365 + VX_base^2/252, where VX_base is the name's Cboe VX close 10 sessions after its previous release, scaled by VIX_pre/VIX_base. Two things must hold: the pooled ratio sum(R^2)/sum(IEV) is below 1; and a MODEL-PRICED 30-day ATM straddle (Black-Scholes at VX), sold at the pre-release close and bought back at the reaction-session close at that close's VX, has a positive mean P&L per unit of premium after 2% of premium per side.
registration.statistic: Pooled variance ratio VR = sum R^2 / sum IEV. Secondary: mean MODEL-PRICED short-straddle P&L per unit of premium. Reported only: the share of events with |R| < sqrt(IEV) against its normal-null 0.68, the worst 5% of events, and the Reg-T max-loss path. Means of log ratios are not used (Jensen bias).
registration.null: VR >= 1 (no event premium) and straddle mean <= 0, tested with a percentile-t bootstrap that resamples calendar quarters (the three names report in the same weeks), 10,000 draws.
registration.procedure: Release dates come from data.sec.gov 8-K items, cross-checked from 2019-06 against the archived XBRL 8-K accepted at most 1 day before each 10-Q/10-K. The pre-release close is the last regular close before available_at; all three names report after the close. Information set (rule 12): the primary reading uses that day's 16:00 stock close and VX close, and the robustness reading uses the previous session's closes for both. If the two disagree on any criterion, the verdict is undecided, which matters because GOOGL and AMZN release around 16:00-16:05 ET. VX_base must come from at least 30 sessions before the release, and events less than 40 sessions after the previous one are dropped. The unscaled-baseline VR is reported, not a criterion. Straddle: K = S_pre, tau = 30/365 at entry and less the calendar days elapsed at exit, r = DTB3 continuous, dividend forward when an AAPL ex-date falls inside (rule 8). Use the share class whose options VXGOG references (verify GOOG vs GOOGL). Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026.
registration.data: cboe-VXAPL-history, cboe-VXGOG-history, cboe-VXAZN-history, cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-AAPL, daily-history-GOOG, daily-history-AMZN, fred-DTB3, daily-events-AAPL, sec-submissions-b006/b020/b025/b033; to fetch: 8-K items for 4 CIKs
registration.pass: All of: upper 95% bound of VR < 1; MODEL-PRICED straddle mean P&L > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; VR < 1 in both halves; no single event contributing more than 20% of total straddle P&L; the result holds at VX x 0.9. The worst-5% loss and max loss on Reg-T margin must be reported. A pass reads as 'sign confirmed', not funding: the deciding arm is quoted (DoltHub 2019-2026, or forward on the capture box).
registration.controls: Placebo: the same IEV construction on pseudo-events 25 sessions after each release, with no event inside, where VR should reflect only the ordinary 1-day VRP. Comparison with the name's non-event 1-day VRP (VX^2/252 vs R^2). Costs 2% of premium per side. One baseline rule, one exit, one entry.

rows.notes: This is the strongest candidate in the cluster. It belongs to the one class Mandel's learnings say survives (structural premia: variance risk premium), it uses the user's implied-vol, realised-vol and days-to-earnings variables, and it needs only a few free SEC calls on top of archived Cboe single-stock VX indices from 2011. Three cautions apply. First, three mega-caps were chosen in hindsight, and the AMZN/GOOGL tails (several 10%+ moves) dominate any P&L. Second, a model-priced pass must be confirmed on quotes before anything is sized. Third, the small-account form must be defined-risk (T-207's iron condor), and Hurst's condor result (one wipe in five erases most of the credit) is the base case to beat. Do the DoltHub single-stock chain verification in the same step: it turns T-248/T-205/T-206/T-207 into historical quoted tests for 2019-2026 instead of waiting about a year for the capture box.

rows.name: Earnings seasonality: firms announcing their seasonally strong quarter earn higher returns

overlaps.note: Same-calendar-month return seasonality on 14 ETFs: a price-based claim on a different variable; net -0.39%/month.
Built XBRL fundamentals from companyfacts; annual concepts only, survivor-limited.
Needs the same expected-announcer flag.

learnings.finding: Calendar-month return seasonality failed on ETFs 2004-2026. It is the closest Mandel test but a different (price) claim.
NetIncomeLoss and the F-score concepts are archived from annual forms only, so quarterly seasonality ranks need a re-fetch of 10-Q facts.
RFS 2017 publication, so the whole 2014-2026 window is near or after publication: expect roughly half the in-sample effect.
The mechanism (anchored forecasters) is an analyst/investor-error story with no sharper public reference behind it, which is the weaker edge class.

rows.missing_data: Quarterly as-filed NetIncomeLoss and EarningsPerShareDiluted from 10-Q facts are missing; free re-fetch of data.sec.gov companyfacts with those tags from every form. Q4 is derived as FY minus Q1-Q3, each value entering at its own acceptance. The expected-announcer month can use archived 10-Q/10-K acceptance months.

registration.claim: Over 2014-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 expected announcers (10-Q/10-K accepted in the same calendar month 12 months earlier), the top quintile by earnings-seasonality score outperforms the bottom quintile in the announcement month, net of 10 bp round trip. The score is the mean rank, among the four fiscal quarters of each of the prior 3 fiscal years, of the quarter now due, using as-filed XBRL quarterly NetIncomeLoss per diluted share.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly top-minus-bottom quintile spread (equal weight); FF5+UMD alpha with Newey-West t (lag 3).
registration.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
registration.procedure: Score formed at the last close of month m-1 from facts accepted before it. The fiscal quarter now due is inferred from the firm's fiscal calendar (period end of the m-12 filing + 12 months). Firms need all 12 prior quarters. Hold month m. Halves 2014-2019 and 2020-2026. Survivorship per rule 9. A 3-year lookback is primary; 4- and 5-year lookbacks count as trials.
registration.data: sec-companyfacts-b* (re-fetched quarterly tags), sec-submissions-b*, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<members>, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
registration.pass: All of: spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; both halves positive; DSR > 0.95 over the 3 lookbacks.
registration.controls: No price input to the signal. One quintile threshold. Costs 10 bp round trip. Placebo: the score for a randomly chosen other fiscal quarter of the same firm. 2020-2021 reported separately (pandemic seasonality breaks).

rows.notes: New to the registry and price-free, which suits the user's 'calendars (fiscal quarter)' and 'days until earnings' variables. But it needs a companyfacts re-fetch with more tags and has no post-publication replication. Bundle the re-fetch with the PEAD SUE tags so one fetch serves rows 1, 7 and any earnings-surprise conditioning later.

Needs the same prior-year release calendar.

learnings.source: web, from memory, not re-verified: Michaely, Rubin & Vedrashko (JFE 2016), 'Are Friday announcements special? Overcoming selection bias'

Inattention anomalies published in 2009 and 2018 are expected to have decayed, and S&P 500 names are the most-watched.
The archive keeps XBRL filings only. NT 10-Q/NT 10-K (Form 12b-25) are not XBRL, so they are absent, as are 8-K items.

registration.claim: Over 2012-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, a firm with no 8-K Item 2.02 filing by the close of session E+3 underperforms its sector SPDR from the E+3 close to the close of the session after its release, net of 10 bp per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short. E is the acceptance date of the same fiscal quarter's Item 2.02 one year earlier, plus 364 days.
registration.statistic: Mean per-event abnormal return (stock minus its GICS-sector SPDR) over the late window. Secondary: the same for NT 10-Q/NT 10-K notices (first open after acceptance to the 20th close) and for Friday or pre-holiday after-close releases signed by CAR(0,+1) and held 20 sessions.
registration.null: Mean >= 0, tested with a bootstrap clustered by the calendar week of E.
registration.procedure: The E+3 rule uses only last year's acceptance date and today's filing list, so it is point-in-time. Sector from the Wikipedia constituents table's GICS sector (current; flagged) or SIC from sec-submissions. Exit at the close of the session after the release, or at E+40 if there is still no release. Halves 2012-2018 and 2019-2026. Survivorship: late filers delist more, so report the unpriced share and the return it would need to flip the bound (T-394 style).
registration.data: sec-submissions-b* (with items and NT forms after re-fetch), fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, wikipedia-sp500-constituents, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY/XLC/XLRE
registration.pass: Both of: one-sided upper 95% bound of the net mean < 0 (the short earns); both halves negative. DSR > 0.95 over 3 trials (late E+3, NT notices, Friday after-close).
registration.controls: One lateness threshold (E+3), no grid. Baseline: on-time releasers of the same week, same window length. Costs 10 bp/side plus 1%/yr borrow. Shifted-calendar placebo: E moved by +/- 30 sessions.

rows.notes: The free proxy for the proprietary Wall Street Horizon date-revision data is the 'not yet filed by E+3' rule above, which uses only EDGAR. In S&P 500 names, delays are mostly calendar drift rather than bad news, which dilutes the signal. NT filings are rare, so the second arm may fall below min_n.

rows.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) predicts returns and earnings news

overlaps.note: Options-implied borrow as a short-sale-cost signal; the same mechanism (costly shorting pushes bad news into options).
Pre-earnings skew as an informed-flow signal.
Another public flow signal (short volume) that showed no anticipation in S&P 500 names.

learnings.finding: The capture box records per-expiry vol_calls/vol_puts and oi by side, but only for AAPL, NVDA and TSLA among single stocks (CHAIN_SYMBOLS), from 2026-10-14.
Informed flow is a pointer to a source, not a signal to follow. Copying it loses the fee at any delay.
Taker order flow over 5-30 minutes predicts nothing worth trading.
The OSAP replication is 1996-2010. Weekly turnover costs in a 30-name universe and post-publication decay leave a small expected net.
