registration.claim: Forward test, starting the first Friday after CHAIN_SYMBOLS is extended to the ML universe's roughly 30 optionable single stocks. Each Friday, the lowest tercile of O/S beats the highest tercile over the next week (Friday close to Friday close), net of 5 bp per side, with a mean weekly spread > 0. O/S = the 5-session sum of option contract volume x 100 (options-surface vol_calls + vol_puts summed over expiries) over 5-session share volume.
registration.statistic: Mean weekly low-minus-high tercile spread with Newey-West t (lag 2). Secondary event arm: O/S over D-5..D-1 before releases, regressed on CAR(0,+1).
registration.procedure: Captures run after the close (18:30 ET), so a day's option volume is available that evening and the Friday signal trades at the next Friday... no: it uses volume through Thursday and trades at Friday's close. The read date is fixed at the 52nd weekly formation (about one year after the extension). The event arm is read at 150 releases. Nothing is read before those dates.
registration.data: options-surface-* (forward capture), daily-history-<symbols> or ml_data daily bars, sec-submissions-b* for release dates
registration.pass: All of: mean weekly spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 at the read date; DSR > 0.95 over 2 variants (all volume vs puts only); both 26-week halves positive.
registration.controls: One tercile threshold. Costs 5 bp/side. A sector-neutral version is reported. If OCC historical per-symbol volume is verified as free, run 2015-2026 on point-in-time S&P 500 members first and use the forward record as the confirmation.

rows.notes: The forward route has two prerequisites: extend CHAIN_SYMBOLS on the capture box, which also serves rows 4-6, and get a historical volume source. Neither is in hand. A 30-name tercile sort has about 10 names per leg, so expect low power even at 52 weeks.

rows.name: Pre-earnings abnormal short volume (FINRA Reg SHO) and long-window shorting flows

overlaps.note: Same FINRA CNMS ratio and point-in-time S&P 500 machinery. Spike events (z > 2): +0.7 bp gross 5-day, no signal. This candidate adds an earnings conditioning (Arm A) and a monthly level sort (Arm B).
DTC deciles: survivor-only net -0.05% per period.
DTC as a lending-fee proxy; survivor-only.
Aggregate short interest.

learnings.finding: 23,101 abnormal-SVR events on point-in-time S&P 500 members 2019-2026, 93.4% priced: +0.7 bp gross 5-day abnormal return. This matches Wang-Yan-Zheng's finding that public-era abnormal shorting does not anticipate news.
Short interest: 110 bi-monthly observations, t -0.6.
Short-interest features carry about zero IC in the swing models, with 0 of 306 cells passing.

In the payment-for-order-flow era, off-exchange short volume in large caps is largely wholesalers selling short against retail buys. A high ratio can therefore mean retail buying, which Boehmer-Jones-Zhang-Zhang find predicts positive returns. The registered sign is a genuine bet, not a given.

rows.missing_data: None for Arm B, the monthly level sort registered here. Arm A (the pre-release event version) needs 8-K Item 2.02 dates (free items re-fetch), and its registered expectation is a null.

registration.claim: Over 2018-11 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, light-minus-heavy shorted names earn a positive mean monthly return, net of 10 bp round trip per leg and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. At each month-end, members are sorted into quintiles of their trailing 60-file-day mean off-exchange short-volume ratio (FINRA CNMS short_volume / total_volume). The bottom quintile minus the top quintile is held from the close of the first session of the next month to the close of the first session of the month after.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly equal-weighted spread (bottom minus top SVR quintile). Value-weighted spread and FF5+UMD alpha (Newey-West lag 6) are secondary criteria.
registration.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the monthly spread (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
registration.procedure: SVR per symbol-day sums all CNMS facilities, using FINRA spellings mapped to members as in T-394. A day's file is available at the end of the trade day (UTC), so the signal at the last session of month m uses files through that session and trades at the next session's close. A name needs at least 40 of 60 file days. VW uses point-in-time caps from SEC cover shares (T-393 rules); names without a usable cap are left out of VW and counted. Halves 2018-11..2022-09 and 2022-10..2026-09. Jan-Mar 2021 reported excluded as a sensitivity. Survivorship: report unpriced member-months and the spread they would need to flip the lower bound.
registration.data: finra-regsho-cnms-*, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, wikipedia-sp500-changes, sec-companyfacts-b*, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
registration.pass: All of: EW spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; VW spread > 0; FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; both halves positive; DSR > 0.95 over 4 trials (EW/VW x 60/20-file-day window); unpriced member-months unable to flip the lower bound at a plausible mean. A significantly negative spread is not_supported, not a reversal.
registration.controls: Baseline: the same sort on the 60-day level of total (not short) volume as a share of shares outstanding, to separate shorting from turnover. Sector-neutral version reported. One quintile threshold. Costs as stated. The T-394 machinery and spellings are reused unchanged.

rows.notes: This is testable today on archived bundles with existing machinery, and it tests the user's 'short volume' variable in the form Wang-Yan-Zheng found persistent (the level, not the spike). The one cheap, untested sibling of T-394. The prior is low: the effect was measured in 2010-2015 across all stocks, and in large caps the ratio is contaminated by wholesaler shorting against retail buys, which may flip the sign. Arm A, conditioned on earnings, is a registered null and can wait for the 8-K items fetch.

rows.name: Analyst earnings-forecast revision momentum

overlaps.note: Same top-minus-bottom FY1 revision decile with a 1-month hold. Blocked: no free point-in-time consensus, and Yahoo quoteSummary returns 401 without a crumb.

learnings.finding: A consensus of sources the crowd already reads is not a leading reference. On 1,048 settled matches it carried no information beyond the price. Sell-side consensus is a read-by-everyone source of that kind.

rows.name: Post-earnings announcement drift (SUE / announcement-return sort), large-cap vs microcap split
rows.source_notes: Martineau CFR draft read (pdftotext). Its abstract says: 'For large stocks, PEAD have been non-existent since 2006 but has only disappeared recently for microcap stocks.' The UCLA Anderson Review page confirms Subrahmanyam (2025 WP, Feb 2001-Dec 2024): t=2.18 for all stocks and t=1.43 excluding microcaps (bottom 20% of NYSE cap, about 3% of market value). It also confirms Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang (RFS 2025) report t of about 14 without a microcap filter. The Griffin-McInnis-Zhao JAAF 2026 title and authors are confirmed, but no abstract was available. OSAP SignalDoc confirms AnnouncementReturn (Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok 1996, 1977-1992, t 9.25). That t is the original paper's figure as recorded in SignalDoc, not an OSAP replication t, so 'OSAP replicates' overstates it. Bernard-Thomas magnitudes and Chordia et al. (2014) were not re-checked. The shared web-search budget was exhausted mid-task, so no further failed-replication searches were possible.
rows.replication_concerns: Large-cap drift has been absent since about 2006 (Martineau). The surviving positive estimates come from microcaps or from designs that do not filter them (Subrahmanyam). Hurst's own 2015-2026 small-cap PEAD was killed by its placebo (+1.77%/month for a placebo entry 25 sessions late vs +1.32% for the real entry), so price-path selection and survivorship produce 'drift' in current-listing panels. A CAR sort is a price-based signal, which starts from a negative base rate per the child learnings.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: sec-submissions b000..b043 cover 9,133 CIKs (all 'ok'), but every archived filing has is_xbrl=1 and no 'items' field. AAPL's 8-Ks appear once in 2017-08 and then only from 2019, so Item 2.02 cannot be identified from the archive. fja-sp500-components and ticker-spells, wikipedia-sp500-changes (412 rows) and sec-cik-lookup exist. french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily end 2026-08-31, so any FF5+UMD alpha stops there. The 901-symbol daily-history is today's universe and survivor-biased. The point-in-time S&P 500 universe priced 82-93% in T-334 and T-394.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) CAR(D-1..D+1) is known only at the D+1 close, so entry must be at D+1 or later (D+2 is fine). (2) The 8-K acceptance can trail the press-release wire by minutes to hours, and Item 2.02 allows up to 4 business days. An 8-K accepted during or after the reaction session misassigns D. Require acceptance before the next 09:30 open of the wire day, or flag and drop. (3) Membership must come from fja point-in-time spells, never the current Wikipedia list. (4) Yahoo drops delisted names and reuses tickers (refuse on identity, as T-394 does). (5) French factors are revised, so record the file date.
rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 release datetimes need a data.sec.gov submissions re-fetch keeping 'items' and non-XBRL forms for the roughly 1,100 historical S&P 500 CIKs. It is free and keyless, and it is shared with rows 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and the ML program's event calendar. The SUE arm additionally needs quarterly as-filed EPS or NetIncomeLoss, which are archived from 10-K forms only.

final.claim: Amendment to T-338's large-cap control arm, not a new trial. Over 2011-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, a dollar-neutral portfolio is long the top and short the bottom decile of the SPY-adjusted CAR(D-1..D+1) around each 8-K Item 2.02 release, where D is the first regular session whose 09:30 open follows the release's acceptance. It enters at the D+2 close and holds 60 sessions. The claim is that it earns a positive calendar-time mean daily return net of 10 bp per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. The registered expectation is a null (Martineau 2022).
final.statistic: Mean calendar-time daily long-short return (equal weight across open cohorts) in bp/day; FF5+UMD alpha with Newey-West t (lag 60) through 2026-08.
final.null: Mean <= 0. Tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily series (block 126 sessions, 5,000 draws). Placebo: each firm's release dates shifted by a uniform random 20-120 sessions, 1,000 shifts.
final.procedure: Releases are 8-Ks whose re-fetched 'items' include 2.02. available_at = acceptance. Events whose acceptance falls after the first regular session following the filing date are dropped and counted. CIKs map to point-in-time members via fja spells and the SEC CIK tables (T-393/T-451 machinery). CAR uses adjusted Yahoo closes minus SPY. Decile breakpoints come from the trailing 63 sessions of releases (at least 50 required). Halves are 2011-2018 and 2019-2026, with 2020-03..06 reported separately. Survivorship (rule 9): report the share of member releases without prices and the mean 60-session return they would need to flip the bootstrap bound. If |x| < 500 bp flips it, the verdict is inconclusive.
