rows.name: Earnings-day unexplained volume predicts post-announcement returns (opinion-divergence / high-volume premium at earnings)
rows.source_notes: Garfinkel-Sokobin JAR 2006 PDF read (pdftotext). Sample: NYSE/AMEX, Jan 1985-Jul 1998, 45,187 announcements. Event window [t-1, t], control window [t-54, t-5], drift = size-adjusted [t+1, t+60]. The market-adjusted turnover change (TO, eq. 2) gives high +1.386% vs low -0.070% (t = 9.49). SUV gives high +1.415% vs low -0.220%. The relation holds controlling for the earnings surprise and in size subsamples; the one exception is a medium-size SUV specification, positive but insignificant. Correction 1: GS's SUV regresses log volume on |R+| and |R-| over [t-54, t-5], so it uses the stock's own price moves as an input. The price-free measure is TO, the abnormal market-adjusted turnover. Correction 2: the cross-checker's 'log-turnover market model' matches neither GS measure. The NYU 2008 working paper was not opened, and no post-2000 replication could be searched because the web-search budget was exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-decimalisation replication was found. Mandel's non-earnings high-volume premium failed on ETFs (T-419: +21 bp against a 50 bp bar) and crypto alts (T-546). ML T-578 relative-volume features give IC of about +0.01. The mechanism needs binding short-sale constraints, which are slack in S&P 500 names. GS's sample is pre-2000 NYSE/AMEX, including small firms.
rows.data_notes: Volume comes from daily-history (Yahoo split-adjusted OHLCV) for point-in-time members (93.4% of T-394 member events priced). dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding is archived from 10-Q and 10-K forms with filed dates (b006: 1,745 10-Q and 568 10-K rows), and daily-events split ratios are archived. Release dates are missing; they need the shared 8-K items re-fetch. French factors end 2026-08-31.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Session-D consolidated volume is final only after the close (late prints), so no entry at the D close. CAR(D-1..D+1) is known at the D+1 close, so enter at the D+2 close. (2) Yahoo volume is split-adjusted retroactively while SEC cover shares are as filed, so adjust shares with daily-events split factors between the cover date and each session. (3) Cover shares are dated at the cover date but usable only from acceptance. (4) Market turnover is computed from priced members only (survivor), so report coverage. (5) Decile breakpoints come from the previous calendar quarter only. (6) The 8-K acceptance vs wire-time trap is the same as in row 1.
rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance datetimes (free data.sec.gov submissions re-fetch with 'items'). Everything else is archived.

final.claim: Over 2011-2026, take point-in-time S&P 500 members' 8-K Item 2.02 releases and compute GS's price-free abnormal-turnover change dTO for each. Events in the top decile of dTO beat bottom-decile events in a dollar-neutral calendar-time portfolio, entered at the D+2 close and held 60 sessions, net of 10 bp per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. dTO = mean market-adjusted turnover over sessions D-1..D minus its mean over D-54..D-5, with deciles from the previous calendar quarter's releases.
final.statistic: Mean calendar-time daily top-minus-bottom dTO-decile return in bp/day. Secondary: the pooled event-level slope of the 60-session SPY-adjusted return (D+2 close to D+62 close) on dTO decile rank, controlling for CAR(D-1..D+1), momentum over D-61..D-2 and log market cap, with t clustered by release week.
final.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily spread (block 126 sessions, 5,000 draws). Placebo: each firm's release dates shifted by uniform 20-120 sessions, 1,000 shifts.
final.procedure: D = the first NYSE session whose 09:30 open follows the 8-K acceptance. Market-adjusted turnover MAT(i,t) = V(i,t)/S(i,t) - sum(V)/sum(S) over priced members that day. V is Yahoo share volume. S is the latest dei cover shares accepted before session t, split-adjusted with daily-events. dTO follows GS eq. 2 exactly; no price or return enters the signal. Long top decile, short bottom decile, equal weight; positions open at the D+2 close and close 60 sessions later. The market leg cancels in a dollar-neutral book. Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026, with 2020-03..06 reported separately. Survivorship is reported as in T-394 (unpriced member releases and the spread they would need to flip the bound).
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-submissions-b*, sec-companyfacts-b*, daily-events-<members>, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily; to fetch: 8-K items
final.pass: All of: spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; both halves positive; controlled slope > 0 with t >= 2; real-date spread above the placebo's 95th percentile; survivorship unable to flip the lower bound; DSR > 0.95 over 2 trials (dTO, plus GS's SUV variant if it is ever run).
final.controls: Baseline: the same dTO sort on non-event pseudo-dates for the same firms (the single-stock analogue of T-419), reported to separate an earnings effect from the general high-volume premium. One window pair (GS's), one decile threshold, one 60-session hold. Costs 10 bp/side plus 1%/yr borrow. No fitted parameters.

rows.reason: Novel and directly tests the volume and shares-outstanding variables at the event where the literature says volume is informative. The design was corrected to GS's price-free dTO with GS's own windows. The cross-checker's hybrid 'turnover market model', which is neither GS measure, is dropped, and the trial count is cut to one primary.

rows.name: Earnings announcement premium (expected announcers outperform), US decay after the 2004 8-K rule
rows.source_notes: Heitz-Narayanamoorthy-Zekhnini, confirmed only through the paperswithbacktest summary: 'this premium has disappeared from the US markets in recent years'. The summary ties this to the 2004 Form 8-K rule, says the premium 'appears to have shifted ... to 8-K filing periods', and says it is robust internationally. No magnitudes or sample period were given. Savor-Wilson 2011 draft read (pdftotext): the 1974-2009 announcer-minus-non-announcer weekly portfolio earns EW +0.39%/week (t 14.31, about 20%/yr) and VW +0.23%/week (t 5.67). The candidate's '9.9% annualised' is not in the draft and may come from the JF 2016 version, which was not verified. Frazzini-Lamont and the PBFJ 2023 paper were not opened; the search budget was exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: The published premium is weekly. A monthly expected-announcer design spreads it over about 4.3 weeks, so the spread is diluted. The US post-2004 null is the pre-registered expectation. Mandel's own scheduled-announcement premia (T-341, T-343) decayed after publication.
rows.data_notes: 10-Q and 10-K acceptances are archived for 9,133 CIKs from 2009 (b006 forms: 1,948 10-Q, 638 10-K, 2,922 XBRL 8-K). 8-K items are absent. Design flaw found: the cross-checker's 10-Q/10-K-month proxy does not equal the announcement month for many S&P 500 firms. The 10-Q is filed days to weeks after the release. The 10-K can be filed up to 60 days after fiscal year-end, so Q4 releases in late January commonly pair with February 10-Ks. That arm therefore tests a filing-month premium, and a null on it says nothing about the claim. Fama-French factors end 2026-08-31.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) The flag uses only m-12 acceptances (known 11 or more months ahead), so it is point-in-time. (2) Membership is taken at the m-1 close from fja spells. (3) VW caps use SEC cover shares at acceptance (T-393 rules) with split adjustment. (4) Survivorship: unpriced members per rule 9. (5) Firms that change fiscal calendars are misflagged, which adds noise toward zero; this is stated in advance.
rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance months from the free submissions re-fetch with 'items' (shared). The 10-Q-month proxy can run today only as a labelled diagnostic, never as the trial.

final.claim: Over 2011-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, expected announcers earn a higher equal-weighted return in calendar month m than the other members, net of 10 bp per leg per month. An expected announcer is a firm with an 8-K whose items include 2.02 accepted in calendar month m-12. The registered expectation is no premium (Heitz-Narayanamoorthy-Zekhnini, post-2004).
final.statistic: Mean monthly EW spread (expected announcers minus the rest) in bp, with Newey-West t (lag 3). VW spread is secondary.
final.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the monthly spread (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
final.procedure: Membership at the last close of month m-1 (fja). Flag from re-fetched submissions: an 8-K whose items include 2.02, accepted in month m-12, with amendments excluded. Returns are close-to-close over month m from adjusted Yahoo closes. VW uses point-in-time caps from SEC cover shares; names without a usable cap are left out of VW and counted. Halves 2011-01..2018-10 and 2018-11..2026-09, with 2020 reported separately. Diagnostic only (not a criterion, runnable today): the same spread with the 10-Q/10-K-month proxy, plus that proxy's agreement rate with the 8-K month once the fetch lands. Survivorship per rule 9.
final.data: sec-submissions-b000..b043, sec-companyfacts-b*, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-cik-lookup, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY; to fetch: 8-K items
final.pass: All of: EW spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; VW spread > 0; both halves positive; DSR > 0.95 counting T-339's 5 declared variants plus this one. Otherwise not_supported, or inconclusive when unpriced members could flip the bound.
final.controls: The flag uses filing dates only, never prices. One threshold (month m-12). Costs 0.10% per leg per month at an assumed 100% turnover. The weekly-to-monthly dilution and the fiscal-calendar change noise are stated in advance as biases toward zero.

rows.reason: Same claim as T-339, but the design differs materially: a point-in-time S&P 500 universe and the SEC 8-K calendar replace the survivor-only Nasdaq calendar that blocked T-339. The cross-checker's 10-Q-month proxy was demoted to a diagnostic because the filing month is not the announcement month for a large share of releases, especially Q4.

rows.name: Pre-announcement run-up conditional on option-implied uncertainty (uncertainty resolution before earnings)
rows.source_notes: Quantpedia summary of Gao, Hu, Zhang, 'Uncertainty Resolution Before Earnings Announcements'. Confirmed: 71% of the earnings announcement premium is earned before release; the 10-day pre-window averages 0.31% of the 21-day window's 0.42%. Stocks are sorted on option IV at 11 days before the announcement. The high-IV group earns +1.52% market-adjusted over 10 days with a 1.8% drop in uncertainty. The low-IV group shows no significant return and its uncertainty rises 5.1%. The sample period is not stated on the page, the paper is a working paper, and costs are not given. No replication could be searched (budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication. The claim inherits the post-2004 decay of the announcement premium (Heitz et al.). Raw IV-level sorts are mostly volatility and beta sorts, so in a 10-day window high-minus-low loads on (beta - 1) x market return unless placebo windows net it out. The cross-checker's 3-name VX pilot has, by its own statement, an MDE (about 1.4 pp) roughly equal to the claimed effect, on three hindsight-selected mega-caps. A pass there would carry no weight and a null would refute nothing.
rows.data_notes: The pilot's data exist: cboe-VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN run 2011-01-07..2026-10-14 (3,961 rows each), and daily-history AAPL, GOOG, GOOGL, AMZN and QQQ are archived. The deciding cross-sectional data are not archived. dolt-volhistory holds only GLD, IWM, QQQ, SLV and SPY. Single-stock coverage of DoltHub post-no-preference/options volatility_history is unverified, and its snapshot calendar is sparse (about 145-244 dates a year in the SPY chain bundle).
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) The IV snapshot must have quote_date <= D-11. Dolt snapshot_date is not quote_date, and the archive's own quote_date rules must be reused. (2) Use the latest snapshot in D-13..D-11, never later. (3) The release date must have been public at entry; S&P 500 dates are typically confirmed weeks ahead, and unconfirmed cases are flagged. (4) Breakpoints come from trailing events only. (5) The exit at the D-1 close must precede the release (BMO releases make D-1 the prior session). (6) The 8-K acceptance vs wire-time issue is as in row 1.
rows.missing_data: Two prerequisites: (a) the shared 8-K Item 2.02 items fetch; (b) verifying single-stock coverage of DoltHub volatility_history (iv_current) for point-in-time S&P 500 members 2019-2026, then fetching it. If (b) fails, park the claim rather than registering the underpowered 3-name pilot. The capture box's options-surface atm_iv covers only AAPL, NVDA and TSLA among single stocks.

final.claim: Over 2019-02 to 2026-09, take point-in-time S&P 500 members' 8-K Item 2.02 releases. Events in the top tercile of DoltHub iv_current observed at the D-11 close earn a higher SPY-adjusted 10-session return (close D-11 to close D-1, the last close before the release) than bottom-tercile events, net of 10 bp per side. The same top-minus-bottom difference measured on placebo windows (close D-41 to close D-31) for the same events must be smaller. Terciles come from the trailing 63 sessions of events.
final.statistic: Difference-in-differences: (top minus bottom tercile mean 10-session SPY-adjusted return in the pre-release window) minus (the same in the placebo window), in pp. Secondary: the event-window top-minus-bottom spread and the top-tercile mean net of costs.
final.null: DiD <= 0, tested with a bootstrap clustered by release week, 10,000 draws, percentile-t.
final.procedure: D = the first NYSE session whose 09:30 open follows the 8-K acceptance. IV = iv_current from the latest Dolt snapshot whose verified quote_date is in D-13..D-11. Events without one are dropped and counted; this selection is calendar-driven and unrelated to returns. Tercile breakpoints come from the iv_current values of the previous 63 sessions' events (at least 150). Halves 2019-02..2022-12 and 2023-01..2026-09. The VIX-tercile split is reported only. MDE stated before the run, from the event count and the per-event s.d.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-submissions-b*, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history; to fetch: DoltHub volatility_history for members (coverage to verify), 8-K items
final.pass: All of: DiD > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; top-tercile event-window mean > 0 after costs; both halves DiD > 0; survivorship unable to flip the bound (rule 9).
final.controls: Placebo windows on the same events net out beta, volatility and sector loadings. One tercile threshold, one window, one IV source. Costs 10 bp/side. The 3-name VX pilot is not registered: it is underpowered by its own MDE and hindsight-selected.

rows.reason: Novel, and it uses the implied-vol and days-to-earnings variables. The cross-checker's 3-name pilot cannot decide anything by its own power calculation. The registration was moved to a cross-sectional design with a placebo difference-in-differences that removes the beta and volatility confound of raw IV sorts, conditional on verifying DoltHub single-stock IV coverage.

rows.name: Pre-earnings long straddle: buy the implied-vol ramp, exit before the release
rows.source_notes: Cambridge abstract page confirms Gao, Xing, Zhang, JFQA 53(6) 2587-2617 (2018): single-stock straddles generally earn negative, significant returns, but ATM straddles held 'from 3 days before an earnings announcement through the announcement date' earn a highly significant 3.34%. Nuance: the hold runs through the announcement date. For BMO releases that includes the event, so 'exit at the last close before the release' is a stricter, purely pre-event variant of GXZ. The sample period is not on the page, and costs were not checked.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication. Quoted ATM straddle spreads on S&P 500 names (often 1-3% of mid per side) can absorb a gross 3.34%. The cross-checker correctly shows that Arm A (VX model-priced ramp) is circular: VX indices are 30-day constant-maturity, so the fixed-expiry ramp is not observable in them. Arm B (COR1M seasonality) is a mechanism diagnostic that earns nothing.
rows.data_notes: cboe-COR1M-history (2006-01-03..2026-10-14) exists. options-chain-AAPL, NVDA and TSLA exist for 2026-10-14/15 only. dolt-chain-SPY is archived, but DoltHub single-stock chain coverage is unverified. The 8-K items are missing.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Dolt snapshot_date vs quote_date: reuse the archive's parity-based quote_date rule. (2) Snapshots must exist on exactly D-3 and the last pre-release session, which is a calendar-driven selection. (3) The release date must be public at entry. (4) Stale or backfilled Dolt rows must be dropped. (5) Quotes should be checked against the archived Cboe chains on 2026-10-14/15 for provenance.
rows.missing_data: Historical quoted single-stock chains (DoltHub option_chain single-name coverage to verify) and the 8-K items fetch.

final.claim: Trial-data amendment to T-204, not a new trial. Over 2019-02 to 2026-10, for point-in-time S&P 500 members with DoltHub option-chain snapshots on both sessions, an ATM straddle in the first standard monthly expiry after an 8-K Item 2.02 release has a positive mean return on debit. It is bought at the snapshot ask on session D-3 and sold at the snapshot bid on the last session before the release.
final.statistic: Mean per-event return on debit: (exit bid - entry ask) / entry ask.
final.null: Mean <= 0, tested with a studentized bootstrap clustered by release week, 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: Verify Dolt single-stock coverage, the snapshot calendar and quote provenance against the archived Cboe chains for 2026-10-14/15 before computing any return. Strike = the listed strike nearest the D-3 close, held to exit. Events need snapshots on both sessions; report the share kept. Halves 2019-02..2022-12 and 2023-01..2026-10.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, sec-submissions-b*, daily-history-<members>, cboe-VIX-history, options-chain-AAPL/NVDA/TSLA (provenance); to fetch: DoltHub single-stock option_chain, 8-K items
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the mean net return > 0 with point estimate > 1% of debit; both halves positive; placebo windows (2 sessions ending 15 sessions before a release, same expiry rule) below the event mean; no release week > 20% of total P&L.
final.controls: Placebo non-event windows. One entry day (D-3). The cost is the full quoted spread. Windows with a VIX change > 10% reported separately.

rows.reason: Same claim as T-204 (same entry, exit and expiry rule). Only the data source changes from forward capture to historical DoltHub quotes, which is a trial-data amendment to T-204, not a new registration. Arm A is circular (constant-maturity VX), and the COR1M arm is a no-money diagnostic.

rows.name: Earnings IV crush: implied event move exceeds realised move (short straddle held through the release)
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck, Seeger, RFS 32(2) 646-687 (2019). The abstract says only that anticipated earnings uncertainty is large, time-varying and informative about future volatility. The NYU 2017 conference slides (pdftotext) confirm the rest: OptionMetrics data after 2000, the 50 most actively traded firms by option dollar volume each year, 'Uniform evidence that implied EAD jump volatility is greater than subsequent return volatility (Qvol>Pvol)', and 'Straddle returns are highly significant: -8%/EAD'. That -8% is gross at close prices; spreads are not netted. The EarningsWatcher vendor beat rates were not re-opened; they are unverified vendor figures.
rows.replication_concerns: Direction is consistent, but the premium is short-vol with fat right-tail losses that cluster by name. No 2015-2026 quoted-spread study was found (search budget exhausted). Three mega-caps were chosen because they have Cboe VX indices, a hindsight-selected sample of the most liquid names, where the premium may be smaller. Small-account form: naked short straddles are generally not available at small-account option levels on retail brokers such as Alpaca (spreads only, to be verified). The executable form is therefore T-207's defined-risk condor or butterfly, where Hurst's IBIT condor (one wipe in five erases most of the credit) is the base case.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: cboe-VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN run 2011-01-07..2026-10-14 (3,961 rows each). cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3 and daily-history AAPL (11,552 rows), GOOG, GOOGL (5,574 each) and AMZN (7,400) are archived, as is daily-events-AAPL. The archived XBRL 8-Ks for AAPL begin 2017-08 (then 2019+), so release dates before 2019 need the 4-CIK items fetch (320193, 1288776, 1652044, 1018724). Expected events: about 63 per name over 2011-2026, about 185 after the first base window.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) GOOGL and AMZN release around 16:00-16:05 ET. If Cboe's VX close reflects quotes after the release, VX_pre leaks the event; the previous-session information-set robustness reading is mandatory. (2) VX_base must come from 10 sessions after the previous release, never the post-event IV of the current one. (3) Use the 8-K acceptance vs wire time to set the pre-release close. (4) VXGOG references one Google share class (verify GOOG vs GOOGL; pre-2014-04 history is the old class A). (5) Use split- and dividend-adjusted closes (AAPL ex-dates often fall the week after earnings). (6) Do not use mean ln(realised/implied) (Jensen bias, E ln chi2_1 = -1.27). The 'share inside the implied move' null is 0.683, not 0.5.
rows.missing_data: Release datetimes 2011-2019 for 4 CIKs: a handful of keyless data.sec.gov calls with 'items'. The deciding quoted arm needs DoltHub single-stock chains 2019-2026 (unverified) or a capture-box CHAIN_SYMBOLS extension.

final.claim: For AAPL, GOOG(L) and AMZN quarterly earnings releases 2011-04 to 2026-10 (8-K Item 2.02), the pooled variance ratio VR = sum(R^2) / sum(IEV) is below 1. Definitions: R = ln(C_react / C_pre). C_pre = the last regular-session close before the 8-K acceptance. C_react = the close of the first session whose 09:30 open follows it. IEV = (VX_pre^2 - VXb^2) x 30/365 + VXb^2/252, with all VX values in decimal annualised terms. VX_pre is the name's Cboe VX close at C_pre. VXb = the VX close 10 sessions after the name's previous release, times VIX_pre/VIX_b. That is, option-implied event-session variance exceeds realised variance.
final.statistic: Pooled VR = sum R^2 / sum IEV. Reported only: the jump-only ratio sum(R^2 - VXb^2/252) / sum((VX_pre^2 - VXb^2) x 30/365); per-name VR; the share of events with |R| < sqrt(IEV) against its normal-null 0.683; the worst 5% of events; and a MODEL-PRICED short iron butterfly diagnostic (wings at 2 x sqrt(IEV)), clearly labelled not a verdict.
final.null: VR >= 1, tested with a percentile bootstrap of the ratio of sums that resamples calendar quarters (the three names report in the same weeks), 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: Release datetimes come from data.sec.gov 8-K items for the 4 CIKs, cross-checked from 2019-06 against the archived XBRL 8-Ks. Primary information set: the C_pre close and the same-day VX and VIX closes. Robustness set: the previous session's VX and VIX with R measured from that session's close. If the two sets disagree on the pass rule, the verdict is undecided. Drop events less than 40 sessions after the previous release, and events whose VX_b is not at least 30 sessions before the release. No flooring of negative jump variance. Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026.
final.data: cboe-VXAPL-history, cboe-VXGOG-history, cboe-VXAZN-history, cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-AAPL, daily-history-GOOG, daily-history-GOOGL, daily-history-AMZN, daily-events-AAPL, fred-DTB3 (diagnostic only); to fetch: 8-K items for CIKs 320193, 1288776, 1652044, 1018724
final.pass: All of: one-sided upper 95% bound of VR < 1; VR < 1 in both halves; point VR < 1 for each of the three names; the same conclusion under the robustness information set. A pass reads 'event variance premium confirmed on three mega-caps'. It is not funding: the deciding arm is quoted (DoltHub 2019-2026 or the capture box) in T-207's defined-risk form.
final.controls: Baseline reported, not a criterion: the ordinary 1-session VRP on non-event days 10-40 sessions after each release (sum R^2 vs sum VX^2/252), to show the event part exceeds the generic VRP. One baseline rule, one VIX scaling rule, one window. No costs enter VR. The model-priced structure diagnostic uses 2% of premium per side and reports the Reg-T max loss.

rows.reason: The strongest candidate in the cluster: a structural variance premium, the class Mandel's learnings say survives, testable from archived Cboe single-stock VX after about four free SEC calls. It is related to T-248 and T-205-T-207 but differs materially: it is a model-free historical 2011-2026 measurement rather than forward chain captures. It was fixed to a single model-free criterion (VR), with the model-priced straddle demoted to a labelled diagnostic and a mandatory information-set robustness reading for the 16:00-16:05 releases.

rows.name: Earnings seasonality: firms announcing their seasonally strong quarter earn higher returns
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon, Soltes, RFS 30(1) 281-323 (2017; received June 2014). The HLS summary confirms the magnitudes: highest-seasonality quintile 65 bps/month vs 31 bps for the lowest (four-factor) in announcement months, the difference significant at 1%, and 55 bps value-weighted ('stronger'). Neither page gives the sample period or the lookback length. The 20-quarter (5-year) ranking used below is from memory and must be checked against the paper before registration. No post-publication replication could be searched (budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: No replication found. The whole feasible window (2014+) is at or after the SSRN posting, so expect roughly half the effect (McLean-Pontiff). The mechanism is analyst and investor error with no sharper reference, the weaker edge class. The closest Mandel test, T-476, is price-based return seasonality on ETFs and failed, but it is a different claim.
rows.data_notes: sec-companyfacts archives NetIncomeLoss from 10-K forms only (b006: 4,110 10-K rows, no 10-Q rows) and no EarningsPerShareDiluted. WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding is archived. The quarterly 10-Q NetIncomeLoss facts need a free re-fetch of the same companyfacts endpoint keeping every form. Expected-announcer months need the 8-K items fetch. XBRL begins 2009-2010 for large filers, so 20 prior quarters are available from about 2014-06.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Each quarterly value enters at its own accession's acceptance. Q4 = FY minus 9-month YTD, available only at 10-K acceptance. Never use later restatements (filter facts to the accession that first reported the period). (2) The fiscal quarter now due is inferred from the m-12 release's period end + 12 months. (3) The score is formed at the m-1 close from facts accepted before it. (4) Membership is point-in-time. (5) Survivorship per rule 9.
rows.missing_data: Quarterly as-filed NetIncomeLoss (and diluted weighted shares by quarter) from 10-Q facts via a companyfacts re-fetch, plus the 8-K Item 2.02 items fetch for the expected-announcer month. Both are free, and both are shared with rows 1-3.

final.claim: Over 2014-06 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 expected announcers, the top quintile by earnings-seasonality score outperforms the bottom quintile in the announcement month, net of 10 bp round trip. An expected announcer is a firm with an 8-K Item 2.02 accepted in the same calendar month 12 months earlier. The score is the mean rank, within the firm's prior 20 fiscal quarters of as-filed quarterly net income per diluted share, of the 5 quarters that share the fiscal quarter now due.
final.statistic: Mean monthly top-minus-bottom quintile spread (equal weight); FF5+UMD alpha with Newey-West t (lag 3) through 2026-08.
final.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
final.procedure: Quarterly NI per diluted share = NetIncomeLoss / WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding for that 3-month period. Q2 and Q3 come from YTD differences where only YTD is tagged, and Q4 = FY - 9M. Each value enters at its first accession's acceptance. Firms need all 20 prior quarters. Form at the last close of month m-1 and hold month m. Halves 2014-06..2020-06 and 2020-07..2026-09, with 2020-2021 reported separately. Survivorship per rule 9.
final.data: sec-companyfacts-b* (re-fetched with 10-Q NetIncomeLoss), sec-submissions-b* (re-fetched with items), fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<members>, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
final.pass: All of: spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; both halves positive; survivorship unable to flip the bound.
final.controls: No price input to the signal. One lookback (20 quarters), one quintile threshold. Costs 10 bp round trip. Placebo: the score computed for a randomly chosen other fiscal quarter of the same firm (it should earn nothing).

rows.reason: Novel and price-free, and it fits the calendar and fiscal-quarter variables. It was fixed to a single lookback with no 3-lookback DSR grid, given restatement-free as-filed rules, and made dependent on the shared SEC re-fetches. Without them, neither the score nor the announcement month can be built point-in-time.

rows.name: Earnings-date timing: late or delayed announcers (and Friday announcers) carry bad news the market prices late
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Johnson and So, JFQA 53(6) 2431-2464 (2018): firms that schedule later than expected report worse news, equities do not reflect it until the announcement, and option markets price the volatility timing. The Wall Street Horizon page confirms the vendor summary: advancers beat delayers by 260 bps the following month, about 19,000 companies over more than 8 years. That figure is unchecked against the JFQA text. The NBER page confirms DellaVigna-Pollet w11683 (JF 2009): 60% vs 40% delayed response for Friday releases, 10% lower volume, a 45% higher probability of a negative surprise and a 50 bp lower abnormal return. Michaely-Rubin-Vedrashko (JFE 2016, selection bias in Friday announcements) could not be verified: the web-search budget was exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: No out-of-sample replication found. Mandel's weekday attention test T-347 failed with halves flipping sign. S&P 500 names are the most watched. The free proxy (not yet released by expected date + k) fires weeks after the firm's public scheduling notice, which Johnson-So say equities ignore, so it can still capture the release reaction. For S&P 500 firms, many 'late' cases are calendar drift (52/53-week years, a Monday/Tuesday shift) rather than bad news.
rows.data_notes: The archive keeps XBRL filings only, so it has no 8-K items and no NT 10-Q/NT 10-K (Form 12b-25, non-XBRL). Both come from the free submissions re-fetch keeping items and all forms. Sector SPDRs XLB..XLY, XLC and XLRE are archived. The sector mapping is only available from current profiles (Wikipedia GICS or the SEC SIC current profile), a mild look-ahead. In S&P 500 names NT filings are rare, likely below min_n, so that arm is dropped.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) E uses only last year's acceptance plus 364 days, and the late flag uses only filings accepted by the E+k close, so it is point-in-time. (2) A 53-week fiscal year shifts a release by exactly 5 sessions, so k must exceed 5 to avoid flagging pure calendar drift. (3) The exit uses the reaction session, which is known only once the release arrives (the position stays open until then, with a cap). (4) Survivorship: late filers delist more, so apply the rule-9 flip test. (5) Current-sector classification is used only for a reported sensitivity.
rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance datetimes (free submissions re-fetch with 'items'; shared).

final.claim: Over 2012-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, a firm with no 8-K Item 2.02 accepted by the close of NYSE session E+7 underperforms SPY from the E+7 close to the close of its reaction session. E = last year's same-fiscal-quarter Item 2.02 acceptance date + 364 days. The reaction session is the first session whose 09:30 open follows the release. The exit is capped at E+40. The underperformance must survive 10 bp per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short.
final.statistic: Mean per-event SPY-adjusted return over the late window, with short P&L = -(return) - costs. Reported only: the GICS-sector-SPDR-adjusted version and the distribution of delay lengths.
final.null: Mean SPY-adjusted return >= -(costs), i.e. the short does not earn. Bootstrap clustered by the calendar week of E, 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: E is computed from re-fetched 8-K items (same fiscal quarter, one year earlier). Firms without a prior-year same-quarter release are skipped. Late = no 2.02 acceptance by the E+7 close. k = 7 sessions exceeds the 5-session shift of a 53-week year. Exit at the reaction-session close, or at E+40 if there is still no release. Halves 2012-2018 and 2019-2026. Survivorship: report unpriced late events and the mean return they would need to flip the bound.
final.data: sec-submissions-b* (re-fetched with items), fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY/XLC/XLRE (sensitivity), wikipedia-sp500-constituents (sector, sensitivity only)
final.pass: All of: one-sided upper 95% bound of the mean SPY-adjusted return plus costs < 0; both halves negative; the placebo mean (same firms, E shifted -60 sessions so no release falls in the window, same window length) above the event upper bound; survivorship unable to flip the bound.
final.controls: One lateness threshold (E+7), one arm. The NT-notice and Friday arms are not run in S&P 500 names: NT is below min_n, and the Friday arm duplicates T-347's failed attention family. Costs 10 bp/side plus 1%/yr borrow. Shifted-calendar placebo.

rows.reason: Novel and directly uses the days-until-earnings variable through a free point-in-time EDGAR proxy. Fixed to one arm with a lateness threshold set above the 53-week-year calendar shift, so calendar drift is not mistaken for delay. The 3-arm DSR grid and the NT and Friday arms are dropped as underpowered or duplicative.

rows.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) predicts returns and earnings news
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Johnson and So, JFE 106(2) 262-286 (2012): lowest-decile O/S beats highest by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualised), and O/S predicts firm-specific earnings news. OSAP SignalDoc confirms OptionVolume1 (Johnson-So, 1996-2010, LS 0.916, t 3.45, 1_clear). That t is the original paper's figure recorded by OSAP, not an independent replication. OptionVolume2 was not reached in the SignalDoc page read. Ge-Lin-Pearson (2016) was not checked (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: There is no post-2010 evidence in hand. Weekly turnover costs and post-publication decay are likely to eat most of a 0.34%/week decile effect. A tercile sort on about 30 names (10 per leg) has a weekly spread s.e. near 0.35% at 52 weeks, so power is about 0.25 at the published effect. The universe must be at least about 100 names and the read pushed out.
rows.data_notes: options-surface (2026-10-14/15) carries per-expiry vol/oi by side, but only 3 single stocks (AAPL, NVDA, TSLA) are in CHAIN_SYMBOLS. DoltHub chains carry no volume (cross-checker). There is no historical per-underlying option volume in the archive. OCC or Cboe per-symbol daily volume history is unverified.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Capture at 18:30 ET gives that day's full option volume (the Cboe delayed feed's cumulative volume). The signal uses sessions through Thursday and trades at Friday's close, never the same session's close. (2) The universe is fixed at the extension date from point-in-time membership, so it is survivor-free going forward. (3) Share volume comes from the Yahoo daily bar after the close. (4) The read date is fixed in advance; no peeking.
rows.missing_data: A historical per-underlying option volume source (OCC/Cboe, unverified), or a forward capture with CHAIN_SYMBOLS extended to at least 100 optionable S&P 500 names (for example the S&P 100 at the extension date). Neither is in hand.

final.claim: Forward test starting the first Friday after the capture box's CHAIN_SYMBOLS is extended to the S&P 100 members on the extension date (at least 100 names). Each Friday, the lowest tercile of O/S beats the highest tercile from Friday's close to the next Friday's close, net of 5 bp per side, with a positive mean weekly spread. O/S = the 5-session sum through Thursday of option contract volume x 100 (all expiries, calls plus puts, from the 18:30 ET capture) divided by the 5-session sum of share volume.
final.statistic: Mean weekly low-minus-high tercile spread (equal weight) with Newey-West t (lag 2).
final.procedure: Universe frozen at the extension date; names leaving the index stay until delisted, and their returns are kept. Read at the 104th weekly formation; nothing is read earlier. Sector-neutral version and the earnings-event arm (O/S over D-5..D-1 against CAR(D..D+1)) are reported, not criteria. If an OCC/Cboe historical per-symbol volume source is verified as free, a 2015-2026 historical run on point-in-time S&P 500 members runs first as a separate registration, and this forward record becomes its confirmation.
final.data: options-surface-* (forward capture, extended CHAIN_SYMBOLS), daily-history-<symbols> or ml_data daily bars, sec-submissions-b* (release dates for the reported arm)
final.pass: All of: mean weekly spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 at the read date; both 52-week halves positive.
final.controls: One tercile threshold, one volume definition (all volume; the puts-only variant is not run). Costs 5 bp/side. Fixed universe.

rows.reason: Novel, and it uses the derivative-volume variable, but it is untestable historically on archived data. It was fixed into a properly powered forward pre-registration (at least 100 names, 104-week read). The cross-checker's 30-name, 52-week design had about 25% power, and its timing sentence was garbled; that is corrected to Thursday signal, Friday-close entry.

rows.name: Pre-earnings abnormal short volume (FINRA Reg SHO) and long-window shorting flows
rows.source_notes: Wang, Yan, Zheng (JFE 2020) Lehigh final PDF read (pdftotext). Data: FINRA daily short volume and FINRA total volume for all CRSP common stocks, Jan 2010-Dec 2015. Daily quintiles on the past 5-day SVR, skip 1 day, hold 20 days: heavy minus light -12.6%/yr EW (t 6.00) and -6.0%/yr VW (t 4.03). The effect is driven mostly by the low-shorting quintile's positive alpha. Large stocks: 2.2 bp/day EW (t 4.95), 1.3 bp/day VW (t 2.17). Long-term flows are measured 'over the 20- or 60-day period prior to the past five days', and the abstract says 'abnormal short-term shorting flows do not predict future returns or anticipate bad news'. Christophe-Ferri-Angel was only quoted secondhand.
rows.replication_concerns: WYZ's sample is 2010-2015 across all stocks; in large caps the effect is a third of the small-cap one. T-394's spike version (z > 2) was null on S&P 500 2019-2026. In the PFOF era, off-exchange short volume in large caps is largely wholesalers selling short to fill retail buys, so a high SVR can mean retail buying (Boehmer-Jones-Zhang-Zhang find retail imbalance predicts positive returns). The sign is a genuine bet.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: finra-regsho-cnms bundles run 2018-08..2026-10 (99 monthly bundles), each day keeping about 605-620 symbols, the point-in-time S&P 500 membership via T-394 machinery, from files of 7,700-10,100 rows. Fields: short_volume, short_exempt_volume, total_volume (off-exchange, FINRA facilities, the same construction as WYZ, who used FINRA total volume for consistency). File-day rows for 2018-2021 carry Last-Modified Oct 2021 and backfilled = True, meaning FINRA re-posted them. Values could differ from the original same-day publication; this cannot be verified, so flag it. French factors end 2026-08-31.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) A file is available after the trade day (FINRA posts about 18:00 ET), so the signal formed at month-end session t trades at the t+1 close (WYZ's skip-one-day). (2) The backfilled 2018-2021 files may embed later corrections (a vintage risk). (3) Membership comes from fja point-in-time spells. (4) FINRA spellings are mapped to Yahoo tickers with T-394's identity checks. (5) VW caps use SEC cover shares at acceptance. (6) Survivorship of members without Yahoo prices (6.6% in T-394).
rows.missing_data: None for this level sort. The pre-release event arm (registered expectation null) needs 8-K items and is not part of this trial.

final.claim: Over 2018-11 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, the light-minus-heavy shorted quintile spread is positive net of 10 bp round trip per leg and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. At each month-end session t, members are sorted into quintiles of their mean daily off-exchange short-volume ratio (FINRA CNMS short_volume / total_volume, summed over facilities) over the 60 file days ending 5 file days before t (WYZ 'quarterly shorting flows'). The bottom-minus-top quintile portfolio is held from the close of t+1 to the close of t+21.
final.statistic: Mean monthly equal-weighted spread (bottom minus top SVR quintile). Secondary: VW spread and FF5+UMD alpha (Newey-West lag 6, through 2026-08).
final.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap of the monthly spread (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
final.procedure: SVR per symbol-day sums all CNMS facilities, with FINRA spellings mapped as in T-394. A name needs at least 40 of the 60 file days. Positions run from the t+1 close to the t+21 close (WYZ skip 1, hold 20). VW uses point-in-time SEC cover-share caps (T-393 rules); names without a cap are left out of VW and counted. Halves 2018-11..2022-09 and 2022-10..2026-09. A sensitivity excludes Jan-Mar 2021. Survivorship: report unpriced member-months and the spread they would need to flip the bound.
final.data: finra-regsho-cnms-2018-08..2026-10, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, wikipedia-sp500-changes, sec-companyfacts-b*, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
final.pass: All of: EW spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; VW spread > 0; FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; both halves positive; survivorship unable to flip the bound; DSR > 0.95 over the shorting-flow family (T-394's 4 trials plus this 1). A significantly negative spread is recorded as not_supported, not as a reversal.
final.controls: Baseline reported: the same sort on the 60-day level of total off-exchange volume / shares outstanding, to separate shorting from turnover. Sector-neutral version reported. One window (WYZ quarterly), one quintile threshold, one hold. The FINRA backfill vintage flag is reported.

rows.reason: A testable-now, untested sibling of T-394 in the form WYZ found persistent (the long-window level, not the spike). The window was fixed to WYZ's exact 'quarterly' definition (60 days ending 5 days before formation, skip 1, hold 20) and the cross-checker's 4-trial grid cut to one primary. The FINRA 2021 re-posting of 2018-2021 files is flagged as a vintage risk.

rows.name: Analyst earnings-forecast revision momentum
rows.source_notes: OSAP SignalDoc confirms AnalystRevision (Hawkins-Chamberlin-Daniel 1984, 1975-1980, LS 0.4606, t 3.17), REV6 (Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok 1996, 1977-1992, t 4.07) and ChangeInRecommendation (Jegadeesh et al. 2004, 1985-1998, 0.225, 4_lack_data). These are original-paper figures as recorded by OSAP. McLean-Pontiff's 26% out-of-sample and 58% post-publication declines are well known but were not re-fetched. Dische was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Published 1984-2004, so heavy post-publication decay is expected. Sell-side consensus is a source everyone reads; the child sportsbook study shows a read-by-everyone consensus carries no information beyond price. A 24-month forward read has exploratory power only.
rows.data_notes: No point-in-time consensus history is archived. T-396's notes record that Yahoo quoteSummary returns 401 without a crumb, and the earningsTrend field names are unverified. IBES and FactSet are paid.
rows.lookahead_risks: A forward snapshot is point-in-time only if each value is stamped with its capture time and never backfilled. Yahoo's 'N days ago' fields are vendor-reconstructed and may be revised, so store the raw current value only and build the history from captures.
rows.missing_data: Point-in-time FY1 consensus history; only a forward collector (Yahoo crumb handshake or Nasdaq forecast pages, both unverified) is possible.

final.claim: Data plan for T-396, not a new trial. Starting from the first month-end with 30 days of daily consensus snapshots, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, the sector-neutral top decile by 30-day % change in the captured FY1 EPS consensus beats the bottom decile over the next calendar month, net of 10 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Mean monthly decile spread with Newey-West t (lag 3); FF5+UMD alpha.
final.procedure: Daily capture after the close of the current FY1 EPS consensus, analyst count and up/down revision counts, each stamped available_at = capture time. Never use vendor 'N days ago' fields as history. Formation at month-end, entry at the next session's close, hold one month. Read at the 24th formation; a pass goes to a further forward period before any sizing.
final.data: new forward capture bundle (endpoint to verify with a crumb from the capture box); fja-sp500-components, daily-history-<members>, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
final.pass: Spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2 at the read date.
final.controls: Sector-neutral deciles, one variant (30-day change). Costs 10 bp round trip.

rows.reason: Same claim and the same forward-capture route already recorded in T-396's notes, so this is a duplicate with no material design change. The capture job belongs to T-396 once the endpoint is verified.

rows.name: Size premium conditional on quality ('size matters if you control your junk')
rows.source_notes: Asness, Frazzini, Israel, Moskowitz, Pedersen draft (Wharton Jacobs Levy PDF, first draft Jan 2015, JFE 2018) read via pdftotext. Abstract: once junk is controlled, 'a significant size premium emerges, which is stable through time, ... not concentrated in microcaps'. US sample: QMJ period Jul 1957-Dec 2012. SMB alpha on Mkt, lagged Mkt, HML and UMD is 14 bps (t 1.23). Adding QMJ gives 49 bps (t 4.89, R^2 15% to 37%). The archived-factor spec (FF5 2x3) is Mkt, lagged Mkt, HML, UMD, RMW and CMA: 33 bps/month (t 2.81); adding QMJ gives 54 bps. The NBER page confirms Hou-Xue-Zhang w23394: 286 of 447 anomalies (64%) insignificant at 5%, 380 (85%) at t < 3. OSAP confirms Banz Size 1.01, t 3.07 (1926-1975). The conditional result is AQR's own and was not independently replicated in this sweep (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: Raw SMB has decayed (T-385: IJR-IWM +0.22%/yr, CI -1.21 to +1.71, with an RMW loading t of 4.68 consistent with the junk channel). Mandel's factor tests HML (T-382) and QUAL (T-383) failed after publication. The size family already has 34 trials, so the DSR bar is high. A pass is a factor-level statement, not directly tradeable.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: french-ff5-daily runs 1963-07-01..2026-08-31 and french-momentum-daily 1926-11-03..2026-08-31, so the test window ends 2026-08. aqr-bab-daily is archived (to 2026-07), but AQR QMJ is not; it is a free download from the same AQR library. daily-history IJR (6,635 rows), SPY and QUAL (3,331 rows, from 2013-07) exist for the diagnostic sleeve. The Asness sample ends 2012-12, so the clean out-of-sample window starts 2013-01, not 2015-01 as the cross-checker set.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) French factors are revised every month, so record the bundle file date and sha. (2) Monthly returns compounded from daily factors differ slightly from French's monthly files; use one method throughout. (3) The diagnostic sleeve's hedge ratio must come from the in-sample (1963-2012) regression only.
rows.missing_data: None for the FF5+UMD arm. The QMJ arm needs AQR's QMJ factors (free), counted as a second trial when fetched.

final.claim: Over 2013-01 to 2026-08, after the Asness et al. sample, the monthly Fama-French SMB return (FF5 2x3) has a positive intercept in a regression on Mkt-RF, lagged Mkt-RF, HML, RMW, CMA and UMD. The intercept's Newey-West t is >= 2 and its 95% lower bound is above zero.
final.statistic: OLS intercept in %/month, with Newey-West t (lag 6) and a studentized block-bootstrap interval (block 12 months).
final.procedure: Compound the daily French factors to calendar months. Specification as in Asness et al. Table 2 Panel D row 2. 1963-07..2012-12 is reported as in-sample context only. Halves 2013-01..2019-10 and 2019-11..2026-08. QMJ arm (SMB on Mkt-RF, lagged Mkt-RF, HML, UMD, QMJ) runs when AQR QMJ is fetched, as a second trial. Executable diagnostic, not a criterion: IJR minus SPY hedged with QUAL minus SPY at the in-sample RMW-implied ratio, net of 5 bp per monthly reset and 0.3%/yr borrow, reported against FF5+UMD.
final.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily; diagnostic: daily-history-IJR, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QUAL; to fetch for the second trial: AQR QMJ factors
final.pass: All of: intercept NW t >= 2; bootstrap lower bound > 0; positive intercept in both halves; DSR > 0.95 over the size family (T-385's 34 trials plus this one).
final.controls: Factor level only, so there is no survivorship issue. One specification. The French file date is recorded. A pass is not a funding signal: an executable long-small/short-junk book needs a stock-level quality screen.

rows.reason: Testable today with one regression on archived factors. It answers whether raw size (T-385) failed because of junk exposure. The out-of-sample start was fixed to 2013-01, right after the paper's sample end of 2012-12, and the paper's lagged-market regressor was added so the specification matches the published one.

rows.name: Net share issuance and buybacks from point-in-time SEC shares outstanding
rows.source_notes: The CXO summary confirms Fu, Huang, Lin (2011 WP; published as Fu-Huang, Management Science 2016): 13,992 repurchases (1984-2008) and 5,917 SEOs (1980-2008). Three-year abnormal returns of about +10% after repurchases and -12% after SEOs before 2003 disappeared over 2003-2008. The authors attribute this mainly to institutional ownership, with firms over 50% institutionally owned rising from 34% to 70% among repurchasers. OSAP confirms ShareIss1Y (Pontiff-Woodgate 2008, 1970-2003, t 7.08) and CompEquIss (Daniel-Titman 2006, 1968-2003, t 4.39). These are original-paper figures as recorded by OSAP.
rows.replication_concerns: The effect is reported gone after 2003 (Fu-Huang-Lin). Mandel's T-449 found the post-2008 spread halved and insignificant (+0.30%/month, CI -0.18 to +0.86, FF5 alpha t 1.35). French's value-weighted NI portfolios are already dominated by large caps, so an S&P 500 subset re-runs nearly the same test with less power.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: sec-companyfacts carries dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding from 10-Q (1,745 rows in b006) and 10-K (568) forms with filed dates and accession numbers, and daily-events split rows exist for 855 symbols. Of the 9,133 CIKs, 1,127 returned 404 for companyfacts, so cover counts are missing for those issuers. The T-393 machinery notes about 63 priced names per date without a usable cover count.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) The cover-share date is not the acceptance date; enter at acceptance. (2) Splits between the two cover dates must be removed with daily-events ratios. (3) Multi-class issuers follow T-393's rules. (4) Survivorship: acquired issuers, which are often stock-financed, are missing from Yahoo.
rows.missing_data: None for a diagnostic. Survivorship is handled by the rule-9 flip test.

final.claim: Executable diagnostic under T-449, not a new trial. Over 2011-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, the bottom decile minus the top decile of the 12-month log change in split-adjusted SEC cover shares outstanding has a positive mean monthly return, net of 10 bp round trip per leg and 1%/yr borrow. Positions are formed at each month-end and entered at the first session's close.
final.statistic: Mean monthly bottom-minus-top decile spread (equal weight); FF3+UMD alpha (CMA absorbs issuance), with FF5+UMD reported.
final.null: Spread <= 0, tested with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 6 months, 5,000 draws).
final.procedure: Each cover count enters at its accession's acceptance, with multi-class issuers handled as in T-393. Split factors come from daily-events. No winsorizing. Halves 2011-2018 and 2019-2026. Survivorship flip test per rule 9.
final.data: sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, daily-events-<members>, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-cik-lookup, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, french-ff3-daily, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
final.pass: Reported against T-449's verdict. It cannot by itself overturn T-449.
final.controls: No price input. One decile threshold. Placebo: the 12-month change lagged a further 12 months.

rows.reason: Same economic claim as T-449 (repurchasers beat issuers after publication), which is not_supported, over an overlapping window. An S&P 500 subset of a failed, value-weight-dominated test is a forking path, and its expected answer is a null. Keep it only as an executable diagnostic under T-449.

rows.name: S&P 500 additions: direct additions vs MidCap migrations
rows.source_notes: Greenwood-Sammon, HBS WP 23-025 (revised Nov 2023), read via pdftotext. Confirmed: additions' abnormal return fell from 7.4% in the 1990s to 0.3% over the past decade. Migrations rose from about 50% of additions to over 70%. In the mid-1990s, migration additions returned 10.2% and non-migration additions 6.7%. Errors in the candidate: (1) in the 2010s 'direct additions had returns of 5.4%, while migrations had returns of 1.8%', so migrations were +1.8%, not -1.8% as the candidate wrote. (2) The main CAR runs 'from the last trading day before the announcement to the first trading day after' the effective date, so it includes the announcement-night jump that a post-announcement entry cannot capture. (3) Deletions: the abstract says 0.1% for 2010-2020, the introduction -0.6%. The paper finds little change in the 20 sessions before announcement.
rows.replication_concerns: Bennett-Stulz-Wang (2020) also document the decline, per GS. The direct-addition split was drawn after the decay was known. The tradable post-announcement remainder is likely far below 5.4%. T-334 (post-effective reversal) was inconclusive.
rows.data_notes: wikipedia-sp500-changes (412 rows, 'announced' from cited press-release titles for 299 rows) and fja bundles exist. The migration flag needs S&P 400 changes, which are not archived; the Wikipedia S&P 400 changes depth and the S&P DJI press-release bodies are unverified. The pooled T-453 arm is runnable now on the archived 'announced' dates.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Entry must be at the first regular open after the announcement's available_at; S&P DJI releases come after the close. (2) Additions without a cited announcement are excluded and counted; this selection is by citation and unrelated to returns. (3) The migration flag must come from contemporaneous S&P 400 change records, not today's S&P 400 membership. (4) Unpriced, acquired additions (T-334: 56 of 322) get the rule-9 flip test.
rows.missing_data: S&P MidCap 400 change history for the migration flag. The pooled arm needs nothing new.

final.claim: Variant arm of T-453, not a new trial. Over 2010-2026, S&P 500 additions not drawn from the S&P MidCap 400 earn a positive mean SPY-adjusted return, net of 10 bp round trip, from the first regular-session open after the announcement's available_at to the effective-date close, and they beat migrations over the same window.
final.statistic: Mean per-event abnormal return of direct additions, and the direct-minus-migration difference.
final.null: Direct mean <= 0; difference <= 0. Bootstrap clustered by announcement date, 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: T-334 matching of fja first appearances to Wikipedia rows with a non-null 'announced' date. Migration = the ticker leaves the S&P 400 on the same effective date, from fetched contemporaneous S&P 400 changes. Halves 2010-2017 and 2018-2026. Tesla 2020 reported with and without. MDE stated before the run.
final.data: wikipedia-sp500-changes, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY; to fetch: S&P 400 change history
final.pass: One-sided lower 95% bound of the direct mean > 0; difference > 0 with p < 0.05; direct mean positive in both halves; placebo windows (60-250 sessions after inclusion) below the real lower bound; survivorship unable to flip the bound.
final.controls: One entry rule (first open after announcement), one exit (effective close). Costs 10 bp round trip. Placebo windows.

rows.reason: T-453 already lists the migration-vs-new-entrant split in its procedure, so this is a duplicate. The candidate also misread the evidence: GS report migrations at +1.8%, not -1.8%, on a window that includes the untradeable announcement-night jump. Run T-453's pooled arm on the archived 'announced' dates instead, and add the split when S&P 400 changes are fetched.

rows.name: Insider open-market purchases (Form 4): opportunistic and cluster buys, and where the return actually sits
rows.source_notes: NBER page confirms Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski w16454 (JF 2012): the opportunistic portfolio earns 82 bps/month value-weighted and routine trades are 'essentially zero'. The 180 bps EW figure was not shown on the page. The Equibles page confirms 47,458 purchases (Jan 2020-Aug 2025). Median abnormal returns are +0.12% (1 month) to +2.56% (1 year) against the median listed stock, but -1.54% to -12.95% against the S&P 500. The 180-session placebo differences are 0.06-1.40 pp (t 0.13-1.58), 'no evidence of a timing premium'. The routine/opportunistic split 'does not reproduce'; routine is in fact higher (9.55% vs 4.35% at 1 year). arXiv 2602.06198 (Zhao, 2026) confirms 13,534 purchase lines, 1,192 microcap issuers, 2018-2024. Day-1 abnormal return is 4.13% far below the 52-week high vs 0.86% near it (t 9.77), falling to 0.94 points (t 2.11) with full controls, below its own bar. There is no significant calendar-time alpha after day 1, and after-close filings are priced 'mostly through an overnight gap'.
rows.replication_concerns: Decayed after 2010. The child stock desk's pre-registered study (EDGE_VERDICT 21e: 28,706 officer/director buys of $25k or more, 2016-2026) earns +0.00% against SPY after the filing. Copying disclosed informed flow loses at any delay (child Result 18).
rows.data_notes: The SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets are not archived; T-391's notes record verified access from 2006q1. No point-in-time S&P 1500 membership is archived, only S&P 500 (fja).
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Entry only at the first regular open strictly after Form 4 acceptance, never at the filing-day close. (2) The routine/opportunistic classification uses only the insider's prior 3 calendar years. (3) Delisted small-cap issuers are missing from Yahoo, which biases vendor studies upward.
rows.missing_data: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (free, not archived).

final.claim: Amendment to T-391, not a new trial. Over 2006-2026, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, Form 4 code-P purchases by opportunistic insiders (no trade in the same calendar month in each of the prior 3 years) earn a positive mean SPY-adjusted 21-session return net of 10 bp per side when bought at the first regular-session open strictly after acceptance. The registered expectation is a null.
final.statistic: Mean per-event 21-session abnormal return, with same-issuer purchases within 21 sessions merged into one event.
final.null: Mean <= 0, tested with a bootstrap clustered by filing week, 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: Acceptance datetimes come from the SEC data sets. Exclude 10b5-1-flagged trades and purchases under $25k. Placebo: entry shifted 180 sessions. Halves 2006-2015 and 2016-2026. Survivorship reported.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY; to fetch: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets
final.pass: One-sided lower 95% bound > 0; both halves positive; the placebo below the real lower bound.
final.controls: One arm, one horizon. Costs 10 bp/side.

rows.reason: Duplicate of T-391. Three independent post-2016 records already answer it: the child's 28,706-event study at +0.00% vs SPY, Equibles' placebo showing no timing premium, where the Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski split does not reproduce, and arXiv showing the residual sits in an untradeable day-1 gap. Spend nothing unless the SEC data sets are fetched for another reason.

rows.name: Dividend initiations and omissions (plus the dividend-month premium)
rows.source_notes: OSAP SignalDoc confirms Michaely-Thaler-Womack (1995, 1964-1988): DivInit 0.625 (t 3.37) and DivOmit 0.9167 (t 6.33). These are original-paper figures as recorded by OSAP. DivSeason (Hartzmark-Solomon 2013, 1927-2011) is 0.36, t 16.19. The Alpha Architect page (the 53 bps figure) was not re-opened. No post-1995 replication of initiation drift could be searched (budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: The 1964-1988 sample predates decimalisation and is equal-weighted, mostly small firms. The dividend-month premium already failed in Mandel (T-374: +5.6 bp net, p 0.16), so that arm is not re-run. In S&P 500 names, omissions cluster in 2008-09 and 2020, are mostly temporary suspensions that later resumed (airlines, cruise lines, hotels), and are often unpriced (failed banks), so the omission leg cannot support a verdict.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed by a light count over the archived daily-events (855 symbols) against fja point-in-time spells. About 103 raw initiation events (first ex-date after more than 730 days without one) fall in S&P 500 members 2005-2026. That count includes duplicate share classes (GOOG/GOOGL), likely spurious corporate-action rows (PARA/PSKY), and about a dozen post-2020 resumptions (MAR, HLT, GM, LUV, DAL, LVS, WYNN, RCL, CCL, EXPE, DIS). Cleaned, n is about 90. Declaration dates are absent (ex-dates only). Members missing from the archive have neither dividend events nor prices, so detection is itself survivor-conditioned.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Entry at the close of the ex-date session uses only a printed ex-date. The declaration came earlier, so this is conservative. (2) Special dividends cannot be identified at entry without future information; keep them and report the ex-post subset that paid a second dividend. (3) Count share classes once. (4) Require 730 days of prior price history so IPOs are not misread as initiations. (5) Survivorship applies to detection and pricing alike: report the share of point-in-time member-years with no archived history.
rows.missing_data: None for the initiation arm. Declaration dates (Nasdaq dividend history, unverified) would allow the paper's timing.

final.claim: Over 2005-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members, a stock whose cash-dividend ex-date follows at least 730 calendar days without one (and at least 730 days of price history) earns a positive mean SPY-adjusted buy-and-hold return over the 252 sessions from the close of that ex-date session, net of 10 bp per side.
final.statistic: Mean per-event 252-session SPY-adjusted return. Secondary: the calendar-time monthly portfolio's FF5+UMD alpha (Newey-West lag 12, through 2026-08).
final.null: Mean <= 0, tested with a bootstrap clustered by calendar month of entry, 10,000 draws.
final.procedure: Detect events from archived Yahoo ex-dates only (point-in-time). Merge share classes of one issuer. Halves 2005-2015 and 2016-2026; the 2021-2024 resumption cluster is reported separately. MDE stated before the run: about 7.4 pp at 80% power for 90 events at a 28% per-event s.d., near MTW's roughly 7.5%/yr. The omission leg is reported descriptively only. Survivorship flip test per rule 9.
final.data: daily-events-<members>, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily
final.pass: All of: one-sided lower 95% bound of the mean > 0; positive in both halves; calendar-time FF5+UMD alpha t >= 2; survivorship unable to flip the bound. With fewer than 60 events after cleaning, the verdict is inconclusive.
final.controls: One gap threshold (730 days), one horizon (252 sessions). Costs 10 bp/side. Placebo: the same firms entered 252 sessions after the real entry (the post-window), which should earn nothing. The dividend-month premium is not re-tested (T-374 stands).

rows.reason: The initiation drift is new to the registry and testable today. It was fixed to a long-only initiation arm with an MDE stated in advance. The cross-checker's omission leg is crisis-clustered, mostly temporary suspensions and largely unpriced, so it cannot support a verdict, and the long-short form would let that weak leg decide the result.

knowledge.title: Earnings, size and corporate events: what still pays around announcements, share counts, index changes and insider filings
knowledge.markdown:
# Earnings, size and corporate events: what still pays around announcements, share counts, index changes and insider filings

- **Authors / kind:** A literature sweep of 16 strategy claims, mostly peer-reviewed: Martineau (CFR 2022), Garfinkel-Sokobin (JAR 2006), Savor-Wilson (JF 2016), Gao-Xing-Zhang (JFQA 2018), Dubinsky-Johannes-Kaeck-Seeger (RFS 2019), Chang-Hartzmark-Solomon-Soltes (RFS 2017), Johnson-So (JFE 2012, JFQA 2018), DellaVigna-Pollet (JF 2009), Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020), Asness et al. (JFE 2018), Greenwood-Sammon (HBS WP 2023) and Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski (JF 2012). The replication databases are OSAP and Hou-Xue-Zhang. Practitioner sources: Equibles, Quantpedia, CXO and Wall Street Horizon.
- **Links:** https://cfr.ivo-welch.info/published/papers/martineau2021rest.pdf · https://www.biz.uiowa.edu/faculty/jgarfinkel/pubs/drift_JAR.pdf · https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/Short_Final_Version.pdf · https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/23-025_563e45c6-df92-4d9c-ae05-608d4d0acab1.pdf · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/master/SignalDoc.csv
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.65 (24 of 35 sources opened: 7 in full text, 17 at abstract or summary level).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** Seven texts were read in full via pdftotext: Martineau, Garfinkel-Sokobin, the Savor-Wilson draft, the Dubinsky et al. slides, Wang-Yan-Zheng, Asness et al. and Greenwood-Sammon. Frazzini-Lamont, PBFJ 2023, Ge-Lin-Pearson, Michaely-Rubin-Vedrashko and the vendor beat-rate pages were not opened. The search budget ran out before most post-2015 replications could be looked for. Vendor figures are unverified.
- **Selected because:** This cluster is where the program's inputs meet scheduled corporate events: days until earnings, volume and turnover, shares outstanding, market cap, short interest and implied volatility. Most of its anomalies also have a measured post-publication decay to test against.

## What it says

- **PEAD** (sort on earnings surprise, hold about 60 days; underreaction). Martineau finds no large-cap drift since about 2006. Subrahmanyam (2001-2024) gets t 2.18 for all stocks and t 1.43 excluding microcaps. **Decayed** in investable names.
- **Earnings-day abnormal turnover.** Garfinkel-Sokobin (45,187 NYSE/AMEX announcements, 1985-1998): the top turnover-change group earns +1.386% over 60 days against -0.070% for the bottom group (t 9.49), controlling for the surprise. The mechanism is opinion divergence under short-sale constraints. No post-2000 replication was found.
- **Earnings announcement premium.** Savor-Wilson (1974-2009): announcers beat non-announcers by +0.39%/week equal-weighted (t 14.3). Heitz et al. (summary only) find it gone in the US since the 2004 Form 8-K rule. **Decayed.**
- **Pre-release implied volatility.** Gao-Hu-Zhang (working paper): 71% of the premium arrives in the 10 sessions before the release, because uncertainty resolves early. High implied-volatility names at T-11 gain +1.52% market-adjusted; low ones show nothing. Not replicated.
- **Pre-earnings straddle.** Gao-Xing-Zhang: an ATM straddle held from T-3 through the announcement earns +3.34%, but quoted spreads of 1-3% per side can absorb that.
- **Earnings IV crush.** Dubinsky et al.: implied earnings-day jump volatility "uniformly" exceeds realised, and straddles held over the release lose 8% per event gross. The short side is short gamma, with fat right tails that cluster by name.
- **Earnings seasonality.** Chang et al. (recency bias: forecasters anchor on the recent weak quarters): firms announcing their seasonally strong quarter earn 65 bp/month alpha against 31 bp for the weak-quarter group. Not replicated.
- **Late and Friday announcers.** Johnson-So: managers delay bad news, so late schedulers report worse news, and equity prices ignore the schedule. DellaVigna-Pollet: Friday releases are 45% more likely to be negative surprises, with 60% of the response delayed.
- **Option-to-stock volume.** Johnson-So (1996-2010): when shorting is costly, informed traders with bad news use options, so low-O/S stocks beat high-O/S stocks by 0.34%/week. No evidence after 2010.
- **Short volume.** Wang-Yan-Zheng (FINRA, 2010-2015): heavily shorted stocks underperform by 12.6%/yr equal-weighted (t 6.0). Abnormal short-term shorting does not anticipate bad news; only 20-60-day flows persist.
- **Analyst revisions.** Investors underreact to consensus EPS changes. OSAP AnalystRevision earns 0.46%/month (t 3.17, 1975-1980). McLean-Pontiff: returns fall 58% after publication.
- **Size premium given quality.** Asness et al. (1957-2012): SMB alpha rises from 14 bp (t 1.23) to 49 bp (t 4.89) with QMJ as a control. The raw small-cap premium has decayed.
- **Share issuance and buybacks.** Managers time the market. Fu-Huang: about +10% over three years after buybacks and -12% after equity offerings before 2003, about 0 for 2003-2008. **Decayed.**
- **Index inclusion.** Greenwood-Sammon: the addition return fell from 7.4% in the 1990s to 0.3% in the past decade. Index-fund rebalancing offsets the effect for migrations. In the 2010s direct additions earned +5.4% and migrations +1.8% (not -1.8%), on a window that includes the announcement-night jump, which cannot be traded. **Decayed.**
- **Insider buying.** Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski (1986-2007): opportunistic purchases earn 82 bp/month. Equibles (2020-2025, 47,458 purchases): buyers trail the S&P 500, with no timing premium. arXiv 2602.06198: what is left sits in a day-1 overnight gap. **Decayed.**
- **Dividend initiations.** Michaely-Thaler-Womack (1964-1988, mostly small firms): a dividend change signals persistent earnings and investors underreact; initiation drift t 3.37. No post-1995 replication was found.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** The sources are peer-reviewed, use large samples and are catalogued in OSAP and Hou-Xue-Zhang. That rigour belongs to measurements that are in-sample, gross of transaction costs and mostly from before 2010. The decay evidence is thinner and partly working-paper or practitioner work.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Earnings event variance ratio** (`earnings-event-variance-ratio-vx3`), the strongest claim. It compares implied event variance from VXAPL, VXGOG and VXAZN (2011-2026, about 185 events) with realised variance, after four free SEC calls. It belongs to the variance risk premium class that Mandel supports in T-244, T-246 and T-148. T-224 found the reverse on macro days, where a flat 30-day GVZ under-prices event-day variance, but single-stock implied volatility is event-aware. A pass does not fund anything: the deciding arm uses quoted prices in T-207's defined-risk form, because Hurst's IBIT condor had a worst month of -168%.
- **FINRA short-volume level** (`finra-svr-quarterly-level-sp500`), testable now. It is the persistent-flow sibling of T-394, whose spike version was null (+0.7 bp gross), and it is deflated together with T-394.
- **SMB alpha after junk controls, out-of-sample from 2013**, testable now. It asks whether T-385 failed through junk exposure (RMW loading t 4.68).
- **Dividend-initiation drift**, testable now. It is long-only, with a minimum detectable effect of about 7.4 pp at n of about 90.
- **Price-free event variables.** These are the turnover change dTO (with a non-event baseline, because T-419, T-546 and T-578's relative-volume IC of about +0.01 were weak), the expected-announcer premium (T-339 on 8-K dates, with a null expected), the late-announcer short, the seasonality score and a pre-release implied-volatility test with a difference-in-differences placebo.
- **O/S as a forward test only:** 100 or more names, read at 104 weeks.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Large-cap PEAD** runs only as T-338's control. Hurst's own small-cap PEAD was killed by its placebo: an entry 25 sessions late earned +1.77%/month against +1.32% for the real entry.
- **Insider buying** duplicates T-391. The child's 28,706-event study (EDGE_VERDICT 21e) earned +0.00% against SPY.
- **Buybacks and share issuance** stay under T-449, which is not_supported (+0.30%/month, CI -0.18 to +0.86).
- **Index inclusion** stays under T-453 (T-334 is inconclusive). The migration split is post-hoc.
- **The pre-earnings straddle** stays under T-204. Pricing it on constant-maturity VX is circular, as T-57 showed.
- **Revisions** stay under T-396. **The dividend-month premium** stays rejected (T-374), and so does Friday attention (T-347).
- **Venue limits.** Alpaca small accounts probably cannot sell naked straddles, so only defined-risk structures are allowed. Short legs need borrow.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Data unlock:** re-fetch data.sec.gov submissions keeping `items` and non-XBRL forms for about 1,100 historical S&P 500 CIKs. That gives 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance times, with D defined as the first session whose open follows acceptance. Seven rows depend on it. A companyfacts re-fetch would add 10-Q NetIncomeLoss as filed.
- **Point-in-time ML features,** with price isolated as the target: days to the expected earnings date, a late flag, the turnover change, the 60-day short-volume level, the 12-month change in shares outstanding, an initiation flag, the implied event variance and a seasonality score. CAR is excluded because it is price-derived.
- **Look-ahead tests:** 8-K acceptance against wire time; 16:00 releases against the VX close; split-adjusted volume against as-filed shares; the FINRA backfill vintage.
- **Statistics:** a survivorship flip test (rule 9) and a block bootstrap on every panel.
- **Option data:** verify DoltHub single-stock implied volatility coverage, and extend the capture box's CHAIN_SYMBOLS to the S&P 100.

## Cross-links

- A4: earnings-day variance is a scheduled fat-tail jump. A5: the decay of PEAD and the day-1 insider reaction both measure how fast information reaches the price.
- 12, 13, 14: earnings features belong there with D+2 entry and placebo dates.
- Theories: T-338, T-452, T-339, T-204-T-207, T-248, T-394, T-396, T-385, T-449, T-453, T-334, T-391, T-374, T-347, T-419, T-546, T-224, T-244, T-521, T-538, T-578.

## Sources used

- Martineau (2022) https://cfr.ivo-welch.info/published/papers/martineau2021rest.pdf
- UCLA Anderson Review https://anderson-review.ucla.edu/is-post-earnings-announcement-drift-a-thing-again/
- Garfinkel-Sokobin https://www.biz.uiowa.edu/faculty/jgarfinkel/pubs/drift_JAR.pdf
- Savor-Wilson https://faculty.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/Draft20111215p_edited.pdf
- Heitz et al. https://paperswithbacktest.com/strategies/the-disappearing-earnings-announcement-premium
- Gao-Hu-Zhang https://quantpedia.com/pre-announcement-returns/
- Gao-Xing-Zhang https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/anticipating-uncertainty-straddles-around-earnings-announcements/7B34877AD5E06304BA3C55FBA3219FDD
- Dubinsky et al. https://www.stern.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/assets/documents/NYU%20conference%20Johannes%20final.pdf
- Chang et al. https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v30y2017i1p281-323..html
- Johnson-So https://ideas.repec.org/a/cup/jfinqa/v53y2018i06p2431-2464_00.html · https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v106y2012i2p262-286.html
- DellaVigna-Pollet https://www.nber.org/papers/w11683
- Wang-Yan-Zheng https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/Short_Final_Version.pdf
- OSAP https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/master/SignalDoc.csv
- Asness et al. https://jacobslevycenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Size-Matters-if-You-Control-Your-Junk.pdf
- Hou-Xue-Zhang https://www.nber.org/papers/w23394
- Fu-Huang (CXO) https://www.cxoadvisory.com/buybacks-secondaries/extinction-of-the-buybacksecondary-offering-effect

- Equibles https://equibles.com/research/what-happens-after-an-insider-buys-evidence-from-47-458-open-market-purchases
