candidates.name: Gamma-conditional market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)
candidates.summary: The return from the prior close to 15:30 ET predicts the last-half-hour return, but only on days when option dealers are net short gamma. Mandel's unconditional version (T-427) failed on 2023-11..2026-10. What is new here is the dealer-gamma conditioning from Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (2021). SqueezeMetrics' free daily GEX file (2011-2026) supplies the conditioner, so the test needs no option chains.
candidates.mechanism: Dealers who are short gamma must buy as prices rise and sell as they fall to stay delta-neutral. Leveraged-ETF sponsors face the same need and rebalance near the close. That hedging trades with the day's move and concentrates late in the session. When dealers are long gamma they trade against the move, which offsets the momentum or reverses it. The other side is the hedgers themselves: their trades are forced and insensitive to price, and a liquidity provider who leans with them earns the price pressure.
candidates.assets: US equity index ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM) or CME E-mini / Micro E-mini futures; the paper also covers bond, commodity and FX futures
candidates.claimed_effect: BDLM (JFE 2021) cover 60+ futures, 1974-2020. Their eta(rROD) timing rule on the equity-index futures basket returns 6.86%/yr at 3.96% vol, a Sharpe ratio of 1.73, before costs. The authors note that S&P futures stay net-positive at a one-tick cost. On S&P 500 futures over 1996-2020, regressing the last half-hour return on the rest-of-day return gives a slope of 6.63 (x100, NW t 4.78, R2 3.58%) when prior-day NGE < 0. When NGE >= 0 the slope is 0.82 (t 1.03, R2 0.05%). Gao-Han-Li-Zhou (SPY 1993-2013) report an out-of-sample R2 of about 1.7% for the first half-hour predictor (working-paper figure).
candidates.replication: Supportive work: Barbon-Buraschi 'Gamma Fragility' (working paper) find negative gamma imbalance gives momentum and positive gives reversal, strongest in illiquid names. Barbon-Beckmeyer-Buraschi-Moerke (2022 WP) find gamma effects persist. Adams et al. (2026) find higher dealer hedging needs dampen intraday momentum, the same sign seen from the other side. Decay: Mandel T-427 tested the unconditional rule on SPY 2023-11..2026-10 and failed, at -2.09 bps/day net, HAC t -2.58, slope -0.004. The conditioning state is now rare: in the SqueezeMetrics file, negative-GEX days numbered 104 in 2022, 23 in 2023, 1 in 2024, 9 in 2025 and 9 in 2026 YTD (my count). A sign-based test on recent data therefore has almost no events, and a percentile conditioner is needed.

sources.title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens), JFE 142 (2021)
Market intraday momentum (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou), JFE 2018
Gamma Fragility (Barbon, Buraschi), working paper
SqueezeMetrics DIX/GEX daily history (free CSV)

candidates.proposed_test: Pre-register this as a conditional successor to T-427. Universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM on Mandel's 60-minute bars (2023-11..2026-10), plus a longer replication if a 1-minute US500 history is archived (e.g. the Dukascopy unlock). Signal: the sign of the prior close to 15:30 return, traded only on days when the PRIOR day's SqueezeMetrics GEX (published after day t-1's close, so known at the t open) sits in the bottom quintile of its trailing-252-day percentile. Report the GEX < 0 subset as a secondary arm. Hold from the 15:30 bar open to the official close, at a cost of 2 bps round trip. Statistic: difference in mean net return between low-GEX and high-GEX days, studentized block bootstrap; DSR over every cell tried, counting T-427's 60. Controls: FOMC/CPI days, OPEX days and the 2022 regime. Snapshot and hash today's GEX file, and diff future downloads against it to detect vendor revisions.

candidates.name: Dealer gamma level dampens next-day volatility: GEX-conditioned 1-day short straddle
candidates.summary: Days after high positive dealer gamma should have smaller realised moves than the VIX implies, so a 1-day short straddle earns more on them. This is the daily-horizon variant of the blocked T-217/T-218, which waited for chain-based GEX. It is now testable from 2011 with the free SqueezeMetrics GEX series. It also gives the ML program a non-price feature family (F4 flow: GEX, DIX, put/call ratios, OI).
candidates.mechanism: Market makers hold net purchased gamma when customers are net option writers (call overwriting, short puts). Rebalancing their delta hedges then means selling into rallies and buying dips, which mechanically compresses realised volatility. When customers are net buyers, dealer gamma turns negative and hedging amplifies moves. The volatility seller collects the implied-minus-realised gap that dealer hedging creates.
adjacent_variables: customer vs market-maker option volume share
candidates.assets: SPX/SPY options (1-day straddles; XSP for small size) or the underlying ETF as a volatility-forecast input
candidates.claimed_effect: Ni-Pearson-Poteshman-White (RFS 2021) report a statistically and economically significant negative relation between stock return volatility and the net purchased option positions of hedgers. Amaya-Garcia-Ares-Pearson-Vasquez (2025) use Cboe trade-level data for Jul 2020-Jun 2023. Their gamma coefficient is negative. The median impact cuts daily volatility by 0.08 pp. The maximum gamma-induced rise is 3.3 pp of annualised daily realised vol (6.4 pp at 30 minutes), against a 4.5 pp SD of daily changes, which they call not large. They also find only 68.7% of SPX/SPXW volume is customer-versus-market-maker, so open-interest GEX misclassifies positions. SqueezeMetrics (2017, vendor, in-sample) reports next-day SPX SDs of 0.55% vs 0.85% between GEX quartiles. A 2026 SSRN working paper (Maurer, abstract only) finds GEX informative for overnight gaps only in low-VIX regimes.
candidates.replication: The sign is consistent across NPPW, Amaya et al. and Adams et al.; the magnitude is small, and the strongest evidence comes from proprietary signed data that public OI-based GEX only approximates. Two Mandel results relate. T-216 (supported, model-priced) shows opex-Friday 1-day short straddles earn +9.14 bps more than other Fridays, consistent with a gamma pin. T-529 (not_supported) shows VIX1D under the /365 convention under-predicts next-day variance, so the base 1-day premium is fragile and conditioning matters.

sources.title: Does Option Trading Have a Pervasive Impact on Underlying Stock Prices? (Ni, Pearson, Poteshman, White), RFS 34(4) 2021
0DTE Index Options and Market Volatility: How Large is Their Impact? (Amaya, Garcia-Ares, Pearson, Vasquez)
Gamma Exposure: Quantifying Hedging Pressure (SqueezeMetrics white paper)
Dealer Gamma Exposure and Overnight Gap Risk (Maurer), SSRN

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY daily OHLC, 2011-05..2026-10 (about 3,890 days with GEX). Signal: the day t-1 GEX as a trailing-252-day percentile tercile, known after the t-1 close. Diagnostic: regress next-day |log return| and the Parkinson range on GEX percentile, controlling for log VIX, HAR realised vol and event dummies. Pass if GEX adds >= 1% out-of-sample R2 on 2019-2026 after fitting on 2011-2018. Trading form, built like T-216: a model-priced 1-day ATM short straddle (sigma = VIX at the t-1 close, T = 1/252, dividend forward) sold at the t-1 close and settled at the t close. Compare top-tercile with bottom-tercile GEX P&L, with block-8 bootstrap CI, a half-spread cost proxy, and both halves positive. Then re-price on captured SPXW chains as they accumulate (this successor unblocks T-217/T-218). Also add GEX percentile to T-578 as part of an F4 flow family and report its ablation IC.

candidates.name: Expiry-day volatility dampening: SPXW daily-expiry natural experiment
candidates.summary: Before May 2022, SPXW options expired on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays but rarely on Tuesdays or Thursdays. Adams et al. use that split to show intraday S&P volatility is lower on days with expiring 0DTEs, because positions that become 0DTE raise dealers' long-gamma hedging needs. A 1-day short-volatility position on expiry days should therefore beat the same position on non-expiry days, and the gap should vanish once every day became an expiry. This generalises Mandel's supported T-216 from monthly OPEX to every expiry.
candidates.mechanism: Longer-dated options that customers sold earlier become 0DTE on their expiry day. Their gamma explodes, leaving market makers net long gamma, and dealers then trade against intraday moves, which lowers realised volatility. New same-day 0DTE trading contributes little. The counterparty is the option buyer, who pays an implied vol that does not reflect the expiry-day dampening.
adjacent_variables: market-maker hedging needs (fraction of index shares per 1% move)
candidates.assets: SPX/XSP/SPY options; SPY or ES as the volatility target
candidates.claimed_effect: Adams, Dim, Eraker, Fontaine, Ornthanalai, Vilkov (2026 draft) estimate on Jan 2018 - May 19, 2022. Days with 0DTE present show 61 annualised bps lower 10-minute realised volatility, about 7% of the 9.10% mean. The two-stage multiplier is about -4: each 1 bp rise in hedging needs lowers realised vol by about 4 bps. Positions that became 0DTE add about 25 bps to hedging needs, while new 0DTE positions add 3 bps. The effect disappears once 0DTEs trade daily. Net gamma predicts lower volatility over the next 10 minutes, fading within about an hour. No trading P&L or costs are reported.
candidates.replication: Cboe's own 2023 analysis found no discernible market impact from 0DTE, with intraday net MM gamma of $170m-$670m. Mandel T-216 (supported, monthly opex Fridays +9.14 bps short-straddle advantage, 1993-2026) is the closest replication. Mandel T-192/T-502 (pin distance) are not_supported, so any dampening shows up in volatility rather than in strike clustering.

sources.title: Do S&P 500 Options Increase Market Volatility? Evidence from 0DTEs (Adams, Dim, Eraker, Fontaine, Ornthanalai, Vilkov)
Do S&P500 0DTEs Options Increase Market Volatility? (Quantpedia summary)
Volatility Insights: Much Ado About 0DTEs (Cboe)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY daily OHLC and VIX, 2016-03..2026-10. Expiry calendar per Adams et al.: regular Mon/Wed/Fri SPXW expiries from 2016, Tuesday expiries from 2022-04-26 and Thursday from 2022-05-19, plus month- and quarter-end Tue/Thu exceptions before then. Statistic: a difference-in-differences of the model-priced 1-day ATM short-straddle P&L (sigma = prior-close VIX, settled on the close-to-close move). The first difference is expiry minus non-expiry Tue/Thu before 2022-05. The second is the same contrast after 2022-05, which should collapse to zero, separating the expiry effect from day-of-week. Secondary: Parkinson range scaled by VIX. Pass if the pre-2022 gap is > 0 with a block-bootstrap CI excluding 0 and the DiD is > 0. The VIX1D/VIX ratio (2023+) serves as an implied-side check. No trading cost applies, since this compares the same instrument across days. Exclude FOMC/CPI days as a control, and cite T-264/T-347 for day-of-week priors.

candidates.name: Single-stock expiration-day strike pinning (high open-interest names)
candidates.summary: On monthly expiration Fridays, closes of optionable stocks cluster at strikes with large open interest, through delta-hedge decay and (per NPP) proprietary-trader manipulation. Mandel only tested SPY, at $1 strikes, and found nothing (T-192/T-502). The literature's effect is in single stocks with coarser strike grids, and for S&P futures at the ATM serial strike. Max pain (T-513 blocked, T-223 not supported on Deribit) is the same idea weighted by OI.
candidates.mechanism: As expiry nears, the delta of near-the-money options swings sharply with the stock price. A market maker who is net long those options, hedged short stock, sells above the strike and buys below it. The resulting push toward the strike transfers wealth from option holders (mostly retail) whose contracts finish just out of the money.
candidates.assets: US single stocks with listed options (Mandel's 901-symbol daily history); ES futures as a second arm
candidates.horizon: days (expiration Thursday close to Friday close)
candidates.claimed_effect: Ni-Pearson-Poteshman (JFE 2005): optionable stocks' closes cluster at strikes on expiration dates. Expiration-date returns are altered by at least 16.5 bps on average, about $9bn of market cap per expiration (abstract figures). Golez-Jackwerth (JFE 2012): S&P 500 futures are pinned to the ATM strike on serial-option expiries, and pushed away from it just before index-option expiry. The working-paper estimate is at least $115m notional per expiration day.
candidates.replication: Zhang et al. (2015) found the same on weekly options (cited secondhand in a search summary, not opened). Decay is likely: the samples predate $1 strikes, weeklies and daily expiries. Mandel's SPY test shows nothing post-2005 (distance ratio 1.03, lower in only 9/22 years). It remains untested here on single names, on OI-heavy strikes, and after 2010.

sources.title: Stock price clustering on option expiration dates (Ni, Pearson, Poteshman), JFE 78 (2005)
Pinning in the S&P 500 futures (Golez, Jackwerth), JFE 106(3) 2012
Pinning slides (Avellaneda, NYU)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: Mandel's 901-symbol daily history, un-adjusted with daily-events (splits/dividends), restricted to names with listed options. Monthly OPEX Fridays 2005-2026. Measure the distance of the raw close to the nearest strike on a grid by price bucket. The grid intervals I recall ($2.50 below $25, $5 to $200, $10 above) are approximate, so rerun with finer grids as a sensitivity. Compare OPEX Fridays with non-OPEX Fridays and with the OPEX-Thursday placebo, by year, and with a Holm adjustment over grids. For 2024-10..2026-10, add an OCC option-volume tercile split; pinning should rise with option activity. Pass if the OPEX-Friday mean distance is >= 10% below the Thursday placebo with permutation p < 0.05, holds after 2015, and holds in the top option-volume tercile. Only then build a traded version: a short ATM iron fly at the max-OI strike from the capture box's OI, priced at captured mids plus half-spread.

candidates.name: OPEX-week drift conditional on falling implied volatility (vanna/charm channel)
candidates.summary: Stivers and Sun found large-cap optionable stocks earn high returns in the monthly OPEX week and give some back the week after. Among the explanations they offer are dealer delta-hedge rebalancing and falling implied volatility, which is the academic counterpart of the practitioner vanna/charm story. Mandel's unconditional SPY test (T-438/T-353) failed after 2010. This candidate tests only the slice where the vanna channel should operate: elevated implied vol that is expected to fall into expiry.
candidates.mechanism: Dealers who are short customer puts hold short stock (or futures) hedges. As expiry approaches, OTM put deltas decay (charm), and if IV falls the deltas shrink further (vanna). Dealers then buy back hedges, creating buying pressure into the third Friday. After expiry the support is gone, and a 'window of weakness' (practitioner term) follows.
candidates.assets: SPY/QQQ/IWM, S&P 100 large caps (OEF), ES futures
candidates.horizon: weeks (OPEX week and the following week)
candidates.claimed_effect: Stivers-Sun (March 2010 WP, summarised by CXO) cover 28 large caps over 1996-2008. Average weekly return was 0.45% in OPEX weeks vs 0.12% otherwise, and 0.83% in the high option-to-stock-volume weeks. The post-OPEX week averaged -0.03% vs 0.18%. Quantpedia's derived S&P 100 timing rule for 1988-2010 shows about 9.3%/yr and a Sharpe of 0.61, costs not reported.
candidates.replication: Index-level decay: Mandel T-438/T-353 on SPY 1993-2026 give an opex-week excess of -1.2 bps, with halves +19.8 and -22.1. The pattern is gone after 2010 at the index level. Practitioner vanna/charm evidence (SpotGamma and others) was not retrieved, because the web-search budget ran out. This is a duplicate family of T-438, kept only because the IV-conditioning mechanism from Stivers-Sun was not tested there.

sources.title: Quantpedia: Option-Expiration Week Effect (Stivers and Sun, SSRN 1571786)
CXO Advisory: Option Expiration Week Stock Return Drill-down

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, OEF, 2010-2026 (the regime where T-438 failed) with 1993-2009 as a check. Signal at the Friday close before OPEX week: VRP = VIX minus 20-day realised vol in its top tercile, AND VIX9D/VIX < 1 (front implied vol expected to fall). Hold Friday close to OPEX-Friday close. Secondary arm: short the week after OPEX on the same condition. Cost 2 bps round trip. Statistic: conditional OPEX-week excess over all other weeks, studentized block bootstrap (block 4), Holm over 4 arms, both halves of 2010-2026 positive. Cross-sectional forward arm: OPEX-week return of the top-tercile OCC option/stock volume names minus the bottom tercile, 2024-10 onward. That gives only about 24 OPEX weeks of history, so register it as a forward record with a checkpoint at 48 weeks.

candidates.name: Market put/call volume ratio as a contrarian timing signal
candidates.summary: Extreme equity or index put/call volume ratios mark fear or complacency and are claimed to predict index returns in the contrarian direction. Free Cboe data covers 2006-2026, so Mandel can test this cleanly out of sample. The prior from careful practitioner work is weak or null.
candidates.mechanism: Retail and hedger put buying spikes after declines, near capitulation, and call buying spikes near euphoria. The contrarian trader supplies liquidity to these crowded, sentiment-driven flows. Index P/C is contaminated by structural institutional hedging, so equity P/C is the cleaner sentiment read.
candidates.assets: SPY/QQQ, ES futures; VIX futures for the VIX P/C arm
candidates.claimed_effect: CXO (SPY, Cboe and ISE ratios, 1995-Feb 2013): correlations are tiny and some have the wrong sign. The best fit, Cboe equity P/C relative to its 63-day average, has R2 0.006 at 21 days. A 250-day-MA rule returned about 19% gross against 50% buy-and-hold, and costs above 0.25% round trip erased it. Farazmand-de Souza (2017; cap-weighted single-stock put/call OI, 1996-2014): R2 0.06 at 3 months for all stocks, 0.12 for high-idiosyncratic-vol stocks. The gains are concentrated in 2008-09, and the signal has lagged the market since. Blau-Nguyen-Whitby (JBF 2014): unsigned P/C carries daily-horizon information in single stocks, but it is fleeting.
candidates.replication: Contested and mostly negative at the index level. There is no peer-reviewed confirmation post-2013 that I could reach. Mandel's social contrarian theories (T-40 blocked, T-41 parked) are a related family.

sources.title: CXO Advisory: Predictive Power of Put-Call Ratios
CXO review of Farazmand and de Souza, 'Stock Return Predictability: Consider Your Open Options'
The information content of option ratios (Blau, Nguyen, Whitby), JBF 43 (2014)
Cboe equity put/call ratio history (CSV)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: Cboe CSVs (total/equity/index from 2006-11, SPX from 2010-07, VIX from 2006-02, all through 2019-10-04), spliced to the Cboe daily JSON (2019-10..2026-10). Check the overlap for definitional breaks: the JSON is all-Cboe-exchange and may differ in scope. Signal: the 10-day mean of equity P/C as a z-score against its trailing 252 days, known after the close. The z-score handles the secular drift from 0DTE and ETP growth. Fit tercile thresholds on 2006-2015 and evaluate on 2016-2026. Targets: SPY forward 1, 5 and 21-day returns, using non-overlapping windows for the 21-day horizon. Rule: long SPY in the top (fear) z tercile, else flat, versus buy-and-hold. Cost 2 bps per switch. Statistic: excess mean, HAC t, DSR over 4 ratios x 3 horizons x 2 rules. VIX P/C arm: next-week front VX futures return. Cboe marks its data as possibly preliminary, so take values from the next-day file in production.

candidates.name: Index-option open-interest growth (call vs put OI) predicts market returns
candidates.summary: Growth in S&P 500 index-option open interest, especially OTM calls, is reported to predict future market returns. For single stocks, call-OI increases relative to put-OI predict next-week returns. Cboe's free daily JSON gives SPX+SPXW call and put OI from 2019-10, enough for a weekly test without chain history.
candidates.mechanism: Hedgers and informed traders open positions in options before the underlying moves, so new open interest reveals expectations that volume does not. Volume mixes opening and closing trades, while OI changes are net new positions. The other side is dealers, who absorb the new positions and hedge them.
variables: open interest changes (index and equity options)
candidates.assets: SPY/ES (index arm); single stocks for the FKD arm once OCC/Cboe per-name OI is captured
candidates.claimed_effect: Seo-Byun-Kim (J. Futures Markets 2020): growth in index-option OI, particularly OTM call OI, is significantly related to future stock market returns (abstract; magnitude and sample not retrieved). Fodor-Krieger-Doran (FMPM 2011): call-OI increases precede higher and put-OI increases lower single-stock returns. The call/put OI ratio predicts the following week's return after controls, and the put-side effect weakens with controls.
candidates.replication: No independent replication or post-publication test found. These are small-journal results with likely data-mining risk. Untested at Mandel; no duplicate theory exists.

sources.title: Index options open interest and stock market returns (Seo, Byun, Kim), J. Futures Markets 40(6) 2020
Do option open-interest changes foreshadow future equity returns? (Fodor, Krieger, Doran), FMPM 25 (2011)
Cboe daily options market statistics (volume and OI by product, JSON)

candidates.proposed_test: Fetch the Cboe daily JSON for every trading day 2019-10-07..2026-10, a light job of about 1,770 small files. Signal at the Friday close: the weekly change in log(SPX+SPXW call OI) minus log(put OI), deseasonalised by position in the monthly expiry cycle. OI collapses at each third Friday, so compare like-for-like cycle weeks, or use weeks not containing an expiry. Target: next-week SPY return, non-overlapping. Statistic: slope and the sign-rule mean net of 2 bps, HAC t. Halves 2019-2022 and 2023-2026 must both be positive. Arms: equity-option and ETP-option OI as robustness checks, and VIX-option OI as a placebo. Pass at p < 0.05 after Holm over 4 arms.

candidates.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (Johnson-So O/S) cross-section
candidates.summary: Stocks with unusually high option volume relative to share volume underperform the next week. The proposed channel is informed traders with bad news who use options because shorting the stock is costly. Option volume was the blocker. OCC's free daily file now gives option volume for every underlying, by account type, for a rolling 2 years, enough for a first test and a forward record.
candidates.mechanism: Short-sale costs push negatively informed traders into options, especially puts and written calls. Dealers on the other side hedge by shorting stock, which moves the information into the price over the following days. A high O/S therefore marks pending negative news. Ge-Lin-Pearson argue the dominant channel is options' embedded leverage, with opening call purchases the strongest predictor.
candidates.assets: US single stocks with listed options (Mandel's 901-symbol universe), long/short via Alpaca
candidates.claimed_effect: Johnson-So (JFE 2012, 1996-2010): the lowest O/S decile outperforms the highest by 0.34%/week, about 19.3%/yr. The effect is stronger with high short-sale costs or low option leverage, and O/S also predicts earnings news. The OSAP signal list rates OptionVolume1 (O/S) a 'clear' predictor with replication quality 'fair' (original paper t 3.45, weekly CAPM alpha), and OptionVolume2 (abnormal O/S) 'likely'.
candidates.replication: Blau-Nguyen-Whitby (2014): O/S predicts negative returns at daily, weekly and monthly horizons, better than P/C beyond a day. Ge-Lin-Pearson (2016) reinterpret it as an embedded-leverage effect. The main threat is Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (JFE 2025): excluding high-borrow-fee stocks removes at least two-thirds of the predictability of option IV spread and skew, and similar patterns hold for other option signals. If O/S works the same way, it is a borrow-fee proxy that a long-short book cannot capture. I could not retrieve OSAP's post-publication returns for this signal (search budget exhausted), so its post-2010 decay is unknown here.

sources.title: The option to stock volume ratio and future returns (Johnson, So), JFE 106(2) 2012
Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc (OptionVolume1/OptionVolume2 entries)
Why does options market information predict stock returns? (Muravyev, Pearson, Pollet), JFE 172 (2025)
Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns? (Ge, Lin, Pearson), JFE 120(3) 2016

candidates.proposed_test: Data: the OCC volume-query CSV per date (all underlyings, 2024-10..2026-10, about 500 files of about 146k rows), summing contracts across exchanges and account types per underlying. Stock share volume comes from daily-history. Signal: weekly O/S = 100 x option contracts / shares traded (the paper's definition; check it). Sort into deciles within names priced >= $5 with options listed all week. Go long D1-D2 and short D9-D10 for the next week, equal weight, entering at Monday's open (the OCC file for Friday may publish late). Cost 10 bps per side, plus 3%/yr borrow on the short leg. Borrow-fee control in the spirit of Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet: drop names in the top decile of FINRA days-to-cover or with a rising Reg SHO short-volume ratio, and report how much of the spread survives. Statistic: mean weekly L/S, NW t. About 100 weeks is under-powered, so pre-register a forward checkpoint at 156 weeks and report the 2-year number as provisional. Controls: earnings weeks (sec-submissions 8-K dates), size, momentum.

candidates.name: Single-stock put/call volume with customer-account split (Pan-Poteshman proxy)
candidates.summary: Pan and Poteshman's open-buy put/call ratio, built from proprietary Cboe data, predicts next-day and next-week single-stock returns. The unsigned public P/C carries a weaker, fleeting daily signal. OCC's free account-type split (customer, firm, market maker) offers a public middle ground. Customer put volume relative to customer call volume is closer to end-user demand than the total P/C.
candidates.mechanism: Informed traders buy options for leverage. Opening put purchases signal negative private information, and opening call purchases positive. Dealers take the other side and hedge, so the information moves into the stock over one to five days. The non-public part of that information is what pays.
adjacent_variables: customer vs market-maker option volume (OCC account type)
candidates.assets: US single stocks with listed options
candidates.claimed_effect: Pan-Poteshman (RFS 2006, 1990-2001): stocks with low open-buy P/C beat high P/C stocks by more than 40 bps the next day and more than 1% the next week, risk-adjusted. The effect held in every year and was stronger where informed traders concentrate and in high-leverage contracts. Blau-Nguyen-Whitby (2014): unsigned P/C also predicts at the daily horizon, but the effect fades by a week.
candidates.replication: Ge-Lin-Pearson (2016): opening call purchases are the strongest component, through the embedded-leverage channel. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (2025) is a borrow-fee critique of option signals generally. A child learning bears on this: the sports child found copying informed wallets loses the fee at any delay (EDGE_VERDICT Result 18), because flow is a pointer to a source, not a signal to follow. That is a prior against copy-the-flow 'unusual options activity' products. No duplicate theory at Mandel.

sources.title: The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices (Pan, Poteshman), NBER w10925 / RFS 2006
The information content of option ratios (Blau, Nguyen, Whitby), JBF 2014
OCC daily option volume by underlying and account type (volume query)

candidates.proposed_test: Data: OCC volume-query files 2024-10..2026-10 (actype C/F/M, porc C/P). Two signals per name per day: customer-only P/C = customer put contracts / customer call contracts, and all-account P/C. Require at least 500 contracts a day. Sort daily into quintiles within the 901-symbol optionable universe. Go long the low-P/C quintile and short the high, entering at the t+1 open (the OCC file for day t is not assumed available at the t close), holding 1 and 5 days. Cost 10 bps per side, plus borrow on shorts. Statistic: mean daily L/S, NW t, DSR over 2 signals x 2 horizons. The key contrast: customer-only must beat all-account P/C for the informed-customer channel to be credible. Controls: earnings days, the high short-interest exclusion, and the MPP borrow concern. This 2-year sample is a first read only; start daily OCC capture now for a forward record.

candidates.name: BTC signed option taker flow (Deribit) predicting next-day spot
candidates.summary: A crypto analogue of Pan-Poteshman and of the Option Volume Imbalance paper. Mandel already archives Deribit BTC option trades with the taker direction, so delta-weighted net taker buying (calls bought minus puts bought, net of sells) can be tested against next-day BTC returns. Trades execute on US-legal venues (Coinbase spot or Coinbase Derivatives BTC futures); Deribit is read only as a public signal.
candidates.mechanism: Traders with directional information use leveraged options. In crypto these are concentrated in Deribit takers, and block trades by funds. Their signed demand moves dealers' hedges into perps and spot over hours to a day. The other side is market makers, who price in only part of the information.
candidates.assets: BTC (signal from Deribit options; execution on Coinbase spot or Coinbase Derivatives BTC/nano-BTC futures)
candidates.claimed_effect: Equities: Pan-Poteshman, figures as in the single-stock candidate. Michael-Cucuringu-Howison (arXiv 2022): a normalised imbalance of option volume tied to bullish versus bearish views predicts excess overnight equity-market returns. The strongest signal is in market-maker volumes and high-IV options, and put volume carries more than call volume. Magnitudes were not retrieved. No crypto-specific published estimate was found before the search budget ran out.
candidates.replication: No crypto replication found. Related Mandel learnings: T-423 (top-decile Deribit funding as sentiment) not_supported, T-459 (Kraken trade-flow imbalance) untested, T-463 (Kalshi taker flow) not_supported. Flow-following has a poor record in this program, so the prior is skeptical.

sources.title: Option Volume Imbalance as a predictor for equity market returns (Michael, Cucuringu, Howison), arXiv 2201.09319
The Information of Option Volume for Future Stock Prices (Pan, Poteshman), NBER WP

candidates.proposed_test: Data: the deribit-option-trades-near-BTC bundles (2024-03..2026-10). First verify the coverage per UTC day; the daily-BTC bundle's recipe suggests a sampled window starting 07:00 UTC, so use only full-day coverage. Signal per UTC day: sum over trades of direction x amount x Black-76 delta (from the trade IV and index price), normalised by total |delta-amount|. Report a block-trade-only variant. Target: next-day Coinbase BTC-USD close-to-close return, signal known at 00:00 UTC. Rule: sign of the z-scored signal, hold 1 day, with a 3-day arm. Cost 10 bps round trip, with a 20 bps sensitivity, and Coinbase Derivatives futures fees plus funding where held. Statistic: IC with HAC t, sign-rule mean net, DSR over 3 normalisations x 2 horizons. Controls: Deribit expiry Fridays (T-223/T-513 family), funding regime, DVOL tercile.

candidates.name: DIX dark-pool short-volume index and 60-day S&P 500 returns
candidates.summary: SqueezeMetrics' DIX aggregates the dollar-weighted share of FINRA off-exchange short volume across S&P 500 members. They argue market makers shorting to fill customer buys makes it a measure of buying, and that high DIX precedes higher 60-day returns. The white paper dates from 2018, so 2018-2026 is a clean out-of-sample period, and Mandel can rebuild DIX from its own finra-regsho-cnms bundles. This is an adjacent short-volume variable published alongside GEX.
candidates.mechanism: Off-exchange wholesalers and market makers often sell short to fill incoming buy orders and cover later. A high short-volume share therefore reflects customer accumulation, and investors buying into dips, rather than bearish bets.
candidates.assets: SPY / ES futures
candidates.claimed_effect: SqueezeMetrics (2018, vendor, in-sample from 2011): DIX >= 45% is associated with a mean 60-market-day SPX return of 5.3% vs 2.8% for all days. Their stock-level evidence (12.74m stock-days, 2010-2018) is contemporaneous, not predictive: open-to-close return -0.059% when short volume is below 50% vs +0.118% when above. No costs or out-of-sample test are reported.
candidates.replication: A structural break makes the vendor rule unusable as written. By my count of the free CSV, the annual mean DIX was 0.395-0.440 in 2011-2021 but 0.454-0.486 in 2022-2026, and DIX >= 0.45 on 75-96% of days in 2022-2025. The fixed 45% threshold is a regime artefact, and any test must use a rolling percentile. Mandel T-394 (single-stock short-volume ratio z > 2 predicting 5-day returns, 2019-2026) is inconclusive. Overlapping 60-day windows leave few independent observations.

sources.title: Short Is Long: Using dark pool short sales as a proxy for buying activity (SqueezeMetrics)
SqueezeMetrics DIX/GEX daily history (free CSV)

candidates.proposed_test: The out-of-sample window starts after the white paper: 2018-04..2026-10. Signal: DIX as a percentile of its trailing 252 days. Use the vendor series, plus Mandel's own rebuild from finra-regsho-cnms (dollar-weighted short-volume share over point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2018-08+, values known after FINRA's evening file), and report their correlation. Rule: when the percentile is >= 80, go long SPY for 60 trading days, non-overlapping (no new entry while one is open). Compare with matched unconditional 60-day windows. Cost 2 bps. Statistic: mean excess per window, block bootstrap. Expect only about 30-40 events, so this is under-powered; treat a pass as provisional. Secondary arm: the 'high DIX and low GEX' combination, with Holm over 3 arms. A pass must hold in both 2018-2021 and 2022-2026 given the level break.

candidates.name: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing demand and end-of-day momentum (decay test)
candidates.summary: Leveraged and inverse ETFs must rebalance near the close by NAV x (x^2 - x) x the day's return, always in the direction of the move. Baltussen et al. show market intraday momentum strengthens with LETF market share. Barbon et al. find LETF-driven end-of-day effects declined significantly over time while option-gamma effects persisted, so this is a pre-registered decay check that keeps the gamma channel honest.
candidates.mechanism: Predictable mechanical flow near the close: bull LETFs buy and bear LETFs cover on up days, and the reverse on down days. Liquidity providers anticipate a fully predictable mandate. Barbon et al. find this improves liquidity provision and shortens the price impact, which is the stated reason for the decay.
candidates.assets: SPY/QQQ (or ES/NQ futures) last 30-60 minutes
candidates.claimed_effect: BDLM (JFE 2021, Table 9): the interaction of LETF indexing share with the rest-of-day return is positive and significant for equity index futures. Coefficients are 1.79 and 2.94 across specifications, at ** and *** levels; I did not extract the units. Barbon-Beckmeyer-Buraschi-Moerke (SFI WP 22-40, 2021-2022): LETF rebalancing and option delta-hedging both create end-of-day momentum and mean-reversion that fades within the next day. LETF effects declined significantly over time; gamma effects persist.
candidates.replication: Decline documented by Barbon et al. Mandel's T-427 (unconditional last-half-hour momentum) failed on 2023-11..2026-10, and T-428 (closing-auction reversal) failed. T-325 (LETF pair decay) is a different, carry claim.

sources.title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens)
Liquidity Provision to Leveraged ETFs and Equity Options Rebalancing Flows: Evidence from End-of-Day Stock Prices (Barbon, Beckmeyer, Buraschi, Moerke), SSRN 3925725
SFI Research Paper 22-40 listing

candidates.proposed_test: Data: daily shares outstanding and NAV for the main S&P/Nasdaq LETFs (SSO, SDS, UPRO, SPXU, SPXL, SPXS, QLD, QID, TQQQ, SQQQ), from issuer daily files (a new fetch; not verified in this sweep), and Mandel's 60-minute bars for 2023-11..2026-10. Signal at 15:00 ET: demand = sum of NAV x (x^2 - x) x the index return from the prior close to 15:00, scaled by 20-day SPY/QQQ dollar ADV. Target: the 15:00 to official-close return. Statistic: slope with HAC t, plus a demand-sized rule net of 2 bps. Pre-registered expectation, per Barbon et al.: no significant effect. Pass requires slope > 0 at p < 0.05 AND the rule net > 0. Report jointly with the GEX-conditioned candidate, so the two channels are separated in one regression: LETF demand, GEX percentile x return, and their interaction.

candidates.name: 0DTE short premium timed by overnight gap and dealer-gamma regime
candidates.summary: Vilkov's 0DTE study finds a variance premium in SPX 0DTEs, but most static held-to-expiry strategies have insignificant mean returns, and P&L is driven by realised skewness. This candidate tests whether a pre-registered conditioner (small overnight gap, positive dealer gamma, no macro event) turns the 0DTE premium into a positive mean. It overlaps T-141/T-142/T-217 (blocked on chain capture) and is in tension with T-529 (VIX1D premium not supported). It is kept only because the web evidence names the realised-skew channel and the conditioning set.
candidates.mechanism: 0DTE buyers, largely retail and including lottery-like demand, overpay for same-day convexity, so sellers collect a variance premium. Losses cluster on days with large directional moves (realised skewness), which are more likely after big gaps, on event days, and when dealers are short gamma.
variables: calendar: FOMC, CPI, time of day
candidates.assets: SPX/SPXW or XSP 0DTE options (US-listed, cash-settled)
candidates.claimed_effect: Vilkov, '0DTE Trading Rules' (SSRN 4641356; Sep 2016 - Jan 2024 per commentary): static rules entered at 10:00, 13:00 or 15:00 and held to 16:00. The commentary says 0DTEs contain a variance premium, but most strategies' average returns are not significant. Positive medians appear for deep ITM call buys and OTM call and put sales. P&L is largely explained by realised skewness. No return figures were retrievable: the CXO page is paywalled and the Hull Tactical piece is qualitative. Cboe 2023 reports 0DTE customer flow balanced between buying and selling, at about 50% of SPX volume in Aug 2023.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Mandel's T-529 shows VIX1D /365 under-predicts next-day variance (implied 0.847 vs realised 1.071 %^2/day, 2022-05..2026-10), but the result flips sign under the /252 convention. The existence of a 0DTE premium therefore depends on the day-count convention and must be measured on traded prices.

sources.title: CXO Advisory: 0DTE Strategy Outcomes (review of Vilkov, '0DTE Trading Rules', SSRN 4641356)
Hull Tactical: 0DTE options, tiny edge, huge distribution
Volatility Insights: Much Ado About 0DTEs (Cboe)

candidates.proposed_test: This is a forward test on the capture box's 10:00 ET SPXW snapshot, the same infrastructure as T-141/T-142/T-217. Sell a 10-delta / 0.5%-wide put spread and call spread (an iron condor) at the mid minus half-spread at 10:00 ET, settled at the 16:00 SPX close. Pre-registered conditioners, all known before 10:00: |overnight gap| below its trailing-60-day median, prior-close SqueezeMetrics GEX percentile >= 50, and no CPI/FOMC/NFP that day. Statistic: mean return on max loss, conditional minus unconditional, block bootstrap; also CVaR(5%). min_n 120 conditional days. Model-priced pre-test now: use VIX1D (2023+) as the 0DTE IV under both day-count conventions and report both, since T-529 shows the sign depends on it. Do not fund before traded-price evidence exists.

rows.name: Gamma-conditional market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)

overlaps.note: Same hold (15:30 bar open to official close) and the same 2 bps cost. It was unconditional, with the signal measured prev close->10:30. Result: -2.09 bps/day net, HAC t -2.58, slope -0.004 (t -0.22), QQQ and IWM also negative. Its 60 cells count toward this test's DSR.
Close-to-open reversal after the last half hour, same window: b -0.084, HAC t -0.48.
Uses the same dealer-gamma conditioner (on a 0DTE condor) and is blocked waiting for chain GEX. A vendor GEX file would give it a conditioner.
Negative-GEX long 0DTE straddle; same conditioner.
The only supported gamma-mechanism result: opex-Friday 1-day short straddle +9.14 bps (CI +1.81..+16.31), model-priced. That is the long-gamma regime, the opposite of the one this candidate needs.
Intraday ML program: 276 non-crypto cells, 0 pass dev, mean annual SR negative in every family.

learnings.finding: The unconditional last-half-hour momentum rule loses its cost on SPY/QQQ/IWM over 2023-11..2026-10. The predictive slope is zero (-0.004).
276 intraday cells, 15 net>0, none passes dev. Price-only intraday features have negative mean Sharpe.
A strategy that uses price alone starts from a negative base rate, and a backtest edge is suspect until outcomes confirm it.

learnings.source: candidate's own count vs Mandel's bar coverage
learnings.finding: The BDLM state (prior-day GEX < 0) occurs on about 19 sessions inside Mandel's only intraday window (2023-11..2026-10). A percentile conditioner there sorts long-gamma days by how long they are, which is not the published mechanism.
Dealer-gamma effects are visible in daily index moves around monthly expiry, so the channel exists in Mandel's data in the long-gamma direction.
Public, predictable information is priced within seconds. Forced end-of-day hedging flow is predictable and likely competed away (Barbon et al. report LETF effects decaying).
Re-testing a failed rule with a new conditioner is a forking-paths step. The DSR must count T-427's 60 cells.

A sign-based (GEX < 0) arm needs pre-2023 intraday S&P data, e.g. Dukascopy US500 1-minute (free, in the pending batch-6c unlocks, not archived), to reach the ~100+ negative-GEX days of 2018-2022.

registration.claim: On SPY from 2023-11 to 2026-10 (QQQ and IWM as replications), holding from the 15:30 ET bar open to the official close in the direction of the prior-close-to-15:30 return earns a positive mean net return after 2 bps round trip, and more than the same rule on top-quintile sessions, when traded only on sessions whose SqueezeMetrics GEX stamped t-1 (posted before the t open) is in the bottom quintile of its trailing 252-row distribution.
registration.statistic: Primary: difference in mean net return per session, bottom-GEX-quintile minus top-GEX-quintile sessions. Secondary: HAC t of the OLS slope of the last-half-hour return on the rest-of-day return interacted with a bottom-quintile dummy.
registration.null: Bottom-quintile mean net <= 0, or bottom-minus-top difference <= 0.
registration.procedure: r_ROD = SPY 15:30 bar open / prior official close - 1, using hourly-SPY bars stamped by start and the prior close from daily-history. Enter sign(r_ROD) at the 15:30 bar open; exit at the official daily close, not the bar's last trade. Drop early closes and sessions missing the 15:30 bar, as in T-427. GEX: snapshot DIX.csv once, hash it and store it as a vintage bundle. Use the row stamped t-1 at the t open; its percentile is taken within the 252 rows ending at t-1. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily difference series, block 5 sessions, 10,000 draws. DSR counts T-427's 60 cells plus this registration's 6 (3 symbols x 2 arms) = 66 trials. GEX < 0 sessions are reported descriptively (about 19). Diff every later GEX download against the snapshot and report any revised historical row.
registration.data: hourly-SPY, hourly-QQQ, hourly-IWM, daily-history-SPY/QQQ/IWM, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation; new: squeezemetrics-dix-gex vintage snapshot
registration.pass: Bottom-quintile mean net > 0, and the bottom-minus-top difference > 0 with deflated one-sided p < 0.05 over 66 trials. The difference has the same sign on QQQ and IWM and is positive in both halves (2023-11..2025-04, 2025-05..2026-10).
registration.controls: Baseline: T-427's rule recomputed with the r_ROD signal. FOMC/CPI/NFP sessions and monthly opex Fridays are excluded and reported separately. Placebo: quintile labels shuffled in 21-session blocks. 2 bps round trip on every trade. One quintile threshold, no grid. LETF rebalancing demand (the LETF candidate) is added as a covariate once its data exist.

rows.notes: The regime that matters, dealers net short gamma, has almost disappeared from the window where Mandel has intraday bars. A percentile test therefore cannot confirm or refute BDLM, whose result is about the sign of dealer gamma. The informative replication needs pre-2023 intraday S&P data (Dukascopy US500, free). The GEX fetch is still worth doing: the same file unlocks the GEX-straddle and 0DTE candidates, gives T-217/T-218 a conditioner and gives T-580 an F4 flow feature. Executable on Alpaca (SPY/QQQ/IWM) or CME (MES).

rows.name: Dealer gamma level dampens next-day volatility: GEX-conditioned 1-day short straddle

overlaps.note: Same instrument and pricing: model-priced 1-day ATM SPY short straddle, sigma = VIX, T = 1/252, dividend forward. Opex Fridays beat other Fridays by +9.14 bps.
Same conditioner (prior-close dealer gamma) on a 0DTE condor; blocked on chain-derived GEX.
Negative-GEX long straddle; mirror image of this claim.
Witching-Friday long straddle not better. On those Fridays the dividend-neutral |r|/(VIX/sqrt252) is 0.51 vs 0.62 on other Fridays, consistent with dampening.
Conditioning the model-priced short straddle on VRP tercile adds +10.8 pts of premium (CI +2.6..+20.7). Any regime conditioner looks good model-priced, so GEX has to beat VIX/VRP.
Scaling short variance by a VIX-minus-HAR z-score did not raise Sharpe.
A non-price variable (StockTwits intensity) added no incremental R^2 to a HAR regression with lagged RV and implied vol. This is the precedent for the diagnostic here.
The sign of the 1-day variance premium depends on the day-count convention (/365 -0.224, /252 +0.156).
The F3 implied family holds only the VIX complex, VX basis and VRP. No flow or GEX feature exists yet.
MSM beats HMM on QLIKE, so the HAR control can be strengthened with Mandel's own variance models.

learnings.finding: Short 1-day premium earns more on monthly expiry Fridays, when dealers are long the most gamma. The proposed mechanism is the same.
Realised/implied is lower on witching Fridays (0.51 vs 0.62). Expiry-related dampening appears in Mandel's own data.
Conditioning short variance on a forecast-based regime variable did not improve Sharpe out of sample.
Non-price variables have so far failed to add incremental next-day volatility information beyond HAR plus implied vol.
A VRP-tercile split already separates model-priced short-straddle P&L. GEX is low after sell-offs, so a raw GEX split partly re-measures that regime.
The BTC volatility premium is real (+5.3 vol pts, t 2.8), but the one-straddle form had a -88% month and needed a 21-rung ladder. Short 1-day premium needs tail-aware sizing.
The edges that exist are reference-price edges and structural premia. The variance risk premium is structural, so conditioning it is the right family.
Dealer gamma exposure is already listed as a planned options-implied feature, waiting on capture-box chains.

registration.claim: Over 2011-05 to 2026-10, within each VIX tercile, a 1-day ATM SPY short straddle sold at the day t-1 close and settled on the t close earns a higher mean P&L per unit premium when SqueezeMetrics GEX stamped t-2 (posted before the t-1 close) is in the top tercile of its trailing 252-row distribution than when it is in the bottom tercile; the straddle is model-priced with sigma = VIX at the t-1 close, T = 1/252, on the dividend forward.
registration.statistic: Primary: the mean over the three VIX terciles (cut-points from the trailing 252 sessions) of [mean P&L per unit premium on top-tercile GEX days] - [mean on bottom-tercile days]. Diagnostic: out-of-sample R^2 gain of the GEX percentile for the day-t log Parkinson range over log VIX(t-1) + HAR(1,5,22) realised variance, fitted 2011-2018 and evaluated 2019-2026.
registration.procedure: Price the straddle by Black-Scholes on the dividend forward exactly as T-216 (dividends from daily-history-SPY close/adjclose) and settle on raw closes |S_t - K|. Store the hashed DIX.csv snapshot as a vintage bundle. The row stamped t-2 conditions a straddle opened at the t-1 close. The t-1 row is posted after that close and is excluded, which removes a look-ahead in the web proposal. GEX and VIX tercile cut-points use the trailing 252 rows only. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap, block 8 sessions, 10,000 draws, on the daily stratified-difference series. Halves: 2011-05..2018-12 and 2019-01..2026-10. Report the IV-scale sensitivity s in {0.81, 0.90, 1.00, 1.10} (not a criterion) and the OOS R^2 diagnostic. Re-price on captured SPXW 1-day chains as they accumulate.
registration.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history--GSPC, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation; new: squeezemetrics-dix-gex vintage snapshot
registration.pass: Stratified difference > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; positive in both halves; OOS R^2 gain of GEX over log VIX + HAR > 0 on 2019-2026.
registration.controls: Baselines: the unconditional short straddle and a VRP-tercile conditioner on the same days; GEX must keep a positive coefficient alongside VRP in a two-variable regression. FOMC/CPI/NFP days are excluded and reported. Monthly opex Fridays are reported separately because of the T-216 overlap. Placebo: shuffled GEX labels. A half-spread cost proxy of 0.5 vol point per leg is reported. One tercile split, no grid. Same VIX close-timing convention as T-216, common to both groups.

rows.notes: The web proposal used day t-1 GEX for a straddle sold at the t-1 close. That is a one-day look-ahead, because SqueezeMetrics posts the day's value after the close; the registration lags it to t-2. Only the within-VIX-tercile contrast and the HAR increment would show anything new, because GEX co-moves with the VIX regime. Model-priced, so a pass is a lead for captured SPXW chains, not a fundable result. One free fetch makes this testable over about 3,900 days. The same file unlocks the gamma-momentum and 0DTE candidates and an F4 flow-feature ablation for T-580.

rows.name: Expiry-day volatility dampening: SPXW daily-expiry natural experiment

overlaps.note: Monthly-expiry version of the same dampening claim: +9.14 bps short-straddle advantage, 1993-2026. This test generalises it to weekday expiries.
Witching Fridays: |r|/(VIX/sqrt252) 0.51 vs 0.62, lower realised/implied on expiry.
No price clustering at $1 strikes on SPY expiries (ratio 1.016). Dampening, if any, shows up in volatility, not pinning.
Earlier wording of the same pinning test.
No weekday return effect; weekday fixed effects are still needed for volatility.
Day-of-week prior cited by the candidate.
1-day implied vs realised variance (VIX1D), 2022-05+; sign depends on day count.
Deribit monthly-expiry 8h short straddle +15.7 bp, CI -15..+45: no expiry effect shown in crypto.

learnings.finding: Short 1-day premium earns more on monthly expiry days (+9.14 bps, holds after removing ex-dividend and FOMC/CPI Fridays).
Realised moves relative to VIX are smaller on witching Fridays (0.51 vs 0.62).
Deribit monthly expiries show no significant dampening in an 8-hour straddle.
Expiry effects do not appear as strike clustering in SPY, so the outcome should be volatility, not distance to strike.
Hundreds of observations cannot settle a small edge from P&L. Use the more efficient range-based variance measure, not straddle P&L, as the primary outcome.
Cboe announced the expiry calendar in advance, so the treatment is point-in-time-clean. The launch dates must be pinned before any outcome is computed.

rows.missing_data: Nothing needed for the primary arm. The SPXW weekday launch dates (Wednesday and Monday 2016; Tuesday and Thursday 2022) must be pinned from Cboe's public notices before the run. The paper's own outcome, 10-minute intraday RV, needs intraday S&P history before 2023, which is not archived (Dukascopy is free), so the daily Parkinson range stands in for it. VIX1D before its 2023-04 launch is a Cboe backfill.

registration.claim: Over 2013-01 to 2026-10, excluding monthly opex Fridays, month-ends and FOMC/CPI/NFP days, the log ratio of ^GSPC's Parkinson daily range to the VIX-implied daily sigma (VIX at t-1 / sqrt 252) is lower on days with an SPXW expiry than on days without; identification comes from the staggered addition of Wednesday and Monday (2016) and Tuesday and Thursday (2022) SPXW expiries, with weekday and year-month fixed effects.
registration.statistic: Primary: beta on the expiry-day dummy in y_t = beta * Expiry_t + weekday FE + year-month FE + e_t, where y_t = ln(Parkinson sigma_t / (VIX_{t-1}/100/sqrt 252)). Secondary: the same regression with the model-priced 1-day ATM short-straddle P&L per unit premium as outcome (sigma = VIX_{t-1}, settled close to close).
registration.procedure: Expiry calendar: SPXW expiries by weekday from Cboe's launch notices, pinned in the registration before any outcome is computed. Friday weeklies run throughout; Wednesday and Monday start from their 2016 first-expiry dates; Tuesday and Thursday from their 2022 first-expiry dates; holiday shifts follow Cboe rules. Parkinson sigma = sqrt(ln(H/L)^2 / (4 ln 2)) from ^GSPC daily high and low; rows with H = L or a stale open are flagged and dropped. The fixed effects absorb the weekday pattern and the regime, so identification comes only from the four weekday switches. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap with 10-session blocks, 10,000 draws. Episode checks: the 2016 switch alone (2014-02..2018-02) and the 2022 switch alone (2020-04..2024-05). VIX1D/VIX on 2023+ is reported as an implied-side description.
registration.data: daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX1D-history, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: beta < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; beta < 0 in each switch episode separately; secondary straddle-P&L coefficient > 0 (point estimate).
registration.controls: Weekday and year-month FE. Excluded: monthly opex Fridays (T-216), month-end days (EOM SPX options and T-345 flows), macro release days. Placebo: the expiry dummy shifted one session later, expected ~0. Drop-Friday robustness check. No trading cost: a volatility claim compared on the same instrument across days. One outcome, one window, no grid.

rows.notes: Testable today from archived daily data. The staggered weekday switches give a within-weekday before/after comparison, which the candidate's simple pre-2022 Tue/Thu contrast lacked (that version is confounded by weekday). The published effect is intraday (10-minute RV, fading within about an hour), so a daily range dilutes it: expect t of roughly 1-1.5 for a 4% range effect. It extends Mandel's only supported options result (T-216). A pass is a volatility fact; the trade (1-day short premium on expiry days) would then be priced on captured SPXW chains before any funding. Executable form: SPX/XSP options.

overlaps.note: SPY at $1 strikes, 2005-2022: distance ratio 1.016, lower in only 7/18 years.

Deribit max-pain vs delivery price; waits on OI captures.

Expiry effects show up as lower volatility, not strike clustering.
Crypto expiry pinning or dampening is not detectable.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members priced at least $10, 2005-01 to 2026-10, the mean normalised distance of the raw (split-unadjusted) close to the nearest strike on a declared price-bucket grid, measured on monthly expiration Fridays relative to the preceding Thursday, is at least 5% smaller than on non-expiration Fridays relative to theirs.
registration.statistic: Ratio of ratios R = [mean d(opex Fri) / mean d(opex Thu)] / [mean d(other Fri) / mean d(other Thu)], with d = |P - nearest strike| / grid spacing (uniform mean 0.25).
registration.procedure: Raw closes: the daily-history close (split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted) multiplied back by the cumulative later split ratios from daily-events. Grid, declared once: $2.50 below $25, $5 from $25 to $200, $10 above $200. A finer grid ($1 below $50, $2.50 to $100, $5 above) is reported as a sensitivity, not a criterion. Membership from fja-sp500-components as of each date. Only (name, Friday, its Thursday) pairs where both closes exist. Monthly opex = third Friday (Thursday when Friday is a holiday). Inference: permute the opex label across Fridays within each calendar year (10,000 draws), resampling whole dates to keep cross-name correlation; studentized block bootstrap over months as a check. By-year table. Holm over the two grids applies to the secondary only.

registration.pass: R < 0.95 with permutation p < 0.05; R < 1 in both 2005-2015 and 2016-2026; R in the top dollar-volume tercile below R in the bottom tercile.
registration.controls: The non-opex Friday/Thursday double difference removes weekday and round-number clustering. ETFs excluded (covered by T-502). Halves reported. Dollar-volume terciles stand in for option activity until OCC capture exists. No trading cost (a market-structure claim). A traded version (iron fly at the max-OI strike from capture-box OI, at captured mids plus half-spread) only after a pass.

The candidate's 10% bar is lowered to 5% here and fixed before the run. SPY shows nothing (T-502). Expect a null.

Holm over 4 arms: SPY, QQQ, IWM, and the post-opex-week short on the same condition. Halves: 2011-2018 and 2019-2026.

registration.claim: Over 2024-03 to 2026-10, the delta-weighted net taker flow in Deribit BTC options expiring within 8 days over UTC day d, normalised by total absolute delta volume, predicts the Coinbase BTC-USD return from 00:00 to 24:00 UTC on day d+1 with a positive rank correlation, and a long/short rule on its sign earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps round trip.

registration.procedure: Per trade, sign = +1 for a taker buy and -1 for a taker sell. Delta from Black-76 using the trade's iv, index_price as the forward, the strike and the time from the trade timestamp to the 08:00 UTC expiry. S_d = sum(sign x amount x delta) / sum(|amount x delta|). Only UTC days whose paging completed are used. Target from coinbase-1m-BTC-USD (close of the 23:59 bar of day d to that of day d+1). Rule: long when S_d is above its trailing 60-day median, short otherwise, executed as Coinbase Derivatives BTC futures; the spot return is the proxy, and basis/funding is charged when the nano future is held. DSR over 3 normalisations (absolute delta volume, total contracts, z-score vs 60 days) x 2 horizons (1 and 3 days). Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap, block 5 days.

rows.name: Gamma-conditional market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)
rows.source_notes: I opened Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens, JFE 142 (2021) 377-403, and extracted the text. Table 7 (S&P 500 futures, Jan 1996-May 2020, NW t, coefficients x100): with NGE_{t-1} >= 0 the slope is 0.82 (t 1.03, R2 0.05%); with NGE_{t-1} < 0 it is 6.63 (t 4.78, R2 3.58%). Both match the candidate. Table 6: the eta(rROD) rule on the 1/N equity-index futures basket earns 6.86%/yr at 3.96% sd, SR 1.73, before costs. The text says S&P futures stay net-positive at a one-tick cost. Both match. The candidate omits a load-bearing detail. NGE assumes market makers are short ALL puts and long ALL calls (OptionMetrics, 1996-2017). It is extended to May 2020 with SqueezeMetrics data, which the authors checked against OptionMetrics for 2002-2017 and call virtually identical. They count 2,930 negative-NGE and 3,158 positive-NGE days over 1996-2020. I did not open Gao-Han-Li-Zhou or Barbon-Buraschi. The web-search budget ran out before I could search for post-publication decay.
rows.replication_concerns: I downloaded the vendor file (DIX.csv on 2026-10-20: 3,891 rows, 2011-05-02..2026-10-20, columns date/price/dix/gex) and confirmed the candidate's counts. GEX < 0 occurs on 185 of 2,435 sessions in 2011-2020, so BDLM's 2,930 negative days are mostly pre-2011 and the state was rare even late in their own sample. It occurs on 162 sessions in 2021-01..2026-10, of which 104 fall in 2022, and on only 19 inside Mandel's intraday window (2023-11-15..2026-10-13). The proposed percentile conditioner ranks long-gamma days by how long dealers are, so it does not test BDLM's sign mechanism, and neither a pass nor a fail would bear on BDLM. The post-publication test therefore has to use the sign, and it needs 2021-2023 intraday data. Its event set is dominated by 2022, so any pass may be a bear-market regime effect. T-427, the same 15:30-to-close hold with an r1 signal, lost 2.09 bps/day net (HAC t -2.58). The GEX series is a single vendor vintage, not point-in-time, and has no documented methodology history.
rows.data_notes: hourly-SPY/QQQ/IWM: 5,080-5,081 rows each, Yahoo 60m stamped by bar start, about 725 sessions 2023-11-15..2026-10-13, with a 15:30 bar (T-427 used it). daily-history-SPY/QQQ/IWM give the official close. fomc-meetings has 276 rows; macro-release-cpi and macro-release-employment-situation are ALFRED release days. GEX is not archived; I fetched and inspected it only to verify the counts. No pre-2023-11 intraday S&P data is archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The vendor posts the GEX row for day t the evening of t: the 2026-10-20 row was already present at 19:13 ET on 2026-10-20. Only row t-1 is usable at the t open. Yahoo 60m bars are stamped by start, and the 15:30 bar's close is the last trade before 16:00, not the official close, so the exit must use the daily official close. The GEX history is a backfilled vintage: hash it and diff every later download against it. A Dukascopy US500 CFD 16:00 print only approximates the official close.
rows.missing_data: Two inputs are missing. First, a GEX vintage snapshot: the DIX.csv fetched 2026-10-20 needs to be hashed and archived (in_git false; licence unstated). Second, 1-minute S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 prices for 2021-01..2023-11 (Dukascopy US500/USATECH, free, in the pending batch-6c unlock), which cover about 143 of the 162 post-2020 GEX<0 sessions.

final.claim: From 2021-01 to 2026-10 (after BDLM's sample, which ends 2020-05), on S&P 500 sessions whose SqueezeMetrics GEX row stamped t-1 is negative, holding the S&P 500 (SPY, or MES as the executable twin) from 15:30 ET to the 16:00 official close in the direction of the prior-close-to-15:30 return earns a positive mean net return after 2 bps round trip. On those sessions the slope of the last-half-hour return on the rest-of-day return is also larger than on GEX >= 0 sessions.
final.statistic: Primary: the mean over GEX<0 sessions of sign(r_ROD) x r_LH - 2 bps. Secondary: the coefficient d in r_LH = a + b r_ROD + d I(GEX_{t-1}<0) r_ROD + e, with NW t (5 lags).
final.procedure: r_ROD = P(15:30) / prior official close - 1, and r_LH = official close / P(15:30) - 1. For 2023-11..2026-10, P(15:30) is the open of the Yahoo 60m 15:30 bar and the close comes from daily-history. For 2021-01..2023-11, both are Dukascopy US500 1-minute prints at 15:30 and 16:00 ET. Check the splice on the overlap: the correlation of r_LH between the two sources must exceed 0.9, otherwise report the Dukascopy segment separately. Drop early closes and sessions with missing bars. GEX comes from one hashed DIX.csv snapshot stored as a vintage bundle; use the row stamped t-1. Diff every later download against the snapshot and report revised rows. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap of the per-session P&L (block 5 sessions, 10,000 draws). The DSR counts T-427's 60 cells plus this registration's 6 (S&P, Nasdaq-100, Russell x 2 statistics) = 66 trials. Report the trailing-252 bottom-quintile GEX arm on the 2023-11..2026-10 Yahoo window descriptively only.
