final.pass: Primary mean net > 0 with deflated one-sided p < 0.05 over 66 trials. d > 0 with NW t >= 2. Primary mean net is positive in both halves, 2021-01..2022-12 (about 120 events) and 2023-01..2026-10 (about 42 events). The point estimate on the Nasdaq-100 replication is positive.
final.controls: Baseline: the same rule on GEX >= 0 sessions. FOMC, CPI and NFP sessions and monthly opex Fridays are excluded and reported separately. The 2022 regime check reports the rule outside 2022 (point estimate). Placebo: GEX sign labels shuffled in 21-session blocks. If issuer AUM data exist, add the LETF share x r_ROD as a covariate (BDLM Table 9). Costs are 2 bps round trip on every trade. One threshold (GEX < 0), no grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified. However, the BDLM state (dealer gamma below zero) occurs on only 19 sessions in Mandel's intraday window, and a percentile conditioner tests a different mechanism. I re-registered it as a sign-based post-publication test on 2021-2026 (162 events), blocked on the GEX snapshot and 2021-2023 intraday data.

rows.name: Dealer gamma level dampens next-day volatility: GEX-conditioned 1-day short straddle
rows.source_notes: Ni-Pearson-Poteshman-White, RFS 34(4) 2021, 1952-1986: confirmed on IDEAS. The abstract describes a non-informational channel: market makers' hedge rebalancing affects stock return volatility and the probability of large moves. The evidence is on single stocks, not the index. I extracted the text of Amaya-Garcia-Ares-Pearson-Vasquez (Cboe PDF dated 2025-01-25) and confirmed every quoted figure. The sample is Jul 2020-Jun 2023 with proprietary Cboe trade data. The median impact is -0.08 pp of daily vol, and the maximum gamma-induced rise is +3.3 pp daily and +6.4 pp at 30 minutes (annualised), against a 4.5 pp SD of daily changes, which they call not large. Customer-vs-MM trades are 68.717% of volume, and OMM gamma is typically positive. I did not open the SqueezeMetrics 2017 white paper (next-day SD 0.55% vs 0.85%, vendor in-sample) or the Maurer SSRN abstract.
rows.replication_concerns: The supporting evidence shows small dampening and relies on signed proprietary positions. Public open-interest GEX assumes dealers are long all calls and short all puts, which the 68.7% customer-vs-MM share says misclassifies about a third of volume. GEX is low after sell-offs, which is when VRP is high and T-101's VRP-tercile effect operates. The cross-checker's VIX-level stratification therefore leaves the VRP channel open, and stratifying on VRP closes it. There is precedent against such conditioners: T-415 (StockTwits) and T-235 (VIX-minus-HAR scaling) added nothing beyond HAR plus implied vol. The test is model-priced, and T-529 shows the sign of the 1-day premium flips between the /365 and /252 conventions, so any pass is a lead for captured SPXW chains, not a fundable result.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY has 8,485 rows from 1993 (close split-adjusted, adjclose for dividends, which T-216 uses for the dividend forward). daily-history--GSPC (24,814 rows, H/L), cboe-VIX-history (9,294 rows), fred-DTB3, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi and macro-release-employment-situation are present. GEX is not archived. The vendor file covers 2011-05-02..2026-10-20 (3,891 rows), so after a 252-row burn-in the test starts 2012-05.
rows.lookahead_risks: GEX row t posts after the t close (verified), so a straddle sold at the t-1 close can use only row t-2. The cross-checker's fix is correct and the web proposal had a one-day look-ahead. The VIX close is 16:15 ET and the SPY sale is at 16:00. This is the T-216 convention, common to both groups, but it should be disclosed. Percentile and VRP cut-points must use trailing windows ending at t-2 and t-1 respectively. Ex-dividend days need the dividend forward, because T-216's verdict depended on it. The GEX series is a vendor backfill, so hash and diff it.
rows.missing_data: A SqueezeMetrics GEX vintage snapshot: one free fetch, not yet archived. For a traded-price version, SPXW 1-day IV history, which exists only from the capture box (2026-10-14 on).

final.claim: Over 2012-05 to 2026-10, within terciles of the variance risk premium (VIX at t-1 minus SPY's trailing 21-day realised vol, with cut-points from the trailing 252 sessions), a model-priced 1-day ATM SPY short straddle sold at the t-1 close (sigma = VIX at t-1, T = 1/252, dividend forward) and settled on the t close earns a higher mean P&L per unit premium when the SqueezeMetrics GEX row stamped t-2 is in the top tercile of its trailing 252 rows than when it is in the bottom tercile.
final.statistic: Primary: the mean over the three VRP terciles of [mean P&L per unit premium, top-GEX-tercile days] minus [mean, bottom-GEX-tercile days]. Diagnostic: the out-of-sample R^2 gain from adding the GEX percentile to a regression of the day-t log Parkinson range on log VIX(t-1) + HAR(1,5,22) realised variance + event dummies, fitted 2012-05..2018-12 and evaluated 2019-01..2026-10.
final.procedure: Price by Black-Scholes on the dividend forward exactly as T-216, and settle |S_t - K| on raw closes. Store the hashed DIX.csv snapshot as a vintage bundle. Row t-2 conditions a straddle opened at the t-1 close. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap of the daily stratified-difference series (block 8 sessions, 10,000 draws). The halves are 2012-05..2018-12 and 2019-01..2026-10. Report, but do not use as criteria: the IV-scale sensitivity s in {0.81, 0.90, 1.00, 1.10}, a two-variable regression of P&L on the GEX percentile and VRP, and the GEX/VIX correlation. Re-price on captured SPXW 1-day chains as they accumulate.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history--GSPC, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation; new: squeezemetrics-dix-gex vintage snapshot
final.pass: The stratified difference is > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves, and the OOS R^2 gain of the GEX percentile over log VIX + HAR on 2019-2026 is > 0.
final.controls: Baselines: the unconditional short straddle, and the VRP-tercile split alone on the same days. FOMC, CPI and NFP days are excluded and reported. Monthly opex Fridays are reported separately because of the T-216 overlap. Placebo: GEX tercile labels shuffled in 21-session blocks. A half-spread proxy of 0.5 vol point per leg is reported; the comparison uses the same instrument, so costs largely cancel. One tercile split, no grid.

rows.reason: The sources are verified and the t-2 lag removes the web proposal's look-ahead. I changed the stratification from VIX level to VRP tercile, because GEX tracks the VRP regime that T-101 already separates; GEX has to add beyond VRP and HAR to count.

rows.name: Expiry-day volatility dampening: SPXW daily-expiry natural experiment
rows.source_notes:
I extracted the text of Adams-Dim-Eraker-Fontaine-Ornthanalai-Vilkov, a draft dated 2026-07-15. Confirmed:
- Sample and identification: the baseline runs Jan 2018 to May 19 2022 and is identified by exception Tuesdays and Thursdays (holiday shifts and month/quarter-end PM expiries).
- Main effect: days with 0DTE expiries show 61 annualised bps lower 10-minute RV, about 7% of the 9.10% mean.
- Earlier sample: Table IA1, starting in 2012, gives a smaller effect that is still significant.
- 2022 introduction: a 2018-2024 DiD shows the higher Tue/Thu vol disappears after it (Tuesday first expiry 2022-04-26, listed 04-18; Thursday first expiry 2022-05-19, listed 05-11).
- Mechanism: positions accumulated earlier that become 0DTE.
- PM-settled history in the paper: Friday weeklies 2005, SPX Quarterly 2006, SPX end-of-month 2014, Mon/Wed weeklies 2016.
Not checked: the -4 multiplier and the 25 vs 3 bps figures. Not opened: the Cboe 2023 note and the Quantpedia summary.
rows.replication_concerns: The effect is intraday (10-minute RV). A daily Parkinson range dilutes it, so expect t of about 1 to 1.5 per switch. Adams identify only from 2018-2022; the 2016 Mon/Wed switch is untested in the paper, and those new weeklies carried little open interest. SPY/QQQ options added their own Tue/Thu expiries separately later in 2022. That is a second treatment on the same weekdays; the date must be pinned from exchange notices, and I could not verify it here because the search budget ran out. Amaya et al. (the same Pearson group) find small net impacts, and Cboe 2023 found none. T-216 (supported, model-priced) is the monthly analogue, and its verdict depended on how the dividend was treated. T-219 reports dividend-neutral |r|/sigma of 0.51 on witching Fridays vs 0.62 on other Fridays.
rows.data_notes: daily-history--GSPC: 24,814 Yahoo rows with H/L. I checked 2010 onwards: the open equals the prior close on 63 sessions in 2012 and 66 in 2013 (stale opens), and on at most 1 per year from 2014. The 2012-2013 range data is suspect, so start in 2014. Also present: cboe-VIX-history (9,294 rows); cboe-VIX1D-history (1,109 rows from 2022-05, pre-2023-04 values backfilled); fomc-meetings; macro-release-cpi and -employment-situation; fred-DTB3; daily-history-SPY.
rows.lookahead_risks: The expiry calendar was announced in advance, so it is point-in-time clean, but it must be pinned in the registration before any outcome is computed. VIX_{t-1} is known before t. Before the switches, month/quarter-end and holiday-shifted Tue/Thu expiries are treated days. Drop them (Adams Table 2 does the same), or they contaminate the control weekdays. Stale ^GSPC opens in 2012-2013 can corrupt H/L.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the primary arm. Cboe launch notices are needed to pin the first Wednesday and Monday SPXW expiries of 2016, and exchange notices for the SPY/QQQ Tue/Thu dates of 2022 (reported as a sensitivity only). Pre-2023 intraday S&P data for the paper's own 10-minute outcome is not archived.

final.claim: Over 2014-01 to 2026-10, the log ratio of ^GSPC's Parkinson daily range to the VIX-implied daily sigma (VIX_{t-1}/100/sqrt 252) is lower on sessions with a PM-settled SPXW expiry than on sessions without one. The sample excludes monthly opex Fridays, month-end sessions, pre-switch holiday-shifted expiry days, FOMC decision days, CPI and NFP days, and early closes. Identification comes only from the staggered addition of Wednesday and Monday (2016) and Tuesday and Thursday (2022) expiries, under weekday and year-month fixed effects.
final.statistic: beta in y_t = beta * Expiry_t + weekday FE + year-month FE + e_t, where y_t = ln(Parkinson sigma_t / (VIX_{t-1}/100/sqrt 252)) and Parkinson sigma_t = |ln(H_t/L_t)| / (2 sqrt(ln 2)). Secondary: the same regression with the outcome replaced by model-priced 1-day ATM short-straddle P&L per unit premium (sigma = VIX_{t-1}, settled close to close).
final.procedure: Pin the Expiry_t calendar before any outcome is computed. Every Friday is an expiry (weeklies since 2005). Wednesdays count from their first 2016 SPXW expiry and Mondays from theirs, per the Cboe notices. Tuesdays count from 2022-04-26 and Thursdays from 2022-05-19. Flag and drop rows with H <= L or a stale open. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap with 10-session blocks, 10,000 draws. Report two switch episodes: 2014-01..2018-02 (the 2016 switches) and 2020-04..2024-05 (the 2022 switches). Report a sensitivity dropping 2022-05..2022-12 (the window before the SPY/QQQ Tue/Thu expiries), a drop-Friday check, and VIX1D/VIX on 2023+ as a description of the implied side. None of these are criteria.
final.data: daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX1D-history, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation, fred-DTB3
final.pass: beta < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; a beta point estimate < 0 in each switch episode; and a secondary straddle-P&L coefficient > 0 (point estimate).
final.controls: Weekday and year-month FE. The exclusions in the claim. Placebo: the expiry dummy shifted one session later, which must not be significant at 5%. No trading cost (a volatility claim on the same index across days). One outcome, one window, no grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the data are archived. I moved the start to 2014 because Yahoo's ^GSPC has stale opens on 63-66 sessions a year in 2012-2013. I also drop pre-switch holiday and month-end exception days so that the control weekdays are clean, and flag the later SPY/QQQ daily-expiry rollout as a second treatment.

rows.name: Single-stock expiration-day strike pinning (high open-interest names)
rows.source_notes: Ni-Pearson-Poteshman, JFE 78(1) 2005, 49-87, is confirmed as a listing; IDEAS has no abstract and ScienceDirect returned 403. Avellaneda's NYU slides (text extracted) reproduce the 2003 preprint. It uses OptionMetrics Jan 1996-Sep 2002 and Cboe OI/volume by investor class 1996-2001, covering 4,395 optionable stocks and 184,449 stock-expiration pairs. Its statistic is the share of closes within $0.25 of a $5 multiple (about 12-13% for non-optionable stocks), and it notes most pinning occurs when market makers are net long. I could NOT confirm the 16.5 bps or $9bn abstract figures. Golez-Jackwerth, JFE 106(3) 2012, 566-585, is confirmed: S&P futures are pulled to the ATM strike on serial-option expiries and pushed away just before index-option expiry, at least $115m notional per expiration day. I did not open Zhang et al. (2015).
rows.replication_concerns: Decay is likely. NPP's sample predates $1 strikes, single-stock weeklies and daily index expiries, all of which spread gamma across more strikes and dates. Mandel's SPY tests are null: T-502 (ratio 1.016, lower in only 7 of 18 years) and T-192. Pinning concentrates mass in a narrow band around the strike, which a mean-distance statistic (the cross-checker's) dilutes, so NPP's own band-hit statistic is the faithful replication. The strike grid is a rule-based approximation: per-name strike listings and OI were never archived.
rows.data_notes: daily-history covers 901 symbols (Yahoo, close split-adjusted to about 6 decimals). Survivorship by ticker match: 677 of the 977 tickers in the S&P 500 at any time since 2005 have history (69%); 609 of 745 since 2016 (82%); 502 of 503 current members. daily-events has 855 per-symbol families with splits. fja-sp500-components has 2,720 change rows from 1996-01-02; wikipedia-sp500-changes has 412 rows.
rows.lookahead_risks: Same-day closes carry no timing look-ahead. Survivorship: the 901-symbol set is today's universe, so leavers are under-represented. Restrict to point-in-time members with history and report coverage by year; this is not a return claim, but the survivor set skews toward large, option-heavy names. Rebuild raw closes from split-adjusted closes using only splits dated after the observation. Holiday rule: when Friday is a holiday, the expiry moves to Thursday.
rows.missing_data: Per-name strike listings and open interest are not archived anywhere free, so the strike grid is declared rather than observed. OCC per-name option volume is a rolling 2 years only; stock dollar volume stands in for option activity.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members priced at least $10 with daily-history coverage, 2005-01 to 2026-10, the share of raw (split-unadjusted) closes within 5% of the grid spacing of a strike on a declared price-bucket grid rises on monthly expiration Fridays relative to the preceding Thursday. The rise is at least 5% larger than on non-expiration Fridays relative to their Thursdays.
final.statistic: Ratio of ratios R = [h(opex Fri) / h(opex Thu)] / [h(other Fri) / h(other Thu)], where h is the share of name-days with |P - nearest strike| / spacing <= 0.05 (uniform expectation 0.10).
final.procedure: Raw close = the daily-history close multiplied by the cumulative split ratios dated after the day (daily-events). The grid is declared once: $2.50 below $25, $5 from $25 to $200, $10 above $200. A finer grid ($1 below $50, $2.50 to $100, $5 above) is a reported sensitivity only. Membership comes from fja-sp500-components as of each date. Use only (name, Friday, its Thursday) pairs where both closes exist. Monthly opex is the third Friday, or Thursday when the Friday is a holiday. Inference: permute the opex label across Fridays within each calendar year, resampling whole dates (10,000 draws). As a check, run a studentized block bootstrap over months. Report a by-year table and coverage by year.
final.data: daily-history (901 symbols), daily-events, fja-sp500-components, wikipedia-sp500-changes
final.pass: R > 1.05 with permutation p < 0.05; R > 1 in both 2005-2015 and 2016-2026; and R in the top dollar-volume tercile above R in the bottom tercile.
final.controls: The Friday/Thursday double difference removes weekday effects and round-number clustering. ETFs are excluded (T-502). Dollar-volume terciles stand in for option activity. No trading cost (a market-structure claim). A traded version (iron fly at the max-OI strike from capture-box OI, at captured mids plus half-spread) comes only after a pass. One band, one grid.

rows.reason: The core source (NPP via the preprint slides) and Golez-Jackwerth are confirmed, and the test is runnable on archived data. I replaced mean distance with NPP's band-hit statistic, which is more sensitive to pinning, and flagged the survivor-biased 69% coverage since 2005.

rows.name: OPEX-week drift conditional on falling implied volatility (vanna/charm channel)
rows.source_notes: Stivers and Sun is a peer-reviewed article, Journal of Banking & Finance 37(11) 2013, 4226-4240 (IDEAS), not only the 2010 working paper the candidate cites. The abstract finds higher S&P 100 returns in option-expiration weeks and modest underperformance in fourth-Friday weeks. It names market makers' delta-hedge rebalancing and falling option-implied volatility as partial explanations. Quantpedia's 9.3%/yr and SR 0.61 (1988-2010) are Quantpedia's own estimate, which combines expiration-week returns with an assumed cash return; they are not a figure from the paper. I did not open the CXO drill-down.
rows.replication_concerns: The index-level effect is already dead after 2010 in Mandel's own tests: T-438 halves +19.8/-22.1 bps, T-353 +18.1/-15.8. Adding two conditioners (VRP tercile AND VIX9D/VIX < 1) after two failures is a forking-paths rescue. Power is the binding problem. About 50 conditional opex weeks compete with about 150 conditional other weeks, and SPY's weekly sd is about 2.2%, so the SE of the difference is about 36 bps. The minimum detectable effect is therefore about 90 bps, against a claimed 20 bps. Practitioner vanna/charm evidence was never retrieved.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-SPY/QQQ/IWM, cboe-VIX-history and cboe-VIX9D-history (3,968 rows from 2011-01) are present. OEF is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: VIX/VIX9D at the Friday 16:15 close print after the 16:00 SPY entry; the Thursday close must be used. The tercile cut-points must be trailing.
rows.missing_data: OEF daily history. VIX9D before 2011, so the 1993-2009 check cannot apply the term condition.

final.claim: Over 2011-01 to 2026-10, buying SPY at the Friday close before a monthly options-expiration week and selling at the expiration-Friday close, only when VIX minus SPY's 20-day realised vol at the preceding Thursday close is in its top tercile (trailing 156 weeks), earns at least 20 bps more after 2 bps round trip than SPY over non-expiration weeks meeting the same condition.
final.statistic: Mean conditional opex-week net return minus mean conditional non-opex-week net return (bps).
final.procedure: Weeks run Friday close to Friday close, with T-438's holiday rule. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap, block 4 weeks. Halves: 2011-2018 and 2019-2026.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, fomc-meetings
final.pass: Difference >= 20 bps with one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves.
final.controls: Baseline: non-opex weeks under the same condition. T-438's unconditional effect is reported. FOMC weeks flagged. One threshold. NOT RECOMMENDED FOR REGISTRATION: the minimum detectable effect is about 90 bps.

rows.reason: This is a duplicate-family rescue of T-438/T-353, with a conditioner added after two failures. At about 50 conditional weeks the test cannot distinguish the claimed 20 bps from zero (MDE about 90 bps), so a run would only add a deflation-costing trial.

rows.name: Market put/call volume ratio as a contrarian timing signal
rows.source_notes: CXO 'Predictive Power of Put-Call Ratios' is confirmed. It covers Cboe and ISE ratios through mid-Feb 2013 (Cboe index and equity series start 2003 on that page, not 1995). All correlations are tiny and some have the wrong sign. The best R2 is 0.006 (Cboe equity relative P/C, 21 days). The 250-day-SMA rule made 68 round trips over 2005-2013, returning about 19% before costs vs about 50% buy-and-hold, and it lost money once round-trip costs exceeded 0.25%. The conclusion is that equity P/C mostly does not usefully predict returns. Blau-Nguyen-Whitby, JBF 43 (2014), is confirmed: unsigned P/C predicts daily returns and is fleeting. I did not open the Farazmand-de Souza CXO review.
rows.replication_concerns: The prior is weak and practitioner work is null. Mandel's sentiment-contrarian rules have failed or stalled (T-423 DSR 0.000; T-40 blocked; T-41 parked). High P/C coincides with high VIX and recent drawdowns, so P/C must beat a VIX-tercile rule on the same windows or it is a VIX or dip proxy. The 0DTE and ETP-option growth produces a secular drift in volumes, which the z-score handles only partly.
rows.data_notes: Not archived; I probed the URLs live. equitypc.csv covers 2006-11-01..2019-10-04 and is labelled 'EXCHANGE: Cboe'. Its header says equity volume excludes ETPs only from 2012-06-11, which is a definitional break inside the fitting window. The daily JSON starts 2019-10-07 (2019-10-04 returns AccessDenied), so the two sources do not overlap. On adjacent days the JSON's EQUITY OPTIONS volume (847,052 on 2019-10-07) is about 56% of the CSV's (1,515,173 on 2019-10-04), so the scope differs. z-score within each source and do not splice levels. daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history and cboe-vx-futures are archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Cboe marks same-day volume as preliminary, so the ratio for day t must be taken from the file captured after t and used at the t+1 close. A z-score window that straddles the 2012-06-11 ETP exclusion or the 2019 source change mixes definitions: restart the window at each break. Tercile cut-points are fitted on 2006-2015 only and then frozen.
rows.missing_data: A Cboe P/C CSV fetch (a few files) and about 1,770 daily JSON files 2019-10-07..2026-10, shared with the OI-growth candidate. Both are free and neither is archived.

final.claim: Over 2016-01 to 2026-10 (with z-score tercile cut-points fitted on 2006-11..2015-12 and frozen), holding SPY for 5 trading days from the next close after the z-score of the 10-day mean Cboe equity put/call ratio enters its top (fear) tercile earns a higher mean net return after 2 bps per switch than SPY's unconditional 5-day return. It also earns more than the same rule triggered by VIX in its top tercile.
final.statistic: Primary: the mean 5-day SPY return over non-overlapping signal windows minus the mean over all non-overlapping 5-day windows, net of 2 bps per switch, with HAC t. Secondary horizons are 1 and 21 days, and the index (SPX+SPXW) ratio is a second arm.
final.procedure: The z-score is taken against the trailing 252 days within each source. The windows restart at 2012-06-11 and at 2019-10-07, so JSON z-scores begin about 2020-10. The day-t ratio is used at the t+1 close. Inference: studentized block bootstrap, block 10 days. The DSR covers 2 ratios (equity, index) x 3 horizons = 6 trials; only equity at 5 days is the criterion.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history; new: cboe-putcall-history (equitypc/indexpc CSVs) and cboe-daily-options-stats JSON
final.pass: Equity P/C 5-day excess > 0 with deflated p < 0.05 over 6 trials. The excess over the VIX-top-tercile rule on the same windows is > 0. Positive in both 2016-01..2019-10 and 2020-10..2026-10.
final.controls: Baselines: buy-and-hold and always-in. The VIX-tercile rule. A drawdown placebo (enter after SPY closes 5% below its 60-day high). 2 bps per switch. One threshold.

rows.reason: The sources are verified and the data are free. The splice the candidate assumed is impossible (no overlap day, about a 2x scope difference, and a 2012 ETP break), so the z-score is computed within each source. The VIX rule becomes a required comparator, because P/C fear spikes coincide with VIX spikes.

rows.name: Index-option open-interest growth (call vs put OI) predicts market returns
rows.source_notes: Seo-Byun-Kim, J. Futures Markets 40(6) 2020, 989-1010: the IDEAS abstract confirms only that growth in OTM call open interest is significantly related to future stock market returns. I could NOT confirm which market is studied (the authors' other work suggests it may be KOSPI 200, not the S&P 500), the sample, or any magnitude; Wiley returned 403. Fodor-Krieger-Doran, FMPM 25 (2011) 265-280, is confirmed for single stocks. Call-OI increases precede higher returns; put-OI increases precede lower returns, but that effect largely fades with controls; changes in the call/put OI ratio predict the following week's return.
rows.replication_concerns: I found no replication. The evidence is small-journal results with likely data-mining. The index claim may be a transfer from another market. OI changes partly follow price (put OI builds after drops), so without prior-week return and VIX controls the test re-measures short-term reversal. End-of-day OI is public and widely read, and the child learnings say a reference must lead the book.
rows.data_notes: Not archived; I probed the URL live. The Cboe daily JSON has VOLUME and OPEN INTEREST by call and put for SPX + SPXW, INDEX OPTIONS, EXCHANGE TRADED PRODUCTS, EQUITY OPTIONS and VIX from 2019-10-07. On 2019-10-07 SPX+SPXW OI was 4,868,638 calls and 11,804,089 puts. 2019-10-04 is not served. daily-history-SPY is archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: It is unclear whether the OI in day t's file is start-of-day OCC OI (reflecting t-1) or end-of-day. Either way, the Friday file drives a Monday-open entry, which is safe. Expiry collapses (every third Friday, plus the weekly SPXW Friday expiries) produce mechanical OI drops, so weeks containing a monthly expiry and the week after it are excluded.
rows.missing_data: About 1,770 Cboe daily JSON files (2019-10-07..2026-10), free and shared with the put/call candidate; not archived.

final.claim: Over 2019-10 to 2026-10, on weeks with no monthly expiration in either the signal week or the prior week, the Friday-to-Friday change in log(SPX+SPXW call OI) minus log(SPX+SPXW put OI) predicts the next week's SPY return (Monday open to Friday close) with a positive slope, controlling for the prior week's SPY return and VIX change. The sign rule also earns a positive mean net return after 2 bps per switch.
final.statistic: The OLS slope on the standardised signal, with the prior-week SPY return and VIX change as regressors, and HAC t (4 lags). Also the sign-rule mean net return.
final.procedure: One daily JSON per date. The Friday value drives the Monday-open entry. The z-score is taken against the trailing 26 eligible weeks. Holm over 4 arms: SPX+SPXW (primary), equity options, ETP options, and VIX-option OI as a placebo that must fail. Halves: 2019-10..2022-12 and 2023-01..2026-10.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history; new: cboe-daily-options-stats JSON
final.pass: SPX slope > 0 with Holm p < 0.05; sign-rule net > 0; both halves positive; VIX-option placebo not significant.
final.controls: Prior-week return and VIX change as regressors. Unconditional long baseline. 2 bps per switch. No grid.

rows.reason: The data source is verified and cheap, but the index-level source could not be confirmed for the S&P 500, so this is registered at the lowest priority as a mechanism-motivated claim, not a replication. min_n is cut to the about 150 eligible weeks the window actually holds.

rows.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (Johnson-So O/S) cross-section
rows.source_notes: Johnson-So, JFE 106(2) 2012, 262-286, is confirmed (IDEAS). The lowest O/S decile outperforms the highest by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualised); the effect is stronger with high short-sale costs or low option leverage; O/S predicts earnings news. I fetched the OSAP SignalDoc.csv. OptionVolume1 is 'clear' with replication quality 'fair', t 3.45 weekly CAPM alpha, sample 1996-2010, defined as option volume / stock volume with long 9+10 and short 1+2. OptionVolume2 (abnormal O/S) is 'likely', t 2.45. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet, JFE 172 (2025), is confirmed: excluding high-fee stocks cuts the IV-spread and skew predictability by at least two-thirds, with similar patterns for other option-implied predictors. Ge-Lin-Pearson, JFE 120(3) 2016, is confirmed: opening call purchases are the strongest predictor, and embedded leverage is the main channel. The web budget ran out before I could get OSAP's post-publication returns.
rows.replication_concerns: MPP's borrow-fee critique covers implied-vol signals directly, and O/S is explicitly stronger where short-sale costs are high, so the spread may be a borrow-fee premium a long-short book cannot earn. Mandel cannot measure borrow fees (T-193 blocked); FINRA days-to-cover is the only proxy, and T-393 and T-375 are inconclusive. Weekly decile turnover at 10 bps a side is about 25 bps a week on two legs, comparable to a decayed spread (T-319 failed on the same cost structure). About 100 weeks is under-powered.
rows.data_notes: Not archived; I probed the OCC volume-query live. Columns are quantity, underlying, symbol, actype (C/F/M), porc (P/C), exchange, actdate. It is strictly a rolling 2 years: 2024-10-21 is served, while 2024-10-01 is refused with 'Report date cannot be prior to 2 years'. Each day is about 4.6 MB, so the window is about 2.3 GB, not a light job. Each trade appears once per side (for example, matching C and F rows of 40,000 on the same contract), so summing all account types double-counts; that is harmless for a ratio sort but must be stated. finra-short-interest has 211 bundles 2017-12-29..2026-09-30, sec-submissions has 36 bundles, and fja is archived. daily-history covers 524 of 545 tickers in the S&P 500 since 2024-10 (96%).
rows.lookahead_risks: The OCC publication time is unverified, so enter at the first close after the formation week's last file is captured (normally the Monday close), not the Monday open. FINRA short interest must enter at its publication date (about 7 business days after settlement), not its settlement date. Earnings weeks come from 8-K item 2.02 acceptance timestamps. Survivorship is about 4% of members missing over 2024-10..2026-10; report it. The rolling OCC window loses a day of history every day it goes uncaptured.
rows.missing_data: An OCC daily volume-query capture from 2024-10-21 forward, starting now before history rolls off. Borrow-fee history is not available free, so FINRA days-to-cover stands in.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members priced at least $5 with listed options and daily-history coverage, 2024-10-21 to 2026-10, an equal-weight portfolio long deciles 1-2 and short deciles 9-10 of the prior week's option-to-stock volume ratio, entered at the first close after the formation week's OCC files are captured and held 5 sessions, earns a positive mean weekly return. Costs are 10 bps per side on actual turnover plus 3%/yr borrow on the short leg.
final.statistic: Mean weekly long-short net return, Newey-West t (4 lags).
final.procedure: O/S per name-week = the sum of OCC option contracts across exchanges and account types, halved because OCC reports each side, divided by the sum of daily-history share volume, following the OSAP OptionVolume1 definition. Deciles are formed within the week's eligible names. Costs are charged on realised turnover. Borrow control: drop the top decile of FINRA days-to-cover, using its publication date, and report the surviving share of the gross spread. Fama-MacBeth controls: size, 12-1 momentum, 1-week reversal, and an earnings-week dummy from 8-K item 2.02 acceptance dates.
final.data: daily-history, fja-sp500-components, finra-short-interest, finra-regsho-cnms, sec-submissions; new: occ-volume-daily
final.pass: Mean weekly net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both years, and at least half the gross spread survives the days-to-cover exclusion. The result is reported as provisional, with a forward checkpoint at 156 weeks.
final.controls: Fama-MacBeth controls, earnings weeks, coverage report, and costs on actual turnover. One decile split, no grid.

rows.reason: The sources and the OCC data are verified, but the window is a strict rolling 2 years. I fixed the entry timing to a captured-file close, the account-side double count, and costs charged on actual turnover; capture must start now or the history disappears.

rows.name: Single-stock put/call volume with customer-account split (Pan-Poteshman proxy)
rows.source_notes: Pan-Poteshman, NBER w10925 (Nov 2004), later RFS 2006, is confirmed. Put-call ratios built from buyer-initiated opening volume predict returns: low-P/C stocks beat high-P/C stocks by more than 40 bps the next day and more than 1% the next week, risk-adjusted. The source is non-public information held by option traders. Blau-Nguyen-Whitby, JBF 43 (2014), is confirmed: unsigned, publicly available P/C also predicts, but the predictability is fleeting (daily, and weekly only to some extent). Ge-Lin-Pearson (2016) is confirmed: opening call purchases are the strongest component.
rows.replication_concerns: OCC account-type volume is unsigned. It mixes buys and sells and opening and closing trades, so it is far from Pan-Poteshman's open-buy ratio and close to the unsigned ratio that BNW find fades within a week. A 5-day hold may therefore miss most of what remains. Every flow-following rule in Mandel and the children has failed: T-463 lost -4.52 c; Hurst's Kalshi perps taker flow had |t| <= 2.5; following informed wallets lost the fee in EDGE_VERDICT Result 14/18. The MPP borrow-fee critique also applies. About 2 years of history is a first read only.
rows.data_notes: I verified the OCC volume-query live: actype C/F/M and porc P/C per underlying and exchange, a strict 2-year rolling window (2024-10-21 earliest today), about 4.6 MB per day, and each trade counted once per side. daily-history (96% member coverage since 2024-10), fja, finra-short-interest and sec-submissions are archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The day-t OCC file's publication time is unverified, so use it at the t+1 close, not the t+1 open, unless captured timestamps prove earlier availability. Short interest enters at its publication date. Earnings windows use 8-K acceptance timestamps. Survivorship of about 4% is reported.
rows.missing_data: An OCC daily capture with the account-type split, starting now; it is shared with the O/S candidate. Signed open/close volume (Cboe Open-Close) is paid only.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with daily-history coverage trading at least 500 option contracts a day, 2024-10-21 to 2026-10, a long-short portfolio long the lowest and short the highest quintile of the day-t customer-account (OCC actype C) put/call volume ratio, entered at the t+1 close and held 5 sessions, earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps per side on turnover plus 3%/yr borrow on shorts. It also earns more than the same sort on all-account put/call.
final.statistic: The mean 5-day long-short net return over 5 staggered daily cohorts, with NW t. The contrast is customer-only minus all-account.
final.null: Customer-only mean net <= 0, or customer minus all-account <= 0.
final.procedure: Use the OCC volume query per date, with puts and calls separately. Customer P/C = C-side put contracts / C-side call contracts. All-account P/C uses all sides; the ratio is unaffected by the double count. Daily quintiles. The DSR covers 2 signals x 2 horizons (1 and 5 sessions); the 5-session customer arm is the criterion. Exclude earnings windows (8-K item 2.02 acceptance +-1 session) and top-decile days-to-cover names.
final.data: daily-history, fja-sp500-components, finra-short-interest, sec-submissions; new: occ-volume-daily (account-type split)
final.pass: Customer-only 5-day net > 0 with deflated p < 0.05 over 4 trials; customer minus all-account > 0; both years positive.
final.controls: All-account sort, reversal and momentum controls, earnings exclusion, days-to-cover exclusion, costs on actual turnover. One quintile split.

rows.reason: The sources are verified, but the public proxy is unsigned and close to the fleeting BNW signal. Registering it is cheap because the OCC capture is shared. I moved entry to the t+1 close, because OCC's posting time is unverified, and charge costs on actual turnover.

rows.name: BTC signed option taker flow (Deribit) predicting next-day spot
rows.source_notes: Michael-Cucuringu-Howison, arXiv 2201.09319 (Jan 2022), is confirmed. A normalised imbalance of option volume tied to positive versus negative views predicts excess overnight equity-market returns. Market-maker volumes carry the strongest signal, high-IV contracts carry most of the predictability, and put volume is more informative than call volume. No magnitudes appear on the abstract page. Pan-Poteshman is confirmed (NBER page). As the candidate itself states, there is no crypto-specific published estimate.
rows.replication_concerns: No crypto replication exists. Short-dated Deribit taker flow is dominated by hedging and gamma trading, and option buying partly pays the BTC variance premium (T-49 supported), so net buying is not purely directional. Deribit is not a leading reference for Polymarket BTC digitals (child learnings). Taker flow predicted nothing on Kalshi perps (Hurst), T-423 Deribit funding failed, and T-463 flow-following failed. The flow partly reflects the day's own return, so 1-day momentum and reversal baselines are mandatory.
rows.data_notes: deribit-option-trades-near-BTC has 32 monthly bundles, 2024-03..2026-10; 2024-03 alone holds 324,242 trades and is tagged complete. They contain whole UTC days for expiries 0-8 calendar days out, with fields iv, index_price, amount, direction, strike, expiry and type, plus per-day sample-day rows with a 'complete' flag. There is no block_trade_id, so the block-only variant is impossible, and no futures underlying_price, so the index price serves as the forward (basis is small within 8 days). The longer-expiry daily bundle covers only a 07:00-09:00 UTC window, so it is excluded. coinbase-1m-BTC-USD has 58 monthly bundles 2022-01..2026-10, stamped by bar start, where a missing minute means no trade. Also present: deribit-dvol-BTC-history (2,032 rows), deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL (65,382 rows), deribit-delivery-prices-btc (2,639 rows).
rows.lookahead_risks: S_d uses trades up to 24:00 UTC of day d, so entry must be at 00:00 d+1 or later. The target close is the last trade of the 23:59 Coinbase bar, stamped by bar start; it is the last print of day d. Use only days whose sample-day row says complete. Deribit is read as public data only; execution is on Coinbase Derivatives (US-legal). Coinbase spot cannot be shorted, so the long/short rule needs CDE nano BTC futures, and their basis or funding must be charged.
rows.missing_data: Block-trade flags; underlying futures prices per trade (the index price is used instead).

final.claim: Over 2024-03 to 2026-10, the delta-weighted net taker flow in Deribit BTC options expiring within 8 days over UTC day d, normalised by total absolute delta volume, predicts the Coinbase BTC-USD return over UTC day d+1 with a positive rank correlation, beyond day d's own return. A rule that is long when the flow is above its trailing 60-day median and short otherwise earns a positive mean net return after 10 bps round trip plus futures basis and funding.
final.statistic: Spearman IC with HAC t (5 lags), and the IC of the flow residual after regressing it on day d's return. Also the sign-rule mean daily net return.
final.procedure: Per trade: sign = +1 for a taker buy and -1 for a taker sell. Delta = Black-76 using the trade iv, index_price as the forward, the strike, and the time from the trade timestamp to the 08:00 UTC expiry. S_d = sum(sign x amount x delta) / sum(|amount x delta|). Use only complete UTC days. Target = Coinbase close of the 23:59 bar of d+1 / that of d - 1. The rule is executed as Coinbase Derivatives nano BTC futures; the spot return is the proxy, and basis/funding is charged while held. The DSR covers 3 normalisations (absolute delta volume, total contracts, 60-day z-score) x 2 horizons (1 and 3 days) = 6 trials; absolute-delta at 1 day is the criterion. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap, block 5 days.
final.data: deribit-option-trades-near-BTC, coinbase-1m-BTC-USD, daily-history-BTC-USD, deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL, deribit-dvol-BTC-history, deribit-delivery-prices-btc
final.pass: IC > 0 and residual IC > 0, with rule mean net > 0 at deflated p < 0.05 over 6 trials; both halves (2024-03..2025-06, 2025-07..2026-10) positive; still positive at a 20 bps round-trip sensitivity.
final.controls: Baselines: buy-and-hold, 1-day momentum and 1-day reversal. Reported splits: Deribit expiry Fridays, funding regime and DVOL tercile. Costs as stated. No cells beyond the 6.

rows.reason: This is testable now on verified, complete-day archived trades. I added a residual-IC requirement, because the flow partly mirrors the day's own return, and fixed execution to US-legal CDE nano futures with basis or funding charged. The prior is low.

rows.name: DIX dark-pool short-volume index and 60-day S&P 500 returns
rows.source_notes: I extracted the text of SqueezeMetrics 'Short Is Long' (March 2018). It confirms: DIX >= 45% is associated with mean 60-market-day returns of 5.3% vs 2.8% across the whole dataset (S&P 500 components since 2011); the stock-level sample is 12.74 million days, with -0.0593% vs 0.1184% contemporaneous returns. No out-of-sample test or costs are reported. I also confirmed the candidate's level-break claim from the downloaded CSV. The annual mean DIX was 0.395-0.440 in 2011-2021 and 0.454-0.486 in 2022-2026. DIX >= 0.45 held on 75%, 96%, 76%, 76% and 58% of days in 2022-2026, against 0-37% in 2011-2021.
rows.replication_concerns: This is a vendor in-sample claim with no independent replication. The fixed 45% threshold is a regime artefact, so a rolling percentile is required. T-394 found no information in single-stock FINRA short-volume spikes. Short-volume share rises into dips, so DIX may be a dip proxy; the drawdown placebo is the real test. Power is low: about 1,800 eligible sessions give at most about 25 non-overlapping 60-day windows. With a 60-day SPY sd of about 7%, the minimum detectable effect is about 4%, against the claimed 2.5%, so any pass is provisional.
rows.data_notes: finra-regsho-cnms has 99 monthly bundles, 2018-08..2026-10, with short_volume, short_exempt_volume, total_volume and market. Pre-2021-10 files were re-posted as sums of per-facility files, which the archive index treats as PIT-equivalent; available_at is end of trade day. fja-sp500-components is point-in-time. daily-history gives closes for dollar weights, with about 82-96% ticker coverage of members since 2016. After a 252-file-day burn-in from 2018-08, the test starts about 2019-08. The vendor CSV is fetched but not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The FINRA file for day t posts in the evening (about 17:20 ET), so use it at the t+1 close. Membership is as of each date. Members missing from daily-history drop out of the weights, so report coverage. The vendor DIX history is a backfill, so it serves only for correlation and a secondary arm. Use no fixed level threshold.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the primary arm. The vendor CSV snapshot is needed only for the correlation check and the DIX-plus-low-GEX secondary arm.

final.claim: Over 2019-08 to 2026-10, buying SPY at the close of the session after Mandel's rebuilt DIX first reaches the 80th percentile of its trailing 252 file days, and holding 60 trading days with no new entry while a position is open, earns a higher mean return after 2 bps round trip than SPY's 60-day windows started on non-signal days. The rebuilt DIX is the dollar-weighted FINRA off-exchange short-volume share over point-in-time S&P 500 members. The rule must also beat the same rule triggered by a 5% drawdown from the 60-day high.
final.statistic: Primary: mean 60-day SPY log return per signal window minus the mean over all 60-day windows starting on non-signal days. Secondary: the signal-window mean minus the drawdown-placebo window mean.
final.procedure: DIX_t = sum_i(dollar volume_i,t x short_volume_i,t / total_volume_i,t) / sum_i dollar volume_i,t, where dollar volume = FINRA total_volume x the daily-history close, over members on day t. Report coverage. The percentile is taken within the 252 file days ending at t, and entry is at the t+1 close. Inference: studentized circular block bootstrap on the daily exposure series (60-session blocks, 10,000 draws). Holm over 3 arms: rebuilt DIX (primary), vendor DIX percentile, and high DIX with low GEX. Report the correlation between rebuilt and vendor DIX where they overlap.
final.data: finra-regsho-cnms, fja-sp500-components, daily-history, daily-history-SPY; optional: squeezemetrics-dix-gex vintage snapshot
final.pass: Primary difference > 0 with Holm one-sided p < 0.05; secondary (vs drawdown placebo) > 0; positive in both 2019-08..2021-12 and 2022-01..2026-10. Reported as provisional, with a forward checkpoint at 40 windows.
final.controls: Matched unconditional windows, the drawdown placebo, and 2 bps. One percentile threshold.

rows.reason: The vendor source and the level break are verified, and Mandel's own FINRA files avoid the vendor backfill. I made the drawdown placebo part of the pass, because short-volume share rises into dips, and set min_n to the about 15-25 windows the period can actually produce.

rows.name: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing demand and end-of-day momentum (decay test)
rows.source_notes: BDLM Table 9 (text extracted) is confirmed. For equity index futures, IndexingLETF x rROD is 1.79 (t 2.20) in columns 1-2 and 2.94 (t 3.10) in the DiD columns 3-4, coefficients x100, sample June 2006 to May 2020. They cite Cheng-Madhavan for 16.8% (50.2%) of MOC volume on 1% (5%) move days as of Feb 2009. The Barbon-Beckmeyer-Buraschi-Moerke SFI WP 22-40 abstract (2022-04-29) is confirmed: 'While gamma effects are persistent throughout our sample, LETFs effects have decreased over time', and LETF flows attract more liquidity provision with shorter-lived price effects. SSRN returned 403.
rows.replication_concerns: The decay is documented, and T-427 and T-428 found no last-half-hour predictability in the only intraday window. In 2023-11..2026-10 the demand variable is D_t = k_t x r_ROD, where k_t (AUM-weighted L^2 - L share over ADV) moves slowly. In a regression that also contains r_ROD, b is separated from the r_ROD slope only by k_t's drift over 3 years, so it is weakly identified. BDLM needed 14 years of growing LETF share to identify it.
rows.data_notes: daily-history exists for SSO, SDS, UPRO, SPXU, TQQQ and SQQQ (4,194-5,111 rows), but not for SPXL, SPXS, QLD or QID. Issuer shares-outstanding and NAV history (ProShares, Direxion) is not archived and its depth is unverified. hourly-SPY/QQQ have no 15:00 boundary, so the signal time becomes 15:30.
rows.lookahead_risks: Issuer AUM for day t is published after t, so use t-1 AUM. Yahoo 60m bars are stamped by bar start. Exit at the official close.
rows.missing_data: Issuer daily shares outstanding and NAV for the S&P and Nasdaq LETFs; histories for SPXL, SPXS, QLD and QID.

final.claim: Not registered separately. In gex-negative-last-half-hour-momentum-post-2020, add IndexingLETF_{t-1} x r_ROD as a covariate (IndexingLETF = sum over the declared S&P LETFs of prior-day AUM x (L^2 - L) / S&P 500 market cap, per BDLM eq. 16-17), so the gamma and LETF channels are separated in one regression.
final.statistic: Coefficient on IndexingLETF_{t-1} x r_ROD, NW t, reported descriptively.
final.procedure: Only if issuer files with at least 2021-2026 depth are fetched. Use AUM at t-1 and the r_ROD and r_LH definitions of the parent registration.
final.data: parent registration data; new: letf-shares-nav (issuer files)
final.pass: None; it is a covariate, not a criterion.
final.controls: As in the parent registration.

rows.reason: It is not separately identifiable in the 3-year intraday window (demand is about a slow-moving scalar times r_ROD), the expected result is null per Barbon et al., and the issuer data are unverified. Its only value is as BDLM's Table 9 covariate inside the gamma-momentum registration.

rows.name: 0DTE short premium timed by overnight gap and dealer-gamma regime
rows.source_notes: The CXO review of Vilkov's '0DTE Trading Rules' (Nov 2023) confirms the setup only. It uses 30-minute 0DTE price data from Sep 2016 to May 2023, with positions opened at 10:00 (13:00 and 15:00 as extensions) and held to the 16:00 expiry, across calls, puts, straddles, strangles, verticals, ratios and risk reversals, and it estimates the VRP while positions are open. The findings, including insignificant mean returns and P&L explained by realised skewness, sit behind CXO's paywall and could NOT be confirmed. I did not open the Hull Tactical piece. The Cboe 2023 customer-flow balance claim was not checked. The cross-checker's GEX facts (vendor posting time, rarity of negative days) are verified from the vendor file.
rows.replication_concerns: This is a T-217 variant. T-217's GEX-sign split is nearly unworkable now: GEX < 0 occurred on 1 session in 2024, 9 in 2025 and 9 in 2026 YTD, so its negative arm would take decades to reach 120 days. A percentile conditioner is the feasible form. Stacking three conditioners (gap, GEX and no-event) is a forking-paths conjunction, so keep GEX as the single conditioner, make events a sample filter, and report the gap split descriptively. T-529: under /365 the 1-day premium stays negative even ex-events. T-109: model-priced condors fail. Hurst: a real VRP still produced a -88% month. Only traded prices can settle it.
rows.data_notes: options-chain-SPX has only 2 archived snapshots (2026-10-14/15, Cboe delayed). The capture box records 10:00 ET SPXW chains forward. cboe-VIX1D-history has 1,109 rows from 2022-05. daily-history--GSPC, fomc-meetings and the macro release calendars are archived. GEX is not archived; the vendor posts row t the evening of t.
rows.lookahead_risks: Use the GEX row stamped t-1 (posted the prior evening) for a 10:00 ET entry on t. The gap uses the SPX 09:30 open, known before 10:00. Settlement on the SPX 16:00 close (SPXW PM). The capture box's delayed-quote timestamp must be checked against 10:00, because Cboe delayed quotes lag about 15 minutes. The VIX1D pre-test is model-priced, and its history before 2023-04 is backfilled.
rows.missing_data: About 240 sessions of 10:00 ET SPXW snapshots (about a year from 2026-10-14), and a daily GEX vintage recorded forward.

final.claim: On SPXW 0DTE options captured at 10:00 ET from 2026-10-14, excluding CPI, FOMC and NFP days, T-217's iron condor (shorts at +/-0.6% of spot, wings at +/-1.0%) sold at mid minus half the quoted spread per leg and settled at the 16:00 SPX close has a higher mean return on max loss when the prior-evening SqueezeMetrics GEX (row t-1) is at or above the median of its trailing 252 rows than when it is below.
final.statistic: Difference in mean return on max loss (GEX >= trailing median minus below), with CVaR(5%) of each group.
final.procedure: Entry from the capture box's 10:00 ET SPXW snapshot, with its quote timestamp verified. GEX row t-1 is recorded daily as a vintage. Settlement on the SPX 16:00 close. Inference: studentized block bootstrap, block 5 days. Reported, not criteria: the |overnight gap| below its trailing-60-day median split; a model-priced 09:30-to-16:00 pre-test using VIX1D under both /365 and /252 (2022-05..2026-10, without GEX); and the GEX-sign split from T-217.
final.data: capture-box SPXW snapshots (options-chain-SPX family), daily-history--GSPC, cboe-VIX1D-history, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation; new: squeezemetrics-dix-gex daily vintage
final.pass: Difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0; the above-median group's mean return on max loss > 0 after costs; that group's CVaR(5%) no worse than the unconditional CVaR.
final.controls: Sell-every-day baseline (shared with T-142), shuffled-label placebo, event-day exclusion, and costs as stated. One strike set, one threshold.

rows.reason: In substance this is a duplicate of T-217, but the design differs materially and necessarily: T-217's GEX-sign split has only 1-9 negative days a year since 2024. I re-registered it as a T-217 successor with a single percentile conditioner on T-217's own strikes, events as a filter and the gap split descriptive. Vilkov's results could not be verified, and they are not load-bearing.

knowledge.title: Options flow and dealer Greeks as market signals: dealer gamma, vanna/charm, put/call volume, open interest, OPEX and 0DTE (literature survey)
knowledge.markdown:
# Options flow and dealer Greeks as market signals: dealer gamma, vanna/charm, put/call volume, open interest, OPEX and 0DTE (literature survey)

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 13 candidate strategies, each source-checked and re-registered by a verifier. Core papers: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021, "BDLM"); Ni, Pearson, Poteshman & White (RFS 2021, "NPPW"); Amaya et al. (2025 WP); Adams et al. (2026 draft); Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (JFE 2005, "NPP"); Golez & Jackwerth (JFE 2012); Johnson & So (JFE 2012); Pan & Poteshman (RFS 2006); Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet (JFE 2025, "MPP"). Practitioner: SqueezeMetrics (GEX, DIX), CXO Advisory, Quantpedia, Cboe.
- **Links:** https://www3.nd.edu/~zda/intramom.pdf · https://cdn.cboe.com/resources/education/research_publications/gammasqueezes.pdf · https://www.jean-sebastienfontaine.com/papers/0dte-options-volatility.pdf · https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v106y2012i2p262-286.html · https://www.nber.org/papers/w10925 · https://squeezemetrics.com/monitor/static/DIX.csv
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.55 (fraction of the sources actually read and verified: about 22 of 33 opened, most as abstracts or listings).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full text of BDLM, Amaya et al., Adams et al., SqueezeMetrics "Short Is Long" and Avellaneda's slides reproducing the NPP preprint; abstracts or listings of the other papers; the CXO put/call page and the OSAP SignalDoc. Data probed live: DIX.csv (3,891 rows, 2011-05-02..2026-10-20), Cboe put/call files, the OCC volume query. Not opened: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou, Barbon-Buraschi "Gamma Fragility", the SqueezeMetrics GEX white paper, Maurer, Cboe's 2023 0DTE note, Hull Tactical. Vilkov's 0DTE results are paywalled.
- **Selected because:** dealer gamma, put/call volume and open interest are inputs in the user's trading-bot program, and Mandel's unconditional tests (T-427, T-216, T-192/T-502, T-438) gave mixed verdicts. This literature supplies the mechanisms and conditioners those tests lacked.

## What it says

- **Gamma-conditioned intraday momentum (BDLM).** Short-gamma dealers and leveraged-ETF rebalancing trade with the day's move near the close. On S&P 500 futures 1996-2020 the slope of the last half-hour return on the rest-of-day return is 6.63 (x100, NW t 4.78, R² 3.58%) after negative-gamma days and 0.82 (t 1.03) otherwise; the timing rule on the index-futures basket has Sharpe 1.73 before costs (verified). Decay: negative-GEX days are now rare (162 sessions 2021-01..2026-10, 104 in 2022, 19 inside Mandel's intraday window). Barbon et al.: the LETF channel decayed, the gamma channel persists.
- **Gamma dampens volatility.** NPPW (single stocks) find hedgers' net purchased option positions lower volatility. Amaya et al. (Cboe trade data, 2020-2023) confirm the sign at a small size: median -0.08 pp of daily vol, maximum +3.3 pp against a 4.5 pp SD of daily changes. Only 68.7% of SPX volume is customer-vs-market-maker, so open-interest GEX misclassifies about a third. SqueezeMetrics' next-day SD contrast is vendor in-sample.
- **Expiry-day dampening (Adams et al.).** Exception Tuesdays and Thursdays before May 2022 show 61 bps (about 7%) lower 10-minute realised volatility on days with an expiring 0DTE, driven by older positions that become 0DTE; the effect vanished once every weekday became an expiry. No trading P&L; Cboe 2023 found no impact.
- **Strike pinning.** NPP (1996-2002, 4,395 stocks): closes cluster at strikes on expiration Fridays, mostly when market makers are net long. Golez-Jackwerth: S&P futures pin to the ATM strike on serial expiries. Both predate $1 strikes, weeklies and daily expiries; NPP's 16.5 bps is unconfirmed.
- **OPEX week and vanna/charm.** Stivers-Sun (JBF 2013): higher S&P 100 returns in OPEX weeks, partly attributed to delta-hedge rebalancing and falling implied volatility, the academic form of the vanna/charm story. Quantpedia's Sharpe 0.61 is its own construction.
- **Put/call volume.** CXO (2003-2013): correlations tiny, best R² 0.006 at 21 days, and a rule's gross edge vanished above 0.25% round-trip costs. Pan-Poteshman (proprietary open-buy volume, 1990-2001): low-P/C stocks beat high by over 40 bps next day. Blau-Nguyen-Whitby: unsigned public P/C predicts only fleetingly.
- **Open interest growth.** Fodor-Krieger-Doran: call-OI increases precede higher single-stock returns. Seo-Byun-Kim: OTM call-OI growth predicts market returns (market unconfirmed, possibly KOSPI 200).
- **Option-to-stock volume (Johnson-So).** Lowest O/S decile beats highest by 0.34%/week (1996-2010; OSAP "clear", t 3.45); Ge-Lin-Pearson attribute it to embedded leverage. MPP: excluding high borrow-fee stocks removes at least two-thirds of option signals' predictability.
- **Signed option flow.** Michael-Cucuringu-Howison: option volume imbalance predicts overnight equity returns; no crypto estimate exists.
- **DIX.** SqueezeMetrics: DIX >= 45% precedes a 5.3% vs 2.8% mean 60-day return, in sample. The level broke in 2022 (annual mean 0.395-0.440 before, 0.454-0.486 after), so the fixed threshold is a regime artefact.
- **0DTE premium.** Vilkov: a variance premium exists, but most static held-to-expiry rules have insignificant means and P&L follows realised skewness (setup verified, results not).

## Evidence quality

**Rating: mainstream-educational.** The academic core is rigorous (JFE/RFS, Newey-West inference, a natural experiment) but rests on proprietary signed positions. Mandel can test only public proxies (vendor OI-based GEX, unsigned OCC volume), practitioner claims are in-sample, and nearly every effect is small or decayed.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Sign-based gamma-conditioned momentum** as a post-publication successor to T-427, whose unconditional rule lost 2.09 bps/day (HAC t -2.58). A percentile conditioner was rejected: it ranks long-gamma days and tests a different mechanism. Blocked on a hashed GEX vintage and 2021-2023 1-minute S&P data; the deflation counts T-427's 60 cells (66 trials).
- **GEX tercile within variance risk premium terciles** for 1-day short straddles (2012-2026), using GEX row t-2 because row t posts after the t close. VRP stratification is required because GEX is low when T-101's VRP effect operates, and GEX must add out-of-sample R² beyond VIX and HAR, where T-415 and T-235 added nothing. This unblocks T-217/T-218 in model-priced form.
- **The SPXW weekday-expiry switch** (testable now, 2014-2026, Parkinson range over VIX-implied sigma, weekday and year-month fixed effects). It generalises T-216 (supported: opex Fridays +9.14 bps for model-priced 1-day short straddles) and agrees with T-219's lower |r|/sigma on witching Fridays.
- **Single-stock strike-band clustering** (testable now, 2005-2026, NPP's band-hit statistic); T-192/T-502 tested only SPY.
- **DIX rebuilt from FINRA Reg SHO short volume** (testable now, 2019-08..2026-10), with a drawdown placebo in the pass, because short volume share rises into dips; T-394 is inconclusive.
- **Deribit signed delta flow on BTC** (testable now), executed on Coinbase Derivatives nano futures; flow must predict beyond the day's own return. Low prior.
- **Equity put/call z-score contrarian**, which must beat a VIX top-tercile rule.
- **OCC captures start now** for O/S, customer put/call and OI tests (a strict rolling 2-year window).

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **OPEX-week drift with an implied-volatility conditioner: dropped.** A forking-paths rescue of T-438/T-353 (not_supported, halves +19.8/-22.1 bps); at about 50 conditional weeks the minimum detectable effect is about 90 bps against a claimed 20. Vanna/charm stays unproven.
- **Leveraged-ETF rebalancing as its own test: dropped.** Decayed per Barbon et al.; T-427 and T-428 found nothing in the last half-hour; kept only as a covariate.
- **0DTE short premium:** a duplicate of T-217. T-529 shows the 1-day premium flips sign between /365 and /252; T-109 model-priced condors fail; Hurst's real BTC VRP still produced a -88% month. Only traded prices settle it.
- **Flow-following.** T-463 (Kalshi taker flow), T-423 (Deribit funding, DSR 0.000) and Hurst's Kalshi perps taker flow (|t| <= 2.5) all failed, and copying informed wallets loses the fee at any delay (EDGE_VERDICT Result 18). "Unusual options activity" is this family; a reference must lead the book, and end-of-day OI and put/call are public.
- **Put/call and OI growth as index timers** (contested or null), and **vendor GEX/DIX as point-in-time data** (a backfilled single vintage).
- **Borrow-fee confound:** O/S and P/C spreads may be MPP's borrow premium, which Mandel cannot measure (T-193 blocked; days to cover is a proxy).
- Deribit is read as public data only, never traded.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **F4 flow feature family** for T-578: GEX percentile (row t-2 at a close entry), sign(GEX), rebuilt DIX percentile, equity put/call z, SPX call-minus-put OI growth, and expiry flags (monthly OPEX, SPXW weekday expiry, quarter-end). Report ablation IC beside F3 (T-580; F0F1F3 mean IC +0.028, 0 cells pass).
- **Data to add:** a hashed DIX/GEX vintage, diffed per download; the daily OCC volume query by account type from 2024-10-21; Cboe put/call CSVs and daily JSON from 2019-10-07; Dukascopy US500/USATECH 1-minute 2021-2023; capture-box chain OI for Mandel's own GEX and max pain (T-513).
- **Point-in-time rules:** GEX row t posts the evening of t; FINRA short volume about 17:20 ET; the OCC posting time is unverified (use the t+1 close); Cboe same-day volume is preliminary.
- **Tests:** block-shuffled GEX placebo; VRP, VIX and drawdown comparators; both halves positive; deflate over predecessors' cells too.

candidates.name: vix-etp-leverage-rebalancing-late-day-pressure
candidates.summary: Leveraged and inverse VIX ETPs (UVXY, SVXY, SVIX, UVIX, formerly TVIX/XIV) must buy VX futures after the index rises and sell after it falls, at the close. The flow is known from shares outstanding x leverage x the day's index move before 15:30 ET. It predicts the VX/VXX move into the settlement. This is the O'Neill-Whaley (JFM 2023) and Brogger (JBF 2021) result. No public post-2018 out-of-sample test was found.
candidates.mechanism: A daily-reset ETP with leverage L and AUM A needs A*L*(L-1)*r of extra index exposure after an index return r. L(L-1) is positive for every L other than 0 and 1 (2x: 2, 1.5x: 0.75, -0.5x: 0.75, -1x: 2), so long and inverse products all trade in the same direction as the move. Issuers execute near the settlement, often via TAS. Liquidity providers (VX market makers, hedge funds) are paid for absorbing a demand that is uninformed and concentrated in time.
variables: derivative volume and open interest (VX futures)
candidates.assets: VX futures (Cboe CFE), VXX/VIXY/UVXY/SVXY/SVIX/UVIX ETPs (Alpaca-tradable)
candidates.claimed_effect: Brogger (sample 2010-11-30..2017-12-31): the mean anticipated rebalancing flow is 6.7% of VX M1+M2 average daily volume, with a maximum of 58% on 2016-06-24. A one-sd flow (9.8% of ADV) moves VX +0.046 vol points over 15:30-16:15, or 0.039 with controls, against a quoted spread of about 0.05. A strategy that front-runs the flow (trade the M1/M2 index mix at 15:30 in the direction of the index move, exit at 16:15) earned 402%/yr with Sharpe 5.14 gross. At 0.02 vol points of cost that falls to 84.7% and Sharpe 1.08, and it turns strongly negative at 0.04 or more. Profits declined steadily through the sample. O'Neill-Whaley 2023 find significantly positive predictive power for end-of-day VX returns, with the impact diminishing over time; the sample and magnitudes were not visible in the abstract. Todorov (RoF 2024): leverage rebalancing is the largest of the three ETF demand components.
candidates.replication: Independent replication exists: three papers (Brogger JBF 2021; O'Neill-Whaley JFM 2023; Todorov RoF 2024) agree that the price impact is real. Decay is documented by both O'Neill-Whaley (impact diminished because of hedge-fund liquidity and issuers' natural hedges) and Brogger (front-running profit competed away; larger and more predictable flows have smaller per-unit impact, consistent with a sunshine equilibrium). One contrary micro-result: the WPI MSP-2020 project finds the lowest price impact in the last 15 minutes, when ETPs rebalance. The structural break in February 2018 matters: XIV terminated, and UVXY went 2x to 1.5x and SVXY -1x to -0.5x on 2018-02-27, which cut L(L-1). SVIX/UVIX (-1x/2x, 2022-03) then raised it again. I found no published post-2018 holdout.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: VXX as the tradable proxy for the S&P VIX short-term futures index, with VX M1/M2 from the archived cboe-vx-futures supplying ADV and OI. Primary out-of-sample data: Yahoo VXX 60-minute bars (about 2024-10..2026-10, roughly 500 sessions, last bar 15:30-16:00) plus a forward 5-minute capture. The pre-2018 years are not used. Signal at the 15:30 bar open: Rebal_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1}*L_k*(L_k-1)*r_t / ($1000*F_bar*ADV20(M1+M2)). A is issuer shares outstanding x NAV, first-seen, published by the morning of t. L comes from the prospectus, including the 2018-02-27 changes. r_t is VXX's return from the prior close to 15:30. Regression: OLS of r(15:30 to close) on Rebal_t, with controls r(prior close to 15:30) (plain intraday momentum failed on SPY in T-427) and the change in VIX, HAC errors. Trading form: sign(Rebal) on top-tercile |Rebal| days, 15:30 open to the close, 4 bp round trip (report 0/4/8). Pass: slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive net mean with block-bootstrap lower bound > 0, same sign in both halves. Placebo: replace L(L-1) by L, the flow/calendar exposure. The placebo must be weaker.

candidates.name: vix-etp-rebalancing-next-day-reversal-fade
candidates.summary: The close-time VX price pressure from leveraged-ETP rebalancing is temporary and fully reversed by the next afternoon. Fading it at the settlement (liquidity provision, the opposite side of the issuer) is the trade, rather than front-running it.
candidates.mechanism: Rebalancing flows are uninformed, so their impact is transitory. Investors in leveraged ETPs buy high and sell low against their own impact. Whoever supplies TAS/close liquidity to issuers earns the reversal plus a premium for bearing variance (Todorov shows the counterparty is short convexity).
variables: derivative volume and open interest (VX futures)
candidates.assets: VX futures, VXX/VIXY
candidates.horizon: intraday to 1 day (settlement t to 15:30 or close t+1)
candidates.claimed_effect: Brogger (2010-2017): in the regression of the 15:30(t-1) to 15:30(t) VX change on the day t-1 flow, the coefficient is insignificant with controls, meaning the late-day impact is fully reversed. The implied cost to leveraged-VIX investors is 2.4%/yr ($34.3m/yr on average AUM of $1.44bn). Todorov (summary): trading against leverage rebalancing gives large abnormal returns with Sharpe ratios above two across markets, gross.
candidates.replication: Reversal shown by Brogger and implied by Todorov's EFG analysis. Bangsgaard-Kokholm (JBF 2025) also find a reversal in the SPX hedging channel. The fade's profitability net of costs on post-2018 data has not been published. The effect should be smaller after 2018 for the same reasons as the impact, and it is contested: the sunshine-trading reading says liquidity providers already compete it away.

Todorov, BIS Working Paper 952, Passive funds affect prices

candidates.proposed_test: Data: archived VX settlements 2018-03-01..2026-10. M1/M2 are weighted as in SPVXSP. ADV and OI also come from the archive. ETP AUM is first-seen issuer shares x NAV. Rebal_t uses the day's index move to the settlement. Because that is known only at the close, the trade is a MOC/TAS order sized from a 15:50 estimate, and the estimate error is reported. Regression: r(settle_t to settle_t+1) on Rebal_t, controlling for r(t-1 to t), the change in VIX and the VIX/VIX3M regime (T-53). Trading form: short VXX at the close when Rebal_t is in its top tercile, long when it is in its bottom tercile, exit at the next day's 15:30 (Brogger's window) or the close; 4 bp round trip on VXX, or 0.02 vol points per VX leg. Pass: slope < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive net mean with block-bootstrap lower bound > 0 in both halves, robust to excluding 2018-02 and 2020-03, deflated jointly with the late-day pressure claim above.

candidates.name: vix-etp-demand-predicts-spx-futures-close
candidates.summary: End-of-day VX futures demand from VIX ETP issuers predicts the last-minutes SPX futures return, in and out of sample, with a later reversal (Bangsgaard-Kokholm, JBF 2025). The channel is VX market makers hedging the vega they sell to the ETPs.
candidates.mechanism: When ETPs buy VX into the close, VX dealers go short vol. They hedge with SPX futures and options, selling ES because VX and SPX are negatively correlated, so the ETP demand passes into ES/SPY near the close. The opposite side is dealer hedging that carries no information.
candidates.assets: ES/MES futures, SPY
candidates.claimed_effect: The abstract reports that VIX ETP demand is a strong predictor of the end-of-day SPX futures return both in and out of sample, that it has historically been possible to profit from the effect, and that there is some subsequent reversal. The sample period and R2 values were not visible to me (paywall).
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Related equity evidence: leveraged-ETF rebalancing and option gamma drive end-of-day momentum that reverts at the next open (Barbon-Beckmeyer-Buraschi-Moerke, HSG WP 2021). Mandel's own T-427 (SPY last-half-hour momentum) and T-428 (closing reversal) were not supported, and T-658 (equity LETF demand) is blocked on data, so this must add over those.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY (and ES_F) local 60-minute bars 2023-11..2026-10, the same window and cost conventions as T-427 and T-658. Signal at the 15:30 bar open: D_VX = Rebal_t from the late-day pressure claim, converted to vega dollars. Pre-registered sign: negative (ETP buys VX, so dealers sell ES). Regression: OLS of SPY r(15:30 to official close) on D_VX, with controls r(prior close to 15:30) and GEX_{t-1} when archived, Driscoll-Kraay/HAC errors. Second equation: the next close-to-open return, where reversal means the opposite sign. Trading form: sign(-D_VX) on top-quintile |D_VX| days, 2 bp round trip. D_VX is nearly collinear with the SPY intraday move on most days. Report the VIF and rely on AUM-driven time variation for identification (SVIX/UVIX launch 2022-03, AUM swings). Pass: one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over at most 4 cells, same sign in both halves, reversal coefficient of the opposite sign.

candidates.name: vix-etp-calendar-roll-pressure-term-structure
candidates.summary: Constant-maturity VIX ETPs roll daily, selling M1 and buying M2. When net long-vol ETP exposure is large relative to VX open interest, this calendar demand steepens M2 over M1 and lifts the VX futures premium. The resulting carry should then be richer for short-M2 / long-M1 or short-VX positions.
candidates.mechanism: Calendar rebalancing is known daily. Long products (VXX, VIXY, UVXY, UVIX) sell M1 and buy M2, and inverse products do the reverse, so net demand scales with net long exposure. Arbitrageurs must close before expiry, so they are exposed to widening gaps. Todorov finds this pushes M2 up and M1 down and raises the non-fundamental part of VX prices.
variables: implied vol term structure (VIX, VIX3M, VX M1-M2)
candidates.assets: VX futures M1/M2, VXX/SVIX
candidates.claimed_effect: Todorov: in a difference-in-differences around ETF inception, ETFs raised the M1 basis by 82.5% and the M2-M1 spread by 59.1%. The non-fundamental VX component is 18.5%/yr (SUERF summary), or 0.61 vol points, 113% of the M1 basis (BIS abstract). A VX strategy trading on the sign of the ETF futures gap has Sharpe 1.78 (BIS abstract; sample not seen). The ETF share of VX futures is about 25%, and often above 40% (two summaries differ).
candidates.replication: Single main source (Todorov). Mandel's T-160 (gated short-M1/long-M2 calendar) was not supported, with the first half negative and the second half positive. T-651 (roll-hedged daily VX carry) and T-652 (VIX premium falls with risk) are untested. This candidate conditions those on ETP net vega relative to OI, which adds the non-price input. Decay is plausible: net long ETP AUM shrank after the XIV/TVIX era.

candidates.proposed_test: Data: archived cboe-vx-futures per-contract settles and OI, 2013-05..2026-10, holdout from 2019-03. ETP shares are first-seen issuer values. Net calendar demand: C_t = (long-vol ETP $index exposure - short-vol ETP exposure) x (w1_t / days left in the roll period) / ($1000*F1) / OI(M1). Daily test: OLS of the change in ln(F2/F1) from settle to settle on C_t, with controls VIX/VIX3M and days to expiry. Monthly test: at each VX cycle start, the next-21-day P&L of short-M2/long-M1 (T-160's construction) or of the T-651 carry rule, top-half C versus bottom-half C months. Costs: $2/contract/leg plus 1 tick, as in T-160. Pass: daily slope > 0 with p < 0.05 in both halves, a positive monthly difference with block-bootstrap lower bound > 0 in the holdout, and a within-year shuffle placebo weaker.

candidates.name: short-opposite-leverage-etp-pair-intraday
candidates.summary: Shorting a matched pair of long and inverse futures-based ETPs on the same underlying from the open to the close earned consistently positive gross returns in Todorov's sample (VIX, natural gas, silver, gold). Neither leg is held overnight, so no borrow fee accrues on most brokers.
candidates.mechanism: Daily-reset funds compound from the prior close. Intraday, the L and -L funds' returns do not offset exactly: the pair is a variance and path bet that pays when the open-to-close move reverses the overnight gap. Todorov reads it as providing liquidity to leverage rebalancing. It also benefits from ETP tracking errors in crises ('right-way risk').
candidates.assets: UVXY/SVXY, VIXY/SVIX, UVIX/SVIX, BOIL/KOLD, AGQ/ZSL, UGL/GLL (US ETPs, Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Gross, before bid-ask and fees, sample to 2018-12 with the pairs mostly starting around 2010 (CXO summary). VIX (L = +1/-1): 21%/yr, Sharpe 0.89. Natural gas (+3/-3): 43%/yr, Sharpe 2.59. Silver (+2/-2): 18%/yr, Sharpe 1.86. Gold (+3/-3): 8%/yr, Sharpe 0.81. The VIX pair gained 51% on 2018-02-05. Todorov reports that Sharpe ratios account for IB borrow fees, but the net figures were not shown in the summary.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. The closest Mandel theory is T-325 (TQQQ/SQQQ short pair, monthly, with borrow), which was not supported. This candidate differs in holding period (intraday) and market (futures-based ETPs). Several original pairs were delisted or deleveraged (XIV gone; UVXY and SVXY are now asymmetric at +1.5/-0.5; 3x commodity ETNs delisted), so post-2018 tests must use the surviving pairs.

candidates.proposed_test: Pairs: UVXY/SVXY 2018-03.. (archived daily OHLC; weights 1:3 so that net index exposure, -1.5w1 + 0.5w2, is zero), VIXY/SVIX and UVIX/SVIX from 2022-03, and BOIL/KOLD, AGQ/ZSL, UGL/GLL (fetch Yahoo daily OHLC).
