Skip days with no locate, and verify that the broker charges no intraday borrow. Statistic: mean daily net P&L, Sharpe, 1% CVaR, DSR over 6 pairs. Pass: mean > 0 with block-bootstrap lower bound > 0 in 2018-03..2026-10 and in both halves. Diagnostics: correlation of the daily P&L with the sign of the overnight gap times the intraday move, so the variance-bet reading is visible.

candidates.name: vix-etp-flows-and-the-vix-futures-premium
candidates.summary: Investors in long-vol VIX ETPs pull money after the VIX rises, betting on mean reversion. Those outflows coincide with the fall in the VX futures premium when risk rises (Cheng's 'low premium response' puzzle). Lagged ETP flows may help predict the premium and hence VX futures returns.
candidates.mechanism: Redemptions force issuers to sell VX (flow rebalancing), lowering futures relative to expected VIX just as risk is high. The premium earned by short-vol holders then depends partly on retail flows, which leaves a predictable component.
adjacent_variables: CFTC TFF VX positions (asset managers, dealers)
candidates.assets: VX futures, VXX/SVIX
candidates.claimed_effect: Nielsen and Posselt (2012-10..2019-02, 6 long-vol ETPs, 8,001 ETP-days): the average daily flow is 0.49% (median 0.11%). A 1-point rise in an ETP's raw return lowers the next day's flow by 0.72 points. Flows of short-term products are positively related to changes in the VIX premium, most strongly when the premium is large, and VAR impulse responses show flow shocks move the premium. Cheng (RFS 2019): ex-ante VIX premiums predict VX returns with a coefficient near one and fall or stay flat when risk rises.
candidates.replication: The flow-to-premium link has one paper. Cheng's premium predictability was published in a top journal, and a later thesis says it held into 2020 (secondary). Mandel's T-652 (VIX futures premium falls with risk) is untested. This candidate adds flows to it, and its holdout starts after Nielsen-Posselt's sample ends (2019-02).

sources.title: Nielsen & Posselt, Betting on mean reversion in the VIX? Evidence from ETP flows (CREATES RP 2022-06; IRFA 95, 2024)
IDEAS: Nielsen & Posselt, IRFA 95 article 103421
Cheng, The VIX Premium, Review of Financial Studies 32(1)

candidates.proposed_test: Extend T-652 rather than duplicate it. Once per VX cycle, 2013-05..2026-10, with the holdout from 2019-03: P_t = F1 settle - E_t[VIX at settlement], with E_t as specified in T-652. Flow_t = trailing-21-day sum of (change in shares x NAV) for long-vol ETPs minus inverse ETPs, first-seen issuer values, scaled by the VX OI vega ($1000 x OI x F). Step 1: regress P_t on Flow_t and on T-652's risk controls; a positive flow coefficient is expected. Step 2: predict the hold-to-settlement short-F1 return with P_t alone and with P_t + Flow_t (expanding window). Pass: Clark-West p < 0.05 and Campbell-Thompson R2_OS > 0 for the flow-augmented model in the holdout. The trading form (size short-F1 or SVIX by the predicted premium) must beat T-652's rule after $2/contract/leg plus 1 tick.

candidates.name: short-vol-etp-convexity-crowding-tail
candidates.summary: The rebalancing convexity of levered and inverse VIX ETPs, measured as the VX contracts they must buy per 1% index rise relative to VX open interest, sizes the next vol-spike feedback loop (Volmageddon). High convexity should predict larger VX up-moves per unit of SPX decline.
candidates.mechanism: Leverage rebalancing is procyclical: VX up, ETPs buy, VX up further, AUM shrinks, more buying. When the required flow is a large share of OI, liquidity providers cannot absorb it and VX gaps. The losers are short-vol ETP holders and short-gamma dealers.
candidates.assets: VX futures, SVXY/SVIX (risk input for short-vol theories)
candidates.claimed_effect: Todorov: in Feb 2018 the net ETF share of VX was close to zero, but the potential price impact of leverage rebalancing was 60% of the total market size of the first two contracts. Augustin, Cheng and Van den Bergen (FAJ 2021) explain Volmageddon by market concentration plus hedge and leverage rebalancing feeding a loop that pushed futures up and shrank short-vol AUM. Short-vol ETPs lost more than 90% in one day. No forecasting statistics are published.
candidates.replication: Descriptive case studies of one event (2018-02-05) plus Todorov's decomposition. No out-of-sample predictive test found. Short-vol AUM recovered with SVIX (-1x) from 2022, so the measure has variation after 2018.

sources.title: Augustin, Cheng & Van den Bergen, Volmageddon and the Failure of Short Volatility Products, FAJ 77(3)
Todorov, SUERF Policy Note 153 (Feb 2018: 60% potential impact)

candidates.proposed_test: Daily, 2013-05..2026-10, with a holdout from 2019-01: K_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1}*L_k*(L_k-1) / ($1000*F_bar) / OI(M1+M2), using first-seen ETP values and the archived OI. Test 1: on days with an SPX close-to-close return below -1%, regress the VX M1 settle return on the SPX return and on SPX return x K_{t-1}. Pass: interaction coefficient < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, holding when 2018-02-05 is excluded. Test 2: 90th and 99th percentile quantile regressions of VX daily up-moves on K_{t-1}. Tradable form: cut short-vol exposure (T-435's SVXY rule) to zero when K is in its trailing-252-day top decile, compared with always-short on Sharpe, max drawdown and 1% CVaR, 10 bp per switch. Pass for the overlay: lower CVaR and max drawdown with the Sharpe difference >= 0 (one-sided).

candidates.name: gsci-bcom-roll-front-running-decay-test
candidates.summary: This registers the classic commodity-index roll front-run as a decay test. Each month the S&P GSCI rolls on business days 5-9 (BCOM on days 6-10), selling the nearby and buying the next contract. Mou's strategies open the same spread 10 or 5 business days early and unwind it into the roll. Later work finds the effect gone after about 2011.
candidates.mechanism: The roll is large, predictable and uninformed. Front-runners or liquidity providers take the other side of index investors at a temporarily depressed nearby/deferred spread. Predicted decay: sunshine trading, electronic markets and arbitrage capital compete it away.
candidates.assets: CME/NYMEX/CBOT commodity futures calendar spreads (CL, HO, RB, NG, GC, SI, HG, grains; micro contracts where listed)
candidates.claimed_effect: Mou (1980-01..2010-03, 19 GSCI commodities): Strategy 1 opens short-nearby/long-next 20% per day on days -10..-6 before the roll and unwinds 20% per day during the roll. With capital in bills, it earned annualized Sharpe 1.09-2.75 in 2000-2010. Strategy 2 (days -5..-1) earned 0.46-1.78. Annualized over trading periods only, Sharpes were up to 3.99 and 4.39. The energy Strategy 1 portfolio earned 4.43%/yr unlevered excess return with Sharpe 2.2. A control group of 18 non-index commodities shows nothing, and 1980-1999 shows nothing. Irwin, Sanders and Yan (AEPP 2023, 19 markets): in 2004-2011 the nearby-deferred log spread fell 32.1 bp pre-roll (t -6.72) and 5.6 bp during the roll, then rose 36.6 bp after it. In 2012-2019 the moves were -3.1 bp (t -0.9) and +0.2 bp (t 0.06). Roll cost during the window fell from 4.36%/yr (2004-2011) to 0.64%/yr (2012-2019).
candidates.replication: Known to have decayed and contested. Irwin, Sanders and Yan find the impact gone in 2012-2019. Dubois and Marechal find positive abnormal price changes before 2004 (+115/+146 bp nearby/deferred), negative ones in 2004-2010 (-60/-40 bp), and a front-run not profitable after costs. Sanders and Irwin (AEPP 2016, daily firm-level data, 13 ag markets) find index-fund roll trades negatively related to calendar-spread changes, the opposite of price pressure. Saverys (Imperial MSc 2024) finds anticipatory strategies profitable until 2010 and near zero in 2010-2024 (total portfolio mean 0.005, t 0.50). Marechal's 2022 slides say roll-period abnormal returns do not survive costs.

sources.title: Mou, Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll (2011)
Irwin, Sanders & Yan, The Order Flow Cost of Index Rolling in Commodity Futures Markets (AEPP 45(2) 2023)
Sanders & Irwin, The 'Necessity' of New Position Limits in Agricultural Futures Markets, AEPP 38(2)
Dubois & Marechal, The valuation effects of index investment in commodity futures (poster)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: CL, HO, RB, NG (energy is about 55-60% of GSCI weight; this weight is from memory), 2012-01..2026-10, with 2020-01.. as the holdout. Per-contract settlements are stitched from EIA's daily futures contracts 1-4 using the CME expiry calendar (contract k before expiry = contract k-1 after), because the pre-window often straddles an expiry. Roll days are business days 5-9 (GSCI) and 6-10 (BCOM), pre-declared. Strategy 1: short nearby/long next, 20% per day at the settle on days -10..-6, unwind 20% per day on roll days 1-5. Strategy 2: the same on days -5..-1. Equal-dollar legs; P&L in bp of one-leg notional per month. Costs: 1 tick per leg per side (report 0.5/1/2). Primary (decay) hypothesis: the 2012-2026 mean is below half of the 2004-2011 mean computed the same way. Trading null: net mean <= 0. A tradable pass needs net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 (HAC, block bootstrap) in both 2012-2019 and 2020-2026, with DSR over the two strategies. Also report Sanders and Irwin's sign test: the roll-day spread change against the size of index positions in the CFTC CIT supplement.

candidates.name: post-index-roll-spread-reversal
candidates.summary: After the GSCI roll ends, the nearby/deferred spread bounces back as roll pressure is removed. Irwin, Sanders and Yan find the bounce even in 2012-2019, when the pre-roll and roll-window moves had vanished. The reversal leg is buying the spread back after day 9.
candidates.mechanism: If index rolling depresses the nearby/deferred spread temporarily, the spread reverts once the flow stops. Liquidity providers who absorbed the roll unwind their inventory. A residual post-roll drift could reflect slower-moving deferred hedging or other index families rolling at different times.
adjacent_variables: other index roll schedules (BCOM days 6-10, DBC/optimized-roll ETFs)
candidates.assets: CME/NYMEX commodity futures calendar spreads
candidates.horizon: about 2 weeks (business days 10-19 of the month)
candidates.claimed_effect: Irwin, Sanders and Yan: the spread rebounded +46.3 bp post-roll in 1991-2003 and +36.6 bp in 2004-2011, a full reversal. In 2012-2019 they report a statistically significant increase in spreads during the post-roll window that they call anomalous, because the pre-roll and roll moves were insignificant. Its magnitude was not in the text I extracted.
candidates.replication: One source, and the 2012-2019 post-roll rise is flagged by its own authors as unexplained, so a forking-path risk is present. It must be tested out of sample (2020-2026) before it counts.

sources.title: Irwin, Sanders & Yan, The Order Flow Cost of Index Rolling (Table 2, post-GR window)
IDEAS listing, AEPP 45(2) 1025-1050

candidates.proposed_test: Same stitched EIA energy panel as the front-run decay test. Enter long nearby/short next at the settlement of roll day 5 (GSCI business day 9) and exit 10 business days later (ISY window t = 5..14), equal-dollar legs, 1 tick per leg per side. The window 2020-01..2026-10 is the confirmatory holdout. 2012-2019 is reported as a replication of ISY's anomalous finding. Statistic: mean spread change in bp per month, HAC t, block bootstrap. Control: the same leg over a 10-day window placed equally far from contract expiry in months shifted by a placebo calendar (block-shifted roll dates), so a generic drift with time to expiry is not mistaken for roll reversal. Pass: holdout net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and the placebo distribution's 95th percentile below the actual mean.

candidates.name: uso-ung-own-roll-window-pressure
candidates.summary: Single-commodity ETFs roll on published schedules separate from the GSCI window. USO rolled over 4 days about two weeks before expiry until 2020, and since 2020 rolls over 10 days at the start of the month. Settlement prices move against USO on its roll days. Is any spread pressure left, and does it scale with USO's share of front-month open interest?
candidates.mechanism: Sunshine trading: predictable, announced liquidation attracts liquidity providers. The fund still pays an execution cost in settlement prices, which is the counterparties' revenue. The bigger the ETF relative to OI, the bigger the cost.
candidates.assets: NYMEX WTI (CL/MCL) and Henry Hub (NG) calendar spreads; USO/UNG/USL
candidates.claimed_effect: Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle and Venkataraman (JFE 2016; order data 2008-03..2009-02, daily to 2013): USO pays about 25 bp per roll round trip (about 3%/yr) in adverse settlement-price changes. Front-month sales grew to 13% of market volume in the Feb 2009 roll. Temporary impact reverses fast: over 95% of second-contract impact reverses within 15 minutes, and more than 99.95% of the front-month order-imbalance impact within 15 minutes. Effective spreads were narrower on roll days (front 2.03 to 1.96 bp, t -3.97), and there is no evidence of predatory strategies. Implied storage cost was 12.38%/yr (t 22.2) after USO's launch versus 0.49% for 1999-2013 as a whole.
candidates.replication: Supports a cost to the fund but not an easy profit for others. The intraday reversal is quick, and the authors find liquidity provision rather than predation. USO's roll method changed in 2020 to a 10-day roll (2024/2025 financial statements). There is no published test of the post-2020 schedule. UNG's schedule was not verified.

sources.title: Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle & Venkataraman, Predatory or Sunshine Trading? Evidence from Crude Oil ETF Rolls (CFTC OCE draft; JFE 121(1) 2016)

candidates.proposed_test: CL (and NG for UNG), 2010-01..2026-10. Per-contract settlements are stitched from EIA contracts 1-4. USO roll days for each period are taken from USCF 10-Q/10-K and prospectus text, first-seen, pre-2020 and post-2020 separately. The scale variable is USO front-month contracts divided by front-month OI, from 10-Q quarter-end history (USCF daily holdings forward). Statistic 1: the mean change in ln(F1/F2) on USO roll days minus that on the 3-7 days before (Bessembinder's control), regressed on the scale variable, HAC errors. Trading form: short F1/long F2 at the settle two business days before USO's first roll day, exit at the settle of the last roll day, 1 tick per leg per side on MCL/CL. Pass: negative roll-day spread change with p < 0.05 in 2012-2026, a positive scale coefficient, and positive net trading mean with block-bootstrap lower bound > 0 in both the pre-2020 and post-2020 periods.

candidates.name: leveraged-commodity-etf-rebalancing-into-settlement
candidates.summary: This carries the leverage-rebalancing mechanism from VIX to commodity LETFs: BOIL/KOLD (natural gas), UCO/SCO (crude), AGQ/ZSL (silver), UGL/GLL (gold). Their benchmarks use settlement prices, so the predicted pressure falls in the minutes before the NYMEX/COMEX settlement window, not at 16:00.
candidates.mechanism: As with the VIX ETPs, AUM*L*(L-1)*r must be bought or sold at the benchmark fix. In thin markets such as nat gas, where Todorov found ETFs above 30% of market cap in some periods, the impact may be measurable. The opposite side is market makers and swap dealers hedging the ETF exposure.
candidates.assets: NYMEX NG/CL, COMEX GC/SI (micro contracts where listed); BOIL/KOLD/UCO/SCO/AGQ/ZSL/UGL/GLL
candidates.claimed_effect: No direct commodity-close evidence was found. Todorov's NG pair return (43%/yr gross, Sharpe 2.59) and the statement that ETFs often hold more than 30% of VIX and natural-gas futures market cap (CXO summary) imply a large LETF footprint. Equity analogue (Barbon et al. 2021): LETF rebalancing effects at the close are larger than option-gamma effects and revert at the next open.
candidates.replication: Untested for commodity futures as far as I found. The equity version is T-658 (blocked) in Mandel. This should be registered as exploratory, with deflation over 4 commodities.

sources.title: CXO Advisory summary of Todorov (NG +3/-3 pair, ETF market share)
Barbon et al., The Role of Leveraged ETFs and Option Market Imbalances on End-of-Day Price Dynamics

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: NG_F, CL_F, GC_F, SI_F local bars. 15m/5m bars (about 60 days) are for development only. The test uses 60m bars (2 years) plus a forward 5m capture, with the window aligned to each contract's settlement period (NYMEX energy about 14:28-14:30 ET, COMEX metals about 13:28-13:30 ET; to be verified from CME rules before registration). D_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1}*L_k*(L_k-1)*r(prior settle to window start) / ADV20(front, $). AUM comes from ProShares first-seen shares x NAV (10-Q quarterly history, daily forward). Regression: OLS of r(window start to settlement) on D_t, controlling for own r(prior settle to window start) (momentum), HAC errors. Trading form: sign(D) on top-tercile |D| days, 1 tick per side on micro contracts. Pass: slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over 4 commodities, positive net mean in both halves, and a next-session reversal coefficient <= 0.

candidates.name: commodity-linked-note-hedging-pricing-dates
candidates.summary: Banks issuing commodity-linked notes hedge by buying the underlying futures on the note's pricing date. Henderson, Pearson and Wang (RFS 2015) find these uninformed trades raise futures prices, and the move does not reverse. Pricing dates are announced in preliminary SEC filings days ahead, which makes the flow forecastable.
candidates.mechanism: Issuer hedging passes retail and structured-product demand into futures at known times. The opposite side is futures liquidity providers. A permanent impact implies limited elasticity of commodity futures supply. Hedge unwinds at final valuation dates may produce the reverse; that part is my hypothesis and is not stated in the source.
candidates.assets: WTI, Brent, gold, silver, natural gas, BCOM/GSCI futures (CME micro contracts where listed)
candidates.horizon: 1-3 days around pricing; days around valuation dates
candidates.claimed_effect: Initial CLN hedging trades raised the underlying futures by an average of 37, 40 and 51 bp for issues with proceeds of at least $2m, $5m and $10m. The impact was permanent, with no sign of reversal (press summary of the working-paper version). The sample period and note count were not visible to me.
candidates.replication: No replication found. The original sample predates 2012, so the post-2015 effect is unknown; CLN issuance has changed with market structure.

sources.title: Henderson, Pearson & Wang, New Evidence on the Financialization of Commodity Markets, RFS 28(5)
Fuel Oil News: GWU study finds direct evidence financial traders affect commodity prices (37/40/51 bp)

candidates.proposed_test: Events: commodity-linked notes from EDGAR full-text search (424B2, FWP, preliminary pricing supplements) 2008-2026 that reference WTI, Brent, gold, silver, natural gas, BCOM or GSCI. Parse the expected pricing date, actual pricing date, principal, and final valuation date. Final 424B2s are filed after pricing (Rule 424(b)(2) timing, to be verified), so only the preliminary filing's expected pricing date is point-in-time. Arm A: buy the underlying front micro future at the settle two business days before the expected pricing date and exit at the pricing-date settle. Arm B (exploratory): short over the two days before the final valuation date. Abnormal return = futures return minus beta x a commodity-index ETF (DBC) return, clustered by date. Pass for Arm A: size-weighted mean abnormal return > 0 net of 1 tick per side with one-sided p < 0.05, positive in 2008-2016 and 2017-2026, and increasing across size buckets (>= $2m, $5m, $10m). Arm B is reported but not judged.

candidates.name: annual-commodity-index-reweighting-flows
candidates.summary: Each January the BCOM (business days 6-10) and S&P GSCI reweight to target weights published months earlier. Commodities that rallied above their caps are sold mechanically and laggards are bought. Bank desks publish flow estimates each year (e.g., Jan 2026 silver and gold selling), but no measured price-impact study was found.
candidates.mechanism: Weight changes are known in advance from the published target weights and the December drift, so the flow is predictable and uninformed. Front-runners or the market absorb it, and a temporary price effect in the window should reverse.
candidates.assets: About 20 US-listed commodity futures (energy, metals, grains, softs, livestock)
candidates.claimed_effect: Practitioner estimates for Jan 2026, from news summaries; no realised impact was measured. Citi estimated about $6.8bn of silver futures selling (about 12% of COMEX OI) and a similar gold amount. TD Securities estimated 13% of COMEX silver OI sold over two weeks, Societe Generale about $5bn each in silver and gold, and JPMorgan about 9% of silver OI and 3% of gold OI. WisdomTree says the 2026 BCOM rebalance ran 9-15 January; other sources say 8-14 January.
candidates.replication: None. This is a new test, and the mechanism is the index-inclusion effect applied to commodity weights. Expect the roll-front-run decay findings to apply as well.

candidates.proposed_test: Years 2010-2026, with 2019+ as the holdout. Target weights come from the Bloomberg BCOM and S&P GSCI annual announcements, first-seen at their publication date. Drifted weights are computed from constituent excess returns through the last December close. Implied flow_i = (target_i - drifted_i) / (front-month OI_i x price), with a pre-declared constant AUM so that only sign and relative size matter. Dependent variables: front-future excess return over the reweight window (BCOM days 6-10) and over the following 5 business days (reversal). Yahoo front continuous series: CL, NG, HO, RB, BZ, GC, SI, HG, ZC, ZS, ZW, KC, SB, CT, LE, HE. Statistic: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional slope of window return on implied flow, about 16-20 commodities x 17 years, with the year-level t. Pass: positive window slope (selling lowers prices) with one-sided p < 0.05 in the holdout and a negative post-window slope. The trading form, long the most-bought and short the most-sold over the window in micro futures at 1 tick per side, must be net positive.

candidates.name: futures-btc-etf-roll-cme-calendar-pressure
candidates.summary: BITO, the first US bitcoin-futures ETF, held about a third of short-term CME bitcoin futures 10 days after its October 2021 launch, and futures-based BTC ETFs were about half of CME OI by October 2022. Its monthly roll sells the expiring contract and buys the next. Commentary links roll periods to basis lows. Does the roll window still move the CME calendar spread?
candidates.mechanism: Calendar rebalancing by a large, predictable holder pushes the expiring contract down and the next contract up (BIS). Basis traders and CME market makers take the other side.
variables: derivative volume and open interest (CME BTC futures)
candidates.assets: CME Bitcoin and Micro Bitcoin futures calendar spread; BITO
candidates.claimed_effect: BIS (Dec 2021): BITO reached about one third of short-term bitcoin futures 10 days after launch. Its calendar rebalancing lowers the price of contracts it sells before expiry and raises deferred ones. Had it launched in 2018, it would have underperformed spot by about 18% cumulatively over four years. Morningstar: the implied annual roll cost rose from 9.7% (2021-10-15) to 11.8% (2021-10-22). K33 (Oct 2022): futures-based BTC ETFs were about half of CME OI, BITO's exposure was 32,520 BTC, and the August 2022 roll plus market conditions pushed the 1-month basis to an all-time low.
candidates.replication: No academic study of the BITO roll found. After spot ETFs launched in January 2024, BITO's share of CME OI likely fell (not verified), so any effect should have decayed.

candidates.proposed_test: CME BTC monthly futures 2021-10..2026-10. This is blocked on per-contract settlement history: CME DataMine is paid, and the alternative is a forward capture of cmegroup.com daily settlements plus any per-contract history obtainable. BITO's roll days come from ProShares disclosures (first-seen), and the scale variable is BITO front-month contracts / CME OI. candidates.name: spot-btc-etf-flows-to-cme-basis-shorts
candidates.summary: Daily creations in US spot bitcoin ETFs are partly the long leg of hedge-fund cash-and-carry trades. Inflows come with new CME futures shorts (CFTC leveraged funds), which links an ETF-flow variable to the CME basis. This is a flow-into-futures mechanism one step from the roll candidates.
candidates.mechanism: When the basis is rich, funds buy ETF shares and short CME futures. The creations are visible the next morning, and the futures leg adds selling pressure on the basis. The opposite side is long-futures demand (leveraged longs, BITO-type products).
candidates.assets: CME BTC/Micro BTC futures, IBIT/FBTC (Alpaca), Coinbase spot
candidates.claimed_effect: NYDIG (2024-11-15): weekly data, with IBIT flows lagged one day; the sample period is not stated. Each $1 of weekly ETF inflow is associated with about $0.30 of added leveraged-fund basis shorts (t 6.4, R2 about 0.51). The CME annualized basis reached the mid-teens during the late-2024 rally. Other commentary (IOSG, Bitwise, traders) disputes the arbitrage share of flows, from under 15% to a majority.

It overlaps Mandel's T-329 (basis z-score carry, inconclusive), T-362 (cash-and-carry, not supported) and T-612 (leveraged-funds change, untested). It is kept because it adds the ETF-flow input those lack.

rows.name: vix-etp-leverage-rebalancing-late-day-pressure

overlaps.note: Same mechanism (A*L*(L-1)*r, 15:30 bar open to the official close, next-day reversal leg) on equity LETFs. Blocked on the same missing input: issuer daily shares outstanding and NAV history. The two should share one data unlock and one deflation family.
Price-only last-half-hour momentum on SPY/QQQ/IWM 60m bars 2023-11..2026-10 failed (-2.09 bp/day net; slope on r1 -0.004, t -0.22). The flow term has to add over r(prior close to 15:30).
No closing-auction reversal on SPY (slope -0.084, t -0.48).
GEX-conditioned last-half-hour momentum; also blocked on data.
Method: the 15:30 bar close is the last regular trade before 16:00, verified on 5m bars. The exit must be the official close.

learnings.finding: There is no price-only late-day momentum in liquid US ETFs on 2023-11..2026-10 60m bars.
A predictable mechanical flow (month-end SPY-vs-TLT rebalancing) leaves a footprint: -45.6 bp net, permutation p 0.002, both halves negative.
The continuous-regression form of a rebalancing-flow signal failed (t -1.29) where the thresholded calendar form passed. Continuous flow regressions are low-powered.

Brogger's 402%/yr, Sharpe 5.14 gross is in-sample 2010-2017 and falls to Sharpe 1.08 at 0.02 vol points of cost. Both Brogger and O'Neill-Whaley document decay. A result that good against a liquid market is a leak or a decayed anomaly until shown otherwise.
Cboe CFE is not on the venue list, so the tradable form must be VXX via Alpaca (MOC 'cls' orders exist), not VX TAS.
276 intraday non-crypto cells with price-derived features: 0 pass after costs.

rows.missing_data: (1) Daily issuer shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY/SVXY (ProShares historical NAV files: free, depth and per-fund shares column unverified) and SVIX/UVIX (Volatility Shares site shows current values only; history from Volatility Shares Trust 10-Q quarter-ends plus forward capture). sec-companyfacts holds only ProShares Trust II aggregate shares, which cannot be used per fund. (2) Yahoo 60m VXX bars: free, last 730 days, not in the local bar set. (3) A forward 5m VXX capture. (4) Verification of the CFE VX daily settlement time against the 16:00 VXX close. VX intraday prices do not exist in the archive, so VXX is the proxy for the index move.

registration.claim: On VXX sessions 2024-10..2026-10 (Yahoo 60m bars, about 500 sessions, extended by a forward 5m capture), VIX-ETP leverage-rebalancing demand has a positive coefficient on VXX's return from the 15:30 ET bar open to the official close, controlling for the day's own move, and holding VXX in sign(Rebal) on top-tercile |Rebal| sessions (15:30 bar open to the closing auction) earns a positive mean net return after a 4 bp round trip. Rebal_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) r_t / ADV20_t, where A = first-seen issuer shares x NAV for UVXY (1.5), SVXY (-0.5), UVIX (2) and SVIX (-1), r_t = VXX return from the prior official close to the 15:30 bar open, and ADV20 = the trailing-20-session dollar volume of VX M1+M2.
registration.statistic: OLS coefficient c in r_late = a + b*r_t + c*Rebal_t + d*dVIX_t (dVIX = VIX change to its 15:30 bar open, local IDX_VIX 60m). Newey-West lag 5, one-sided. Secondary: the rule's mean net return per trade, studentized circular block bootstrap (10-session blocks, 5,000 draws). The VIF of Rebal on r_t is reported.
registration.null: c <= 0 (the AUM-weighted leverage term adds nothing beyond the day's own move), and the rule's mean net return <= 0.
registration.procedure: A_{k,t-1} is the issuer value dated t-1 and enters at 09:30 ET on t. Backfilled issuer history is flagged as not first-seen; first-seen capture runs from registration. L_k comes from prospectus/8-K text at SEC acceptance: UVXY 2x and SVXY -1x until 2018-02-27, 1.5x/-0.5x from 2018-02-28; UVIX/SVIX from launch on 2022-03-30. 1x products (VXX, VIXY) have L(L-1) = 0. ADV20 = mean over t-20..t-1 of $1000 x settle x volume for the two contracts SPVXSP holds, from cboe-vx-futures. The signal price is the 15:30 bar open; the exit is the official close from daily-history-VXX. Tercile cutoffs are expanding, after a 120-session burn-in that is not traded. Early closes and sessions without a 15:30 bar are dropped. Before the run, verify the CFE VX daily settlement time and record whether the 16:00 VXX close falls before or after it. Halves split at the median session.
registration.data: Archived: daily-history-VXX, daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY, cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history; local 60m IDX_VIX. To fetch: Yahoo 60m VXX (730 days); ProShares UVXY/SVXY and Volatility Shares SVIX/UVIX daily shares outstanding and NAV; a forward 5m VXX capture.
registration.pass: All of: c > 0 with one-sided HAC p < 0.05; c > 0 in both halves; rule mean net > 0 with a one-sided bootstrap lower bound > 0 at 4 bp; deflated p < 0.05 over the VIX-ETP flow family (this row, the settle-reversal row, the SPY-close row, the convexity row, and T-658's cells if run).
registration.controls: r_t (momentum, cf. T-427) and dVIX are in the regression. Placebo 1: replace L(L-1) by L (net signed exposure); it must give a smaller t. Placebo 2: shuffle A_{t-1} across calendar quarters (1,000 draws); the actual c must exceed the 95th percentile. FOMC/CPI/OPEX/month-end sessions are flagged and the result is also reported without them. Costs 0/4/8 bp reported. One threshold (top tercile), no grid. No pre-2018 data.

rows.notes: This is the best-replicated claim in the cluster (Brogger, O'Neill-Whaley, Todorov), but all evidence is pre-2018 and decay is documented. Identification is weak. Rebal = K_{t-1} x r_t, so after controlling for r_t only the time variation in K (AUM/ADV) identifies c, and 500 sessions with slowly moving AUM give little power; report the VIF. The 2018-02-28 deleverage and the 2022-03-30 SVIX/UVIX launch are the only large shifts in K, and both fall outside the 60m window. The settle-reversal row uses daily data over 2018-2026 and is the better-powered companion. The issuer shares-outstanding fetch is the single unlock for this row, rows 2/3/4/6/7, row 11 and T-658, and should be built once.

rows.name: vix-etp-rebalancing-next-day-reversal-fade

overlaps.note: T-658's second equation (d < 0 on the next close-to-close return) is the same reversal claim for equity LETFs, and it is blocked on the same data.
There was no close-to-open reversal of the last half hour on SPY.
The next-session premium after VIX spikes overlaps the reversal window on spike days.
The VIX/VIX3M regime predicts VIX declines and must be a control.
Same VX family and the same rule that a pass licenses only the ETP form.

learnings.finding: Liquidity provision pays at the front of the queue (+0.6 to +0.9 pt per fill) and about zero on strict through-fills. The premium for absorbing predictable flow accrues to queue position; a retail closing-auction order receives the auction price, which already contains the impact.
Forward variance exceeds realised by +6.2 vol pts on 87% of days. The short-convexity side (where Todorov places the counterparty to rebalancing) earns a structural premium.
No reversal of the last-half-hour move by the next open on SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD.
The edges that exist are reference-price edges and structural premia (VRP, carry, month-end flows). A reversal of uninformed, scheduled flow belongs to the structural class.

Brogger reports the cumulative 15:30-to-15:30 effect is insignificant, i.e. the reversal is already full in-sample. A post-2018 reversal should be smaller because L(L-1)*AUM fell after XIV's termination.

rows.missing_data: Daily issuer shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY/SVXY (ProShares; free, unverified depth) and SVIX/UVIX (Volatility Shares; history only from 10-Q quarter-ends plus forward capture). Everything else is archived: VX per-contract settles, volume and OI 2013-01..2026-10; VXX daily from 2018-01-25. The VXX trading form also needs an intraday price at the MOC cutoff, from Yahoo 60m (730 days) or a forward capture.

registration.claim: Over 2018-03-01..2026-10-14 (halves split at 2022-06-30), VIX-ETP leverage-rebalancing demand has a negative coefficient on the SPVXSP-weighted VX M1/M2 settlement portfolio's return from settle t to settle t+1, controlling for R_t, the VIX change and log(VIX/VIX3M) at t. Rebal_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) R_t / ADV20_t, with R_t the same portfolio's return from settle t-1 to settle t and A = first-seen issuer shares x NAV of UVXY, SVXY, UVIX and SVIX. A pass licenses only a forward paper test of the VXX closing-auction form.
registration.statistic: OLS slope g in R_{t+1} = a + b*R_t + g*Rebal_t + d*dVIX_t + e*log(VIX/VIX3M)_t. Newey-West lag 5, one-sided, cross-checked by a studentized circular block bootstrap (21-session blocks, 5,000 draws). Reported: the same regression with VXX official close t to close t+1 as the target, and the reversal share g/c once the late-day row has run.
registration.null: g >= 0 (no reversal of the ETP-driven settlement move beyond plain daily autocorrelation).
registration.procedure: R_t comes from cboe-vx-futures settles (Settle = 0 rows dropped), using SPVXSP roll weights on the two contracts the index holds. The target starts exactly where the regressor ends, so both are known at settlement and the test is point-in-time for a trade-at-settlement order. A_k and L_k follow the late-day row: UVXY 1.5 and SVXY -0.5 from 2018-02-28; UVIX 2 and SVIX -1 from 2022-03-30. A dated t-1 enters at 09:30 ET t. ADV20 is computed through t-1. VIX and VIX3M closes enter at 21:30 UTC. The 2022-03-30 SVIX/UVIX launch is the identifying jump in K = Rebal/R; a post-launch x Rebal interaction is reported.
registration.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, daily-history-VXX, daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY. To fetch: ProShares and Volatility Shares daily shares outstanding and NAV.
registration.pass: All of: g < 0 with one-sided HAC p < 0.05 and bootstrap agreement; g < 0 in both halves; same sign excluding 2020-03 and 2024-08-05; deflated jointly with the VIX-ETP flow family.
registration.controls: R_t (plain reversal) and the VIX/VIX3M regime (T-53) are in the regression. Placebo: replace L(L-1) by L. Within-quarter AUM shuffle (1,000 draws). FOMC/CPI days are also reported without. The VXX trading form (short at the close on top-tercile Rebal, long on bottom tercile, exit at the next close, 4 bp round trip, Rebal estimated from the 15:30 price) is reported on the 60m window only, with the estimate error, and is never judged on daily data.

rows.notes: This is the best-powered test of the VIX-ETP mechanism Mandel can run once the issuer shares data exist: about 2,150 daily observations, and the 2022 SVIX/UVIX launch acts as a natural experiment in K. As the candidate's procedure notes, Rebal_t is only fully known at settlement, so the daily regression is a mechanism test for a TAS trader, and CFE is off the venue list. The executable form is VXX MOC sized from an intraday estimate, which is reported, not judged. Deflate jointly with the late-day row, as the candidate asks.

rows.name: vix-etp-demand-predicts-spx-futures-close

overlaps.note: Same SPY window and cost convention; SPY's last half hour is unpredictable from the day's own path.
No reversal at the next open on SPY.
Equity LETF demand on SPY/QQQ in the same window. D_VX must add over T-658's D.
The GEX-conditioned version is blocked on GEX history.
OPEX gamma pinning shows dealer hedging can shape SPY's close; there it is option gamma, not VX vega.

learnings.finding: In 2023-11..2026-10, SPY's 15:30-to-close return and the following close-to-open return carry no detectable price-based predictability.

learnings.source: size arithmetic from the candidate's own numbers
learnings.finding: A large VIX-ETP rebalance day (about $100m of VX) implies roughly $5m of vega per vol point, which hedges with a few hundred million dollars of ES. That is small against ES volume and multi-billion MOC imbalances, so the expected SPY footprint is tiny.
The Bangsgaard-Kokholm effect has no independent replication and its sample is mostly pre-2018, when L(L-1)*AUM was several times larger.
Intraday price features on SPY-class ETFs: 0 of 276 cells pass after costs.

rows.missing_data: VIX-ETP daily shares and NAV (as the late-day row); Yahoo 60m VXX for r_t to 15:30. Optional: SqueezeMetrics GEX/DIX history (free CSV, not archived). D_VX is nearly collinear with SPY's own intraday move, so identification needs AUM variation that the 2023-11..2026-10 window may not contain.

registration.claim: On SPY sessions 2023-11-15..2026-10 (local 60m bars; ES_F 60m as replication), VIX-ETP rebalancing demand D_t has a negative coefficient on SPY's return from the 15:30 bar open to the official close after controlling for SPY's own return to 15:30, and a positive coefficient on SPY's next close-to-open return. D_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) r_t in VX dollars, with r_t the VXX return to the 15:30 bar open, divided by SPY's trailing-20-session dollar volume.
registration.statistic: OLS slope h in r_SPY,late = a + b*r_SPY,ROD + h*D_t (+ GEX_{t-1} when archived), Newey-West lag 5, one-sided. Second equation: slope of the next close-to-open return (dividends added back) on D_t. The VIF of D on r_SPY,ROD is reported.
registration.procedure: A, L and timing as in the late-day row. SPY official close and open come from daily-history-SPY and daily-events-SPY; the 15:30 bar open from local 60m SPY. Early closes are dropped. If VIF > 10 the arm is reported but not judged, as in T-658. Trading form (reported): sign(-D) on top-quintile |D| sessions, 15:30 bar open to the closing auction, 2 bp round trip. At most 4 cells (SPY/ES x close/next open) are deflated.
registration.data: Archived: local 60m SPY and ES_F, daily-history-SPY, daily-events-SPY, daily-history-VXX, cboe-vx-futures. To fetch: VIX-ETP shares/NAV, Yahoo 60m VXX; optional SqueezeMetrics GEX history.
registration.pass: All of: h < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over 4 cells; h < 0 in both halves; close-to-open coefficient positive as a point estimate; h still significant with T-427's r_ROD and T-658's equity-LETF D (if archived) in the regression.
registration.controls: r_ROD (T-427), GEX_{t-1} where available (T-656), T-658's D_LETF. AUM-shuffle placebo. FOMC/CPI/OPEX/month-end flagged. 2 bp costs. No grid on the quintile.

rows.notes: This is the weakest of the VIX-ETP rows. Mandel's two direct tests of SPY's last half hour and next open (T-427, T-428) are null in the same window, there is no independent replication, and the size arithmetic puts the ES footprint at noise level. Run it only as a cheap extra cell once the VIX-ETP shares data exist and the late-day row has a verdict.

rows.name: vix-etp-calendar-roll-pressure-term-structure

overlaps.note: Same VX M1/M2 spread instrument. The gated short-M1/long-M2 calendar was not supported (mean $3.9/day, CI spans 0; first half negative, second half positive). The candidate mislabels T-160's direction: the liquidity-provider side of the ETP roll is long M1 / short M2, the opposite of T-160.
Roll-hedged VX carry; the conditioning input would feed its ETP form.
VIX futures premium vs risk; the same family deflation applies.
VIX curve PC2 predicts VX returns; a competing term-structure state.
Notes that a VX basis-momentum claim would be registered separately in the VX family.

learnings.finding: The VX M1-M2 spread has no reliable unconditional premium after $2/contract/leg in 2013-2026, and its sign flips between halves.
vx_basis has a confirmed inverse 20-day IC on equity ETFs (t -7.3) and futures (t -7.1). The VX curve carries risk-premium information, so any ETP-demand effect must be separated from it.
Cboe CFE is not on the venue list, and no ETP isolates M1 vs M2, so a pass is a mechanism verdict only.
Todorov's estimates come from the XIV/TVIX era of large net long-vol AUM; net long ETP exposure shrank after 2018.

rows.missing_data: Daily shares/NAV for every VIX ETP. The binding gap is VXX: Barclays iPath ETN outstanding history is unverified, 424B3 supplements give only issuance dates, and sec-companyfacts carries only Barclays Bank PLC totals. Also needed: VIXY/UVXY/SVXY (ProShares) and SVIX/UVIX (Volatility Shares). A possible proxy is CFTC TFF positions in VIX futures (contract 1170E1, free Socrata, not archived).

registration.claim: Daily over 2019-03..2026-10 (2013-05-20..2019-02 reported in-sample), net VIX-ETP calendar roll demand C_t, which is computable before the session, has a positive coefficient on the settle t-1 to settle t change in ln(F2/F1), controlling for log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1} and days to M1 expiry. In VX cycles with above-median mean C, the liquidity-provider spread (long M1 / short M2, the opposite side of the ETP roll) held 21 sessions earns more than in below-median cycles, after $2 per contract per leg plus one tick. C_t = (long-product A_{k,t-1} x L_k minus inverse-product A_{k,t-1} x |L_k|) x (1 / roll days in the current SPVXSP period) / ($1000 x F1_{t-1}) / OI(M1)_{t-1}.
registration.statistic: (a) Daily slope, Newey-West lag 10, one-sided. (b) Mean cycle P&L in top-half-C cycles minus bottom-half-C cycles, studentized block bootstrap over cycles (block 3).
registration.procedure: A_k is first-seen (as in the late-day row) for VXX, VIXY, UVXY, UVIX (long products) and SVXY, SVIX (inverse). C_t uses only t-1 values plus the deterministic roll schedule, so it is known before the day. Settle = 0 rows are dropped. The holdout splits into halves at 2022-12-31. The cycle split uses an expanding median. Placebo: shuffle C across days within each year.
registration.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history. To fetch: ETP shares/NAV for VXX (Barclays), VIXY/UVXY/SVXY (ProShares) and SVIX/UVIX (Volatility Shares); optional CFTC TFF VIX futures.
registration.pass: All of: (a) slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 in both holdout halves; (b) difference > 0 with bootstrap lower bound > 0 in the holdout; placebo 95th percentile below the actual value; DSR >= 0.95 over the VX family (T-160, T-379, T-435, T-242, T-651, T-652, T-653 and this row). A pass is a mechanism verdict that may only condition T-651's ETP form.
registration.controls: VIX/VIX3M and days to expiry. T-160's unconditional spread as the baseline. Ex-2020-03 reported. Costs as T-160. One median split, no grid.

rows.notes: The trading leg cannot be executed on the listed venues, since VX trades on CFE and no ETP isolates M1/M2, so the value is diagnostic. The VXX outstanding history is the hardest input in the cluster. Do not run before T-651/T-652, which test the same curve without the flow input.

rows.name: short-opposite-leverage-etp-pair-intraday

overlaps.note: Same short-pair construction held monthly (variance decay). Its UVXY/SVXY arm made +2.61%/month (+1.70% after 2018-02-28) at an assumed 3% borrow, with P&L loading on realised variance (t 19.6), but DSR over 8 trials failed, and real UVXY borrow is far above 3%. The intraday form avoids borrow but is a different bet.
The open-to-close pair is algebraically a gap-continuation bet. On SPY, corr(overnight gap, intraday return) is +0.018 (CI -0.036..+0.069).
SVXY timing, same instrument family.

learnings.finding: Shorting an L fund and a -L fund at the open nets an index delta of about 2L^2 x g per unit of each, where g is the overnight gap. Daily P&L is about g x i x sum_k w_k L_k^2 per unit gross (i = intraday index return), so the pair pays when the intraday move CONTINUES the gap. The candidate says it pays on reversal; that is the wrong sign. The exposure factor is 0.75 for UVXY/SVXY (1:3), 2 for UVIX/SVIX (1:2), 1 for VIXY/SVIX and 4 for the 2x/-2x commodity pairs.
There is no gap continuation or reversal on SPY 2000-2026 (corr +0.018).
LETF short pairs earn mostly through multi-day variance decay that loads on realised variance; that channel is absent intraday.

At a 5 bp floor per leg per side, the UVXY/SVXY pair needs E[g x i] above about 13 bp/day of the VIX index to break even. Todorov's VIX pair (21%/yr gross, L = 1) implies roughly 8 bp/day, so the testable-now pair is expected to fail. Only higher-leverage pairs (UVIX/SVIX, BOIL/KOLD) have room.
Strategies that use price alone start from a negative base rate.

rows.missing_data: Yahoo daily OHLC with events (free, quick fetch) for SVIX, UVIX, VIXY, BOIL, KOLD, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL. No historical locate/ETB record exists for any leg, so the result is an upper bound for a shortable account; Alpaca shortability must be recorded forward. The UVXY/SVXY arm alone could run now from archived bundles, but cost arithmetic makes it a near-certain fail.

registration.claim: Over 2018-03-01..2026-10-14 (VIXY/SVIX and UVIX/SVIX from 2022-03-30), shorting each declared long/inverse ETP pair at the official open and covering at the official close every session earns a positive mean net return on gross short notional, pooled with equal weight per pair-session. Pairs and dollar ratios (zero index exposure at the prior close): UVXY/SVXY 1:3, UVIX/SVIX 1:2, VIXY/SVIX 1:1, BOIL/KOLD 1:1, AGQ/ZSL 1:1, UGL/GLL 1:1. Costs: max(5 bp, prior-20-session Corwin-Schultz half-spread) per leg per side for VIX ETPs, with a 3 bp floor for metals and gas; no borrow (intraday).
registration.statistic: Pooled mean daily net return on gross notional, studentized circular block bootstrap (10-session blocks, 5,000 draws); per-pair means, Sharpe and 1% CVaR; DSR over the 6 pairs. Diagnostic: the slope of each underlying index's open-to-close return on its overnight gap, which per the identity determines gross P&L.
registration.procedure: Daily OHLC from Yahoo; split adjustment leaves same-day open/close ratios unchanged. A pair enters on the first session both legs trade. UVXY/SVXY use 1.5/-0.5 leverage from 2018-02-28; earlier sessions are excluded. Sessions with a split, distribution or leverage change in either leg are dropped. Costs use only prior-session high/low. Halves split at 2022-06-30. Alpaca ETB status of every leg is recorded forward before any paper form.
registration.data: Archived: daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY, daily-events-UVXY, cboe-VIX-history. To fetch (Yahoo daily, free): SVIX, UVIX, VIXY, BOIL, KOLD, AGQ, ZSL, UGL, GLL with events.
registration.pass: All of: pooled mean net > 0 with one-sided bootstrap lower bound > 0 over the full window; positive in both halves; DSR > 0.95 over the 6 pairs. Per-pair results are reported.
registration.controls: T-333's gap correlation sets the expectation. T-325's multi-day pair is reported for contrast. Cost grid 0/5/10 bp per leg per side reported. 2020-03 and 2024-08-05 also reported without. One exposure-neutral weighting rule, no grid.

rows.notes: Correction to the candidate: the intraday short pair is linear within the day. Its net index delta at the open is proportional to the overnight gap, so it is a gap-continuation bet. It is not a variance bet and does not pay on reversal. Todorov's leverage-rebalancing story (closing demand in the direction of the day's move) is compatible with continuation. The test is cheap: one Yahoo fetch, and UVXY/SVXY is archived. Expect a fail on costs for low-leverage pairs. testable_now is false because 5 of the 6 pairs need the fetch.

rows.name: vix-etp-flows-and-the-vix-futures-premium

overlaps.note: The candidate extends T-652's premium P_t with a flow input. T-652 must have a verdict first.
For GLD, flows follow price: returns Granger-cause flows (p 0.0000), flows do not predict returns (p 0.99).
Forward issuer shares-outstanding capture for an ETF flow-reversal cross-section; same infrastructure.
The VIX curve under-prices mean reversion in contango months.
The VIX curve under-prices mean reversion after spikes (19/23 events).

learnings.finding: ETF flows are driven by past returns and carry no information about the next week's return.
The VIX curve systematically under-prices mean reversion, so a VX premium exists to be predicted.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md (in-house models lose to the price)
learnings.finding: A forecast built from the market's own state rarely beats the price. The flow input must add over T-652's premium out of sample (Clark-West), not merely in-sample.
Nielsen-Posselt's flow-to-premium link has a single source ending 2019-02, and long-vol ETP AUM is smaller since 2018.

rows.missing_data: Daily shares/NAV for VXX (Barclays, unverified), VIXY/UVXY/SVXY (ProShares) and SVIX/UVIX (Volatility Shares), first-seen. T-652's verdict is a prerequisite.

registration.claim: Once per VX settlement cycle (T-652's entry session: the first with <= 21 trading days to F1's final settlement), 2013-05..2026-10 with 2019-03.. as holdout, adding Flow_t to T-652's premium P_t raises the out-of-sample accuracy of an expanding-window forecast of the hold-to-final-settlement short-F1 return. Flow_t = trailing-21-session net creations in dollars of long-vol VIX ETPs minus inverse ETPs, first-seen, scaled by $1000 x OI(F1) x F1.
registration.statistic: Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (one-sided) and Campbell-Thompson R2_OS of the P+Flow model against the P-only model over holdout cycles. Reported: the step-1 slope of P_t on Flow_t with T-652's controls.
registration.procedure: Run only after T-652 has a verdict, reusing its E_t AR(1) construction unchanged. Expanding-window OLS from 2013-05; the first forecast is at 2019-03. Flow uses shares dated through t-1, entering at 09:30 ET t. One observation per cycle, so there is no overlap. The 2020-02..04 window is also reported without.
registration.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, cboe-VVIX-history, daily-history-SPY. To fetch: daily shares/NAV for VXX, VIXY, UVXY, UVIX, SVXY and SVIX.
registration.pass: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 and R2_OS > 0 in the holdout, both positive in each holdout half (split at 2022-12-31). A trading form (short F1 or long SVIX sized by the predicted premium) needs its own registration with DSR over the VX family.
registration.controls: Benchmarks: P-only (T-652) and the raw basis F1 - VIX. T-652's VVIX and RV21 controls. Reverse causality, per T-404: Flow is lagged and the trailing 21-session VX return is in the model.

rows.name: short-vol-etp-convexity-crowding-tail

overlaps.note: The SVXY overlay baseline. Contango timing lowered Sharpe in 2018-2026 (diff -0.18).
The same SVXY contango filter.
Spike dynamics: the curve under-prices the reversion after spikes.
A curve-state predictor of VX returns; a competing state variable.

learnings.finding: Curve-state timing of short-vol ETPs has not improved risk-adjusted returns after 2018. An overlay must beat always-short on tail metrics without losing Sharpe.

Short-vol carry is a structural premium (T-148/T-510 forward VRP +6.2 vol pts). The use here is risk control of that premium, not a new edge, which fits Mandel's lesson that loss response only reduces risk.
The evidence is one event (2018-02-05) plus a decomposition; there is no published predictive test.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md (PnL cannot settle an edge claim)
learnings.finding: Tail events are rare. About 200 SPX down-days over 2019-2026 support an interaction test, but very few true spikes inform the 99th-percentile claim.

rows.missing_data: Daily shares/NAV for UVXY, SVXY (ProShares) and SVIX, UVIX (Volatility Shares). K needs only leveraged/inverse products, so the VXX gap does not bind here.

registration.claim: Over 2019-01..2026-10 (2013-05..2018-12 reported), on sessions with an S&P 500 close-to-close return below -1%, the VX M1 settle return's sensitivity to the S&P 500 return is more negative when K_{t-1} is high. The coefficient on SPX_t x z(K_{t-1}) is negative after controlling for SPX_t x VIX_{t-1} and SPX_t x log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1}. K_{t-1} = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) / ($1000 x mean(F1,F2)_{t-1}) / OI(M1+M2)_{t-1}.
registration.statistic: OLS interaction coefficient with HC3 errors, one-sided; cluster-robust errors (down-days within 5 sessions share a cluster) reported. Secondary: 90th/99th-percentile quantile regressions of the VX M1 daily up-move on K_{t-1} over all sessions. Overlay: SVXY held except when K is in its trailing-252-session top decile (cash at DTB3), against always-SVXY: Sharpe difference, max drawdown and 1% CVaR, 10 bp per switch.
registration.procedure: Down days are defined from ^GSPC close-to-close (daily-history--GSPC). VX M1 = the nearest monthly with > 1 session to expiry, settle-to-settle on the same contract. K uses A dated t-1 (first-seen, entering at 09:30 ET t) and OI/F through t-1. z(K) uses an expanding window. Overlay positions are decided at close t and applied from close t+1.
registration.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SVXY, fred-DTB3. To fetch: UVXY/SVXY/SVIX/UVIX daily shares and NAV.
registration.pass: Interaction < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 in 2019-01..2026-10, with the same sign excluding 2020-03 and 2024-08-05. Overlay: lower 1% CVaR and lower max drawdown than always-SVXY, and a Sharpe difference >= 0 as a point estimate.
registration.controls: VIX-level and term-structure interactions: K rises when short-vol AUM swells in calm regimes, so K partly proxies low VIX. T-435's VIX3M/VIX timing is the competing overlay; always-SVXY is the baseline. 2018-02-05 lies outside the judged window. One decile cut, no grid. 10 bp per switch.

rows.notes: This is a risk overlay for any short-vol sleeve, not a return edge, and it fits Mandel's rule that loss response only reduces risk. The K series shares its data with rows 1 and 2. Mechanism evidence is anecdotal (one event), so the interaction test is the real content. SVIX's 2022-03 launch and the 2024-08-05 shock give post-2018 variation.

rows.name: gsci-bcom-roll-front-running-decay-test

overlaps.note: Needs the same EIA contract 1-4 fetch (free, ends 2024-04-05). One fetch unblocks T-687, T-688 and rows 8-10.
Energy basis momentum on the same panel.
Commodity curve carry is blocked for lack of contract histories.

learnings.finding: Published anomalies decay. Irwin-Sanders-Yan put the 2012-2019 pre-roll move at -3.1 bp (t -0.9), and Saverys finds near-zero profits 2010-2024. The decay hypothesis is near-certain, and a tradable pass is very unlikely.
The EIA curves end 2024-04-05 and no free per-contract curve exists after that, so the confirmatory window is 2020-01..2024-03 (51 months) and any live form needs a forward settlement capture.
One tick per leg per side is about 1.4 bp of CL notional per fill, roughly 5-6 bp per round trip of the spread. That is above the entire 2012-2019 pre-roll move.
Futures-based funds pay structural costs (GLD vs futures plus bills, +1.07%/yr), but that is the fund's cost, not a harvestable trade.

rows.missing_data: EIA NYMEX daily contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG: free, verified on eia.gov, not archived, end 2024-04-05. CME expiry calendar rules. No per-contract source after 2024-04 (CME settlements paid; Yahoo carries only listed contracts), so live use needs a forward cmegroup.com settlement capture. CFTC index-trader supplement positions are not archived.

registration.claim: Over 2020-01..2024-03 (EIA's contract 1-4 settlements end 2024-04-05), for NYMEX CL, HO, RB and NG, Mou's Strategy 1 earns a positive pooled mean net P&L per month, in bp of one-leg notional, after 1 tick per leg per side. Strategy 1: short nearby / long next, 20% added per day at the settle on GSCI roll days -10..-6, unwound 20% per day on roll days 1-5 (business days 5-9).
registration.statistic: Pooled mean monthly net P&L (equal weight across the 4 commodities), Newey-West lag 3 t and a studentized block bootstrap over months (6-month blocks); per-commodity means. Second trial: Strategy 2 (days -5..-1). Reported: the decay ratio (2012-2024 mean over the 2004-2011 mean, computed identically).
registration.procedure: Per-contract settlements are stitched from EIA contracts 1-4 using the CME expiry calendar (contract k before expiry = contract k-1 after), so each position is held in the two delivery months the GSCI rolls from and to. Roll business days follow the NYMEX calendar. Marks are at settles only. 2020-04 (negative WTI) is kept and also reported without. 2012-2019 is reported as the ISY in-sample replication and not judged.
registration.data: To fetch: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 daily settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (the same fetch as T-687/T-688); CME expiry rules.
registration.pass: Pooled mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 (HAC and bootstrap) in 2020-01..2024-03 and in 2012-2019, and DSR > 0.95 over the 2 strategies counted with the energy-curve family (T-687, T-688, the post-roll row, the USO row).
registration.controls: Placebo: the same legs on calendar-shifted windows at equal distance from expiry. Cost grid 0.5/1/2 ticks. The ISY 2012-2019 numbers set the expectation. Sanders-Irwin's CIT sign test is not run because CIT positions are not archived.

rows.notes: Registered with the tradable claim as primary and decay as a reported secondary: the decay hypothesis is already established by ISY and Saverys and licenses nothing. Worth running only because the EIA fetch is shared with T-687, T-688 and rows 9-10, which makes the marginal cost small. A live form would need micro contracts (MCL) and a forward curve capture.

rows.name: post-index-roll-spread-reversal

overlaps.note: Same EIA panel and the same basis control.
Same panel; basis momentum is a competing drift.

learnings.finding: The authors call the 2012-2019 post-roll rise anomalous, because pre-roll and roll-window pressure had vanished. A rebound without prior pressure points to a generic time-to-expiry drift, not roll reversal.
A single-source, self-flagged anomaly is a forking-path risk, so it counts only if it holds in a post-sample window against a placebo calendar.
The data end in 2024-03, which caps the holdout at 51 months x 4 commodities.

rows.missing_data: The same EIA contract 1-4 settlements (free, ends 2024-04-05, not archived) and CME expiry rules. No free per-contract history after 2024-04.

registration.claim: Over 2020-01..2024-03, for NYMEX CL, HO, RB and NG, buying the nearby and selling the next contract that the GSCI rolled (equal dollars) at the settle of GSCI roll day 5 (business day 9), and closing 10 business days later or 2 business days before the nearby's last trade if earlier, earns a positive pooled mean net P&L per month after 1 tick per leg per side, and more than the same position on placebo dates.
registration.statistic: Pooled mean monthly net P&L in bp of one-leg notional, Newey-West t and a studentized block bootstrap (6-month blocks). The placebo distribution comes from 200 block-shifted roll calendars with distance to expiry held fixed.
registration.null: Pooled mean net <= 0, or the actual mean below the placebo 95th percentile.
registration.procedure: The EIA panel is stitched as in the front-run row. Positions are held only in the two contracts the index rolled, marked settle to settle. 2012-2019 is reported as the ISY replication of their flagged anomaly and never judged.
registration.data: To fetch: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG; CME expiry rules.
registration.pass: Holdout mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and above the placebo 95th percentile, positive in 3 of the 4 commodities, and DSR > 0.95 within the energy-curve family.
registration.controls: The placebo calendar covers generic time-to-expiry drift and contango roll-down. A regression variant adds the T-687 basis (annualised log F1/F2 at entry). Costs 0.5/1/2 ticks. The front-run row runs on the same panel.

rows.notes: This is cheap only as a co-passenger on the shared EIA fetch. The placebo calendar decides the result: if the rebound appears on shifted dates at the same distance from expiry, it is curve drift, not roll reversal.

rows.name: uso-ung-own-roll-window-pressure

overlaps.note: Needs the same EIA panel.
A USO/BNO spread trade; same fund family, unrelated mechanism.
Funds pay roll/structure costs.

learnings.finding: USO's roll cost is real, but over 95% of impact reverses within 15 minutes and spreads narrow on roll days: sunshine trading, not predation. There is a cost to the fund but no evident trade for others.
USO and UNG units outstanding are archived quarterly from 10-Q covers (2010..2026, point-in-time at filing). USO's scale fell to about $0.9bn of assets by 2025, a small share of CL open interest.
Fund structural costs are measurable, but that does not imply anyone can harvest them.

rows.missing_data: EIA contract 1-4 settlements (free, ends 2024-04-05). USCF roll-schedule text from 10-K/10-Q/prospectus (free EDGAR; the filing list is archived, the text is not parsed). USO front-month holdings by quarter (10-Q schedule of investments). Per-contract OI is paid (CME); CFTC legacy crude (067651) and natural gas (023651) total OI is free but not archived and would serve as the proxy denominator.

registration.claim: Over 2012-01..2024-03, split at USO's 2020-04 methodology change, three things hold in both regimes: (a) the mean change in ln(F1/F2) of NYMEX WTI on USO's published roll days, minus the mean over the 3-7 business days before, is negative; (b) the per-roll pressure is larger when USO's front-month holdings are a larger share of CL open interest; (c) a short F1 / long F2 position from the settle two business days before USO's first roll day to the settle of its last roll day nets > 0 after 1 tick per leg per side.
registration.statistic: (a) Mean difference with HAC t. (b) Slope of the per-roll pressure (minus the difference) on S = USO front-month contracts / CL total open interest, from the last 10-Q and the CFTC report before the roll. (c) Mean net P&L per roll, studentized bootstrap (block 3 rolls).
registration.procedure: Roll days for each period come from USCF filing text, first-seen at SEC acceptance. USO units outstanding come from sec-companyfacts at filing date; front-month contracts from the 10-Q schedule of investments. EIA contract 1-4 settlements are stitched with the CME expiry calendar. CFTC legacy crude total OI enters at its release time. UNG/NG is reported, not judged. 2020-04 is also reported without.
registration.data: Archived: sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, daily-history-USO, daily-history-UNG. To fetch: EIA contract 1-4 settlements, USCF filing text, CFTC legacy reports for crude (067651) and natural gas (023651).
registration.pass: (a) < 0 with p < 0.05 over 2012-2024 and the same sign in both regimes; (b) one-sided p < 0.05; (c) mean net > 0 with bootstrap lower bound > 0 in both regimes.
registration.controls: Bessembinder's pre-window control. GSCI-window overlap days are flagged. Placebo roll calendars. Cost grid 0.5/1/2 ticks.

rows.notes: The published evidence says the fund pays the cost and liquidity providers earn it within minutes, which is invisible at daily settles. USO's shrinking share of OI makes post-2020 pressure small. The candidate's '10-day roll since 2020' must be verified from filing text before any registration.

rows.name: leveraged-commodity-etf-rebalancing-into-settlement

overlaps.note: The same LETF rebalancing mechanism, here at commodity settlement windows; also blocked on issuer shares/NAV history.
A fixing-window flow analogue (USD fix pre/post reversal).
No late-window momentum in the equity analogue.

learnings.finding: A 2x commodity LETF rebalance on a large move is roughly 1% of NG front-month dollar volume and far less for CL, GC or SI. Only natural gas plausibly has a measurable footprint.
Issuer daily shares/NAV history is free but its depth is unverified and it is not archived.
60m futures bars cannot isolate the 14:28-14:30 / 13:28-13:30 ET settlement windows, and the 5m/15m bars cover only about 60 sessions. A test needs a forward capture.

data: local 5m/15m CL_F, NG_F, GC_F, SI_F (about 60 sessions, development only)
rows.missing_data: ProShares daily shares/NAV for BOIL, KOLD, UCO, SCO, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL (free, unverified, not archived). Daily OHLC for these LETFs is not archived. A forward 5m capture of the four fronts aligned to settlement windows is needed. CME settlement-window rules must be verified per contract.

registration.claim: Over the first 250 sessions of a forward 5m capture of the NG, CL, GC and SI front futures (the ~60 archived 5m/15m sessions are development only), commodity-LETF rebalancing demand D_t has a positive coefficient on the return from 30 minutes before the settlement window to the settlement price. D_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) r_t / ADV20_t in dollars, for BOIL/KOLD (NG), UCO/SCO (CL), UGL/GLL (GC) and AGQ/ZSL (SI), with r_t the front future's return from the prior settlement to window start.
registration.statistic: Pooled panel OLS with commodity fixed effects and Driscoll-Kraay errors, one-sided; per-commodity slopes; the next-session reversal coefficient.
registration.procedure: Settlement windows from CME rules (NYMEX energy about 14:28-14:30 ET, COMEX metals about 13:28-13:30 ET), verified per contract before the capture starts. ProShares shares/NAV dated t-1 enter at 09:30 ET t, first-seen. ADV20 comes from the capture. The own return to window start is a control. Trading form (reported): sign(D) on top-tercile |D| sessions in micro contracts where listed, 1 tick per side.
registration.data: Local 5m/15m CL_F, NG_F, GC_F, SI_F (development). To capture: forward 5m bars. To fetch: ProShares daily shares/NAV for the 8 LETFs.
registration.pass: Slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over 4 commodities, positive in both halves of the forward window, and a next-session reversal coefficient <= 0.
registration.controls: Own-return momentum. Placebo L(L-1) -> L. AUM shuffle. EIA storage-report Thursdays (NG) and CPI/FOMC flagged. 1 tick per side.

rows.notes: Exploratory. Only NG has a plausible footprint. It is forward-only and needs a year of capture, though the shares fetch is shared with the VIX rows.

rows.name: commodity-linked-note-hedging-pricing-dates

overlaps.note: A commodity flow signal (COT hedger flow) on ETF proxies.
An event-driven flow study (index inclusion) blocked on building the event set.

learnings.finding: Typical CLN principal ($2-20m) is negligible against WTI or gold futures volume (tens of billions a day). A 37-51 bp average move is implausible as hedging impact and suggests confounded event dates.

Only the preliminary filing's expected pricing date and acceptance time are point-in-time. Final size is known only from the post-pricing 424B2, so the size-monotonicity pass uses future information and can only be reported.
The sample predates 2012 and there is no replication.

registration.claim: For commodity-linked notes referencing WTI, Brent, gold, silver, natural gas, BCOM or GSCI found by EDGAR full-text search of preliminary pricing supplements and FWPs filed 2008-2026, buying the referenced front future at the settle two business days before the preliminary filing's expected pricing date and selling at the pricing-date settle earns a positive mean abnormal return (futures return minus beta x DBC return) after 1 tick per side.

registration.controls: Placebo: the same commodity on random weekday-matched non-event dates. FOMC/CPI/EIA inventory days flagged. 1 tick per side.

Index inclusion effect.
A calendar-predictable rebalancing flow that passed.
Multi-commodity futures panel blocked on curves; this row needs only fronts.

The index-inclusion return fell from 7.4% in the 1990s to 0.3% in the past decade. Anticipated index flows get front-run away.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md (PnL cannot settle an edge claim)
learnings.finding: There is one event per year, so the 2019-2026 holdout has 8 cross-sections. A year-level t on 8 observations is low-powered whatever the commodity count.
Bank desks publish flow estimates weeks ahead (Jan 2026 silver/gold), so the flow is public, and sunshine-trading logic predicts small impact.

Yahoo front continuous daily for HO, RB, ZC, ZS, ZW, KC, SB, CT, LE, HE and other members (free; not archived). Per-commodity open interest from CFTC legacy reports (free; only gold and silver archived).

registration.claim: Over 2019-2026 (2010-2018 reported), across about 16-20 BCOM/GSCI commodities, the implied January reweighting flow has a positive Fama-MacBeth slope on the front-future excess return over BCOM business days 6-10 and a negative slope over the following 5 business days. flow_i = (target weight_i - December-drifted weight_i) / (front-month OI_i x price_i), with target weights first-seen at their announcement and drift computed through the last December close.

To fetch: Yahoo fronts for the other members, target-weight announcements, CFTC legacy OI per commodity.
registration.pass: Window slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 over 2019-2026, post-window slope < 0, and the long-short form net > 0.
registration.controls: Placebo: the same cross-section in non-January months (block-shifted). December-return momentum control, because drifted weights load mechanically on past returns. Costs. One tercile cut.

rows.name: futures-btc-etf-roll-cme-calendar-pressure

rows.name: spot-btc-etf-flows-to-cme-basis-shorts

overlaps.note: The same flow input (Farside, 13:30 UTC t+1 availability) predicting IBIT returns. Blocked on the same farside-btc-etf-flows bundle; one fetch unblocks both.

Point-in-time requires first-seen capture from registration; earlier values are backfill and flagged.

registration.claim: Over 2025-01..2026-10 (2024-01-11..2024-12 reported as the NYDIG-era replication), US spot BTC ETF net flow for day t (Farside sum, first-seen no earlier than 13:30 UTC t+1) predicts the change in the CME front-month annualised basis from the settle of t+1 to the settle of t+5, controlling for the basis level at t+1 and the BTC return over t-4..t. As the mechanism check, the weekly change in CFTC TFF leveraged-funds net short (per OI) is positively related to the week's flows.
registration.statistic: Daily: Newey-West (lag 5) slope of the basis change on Flow_t ($bn), two-sided as pre-registered. Weekly: slope of the change in leveraged-funds net short / OI on the week's flows, one-sided, measured at each report's release time.
registration.procedure: Basis = ln(BTC=F settle / Coinbase spot at the CME settle hour) x 365 / days to the front's expiry (T-329's synchronous construction), excluding the 5 sessions before expiry. IBIT dShares x NAV from iShares is a cross-check. T-611's forward Farside capture supplies revision sizes. A trading form (T-362's cash-and-carry entered when predicted compression is lowest) is tested only if the daily prediction passes.
registration.data: Archived: daily-history-BTC-F, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, cftc-cot-tff-f-133741, daily-history-IBIT, daily-history-FBTC, ishares-ibit-premium-discount, fred-DTB3. To fetch: farside-btc-etf-flows; iShares IBIT daily shares/NAV history.
registration.pass: Daily slope nonzero with HAC p < 0.05 in 2025-01..2026-10 and the same sign in both halves (split at 2025-12-31); weekly slope > 0 with p < 0.05 in 2025-01..2026-10.
registration.controls: Basis level and lagged BTC return. Reverse direction (the basis change over t-4..t predicting flows) reported. DTB3 change. T-612's leveraged-funds change as a competing regressor. ETH ETFs excluded.

rows.notes: The weekly association (inflows alongside basis shorts) will probably replicate, but it is contemporaneous and licenses nothing. The daily predictive slope is the real claim and has a low prior given T-404, T-362 and T-329. The Farside fetch is shared with T-611, which makes this cheap. Any tradable output would feed Hurst's IBIT carry sleeve, which is US-legal (IBIT on Alpaca, CME/Coinbase Derivatives).

rows.name: vix-etp-leverage-rebalancing-late-day-pressure
rows.source_notes: Brogger thesis PDF, text extracted. Sample 2010-11-30..2017-12-31. Mean flow 6.7% of ADV, maximum 58% on 2016-06-24. One-sd flow (9.8%) moves VX 0.046 vol points without controls and 0.039 with them, against a quoted spread of about 0.05. Front-running earns 402.4%/yr and Sharpe 5.14 gross, 84.7% and 1.08 at 0.02 vol points of cost, and turns strongly negative at 0.04 and above. In the sample the VX settlement was at 16:15 EST. The JBF 133 (2021) abstract on IDEAS says there were 'no excess profits from trading ahead of rebalancing flows during the sample period', and that larger, more predictable flows have smaller impact coefficients. O'Neill-Whaley, JFM 43(1) 2023: the abstract confirms positive end-of-day predictive power and that the impact diminished through time because of hedge-fund liquidity and issuers' natural hedging; no sample is given. Todorov's BIS WP 952 abstract (2021-07-02) confirms that leverage rebalancing has the largest effect. CFE filings show the VX daily settlement now at 15:00 CT (16:00 ET), with TAS closing at 15:58 ET. That timing matches the 16:00 VXX close.
rows.replication_concerns: All three papers use pre-2018 or XIV/TVIX-era samples, and two document decay. Brogger's own JBF abstract reports no net front-running profit. L(L-1) x AUM fell after 2018-02 (UVXY 0.75 and SVXY 0.75, from 2 each). It rose again with UVIX and SVIX (2 each) from 2022-03, but both of those shifts fall outside the 60m window. Rebal = K x r_t, so once r_t is controlled, c is identified only by slow time variation in AUM/ADV over about 500 sessions. Power is low, and a sign(Rebal) rule is mostly price-only momentum on large-move days unless K varies. That rule must beat its price-only twin, which the candidate omitted. K also moves with the vol regime: short-vol AUM swells in calm markets and long-vol AUM decays after spikes. K x r_t could therefore proxy regime-dependent momentum, which needs an r_t x VIX_{t-1} control. The L placebo (net signed exposure) can change sign and is uninformative as a pass criterion.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-VXX 2018-01-25..2026-10-14 (series B), daily-history-UVXY and daily-history-SVXY 2011-10-04..2026-10-14. cboe-vx-futures covers 2013-01-02..2026-10-14: 174 monthly expiries with settle, volume and OI, volume and OI nonzero on about 98% of rows, and Settle = 0 rows in 2013. Local 60m IDX_VIX and SPY start 2023-11-21. VXX has no local intraday bars (absent from the 5m/15m/60m universe), so Yahoo 60m VXX must be fetched; 730 days reaches back to about 2024-10-22. No issuer shares/NAV bundle exists. sec-companyfacts carries only the trust-level cover shares of ProShares Trust II (CIK 1415311) and VS Trust (CIK 1793497), quarterly, which cannot be split by fund.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) Issuer shares/NAV dated t-1 are published after the t-1 close, so they enter at 09:30 t. Backfilled history files must be flagged. (2) Yahoo 60m bars are stamped by bar open: the 15:30 bar spans 15:30-16:00, and the zero-length 16:00 bar is the closing print, which must never be used as the 15:30 price. (3) The 15:30 bar open is both the signal price and the fill, a mild same-price fill that the 4 bp round trip covers. (4) ADV20 must end at t-1, and tercile cutoffs must expand. (5) The settlement time changed from 16:15 ET (Brogger's sample) to 16:00 ET; the window lies after the change, but a run must not mix eras. (6) VX final-settlement (SOQ) mornings and early closes distort the window.
rows.missing_data: Yahoo 60m VXX (free, about 2024-10-22 on); daily shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares historical files; free, depth and per-fund columns unverified) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares; only current values seen, so history needs quarterly 10-Q per-fund schedules plus forward capture); a forward 5m VXX capture.

final.claim: On VXX sessions with Yahoo 60-minute bars (2024-10-22..2026-10, about 500 sessions; the forward 5m capture is reported separately), VIX-ETP leverage-rebalancing demand Rebal_t has a positive coefficient on VXX's return from the 15:30 ET bar open to the official close. The official close is 16:00 ET, which is the CFE VX daily settlement time (15:00 CT). The regression controls for VXX's own return to 15:30, that return interacted with the prior VIX close, and the VIX change to 15:30. In addition, holding VXX in the direction of Rebal_t on top-tercile |Rebal_t| sessions earns a positive mean net return after a 4 bp round trip, and beats the price-only rule (sign of r_t on top-tercile |r_t| sessions) at the same cost. Definitions: Rebal_t = K_{t-1} x r_t and K_{t-1} = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) / ADV20_t. The products are every US-listed daily-reset VIX-futures ETP with L outside {0, 1}: UVXY 1.5, SVXY -0.5, UVIX 2 and SVIX -1, frozen at registration; later launches enter at their first session. A = issuer shares x NAV dated t-1. r_t = VXX return from the prior official close to the 15:30 bar open. ADV20 = mean over t-20..t-1 of $1000 x settle x volume of the two VX contracts SPVXSP holds.
final.statistic: OLS c in r_late = a + b*r_t + e*(r_t x VIX_{t-1}) + c*Rebal_t + d*dVIX_t, where dVIX is the VIX change from the prior close to its 15:30 bar open (local IDX_VIX 60m). Newey-West lag 5, one-sided. Secondary: the rule's mean net return per trade, and its paired difference from the price-only rule on the same sessions, each by studentized circular block bootstrap (10-session blocks, 5,000 draws). Reported: the VIF of Rebal on (r_t, r_t x VIX_{t-1}), max/min of K over the window, and the reversal leg (official close to the next session's 15:30 bar open).
final.null: c <= 0, or the rule's mean net return <= 0, or the rule's net return minus the price-only rule's <= 0.
final.procedure: A_{k,t-1} enters at 09:30 ET on t. An issuer file is used only for the dates it states; values backfilled from history files are flagged, and first-seen capture runs from registration.
