L_k comes from prospectus or 8-K text at SEC acceptance. VXX's 15:30 bar open is both the signal price and the entry. The exit is the official close from daily-history-VXX (a MOC order). The 15:30 bar spans 15:30-16:00, and the zero-length 16:00 bar is never used. Tercile cutoffs expand after a 120-session burn-in that is not traded. Early closes, VX final-settlement Wednesdays and sessions without a 15:30 bar are dropped. If the VIF exceeds 10 or K's max/min over the window is below 1.5, the regression arm is reported but not judged and the row is inconclusive, because c is identified only by time variation in K. Halves split at the median session. No pre-2018 data are used.
final.data: Archived: daily-history-VXX, daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY, cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, local 60m IDX_VIX. To fetch: Yahoo 60m VXX; daily shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares); a forward 5m VXX capture.
final.pass: All of: c > 0 with one-sided HAC p < 0.05; c > 0 in both halves; rule mean net > 0 with a one-sided bootstrap lower bound > 0 at 4 bp; rule minus price-only rule > 0 with one-sided bootstrap p < 0.05; deflated p < 0.05 over the VIX-ETP flow family (this row, vix-etp-rebal-vx-settle-reversal-post-tvix, vix-etp-vega-demand-spy-last-half-hour and vix-etp-rebal-convexity-downday-vx-beta, plus T-658's cells if run).
final.controls: r_t and r_t x VIX_{t-1} (regime-dependent momentum) and dVIX are in the regression. The price-only rule is a required benchmark. AUM-path shuffle across calendar quarters (1,000 draws): the actual c must exceed the 95th percentile. The L-instead-of-L(L-1) placebo is reported only. FOMC, CPI, OPEX and month-end sessions are flagged and also reported without. Costs 0/4/8 bp are reported. One tercile cut, no grid.

rows.reason: Real, peer-reviewed mechanism, and the window is out of sample for every source. But c is identified only by AUM variation, the rule as proposed is indistinguishable from price momentum, and the VX settlement time had to be pinned to 16:00 ET. The registration now requires the flow rule to beat its price-only twin, adds a regime control, and makes the row inconclusive when K does not vary enough.

rows.name: vix-etp-rebalancing-next-day-reversal-fade
rows.source_notes: Brogger thesis section 1.3.4 (extracted). The regression is the 15:30 t-1 to 15:30 t change on Rebal_{t-1}, with controls for the contemporaneous VIX change and late-day realised vol. The coefficient is 'not significantly different from zero' with both controls, and Brogger reads that as complete reversal. The implied cost is $34.3m/yr, or 2.4% p.a. on $1.44bn average AUM. The SUERF note (text extracted) says trading against leverage rebalancing 'delivers large abnormal returns and Sharpe ratios above two across markets', gross. The Bangsgaard-Kokholm reversal is in the SPX channel (the JBF 180 abstract confirms a subsequent reversal).
rows.replication_concerns: Brogger's reversal is inferred from a non-significant 24h coefficient, an absence of evidence rather than a measured fade. The fade can earn at most the late-day impact (about 0.04 vol points per one-sd flow pre-2018, of the same order as the spread), and post-2018 K is smaller. The cross-check registration has two errors. First, it omits TVIX (2x ETN, about $1.5bn in June 2020, delisted 2020-07-12) from K over 2018-03..2020-07, which understates K exactly in March 2020. Second, its controls dVIX_t and log(VIX/VIX3M)_t use VIX/VIX3M closes printed at 16:15 ET, 15 minutes after the 16:00 VX settle, which leaks the start of the target window. The sunshine-trading reading (liquidity providers already compete it away) predicts a null.
rows.data_notes: Archived: cboe-vx-futures 2013-01-02..2026-10-14 (settle, volume, OI), cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history 2009-09-18..2026-10-14, daily-history-UVXY and daily-history-SVXY 2011-10..2026-10, and daily-history-VXX from 2018-01-25. Issuer shares/NAV are not archived, and TVIX (Credit Suisse ETN) outstanding history is not obtainable, so the judged window must start after its delisting. From 2020-07-13 to 2026-10-14 there are about 1,570 sessions.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) The signal ends at settle t, which is also the entry price. TAS orders close at 15:58 ET, before settlement, so the regression is a mechanism test, not an executable one. (2) VIX and VIX3M closes are stamped at 16:15 ET, after the 16:00 settle, so all VIX controls must be dated t-1. (3) Issuer shares dated t-1 enter at 09:30 t. (4) SPVXSP weights must come from the expiry calendar, not from realised holdings. (5) Settle = 0 rows must be dropped.
rows.missing_data: Daily shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares). TVIX outstanding history only for the reported pre-2020-07 arm.

final.claim: Over 2020-07-13..2026-10-14 (the session after TVIX's delisting on), VIX-ETP leverage-rebalancing demand has a negative coefficient on the return of the SPVXSP-weighted VX M1/M2 settlement portfolio from settle t to settle t+1. Starting after TVIX means every leveraged or inverse VIX ETP in the window has fund-level issuer shares; halves split at the median session. The regression controls for the portfolio's own return R_t, R_t x VIX_{t-1}, and log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1}. Rebal_t = K_{t-1} x R_t, with K as in vix-etp-leverage-rebal-vxx-last-half-hour: UVXY 1.5 and SVXY -0.5 throughout, and UVIX 2 and SVIX -1 from each fund's first daily bar (late March 2022). R_t = the portfolio's return from settle t-1 to settle t. This is a mechanism test only. Rebal_t ends at the settle that would be the entry, after the 15:58 ET TAS cutoff, so it cannot be executed. A pass licenses only a separately registered forward paper test of the VXX closing-auction form, with Rebal estimated from a price taken before the MOC cutoff.
final.statistic: OLS g in R_{t+1} = a + b*R_t + f*(R_t x VIX_{t-1}) + g*Rebal_t + e*log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1}. Newey-West lag 5, one-sided, cross-checked by a studentized circular block bootstrap (21-session blocks, 5,000 draws). Reported: a post-2022-03 x Rebal interaction (the UVIX/SVIX jump in K); the reversal share g/c once the late-day row has run; and 2018-03-01..2020-07-10 with TVIX outstanding imputed (flagged, never judged).
final.procedure: R comes from cboe-vx-futures settles with Settle = 0 rows dropped, using SPVXSP weights on the two contracts the index holds, derived from the expiry calendar. A dated t-1 enters at 09:30 ET t. ADV20 is computed through t-1. VIX and VIX3M enter only at t-1, because their closes print at 16:15 ET, after the 16:00 settle. The VXX trading form (short at the close on top-tercile Rebal, long on bottom-tercile, exit at the next close, 4 bp round trip, Rebal from the 15:30 VXX bar) is reported on the 60m window with the estimate error, and is never judged here.
final.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, daily-history-VXX, daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY. To fetch: daily shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares).
final.pass: All of: g < 0 with one-sided HAC p < 0.05 and the bootstrap agreeing; g < 0 in both halves; the same sign without 2024-08-05 and 2025-04-03..2025-04-09; deflated p < 0.05 over the VIX-ETP flow family.
final.controls: R_t (plain daily autocorrelation), R_t x VIX_{t-1}, and the VIX/VIX3M regime at t-1 (T-53). Placebo: L in place of L(L-1), reported. Within-quarter AUM shuffle (1,000 draws): g must fall below the 5th percentile. FOMC and CPI days are also reported without. One specification, no grid.

rows.reason: This is the best-powered test of the VIX-ETP mechanism, but the proposed version leaked 15 minutes of the target through 16:15 ET VIX controls and left TVIX out of K. Starting after TVIX's delisting, lagging every VIX control, and stating plainly that it is a mechanism test fixes both.

rows.name: vix-etp-demand-predicts-spx-futures-close
rows.source_notes: IDEAS listing for Bangsgaard and Kokholm, JBF 180 (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.jbankfin.2025.107556. The abstract says VIX ETP demand is 'a strong predictor of the end-of-day SPX futures return in-sample and out-of-sample' and finds 'evidence of a subsequent reversal', through VX market makers hedging in SPX options and futures. The candidate's statement that the abstract says the effect was historically profitable was not found on the listing. The sample was not visible.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication. Mandel's T-427 and T-428 found no SPY last-half-hour momentum or next-open reversal in this window. Size arithmetic puts the ES hedge at a few hundred million dollars on large days, which is small against MOC imbalances. D_t is nearly collinear with both VXX's and SPY's own moves to 15:30 (VX and SPX are strongly negatively correlated), so after those controls only AUM variation identifies h. Since D > 0 on SPY down days, the claim is a conditional late-day continuation, the pattern T-427 rejected on price alone. The cross-check's window (2023-11..) cannot be built, because D needs the VXX move to 15:30, and VXX 60m bars reach back only to about 2024-10-22.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m SPY and ES_F run 2023-11-21..2026-10-20. daily-history-SPY runs 1993..2026-10-14. daily-events-SPY does NOT exist in the archive, although the cross-check lists it; dividends must come from the adjclose/close ratio in daily-history-SPY. There are no VXX intraday bars, so the window is capped at the Yahoo 60m VXX fetch (about 2024-10-22 on). GEX history is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The same issuer-shares timing as the late-day row. The SPY 15:30 bar open is both signal and fill. The ES_F daily settlement time differs from SPY's 16:00 close, so ES_F is reported only. Ex-dividend nights need the dividend added back to the close-to-open return.
rows.missing_data: Yahoo 60m VXX; VIX-ETP daily shares outstanding and NAV (as in the late-day row); optional SqueezeMetrics GEX history.

final.claim: On SPY sessions where Yahoo 60m VXX bars exist (2024-10-22..2026-10), VIX-ETP rebalancing demand D_t = K_{t-1} x r^VXX_t has two signs. Here K is the late-day row's VX-dollar convexity, scaled by SPY's trailing-20-session dollar volume instead of VX ADV, and r^VXX_t is VXX's return from the prior official close to the 15:30 bar open. D_t has a negative coefficient on SPY's return from the 15:30 bar open to the official close, controlling for SPY's own return to 15:30, r^VXX_t, and r_SPY,ROD x VIX_{t-1}. It has a positive coefficient on SPY's next close-to-open return, with dividends added back. Mechanism: when VIX ETPs buy VX, VX dealers who sold it are short vega and sell ES/SPY into the close.
final.statistic: OLS h in r_SPY,late = a + b*r_SPY,ROD + k*r^VXX_t + m*(r_SPY,ROD x VIX_{t-1}) + h*D_t. Newey-West lag 5, one-sided. Second equation: the slope of the next close-to-open return on D_t with the same controls. The VIF of D on the controls is reported.
final.procedure: A, L and timing follow vix-etp-leverage-rebal-vxx-last-half-hour. SPY's official close and next open come from daily-history-SPY, with the dividend inferred from the adjclose/close ratio on ex-dates. The 15:30 price is the SPY and VXX 15:30 bar open. Early closes are dropped. If the VIF exceeds 10, the row is reported but not judged (as in T-658). Trading form, reported only: sign(-D) on top-quintile |D| sessions, 15:30 bar open to the closing auction, 2 bp round trip. ES_F is a reported replication and not judged.
final.data: Archived: local 60m SPY and ES_F, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-VXX, cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history. To fetch: Yahoo 60m VXX; VIX-ETP shares and NAV; optional SqueezeMetrics GEX.
final.pass: All of: h < 0 with one-sided HAC p < 0.05 after deflation over the VIX-ETP flow family; h < 0 in both halves; the close-to-open coefficient positive as a point estimate; h still significant with T-658's equity-LETF D in the regression if that has been archived.
final.controls: r_SPY,ROD (T-427), r^VXX_t, and the regime interaction. GEX_{t-1} where available (T-656). AUM-path shuffle placebo. FOMC, CPI, OPEX and month-end sessions are flagged. 2 bp costs. One quintile cut.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the cross-check's window and the daily-events-SPY bundle do not exist. The window shrinks to the VXX 60m span and min_n to 450, and r^VXX enters as a control so that only K identifies h. The prior is low given T-427 and T-428.

rows.name: vix-etp-calendar-roll-pressure-term-structure
rows.source_notes: SUERF Policy Note 153 (text extracted): ETF inception raises the first-month basis by 82.5% and the M2-M1 spread by 59.1% (difference-in-differences). The gap is 18.5% per year on average. ETFs sell M1 and buy M2 daily in calendar rebalancing. BIS WP 952 (fetched): the Findings section gives the EFG of 0.61 vol points (113% of the M1 basis) and the EFG-sign strategy Sharpe of 1.78. The ETF share of VIX futures 'often exceeds 40%'.
rows.replication_concerns: Single source, from the XIV/TVIX era. T-160 (the VX M1-M2 calendar) failed, with the sign flipping between halves. The candidate's 'short-M2/long-M1 (T-160's construction)' contradicts itself: T-160 is short M1 / long M2. The liquidity-provider side of the ETP roll is long M1 / short M2. C_t requires the outstanding of VXX and TVIX, which are ETNs, and whether those issuers hedge in VX at all is unobservable.
rows.data_notes: cboe-vx-futures (per-contract settle and OI, 2013-01..2026-10), cboe-VIX-history and cboe-VIX3M-history are archived. No ETP shares exist. VXX (Barclays) and TVIX (Credit Suisse) ETN outstanding history is not obtainable from the archive or from verified free sources; sec-companyfacts holds only issuer-level totals.
rows.lookahead_risks: ETN outstanding is disclosed only sporadically, in 424B3 supplements, and Barclays suspended VXX issuance in 2022 after over-issuing. Any C_t built from that is partly ex post.
rows.missing_data: Daily outstanding for VXX and TVIX ETNs; daily shares and NAV for VIXY, UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares).

final.claim: Not registered; recorded as a diagnostic only. Daily over 2020-07-13..2026-10, net VIX-ETP calendar-roll demand C_t, computable before the session, has a positive coefficient on the settle t-1 to settle t change in ln(F2/F1), controlling for log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1} and days to M1 expiry. C_t = (sum over long products of A_{k,t-1} L_k minus sum over inverse products of A_{k,t-1} |L_k|) / (roll days in the current SPVXSP period) / ($1000 x F1_{t-1}) / OI(M1)_{t-1}. The liquidity-provider side of the ETP roll is long M1 / short M2.
final.statistic: Daily OLS slope, Newey-West lag 10, one-sided.
final.procedure: A first-seen at t-1, including VXX (an ETN, flagged). Settle = 0 rows are dropped. Halves split at 2023-08-31. Placebo: shuffle C across days within each year.
final.data: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history; ETP and ETN outstanding (to fetch).
final.pass: Slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 in both halves, and above the placebo's 95th percentile.
final.controls: VIX/VIX3M regime, days to expiry, T-160's unconditional spread as a baseline.

rows.reason: There is no executable form on Mandel's venues: VX trades on Cboe CFE, which is not on the list, and no ETP isolates M1 versus M2. The decisive input (VXX and TVIX ETN outstanding, and whether those issuers hedge in VX) is unobtainable. A pass would license nothing while still taking a slot in the VX-family deflation.

rows.name: short-opposite-leverage-etp-pair-intraday
rows.source_notes: CXO Advisory summary of Todorov (Nov 2019 paper), fetched. Daily data 2000-01..2018-12, with pairs starting around 2010. The strategy 'shorts at the open and covers at the close each day'. Gross annual return and Sharpe: VIX (+1/-1) 21% and 0.89, natural gas (+3/-3) 43% and 2.59, silver (+2/-2) 18% and 1.86, gold (+3/-3) 8% and 0.81. The VIX pair gained 51% on 2018-02-05, and ETFs often hold more than 30% of VIX and natural-gas futures. The SUERF note (extracted) confirms 21% and 43% with Sharpe 0.89 and 2.59, and the 'right-way risk' from tracking errors.
rows.replication_concerns: The candidate's mechanism has the wrong sign. By the daily-reset identity, a short L / short -L pair entered at the open nets about g x i x sum_k w_k L_k (L_k - 1), where g is the overnight move and i the intraday move. It pays when the intraday move continues the gap. Arithmetic also casts doubt on Todorov's VIX number: for the +1/-1 pair the factor is 1, so 21%/yr is about 8 bp/day of E[g x i]. With daily sd(g) of about 2.5% and sd(i) of about 3.5% that implies a correlation near 0.9, which is implausible. Opening-print deviations from NAV and the single 2018-02-05 day are the likelier source. T-333 (no gap continuation on SPY) and T-325 (the multi-day LETF pair failed after deflation) set a low prior. A Corwin-Schultz cost floor is inflated by volatility for leveraged volatility ETPs and would fail the test mechanically. Most 3x commodity ETNs in Todorov's sample are delisted.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-UVXY and daily-history-SVXY 2011-10-04..2026-10-14, and daily-events-UVXY (13 events, 2012-03..2025-11). daily-events-SVXY is not archived; split-adjusted closes keep same-day ratios. SVIX, UVIX, VIXY, BOIL, KOLD, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL are not archived and need a free Yahoo daily fetch. No historical locate or easy-to-borrow (ETB) record exists.
rows.lookahead_risks: Yahoo daily open and close are official auction prints, which OPG and MOC orders reach, so fills are realistic only for shortable legs. Historical shortability is unknown (UVXY is often hard to borrow, and Alpaca shorts only ETB names), so the result is an upper bound. Leverage changes and reverse splits must be dropped by date. Any cost estimate from a day's high-low must use only prior sessions.
rows.missing_data: Yahoo daily OHLC with events for SVIX, UVIX, VIXY, BOIL, KOLD, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL; per-pair leverage histories from 8-K and prospectus text; a forward Alpaca ETB record.

final.claim: Over 2018-02-28..2026-10-14, shorting each declared long/inverse ETP pair at the official open and covering at the official close every session earns a positive mean net return on gross short notional, pooled with equal weight per pair-session. Each pair starts on the first session both legs trade, at dollar ratios that make index exposure zero at the prior close: UVXY/SVXY 1:3, UVIX/SVIX 1:2, VIXY/SVIX 1:1, BOIL/KOLD 1:1, AGQ/ZSL 1:1, UGL/GLL 1:1. Fixed costs per leg per side: 5 bp for VIX ETPs, 3 bp for metals and gas. No borrow is charged, since nothing is held overnight. Mechanism, stated as pre-registered: gross P&L is about g x i x sum_k w_k L_k (L_k - 1), so the pair pays when the intraday move continues the overnight gap. The exposure factor is 0.75 for UVXY/SVXY, 2 for UVIX/SVIX, 1 for VIXY/SVIX and 4 for the 2x/-2x pairs.
final.statistic: Pooled mean daily net return on gross notional, studentized circular block bootstrap (10-session blocks, 5,000 draws, resampling calendar days jointly across pairs). Per-pair mean, Sharpe and 1% CVaR. DSR over the 6 pairs. Diagnostic: each pair's slope of open-to-close P&L on g x i of its underlying (from the long leg's own prices divided by its leverage), and the share of gross P&L earned on 2024-08-05 and in 2025-04.
final.procedure: Daily OHLC from Yahoo. Leverage histories come from SEC 8-K and prospectus text at acceptance. Any session with a leverage change, split or distribution in either leg is dropped, together with the following session. Halves split at 2022-06-30. Corwin-Schultz spreads from prior sessions are reported as a cost sensitivity only. Alpaca ETB status of every leg is recorded forward before any paper form, and the historical result is labelled an upper bound for an account that can locate every leg.
final.data: Archived: daily-history-UVXY, daily-history-SVXY, daily-events-UVXY. To fetch (Yahoo daily, free): SVIX, UVIX, VIXY, BOIL, KOLD, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL with events; leverage histories from EDGAR.
final.pass: All of: pooled mean net > 0 with one-sided bootstrap lower bound > 0; positive in both halves; DSR > 0.95 over the 6 pairs.
final.controls: T-333's gap correlation sets the expectation. T-325's monthly pair is reported for contrast. A cost grid of 0/5/10 bp per leg per side is reported. Results without 2024-08-05 and 2025-04 are reported. One exposure-neutral weighting rule, no grid.

rows.reason: The source checks out, including the open-to-close holding. But the candidate's mechanism has the wrong sign: the pair is a bet that the intraday move continues the overnight gap. The proposed volatility-inflated Corwin-Schultz cost would fail it mechanically, so costs are now fixed. Cheap to run once the data are fetched, but expected to fail on costs.

rows.name: vix-etp-flows-and-the-vix-futures-premium
rows.source_notes: Nielsen and Posselt, CREATES RP 2022-06 (text extracted), published as IRFA 95 (2024). Sample October 2012 to February 2019: six VIX ETPs, 8,001 ETP-day observations, mean daily flow 0.49%, median 0.11%. The paper finds a positive relation between short-term product flows and VIX premiums, strongest when the premium is large, and VAR impulse responses in which flow shocks move the premium. The IRFA abstract says VIX increases are followed by outflows, which may help explain the 'low premium response puzzle'. Cheng (RFS 2019) was not fetched; the claim relies on the listing.
rows.replication_concerns: A single source for the flow-to-premium link. T-404 found that ETF flows follow price and do not predict it. About 92 holdout cycles give little power for a Clark-West increment. The largest long-vol products are ETNs: VXX throughout, and TVIX to 2020-07. Their outstanding is not disclosed daily, and Barclays suspended VXX issuance in 2022, so Flow is badly measured without them. The cross-check's unweighted 'net creations' is not the VX demand the mechanism implies. That demand is sum_k L_k x NAV_k x dShares_k: a $1 inflow to UVXY buys $1.5 of VX, and a $1 inflow to SVXY sells $0.5.
rows.data_notes: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history (2009-09-18..), cboe-VVIX-history (2006-03..) and daily-history-SPY. No ETP or ETN shares are archived. T-652, the prerequisite, is untested.
rows.lookahead_risks: Shares dated t-1 enter at 09:30 t. ETN outstanding reconstructed from sporadic 424B3 supplements is partly ex post and must be flagged. E_t must reuse T-652's expanding AR(1) unchanged. One observation per cycle avoids overlap.
rows.missing_data: Daily outstanding for VXX, plus TVIX and XIV for the in-sample years (Barclays and Credit Suisse ETNs); daily shares and NAV for VIXY, UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares); T-652's verdict.

final.claim: Once per VX settlement cycle (T-652's entry session, the first with <= 21 trading days to F1's final settlement), 2013-05..2026-10 with 2019-03.. as the holdout: adding Flow_t to T-652's premium P_t improves the out-of-sample accuracy of an expanding-window forecast of the hold-to-final-settlement short-F1 return. Flow_t is the VX demand implied by fund flows: sum_k L_k x NAV_k x dShares_k summed over the 21 sessions to t-1, divided by $1000 x mean(F1, F2) x OI(F1+F2) at t-1. It covers every US-listed short-term VIX-futures ETP and ETN: VXX and VIXY (1), UVXY (2, then 1.5 from 2018-02-28), TVIX (2, to 2020-07-10), XIV (-1, to 2018-02-15), SVXY (-1, then -0.5 from 2018-02-28), and UVIX (2) and SVIX (-1) from 2022-03.
final.statistic: Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (one-sided) and Campbell-Thompson R2_OS of the P + Flow model against the P-only model over holdout cycles. Reported: the step-1 slope of P_t on Flow_t with T-652's controls.
final.procedure: Run only after T-652 has a verdict, reusing its E_t construction unchanged. Expanding-window OLS from 2013-05; the first forecast is at 2019-03. ETN outstanding taken from sporadic supplements is flagged. If daily outstanding for VXX cannot be obtained, the row stays blocked and is never run with VXX left out. 2020-02..04 is also reported without.
final.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, cboe-VVIX-history, daily-history-SPY. To fetch: daily outstanding for VXX, TVIX and XIV; daily shares and NAV for VIXY, UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares).
final.pass: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 and R2_OS > 0 in the holdout, with both positive in each holdout half (split at 2022-12-31). Any trading form (short F1 via SVXY/SVIX, sized by the predicted premium) needs its own registration with DSR over the VX family.
final.controls: Benchmarks: P-only (T-652) and the raw basis F1 - VIX. T-652's VVIX and RV21 controls. The trailing 21-session VX return is in the model, against reverse causality (per T-404).

rows.reason: The source is verified. The flow measure is corrected to the leverage-weighted VX demand, the ETNs are named explicitly, and the row stays blocked rather than run without VXX. It must wait for T-652's verdict and has low power.

rows.name: short-vol-etp-convexity-crowding-tail
rows.source_notes: CFA summary of Augustin, Cheng and Van den Bergen, FAJ 2021 Q3: a feedback loop of ETP rebalancing pushed VIX futures up on 2018-02-05, leveraged ETPs held a large share of VX, and short-vol ETPs lost more than 90% in one day. It is a case study with no forecasting statistics. The SUERF note (extracted) says the net ETF share was near zero in February 2018, while the potential price impact of leverage rebalancing was 60% of the total market size of the first two contracts.
rows.replication_concerns: The evidence is one event plus a decomposition, with no predictive test anywhere. K rises when short-vol AUM swells in calm regimes, so it partly proxies low VIX, which is why the interaction controls are essential. The cross-check's judged window (2019-01..) leaves out TVIX (a 2x ETN of about $1.5bn, delisted 2020-07-12), which understates K in exactly March 2020. Fixing that by starting at 2020-07-13 loses March 2020 from the judged set. The 99th-percentile claim rests on very few spikes.
rows.data_notes: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, daily-history--GSPC (1927..2026-10-14), daily-history-SVXY and fred-DTB3 (to 2026-10-13). There are 192 S&P 500 sessions below -1% from 2020-07-13 to 2026-10, and 47 from 2019-01 to 2020-07-10. ETP shares are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: K uses A and OI dated t-1. The VX settle (16:00 ET) and the S&P close (16:00) are synchronous in the window; the pre-2021 16:15 settle applies only to the reported years. Overlay positions are decided at close t and applied from close t+1. z(K) and the overlay's decile cut use expanding and trailing windows.
rows.missing_data: Daily shares outstanding and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares); TVIX outstanding only for the reported 2019-01..2020-07 arm.

final.claim: Over 2020-07-13..2026-10 (complete fund-level coverage after TVIX's delisting; 2019-01..2020-07-10 reported with TVIX imputed), on sessions where the S&P 500's close-to-close return is below -1%, the VX M1 settle return is more sensitive to the S&P 500 return when K_{t-1} is high. The coefficient on SPX_t x z(K_{t-1}) is negative after controlling for SPX_t x VIX_{t-1} and SPX_t x log(VIX/VIX3M)_{t-1}. K_{t-1} = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) / ($1000 x mean(F1, F2)_{t-1}) / OI(M1+M2)_{t-1}, over UVXY (1.5), SVXY (-0.5), UVIX (2) and SVIX (-1). In addition, an SVXY overlay that moves to cash when K is in its trailing-252-session top decile has a lower 1% CVaR and a lower maximum drawdown than always holding SVXY, with a non-negative Sharpe difference.
final.statistic: OLS interaction coefficient on down days, HC3 errors, one-sided. Cluster-robust errors (down days within 5 sessions share a cluster) are reported. Secondary: 90th- and 99th-percentile quantile regressions of the VX M1 daily up-move on K_{t-1} over all sessions. Overlay against always-SVXY: Sharpe difference, maximum drawdown and 1% CVaR, at 10 bp per switch.
final.procedure: Down days come from daily-history--GSPC closes. VX M1 is the nearest monthly with more than one session to expiry, measured settle to settle on the same contract. z(K) uses an expanding window. Overlay positions are decided at close t, applied from close t+1, with cash at DTB3.
final.data: Archived: cboe-vx-futures, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SVXY, fred-DTB3. To fetch: daily shares and NAV for UVXY and SVXY (ProShares) and for UVIX and SVIX (Volatility Shares).
final.pass: Interaction < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, the same sign without 2024-08-05 and 2025-04-03..2025-04-09, and deflated within the VIX-ETP flow family. Overlay: lower 1% CVaR and lower maximum drawdown than always-SVXY, and a Sharpe difference >= 0 as a point estimate.
final.controls: VIX-level and term-structure interactions (K proxies the calm regime). T-435's VIX3M/VIX timing as the competing overlay; always-SVXY as the baseline. One decile cut, no grid. 10 bp per switch.

rows.reason: A sensible, loss-reducing risk overlay with verified anecdotal sources. The window must start after TVIX's delisting, or K is wrong in the crash it is meant to measure.

rows.name: gsci-bcom-roll-front-running-decay-test
rows.source_notes: Mou 2011 (Columbia, CFTC copy, text extracted): 19 GSCI commodities, sample 1980-01..2010-03. Strategy 1 shorts the maturing and buys the deferred contract, 20% per day on days -10..-6, and unwinds during the roll. Annualised Sharpe in 2000-2010 is 1.09-2.75 for Strategy 1 and 0.46-1.78 for Strategy 2, with up to 3.99 and 4.39 counting trading periods only. Energy under Strategy 1 earned 4.43%/yr at Sharpe 2.2. The control group of 18 non-index commodities shows nothing. Irwin, Sanders and Yan (preprint dated 2022-01-20; Table 2 extracted): in 2004-2011, pre-GR -32.1 bp (t -6.72), GR -5.6 bp, post-GR +36.6 bp. In 2012-2019, pre-GR -3.1 bp (t -0.90), GR +0.2 bp (t 0.06). Roll-window cost 4.36%/yr in 2004-2011 versus 0.64%/yr in 2012-2019. Dubois-Marechal, Sanders-Irwin 2016 and Saverys 2024 were not fetched.
rows.replication_concerns: Decay is established, and a tradable pass is very unlikely. One tick per leg per side is about 1.4 bp of CL notional, so roughly 5.6 bp per round trip of the spread, which exceeds the whole 2012-2019 pre-roll move. The holdout 2020-01..2024-03 is not fresh: Saverys' MSc covers 2010-2024 and finds near-zero profits. ISY pool all index commodities, while this panel is energy only.
rows.data_notes: No EIA bundle is archived. A web check confirms that EIA's NYMEX daily contract 1-4 settlements stop at 2024-04-05. T-687 and T-688 are blocked on the same fetch.
rows.lookahead_risks: EIA labels contracts 1-4 by position, so a label changes contract at each expiry and must be mapped through the CME expiry calendar. The GSCI contract-month schedule (which contract is rolled out of and into, by month) must come from the S&P GSCI methodology, not be inferred. Signals are calendar-only, and settles are fillable with TAS orders.
rows.missing_data: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 daily settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (free, to 2024-04-05); CME expiry rules; the S&P GSCI contract-roll schedule. Any live form needs a forward cmegroup.com settlement capture.

final.claim: Over 2020-01..2024-03, for NYMEX CL, HO, RB and NG, Mou's Strategy 1 earns a positive pooled mean net P&L per month, in bp of one-leg notional, after 1 tick per leg per side. Strategy 1 shorts the contract the S&P GSCI will roll out of and buys the one it rolls into, adding 20% per day at the settle on business days -10..-6 before GSCI roll day 1 (business day 5), and unwinds 20% per day at the settles of roll days 1-5.
final.statistic: Pooled mean monthly net P&L, equal weight across the 4 commodities. Newey-West lag 3 t and a studentized block bootstrap over months (6-month blocks); per-commodity means. Second trial: Strategy 2 (days -5..-1), counted in the DSR. Reported: the decay ratio, the 2012-2024 mean over the 2004-2011 mean computed identically.
final.procedure: Per-contract settlements are stitched from EIA contracts 1-4 using the CME expiry calendar (contract k before an expiry is contract k-1 after it). Positions are held only in the two delivery months named by the GSCI roll schedule for that month. Marks are at settles only. 2020-04 (negative WTI) is kept and also reported without. 2012-2019 is reported as the ISY replication and not judged.
final.data: To fetch: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (shared with T-687 and T-688); CME expiry rules; the S&P GSCI roll schedule.
final.pass: Pooled mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 (HAC and bootstrap) in 2020-01..2024-03 (51 months) and also in 2012-2019, and DSR > 0.95 over the 2 strategies counted with the energy-curve family (T-687, T-688, energy-post-gsci-roll-spread-rebound-holdout-2020, uso-disclosed-roll-day-spread-pressure).
final.controls: Placebo: the same legs on calendar-shifted windows at equal distance from expiry. Cost grid 0.5/1/2 ticks. ISY's 2012-2019 numbers set the expectation. The CIT sign test is not run because CIT positions are not archived.

rows.reason: The sources are verified and the decay is already documented, so this is worth running only as a cheap passenger on the shared EIA fetch. The fix pins the GSCI contract schedule and the expiry stitching.

rows.name: post-index-roll-spread-reversal
rows.source_notes: ISY Table 2 (extracted), nearby-minus-deferred changes in bp. In 2012-2019: pre-GR -3.1 (t -0.90), GR +0.2 (t 0.06), post-GR +15.9 (t 4.11), full window +13.0 (t 2.57). Earlier periods: post-GR +46.3 in 1991-2003 and +36.6 in 2004-2011. The authors call the 2012-2019 post-GR rise anomalous ('It is not clear why this occurs'). Table 3 (out-of-index commodities, 2012-2019) shows post-GR -12.8 (t -0.75), so the rise is not a generic drift visible in the control group. Windows: pre-GR is the 10 business days before day 5, GR is business days 5-9, post-GR is the 10 business days after day 9.
rows.replication_concerns: A single source whose own authors flag the result as unexplained, which is a forking-path risk. The 2012-2019 full-window rise of +13.0 bp is a drift, not a reversal of prior pressure. ISY pool 19 index commodities, and the energy-only subset is unmeasured. For CL, the contract the GSCI rolls out of expires around business day 14-16, inside the post-GR window, so the CL leg is truncated and the window differs by commodity.
rows.data_notes: The EIA panel is not archived and ends 2024-04-05 (verified), so the holdout is at most 51 months x 4 commodities, with months correlated across commodities.
rows.lookahead_risks: Expiry-calendar stitching of the EIA labels. The truncation date must come from exchange rules, not from the data. The placebo must hold distance to expiry fixed.
rows.missing_data: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG; CME expiry rules; the S&P GSCI roll schedule.

final.claim: Over 2020-01..2024-03, for NYMEX CL, HO, RB and NG, a position long the contract the S&P GSCI just rolled out of and short the contract it rolled into (equal dollars) earns a positive pooled mean net P&L per month after 1 tick per leg per side, and more than the same position on placebo dates. Entry is at the settle of GSCI roll day 5 (business day 9). Exit is at the settle 10 business days later, or 2 business days before the nearby's last trading day if that is earlier.
final.statistic: Pooled mean monthly net P&L in bp of one-leg notional; Newey-West t and a studentized block bootstrap (6-month blocks). The placebo distribution comes from 200 block-shifted roll calendars with distance to expiry held fixed.
final.null: Pooled mean net <= 0, or the actual mean below the placebo's 95th percentile.
final.procedure: The panel is stitched as in energy-gsci-roll-frontrun-holdout-2020, and positions are marked settle to settle in the two contracts the index rolled. The CL holding window is truncated by the expiry rule, and per-commodity holding lengths are reported. 2012-2019 is reported as the replication of ISY's flagged result and never judged.
final.data: To fetch: EIA NYMEX contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG; CME expiry rules; the S&P GSCI roll schedule.
final.pass: Holdout mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and above the placebo's 95th percentile, positive in at least 3 of the 4 commodities, and DSR > 0.95 within the energy-curve family.
final.controls: The placebo calendar (generic time-to-expiry drift and roll-down). A regression variant adds the T-687 basis at entry. Costs 0.5/1/2 ticks.

rows.reason: Verified, and the source's own 2012-2019 magnitude (+15.9 bp, t 4.11) is now known. That roughly 5.6 bp of round-trip cost leaves room is what makes a holdout worth running. The fix pins the CL expiry truncation and keeps the placebo decisive.

rows.name: uso-ung-own-roll-window-pressure
rows.source_notes: Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle and Venkataraman, CFTC OCE draft (March 2014, text extracted), published in JFE 2016. USO pays about 25 bp per roll, roughly 3% per year, in adverse settlement-price changes. More than 95% of the temporary impact reverses within 15 minutes. Spreads are narrower and depth greater on roll days: liquidity provision rather than predation. The 2020 change is confirmed by search results (etf.com): in April 2020 USO moved from front-month-only to a multi-month blend, with a 10-day roll from May 2020, and later to an actively managed mix. The current '10-day roll at the start of the month' was not verified, and the USCF statement PDF returned empty.
rows.replication_concerns: The source finds the cost falls on the fund and is earned by liquidity providers within minutes, which daily settles cannot see. Post-2020, USO spreads holdings across many months at its own discretion, so 'USO front-month contracts / OI' is ill-defined, and roll days may not be disclosed in advance. USO's assets were $890m at 2025-12-31 (sec-companyfacts), well under 1% of CL open interest, so post-2020 pressure should be tiny. Bessembinder's daily data run to 2013, so 2012-2013 is in-sample.
rows.data_notes: sec-companyfacts holds USO (CIK 1327068): 66 quarterly cover-share values 2010-07..2026-08, and Assets of $889.6m at 2025-12-31. UNG (CIK 1376227) has 496 rows. daily-history-USO starts 2006-04-10 and daily-history-UNG 2007-04-18. sec-submissions lists filings, but the text is not parsed. CFTC legacy crude (067651) and natural gas (023651) are not archived; only gold and silver are. The EIA panel is not archived and ends 2024-04-05.
rows.lookahead_risks: Roll days must be taken from filing text accepted before the roll; a period without ex-ante disclosure has no claim. Quarter-end holdings enter at 10-Q acceptance. CFTC open interest enters at its Friday release.
rows.missing_data: EIA contract 1-4 settlements; USCF roll-schedule text from 10-K, 10-Q and prospectus filings (free EDGAR, to parse); USO holdings by contract month from the 10-Q schedules of investments; CFTC legacy reports 067651 and 023651.

final.claim: Over 2014-01..2024-03 (after Bessembinder et al.'s daily sample), counting only USO roll periods whose dates were disclosed in SEC filing text accepted before the roll, three things hold. (a) The mean change in ln(F1/F2) of NYMEX WTI on USO's roll days, minus the mean over the 3-7 business days before, is negative. (b) The per-roll pressure (minus that difference) rises with S = USO's contracts in the contract month it rolls out of, divided by CL total open interest. (c) Short the rolled-out contract and long the rolled-into contract from the settle two business days before the first disclosed roll day to the settle of the last nets more than zero after 1 tick per leg per side. Each holds in the pre-2020-04 regime (fixed 4-day roll) and in the post-2020-05 regime (multi-month holdings).
final.statistic: (a) Mean difference with HAC t. (b) Slope of per-roll pressure on S, with S from the last 10-Q and CFTC report before the roll, HAC. (c) Mean net P&L per roll, studentized bootstrap (blocks of 3 rolls).
final.procedure: Roll days come from USCF filing text, first-seen at SEC acceptance. A roll whose dates were not disclosed in advance is excluded and counted. A regime with fewer than 20 disclosed rolls is reported as inconclusive and not judged. Contracts are identified by delivery month through EIA stitching. UNG/NG is reported, not judged. 2020-04 is excluded from the judged set and reported.
final.data: Archived: sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, daily-history-USO, daily-history-UNG. To fetch: EIA contract 1-4 settlements, USCF filing text, CFTC legacy reports for 067651 and 023651.
final.pass: (a) < 0 with p < 0.05 pooled and the same sign in each judged regime; (b) one-sided p < 0.05; (c) mean net > 0 with bootstrap lower bound > 0 in each judged regime; DSR within the energy-curve family.
final.controls: Bessembinder's pre-window control. Days overlapping the GSCI window are flagged. Placebo roll calendars. Cost grid 0.5/1/2 ticks.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the 2020 methodology change undermines the 'front-month share' scale and the assumption that roll days are known in advance. The registration now judges only disclosed rolls, starts after the source's sample and needs 20 rolls per regime. The expected footprint post-2020 is tiny.

rows.name: leveraged-commodity-etf-rebalancing-into-settlement
rows.source_notes: No direct commodity evidence exists, as the candidate itself states. The CXO summary of Todorov (fetched) confirms the natural-gas pair figures (43%/yr gross, Sharpe 2.59) and that ETFs often hold more than 30% of VIX and natural-gas futures. Barbon et al. (the equity analogue) was not fetched; it is cited only as an analogue.
rows.replication_concerns: Exploratory, with no source testing the claim. Size arithmetic gives about 1% of NG front-month dollar volume on large moves, and much less for CL, GC and SI, though perhaps around 10% of settlement-window volume for NG. The settlement windows differ by contract: COMEX silver settles about 13:24-13:25 ET, not 13:28-13:30. Leverage histories of the LETFs have changed over time and must be verified. Yahoo intraday futures bars are stamped by bar open and follow Yahoo's own front-month roll.
rows.data_notes: The local 5m universe contains CL_F, NG_F, GC_F and SI_F, about 60 sessions (development only). 60m bars exist from 2023-11 but cannot isolate 2-minute settlement windows. No LETF daily OHLC or shares/NAV are archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: 5m bars are stamped by bar open, so the settlement price is the close of the bar containing the window. ProShares shares dated t-1 enter at 09:30 t. ADV20 must come from the capture through t-1. Contract-specific settlement windows must be taken from CME rules before the capture starts.
rows.missing_data: A forward 5m capture of the NG, CL, GC and SI fronts aligned to settlement windows; ProShares daily shares and NAV for BOIL, KOLD, UCO, SCO, AGQ, ZSL, UGL and GLL; their leverage histories; CME settlement-window rules per contract.

final.claim: Over the first 250 sessions of a forward 5m capture of the NG, CL, GC and SI front futures (the about 60 archived 5m sessions are development only), commodity-LETF rebalancing demand D_t has a positive pooled coefficient on the front future's return from 30 minutes before its CME settlement window to the settlement price. D_t = sum_k A_{k,t-1} L_k (L_k - 1) r_t / ADV20_t in dollars, for BOIL/KOLD (NG), UCO/SCO (CL), UGL/GLL (GC) and AGQ/ZSL (SI), with leverage taken from prospectus text at each date. r_t is the front future's return from the prior settlement to the window start.
final.statistic: Pooled panel OLS with commodity fixed effects and Driscoll-Kraay errors, one-sided. Per-commodity slopes are reported, with NG where the footprint is expected. The next-session reversal coefficient is reported.
final.procedure: Settlement windows are taken per contract from CME rules (NYMEX energy about 14:28-14:30 ET, COMEX gold about 13:28-13:30, silver about 13:24-13:25) and frozen before the capture starts. ProShares shares and NAV dated t-1 enter at 09:30 t, first-seen. ADV20 comes from the capture. The own return to the window start is a control. Trading form, reported only: sign(D) on top-tercile |D| sessions in micro contracts where listed, 1 tick per side.
final.data: Local 5m and 15m CL_F, NG_F, GC_F and SI_F (development only). To capture: forward 5m bars. To fetch: ProShares daily shares, NAV and leverage history for the 8 LETFs.
final.pass: Pooled slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves of the forward window, and a next-session reversal coefficient <= 0 as a point estimate.
final.controls: Own-return momentum. Placebo: L in place of L(L-1). AUM shuffle. EIA storage-report Thursdays (NG), CPI and FOMC days flagged. 1 tick per side.

rows.reason: Exploratory, forward-only, low prior. The fix pins contract-specific settlement windows (silver differs), leverage-history verification and a single pooled test rather than four separately deflated cells.

rows.name: commodity-linked-note-hedging-pricing-dates
rows.source_notes: The Illinois experts listing confirms Henderson, Pearson and Wang, RFS 28(5) 1285-1311 (2015). The abstract says CLN issuers' hedging trades transmit uninformed flows that raise and lower futures prices. The Fuel Oil News press summary (2012) confirms the 37, 40 and 51 bp impacts for issues of at least $2m, $5m and $10m, and that the impacts are 'permanent, showing no signs of reversal'. Sample and note count were not visible.
rows.replication_concerns: No replication, and the sample is pre-2012. Note principals of $2-20m are tiny against WTI or gold futures volume, so a 37-51 bp mean is hard to reconcile with hedging impact. Structured-note pricing dates cluster at month ends and on fixed weekdays, which a weekday-matched placebo does not control. The arm B reversal is the candidate's own hypothesis. The build cost is very high relative to the prior.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-CL-F (2000-08..2026-10-15), BZ-F (2007-07..), GC-F and SI-F (2000-08..), and DBC (2006-02..). Local NG_F 1d bars cover about 10 years. sec-submissions holds filing lists only, with no full text and no parsed note terms.
rows.lookahead_risks: Only the preliminary supplement's expected pricing date and its acceptance time are point-in-time. Final sizes come from post-pricing 424B2 filings, so size buckets are report-only. Yahoo continuous fronts jump at rolls, so events within 2 days of a front roll must be masked. The beta is estimated on the prior 250 sessions only.
rows.missing_data: An EDGAR full-text-search event set (424B2, FWP and preliminary pricing supplements, 2008-2026) parsed for underlying, expected pricing date, principal and final valuation date.

final.claim: Take commodity-linked notes referencing WTI, Brent, gold, silver, natural gas, BCOM or GSCI, found by EDGAR full-text search of preliminary pricing supplements and FWPs filed 2008-2026. Buying the referenced front future at the settle two business days before the preliminary filing's expected pricing date, and selling at the pricing-date settle, earns a positive mean abnormal return after 1 tick per side. The abnormal return is the futures return minus beta x the DBC return.
final.statistic: Mean abnormal return per event, with date-clustered standard errors, one-sided. Size buckets are reported only, using sizes stated in the preliminary filing.
final.procedure: Events whose preliminary filing was accepted after the entry settle are dropped. Events on the same date and underlying are merged. Beta comes from the prior 250 sessions. Events within 2 business days of a Yahoo front roll are masked. Arm B (final valuation dates) is reported, not judged. The row stays blocked until the parser exists.
final.data: Archived: daily-history-CL-F, daily-history-BZ-F, daily-history-GC-F, daily-history-SI-F, daily-history-DBC, local NG_F 1d, sec-submissions. To build: an EDGAR full-text-search parser.
final.pass: Mean net abnormal return > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 in both 2008-2016 and 2017-2026, with at least 40 events in each half, and above the 95th percentile of the month-position placebo.
final.controls: Placebo: the same commodity on non-event dates matched by position in the month (business days from month end) and weekday, because note pricing clusters at month ends. FOMC, CPI and EIA inventory days are flagged. 1 tick per side.

rows.reason: The source is verified via the abstract and press summary, but the size arithmetic and month-end clustering point to confounding. The fix adds a month-position placebo, roll masking and minimum event counts per half, and keeps the row blocked on the parser.

rows.name: annual-commodity-index-reweighting-flows
rows.source_notes: Kitco (2026-01-07) confirms Societe Generale's estimate of about $5bn of net selling each in silver and gold, and TD Securities' estimate of about 13% of COMEX silver open interest sold over two weeks, for BCOM only. The Citi ($6.8bn, about 12% of OI) and JPMorgan figures were not in Kitco, and the Futu page returned no text, so they are unverified. WisdomTree's 9-15 January 2026 window is consistent with BCOM business days 6-10, counting from 2 January as day 1.
rows.replication_concerns: No measured impact study exists; the flow estimates are practitioner forecasts. The flow is public weeks ahead, and sunshine-trading logic and the decay in index inclusion effects (Greenwood-Sammon) predict a small impact. Implied flow loads mechanically on December returns, a momentum/reversal confound. The January reweight overlaps the January roll on the same days. With 8 holdout years, a year-level Fama-MacBeth t has 7 degrees of freedom and very low power.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-CL-F, GC-F, SI-F and HG-F (2000-08..2026-10) and BZ-F (2007-07..); local NG_F 1d; cftc-cot-legacy-f-088691 (gold) and cftc-cot-legacy-f-084691 (silver), 1,937 rows each. Fronts for HO, RB, grains, softs and livestock, other CFTC open interest, and the annual target-weight announcements are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Target weights enter at their announcement dates. Index membership must be point-in-time per year (BCOM added a constituent for 2026), not today's list. Yahoo continuous fronts roll on expiry, so January roll jumps must be masked or same-contract returns used. CFTC open interest enters at its Friday release.
rows.missing_data: BCOM and S&P GSCI annual target-weight announcements 2010-2026 with publication dates; Yahoo fronts for the remaining members; CFTC legacy open interest per commodity.

final.claim: Over the January reweights of 2019-2026 (2010-2018 reported), across the point-in-time BCOM members with US-listed futures (about 16-20), the implied January reweighting flow has two signs. It has a positive Fama-MacBeth slope on each front future's excess return over BCOM business days 6-10, and a negative slope over the following 5 business days. flow_i = (target weight_i - December-drifted weight_i) / (front-month OI_i x price_i). Target weights are first-seen at their announcement; drift is computed from constituent excess returns through the last December close; AUM is a pre-declared constant.
final.statistic: Fama-MacBeth slope per year for the window and for the reversal; the mean across years with the year-level t. The long-short form (long the top tercile by flow, short the bottom tercile, micro futures where listed, 1 tick per side) is reported.
final.procedure: Membership and target weights come from the announcement for that year, first-seen at publication. Returns are measured on the same contract through each window, with Yahoo front-roll jumps masked as in T-370 and T-555. Open interest comes from the CFTC legacy report released before the window. GSCI weights are reported as a second flow definition and not judged. Each year after 2026 is appended as a forward yearly record.
final.data: Archived: daily-history-CL-F, GC-F, SI-F, HG-F, BZ-F, local NG_F 1d, cftc-cot-legacy-f-088691, cftc-cot-legacy-f-084691. To fetch: Yahoo fronts for the other members, the annual target-weight announcements, CFTC legacy open interest per commodity.
final.pass: Window slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 over 2019-2026, post-window slope < 0, and long-short net > 0. With fewer than 8 holdout years the row is inconclusive.
final.controls: December-return momentum and reversal as a control, since drifted weights load on past returns. Placebo: the same cross-section in non-January months (block-shifted). Costs. One tercile cut.

rows.reason: A clean mechanism with only partly verified practitioner sources. The fix adds point-in-time membership, same-contract returns through the coinciding January roll, and an honest inconclusive rule for 8 holdout years.

rows.name: futures-btc-etf-roll-cme-calendar-pressure
rows.source_notes: The BIS Quarterly Review (December 2021) is verified: BITO reached about one third of short-term bitcoin futures roughly 10 days after its 2021-10-19 launch, its calendar rebalancing lowers expiring prices and raises deferred ones, and a 2018 launch would have trailed spot by about 18% cumulatively over four years. K33 (2022-10-18) is verified on 'half the open interest on CME' and BITO's 32,520 BTC. It does NOT say that the August 2022 roll pushed the 1-month basis to an all-time low; the candidate misattributed that. A search found no published fixed BITO roll calendar, only the generic sell-near-expiry description.
rows.replication_concerns: No academic study exists; the evidence is practitioner commentary with one misattributed claim. BITO's share of CME open interest has likely fallen since spot ETFs launched in January 2024 (unverified), so decay is expected by construction. T-329 found basis-based edges shrank after the spot ETFs.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-BTC-F (front only, 2017-12-18..2026-10-15), coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD (2019-01-01..2026-10-15) and cftc-cot-tff-f-133741 (2018-04-10..2026-10-06). Expired per-contract CME BTC settlements are not on Yahoo, and CME DataMine is paid.
rows.lookahead_risks: BITO's roll days are not published as an ex-ante schedule, so 'three business days before BITO's first roll day' uses ex-post holdings, which is look-ahead. A point-in-time version must use a fixed window relative to expiry.
rows.missing_data: Per-contract CME BTC and MBT daily settlements and open interest for 2021-10..2026-10 (paid), or about 30 months of forward capture; BITO holdings history.

final.claim: Not registered; recorded for revival if CME per-contract BTC settlements are captured for T-552. Over at least 30 forward monthly expiries, the change in the annualised CME BTC calendar spread ln(F2/F1) over a fixed window of business days -8..-3 before the front's last trading day exceeds the change over matched non-window days at the same days to expiry, and rises with BITO's front-month contracts / CME open interest from the latest disclosure.
final.statistic: Mean window-minus-matched change with HAC t; slope on the scale variable.
final.procedure: Forward capture of cmegroup.com daily settlements. Fixed calendar window, declared now. BITO holdings first-seen at publication.
final.data: daily-history-BTC-F, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, cftc-cot-tff-f-133741; forward CME settlement capture.
final.pass: Mean change > 0 with p < 0.05 and a positive scale slope over at least 30 forward expiries.
final.controls: Matched days to expiry, DTB3 drift, T-362 and T-329 as context.

rows.reason: Not testable on any data Mandel can get for years. The historical test needs paid CME per-contract data, the forward test needs about 30 monthly rolls of an effect that has probably decayed, BITO's roll days are not published in advance (so the proposed trading rule is not point-in-time), and one cited practitioner claim is not in its source.

rows.name: spot-btc-etf-flows-to-cme-basis-shorts
rows.source_notes: NYDIG 'Notes on a rally', 2024-11-15 (fetched). Weekly change in leveraged-fund basis shorts on weekly ETF flows, IBIT flows lagged one day: about $0.30 per $1, t 6.4, R2 about 0.51. Leveraged funds are the proxy for hedge funds. The sample period is not disclosed in the text; the charts are images. The Blockworks dispute over the arbitrage share of flows was not fetched.
rows.replication_concerns: A single practitioner regression, contemporaneous, over an undisclosed sample. The weekly association will probably replicate, but it licenses nothing. The predictive daily slope has a low prior given T-404 (flows follow price), T-362 (cash-and-carry failed) and T-329 (the basis edge shrank after the ETFs). The sign of any predictive effect is ambiguous: arbitrage inflows imply compression, directional inflows imply widening. A two-sided test is honest, but it requires a stable sign across halves.
rows.data_notes: Archived: daily-history-BTC-F (2017-12-18..2026-10-15), coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD (2019-01-01..2026-10-15), cftc-cot-tff-f-133741 and cftc-cot-tff-fo-133741 (2018-04-10..2026-10-06), daily-history-IBIT and daily-history-FBTC (2024-01-11..2026-10-14), ishares-ibit-premium-discount (2024-01-31..2026-10-14, 480 rows), ishares-ibit-snapshots (1 row) and fred-DTB3. Farside flows are not archived; T-611 is blocked on the same bundle.
rows.lookahead_risks: Farside day-t flows are complete only by 13:30 UTC t+1, and the table is revised, so forward first-seen capture is needed and earlier values are flagged backfill. The TFF report enters at its Friday 15:30 ET release for the Tuesday as-of date, and the weekly flows must match the Wednesday-Tuesday as-of week. The basis must use Coinbase spot at the CME settlement hour (T-329's construction), never daily 00:00 UTC closes. The 5 sessions before expiry are excluded.
rows.missing_data: Daily US spot BTC ETF net flows (Farside, free, revised); IBIT daily shares and NAV history (only one snapshot is archived).

final.claim: Over 2025-01..2026-10, after NYDIG's 2024-11-15 note (2024-01-11..2024-12 reported as replication), US spot BTC ETF net flow for day t, used no earlier than 13:30 UTC t+1, predicts the change in the CME front-month annualised basis from the settle of t+1 to the settle of t+5. The regression controls for the basis level at t+1, the BTC return over t-4..t, and T-612's latest leveraged-funds change. Mechanism check: the weekly change in CFTC TFF leveraged-funds net short, divided by open interest, is positively related to the week's flows.
final.statistic: Daily: Newey-West (lag 5) slope of the basis change on Flow_t ($bn), two-sided as pre-registered. Weekly: slope of the change in leveraged-funds net short / OI on the week's flows, one-sided, each report measured at its release.
final.procedure: Basis = ln(BTC=F settle / Coinbase spot at the CME settle hour) x 365 / days to the front's expiry (T-329's construction), on the same contract over each 4-session window, excluding the 5 sessions before expiry. Flow_t is the Farside all-fund sum for day t; IBIT dShares x NAV from iShares is a cross-check. Revisions are measured on the forward capture. A trading form (T-362's cash-and-carry entered when predicted compression is lowest) is registered separately, and only if the daily slope passes.
final.data: Archived: daily-history-BTC-F, coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD, cftc-cot-tff-f-133741, cftc-cot-tff-fo-133741, daily-history-IBIT, daily-history-FBTC, ishares-ibit-premium-discount, fred-DTB3. To fetch: farside-btc-etf-flows (shared with T-611); IBIT daily shares and NAV history.
final.pass: Daily slope nonzero with HAC p < 0.05 in 2025-01..2026-10 and the same sign in both halves (split at 2025-12-31); weekly slope > 0 with p < 0.05 over 2025-01..2026-10.
final.controls: Basis level, lagged BTC return, the DTB3 change, and T-612's leveraged-funds change as a competing regressor. The reverse direction (the basis change over t-4..t predicting flows) is reported. ETH ETFs are excluded.

rows.reason: The source is verified, and the fetch is shared with T-611, so this is cheap. The fix adds T-612's change as a control, pins the weekly flow window to the TFF as-of week, and keeps the trading form gated on the daily slope.

knowledge.title: Mechanical ETP and index flows in futures: VIX-ETP leverage and roll rebalancing, commodity index and ETF rolls, and how much survived decay (literature survey)
knowledge.markdown:
# Mechanical ETP and index flows in futures: VIX-ETP leverage and roll rebalancing, commodity index and ETF rolls, and how much survived decay (literature survey)

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 15 candidate strategies, each source-checked and re-registered by a verifier (13 fixed, 2 dropped). Core papers: Brogger (JBF 2021); O'Neill & Whaley (JFM 2023); Todorov (RoF 2024, BIS WP 952); Bangsgaard & Kokholm (JBF 2025); Nielsen & Posselt (IRFA 2024); Augustin, Cheng & Van den Bergen (FAJ 2021); Mou (2011); Irwin, Sanders & Yan (AEPP 2023, "ISY"); Bessembinder et al. (JFE 2016); Henderson, Pearson & Wang (RFS 2015). Practitioner: CXO, BIS, K33, NYDIG, Kitco.
- **Links:** https://research-api.cbs.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/64811551/s_ren_bundgaard_br_gger_03_2021.pdf · https://www.bis.org/publ/work952.pdf · https://scotthirwin.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Irwin_Sanders_Yan_AEPP_All.pdf · https://www.cftc.gov/sites/default/files/idc/groups/public/@economicanalysis/documents/file/oce_predatorysunshine0314.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.60 (fraction of the sources actually read and verified: 20 of 32 opened, about 12 in full text or the relevant sections, the rest as abstracts, listings or summaries).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-21. **How much was read:** extracted text of Brogger, Todorov (SUERF, BIS), Nielsen-Posselt, Mou, ISY Tables 2-3, the Bessembinder CFTC draft and the practitioner pages; abstracts for the rest. Not opened: Barbon et al., Cheng, Sanders-Irwin 2016, Dubois-Marechal, Saverys 2024. Archive: VX futures (2013-01..2026-10, settle, volume, open interest) and daily VXX/UVXY/SVXY exist; issuer shares outstanding do not; EIA curves end 2024-04-05.
- **Selected because:** shares outstanding, open interest, derivative volume, the VIX term structure and calendars are program inputs, and these flows are uninformed and forecastable before the trade.

## What it says

- **VIX-ETP leverage rebalancing into the close.** A daily-reset fund with leverage L and AUM A must add A·L(L−1)·r of exposure after an index return r; L(L−1) > 0 outside [0, 1], so long and inverse funds both trade with the move at the settlement. Brogger (2010-11..2017-12): mean flow 6.7% of VX M1+M2 volume; a one-sd flow moves VX +0.046 vol points over 15:30-16:15 against a ~0.05 spread; front-running made 402%/yr gross (Sharpe 5.14), negative at 0.04 points of cost. O'Neill-Whaley: the predictability diminished over time. On 2018-02-27 UVXY (2x→1.5x) and SVXY (−1x→−0.5x) cut L(L−1) from 2 to 0.75; UVIX/SVIX (2022) raised it again. No post-2018 holdout exists.
- **Next-day reversal.** Brogger's 24-hour coefficient is insignificant, read as full reversal (absence of evidence, not a measured fade); investors lose 2.4%/yr. Todorov: fading leverage rebalancing has Sharpe above two, gross.
- **Spillover to S&P futures.** Bangsgaard-Kokholm: VIX-ETP demand predicts the end-of-day SPX futures return in and out of sample, through dealers' ES hedges, with a later reversal. Unreplicated.
- **Calendar-roll pressure.** Constant-maturity ETPs sell M1 and buy M2 daily. Todorov: ETF inception raised the M1 basis 82.5% and the M2−M1 spread 59.1%; a 0.61-point non-fundamental component traded at Sharpe 1.78. Single source.
- **Short both legs of an opposite-leverage pair, open to close.** Todorov via CXO (to 2018, gross): VIX ±1 21%/yr (Sharpe 0.89), natural gas ±3 43% (2.59), silver ±2 18% (1.86), gold ±3 8% (0.81). Corrected sign: P&L ≈ gap × intraday × Σw·L(L−1), a bet on the intraday move continuing the overnight gap.
- **ETP flows and the VIX futures premium.** Nielsen-Posselt (2012-10..2019-02): flows bet on mean reversion (a 1-point return rise cuts next-day flow 0.72 points) and move the premium, which predicts VX returns (Cheng, RFS 2019).
- **Convexity crowding.** In February 2018 potential rebalancing impact was 60% of the first two contracts' size; the FAJ case study ties the 2018-02-05 spiral to it (short-vol ETPs lost over 90% in a day). One event.
- **Commodity-index roll front-run.** GSCI rolls on business days 5-9, BCOM 6-10. Mou (1980-2010): opening the spread 10 days early had Sharpe 1.09-2.75 in 2000-2010. ISY: the pre-roll move fell from −32.1 bp (t −6.72, 2004-2011) to −3.1 bp (t −0.90, 2012-2019), roll cost from 4.36% to 0.64%/yr. Decayed.
- **Post-roll rebound.** ISY: +36.6 bp (2004-2011), still +15.9 bp (t 4.11) in 2012-2019, absent outside the index; the authors cannot explain it.
- **USO's own roll.** Bessembinder et al. (2008-2013): ~25 bp per roll in adverse settlements, over 95% of temporary impact reversed within 15 minutes, narrower spreads on roll days: liquidity provision, not predation.
- **Commodity LETFs into settlement.** No direct evidence; the VIX formula applied to BOIL/KOLD, UCO/SCO, AGQ/ZSL, UGL/GLL before NYMEX/COMEX settlement windows.
- **Commodity-linked note hedging.** Henderson-Pearson-Wang: futures rose 37-51 bp on pricing dates, permanently (press summary, pre-2012).
- **January index reweighting.** BCOM 2026 bank estimates: ~$5bn of selling each in silver and gold, ~13% of COMEX silver open interest. No measured impact.
- **Spot BTC ETF flows and CME basis shorts.** NYDIG: ~$0.30 of leveraged-fund basis shorts per $1 of weekly inflow (t 6.4), contemporaneous.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: mainstream-educational.** Rigorous for the existence and decay of the price impact (three peer-reviewed VIX-ETP papers; Mou, ISY and Bessembinder on rolls). But every positive profit figure is gross and pre-2018 (VIX) or pre-2012 (commodities), and the reweighting, BTC-ETF and commodity-LETF claims are practitioner estimates or extrapolation.

## What Mandel adopts

- **The VIX-ETP flow family, pre-registered and deflated jointly** (four rows plus T-658's cells), with issuer shares point-in-time at 09:30 the next session. `vix-etp-leverage-rebal-vxx-last-half-hour` must beat its price-only momentum twin, since T-427 lost 2.09 bps/day (HAC t −2.58) and T-428's reversal slope was −0.084; it is inconclusive if K varies less than 1.5x. `vix-etp-rebal-vx-settle-reversal-post-tvix` is best-powered (about 1,570 sessions from 2020-07-13) but a mechanism test only: TAS closes at 15:58 ET and VIX at 16:15, so VIX controls are lagged.
- **The convexity overlay** (`vix-etp-rebal-convexity-downday-vx-beta`): cut short-vol exposure when convexity crowds open interest, judged on maximum drawdown and CVaR. It only reduces risk; always-long SVXY drew down 95% (T-379), T-435's contango filter failed, and the VIX/VIX3M term structure (T-53, supported) enters as a control.
- **ETF flows into T-652**, leverage-weighted (Σ L·NAV·dShares), with a reverse-causality control because T-404 parked GLD flows as following price. Blocked until VXX's ETN outstanding exists and T-652 has a verdict.
- **The opposite-pair short as a gap-continuation bet**, at fixed costs (5 bp per VIX leg per side, 3 bp metals and gas), no borrow fee (nothing held overnight); an upper bound, as historical locates are unknown. T-333 (SPY gap-intraday corr +0.018) and T-325 (DSR 0.000) set a low prior.
- **The energy-curve family on one EIA fetch** with T-687/T-688: the GSCI front-run as a 2020-01..2024-03 holdout, the post-roll rebound (its 2012-2019 +15.9 bp still exceeds the ~5.6 bp round-trip cost), and USO's disclosed roll days.
- **Spot BTC ETF flow to the CME basis**, sharing T-611's Farside fetch, with T-612 as a competing regressor.
- **Agreement with the children:** Bessembinder's liquidity providers earn within 15 minutes, as Brier and Shannon find that takers lose to makers and the touch-maker edge (+0.80 to +0.93c) depends on queue position, zero on strict through-fills (Results 15, 24). And T-345 (month-end rebalancing, −45.6 bps net, supported) shows a calendar-known flow can survive.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Front-running VIX-ETP flows: decayed.** Brogger's JBF abstract finds no excess profits from trading ahead of the flow.
- **Calendar-roll pressure: dropped** to a diagnostic. VX trades on Cboe CFE, not on Mandel's venue list; no ETP isolates M1 against M2; ETN outstanding is unobtainable; T-160 failed (halves −$7.6 and +$15.3 a day).
- **The BITO roll: dropped.** Paid per-contract data, roll days not published in advance, a K33 claim missing from its source, and decay after the 2024 spot ETFs (T-329, inconclusive: +0.229% pre-2024, +0.039% after).
- **The GSCI front-run as an edge** (−3.1 bp is below cost) and **the post-roll rise** (one source, unexplained: a forking paths risk until the holdout speaks).
- **USO after 2020** (discretionary holdings, $890m), **note hedging** (37-51 bp is implausible for $2-20m notes), **January reweights** (forecasts, eight holdout years).
- **Todorov's gross Sharpes**, including a VIX pair return that needs an implausible gap-intraday correlation. The SPX channel faces T-427/T-428's nulls; NYDIG's sign is ambiguous and T-362 failed.
- **Venues:** VX futures are data only; trading uses VIX ETPs on Alpaca and CME futures. Nothing needs an offshore venue.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **F4 flow features** for T-577/T-578: K = Σ A·L(L−1)/VX dollar volume, Rebal = K × r, leverage-weighted VIX-ETP flow, commodity-LETF demand, and roll calendar flags (GSCI, BCOM, post-roll, USO, January reweights). They must add over vx_basis (20-day IC −0.13 on equity ETFs, t −7.3 in T-580's F3 scan, where 0 of 132 swing cells pass).
- **Data to add, first-seen, backfill flagged:** ProShares and Volatility Shares daily shares outstanding and NAV; leverage histories; Yahoo 60-minute VXX (from 2024-10-22); forward 5-minute VXX and NG/CL/GC/SI captures; EIA contracts 1-4 plus forward CME settlements; GSCI roll schedule and target weights; USCF filings; Farside flows.
- **Point-in-time rules:** Yahoo bars are stamped by open and the zero-length 16:00 bar is the closing print; VIX closes after the 16:00 VX settle; Farside counts from 13:30 UTC t+1; drop Settle = 0 rows; mask front-roll jumps; flag FOMC and CPI days.
- **Tests:** a price-only twin; AUM-path shuffles and block bootstrap; L instead of L(L−1) as a reported placebo; block-shifted roll calendars at fixed distance to expiry; inconclusive rules (VIF > 10, little K variation, under 20 disclosed rolls).

## Cross-links

- A6 (LETF rebalancing as a covariate), A13 (closing-auction pressure), A9 (futures curves, commodity carry), A11 (variance risk premium), A8 (crypto basis, funding rates), A14 (month-end flows), A15 (COT hedging pressure).
- A4 (MMAR): Volmageddon as a fat-tail event. A5: how fast information reaches price. 12, 13, 14: pipelines these features feed.
- Theories T-53, T-160, T-325, T-329, T-333, T-345, T-362, T-379, T-404, T-427, T-428, T-435, T-611, T-612, T-651, T-652, T-658, T-687, T-688.

## Sources used

- Brogger (2021): https://research-api.cbs.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/64811551/s_ren_bundgaard_br_gger_03_2021.pdf
- O'Neill & Whaley (2023): https://research.bond.edu.au/en/publications/effects-of-nondiscretionary-trading-on-futures-prices/

candidates.name: Currency VRP cross-sectional sort: buy cheap-to-insure, sell expensive-to-insure currencies (Della Corte-Ramadorai-Sarno 2016)
candidates.summary: Each month, sort currencies on their volatility risk premium, VRP = expected realised vol (trailing 1-year daily RV) minus 1-year model-free implied vol (volatility swap rate). Buy the currencies whose vol insurance is cheap (high RV - IV) and sell the ones where it is expensive. The returns come almost entirely from spot moves, not from interest differentials, so this is not carry in disguise.
candidates.mechanism: Natural hedgers (corporates) pay up for vol insurance on currencies they fear will fall. When insurance is expensive, the same hedgers also sell those currencies, which pushes spot below fair value. Speculators with time-varying limits to arbitrage (funding liquidity, hedge-fund flows) absorb this flow and earn the later recovery. DRS show that CFTC commercial traders sell expensive-to-insure currencies while financial traders take the other side.
variables: derivative open interest (CFTC positioning as mechanism check)
adjacent_variables: CFTC commercial vs non-commercial FX futures positions
CME CVOL ATM and full-curve variance
candidates.assets: G10 FX vs USD, 6-8 pairs (EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD, CHF, optionally NZD, MXN), traded as CME FX futures or OANDA spot/forwards
candidates.claimed_effect: 1998-01 to 2013-12, monthly, 1-year OTC implied vols (JP Morgan/Bloomberg). Developed currencies: 4.95% p.a., Sharpe 0.61, net of spot/forward bid-ask. Developed plus emerging: 4.16% p.a., Sharpe 0.51. Correlation with carry is -0.08/-0.06. A static (full-sample-average) VRP sort earns 3.51% gross, but all of it from rate differentials, so the predictive content is the time variation. Quantpedia #669 lists 4.95% return at 8.15% vol.
candidates.replication: DECAYED / CONTESTED. Li-Sarno-Zinna (JFQA 2025, footnote 22) say performance becomes much weaker when the sample is extended to Dec 2021, and VRP is not significant in their 28-currency 1998-2021 panel. Babiak-Barunik (arXiv 2101.09738 v3) report a 1-month-VRP long-short at -0.29% p.a., Sharpe -0.03, over 2005-03 to 2021-12. They state that VRP has been unprofitable recently, and that Li-Sarno-Zinna's appendix runs the opposite sort. In Ornelas-Mauad's G10 2002-2016 sample, the VRP portfolio has a currency-only Sharpe of 0.18 (total return 0.35). Wider FX-anomaly decay: Hutchinson et al. (IRFA 2022) find an average out-of-sample Sharpe falling from +0.39 to -0.32 after publication, and Bartram et al. (JFQA 2025) find profits fall after publication. Mandel's own G10 carry/momentum books (T-368, T-431, T-478) all failed 2013-2026.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the CME CVOL FX pairs with history (EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD confirmed; CHF/MXN/NZD to verify), quoted as USD per foreign unit. Signal at the last business day of month t: VRP_i = RV_i (trailing 252-day RV from fx-spot-g10 noon fixes) - CVOL_i (both in vol points, DRS sign). Primary trial uses 30-day CVOL; the tenor mismatch with DRS's 1-year IV is flagged, and a 1-year analog is reported if DataMine provides one. Hold long the top-2-VRP currencies and short the bottom 2, equal weight, filled at the first noon fix of t+1. Return = spot change + lagged OECD 3-month differential (fx-rates-3m). Costs: 2 bp per leg per rebalance plus 1%/yr financing per leg (the T-368 convention). Window: CVOL availability (about 2018-2026, roughly 100 months; power is low, so a Sharpe below about 0.7 cannot pass). Statistic: annualised net Sharpe with a stationary bootstrap (block 12). Pass: Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, both halves positive, DSR > 0.95 with T-368/T-431/T-478/T-605 counted in the family. Controls: a static-ranking placebo (the DRS check), correlation with T-368, and the DRS sign versus its inverse reported (Li-Sarno-Zinna suggest the sign flipped).

candidates.name: Per-currency time-series VRP z-score (implied minus short-window realised vol) for 6-8 pairs
candidates.summary: This variant suits the small cross-section. For each currency separately, standardise its own short-window VRP = IV(1-month) - RV(recent, intraday or EWMA) against its trailing history, and trade that currency against USD on the sign of the z-score. Ornelas finds a positive IV-RV gap predicts foreign-currency appreciation. Macrosynergy reports VRP is positively correlated with subsequent FX forward returns, mostly in EM.
candidates.mechanism: A high implied-over-realised premium marks elevated risk aversion toward that currency. The risk premium priced into spot then mean-reverts, so the currency undershoots and later recovers (the Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou equity logic applied to FX, with the foreign currency as the risky asset). Safe havens (JPY, CHF) can flip the sign because they appreciate when risk aversion rises.
candidates.assets: EUR/USD first (EVZ history), then the CVOL G10 pairs; CME FX futures (6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C) or OANDA
candidates.claimed_effect: Ornelas (BCB WP 454, 2017): 1 percentage point of annualised currency VRP leads to 0.28% average appreciation over the next month (daily sample of 1-month options, 2007-10 to 2014-08, 20 currencies) and 0.16% over the next week (weekly sample 2003-2014, 6 currencies), with predictability up to 4 months. The out-of-sample MSE beats a zero-mean random walk, but significantly only for EM/LatAm, and for the full group only at a 4-year estimation window. JPY is the only significantly negative coefficient. Macrosynergy notebook (practitioner): VRP significantly positively correlated with subsequent weekly, monthly and quarterly FX forward returns, mainly EM; the developed-market evidence is weaker.
candidates.replication: CONTESTED SIGN. Ornelas notes the relationship flips with the RV window: Londono-Zhou (6-month options and RV) find a higher world currency VRP predicts depreciation, and DRS sort the other way on 1-year windows. Evidence is stronger in EM than in the G10 pairs Mandel can trade. No post-2015 replication found.
