candidates.proposed_test: Data: FRED EVZCLS (30-day EUR implied vol on FXE options, 2007-11-01 to 2025-03-11) plus DEXUSEU. Later, CVOL for the other pairs, forward or via DataMine. Signal each Wednesday at the 16:00 ET close: gap = EVZ - RV, where RV is an EWMA of squared daily log returns with an 11-day half-life (Macrosynergy's choice). z = gap standardised over the trailing 252 sessions. Hold long EUR vs USD (6E) for 1 week when z > +0.5 and short when z < -0.5. A second pre-registered horizon is 1 month (Holm over 2). Sign is fixed on 2007-11 to 2015-12, out-of-sample 2016-01 to 2025-03. Costs: 1 bp per side on 6E plus quarterly roll. Statistic: out-of-sample mean net return per trade with Newey-West t; Clark-West versus a zero forecast; permutation of z-dates. Pass: t > 2 out of sample, both out-of-sample halves positive. For CVOL pairs, JPY and CHF get their own pre-registered (negative) sign. Leakage: EVZ close and the FRED noon fix are not synchronous, so use the next day's noon fix as the fill.

candidates.name: Global currency volatility (level) and world currency VRP timing the dollar basket at 3-6 months
candidates.summary: Average implied (or realised) vol across currencies, or the average currency VRP, used as a time-series predictor of the equal-weight foreign-vs-USD basket (the dollar factor). Li-Qiao-Wang (2026) find global currency vol positively predicts currency returns beyond 3 months. Londono-Zhou find a rise in world currency VRP predicts foreign-currency depreciation at 4-6 months.
candidates.mechanism: Global FX vol proxies global uncertainty. Countercyclical risk premia mean that foreign (risky) currencies sell off as vol jumps and earn higher expected returns afterwards. The VRP part (the insurance price) captures crash-risk pricing that precedes further dollar strength. The two signals (level vs premium) may carry opposite signs.
candidates.assets: Equal-weight basket of 9 G10 currencies vs USD (CME FX futures basket or OANDA)
candidates.horizon: months (3-6 month predictive horizon, monthly decisions)
candidates.claimed_effect: Londono-Zhou (JFE 2017; 2000-2011, 22 currencies, 6-month ATM IV minus RV): world currency VRP is significant for 18 of 22 currencies at 4 months (not JPY). The R2 gain over the interest differential peaks at about 8% at 4 months. Li-Qiao-Wang (J. Empirical Finance 88, 2026; 17 currencies): global option-implied vol has in-sample R2 2.49-5.02% and global realised vol 2.64-7.13%. Out-of-sample R2 is reported as somewhat higher (search snippet). Predictability rises with inflation risk.
candidates.replication: Partly independent (two author teams, different samples). The direction of 'currency returns' in Li-Qiao-Wang was not verified beyond the abstract snippet (paywalled). No test on 2015-2026 found beyond Li-Qiao-Wang's sample, whose end date is unknown. Related to but distinct from T-605 (dollar carry AFD timing, untested).

candidates.proposed_test: TESTABLE NOW (realised version). GV_t = equal-weight mean of the 9 G10 21-day realised vols from fx-spot-g10 at month-end t. The implied version uses EVZ (2007-2025) as a one-currency proxy now and CVOL FXVL when available. Target: DOL basket excess return (mean spot change + one-month-lagged AFD/12) over the next 3 and 6 months, with overlapping monthly observations and Hodrick (1992) standard errors. Expanding-window OLS from 2000 with out-of-sample forecasts from 2013-01. Statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R2 and Clark-West p. Trading rule: long DOL when the forecast is > 0, else short, rebalanced monthly at the noon fix. Costs: 2 bp per leg per rebalance plus 1 bp roll. Pass: out-of-sample R2 > 0 with CW p < 0.05 at the pre-registered 3-month horizon, net Sharpe > 0.3 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, and DSR counting T-605. The level sign and the VRP sign are registered separately (level +, VRP -).

candidates.name: US equity variance risk premium (VIX^2 minus realised SPX variance) predicts foreign-currency appreciation vs USD at 1 month
candidates.summary: Londono-Zhou find that a rise in the US stock variance risk premium predicts that the dollar depreciates against essentially all currencies over the next 1-4 months. This is the opposite sign to the currency VRP. Brunnermeier-Nagel-Pedersen similarly find high VIX levels predict higher subsequent carry returns. The input is non-price, and every series is already archived.
candidates.mechanism: A high equity VRP is compensation for local (US) uncertainty. In a two-country model with orthogonal local and global uncertainty, high US-specific uncertainty raises the expected return on foreign currencies held by US investors. Practically, after equity-vol spikes, risk-off dollar demand and forced carry unwinds reverse.
candidates.assets: G10 FX basket and individual pairs vs USD (CME FX futures / OANDA)
candidates.claimed_effect: Londono-Zhou (2000-2011): a 100-unit rise in the monthly US VP corresponds to 2.10% annualised 1-month-ahead appreciation of foreign currencies vs USD, significant above the 1% level for all currencies at 1-4 months. BNP (1986-2006): high VIX and TED predict higher future carry returns, and controlling for them reduces the forward-premium predictability. Mandel's own ML F3 IC scan lists 'daily fx 5d own_iv (VIX for FX) positive IC +0.054, t 6.0, confirmed'. Its quote direction across USD-base and USD-quote pairs must be checked before treating it as support.
candidates.replication: Not independently replicated after 2011 that I found. The Mandel ML IC row is suggestive but pooled over mixed quote conventions. Partial overlap with T-368's VIX > 30 filter, which ran the other direction (cut carry when VIX is high) and failed.

candidates.proposed_test: TESTABLE NOW on archived data (cboe VIX, daily-history SPY, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3). VP_t = VIX_t^2/12 - RV^2_SPY (sum of squared daily log returns over the trailing 21 sessions, monthly units) at the month-end close. Target: next-month DOL basket spot return (9 G10 vs USD, FRED noon fix, filled at the first noon fix after the VIX close), plus the per-currency panel with currency fixed effects. Window: out-of-sample 2012-01 to 2026-09, after the paper's sample; slope estimated expanding from 1999. Rule: long DOL when VP is above its trailing 60-month median, else short (a flat-instead-of-short variant is reported). Costs: 2 bp per leg per switch plus 1 bp/month roll. Statistic: out-of-sample slope with HAC t, out-of-sample R2 (CW), and net Sharpe with stationary bootstrap. Pass: positive slope with t > 2, Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, both halves positive. Controls: VIX level alone, last-month SPY return, AFD (T-605), and a shuffled-month placebo.

candidates.name: FX volatility carry: sort forward volatility agreements on implied-vol term-structure slope (Della Corte-Kozhan-Neuberger 2021)
candidates.summary: Buy forward volatility (FVAs) on currencies whose implied-vol curve slopes down and sell it on currencies whose curve slopes up. This earns large returns that are uncorrelated with spot carry, and a single slope factor prices the FVA cross-section. The payoff is on volatility, not spot. The slope also feeds a separate spot-return claim (next candidate).
candidates.mechanism: An upward-sloping term structure embeds a volatility term premium: forward vol is upward-biased, and Della Corte-Sarno-Tsiakas 2011 show forward IV over-predicts future spot IV. Sellers of long-dated insurance on currencies with steep curves are compensated for permanent volatility shocks. The volatility-carry Sharpe barely changes with maturity, which DKN read as pricing of permanent shocks. Demand comes from long-dated hedgers, and dealers warehouse vega under limits to arbitrage.
adjacent_variables: CME FX option settlements by expiry
candidates.assets: FX options on G10 pairs (CME options on 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S; calendar straddles approximate an FVA)
candidates.claimed_effect: 1996-01 to 2015-12, 20 developed and emerging currencies, OTC vols (JP Morgan/Bloomberg). VCA earns 5.15%/month (t 5.91) for 1/3-month FVAs down to 2.50%/month (t 5.67) for 12/24, with Sharpe 1.46 down to 1.25. The average Sharpe of 1.32 drops to 0.83 when charging the largest quoted FVA spread (about 100 bp of vol at short maturities, 80 bp at long). Results hold for a 10-developed subset. Returns are countercyclical (best in 1997-99, 2008 and the euro crisis).
candidates.replication: No independent post-2015 replication found. The forward-vol bias is consistent with Della Corte-Sarno-Tsiakas (JFE 2011). DKN state their returns are on FVAs (total vol returns), not spot (per Ornelas-Mauad). Executability for Mandel depends on CME FX option calendar liquidity outside EUR and JPY.

candidates.proposed_test: Not testable on archived data; CVOL is a single 30-day tenor. Data: CME FX option settlements per expiry (DataMine back-history, or forward capture of the daily settlement files). Per currency (EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD, CHF), take ATM IV at about 1 and 3 months by interpolating the listed expiries. Slope = IV3m - IV1m, scaled by IV1m. At the first business day of each month: long a vega-matched calendar (buy the 3m straddle, sell the 1m straddle, i.e. long forward vol) on the 2 lowest-slope currencies and the opposite on the 2 highest. Unwind at the 1m expiry, marking the remaining leg at its settlement IV. Costs: half the captured CME bid-ask per leg; if only settlements exist, assume 0.3 vol points per leg (my assumption, flag and replace with measured quotes). Statistic: mean P&L per unit of forward vega, HAC t, sign test, and correlation with T-368. Pass: t > 2 on at least 36 months and both halves positive. Until then, register as blocked (data) with a forward-capture start date.

candidates.name: Implied-vol term slope predicts G10 spot returns (Ornelas-Mauad 2019): long low-slope, short high-slope currencies
candidates.summary: Fit the slope of each currency's implied-vol term structure (1 week to 10 years) every day. In developed currencies a steep slope predicts weak future spot returns; in EM the sign reverses. A G10 portfolio long the 2 lowest-slope and short the 2 highest-slope currencies beat carry, risk-reversal and VRP portfolios on currency-only Sharpe.
candidates.mechanism: In developed currencies, a steep slope reflects expected rising physical volatility and risk premium that is not yet in spot, so the currency later weakens. In EM, the slope mostly reflects a risk premium that is paid through later appreciation. The authors also split the curve into the 10-delta put wing, the ATM and the 10-delta call wing.
adjacent_variables: CME FX option settlements by expiry
FX ETF option chains (FXE, FXY) for a free forward term structure
candidates.assets: G10 FX vs USD via CME FX futures / OANDA
candidates.horizon: months (3- and 6-month holding in the regressions; daily-rebalanced overlapping portfolios)
candidates.claimed_effect: 2002-2016 daily, 18 currencies (10 G10 + 8 EM), JP Morgan OTC vols at 10 tenors. G10 ATM-slope portfolio: currency-only return 2.33% p.a., vol 7.00%, Sharpe 0.33 (total 2.29%, Sharpe 0.33). The right-tail slope portfolio has currency Sharpe 0.33 and total Sharpe 0.50. In the same sample, G10 carry has currency-only Sharpe 0.01 and total 0.33, and VRP has 0.18 / 0.35. EM ATM slope: Sharpe 0.43 (total 0.69). Costs were not stated in the text I read.
candidates.replication: CONTESTED: the developed-market sign is opposite to the working-paper version of Della Corte-Kozhan-Neuberger, where a steep slope predicts higher returns in a pooled sample. Ornelas-Mauad attribute the difference to pooling, composition bias, model-free IV and target (spot vs total). No out-of-sample test after 2016 found.

candidates.proposed_test: Needs multi-tenor IV; not archived. A free forward route is daily capture of FXE and FXY option chains (two currencies only) plus CME settlement files for 6 pairs. Signal at month-end: slope_i = OLS slope of ATM IV on log(tenor) across available expiries from 1 to 6 months, standardised cross-sectionally. Hold long the 2 lowest-slope and short the 2 highest via 6x futures. Pre-register the G10 negative sign from the paper. Holding periods are 1 and 3 months, with Holm across the two. candidates.name: Low-IV vs high-IV currency straddles: buy straddles where implied vol is low, sell where it is high (Fullwood-James-Marsh 2021)
candidates.summary: Each week, sort G10 currencies on 1-month ATM implied vol. Buy 1-month ATM-forward straddles on the low-IV currencies and sell them on the high-IV ones. FJM report large returns after transaction costs that standard FX, equity-option or risk factors do not explain. It is directly expressible on CME FX options.
candidates.mechanism: Hedging demand is concentrated in the currencies that already look risky (high IV), so their options are overpriced relative to subsequent movement. Low-IV currencies are under-hedged and their options are cheap. Dealers face limits to arbitrage in warehousing the imbalance, the FX version of the low-risk anomaly. The authors say total volatility matters, not any component or transformation of it.
adjacent_variables: FX option open interest / volume by currency (CME)
candidates.assets: FX options: CME options on 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S (DKK/NOK/SEK are not available on CME)
candidates.horizon: weeks to 1 month (weekly formation, 1-month straddles held to expiry)
candidates.claimed_effect: 1999-03-31 to 2016-09-28, weekly (Wednesday NY close), 1-month options on 9 G10 currencies (Bloomberg). The lowest-IV straddle returns about +25% per month and the highest-IV about -14%. Long-short returns 34% per month after transaction costs, Sharpe 1.03; diversified straddle, butterfly and delta-hedged versions reach Sharpe 1.38. On notional, about 40 bp per month (about 4.7% p.a.). The authors report the pattern holds consistently through the sample, and the coefficient is smaller but not significantly different in the more recent period.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found; no post-2016 evidence. Risk: in a 6-pair universe the IV ranking is persistent (for example AUD/JPY high, EUR/CHF low), so it may be a static bet; test a demeaned variant.

candidates.mechanism: Option buyers (corporate and real-money hedgers, structured-product desks) pay for convexity, and dealers and vol sellers earn the premium for bearing crash/vol-jump risk. Low-Zhang find the premium is negative in all majors and shrinks with maturity. Ammann-Buesser find it time-varying and larger when risk-neutral variance is high.

Report event days (ECB, FOMC, US CPI) separately, since vol sellers lose there.

candidates.name: Risk-reversal / CVOL skew filter on Mandel's carry books (T-368, T-431, T-605): crash filter versus contrarian re-entry
candidates.summary: Use option-implied skew (25-delta risk reversals, or CME CVOL Skew = UpVar - DnVar) on the long-carry currencies to cut, or add, carry exposure. The literature splits on the sign. BNP find that a higher price of crash insurance after losses predicts lower future crash risk, and that high VIX predicts higher carry returns. CME's 2023 study finds skew contrarian for AUD/USD. A naive 'exit when skew is steep' rule may sell insurance at the worst time.
candidates.mechanism: Speculators build carry positions, and high-yield currencies acquire negative skew because unwinds cluster when funding tightens. Option skew prices that crash risk. After a crash the insurance price rises, speculator positions shrink, and future crash risk falls (BNP), so steep skew can be a contrarian buy. Alternatively, crash-hedged carry (Jurek; Caballero-Doyle) holds that options are cheap insurance, so hedging the long leg keeps most of the premium while removing the left tail.
candidates.assets: G10 (+MXN, ZAR) carry books via CME FX futures / OANDA; hedge variant with CME FX puts
candidates.claimed_effect: BNP (1986-2006, quarterly; risk reversals 1998-2006): high-rate currencies have negatively skewed returns, and implied skew is cross-sectionally tied to the rate differential. VIX rises coincide with carry losses and falling risk-reversal prices, and high VIX/TED predict higher future carry returns. Jurek (2014; G10 1999-2012): crash-hedged carry still earns significant excess returns, and crash premia are at most one-third of carry (G10 point estimates 0.20-0.50% p.a.). Farhi et al.: disaster risk is more than one-third of the carry premium in advanced countries (1996-2014 version; about 25% in the 2009 version). CME (2023, 2007-2023): CVOL skew normalised to a 2-year 0-100 diffusion index is contrarian over the next 3 months for some markets including AUD/USD; no numbers were given for other FX.
candidates.replication: CONTESTED DIRECTION. The crash-premium share differs across versions and authors (Jurek <= 1/3, Farhi et al. > 1/3). Caballero-Doyle (NBER w18644, 67 currencies 2004-2012) find FX-option hedges cheap, but price options from IV quotes rather than trades. The underlying carry books already fail 2013-2026 (T-368 net Sharpe -0.30; T-431 failed). T-368's train-chosen VIX > 30 flat filter was part of that failure, so any skew filter must be deflated against those trials.

sources.title: Carry Trades and Currency Crashes (NBER w14473)
Crash-Neutral Currency Carry Trades (Jurek)
Crash Risk in Currency Markets (Farhi, Fraiberger, Gabaix, Ranciere, Verdelhan; NBER w15062)
Is CVOL Skew a Leading Indicator of Price Trends in Commodities, Bonds, and Currency Markets? (CME Group, read via mirror)

candidates.proposed_test: Overlay on the frozen T-368 and T-431 books (same rates, costs and rebalance). Signal per long-leg currency at month-end: CVOL Skew or SkewRatio, oriented so negative means foreign-currency puts are rich (flip for USD-base pairs). Convert to its trailing 24-month percentile (CME diffusion-index style). Rule A (crash filter): zero any long-leg currency below its 20th percentile. Rule B (contrarian, BNP/CME): double-weight it. Rule C (hedged): buy a 1-month 25-delta put on each long leg at CVOL-implied prices, model-priced. Window: CVOL history (about 2018-2026). A free proxy now is the Cboe SKEW/VIX ratio as a global crash price (archived), flagged as equity-based. Statistics: Sharpe difference versus the unfiltered book (stationary bootstrap) and changes in monthly skewness and MDD. The primary pre-registered criterion for A and C is an MDD cut of at least 30% at a Sharpe loss of at most 0.1; for B it is a Sharpe gain > 0 with p < 0.05. DSR counts T-368's 6 trials plus these 3.

candidates.name: Skew-neutral carry by rank difference (interest-rate rank minus implied-skewness rank) (Torok 2022)
candidates.summary: Combine carry with option-implied skewness in a small universe by weighting each currency by the difference between its interest-rate rank and its implied-skewness rank. Long high-yielders that are not priced for crashes, short low-yielders priced with high skew. Torok's 'RDF' portfolio and a 'crash-hedged carry' variant both show positive realised skew and higher Sharpe than plain carry over 2006-2022, which covers part of Mandel's test window.
candidates.mechanism: Part of carry's premium is compensation for crash risk that options already price. Currencies whose rate differential is high relative to their priced crash risk offer carry 'cheaply', while those with high skew relative to their rate are crowded crash risk. The rank-difference construction solves the problem of double-sorting few assets on two correlated signals.
variables: options skew (risk reversals / butterflies -> implied skewness)
candidates.assets: G10 (+EM in the paper) FX via CME futures / OANDA forwards
candidates.horizon: 1 month (monthly rebalance; only the 1-month holding is significant)
candidates.claimed_effect: 2006-01 to 2022-08, monthly, 1-month OTC options (about 27+ currencies incl. EM). Plain carry has Sharpe 0.48. CARhedged returns 3.2% p.a. with Sharpe 0.12 higher than carry and positive skew. RDF returns 2.8% p.a., Sharpe 0.54, nearly uncorrelated with carry (highest correlation 0.25, with value). Signals from longer-tenor options lose 30-40 bp p.a. Costs are not stated (appears gross).
candidates.replication: Single-author working paper (SSRN 4040261), not replicated. Li-Sarno-Zinna's related skew-premium sort is insignificant in G10 alone, which warns that this may also shrink to nothing in Mandel's 6-8 pairs.

sources.title: Implied Skewness and the Cross Section of Foreign Exchange Returns (Torok, SSRN 4040261)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: CVOL pairs (6-8) plus USD. At month-end, implied skewness proxy_i = log(CVOL SkewRatio_i), oriented to foreign-currency downside. Rate from fx-rates-3m with a one-month lag. Weights proportional to rank(rate) - rank(skew per foreign-currency crash pricing) per Torok's formula 7, normalised to $1 long and $1 short. Filled at the first noon fix of t+1 and held 1 month. Costs: 2 bp per leg per rebalance plus 1%/yr financing per leg (T-368 convention). Window: CVOL history. Statistics: net Sharpe (stationary bootstrap), monthly skewness, correlation with T-368. Pass: Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, skewness > 0, alpha versus T-368 carry > 0. DSR counts T-368/T-431. Report 2018-2022 (overlap with the paper) and 2022-09 onward (true out-of-sample) separately.

candidates.name: Currency skewness risk premium from semivariances; upside/downside VRP sorts (Li-Sarno-Zinna JFQA 2025)
candidates.summary: SRP = expected physical skewness minus risk-neutral skewness, where both are measured by the asymmetry of upside and downside semivariances. Sort currencies on SRP: long high-SRP, short low-SRP. CME CVOL publishes exactly the risk-neutral pieces (UpVar from OTM calls, DnVar from OTM puts), so a close replication is feasible. The same paper's upside VRP (VRPU) and asymmetric VRP (VRPUD) sorts rank second and third.
candidates.mechanism: Investors pay to insure against large foreign-currency depreciations (dollar safe-haven demand), so risk-neutral skew is more negative than physical skew. Currencies with a high skewness premium are the ones whose crash insurance is most expensive relative to realised asymmetry, and they earn higher returns, mostly through interest differentials. The authors find that SRP prices a broad cross-section of currency strategies, not just carry.
adjacent_variables: intraday FX returns for realised semivariance
candidates.assets: FX vs USD (paper: 28 currencies; Mandel: 6-8 G10 via CME futures / OANDA)
candidates.claimed_effect: 1998-02 to 2021-12 monthly, 28 currencies, OTC options. SRP HML earns 5.47% p.a. (t 3.31), Sharpe 0.75 (0.82 de-noised); the long leg contributes 4.85%. It is driven mainly by interest differentials and is left-skewed (large drops in the GFC and COVID). VRPU and VRPUD sorts reach Sharpe 0.52 and 0.47, carry 0.72. RR, VRP and long-term momentum are not significant in this sample. G10-only SRP is 2.31% p.a. and NOT significant; EM-only is 6.42% (t 3.26). I did not find a transaction-cost treatment in the text I searched.
candidates.replication: New (2025); not replicated. Sample ends 2021-12, so 2022-2026 is out of sample. The paper itself documents the decay of the earlier DRS VRP sort. The weak G10-only result is the binding problem for Mandel's universe.

sources.title: Skewness Risk Premia and the Cross Section of Currency Returns (Li, Sarno, Zinna; JFQA, open access)
CME Group Volatility Indexes - CVOL (UpVar, DnVar, Skew, ATM, Convexity definitions)

candidates.proposed_test: Risk-neutral side: CVOL UpVar_i and DnVar_i (30-day) at month-end. Physical side: realised up/down semivariances from fx-spot-g10 daily returns, or Mandel's 60-minute bars for 2024-2026 as a robustness check. Forecast with the paper's ARX(1) (footnote 21: random walk for the first 12 months, then an expanding window including the implied semivariance). SRP_i is built with the paper's exact normalisation, fixed from the paper before any run. Sort: long the top 2, short the bottom 2 (and a rank-weighted version), filled at the next noon fix and held 1 month. Costs: 2 bp per leg plus financing (T-368). Primary trial: SRP. Secondary: VRPU and VRPUD, with Holm across the three. Statistics: net Sharpe with bootstrap, and alpha versus T-368 carry and DOL (required, since the paper says SRP rides rate differentials). Expect weak results in G10, so register the expected-null bar honestly: pass needs Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0 and alpha t > 2.

candidates.name: Global FX volatility innovations as a carry-timing and hedging signal (Menkhoff-Sarno-Schmeling-Schrimpf 2012; Bakshi-Panayotov 2013)
candidates.summary: High-interest currencies lose when global FX volatility rises unexpectedly, and that single factor explains most of the carry cross-section. Changes in currency volatility (with commodity returns and liquidity) also forecast carry payoffs out of sample. Time the registered carry books by the latest global FX vol innovation. The realised version is testable today; the implied version uses CVOL FXVL/EVZ.
candidates.mechanism: Carry is short global volatility. Funding-constrained speculators unwind when vol jumps, and low-rate funding currencies hedge those states. If vol shocks are persistent, cutting exposure after a positive innovation avoids part of the drawdown cluster. Bekaert-Panayotov caution that this mainly predicts 'bad carry' trades.
candidates.assets: G10 (+MXN, ZAR) carry books via CME FX futures / OANDA
candidates.claimed_effect: MSSS (JF 2012): high-rate currencies co-move negatively with global FX vol innovations, and the vol proxy captures more than 90% of the cross-sectional variation in five carry portfolios (search abstract; the sample, about 1983-2009, is from memory). Cenedese-Sarno-Tsiakas (JBF 2014): higher market variance predicts large carry losses in quantile regressions. Bakshi-Panayotov (JFE 2013): changes in a commodity index, currency volatility and (less) liquidity predict carry payoffs in-sample and out-of-sample up to 6 months, and a decision rule improves Sharpe and skewness.
candidates.replication: Bekaert-Panayotov find the predictors forecast bad, not good, carry trades. PARTIAL DUPLICATE: T-368 already tried a VIX > 30 flat filter chosen on 2002-2012 (test Sharpe -0.30), and T-682 (untested) covers vol-targeting with FX pairs as a non-risk unit. Keep only because the signal is FX-specific vol innovations, not equity VIX level, and carries an out-of-sample-rule claim.

candidates.proposed_test: TESTABLE NOW. GV_t = mean over 9 G10 pairs of the absolute daily log change averaged within month t (the MSSS construction) from fx-spot-g10. Innovation u_t = AR(1) residual, estimated on an expanding window from 1999. Rule: hold the frozen T-368 (and T-431) book at weight 1 when u_t <= its trailing 80th percentile and at 0 otherwise, switching at the next noon fix. Second trial (Bakshi-Panayotov): out-of-sample regression of the next-month carry return on delta-GV and the DBC monthly return (daily-history-DBC), expanding from 2005, trading carry with weight sign(forecast). Window: out-of-sample 2013-01 to 2026-09. Costs: T-368's plus 2 bp per leg per switch. Statistics: Clark-West out-of-sample R2, net Sharpe difference versus the untimed book with stationary bootstrap, and MDD change. Pass: CW p < 0.05 and a Sharpe gain > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05. DSR counts T-368's VIX filter and T-682.

candidates.name: Kalshi EUR/USD event contracts vs CME-options-implied digital probabilities (reference-price test)
candidates.summary: Kalshi self-certified a 'Will EUR/USD be above/below/between X at time T' contract family (rulebook FXEURUSD) on 2026-07-16. Robinhood also lists FX event contracts settling on the ECB reference rate. A deep, liquid CME EUR options market prices nearly the same digital. Test whether the thin event-contract book deviates from the options-implied probability by more than fees, using Mandel's reference-price framework.
candidates.mechanism: Mandel's learnings say the edges that exist are reference-price edges in which a deep market prices the identical event against a thin crowd (the FOMC buckets vs fed-funds futures). CME FX options are deep; a newly listed Kalshi FX ladder is thin. The prior is negative, though. Mandel already found Kalshi's BTC/ETH hourly ladders and S&P/Nasdaq hourly ladders are not slow to their underlyings (book Brier beats a lognormal model by t about 8), and Polymarket BTC digitals vs Deribit (T-337) were not_supported. So the bar is whether FX is an exception.
variables: calendars (time of day, ECB fixing time)
adjacent_variables: Kalshi FX order book and trades
candidates.assets: Kalshi FX event contracts (US-legal DCM), with CME 6E futures/options as the reference
candidates.claimed_effect: No published evidence. Contract terms per the CFTC filing: $1 notional, $0.01 tick, prices bounded 0.01-0.99, listed on a custom basis. An older Kalshi EUR/USD rulebook used the ICE EUR/USD price at a specified time (search snippet). A Robinhood example (2026-03-30) showed 'Over' strikes 1.14 to 1.16 settling on the ECB rate, last trade 7:10 CT.
candidates.replication: None; untested venue. Analogous Kalshi and Polymarket underlying-ladder studies in Mandel's record are non-members (EDGE_VERDICT 21d, Result 22, T-337), so expect a null.

sources.title: KalshiEX LLC CFTC 40.2(a) notification: Will EUR/USD be above/below/exactly/at least/between value (FXEURUSD)

candidates.proposed_test: FORWARD RECORD (capture box). Every 15 minutes, record each live Kalshi FXEURUSD market's best bid/ask, size and strike. Reference probability at the same timestamp: a call-spread digital from captured CME 6E option mids bracketing the strike (preferred), or Black-76 on the front 6E future with CVOL EUVL ATM plus a skew adjustment. Correct for the settlement source and time (ICE or ECB vs CME futures) and the futures-spot basis. Pre-registered after at least 300 settled strike-expiries: (a) Brier of the Kalshi mid vs the options digital against settlement outcomes, paired per event with event-clustered t; (b) a taker trade toward the options digital when |gap| > Kalshi fee + half-spread. The Kalshi fee schedule is quoted from memory as a taker fee of 0.07 x P x (1-P) per contract; re-verify. Report mean net P&L per contract with event-clustered CI. Pass: (b) mean > 0 with t >= 2, both halves positive, and no single day > 25% of P&L. Otherwise record as a non-member. Paper-only until the pre-live gate.

candidates.name: CFTC positioning in CME FX futures (leveraged funds / speculators) as crash and reversal signal, interacted with option skew
candidates.summary: Speculators' net long futures positions in investment currencies come before crashes. Commercial hedgers sell expensive-to-insure currencies while speculators take the other side. Use weekly CFTC Traders-in-Financial-Futures positioning for the eight CME FX contracts as an adjacent (non-price) input, alone and together with CVOL skew, to cut crowded long-carry legs.
candidates.mechanism: Crowded speculative carry positions unwind together when funding tightens, and the unwind amplifies losses (BNP). Positioning is the stock of potential unwind, skew is its price, and together they flag fragile currencies. DRS use the same data to show hedger/speculator transfer of volatility risk.

options open interest on CME FX options
candidates.assets: CME FX futures (6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S, 6N, 6M)
candidates.claimed_effect: BNP (1986-2006, CFTC data for CAD, JPY, CHF, GBP, EUR from 1986): high rate differentials predict positive speculator positions and negative skewness. Carry losses lead to lower speculator positions, higher risk-reversal prices and lower future crash risk. VIX increases coincide with unwinds. DRS (1998-2013): CFTC data show commercial traders sell the currencies that are more expensive to insure. No trading-rule Sharpe is reported for positioning alone.
candidates.replication: Not tested by Mandel for FX; FX COT is not archived (only gold, silver and BTC). DUPLICATE-ADJACENT to T-606 (blocked: cross-asset COT speculative pressure across about 25 futures including currencies). Keep only as the FX-specific crash-filter variant with the skew interaction.

candidates.proposed_test: Fetch the CFTC TFF futures-only reports (Socrata) for the eight CME FX contracts (TFF from 2006-06; legacy from 1986 for the majors). Signal: leveraged-fund net / open interest, z-scored over the trailing 156 reports. Available at the Friday 15:30 ET release (positions as of Tuesday), traded at the Monday open of the 6x future. Trial 1: the next-4-week return of currency i vs USD for z > +2 vs all other weeks, with a date permutation (10,000 draws) and the 13-week realised skewness as a secondary. Trial 2 (overlay): drop T-368 long-leg currencies with z > +1.5 and CVOL skew in their bottom tercile. Thresholds fixed on 2006-2012, out of sample 2013-2026. Costs: 1 bp per side plus roll. Pass: a negative mean 4-week difference with permutation p < 0.05 in both out-of-sample halves for Trial 1, and an MDD reduction of at least 30% at a Sharpe cost of at most 0.1 for Trial 2. Count with T-606.

candidates.name: Equity option-implied tail-risk beta sort of currencies (Fan-Londono-Xiao JFE 2022)
candidates.summary: A US equity tail-risk factor built from out-of-the-money S&P 500 put prices is priced in currency returns. Currencies that hedge equity tail risk (gain when tail risk rises) earn less, and currencies exposed to it earn more. A long-high-tail-beta / short-low-tail-beta portfolio captures a global factor that explains part of carry and momentum. The input is an options variable Mandel archives (Cboe SKEW and VIX as proxies).
candidates.mechanism: Investors pay for currencies that hedge equity crashes (JPY, CHF, USD), giving them low expected returns. Currencies that crash with equities must offer a premium. The paper finds the estimated price of the global tail factor is consistently negative across carry, momentum and other asset portfolios, consistent with a common crash-risk premium.
adjacent_variables: SPX OTM put-implied tail measures (Bollerslev-Todorov style)
candidates.assets: G10 + MXN + ZAR vs USD via CME FX futures / OANDA
candidates.claimed_effect: Published JFE 143(1) 2022, earlier Fed IFDP 1253 (2019). The tail factor from OTM S&P 500 puts explains cross-sectional currency excess returns, and a high-minus-low equity-tail-beta currency portfolio extracts its global component. I did not open the full text, so no return or Sharpe figure is quoted and the sample period is unverified.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Likely heavy overlap with carry (high-rate currencies tend to have high tail beta), and carry has failed in Mandel's 2013-2026 tests, so alpha versus carry is the real question.

sources.title: Equity tail risk and currency risk premiums (Fan, Londono, Xiao; JFE 2022, accepted manuscript)
US Equity Tail Risk and Currency Risk Premia (Fed IFDP 1253)

candidates.proposed_test: TESTABLE NOW with proxies (archived cboe-SKEW and VIX history, fx-spot-g10 incl. MXN/ZAR, fx-rates-3m). Tail innovation dT_t = monthly change in SKEW (proxy 1) and in VIX (proxy 2), each pre-registered (Holm over 2). At each month-end, beta_i = the 60-month rolling slope of currency i's excess return (spot + lagged rate differential) on dT. Positive beta means the currency rises with tail risk (a hedge). Hold long the 3 lowest-beta currencies and short the 3 highest, equal weight, filled at the next noon fix and held 1 month. Costs: 2 bp per leg plus 1%/yr financing (T-368). Window: out-of-sample 2013-01 to 2026-09 (betas from 2008). Statistics: net Sharpe with stationary bootstrap, and alpha versus T-368 carry and DOL with HAC t. Pass: Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, alpha t > 2. Note that SKEW is a weak stand-in for the paper's put-based tail measure, so a fail on the proxy does not refute the paper.

registration.claim: Universe: EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD, CHF vs USD, monthly over the CVOL history (about 2018-01..2026-09). At the last business day of month t, compute VRP_i = trailing-252-session realised vol from noon fixes minus 30-day CVOL ATM_i, in vol points (DRS sign). Go long the 2 highest-VRP (cheap-insurance) currencies and short the 2 lowest, equal weight, filled at the first noon fix of t+1 and held 1 month. After 2 bp per leg per rebalance plus 1%/yr financing per leg, the book earns an annualised net Sharpe above 0.3.
registration.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe of the monthly long-short return (spot change plus lagged OECD 3m differential) with a stationary-bootstrap 95% interval (block 12, 5,000 draws). Reported: spot-only Sharpe, correlation with T-368, and the inverse sort.
registration.procedure: CVOL month-end close, taken at its CME publication time (after the 14:00 CT settlement). RV is annualised from the 252 noon-fix log returns ending at fix t (available 21:00 UTC t). Fill is at fix t+1. Rates use month t-1 OECD averages (T-368 convention). The tenor mismatch with DRS's 1-year IV is disclosed. A 1-year analogue is reported if DataMine provides one. The stale EUR/GBP rate splice is flagged, as in T-368. Halves are split at the sample midpoint.
registration.data: new cme-cvol-<ccy> (DataMine, paid) or forward capture; fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m; fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Net Sharpe > 0.3 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, both halves positive, and DSR > 0.95 counting T-368 (6), T-431 (4), T-478 (16) and T-605 (2) in the family.
registration.controls: Static-ranking placebo (full-sample-mean VRP ranks, the DRS check that the content is time variation, not rate differentials). Inverse sort reported (Li-Sarno-Zinna suggest a sign flip). Correlation with T-368 carry. One sort (top 2 / bottom 2), no grid. Costs and financing as in T-368.

rows.notes: Blocked on paid CVOL history. Even with it, about 100 months gives little power: a true Sharpe of 0.5 passes rarely. Out-of-sample decay is documented by the paper's own successors, and every G10 cross-sectional book Mandel tested has failed. Fund the data only if the EUR-only VRP existence test (eur-vrp-evz-vs-realised) passes. Hold as blocked (data).

rows.name: Per-currency time-series VRP z-score (implied minus short-window realised vol) for 6-8 pairs

overlaps.note: Same design (VRP predicts the underlying's next-week return) on BTC with DVOL.
SPX VRP predicts the equity premium out of sample. Same signal class, different asset.
SPX VRP predicts SPY 3-month return post-2010.
The IV-minus-RV z-score did not improve SPX short-variance timing (p 0.29, PBO 0.34).
On SPX, VIX-RV21 terciles separate short-straddle P&L in sample, but only 8 of 21 offsets pass.
FX direction rules on noon fixes (momentum) failed.

learnings.finding: For the FX class, own_iv_rv is not IC-discovered at 1d/5d/20d (t -0.05/-0.25/+0.28). In mandel/ml/implied.py FX symbols map own_iv to VIX, not EUR implied vol, so this is VIX vs the FX pair's RV and does not test the EUR-specific gap.
There are 12 FX swing cells with options-implied features at 1/5/20-day horizons. None pass dev; the best DSR is 0.019.
Liquid markets are calibrated, and in-house signal models usually lose to the price. EUR/USD is the deepest market there is.
Out-of-sample gains are significant only for EM/LatAm, and for G10 only at a 4-year estimation window. The sign flips with the RV window (Londono-Zhou, DRS).

data: local ML daily bars 6E_F / EURUSD_X (10 years) for a same-time check
rows.missing_data: EVZ is not archived. One free fetch is needed: FRED EVZCLS (Cboe EuroCurrency ETF Volatility Index, 2007-11-01..2025-03-11, discontinued). Cboe's EVZ_History.csv may also still be served. For the other pairs, per-currency 30-day IV (CME CVOL) is paid (DataMine) or forward-capture only, so the JPY/CHF and multi-pair extension is blocked.

registration.claim: Over out-of-sample Wednesdays 2015-01-07..2025-03-05, the sign is pre-registered positive from Ornelas (2017). Let z_t be the trailing-252-session z-score of gap_t = EVZ_t - RV_t, where RV_t is the annualised EWMA vol (11-day half-life) of DEXUSEU noon-fix log returns through fix t; z_t is known at the EVZ close at 21:30 UTC on Wednesday t. The rule holds EUR long vs USD from the noon fix of t+1 for 5 sessions when z_t > +0.5 and short when z_t < -0.5. After 1 bp per side plus the quarterly 6E roll, it earns a positive mean net return per trade with Newey-West t >= 2.
registration.statistic: Mean net log return per active week (position x EUR return fix t+1 -> fix t+6, plus the lagged EZ-minus-US 3m differential accrued daily), with Newey-West t (lag 4). Clark-West t of the signed-z forecast vs a zero forecast. Percentile against a z-date permutation (10,000 draws). Secondary horizon: 21-session hold on the first Wednesday of each month (non-overlapping), with Holm over the two horizons.
registration.null: Mean net return per active week <= 0.
registration.procedure: The EVZ close enters at 21:30 UTC on day t. RV uses noon fixes through fix t (available 21:00 UTC t), so both inputs are known before the fill at noon t+1. Weeks are dropped when EVZ is stale (unchanged for 3 or more sessions) or when the fix is missing. 2007-11..2014-12 is z warm-up and in-sample report only; the sign is not refitted. Out-of-sample halves are 2015-01..2019-12 and 2020-01..2025-03. Weeks containing an ECB or FOMC decision or a US CPI release are reported separately (not excluded). The archived 6E_F daily settlements (2016-2025) serve as a same-time fill check.
registration.data: new fred-EVZCLS; fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m; fomc-meetings; macro-release-cpi; local 6E_F daily bars
registration.pass: All of: out-of-sample mean net > 0 with Newey-West t >= 2 (Holm-adjusted over the 2 horizons); Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05; both out-of-sample halves positive; above the 95th percentile of the z-date permutation.
registration.controls: Always-long-EUR baseline. EVZ level alone and RV alone as signals (the gap must beat both). Placebo with the US equity gap (VIX - SPY RV) in place of the EUR gap. One threshold (|z| > 0.5), no grid. Costs of 1 bp per side plus roll charged. JPY/CHF negative signs are pre-noted for a later CVOL extension but are not part of this trial.

rows.notes: Testable after one free fetch (EVZCLS). A single-currency, single-sign test with about 530 out-of-sample weeks is the cleanest form of the claim. Evidence is weakest in exactly the G10 majors, and EUR/USD is maximally liquid. Running eur-vrp-evz-vs-realised first is cheap, because it uses the same fetch and its RV leg can be shared. EVZ is built from thin FXE options, so stale-print handling matters.

rows.name: Global currency volatility (level) and world currency VRP timing the dollar basket at 3-6 months

overlaps.note: Same DOL target and timing frame, with the AFD as the signal. It must be a control and is in the DSR family.
Uses G10 FX realised vol (vol targeting with FX as a non-risk unit). Same variable, different claim.
Its train-chosen VIX > 30 filter (a risk-level timing rule) was part of a failed book.
DOL basket month-end effect: +3.8 bp, p 0.20. Shows DOL rules are hard to pass.

learnings.finding: For the FX class, the VIX level (iv_vix = own_iv) has positive IC at 1d/5d/20d (5d disc +0.054 t 6.0, confirmed +0.063). It is pooled over mixed quote conventions (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD vs USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF, DXY), so its direction for DOL is not identified.
FX swing models with implied features: 12 cells, 0 pass dev.
With 3-6 month overlapping targets and about 160 out-of-sample months there are only about 40 independent observations. A positive out-of-sample R^2 at p < 0.05 needs a large true effect.
Structural premia (risk compensation) are the surviving class. Countercyclical currency risk premia after vol spikes are a premium story, not a forecast of the price.

rows.missing_data: Realised version: nothing missing. Implied/VRP version: a G10 implied-vol index (CME CVOL FXVL/G5) is paid (DataMine); FRED EVZCLS (free, EUR only, to 2025-03) is a one-currency proxy and should be reported only.

registration.claim: At each month-end t from 2013-01 to 2026-06, let GV_t be the equal-weight mean of the nine G10 currencies' annualised 21-session realised vols from FRED noon fixes through t. GV_t positively predicts the DOL basket's next-3-month excess return: the mean log spot change of the 9 currencies vs USD from the first noon fix after t, plus one-month-lagged AFD/12 per month. Expanding OLS fitted from 2002-06 gives a positive Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05. The long/short-DOL rule on the forecast's sign also earns a positive net Sharpe after 2 bp per leg per switch plus 1 bp/month roll.
registration.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 against the expanding historical mean, with the Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (Newey-West lag 3 for the overlap) at the 3-month horizon. Secondary: the rule's net Sharpe with a stationary bootstrap (block 12) and the Hodrick (1992) slope t over the out-of-sample window. Reported only: the 6-month horizon and an EVZ-based implied variant (2007-11..2025-03).
registration.procedure: RV_i = sqrt(252 x mean squared daily log noon-fix change over the 21 sessions ending at month-end t). Fixes enter at their 21:00 UTC available_at, and the signal is formed after the last fix of month t. The target starts at the first business day's noon fix of t+1 and ends 3 months later (overlapping monthly observations). AFD = mean foreign IR3TIB minus US IR3TIB, using month t-1 averages. Forecasts are expanding OLS from 2002-06 (127 training months), with the first forecast for 2013-01 (162 forecasts). The positive level sign is pre-registered (Li-Qiao-Wang); no sign fitting. Only months where all 9 currencies print are used. The stale EUR/GBP rate splice is flagged.
registration.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Out-of-sample R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 at 3 months, AND rule net Sharpe > 0 with both halves (2013-2019, 2020-2026) positive, AND DSR >= 0.95 counting T-605's 2 trials and this one.
registration.controls: AFD alone (the T-605 signal) and the VIX level alone as competing predictors. An encompassing regression in which the GV coefficient must stay positive. Always-long and always-short DOL baselines. A 12-month-shifted placebo. 2020-03 and the 2022 dollar spike reported excluded. Costs as stated. One horizon judged.

rows.notes: Testable now in its realised form, and cheap: the inputs are those of T-605, T-575 and T-682. The low prior comes from the low independent-observation count and from the failed DOL/FX rules. The world-VRP half of the claim (sign negative) needs per-currency implied vols and stays blocked; do not proxy it with EVZ for a verdict.

rows.name: US equity variance risk premium (VIX^2 minus realised SPX variance) predicts foreign-currency appreciation vs USD at 1 month

overlaps.note: Identical VP construction ((VIX/100)^2/12 minus 21-session ^GSPC squared returns, month-end) predicting the equity premium out of sample. Share the code.
Same VP, SPY 3-month target, post-2010 (Dew-Becker-Giglio predict a fail).
The SPX premium exists (positive on 84% of days).
SPX short variance has a positive mean.
VIX > 30 'cut carry' filter, the opposite direction to BNP, inside a failed book. Not informative about the sign here.
Same DOL target. Use the AFD as a control.

learnings.finding: The US equity VRP feature (vrp_spx) on the FX class is not discovered at any horizon: disc IC +0.0055 t 0.95 (1d), +0.010 t 1.08 (5d), +0.0035 t 0.33 (20d), with negative confirm-window ICs at 5d/20d. It is pooled over mixed quote conventions, so a DOL-direction effect could cancel; weak evidence against.
The candidate's cited 'fx 5d own_iv IC +0.054' is the VIX LEVEL (FX symbols map own_iv to VIX), not the VRP, and is also convention-mixed. It is not support for this claim.
Most published anomalies decay after publication. Londono-Zhou's sample ends 2011, and no post-2011 replication is known.
The input is non-price and a priced risk premium (Mandel's surviving class); the target is the most liquid market there is.

rows.missing_data: Nothing for the primary trial.

registration.claim: The window is month-end decisions 2012-01..2026-08, after Londono-Zhou's 2000-2011 sample. VP_t = (VIX close_t/100)^2/12 minus the sum of squared ^GSPC daily log returns over the 21 sessions ending at the month's last NYSE session t. VP_t positively predicts the next-month excess return of the equal-weight 9-currency G10 basket against USD: spot from the first noon fix after the VIX close to the first noon fix after the next month's last session, plus one-month-lagged AFD/12. The post-sample slope is positive with Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05. The expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 (fit from 2002-06) is positive with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05.
registration.statistic: Slope of the next-month DOL excess return on standardised VP_t over the 2012-01..2026-08 decisions (Newey-West, lag 2). Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with the Clark-West t. Reported: the 3-month horizon (Hodrick SEs); the per-currency panel with currency fixed effects and JPY/CHF separately; a trading arm (long DOL when VP is above its trailing 60-month median, else short; plus a flat-instead-of-short variant), net of 2 bp per leg per switch plus 1 bp/month roll, with stationary-bootstrap Sharpe.
registration.procedure: The VIX close enters at 21:30 UTC on the last NYSE session of month t; RV comes from ^GSPC closes through t. The fill is at the next business day's noon fix, which is after the VIX close. VP code is shared with T-649/T-685 so the signal is identical. No winsorising. 2020-03..2020-06 is reported excluded. Only months where all 9 currencies print are used. The stale EUR/GBP rate splice is flagged. Halves are 2012-2018 and 2019-2026.
registration.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: All of: post-sample slope > 0 with Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05; Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05; slope positive in both halves; DSR >= 0.95 counting the 1- and 3-month horizons.
registration.controls: VIX^2 alone and RV alone as competing predictors (VP must beat both). A multiple regression with AFD (T-605), last-month DOL return and the VIX level, in which the VP coefficient must stay positive. A 12-month-shifted placebo and a shuffled-month placebo. Costs charged on the trading arm. No threshold beyond the pre-stated 60-month median in the reported rule.

rows.notes: Testable now on archived data with code shared with T-649/T-685, so marginal cost is near zero. It also gives the FX ML family a clean single-direction read: the ML rows are convention-mixed. The prior is low because the ML scan shows no VRP IC for FX and the effect is unreplicated after 2011. The mechanism is a risk premium rather than a price pattern, which is why it ranks above the other FX timing ideas.

rows.name: FX volatility carry: sort forward volatility agreements on implied-vol term-structure slope (Della Corte-Kozhan-Neuberger 2021)

overlaps.note: SPX forward variance (VIX/VIX3M, days 21-63) exceeds realised by +6.2 vol points. A forward-vol premium exists in equities.
SPX forward premium minus spot premium is +0.010 pooled, but only 24 of 63 grid starts pass. The term-premium trade was not implemented.
The SPX VIX/VIX3M term-structure regime did not separate the VRP within VIX terciles.
SPY double calendar: the calendar structure did not deliver its claimed P&L property.
SPY skew term structure needs captured chains: the same data block.

learnings.finding: Forward implied variance is upward-biased in SPX, so the DKN mechanism (forward vol over-predicts) has a Mandel analogue.

Flat-index pricing overstated ATM option value (ATM IV/VIX measured 0.80). The delta-hedged short straddle at 0.81 x VIX was not supported even though the SPX VRP is. Option-form trades fail where index-form premia pass.
Costs decide: DKN's Sharpe of 1.32 falls to 0.83 at quoted OTC FVA spreads, and CME calendar spreads outside 6E/6J are thinner than OTC.

rows.missing_data: Per-expiry FX option IVs (1- and 3-month) for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S are missing. CME FX option settlement history is paid (DataMine). CME publishes daily settlements free on its site, but only for the current day, so forward capture would have to start now. CVOL is a single 30-day tenor and cannot form a slope. FXE/FXY chains could be added to the capture box (free, Cboe delayed) but cover two currencies and are thin.

registration.claim: Monthly, from the start of a per-expiry CME FX option settlement record for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S, the strategy buys forward volatility on the 2 currencies with the lowest scaled IV term slope (IV3m - IV1m)/IV1m and sells it on the 2 highest. Long forward volatility means a vega-matched calendar: long the 3-month ATM straddle, short the 1-month. Positions are unwound at the 1-month expiry, with the remaining leg marked at its settlement IV. After half the captured bid-ask per leg (or 0.3 vol points per leg if only settlements exist), mean P&L per unit of forward vega is positive.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly P&L per unit of forward vega with HAC t, a sign test, and correlation with the T-368 carry return.
registration.null: Mean P&L per unit forward vega <= 0.
registration.procedure: ATM IV per expiry is obtained by inverting Black-76 on the settlement price with the matching futures settlement, then interpolated in total variance to 30 and 91 days. The sort runs on the first business day using the prior day's settlements; fills are at settlements plus the cost. Hold to the front expiry. Assumed costs are replaced by measured CME quotes before any verdict. No thresholds.
registration.data: new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy> (DataMine or forward capture), CME FX futures settlements, fx-rates-3m, fx-spot-g10
registration.pass: HAC t > 2 over at least 36 monthly formations, both halves positive.
registration.controls: An unconditional long-forward-vol book on all 6 currencies, separating the term premium from the slope sort. A static-slope placebo (full-sample mean slope ranks). Correlation with T-368 reported. Measured spreads, not assumed ones, for the verdict.

rows.notes: Blocked (data). This is a vol-payoff claim, not a spot claim, and is executable only through CME calendar straddles with uncertain liquidity outside EUR and JPY. Register as blocked with a forward-capture start date if the capture box adds CME FX settlements. 36 months is the earliest read.

rows.name: Implied-vol term slope predicts G10 spot returns (Ornelas-Mauad 2019): long low-slope, short high-slope currencies

overlaps.note: SPX term-structure regime carried no VRP information within VIX terciles.
The alpha-versus-carry control book has itself failed 2013-2026.
A failed G10 cross-sectional spot sort; same deflation family.

learnings.finding: For FX, iv_term (the VIX term structure, not FX) has a positive IC at 1d (confirmed) and 5d/20d (discovered, not confirmed). It says nothing about currency-specific slopes.
The developed-market sign is opposite to the DKN working paper's. A contested sign that is untested after 2016 has a weak prior.
G10 cross-sectional spot books fail after costs in 2013-2026.

rows.missing_data: Multi-tenor ATM IV per currency (1-6 months) is missing. CME FX option settlement history is paid (DataMine, about 2018 onward); OTC 10-tenor vols (the paper's input) come from Bloomberg/JPM (paid). The free route is forward capture only: FXE/FXY chains (2 currencies) or CME daily settlements.

registration.claim: At each month-end from the start of a multi-tenor ATM IV record for the 6 CME-optionable G10 currencies, the book goes long the 2 lowest and short the 2 highest currencies by the cross-sectionally standardised OLS slope of ATM IV on log(tenor) across listed expiries from 1 to 6 months. The G10 sign is negative, pre-registered from Ornelas-Mauad. The book is held 1 month in 6x futures. After 1 bp per side plus roll, it earns a net Sharpe (spot plus carry) above 0.3.
registration.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe of spot plus carry with a stationary bootstrap (block 12); spot-only Sharpe reported; alpha vs the T-368 carry and DOL baskets with HAC t. Holm across 1- and 3-month holds.
registration.procedure: Expiries come from CME settlements at month-end (Black-76 inversion), with at least 3 expiries required in 1-6 months. Fills are at the first noon fix (or 6x settlement) of t+1. If DataMine history (about 2018) is bought, run as a historical trial immediately; otherwise accrue forward. No sign fitting.
registration.data: new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy>, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m
registration.pass: Net Sharpe > 0.3, bootstrap lower bound > 0, both halves positive, alpha t > 2 vs T-368 carry and DOL (Holm over 2 holds), and DSR counting the FX cross-sectional family (T-368, T-431, T-478).
registration.controls: Static-slope placebo; carry and DOL as alpha controls; the right-tail (10-delta call) slope reported only; costs charged.

rows.notes: Blocked on multi-tenor IV. The sign is contested, the reported G10 Sharpe is only 0.33 before costs, and there is no post-2016 evidence. Not worth buying data for. Keep it as a free add-on if forward FX option settlements are ever captured for another reason (for example the FJM or DKN rows).

rows.name: Low-IV vs high-IV currency straddles: buy straddles where implied vol is low, sell where it is high (Fullwood-James-Marsh 2021)

overlaps.note: Bought SPY straddles lose on average; consistent with high-IV options being rich, but on equities.
Model-pricing at the index vol overstated ATM by about 20%, so model-priced straddle results are not verdicts.
The hedged short ATM straddle at measured ATM/VIX 0.80 failed even though the SPX VRP is supported. The short-high-IV leg is the one at risk.
Long straddles gamma-scalped at entry vol lose per unit of vega on SPY.
The BTC delta-hedged short straddle (model-priced at DVOL) passes. Short vol can survive pricing where the premium is large.

learnings.finding: A model-priced short-straddle edge vanished at realistic ATM pricing on SPX (+0.06%/month at 0.81 x VIX, p 0.36).
The BTC vol premium is real (+5.3 vol points per trade, t 2.8), but its small-account form had a -88% month. Short-vol tails dominate small books.
Structural premia such as the VRP are where edges survive. Selling the expensive-to-insure leg is a premium claim, not a forecast.

rows.missing_data: Weekly 1-month ATM IV per currency (CME CVOL ATM per pair) is paid (DataMine) or forward capture only. For the confirming step, CME FX option settlements or quotes are paid or forward only. FRED EVZCLS (free) covers EUR only and cannot rank currencies.

registration.claim: Each Wednesday over a per-currency 1-month ATM IV record (CVOL ATM or captured CME settlements) for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S, the strategy buys a 1-month ATM-forward straddle on the lowest-IV currency and sells one on the highest-IV currency, both held to expiry. After 0.25 vol points per leg per side, it earns a positive mean net return per unit notional. A demeaned variant (IV_i minus its own trailing 1-year mean) must also be positive.
registration.statistic: Mean net P&L per unit notional and per unit premium with HAC t (overlapping 4-5 week holds); Sharpe; 5% CVaR of the short leg; the tercile version (2 vs 2 of 6) reported.
registration.null: Mean net P&L per unit notional <= 0.
registration.procedure: MODEL-PRICED first: Garman-Kohlhagen at the CVOL ATM vol with fx-rates-3m, settled at expiry on fx-spot-g10 noon fixes or 6x settlements. This first pass can be inconclusive at most (T-57 precedent). Confirmation on real CME settlements or quotes is required before any supported or not_supported verdict. The Wednesday CVOL close is the signal; fill is at Thursday settlement. The assumed 0.25 vol points per leg is replaced by measured quotes.
registration.data: new cme-cvol-atm-<ccy> (or forward capture), new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy>, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m
registration.pass: Net mean on notional > 0 with HAC t > 2, both halves positive, AND the demeaned-IV variant mean > 0 with HAC t > 1.65. The verdict requires real-settlement confirmation.
registration.controls: The demeaned variant guards against a static AUD/JPY-high, EUR/CHF-low ranking. An equal-weight short-straddle-on-all-6 baseline separates the cross-section from the level VRP. CVaR and worst-week reported. Cross-check against EVZ for EUR.

rows.notes: Blocked on per-currency IV. In a 6-pair universe the ranking is persistent, so the demeaned control is essential. The short high-IV leg carries the tail. If CME FX settlements are ever captured, this is the most direct FX option-premium test, ahead of DKN and Ornelas-Mauad.

rows.name: EUR/USD variance risk premium harvest: EVZ / CVOL implied variance exceeds subsequent realised variance (short 1-month straddles)

overlaps.note: Same design on gold (GVZ^2 vs GLD RV): +0.0062 variance, all 21 phases pass. The direct template.
BTC DVOL^2 vs realised: +0.094, 30 of 30 phases pass.
SPX VRP: 21.0 vs 18.6 vol points.
SPX short variance positive mean (skew -7.6).
Gold premium +2.35 vol points but lower CI 1.76 < 2: the existence passed, the size bar failed. A cost margin matters.
Adding GLD/USO/TLT short variance did not beat SPX alone.
The SPX option-form (hedged short straddle at realistic ATM) failed where the variance form passed. This applies to Trial 2.
The BTC model-priced hedged short straddle passed after fees.

learnings.finding: The variance premium is positive in every asset where Mandel has a model-free implied-variance index (SPX, gold, BTC). Structural premia are Mandel's surviving class.
Small premia can pass existence and still fail a cost-sized bar, so the FX test must charge the straddle round trip.

Option-form harvests model-priced at the index level overstate value (ATM/VIX 0.80). EVZ is model-free variance and sits above ATM IV by the smile convexity, so the trade form needs a separate, measured-price trial.
The BTC vol premium is real, but small-account short vol had a -88% month and needs about $25,000 of margin. Tail sizing decides deployability.

data: local ML 6E_F daily bars (2016-2026, same-time RV check)
rows.missing_data: EVZ is not archived. One free fetch is needed: FRED EVZCLS (2007-11-01..2025-03-11; Cboe ceased EVZ in 2025-03), or Cboe's EVZ_History.csv if still served. After 2025-03 a live signal needs CME CVOL EUVL (paid history; the daily value is visible on CME's site) or captured 6E/FXE option chains (not in CHAIN_SYMBOLS). The option-form Trial 2 needs measured 6E option quotes for a verdict.

registration.claim: Pooled over every daily entry 2007-11-01..2025-03-11, the 30-day EUR/USD variance premium is positive on average. It is defined as (EVZ close_t/100)^2 minus the annualised realised variance of the next 21 DEXUSEU noon-fix log returns, starting at fix t+1 (252-day annualisation). In addition, the mean of EVZ_t minus the matching realised vol has a one-sided 95% lower bound above 0.5 vol points, the assumed round trip of a 1-month 6E ATM straddle.
registration.statistic: Mean of VP_t in annualised variance units over all daily entries (house rule 10: every phase of the non-overlapping 21-session grid pooled), studentized circular block bootstrap with 42-session blocks. Secondary pass statistic: the mean vol-point gap EVZ_t - RV_t with the same bootstrap. Reported: per-phase results (21 phases); the premium as a fraction of implied variance beside VIX/SPY and GVZ/GLD on common dates.
registration.null: Mean VP_t <= 0, or the vol-point gap's one-sided lower bound <= 0.5.
registration.procedure: The EVZ close enters at 21:30 UTC on day t. RV uses the 21 log returns from noon fix t+1 to fix t+22 (fixes available 21:00 UTC), so no return before the EVZ observation is used. Entries are dropped whose 21-session window has a missing fix. EVZ stale prints (unchanged 3 or more sessions) are flagged, and the result is reported excluding them. Halves are 2007-11..2016-06 and 2016-07..2025-03. The same-time check uses 6E_F daily settlements for the RV leg over 2016-2025. Windows containing ECB, FOMC or US CPI days are reported separately. 2008-09..2009-03 and 2020-03 are reported excluded (sensitivity, not verdict). Trial 2, the MODEL-PRICED short 1-month ATM 6E straddle at s x EVZ (s in {0.90, 1.00}), delta-hedged daily, with a 0.5 vol-point round trip, unconditional and conditional on EVZ minus trailing 21-day RV above its trailing median, is reported as inconclusive-at-most until measured 6E quotes exist.

Kalshi S&P daily threshold vs SPXW vertical replication.
S&P event contract vs call-spread digital convergence.

learnings.finding: Kalshi's hourly ladders are not slow to their own underlying: BTC/ETH vs Coinbase (328 events) and S&P/Nasdaq vs the index (5,597 events). The book's Brier beats a lognormal by t about 8, and taking the model's side loses 3.6 points.

Kalshi already lists hourly EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/JPY ladders: 'the same construction against an even deeper reference. Measure them only with a new registration, and expect the same answer.' The 2026-07-16 filing is not the first FX product.
A deep option market is not enough. The Fed reference works because it prices the identical event against a thin crowd. 17,425 BTC/ETH digitals scored the same Brier as the price.
The edges that exist are reference-price edges. FX options are a deep reference, so the test is well posed, but every underlying-ladder analogue so far is a non-member.

The Trial 2 overlay base book fails.

High SKEW does not raise realised -2 sigma tail frequency.
SKEW-implied tail probabilities overstate realised tails, with no information about them.

The same 11-currency universe (G10+MXN+ZAR) failed as carry.

Carry-like currency sorts earned about zero gross in 2013-2026, so alpha vs carry is the binding question.
Crash-risk premia (structural) are a surviving class in principle, but in FX they have so far shown up only through carry, which fails.

The VIX change is the primary proxy for the S&P 500 put-implied tail factor, and positive beta means the currency hedges tail risk. The book is filled at the next noon fix and held 1 month. After 2 bp per leg plus 1%/yr financing per leg, it earns a net Sharpe above 0.3 with alpha over T-368 carry and DOL with HAC t above 2.
