rows.name: Currency VRP cross-sectional sort: buy cheap-to-insure, sell expensive-to-insure currencies (Della Corte-Ramadorai-Sarno 2016)
rows.source_notes: I opened the DRS accepted manuscript (City openaccess 13156; JFE 120(1) 2016). It confirms: monthly data 1998-01 to 2013-12; 1-year model-free volatility swap rates; VRP = trailing 1-year RV minus the swap rate (SW); long low-insurance-cost and short high-insurance-cost currencies. Developed: 4.95% p.a., Sharpe 0.61. Developed+EM: 4.16%, Sharpe 0.51. Correlation with carry -0.08/-0.06. Returns are adjusted for bid-ask costs, and the static VRP sort is reported gross. Decay is confirmed in three places. (1) Li-Sarno-Zinna (JFQA 2025, read in full), footnote 22: 'performance becomes much weaker when extending the sample to December 2021'; Sarno is a DRS co-author. (2) Babiak-Barunik (arXiv 2101.09738), Table 3: the 1-month VRP long-short earns -0.29% p.a., Sharpe -0.03, over 2005-03..2021-12; their footnote 10 says LSZ 'acknowledge ... the original VRP strategy does not work anymore' and run the opposite sort. (3) Bartram et al. (JFQA 2025, via search snippet): FX strategy profits fall after publication. I did not open Quantpedia #669 or Hutchinson et al.
rows.replication_concerns: Two independent samples show decay through 2021, one by an original co-author. The proposed test is not a DRS replication: CVOL is a single 30-day tenor. Ornelas (BCB WP 454, fn 3) measures the 1-month VRP's correlation with the 6-month and 1-year VRP at -8% and -3%, and finds that short-window VRP predicts in the OPPOSITE direction. So a hybrid of 30-day IV and 252-day RV has no sign that can be pre-registered. The whole CVOL window (about 2018 onward) falls inside the decay period. Power is also low: 6 currencies traded top-2 vs bottom-2 over about 100 months needs a true Sharpe near 0.7 to reach t = 2.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10 (11 currencies): EUR runs 1999-01-04..2026-10-09; the others start 1971 (MXN 1993, ZAR 1980). fx-rates-3m: JPY starts 2002-04 and CHF 1999-07; EUR and GBP end 2026-01 (stale splice); the rest run to 2026-08. fred-DTB3 exists. No implied-vol bundle exists for any currency: searching EVZ|cvol|EUVL returns 0 bundles. Per-currency IV is the blocking input.
rows.lookahead_risks: (1) The fx-spot-g10 bundle stamps each FRED noon fix available_at 21:00 UTC on the same day. But H.10 is published weekly, on Mondays at 16:15 ET (FRED updated Mon 2026-10-19 with observations through Fri 10-16). RV through the month-end fix is therefore not public at noon t+1, so use only fixes published by the decision. (2) OECD IR3TIB monthly averages: T-433's ALFRED check found OECD MEI prints arrive well after one month, so any rate-based rank or control (the T-368 correlation) needs vintages. The rate accrual in returns is only an approximation and is acceptable. (3) Take CVOL or settlement IVs at their CME publication time. (4) Using the noon fix as a fill is acceptable only because the decision precedes noon t+1.
rows.missing_data: A per-currency 1-year ATM IV for EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD and CHF. It can come from Bloomberg/JPM OTC (paid), or be interpolated from CME FX option settlement history on the quarterly expiries (DataMine, paid). CVOL alone (30-day) cannot replicate this claim.

final.claim: Data: a per-currency 12-month ATM implied-vol record for EUR, JPY, GBP, AUD, CAD and CHF, built from CME FX option settlements (expected about 2018-01..2026-09). Signal at the last business day of month t: VRP_i = realised vol over the trailing 252 sessions of noon fixes published by the decision, minus the 12-month ATM IV interpolated in total variance from the listed expiries. This is the DRS sign and tenor. Trade: long the 2 highest-VRP (cheap-insurance) currencies and short the 2 lowest, equal weight vs USD, entered at the first noon fix after both inputs are published, held one month. Claim: after 2 bp per leg per rebalance plus 1%/yr financing per leg, the book earns an annualised net Sharpe above 0.3.
final.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe of the monthly long-short return (spot change plus the accrued 3-month rate differential), with a stationary-bootstrap 95% interval (block 12, 5,000 draws). Reported: spot-only Sharpe, correlation with T-368, and the inverse sort.
final.procedure: IV per expiry comes from Black-76 inversion of the settlement price against the matching futures settlement, using CME's publication time. RV uses noon fixes published by H.10 at the decision (weekly Monday 16:15 ET release). The fill uses the first noon fix after that; there is no same-day fill on unpublished fixes. Rates are used for the return accrual only. The stale EUR/GBP splice after 2026-01 is flagged. Halves split at the sample midpoint. Single sort (top 2 / bottom 2), no grid.
final.data: new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy> plus cme-fx-futures-settlements-<ccy> (DataMine, paid); fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: net Sharpe > 0.3; bootstrap lower bound > 0; both halves positive; DSR > 0.95 counting T-368 (6), T-431 (4), T-478 (16), T-605 (2) and this trial.
final.controls: Static-ranking placebo: rank on full-sample mean VRP (the DRS check that the content is time variation). Inverse sort reported, not judged. Correlation with T-368 carry. Costs and financing as in T-368. A 30-day CVOL version is NOT this claim: it is a near-uncorrelated signal with a contested sign and needs its own registration.

rows.reason: Fix and hold as blocked. The source is verified, but the strategy has decayed through 2021 in two independent samples, and the proposed 30-day CVOL test measures a different, near-uncorrelated signal. The registration now requires a DRS-tenor (12-month) IV from CME settlements and point-in-time fills that respect the weekly H.10 release.

rows.name: Per-currency time-series VRP z-score (implied minus short-window realised vol) for 6-8 pairs
rows.source_notes: I read Ornelas, BCB WP 454 (Jan 2017), in full. The headline 0.28% per month (daily 1-month options, 2007-2014) and 0.16% per week (2003-2014) come from a multivariate model of the GLOBAL currency VRP (an equal-weighted average across currencies) predicting average currency returns, with PPP, lagged returns and rate differentials as controls. RV is intraday (30- and 5-minute), and the preferred VRP is the 'forward' construction: IV lagged T minus RV over the same T. Table IX (individual VRP, weekly, 2003-02..2014-12, 622 weeks): EUR is NOT significant (model-free t 0.71, ATM t 1.42, R2 0.16-0.46%); AUD, CAD and GBP are positive; JPY is significantly negative. Results are 'weaker for Europe'. Out-of-sample gains are significant only for EM/LatAm, and for the full group only at the 4-year window. Ornelas explicitly attributes the opposite signs in Londono-Zhou and DRS to the RV window. The Macrosynergy notebook returned 403 and is unverified, including its 11-day EWMA choice. Data: FRED EVZCLS is verified (fetched): 2007-11-01..2025-03-11. Cboe's notice says EVZ ceased effective 2025-01-27, and FRED's prints after that repeat for 3-5 days.
rows.replication_concerns: The source's own EUR coefficient is insignificant, so a EUR-only test expects a null. The evidence is EM-driven, with no post-2014 replication. EVZ is built from thin FXE options: 30 runs of 3 or more identical prints in 2007-2025, clustered in 2021 and 2024-25. Using daily-fix EWMA RV in place of intraday RV departs from the source. The original z threshold of 0.5 and the second horizon added a small grid; both are removed below.
rows.data_notes: Fetched FRED EVZCLS into the scratchpad: 4,360 non-missing prints, 2007-11-01..2025-03-11. The 2021 mean is 5.9 and the 2008 mean 14.0. 30 stale runs of 3 or more sessions, including 2025-02 runs of 5 after the cessation. fx-spot-g10 EUR: 1999-01-04..2026-10-09. fx-rates-3m EUR ends 2026-01 (outside this window). Local 1d bars: 6E_F and EURUSD_X from 2016-10, usable for a same-time check. fomc-meetings and macro-release-cpi exist.
rows.lookahead_risks: The registration as proposed assumed DEXUSEU fixes are available at 21:00 UTC the same day. They are not: H.10 is released weekly (Monday 16:15 ET), so RV 'through fix t' is not known at noon t+1. RV must use only fixes published by the decision, which for a Wednesday decision means through the previous Friday. Other risks: EVZ prints after 2025-01-24 are post-cessation; stale prints must be dropped; the EVZ close (about 16:15 ET) and the noon fix are not synchronous, so the fill is the next day's noon.
rows.missing_data: Needs one free fetch, FRED EVZCLS (checked to be live). Nothing exists after 2025-01 (CVOL EUVL is paid). The extension to JPY and CHF needs per-currency IV (paid or forward capture).

final.claim: Window: Wednesday decisions 2015-01-07..2025-01-22. Signal: gap_t = EVZ close_t minus RV_t. RV_t is the annualised standard deviation of the 21 most recent DEXUSEU noon-fix log returns published by H.10 before the decision, i.e. fixes through the Friday covered by the latest Monday 16:15 ET release. Rule: hold EUR long vs USD when gap_t is above its trailing-252-session mean and short otherwise, from the Thursday noon fix to the following Thursday noon fix. Claim: the rule earns a positive mean net weekly return with Newey-West t >= 2. The return is spot plus the accrued euro-area-minus-US 3-month differential, less 1 bp per side on each switch and the quarterly 6E roll. The positive sign is pre-registered from Ornelas (2017).
final.statistic: Mean net weekly log return of the signed position over non-overlapping weeks, Newey-West t (lag 4). Reported: Clark-West t of the signed gap vs a zero forecast; the 21-session hold on the first Wednesday of each month; Ornelas's forward construction (EVZ_{t-21} minus RV over the same 21 sessions).
final.procedure: EVZ (FRED EVZCLS) enters at 21:30 UTC on Wednesday t. The fill is at the Thursday noon NY price, proxied by the noon fix (6E or OANDA). Weeks with stale EVZ (unchanged for 3 or more sessions) or a missing fix are dropped and counted. Entries after 2025-01-22 are excluded because of the Cboe cessation on 2025-01-27. 2007-11..2014-12 is warm-up and in-sample report only; no sign or threshold is fitted. Halves are 2015-01..2019-12 and 2020-01..2025-01. Weeks containing an ECB or FOMC decision or a US CPI release are reported separately, not excluded. 6E_F daily bars (2016-10 onward) give a same-time fill check.
final.data: new fred-EVZCLS (free); fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m; fomc-meetings; macro-release-cpi; local 1d 6E_F
final.pass: All of: out-of-sample mean net weekly return > 0 with Newey-West t >= 2; both halves positive; above the 95th percentile of a circular-shift placebo of the signal series (1,000 shifts).
final.controls: Always-long-EUR baseline. EVZ level alone and RV alone as signals (the gap must beat both). The US equity gap (VIX minus SPY 21-day RV) as a placebo signal. One threshold (the trailing mean), no grid. Costs and roll charged. JPY/CHF negative signs are not part of this trial.

rows.reason: Fix. The design is cheap and clean, but its own source shows no significant EUR effect, and the proposed timing used noon fixes that H.10 publishes only weekly. The registration now uses only published fixes, ends EVZ at its cessation, removes the 0.5-z threshold and the second horizon, and states an expected null.

rows.name: Global currency volatility (level) and world currency VRP timing the dollar basket at 3-6 months
rows.source_notes: Londono-Zhou (IFDP 1068, July 2014 text read in full) is verified: 2000-01..2011-12, 22 currencies, 18 with ATM IV. The world XVP uses 6-month ATM IV minus trailing realised variance. A rise in world XVP predicts DEPRECIATION of foreign currencies vs USD, significant at 1% for all horizons and maximised at 4-6 months; it is significant for 18 of 22 currencies at 4 months (not JPY, HKD, MYR, PHP), and the R2 gain over the rate differential is about 8% at 4 months. The level paper is misattributed: the UIBE page and search snippet credit Qiao Fang and Wang Tianyi, not 'Li-Qiao-Wang' (J. Empirical Finance 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.jempfin.2026.101740). Its abstract confirms an equal-weight IV or RV average over 17 currencies that 'positively predicts currency returns', especially beyond 3 months, with R2 of 2.49-5.02% for IV and 2.64-7.13% for RV in sample, and higher out of sample (3.00-6.84% / 3.53-10.06%). The ScienceDirect page returned 403. The return definition (DOL basket vs another portfolio) and the sample period are NOT verified. The direction is consistent with Londono-Zhou, since higher trailing RV lowers XVP.
rows.replication_concerns: Independent author teams, but there is no test beyond about 2011 except Qiao-Wang, whose window is unknown. 3-month overlapping targets over about 160 out-of-sample months give about 53 independent observations. Mandel's DOL-type rules have failed (T-575). Qiao-Wang say global vol closely tracks the VIX, so the encompassing test against the VIX is binding. The world-VRP half needs IV and stays blocked.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10: all 9 non-USD G10 currencies present, EUR from 1999-01-04, all through 2026-10-09. fx-rates-3m: JPY from 2002-04, which bounds the AFD and the fit start at 2002-06; EUR and GBP stale after 2026-01. cboe-VIX-history runs 1990-01-02..2026-10-14. fred-DTB3 exists.
rows.lookahead_risks: GV_t was specified from fixes 'through t', with the fill at the first noon fix of t+1. H.10 publishes fixes weekly (Mon 16:15 ET), so the last few month-end fixes are not public at that fill; use only fixes published by the decision. The AFD control from OECD monthly averages needs ALFRED vintages: T-433 found OECD MEI publication lags well beyond one month. Using rates as a return accrual is acceptable. The stale EUR/GBP splice after 2026-01 affects the last 8 months.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the realised version. The implied/world-VRP version needs per-currency IV (CVOL, paid). An EVZ-only variant is a one-currency proxy and is reported only.

final.claim: Decisions: each month-end t from 2013-01 to 2026-06. Signal: GV_t = the equal-weight mean, over the 9 non-USD G10 currencies, of the annualised realised vol of the 21 most recent noon-fix log returns published by H.10 at the decision. Target: the DOL basket's excess return over the next 3 months, i.e. the mean log spot change of the 9 currencies vs USD from the first noon fix of t+1, plus the accrued average foreign-minus-US 3-month differential. Claim: GV_t positively predicts the target. Expanding OLS fitted from 2002-06 gives a positive Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05. In addition, a long/short DOL rule on the sign of the forecast excess return earns a positive net Sharpe after 2 bp per leg per switch plus 1 bp/month roll.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 against the expanding historical mean, with the Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (Newey-West lag 2 for the 3-month overlap). Secondary: the rule's net Sharpe with a stationary bootstrap (block 12). Reported only: the Hodrick (1992) slope t, the 6-month horizon, and an EVZ-based implied variant (2007-11..2025-01).
final.procedure: RV_i = sqrt(252 x mean squared daily log noon-fix change) over the 21 most recent published sessions. The target starts at the first noon fix of t+1, after the signal is public. Expanding OLS from 2002-06 gives the first forecast for 2013-01 (162 forecasts). The positive level sign is pre-registered (Qiao and Wang 2026); no sign fitting. Only months in which all 9 currencies print are used. The return accrual uses month t-1 OECD averages and is flagged as an approximation. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026. The stale EUR/GBP rates after 2026-01 are flagged.
final.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3; ALFRED vintages of the OECD 3-month rates for the AFD control
final.pass: All of: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 at 3 months; rule net Sharpe > 0 in both halves; DSR >= 0.95 counting the DOL-target family, which is T-605 (2), T-575 (1), us-equity-vrp-predicts-dol-1m (2) and this trial.
final.controls: AFD alone (vintage rates) and VIX level alone as competing predictors. An encompassing regression in which the GV coefficient must stay positive. Always-long and always-short DOL baselines. A 12-month-shifted placebo. 2008-09..2009-03, 2020-03 and 2022 reported excluded. One horizon judged.

rows.reason: Fix. It is testable now and cheap. Changes: the level paper is re-attributed to Qiao and Wang, and its return definition is flagged as unverified. The signal uses only H.10-published fixes, the AFD control uses vintages, and the DSR family now covers every DOL-timing trial.

rows.name: US equity variance risk premium (VIX^2 minus realised SPX variance) predicts foreign-currency appreciation vs USD at 1 month
rows.source_notes: Londono-Zhou (July 2014 text read in full; IFDP 1068 abstract) is verified on several points. Sample: 2000-01..2011-12, 22 currencies vs USD. VP_US = model-free implied minus trailing 1-month realised variance, so VIX^2 minus trailing RV matches. Panel result: 'a one hundred units increase in the monthly U.S. VP corresponds to a 1-month ahead annual appreciation of 2.10 percent of the foreign currencies', significant at 1% for horizons of 1-4 months. Table 10: individually significant at 1 month for all currencies EXCEPT EUR, HKD, INR and PHP. The regressions control for the rate differential. BNP's NBER abstract is verified on funding liquidity and crash risk; its VIX/carry predictability claim is in the body and was not opened. The Mandel ML row (fx own_iv IC +0.054) is the VIX level (implied.py maps own_iv for FX to VIX), and the vrp_spx FX ICs are not discovered. Both points are confirmed.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2011 replication found. EUR, the largest and most liquid leg, is insignificant in the source itself. VP is extremely spiky: it turns sharply negative inside crashes (2008, 2020-03) and then positive, so a few months can drive the slope. The ML scan's vrp_spx feature shows no FX IC, although that test pools quote conventions. This is one of several DOL-timing trials, so DSR must count the family.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX-history runs 1990-01-02..2026-10-14. daily-history--GSPC (24,814 rows) and daily-history-SPY exist. fx-spot-g10 has 9 G10 currencies through 2026-10-09. fx-rates-3m: JPY from 2002-04, which sets the expanding fit start of 2002-06; EUR and GBP stale after 2026-01. fred-DTB3 exists. VP code can be shared with T-649 and T-685, which are untested equity-target variants, not duplicates.
rows.lookahead_risks: The signal is clean: the VIX and ^GSPC closes on t precede the noon fix of t+1, which is used as the price. The FX-based controls (last-month DOL return, AFD) must use only fixes published by H.10 at the decision (weekly Monday release) and ALFRED-vintage OECD rates. Use no winsorising chosen after looking.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the primary trial.

final.claim: Decisions: month-ends 2012-01..2026-08, after Londono-Zhou's 2000-2011 sample. Signal: VP_t = VIX close_t^2/12 minus 10,000 x the sum of squared ^GSPC daily log returns over the 21 sessions ending at the month's last NYSE session t, both in monthly squared-percent units. Target: the next-month excess return of the equal-weight 9-currency G10 basket vs USD, i.e. spot from the first noon fix of t+1 to the first noon fix after the next month's last session, plus the accrued foreign-minus-US 3-month differential. Claim: VP_t positively predicts the target. The slope over the 2012-2026 decisions is positive with Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05, and the expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 (OLS from 2002-06) is positive with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05.
final.statistic: Slope of the next-month DOL excess return on standardised VP_t (Newey-West, lag 2). Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with the Clark-West t. Reported only: the 3-month horizon (Hodrick SEs); the per-currency panel with currency fixed effects, with EUR shown separately since it is insignificant in the source; a trading arm (long DOL when VP is above its trailing 60-month median, else short) net of 2 bp per leg per switch plus 1 bp/month roll, with stationary-bootstrap Sharpe.
final.procedure: The VIX close enters at 21:30 UTC on t, and ^GSPC closes run through t. The fill is the next business day's noon fix. No FX input enters the signal. Controls built from FX data use only published fixes. The VP code is shared with T-649 and T-685. No winsorising. 2008-09..2009-03 and 2020-03..2020-06 are reported excluded. Only months in which all 9 currencies print are used. The EUR/GBP splice is flagged. Halves are 2012-2018 and 2019-2026.
final.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3; ALFRED vintages for the AFD control
final.pass: All of: post-sample slope > 0 with Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05; Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05; slope positive in both halves; DSR >= 0.95 counting this trial's 1- and 3-month horizons plus T-605 (2), T-575 (1) and global-fx-rv-level-predicts-dol-3m (1).
final.controls: VIX^2 alone and RV alone as competing predictors (VP must beat both). A multiple regression with AFD (vintage rates), last-month DOL return (published fixes) and the VIX level, in which the VP coefficient must stay positive. 12-month-shifted and shuffled-month placebos. Costs on the trading arm. No threshold beyond the 60-month median in the reported arm.

rows.reason: Fix (minor). The source is verified and the claim is testable now at near-zero marginal cost. The DSR family is widened to all DOL-timing trials, the FX-based controls are made point-in-time, and the source's insignificant EUR result is recorded.

rows.name: FX volatility carry: sort forward volatility agreements on implied-vol term-structure slope (Della Corte-Kozhan-Neuberger 2021)
rows.source_notes: I read the DKN accepted manuscript (City openaccess 24178; JFE 139(3) 2021) in full. Sample: January 1996..December 2015, 20 developed and emerging currencies. The strategy goes long FVAs with downward-sloping IV curves (low slope) and short upward-sloping ones. Returns run from 5.15% per month (t 5.91) to 2.50% per month (t 5.67) for 1/3- to 12/24-month FVAs, with Sharpe ratios of 1.46 to 1.25. The returns 'remain economically significant after accounting for the average bid-ask spreads'. The paper also uses DTCC transaction-level option data. The 0.83 Sharpe net of the largest quoted spread is not re-checked.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent post-2015 replication. The payoff is on volatility (FVA), not spot. CME listed options only approximate an FVA: a calendar of ATM straddles is not a forward-start straddle once spot moves. CME liquidity outside 6E and 6J (and especially in 6S) is thin, so measured spreads may consume a 1-2 vol point edge. Six currencies traded 2-vs-2 is a coarse cross-section.
rows.data_notes: fx-rates-3m and fx-spot-g10 exist. No FX option data is archived (0 bundles for cvol/EVZ), and FX roots are not in the capture box's chain list. CVOL is a single 30-day tenor and cannot form a slope.
rows.lookahead_risks: Use settlement IVs at publication. Interpolate in total variance between listed expiries only. Mark the remaining leg at an actual settlement, not a model. Before any verdict, replace assumed spreads with captured quotes.
rows.missing_data: Per-expiry CME FX option settlements and matching futures settlements for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S. History is paid (DataMine). The free route is forward capture of CME's daily settlement files, and the first verdict comes after 36 months.

final.claim: Data: per-expiry CME FX option settlements for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S (DataMine history or forward capture). Inputs on the first business day of month t: each currency's ATM IVs at 1 and 3 months, from Black-76 inversion of settlement prices against the matching futures settlement, interpolated in total variance; and the 1-to-3-month forward vol FV_i = sqrt((3 sigma3^2 - sigma1^2)/2). Trade: long forward vol on the 2 currencies with the lowest scaled slope (sigma3 - sigma1)/sigma1 and short it on the 2 highest. The return of a long FVA is (sigma2_i(t+1m) - FV_i(t))/FV_i(t), where sigma2 is the 2-month ATM IV one month later. Claim: after a round-trip cost of 1.0 vol point per FVA (DKN's largest quoted short-maturity spread), the long-short earns a positive mean return.
final.statistic: Mean monthly long-short FVA return with HAC t and a sign test. Reported: the executable form, a vega-matched calendar (long 3-month, short 1-month ATM straddles) marked at settlements with measured half-spreads; correlation with T-368.
final.procedure: The sort uses the prior day's settlements, and entry is at the settlement plus cost. At least 3 listed expiries are required to interpolate, and no extrapolation beyond the longest listed expiry. The assumed 1.0 vol point cost is replaced by measured CME quotes before any verdict. No thresholds. Halves split at the midpoint.
final.data: new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy> and cme-fx-futures-settlements-<ccy> (DataMine, paid, or forward capture); fx-rates-3m; fx-spot-g10
final.pass: All of: HAC t > 2 over at least 36 monthly formations; both halves positive; the calendar-straddle form's mean net P&L at measured spreads > 0.
final.controls: An unconditional long-FVA book on all 6 currencies, which separates the term premium from the slope sort. A static-slope placebo (full-sample mean slope ranks). Correlation with T-368. Measured spreads, not assumed ones, for the verdict.

rows.reason: Fix and hold as blocked (data). The source is verified. The registration now measures the FVA payoff directly from settlement IVs, rather than equating it with a calendar, charges DKN's own spread, and requires the executable calendar to survive measured costs.

rows.name: Implied-vol term slope predicts G10 spot returns (Ornelas-Mauad 2019): long low-slope, short high-slope currencies
rows.source_notes: Verified via the IDEAS/RePEc listing and the abstract in a search snippet: Ornelas and Mauad, BCB WP 492 (March 2019), later Int. J. Forecasting 35(4), 1800-1813. Uses 10 tenors (1 week to 10 years), 10 developed and 8 emerging currencies, daily 2002-2016. Developed: a high slope predicts low future returns; emerging: the reverse. Strategy: long the 2 lowest-slope and short the 2 highest. In the WP text (font-encoded; decoded), the ATM-slope portfolio beats carry, risk-reversal and VRP on currency-only Sharpe for G10. The specific numbers (2.33%, Sharpe 0.33) could not be read because the digits are garbled, so they are unverified. DKN's contrasting sign is described in DKN's paper.
rows.replication_concerns: The sign is contested against the DKN working-paper version. There is no out-of-sample evidence after 2016. The reported G10 Sharpe of about 0.33 is before costs, and the source used OTC vols out to 10 years, whereas CME lists liquid expiries only out to a few months. A 6-currency 2-vs-2 sort is coarse.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10 and fx-rates-3m exist with the stated spans. No multi-tenor FX IV is archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Settlement IVs at publication. Fills at the first noon fix or 6x settlement after the signal. OECD rates for any carry alpha control must be ALFRED vintages.
rows.missing_data: Multi-tenor ATM IV per currency (CME settlements; DataMine paid or forward capture).

final.claim: Data: a multi-tenor ATM IV record for the 6 CME-optionable G10 currencies, with at least 3 listed expiries between 1 and 6 months, from Black-76 inversion of settlements. Signal at each month-end: the cross-sectionally standardised OLS slope of ATM IV on log(tenor). Trade: long the 2 currencies with the lowest slope and short the 2 with the highest, held one month in 6x futures or OANDA. Claim: after 1 bp per side plus roll, the book earns a net Sharpe (spot plus carry) above 0.3. The developed-market negative sign is pre-registered from Ornelas-Mauad (2019).
final.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe with a stationary bootstrap (block 12). Spot-only Sharpe reported. Alpha vs the T-368 carry (rebuilt on vintage rates) and DOL baskets, with HAC t.
final.procedure: Expiries come from month-end CME settlements. Fills are at the first noon fix or 6x settlement of t+1. One holding period (1 month). If DataMine history (about 2018 onward) is bought, run as a historical trial at once; otherwise accrue forward. No sign fitting.
final.data: new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy>; fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m
final.pass: All of: net Sharpe > 0.3; bootstrap lower bound > 0; both halves positive; alpha HAC t > 2 vs carry and DOL; DSR counting T-368 (6), T-431 (4) and T-478 (16).
final.controls: Static-slope placebo. Carry and DOL as alpha controls. The right-tail (10-delta call) slope reported only. Costs charged.

rows.reason: Fix and hold as blocked. The source is confirmed qualitatively, but the sign is contested and there is no post-2016 evidence. The registration drops the second holding period, so only one trial remains. It is worth running only as a free add-on if CME FX settlements are captured for the FJM or DKN rows.

rows.name: Low-IV vs high-IV currency straddles: buy straddles where implied vol is low, sell where it is high (Fullwood-James-Marsh 2021)
rows.source_notes: I read the FJM accepted manuscript (City openaccess 24959; JFE 141(3) 1262-1284, 2021) in full. Bloomberg data, 31 March 1999..28 September 2016, weekly Wednesday NY closes, 9 G10 currencies, 1-month options. Long the lowest-IV straddle: +25% per month. Highest-IV straddle: -14% per month. The long-short returns 34% per month after transaction costs, Sharpe 1.03. Diversified straddle, butterfly and delta-hedged versions reach Sharpe 1.38. On notional, almost 40 bp per month (4.7% p.a.). The 1999-2007 and 2008-2016 coefficients are both significantly negative, smaller recently but not significantly different. Payoffs as a share of notional are flat (about 1.2%) across IV portfolios, while premiums rise with IV. Excluding 2008 has the largest effect on returns.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent or post-2016 replication. Flat payoffs and rising premiums mean the edge is a static-premium effect, and in a 6-pair universe the IV ranking is persistent (AUD/JPY high, EUR/CHF low). A demeaned control is therefore essential. The short high-IV leg carries the tail risk. Model-pricing at CVOL ATM is closer to the traded ATM than the VIX-based T-57/T-233 pricing, but it is still not a verdict.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10 and fx-rates-3m exist (Garman-Kohlhagen inputs and settlement). No per-currency IV is archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The Wednesday CVOL close is the signal, and the fill is at Thursday settlement. The expiry settlement must use the 6x settlement or the noon fix matched to the option's expiry time. The assumed 0.25 vol-point cost per leg must be replaced by measured quotes; 6A, 6C and 6S spreads are likely wider.
rows.missing_data: Weekly 1-month ATM IV per currency (CVOL ATM, paid or forward capture), plus CME FX option settlements or quotes for the confirming step.

final.claim: Data: a per-currency 1-month ATM IV record (CVOL ATM or captured CME settlements) for 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S. Trade each Wednesday: buy a 1-month ATM-forward straddle on the lowest-IV currency and sell one on the highest-IV currency, both held to expiry. Claim, on real CME settlement prices and after measured half-spreads (0.25 vol points per leg per side until measured): (a) the book earns a positive mean net return per unit notional; (b) the same book ranked on IV minus each currency's own trailing 52-week mean IV is also positive.
final.statistic: Mean net P&L per unit notional and per unit premium with HAC t over 4 overlapping weekly cohorts. Sharpe; 5% CVaR of the short leg; worst week. The tercile version (2 vs 2 of 6) reported.
final.null: Mean net P&L per unit notional <= 0.
final.procedure: A model-priced first pass (Garman-Kohlhagen at CVOL ATM with fx-rates-3m, settled on 6x settlements) can be inconclusive at most. A supported or not_supported verdict requires real settlement prices or quotes. The Wednesday CVOL close is the signal; entry is at Thursday settlement and the hold runs to expiry. The trailing 52-week mean uses only data through the signal.
final.data: new cme-cvol-atm-<ccy> (or forward capture); new cme-fx-option-settlements-<ccy>; fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m
final.pass: All of, on real-settlement prices: net mean on notional > 0 with HAC t > 2; both halves positive; the demeaned-IV variant mean > 0 with HAC t > 1.65.
final.controls: Demeaned variant (required: it guards against a static ranking). An equal-weight short-straddle-on-all-6 baseline, which separates the cross-section from the level VRP. CVaR and worst week reported. EVZ cross-check for EUR before 2025-01.

rows.reason: Fix and hold as blocked. The source is fully verified. The registration makes the verdict depend on real CME settlement prices and requires the demeaned ranking to pass as well, because flat payoffs and a persistent 6-pair IV ranking make the raw sort look like a static bet.

rows.name: EUR/USD variance risk premium harvest: EVZ / CVOL implied variance exceeds subsequent realised variance (short 1-month straddles)
rows.source_notes: Verified: Low-Zhang (JFQA 40(4) 2005, IDEAS abstract): delta-neutral straddle quotes on GBP, EUR, JPY and CHF; volatility risk is priced in all four, the premium is negative and declines with maturity. Ammann-Buesser (St Gallen WP 2013/04, abstract): significantly negative variance premia with low-frequency intraday RV, ambiguous with high-frequency RV, and time-varying (inversely related to risk-neutral variance). Data source verified by fetch: FRED EVZCLS runs 2007-11-01..2025-03-11. Cboe's consultation-results notice states EVZ cessation was effective before the open on 27 January 2025, so FRED prints after 2025-01-24 are post-cessation (repeated values for 3-5 days). Dierckx-Davis-Schoutens and Della Corte-Sarno-Tsiakas 2011 not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: That the premium exists is well replicated in the literature. Mandel's analogues (T-48, T-50, T-244, T-246) pass, but T-51 and T-65 (Nasdaq, Russell) did not reach significance, so existence is not automatic. The size bar is the binding question: EVZ is model-free variance on thin FXE options, so it sits above ATM IV by the smile convexity, and EVZ minus RV overstates the straddle's edge (the T-57/T-233 lesson). A size-bar pass is therefore necessary, not sufficient, for a trade. The option-form Trial 2 belongs in its own registration once 6E quotes exist.
rows.data_notes: EVZCLS (fetched): 4,360 prints. Yearly means are 14.0 in 2008 and 5.9 in 2021. 30 stale runs of 3 or more sessions (2009-04, several in 2021, 2023, 2024-12, 2025-01/02). fx-spot-g10 EUR: 1999-01-04..2026-10-09. cboe-VIX-history and cboe-GVZ-history (2009-09-18..2026-10-14) exist for the scale comparison. Local 1d 6E_F from 2016-10 serves as the same-time RV check. fomc-meetings and macro-release-cpi exist.
rows.lookahead_risks: RV is an ex-post outcome measured from fix t+1, so H.10's weekly publication does not bias it. Post-cessation EVZ prints and stale prints must be excluded. EVZ is a calendar-day (30-day) measure compared with 21 trading sessions, so annualise RV with 252. The EVZ close (about 16:15 ET) and the noon fix are not synchronous, so the window starts the next day.
rows.missing_data: Needs one free fetch: FRED EVZCLS, checked live. After 2025-01 there is no free implied series (CVOL EUVL is paid; 6E/FXE chains are not captured). The option-form trade needs measured 6E option quotes.

final.claim: Window: every daily entry from 2007-11-01 to 2025-01-24, the last EVZ print before Cboe's cessation on 2025-01-27. Definition: VP_t = (EVZ close_t/100)^2 minus the annualised realised variance of the next 21 DEXUSEU noon-fix log returns starting at fix t+1 (252-day annualisation). Claim: the pooled mean of VP_t is positive. In addition, the one-sided 95% lower bound of the mean vol-point gap (EVZ_t minus the matching realised vol) exceeds 0.5 vol points, the assumed round trip of a 1-month 6E ATM straddle.
final.statistic: Mean of VP_t in annualised variance units over all daily entries, pooling every phase of the non-overlapping 21-session grid (house rule 10), with a studentized circular block bootstrap (42-session blocks). Secondary pass statistic: the mean vol-point gap, same bootstrap. Reported: per-phase results (21 phases); the premium as a fraction of implied variance, beside VIX/SPY and GVZ/GLD on common dates.
final.null: Mean VP_t <= 0, or the vol-point gap's one-sided 95% lower bound <= 0.5.
final.procedure: The EVZ close enters at 21:30 UTC on day t. RV uses fixes t+1..t+22. Entries whose window has a missing fix are dropped. Entries on stale EVZ prints (unchanged for 3 or more sessions) are dropped and counted, and the result including them is reported. Halves are 2007-11..2016-06 and 2016-07..2025-01. 6E_F daily settlements give a same-time RV check for 2016-10..2025-01. Windows containing ECB, FOMC or US CPI days are reported separately. 2008-09..2009-03 and 2020-03 are reported excluded as a sensitivity, not a verdict. The model-priced short-straddle trial is NOT part of this registration.
final.data: new fred-EVZCLS (free); fx-spot-g10; cboe-VIX-history; daily-history-SPY; cboe-GVZ-history; daily-history-GLD; fomc-meetings; macro-release-cpi; local 1d 6E_F
final.pass: All of: mean VP_t > 0 with the studentized 95% CI excluding 0; positive in both halves; the one-sided 95% lower bound of the mean vol-point gap > 0.5 vol points. min_n counts distinct 21-session cycles (about 205 available). A pass establishes existence and a necessary cost margin only, not a tradable straddle.
final.controls: Circular-shift EVZ placebo. VIX/SPY and GVZ/GLD premia on the same dates for scale. Stale-print and post-cessation exclusion. Crisis-window sensitivity. The EVZ (FXE options, Cboe) vs 6E (CME) settlement-time mismatch is disclosed. The cost margin is fixed ex ante; no threshold grid.

rows.reason: Fix. This is the strongest prior in the cluster and a direct twin of supported T-50/T-244, but the window must end at EVZ's actual cessation (2025-01-27, not FRED's 2025-03 tail), stale prints must be handled, and the model-priced straddle trial must come out into its own registration. The size bar is labelled necessary, not sufficient, because EVZ exceeds ATM IV.

rows.name: Risk-reversal / CVOL skew filter on Mandel's carry books (T-368, T-431, T-605): crash filter versus contrarian re-entry
rows.source_notes: BNP's NBER w14473 abstract is verified: carry crash risk, funding-liquidity predictability, and 'carry-trade losses reduce future crash risk but raise its price'. It contains no skew-filter trading rule. The 'CME 2023' study was read only on an unattributed mirror on a cattle-auction website (cattlemensharrison.com). It describes a 2-year 0-100 diffusion index of CVOL skew, 2007-2023, with 3-month-ahead futures returns, and AUD/USD contrarian 'to a lesser extent'. It names no other FX pair and gives no numbers, and I could not confirm it as CME's own publication. Jurek and Farhi et al. were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The literature splits on the sign. Registering a crash filter (A) and a contrarian (B) together is forking paths. The base books earn about zero gross: T-368's gross Sharpe is 0.01 and its trained VIX > 30 risk filter is already deflated inside a failed book. The free proxy (Cboe SKEW) is refuted as a tail signal by T-52, T-227 and T-228.
rows.data_notes: CVOL skew is not archived (paid). The frozen T-368 harness exists, but its OECD rate ranks are lagged only one month, while T-433's ALFRED check shows OECD MEI publication lags well beyond that, so the base book itself is not point-in-time.
rows.lookahead_risks: OECD rate ranks in the base book (vintages needed). CVOL publication time. Percentile windows must use trailing data only.
rows.missing_data: CME CVOL Skew/SkewRatio per currency (DataMine, paid), and a vintage-corrected carry base book.

final.claim: Window: the CVOL history (about 2018-01..2026-09). Base book: the T-368 G10 carry book, rebuilt on vintage OECD rates with T-368 costs. Rule: zero any long-leg currency whose month-end CVOL skew (oriented so negative means foreign-currency puts are rich) is below its trailing 24-month 20th percentile. Claim: the rule cuts the book's maximum drawdown by at least 30% at a Sharpe cost of at most 0.1, and beats a random-leg-removal placebo.
final.statistic: MDD ratio and paired stationary-bootstrap Sharpe difference vs the unfiltered book. Percentile of the MDD cut against a random-leg-removal placebo.
final.null: MDD cut < 30%, or Sharpe loss > 0.1, or not above the placebo's 95th percentile.
final.procedure: CVOL taken at its CME publication time. Skew flipped for USD-base pairs. Trailing-only percentile. Switch at the first noon fix of t+1 after inputs are published. One rule only; the contrarian rule is not registered.
final.data: new cme-cvol-skew-<ccy> (paid); fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m with ALFRED vintages; fred-DTB3
final.pass: MDD cut >= 30% with Sharpe loss <= 0.1, above the 95th percentile of the random-leg-removal placebo, and DSR counting T-368's 6 trials plus this one.
final.controls: Random-leg-removal placebo; unfiltered book; T-368's VIX > 30 filter as comparator.

rows.reason: Drop. The CME source could not be verified (an unattributed mirror with no FX numbers), the rule is another filter on a carry book that earns zero gross and already failed a risk filter (T-368), the literature does not agree on the sign, and the only free proxy is refuted. Revisit only if a carry book passes on its own.

rows.name: Skew-neutral carry by rank difference (interest-rate rank minus implied-skewness rank) (Torok 2022)
rows.source_notes: Found and read the paper (WU VSFX 2023 conference PDF, A. Torok, dated 9 Dec 2022, SSRN 4040261). Universe: 9 developed and 22 emerging currencies, monthly 2006-01..2022-08, Bloomberg option data. The rank-difference RDF portfolio has a 0.54 Sharpe over the 16-year period, and the CARhedged and skew-neutral strategies show positive realised skewness. I found no cost treatment, so the results appear gross. The paper notes that the option-data bottleneck constrains the universe to G10 for older periods. I found no G10-only result.
rows.replication_concerns: Single-author working paper, unreplicated, gross of costs, with evidence dominated by EM (22 of 31 currencies). Li-Sarno-Zinna find option-skew sorts insignificant in G10 alone. The carry half fails in Mandel's 2013-2026 tests (T-368 gross Sharpe 0.01, T-431, T-381). With 6-7 currencies, rank-difference weights are very coarse.
rows.data_notes: CVOL SkewRatio is not archived (paid). fx-rates-3m exists, but the rate rank is a signal, and OECD monthly prints are published with lags beyond one month (T-433, ALFRED). A one-month-lagged rank is not point-in-time.
rows.lookahead_risks: The OECD rate rank needs ALFRED vintages. CVOL publication timing. The 2018-2022 overlap with the paper's sample is in-sample.
rows.missing_data: Per-currency implied skewness (CVOL SkewRatio or OTC RR/BF, paid) and vintage rates.

final.claim: Window: monthly over the CVOL history after the paper's sample (2022-09..2026-09). Universe: USD plus the 6 CVOL currencies. Weights: proportional to rank(vintage OECD 3-month rate) minus rank(-log CVOL SkewRatio, oriented to foreign-currency downside), normalised to $1 long and $1 short. Filled at the first noon fix after the inputs are published and held one month. Claim: after 2 bp per leg plus 1%/yr financing per leg, the book earns net Sharpe > 0.3 with positive skewness and alpha over vintage-rate carry.
final.statistic: Net Sharpe (stationary bootstrap); monthly skewness; alpha vs carry with HAC t.
final.procedure: Fixed formula; no tuning; the out-of-sample window is the verdict.
final.data: new cme-cvol-skewratio-<ccy> (paid); fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m ALFRED vintages; fred-DTB3
final.pass: Net Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, skewness > 0, alpha t > 2, DSR counting T-368 and T-431.
final.controls: Plain carry on the same currencies; skew-only rank book; shuffled-skew placebo.

rows.reason: Drop. The evidence is EM-dominated, gross of costs, unreplicated and shows no G10 result. Its carry leg fails in Mandel's own tests, the related LSZ G10 skew sort is insignificant, and the data are paid. A 6-currency test would be underpowered and add trials to a failed family.

rows.name: Currency skewness risk premium from semivariances; upside/downside VRP sorts (Li-Sarno-Zinna JFQA 2025)
rows.source_notes: I read the LSZ JFQA open-access text in full (DOI 10.1017/S0022109025102123). Sample: February 1998..December 2021, 28 currencies, T = 287 months. SRP HML earns 5.47% p.a. (t 3.31), Sharpe 0.75 (0.82 de-noised), and the long leg contributes 4.85%. G10-only: 'an annualized mean return of only 2.31%, which is not statistically significant'. EM-only: 6.42% (t 3.26). Footnote 21 gives the ARX(1) forecasting procedure. Footnote 22 documents the decay of the DRS VRP sort. I found no transaction-cost adjustment in the text.
rows.replication_concerns: In Mandel's executable universe (6-8 G10 pairs) the source itself reports no significant premium. The paper says SRP returns come mainly from interest differentials, a channel that fails in Mandel's 2013-2026 carry tests. The result is new and unreplicated, and its sample ends 2021-12.
rows.data_notes: CVOL UpVar/DnVar is not archived (paid). fx-spot-g10 exists for realised semivariances, and local 60m FX bars exist from 2024-01.
rows.lookahead_risks: The ARX(1) must be expanding-window only. OECD rates for any carry alpha control need vintages. CVOL publication timing.
rows.missing_data: CME CVOL UpVar/DnVar per currency (DataMine, paid).

final.claim: Window: monthly over the CVOL history after 2021-12. Universe: the 6 CVOL G10 currencies. Signal: SRP_i = an ARX(1) forecast of realised up-minus-down semivariance from noon-fix returns (LSZ footnote 21) minus the risk-neutral asymmetry from 30-day CVOL UpVar and DnVar. Trade: long the top 2 and short the bottom 2. Claim: net Sharpe > 0.3 with alpha HAC t > 2 over vintage-rate carry and DOL.
final.statistic: Net Sharpe (stationary bootstrap); alpha vs carry and DOL with HAC t.
final.procedure: Normalisation fixed from the paper before any run; random-walk forecasts for the first 12 months, then expanding ARX(1).
final.data: new cme-cvol-upvar-dnvar-<ccy> (paid); fx-spot-g10; fx-rates-3m ALFRED vintages
final.pass: Net Sharpe > 0.3, lower bound > 0, alpha t > 2.
final.controls: Carry and DOL alpha controls; static-rank placebo.

rows.reason: Drop. The source's own result for the G10 universe Mandel can trade is a null (2.31% p.a., not significant). The effect is EM-driven and rides interest differentials, which fail in Mandel's carry tests, and the data are paid. No pre-registrable positive claim remains for the executable universe.

rows.name: Global FX volatility innovations as a carry-timing and hedging signal (Menkhoff-Sarno-Schmeling-Schrimpf 2012; Bakshi-Panayotov 2013)
rows.source_notes: Verified: MSSS (City openaccess 3391; JF 67(2) 681-718, 2012) abstract: high-rate currencies fall when global FX volatility rises unexpectedly, and the proxy captures more than 90% of the cross-sectional excess returns of five carry portfolios. This is a contemporaneous pricing result, not a timing rule; sample not stated on the page. Bakshi-Panayotov (JFE 110(1) 139-163, 2013, IDEAS abstract): changes in a commodity index, in currency volatility and, less so, liquidity predict carry payoffs in-sample at up to 6 months. 'Out-of-sample metrics also support predictability', and a decision rule improves Sharpe and skewness, with predictability coming from the long legs. Bekaert-Panayotov's 'bad carry' point is from the candidate, not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Partial duplicate of T-368's failed risk filter (VIX > 30, trained 2002-2012, test Sharpe -0.30). Timing a book with gross Sharpe 0.01 can at best avoid drawdowns, so even a pass would not yield a deployable strategy. MSSS is contemporaneous, so predictive content depends on the persistence of vol shocks. The base book's OECD ranks were lagged only one month, which T-433's vintage check suggests is not point-in-time.
rows.data_notes: fx-spot-g10: 9 non-USD G10 currencies, available from 1999 (EUR 1999-01-04) for the expanding AR(1). cboe-VIX-history exists. daily-history-DBC exists (5,205 rows, from 2006). fx-rates-3m: JPY from 2002-04. The T-368 harness exists. ALFRED vintages of the OECD rates must be fetched (free), as T-433 did.
rows.lookahead_risks: GV for month t needs month-end fixes, which H.10 publishes only the following Monday. Average only the sessions published by the decision. T-368 ranked on month t-1 OECD averages; T-433's ALFRED check shows those prints are usually not out yet, so rebuild the base on vintages. DBC is a daily-history close with available_at the next day, so use DBC through t-1 or the t close only after it is published.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the realised version except a free ALFRED vintage fetch for the OECD 3-month rates. The implied version (CVOL FXVL) is paid.

final.claim: Window: 2013-01 to 2026-09. Base book: the T-368 G10 carry book (top 3 minus bottom 3 of 10 incl. USD, equal weight, T-368 costs), rebuilt with ranks on OECD 3-month rates as published by each decision date (ALFRED vintages, T-433 rule). Signal: GV_t = mean over the 9 non-USD G10 currencies of the average absolute daily log noon-fix change over the sessions of month t published by H.10 by the decision; u_t = its AR(1) residual on an expanding window from 1999-06. Rule: hold the book at weight 0 in month t+1 when u_t is above its expanding 80th percentile, and at weight 1 otherwise. Claim: the rule raises the book's net Sharpe over the untimed book, with paired stationary-bootstrap one-sided p < 0.05.
final.statistic: Sharpe(timed) minus Sharpe(untimed) over 2013-01..2026-09, with a paired stationary bootstrap (block 12, 5,000 draws). Changes in MDD and skewness reported. Reported only: the Bakshi-Panayotov expanding regression of next-month carry on the change in GV and the DBC monthly return, with Clark-West out-of-sample R^2.
final.procedure: The AR(1) and the percentile use only data through t. Switches happen at the first noon fix of t+1, at 2 bp per leg per switch on top of T-368's costs. The frozen non-vintage T-368 book is reported beside the vintage base. The EUR/GBP stale-rate splice after 2026-01 is flagged. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026.
final.data: fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m plus ALFRED vintages (new, free), cboe-VIX-history, daily-history-DBC, fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: Sharpe gain > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; gain positive in both halves; timed Sharpe above T-368's VIX > 30 filter on the same base; DSR >= 0.95 counting T-368 (6), T-431 (4), T-682 (1) and this trial.
final.controls: Untimed book. T-368's VIX > 30 filter on the same base. A random-switch placebo with the same number of flat months (1,000 draws). One threshold (80th percentile), no grid. Costs charged on every switch.

rows.reason: Fix. The design differs materially from T-368's trained VIX-level filter, since it uses FX-specific vol innovations with an out-of-sample rule, and it is testable now. The base book must be rebuilt on vintage rates, GV must use only H.10-published fixes, and the second trial is cut to report-only, leaving one judged trial.

rows.name: Kalshi EUR/USD event contracts vs CME-options-implied digital probabilities (reference-price test)
rows.source_notes: I opened the CFTC 40.2(a) filing (ptc07162610487, 2026-07-16, KalshiEX). It differs from the candidate's description. The Source Agency is Pyth Network (feed 'FX.EUR/USD', midpoint governs), not ICE or ECB. The expiration time is 10:00 AM ET, the contracts are listed on a custom basis, tick is $0.01, notional $1, and position accountability is $25,000 per strike. Crucially, the family includes '<in> <time period>' contracts that pay if the threshold is touched at any point (path-dependent one-touch), as well as '<at>' point-in-time contracts. The older hourly series is confirmed by Kalshi rule filing rules042623963 ('EURUSD') and a live KXEURUSDH market URL. In that series the Underlying is 'the open EUR/USD price at <time> ... according to ICE', the last trading time is <time>, the expiration is one hour later, and it resolves No if no data. MASTER_PLAN.md (child docs, line 383) lists Kalshi's hourly EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/JPY ladders as the same construction as the S&P/Nasdaq ladders and says to 'expect the same answer'. The Robinhood ECB-rate example was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Every analogue is a non-member: T-544 (Kalshi KXBTCD vs Deribit digital, -5.21c), T-337 (Polymarket vs Deribit), EDGE_VERDICT 21d and Result 22 (book Brier beats lognormal by t about 8). A European-digital reference is wrong for the touch ('in') contracts and would manufacture edge. ICE, Pyth and Yahoo prices differ by small amounts, and near-the-money strikes at short horizons are sensitive to that basis.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars: EURUSD_X 2024-01-03..2026-10-19 (17,266 rows) and 6E_F 2024-05..2026-10; local 1d from 2016-10. No Kalshi FX bundle is archived; the pm_history fetcher exists per the cross-check (not opened). EVZ ends 2025-01, so it cannot serve as the vol source for most of the window, and a single realised-vol source is used instead. Hourly reference prices exist only from 2024-01, so the historical test starts 2024-02.
rows.lookahead_risks: Yahoo FX 60m bars are stamped by bar start (archived hourly schema: 't (bar start)'), so re-key by close before taking 'the price at H'. Kalshi candles are stamped by period end: use only candles ending before the market's <time> (its last trading time) and reference prices stamped at or before the candle end. Exclude 'in' (touch) contracts. Correct for the ICE vs Yahoo source basis. The /historical cutoff (about 2 months) means settled markets come from /historical/markets.
rows.missing_data: Settled KXEURUSDH markets and hourly candles via Kalshi /markets, /historical/markets and candlesticks (free; fetcher exists). The series fee multiplier must be re-verified from Kalshi series metadata and docs. CME 6E option mids for a call-spread digital reference are forward-capture only.

final.claim: Markets: settled Kalshi KXEURUSDH 'above/below' and 'between' markets from 2024-02 to the latest settled market in 2026-10, i.e. the ICE-settled hourly EUR/USD contracts with settlement on the ICE price at <time> and last trading at <time>. Reference: a driftless lognormal probability on the EURUSD_X price at the candle end, with vol from a 20-session EWMA of hourly log returns through the candle end, scaled to the time remaining to <time>. Rule: at the first hourly candle that ends before <time> with a two-sided book (spread <= 10 cents), buy the side whose executable price (YES ask, or 1 - YES bid for NO) plus the taker fee is at least 5 cents below that reference, and hold to settlement. Claim: the rule earns a positive mean net P&L per contract.
final.statistic: Mean net P&L per contract in cents, with an event-clustered (per <date, time>) one-sided 95% lower bound. Reported: paired Brier of the Kalshi mid vs the reference at matched candles (event-clustered t); splits by hours to <time>, by year and by moneyness; Pyth-settled FXEURUSD 'at' contracts separately.
final.procedure: Kalshi candles stamped by period end. Yahoo 60m bars re-keyed to close time. Only prices stamped at or before the candle end are used. One entry per market. Taker fee from the series' published fee schedule (re-verified at docs.kalshi.com, rounded per Kalshi rules). 'In'/touch contracts and any market whose rules name a different source agency are excluded. The ICE vs Yahoo basis is measured on settled markets and disclosed. Halves split at the median event date.
final.data: new kalshi-settled-markets-KXEURUSDH and kalshi-candles-hourly-KXEURUSDH (free); local 60m EURUSD_X and 6E_F bars; fx-spot-g10
final.pass: All of: mean net > 0 with event-clustered t >= 2; both halves positive; no single day > 25% of P&L; at least 100 distinct events. Otherwise record as the eighth reference-price non-member.
final.controls: Kalshi-mid Brier vs the reference (the book is expected to win, as in Result 22). Favourite-longshot buckets. A random-side placebo at the same entries. Candle selection bias (only traded strikes have candles) reported. Paper-only until the pre-live gate.

rows.reason: Fix. The filing names Pyth, not ICE/ECB, and includes path-dependent touch contracts, while the hourly ladder that has history (KXEURUSDH) settles on ICE. The registration restricts to point-in-time ICE contracts, uses a single vol source (EVZ ends 2025-01), re-keys Yahoo's bar-start stamps, and drops the 2x2 DSR grid. It is still expected to be a non-member.

rows.name: CFTC positioning in CME FX futures (leveraged funds / speculators) as crash and reversal signal, interacted with option skew
rows.source_notes: Verified the BNP NBER w14473 abstract (carry crash risk, unwinds, losses reduce future crash risk). The speculator-position regressions are in the body and were not opened. The DRS manuscript confirms CFTC data collection from 1998-01 to 2013-12 on the major currencies (text line 766 region). Neither paper reports a trading-rule Sharpe for positioning alone, which matches the candidate's statement. Data verified live via Socrata (TFF futures-only gpe5-46if): codes 099741 EUR, 097741 JPY, 096742 GBP, 232741 AUD, 090741 CAD, 092741 CHF, 112741 NZD and 095741 MXN all exist, each with 1,062 reports from 2006-06-13 to 2026-10-13. GBP and NZD market names changed on 2022-02-08, so join on the code.
rows.replication_concerns: Mandel's only executed COT test (T-405, gold) found no effect and too few extremes. The weekly public data with a 3-day lag is widely read. BNP is a mechanism paper, not a rule. Crowding may simply be carry, so a carry-rank control is needed. Duplicate-adjacent to T-606 (blocked; legacy non-commercial vs a 52-week mean across about 25 futures in an equal-risk book). The design differs: TFF leveraged funds, an extreme-z event study, and currencies only. Count it in that family.
rows.data_notes: FX COT is not archived (archived COT covers 088691, 084691 and 133741 only), but Socrata is free and the fetch code with release_rule exists. TFF was first published in September 2009 with history backfilled to 2006-06, so the earlier rows are backcast.
rows.lookahead_risks: Positions are as of Tuesday and released Friday 15:30 ET (with holiday shifts), or at the Socrata stamp if later. Backcast TFF rows (2006-06..2009-08) are only knowable from the 2009-09 publication onward; with a 156-report window, z in 2013 onward uses post-2009 data only. Handle superseded rows as in T-405. A carry-rank control needs ALFRED-vintage rates. The noon fix as a Monday fill is acceptable.
rows.missing_data: A free Socrata fetch of the 8 TFF futures-only series. The skew interaction (Trial 2) needs paid CVOL and is dropped from this registration.

final.claim: Data: the 8 CME FX futures (6E 099741, 6J 097741, 6B 096742, 6A 232741, 6C 090741, 6S 092741, 6N 112741, 6M 095741) and TFF futures-only reports released 2013-01..2026-09, pooled. Signal: leveraged-funds net position / open interest, z-scored against the trailing 156 reports; flag currency-weeks with z above +2. Outcome: the 4-week excess return of that currency vs USD, from the first noon fix after the Friday 15:30 ET release, as spot plus the accrued rate differential, less 1 bp per side plus roll. Claim: flagged currency-weeks are followed by a lower 4-week excess return than all other currency-weeks.
final.statistic: Difference in mean 4-week forward excess return (z > +2 weeks minus other weeks), pooled. One-sided p from a within-currency circular-shift placebo of the z series (10,000 shifts, preserving autocorrelation), plus a currency-clustered bootstrap CI. Reported: the z < -2 tail, 13-week realised skewness after events, and the predictive slope on z (NW t).
final.procedure: available_at follows the release rule (Friday 15:30 ET with holiday shifts, or the Socrata stamp if later). Series are keyed by contract code. Backcast rows are usable only after their 2009-09 publication. z uses only reports available by the decision. Positions start at the first noon fix after release (6x futures or OANDA). 2009-09..2012-12 is warm-up, reported only. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026. If fewer than 50 z > +2 currency-weeks exist, report 'insufficient extremes' and park (T-405 rule).
final.pass: All of: difference < 0 with placebo one-sided p < 0.05; negative in both halves; at least 50 z > +2 currency-weeks; DSR >= 0.95 counting T-606 and T-405's cells.
final.controls: Carry rank at the same date (vintage rates) as a covariate, to test whether crowding is just carry. Asset-manager and dealer net positions reported. Release timing enforced. One threshold (z > 2), no grid. Costs charged. No skew interaction in this trial.

rows.reason: Fix. The data source is live and verified, and this is the cluster's only FX-specific non-price flow test. The registration fixes contract-code joins, TFF backcast timing and the placebo, and drops the paid-data skew interaction, leaving one trial counted with T-606 and T-405.

rows.name: Equity option-implied tail-risk beta sort of currencies (Fan-Londono-Xiao JFE 2022)
rows.source_notes: Verified on the City openaccess 29716 page: Fan, Londono and Xiao, 'Equity tail risk and currency risk premiums', JFE 143(1) 484-503, 2022. Abstract: an option-based equity tail factor is priced in currency returns. Currencies more exposed to it (that hedge equity tail risk) earn lower premiums. A high-minus-low equity-tail-beta currency portfolio isolates the global component, and its price of risk is consistently negative across carry, momentum and other assets. The sample period, factor construction details and return figures were not on the page and are unverified, matching the candidate's own caveat.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication. A VIX-change beta is a crude stand-in for an OTM-put tail factor and is likely collinear with carry and MSSS's FX-vol beta. Carry fails in Mandel's tests. A result on the proxy says little about the paper either way. Cboe SKEW is uninformative about tails (T-52, T-227, T-228), so a SKEW proxy only adds a dead trial.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX-history runs 1990-01-02..2026-10-14. fx-spot-g10 has 9 G10 currencies plus MXN (1993-11) and ZAR (1980), all through 2026-10-09. fx-rates-3m: MXN from 1997-01, ZAR from 1980-12, JPY from 2002-04 (60-month betas from 2008-01 need rates from 2003-01, which is fine); EUR/GBP stale after 2026-01. fred-DTB3 exists.
rows.lookahead_risks: Month-t returns need the month-end fixes, which H.10 publishes the following Monday, so estimate betas on the 60 months ending t-1 (a one-month skip). OECD rate accruals are approximations, and the carry alpha control needs vintage ranks. The VIX close enters at 21:30 UTC.
rows.missing_data: Proxy version: nothing. Faithful version: SPX OTM put tail measures over 2003 onward (Cboe DataShop, paid; DoltHub chains start about 2019, too short).

final.claim: Window: monthly from 2013-01 to 2026-09. Universe: 11 currencies vs USD (9 G10 + MXN + ZAR). Signal: each currency's 60-month rolling beta, over the months ending t-1, of monthly excess return (spot plus accrued rate differential) on the monthly change in VIX. This is a proxy for Fan-Londono-Xiao's option-implied equity tail factor; a positive beta means the currency rises when VIX rises, i.e. it is a hedge. Trade: long the 3 lowest-beta and short the 3 highest-beta currencies, filled at the first noon fix of t+1 and held one month. Claim: after 2 bp per leg plus 1%/yr financing per leg, the book earns a net Sharpe above 0.3, with alpha over vintage-rate carry and DOL at HAC t above 2.
final.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe (stationary bootstrap, block 12). Alpha vs carry (T-368 construction on vintage rates) and DOL with HAC t. Rank correlation of betas with lagged rate ranks reported.
final.procedure: VIX month-end closes enter at 21:30 UTC. Betas use the 60 months ending t-1. Only months in which all 11 currencies print are used. The stale EUR/GBP splice is flagged. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026. Single proxy (VIX change); no SKEW variant, no beta-window grid.
final.data: cboe-VIX-history, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m (plus ALFRED vintages for the carry control), fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: net Sharpe > 0.3; bootstrap lower bound > 0; alpha HAC t > 2 vs carry and DOL; both halves positive; DSR counting T-368 (6), T-431 (4), T-478 (16) and this trial.
final.controls: Carry and DOL as alpha controls. A static (full-sample) beta ranking placebo. A shuffled-VIX-series placebo. Costs as in T-368/T-431. A fail on this proxy is recorded as not refuting the paper's put-based factor.

rows.reason: Fix. It is testable now, but only through a proxy. The registration drops the SKEW proxy, which Mandel has already shown uninformative, so only one trial remains. It also skips a month in the beta window to respect H.10's weekly publication and requires alpha over vintage-rate carry, since the sort likely reloads on carry.

knowledge.title: Currency option-implied signals: the FX variance risk premium, implied-vol level and term slope, skew and positioning for currency selection and dollar timing (literature survey, 1998-2026)
knowledge.markdown:
# Currency option-implied signals: the FX variance risk premium, implied-vol level and term slope, skew and positioning for currency selection and dollar timing (literature survey, 1998-2026)

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 15 sweep candidates.
  - Peer-reviewed: Della Corte-Ramadorai-Sarno (DRS; JFE 2016), Londono-Zhou (JFE 2017), Della Corte-Kozhan-Neuberger (DKN; JFE 2021), Fullwood-James-Marsh (FJM; JFE 2021), Ornelas-Mauad (IJF 2019), Li-Sarno-Zinna (LSZ; JFQA 2025), Qiao-Wang (J. Empirical Finance 2026), Low-Zhang, MSSS (JF 2012), Bakshi-Panayotov, Brunnermeier-Nagel-Pedersen (BNP), Fan-Londono-Xiao.
  - Working papers: Ornelas (BCB 454), Torok, Babiak-Barunik (decay benchmark).
  - Exchange and data: a Kalshi CFTC filing, Cboe's EVZ notice, CFTC Socrata.
- **Links:** https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/13156/ · https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/bitstreams/70b926af-1044-455e-abf9-be49a31c323b/download · https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/24959/ · https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/24178/ · https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/EVZCLS
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.55 (22 of 38 distinct sources opened and checked, eight in full text; rounded down because many reads were abstract-only).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-21. **How much was read:**
  - Full text: DRS, LSZ, Ornelas, Londono-Zhou, DKN, FJM, Torok and the Kalshi filing.
  - Abstracts only for the rest. Ornelas-Mauad's digits are garbled, so its numbers are unverified.
  - Not opened: Quantpedia, Hutchinson et al., Jurek, Farhi et al., Macrosynergy (403).
  - FRED EVZCLS and the CFTC TFF series were checked live.
- **Selected because:** implied volatility, skew, term structure and the variance risk premium are program inputs, but Mandel has tested them only on equity, commodity and BTC underlyings. T-580's FX "own_iv" is just the VIX level. The G10 carry and currency momentum books T-368, T-431 and T-478 all failed over 2013-2026.

## What it says

- **Cross-sectional currency VRP (DRS).** Hedgers overpay to insure feared currencies and sell them spot, and speculators with limited funding liquidity absorb the flow (CFTC commercials sell expensive-to-insure currencies).
  - Long cheap insurance (high RV minus 1-year IV), short expensive: 4.95% p.a., Sharpe 0.61, developed currencies 1998-2013, net of bid-ask. Carry correlation -0.08.
  - **Decayed.** LSZ (including a DRS co-author) find it "much weaker" through 2021. Babiak-Barunik measure -0.29% p.a. over 2005-2021.
- **Per-currency VRP gap (Ornelas).** IV minus intraday RV predicts appreciation.
  - The headline 0.28%/month uses the global average VRP. EUR alone is insignificant (t 0.71-1.42); JPY is significantly negative.
  - Out-of-sample gains are significant only for EM.
  - The sign flips with the RV window: the 1-month VRP correlates -8% and -3% with the 6- and 12-month VRPs.
- **World currency VRP and global FX vol (Londono-Zhou; Qiao-Wang).** A rising world VRP predicts foreign-currency depreciation at 4-6 months (2000-2011, 18 of 22 currencies). Global implied and realised vol positively predict currency returns beyond 3 months (in-sample R² 2.5-7.1%); Qiao-Wang's return definition and sample end are unverified.
- **US equity VRP (Londono-Zhou).** VIX² minus trailing realised variance predicts dollar depreciation: 2.10% annualised per 100 units at 1 month, 2000-2011. It is not significant for EUR alone, and there is no replication after 2011.
- **Volatility carry (DKN).** Long forward vol on currencies with a downward-sloping term structure, short on upward-sloping ones: 5.15%/month (t 5.91) on 1/3-month FVAs, falling to 2.50% at 12/24 months, Sharpe 1.46-1.25, 1996-2015. It is a payoff on volatility, not spot, and has no replication after 2015.
- **Term slope and spot (Ornelas-Mauad).** In G10 a steep slope predicts weak spot returns, and in EM strong ones (2002-2016). The ATM-slope book beats carry, risk reversal and VRP on currency-only Sharpe. **Contested** by DKN's pooled sign.
- **Low-IV minus high-IV straddles (FJM).** 34%/month of premium after costs, Sharpe 1.03, about 40 bp/month of notional (9 G10, weekly, 1999-2016). Payoffs are flat while premiums rise with IV, so in six pairs it may be a static ranking.
- **EUR VRP existence (Low-Zhang; Ammann-Buesser).** The premium is negative in GBP, EUR, JPY and CHF and shrinks with maturity; significance depends on the RV sampling. EVZ ran from 2007-11 until it ceased on 2025-01-27.
- **Skew filters on carry (BNP; CME 2023).** Carry losses lower future crash risk but raise its price. The CME study was readable only on an unattributed mirror. **Dropped.**
- **Skew-neutral carry (Torok).** Sharpe 0.54 over 2006-2022, gross, EM-dominated, with no G10 result. **Dropped.**
- **Skewness risk premium (LSZ).** 5.47% p.a. (t 3.31) on 28 currencies, carried by interest differentials. G10-only it is 2.31% and insignificant. **Dropped.**
- **Global FX vol innovations (MSSS; Bakshi-Panayotov).** Carry is short global FX vol (a contemporaneous result). Changes in currency vol and commodity prices forecast carry payoffs out of sample.
- **Kalshi EUR/USD ladders.** FXEURUSD (2026-07) settles on Pyth and includes touch contracts. The hourly KXEURUSDH settles on ICE. There is no evidence either way.
- **CFTC positioning (BNP; DRS).** Speculator crowding comes before carry crashes. Eight TFF FX series run from 2006-06. No published trading rule exists.
- **Equity tail-beta sort (Fan-Londono-Xiao).** Currencies that hedge S&P tail risk earn less. The figures are unverified.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** Twelve of the fifteen claims are peer-reviewed, and five of those journal papers were read in full. Survival is weak:
- The one effect with independent post-publication tests (DRS) has decayed.
- Nothing else has evidence after 2016.
- Results lean on EM currencies.
- The OTC 1-year vols and FVAs the papers trade are not retail instruments.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Testable now:**
  - `us-equity-vrp-predicts-dol-1m`, out of sample after the paper (2012-2026), sharing VP code with T-649 and T-685.
  - `global-fx-rv-level-predicts-dol-3m`, with the positive level sign pre-registered.
  - `fx-vol-innovation-carry-timing`: T-368 rebuilt on ALFRED vintages, judged against its VIX > 30 filter.
  - `vix-beta-currency-sort-flx-proxy`.
- **After the free EVZCLS fetch:**
  - `eur-vrp-evz-vs-realised` is the strongest prior, a twin of the supported T-48, T-50, T-244 and T-246. It carries a 0.5-vol-point cost bar, because EVZ sits above ATM IV (the T-57/T-233 lesson).
  - `eur-evz-gap-predicts-eurusd-week` is registered with an expected null, since EUR is insignificant in its source. FOMC, ECB and CPI weeks are reported separately.
- **After free fetches:**
  - `fx-tff-leveraged-crowding-4w`, Commitments of Traders data under T-405's park rule, counted with T-606.
  - `kalshi-eurusd-hourly-vs-spot-digital`, a reference-price test (net of the taker fee, with Brier reported) expected to be the eighth non-member. Kalshi's index ladders (Result 22), BTC/ETH ladders (21d) and T-544 (-5.21 cents) all lost to the book.
- **Blocked on CME option settlements:**
  - `fx-vrp-xs-sort-drs-1y-cme` (12-month IV only).
  - `fx-fva-term-slope-sort-cme`.
  - `fx-atm-iv-term-slope-spot-sort`.
  - `fx-low-minus-high-iv-straddles-cme`, whose demeaned variant must also pass.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Decayed:** the DRS sort (LSZ footnote 22, Babiak-Barunik, Bartram et al.). The whole CVOL window falls inside the decay.
- **Contested sign:**
  - Short-window against 1-year VRP.
  - Term slope (Ornelas-Mauad against DKN).
  - JPY and CHF as safe havens.
- **Contradicted by Mandel:**
  - Anything that rides carry. T-368 (gross Sharpe 0.01, DSR 0.008), T-431, T-478, T-381 and T-433 failed, so the skew filters, Torok and LSZ are dropped.
  - SKEW as a tail proxy: T-52 and T-227 refuted it.
  - VRP existence is not automatic: T-51 and T-65 missed at p 0.095.
- **Not US-executable as published:** OTC variance swaps and FVAs. Mandel uses CME options on 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C and 6S (none exist on DKK, NOK or SEK), CME futures and OANDA.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Leak to fix first:**
  - `fx-spot-g10` stamps noon fixes as available on the same day, but H.10 publishes them only weekly (Mondays 16:15 ET). Re-stamp every fix to its release date.
  - OECD rates need ALFRED vintages (T-433 measured a mean lag of 3.8 months).
- **F3 features for FX, quoted as USD per foreign unit:**
  - Per-currency IV, realised vol and VRP at matched tenors.
  - Demeaned IV and the IV term slope.
  - Global FX vol and its AR(1) innovation.
  - US equity VRP and a VIX-change beta.
  - The TFF net position over open interest, as a z-score.
  - These replace the VIX-level "own_iv" (IC +0.054, pooled over mixed quote conventions).
- **Data:**
  - fred-EVZCLS, minus stale and post-2025-01-24 prints.
  - TFF futures for the eight FX codes, joined on contract code.
  - Kalshi KXEURUSDH via `/historical`.
  - Forward capture of CME FX option and futures settlements.
  - CME DataMine history is a paid decision for the user.
- **Pipeline rules:**
  - Black-76 inversion against the matching futures settlement.
  - Total-variance interpolation.
  - Yahoo bars re-keyed from bar start to bar close; Kalshi candles read by period end.
- **Tests:**
  - Separate DSR families for DOL timing (T-605, T-575 and the new trials), the FX cross-section (T-368, T-431, T-478) and FX options.
  - Stationary-bootstrap intervals; static-rank and circular-shift placebos act as gates.
  - Six currencies over about 100 months need a true Sharpe near 0.7 to reach t = 2.

## Cross-links

- A11: BTZ's VRP timing is the equity twin of this cluster (T-649, T-685).
- A15: T-605 dollar carry and T-606 COT pressure share its DSR families.
- A9: vol-managed carry and T-682.
- A14: month-end dollar flows (T-575).
- A6: open interest.
- A4: the Calvet-Fisher MSM can supply the realised leg of a currency VRP.
- A5: the Kalshi ladder is scored against the price paid.
- 12, 13, 14: regime features.
- Theories: T-48, T-50, T-51, T-52, T-57, T-65, T-227, T-228, T-233, T-244, T-246, T-337, T-368, T-381, T-405, T-431, T-433, T-478, T-544, T-575, T-580, T-605, T-606, T-649, T-682, T-685.
- Children: EDGE_VERDICT 21d, Result 22, MASTER_PLAN 2026-10-15.

## Sources used

- DRS: https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/13156/
- LSZ: https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/bitstreams/70b926af-1044-455e-abf9-be49a31c323b/download
- Babiak-Barunik: https://arxiv.org/html/2101.09738
- Ornelas: https://www.bcb.gov.br/pec/wps/ingl/wps454.pdf

- Qiao-Wang (abstract): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0927539826000551
