candidates.name: Realised-minus-implied vol spread predicts single-stock returns (Bali-Hovakimian RIVolSpread)
candidates.summary: Stocks whose 30-day realised vol is high relative to their ATM implied vol earn lower returns the next month, and stocks whose IV is rich relative to RV earn more. This is the cheapest single-stock options test available to Mandel. It needs only DoltHub volatility_history (hv_current, iv_current: about 1,500 US stocks since 2019-02), not full chains.
candidates.mechanism: The option market prices forward-looking volatility risk and information; the stock market is slow to absorb it. A high IV relative to RV means option buyers pay for risk the stock has not yet shown: a priced volatility-risk / information premium. A low IV relative to RV marks names whose recent turbulence the option market expects to fade, often losers after jumps. The other side is equity investors who anchor on realised risk; short-sale and liquidity limits slow the arbitrage.
variables: variance risk premium (single-stock IV minus RV)
adjacent_variables: days until earnings (IV inflation before announcements)
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks, about 1,500 names in DoltHub; the trade is in the stock on Alpaca (long-short, or long-only top decile versus the universe)
candidates.claimed_effect: OSAP replication of Bali & Hovakimian (2009, Management Science), 1996-2004, value-weighted portfolio sort: 0.732%/month, t 2.9. The sign is negative: low (RV - IV) minus high (RV - IV) earns the premium. The same paper's ATM call-minus-put IV spread (CPVolSpread) earns 1.045%/month, t 4.2. All figures are gross of costs.
candidates.replication: Chen-Zimmermann Open Source Asset Pricing reproduce both signals on the original sample (predictability '1_clear', replication quality '1_good'). I found no 2015-2026 source for this specific spread. From memory: McLean-Pontiff find published anomalies are on average about 26% weaker out of sample and about 58% weaker after publication, and the HXZ and JKP factor zoos do not include OptionMetrics-based signals. So no independent post-2015 replication exists, and the test should expect half the original effect at most. Not duplicated in Mandel's registry: the only cross-sectional options theory there is T-193 (implied borrow, blocked).

sources.title: Open Source Asset Pricing SignalDoc.csv (RIVolSpread, CPVolSpread rows)
Chen & Zimmermann, Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing (Critical Finance Review 2022)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: DoltHub volatility_history stocks that also have daily bars (daily-history plus a Yahoo/Alpaca fetch for the rest), price >= $5, both hv_current and iv_current present. Signal: at each Friday-close snapshot, RVIV = hv_current - iv_current. Mandel's probe verified hv_current as the 30-session close-to-close vol. The snapshot is available at 22:00 UTC on the quote date, so enter at the next session's close. Sort into deciles, long the lowest RVIV decile and short the highest, hold 21 trading days (5 days as secondary), equal and value weight. Costs: 10 bp per side; borrow 50 bp/yr on shorts, or 5%/yr when FINRA days-to-cover is in the top decile. Also run a long-only top-decile-minus-universe version that can trade on Alpaca without shorting. Statistic: mean monthly net long-short return with Newey-West t and FF5+UMD alpha (Mandel's archived factors). Discovery 2019-02..2022-12, confirmation 2023-01..2026-09. Pass: confirmation mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and DSR >= 0.95, counting all variants in this cluster's single-stock family. Controls: identical sorts on iv_current alone and hv_current alone, to separate this from the low-vol anomaly (T-384 not supported); drop stock-months with an 8-K item 2.02 (sec-submissions) inside the IV window.

candidates.name: HV-minus-IV straddle cross-section (Goyal-Saretto)
candidates.summary: Buy ATM one-month straddles on stocks where historical vol is far above implied vol (options cheap), and sell them where IV is far above HV. Option prices overreact, and IV mean-reverts toward realised vol. This is an option-return strategy on single-stock chains.
candidates.mechanism: Investors overreact to recent news when pricing options, so IV drifts too far from the vol that later realises. Option buyers of rich vol, often retail chasing movers or hedgers, are the other side. Market makers price inventory risk, not this forecast error. Delta-hedged versions isolate the vol mispricing from direction.
adjacent_variables: share issuance / profitability / cash (Cao-Han-Tong-Zhan option-return predictors)
candidates.assets: US single-stock options (ATM straddles), executable on Alpaca options; delta hedges in the stock
candidates.horizon: months (enter after monthly expiry, hold to next monthly expiry)
candidates.claimed_effect: Goyal & Saretto (2006 working paper, JFE 2009): all US equity options Jan 1996-May 2005, long-short straddle on HV-IV extremes 15.0%/month with a monthly Sharpe of 0.626. After paying half the quoted spread it falls to 5.3%/month (6.7% in less liquid options), per CXO's summary of the working paper. A EURO STOXX 50 replication thesis reports 4.96%-9.26%/month depending on the sort.
candidates.replication: Replicated in a different market (EURO STOXX 50 options, Univ. of Vaasa thesis 2019). That thesis cites Do, Foster & Gray (2016) as questioning whether the returns survive transaction costs, so profitability is contested; I did not read DFG directly. Cao, Han, Tong & Zhan (RFS 2022) extend the idea: delta-hedged call-writing returns vary with firm characteristics, with Sharpe above 2 that stays profitable after costs (abstract-level). No post-2015 US source found. Not in Mandel's registry: Mandel's straddle theories (T-100..T-123) are SPY-only and model-priced.

sources.title: CXO Advisory: Making Money with Options Based on Superior Volatility Forecasts (summary of Goyal-Saretto WP)
Goyal & Saretto, Cross-section of option returns and volatility, JFE 2009 (record)
The Profitability of Volatility Spread Trading on European Equity Options (thesis)
Zhan, Han, Cao & Tong, Option Return Predictability, RFS 2022

candidates.proposed_test: Fetch DoltHub option_chain for the DoltHub stock universe at the first snapshot after each standard monthly expiry, 2019-2026. Mandel already has the windowed fetcher. Choose the expiry at 21-45 DTE and the strike nearest the dividend-adjusted forward. Compute IV from the bid/ask mids yourself rather than the vendor 'vol', and take HV = hv_current. Liquidity filter: both legs bid > $0.10, spread/mid < 25%. Sort on HV - IV into deciles; buy top-decile straddles at the ask and sell bottom-decile straddles at the bid, held to expiry and settled at intrinsic on raw (unadjusted) closes. Report return per unit premium and per Reg-T margin. Second variant: delta-hedged at each DoltHub snapshot with vendor deltas, 1 bp stock cost. Statistic: mean monthly long-short return net of full spreads, Newey-West t, DSR over the variants. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026. Pass: confirmation net mean > 0 with p < 0.05 and DSR >= 0.95. Report the short leg alone, because short single-stock straddles carry the earnings/jump risk; exclude names with earnings before expiry in a robustness run.

candidates.name: Call-minus-put implied vol spread predicts weekly stock returns (Cremers-Weinbaum)
candidates.summary: Stocks whose calls are expensive relative to matched puts (positive call-put IV spread, a deviation from put-call parity) outperform stocks with relatively expensive puts over the next week to month. This is the option signal with the best 2015-2026 survival evidence found in this sweep.
candidates.mechanism: Informed traders use options for leverage and to avoid short-sale constraints. Their buying pressure pushes the IV of the contract they favour (calls if bullish, puts if bearish) away from parity before the stock adjusts. Uninformed equity holders and option market makers who sell the demanded side are the counterparty. The effect is strongest where option liquidity is high and stock liquidity is low, and where information risk is high.
variables: implied vol level (call vs put at matched strikes)
adjacent_variables: short interest and borrow fee (control: CW show rebate rates do not explain it)
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks; the trade is in the stock (Alpaca), the signal comes from the options
candidates.claimed_effect: Cremers & Weinbaum (JFQA 2010): stocks with relatively expensive calls outperform those with relatively expensive puts by about 50 bp per week (value-weighted risk-adjusted 0.51%/week). Predictability declined over their sample (1996-2005, sample end from memory). A Copenhagen Business School thesis on 2011-2015 finds 19 bp at 1 week (t 2.45) and 73 bp at 4 weeks (t 2.79), 4-factor adjusted (search snippet). Li & Wang (arXiv 2608.26115, 2015-Apr 2026, 12.36M firm-days, OPRA end-of-day): the univariate 21-day panel coefficient on the ATM call-minus-put IV spread is +0.0214 (t 7.0) over the full sample and +0.0151 (t 4.2) in 2023-2026; it is +0.040 (t 5.4) in the joint six-signal regression for 2023-2026.
candidates.replication: Replicated, and it survives into the 2020s, though smaller than the original. The original authors document decay within their own sample. The Li-Wang preprint has |t| > 4 in every regime 2015-2026, but it uses firm and date fixed effects with no size, value or momentum controls and no transaction costs, and it is unrefereed. Neuhierl, Tang, Varneskov & Zhou (Management Science) find only a few option characteristics keep incremental power after the full set of firm characteristics. So expect a smaller net effect. OSAP's related CPVolSpread replicates (1.045%/month, t 4.2). Not in Mandel's registry: T-137, T-181 and T-505 test index parity arbitrage, not cross-sectional return prediction.

candidates.proposed_test: From weekly DoltHub option_chain snapshots (Friday quote dates; available 22:00 UTC), compute for each stock the mean (call IV - put IV) over strike pairs within +/-10% moneyness that have both quotes, in the nearest expiry with >= 7 DTE. Recompute IVs from mids with a dividend-adjusted forward and drop deep-ITM puts, where American early exercise biases put IV. Equal-weight the pairs: DoltHub has no open interest, CW weight by OI. Sort into deciles, long the highest-spread decile and short the lowest, entering at the next close; hold 5 and 21 trading days. Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow, as in candidate 1. Statistic: weekly long-short net return, Newey-West t, FF5+UMD alpha, and a Fama-MacBeth slope controlling for log market cap (sec-companyfacts shares x price, point in time), 12-1 momentum, 1-month reversal and RV. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026, DSR across the family. Pass: confirmation alpha > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and DSR >= 0.95. Executable form: Alpaca long-short or long-only top decile.

candidates.name: Individual option volatility smirk predicts lower returns (Xing-Zhang-Zhao) - decayed
candidates.summary: Stocks with the steepest smirk (OTM put IV minus ATM call IV) underperform. This is the canonical result, but the best 2015-2026 evidence says it has decayed to nothing and even flips sign at three months in 2023-2026. It is worth one pre-registered decay test, and it serves as a control for candidates 3 and 5.
candidates.mechanism: Informed traders anticipating bad news buy OTM puts, steepening the smirk before the stock falls. The equity market is slow to absorb this. After 2020, retail demand for short-dated OTM contracts shapes the smirk with uninformed flow, which would explain the decay.
variables: skew (OTM put IV minus ATM call IV)
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks (trade the stock)
candidates.claimed_effect: Xing, Zhang & Zhao (JFQA 2010), 1996-2005: steepest-smirk stocks underperform the flattest by 10.9%/year risk-adjusted. OSAP's replication (skew1) is weaker: 0.64%/month, t 2.19, rated '2_likely'. Li-Wang 2015-2017 replication: high-minus-low quintile -0.41% per 21 days (about -4.9% annualised, half the original). The 21-day panel coefficient decays from -0.0234 (t -5.5) in 2015-2019 to -0.0150 (t -4.2) in 2020-2022 to -0.0060 (t -1.5) in 2023-2026. At 63 days it is +0.0156 (t +2.1) in 2023-2026, and it is insignificant in every regime once the IV spread and risk-neutral skewness enter.
candidates.replication: Contested and decayed. OSAP replicates only weakly (t 2.19). The 2015-2026 preprint shows monotone decay and a sign reversal in 2023-2026. Treat it as a decay check and as a control variable, not as a strategy. Not in Mandel's registry. Mandel's index-skew tests (SKEW-based T-52, T-138, T-227) all failed, which agrees with skew levels being poor directional signals.

candidates.proposed_test: Use the same DoltHub pipeline as candidate 3. Smirk = IV of the OTM put nearest moneyness 0.90-0.95, or vendor delta about -0.2, minus the ATM call IV, in the expiry at 10-60 DTE, at month-end snapshots. Pre-register two claims. (a) The original: the low-minus-high smirk quintile earns a positive 21-day return net of 10 bp per side, 2019-2026. (b) Decay: the 2023-2026 long-short mean is below the 2019-2022 mean. Statistic: Newey-West t and the per-period means with block-bootstrap CIs, plus a Fama-MacBeth version with the call-put spread (candidate 3) and the OTM-IV skewness (candidate 5) as controls. Expect (a) to fail in confirmation. A pass needs one-sided p < 0.05 in 2023-2026 alone.

candidates.name: Risk-neutral skewness (OTM IV skewness / BKM) predicts lower stock returns
candidates.summary: Stocks whose option-implied distribution is more right-skewed (lottery-like) earn lower returns over the next 1-3 months. In the 2015-2026 re-estimation this is the single most significant option signal, at every horizon and in every regime.
candidates.mechanism: Investors with a preference for skewness overpay for stocks with lottery-like upside, and option prices reveal which stocks they are. Informed put buying also lowers measured skewness before bad news. The other side is skew-seeking retail and option buyers. Arbitrage is limited because shorting high-skew, often small and volatile, names is costly.
variables: skew (cross-strike skewness of OTM IVs / model-free risk-neutral skewness)
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks (trade the stock)
candidates.horizon: weeks to months (21 and 63 trading days)
candidates.claimed_effect: Li & Wang (arXiv 2608.26115, 2015-Apr 2026) use the cross-strike sample skewness of OTM IVs as a BKM proxy. Univariate panel coefficient on the 21-day return: -0.0030 (t -13.1) full sample, -0.0040 (t -11.7) in 2023-2026. At 63 days: -0.0081 (t -16.5) full, -0.0104 (t -14.3) in 2023-2026. It stays at |t| > 8 jointly with the other five signals. No portfolio returns or costs are reported. Conrad, Dittmar & Ghysels (JF 2013) is the peer-reviewed anchor: ex-ante option-implied skewness is priced, with a negative relation (sign from memory; the preprint cites it).
candidates.replication: The sign is contested in the literature. From memory, some studies using model-free BKM skewness report a positive relation, and Conrad et al. report a negative one, so the result depends on the measure. The strongest 2015-2026 evidence is one unrefereed preprint without size, momentum or IV-level controls; its proxy may partly be an IV-level or vol effect. Neuhierl et al. (Management Science) say only a few option characteristics survive firm controls. Not in Mandel's registry.

candidates.proposed_test: At month-end DoltHub snapshots, compute two measures per stock in the expiry nearest 30 DTE. (i) The preprint's proxy: the sample skewness of IVs across OTM strikes. (ii) BKM model-free skewness from OTM call and put mids. The thin chains (about 11-27 strikes a side for SPY, fewer for single names) need a minimum of 4 OTM strikes a side. Pre-register a negative relation and report the two-sided test as well, given the contested sign. Sort into quintiles, long the lowest skewness and short the highest, hold 21 and 63 trading days (non-overlapping cohorts, or Jegadeesh-Titman overlapping with NW lags). Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow. Also run a Fama-MacBeth with log market cap, 12-1 momentum, RV, ATM IV level and candidates 1 and 3 as controls. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026, DSR over measures x horizons. Pass: the confirmation long-short net mean > 0 with p < 0.05, and the Fama-MacBeth slope keeps its sign with |t| > 2 after controls.

candidates.name: Monthly changes in call and put implied vol predict stock returns (An-Ang-Bali-Cakici)
candidates.summary: Stocks whose call IV rose over the past month earn higher returns; stocks whose put IV rose earn lower returns. The effect persists up to about six months. The signal is option-market information diffusing slowly into the stock.
candidates.mechanism: Informed traders act first in options. Rising call IV reflects bullish demand pressure, rising put IV bearish pressure. Equity investors who do not watch the option surface are slow to respond. The effect is idiosyncratic, not market-wide.
variables: implied vol level (change in call IV, change in put IV)
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks (trade the stock)
candidates.claimed_effect: An, Ang, Bali & Cakici (JF 2014), 1996-2011: decile sorts on the past change in call IV give return spreads of about 1%/month, persisting up to six months. CXO's summary of the 1996-2008 version reports a 0.97%/month gross high-minus-low quintile spread. OSAP replications, equal-weighted, 1996-2011: dVolCall 1.09%/month (t 3.45), dVolPut 0.42%/month (t 2.03), dCPVolSpread (change in put IV minus change in call IV, sign negative) 1.68%/month (t 6.77).
candidates.replication: OSAP replicates on the original data. Note that its strongest numbers are equal-weighted, so small caps likely dominate. No post-2015 out-of-sample source found; the shared web-search budget ran out before a targeted decay search. Not in Mandel's registry.

candidates.proposed_test: Stage 1, cheap: from DoltHub volatility_history, dIV = iv_current - iv_month_ago (a blended IV; both are in the same point-in-time row), month-end sort into quintiles, long high dIV and short low dIV. The sign is ambiguous because the blend mixes call and put, so pre-register stage 1 as two-sided and treat it as exploratory. Stage 2, confirmatory: from option_chain snapshots 21 trading days apart, compute dCallIV and dPutIV at the ATM strike in the nearest >= 21 DTE expiry, then sort on dCallIV - dPutIV. Long the top quintile, short the bottom, hold 21 days; also report months 2-6 for persistence. Equal and value weight, with value weight primary to limit small-cap dominance. Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026, DSR. Pass: value-weighted confirmation mean > 0 with p < 0.05.

candidates.name: Single-stock IV term-structure slope predicts stock returns
candidates.summary: Stocks whose 60-day ATM IV is above their 30-day IV (upward slope, calm near term) earn higher next-month returns than stocks with inverted near-term IV. In the 2015-2026 re-estimation this survives every regime, including 2023-2026.
candidates.mechanism: An inverted single-stock term structure means the option market expects news or stress within a month: event risk, informed demand for short-dated protection. Short-dated demand pressure from informed or hedging buyers precedes negative drift. Part of the effect may be an earnings-event confound, which the test must control.
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks (trade the stock)
candidates.claimed_effect: Li & Wang (arXiv 2608.26115, 2015-2026), slope = ATM IV (46-75 DTE) minus ATM IV (15-45 DTE). Univariate 21-day panel coefficient: +0.0106 (t 4.8) full sample, +0.0091 (t 3.1) 2015-2019, +0.0106 (t 3.8) 2020-2022, +0.0118 (t 3.7) 2023-2026. Multivariate 2023-2026: +0.016 (t 3.3). Park, Kim & Kim (Journal of Futures Markets), 2000-2013: the shape of the long-term IV curve predicts next-month stock returns beyond short-term components and stock characteristics.
candidates.replication: Two independent samples point the same way (2000-2013 peer-reviewed; 2015-2026 preprint), but neither reports net portfolio returns. The preprint omits firm controls and does not separate earnings months. Not in Mandel's registry: T-262 is a BTC calendar spread, not this.

sources.title: Li & Wang, Option-Implied Signals and Crash Risk 2015-2026 (arXiv 2608.26115)
Park, Kim & Kim, Informed options trading on the implied volatility surface: A cross-sectional approach (J. Futures Markets)

candidates.proposed_test: At month-end DoltHub snapshots, compute slope = ATM IV in the 46-75 DTE expiry minus ATM IV in the 15-45 DTE expiry, interpolated to constant 30/60 days where two expiries bracket. Single names often list only monthlies, so require both buckets. Flag stock-months with an 8-K item 2.02 (sec-submissions; next date projected from the prior year's pattern, point in time) between the two expiries, and run the test on all names and on non-earnings names. Sort into deciles, long the highest slope and short the lowest, hold 21 days. Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow. Statistic: long-short net mean with NW t, FF5+UMD alpha, and a Fama-MacBeth slope with candidates 1, 3 and 5 as controls. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026, DSR across the family. Pass: confirmation mean > 0 with p < 0.05 in the non-earnings subset, with the earnings subset reported separately.

candidates.name: IV term-structure slope predicts single-stock straddle returns (Vasquez)
candidates.summary: Straddles on stocks with an upward-sloping IV term structure (short-dated IV low relative to long-dated IV) outperform straddles on stocks with an inverted slope. Buy cheap short-dated vol and sell rich short-dated vol, cross-sectionally.
candidates.mechanism: Short-dated IV overshoots its mean-reverting long-run level, sitting too high after stress (inverted slope) and too low in calm (steep contango). Straddle buyers chasing recent movers pay for the overshoot. Option dealers, who manage inventory rather than forecast vol, are the counterparty.
candidates.assets: US single-stock options (ATM straddles), Alpaca options
candidates.claimed_effect: Vasquez (2011 working paper; JFQA 2017), Jan 1996-Jun 2007, about 260 stocks/month. Average slope ranges from -15.0% in decile 1 to +8.5% in decile 10. Long top-decile minus short bottom-decile straddles: 27.1%/month gross (14.8% long, 12.2% short side), 81% positive months, and 12.3%/month net of a friction of 1.1x the bid-ask spread (CXO summary of the WP; no commissions; returns on option price, not margin). Jones & Wang (USC working paper): the slope strongly predicts short-term straddle returns for indexes and individual equities.
candidates.replication: Two papers agree (Vasquez; Jones & Wang). A 2025 CDS-term-structure paper (Strathclyde) cites Vasquez's slope-to-delta-hedged-straddle result as established. The sample ends before 2008, and I found no post-2015 replication. The large net figure is on option premium, not capital, and a short straddle leg on inverted-slope names carries event risk. Not in Mandel's registry.

candidates.proposed_test: Use the candidate 2 pipeline (DoltHub chains 2019-2026, liquidity filters, IVs recomputed from mids), entering at the first snapshot after each monthly expiry. Sort on slope = IV(back expiry) - IV(front expiry) at ATM. Buy top-decile front-month ATM straddles at the ask, sell bottom-decile straddles at the bid, hold to front expiry, settle at intrinsic on raw closes. Report per-premium and per-margin returns, both legs separately, and the earnings-free subset (no 8-K 2.02 before the front expiry). Statistic: monthly net long-short mean with NW t and DSR, counted jointly with candidate 2 as one option-return family. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026. Pass: confirmation net mean > 0 with p < 0.05 on the earnings-free subset.

candidates.name: S&P variance risk premium predicts 1-6 month equity returns (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou)
candidates.summary: A high gap between implied variance (VIX squared) and realised variance forecasts higher S&P 500 returns over the next quarter. This is a time-series timing signal for SPY exposure, and its out-of-sample record is weak.
candidates.mechanism: The VRP measures the market's aversion to variance risk: when investors pay a lot for variance protection, expected equity returns are high. The counterparty is hedgers who buy index puts and variance and accept lower expected returns in exchange for insurance.
adjacent_variables: tail risk premium (SKEW, OTM put prices)
candidates.assets: SPY / ES (CME) versus T-bills
candidates.claimed_effect: BTZ (RFS 2009) Table 2, monthly observations Jan 1990-Dec 2007, Hodrick t-stats, VRP = VIX squared minus past-month realised variance from high-frequency data. 1 month: slope 0.39, t 1.76, adj R2 1.07%. 3 months: 0.47, t 2.86, adj R2 6.82%. 6 months: 0.30, t 2.15, adj R2 5.42%. 12 months: 0.12, t 1.00.
candidates.replication: Contested out of sample. Pyun (JFE 2019) states that BTZ's predictability is weak out of sample and proposes a beta-representation method (working-paper monthly OOS R2 of 8%). Bollerslev, Marrone, Xu & Zhou (JFQA 2014) argue finite-sample bias does not explain it and find it internationally. A 2026 GitHub replication on 1990-2026 daily data (VIX squared minus trailing 21-day close-to-close RV) finds the 63-day coefficient z 0.58, out-of-sample R2 -0.074; winsorising at 1/99% lifts it to z 1.91, an in-sample choice. It attributes the failure to COVID-era RV artefacts. Partial duplicate in Mandel: T-48 (supported) confirms the VRP exists, and T-580's F3 family includes log(VIX/RV20) as an ML feature. A standalone pre-registered OOS test would add a clean verdict.

kahtongtan/variance-risk-premium: 36 years of VIX and SPX, in- and out-of-sample

candidates.proposed_test: Monthly, at the last close: VRP = (VIX/100)^2/12 - the past 21-day SPY close-to-close variance. Second variant: replace the trailing RV with a HAR-RV forecast fitted on prior data only, which addresses the COVID artefact. Targets: SPY excess return (DTB3) over the next 1, 3 and 6 months. Expanding-window OOS from 2008-01, with the 1990-2007 training window equal to BTZ's sample, so 2008-2026 is fully post-publication. Statistics: Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 and Clark-West test per horizon; a timing rule with SPY weight = clip(forecast / trailing mean premium, 0, 1.5), the rest in bills, 2 bp per rebalance; Sharpe difference versus buy-and-hold with block-bootstrap CI and DSR, counting the 3 horizons x 2 RV variants. Report 2015-2026 separately. Pass: Clark-West p < 0.05 at 3 months and a positive Sharpe difference with lower bound > 0. Expect a fail, given Pyun and the 2026 replication.

candidates.name: Option-implied correlation (COR1M) predicts market returns up to one year
candidates.summary: Expected average correlation among index constituents, extracted from index versus single-stock option prices, forecasts market excess returns for up to a year. In the source it is stronger and longer-lived than the variance risk premium. Mandel holds the Cboe COR1M and DSPX histories but has never used them to time the market.
candidates.mechanism: High implied correlation means investors expect diversification to fail: market exposure is concentrated and idiosyncratic risk and beta dispersion are expected to shift. It is a non-diversifiable risk the market is paid for. Index-option buyers (portfolio hedgers) pay the correlation risk premium; dispersion traders who sell it are capital- and friction-limited.
variables: implied vol level (VIX and single-stock IVs)
adjacent_variables: realised average pairwise correlation of top-50 SPX names
candidates.assets: SPY / ES (CME) versus T-bills
candidates.claimed_effect: Buss, Schönleber & Vilkov (CEPR DP12760, 2018): expected correlation predicts market excess returns at horizons up to 1 year, in and out of sample, incremental to variance-based measures. An earlier version reports that the VRP predicts only about one quarter ahead. CXO's summary gives a 1996-Aug 2015 sample and notes value-weighted prediction is much stronger than equal-weighted. No R2, trading strategy or costs are reported in the sources I opened. Driessen, Maenhout & Vilkov (JF 2009): correlation risk is priced (the 2013 version has average implied 39.5% vs realised 32.5% for the S&P 500), but the correlation premium cannot be harvested after realistic frictions.
candidates.replication: Not independently replicated in what I found. CXO flags data-snooping across correlation variants and notes that Cboe's public indices use a different specification from the paper. Publication status was not confirmed (search budget exhausted). Mandel duplicates are related but not the same: T-236 (blocked) and T-538 (inconclusive) test COR1M versus realised correlation, and T-250 (not supported) tests sector implied versus realised correlation. None tests return prediction.

candidates.proposed_test: Monthly, at the last close: COR1M (archived, 2006-), COR3M (free Cboe CSV from 2006-01-03, to be archived) and DSPX (2013-). Also CRP = COR1M - the trailing 21-day cap-weighted average pairwise correlation of the top-50 SPX names, computed from daily-history with point-in-time weights from sec-companyfacts shares outstanding x close. Targets: SPY excess return at 3, 6 and 12 months, non-overlapping or with Hodrick SEs. Expanding-window OOS from 2013 (training 2006-2012). Statistics: Campbell-Thompson OOS R2 and Clark-West p, alone and jointly with the candidate 9 VRP, to check that the claim of incremental information holds. Trading form: SPY weight in [0, 1.5] proportional to the forecast, 2 bp per change, Sharpe difference versus buy-and-hold with block bootstrap and DSR over measures x horizons. Note that COR1M's history before its launch is Cboe's backfill, so treat the index definition as one pre-registered choice and add no variants. Pass: Clark-West p < 0.05 at 6 or 12 months with a positive OOS R2 in 2019-2026.

candidates.name: VIX futures basis (daily roll) predicts VIX futures returns, not spot VIX (Simon-Campasano)
candidates.summary: When front VIX futures trade far above spot VIX (large positive daily roll), short them; when they trade far below (backwardation), buy them. Hedge the equity beta with E-mini S&P futures. The basis is a harvestable premium, not a forecast of spot VIX.
candidates.mechanism: VIX futures embed a volatility risk premium paid by hedgers and long-volatility ETP holders (VXX/VIXY roll buying). The basis shows how large the premium is today. Spot VIX does not move to close it, so the futures price converges down to spot. The ETP rebalancing flows and hedgers are the counterparty.
variables: derivative volume and open interest (VX futures)
adjacent_variables: VIX ETP assets and rebalancing flows (VXX, SVXY, UVXY)
CFTC COT positioning in VX futures
candidates.assets: VX futures (Cboe CFE: not on Mandel's named venue list); executable proxies are VIXY/VXX/SVXY/SVIX on Alpaca, hedged with ES/MES on CME
candidates.claimed_effect: Simon & Campasano (EFMA 2013 version; from memory, later in the Journal of Derivatives). 2006-2011: the basis does not forecast spot VIX changes but does forecast VX futures returns. Quantpedia's rules: daily roll = (front VX - VIX) / business days to settlement, front contract with >= 10 trading days; short when roll > +0.10, long when roll < -0.10; hold 5 days; ES hedge from regressions. Profitable in both subsamples (2007-mid 2009, mid 2009-2011) after about $140 per round trip. Quantpedia estimates about 19.67%/year on 5x initial margin; CXO's summary reports about 53%/year for a hedged version over 2006-2011 (secondary).
candidates.replication: Decayed or contested. Quantpedia rates confidence 'moderate' and says its own out-of-sample backtest shows slightly negative performance. The February 2018 short-vol ETP blow-up (XIV terminated) postdates the sample. Related Mandel verdicts are all not supported: T-160 (VX M1-M2 calendar), T-379 and T-435 (SVXY contango filter, excess Sharpe -0.17 vs 0.01), T-242 (VXX after VIX3M/VIX > 1.10). T-534 and T-538 support that the curve over-predicts spot VIX in contango. This candidate is a near-duplicate family. It is kept because its signal (roll per day on the actual front future), 5-day hold and ES hedge differ from every tested rule, and because Mandel's cboe-vx-futures (2013-) is entirely post-publication.

candidates.proposed_test: Data: cboe-vx-futures daily settlements (2013-05..2026-10), cboe-VIX-history, ES via Yahoo ES_F daily or SPY. Rule exactly as published: roll_t = (F1_settle - VIX_close) / business days to F1 settlement, using the nearest contract with >= 10 trading days. Short 1 F1 if roll > 0.10, long if roll < -0.10, enter at the next day's settle, hold 5 trading days. Hedge ratio from a rolling 1-year regression of F1 changes on ES % changes (and their product with days to settlement), estimated only on data before each trade. Cost: 1 tick each side plus $2.50/contract/side (about $140 round trip as in the paper). Statistic: mean net P&L per 5-day trade in $/contract, Newey-West t, Sharpe, max drawdown, and DSR counting T-160/T-379/T-435/T-242 as prior trials in the VX family. Pass: mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 over 2013-2026 and both halves positive. ETP-executable variant: hold SVXY (short) or VIXY (long) under the same signal with SPY hedges, 5 bp per trade.

candidates.name: The VIX futures premium falls when risk rises and predicts VX returns (Cheng)
candidates.summary: The ex ante premium in VIX futures (futures price minus the expected VIX at expiry) predicts subsequent VX futures returns with a coefficient near one. Unexpectedly, the premium shrinks or turns negative when risk measures rise. A low or negative premium flags coming vol spikes and is a time not to be short volatility.
candidates.mechanism: Hedging demand: when risk rises, volatility hedgers reduce exposure instead of buying more, so the insurance premium falls exactly when risk is high. Short-vol carry sellers on the other side are underpaid in those states. Cheng presents the pattern as a puzzle for theories of why investors hedge volatility.
variables: term structure (VX futures vs expected VIX)
candidates.assets: VX futures (Cboe CFE) / VIX ETPs on Alpaca; SPY as the risk asset being timed
candidates.claimed_effect: Cheng (RFS 2019): ex ante premiums reliably predict ex post VX futures returns with a coefficient near one, and they fall or stay flat when ex ante risk measures rise. Risk.net coverage: VIX futures typically trade at a premium but cheapen ahead of volatility episodes. An ISCTE thesis extending the sample reports the pattern persisting through March 2020. Effect magnitudes are not given in the abstracts I saw.
candidates.replication: Partially replicated: the ISCTE master's thesis extends the sample to March 2020. No post-2020 source found. Near-duplicate family with candidates 11 and 13 and Mandel's T-53/T-160/T-435. It is kept because the signal is the model-based premium (basis minus expected VIX change), not raw contango, and because it adds a testable second claim (premium falls with risk) that no Mandel theory covers.

sources.title: Cheng, The VIX Premium, RFS 2019
Risk.net: Negative VIX premium signals vol spikes, research finds
ISCTE thesis replicating and extending the VIX premium puzzle to March 2020

candidates.proposed_test: Daily, 2013-2026 (cboe-vx-futures, VIX, VIX9D/VIX3M/VIX6M, VVIX). Premium_t = F1_t - E_t[VIX at F1 settlement]. The expectation comes from an AR(1)/HAR model of log VIX (plus the term-structure slope) estimated on an expanding window ending at t, so no look-ahead. Claim (a): in a regression of the F1 return to settlement (or 5 days) on the premium, the slope is > 0, and 1 lies in its 95% CI. Claim (b): the premium's regression on risk proxies (VIX level, VVIX, trailing 21-day RV) has a non-positive slope. Trading form: short F1 (or hold SVXY) only when the premium is above its trailing-training-quantile median, flat otherwise, against always-short. Costs as in candidate 11. Statistics: NW t, block-bootstrap CI, Sharpe difference, and DSR including the VX-family trials. Pass: (a) one-sided p < 0.05 and (b) slope <= 0, both holding in 2013-2019 and in 2020-2026.

candidates.name: VIX term-structure slope (PC2) predicts variance-asset returns (Johnson)
candidates.summary: The second principal component of the VIX term structure (VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M/VIX6M/VIX1Y) carries nearly all the term structure's information about variance risk premia. A low slope predicts higher returns on variance swaps, VIX futures and S&P straddles at all maturities; a steep slope predicts lower ones.
candidates.mechanism: The shape of the term structure reveals the current price of variance risk, not expected VIX changes. When the curve is flat or inverted, insurance has already repriced and variance assets are cheap relative to their risk; a steep contango means rich insurance. Hedgers and long-vol ETP holders are the counterparty.
variables: term structure (VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VIX6M, VIX1Y)
candidates.assets: VX futures / VIX ETPs (VIXY, SVXY) on Alpaca; SPY options straddles (Alpaca) for the straddle leg
candidates.claimed_effect: Johnson (JFQA 2017; 1996-2013 sample per CXO): SLOPE predicts excess returns of synthetic S&P 500 variance swaps, VIX futures and S&P 500 straddles for all maturities, incremental to other VRP proxies. CXO reports next-day lowest-minus-highest slope quintile spreads of 0.29% to 1.81% across 18 asset/maturity combinations, with next-day returns positive for 17 of 18 in the lowest-slope quintile. All gross.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Mandel has related results: T-53 supported (VIX falls 6.5 points more after backwardation than after contango); T-159 not supported (VRP not higher in contango within VIX terciles); T-530 not supported; T-534 supported. This candidate is distinct because the predictor is the PC2 of the whole curve and the targets are next-day/week returns on tradable variance assets. Count it in the same DSR family as candidates 11 and 12.

sources.title: Johnson, Risk Premia and the VIX Term Structure, JFQA 2017
CXO Advisory: VIX Term Structure Slope and Variance Asset Future Returns

candidates.proposed_test: Daily 2011-2026 (VIX9D starts 2011). Fit PCA on standardised log(VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VIX6M) on an expanding window, with VIX1Y added once archived from the free Cboe CSV; sign-normalise PC2 so that higher = steeper. Targets: (i) next-day and next-5-day return of the front VX future (constant-maturity 30-day interpolation of F1/F2) from cboe-vx-futures; (ii) next-day SVXY and VIXY returns; (iii) the 21-day variance swap P&L (VIX squared minus realised, Mandel's T-540 construction). Statistic: lowest-minus-highest quintile mean with NW t and a predictive regression slope; a trading form that is short the front future (or long SVXY) only in the top-2 slope quintiles, with $140 round trip or 5 bp for ETPs. DSR counting the VX family (T-53, T-159, T-160, T-435, T-530 and candidates 11-12). Discovery 2011-2018, confirmation 2019-2026. Pass: confirmation quintile spread of the correct sign with p < 0.05 for target (i) or (ii).

candidates.name: VVIX predicts lower returns on tail hedges (SPX/SPY OTM puts, VIX calls)
candidates.summary: A high VVIX (implied vol of the VIX) raises today's price of tail-risk hedges and predicts lower returns on OTM index puts and VIX calls over the next 1-4 weeks. In reverse: selling tail protection is better paid after VVIX spikes.
candidates.mechanism: The VVIX measures demand for, and the price of, volatility-of-volatility and tail risk. When it is high, hedgers bid up puts and VIX calls beyond what subsequently realises (a rare-disaster premium), so hedge returns fall. Persistence (weekly autocorrelation 0.759) carries the effect over several weeks. Option writers with capital collect the premium.
adjacent_variables: SKEW index (Mandel's T-52/T-138/T-227 SKEW tests failed)
vol-of-vol term structure (Branger et al.; no free data found)
candidates.assets: SPY options (Alpaca), VIX options (Cboe index options, venue support to confirm), SPX
candidates.claimed_effect: Park (Federal Reserve FEDS 2013-54), May 2006-Jan 2012: a one-standard-deviation increase in VVIX lowers next-day SPX put returns by 1.32% to 2.19% (t -4.48 to -5.54) and next-day VIX call returns by 0.68% to 1.01% (t -3.55 to -4.44). The effect is larger for deeper OTM strikes and persists 3-4 weeks; VVIX weekly autocorrelation is 0.759. Huang & Shaliastovich (2014; CXO summary, Feb 2006-Jun 2013): higher VVIX predicts more negative hedged S&P and VIX option returns, with average monthly losses on hedged VIX calls of -0.57% (ITM) to -1.41% (OTM) of the index, gross. No evidence that VVIX predicts S&P index returns themselves.
candidates.replication: Two independent studies agree on 2006-2013 data. No post-2013 replication found. Mandel has tested VVIX only as a vol-of-vol premium (realised VIX vol versus VVIX: T-243 and T-536 not supported, T-240 not supported) and VIX-call hedges (T-239 not supported, T-541 blocked). The claim here, VVIX timing tail-hedge returns, is untested.

candidates.proposed_test: Use DoltHub SPY end-of-day chains, 2019-02..2026-10 (1,232 quote days archived as dolt-chain-SPY). At each snapshot take the 5%- and 10%-OTM puts in the expiry nearest 30 DTE and compute the return to the next snapshot 5 trading days later (mid-to-mid, and ask-to-bid as the cost-inclusive version), plus the same for a 5/10 put spread. Regress on z(VVIX) and on z(VVIX residual from VIX), with VIX and the trailing 21-day SPY RV as controls; VVIX is taken at the entry close (Cboe publishes after the close, so enter at the next close if timing is strict). Use Newey-West SEs with lag 5. Pre-registered sign: negative. Trading form: sell the 1-week 5/10 put spread only when z(VVIX) is in its training top tercile, against every week, at bid/ask fills with defined risk on Alpaca. Statistic: slope t, the tercile spread in short-spread P&L per unit max loss with a block-bootstrap CI, DSR. Discovery 2019-2022, confirmation 2023-2026. Pass: negative slope with p < 0.05 in confirmation and positive net P&L of the conditional short spread.

candidates.name: Bitcoin option risk reversal (25-delta skew) predicts BTC returns
candidates.summary: Deribit's 25-delta risk reversal (call IV minus put IV), and the butterfly, carry information about future BTC returns beyond 12 other controls. The signal is strongest at 30-180 day tenors and concentrated on the next day. The most recent evidence says it weakened after the 2024 spot-ETF regime change, and an independent backtest finds the plain RR is noise.
candidates.mechanism: The option market is where leveraged directional views and hedging show first. Skew toward calls signals bullish positioning or demand for upside; skew toward puts signals hedging demand. If the spot market lags, the skew leads returns. After 2024, ETF-driven institutional flow (IBIT options, covered-call ETFs selling calls) changed who sets the skew, which would weaken the signal.
candidates.assets: BTC spot on Coinbase, IBIT on Alpaca, BTC futures on Coinbase Derivatives / CME, or Kalshi BTC perps; the signal comes from Deribit (public data only)
candidates.claimed_effect: Neo (SMU PhD dissertation, May 2026), daily Deribit data Apr 2021-Dec 2025, 1,723 observations. The 25-delta 90-day RR is significant at the 1% level in a 13-variable Newey-West regression; its t rises from 1.91 univariate to 3.73 with controls. The butterfly t goes from 2.13 to 2.34. The effect is concentrated on the first day after the signal and deteriorated after early 2024; the coefficient sign is not stated in the abstract I saw. Contra: an independent GitHub backtest (Deribit, about 4.5 years) finds RR sign accuracy of 58.9% at T-30 (33/56, z 1.33, p about 0.18), 77.4% at T-90 (24/31, untested), and an RR-to-move correlation of 0.076 (R2 about 0.006). Its verdict: 'effectively noise'.
candidates.replication: Contested, with a reported decay after 2024. The dissertation's significance appears only with controls, so a forking-paths risk needs deflation. The independent backtest is underpowered. Deribit's own 2019-2022 study, on mark prices, found that selling the BTC risk reversal gave the best risk-adjusted returns but expected it to fade as institutions entered. Mandel's T-257 (delta-hedged RR P&L when |RR25| > 5) is inconclusive: 24 of 40 entries, mean +0.04% of S, hit rate 0.50, and 257 of 262 signals sold the put wing. The child Brier finding that DVOL adds nothing over Polymarket prices for BTC digitals argues the same way. This candidate (direction of the spot return) is not yet tested.

candidates.proposed_test: Rebuild daily BTC smiles from Mandel's archived deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC sample (07:00-09:00 UTC, the T-257 harness, 2021-12..2026-10), and backfill 2021-04..2021-11 from the same free endpoint. Compute 25-delta RR and butterfly at constant 30- and 90-day tenors, available at 09:00 UTC. Targets: BTC log return from 09:00 UTC to +1, +7 and +30 days (Coinbase 1m BTC, archived). Pre-register the sign as positive RR -> higher returns. Controls: DVOL, 7-day momentum, funding (deribit-funding), quarterly basis. Discovery 2021-04..2023-12, confirmation 2024-01..2026-09; the confirmation period is the post-ETF one where decay was reported. Statistics: Newey-West slope t and IC, OOS R2, and a long/flat BTC rule (long when RR z > 0) net of 0.6% Coinbase taker round trip (as in T-320) or 10 bp for IBIT, with Sharpe versus buy-and-hold and DSR over tenors x horizons x {RR, butterfly}. Pass: confirmation slope of the pre-registered sign with p < 0.05 and a positive net Sharpe difference.

candidates.name: BTC variance risk premium is larger in low-volatility regimes (selling vol pays more when DVOL is low)
candidates.summary: Bitcoin's variance risk premium (implied minus subsequently realised variance) is real and several times the S&P's. Option-implied densities say it is highest in the low-volatility regime, which contradicts the long-straddles-when-DVOL-is-low idea (Mandel T-256). This conditions Mandel's supported BTC short-vol results (T-246, T-255) on the DVOL regime.
candidates.mechanism: In calm regimes investors still pay for crash and rally insurance while realised variance collapses, so the premium widens. In high-vol regimes realised variance catches up with implied and the premium compresses. Short-vol sellers are paid most when it feels least necessary. The counterparty is BTC holders and leveraged traders buying protection and upside lottery tickets.
variables: variance risk premium (DVOL squared minus realised)
adjacent_variables: IBIT option IV (US-listed; Hurst records it)
covered-call ETF supply of BTC calls
candidates.assets: BTC options on Deribit as the signal; execution via IBIT options on Alpaca (US-legal), defined-risk structures
candidates.claimed_effect: Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (arXiv 2410.15195), Deribit options Jul 2017-Dec 2022, 7.8M trades, 27-day horizon. Unconditional annualised BTC VRP is 0.07 (from risk-neutral density) or 0.14 (BVIX-based), versus about 2% cited for the S&P 500. Low-vol regime VRP 0.10 / 0.17 versus high-vol regime 0.04 / 0.12. Realised variance exceeded BVIX squared from 15 Mar to 8 Apr 2020 (VRP below -2). Deribit Insights (2019-2022, mark prices): IV exceeded RV about 70% of the time, the VRP averaged about +15 vol points in contango, and selling was more reliable in positive-skew regimes. The paper reports no regression of returns on the VRP.
candidates.replication: The unconditional premium is replicated inside Mandel: T-49, T-175, T-246 and T-255 are all supported (hedged short 30-day ATM straddle +14.3% of premium, CI +10.2% to +18.1%). The child Hurst reports the premium at about 5 vol points but with catastrophic pin-gamma months unless it is laddered (about $25,000 of margin). The regime claim rests on one unrefereed paper ending in 2022. Mandel's T-256 (long straddles when DVOL is below its 20th percentile) is inconclusive (+29.2% vs +14.1%, difference CI -13.0 to +43.3, n 18), so this candidate directly tests the opposite direction. For ETH, T-67 is not supported (ETH VRP).

sources.title: Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang, Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market (arXiv 2410.15195)
Deribit Insights: Bitcoin Options - Finding edge in four years of volatility regimes

candidates.proposed_test: Daily 2021-04..2026-09: VRP_t = (DVOL_t/100)^2 - the realised variance of BTC over the next 30 calendar days (Mandel's T-246 construction, 365-day annualisation). DVOL is keyed by close time to avoid the child's documented open-time-stamp look-ahead. Regime = DVOL tercile against its trailing 365-day distribution, point in time. Claim: mean VRP in the low tercile > mean VRP in the high tercile, measured both in variance units and as a ratio to implied variance. Second measure: the T-255 model-priced daily-hedged short 30-day ATM straddle P&L per unit vega by tercile, net of the T-255 fees. Statistic: tercile difference with a studentized circular block bootstrap (90-day blocks), pooled over all 30 start offsets (house rule 10), halves 2021-2023 and 2024-2026 reported. Pass: lower 95% bound of (low - high) > 0 in variance-ratio terms with both halves positive. Forward confirmation on Hurst's IBIT surface captures before any capital; the executable form is a defined-risk IBIT iron fly ladder.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with a DoltHub volatility_history row and price >= $5, 2019-02 to 2026-09: the value-weighted portfolio long the lowest and short the highest decile of RVIV = hv_current - iv_current earns a positive mean monthly return in 2023-01..2026-09, net of 10 bp per side on turnover and short borrow (50 bp/yr; 5%/yr in the top FINRA days-to-cover decile). RVIV comes from the last snapshot quoting each month's final session (available 22:00 UTC); positions enter at the next session's close and are held 21 sessions.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly long-short net return, value-weighted primary and equal-weighted reported, with Newey-West t (lag 2) and a studentized circular block bootstrap (6-month blocks); FF5+UMD alpha from the archived daily factors compounded to the holding windows; DSR counting every variant of the single-stock options family (RIVol, CW spread, smirk, skewness, dIV and term-slope rows x weights x holds).
registration.procedure: 1) Fetch DoltHub volatility_history on the snapshots nearest each month-end (Saturday-only 2019, Mon/Wed/Fri 2020-2023, daily 2025-); keep quote_date = the month's last NYSE session; drop stale=True and rows missing either field; drop an iv_current more than 3 MAD from the name's prior-5-snapshot median as a vendor glitch (rule fixed now). 2) Universe = fja-sp500-components members on the formation date with daily-history close >= $5. 3) Market cap = latest sec-companyfacts dei shares outstanding accepted before formation x close; names without shares appear only in the equal-weight run. 4) Deciles from that date's cross-section: long D1 (IV rich vs RV), short D10. 5) Returns from adjclose over 21 sessions from the next close. Names that stop pricing are carried at their last close, flagged and counted; if removed members lack prices the result is labelled SURVIVOR-ONLY. 6) Costs 10 bp per side on turnover; borrow accrued daily. FINRA days-to-cover enters at publication (8th NYSE business day after settlement), never at settlement. 7) Nothing is fitted. Discovery 2019-02..2022-12 is reported; confirmation 2023-01..2026-09 decides.
registration.data: DoltHub volatility_history (single names, to fetch); daily-history-<symbol>; fja-sp500-components; wikipedia-sp500-changes; sec-companyfacts; finra-short-interest; french-ff5-daily; french-momentum-daily; fred-DTB3
registration.pass: All of: confirmation value-weighted mean net > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 by both Newey-West and the bootstrap; discovery mean > 0; FF5+UMD alpha > 0; DSR >= 0.95 over the family. A SURVIVOR-ONLY label caps the verdict at inconclusive.
registration.controls: Same deciles on iv_current alone and on hv_current alone (RVIV must beat both, to separate it from T-384's low-vol failure); equal-weighted version; long-only D1 minus universe (Alpaca, no borrow); earnings-free subset using the projected next 8-K 2.02 date (prior year's same-quarter date + 364 days, point in time); random-decile placebo; deciles only, no threshold grid.

learnings.finding: On the index, short-dated implied below trailing realised still over-predicted the next realised variance on 82% of windows. Recent RV above IV is not evidence that options are cheap.
Long index straddles lose on average, delta-hedged or not: the long leg starts from a negative base rate.
SPY structures filled at DoltHub bid/ask were inconclusive or not supported. Full-spread fills are decisive even on the most liquid chain; single-name ATM spreads are wider.

The BTC vol premium is real, but one-straddle forms have catastrophic pin-gamma months (worst -88%); only a 21-rung ladder (~$25,000 margin) tames it. The short-straddle leg carries the same jump risk.

overlaps.note: Same claim already registered (weekly long-short quintiles of US large caps on the ATM call-minus-put IV spread, 10 bp per side, both halves positive); blocked only because the chain capture holds 3 single names.
Options-implied borrow is the same parity deviation read as a cost; borrow must be controlled.
16% of near-ATM SPY/GLD/IBIT pairs sat outside parity +/- (half-spreads + 10 bp) on 2 captured days: end-of-day parity deviations are mostly quote noise.
SPX implied-forward dispersion above the half-spread band on 2.2% of pairs on day one.
Single-stock skew around earnings; same chain dependency.
S&P 500 point-in-time short-volume study: 93.4% of member-days priced (survivorship).

learnings.finding: The claim was pre-registered before this sweep, and its design (quintiles, nearest-ATM ~30 DTE, 10 bp per side, both halves) is the one to run. Running it records T-531's verdict instead of a parallel theory.

End-of-day parity deviations outside the spread band are common (16% of near-ATM ETF pairs), so a measured call-put IV spread is partly staleness, dividends, early exercise or borrow. It needs mids, a parity forward and staleness filters.
Borrow is unobserved. FINRA days-to-cover sorts were inconclusive (survivor-only), so DTC can serve only as a borrow proxy.

A lead can be real and still not pay: Polymarket's book follows Kalshi's (t 4.6-6.0), yet hitting the lagging ask marks out at -1.9 to -2.2 points. With ~60-80% weekly turnover, 10 bp per side costs ~25 bp/week against a 2011-2015 gross of 19 bp/week.

The best post-2015 evidence (Li-Wang 2015-2026: t 4.2 in 2023-2026) is an unrefereed panel with fixed effects, no firm controls and no costs. Neuhierl et al. find few option characteristics survive firm controls.

No post-2004 evidence was found, and the shared web-search budget ran out before a decay search, so this rests on the original sample alone.
rows.replication_concerns: No out-of-sample evidence after 2004. Published cross-sectional anomalies decayed in Mandel's own tests (T-445, T-446, T-382). RVIV sorts partly on RV, so it can inherit the failed low-volatility anomaly (T-384, T-448). The original universe is all optionable stocks; S&P 500 large caps will show a smaller effect. Power: about 91 month-end formations over 2019-02..2026-09. A value-weighted quintile spread of 0.3-0.4%/month at about 2.5% monthly SD gives a t of roughly 1.1-1.5, so a split-sample confirmation of 45 months alone is hopeless (t about 0.7). Because nothing is fitted, the whole post-publication period is out of sample, so the verdict should use all of it and require both halves to be positive.
rows.data_notes: The archived dolt-volhistory holds only SPY and the nine sector SPDRs (3,604 SPY+SPDR rows checked; symbols SPY, XLB..XLY), so single names must be fetched. DoltHub post-no-preference/options volatility_history was probed live for 2019-03-02 and 2019-03-09. It returned hv_current and iv_current for AAPL, AGN, APC, ATVI, BBT, CELG, ETFC, FRC, MYL, RHT, RTN, SIVB, STI, TIF, TSS and TWTR. Several of these were delisted before the 2021 bulk import, so the vol data is NOT survivor-only. Prices: daily-history lacks SIVB, FRC, TWTR, ATVI, PXD, HES, DFS, WBA, CELG, RHT, AGN, ETFC, MYL, TIF, XLNX, CTXS, NLSN and ABMD. However, DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks (tables ohlcv, split, dividend, symbol; free, keyless) returns raw OHLCV for delisted names: SIVB and FRC through 2023-03-09, CELG and RHT in 2019. Use the latest quote_date on or before it, never a later one. Rows are available at 22:00 UTC on the quote date, so entry is at the next session's close. About 2-4% of snapshots are stale; use quote_date, never snapshot_date. Pre-2021-04-20 rows come from a 2021 bulk import, which is provenance only (content is correctly dated). The vendor's iv_current method is unknown; T-250 validated it only for SPY. Split days can corrupt vendor hv_current, so recompute and filter. Market cap must use raw close x sec-companyfacts shares 'filed' before formation; a split-adjusted close understates it by the later split factor. FINRA days-to-cover enters at publication (settlement + 8 business days), not at settlement. Failure delistings (SIVB halted 2023-03-10) carried at the last close overstate returns. Names with a pending merger have deal-pinned vols (RHT hv 0.036) and cluster in one tail.

Fama-French factors for 2026-09 (not yet published).

The portfolio is formed on the latest snapshot quoting a session on or before each month's last NYSE session, entered at the next session's close and held 21 sessions.

Also reported: per-half means; FF5+UMD alpha (factors end 2026-08-31); the same statistic for hv_current-only and iv_current-only quintile sorts. DSR is computed over every variant registered in the single-stock options family: this row, T-531, the smirk, skewness, IV-change and term-slope rows. Weighting and hold variants count as trials; controls do not.
final.procedure: 1) Universe on each formation date: fja-sp500-components members (wikipedia-sp500-changes after 2026-08-18), mapped to DoltHub act_symbol via fja-sp500-ticker-spells. 2) Signal: DoltHub volatility_history. The formation row is the latest snapshot whose quote_date is on or before the month's last NYSE session; a name whose quote_date is more than 4 sessions early is skipped and counted. Drop stale=True rows. Drop a row whose hv_current differs by more than 2 vol points from the 30-session close-to-close vol recomputed from split-adjusted DoltHub closes, or whose iv_current is more than 3 MAD from the name's prior 5 snapshots (glitch rules fixed now). 3) Prices: DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks ohlcv (raw) with its split and dividend tables gives total returns. The $5 filter and market cap use the RAW close, never daily-history 'close'. 4) Market cap = the latest sec-companyfacts dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding filed before formation x raw close. Names without shares are left out of the value-weighted run and kept in the equal-weighted one. 5) Quintiles of that cross-section: long Q1 (IV rich versus RV), short Q5, value-weighted within each leg. 6) Enter at the close of the session after the formation quote_date and hold 21 sessions. rows.name: HV-minus-IV straddle cross-section (Goyal-Saretto)
rows.source_notes: The JFE 2009 record (ideas.repec, vol 94(2) 310-326) confirms that stocks are sorted on historical realised vol minus ATM implied vol and that the long-short straddle strategy has an economically and statistically significant monthly return. No figures appear in the abstract. The CXO page cited for the effect describes a DIFFERENT strategy from the August 2006 working paper: straddles on stocks with the largest forecast IV changes, where the forecast uses IV relative to the cross-section and to the stock's own 12-month mean. The 15.0%/month, monthly Sharpe 0.626, 5.3% after half-spreads and 6.7% (illiquid) figures belong to that strategy, not to the HV-IV sort, so the claimed effect is unverified. The Vaasa thesis page was blocked (Anubis). Do-Foster-Gray and Cao-Han-Tong-Zhan were not opened, and the web-search budget ran out before a decay search.
rows.replication_concerns: The effect size is unknown for the HV-IV sort itself. Costs decide this test: buying at the ask and selling at the bid on single-name ATM straddles costs several percent of premium. Mandel's index evidence contradicts the mechanism: on SPY, HV above IV did not make options cheap (T-232/T-533, 82% of windows), the long-straddle base rate is negative (T-123), and quote-priced SPY structures were inconclusive (T-550). The short leg carries earnings and jump risk, and Alpaca cannot hold naked short straddles. All published samples end by 2005.
rows.data_notes: Live DoltHub probes show single-name chains with three listed expiries: about 2, 4 and 7 weeks (AAPL/CPB on 2023-01-23: 11/25/53 DTE; 2023-01-27: 14/28/49). Strikes run about 10-11 a side in 2019 and 17-27 a side from 2020; the back expiry has 7-19. Chains carry bid, ask, vendor vol and greeks, but no open interest or volume. The post-expiry Monday lists a 25-27 DTE expiry, so the 21-45 DTE front exists. option_chain is sparse in 2019 (no rows on 2019-06-29). daily-history 'close' is adjusted for later splits: AAPL 2019-03-01 shows 43.74 there against a raw DoltHub close of 174.97, with listed strikes of 100-190. The cross-checker's 'settle at intrinsic on the split-adjusted close' would therefore settle every pre-split straddle wrongly. DoltHub stocks ohlcv is raw and covers delisted names.
rows.lookahead_risks: Settlement and the ATM forward must use RAW closes on the expiry date (see data notes). Fills must come from the NEXT snapshot, which can be 2 sessions later in 2020-2023 (Mon/Wed/Fri) and a week later in 2019. A missing next snapshot must skip the name, never fill at the signal quotes. hv_current comes from the same snapshot as the signal, which is fine. Earnings inside the hold. Early exercise of short American puts or calls ahead of a dividend is ignored by hold-to-expiry. Corporate actions inside a hold change the deliverable.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain and volatility_history on post-expiry and expiry-day snapshots for about 500 point-in-time names (10-20k point-lookup calls). DoltHub stocks ohlcv/split/dividend. 8-K item 2.02 dates (SEC submissions refetch keeping 'items') for the earnings-free run.

final.claim: At the first DoltHub snapshot after each standard monthly expiry, 2019-03..2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members whose ATM call and put in the listed 21-45 DTE expiry both bid > $0.10 with spread/mid < 25%: buy top-decile straddles of HV - IV (hv_current minus the recomputed ATM IV) at the NEXT snapshot's ask, and sell bottom-decile straddles at that snapshot's bid. Held to expiry and settled at intrinsic on the RAW expiry-day close, this earns a positive mean monthly net return per unit of premium over the full period and in each half (2019-03..2022-12, 2023-01..2026-09).
final.statistic: Equal-weighted mean monthly long-short net return per unit of premium, with a Newey-West t (lag 1) and a studentized circular block bootstrap (6-month blocks), one-sided. Per-half means, each leg, and the return per Reg-T margin are reported. DSR is computed over the option-return family: this row, the Vasquez row and delta-hedged variants.
final.null: Mean monthly net long-short return per unit premium <= 0.
final.procedure: Universe, prices and delisting rules as in rv-minus-iv-spread-sp500-xs (DoltHub raw closes, never split-adjusted ones). ATM strike = the strike nearest the dividend forward F = S_raw e^{rT} - PV(dividends projected from the DoltHub dividend table), with r = DTB3 on the quote date. IV is recomputed (European Black-Scholes) from the mid of the OTM leg at that strike; vendor 'vol' is reported only. HV = hv_current on the signal snapshot. Sort into deciles. Fill at the next snapshot's ask (buys) and bid (sells); names with a missing or illiquid next snapshot are skipped and counted. Settle at intrinsic on the expiry session's raw close. A split, special dividend or merger inside the hold drops the name (counted). Delta-hedged variant: vendor delta at each snapshot, stock traded at 1 bp. Nothing is fitted.

rows.name: Call-minus-put implied vol spread predicts weekly stock returns (Cremers-Weinbaum)
rows.source_notes: CW, JFQA 45(2) 335-367 (2010), on ideas.repec: expensive-call stocks beat expensive-put stocks by about 50 bp/week, rebate rates do not explain it, the effect is stronger with high option and low stock liquidity, and predictability declines over the sample. The CBS thesis PDF was extracted: daily data 2011-01..2015-12, Carhart 4-factor alpha 19 bp (t 2.45) at 1 week and 73 bp (t 2.79) at 4 weeks. Li and Wang, arXiv 2608.26115 (submitted 2026-06-10), was read in full HTML. It uses a proprietary OPRA end-of-day extract for 2015-01..2026-04, 12.36M firm-days and 10,026 underlyings. iv_spread univariate 21-day coefficient: +0.0214 (t 7.0) full sample, +0.0291 (6.6) 2015-19, +0.0166 (4.8) 2020-22, +0.0151 (4.2) 2023-26. Multivariate 2023-26: +0.040 (5.4). Regressions use firm and date fixed effects, double-clustered SEs and a random 1.5M-row subsample. Controls are only option liquidity (relative spread, zero-volume share, OI-weighted vega): no size, value, momentum, reversal or RV, no portfolio sorts and no costs. The coefficient units are not stated, so the economic size is unknown. The cross-checker missed that OSAP's SmileSlope (Yan 2011 JFE, put minus call ATM IV at delta 0.5, 1996-2005, equal-weighted quintiles, 1.8%/month, t 8.17) is the same signal with the opposite sign. CPVolSpread (value-weighted quintiles, 1.045, t 4.2, 1996-2004) is confirmed. Neuhierl et al. (INFORMS 403; Frankfurt page blocked) was not verified.
rows.replication_concerns: Firm fixed effects in a return panel subtract each firm's full-sample mean return, which is look-ahead, and they measure within-firm timing rather than a cross-sectional sort. Daily-sampled overlapping 21-day returns with firm-and-date clustering do not absorb cross-firm, cross-date overlap (Driscoll-Kraay would), so the t-statistics are likely inflated. Weekly turnover at 10 bp a side costs about 25 bp a week, the same order as the 2011-2015 gross of 19 bp. Selection: this row's priority comes from the preprint's 2023-2026 result, so a 2023-2026 confirmation window is not out of sample with respect to that selection. The historical run is a vendor-independent, in-period replication, and capital needs a forward test.
rows.data_notes: T-531 is registered (blocked on data) with the same claim: weekly equal-weighted quintiles of US large caps, nearest-ATM ~30 DTE, 10 bp per side, positive in both halves, min_n 52. DoltHub single-name chains exist for 2019-2026, including delisted names (SIVB chains on 2023-01-27; 2019 vol rows for CELG, RHT and others). Three expiries are listed, one near 25-30 DTE; strikes run about 11 a side in 2019 and 17-27 from 2020. DoltHub stocks ohlcv supplies delisted-inclusive raw prices. finra-short-interest runs 2017-12..2026-09, sec-companyfacts is present, and French factors end 2026-08-31.
rows.lookahead_risks: Design flaw in the cross-checker's procedure: a forward implied from put-call parity on the nearest strikes absorbs exactly the call-put deviation the signal measures, so the ATM call-minus-put IV spread becomes about 0 by construction. The forward must be S_raw e^{rT} - PV(projected dividends). European IVs on American options bias ITM puts, so restrict to |K/S - 1| <= 5% and <= 60 DTE. Stock closes at 16:00 ET while options close at 16:15 ET, which adds noise. 2019 option_chain snapshots are sparse; skip weeks without one rather than reaching forward. Borrow is unobserved, so the DTC proxy must use published FINRA values only. Use raw closes, never split-adjusted ones. Delisting returns need the same treatment as in the RIVol row.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain at each week's last snapshot (about 400 dates x 50-100 calls). DoltHub stocks ohlcv/split/dividend. No open interest exists on DoltHub, so equal weights across pairs replace CW's OI weights.

final.claim: This is T-531 re-specified on history. Weekly 2019-02..2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members with a DoltHub chain, the equal-weight portfolio long the top and short the bottom quintile of the call-minus-put IV spread earns a positive mean 5-session net return over the full period and in each half (2019-02..2022-12, 2023-01..2026-09). The spread is taken at the same strike (nearest the dividend forward) in the listed expiry nearest 30 DTE within 14-60, with European IVs from mids on a dividend-projected forward, never a parity-implied one.
final.statistic: Mean weekly long-short net return, with a Newey-West t (lag 4) and a studentized circular block bootstrap (8-week blocks), one-sided. Also: per-half means; FF5+UMD alpha; a Fama-MacBeth slope controlling for log market cap, 12-1 momentum, 1-month reversal, 30-day RV, RVIV and the smirk. DSR is computed over the spread definitions (ATM primary; mean over strike pairs within +/-10% moneyness), the holds (5 and 21 sessions) and the family.
final.procedure: Formation uses the week's last snapshot whose quote_date is the week's last NYSE session; weeks without one are skipped and counted. Forward F = S_raw e^{rT} - PV(dividends projected from the DoltHub dividend table), with S_raw the DoltHub raw close and r = DTB3. Drop pairs with a zero bid, spread/mid > 50%, or |K/S - 1| > 5%. Form quintiles weekly and enter at the next session's close; 5-session returns come from DoltHub total returns. Costs: 10 bp per side on turnover; borrow at 50 bp/yr, or 5%/yr in the top published FINRA days-to-cover decile. Universe, raw-close and delisting rules as in rv-minus-iv-spread-sp500-xs. The verdict is recorded on T-531.
final.data: DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain (single names, weekly, to fetch); DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks ohlcv/split/dividend (to fetch); fja-sp500-components; fja-sp500-ticker-spells; wikipedia-sp500-changes; finra-short-interest; sec-companyfacts; french-ff5-daily; french-momentum-daily; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of (T-531's rule, tightened): full-sample mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 by Newey-West and the bootstrap after 10 bp per side; both half means > 0; DSR >= 0.95. A historical pass counts as an in-period replication of the preprint. Capital requires a separately registered forward test on DoltHub snapshots after 2026-10-20.
final.controls: T-531's: drop names with put IV - call IV > 5 points in the top DTC decile (borrow proxy); a size- and momentum-neutral version; a random-quintile placebo. Also: a vendor-IV version; long-only top quintile minus the universe (Alpaca); the 21-session hold (counted in the DSR); quintiles only.

rows.name: Individual option volatility smirk predicts lower returns (Xing-Zhang-Zhao) - decayed
rows.source_notes: XZZ, JFQA 45(3) 641-662 (2010), on repec: steepest-smirk stocks underperform the least pronounced by 10.9%/year risk-adjusted, predictability lasts at least 6 months, and steep-smirk firms have the worst earnings shocks the next quarter. OSAP skew1: XZZ 2010, sample 1996-2005, equal-weighted quintiles, 0.64, t 2.19, predictability 2_likely, replication quality 2_fair, 'port sort weekly'; its definition is a near-the-money variant. Li-Wang (read in full) define smirk as OTM put IV (0.80 <= K/S <= 0.95) minus ATM call IV (0.95-1.05). Univariate 21-day coefficients: -0.0234 (t -5.5) 2015-19, -0.0150 (-4.2) 2020-22, -0.0060 (-1.5) 2023-26. At 63 days, 2023-26 is +0.0156 (t +2.1). Multivariate 2023-26 is +0.016 (t 2.6). The only portfolio sort, 2015-2017, gives -0.409% per 21 days. All of these are as claimed.
rows.replication_concerns: The smirk decays monotonically and flips sign in the preprint's own data. Its panel has firm fixed effects and no firm controls (see the CW row). Mandel's index skew tests all failed (T-52, T-227, T-138), and T-228 shows OTM puts carry an insurance premium, so a steep smirk is partly a premium rather than information. The row's value is as a control variable and a decay record, not as a strategy.
rows.data_notes: DoltHub single-name chains reach K/S of about 0.7-1.3 in the front expiries (AAPL strikes 100-190 at spot about 146 on 2023-01-27; CPB 35-66). An OTM put inside 0.80-0.95 exists for liquid names. The 2019 chains are thinner, at about 11 strikes a side. No single-name chains are archived, so it shares the fetch with the CW, skewness and term rows. Delisted-inclusive raw prices come from DoltHub stocks.
rows.lookahead_risks: The same as the CW row: forward from dividends, not parity; raw closes; month-end snapshot on or before the session; stale snapshots; delisting returns. The cross-checker's 0.925 target moneyness departs from XZZ (put nearest 0.95, call nearest 1.00), which is a hidden parameter choice.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain at month-ends (about 92 dates; shared fetch). DoltHub stocks prices.

final.claim: Month-end 2019-02..2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members with DoltHub chains, SMIRK = IV of the OTM put with K/S nearest 0.95 (within 0.80-0.95) minus IV of the call with K/S nearest 1.00 (within 0.95-1.05), both in the listed expiry nearest 30 DTE within 10-60 (XZZ's definition). The equal-weight portfolio long the lowest and short the highest SMIRK quintile, entered at the next session's close and held 21 sessions, earns a positive mean net return over the full period and in each half. The pre-registered expectation is that it fails in 2023-2026.
final.statistic: (a) Mean 21-session long-short net return, with a Newey-West t (lag 2) and a studentized block bootstrap (6-month blocks), one-sided; per-half means. (b) Descriptive: the 2023-2026 mean minus the 2019-2022 mean, with a block-bootstrap CI. A Fama-MacBeth slope is reported with the call-put spread, the OTM-IV skewness proxy, ATM IV, RV, size and momentum as controls. DSR is over the family.
final.null: (a) The full-sample mean <= 0, or either half's mean <= 0.
final.procedure: Pipeline, universe, dividend-projected forward (not parity-implied), costs and point-in-time rules as in t531-call-put-iv-spread-dolthub, using the latest snapshot that quotes a session on or before each month's last NYSE session. IVs are European Black-Scholes values recomputed from mids. Names with no put inside 0.80-0.95 or no call inside 0.95-1.05 are dropped and counted. A delta-defined variant (vendor put delta nearest -0.20) is reported and counted in the DSR.

rows.name: Risk-neutral skewness (OTM IV skewness / BKM) predicts lower stock returns
rows.source_notes: Li-Wang was read in full HTML. Their 'rns_bkm' is explicitly a proxy, not the BKM estimator: the cross-strike third central moment of OTM IVs divided by the cube of their sample SD, with at least five OTM strikes per firm-day. Univariate 21-day coefficients: -0.0030 (t -13.1) full, -0.0028 (-10.5) 2015-19, -0.0047 (-12.2) 2020-22, -0.0040 (-11.7) 2023-26. 63-day: -0.0081 (-16.5) full, -0.0104 (-14.3) 2023-26. 1-day: -1e-4 (t -3.3). Multivariate 2023-26: -0.0036 (t -8.8). All as claimed. There are no portfolio sorts or costs. Conrad-Dittmar-Ghysels was not opened (sign from memory only). Neuhierl et al. could not be fetched (403/Anubis). The web-search budget is exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: The mechanism in the candidate is likely wrong. The proxy is the skewness of IV VALUES across strikes, which is high when a few wing strikes carry much higher IVs than the rest on EITHER wing. A steep put smirk raises it as much as a rich call wing, so it is not risk-neutral skewness and does not identify lottery-like right skew. Its negative coefficient may be the XZZ smirk effect or a smile-convexity or strike-coverage effect. The t-statistics grow with horizon (-3.3 at 1 day to -16.5 at 63), consistent with overlap inflation in daily-sampled overlapping returns. Firm fixed effects add look-ahead. Mandel's index skew tests failed (T-52, T-227, T-138). The 2023-2026 window is where the preprint motivated selection, so the historical run is an in-period replication.
rows.data_notes: DoltHub chains in the expiry nearest 30 DTE list about 10-11 strikes a side in 2019 (AAPL/CPB 2019-03-02: 22 rows per expiry) and about 17-27 a side from 2020 (2023-01-30: 48-50 rows per expiry). Five OTM strikes in total is usually met, but strike spacing and range vary across names and price levels, which mechanically moves the proxy. BKM truncation is severe with about 12 OTM strikes. Prices come from DoltHub stocks (delisted-inclusive).
rows.lookahead_risks: As in the CW row: forward from dividends, raw closes, month-end snapshot rules, stale snapshots, delisting returns. Also, the proxy depends on which strikes the vendor lists that day, which is a data-generation artefact rather than information. Overlapping 63-session cohorts need overlap-robust SEs.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain at month-ends (shared fetch). DoltHub stocks prices.

final.claim: Month-end 2019-02..2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members with at least 5 OTM strikes (puts K < F, calls K > F, F the dividend forward) in the DoltHub expiry nearest 30 DTE (14-60), the equal-weight portfolio long the lowest and short the highest quintile of the cross-strike sample skewness of those OTM IVs (Li-Wang's proxy) earns a positive mean net return over the full period and in each half. BKM model-free skewness (trapezoid over listed OTM strikes, no extrapolation) and the 63-session hold are diagnostics only and count in the DSR together with the family.
final.null: The full-sample mean <= 0, or either half's mean <= 0, or the Fama-MacBeth slope >= 0.
final.procedure: Pipeline, universe, dividend-projected forward, costs and point-in-time rules as in t531-call-put-iv-spread-dolthub, at month-end snapshots. OTM IVs are recomputed from mids. The proxy is the sample skewness of the OTM IV values. Two-sided p is reported because the sign is contested. No mechanism is asserted: the proxy is not a left/right risk-neutral skew measure. The 63-session cohorts are overlapping Jegadeesh-Titman portfolios with Newey-West lag 3.
final.data: DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain (single names, month-ends, to fetch); DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks ohlcv/split/dividend (to fetch); fja-sp500-components; fja-sp500-ticker-spells; wikipedia-sp500-changes; sec-companyfacts; finra-short-interest; french-ff5-daily; french-momentum-daily; fred-DTB3
