The pass now requires survival against the smirk and the strike-coverage controls, and the 5-strike rule matches the source.

rows.name: Monthly changes in call and put implied vol predict stock returns (An-Ang-Bali-Cakici)
rows.source_notes: NBER w19590 (October 2013; JF 2014, 69(5)): large increases in call IV over the past month predict high returns, put IV increases predict low returns, the decile spreads are about 1%/month, and they persist up to six months. The CXO summary of the 2012 version covers 1996-01..2008-09, with an equal-weighted quintile spread of 0.97%/month gross that persists at least three months; the predictability comes from idiosyncratic volatility, and CXO flags data-snooping. OSAP rows confirmed (1996-2011, equal-weighted deciles): dVolCall 1.09 (t 3.45), dVolPut 0.42 (t 2.03, 2_likely), dCPVolSpread 1.68 (t 6.77, sign -1). OSAP computes these on the OptionMetrics surface at 30 days and delta 0.5. These are the original paper's figures, not OSAP's own estimates. No post-2011 evidence was found, and the search budget is exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: There is no out-of-sample evidence after 2011. The strength reported is equal-weighted, so small caps dominate, while Mandel's executable universe is large caps. The signal is the change in the CW spread (T-531), so it must add something beyond the level. Data-snooping across call, put and spread variants was flagged by CXO.
rows.data_notes: In the archived dolt-volhistory rows, vendor iv_month_ago is non-null for every row 2019-2022, for 1,299 of 1,449 rows in 2023, and for none in 2024-2026, so lagged snapshots are required. The three listed expiries at month-ends (for example 11/25/46, 14/28/49, 16/30/51 DTE) bracket 30 days, so constant-30-day interpolation in total variance is feasible. The cross-checker's 'nearest >= 21 DTE expiry' would instead compare different expiries a month apart.
rows.lookahead_risks: Using the nearest-expiry ATM IV on two dates confounds the roll from about 30 to 25 DTE and the term-structure kinks (earnings in one expiry) with IV changes; interpolate to constant 30 days. The ATM strike must be chosen on each date's own dividend forward. Use raw closes and delisting rules as in the other rows. The blended vendor iv_current stage-1 has an ambiguous sign and only adds a DSR trial without being able to pass, so it is removed.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain at month-ends (shared fetch). DoltHub stocks prices. 8-K item dates for the earnings flag (SEC refetch).

final.claim: Month-end 2019-03..2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 members with DoltHub chains on both month-end snapshots, dCP is the one-month change in the constant-30-day ATM call IV minus the constant-30-day ATM put IV. Each IV is interpolated in total variance between the two listed expiries bracketing 30 days, at the strike nearest that date's dividend forward. The value-weighted portfolio long the top and short the bottom dCP quintile, entered at the next session's close and held 21 sessions, earns a positive mean net return over the full period and in each half.
final.statistic: Value-weighted mean monthly long-short net return, with a Newey-West t (lag 2) and a studentized block bootstrap (6-month blocks), one-sided. Also: per-half means; the equal-weighted version; cumulative months 2-6 for persistence. A Fama-MacBeth slope controls for the LEVEL of the call-put spread, the change in RV, size and momentum. DSR is over the family.
final.procedure: Pipeline, universe, dividend-projected forward, raw-close, costs and point-in-time rules as in t531-call-put-iv-spread-dolthub. IVs are recomputed from mids. Names missing either month-end snapshot, or with no pair of expiries bracketing 30 DTE, are dropped and counted. Names with a projected 8-K 2.02 date inside either date's interpolation window are flagged and reported separately. Market caps come from sec-companyfacts shares x raw close, point in time. No vendor iv_month_ago is used.
final.data: DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain (single names, month-ends, to fetch); DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks ohlcv/split/dividend (to fetch); fja-sp500-components; fja-sp500-ticker-spells; wikipedia-sp500-changes; sec-companyfacts; finra-short-interest; french-ff5-daily; french-momentum-daily; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: value-weighted full-sample mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 by Newey-West and the bootstrap; both half means > 0; the Fama-MacBeth slope on dCP stays positive with t > 1.65 when the level of the call-put spread is a control; DSR >= 0.95.

rows.reason: The sources are verified, but there is no post-2011 evidence. The fix is constant-maturity interpolation so that roll and term structure are not read as IV changes, removing the uninformative vendor-IV stage, and requiring the change to add to the CW level.

rows.name: Single-stock IV term-structure slope predicts stock returns
rows.source_notes: Li-Wang (read in full) define ts_slope_30_60 as mean ATM IV at 46-75 days minus mean ATM IV at 15-45 days (calendar or trading days not specified). Univariate 21-day coefficients: +0.0106 (t 4.8) full, +0.0091 (3.1) 2015-19, +0.0106 (3.8) 2020-22, +0.0118 (3.7) 2023-26. Multivariate: +0.019 (6.4) full, +0.016 (3.3) 2023-26. All as claimed. Their controls are firm and date fixed effects and option liquidity only, with no earnings separation, no sorts and no costs. Park, Kim and Kim (J. Futures Markets, vlex) was not opened, so that 2000-2013 support is unverified. The search budget is exhausted.

The preprint's firm fixed effects and overlap problems apply, as in the CW row. The 2023-2026 window is where the preprint motivated selection, so the historical run is an in-period replication. T-53 and T-535 (index curves mean-revert) say nothing about stock drift.
rows.data_notes: DoltHub probes show three listed expiries per name at month-ends: AAPL/CPB 2021-06-30 at 16/30/51 DTE, 2023-01-30 at 11/25/46, 2024-05-31 at 14/28/49, 2025-06-30 at 11/25/46, 2026-09-30 at 16/30/51, and 2019-03-02 at 13/27/47. rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain at month-ends (shared fetch). A SEC submissions refetch keeping 8-K 'items'. DoltHub stocks prices.

final.null: Non-earnings full-sample mean <= 0, or either half's mean <= 0.

rows.name: IV term-structure slope predicts single-stock straddle returns (Vasquez)
rows.source_notes: Vasquez, JFQA 52(6) 2727-2754 (December 2017, Cambridge abstract): straddle portfolios with high term-structure slopes outperform low-slope portfolios, and the result is not explained by traditional or higher-order option factors or by jump risk. The CXO summary of the October 2011 working paper: January 1996 to June 2007; ATM options at moneyness 0.95-1.05; about 260 stocks a month; decile slopes from -15.0% to +8.5%; long-short straddles 27.1%/month gross (14.8% long, 12.2% short); 81% positive months; 12.3%/month net at 1.1x the bid-ask spread. Returns are on option price, not margin, and the sample excludes 2008. Jones and Wang was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The sample is pre-2008 and returns are measured per premium. Every term-structure-conditioned vol trade Mandel ran failed: T-262 (BTC calendars), T-143 and T-144 (SPY calendars by regime). T-53 and T-535 support only the short-front leg in inversion. The short leg carries jump risk that requires laddering (child Hurst). Full-spread fills on single names will be costly.
rows.data_notes: The post-expiry Monday DoltHub listing has a front expiry at about 25 DTE and a later one at about 53 (AAPL/CPB 2023-01-23: 11/25/53). Bid and ask exist. The raw-close bug of the Goyal-Saretto row applies: daily-history close is split-adjusted for later splits.
rows.lookahead_risks: Settle at intrinsic on the RAW expiry close. Fill at the next snapshot's quotes. Earnings before the front expiry is the dominant confound and needs the 8-K items refetch. Corporate actions inside the hold drop the name.
rows.missing_data: Single-name DoltHub option_chain on post-expiry and expiry-day snapshots (the same fetch as Goyal-Saretto). The SEC 8-K items refetch. DoltHub stocks prices.

final.claim: At the first DoltHub snapshot after each standard monthly expiry 2019-03..2026-09, the universe is point-in-time S&P 500 members with a liquid front expiry (21-45 DTE; both legs bid > $0.10 with spread/mid < 25%) and a later listed expiry at 40-60 DTE. SLOPE = ATM IV(later) - ATM IV(front). Buy front ATM straddles at the next snapshot's ask on the top SLOPE decile and sell them at its bid on the bottom decile, hold to front expiry and settle at intrinsic on the raw expiry close. On names with no projected earnings date before the front expiry, this earns a positive mean monthly net return per unit of premium over the full period and in each half.
final.statistic: Equal-weighted mean monthly long-short net return per unit premium, with a Newey-West t (lag 1) and a studentized circular block bootstrap (6-month blocks), one-sided. Per-half means, each leg and the per-Reg-T-margin return are reported. DSR is counted jointly with hv-iv-straddle-xs-sp500 as one option-return family.
final.null: Earnings-free mean net return per unit premium <= 0.
final.procedure: Pipeline of hv-iv-straddle-xs-sp500: dividend forward, IVs recomputed from OTM-leg mids, liquidity filter, fills at the next snapshot, settlement at intrinsic on the raw expiry-session close. Corporate actions drop the name. The earnings flag is a projected 8-K 2.02 date (point in time) on or before the front expiry. Nothing is fitted.
final.data: DoltHub post-no-preference/options option_chain (single names, to fetch); SEC submissions JSON with 8-K items (to refetch); DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks ohlcv/split/dividend (to fetch); fja-sp500-components; fja-sp500-ticker-spells; wikipedia-sp500-changes; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: earnings-free full-sample net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 by Newey-West and the bootstrap; both half means > 0; the long leg alone has a net mean > 0; DSR >= 0.95 over the option-return family.
final.controls: Each leg separately; per Reg-T margin; a delta-hedged variant; the iron-fly short leg (executable on Alpaca); a vendor-IV version; a random placebo; deciles only.

rows.name: S&P variance risk premium predicts 1-6 month equity returns (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou)
rows.source_notes: The BTZ RFS 22(11) 2009 PDF was extracted. Table 2 covers January 1990 to December 2007, monthly, with Hodrick t-statistics. IV - RV slopes (t, adj R2%): 1 month 0.39 (1.76, 1.07); 3 months 0.47 (2.86, 6.82); 6 months 0.30 (2.15, 5.42); 9 months 0.17 (1.36, 2.30); 12 months 0.12 (1.00, 1.23). RV is the BACKWARD month of 22 x 78 five-minute squared returns. All as claimed. kahtongtan/variance-risk-premium README: 1990-2026 daily; 21-day z 0.41, R2 0.001; 63-day z 0.58, R2 0.004; winsorised at 1/99% z 1.91 with full-sample cutoffs (look-ahead); 63-day out-of-sample R2 -0.074; VRP -0.709 in April 2020. As claimed. Pyun (JFE 2019) abstract: proposes a beta-representation out-of-sample method. The specific claim that 'BTZ's predictability is weak out of sample' is not in the abstract and is unverified. Bollerslev-Marrone-Xu-Zhou was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The published out-of-sample record is poor (the 2026 replication's R2 is -0.074). Every SPY timing rule Mandel tested failed (T-318, T-561, T-458). T-580, which the cross-checker listed as untested, is now NOT SUPPORTED: no options-implied ML cell (vrp_spx among its F3 features) passed development, with a best DSR of 0.368. T-235: the IV-RV gap did not time variance returns. The VRP collapses in crises and is followed by rallies, so a clipped timing rule goes flat before rebounds.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX-history: 1990-01-02..2026-10-14, observed 21:15 UTC, available 21:30 UTC. daily-history--GSPC: 1927-12-30..2026-10-14. daily-history-SPY: 1993-01-29..2026-10-14 (Yahoo bars stamped at the open, available the next day). fred-DTB3: 1954-01-04..2026-10-13. 5-minute RV is not archived, so close-to-close is used.
rows.lookahead_risks: The VIX closes at 16:15 ET, after the SPX close at 16:00 ET, so positions enter at the next session's close. VIX for 1990-2003 is Cboe's reconstruction (methodology change in 2003). Yahoo daily bars are stamped by open time, so use the close only as of that session's end. Winsorising with full-sample cutoffs is look-ahead and is banned. The HAR variant must be refitted on data before t only. ^GSPC price returns (without dividends) are used for the forecasting regression and SPY total returns for the trading rule, as declared.
rows.missing_data: None for the registered version.

final.claim: Monthly at each month's last NYSE session t, VRP_t = (VIX close_t/100)^2/12 minus the sum of squared ^GSPC daily log returns over the 21 sessions ending at t. An expanding OLS from 1990-01 (each fit uses only returns ending by t) forecasts the ^GSPC excess return over DTB3 from the close of t+1 over the next 63 sessions. Over forecasts 2008-01..2026-06 it achieves a positive Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with Clark-West p < 0.05. In addition, the SPY timing rule built on the forecast beats buy-and-hold on Sharpe.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 against the prevailing mean, with the Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (Newey-West lag equal to the overlap) at 21, 63 and 126 sessions. The Sharpe difference between the timing rule and buy-and-hold uses a studentized circular block bootstrap (12-month blocks). The timing rule sets the SPY weight to clip(forecast / expanding mean excess return, 0, 1.5), with the rest in bills, 2 bp per rebalance, and leverage financed at DTB3 + 50 bp. DSR is over 3 horizons x 2 RV definitions (trailing RV; a HAR(1,5,22) forecast refitted monthly on prior data).
final.null: Out-of-sample R^2 <= 0 (Clark-West t <= 0) at 63 sessions, or a Sharpe difference <= 0.
final.procedure: VIX close is taken at its 21:30 UTC availability. RV comes from ^GSPC closes. Positions and targets start at the close of t+1. Fit an expanding OLS against the prevailing-mean benchmark. No winsorising. The HAR variant counts as a trial but cannot stand in for the primary trailing-RV (BTZ-like) definition. 2015-2026 and ex-2020 are reported, never as the verdict. The premium's existence (T-48, T-540) is taken as given.
final.data: cboe-VIX-history; daily-history--GSPC; daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 at 63 sessions on the primary trailing-RV VRP; a Sharpe-difference lower 95% bound > 0; DSR >= 0.95 over the 6 trials.
final.controls: VIX-level-only and trailing-RV-only predictors (the VRP must beat both); the prevailing-mean benchmark; buy-and-hold at the same average exposure.

rows.name: Option-implied correlation (COR1M) predicts market returns up to one year
rows.source_notes: cepr.org DP12760 returned 403, so the primary was not read. The CXO summary (2017-03-02) of Buss, Schoenleber and Vilkov, 'Option-Implied Correlations, Factor Models, and Market Risk' (January 2017), confirms the substance. Sample: S&P 500 and S&P 100 from 1996, DJIA from 1997-10, sector ETFs from 1998-12, all through 2015-08. Implied correlation predicts index returns up to one year, more strongly than VRP beyond a quarter, and survives jointly with VRP. Value-weighted prediction is much stronger than equal-weighted. The signal comes mostly from predicting the dispersion of betas. CXO mentions NO out-of-sample tests, so the candidate's 'in and out of sample' is unverified. Results are gross with no trading tests, data-snooping across variants is a risk, and Cboe's indices use a different methodology (SPX plus the top-50 stocks). The working-paper title differs from the CEPR DP title cited. The search budget is exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: There is no independent replication. The out-of-sample claim is unconfirmed. Mandel's market-timing predictors all failed (T-318, T-458, T-561). T-580, now not supported, included iv_cor and iv_dspx features. Power is the binding limit: 2013-2026 holds about 27 independent 6-month windows. The Cboe COR1M definition differs from the paper's.
rows.data_notes: cboe-COR1M-history: 2006-01-03..2026-10-14 (5,228 rows). cboe-DSPX-history: 2014-06-19..2026-10-14. daily-history-SPY and fred-DTB3 are present. COR3M is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: COR1M closes at 16:15 ET, so trade at the next session's close. The pre-launch history is Cboe's backfill; the definition is Cboe's, not chosen by Mandel. Choosing among 3 horizons and 2 indices after seeing results is forking paths, so declare a primary horizon. The out-of-sample start (2013) must follow the 2006-2012 training window.
rows.missing_data: None for the COR1M primary. COR3M (free Cboe CSV) is not archived and not used.

final.claim: Monthly at each month's last NYSE session t, COR1M_t (Cboe, archived from 2006-01, its published definition including the backfill) forecasts the SPY total-return excess over DTB3 from the close of t+1 over the next 126 sessions, with a positive pre-registered slope. An expanding OLS trained from 2006-01 gives a positive Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 with Clark-West p < 0.05 over forecasts 2013-01..2026-03, and a positive out-of-sample R^2 over 2019-01..2026-03.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 and the Clark-West t (Newey-West lag 126 sessions, equivalent to Hodrick for the overlap) at 63, 126 (primary) and 252 sessions. Fitted slopes below zero are replaced by the prevailing mean (Campbell-Thompson restriction, declared now). DSR is over 3 horizons x {COR1M, DSPX}. DSPX gets its own expanding window from 2014-06, out of sample from 2017-01.
final.procedure: COR1M close is available at 21:30 UTC; positions and targets start at the close of t+1. One index definition. No CRP or COR3M variants. SPY adjclose total return in excess of DTB3 is compounded over the target window.
final.data: cboe-COR1M-history; cboe-DSPX-history; cboe-VIX-history; daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 at 126 sessions for COR1M; out-of-sample R^2 > 0 over 2019-01..2026-03; DSR >= 0.95 over the 6 trials. The 'incremental to VRP' claim is recorded only if the encompassing test also rejects the VRP-only forecast at p < 0.05.

rows.name: VIX futures basis (daily roll) predicts VIX futures returns, not spot VIX (Simon-Campasano)
rows.source_notes: The EFMA PDF returned 503 twice, so the primary was not read. Two secondary sources agree on the rules. Quantpedia: nearest VX with >= 10 trading days; daily roll = (F1 - VIX) / business days to settlement; short above +0.10, long below -0.10; 5-day hold; ES hedge from regressions on ES % changes and their product with days to settlement; about 19.67%/year on 5x margin over 2007-2011; about $140 per round trip; confidence 'moderate'; Quantpedia's own out-of-sample backtest is 'slightly negative'. CXO (2012-07-06, SSRN June 2012 version): sample 2006-2011; hedge ratio fixed per trade (about 1 ES per VX, range 0.5-2); average net $539 per contract on shorts and $908 on longs; about 53%/year on minimum margin, about 20% at 5x; costs about $60 per complete trade; about HALF the profit came from 2008; and 'since mid-2010 the strategy has produced little or no profit'.
rows.replication_concerns: The decay is documented by the source summaries themselves. The rule made little or nothing after mid-2010, and Mandel's VX data (2013-05 onward) lie entirely in that era. The prior should fall from 0.20 to about 0.08. Mandel's tradable VX siblings all failed (T-160, T-379, T-435, T-242), and T-580's vx_basis feature did not pass. T-53 and T-535 (VIX falls more than the curve implies after backwardation) argue against the long leg. Tail months (2018-02, 2020-03) decide the halves test.
rows.data_notes: cboe-vx-futures: 3,375 days with a settle, 2013-05-20..2026-10-14; 852 zero-settle rows in early 2013 are dropped. With the front contract at >= 10 trading days (VIX-history trading calendar), there are 1,037 short-signal days (roll > +0.10) and 184 long-signal days (< -0.10) out of 3,364. That gives about 200-250 non-overlapping 5-day trades, of which only about 35-40 are long, so the long leg is underpowered. daily-history-ES-F (Yahoo ES=F, 6,584 rows) is a continuous front series with unadjusted roll gaps. SVXY runs from 2011-10 and VXX from 2018-01; VIXY is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The VX settlement is fixed at 15:00 CT and the VIX closes at 16:15 ET, so the signal is known after day t; enter at the t+1 settle. The hedge ratio uses only the prior 252 sessions and stays fixed per trade. The ES=F continuous series has roll gaps and a different close time, so hedge with SPY. Do not roll inside a hold. Count days to settlement in trading days (CXO), not calendar days. The ETPs hold a constant-maturity F1/F2 mix, so the ETP variant is a different instrument. Cboe CFE is not on Mandel's venue list.
rows.missing_data: None for the futures test. VIXY and SVIX histories (free Yahoo) only if wanted; SVXY and VXX are archived.

final.claim: On Cboe VX settlements 2013-05-20..2026-10-14, let F1 be the nearest monthly VX with >= 10 trading days to final settlement, and roll_t = (F1 settle_t - VIX close_t) / trading days to F1 settlement. Short one F1 when roll_t > +0.10 and buy one when roll_t < -0.10. Enter at the settle of t+1, hold 5 trading days in the same contract, and hedge with SPY at a ratio fixed per trade from the prior 252 sessions only. This earns a positive mean net P&L per trade after $140 per round trip (VX plus hedge).
final.statistic: Mean net P&L per trade ($ per VX contract), pooled over the 5 start offsets of the non-overlapping 5-day grid (house rule 10), with a Newey-West t and a studentized circular block bootstrap (blocks of 12 trades), one-sided. Each leg (short in contango, long in backwardation) is reported separately, with Sharpe, max drawdown and 1% CVaR. DSR counts T-160, T-379, T-435 and T-242 as prior VX-family trials plus this row, vix-futures-premium-falls-with-risk and vix-curve-pc2-vx-returns.
final.procedure: The trading-day calendar comes from cboe-VIX-history; Settle = 0 rows are dropped. Signal at the close of t, entry at the settle of t+1, exit at the settle of t+6. No new entry while a trade is open on that offset grid. Hedge ratio: OLS of daily F1 settle changes on SPY % changes and on SPY % changes x trading days to settlement, over the 252 sessions before entry, fixed for the trade (Simon-Campasano). The hedge trades SPY at its close; ES=F is a reported sensitivity only. Costs: $140 per round trip all in, with CXO's $60 as a sensitivity. Halves split at 2019-12-31.
final.data: cboe-vx-futures; cboe-VIX-history; daily-history-SPY; daily-history-SVXY; daily-history-VXX; daily-history-ES-F (sensitivity only); fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: pooled mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 by Newey-West and the bootstrap; both half means > 0; DSR >= 0.95 over the VX family. Because Cboe CFE is not on the venue list, a pass licenses only a separately registered paper forward test of the ETP form.
final.controls: Unhedged; always-short F1; the ETP form (short signal = long SVXY, long signal = long VXX, SPY hedge, 5 bp per trade); results excluding 2018-02 and 2020-03, reported only; one threshold (0.10); the $60 cost sensitivity.

rows.reason: The rules are verified through two summaries, but the source itself reports no profit after mid-2010, which covers all of Mandel's data. The registration is kept as a cheap decay test with the prior lowered, an SPY hedge (ES=F roll gaps), the long leg reported separately, and min_n set from the measured signal count.

rows.name: The VIX futures premium falls when risk rises and predicts VX returns (Cheng)
rows.source_notes: Cheng, RFS 32(1) 180-227 (2019), on repec: ex ante premiums 'reliably predict ex post returns to VIX futures with a coefficient near one'; they fall or stay flat when ex ante risk measures rise, which the author argues is not a measurement artefact; falling premiums predict higher ex post market and investment risk; the explanation offered is falling hedging demand (premiums and trader exposures fall together). The sample is not stated on the page. The Risk.net and ISCTE sources were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Claim (a) is close to mechanical if the expectation model is well specified, so it mainly tests that the AR model is not badly biased. Claim (b) is the novel one. Mandel's verdicts split: T-535 (19 of 23 spike events below the forward) leans against it, though that F is the SPX variance forward, not VX; T-159's high-VIX tercile point estimate leans for it. If VIX is used as a risk proxy in (b), P_t is built from VIX, so the slope is mechanically correlated.
rows.data_notes: cboe-vx-futures holds expiry-day rows whose 'settle' is the exiring contract's Cboe FINAL settlement value (165 rows, usable from 2013-05-22). For example, 2024-02-14 settled at 14.32 while the VIX opened at 15.38, and 2013-10-16 settled at 17.21 against an open of 17.14. The cross-checker's 'VIX open as a SOQ proxy' is avoidable and can be more than 1 point off. VIX3M runs from 2009-09-18, VVIX from 2006-03-06, VIX from 1990, and VX from 2013-05-20.
rows.lookahead_risks: E_t[VIX_T] must be refitted on data to t only, starting 2009-09-18. The VX settle (15:00 CT) comes before the VIX close (16:15 ET), so compute P_t with the VIX close and the F1 settle of the same day, treated as known after the close. Daily overlapping observations with horizons up to about 30 sessions need more than NW lag 21, so sample one observation per settlement cycle. Use the final settlement value, not the VIX open.
rows.missing_data: None. The VIX SOQ is not needed, because the expiring contract's final settle is in the bundle.

final.claim: Once per VX settlement cycle, 2013-05..2026-10, on the first session with <= 21 trading days to F1's final settlement: P_t = F1 settle_t - E_t[VIX at settlement]. E_t comes from an AR(1) on daily log VIX plus log(VIX/VIX3M), fitted on an expanding window from 2009-09-18 ending at t and iterated to the settlement date, with a lognormal half-variance correction. (a) The realised short-futures return F1_t - FinalSettle (the expiring contract's Cboe final settlement value) has a positive slope on P_t whose 95% CI contains 1. (b) P_t has a non-positive slope on standardised VVIX and on trailing 21-session SPY realised vol, each fitted alone. Both (a) and (b) must hold in 2013-05..2019-12 and in 2020-01..2026-10.
final.statistic: (a) OLS slope across settlement cycles, with Newey-West SE (lag 1) and a studentized bootstrap resampling cycles. (b) OLS slopes of P_t on z(VVIX) and on z(RV21), with Newey-West SE. Secondary: the Sharpe difference of short F1 only when P_t is above its expanding median versus always short, with costs as in vx-daily-roll-hedged-carry-2013.
final.null: (a) Slope <= 0 in either half, or 1 outside the CI. (b) Either slope > 0 in either half.
final.procedure: One observation per cycle, so overlap is avoided. The VIX level is excluded from (b) because E_t is built from VIX. The raw basis F1 - VIX is reported as a benchmark in (a). A HAR forecast in place of the AR(1) is a reported control only. Excluding 2020-02..04 is reported.
final.data: cboe-vx-futures (incl. final settlement rows); cboe-VIX-history; cboe-VIX3M-history; cboe-VVIX-history; daily-history-SPY
final.pass: (a) Slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 and 1 inside the 95% CI, in both halves; and (b) both slopes <= 0 in both halves. A pass is a mechanism verdict only; any trading rule on P needs its own registration with DSR over the VX family.
final.controls: The raw basis in place of P; the HAR forecast; the ex-2020 crash run; the T-534/T-535 consistency report.

rows.reason: The source is verified. The fixes are the exact final settlement value already in the bundle (in place of the VIX-open proxy), one non-overlapping observation per cycle, and dropping VIX from the risk proxies in (b), where it would be mechanically tied to P.

rows.name: VIX term-structure slope (PC2) predicts variance-asset returns (Johnson)
rows.source_notes: Johnson, JFQA 52(6) 2461-2490 (2017), Cambridge abstract: SLOPE, the second principal component of the VIX term structure, predicts excess returns of synthetic S&P variance swaps, VIX futures and S&P straddles at all maturities, incrementally to other VRP proxies. The CXO summary (2015-01-28): daily 1996-2013; the term structure is built from SPX options at 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months; next-day lowest-minus-highest quintile spreads of 0.29% to 1.81% across 18 asset/maturity pairs, 17 of 18 positive in the lowest quintile; gross.
rows.replication_concerns: Mandel's 4-tenor PCA (VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VIX6M) is NOT Johnson's curve: it adds a 9-day tenor and lacks the 2-, 9- and 12-month tenors, so its PC2 is a different object. The trading form, short vol only in steep contango, already failed (T-435, T-379), and T-580's iv_term and iv_term9 features did not pass. T-159 and T-530 show the slope adds little to the VIX level.
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX9D-history: 2011-01-04..2026-10-14. VIX3M: 2009-09-18. VIX6M: 2008-01-02. cboe-vx-futures from 2013-05-20, so the CM VX target starts then and the discovery window for target (i) is 2013-05..2018-12. VXX runs from 2018-01-25, so target (ii) has no discovery window before confirmation. SVXY runs from 2011-10. VIX1Y is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: VIX-family indices close at 16:15 ET, after the 16:00 ET ETP close and the 15:00 CT VX settle. 'Next-day' returns measured close-to-close from day t would carry a 15-minute look-ahead, so returns must start at the t+1 close or settle. PCA standardisation and quintile cutoffs must be expanding, and PC2's sign must be normalised point in time.
rows.missing_data: VIX1Y is not archived (it would be needed for a closer Johnson curve; not used).

final.claim: Daily 2013-05..2026-10, PC2 is the sign-normalised second principal component of standardised log VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M and VIX6M closes, with the PCA and standardisation on an expanding window from 2011-01 ending at t; higher means steeper contango. Over 2019-01..2026-10, the mean return from the t+1 settle to the t+6 settle on the 30-day constant-maturity VX (interpolated from F1/F2 settles) is higher in the lowest PC2 quintile than in the highest, with quintile cutoffs from data before t. In addition, PC2 keeps a negative predictive slope with log(VIX/VIX3M) and log VIX in the regression.
final.statistic: The lowest-minus-highest quintile mean and the predictive slope, with Newey-West t (lag 5). Targets: (i) the 30-day CM VX settle-to-settle return; (ii) the VXX adjclose return from the t+1 close to the t+6 close (SVXY is a mirror, not a trial). Bonferroni over the two targets. Trading form: short CM VX (or long SVXY) only in the top two PC2 quintiles versus always, at $140 per round trip or 5 bp for ETPs. DSR is over the VX family (T-53, T-159, T-160, T-379, T-435, T-530, vx-daily-roll-hedged-carry-2013, vix-futures-premium-falls-with-risk).
final.null: Confirmation quintile spread <= 0 for both targets.
final.procedure: The four tenors are pre-registered; the curve is not Johnson's six-tenor SPX curve, and that is stated. PCA uses expanding standardisation, with the sign fixed so that the loading on log VIX6M minus the loading on log VIX9D is > 0. Returns start one session after the signal. Discovery is 2013-05..2018-12 for (i) only; confirmation is 2019-01..2026-10.
final.data: cboe-VIX9D-history; cboe-VIX-history; cboe-VIX3M-history; cboe-VIX6M-history; cboe-vx-futures; daily-history-VXX; daily-history-SVXY
final.pass: All of: confirmation spread > 0 with Bonferroni one-sided p < 0.05 for (i) or (ii); the PC2 slope is negative with one-sided p < 0.05 controlling for log(VIX/VIX3M) and log VIX; trading-form DSR >= 0.95 over the VX family.
final.controls: VIX/VIX3M alone (T-435's gate); VIX level alone; PC1; a random placebo.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but Mandel's archived tenors make a different PC2 than Johnson's. The fixes are a target window that actually exists in the archive, an encompassing condition against T-435's ratio, and removal of the same-day close look-ahead in 'next-day' returns.

rows.name: VVIX predicts lower returns on tail hedges (SPX/SPY OTM puts, VIX calls)
rows.source_notes: The Park FEDS 2013-54 PDF was extracted. Sample: May 1, 2006 to January 31, 2012. A 1-SD VVIX increase lowers next-day SPX put returns by 1.32-2.19% (t -4.48 to -5.54) and VIX call returns by 0.68-1.01%. The effect persists 3-4 weeks, and VVIX's weekly autocorrelation is 0.759. All as claimed. Critical detail the candidate missed: these are RESIDUAL option returns. They are delta-hedged excess returns (OptionMetrics delta, 8-90 DTE, SPX moneyness bins 0.85-0.90/0.90-0.95/0.95-1.00) further regressed on CONTEMPORANEOUS changes in the underlying price and volatility, so the measured return is not tradable. CXO's summary of Huang and Shaliastovich (monthly 2006-02..2013-06) likewise concerns HEDGED S&P and VIX option returns (hedged VIX calls -0.57% to -1.41% a month, gross) and does not report index-return prediction. Neither source tests unhedged puts or a short put spread.
rows.replication_concerns: Raw put returns are dominated by SPY's direction, so a regression on unhedged returns tests something else. A conditional short put spread is a new claim with no published support. Mandel: T-229 (SKEW-timed put spreads) failed; T-243, T-536 and T-240 show VVIX sits below realised VIX vol; T-228 and T-131 show the put premium exists unconditionally. The confirmation window contains the 2024-08 and 2025-04 shocks.
rows.data_notes: dolt-chain-SPY has 1,232 quote days, 2019-02-08..2026-10-14: 47 in 2019 (Saturday snapshots quoting Friday), 145-149 a year in 2020-2023 (Mon/Wed/Fri), 175 in 2024, 244 in 2025 and 181 in 2026. Weekdays: Mon 305, Tue 107, Wed 334, Thu 111, Fri 375. 2,826 rows are stale. Chains carry bid, ask and vendor delta. cboe-VVIX-history runs 2006-03-06..2026-10-14; VIX, SKEW, SPY and DTB3 are present.
rows.lookahead_risks: VVIX closes at 16:15 ET (available 21:30 UTC), concurrent with the SPY option close, so it cannot be seen before trading at that close. Use VVIX from the session before the entry quote_date. Use quote_date, not snapshot_date, and skip stale snapshots. An expiry inside the hold settles at intrinsic on the raw SPY close. z-scores must use a trailing window only, and tercile cutoffs come from the training period only.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the SPY version. VIX option history (2 capture days) blocks the VIX-call half.

final.claim: Weekly 2019-02..2026-10 on dolt-chain-SPY, entering at each week's last quote day and exiting at the next week's last quote day, with z(VVIX) from the session before the entry quote_date. (a) The delta-hedged return of SPY OTM puts with K/S in 0.90-0.95, in the expiry nearest 30 DTE (14-60), falls with z(VVIX) after controlling for z(VIX) and trailing 21-session SPY RV. Returns are equal-weighted across strikes in the bin, mid-to-mid, hedged once with the vendor delta at the entry SPY close. (b) Over 2023-01..2026-10, selling the 5%/10% OTM put spread in that expiry at entry bid/ask only when z(VVIX) is in its 2019-2022 top tercile, and closing it at exit ask/bid, earns a positive net P&L per unit of max loss and more than the other weeks' short spreads.
final.statistic: (a) The z(VVIX) slope with Newey-West t (lag 2) on non-overlapping weekly observations, discovery 2019-2022 and confirmation 2023-2026. (b) The conditional mean net P&L per unit max loss and the top-minus-other-terciles difference, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (8-week blocks). DSR is over {raw z(VVIX), VVIX residual on VIX} x {(a), (b)}.
final.null: (a) Confirmation slope >= 0; or (b) conditional net P&L <= 0, or the difference <= 0.
final.procedure: z(VVIX) = (VVIX - its trailing 252-session mean) / SD. Strikes are chosen by K/S on the quote-day raw close. The delta hedge uses SPY adjclose with the vendor delta at entry. Hedged return = (P_exit - P_entry - delta x (S_exit - S_entry)) / P_entry, minus the bill rate. A missing exit snapshot uses the next within 3 sessions, otherwise the week is skipped and counted. An expiry inside the hold settles at intrinsic on the raw close. Mon/Wed/Fri spacing in 2020-2023 is accepted and stated.
final.data: dolt-chain-SPY; cboe-VVIX-history; cboe-VIX-history; cboe-SKEW-history; daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3
final.pass: All of: (a) confirmation slope negative with one-sided p < 0.05; (b) conditional short-spread net P&L > 0 and top-minus-other difference > 0, both with bootstrap lower bound > 0; DSR >= 0.95.
final.controls: Unconditional every-week short spread; VIX-only and SKEW-only terciles (the analogue of T-229); unhedged put returns reported; a random-tercile placebo; bid/ask fills only; the defined-risk spread is executable on Alpaca.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but its returns are hedged and residualised on contemporaneous moves, which the cross-checker's raw-put regression does not test. The fixes are a tradable delta-hedged target, a one-session VVIX lag, and an explicit condition that timing beats the unconditional short spread.

rows.name: Bitcoin option risk reversal (25-delta skew) predicts BTC returns
rows.source_notes: The main source (Neo, SMU dissertation, ink.library.smu.edu.sg/etd_coll/887) returned an empty page on two fetches, so neither the claimed t-statistics (1.91 univariate to 3.73 with 12 controls) nor the coefficient's sign could be confirmed; the candidate admits the sign is not in the abstract. The independent deribit-rr README was verified: about 4.5 years of monthly expiries; T-30 sign accuracy 33 of 56 (58.9%, p about 0.18); T-90 24 of 31, untested; RR-to-move correlation 0.076 (R2 about 0.006); accuracy does not improve at |RR| > 5%; the author concludes there is no predictive power. Deribit Insights (Amberdata, 2019-04..2022-12, mark-price P&L) was verified: selling the RR gave the best risk-adjusted returns, and the authors expect the edge to fade as institutions enter. That concerns the RR as a premium, not as a directional signal. The search budget is exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: The significance appears only with 12 controls (forking paths). The sign is unknown, so any pre-registered direction would be a guess. The only checkable independent evidence finds noise. Mandel and its children contradict it: T-423 and T-364 not supported; every crypto direction signal failed; T-578 had no crypto pass; the child Brier result shows Deribit prices carry nothing the Polymarket crowd lacks. T-257: 257 of 262 large-|RR| days were put-skewed, so the level has little sign variation.
rows.data_notes: deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC: 2,465,638 rows, days stored 2021-12-01..2026-10-14 (1,779), 07:00-09:00 UTC samples. coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD: 2019-01-01..2026-10-15. deribit-dvol-BTC-history: 2021-03-24..2026-10-15, available the next day. deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL: 2019-05..2026-10. deribit-quarterly-futures-btc: bars stamped at the open.
rows.lookahead_risks: Deribit candles and DVOL are stamped at the bar open, so a control keyed as a close leaks a day. The smile fit uses 07:00-09:00 UTC trades, so the signal is available at 09:00. Coinbase hourly bars are stamped at the start.
rows.missing_data: An accessible copy of the dissertation (to confirm the sign and specification). Deribit trades for 2021-04..2021-11 (optional).

final.claim: NOT FOR REGISTRATION unless the source is confirmed. If revived: daily 2021-12..2026-09, the 30-day constant-tenor 25-delta BTC risk reversal from the T-257 smile fit (available 09:00 UTC) has a non-zero slope, tested two-sided because the sign is unknown, on the Coinbase BTC-USD log return from 09:00 UTC to +7 days over 2024-01..2026-09, with DVOL (the previous day's bar), 7-day momentum, funding to 09:00 UTC and the quarterly basis as controls.
final.statistic: Newey-West slope t (lag 7) and rank IC; a long/flat rule in the direction of the discovery-period slope sign versus buy-and-hold on net Sharpe after 0.6% per round trip, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (30-day blocks); DSR over {30, 90-day tenor} x {1, 7, 30-day horizon} x {RR, butterfly} = 12.
final.procedure: Smiles as in T-257. Discovery 2021-12..2023-12 fixes the sign; confirmation 2024-01..2026-09 tests that sign one-sided.
final.data: deribit-option-trades-daily-BTC; coinbase-hourly-BTC-USD; deribit-dvol-BTC-history; deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL; deribit-quarterly-futures-btc
final.pass: Confirmation slope with the discovery sign at one-sided p < 0.05 with controls; net Sharpe difference lower 95% bound > 0; DSR >= 0.95.
final.controls: Random-sign placebo; DVOL-only and funding-only predictors; IBIT form at 10 bp per switch.

rows.reason: Dropped: the main source could not be read and the claim's sign is unknown, so any pre-registered direction would be a guess. The only verifiable independent evidence calls it noise, and every crypto direction test in Mandel and its children failed.

rows.name: BTC variance risk premium is larger in low-volatility regimes (selling vol pays more when DVOL is low)
rows.source_notes: Almeida, Grith, Miftachov and Wang, arXiv 2410.15195 (v1 2024-10-19, v2 2025-08-01), read in full HTML. Options 2017-07..2022-12 on a 27-day horizon. The trade counts are internally inconsistent (5.38M vs 7.83M). BVIX-based annualised VRP: overall 0.14 (0.72 - 0.58), high-vol 0.12 (0.86 - 0.74), low-vol 0.17 (0.46 - 0.29). The RND-based figures (0.07, 0.10, 0.04) are NOT in the text ('available upon request'), so those three candidate numbers are unverified. Critical: (1) regimes come from full-sample Ward clustering of risk-neutral densities, which is not point in time; (2) the physical variance is BACKWARD-looking (the past 27 days), so the low-vol regime's larger 'VRP' is partly mechanical, since trailing RV is low in calm regimes by construction. The paper does not show that implied exceeds FORWARD realised variance more in calm regimes. Deribit Insights (2019-04..2022-12, mark prices) was verified: IV above RV about 70% of the time, contango 77.5% of days, about +15 points in contango.
rows.replication_concerns: Only one unrefereed paper supports it, its sample ends in 2022, and its construction is backward-looking. Mandel leans the other way: T-246's halves give +0.1535 (2021-2023, higher vol) versus +0.0344 (2024-2026) in variance units, and T-256's low-DVOL long straddles did better (+29.2% vs +14.1%, n 18, inconclusive). The reverse result would be just as actionable for gating Hurst's IBIT ladder, which already gates on IV - RV >= 5 points rather than on the DVOL level.
rows.data_notes: deribit-dvol-BTC-history: 2,032 daily bars, 2021-03-24..2026-10-15, stamped at the open, available the next day 00:00 UTC. coinbase-daily-BTC-USD: 2015-07-20..2026-10-14, bars stamped at the start, available the next day. The first day with a trailing 365-day tercile is 2022-03-24. The last entry with 30 days of forward RV is 2026-09-14. deribit-dvol-ETH-history spans the same dates. fred-DTB3 is present.
rows.lookahead_risks: DVOL bar D (stamped D 00:00) closes at D+1 00:00, so the entry time is D+1 00:00 UTC. Forward RV must use Coinbase closes from bar D (the close at D+1 00:00) through bar D+30, exactly aligned to the entry time. Terciles must use the trailing 365 days only, not the full-sample clustering used in the source. Overlapping daily entries need blocks of at least 2x the horizon.
rows.missing_data: None for the registered test. The IBIT option-surface history for the executable form is recorded forward by Hurst only.

final.claim: Daily entries 2022-03-24..2026-09-14 at D+1 00:00 UTC. The BTC variance risk premium as a fraction of implied variance is ratio = 1 - RV_fwd / (DVOL_D/100)^2. DVOL_D is the close of the DVOL bar stamped D. RV_fwd is (365/30) x the sum of the 30 squared log returns of Coinbase BTC-USD daily closes from bar D through bar D+30. The ratio is higher on days whose DVOL_D is in the bottom tercile of its trailing 365 days than on top-tercile days.
final.statistic: The bottom-minus-top tercile mean ratio, pooled over every daily entry (all 30 start offsets, house rule 10), with a studentized circular block bootstrap (90-day blocks), plus per-half values. Also reported: the variance-unit difference, and the T-255 model-priced hedged short-straddle P&L per unit vega by tercile.
final.procedure: Terciles are point in time from trailing DVOL closes known at the entry time. Halves are 2022-03-24..2024-06-30 and 2024-07-01..2026-09-14. A reverse result (top > bottom with lower bound > 0) is recorded as the reverse finding, not a pass. Nothing is fitted.
final.data: deribit-dvol-BTC-history; coinbase-daily-BTC-USD; deribit-funding-BTC-PERPETUAL; deribit-dvol-ETH-history; fred-DTB3
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of (bottom - top) in ratio terms > 0, with both halves positive. Forward confirmation on Hurst's IBIT surface captures is required before any capital.
final.controls: Shuffled-tercile placebo; middle tercile reported; T-256's opposite claim read on the same terciles; ETH DVOL as an out-of-asset check (T-67); a gate on IV minus trailing RV >= 5 points (Hurst's) as a comparison.

rows.reason: The paper exists and its BVIX figures check out. But its regimes are full-sample clusters and its 'realised' variance is backward-looking, so the claimed regime gap is partly mechanical. The registration, with point-in-time terciles and exactly aligned forward RV, is the honest test, and Mandel's T-246 halves predict it fails.

knowledge.title: Options-implied information as a return predictor: implied volatility level, skew, term structure and the variance risk premium (literature survey, 1996-2026)
knowledge.markdown:
# Options-implied information as a return predictor: implied volatility level, skew, term structure and the variance risk premium (literature survey, 1996-2026)

- **Authors / kind:** 15 published strategies. Peer-reviewed: Bali-Hovakimian (Management Science 2009), Goyal-Saretto (JFE 2009), Cremers-Weinbaum and Xing-Zhang-Zhao (JFQA 2010), An-Ang-Bali-Cakici (JF 2014), Vasquez and Johnson (JFQA 2017), Cheng (RFS 2019) and Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou (BTZ; RFS 2009). Working papers: Buss-Schönleber-Vilkov, Simon-Campasano, Park (FEDS 2013-54), Almeida et al., and Li-Wang (arXiv 2608.26115), the only 2015-2026 re-estimation. Replications and summaries: Open Source Asset Pricing (OSAP), theses, GitHub backtests, CXO, Quantpedia.
- **Links:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26115 · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/master/SignalDoc.csv · https://public.econ.duke.edu/~boller/Published_Papers/rfs_09.pdf · https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2013/201354/201354pap.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.55 (25 of 39 cited sources opened, six of them in full text).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full text for Li-Wang, Almeida et al., BTZ Table 2, Park, a CBS thesis and the OSAP rows. Abstracts only for the other journal papers; practitioner summaries otherwise. Unreadable: CEPR DP12760, Simon-Campasano, Neuhierl et al., Neo's dissertation. The search budget ran out before targeted decay searches.
- **Selected because:** implied volatility, skew, term structure and the VRP are inputs in the user's training program. T-580's market-level options-implied ML family is not supported (best DSR 0.368), and no cross-sectional single-stock options signal has been tested: T-531 and T-193 are blocked.

## What it says

- **RV-minus-IV spread (Bali-Hovakimian).** Stocks whose implied vol is rich relative to 30-day realised vol earn more. The value-weighted quintile spread is 0.732%/month (t 2.9) over 1996-2004, the original figures that OSAP's replication matched. There is no evidence after 2004.
- **HV-minus-IV straddles (Goyal-Saretto).** Long straddles where options are cheap relative to historical vol and short where they are rich earn a significant return over 1996-2005. The widely quoted 15%/month belongs to a different working-paper strategy, so this sort's effect size is unverified.
- **Call-minus-put IV spread (Cremers-Weinbaum).** Informed demand pushes the favoured side's IV off put-call parity. Expensive-call stocks beat expensive-put stocks by about 50 bp/week over 1996-2005, with decay inside that sample. A CBS thesis finds 19 bp/week (t 2.45) for 2011-2015. Li-Wang's 21-day slope has t 7.0 over 2015-2026 and t 4.2 in 2023-26. This is the cluster's best survival record, but every figure is gross.
- **Volatility smirk (Xing-Zhang-Zhao).** The steepest OTM-put-minus-ATM-call smirks underperformed by 10.9%/year over 1996-2005. OSAP rates it only 'likely' (0.64%/month, t 2.19). The effect has **decayed**: t -5.5 (2015-19), t -4.2 (2020-22), t -1.5 (2023-26), and the sign flips at 63 days.
- **OTM-IV skewness proxy (Li-Wang).** The cross-strike skewness of OTM IVs predicts lower returns (21-day t -11.7 in 2023-26). It measures the dispersion of IV values, not risk-neutral skewness, and its t-statistics grow with horizon, as overlapping returns would make them.
- **IV changes (An-Ang-Bali-Cakici).** A rising call IV predicts higher returns and a rising put IV lower ones, about 1%/month, persisting up to six months (1996-2011). Equal-weighted, small-cap heavy, with no evidence after 2011.
- **Single-stock term structure (Li-Wang).** An upward 60-minus-30-day IV slope predicts higher returns (t 3.7 in 2023-26). The earnings confound is uncontrolled.
- **Term-slope straddles (Vasquez).** High-slope straddles beat low-slope ones by 27.1%/month gross and 12.3% net over 1996-2007, per unit of premium.
- **S&P VRP timing (BTZ).** VIX² minus the past month's realised variance predicts 3-month returns (t 2.86, adj R² 6.82%) over 1990-2007. A 2026 replication finds an out-of-sample R² of -0.074 at 63 days.
- **Implied correlation (Buss-Schönleber-Vilkov, via CXO).** COR-type measures predict market returns up to a year ahead, beyond the VRP (1996-2015). The out-of-sample claim is unverified.
- **VX daily roll (Simon-Campasano).** Short front VIX futures in steep contango and buy them in backwardation, holding 5 days with a hedge. Half the profit came from 2008, with "little or no profit since mid-2010". **Decayed.**
- **VIX futures premium (Cheng).** The ex ante premium predicts VX returns with a coefficient near one, and it falls when risk rises, as hedging pressure drops.
- **VIX curve PC2 (Johnson).** The slope component predicts returns on variance swaps, VX futures and straddles over 1996-2013, gross.
- **VVIX and tail hedges (Park).** A one-SD rise in VVIX lowers next-day SPX put returns by 1.32-2.19% (t -4.5 to -5.5) over 2006-2012. These are delta-hedged returns residualised on same-day moves, so they are untradable as measured.
- **BTC VRP by regime (Almeida et al.).** The BVIX-based VRP is 0.17 in low-DVOL regimes against 0.12 in high-DVOL regimes (2017-2022). The regimes are full-sample clusters and the realised leg is backward-looking, so the gap is partly mechanical.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** The primary literature is peer-reviewed, and OSAP replicates the cross-sectional signals on the original samples. The case for survival into the 2020s is **speculative**. It rests on one unrefereed preprint with firm fixed effects (look-ahead), overlapping returns, no size or momentum controls and no transaction costs. Most magnitudes are gross and in-sample.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Testable now (archived data), pre-registered:** `spx-vrp-predicts-equity-premium-oos` (expanding out-of-sample 2008-2026, one primary RV definition); `cor1m-predicts-equity-premium-oos` (126-session horizon, sign-restricted, must encompass the VRP); `vx-daily-roll-hedged-carry-2013` (a decay test); `vix-futures-premium-falls-with-risk` (one observation per settlement cycle, final settlement values); `vix-curve-pc2-vx-returns` (must beat T-435's VIX3M/VIX gate); `vvix-spy-put-hedged-returns` (a delta-hedged target, plus a conditional defined-risk short put spread on Alpaca); `btc-vrp-ratio-by-dvol-tercile` (point-in-time terciles).
- **The premium itself is taken as given**, in agreement with T-48, T-540, T-148, T-49, T-246, T-255, T-228 and T-534/T-535/T-53. The open question is whether its size times anything.
- **Cross-sectional family, blocked on the DoltHub fetch:** `rv-minus-iv-spread-sp500-xs`, `t531-call-put-iv-spread-dolthub` (with the verdict recorded on T-531), `call-put-iv-change-xs`, `single-stock-iv-term-slope-xs` (excluding earnings names), `otm-iv-skewness-proxy-xs`, and `single-stock-smirk-xzz-replication` (as a control and decay record). The option-return straddle rows (`hv-iv-straddle-xs-sp500`, `iv-term-slope-straddle-xs-sp500`) are low priority.
- **Lessons from the children:** a reference-price source must lead the market; option-to-stock lead-lag exists only where informed flow trades options first. Deribit DVOL is a measured non-member for Polymarket BTC digitals. The child's Deribit open-time-stamp leakage fixes DVOL timing. Hurst's IBIT ladder forward test (H-ibit-ladder) is the executable home for any BTC regime gate, against Hurst's IV minus RV >= 5 point gate.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Decayed:** the smirk, whose index analogues also failed in Mandel (T-52, T-138, T-227, T-229). The VX roll, decayed by the source's own account, is consistent with T-160, T-379, T-435 and T-242 (not supported). Mandel's own post-publication anomaly tests decayed too (T-445, T-446, T-382).
- **Contested by Mandel verdicts:**
  - VRP timing: the out-of-sample R² is negative; T-580 F3, T-235 and T-318 are not supported.
  - Implied correlation: T-538 inconclusive, T-236 blocked, T-250 not supported.
  - VVIX: T-243, T-536, T-240 and T-239 not supported.
  - HV-IV straddles: T-232/T-533, T-123 and T-550.
  - Term-slope straddles: T-262, T-143 and T-144.
  - RVIV: it carries a low-vol tilt (T-384, T-448 failed).
- **Rejected:** the claim that the BTC 25-delta risk reversal predicts spot. The source was unreadable and the sign is unknown. An independent backtest finds noise (correlation 0.076), and T-423, T-364 and T-257 argue against it.
- **Mechanism dropped:** the skewness "lottery" story, and the calm-regime BTC VRP. T-246's halves (+0.1535 against +0.0344) and T-256 lean the other way, and T-67 (ETH) is not supported.
- **Not US-executable as published:** Deribit (signal only; trade via IBIT or Coinbase), Cboe CFE VX futures (only the SVXY/VXX proxies) and naked short straddles (Alpaca iron-fly form instead).

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Features:** RVIV, call-put IV spread, smirk, OTM-IV skewness, dCP, single-stock term slope, VRP, COR1M/DSPX, VX roll per day, Cheng's P_t, VIX-curve PC2, z(VVIX), DVOL tercile. The single-stock features were absent from T-580's F3 family. They enter ML only after passing one at a time.
- **Data to add:** DoltHub single-name volatility_history and option_chain; DoltHub stocks ohlcv/split/dividend (delisted names included, so no survivorship bias); SEC 8-K item numbers for an earnings flag; FINRA days-to-cover as a short-interest borrow-cost proxy; VIXY/SVIX.
- **Pipeline rules:**
  - Use raw closes, never split-adjusted ones (AAPL 43.74 adjusted against 174.97 raw).
  - Use a dividend-projected forward: a parity-implied forward erases the call-put signal.
  - Restrict moneyness for American puts.
  - Interpolate in total variance, and use no tenor beyond about 55 DTE.
  - VIX-family indices close at 16:15 ET, so enter at the next session.
- **Tests:**
  - Separate DSR families for single-stock options, option returns, VX (counting T-53, T-159, T-160, T-379, T-435, T-530, T-242) and market timing.
  - Fama-MacBeth regressions with the signals as each other's controls.
  - Both halves must be positive over the full post-publication window, because about 91 month-ends give only t ≈ 1.1-1.5 at half the published effect.
  - A forward test on DoltHub snapshots after 2026-10-20 before any capital.

## Cross-links

- 12, 13, 14 (Claude trading videos): DVOL terciles and the VIX-curve contango/backwardation regimes are the regime features 13's HMM approximates.
- A4 (MSM): a HAR or MSM variance forecast supplies BTZ's RV leg and Cheng's E_t[VIX].
- A5 (Halawi): option prices as an aggregated forecast, scored against the price paid.
- OPTIONS-STRATEGIES.md, UNDERLYING-STRATEGIES.md, venues/US-LEVERAGE-VENUES-2026-10-20.md; T-48, T-53, T-246, T-531, T-534, T-580.

candidates.name: Gamma-conditioned market intraday momentum (rest-of-day return predicts the last half-hour)
candidates.summary: The return from the prior close to 15:30 ET predicts the 15:30-16:00 return of index futures and ETFs. According to Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens the effect appears only when option market makers are net short gamma, and it reverses over the following days. This is the conditional, hedging-demand version of the Gao-Han-Li-Zhou intraday momentum.
candidates.mechanism: Short-gamma hedgers must trade with the move to stay delta-neutral: option dealers when net gamma exposure (NGE/GEX) is negative, leveraged-ETF sponsors and vol-target funds. MOC fill risk means they start about 30 minutes before the close, which concentrates price pressure in the last half-hour. On the other side are liquidity providers and next-day mean-reversion traders, paid by the reversal over the following days. When dealers are long gamma, their hedging damps moves and the momentum disappears.
variables: options Greeks: dealer gamma exposure (GEX / net gamma exposure)
derivative open interest (SPX options OI by strike)
candidates.assets: US equity index futures (ES/MES, NQ/MNQ) and SPY/QQQ/IWM. The paper also covers bond, commodity and currency futures.
candidates.horizon: intraday (last 30 minutes), with reversal over the next days
candidates.claimed_effect: Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021), 60+ futures, 1974-2020. For equity futures r_ROD predicts r_LH with t = 7.29 and out-of-sample R2 of 2.88%. Simple timing strategies have Sharpe 0.87-1.73 per asset class before costs, and S&P 500 futures keep a positive net Sharpe at one tick of cost. S&P NGE over 1996-2020 (OptionMetrics, then SqueezeMetrics) gives 2,930 negative and 3,158 positive days. Momentum is 'much more pronounced' on negative-NGE days and insignificant on positive-NGE days. A leveraged-ETF market-share interaction also predicts r_LH (2006-2020). Gao et al. (JFE 2018), SPY 1993-2013: first-half-hour predictor R2 1.6%, out-of-sample R2 1.4%, sign-timing strategy 6.67%/yr at 6.19% volatility (Sharpe 1.08).
candidates.replication: Replicated across 60+ markets in the Baltussen paper and in both its 1974-1999 and 2000-2020 subsamples. Mandel's T-427 (unconditional; predictor = prior close to 10:30; SPY/QQQ/IWM 2023-11 to 2026-10 on hourly bars) is NOT SUPPORTED: slope -0.004 (t -0.22), net -2.09 bp/day. New reconciliation from this sweep: in SqueezeMetrics' free daily GEX series only 19 of the 734 sessions in T-427's window had negative GEX (2022 had 104, 2024 had 1). The hedging-demand theory therefore predicts the null T-427 found. This candidate partly duplicates T-427 but is new in two ways: the predictor is r_ROD (to 15:30), and the condition is dealer gamma. No post-2020 independent replication was found.

candidates.proposed_test: Register as a T-427 successor and count T-427's 60 cells in the deflation. Universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM 60m bars (2023-11 to 2026-10) plus ES_F and NQ_F 60m. Signal at the 15:30 ET bar open: r_ROD = log(open_15:30 / prior official close). Gamma state: SqueezeMetrics GEX for day t-1 only. Negative-GEX days are too rare in this window (19 of 734), so pre-register the low-gamma state as GEX_{t-1} in its trailing-252-day bottom quintile (about 147 days). Trade sign(r_ROD) from the 15:30 bar open to the official close (MOC), at 2 bp round trip for ETFs or 1 tick plus commission for MES. Primary statistic: slope c in r_LH = a + b*r_ROD + c*r_ROD*1[low GEX], with HAC t. Secondary: mean net return on low-GEX days versus high-GEX days, the high-GEX days serving as a placebo. Pass if c > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 and the same sign on SPY and QQQ. Two caveats: the free CSV is a current-methodology backfill, not a point-in-time vintage, so archive each day's published value from now on; and the decisive test is 2011-2026 once multi-year intraday index bars exist (Dukascopy USA500 CFD minutes or Alpaca/Polygon), because 2022's 104 negative-GEX days give the real power.

candidates.name: Volume- and news-conditioned intraday momentum and the 'noise-area' breakout
candidates.summary: Gao et al. find first-half-hour predictability strongest on high-volume, high-volatility and macro-news days. Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon turn intraday momentum into an all-day breakout from a volatility band (the 'noise area') with trailing stops on SPY.
candidates.mechanism: Two mechanisms are offered: infrequent rebalancers (Bogousslavsky 2016) trade in the same direction at the open and the close, and late-informed traders act near the close on news absorbed early in the day. A heavy, volatile first half-hour means more information is still to be traded on later, so the direction carries forward. On the other side are liquidity providers and early-day contrarians.
variables: volume in units (first-half-hour volume tercile, volume relative to its time-of-day profile)
calendars: CPI / employment / FOMC release days, time of day
adjacent_variables: relative volume vs the same bar's trailing average
candidates.assets: SPY, QQQ, IWM and other liquid index ETFs, plus index futures
candidates.claimed_effect: Gao et al., SPY 1993-2013: R2 1.6% in-sample (first half-hour), 2.6% combined with the twelfth half-hour, and 3.3% on high-first-half-hour-volatility days. R2 rises with the first-half-hour volume tercile. Out-of-sample R2 1.4% / 2.0%. Sign-timing strategy 6.67%/yr at 6.19% volatility; the authors say it remains significant after costs. Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon (Swiss Finance Institute WP 24-97, not peer reviewed): SPY 2007 to early 2024, band = open +/- the average absolute open-to-minute move over 14 days, with trailing stops. Reported 1,985% total, 19.6%/yr, Sharpe 1.33 net of commissions and slippage.
candidates.replication: Li-Sakkas-Urquhart (J. Futures Markets, 'Intraday time series momentum: global evidence') report significance in 12 of 16 markets; this comes from a search summary, as the full text was blocked. No independent replication of the noise-area paper was found; it placed 4th at the Quantpedia Awards 2025. Mandel: T-427 (unconditional, 2023-2026) is not supported. T-577 intraday ML (with time-of-day volume profile, tod_sin/cos and return-since-open features) passed 0 of 276 cells, but it did not target the last half-hour or condition on first-bar volume.

candidates.proposed_test: On SPY, QQQ and IWM 60m bars (2023-11 to 2026-10), keep T-427's rule (sign of prior close to 10:30, held from the 15:30 bar open to the official close, 2 bp round trip). Apply it only on pre-registered condition days: (a) the 09:30 bar's volume is in the top tercile relative to that bar's trailing-20-session mean (Mandel feature lv_rel_tod); (b) scheduled CPI, NFP or FOMC days; (c) the 09:30 bar's range is in the top tercile. Statistic: mean net return per conditioned day with HAC t. Use Holm across 3 conditions x 3 ETFs, then deflate together with T-427's 60 cells. Pass needs deflated p < 0.05 on SPY and the same sign on QQQ and IWM. The noise-area rule needs minute bars back to 2007, because Yahoo 5m bars reach only 60 days. Register it as blocked until Alpaca, Polygon or Dukascopy minute data arrive, with a random-direction benchmark and 1 bp plus one tick per stop fill.

candidates.name: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing flow into the close
candidates.summary: Leveraged and inverse ETFs must rebalance in the direction of the day's move near the close, by an amount equal to NAV x (x^2 - x) x the day's return. That flow should push the last half-hour in the day's direction and reverse afterwards.
candidates.mechanism: To keep a constant daily multiple, a 3x or -3x fund must buy after up days and sell after down days, mostly through swaps and futures hedged at or near the MOC. The flow is mechanical and predictable from public AUM and the intraday return. Liquidity providers who pre-position, then unwind into the reversal, sit on the other side.
variables: ETF flows / AUM (shares outstanding x NAV of LETFs)
market cap of the underlying index (normaliser)
adjacent_variables: LETF creations/redemptions (daily change in shares outstanding)
candidates.assets: QQQ / NQ (TQQQ, SQQQ, QLD, QID), SPY / ES (UPRO, SPXU, SSO, SDS, SPXL, SPXS), sector LETFs such as SOXL
candidates.horizon: intraday (last 30 minutes), with reversal over the next day
candidates.claimed_effect: Cheng and Madhavan (2010, as cited in Baltussen et al. 2021) estimated that at end-February 2009 LETF rebalancing made up 16.8% of market-on-close volume on a day the market moved 1%, and 50.2% on a 5% day. In Baltussen et al. Table 9 (June 2006 to May 2020), the LETF market share interacted with r_ROD adds to last-half-hour predictability. Across markets, higher LETF share goes with a larger intraday-momentum t-statistic. Shum et al. (2015) argue MOC fill risk moves hedging up to about 30 minutes before the close.
candidates.replication: Contested. From memory (not opened here): Ivanov and Lenkey (J. Financial Markets 2018) argue that capital flows into and out of LETFs offset much of the rebalancing, so late-day amplification is small. Mandel: T-325 (TQQQ/SQQQ short-pair decay) is not supported. No LETF-flow intraday test exists in the registry. This channel overlaps the gamma candidate above, so the test must separate them.

sources.title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum, Section 4.2 and Table 9 (LETF hedging demand)
Harbourfront Quant: market intraday momentum and hedging (practitioner summary)

candidates.proposed_test: Use QQQ (with NDX LETFs) and SPY (with SPX LETFs) 60m bars, 2023-11 to 2026-10. At the 15:30 bar open, compute demand D_t = sum over LETFs of AUM_{k,t-1}*(x_k^2 - x_k)*r(prior close to 15:30), scaled by the index ETF's trailing-20-day dollar volume. AUM is issuer-published daily shares outstanding x NAV for day t-1 (adjacent data, to archive). Run two regressions: r(15:30 to close) = a + b*r_ROD + c*D_t, so the LETF channel is separated from generic momentum and gamma, adding GEX as a control; and r(close to next close) on D_t for the reversal. Trading rule: sign(D_t) on top-quintile |D| days only, 2 bp round trip. Pass if c > 0 with HAC p < 0.05 on both QQQ and SPY and the next-day coefficient is negative. Cap the search at 8 cells for deflation.

candidates.name: Overnight drift at the European open (2-3 a.m. ET in S&P futures) after US sell-offs
candidates.summary: S&P 500 futures earn their largest hourly returns at the European cash open, 02:00-03:00 ET, as dealers unload order imbalances left from the US close. The drift is strongest after US sell-offs and high uncertainty.
candidates.mechanism: Inventory risk. Market makers absorb end-of-US-day imbalances, usually net selling, and hold them through thin Asian hours, where volume is 50-100x lower than in US hours. When European liquidity arrives they unload the inventory and shade quotes so that liquidity takers pay the spread. Compensation rises when dealer risk capacity is tight (sell-offs, rising volatility). Takers who must trade at the close or overnight pay it.
variables: calendars: time of day (European open; US/Europe/Japan DST asynchrony)
cross-asset leaders (ES futures, SPY session return)
candidates.assets: CME E-mini / Micro E-mini S&P (ES/MES), NQ/MNQ, RTY. The same window is tradable on Kalshi US500 perps, but at a cost that kills it.
candidates.claimed_effect: Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan (RFS 2023; NY Fed SR 917), ES futures 1998-2020. The 02:00-03:00 ET mean is 3.7% annualized (1.48 bp/day). It is positive in 20 of 23 years, significant in 17 and significant on every weekday, and it is the only hour that survives Bonferroni and Benjamini-Yekutieli corrections. Reversals after sell-offs are robustly positive and much smaller after rallies. The effect shifts with DST asynchrony, which works as a natural experiment. Going long 02:00-03:00 has Sharpe 1.1 before costs and -0.5 after the bid-ask spread; 01:30-03:30 has Sharpe 1.3 before and 0.3 after.
candidates.replication: Per the drift paper, Bondarenko and Muravyev (2020) replicate that most close-to-close futures returns are earned around the European open. Mandel: T-549 is supported (QQQ/IWM overnight beats intraday, net +3.4 to +3.6 bp per night). T-348 on SPY failed its 3 bp bar (gap +3.29 bp, lower bound 1.44). T-428 (last half-hour to close-to-open) slope is -0.08, not significant. Hurst's H-us500-overnight forward test is proposed but not pre-registered. Hurst measured US500 funding at 0.019-0.030%/day and perp round trips at 16-18 bp, which kills hour-scale rules there. Cost arithmetic (mine): the ES tick is 0.25 points, about 1.25 bp at S&P 2000 but about 0.32 bp at S&P ~7,700 (the 2026-10-20 level in the SqueezeMetrics file). The spread charge that turned the paper's Sharpe negative is therefore roughly 4x smaller today in ES/MES.

candidates.proposed_test: Use ES_F, NQ_F and RTY_F Yahoo 60m bars, 2023-11 to 2026-10, which include Globex hours. Window: the hour starting at the European cash open in ET, which is 02:00 ET normally and shifts by an hour in the roughly three DST-asynchronous weeks. Variant: 01:00-04:00. Pre-registered condition: the prior US cash session return (SPY 09:30 to 16:00) is in its trailing bottom tercile, with VIX up on the day as a secondary condition. Go long MES at the window open and exit at its close. Cost: 1 tick plus $1.00 round-trip commission per contract, about 0.6 bp at current levels; report a maker-entry variant separately. Statistic: mean net per trade, HAC t, positive in each calendar year. Placebos: the same hour after top-tercile days, and a bootstrap distribution over all 24 hourly means, as in the paper. Pass if the lower 95% bound of the mean net is above 0 and the hour lies above the pooled 97.5th percentile. Extend to 2012-2026 on Dukascopy USA500 minute data. Hand the verdict to Hurst's H-us500-overnight.

candidates.name: Tug of war: persistence of overnight vs intraday return components in the cross-section
candidates.summary: A stock's past-month overnight return predicts its future overnight returns, and its past intraday return predicts its future intraday returns, with an offsetting cross-component reversal. Momentum is earned entirely overnight, while most other anomalies are earned intraday.
candidates.mechanism: Clienteles. Individuals tend to trade at the open, which sets the overnight component. Institutions trade during the day and against the momentum characteristic. Each clientele's persistent demand creates persistent component returns that cancel in close-to-close returns. Institutions with rebalancing needs strengthen the effect.
variables: calendars: time of day (open vs close auction)
adjacent_variables: retail share of volume (FINRA off-exchange / TRF volume share)
candidates.assets: US single stocks, mainly large-cap and high-price; also international equities and index futures
candidates.horizon: months (signal); positions held overnight only (close to open), rebalanced monthly
candidates.claimed_effect: Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019), CRSP/TAQ 1993-2013, value-weight decile sorts. On past one-month overnight return the spread earns +3.47%/month overnight (t 16.57) and -3.24%/month intraday (t -9.34). On past one-month intraday return it earns +2.19%/month intraday (t 6.72) and -1.81%/month overnight (t -8.44). The result is robust to midquote opens: overnight three-factor alpha 1.88% (t 8.75). Momentum profits accrue entirely overnight, and the pattern is stronger for large-cap and high-price stocks.
candidates.replication: The paper's US sample ends in 2013, and no post-2013 out-of-sample replication was opened in this sweep. Akbas et al. (2022) and Baltussen-Da-Soebhag (2025) build on it. Cooper, Cliff and Gulen show that equities earn their returns overnight in general. Mandel tested only the index level (T-549 supported, T-348 failed its bar, T-333 gap fade failed), so the cross-sectional version is new.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: Mandel's 901-symbol adjusted daily history, restricted to stocks with price > $10 and top-500 dollar volume as of each formation date. The list is survivorship-biased, so report this caveat and a robustness run on names present throughout. Overnight return = close(t-1) to open(t), with dividends added back on ex-dates as in T-348; intraday return = open(t) to close(t). At each month-end, sort on the sum of the past 21 overnight returns. Hold the top decile overnight only (buy the MOC, sell the next MOO) for the next month, against SPY overnight-only as benchmark. Long-only, so no borrow is needed. Cost: 3 bp per side per auction crossing (6 bp a night). Split 2000-2013 (paper period, replication) from 2014-2026 (out-of-sample). Statistic: mean monthly net excess over SPY overnight, Newey-West t, both halves positive, deflated over at most 12 cells (lookbacks 5/21/63 x VW/EW x decile/quintile). Check one point first: Yahoo's open must equal the primary-listing opening auction price, so spot-check it against a few published official opens.

candidates.name: Tug-of-war intensity: frequent daytime reversals of overnight gains predict higher monthly returns
candidates.summary: Some stocks often rise overnight and then fall during the day (negative daytime reversals). When such days are more frequent than the stock's own 12-month norm, the stock earns higher returns over the following months.
candidates.mechanism: Overnight noise traders push prices up at the open, and daytime arbitrageurs correct them. According to Akbas et al., the arbitrageurs over-correct, discounting the chance that the overnight buying reflects real positive news. A more intense tug of war therefore leaves the stock underpriced. Daytime arbitrageurs are on the other side.
variables: calendars: time of day (overnight vs daytime components)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (strongest in small, volatile, illiquid names; economically tiny for SPY)
candidates.horizon: months (monthly rebalance, effect persists up to six months)
candidates.claimed_effect: Akbas-Boehmer-Jiang-Koch (JFE 2022; WP sample May 1993 to December 2017, per CXO). The top minus bottom decile by negative-reversal intensity earns 0.92%/month equal-weighted, with alphas of 0.85% (3-factor), 0.81% (4-factor) and 0.88% (5-factor). By size group: 0.97% (small), 0.75% (mid), 0.43% (big) per month. The effect persists up to six months and does not reverse. Only negative reversals predict. All figures are gross of costs.
candidates.replication: A search summary, not opened, reports mixed replications: a G7 study confirms the effect in the US and Canada but not in France, Germany, Italy, the UK or Japan, and a China study finds no significant spread. The effect is concentrated where trading and shorting are costliest, so equal-weight figures overstate what can be harvested. Not in Mandel's registry.

candidates.proposed_test: Use Mandel's 901-symbol daily history over 2000-2026, with 2018-2026 as the post-publication out-of-sample window. For each stock-month, NR = (share of days with overnight > 0 and intraday < 0) divided by the stock's mean of that share over the prior 12 months. At month-end, form long top-quintile/decile versus bottom portfolios, VW and EW. Also run a long-only top-quintile portfolio versus an equal-weight universe benchmark, which a small account can trade. Cost: 10 bp per side per rebalance. Statistic: monthly FF5+UMD alpha (factors archived) with Newey-West t, positive in both halves of 2018-2026, deflated over at most 8 cells. As a diagnostic, split by size tercile and FINRA days-to-cover tercile (capacity to arbitrage).

candidates.name: End-of-day reversal in the cross-section (intraday losers bounce in the last half-hour)
candidates.summary: A stock's return from the prior close through mid-afternoon negatively predicts its own last-half-hour return in the cross-section. Most of this is positive price pressure on intraday losers into the close.
candidates.mechanism: Two channels, per Baltussen-Da-Soebhag. First, retail investors buy the dip late in the day in attention-grabbing big movers, especially losers; retail investors rarely short. Second, short sellers manage overnight risk by opening fewer new shorts in the last half-hour, three times fewer for losers. Together these push intraday losers up into the close. The paper says liquidity and gamma hedging do not explain it.
variables: short interest (days to cover, short volume, new short positions)
adjacent_variables: retail order imbalance (BJZZ sub-penny, Robinhood holdings)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (large and small; liquid and illiquid subsamples)
candidates.claimed_effect: Baltussen-Da-Soebhag (WP, April 2025), January 1993 to December 2019. A long-short portfolio sorted on ROD3 (prior close to 15:00 ET, skipping 15:00-15:30) earns 3.78 bp/day in the last half-hour value-weighted (about 9.5%/yr) and 6.86 bp/day equal-weighted (about 17.3%/yr), with t above 10 in simple sorts. A six-factor alpha for extreme intraday losers is 14.71 bp/day. Three-year rolling slopes are almost always negative, including the late sample. All figures are gross; the authors say retail investors may not be able to exploit it after costs.
candidates.replication: Distinct from market intraday momentum (opposite sign at the stock level) and from the Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka seasonality. No independent replication found. Mandel's T-428 (SPY last half-hour to next open) is a different, index-level claim and is not supported. Not in the registry.
