candidates.proposed_test: Universe: single stocks in Mandel's 60m set (about 50 names, 2023-11 to 2026-10), with a full run once minute bars exist for the 901 names. ROD3 = log(close of the 13:30-14:30 bar / prior official close). Skip the 14:30-15:30 bar so the bid-ask bounce cannot drive the result. Target: 15:30 bar open to official close. Each day, buy the bottom quintile by ROD3 at the 15:30 open, equal-weight, and sell at the MOC; the main test is against an equal-weight-universe short leg as a paper L-S, with the long-only leg reported. Cost: half-spread plus 1 bp at 15:30, zero spread at the MOC, plus the SEC fee on sells. Statistic: mean daily L-S net with Newey-West t and the two years separately. Pre-registered interaction: the effect is larger in the top FINRA days-to-cover tercile (as published) and the top off-exchange-volume-share tercile (Reg SHO total_volume / consolidated volume, a retail proxy Mandel already archives). At most 6 cells.

candidates.name: Anomaly returns at the close: arbitrageurs de-risk before the overnight borrow and margin charge
candidates.summary: Mispricing-factor returns accrue during the day but turn sharply negative at the end of the day and overnight. Size and illiquidity premia are realised in the last 30 minutes, while profitability and idiosyncratic-volatility premia accrue gradually during the day but lose large amounts overnight.
candidates.mechanism: Overnight margin requirements are higher, and securities-lending fees are charged only on positions held overnight. Arbitrageurs and short sellers therefore cut mispriced positions before the close, which lets overpriced stocks rebound into the close. The mispricing is re-established at the open. Uninformed overnight and opening demand is on the other side.
variables: short interest (days to cover, short volume)
calendars: time of day (last 30 minutes, overnight)
candidates.assets: US single stocks
candidates.horizon: intraday plus overnight (component decomposition); signal monthly
candidates.claimed_effect: Bogousslavsky (JFE 141, 2021): a mispricing factor earns positive returns during the day but performs poorly at the end of the day, and the pattern is stronger in the second half of the sample. Size and illiquidity premia are realised in the last 30 minutes. Profitability and IVOL premia incur large negative overnight returns. Magnitudes were not extracted; only the abstract was opened.
candidates.replication: The author says institutional and information-asymmetry theories support it but do not fully explain it. Related: Baltussen-Da-Soebhag's short-seller end-of-day channel and Lou-Polk-Skouras. Mandel's T-375 (top vs bottom FINRA days-to-cover decile, monthly) and T-393 are inconclusive; their overnight/intraday split has not been looked at.

candidates.proposed_test: This is a diagnostic first, which can be promoted to a trading claim. On Mandel's 901-symbol daily OHLC, 2018-01 to 2026-09, form monthly deciles on FINRA days-to-cover by available_at, and separately on trailing-60-day idiosyncratic volatility against SPY. Decompose each decile's daily return into overnight (close to open, dividend-adjusted) and intraday (open to close). Claim: the high-minus-low DTC spread has overnight mean < intraday mean, with the difference below -2 bp/day, Newey-West t, both halves. On the 60m single-stock set, also test whether the high-DTC portfolio's 15:30-to-close return is positive. If supported, two small-account forms follow: avoid carrying high-DTC longs overnight (an execution rule for the existing sleeves), or hold the high-DTC long leg intraday only. The second must clear 4 bp/day of costs. Pre-register at most 6 cells.

candidates.name: Closing-auction price pressure and auction-volume share (disagreement)
candidates.summary: Closing-auction volume has more than doubled with indexing and ETFs. Official closing prices deviate from the pre-close midquote and revert overnight. The ratio of intraday to auction volume, a disagreement proxy, predicts higher returns over the next week and month.
candidates.mechanism: Passive and ETF rebalancers, benchmarked to the close, concentrate uninformed demand in the auction. Exchange fees and execution uncertainty limit outside liquidity in the auction, so prices move and then revert, half within about 30 minutes after the close. High intraday-to-auction volume means more active, disagreeing trading, which Banerjee-Kremer-type models link to higher expected returns.
variables: calendars: month-end, index rebalance days, time of day
adjacent_variables: closing quote midpoint vs official close
candidates.assets: US single stocks and ETFs
candidates.claimed_effect: Bogousslavsky-Muravyev (WP December 2020; forthcoming in J. Financial Markets per the author's CV). The auction was 7.48% of daily dollar volume in 2018, up from 3.11% in 2010. The mean absolute deviation of the closing price from the 16:00 midquote is 8.1 bp, and above 0.63% on 1% of stock-days. Deviations revert by half shortly after the close and fully overnight, even net of the half-spread. Disagreement-ratio decile sorts yield 4.2% annualized alpha, robust to excluding hard-to-borrow, attention-grabbing, volatile and illiquid stocks.
candidates.replication: A related NYSE vs Nasdaq study (Management Science, floor brokers at the close) finds auction price changes reverse more often on NYSE. Mandel's T-428 (SPY last half-hour to next open) is not supported, slope -0.084. Methodological learning for Mandel: official closes carry auction pressure that reverts overnight. Any close-to-open regression whose input ends at the official close (as T-428's does) mixes auction noise into the signal, and the paper finds the last midquote more efficient than the official close.

candidates.proposed_test: (a) Testable now: on Mandel's 5m bars (about 60 days x about 80 equity symbols), define deviation = log(official daily close / close of the 15:55 bar). Regress the next close-to-open return on the deviation, clustered by day. Claim: slope < -0.5, i.e. at least half reverts overnight. This is a cost diagnostic for any rule that buys or sells at the MOC. (b) Blocked: the disagreement sort needs per-stock auction volume. Validate a proxy first, auction volume ≈ Yahoo daily volume minus the sum of that day's intraday bars, against officially published closing-cross volumes on a sample of days. Then run weekly decile sorts on the 20-day mean ratio, next-week return, 10 bp per side, FF5 alpha, on at least 300 names.

candidates.name: FX fixing 'W' pattern: the dollar appreciates into the Tokyo and London fixes and depreciates after
candidates.summary: Around the clock, the US dollar strengthens in the run-up to the Tokyo (9:55 JST) and London WMR (16:00) fixes and weakens afterwards, which traces a W-shaped intraday return pattern in G9 currencies.
candidates.mechanism: Inventory risk. Corporates and asset managers have unconditional dollar demand executed at the fixes. Dealers pre-hedge by buying dollars before the fix and unwind afterwards, earning compensation for the inventory risk. Dealer order flow before the fix predicts the post-fix reversal. Fix-benchmarked clients are on the other side.
variables: calendars: time of day (Tokyo 9:55 JST, ECB 14:15 CET, London 16:00 fix; month-end fix)
cross-asset leaders: the dollar (DXY, G9 crosses)
candidates.assets: Spot FX majors vs USD (OANDA), CME FX futures (6E, 6J, 6B, ...)
candidates.claimed_effect: Krohn-Mueller-Whelan (JF 79(1) 2024; BoC SWP 2021-48), G9 currencies January 1999 to December 2019. The equal-weight portfolio long foreign currencies against USD falls 5.0% p.a. into the Tokyo fix and rises 5.3% after. It falls 4.2% p.a. from the European open to the ECB fix and rises about 4.6% from the London fix to the NY close, with t between 4.5 and 11.7. A pre-fix order-imbalance shock gives a post-fix reversal of about 2.5-3.5 bp. Implied daily swings exceed $1 billion. The 2014-2019 Tokyo reversal is notably smaller but still significant. Ignoring costs, $1 in 1999 grows to $12 (yen) and $9 (euro) by 2019 around the Tokyo fix, but most profits disappear after transaction costs.
candidates.replication: Robust in four subsamples and across RTH indicative quotes, RTH forwards, CME futures and Refinitiv Matching VWAPs. Decay: the Tokyo fix effect is smaller in 2014-2019. Mandel's FX tests (T-368 carry, T-431 EM carry) are monthly and not supported; no intraday FX theory exists in the registry.

candidates.proposed_test: Use Mandel's 60m bars for EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD and USDCHF (2 years), with the DXY as a check. Extend to 2012-2026 on Dukascopy minute data, which reproduces the paper's post-2014 out-of-sample window. Equal-weight dollar portfolio. Windows in UTC with DST handled: Tokyo pre-fix = NY 17:00 ET to 01:00 UTC, post-fix = 01:00 UTC to the European open; London pre-fix = ECB fix to the London 16:00 fix, post-fix = 16:00 London to 17:00 ET. Claims: pre-fix USD return > 0 and post-fix < 0, each with HAC t, in both years. Tradable rule: long USD into the fix, short after. Cost: 1 bp per side on EURUSD and USDJPY and 2 bp on the rest, or OANDA quoted spreads where recorded. Statistic: mean net per day. Pre-register the expectation that net is not above 0. A gross-only pass is still useful as an execution-timing rule for FX conversions and hedges, and as a time-of-day feature for the ML program.

candidates.name: Intraday periodicity: same-half-hour return continuation across days (Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka)
candidates.summary: In the cross-section, a stock's return in a given half-hour predicts its return in the same half-hour on later days, for up to 40 trading days, most strongly at the first and last half-hours. Short lags reverse.
candidates.mechanism: Predictable, repetitive demand for immediacy at particular times of day. Institutions with infrequent rebalancing (Bogousslavsky 2016) and repetitive institutional net order activity trade at the same clock time day after day. Liquidity providers earn the premium. Volume, order imbalance and volatility show the same periodicity, but do not explain the return pattern.
adjacent_variables: bid-ask spread by time of day
candidates.assets: US single stocks (also UK and Brazil; weak in China)
candidates.claimed_effect: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (JF 65(4) 2010): continuation at lags that are multiples of 13 half-hours, still significant at 40 days (520 half-hours). The authors note that timing trades to the pattern can cut execution costs by about the effective spread. Their sample period is from memory, not verified here: post-decimalization, roughly 2001-2005.
candidates.replication: Decaying. A 2024 EFMA paper on interday cross-sectional momentum reports, per its search snippet (full text returned 503), that the first-lag effect fell by about 75%, which it reads as greater market efficiency. A public replication of Andersen-Bollerslev-style same-interval momentum on FX, S&P CFD and BTC finds the effect significant gross (t = 9.0) but only 0.05 bp against a 0.6 bp cost. Out of sample, the in-sample Sharpe of 6.8 falls to 0.4. The option-straddle version (Da et al. 2026) is strong at mid quotes. Not in Mandel's registry. Mandel's ML F2 family uses consecutive-bar lags, not same-time-of-day lags.

candidates.proposed_test: Use Mandel's 60m bars (about 90 symbols, 2023-11 to 2026-10; 7 bars per session) and 30m bars (60 days). For each bar h on day d, regress cross-sectional returns r(i,h,d) on the mean of r(i,h,d-k) for k = 1, 1..5, 1..20 and 1..40 (Fama-MacBeth, Newey-West), controlling for the previous two bars to absorb bid-ask reversal. Claim: the same-bar coefficient is positive at the open and close bars, with t > 2 pooled. Trading form: no standalone strategy, because the cost evidence says it is too small. Instead, (a) add same-time-of-day lag features to the T-577 F2 family and measure the IC uplift out of sample, and (b) shift T-559 sleeve rebalances to the bar whose predicted same-bar return favours the trade side, and measure implementation shortfall against the fixed-time baseline in Alpaca paper.

candidates.name: Intraday option-straddle momentum (open and close) and within-day straddle reversal
candidates.summary: The same-half-hour continuation extends to delta-neutral equity-option straddles. The 9:35-10:00 straddle return predicts the next day's 9:35-10:00 return, likewise for 15:30-16:00, and straddle returns reverse within the day at nearly every half-hour.
candidates.mechanism: Morning momentum reflects delayed reaction to overnight volatility news. Afternoon momentum and the within-day reversal reflect transitory price pressure from end-user option demand that market makers absorb, visible in market-maker inventories and option order imbalances. Market makers who trade inside the spread earn it.
variables: derivative volume and open interest (option order imbalance, open/close volume)
candidates.assets: Equity options on S&P 500 constituents (straddles); SPY/QQQ options plausibly
candidates.horizon: intraday (half-hours), signal from the prior day
candidates.claimed_effect: Da-Filippou-Goyenko-Zhang-Zhou-Zhou (WP, October 2026), point-in-time S&P 500 constituents, January 2010 to December 2024 (OptionMetrics plus ThetaData 1-minute OPRA quotes). The high-minus-low spread on the prior day's 9:35-10:00 straddle return earns 73 bp/day (t 21.96, Sharpe 3.5, monthly six-factor alpha 15.2%). The 15:30-16:00 spread earns 37 bp/day (t 13.96, Sharpe 2.3). Within-day reversal is about 3-9 bp per half-hour. All returns are at quote midpoints with no costs. The authors say the profits may not be achievable by the average investor, but are within reach of market makers.
candidates.replication: This paper merges two earlier working papers (Da-Goyenko-Zhang; Beckmeyer-Filippou-Zhou-Zhou), which agree; it is too new for independent replication. Retail-relevant decay is effectively total: straddle bid-ask spreads on single names are usually several percent of premium (my estimate, not from the paper), far above a 37-73 bp mid-to-mid edge. Mandel's 0DTE theories T-141, T-142, T-217 and T-218 are blocked for lack of intraday chains.

candidates.proposed_test: Blocked on intraday option quotes. Use the Linode capture box: if it can snapshot chains at 9:35, 10:00, 15:30 and 16:00 ET for SPY, QQQ, IWM and the 20 most liquid single-name option underlyings, record ATM straddle bid/ask/mid forward. After 120 sessions, pre-register: (a) mid-to-mid replication of the morning same-interval momentum sign (cross-sectional rank correlation > 0, t > 2), and (b) the executable version, buying winners at the ask at 9:35 and selling at the bid at 10:00, expected to be negative net. If (a) passes and (b) fails, the use is as a signal: when to buy planned straddles, e.g. avoid 9:35 entries on prior-day morning winners. It also gives a strong opening-implied-vol feature for the F3 (options-implied) family.

candidates.name: Bitcoin overnight seasonality (long 22:00-00:00 UTC) and crypto hour-of-day effects
candidates.summary: Quantpedia's Padysak-Vojtko study finds BTC returns concentrated in the 22:00 and 23:00 UTC hours, about 1-2 hours after the US equity close and before the Asian open. A long position held for only those two hours earned most of BTC's return in 2015-2021.
candidates.mechanism: Unclear and contested. Candidates are US-close spillover: CME BTC futures halt 17:00-18:00 ET and settle at the 16:00 ET equity close, and post-2024 spot-ETF hedging is pinned to the 16:00 ET NAV. The Asian open is another candidate. On the other side are hedgers and liquidity takers trading at US-close-linked times. Weekend and Monday effects are a related calendar family.
variables: calendars: time of day (UTC hour), weekend
candidates.assets: BTC (Coinbase spot, Coinbase Derivatives nano BTC futures, CME micro BTC, Kalshi perps)
candidates.claimed_effect: Quantpedia 'Overnight Seasonality in Bitcoin' (Padysak and Vojtko, SSRN 4081000), Gemini BTC data 2015-2021, long 22:00 to 00:00 UTC: about 33% annualized, 20.93% volatility, Sharpe 1.58, maximum drawdown -34.04%. No transaction costs. The page notes poor performance in bear markets.
candidates.replication: No peer-reviewed replication found. The public Andersen-Bollerslev replication finds BTC's US-hours share of variance rose from 40.8% to 45.2%, mostly in 2022-23, before the spot ETFs. Mandel: T-436 Monday effect supported (+36.5 bp, p 0.013); T-62 weekend vs weekday returns not supported; T-515 weekend variance lower (supported); T-264 not supported. Hurst found that hour-of-day, hourly reversal and momentum rules on 20 Kalshi perps (45,419 hours) do not clear the 16-18 bp round trip: the best gross of 26 rules was +26 bp, walk-forward -45 bp per trade. Sweep note: the shared web-search budget ran out during this sweep, so this candidate's evidence came from fetching Quantpedia directly. No 2022-2026 out-of-sample study was found.

Replication of Andersen & Bollerslev intraday periodicity incl. BTC (GitHub)

candidates.proposed_test: This is a clean out-of-sample test, since the source sample ends in 2021. Use Mandel's Coinbase 1m BTC-USD bundles (2022-01 to 2026-10) and the Kraken 1m trades with buy/sell volume (2022-01 to 2025-11) as a second venue. Claim: the mean log return over 22:00-00:00 UTC exceeds the mean of the other eleven 2-hour UTC blocks by > 5 bp/day. Use a block bootstrap by day, with Holm correction over the 12 blocks, both halves (2022-2024, 2024-2026), and a pre/post-IBIT split (2024-01-11). Cost: 2 bp round trip for CME micro or Coinbase Derivatives nano futures (verify fee schedules), 16-18 bp on Kalshi perps, and Coinbase spot maker fees at the account tier. Pre-register the expectation that the net is not above 0 on any retail venue. As a diagnostic, test whether the block's return is explained by the same day's US equity close-to-close return, the spillover mechanism.

candidates.name: Intraday volatility seasonality and event-hour variance in short-dated (0DTE/1DTE) option pricing
candidates.summary: Intraday variance follows a stable U-shape (high at the open and close, a midday or lunch trough) with large spikes at 08:30 releases and 14:00 FOMC. Implied 1-day volatility (VIX1D) may misprice this event-hour variance, which matters for any 0DTE or 1DTE straddle, condor or theta rule and for time-of-day vol normalisation of features.
candidates.mechanism: Information arrival and liquidity are concentrated at the open (overnight news) and the close (rebalancing and auctions), with scheduled macro releases on top. Option pricing that spreads theta evenly over calendar time, or that underweights event hours, leaves sellers short variance at the wrong times. The other side is end-user 0DTE demand and dealers who hedge it.
variables: calendars: CPI/NFP 08:30, FOMC 14:00, OPEX, time of day, lunch hour
candidates.assets: SPX/XSP/SPY options (0DTE, 1DTE), ES/MES futures
candidates.claimed_effect: Andersen-Bollerslev (1997) periodicity, reproduced on 2010-2025 S&P CFD and 2004-2025 EUR/USD 5-minute data in a public replication. The year-to-year intraday profile correlation is 0.91 for the S&P and 0.96 for FX. On payroll Fridays the 08:30 NY interval runs at 10.9x the day's average volatility, and the S&P last-to-first-hour volatility ratio rises from 0.755 to 0.810 on high-volatility days. Mandel's T-529 found VIX1D at the close under-prices next-day close-to-close variance under the /365 convention (-0.2241 %^2/day, CI -0.4693 to -0.1012), and by more ahead of CPI/FOMC/NFP days (-0.6920 vs -0.1580 ex-events).
candidates.replication: The periodicity is among the most replicated facts in high-frequency finance. Its trading implication for 0DTE has no out-of-sample record here; the Dim-Eraker-Vilkov 0DTE gamma paper (SSRN 4692190) could not be opened (403). From memory, it argues market-maker 0DTE gamma has not amplified intraday volatility. Mandel: T-529 not supported (sign reversed: VIX1D cheap), T-216 OPEX pin short straddle supported, T-224 GLD event straddle supported, and T-141, T-142, T-217 and T-218 blocked for lack of intraday chains. Sweep note: the web-search budget was exhausted, so the 0DTE literature is under-covered.

sources.title: Replication & extension of Andersen & Bollerslev (1997) intraday periodicity (GitHub)
Market Intraday Momentum (Gao et al.) - U-shaped volume and volatility documentation

candidates.proposed_test: Data: Cboe VIX1D daily OHLC (archived, 2022-05 onward) and SPY 60m bars (2023-11 to 2026-10). Statistic per day: R = realised open-to-close variance from hourly log returns divided by (VIX1D_open/100)^2 x (6.5/24)/365. Report the variance convention and use ratios across day types, so the convention cancels. Claims: (a) mean log R on CPI/NFP/FOMC days exceeds its mean on matched non-event days by more than 0.2 (VIX1D at the open under-prices event days), with a day-clustered bootstrap CI; (b) the share of daily realised variance in the 15:30-16:00 bar is stable year to year (profile correlation > 0.8). These checks inform the 0DTE straddle and condor claims (T-217, T-218) before any capture-box chains exist. The tradable version, buying a 0DTE XSP or SPY straddle at 10:00 on event days at the ask, waits for 120 or more captured sessions.

candidates.name: Opening-range breakout on 'stocks in play' (relative-volume filter)
candidates.summary: A 5-minute opening-range breakout traded only on the 20 stocks with the highest opening-range relative volume each day (stocks in play), with tight ATR stops and exits at the close. This is the volume-filtered successor to the index ORB.
candidates.mechanism: Unusual opening volume marks stocks with news or flow imbalances whose direction carries through the session, as institutions keep working orders and retail attention follows. The other side is early-day liquidity providers and faders. Unfiltered index ORB carries little directional information.
variables: volume in units (opening-range relative volume vs 14-day average)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (price > $5, 14-day ADV >= 1M shares, ATR > $0.50); index ETFs and futures for the plain ORB
candidates.claimed_effect: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz, 'A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market' (SSRN, February 2024), all US stocks 2016-2023, $0.0035/share commission, 1% risk per trade, 4x leverage cap. A secondary summary reports 1,637% total and 41.6% annualized for the top-20 relative-volume version. CXO's summary is paywalled, so returns are unverified here. Zarattini-Aziz (SSRN 4416622) report about +0.13 R per trade for the plain QQQ 5-minute ORB.
candidates.replication: A public replication of the plain 5-minute ORB on NQ, SPX, Dow, DAX and FTSE CFDs (2015 to June 2026) reproduces the gross edge (NQ +0.131 R, hit rate 23.2%). Net of realistic spread and slippage, no market is distinguishable from zero (NQ +0.002 R, the others -0.038 to -0.081 R). The rule was negative in 2015-2017, and 2021-2026 NQ reached only +0.06 R at best. It does beat a random-direction benchmark by about +0.10 to +0.13 R, so the first candle carries information about the size of the costs. Mandel: T-426 (QQQ 5m ORB) is blocked for lack of multi-year minute bars. No independent test of the stocks-in-play filter was found.

candidates.proposed_test: Keep T-426 blocked for the full test, but pre-register the stocks-in-play variant now so it is not fitted later. Universe: Mandel's 5m bars (123 symbols, 60 days) as a pilot only. Once Alpaca/Polygon minute history lands, the full universe is the 901 names, 2016-2026, with 2024-2026 as out-of-sample. Each day rank names by first-5-minute volume divided by the trailing-14-day mean first-5-minute volume, and take the top 20 (top 5 in the pilot). Enter on a stop at the opening-range extreme in the first bar's direction, with the stop at 10% of the 14-day ATR, exit at the close. Cost: half-spread plus 1 tick slippage per stop fill, SEC fee, no leverage. Statistics: mean net R per trade and daily Sharpe, the excess over a random-direction benchmark (bootstrap), DSR over at most 24 cells, and PBO < 0.3.

candidates.name: Attention-driven buying at the open: high-attention stocks gain overnight and reverse intraday
candidates.summary: Stocks that recently drew retail attention open high relative to later prices: positive overnight returns followed by intraday reversals. Buying such stocks at the open carries a hidden cost larger than the effective half-spread.
candidates.mechanism: Retail investors buy attention-grabbing stocks, and they trade disproportionately before and at the open. Their concentrated buying inflates opening prices, which daytime arbitrage then corrects. The effect is strongest in hard-to-value, costly-to-arbitrage names and when aggregate retail sentiment is high. Opening-auction liquidity providers are on the other side.
variables: volume in units (abnormal volume as attention)
adjacent_variables: off-exchange (FINRA TRF) volume share as a retail-activity proxy
news and earnings days (days until earnings)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (attention-grabbing, hard-to-value names)
candidates.claimed_effect: Berkman-Koch-Tuttle-Zhang (JFQA 47(4) 2012): high-attention stocks show positive overnight returns and intraday reversals. The effect is stronger for hard-to-value, costly-to-arbitrage stocks and rises with retail sentiment. For retail buyers at the open, the implicit cost often exceeds the effective half-spread. Precise magnitudes were not extracted; only the abstract was opened. Baltussen-Da-Soebhag (2025) confirm retail-attention opening price pressure in later data.
candidates.replication: Consistent with Lou-Polk-Skouras (individuals trade at the open) and Akbas et al. (overnight noise-trader pressure). Mandel: T-414 (pre-open StockTwits bullish ratio predicts open-to-next-open) and T-38 (attention predicts absolute return) are inconclusive; T-399 and T-412 (attention reversal over 10-20 days) are blocked. Mandel's StockTwits intensity archive begins only at 2025-W43, so a longer test needs a volume- or off-exchange-based attention proxy.

sources.title: Paying Attention: Overnight Returns and the Hidden Cost of Buying at the Open (JFQA 2012)

candidates.proposed_test: Use Mandel's 901-symbol daily OHLC with FINRA Reg SHO daily files (2018-08 to 2026-10). Attention at the close of day t-1, known before the next open: (a) abnormal volume, the log of volume over its trailing-20-day mean, in the top decile; (b) off-exchange share = FINRA total_volume / consolidated volume, as a z-score against its own 60-day history. For StockTwits-covered symbols from 2025-W43, add the message-intensity z-score as a third, short-sample variant. Claim: for top-decile attention stocks, next-day overnight return minus intraday return > 10 bp, with Newey-West t and both halves (2018-2022, 2022-2026). Small-account execution rule: hold planned buys of high-attention names to the MOC instead of the MOO, measuring the saving against the open. The long-only trade is to buy high-attention names at the MOC on day t and sell at the MOO on t+1, at 3 bp per side. At most 6 cells.

Last half-hour to next open on SPY, slope -0.084 (t -0.48). This is the reversal leg the candidate predicts.
0DTE condor split by the sign of prior-close GEX. Mandel's own GEX estimator exists only from the 2026-10-14 chain captures.

learnings.source: SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv, counted in this cross-check (GEX column only, no returns looked at)
learnings.finding: Negative-GEX sessions: 19 of 730 in T-427's window 2023-11-21..2026-10-20 (2024: 1 of 252); 167 of 1,562 in 2020-08..2026-10; 297 of 2,967 in 2015-2026 (2022: 104). The hedging-demand theory therefore predicts T-427's null, and the statistical power sits in 2020-2022.
In Mandel's tests dealer positioning shows up at monthly OPEX but not at triple witching, so a gamma effect is plausible but not reliable.
Liquid markets are calibrated. Price-only rules start from a negative base rate. A result that looks too good against a liquid market is a leak until the leak is found.
Yahoo stamps intraday bars by their OPEN time, and a zero-length 16:00 bar is the closing print. Entry must be the 15:30 bar's open and the exit the official daily close, never the 16:00 stub.
Generic time-of-day and return-since-open features carried no tradable intraday signal in 2026, a long-gamma regime. This matches the unconditional null.
No independent replication of the NGE conditioning after 2020 was found, and the paper's sample ends in 2020.

registration.claim: On SPY and QQQ from 2020-08 to 2026-10, define r_ROD = log(price at 15:30:00 ET / prior official close) and r_LH = log(official close / price at 15:30:00 ET); the slope c in r_LH = a + b*r_ROD + c*r_ROD*1[GEX_{t-1} < 0] is positive, and trading sign(r_ROD) from 15:30 to the official close (MOC) on days after a negative SqueezeMetrics GEX earns a positive mean net return after a 2 bp round trip.
registration.statistic: Primary: OLS interaction slope c with a Newey-West (5 lags) t. Secondary: mean net return per trade of the sign rule on GEX<0 days against GEX>0 days (the placebo), with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 10 sessions).
registration.null: c <= 0, and the rule's mean net return on negative-GEX days <= 0.
registration.procedure: The 15:30 price is the open of the first 1-minute bar at or after 15:30:00 ET (Alpaca IEX). The 2015-2020 replication arm uses Dukascopy USA500 returns applied to SPY. r_LH ends at the official daily close from daily-history, never at a 16:00 stub bar. GEX_{t-1} is the value SqueezeMetrics dates t-1; it is built from OI published before the open of t, so only t-1 enters day t, and the series is flagged as a backfill. Early closes and sessions without the 15:30 bar are excluded. Also reported: b alone (unconditional r_ROD), the T-427 r1 predictor on the same days, and one pre-declared secondary state, GEX_{t-1} below its trailing-252-day 20th percentile. Reversal: regress close(t)->close(t+1) on r_LH*1[GEX<0]. Deflation counts T-427's 60 cells plus at most 8 here (68 trials).
registration.data: SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (to archive); Alpaca IEX 1-minute SPY/QQQ 2020-08..2026-10 (to fetch); daily-history-SPY and daily-history-QQQ (official closes); Dukascopy USA500 minutes (replication arm); fomc-meetings.
registration.pass: On SPY, c > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (68 trials). QQQ has the same sign. The sign rule's mean net on GEX<0 days is above 0 with a bootstrap 90% lower bound above 0. The GEX>0 placebo is not significantly positive.
registration.controls: Baselines: T-427 (unconditional, 10:30 predictor) and the unconditional r_ROD rule. Placebo: GEX>0 days. One threshold (GEX < 0), no grid. FOMC 14:00 days and OPEX days are flagged and reported with and without. Costs: 2 bp round trip on ETFs, 1 tick + $1 round trip on MES. The 2023-11..2026-10 hourly pilot (19 negative-GEX days) is reported as underpowered and not judged. LETF demand D_t enters as a control once its data exist.

rows.notes: The decisive window is moved to 2020-08..2026-10, with 2015-2020 as a replication arm, because the candidate's 2023-2026 window has only 19 negative-GEX days. I counted these from a copy of the free CSV at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d0ec309-c258-503a-9a0c-4c2984e42dd2/scratchpad/dl_dix/DIX.csv, reading GEX only. The candidate's bottom-quintile state is still long gamma, so the theory predicts little there; it stays a secondary. Archiving the GEX series also unblocks a historical design for T-217 and T-218. The test needs a separation from the LETF channel (row 3).

learnings.source: Ivanov-Lenkey (J. Financial Markets 2018), as cited from memory by the sweep
learnings.finding: LETF capital flows offset much of the rebalancing, so late-day amplification is small.

On an index-only sample D_t = AUM*(x^2-x)*r_ROD/ADV is almost a rescaled r_ROD, because AUM/ADV moves slowly. Its coefficient cannot be separated from generic momentum or gamma without cross-sectional variation.

data: local 60m bars QQQ, SPY, TQQQ, SQQQ, TSLA, NVDA, MSTR, COIN, PLTR, AMD (2023-11-21..2026-10-20)
rows.missing_data: Daily LETF shares outstanding / AUM history. Issuer historical NAV and shares files (ProShares, Direxion, GraniteShares, Defiance) are free but not archived; SEC N-PORT monthly net assets are a coarse fallback. The row-1 GEX bundle is needed for the control.

registration.claim: Over 2023-11..2026-10, in a pooled daily panel of QQQ, SPY and the single stocks with 2x/3x single-stock LETFs (TSLA, NVDA, MSTR, COIN, PLTR, AMD), the rebalancing demand D = sum_k AUM_{k,t-1}*(x_k^2 - x_k)*r(prior close->15:30), divided by the underlying's trailing-20-day dollar volume, has a positive coefficient on the 15:30-to-official-close return after controlling for r(prior close->15:30) and GEX_{t-1}, and a negative coefficient on the next close-to-close return.
registration.statistic: Panel OLS with underlying fixed effects and Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Coefficients: c on D for the last half-hour, d on D for the next day. The VIF of D against r_ROD is reported.
registration.procedure: AUM_{k,t-1} = issuer shares outstanding at t-1 x NAV at t-1, published the evening of t-1 and so known at t. x_k comes from the prospectus (+2, +3, -1, -2, -3). r to 15:30 is measured to the 15:30 bar open. The cross-section of AUM/ADV, near zero for some names and large for MSTR/TSLA, supplies the variation that separates D from r_ROD. If the VIF exceeds 10 on the index-only sample, that arm is reported but not judged. Trading form: sign(D) on top-quintile |D| days, 15:30 bar open to MOC, 2 bp round trip for ETFs and 3 bp for stocks. At most 8 cells are deflated.
registration.data: local 60m bars; daily-history; LETF issuer NAV/shares files (to archive); SqueezeMetrics GEX (to archive).
registration.pass: c > 0 with Driscoll-Kraay one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over 8 cells, d < 0, and c > 0 in both halves of the window.
registration.controls: Controls: r_ROD and GEX_{t-1}. Placebo: D computed with the wrong sign of x for inverse funds. Days with LETF creations or redemptions above 5% of AUM are flagged (the flow-offset channel). Costs are charged. No grid on the quintile.

rows.notes: Index-only D cannot separate the LETF channel from momentum or gamma. The single-stock LETF boom of 2024-2026 supplies the cross-sectional variation, so the panel design is what makes this testable at all. registration.claim: On ES futures Yahoo 60m Globex bars from 2024-05-29 to 2026-10 (NQ and RTY as replications; Dukascopy USA500 2012-2024 as the extension), a long MES position held over the hour beginning 08:00 Europe/Berlin (02:00 ET, 03:00 ET in DST-asynchronous weeks), on nights after SPY's 09:30-16:00 return falls in its trailing-252-session bottom tercile, earns a positive mean net return after 1 tick plus $1.00 round-trip commission (about 0.6-0.7 bp).
registration.statistic: Mean net return per trade with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 5 sessions). Secondary: the unconditional same-hour mean, the top-tercile placebo, and the hour's rank among all 24 conditional hourly means.
registration.procedure: The window is located with zoneinfo: 08:00 Europe/Berlin is converted to UTC and matched to the Yahoo bar stamped at that UTC hour, which is that bar's open. Entry is the bar open and exit the bar close (the next bar's open). The conditioning return runs from the SPY 09:30 bar open to the official 16:00 close of the preceding session and is known at 16:00. The tercile cut uses the trailing 252 sessions only. Sunday-evening reopenings and holiday-shortened sessions are excluded. Cost per trade = 0.25 index points + $1.00 / ($5 x index level). A maker-entry variant (limit at the bid, filled only if the bar trades through it) is reported separately.
registration.data: local 60m ES_F, NQ_F, RTY_F, SPY; daily-history-SPY; daily-history--VIX; Dukascopy USA500 minutes (extension, to fetch).
registration.pass: On ES the lower 95% bound of the mean net return is above 0, and the conditional hour's gross mean is above the 97.5th percentile of the 24 conditional hourly means (bootstrap). NQ has the same sign, and the return is positive in each calendar year. The Dukascopy extension must agree before any forward test.
registration.controls: Placebo: top-tercile nights. Baseline: the unconditional hour. Alternative exposure: T-549's overnight-only hold. DST-asynchronous weeks are reported separately; this is the natural experiment, since the drift should follow Berlin time rather than New York time. One threshold (bottom tercile), no grid. Costs: 1 tick + commission; the maker variant is reported separately.

rows.name: Tug of war: persistence of overnight vs intraday return components in the cross-section

overlaps.note: The overnight premium at index level. This candidate is the cross-sectional version.
SPY overnight minus intraday gap is +3.29 bp, under its 3 bp bar.
Fading SPY opening gaps intraday loses -6.25 bp.
The UMD factor earns +0.12%/yr over 2009-2026. Lou-Polk-Skouras say momentum is earned entirely overnight, so the decomposition may be where any remaining momentum sits.
Point-in-time S&P members with Yahoo prices: only 622 of 903 fja tickers since 2008 are usable, so the universe is survivorship-biased.
Stock cross-sections are blocked on delisted prices.
MOC/MOO execution within 1.5 bp per side is the execution model this needs.

learnings.finding: The overnight premium is real at index level. Yahoo's daily open matches the first hourly bar's open to a median 0.4 bp for ETFs, so Yahoo opens are usable as auction opens; this must be re-checked for single stocks.

Mandel's stock cross-sections were judged as upper bounds or inconclusive because delisted names lack free prices (90% of the FINRA universe unpriced, about 27% of S&P tickers since 2008). A coverage gate is mandatory.
The paper's US sample ends in 2013. 2014-2026 is a genuine out-of-sample window, and the effect may be smaller there.
An overnight-only hold crosses two auctions a night: at 3 bp a side that is about 126 bp a month, so the long-only top-decile excess over SPY overnight must be large to survive.

data: local 60m bars of the 28 single stocks (open check)
rows.missing_data: Prices for delisted S&P 500 members: about 27% of fja tickers since 2008 have no Yahoo series (T-473). No free complete source exists (CRSP is paid). The claim is therefore registered on priced members with a coverage gate.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2014-01 to 2026-09, the value-weighted top decile by the sum of the past 21 overnight returns (prior official close to official open, dividends added back on ex-dates), held overnight only (buy at the official close, sell at the next official open) for the following month, earns a higher mean monthly overnight return than SPY overnight-only, net of 3 bp per side per auction for the stocks and 1 bp per side for SPY.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly net excess return with a Newey-West t (3 lags). Secondary: the same decile's intraday (open-to-close) return, expected negative (the tug of war).
registration.procedure: Membership is taken as of each formation date from fja-sp500-components, available at 09:30 ET on the change date. Value weights are price x point-in-time SEC cover shares (sec-companyfacts, by filing acceptance), with equal weight where shares are missing (reported). Formation is at the month-end close, using returns through that close. Dividends come from daily-events by ex-date; split-adjusted opens and closes from daily-history. Coverage gate (rule 9): if fewer than 90% of member-months in 2014-2026 are priced, the verdict is capped at inconclusive. 2000-2013 is run as a replication of the paper period, reported but not judged. At most 12 cells (lookback 5/21/63 x VW/EW x decile/quintile) are deflated; the primary cell is the one fixed above.
registration.data: daily-history (901 symbols), daily-events, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-companyfacts, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily.
registration.pass: Mean monthly net excess > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (12 cells), positive separately in 2014-2019 and 2020-2026, and the coverage gate met.
registration.controls: Benchmark: SPY overnight-only (T-549 style). Mirror: the bottom decile. Spot-check Yahoo's daily open against the first 60m bar open for the 28 local single stocks, as T-549 did for ETFs. Robustness: names present throughout the window. Costs are charged per auction crossing. Long-only, so no borrow is needed.

rows.notes: New to the registry, which so far has only index-level overnight tests. The cost arithmetic is decisive. Survivorship is the main threat: the claim is registered on priced members as an explicit upper bound plus a coverage gate, and a pass would still need a survivorship-free refutation before anything is built. Share the overnight/intraday decomposition code with rows 6, 8 and 16.

rows.name: Tug-of-war intensity: frequent daytime reversals of overnight gains predict higher monthly returns

overlaps.note: Overnight premium at index level.
SPY gap fade (an intraday reversal trade) lost money.
Retail-sentiment pre-open signal, too few StockTwits days.
FINRA days-to-cover deciles; proposed here as the arbitrage-capacity diagnostic.
Survivorship of the priced S&P member universe.

learnings.source: Akbas et al. as summarised in the sweep
learnings.finding: The big-stock spread is only 0.43%/month gross, a G7 replication fails outside the US and Canada, and a China study finds nothing. An all-large-cap S&P universe sits where the effect is smallest.
The paper's sample ends in 2017. Mandel's out-of-sample window is 2018-2026, after publication.
A coverage gate is needed; survivor-universe results are upper bounds.

rows.missing_data: Delisted-member prices (survivorship), as in row 5. Small-cap coverage, where the effect is said to live, is absent from the archive.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2018-01 to 2026-09 (after the paper's sample), the equal-weighted top quintile by negative-reversal intensity NR (the month's share of days with overnight return > 0 and intraday return < 0, divided by the stock's mean of that share over the prior 12 months), formed at each month-end close and held one month, earns a positive monthly Fama-French five-factor plus momentum alpha net of 10 bp per side.
registration.statistic: Monthly FF5+UMD alpha of the long-only top quintile minus the equal-weight member universe, with a Newey-West t (3 lags). The top-minus-bottom long-short is a secondary.
registration.procedure: Overnight return = prior official close to official open, with dividends added on ex-dates; intraday return = open to close. NR needs at least 15 valid days in the month and 12 prior months. Factors come from french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily, compounded to months. Formation uses data through the month-end close, and trades fill at the next close. Coverage gate as in row 5. At most 8 cells (VW/EW x quintile/decile x long-only/long-short) are deflated.
registration.data: daily-history, daily-events, fja-sp500-components, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, finra-short-interest.
registration.pass: Long-only alpha > 0 with deflated one-sided p < 0.05, positive in 2018-2021 and in 2022-2026, and the coverage gate met.
registration.controls: Placebo: positive-reversal intensity (overnight < 0, intraday > 0), which the paper says does not predict. Diagnostics: size and FINRA days-to-cover terciles. Costs scale with turnover. No grid.

rows.notes: In an S&P 500 universe every stock is big, so the expected net is near zero even before decay. Run it once as a sibling of row 5 (same data, same decomposition code), not as its own build.

Index-level continuation. The paper finds the opposite sign at stock level, so there is no contradiction.
On SPY, buying weakness at the close (IBS < 0.2) pays +12.03 bp the next day. A daily-horizon cousin of buying losers late in the day.
The FINRA short-volume ratio, used here for the interaction.
Days-to-cover deciles; the paper's interaction is on short sellers.

Own-past-price features at the 60m interval carried no tradable signal. The target there was the next bar, not a cross-sectional last-half-hour.
Yahoo bars are stamped by their open, and the 16:00 stub is the closing print, so the exit must be the official close.
The local 60m set holds only 28 single stocks, so the bottom quintile is about 6 mega-cap names a day.

registration.claim: Across the 28 single stocks with local 60m bars from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, buying the equal-weighted bottom quintile by ROD3 = log(close of the 13:30 ET bar / prior official close) at the 15:30 bar open and selling at the official close earns more than the equal-weighted 28-stock universe over the same half-hour, net of the long leg's costs (1 bp half-spread proxy + 1 bp at entry, plus the SEC Section 31 fee on the sale).

The exit is the official daily close, never the 16:00 stub. Early closes are excluded. Pre-declared interactions: top-tercile FINRA days to cover (by publication date) and top-tercile off-exchange share (finra-regsho-cnms total_volume divided by daily-history volume, for t-1). rows.name: Anomaly returns at the close: arbitrageurs de-risk before the overnight borrow and margin charge

overlaps.note: Same variable (FINRA days to cover), different design. Survivor-only EW spread net +0.36%/month against a 0.83% bar, NW t -1.30.
Bottom-minus-top DTC decile, survivor-only net -0.05% per period, FF5 alpha t -1.0.
FINRA daily short-volume ratio. 93.4% of point-in-time S&P events are priced.
The overnight premium in general.
Survivorship of the priced universe.

learnings.finding: Close-to-close DTC spreads are small on the survivor universe, which covers only about 9% of the FINRA universe. A decomposition can still be informative as a labelled upper bound.

learnings.source: Bogousslavsky 2021 and Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019 (as summarised in the sweep)
learnings.finding: The short legs of mispricing factors (overpriced, heavily shorted names) do well at the end of the day and overnight and badly intraday. High-minus-low DTC should therefore show overnight > intraday, the opposite of the sign the candidate wrote.
Overnight returns carry the equity premium, so any decomposition must be read against the overnight mean.

rows.missing_data: Delisted-name prices (survivor universe only, as T-375). Actual borrow fees need the IBKR shortable file captured daily from now, or paid data. Margin requirements are not archived.

registration.claim: Among FINRA-reported stocks with archived prices, price > $5 and ADV > $5m (T-375's eligible universe), from 2018-01 to 2026-09, the high-minus-low days-to-cover decile portfolio (formed at each FINRA publication, held to the next) has a mean overnight return (prior close to open, dividend-adjusted) that exceeds its mean intraday return (open to close) by more than 2 bp per day, meaning high-DTC stocks earn their underperformance during the day and recover overnight.
registration.statistic: Mean daily (overnight minus intraday) of the equal-weighted high-minus-low DTC spread, Newey-West t (10 lags). IVOL deciles (trailing-60-day residual volatility against SPY) are the second family member; Holm over 2.
registration.procedure: DTC = FINRA short interest / FINRA average daily volume as published. It enters at the first open after publication (about the 8th business day after settlement), never at settlement. Deciles are formed on the eligible priced universe at each publication. Daily components come from daily-history open and close, with dividends added on ex-dates (daily-events). The two-sided p is reported so that the candidate's opposite sign is also visible. Diagnostic on the 28-stock 60m set: high-DTC names' 15:30-to-close return (descriptive only).
registration.data: finra-short-interest, daily-history, daily-events, local 60m bars (diagnostic).
registration.pass: Difference > 2 bp/day with Holm one-sided p < 0.05, positive in 2018-2021 and in 2022-2026, and also positive without the Jan-Mar 2021 squeeze. The verdict is labelled survivor-universe (an upper bound), as in T-375.
registration.controls: Placebo: the middle deciles. A value-weighted version is reported. Ex-2021-squeeze run. Delisting sensitivity as in T-375. No grid.

rows.notes: Sign correction: the cited mechanism (arbitrageurs cover before the overnight borrow and margin charge; uninformed demand re-inflates overpriced names overnight) implies high-DTC names gain overnight and lose intraday. The registration therefore uses the theory's sign, with a two-sided report. If supported, the small-account form is an intraday-only short of high-DTC names, which pays no overnight borrow. It must clear about 4 bp/day of costs plus the locate, and Alpaca's hard-to-borrow limits apply.

Yahoo stamps bars by their open, and a zero-length 16:00 bar is the closing print. The 15:55 5m bar may or may not contain the cross, so equal values must be checked and dropped.
Auction opens from Yahoo agree with intraday bars for ETFs. The measurement is feasible with local data.

data: local 5m bars (~80 US equities/ETFs, 2026-07-28..2026-10-20, about 60 sessions)

registration.claim: On the ~80 US equity symbols with local 5m bars (2026-07-28 to 2026-10-20, about 60 sessions, extended forward as bars accumulate), the next close-to-open return has a slope below -0.5 on dev = log(official close / close of the last regular 5m bar before 16:00), so at least half of the closing-auction deviation reverts by the next open.

registration.procedure: The last regular bar is the 5m bar stamped 15:55 (the stamp is the bar's open). The zero-length 16:00 stub is dropped. Symbol-days whose 15:55 bar close equals the official close to 1e-6 are dropped, because that bar already contains the cross; the share dropped is reported. The next open is the daily-history open of t+1. Ex-dividend nights add back the dividend. Early closes are excluded; month-end and index-rebalance days are flagged. Part (b), the disagreement sort, is registered as blocked until the auction-volume proxy is validated.

The 00:00 UTC bar contains the 00:55 UTC Tokyo fix, so 'pre' ends at 01:00 UTC, 5 minutes after the fix; this biases against the claim.
