rows.name: Gamma-conditioned market intraday momentum (rest-of-day return predicts the last half-hour)
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens, JFE 142 (2021) 377-403. Over 60+ futures, 1974-2020, r_ROD (prior close to 30 minutes before the close) predicts r_LH with t 7.29 and R2OOS 2.88% for equities. Timing Sharpes are 1.73 for equity, 1.62 bond, 1.42 commodity and 0.87 currency, all before costs. S&P futures keep a positive net Sharpe at one tick. The results revert over the next days. ES is measured on the 09:30-16:00 cash hours. NGE comes from OptionMetrics 1996-2017 and SqueezeMetrics to May 2020: 2,930 negative days and 3,158 positive. Table 7, conditioned on NGE_{t-1}: slope 6.63 (t 4.78) when NGE<0, against 0.82 (t 1.03) when NGE>=0. I also opened the Gao-Han-Li-Zhou SSRN version (SPY 1993-2013): R2 1.6% / 2.6% / 3.3%, ROS 1.4% / 2.0%, 6.67%/yr at 6.19% volatility, Sharpe 1.08.
rows.replication_concerns: (1) The free SqueezeMetrics GEX is not the paper's NGE. The paper has 48% negative days over 1996-2020. The free CSV, counted here on GEX only, has about 6% negative days over the 2011-2020 overlap (2011 30/170, 2012 13, 2013 2, 2014 5, 2015 23, 2016 22, 2017 2, 2018 39, 2019 18, 2020 31). The sign threshold therefore marks a different state from the published one. (2) 104 of the 167 negative-GEX days in 2020-08..2026-10 fall in 2022, a high-volatility bear year, and Gao finds momentum is stronger on volatile days. The interaction is close to a '2022 x high-vol' dummy unless volatility is controlled. (3) T-427's null in 2023-26 fits a long-gamma regime, but no post-2020 independent replication was found. The shared web-search budget ran out in this run, so no targeted replication or decay search was possible.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars: SPY/QQQ/IWM 2023-11-21..2026-10-20 (about 718 15:30 bars) and ES_F/NQ_F from 2024-05-29. daily-history-SPY/QQQ carry open/close/adjclose. fomc-meetings and macro-release-* bundles exist. The DIX.csv copy (2011-05-02..2026-10-20) sits in the scratchpad but is NOT an archived bundle. No SqueezeMetrics, Alpaca IEX minute or Dukascopy bundle exists, so the decisive 2020-08..2026-10 run cannot be made from the archive.
rows.lookahead_risks: GEX dated t is built from the OI at the close of t, so only GEX_{t-1} may enter day t. The CSV is a current-methodology backfill, not a vintage. r_ROD spans the prior close: on SPY/QQQ ex-dividend days the dividend drop would read as a negative r_ROD unless the adjclose/close factor is applied, as T-427's harness does. The 15:30 price must be the first trade at or after 15:30:00 (the bar open). The exit is the official daily close, never a 16:00 stub. Early closes are excluded. The MOC exit order must be sent before the 15:50 cutoff.
rows.missing_data: Archive DIX.csv as a dated bundle and capture each day's published GEX from now on. Fetch Alpaca IEX 1-minute SPY and QQQ for 2020-08..2026-10. Dukascopy USA500 minutes are needed for the 2015-2020 replication arm.

final.claim: On SPY from 2020-08 to 2026-10, with QQQ as a replication: in r_LH = a + b*r_ROD + c*r_ROD*1[GEX_{t-1} < 0] + d*r_ROD*z(RV_{t-1}) + e*1[GEX_{t-1} < 0] + u, the gamma interaction c is positive. Here r_ROD = log(price at 15:30 ET / dividend-adjusted prior official close), r_LH = log(official close / price at 15:30), and GEX is the SqueezeMetrics value. Trading sign(r_ROD) from 15:30 to the MOC on days after a negative GEX also earns a positive mean net return after a 2 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Primary: OLS slope c, Newey-West (5 lags) t. Secondary: mean net return per trade of the sign rule on GEX_{t-1}<0 days, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 10 sessions); the GEX_{t-1}>=0 days serve as placebo.
final.procedure: P_15:30 = open of the first Alpaca IEX 1-minute bar at or after 15:30:00 ET. The prior close is scaled by f_{t-1}/f_t (f = adjclose/close) so ex-dividend drops are not read as returns. r_LH ends at the daily-history official close. GEX_{t-1} is the value SqueezeMetrics dates t-1, flagged as backfill. RV_{t-1} = trailing-20-session close-to-close realised volatility through t-1, z-scored on its trailing 252 sessions. Early closes and sessions without a 15:30 minute bar are excluded. Also reported, not judged: b alone, T-427's r1 predictor on the same days, a regression without the RV control, and a 2015-2020 Dukascopy USA500 replication arm. Deflation counts T-427's 60 cells plus 8 here (68 trials). The 2023-11..2026-10 hourly pilot has 19 negative-GEX days; it is reported as underpowered and not judged.
final.data: SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (to archive), Alpaca IEX 1-minute SPY/QQQ 2020-08..2026-10 (to fetch), daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, fomc-meetings; Dukascopy USA500 minutes (replication arm, to fetch).
final.pass: On SPY, c > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (68 trials); QQQ's c > 0; c > 0 as a point estimate with 2022 excluded; the sign rule's mean net on GEX<0 days > 0 with a bootstrap 90% lower bound above 0; and the GEX>=0 placebo not significantly positive.
final.controls: Volatility-interaction control in the main regression, because negative-GEX days cluster in high-volatility 2022. Placebo: GEX>=0 days. Baselines: T-427 and unconditional r_ROD. One threshold (GEX < 0); the bottom-quintile state is dropped. FOMC and OPEX days are flagged and reported with and without. Costs: 2 bp round trip on ETFs, 1 tick + $1 on MES. LETF demand enters as a control once its data exist.

rows.reason: The sources verify. The registration still needs three changes: an explicit volatility-interaction control, dividend-adjusted r_ROD and no secondary state. The free GEX series does not reproduce the paper's NGE sign mix, and its negative days are mostly 2022. It stays blocked until the GEX history and IEX minutes are archived.

rows.name: Volume- and news-conditioned intraday momentum and the 'noise-area' breakout
rows.source_notes: In the Gao et al. text (SPY 1993-2013), predictability is stronger on more volatile, higher-volume, recession and macro-news days. The volume terciles are on first-half-hour volume, formed within each year. R2 1.6% / 2.6% / 3.3%, ROS 1.4% / 2.0%, timing strategy 6.67% at 6.19% (Sharpe 1.08), said to survive costs. RePEc confirms Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon, SFI RP 24-97 (2024): SPY 2007 to early 2024, 1,985% total net of costs, 19.6%/yr, Sharpe 1.33. The band definition is not on the abstract page. Li-Sakkas-Urquhart was not verified.
rows.replication_concerns: Gao's within-year volume terciles use same-year future data, so its conditional R2s are in-sample. T-427's harness already printed regime diagnostics for scheduled FOMC and CPI-release days on this exact rule and window (batch5_hourly.py), so the event-day condition is no longer out-of-sample and must be dropped. T-427's 60-cell grid already charged a high-VIX conditioning, which is close to the first-bar-range condition. The base rule is flat gross (-0.09 bp on 720 days), so any positive subset implies a negative complement: a forking-path risk. T-577 used lv_rel_tod with no pass. The noise-area rule has no independent replication. The search budget was exhausted, so no new replication search was possible.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m SPY/QQQ/IWM from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10-20 are verified: 7 bars per session, stamped by bar open, 15:30 bar = last half-hour. daily-history for SPY/QQQ/IWM has open/close/adjclose. The noise-area rule needs 2007+ minute bars, which are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Tercile cut-offs must come from sessions up to t-1 only; Gao's within-year terciles are a leak. The 09:30 bar volume is known at 10:30. r1 crosses the prior close and needs dividend adjustment on ex-dates. The exit is the official close, not a 16:00 stub. Early closes are excluded.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the volume and range arms. The noise-area breakout needs Alpaca IEX or Dukascopy minute bars back to 2007 or 2020; register it separately as blocked.

final.claim: On SPY from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, with QQQ and IWM as replications, T-427's rule earns a positive mean net return after a 2 bp round trip on days whose 09:30-bar volume ratio is in the top tercile of its own trailing distribution. The rule takes the sign of the dividend-adjusted prior-close-to-10:30 return and holds from the 15:30 bar open to the official close. The ratio is the 09:30-bar volume over the trailing-20-session mean 09:30-bar volume.
final.statistic: Mean net return per condition day with a Newey-West (5 lags) t. Second family member: 09:30-bar range ((high-low)/prior close) in its trailing top tercile.
final.null: Mean net return on condition days <= 0.
final.procedure: Tercile cut-offs use an expanding window of prior sessions only, with at least 60 sessions, so the first 80 sessions are a burn-in and are dropped. The condition is known at 10:30. Entry at the 15:30 bar open, exit at the daily-history official close. Early closes are excluded. The event-day (CPI/NFP/FOMC) arm is dropped because T-427 already reported it. Holm over 2 conditions x 3 ETFs, then deflation together with T-427's 60 cells (66 trials). Complement days and T-427's unconditional result are reported side by side.
final.data: Local 60m bars SPY/QQQ/IWM; daily-history-SPY/QQQ/IWM.
final.pass: On top-tercile-volume days, SPY's mean net > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (66 trials); QQQ and IWM have the same sign; the complement days' mean net is not also > 0 (placebo).
final.controls: Placebo: complement days. Baseline: T-427 unconditional. One threshold per condition (top tercile), no grid. Costs: 2 bp round trip. The noise-area rule is registered separately as blocked, with a random-direction benchmark and 1 bp plus 1 tick per stop fill.

rows.reason: This is the lowest-value member of the family. It is cheap, but the news-day arm was already seen in T-427's regime diagnostics and is removed. The volume condition must use trailing cut-offs, not Gao's within-year terciles.

rows.name: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing flow into the close
rows.source_notes: Section 4.2 and Table 9 of Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021) are verified. Demand = NAV_{t-1}(x^2-x)r_t (Cheng-Madhavan), which made up 16.8% / 50.2% of MOC volume on 1% / 5% days in Feb 2009. Shum et al. place MOC fill risk about 30 minutes before the close. In pooled equity-futures regressions, June 2006-May 2020, IndexingLETF*r_ROD is 1.79 (t 2.20) and 2.94 (t 3.10). IndexingLETF is LETF NAV x (x^2-x) over index market value. The cross-market scatter shows LETF share rising with the momentum t-stat. Ivanov-Lenkey (flow offset) was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The paper identifies the effect from cross-market and time variation in LETF share over 2006-2020. In a single index, D_t is almost a rescaled r_ROD (AUM/ADV moves slowly), so only a cross-sectional panel separates it. T-427 finds no last-half-hour continuation in the record-AUM years 2023-26. The flow-offset critique is unverified. No search was possible (budget exhausted).
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars are verified for QQQ, SPY, TQQQ, SQQQ, TSLA, NVDA, MSTR, COIN, PLTR and AMD (2023-11-21..2026-10-20). daily-history has TQQQ/SQQQ/SSO/SDS/UPRO/SPXU prices and volume but not shares outstanding or NAV. No LETF AUM bundle exists, and no GEX bundle.
rows.lookahead_risks: AUM_{t-1} must be the issuer's shares outstanding x NAV as published on the evening of t-1. Issuer history files can be restated, so archive first-seen values. Single-stock LETFs must enter only from their launch date. The GEX control exists only for the index; single stocks have no free dealer-gamma series, so that control is index-only. r to 15:30 needs dividend adjustment on ex-dates.
rows.missing_data: Daily shares outstanding and NAV history for SPX/NDX LETFs and for the single-stock 2x/-2x funds (TSLL, NVDL, MSTU/MSTX, CONL, PLTU, AMDL and others) from issuer files. Capture them forward on the Linode box. Also needed: the SqueezeMetrics GEX bundle.

final.claim: Over 2023-11..2026-10, in a pooled daily panel of QQQ, SPY and the single stocks with 2x/3x or inverse single-stock LETFs (TSLA, NVDA, MSTR, COIN, PLTR, AMD), LETF rebalancing demand D has a positive coefficient on the 15:30-to-official-close return and a negative coefficient on the next close-to-close return. D = sum_k AUM_{k,t-1}*(x_k^2 - x_k)*r(dividend-adjusted prior close -> 15:30), divided by the underlying's trailing-20-day dollar volume. The last-half-hour regression controls for r(prior close -> 15:30), and on SPY/QQQ also for GEX_{t-1}.
final.statistic: Panel OLS with underlying fixed effects and Driscoll-Kraay standard errors: c on D for the last half-hour, d on D for the next day. The VIF of D against r_ROD is reported.
final.procedure: AUM_{k,t-1} = issuer shares outstanding x NAV at t-1, first-seen values only. x_k comes from the prospectus. The 15:30 price is the 15:30 bar open; the exit is the official close. A fund enters on its launch date. If the index-only VIF exceeds 10, that arm is reported but not judged; the cross-section of AUM/ADV supplies the identification. Normaliser: trailing-20-day dollar volume (pre-declared; the market-cap version from sec-companyfacts is reported). Trading form: sign(D) on top-quintile |D| days, 15:30 bar open to MOC, 2 bp round trip for ETFs and 3 bp for stocks. At most 8 cells are deflated.
final.data: Local 60m bars (listed symbols), daily-history, daily-events, LETF issuer NAV/shares files (to archive), SqueezeMetrics GEX (to archive).
final.pass: c > 0 with Driscoll-Kraay one-sided p < 0.05 after deflation over 8 cells; c > 0 in both halves of the window; d < 0 as a point estimate.
final.controls: r_ROD and, for the index names, GEX_{t-1}. Placebo: D built with x_k replaced by +|x_k| for inverse funds. Days with creations or redemptions above 5% of AUM are flagged (the flow-offset channel). Costs charged. No grid on the quintile.

rows.reason: The source verifies, and the panel design is the only way to separate the LETF channel from momentum. It stays blocked until the LETF AUM history and the GEX series are archived.

rows.name: Overnight drift at the European open (2-3 a.m. ET in S&P futures) after US sell-offs
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of NY Fed SR 917 (revised Aug 2022): Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan, ES and SP 1998-2020. 02:00-03:00 ET averages 3.7% annualised (1.48 bp/day). It is positive in 20 of 23 years and significant in 17. It is the only hour that survives Bonferroni/BY and is significant on every weekday. Going long 2-3 has Sharpe 1.1 before costs and -0.5 after the spread; 1:30-3:30 has 1.3 and 0.3. The documented conditional is buy-the-dip (BtD): hold over 1:30-3:30 only after negative closing relative signed volume (RSV, 15:15-16:15). BtD has Sharpe 1.8 before costs and 1.1 after (2004-2020, when the overnight spread was at the minimum tick). DST test: in the roughly three asynchronous weeks, predictability at 2-3 ET disappears and shifts to 4-5 ET (fewer than 300 days, 'not well measured').
rows.replication_concerns: (1) The paper's conditioning variable is closing signed volume, not the session return. The candidate's 'SPY session return bottom tercile' is untested in the source; the closest observable proxy is the sign of ES's last US-session hour. (2) The cross-check anchored the window to 08:00 Berlin, which implies 03:00 ET in asynchronous weeks. That contradicts the paper's own DST result (4-5 ET), so the pre-declared 'natural experiment' would test something the source does not claim. (3) T-563 shows return-state conditioning of overnight holds added nothing. (4) The sample ends 2020. Bondarenko-Muravyev was not opened, and no post-2020 replication search was possible (budget exhausted). (5) Power: about 290 conditional nights, and at the paper's per-trade volatility the expected t is about 1.5-2, so the local run is close to a pilot.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m ES_F, NQ_F and RTY_F are verified from 2024-05-29 to 2026-10-20 (about 13,700 rows each, about 23 bars per day). Bars sit on the UTC hour and are stamped by open, so the 02:00 ET hour is exactly one bar. Yahoo futures bars carry volume 0, so stale bars cannot be found by volume. Also verified: SPY 60m and daily-history--VIX.
rows.lookahead_risks: The conditioning bar (ES 15:00-16:00 ET) is complete at 16:00. ET-to-UTC mapping uses zoneinfo. Continuous-contract roll gaps: exclude roll dates. Stale bars (open=high=low=close) in thin hours must be flagged. Sunday reopenings and CME holiday or early-close sessions are excluded. A maker-entry variant must not assume fills: a resting bid fills only if the bar trades through it.
rows.missing_data: The decisive 2012-2026 run needs Dukascopy USA500 minute data (free, fetch planned).

final.claim: On Yahoo 60m ES_F bars from 2024-05-29 to 2026-10, with NQ_F and RTY_F as replications, a long MES position from 02:00 to 03:00 ET on nights after the ES bar 15:00-16:00 ET of the preceding US session closed below its open earns a positive mean net return after 1 tick plus $1.00 round-trip commission. That down closing hour is the observable proxy for the paper's negative closing signed volume. DST-asynchronous weeks are excluded.
final.statistic: Mean net return per trade, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (block 5 sessions) and HAC t. Secondaries: the unconditional 02:00-03:00 mean, the complement (closing hour up) nights, and the hour's rank among all 24 conditional hourly means.
final.procedure: Fixed ET clock as in the paper. The 02:00 ET bar (06:00 UTC in EDT, 07:00 UTC in EST) opens the trade and its close is the exit. The condition is the close vs open of the ES bar stamped 15:00 ET on the preceding US session, known at 16:00. Excluded: weeks when the New York-London offset is 4 hours (reported separately, including the 04:00-05:00 ET hour the paper points to), contract-roll dates, Sunday reopenings, CME holiday and early-close sessions, and bars with open=high=low=close. Cost per trade = (0.25 + 1.00/5) index points / level, about 0.6 bp at current levels.
final.data: Local 60m ES_F, NQ_F, RTY_F; daily-history--VIX (diagnostic); Dukascopy USA500 minutes (2012-2024 extension, to fetch).
final.pass: On ES, the one-sided 95% lower bound of the mean net is above 0. NQ has the same sign, the mean net is positive in both halves of the window, and the conditional mean exceeds the complement-night mean.
final.controls: Placebos: complement nights and the adjacent hours 01:00-02:00 and 03:00-04:00 ET. Baseline: T-549's overnight-only hold. The maker variant is reported separately and expected to do worse (Hurst adverse-selection learning). One threshold (closing-hour return < 0), no grid. The Dukascopy 2012-2026 extension must agree before any forward test. Verdict goes to Hurst's H-us500-overnight.

rows.reason: The source is verified. Two of the candidate's design choices conflict with it: the DST anchoring contradicts the paper's own asynchronous-week result, and the return-tercile condition is not the paper's order-imbalance condition. Both are replaced with the paper's fixed 02:00 ET hour and a closing-hour selling proxy.

rows.name: Tug of war: persistence of overnight vs intraday return components in the cross-section
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Lou, Polk and Skouras, JFE 134 (2019) 192-213, CRSP/TAQ 1993-2013. It excludes price < $5 and the bottom NYSE size quintile. The VW decile on past one-month overnight return earns +3.47%/month overnight (t 16.57) and -3.24% intraday (t -9.34). On past intraday return: +2.19% intraday (t 6.72) and -1.81% overnight (t -8.44). The open is a VWAP-based opening price. Replacing it with the opening midquote leaves an overnight 3-factor alpha of 1.88% (t 8.75). Momentum profits accrue overnight.
rows.replication_concerns: The sample ends in 2013, so 2014-2026 is a true out-of-sample window, but post-2013 decay could not be searched (budget exhausted). The paper's 'open' is a VWAP open; a MOO fill at the official opening print is a different and arguably harsher price. The long-only leg gets roughly half the long-short spread, while an overnight-only hold crosses two auctions a night (about 126 bp/month at 3 bp per side). The expected net is small even before decay.
rows.data_notes: daily-history bundles include open/high/low/close/adjclose (901 symbols). daily-events carries dividends and splits. fja-sp500-components runs from 1996, with spells. sec-companyfacts carries cover shares by filing. french-ff5-daily exists. T-473: 247 of 903 fja tickers since 2008 have no Yahoo series, 13 tickers were reused as ETFs and 17 have name mismatches. T-549 checked the Yahoo open only for ETFs.
rows.lookahead_risks: Survivorship (delisted members absent), so a coverage gate is needed. Ticker reuse: a price series must match the member's company over its spell. Membership is point-in-time from fja, available at 09:30 on the change date. Value weights use SEC shares by filing acceptance and the prior close. Overnight returns need the dividend added back on ex-date nights. The formation signal uses overnight returns through the formation day's open, so it is known before the MOC buy. Yahoo's single-stock open must be spot-checked against the first 60m bar open.
rows.missing_data: Delisted-member prices (CRSP is paid). The claim is registered on priced members with a coverage gate.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2014-01 to 2026-09, the value-weighted top decile by the sum of the past 21 overnight returns earns a higher mean monthly overnight return than SPY overnight-only. Overnight return = prior official close to official open, with dividends added back on ex-dates. The decile is held overnight only (buy the MOC, sell the next MOO) for the following month. Costs: 3 bp per side per auction for the stocks and 1 bp per side for SPY.
final.statistic: Mean monthly net excess return with a Newey-West t (3 lags). Secondary: the same decile's intraday (open-to-close) return, expected negative.
final.procedure: Formation at each month-end session uses the 21 overnight returns through that session's open, and the first buy is that session's MOC. Membership comes from fja-sp500-components as of the formation date. Value weights = prior close x the latest SEC cover shares accepted before formation, equal weight where shares are missing (share reported). Each price series is checked against the member's ticker spell; reused tickers are refused. Coverage gate: if fewer than 90% of member-months in 2014-2026 are priced, the verdict is capped at inconclusive. 2000-2013 runs as an unjudged replication of the paper period. At most 12 cells (lookback 5/21/63 x VW/EW x decile/quintile) are deflated; the primary cell is VW decile, 21-day lookback.
final.data: daily-history (901 symbols), daily-events, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-companyfacts, daily-history-SPY, french-ff5-daily; local 60m bars of 28 stocks (open check).
final.pass: Mean monthly net excess > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (12 cells), positive separately in 2014-2019 and 2020-2026, and the coverage gate met.
final.controls: Benchmark: SPY overnight-only. Mirror: the bottom decile. Open spot-check on 28 stocks (median |Yahoo open - first 60m open| reported). Robustness: names present throughout. Costs per auction crossing. Long-only, so no borrow.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the claim is new to the registry. It is fixed to state point-in-time signal timing, ticker-reuse checks and the coverage gate, since survivorship and costs are the main threats.

rows.name: Tug-of-war intensity: frequent daytime reversals of overnight gains predict higher monthly returns
rows.source_notes: CXO's review (Mar 2019) of Akbas, Boehmer, Jiang and Koch (WP Jan 2019; US common stocks May 1993-Dec 2017) confirms the details. Intensity = the month's share of negative daytime reversal days divided by its prior-12-month average. The EW top-minus-bottom decile earns 0.92%/month gross, with alphas of 0.85% (3-factor), 0.81% (4-factor) and 0.88% (5-factor). By size: 0.97% small, 0.75% mid, 0.43% big. The effect persists up to six months without reversal. Returns are gross, and shorting may be infeasible. The JFE 2022 publication was not separately opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The mixed G7 and China replications come from a search summary and are unverified; no new search was possible (budget exhausted). In an all-large-cap S&P universe the documented spread is 0.43%/month gross before any post-2017 decay. With about 105 months and a monthly tracking volatility of about 1%, the standard error is about 0.1%/month, so any net alpha under 0.2%/month cannot be detected. Expect inconclusive or not supported.
rows.data_notes: Verified: daily-history OHLC, daily-events, fja-sp500-components, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily and finra-short-interest (2017-12-29..2026-09-30). The archive has no small-cap coverage, which is where the effect lives.
rows.lookahead_risks: Survivorship and ticker reuse, as in the tug-of-war candidate. The NR denominator needs 12 prior months: 2017 data are used for formation only. Factors must be compounded from daily data within each holding month. FINRA days to cover enters by publication date.
rows.missing_data: Delisted-member prices; a small-cap universe.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2018-01 to 2026-09, after the paper's sample, the equal-weighted top quintile by negative-reversal intensity NR earns a positive monthly FF5+UMD alpha against the equal-weight member universe, net of 10 bp per side on traded weight. NR = the month's share of days with overnight return > 0 and intraday return < 0, divided by the stock's mean of that share over the prior 12 months. The quintile is formed at each month-end close and held one month.
final.statistic: Monthly FF5+UMD alpha of the top-quintile-minus-universe return, with a Newey-West t (3 lags). The top-minus-bottom long-short is secondary.
final.procedure: Overnight = prior official close to official open, with dividends added on ex-dates; intraday = open to close. NR needs at least 15 valid days in the month and 12 prior months. Formation uses data through the month-end close and fills at the next session's close. Factors come from french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily, compounded to months. Same coverage gate and ticker-spell check as the tug-of-war candidate. At most 8 cells deflated.
final.data: daily-history, daily-events, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, finra-short-interest (diagnostic).
final.pass: Long-only alpha > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05, positive in 2018-2021 and in 2022-2026, and the coverage gate met.
final.controls: Placebo: positive-reversal intensity (overnight < 0, intraday > 0), which the paper says does not predict. Diagnostics: size and FINRA days-to-cover terciles. Costs scale with turnover. No grid.

rows.reason: Verified and new, but it lives where the effect is smallest (big stocks) and the test is underpowered. Register it once as a sibling of the tug-of-war test, sharing its decomposition code, with that power stated in advance.

rows.name: End-of-day reversal in the cross-section (intraday losers bounce in the last half-hour)
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Baltussen, Da and Soebhag, End-of-Day Reversal (April 2025), sample from 1993. ROD3 = overnight + first half-hour + middle of day, ending one hour before the close; the 15:00-15:30 window is skipped; LH is 15:30-16:00. Long-short returns are 3.78-6.86 bp/day (9.5-17.3%/yr) depending on weighting and price filter, with t typically above 10. The effect is present in almost every 3-year rolling window and in the largest and most liquid stocks. It is not explained by liquidity or gamma hedging; the channels are retail buy-the-dip and short-seller risk management. Returns are gross, and the authors say it 'might not be exploitable by many investors after accounting for transaction costs'.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication exists; it is a working paper and the search budget was exhausted. With 28 mega-caps the bottom quintile is about 6 names, so breadth is small. The 28 names (PLTR, SMCI, MSTR, COIN ...) were chosen with hindsight; this matters little for a half-hour reversal but should be stated.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars are verified for the 28 single stocks, 2023-11-21..2026-10-20. Bars are stamped by open, and the 15:30 bar is the last half-hour. daily-history, finra-short-interest and finra-regsho-cnms (2018-08..2026-10) exist.
rows.lookahead_risks: ROD3 spans the prior close: on ex-dividend days (CVX, XOM, JPM, BAC ...) the drop would push names into the loser quintile spuriously, so add the dividend back. ROD3 uses bars through 14:30; the 14:30-15:30 bar is skipped. The exit is the official close. FINRA days to cover enters by publication date. The CNMS off-exchange share uses t-1. Earnings days are included but reported.
rows.missing_data: The decisive run needs intraday bars for about 500 names (Alpaca IEX from 2020).

final.claim: Across the 28 single stocks with local 60m bars, from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, the equal-weighted bottom quintile by ROD3 beats the equal-weighted 28-stock universe from the 15:30 bar open to the official close, net of the long leg's costs. ROD3 = log(close of the 13:30 ET bar / dividend-adjusted prior official close). Costs: 1 bp half-spread plus 1 bp at entry, and the SEC Section 31 fee on the sale.
final.statistic: Mean daily net excess in bp with a Newey-West t (5 lags). Secondaries: the long-only absolute net return; the hedged trade (long bottom quintile, short equal-dollar QQQ over the same half-hour, both legs charged); and the Fama-MacBeth slope of r(15:30 -> close) on ROD3.
final.procedure: The prior close is adjusted for dividends on ex-dates. The 14:30-15:30 bar is skipped so bid-ask bounce cannot drive the result. Entry at the 15:30 bar open, exit at the daily official close. Early closes excluded. The FINRA days-to-cover and off-exchange-share interactions are reported but not judged (about 3 names per cell). At most 6 cells deflated.
final.data: Local 60m bars (28 single stocks), daily-history, daily-events, finra-short-interest, finra-regsho-cnms.
final.pass: Mean net excess > 0 with one-sided deflated p < 0.05 (6 cells), positive in each half of the window (split at 2025-05), and a negative Fama-MacBeth slope.
final.controls: Mirror: the top quintile. Placebo: a random quintile. Costs on the traded legs. No grid. A 500-name Alpaca IEX version is registered separately as blocked.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the claim is new. Fixed for dividend adjustment of ROD3 and a hedged executable form; low breadth means the 28-name run is a pilot of the decisive 500-name test.

rows.name: Anomaly returns at the close: arbitrageurs de-risk before the overnight borrow and margin charge
rows.source_notes: RePEc abstract of Bogousslavsky, JFE 141(1) 2021 172-194: margin requirements are higher overnight and lending fees are charged only on overnight positions. Arbitrageurs therefore cut mispricing positions before the close, so a mispricing factor earns positive returns during the day but poor returns at the end of the day. The effect is stronger in the second half of the sample and shared by several anomalies. Magnitudes and the size/IVOL details were not verified (abstract only).
rows.replication_concerns: Only the abstract was verified, so magnitudes are unknown. T-375 and T-393 were inconclusive because about 91% of the FINRA universe has no archived price; the same design on the FINRA universe would be NOT JUDGED by construction. The cross-check's sign correction is right: the theory implies high-DTC names lose intraday and recover overnight. No search was possible (budget exhausted).
rows.data_notes: finra-short-interest (211 bundles, 2017-12-29..2026-09-30, incl. averageDailyVolumeQuantity) exists. daily-history has OHLC and daily-events has dividends. Restricting to point-in-time S&P 500 members makes coverage passable: T-394 had 93.4% of S&P events priced 2019-2026.
rows.lookahead_risks: FINRA publishes about 8 business days after settlement, so days to cover enters at the first open after publication, never at settlement. Membership is point-in-time. Dividends are added on ex-date nights. The Jan-Mar 2021 squeeze needs an exclusion run. Survivorship gate applies.
rows.missing_data: Borrow fees (IBKR shortable file, captured forward), margin requirements, and delisted names.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2018-01 to 2026-09, the equal-weighted high-minus-low FINRA days-to-cover decile spread has a mean overnight return that exceeds its mean intraday return by more than 2 bp per day. The deciles are formed at each FINRA publication and held to the next. Overnight = prior close to open, dividend-adjusted; intraday = open to close.
final.statistic: Mean daily (overnight minus intraday) of the spread, with a Newey-West t (10 lags). Second family member: deciles on trailing-60-day idiosyncratic volatility against SPY; Holm over 2.
final.procedure: DTC = FINRA short interest / FINRA average daily volume, as published. It enters at the first open after the publication date. Deciles are formed within priced members at each publication. Daily components come from daily-history opens and closes, with dividends from daily-events. The two-sided p is reported so the opposite sign is also visible. Coverage gate: at least 90% of member-days priced, else inconclusive. Descriptive only: high-DTC names' 15:30-to-close return on the 28-stock 60m set.
final.data: finra-short-interest, daily-history, daily-events, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, local 60m bars (diagnostic).
final.pass: Difference > 2 bp/day with Holm one-sided p < 0.05, positive in 2018-2021 and in 2022-2026, positive without Jan-Mar 2021, and the coverage gate met.
final.controls: Placebo: middle deciles. Value-weighted version reported. Ex-2021-squeeze run. No grid. If supported, an intraday-only short of high-DTC names must clear about 4 bp/day plus the locate before any build.

rows.reason: The sign is corrected to what the theory implies. The universe moves to point-in-time S&P 500 members, because the FINRA-wide universe is about 91% unpriced and would be NOT JUDGED, as T-375 and T-393 were.

rows.name: Closing-auction price pressure and auction-volume share (disagreement)
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Bogousslavsky and Muravyev, 'Who Trades at the Close?' (Dec 3, 2020; TAQ 2010-2018). The auction was 7.48% of dollar volume in 2018 against 3.11% in 2010. The mean absolute deviation of the closing price from the closing midquote is 8.12 bp: 20.6 bp for small stocks and 2.66 bp for large. On 1% of stock-days it exceeds 0.63%. Deviations revert half-way within 20 minutes after the close and fully overnight. Disagreement: the CHANGE in the intraday-to-auction volume ratio predicts returns (decile spread 12 bp/week, 34 bp/month, 4.2%/yr, t 3.3/4.9); the level does not.
rows.replication_concerns: Large-cap deviations (about 2.7 bp) are close to the last trade's bid-ask bounce. Yahoo gives the last trade, not the midquote, so errors-in-variables attenuate the slope toward 0, which biases against the claim. T-428's regressor L (15:30 open to official close) contains this deviation for SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD, so those four were partly seen. The cross-check's blocked part (b) sorted on the 20-day LEVEL of the ratio, but the paper says only the change predicts; it must use the change.
rows.data_notes: Checked here (prices only, no returns regressed). The 60m 15:30 bar's close equals the 5m 15:55 bar's close on all 60 overlap days for SPY, AAPL and NVDA, so it is the last regular trade before 16:00. It equals the official close on only 33/718 (SPY), 72/718 (AAPL), 61/718 (NVDA), 110/718 (XLU) and 82/718 (JPM) days. Median |deviation|: SPY 0.76 bp, AAPL 1.41, NVDA 2.16. The test can therefore run on 60m bars for 2023-11-21..2026-10-20, about 718 sessions x about 55 equity symbols, instead of 60 sessions of 5m bars. A 16:00 stub bar exists only for the current day. daily-history ends 2026-10-14; the local 1d bars run to 2026-10-20.
rows.lookahead_risks: Drop symbol-days where the 15:30 bar close equals the official close, since that bar already contains the cross; report the share dropped. Dividends on ex-date nights. Early closes. The next open is the official opening print. Month-end, index-rebalance and quad-witching days are flagged. Day fixed effects are needed because overnight shocks are common across names.
rows.missing_data: Part (b) needs validated per-stock closing-cross volume; register it separately as blocked, sorting on the change in the ratio. 15:59:50 NBBO mids would remove bounce; capture them forward.

final.claim: On the US equity symbols with local 60m bars (28 single stocks, 11 sector SPDRs and the other equity ETFs), from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, the next close-to-open return has a slope below -0.5 on dev = log(official close / close of the 15:30 ET bar), with day fixed effects. At least half of the closing-auction deviation reverts by the next open.
final.statistic: Pooled OLS slope with day fixed effects; day-clustered wild bootstrap (Rademacher, 9,999 draws). Secondaries: the slope without fixed effects, per-symbol slopes, and stocks only.
final.procedure: The 15:30 bar's close is the last regular trade before 16:00; this was verified against 5m bars. Symbol-days where it equals the official close are dropped. The official close and the next official open come from daily-history or the local 1d bars. Ex-dividend nights add the dividend back. Early closes are excluded. Month-end and rebalance days are flagged. No trading costs are charged: this is a cost diagnostic for MOC-based rules (T-559, the overnight cross-sections).
final.data: Local 60m bars (equity symbols), local 1d bars, daily-history, daily-events; local 5m bars (60-session cross-check).
final.pass: Slope < -0.5 with one-sided wild-cluster p < 0.05, slope < 0 in both halves of the sessions, and the stocks-only slope < 0.
final.controls: Robustness: SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD excluded (partly seen through T-428's L). Placebo: the previous day's dev against today's close-to-open (expected about 0). |dev| winsorised above 20 bp. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified. Its decisive fix is that the 60m 15:30 bar close is the pre-auction last trade, which turns a 60-session pilot into a 718-session test. Day fixed effects and the paper's 'change, not level' correction for part (b) are added.

rows.name: FX fixing 'W' pattern: the dollar appreciates into the Tokyo and London fixes and depreciates after
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Krohn, Mueller and Whelan, BoC SWP 2021-48 (Oct 2021; G9 1999-2019, Refinitiv tick history). Windows in ET: pre-T is 17:00 to the 9:55 JST fix; post-T runs to 02:00 ET (08:00 Frankfurt); pre-E is 02:00 to the 14:15 CET ECB fix; E-L runs to 11:00 (London 16:00); post-L is 11:00-17:00. Annualised dollar-portfolio (long foreign) returns: pre-T -5.02 (t -11.69), post-T +5.28 (t 9.19), pre-E -4.21 (t -4.50), E-L +0.34 (t 0.37), post-L +4.63 (t 5.48). In 2014-19 the figures are -1.59 / +2.08 / -3.14 / +2.16. Full indicative spreads reverse the profits; 50% spreads leave them positive.
rows.replication_concerns: The cross-check's registration has a substantive error. It used ECB fix -> London fix (E-L) as the 'pre' window of the European arm, which is the flat window in the paper (+0.34, t 0.37). The paper's European reversal is pre-E (European open to ECB fix) against post-L. Its post-Tokyo window also ended at 08:00 London instead of 08:00 Berlin (02:00 ET), mixing an hour of pre-E into post-T. Power: at 2014-19 magnitudes (about 0.8 bp/day per window), about 700 days of 60m data give an expected t of about 1.2-1.6. The 'positive in each calendar year' rule is therefore too strict. No decay search was possible (budget exhausted).
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars are verified for EURUSD_X, GBPUSD_X, AUDUSD_X, NZDUSD_X, USDJPY_X, USDCAD_X and USDCHF_X from 2024-01-03 to 2026-10-20 (about 17,200 rows each), on UTC hours, stamped by open, volume 0 (indicative quotes). DX-Y.NYB runs from 2024-05-29. The basket is 7 currencies, not G6. fx-spot-g10 (FRED noon) is available as a daily cross-check.
rows.lookahead_risks: The ECB fix (14:15 CET) is not on a bar boundary; ending pre-E at the 14:00 Berlin boundary misses the last 15 pre-fix minutes, which biases against the claim. The Tokyo fix (00:55 UTC) sits inside the 00:00 UTC bar; pre-T ends at 01:00 UTC, also biased against. DST is handled with zoneinfo. Stale quotes in the 17:00-18:00 ET rollover hour and the Sunday open are excluded. Japanese holidays (no Tokyo fix) are reported separately.
rows.missing_data: Dukascopy FX minutes for exact fix minutes and the 2012-2026 window; OANDA spread history only if recorded.

final.claim: On Yahoo 60m bars from 2024-01 to 2026-10, for an equal-weight USD-versus-7-currency basket (EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, JPY, CAD, CHF), the USD return before each fix exceeds the USD return after it, each by more than 0 bp per day. Tokyo: pre-T [17:00 America/New_York -> 01:00 UTC] against post-T [01:00 UTC -> 08:00 Europe/Berlin]. Europe: pre-E [08:00 Europe/Berlin -> 14:00 Europe/Berlin] against post-L [16:00 Europe/London -> 17:00 America/New_York].
final.statistic: Mean daily (pre minus post) basket return per fix, with a Newey-West t (5 lags) and per-currency signs. Secondary: net P&L of long USD pre / short USD post at 1 bp per side (EURUSD, USDJPY) and 2 bp (others), pre-registered as expected <= 0.
final.null: Mean (pre minus post) <= 0 for a fix.
final.procedure: Window edges are built in local time with zoneinfo and mapped to bars by their UTC open stamps. The basket is the mean of sign-aligned log returns (positive = USD up). The E-L window (ECB fix to London fix) is excluded, as in the paper. Japanese holidays and month-end days (T-575) are reported separately. Bars with open=high=low=close are treated as stale and the window is dropped for that currency-day.
final.data: Local 60m bars EURUSD_X, GBPUSD_X, AUDUSD_X, NZDUSD_X, USDJPY_X, USDCAD_X, USDCHF_X, DX-Y.NYB; fx-spot-g10 (cross-check).
final.pass: For both fixes, (pre minus post) > 0 with Holm one-sided p < 0.05 and positive in both halves of the window, with at least 5 of 7 currencies having the same sign. The trading-rule net is reported, not required.
final.controls: Placebo windows of the same lengths shifted by 6 hours. DXY as a check. The E-L window is reported as an expected-flat placebo. No grid over window edges. Framed as execution timing for FX conversions and hedges: both arms pay one spread.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the cross-check's registration put the European arm on the paper's flat window (E-L) and cut post-Tokyo at the wrong city's open. Windows are corrected to pre-E vs post-L and 08:00 Berlin, and the pass rule is relaxed to halves given the known power.

rows.name: Intraday periodicity: same-half-hour return continuation across days (Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka)
rows.source_notes: arXiv 1005.3535 (Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka, JF 65(4) 2010, 1369-1407): continuation at half-hour lags that are exact multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 trading days. Reversals at under one hour come from liquidity imbalances and bounce. Timing trades can cut execution costs by about the effective spread. Sample years were not stated on the page. The GitHub Andersen-Bollerslev replication is verified: same-interval momentum gross t 9.0, break-even 0.05 bp against a 0.6 bp stylised cost. The EFMA 2024 decay paper returned 503 and is unverified.
rows.replication_concerns: The reported 75% decay of the first-lag effect is unverified. Hurst's crypto hour-of-day null (549 trials) and T-476's monthly-seasonality failure argue for a modest prior. On 60m bars the test is same-hour (7 bars per day), not same-half-hour, except that the last bar is a half-hour. Breadth is 39 names, chosen with hindsight.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars are verified for the 28 stocks and 11 sector SPDRs, 2023-11-21..2026-10-20. The 30m bars cover 60 sessions (2026-07-28 on). daily-history provides official closes and opens.
rows.lookahead_risks: Regressors use sessions before d only. For the 09:30 bar the 'previous bars' control must include the overnight return (official close to official open, dividend-adjusted) and the prior 15:30 bar. The 15:30 bar ends at the official close, not a stub. Early closes are dropped.
rows.missing_data: Multi-year half-hour bars for about 500 names (Alpaca IEX 2020+) for the decisive run.

final.claim: Across the 28 single stocks and 11 sector SPDRs with local 60m bars, from 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, the Fama-MacBeth slope of a name's cross-sectionally demeaned hour-h return on the mean of its own demeaned hour-h returns over the previous 20 sessions is positive for the 09:30 and 15:30 bars. The regression controls for the name's two preceding intervals (for 09:30: the overnight return and the prior day's 15:30 bar).
final.statistic: Mean of daily cross-sectional slopes per bar, with a Newey-West t (5 lags). Lags 1 and 1-5 are reported as secondaries.
final.procedure: Bar returns run from bar open to bar close; the 15:30 bar ends at the official close. Returns are demeaned across names per bar-day. Early closes are dropped. Only if the primary passes: (a) add same-time-of-day lag features to T-577's F2 family under a new pre-registered ablation; (b) shadow T-559's rebalance timing in Alpaca paper against the fixed-time baseline, measuring implementation shortfall.
final.data: Local 60m bars (28 stocks + 11 sector SPDRs), daily-history, daily-events.
final.pass: Both the 09:30 and 15:30 slopes > 0 with Holm one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves of the window.
final.controls: Placebos: the 11:30 and 12:30 bars. Stocks-only and ETFs-only splits. No standalone trading claim, since the cost evidence says it is far below cost. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the feature family is untested in Mandel. Fixed so the 09:30 bar's bounce and overnight controls are explicit; a pass is a feature or execution input, not an edge.

rows.name: Intraday option-straddle momentum (open and close) and within-day straddle reversal
rows.source_notes: I opened the full text of Da, Filippou, Goyenko, Zhang, Zhou and Zhou, 'Intraday Option Return Predictability' (Oct 2, 2026). It covers January 2010 to December 2024, with CBOE 1-minute NBBO for 2010-18 and ThetaData OPRA for 2019-24. The prior-day open-interval winner-minus-loser earns 73 bp/day (Sharpe 3.5, monthly six-factor alpha 15.2%); the afternoon earns 37 bp/day (Sharpe 2.3). Within-day reversal is about 3-9 bp per half-hour. Returns are at quote midpoints and ignore costs, and the paper says the profits 'may not be achievable by the average investor'. It merges two earlier working papers.
rows.replication_concerns: Too new for independent replication. Single-name straddle spreads of several percent of premium dwarf the mid-to-mid edge. Scaling the paper's power down, 23 names x 120 sessions gives an expected t below 1, so the capture must grow to about 100 names x 250 sessions.
rows.data_notes: options-chain bundles hold only 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 snapshots (SPY 13,470 rows etc., Cboe delayed 15 minutes). No intraday history exists; forward capture only.
rows.lookahead_risks: Cboe delayed quotes are 15 minutes late: fetch at mark + 15 minutes and stamp by the quote's own time. The ATM strike is fixed at 09:35 and held through 10:00 (the same contract at both marks). Delta-neutralise at the mark's underlying mid. Exclude earnings days. ETF options trade to 16:15, single names to 16:00.
rows.missing_data: Intraday chain snapshots at 09:35, 10:00, 15:30 and 16:00 ET for SPY, QQQ, IWM and about 100 option-liquid single names over 250 sessions, from the capture box.

final.claim: Over the first 250 capture sessions after registration, across SPY, QQQ, IWM and the 100 most option-liquid US single names captured at 09:35, 10:00, 15:30 and 16:00 ET, the mean daily cross-sectional rank correlation is positive. It correlates each name's prior-session 09:35-to-10:00 ATM straddle mid return with its same-window return today.
final.statistic: Mean daily cross-sectional Spearman correlation with a Newey-West t. Executable P&L per straddle (buy at the ask at 09:35, sell at the bid at 10:00 on prior-session winners) with a block bootstrap, reported.
final.procedure: ATM straddle = the strike nearest spot in the first expiry at least 7 days out, fixed at 09:35. Mid = (bid+ask)/2 at each mark, by quote timestamp. Delta-neutralised at the underlying mid. Names with a 09:35 quoted spread above 10% of mid are excluded, as are earnings days. The afternoon window (15:30-16:00) is the second family member; Holm over 2.
final.data: Linode capture-box chains (to accumulate), daily-history.
final.pass: Morning mean rank correlation > 0 with Holm one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves. The executable net is reported and pre-registered as expected below 0.
final.controls: Within-day reversal (09:35-10:00 against 10:00-10:30) reported. Placebo: random pairing across names. The spread filter is fixed in advance. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified. The capture plan must be scaled to about 100 names x 250 sessions to have power. Its only small-account value is as an F3 timing feature, since spreads kill the trade.

rows.name: Bitcoin overnight seasonality (long 22:00-00:00 UTC) and crypto hour-of-day effects
rows.source_notes: The Quantpedia page confirms Padysak and Vojtko, 'Seasonality, Trend-following, and Mean reversion in Bitcoin' (SSRN 4081000), Gemini BTC 2015-2021. The rule goes long at 22:00 UTC for two hours: about 33% annualised, volatility 20.93%, Sharpe 1.58, max drawdown -34.04%. Costs are not reported, and the strategy does poorly in bear markets. The GitHub replication confirms BTC's US-hours variance share rose from 40.8% to 45.2%, mostly in 2022-23.
rows.replication_concerns: It is practitioner work with no peer-reviewed replication. Hurst's 549-trial calendar scan (478 coin-hours at the null rate) and its off-hours block (post-publication t 0.14) almost surely already cover these hours. Nothing in the US session leads BTC after the close (t +1.2), so the spillover mechanism is unsupported. The prior is very low.
rows.data_notes: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD: 58 monthly bundles 2022-01..2026-10 (bar start stamps; missing minutes = no trade). kraken-trades-1m-XBTUSD: 48 bundles 2022-01..2025-12, not 2025-11 as the cross-check said, with buy/sell volume. daily-history-SPY is present.
rows.lookahead_risks: Coinbase minute bars are stamped by bar start: the block close is the close of the 23:59 bar and the block open the close of the 21:59 bar. Stale minutes are forward-filled. The IBIT split uses the 2024-01-11 launch. The pre-publication / post-publication boundary is 2022 (SSRN 4081000 was posted in 2022).
rows.missing_data: Verified fee schedules for CME micro BTC and Coinbase Derivatives nano BTC before any net figure.

final.claim: On Coinbase 1m BTC-USD from 2022-01 to 2026-10, with Kraken 1m 2022-01..2025-12 as the second venue, the mean log return over 22:00-00:00 UTC exceeds the mean of the other eleven 2-hour UTC blocks by more than 5 bp per day.
final.statistic: Mean daily block-minus-rest difference, with a studentized circular block bootstrap by day (block 7 days).
final.procedure: Block return = log(close of the 23:59 UTC minute / close of the 21:59 UTC minute), with missing minutes forward-filled. All 12 blocks are tested with Holm, and the write-up counts Hurst's 478 coin-hour scan in the multiplicity. Splits: 2022-2024 / 2024-2026 halves, before/after 2024-01-11 (IBIT), weekday/weekend. Diagnostics: the same block in ET-anchored time (the US-close spillover story) and regression of the block return on the same day's SPY close-to-close return.
final.data: coinbase-1m-BTC-USD-*, kraken-trades-1m-XBTUSD-*, daily-history-SPY.
final.pass: Holm one-sided p < 0.05, positive in both halves, in both IBIT periods and on Kraken. The net at CME micro / Coinbase nano fees is reported and pre-registered as expected <= 0.
final.controls: Placebos: the other 11 blocks. Second venue: Kraken. Costs: about 2 bp round trip on CME micro / Coinbase nano (to verify), 16-18 bp on Kalshi perps, Coinbase spot maker tier. Before building, ask Hurst for its BTC 22:00 and 23:00 UTC cells; if those cells already cover 2022-2026 Coinbase, record them under this registration instead of rerunning.

rows.reason: This is a clean post-publication test of a practitioner claim on archived data. Corrections: the Kraken span, block construction from minute stamps, and an explicit step to reuse Hurst's cells, which make the expected verdict not supported.

rows.name: Intraday volatility seasonality and event-hour variance in short-dated (0DTE/1DTE) option pricing
rows.source_notes: The GitHub Andersen-Bollerslev replication is verified: S&P CFD 2010-2025 and EUR/USD 2004-2025, profile correlation 0.91 / 0.96, payroll-Friday 08:30 interval at 10.9x average volatility, last/first-hour ratio 0.755 -> 0.810 on high-volatility days. The registry confirms T-529: VIX1D close at /365 under-prices next-day variance, -0.2241 %^2/day; -0.6920 before CPI/FOMC/NFP days against -0.1580 ex-events. Cboe's VIX methodology PDF returned 403, so the VIX1D time convention and the hours in which it is computed were not verified.
rows.replication_concerns: (1) Partly in-sample: T-529 already reported the event versus non-event VIX1D premium on 2022-05..2026-10, so an event-day claim on the same window has been partly seen. A pass must be confirmed on FOMC days after registration. (2) CPI and NFP print at 08:30, before the VIX1D open. Checked here on the regressor only: the median VIX1D open / prior close is 0.71 on CPI days against 0.80 on other days, consistent with the open being struck after the release. Those days therefore test the post-release session, not event-hour pricing, and belong in a placebo, not in a pooled primary. (3) FOMC is the only in-session scheduled event, with about 23-24 days in the window, so power is low. Each day's RV from 7 hourly returns is noisy (sd of log RV about 0.5).
rows.data_notes: cboe-VIX1D-history has 1,109 rows from 2022-05-13 (open = close until about 2023-04-03, per the cross-check, and visible in the first rows). The archive holds local 60m SPY from 2023-11-21, daily-history-SPY, fomc-meetings (decision_day, scheduled), macro-release-cpi and macro-release-employment-situation.
rows.lookahead_risks: VIX1D open is used only as of the open. Realised variance comes from bar-to-bar returns from the 09:30 open to the official close (the last bar is 30 minutes). Matched non-event days must be chosen by calendar rules only (same weekday, +/-10 sessions, excluding OPEX and other events). Do not use the T-529 window's event results to pick thresholds.
rows.missing_data: Nothing for the variance check. The tradable 0DTE straddle needs 120+ captured intraday SPX/XSP/SPY chain sessions.

final.claim: From 2023-11-21 to 2026-10, define R = SPY's open-to-close realised variance (sum of squared log returns of the 60m bars from the 09:30 open to the official close) divided by (VIX1D_open/100)^2 x 390/525,600. The mean of log R on scheduled FOMC decision days, the only scheduled release inside the session, exceeds its mean on matched non-event days by more than 0.2.
final.statistic: Difference in mean log R (FOMC minus matched non-event days), with a day-level stationary bootstrap (mean block 5) and a permutation p over the matched sets. Placebo member: CPI and Employment Situation days, whose 08:30 release precedes the VIX1D open.
final.procedure: VIX1D open from cboe-VIX1D-history (rows from 2023-04-03 on). Event dates: fomc-meetings decision_day where scheduled. Each event day gets up to 3 matched days: same weekday, within +/-10 sessions, excluding OPEX, FOMC, CPI, NFP and early closes. The variance convention cancels in the difference. Diagnostic (b): the share of daily realised variance in the 15:30-to-close bar, with year-by-year profile correlation reported.
final.data: cboe-VIX1D-history, local 60m bars SPY, daily-history-SPY, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, macro-release-employment-situation.
final.pass: FOMC difference > 0.2 with one-sided p < 0.05 and a lower 95% bound above 0, and the CPI/NFP placebo difference not significantly different from 0. Any pass is labelled partly in-sample (T-529) and must be confirmed on the next 8 FOMC days before it informs T-217/T-218.
final.controls: Robustness: VIX1D at the prior close (T-529's convention) with close-to-close realised variance. OPEX days kept separate (T-216). Random-date placebo. No grid. No trade claimed.

rows.reason: Every input is archived and the question matters for T-217/T-218. But the pooled event set mixed an in-session event with pre-open releases and overlaps T-529's already-reported split. FOMC becomes the primary, CPI/NFP a placebo, and an out-of-sample confirmation is required.

rows.name: Opening-range breakout on 'stocks in play' (relative-volume filter)
rows.source_notes: CXO's review confirms the paper and its rules: Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz, 'A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market' (SSRN, Feb 2024), all US stocks 2016-2023. Filters: open > $5, 14-day ADV >= 1M shares, ATR14 > $0.50, opening-range relative volume >= 100% of the 14-day mean, then the top 20 by relative volume. Stop at 10% of ATR, 1% risk per trade, leverage capped at 4x, $0.0035/share commission. The returns (1,637% / 41.6%) are behind CXO's paywall and could NOT be confirmed. The MQL5 replication of the plain ORB (Zarattini-Aziz SSRN 4416622, five CFDs, 2015-06/2026) is verified: NQ gross +0.131 R, hit rate 23.2%; net NQ +0.002 R, others -0.038 to -0.081 R; rule minus random direction +0.02 to +0.13 R; 2015-2017 negative everywhere; 2021-2026 at best +0.06 R.
rows.replication_concerns: The headline returns are unverified. Independent replication of the plain ORB finds zero net. Relative volume needs consolidated volume, while Alpaca IEX carries a small, uneven slice. Hurst's QQQ ORB (+0.26 R per session on IEX, 2020-2026) is alive only in backtest, with 0 trades in 5 paper sessions. T-419 and T-546 found abnormal volume carries no direction.
rows.data_notes: Local 5m bars cover 123 symbols over 60 sessions (2026-07-28..2026-10-20): a pilot only. daily-history and daily-events exist. No multi-year minute bars and no delisted names are archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Universe filters, ATR and ADV must use data through the prior close; relative volume is known at 09:35. Stop fills at the stop price plus 1 tick. Survivorship: delisted names must be present. IEX-only volume is not consolidated relative volume.
rows.missing_data: Multi-year 1-5 minute bars for about 900+ names including delisted (Polygon consolidated is paid). Or Alpaca IEX plus a validated IEX-to-consolidated volume ratio against daily-history volume.

final.claim: Over US stocks priced above $5 with 14-day ADV >= 1M shares and ATR14 > $0.50, from 2020-08 to 2026-10 (2024-01 onward out-of-sample), trading each day the up to 20 names whose first-5-minute volume is at least 100% of, and highest relative to, their trailing-14-session first-5-minute mean earns a positive mean net R per trade and beats a random-direction benchmark. Entry on a stop at the first 5-minute bar's extreme in that bar's direction; stop 10% of ATR14 from entry; exit at the close.
final.statistic: Mean net R per trade and daily Sharpe; excess over a random-direction benchmark (1,000 random-direction books); DSR over 24 cells; PBO by CSCV.
final.procedure: Universe, ATR and ADV come from data through the prior close; relative volume is known at 09:35. Stop entries and exits fill at the stop plus 1 tick; the close exit fills at the official close. Half-spread and the SEC fee are charged. No leverage: 1% risk per trade, capped at 25% of equity per name. The local 5m pilot (123 symbols, 60 sessions, top 5) is reported but not judged.
final.data: Consolidated or validated-IEX minute bars (to fetch), daily-history, daily-events, local 5m bars (pilot).
final.pass: Out-of-sample mean net R > 0 with bootstrap p < 0.05, excess over random direction > 0, DSR >= 0.95 over 24 cells, and PBO < 0.3.
final.controls: Random-direction benchmark. Comparison arm: Hurst's plain QQQ ORB. Delisted names must be included, else the verdict is capped at inconclusive. No leverage. Costs per stop fill.

rows.reason: The rule set is confirmed but the headline returns could not be. It is registered as blocked now, with the paper's >=100% relative-volume floor added, so the filter cannot be fitted later. A live form needs the PDT $25k margin account.

rows.name: Attention-driven buying at the open: high-attention stocks gain overnight and reverse intraday
rows.source_notes: Cambridge's abstract confirms Berkman, Koch, Tuttle and Zhang, JFQA 47(4) 2012. Stocks that recently attracted retail attention show positive overnight returns and intraday reversals, driven by a high opening price. The implicit cost to retail buyers at the open often exceeds the effective half-spread. The effect is stronger for hard-to-value, costly-to-arbitrage stocks and in high-sentiment periods. Magnitudes and the sample were not on the page. The EOD paper's text confirms retail-attention opening price pressure in later data.
rows.replication_concerns: Magnitudes are unverified, and an S&P 500 universe is where the effect should be weakest; I would lower the prior to about 0.2. Abnormal volume is a crude attention proxy (T-419: it predicts no multi-day direction). StockTwits data from 2025-W43 is a short sample. No search was possible (budget exhausted).
rows.data_notes: Verified: daily-history OHLCV, daily-events, fja-sp500-components and finra-regsho-cnms (99 monthly bundles 2018-08..2026-10; T-394 verified the CNMS files from 2019-01-02). stocktwits-intensity weekly bundles run from 2025-W43. T-394: 93.4% of point-in-time S&P events priced 2019-2026.
rows.lookahead_risks: The archive stamps a daily bar available at bar time + 24h, i.e. 09:30 ET the next day, after the 09:28 MOO cutoff. Using t-1 volume for a day-t open decision therefore needs a declared publication-time justification (consolidated volume is final by about 20:00 ET on t-1), and a t-2 robustness run. The CNMS file is available at the end of the trade day. Membership is point-in-time. Ticker reuse and survivorship gate apply. Earnings days are reported separately.
rows.missing_data: Delisted-member prices (coverage gate); long-history retail attention.

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices from 2018-08 to 2026-09, stock-days whose abnormal volume at t-1 is in the top cross-sectional decile have a mean day-t intraday return (official open to official close) more than 10 bp below the equal-weighted mean intraday return of the other members. Abnormal volume = log of t-1 consolidated volume over its trailing-20-session mean. A planned buy of such a name is therefore cheaper at day t's closing auction than at its opening auction.
final.statistic: Mean of daily (top-decile EW intraday return minus rest-of-universe EW intraday return), with a Newey-West t (5 lags). Secondaries: overnight(t) minus intraday(t), and the off-exchange-share attention variant.
final.procedure: Attention uses t-1 volume, admitted for a day-t open decision because consolidated daily volume is published by about 20:00 ET on t-1. This overrides the archive's conservative +24h stamp, and a t-2-volume robustness run is reported. Variant: off-exchange share = finra-regsho-cnms total_volume / daily-history volume, z-scored on its own 60-day history, using t-1 files. The StockTwits variant from 2025-W43 is reported, not judged. Tradable form reported separately: buy the top decile at the t-1 MOC using attention through t-2 and sell at the t MOO, at 3 bp per side. Coverage gate: at least 90% of member-days priced. At most 6 cells; Holm.
final.data: daily-history, daily-events, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, finra-regsho-cnms, stocktwits-intensity-*.
final.pass: Mean < -10 bp with Holm one-sided p < 0.05, negative in both 2018-08..2022-06 and 2022-07..2026-09, the t-2 robustness of the same sign, and the coverage gate met.
final.controls: Placebo: the bottom attention decile. Earnings days reported separately. The execution comparison is cost-neutral (both arms cross one auction). The tradable overnight form is charged 3 bp per side. No grid.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the execution reframing is sound. Fixed so the use of t-1 volume is justified explicitly against the archive's conservative availability stamp, with a t-2 robustness run, and the prior is lowered for a large-cap universe.

knowledge.title: Intraday and time-of-day return patterns: a survey of intraday momentum, overnight drift, closing-auction pressure, fix flows and clock seasonality
knowledge.markdown:
# Intraday and time-of-day return patterns: a survey of intraday momentum, overnight drift, closing-auction pressure, fix flows and clock seasonality

- **Authors / kind:** cluster survey of 15 claims from the 2026-10-20 web sweep. Peer-reviewed core: Gao et al. (JFE 2018), Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021), Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan (RFS 2023), Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019), Akbas et al. (JFE 2022), Bogousslavsky (JFE 2021), Krohn-Mueller-Whelan (JF 2024), Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (JF 2010), Berkman et al. (JFQA 2012). Working papers: Bogousslavsky-Muravyev, Baltussen-Da-Soebhag, Da et al., Zarattini et al.
- **Links:** https://academicweb.nd.edu/~zda/intramom.pdf · https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr917.pdf · https://personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/TugOfWar.pdf · https://academicweb.nd.edu/~zda/EOD.pdf · https://www.bankofcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/swp2021-48.pdf · https://academicweb.nd.edu/~zda/IntraOption.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.45 (8 of 27 cited sources read in full; 9 checked at abstract, review or replication level, counted at half weight; 10 cited but not opened).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full texts of the six linked papers, Gao et al. and Bogousslavsky-Muravyev; abstracts or reviews for the rest. The stocks-in-play ORB returns are paywalled and unverified, and the web-search budget ran out, so most post-2020 decay searches were impossible.
- **Selected because:** time of day is an input on every bar of the learning program (T-577), Mandel's best-known intraday tests failed (T-427, T-428), and every auction-timed rule it runs (T-549, T-559) pays the costs this literature measures.

## What it says

- **Gamma-conditioned intraday momentum.** Short-gamma hedgers (dealers at negative gamma exposure, built from open interest; leveraged ETFs) trade with the move into the close. The prior-close-to-15:30 return predicts the last half-hour: equity futures t 7.29, out-of-sample R² 2.88% (60+ futures, 1974-2020); slope 6.63 (t 4.78) after negative-NGE days, 0.82 (t 1.03) otherwise. Gao et al. (SPY 1993-2013): out-of-sample R² 1.4%. No post-2020 independent replication.
- **Volume/news conditioning.** Stronger on high first-half-hour volume, volatile and macro-news days, but Gao's terciles are formed within each year (a look-ahead). The noise-area breakout (Sharpe 1.33 net) is unreplicated.
- **Leveraged-ETF rebalancing.** Demand = AUM × (x²−x) × the day's return, executed near the closing auction (16.8% of MOC volume on a 1% day in 2009); interaction t 2.2-3.1 (2006-2020). Contested: ETF flows into and out of LETFs may offset it.
- **Overnight drift at the European open.** Dealers unload US-close inventory when European liquidity arrives: ES 02:00-03:00 ET earns 1.48 bp/day (1998-2020), positive in 20 of 23 years, the only hour surviving Bonferroni. Sharpe 1.1 before costs, −0.5 after the spread; after negative closing signed volume, 1.1 net.
- **Tug of war.** Past-month overnight return predicts overnight returns (+3.47%/month, t 16.6) and intraday reversal (−3.24%), 1993-2013.
- **Daytime-reversal intensity.** More overnight-up/intraday-down days than a stock's norm predicts +0.92%/month EW (1993-2017, gross), 0.43% in the top market cap group; non-US replications reportedly fail.
- **End-of-day reversal.** Intraday losers bounce in the last half-hour, 3.78-6.86 bp/day gross (t > 10, 1993-2019), via retail dip-buying and short sellers avoiding new overnight positions. Unreplicated; the authors doubt it survives costs.
- **Anomalies de-risked at the close.** Overnight margin and securities lending fees make arbitrageurs cut mispriced positions before the close (abstract only).
- **Closing auction pressure.** The auction reached 7.48% of dollar volume (2018); the official close sits 8.1 bp from the last midquote (2.7 bp for large caps) and reverts half within 20 minutes, fully overnight. Only the change in intraday-to-auction volume predicts returns (4.2%/yr).
- **FX fixing W.** The dollar rises into the Tokyo and London fixes and falls after (a long-foreign basket −5.0%/yr before Tokyo, +5.3% after; G9 1999-2019). Decayed to −1.6/+2.1 in 2014-2019; full spreads erase it.
- **Same-half-hour continuation** for up to 40 days (JF 2010). Decaying: the first lag reportedly fell ~75%; an FX/S&P/BTC replication breaks even at 0.05 bp against 0.6 bp of cost.
- **Straddle same-interval momentum.** Prior-day 09:35-10:00 straddle winners repeat (73 bp/day, t 22, 2010-2024). Mid-quote only; single-name spreads of several percent swamp it.
- **BTC 22:00-00:00 UTC.** Two hours a day earned most of BTC's 2015-2021 return (Sharpe 1.58, no costs, weak in bear markets); a US-close spillover is the guess. Practitioner, no post-publication replication.
- **Intraday volatility U-shape.** Realised volatility peaks at the open and close and spikes at 08:30 releases and the 14:00 FOMC (10.9× on payroll Fridays); year-to-year profile correlation 0.91. Whether 0DTE implied volatility prices it is untested.
- **Opening range breakout.** The plain 5-minute ORB replicates gross (NQ +0.131 R) but nets +0.002 R on NQ and −0.04 to −0.08 R on four other indices (2015-2026).
- **Attention buying at the open.** High-attention stocks gain overnight and reverse intraday; buying them at the open costs more than the half-spread (JFQA 2012).

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** The core is peer-reviewed, with long samples, out-of-sample R² and multiple-testing corrections. The rating is for the sources, not tradability: nearly every figure is gross, samples end 2013-2020, and three claims (noise-area, stocks-in-play, BTC block) are practitioner grade.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Costs first.** `closing-auction-deviation-overnight-reversal-60m` is testable now on 718 sessions (the 60m 15:30 bar's close is the last regular trade, checked against 5m bars). It prices the auction for T-559's sleeve, T-549's overnight hold and the cross-sections below, and reframes T-428 (slope −0.084), whose regressor partly measured auction deviation. `attention-open-pressure-intraday-shortfall-sp500` is its opening-auction twin.
- **Flow-conditioned T-427 successors.** T-427's null (gross −0.09 bp, slope −0.004, t −0.22, 2023-2026) is what hedging-demand theory predicts: only 19 of 734 sessions had negative free GEX. `gex-conditioned-rod-last-half-hour-momentum` (volatility control, T-427's 60 cells deflated in) and `letf-rebalancing-demand-last-half-hour-panel` are pre-registered as blocked; `intraday-momentum-high-opening-volume` is testable now, with trailing cut-offs. A reconciliation, not a confirmation.
- **Overnight cross-section.** T-549 (QQQ/IWM overnight +3.4 to +3.6 bp/night net, supported) agrees with Lou-Polk-Skouras at index level. `overnight-return-persistence-sp500-top-decile`, `negative-daytime-reversal-intensity-sp500` and `dtc-decile-overnight-minus-intraday-sp500` (FINRA short interest days to cover) share T-348's decomposition, point-in-time membership and a 90% survivorship coverage gate (coverage left T-375/T-393 inconclusive).
- **`es-0200-et-drift-after-closing-hour-selling`** on ES/MES, verdict to Hurst's proposed H-us500-overnight (drift against the perp funding rate). An ES tick has shrunk from ~1.25 bp to ~0.32 bp since the paper's era.
- **Timing and features, not trades:** `usd-fix-pre-post-reversal-7ccy` (FX conversions on OANDA), `same-hour-return-continuation-60m-xs` (into T-577's F2 only if it passes), `vix1d-open-fomc-session-variance-ratio` (an event-hour variance risk premium; informs T-217/T-218 after T-529 found VIX1D cheap), `end-of-day-reversal-28-megacaps` as a pilot, and `btc-2200-0000-utc-block-seasonality`, reusing Hurst's coin-hour cells first.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Unconditional intraday momentum.** Absent in Mandel's window (T-427: SPY −2.09, QQQ −2.42, IWM −1.04 bp/day net). The T-579 scan points the other way: return since the open and VWAP distance predict the next bar inversely for equity ETFs from 5m to 60m (60m confirmed IC −0.108, t −3.7) and for crypto; tod_sin/cos and lv_rel_tod never confirmed, and T-577 passed 0 of 276 intraday cells. The measured regime is reversal, too small to trade.
- **Free GEX is not the paper's NGE** (~6% negative days against 48%, backfilled, clustered in 2022): its sign is a regime dummy unless volatility is controlled.
- **Decayed:** same-half-hour periodicity, the Tokyo fix, the 02:00 drift after spread. **Unreplicated:** noise-area, stocks-in-play, BTC block, end-of-day reversal. Hurst's H-orb-qqq has 0 trades in 5 paper sessions.
- **Hour-scale crypto rules** fail on US venues: Hurst's best hourly rule on 20 Kalshi perps made +26 bp gross, −45 bp walk-forward, against a 16-18 bp round trip; 6,096 rules deflate to nothing. The BTC day-of-week effect passed (T-436) but not under Bonferroni (T-354, p 0.077).
- **Return-state conditioning of overnight holds** added nothing (T-563) and T-333's gap fade lost 6.25 bp/trade, so the ES test uses a signed-volume proxy, not a return tercile.
- **LETF flow** is contested and T-325 failed; USD month-end flows failed (T-575); straddle momentum is a market maker's edge. Nothing here needs an offshore venue.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Archive, first-seen stamped:** SqueezeMetrics DIX/GEX; Alpaca IEX 1-minute SPY/QQQ from 2020-08; Dukascopy USA500 and FX minutes from 2012; LETF shares outstanding × NAV; capture-box chains at 09:35/10:00/15:30/16:00; 15:59:50 NBBO mids.
- **Features (T-577/T-578):** same-time-of-day lagged returns; overnight/intraday components; auction deviation; r_ROD × GEX_{t-1}; LETF demand; ET clock with DST asynchrony; FOMC/CPI/payrolls/OPEX/month-end/earnings flags; Reg SHO off-exchange share; realised volatility over its time-of-day profile.
- **Harness rules:** exit at the official close, never a 16:00 stub; dividend-adjust returns spanning the prior close; drop early closes; verify bar stamps (Yahoo stamps by open); trailing cut-offs only; a maker entry fills only on a print through it (the children's adverse-selection learning); deflate for T-427's 60 cells and Hurst's 478 coin-hours.

candidates.name: Downward migrants (Russell 1000 to 2000): run-up from Rank Day to recon close
candidates.summary: A stock that drops from the bottom of the R1000 to the top of the R2000 goes from a tiny weight to a large one, so passive and benchmarked demand for it rises. Buy predicted downward migrants at Rank Day (or at the preliminary list) and exit at the recon-day close.
candidates.mechanism: Both indices are value-weighted, and banding is +/-2.5% of cumulative market-cap percentile around the rank-1000 breakpoint. CHL find a migrant's index weight jumps about 10-15x, from roughly 0.01% to 0.10-0.15%. Pavlova-Sikorskaya (1998-2018) show passive funds benchmarked to the R2000 buy an extra 112 bp of the added stocks' shares. Index trackers buy at the recon close to minimise tracking error. On the other side are pre-positioned arbitrageurs and holders who sell into that closing demand.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca), hedged with IWM
candidates.horizon: weeks (about 6 weeks from Rank Day to recon, about 4 from the preliminary list)
candidates.claimed_effect: Chang-Hong-Liskovich (RFS 2015), 1996-2012: R1000 stocks that just landed in the R2000 earn +5.6% (t 2.65) more in June than stocks that just missed (local linear, bandwidth 100). The paper says all of the adjustment happens in June, with no effect in July or August. Dimensional, 2014-2023 (about 20 migrants a year): downward migrants beat the R2000 by +1.2% over the 20 trading days before recon, then gave back -0.95% over the next 20. Neither source states costs.
candidates.replication: Dimensional's practitioner out-of-sample 2014-2023 confirms the sign at about a fifth of CHL's size. Decay and contest: banding (from 2007) cut switching from about 10% to about 3% of R1000 names a year (CHL). Chinco-Sammon (JFE 2024) find recon-day returns to buying additions and selling deletions converged to nearly zero over 2000-2021. Greenwood-Sammon cite them: Russell inclusion and reconstitution effects have declined over the past decade. FTSE Russell (2026) says short-term price effects 'have not reliably followed the expected pattern'. Appel-Gormley-Keim show sharp-RD estimators at this cutoff are biased.
