candidates.proposed_test: Universe: US common stocks ranked within +/-300 of rank 1000 by Rank-Day total market cap. Market cap = SEC dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding (all classes, latest filed before Rank Day, available_at = filed + 1 day) x Rank-Day close. Prior membership comes from point-in-time lists (FTSE Russell preliminary PDFs or iShares IWB/IWM holdings). Apply the +/-2.5% cumulative-percentile band, then check predictions against the published preliminary lists; report accuracy against Madhavan's broker benchmark of 90-95%. Signal: prior-R1000 members predicted to move to the R2000. Entry: first close after Rank Day; variant: first close after the list is published (published after the close). Exit: recon-day official close. Benchmark: IWM; control: prior-R1000 stayers inside the band, matched on rank. Cost: 15 bp per stock leg plus 5 bp on the IWM hedge. Statistic: mean net excess return of each event's portfolio, with a t-test across events and a stock bootstrap clustered by event. Halves: 2007-2016 and 2017-2026. Placebo: the same calendar windows shifted 3 months. Holm across the cluster's variants. Pass: net mean > 0 with lower 95% bound > 0 and both halves positive. Pre-register before 2026-10-30 and log December 2026 as the first forward observation. Data gap: most names near rank 1000 are not in the 901-symbol archive, and delisted names need a survivorship check (T-334 could price only 82.6% of its additions).

candidates.name: Upward migrants (Russell 2000 to 1000): underperformance before recon
candidates.summary: A stock that crosses up from the top of the R2000 to the bottom of the R1000 loses most of its index weight and its R2000-benchmarked demand. Short (or avoid) predicted upward migrants from Rank Day or the preliminary list to the recon close.
candidates.mechanism: This is the mirror of the downward migrant. R2000 index funds and active R2000-benchmarked funds must sell (Pavlova-Sikorskaya: active R2000 funds cut ownership of deletions by 46 bp), while R1000 trackers buy only a sliver. The net forced selling at the close is absorbed by liquidity providers, who are paid a discount.
variables: calendars (Rank Day, preliminary list, recon day)
short interest / days to cover (borrow feasibility)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca short), hedged with IWM
candidates.claimed_effect: CHL, 1996-2012: stocks crossing from the R2000 into the R1000 return 5.4% less in June than stocks just staying in the R2000 (t 3.0, bandwidth 100). Dimensional, 2014-2023: upward migrants return -1.1% vs the R2000 over the 20 trading days before recon, then rebound about +2% over the 20 after. Costs not stated.
candidates.replication: The sign holds in Dimensional's 2014-2023 sample, with a much smaller pre-recon move than CHL. The same decay evidence applies as for downward migrants (Chinco-Sammon, Greenwood-Sammon, FTSE Russell 2026). For scale, June 2026 had 42 upward and 39 downward migrants, and June 2025 had 25 downward migrants (FTSE Russell summaries). Each event is a small cross-section.

candidates.proposed_test: Same membership engine as for downward migrants. Signal: prior-R2000 members whose Rank-Day cumulative percentile clears the upper band (predicted to move up). Short from the first close after Rank Day (variant: after the preliminary list) to the recon close, hedged long IWM. Control: the largest R2000 stayers inside the band, matched on rank. Cost: 15 bp per leg plus borrow. Charge an assumed general-collateral 0.3%/yr, and a stated hard-to-borrow surcharge where FINRA days-to-cover is in the top decile. Statistic: mean net excess return of the short-minus-IWM portfolio per event, clustered by event, with halves 2007-2016 and 2017-2026 and a shifted-window placebo. Pass: net > 0 with lower 95% bound > 0 and both halves positive. Run it in the same Holm family as the downward-migrant test. Forward observation: 2026-10-30 to 2026-12-11.

candidates.name: Migrant reversal in the 20 sessions after recon
candidates.summary: After the recon close, forced demand is gone and pre-positioned arbitrageurs unwind. Buy the upward migrants (R2000 to R1000) and short the downward migrants (R1000 to R2000) for 20 sessions.
candidates.mechanism: Temporary price pressure reverts once index funds have traded. Hedge funds that front-ran the change sell or cover on or soon after recon day (Madhavan 2003). The counterparty is the indexer who traded at the pressured close.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca long/short)
candidates.claimed_effect: Dimensional, 2014-2023: upward migrants rebound about +2% and downward migrants give back about -0.95% vs the R2000 over the 20 days after recon. Madhavan (FAJ 2003), 1996-2002: the R3000 additions-minus-deletions spread averaged -4.97% in July, negative in 5 of 7 years; the R2000 spread was negative in July in 6 of 7 years. Shankar-Miller (2006): S&P 600 changes are 'fully reversed within 60 days'.
candidates.replication: Contested. CHL find no significant reversal in July or later months at the 1000 cutoff (1996-2012). Onayev-Zdorovtsov (as summarised by CXO) find price-pressure reversals 'much smaller to nonexistent in the recent years'. The closest Mandel analogue is T-334 (S&P 500 additions, 20-day post-effective reversal), which is inconclusive; Russell is untested.

candidates.proposed_test: Use the actual (published) migrant lists, which are public by recon day. Long upward migrants and short downward migrants, equal-weighted, entered at the recon-day official close. Variant: next-day open, to avoid relying on closing-auction fills. Exit at the close of session +20; report +5 and +60 for the shape only. Cost: 15 bp per leg per side plus borrow on the short. Statistic: mean net spread per event, with an event bootstrap, halves, and a placebo of the same stocks entered 60 sessions later. Pass: lower 95% bound > 0 and both halves positive. Note that the December 2026 window (2026-12-14 to about 2027-01-13) spans the turn of the year. Register a separate December arm rather than pooling it with June until several December events exist.

candidates.name: Passive demand in days of volume (benchmarking-intensity change) as a continuous predictor
candidates.summary: Instead of a yes/no addition flag, rank predicted index changes by the predicted inelastic demand shock, measured as the change in benchmark weight times benchmarked AUM, divided by average dollar volume. The bigger the shock relative to liquidity, the larger the run-up and the later reversal.
candidates.mechanism: The index effect scales with the change in a stock's benchmarking intensity (BMI): the AUM-weighted sum of its weights across benchmarks. Demand curves for stocks are downward sloping and fairly inelastic, so price impact grows with demand relative to the liquidity available.
adjacent_variables: passive AUM per benchmark (ETF shares outstanding x NAV)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Pavlova-Sikorskaya (RFS 2023; WP data 1998-2018, 34 US indices): stocks in the top quartile of BMI change earn 80 bp more in June than the average stock that year; the bottom quartile earns 110 bp less. They use an average index effect of 2.3% and an implied demand elasticity of -3.03. Chinco-Sammon (2000-2021): the typical addition or deletion trades 9.5x normal volume on recon day, and R2000 additions trade 14.2 days' worth of volume that day against 1.4x the day before. Practitioner screens (passive buying at least 5x ADV, float under 40%, short interest over 10%) are untested heuristics.
candidates.replication: The BMI design relies on the Russell cutoff. Wei-Young (CFR 2024) argue that institutional ownership already differs at the cutoff under common ranking methods (selection bias). A later Pavlova-Sikorskaya version notes changing incentives around the cutoff and the growing role of CRSP indexes. No independent post-2018 replication of the June quartile spread was found.

candidates.proposed_test: For every predicted change (migrants, plus additions and deletions at the 3000 cutoff), compute D_i = sum over b of AUM_b x (w_new - w_old), with b in {R1000, R2000, R3000, Midcap, R2500}. Proxy AUM_b by the tracking ETFs' shares outstanding x NAV as of Rank Day; this is a lower bound. Weights come from the predicted float-adjusted cap. Divide by the 20-day median dollar volume as of Rank Day. Outcomes: excess return vs IWM from the first close after Rank Day to the recon close (expect IC > 0), and the 20-session post-recon return (expect IC < 0). Statistic: Spearman IC per event, averaged across events, with a t-test over events. Halves and the migrant-only subset are reported separately. Pass: mean IC > 0 pre-recon with t > 2 and both halves positive, and the post-recon IC negative. Costs enter through a top-minus-bottom tercile portfolio at 15 bp per leg. Forward: compute D on 2026-10-30 data before the preliminary list.

candidates.name: Long-run benchmarking-intensity discount: just-moved-up R2000 stocks beat just-moved-down stocks for 12 months
candidates.summary: Stocks whose benchmarking intensity rises at recon (newly at the top of the R2000) have lower expected returns for years afterwards. Stocks whose intensity falls (newly at the bottom of the R1000) have higher ones. Hold long the new bottom-of-R1000 names against the new top-of-R2000 names near the cutoff for 12 months.
candidates.mechanism: Inelastic benchmarked demand raises a stock's price relative to fundamentals (a preferred-habitat premium), which lowers its future expected return. Analysts also revise their cost-of-equity estimates in the same direction (Pavlova-Sikorskaya). The counterparty is benchmarked managers who hold the stock because it is in their benchmark.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca long/short)
candidates.horizon: months (12 months; the paper tests up to 5 years)
candidates.claimed_effect: Pavlova-Sikorskaya (IV design, R2000 membership as instrument; reduced form, 1998-2006): addition to the R2000 lowers returns by about 60 bp a month over the next five years, and deletion raises them by about 48 bp a month. After 2007 the figures fall to about -26 bp and +28 bp a month. No costs stated.
candidates.replication: Already decaying (halved after 2007 in the paper itself). Identification at the cutoff is contested: Wei-Young (CFR 2024) find selection bias; Appel-Gormley-Keim (CFR) show some estimators are biased and that the 2007 banding change requires modifying the methods. The same natural experiment has been reused by many papers, so Heath-Ringgenberg-Samadi-Werner's multiple-testing warning applies. Overlaps in direction with the 20-session migrant reversal; nest both in one family.

candidates.proposed_test: Cohorts are formed at each recon close from 2007 to 2025. Long: stocks that moved R2000 to R1000 and sit within 150 ranks of the cutoff. Short: stocks that moved R1000 to R2000 within the same window. Variant: each side against its own band stayers. Hold 12 months, with overlapping annual cohorts combined into one monthly calendar-time return. Statistic: FF5 + UMD alpha with Newey-West t (Mandel archives the factors), plus the raw spread with a bootstrap over cohorts. Cost: 10 bp per leg at formation and exit, plus assumed borrow of 0.3%/yr general collateral. Pass: alpha > 0 with t > 2, both halves of the cohorts (2007-2015 and 2016-2025) positive, and the family-wide DSR above 0.95. Because only about 19 cohorts exist, report a fail-to-reject as inconclusive rather than not_supported unless the point estimate is negative.

candidates.name: Lower cutoff (rank about 3000): Microcap graduates into the R2000 and R2000 drop-outs
candidates.summary: Stocks that enter the R2000 from the Microcap index or from outside get large, fully passive-driven buying. Stocks falling out of the R3000 get forced selling. Buy predicted entrants and avoid or short predicted drop-outs from the preliminary list to the recon close.
candidates.mechanism: There is no band at the bottom of the R2000 (FTSE Russell 2026 summary), so membership follows directly from rank. These names have thin liquidity, so trading 14x average volume at the close moves prices. Microcap and R2000 funds trade in opposite directions, but the R2000's tracked AUM dominates.
candidates.assets: US small/micro-cap stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Madhavan (FAJ 2003), 1996-2002: a portfolio long R2000 additions and short deletions earned +10.78% on average in June (all 7 Junes positive) and +29.04% cumulative over March-June; July was negative in 6 of 7 years. Brokers' membership predictions were 90-95% accurate by the end of May. CHL at the 3000 cutoff, 2005-2012: June coefficients of 0.036 (t 1.45) for additions and 0.033 (t 1.25) for deletions, not significant. June 2026: 83 R2000 additions came from the Microcap index; the smallest R2000 member was $146.4M.
candidates.replication: Madhavan's March-May returns are mechanically inflated: portfolios formed on actual membership pick up the price moves that caused membership. Only returns after the ranking date are tradable. CHL find no significant effect at this cutoff (with limited data). Dimensional's 2012-2021 piece shows pre-recon gains and reversals for non-migrating changes, but no figures are stated in its text. Costs are much higher here.

sources.title: The Russell Reconstitution Effect (Madhavan, FAJ 2003)
Regression Discontinuity and the Price Effects of Stock Market Indexing (NBER w19290; 3000 cutoff section)
Beware the Hidden Costs of Indexing (Dimensional, 2012-2021)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: Rank-Day ranks 2700-3300 of eligible companies (market cap from SEC shares x Rank-Day close). Signal: non-members ranked 3000 or better are predicted additions (IPO additions are a separate candidate). R2000 members ranked below 3000 are predicted deletions. Entry: first close after Rank Day (variant: after the preliminary list); exit: recon close. Benchmark: IWM. Cost: 40 bp per leg, to be recalibrated with a Corwin-Schultz high-low spread estimate per stock (stated as an assumption). Shorts are only taken where FINRA days-to-cover is below the median; otherwise the deletion arm is avoid-only, scored against IWM. Statistic: event-clustered mean net excess return, with halves and placebo windows. Pass: lower 95% bound > 0 net. The deletion arm needs delisting-aware prices; report the share of names priced, as T-334 did.

candidates.name: R2000 deletions beat additions over the next year (index-turnover drag)
candidates.summary: Index deletions are sold at depressed prices and then outperform. Non-migrant additions, often new issues, underperform. Twelve-month buy-and-hold deletions minus additions earns what the index loses by rebalancing.
candidates.mechanism: Index funds buy additions at prices pushed up by the forced flows and sell deletions at depressed prices. Deletions also carry short-term reversal and momentum effects, and new-issue additions carry the IPO long-run underperformance. The counterparty is the rigid annual rebalancer.
candidates.assets: US small-cap stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Cai-Houge (FAJ 2008), 1979-2004: a buy-and-hold R2000 beat the annually rebalanced index by 2.22% over one year and 17.29% over five. Deletions had significantly higher factor-adjusted returns than additions. The best small-cap funds earned +1.45%/yr factor-adjusted by holding deletions or avoiding additions. Petajisto (JEF 2011), 1990-2005: index-turnover cost has a lower bound of 38-77 bp/yr for the R2000 (21-28 bp for the S&P 500).
candidates.replication: Not independently replicated after 2004 in what I found. The Petajisto cost estimate is a related but distinct measure. Likely smaller since banding (2007) and since the post-2016 decline. The deletion arm is exposed to delisting bias in free data.

sources.title: Long-Term Impact of Russell 2000 Index Rebalancing (Cai, Houge; FAJ 2008)
The index premium and its hidden cost for index funds (Petajisto; JEF 2011)
Strategies for Exploiting Index Rebalancing? (CXO summary of Cai-Houge 2007 WP)

candidates.proposed_test: Annual cohorts at each recon close from 2005 to 2025 (from published lists). Long: R2000 deletions that left the R3000 or fell to the Microcap index. Short: R2000 additions that are not migrants and not IPOs. Hold 12 months as equal-weighted buy-and-hold, credit delisting proceeds where they can be found, and report the share of names priced. Statistic: calendar-time FF5 + UMD alpha (Newey-West) and the cohort-mean spread with a cohort bootstrap. Cost: 40 bp per leg at entry and exit, plus assumed borrow of 1%/yr on the short side. Pass: alpha > 0 with t > 2, both halves positive, and family DSR above 0.95. Report an inconclusive result if under 80% of names are priced.

candidates.name: Short interest and short volume condition the recon effect
candidates.summary: Short interest changes how reconstitution moves prices. For additions with high short interest, the recon run-up is a squeeze followed by a reversal. Deletions see short interest rise persistently along with lasting losses. Use FINRA short interest, days-to-cover and RegSHO short volume to sort predicted changes.
candidates.mechanism: Arbitrageurs short additions to hedge or to sell into the index demand, and short deletions ahead of forced selling. Covering into the recon close amplifies the price pressure on additions. Persistent shorting of deletions reflects imperfect-substitute downward demand.
variables: short interest (days to cover, short volume)
adjacent_variables: securities lending supply from index funds
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Akhigbe, Martin, Newman, de Souza (QREF 2022): for R2000 additions, short interest is inversely related to returns during the recon period (price pressure dominates) and positively related after recon. For deletions, they find lasting negative wealth effects and persistent increases in short interest. The abstract gives no magnitudes or sample period.
candidates.replication: Single study and unreplicated as far as I found; sample period and magnitudes not visible from the abstract. Ahn-Patatoukas (JFQA 2022), using the same Russell experiment, find indexing speeds up price discovery only for micro-caps, which are hard to borrow and hard to trade.

sources.title: Russell index reconstitutions and short interest (Akhigbe et al., QREF 84, 2022)
Identifying the Effect of Stock Indexing: Impetus or Impediment to Arbitrage and Price Discovery? (Ahn, Patatoukas; JFQA 2022)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: predicted changes from the four cutoff candidates (downward and upward migrants, lower-cutoff entrants and drop-outs), June 2018 to June 2026 plus December 2026. FINRA SI starts 2017-12 and RegSHO short volume 2018-08 in the archive. Short-interest data enter only after FINRA's publication date: settlement date plus about 7 business days, with the exact date recorded per row. Signals at the preliminary list: days-to-cover, SI / shares outstanding, and the 10-day RegSHO short-volume ratio change. Outcomes: excess return to the recon close and over recon to +20 sessions. Statistic: within-event cross-sectional regression slopes, averaged over events. Pass: the predicted sign (additions with high days-to-cover have larger pre-recon gains and larger post-recon reversals) with t > 2. With about 9 events, expect inconclusive unless the effect is large; report as such.

candidates.name: Recon-day closing-auction pressure and overnight reversal
candidates.summary: Over $200bn changes hands in the recon-day closing auctions. If the closing price is pushed by imbalance, additions should fall and deletions rise from the close to the next open. A liquidity provider would take the other side at the close.
candidates.mechanism: Index funds trade market-on-close to match the index price. Liquidity providers absorbing the published imbalance demand a premium, which reverts overnight. Bogousslavsky-Muravyev find closing-auction deviations revert by the next open, and Madhavan documented extreme intraday volatility on recon day.
variables: time of day (close vs next open)
candidates.assets: US single stocks and IWM (Alpaca MOC/LOC orders)
candidates.horizon: intraday/overnight (close to next open to next close)
candidates.claimed_effect: LSEG: June 2025 recon day traded $102.5bn on Nasdaq and $114.7bn on NYSE at the close ($219.6bn across US exchanges), with 2.5bn shares in the Nasdaq closing cross. Chinco-Sammon: recon-day abnormal returns to buying additions and selling deletions 'steadily converged to nearly zero' over 2000-2021, even as the passive share rose from 12.8% to 33.3%. Bogousslavsky-Muravyev: closing-auction share of volume rose from 3.1% (2010) to 7.5% (2018), and close-vs-midpoint deviations of about 8.1 bp reverse about half shortly after the close and fully overnight. These BM figures come from a search summary; I did not open the paper.
candidates.replication: Decayed. Chinco-Sammon show near-zero recon-day price pressure in recent years, so this is mainly a falsification check. It also tells you whether recon-day closing fills distort the exit leg of the other candidates.

sources.title: The Passive-Ownership Share Is Double What You Think It Is (Chinco, Sammon)
More key facts ahead of the 2026 Russell US indexes reconstitution (LSEG)
Who Trades at the Close? (Bogousslavsky, Muravyev; AEA 2021 session listing)

candidates.proposed_test: Events: every June recon (2005-2026) plus December 2026. For the published additions, deletions and migrants, compute the recon-day close to next-day open and next-day open to close returns vs IWM's same legs. Separately, test IWM's own recon-day close to next open against all other Fridays. Signal: side (addition vs deletion). Statistic: mean overnight reversal per event (additions negative, deletions positive), with an event bootstrap and a placebo on non-recon Fridays. Cost: 5 bp per leg for IWM and stocks above $5bn, 15 bp for smaller names (MOC fills assumed at the official close). Pass: net reversal > 0 with lower 95% bound > 0 in both halves (2005-2015, 2016-2026). Given Chinco-Sammon, the pre-registered expectation is a null for 2016 onward.

candidates.name: Russell 2000 vs S&P 600 (IWM vs IJR) around the recon windows
candidates.summary: The Russell 2000 carries its recon trading cost at index level, while the S&P 600 rebalances continuously by committee. Test whether IJR minus IWM is predictably positive after the recon close (and negative before it), using archived daily ETFs.
candidates.mechanism: The index level buys additions high at the recon close and sells deletions low, then gives back the overshoot in the following weeks. The S&P 600's continuous, harder-to-front-run changes do not carry this pattern.
candidates.assets: US ETFs IJR, IWM (Alpaca); optional RTY futures (CME)
candidates.horizon: weeks (recon to +20 sessions; Rank Day to recon)
candidates.claimed_effect: From a search summary of S&P DJI's Indexology (2015), not opened (403): over 1994-2014, the S&P 600 beat the R2000 by +0.68% on average in July (t 2.54), and only part of the S&P 600's overall advantage is attributable to the recon effect. S&P DJI (2020) claims 'persistent outperformance after the Russell reconstitution' (title only). Mandel T-385 found unconditional IJR-IWM at +0.22%/yr (not supported), and +0.32%/yr with June excluded.
candidates.replication: Practitioner claims from a competing index provider (commercial interest). Most of the sample predates Russell's 2004 process changes (provisional lists, use of the closing cross). Unconditional size and quality spreads already fail in Mandel (T-385). Partly duplicates T-385 (unconditional) and T-340's ETF arm (IWM vs SPY around the last Friday of June, blocked). The web evidence adds a specific post-recon July window, so it is kept.

sources.title: A Tale of Two Benchmarks: Reconstitution Effect (S&P DJI Indexology)
Recalled to Life: The S&P SmallCap 600's Persistent Outperformance after the Russell Reconstitution (S&P Global)
Beware the Hidden Costs of Indexing (Dimensional)

candidates.proposed_test: Testable now with daily-history-IJR and daily-history-IWM (both from 2000). Events: each June recon (2000-2026) from FTSE Russell's published dates, plus December 2026 forward. Primary window: recon-day close to the close 20 sessions later. Secondary windows: Rank-Day close to recon close (expect IJR-IWM < 0), and full July. Spread = IJR adjusted-close return minus IWM. Cost: 5 bp per leg per trade plus IWM borrow of 0.3%/yr pro rata. Statistic: mean net spread per event, with a permutation p-value against same-length windows drawn from non-recon months of the same year, halves 2000-2013 and 2014-2026, and Holm over the 3 windows. Pass: primary window net mean > 0 with permutation p < 0.05, both halves positive, and placebo windows centred on zero.

candidates.name: Nasdaq-100 December reconstitution: predicted additions and deletions
candidates.summary: The Nasdaq-100 annual ranking is fixed on the last trading day of October (2026-10-30, the same day as Russell Rank Day), announced around the second Friday of December, and effective after the third Friday (expiry day). Trade the predicted adds and deletes, and the deletion rebound.
candidates.mechanism: Rule-based, value-weighted demand from QQQ and other Nasdaq-100 trackers creates predictable flows. First-time additions also gain investor attention, which may make their gains permanent, while repeat additions and deletions see temporary pressure.
variables: calendars (Oct 30 ranking, Dec 11 announcement, Dec 18 effective/OPEX)
adjacent_variables: free float (2026 rule caps modified cap at 3x float)
candidates.assets: US single stocks and QQQ (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Biktimirov-Xu (J. Asset Management 2019; EFMA 2018 version covers 1997-2015): first-time additions show permanent price gains and higher investor awareness; repeat additions and new deletions show temporary changes. No magnitudes visible. QuanterLab (non-peer-reviewed; 18 Decembers 2007-2024, one-year holds, 10 bp costs): deletions beat QQQ by 18.7 points per window before 2016 and trailed by 16.3 after. Its verdict: 'a large early effect faded to roughly a coin flip'.
candidates.replication: The decline is consistent with Greenwood-Sammon's disappearing index effect, though for Nasdaq-100 that comes only via a secondary summary. Regime change in 2026: Nasdaq replaced the 10 bp rule with quarterly reviews that remove names ranked outside the top 125, and added fast entry for large IPOs (2026 NDX changes FAQ, from search results). Pre-2026 history may not represent the new regime.

sources.title: Asymmetric stock price and investor awareness reactions to changes in the Nasdaq 100 index (Biktimirov, Xu; JAM 2019)
Impact of Changes in the Nasdaq 100 Index Membership (Biktimirov; EFMA 2018)
NASDAQ-100 Additions versus Deletions: Eighteen Decembers, an Effect That Died Around 2016 (QuanterLab)
2026 May NDX Changes FAQ (Nasdaq)

candidates.proposed_test: Events: December annual changes 2007-2025 from Nasdaq press releases, plus the 2026 forward event. Predicted lists come from Oct-30 market caps (SEC shares x close) under Nasdaq's published ranking and buffer rule; record prediction accuracy. Arm A: long predicted first-time additions from the first close after the ranking date to the effective close (the third Friday). Arm B: long actual deletions from the effective close to +20 sessions (the rebound). Benchmark: QQQ, plus equal-weight QQQE where available. Cost: 10 bp per leg. Statistic: event-clustered mean net excess return, with halves 2007-2015 and 2016-2025 reported separately because the claimed break is 2016, and Holm over 2 arms. Pass: lower 95% bound > 0 in the 2016-2025 half (Mandel tests recent data). Most Nasdaq-100 names are likely in the 901-symbol archive; check deletions for survivorship.

candidates.name: S&P MidCap 400 / SmallCap 600 changes: direct entrants vs migrations, with 60-day reversal
candidates.summary: Committee changes to the S&P 400/600 carry announcement-to-effective price pressure that reverses within about 60 days. Migrations between S&P indices net out much of the demand, while direct entrants from outside the S&P 1500 do not.
candidates.mechanism: When a stock migrates (e.g. MidCap to 500), MidCap trackers sell while 500 trackers buy, so net demand is small or negative. Direct additions have one-sided buying. The pressure is temporary because demand curves are only short-run inelastic.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: days to weeks (announcement to effective about 5 trading days; 60-day reversal)
candidates.claimed_effect: Shankar-Miller (Financial Review 2006): S&P 600 additions rise and deletions fall significantly at announcement. Moves between S&P indices react less than entries from outside, and the effects are 'fully reversed within 60 days'. Greenwood-Sammon (NBER 2022): migrations rose from about 40% to over 80% of S&P 500 additions. Mid-1990s returns were 6.7% for migrations vs 6.4% for direct additions; by the late 2010s, direct additions earned +2.2% and migrations -2.3%.
candidates.replication: Greenwood-Sammon document the S&P 500 index effect falling from 7.6% (1990s) to 0.8% (past decade). They also report a similar decline in other index families, and say the migration gap coincides with the rise of MidCap funds. Mandel has S&P 500 versions (T-334 inconclusive, T-340/T-453 blocked); the 400/600 and migration-split arms are untested.

sources.title: Market Reaction to Changes in the S&P SmallCap 600 Index (Shankar, Miller; Financial Review 2006)
The Disappearing Index Effect (Greenwood, Sammon; NBER w30748, JF 2025)

candidates.proposed_test: Events: S&P 400 and 600 additions and deletions 2010-2026 from S&P DJI press releases (announcement timestamp = available_at) and Wikipedia change tables (effective dates). Tag each as a direct entrant/exit or a migration (between the 500, 400 and 600). Arm 1: first close after announcement to effective close, vs IJH (400) or IJR (600). Arm 2: effective close to +60 sessions (reversal). Cost: 15 bp per leg for the 400, 30 bp for the 600. Statistic: mean net abnormal return, bootstrapped over events clustered by effective date, with halves. Holm over the 2 arms x 2 indices x direct/migration. Pass: direct-addition pressure > 0 and reversal < 0, each with a 95% bound excluding zero in 2018-2026. Reuse the index_event_study harness from T-334, including its survivorship accounting.

candidates.name: Membership-driven shifts in realised volatility, turnover and index beta for migrants (options angle)
candidates.summary: Moving into the R2000 sharply raises a stock's ETF ownership, which raises its daily volatility, turnover and co-movement with IWM; moving up does the reverse. Test the volatility and beta shift, and whether implied vol prices it before recon.
candidates.mechanism: ETF arbitrage passes ETF-level noise into the underlying stocks (Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi), and common index-fund flows create excess co-movement with the new index (CHL report larger correlation effects for deletions). If option sellers price vol from history, downward migrants' implied vol would lag the change.
candidates.assets: US single stocks and listed single-stock options (Alpaca options)
candidates.horizon: months (60 sessions pre vs post recon)
candidates.claimed_effect: Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi (JF 2018; NBER w20071, 2000-2012): a one-standard-deviation increase in ETF ownership raises daily volatility and turnover by about 16%, identified from R1000/R2000 switchers. The price impact of ETF flows decays after a few days. CHL find return-correlation (co-movement) increases with new index membership but I extracted no magnitude.
candidates.replication: Identified on 2000-2012 data. Glossner (CFR), from a search summary, finds passive mutual fund ownership 0.4-0.6 pp higher at the top of the R2000 in 1998-2006. Not tested on 2015-2026 data that I found. The cutoff-design critiques (Wei-Young, Appel-Gormley-Keim) also apply here.

sources.title: Do ETFs Increase Stock Volatility? (NBER Digest of w20071; Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi, JF 2018)
An Improved Method to Predict Assignment of Stocks into Russell Indexes (Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi; NBER w26370)
Regression Discontinuity and the Price Effects of Stock Market Indexing (NBER w19290; correlation section)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: published migrants each June 2007-2026, plus rank-matched band stayers on each side. Outcome 1: change in 21-day realised vol, averaged over 60 sessions after recon vs 60 sessions before Rank Day. Outcome 2: change in turnover (volume / shares outstanding). Outcome 3: change in 60-session beta to IWM, controlling for SPY. Statistic: difference-in-differences of migrants vs stayers, clustered by event. Pass: realised vol and turnover up for downward migrants and down for upward migrants, t > 2 and both halves agreeing. Options leg, forward only, since chains are captured from 2026-10-14: for December 2026 predicted migrants, record 30-day ATM IV at the preliminary list and compare it with realised vol over the 30 sessions after 2026-12-11, against stayers. Treat this as a pre-registered descriptive record; no verdict until several events.

candidates.name: Russell quarterly IPO additions
candidates.summary: IPOs join Russell indices at quarterly IPO additions and at the recons. The FTSE Russell IPO lists are published and the dates fixed, so the IPO-addition flow can be predicted. Test pressure into the effective date and the reversal after.
candidates.mechanism: Index funds must buy new IPO constituents on a fixed date, and lock-up float limits supply. Micheli-Neuman argue that portfolios tracking the annual schedule are more crowded than quarterly ones, so quarterly additions may carry different pressure.
variables: calendars (quarterly IPO add dates; Dec 2026 alongside recon)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Micheli-Neuman (arXiv 2006.07456, revised 2022; 1989-2019, replicated from CRSP): portfolios following the R3000 on an annual basis are 'more crowded' than quarterly ones. Buying new IPO additions near quarterly rebalance dates could cut indexing costs. Magnitudes not extracted. June 2026: 17 IPOs joined the R2000; SpaceX joined the R1000 under the new fast-entry IPO framework.
candidates.replication: Thin. One older SFU working paper (Lapalme-Jelusic 2009, from a search summary only) reports mixed temporary and permanent effects. No 2015-2026 study found.

sources.title: Evidence of Crowding on Russell 3000 Reconstitution Events (Micheli, Neuman; arXiv)
Russell indexes quarterly IPO update (FTSE Russell)
June 2026 Russell US Indexes reconstitution: summary of changes

candidates.proposed_test: Events: FTSE Russell quarterly IPO addition lists (PDFs with publication dates), roughly 2015-2026. Arm 1: first close after the list's publication to the effective close, vs IWM. Arm 2: effective close to +20 sessions. Exclude names within 10 sessions of lock-up expiry, or report them separately. Cost: 30 bp per leg. Statistic: event-clustered mean net excess return, with halves. Pass: lower 95% bound > 0 for arm 1, or < 0 for arm 2, in 2019-2026. Requires fetching the IPO lists and IPO-era prices; Yahoo histories for IPOs are generally intact, which limits survivorship bias.

candidates.name: First December recon x year-end flows (forward-only)
candidates.summary: From 2026, R2000 deletions and downward migrants face index selling on 2026-12-11. That falls inside tax-loss season, one week before the Nasdaq-100 effective date and quarterly expiry on 2026-12-18, and the 20-session reversal window runs over the turn of the year. Pre-register a separate December arm instead of assuming June's behaviour carries over.
candidates.mechanism: This is a hypothesis built from separate sources, not a documented effect. Index selling of names that are also year-to-date losers could stack with tax-motivated selling. The January rebound literature is from memory (Reinganum 1983; Grinblatt-Moskowitz 2004) and was not opened in this sweep. FTSE Russell limits December style changes to additions and movers, which shrinks style-driven turnover.
variables: calendars (recon 2026-12-11, OPEX 2026-12-18, holidays, turn of year)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: No direct evidence; December 2026 is the first December Russell recon in over three decades (FTSE Russell). The November 2025 parallel run found turnover in line with expectations and style turnover well below June 2025. Mandel's January small-cap tests failed: T-351 and T-444, R2000 minus S&P 500 over the turn of the year +0.87 pp over 39 years, halves +1.91 / -0.13.
candidates.replication: None; a new regime. Use it as a forward record only.

sources.title: FTSE Russell announces December 2026 Russell US Indexes reconstitution schedule
Insights from the November 2025 Russell US Indexes parallel run (FTSE Russell)

candidates.proposed_test: Pre-register before 2026-10-30. For December predicted downward migrants and drop-outs, record their year-to-date return at Rank Day; flag the bottom tercile as tax-loss candidates. Log excess returns vs IWM for three windows: preliminary list to recon close, recon close to 2026-12-31, and 2026-12-31 to +10 sessions in January. Compare tax-loss candidates with the rest and with the June 2026 cohort's same windows. This is report-only: no verdict until at least 5 December events. If a pattern persists by about 2031, it graduates to a ledgered trial with the pass rules used for the June migrant and reversal candidates.

candidates.name: RUT/IWM implied-vol premium in recon windows (RVX vs realised)
candidates.summary: Cboe notes RVX has tended to sit below its annual average in May-June since 2015, while recon day concentrates huge volume. Test whether the RVX minus subsequent realised IWM variance gap is different in 21-day windows that contain a recon day.
candidates.mechanism: A known, scheduled liquidity event may be priced into small-cap vol differently from ordinary windows. Alternatively, the abundant recon-day liquidity damps realised vol, which would favour selling vol into the window.
adjacent_variables: RTY futures open interest and roll
candidates.assets: IWM/RUT options (Alpaca options, Cboe), RTY futures (CME)
candidates.claimed_effect: Cboe (2022): since 2015 RVX has generally been below its annual average in May-June (exceptions 2019 and 2020). The RVX minus RUT 30-day historical vol gap averaged about 3.65 points over seven years, and the RUT put/call ratio averaged 1.71 in recon periods vs 1.84 annually. No strategy returns stated.
candidates.replication: Exchange marketing research with no statistical tests. Mandel T-65 (unconditional RVX VRP vs IWM) is not supported (p 0.0945). This conditional variant partly duplicates T-65 and is kept because the recon-window conditioning is new.

sources.title: Russell Reconstitution: Opportunities to Harvest Volatility (Cboe)

candidates.proposed_test: Testable now: archived RVX history (from 2009) and daily-history-IWM. For each trading day t, gap_t = RVX_t^2 minus annualised realised variance of IWM over t+1..t+21. The treatment indicator is whether the window contains a June recon day (FTSE Russell dates). Statistic: difference in mean gap, treated minus untreated, with a 42-day block bootstrap and all 21 entry offsets pooled per Mandel rule 10. Halves: 2009-2017 and 2018-2026. Pass: the difference excludes zero at 95% with both halves agreeing. Report the sign either way. If positive, a recon-window IWM short-straddle claim can be registered later, model-priced first (as in T-57) until chain captures cover several recon windows.

rows.name: Downward migrants (Russell 1000 to 2000): run-up from Rank Day to recon close

overlaps.note: Its library variants include 'Russell 2000 predicted adds from May rank to reconstitution day', which was never run. The S&P 500 announcement-to-effective claim is blocked because there is no point-in-time change list with announcement dates.
S&P 500 announcement-to-effective run-up, blocked on the same missing list.
S&P 500 additions 2010-2026. The reported announcement-to-effective run-up variant was +0.00% on 210 events. The verdict stayed inconclusive because only 82.6% of additions could be priced.
Options (call-spread) form of the inclusion run-up.

learnings.finding: The tradable run-up from A+1 to the effective close for S&P 500 additions was +0.00% on 210 events with a cited announcement date. Once forced demand is announced, the post-announcement run-up in large caps is gone.
The index-addition return fell from 7.4% (1990s) to 0.3% (past decade). The sweep rates it 'Decayed', and the Russell decline was not statistically significant.

90.8% of the FINRA stock universe has no archived price, and at most ~620 stocks per date have both a price and a point-in-time market cap. A rank-1000 membership engine cannot be built from archived data.
Month-end rebalancing flow in SPY: -45.6 bp net with both halves negative. Mechanical flows on a known calendar can leave a footprint that survives costs in Mandel's tests.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md (closedTime landmine; Madhavan inflation analogue)
learnings.finding: Anchoring on an outcome-dependent time manufactured a +18% ROI. In the same way, portfolios formed on ex-post membership pick up the price moves that caused membership, so only published lists or Rank-Day predictions are admissible.
PnL from hundreds of bets cannot settle an edge. About 20 events of 20-40 names each give wide event-clustered intervals.
0 of 582 cells pass on price-derived features. Flow and calendar mechanisms are the class Mandel has not exhausted.

data: daily-history-* (901 archived symbols; few near rank 1000)
rows.missing_data: Point-in-time Russell membership. FTSE Russell preliminary and final addition/deletion lists with publication timestamps are free PDFs on lseg.com/ftse-russell, but how many years are archived is unverified. iShares IWB/IWM month-end holdings history is free via the holdings CSV with asOfDate (depth to verify). Daily prices are needed for ~600 names ranked 700-1300, including later-delisted ones: Yahoo covers survivors, and DoltHub post-no-preference/stocks or Stooq may cover delisted names (free, coverage unverified). Historical Rank-Day dates come from FTSE Russell press releases.

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2007-2026, take the Russell 1000 members that FTSE Russell's preliminary list moves to the Russell 2000. An equal-weighted portfolio of them, bought at the first NYSE close after the list's publication and sold at the recon-day official close, hedged short IWM in equal dollars, earns a positive mean net excess return per event. Costs are 15 bp per stock leg per side, 5 bp per IWM leg per side and 0.3%/yr IWM borrow. The event-clustered lower 95% bound must be > 0 and both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean over events of (event portfolio net return minus IWM over the same window). Inference is a studentized bootstrap over events; a stock bootstrap clustered by event must agree. Holm runs across a 6-trial migrant family: downward run-up, upward short and post-recon reversal, each with a Rank-Day-entry variant.
registration.null: Mean net excess return <= 0. Placebo: the same stocks over a same-length window shifted 3 months later, which should be centred on zero.
registration.procedure: available_at of a list is its publication time (posted after the US close), so entry is the next session's close. A migrant is on the R2000 additions list and was an R1000 member at the prior recon (prior final list, or iShares IWB holdings at the last month end before Rank Day). Rank-Day variant: market cap = SEC dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding (all classes, latest with filing acceptance before Rank Day) x Rank-Day close. Apply the +/-2.5% cumulative-percentile band around rank 1000 and report prediction accuracy against the published lists. Exit at the recon-day Yahoo close (the closing auction). A name that delists inside the window exits at its last close. Report the share priced; an event with < 90% priced is inconclusive (rule 9). Halves are 2007-2016 and 2017-2026. December 2026 (list 2026-11-13, recon 2026-12-11) is logged as the first forward observation and never pooled with June.
registration.data: daily-history-IWM, sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions. New: FTSE Russell preliminary and final lists, iShares IWB/IWM holdings history, delisting-aware prices for non-archived names.
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with event-clustered one-sided lower 95% bound > 0, both halves positive, the placebo CI covering 0, and Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 in the 6-trial migrant family.
registration.controls: Benchmark is IWM. Secondary control (Rank-Day variant only): prior-R1000 band stayers matched on rank. One window, no grid, costs as stated. Ex-post membership is forbidden as a signal. Survivorship accounting as in T-334, with at least 200 stock-events in total.

rows.notes: The best-supported claim in the cluster: CHL +5.6% June 1996-2012, Dimensional +1.2% 2014-2023 (gross). It has decayed about 5x and is contested (Chinco-Sammon; FTSE Russell 2026). The historical test is blocked by T-393's universe-coverage gap. The cheapest unblock is the published-list variant, which needs prices only for the listed migrants. This is time-critical: register before Rank Day 2026-10-30 so December 2026 is a clean forward event. For that event every name is currently listed, so survivorship does not arise. One forward event decides nothing.

rows.name: Upward migrants (Russell 2000 to 1000): underperformance before recon

overlaps.note: The 'deletion decline A+1 -> E (short)' arm of the same index-flow family; never run.
Index-event harness and survivorship accounting to reuse.
Days-to-cover as a borrow-cost proxy, plus FINRA's publication-lag convention.
Its universe-coverage failure is the data gap here too.

learnings.finding: The FINRA days-to-cover top-decile diagnostic is survivor-only and inconclusive. Rows enter at the first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement, and this is the rule to reuse for the hard-to-borrow flag.
No archived prices for 90.8% of FINRA-listed stocks, so rank-1000 predictions cannot come from the archive.
Index-flow returns have decayed in every family measured, and deletion pressure fell from -16.1% to -0.6% for the S&P 500.
About 10-20 cross-sections cannot settle a 1% effect. Event-clustered intervals are required.

rows.missing_data: Same as the downward-migrant candidate: FTSE Russell preliminary lists, iShares IWM/IWB holdings history, and prices for non-archived names ranked near 1000 (Yahoo survivors, DoltHub or Stooq for delisted names, free, coverage unverified). Historical borrow fees have no free source, so they are assumed: 0.3%/yr GC plus a stated surcharge.

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2007-2026, take the Russell 2000 members that FTSE Russell's preliminary list moves to the Russell 1000. An equal-weighted short of them, entered at the first close after publication and covered at the recon-day close, hedged long IWM, earns a positive mean net return per event. Costs are 15 bp per stock leg per side, 5 bp per IWM leg per side, 0.3%/yr borrow, and a 5%/yr surcharge on names in the top FINRA days-to-cover decile. The event-clustered lower 95% bound must be > 0 and both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean over events of (IWM return minus the equal-weighted migrant return) net of costs and borrow. Studentized bootstrap over events. Holm runs in the 6-trial migrant family.
registration.null: Mean net return <= 0. Placebo: the same names over a same-length window 3 months later.
registration.procedure: Lists and entry timing are as in russell-downward-migrant-runup. Days-to-cover is the latest FINRA row whose publication (first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement) precedes entry; the decile is cross-sectional over that date's priced names. Rank-Day variant uses the SEC-shares market-cap engine. Exit is the recon-day official close. Delisting handling and the < 90%-priced inconclusive rule are as in the downward test. Halves are 2007-2016 and 2017-2026, and December 2026 is a separate forward arm.
registration.data: daily-history-IWM, finra-short-interest, sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions. New: FTSE Russell lists, iShares holdings, delisting-aware prices.
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided event-clustered lower 95% bound > 0, both halves positive, placebo CI covering 0, and Holm p < 0.05 in the migrant family.
registration.controls: Benchmark is IWM. Control: the largest R2000 stayers inside the band, matched on rank (Rank-Day variant). One window. Borrow assumptions stated, not fitted. At least 200 stock-events.

rows.notes: The mirror of the downward-migrant test (CHL -5.4% June; Dimensional -1.1%). Shorting $4-8bn names on Alpaca is usually easy-to-borrow, but historical fees are unobservable, hence the stated surcharge. Run it in the same family and data build as the downward test; there is no separate unblock.

rows.name: Migrant reversal in the 20 sessions after recon

overlaps.note: Same post-effective 20-session reversal design on S&P 500 additions. Survivor mean -0.605% net with a one-sided upper bound of +0.368%; inconclusive at 82.6% priced.
Its 'post-effective reversal E -> E+20' variant.
Its options form includes the post-effective +20d variant.

learnings.finding: Survivor-only S&P 500 additions reversed -0.605% net over 20 sessions. The 5-year buckets are all negative (-0.63, -0.14, -1.85, -0.73), but the upper bound is +0.368% and survivorship blocks the verdict.
The dollar-volume-matched placebo gave -0.117% (CI -0.467% to +0.244%), so part of any reversal can be generic post-event drift.
Small-cap drift was survivorship: a placebo entry 25 sessions late (+1.77%/month) beat the real entry (+1.32%). The 60-session-later placebo is required.
Index effects decayed. A smaller pre-recon overshoot implies a smaller reversal.

rows.missing_data: Published final migrant lists: FTSE Russell final add/delete PDFs, or reconstruction from iShares IWB/IWM month-end holdings straddling recon (free, depth to verify). Prices for migrants not in the 901-symbol archive, including later-delisted ones (DoltHub or Stooq, unverified). This is the least data-hungry migrant test, because no ranking engine is needed.

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2007-2026, an equal-weighted portfolio long the stocks that moved from the Russell 2000 to the Russell 1000 and short those that moved the other way, entered at the recon-day official close and closed 20 sessions later, earns a positive mean net spread per event. Costs are 15 bp per leg per side plus 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg. The event-clustered lower 95% bound must be > 0 and both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean over events of the net long-minus-short spread. Studentized bootstrap over events, with a stock bootstrap clustered by event that must agree. Report +5 and +60 sessions for shape only.
registration.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Placebo: the same stocks entered 60 sessions after recon and held 20.
registration.procedure: The migrant list is the final published list, which is public before recon day; iShares holdings diffs may only reconstruct it. Entry is at the recon-day close (Yahoo close = closing auction). Variant: next-session open (Yahoo open), so that closing-auction fills are not assumed. The variant is in the Holm family. Delisted names exit at their last close with proceeds credited; report the share priced and treat < 90% as inconclusive. Halves are 2007-2016 and 2017-2026. A December arm (2026-12-11 to about 2027-01-13) is registered separately because it spans the turn of the year.
registration.data: daily-history-IWM, archived daily-history names. New: final lists or iShares holdings, delisting-aware prices.
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided lower 95% bound > 0, both halves positive, placebo CI covering 0, and Holm p < 0.05 in the migrant family.
registration.controls: One 20-session window, no grid. Costs on both legs. Survivorship is reported per event, with at least 300 stock-events. December is never pooled with June.

rows.notes: Dimensional's post-recon figures (+2% for upward, -0.95% for downward) imply a large spread, but CHL find no July reversal. T-334's S&P analogue has the right sign and is not significant. Building the holdings-diff list unblocks this, candidate 13 and part of candidate 5.

rows.name: Passive demand in days of volume (benchmarking-intensity change) as a continuous predictor

overlaps.note: Same demand-over-liquidity construction for LETF rebalancing. Blocked on daily ETF shares-outstanding/NAV history, the same AUM gap as here.
Forward capture of ETF flows / AUM.
Binary index-change design that this candidate generalises.
The binary-event analogue.

learnings.finding: Daily ETF shares outstanding and NAV history from issuer files are not archived, so passive AUM per benchmark has no point-in-time source yet.
The binary S&P addition run-up after announcement is +0.00%, which leaves little for a continuous version to rank in large caps.
Volume-based ICs in the swing program are about +0.01 and weak. Volume-scaled signals have not carried edge net of costs.

rows.missing_data: Everything in the membership engine, plus passive AUM per benchmark at Rank Day. Monthly AUM for IWB, IWM, IWV, VTWO and the Russell Midcap trackers is available from SEC N-PORT filings (free, 2019 on). Earlier dates need issuer shares-outstanding history, which has no free archive. Free-float factors are proprietary, so they are approximated from SEC public float. Dollar volume is needed for non-archived names.

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2019-2026, predicted passive demand in days of volume, D_i = sum over b in {R1000, R2000, R3000, Midcap} of AUM_b x (w_new - w_old) / 20-day median dollar volume at Rank Day, has a positive mean Spearman IC with the excess return vs IWM from the first close after Rank Day to the recon close (t > 2 over events, both halves positive). Its IC with the 20-session post-recon return must be negative.
registration.statistic: Per-event cross-sectional Spearman IC, averaged over events and t-tested over events. The top-minus-bottom tercile portfolio at 15 bp per leg per side is reported.
registration.procedure: AUM_b = N-PORT net assets of the benchmark's trackers in the latest filing accepted before Rank Day; this is a lower bound. Weights come from the predicted cap x SEC public-float ratio. Dollar volume comes from the 20 sessions before Rank Day. Universe: all predicted changes (migrants and 3000-cutoff adds and deletes). Report the migrant-only subset and halves (2019-2022 and 2023-2026). The D values for 2026-10-30 are computed and frozen before the preliminary list as a forward observation.
registration.data: sec-companyfacts. New: N-PORT tracker AUM, membership engine, prices and volume for non-archived names.
registration.pass: Mean pre-recon IC > 0 with t > 2, both halves positive, and the post-recon mean IC < 0.
registration.controls: One horizon pair, no grid. The tercile portfolio carries costs. The binary migrant flag is a nested baseline: D must add IC over it.

rows.notes: Elegant, but it needs the most data in the cluster: membership, float, AUM and liquidity. The AUM proxy only exists from 2019, giving about 8 events. It is only worth doing after the migrant tests show any pre-recon signal.

rows.name: Long-run benchmarking-intensity discount: just-moved-up R2000 stocks beat just-moved-down stocks for 12 months

overlaps.note: Mandel's size/quality spread failed: IJR-IWM +0.22%/yr, family DSR 0.001. Long-horizon cross-sectional premia face the same deflation bar.
Index-event survivorship accounting.
Factor-tilt alphas have not survived in Mandel.

learnings.finding: Most published anomalies decay after publication. The source paper itself shows the effect halving after 2007 (-60/+48 bp a month falling to -26/+28 bp).
The family-wide DSR is 0.001 over 34 trials. A 12-month cross-sectional spread with about 19 cohorts will struggle to clear DSR > 0.95.
Long holds in small caps are dominated by survivorship unless delisting returns are credited.

rows.missing_data: Published migrant lists 2007-2025 (FTSE Russell PDFs or iShares holdings diffs) and 12-month delisting-aware prices for about 40-80 names a year. Acquisitions within 12 months are common, so DoltHub or Stooq coverage must be verified and merger proceeds sourced.

registration.claim: For annual cohorts formed at each June recon close 2007-2025, take stocks within 150 ranks of the 1000 cutoff. An equal-weighted portfolio long those that just moved from the Russell 2000 to the Russell 1000 and short those that moved the other way, held 12 months, earns positive calendar-time FF5+UMD alpha (Newey-West t > 2). Costs are 10 bp per leg at formation and exit plus 0.3%/yr borrow. Both cohort halves must be positive and the family DSR > 0.95.
registration.statistic: Monthly calendar-time return of the overlapping annual cohorts, regressed on FF5 + UMD with Newey-West t (lag 12). Also the raw cohort-mean spread with a bootstrap over cohorts.
registration.procedure: Cohorts are formed from published lists only. Rank within 150 of the cutoff is approximated by the migrants' holdings-weight rank in IWB/IWM. Factors are compounded from french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily. Delisted names take merger proceeds where found. Where proceeds cannot be found, performance delistings take -30% (stated assumption). Halves are cohorts 2007-2015 and 2016-2025. A fail-to-reject with a positive point estimate is inconclusive, not not_supported. Variant: each side against its own band stayers.
registration.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily. New: lists or holdings, delisting-aware prices.
registration.pass: Alpha > 0 with NW t > 2, both halves positive, and family DSR > 0.95 (nested with russell-migrant-post-recon-reversal).
registration.controls: One horizon (12 months), no grid. Costs and borrow as stated. Delisting share reported. The 20-session reversal family is nested, because it has the same direction.

rows.notes: Identification at the cutoff is contested (Wei-Young; Appel-Gormley-Keim), and the natural experiment has been reused by many papers, so the Heath et al. multiple-testing warning applies. There are only about 19 cohorts. Run it, if at all, as a by-product of the migrant data build.

rows.name: Lower cutoff (rank about 3000): Microcap graduates into the R2000 and R2000 drop-outs

overlaps.note: Its 'Russell 2000 predicted adds from May rank to reconstitution day' variant is mostly this cutoff.
Survivorship accounting; deletions are the arm where Yahoo fails.
Coverage gap: no archived prices for most small and micro caps.

learnings.finding: In small caps a placebo entry beat the real one, because of survivorship. Delisting-aware prices and a placebo window are mandatory.
Conditioning on an outcome-determined anchor manufactures edge. Madhavan's March-June returns on actual membership are the same mechanism, so only post-Rank-Day or post-list returns count.
At most ~620 stocks per date have a price and market cap, so ranks 2700-3300 are entirely outside the archive.
Index effects decayed overall, although demand relative to liquidity is largest at this cutoff (14x ADV on recon day).

rows.missing_data: Several sources are missing. FTSE Russell preliminary lists (additions and deletions with reasons). Russell Microcap membership (iShares IWC holdings history, free, depth unverified). Daily OHLC for about 1,000 micro and small caps a year, including delisted ones (DoltHub or Stooq, unverified). IPO flags to exclude IPO additions (sec-submissions has S-1/424B filings, so these are partly available).

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2010-2026, take the non-IPO stocks that FTSE Russell's preliminary list adds to the Russell 2000 from outside the Russell 3000 or from the Microcap index. An equal-weighted portfolio of them, bought at the first close after publication and sold at the recon close, earns a positive mean net excess return over IWM per event. Costs are 40 bp per leg per side. The event-clustered lower 95% bound must be > 0 and both halves positive.
registration.statistic: Mean over events of the net excess return vs IWM. Studentized bootstrap over events. The deletion arm (R2000 members on the deletion list) is shorted only where FINRA days-to-cover is below the median; otherwise it is avoid-only and scored against IWM. It is a separate trial in the Holm family.
registration.null: Mean net excess <= 0. Placebo: the same names over the same window 3 months later.
registration.procedure: Lists are point-in-time by publication timestamp, with entry at the next close. A Rank-Day variant ranks eligible companies 2700-3300 by SEC shares x Rank-Day close, with no band at this cutoff. Costs: 40 bp per leg, recalibrated per stock with a Corwin-Schultz high-low spread estimate from the 20 sessions before entry (stated assumption; the larger of the two is used). FINRA rows enter at the first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement. Delisted names exit at their last close. Report the share priced; < 90% means inconclusive. Halves are 2010-2017 and 2018-2026.
registration.data: finra-short-interest, finra-regsho-cnms, sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, daily-history-IWM. New: lists, IWC holdings, delisting-aware microcap prices.
registration.pass: Net mean > 0 with one-sided lower 95% bound > 0, both halves positive, placebo CI covering 0, and Holm p < 0.05 over the 2 arms x 2 entry variants.
registration.controls: Benchmark is IWM. One window, no grid. Costs are spread-calibrated, not assumed small. At least 500 stock-events. IPO additions are excluded (separate candidate).

rows.notes: The mechanism is strongest here, with forced demand far above liquidity. The evidence is weakest: CHL finds t 1.25-1.45 at this cutoff, and Madhavan's figures are pre-2003 and inflated. Costs and the delisting bias dominate. Capacity for a small account exists, but fills at the recon close in microcaps are uncertain.

rows.name: R2000 deletions beat additions over the next year (index-turnover drag)

overlaps.note: Small-cap long-horizon spreads have not passed Mandel's DSR.
Deletions are the arm Yahoo cannot price, because they are delisted.

learnings.finding: S&P 500 deletion pressure fell from -16.1% (1990s) to -0.6% (2010-2020). Less depression at deletion means less to recover.
Small-cap long-hold returns in free data are survivorship-inflated.
53 of 56 unpriced S&P additions were names no longer in the index. In free data, deletions are the worst-covered arm.

rows.missing_data: Published R2000 addition and deletion lists 2005-2025, with migrant and IPO flags. 12-month delisting-aware prices and delisting proceeds for microcaps; the CRSP-equivalent is not free, and DoltHub/Stooq coverage is unverified. Shumway-style delisting returns are only an assumption.

registration.claim: For annual cohorts formed at each June recon close 2005-2025, an equal-weighted buy-and-hold portfolio, held 12 months, is long Russell 2000 deletions that left the Russell 3000 or moved to the Microcap index and short Russell 2000 additions that are neither migrants nor IPOs. It earns positive calendar-time FF5+UMD alpha (Newey-West t > 2) after 40 bp per leg per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg. Both cohort halves must be positive and the family DSR > 0.95.
registration.statistic: Calendar-time monthly alpha on FF5 + UMD (NW lag 12), plus the cohort-mean spread with a bootstrap over cohorts.
registration.procedure: Lists are published lists only. Buy-and-hold is equal-weighted at formation. Delisting proceeds are credited where found. Otherwise performance delistings take -30% and mergers their last close (stated assumptions, with a sensitivity run at -50%). Report the share of names priced; < 80% is inconclusive. Halves are cohorts 2005-2014 and 2015-2025.
registration.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, daily-history-IWM. New: lists, delisting-aware prices and proceeds.
registration.pass: Alpha > 0 with NW t > 2, both halves positive, family DSR > 0.95, and >= 80% of names priced.
registration.controls: One horizon, no grid. Costs and borrow as stated. The IPO long-run underperformance confound is removed by excluding IPOs. Momentum and short-term reversal are absorbed by UMD.

rows.notes: Cai-Houge (1979-2004) is unreplicated. The deletion arm sits exactly where free data are worst (delisted microcaps). Its expected value is low next to its build cost. Keep it registered but parked behind the migrant build.

rows.name: Short interest and short volume condition the recon effect

overlaps.note: Days-to-cover cross-section; universe coverage failed.
Top-decile days-to-cover underperformance; survivor-only diagnostic.
FINRA short-volume-ratio level quintiles among S&P 500 members.
Short-interest surprise among S&P 500 members.

learnings.finding: Bottom-minus-top days-to-cover decile: net -0.048% per period, CI -0.371% to +0.290%. Days-to-cover alone carried nothing in the priced universe.
FINRA publication lag: rows enter at the first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement.
About 9 events of cross-sectional slopes cannot detect a moderate effect. The registration must expect inconclusive.

rows.missing_data: The predicted or published change lists from the migrant and lower-cutoff candidates (FTSE Russell lists or iShares holdings), and prices for the changed names. FINRA short interest and RegSHO are archived from 2017-12 and 2018-08.

registration.claim: For Russell index changes at the June recons 2018-2026 plus December 2026 (downward and upward migrants, 3000-cutoff entrants and drop-outs), the within-event cross-sectional slope of excess return vs IWM on FINRA days-to-cover is tested in two windows. From the first close after the preliminary list to the recon close the slope is positive for additions; from recon to +20 sessions it is negative. Each slope is averaged over events with t > 2.
registration.statistic: Fama-MacBeth: per-event OLS slope of excess return on days-to-cover (z-scored within event), with controls for log market cap and 20-day return. Mean over events with t over events. SI/shares outstanding and the 10-day RegSHO short-volume-ratio change are reported as secondaries.
registration.procedure: Days-to-cover is the latest FINRA row whose publication (first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement) precedes the preliminary-list entry. Shares outstanding come from SEC dei facts at filing acceptance. RegSHO ratios come from CNMS file days ending the day before entry. Change lists are point-in-time as in the migrant tests. Additions and deletions are separate trials (Holm over 4).
registration.data: finra-short-interest, finra-regsho-cnms, sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions. New: change lists, prices.
registration.pass: Predicted sign with t > 2 in both windows for additions. Below 8 events only a decisive wrong sign counts (rule 5); otherwise inconclusive.
registration.controls: One signal per trial, no grid. Size and recent-return controls. Costs do not enter a slope test. A tradable version would need the migrant tests' cost rules.

rows.notes: A single unreplicated QREF study with no magnitudes. It is a conditioning layer on effects not yet shown to exist in Mandel. Only worth running as a free secondary once change lists exist.

rows.name: Recon-day closing-auction pressure and overnight reversal

overlaps.note: On SPY 2023-11..2026-10, last-half-hour pressure into the close did not reverse overnight.
Closing-auction deviation (official close vs the 15:30 bar) as an overnight-reversal predictor on 60m bars.
IWM's positive overnight drift (+3.4 to +3.6 bp a night) is the baseline that any recon-night reading sits on.
Paper test of IWM closing-auction fills within 1.5 bp of the official close.
Triple-witching close gamma: scheduled close events did not raise next-day realised moves.

learnings.finding: There is no overnight reversal slope on SPY's last-half-hour move. Liquid ETF closing pressure is absorbed.
IWM's close-to-open drift is positive. Compare the recon night against other Friday-to-Monday nights, not against zero.
Only two years of 60m bars exist, covering 2 recons. Intraday auction-deviation measures cannot be built historically.

rows.missing_data: Published addition, deletion and migrant lists for 2005-2026, and their official close and next-open prices (Yahoo for survivors; delisted names via DoltHub or Stooq). Nasdaq NOII and NYSE imbalance history is not free. The IWM-only arm (recon-day close to Monday open vs all other Fridays) can run now on daily-history-IWM as a descriptive check.

registration.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2005-2026, published Russell 2000 additions (including downward migrants) earn a negative return vs IWM, and deletions a positive one, from the recon-day official close to the next session's open. The deletion-minus-addition overnight spread is positive net of 5 bp per leg per side for names above $5bn and IWM, and 15 bp for smaller names. The event-bootstrap lower 95% bound must be > 0 in both halves (2005-2015, 2016-2026).

registration.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Placebo: the same names on each of the four preceding Fridays. IWM arm: IWM's recon close-to-Monday-open vs all other Friday close-to-Monday-open returns, two-sided, reported.
registration.procedure: Lists are published before recon. Prices are the Yahoo daily close (official closing auction) and next open (first print; stated limitation). registration.pass: Net spread > 0 with lower 95% bound > 0 in both halves, and the placebo-Friday CI covering 0.
registration.controls: One overnight window, no grid. Size-tiered costs. The IWM baseline is taken from same-weekday nights. December 2026 is logged separately.

registration.claim: Over the 27 June Russell reconstitutions 2000-2026 (FTSE Russell's published recon dates), a dollar-neutral long IJR / short IWM position earns a positive mean net return per event. It is entered at the recon-day close and closed at the close 20 NYSE sessions later. Costs are 5 bp per leg per side and 0.3%/yr IWM borrow pro rata. The test requires one-sided permutation p < 0.05 against same-length windows from the same year's non-recon months, and both halves (2000-2013, 2014-2026) positive.
registration.statistic: Mean over events of (IJR adjclose return - IWM adjclose return) from the recon close to the close at +20 sessions, minus 20 bp round-trip costs and 0.3% x 20/252 borrow. Inference is a permutation p-value plus a studentized bootstrap 95% CI over events. Two secondary windows are reported with Holm over all 3, not deciding: (a) close at recon - 20 sessions to recon close, expected < 0; (b) last June close to last July close.
registration.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Permutation: each draw takes, for each year, a 20-session window starting at a uniformly random session in Jan, Feb, Apr, May, Aug, Oct or Nov. Those months have no Russell recon, no S&P quarterly rebalance and no Russell quarterly IPO additions. 10,000 draws; p = share of draw means >= the observed mean.
registration.procedure: Recon dates: one published date per year with its source URL. The calendar is announced months ahead, so it is point-in-time. Entry and exit use Yahoo closes (official closing auctions). The spread uses adjclose, so dividends are reinvested and the short leg pays them. Halves split by event year. Placebo: the identical rule anchored on the last Friday of each placebo month; its pooled mean's 95% CI must include 0. The December 2026 recon (2026-12-11) is a separate forward arm, never pooled with June. The result enters T-385's family for the DSR.
registration.data: daily-history-IJR, daily-history-IWM (2000-05-26..2026-10-14), FTSE Russell recon-date list
registration.pass: Primary-window net mean > 0 with one-sided permutation p < 0.05, both halves' net means > 0, and the placebo CI covering 0.
registration.controls: One window (20 sessions), no grid, no thresholds, costs and borrow charged. T-385's unconditional drift is absorbed by same-year permutation windows. The S&P 600 quarterly rebalance (third Friday of June) falls before the primary window, and the window's July 4 pre-holiday session affects both legs.

rows.notes: The only cluster candidate testable today with archived data, and very cheap. The prior is low because the effect is a practitioner claim from a competing index provider, and Mandel's small-cap calendar spreads have decayed. With about 13 events per half, both halves positive at p < 0.05 needs a robust effect of about 0.5% per event. registration.claim: For published Russell 1000/2000 migrants at the June recons 2007-2026, three measures are compared against rank-matched band stayers on the same side: mean 21-day realised volatility, share turnover, and 60-session beta to IWM (controlling for SPY). From the 60 sessions before Rank Day to the 60 sessions after recon, they rise for downward migrants and fall for upward migrants. Each difference-in-differences needs event-clustered t > 2 and both halves agreeing in sign.
registration.statistic: Difference-in-differences of migrants vs matched stayers for each outcome: log of realised vol, log of turnover, and beta. Standard errors are clustered by event. Halves are 2007-2016 and 2017-2026.
registration.null: DiD = 0 for each outcome and direction.
registration.procedure: Turnover = Yahoo volume / SEC dei shares (latest accepted before each day). Beta comes from the regression r_i = a + b r_IWM + c r_SPY over 60 sessions. Pre-window: 60 sessions ending at Rank Day. Post-window: 60 sessions starting the session after recon, so the pressure window is excluded. Stayers are the R1000 names with the smallest IWB weights that stayed and the R2000 names with the largest IWM weights that stayed, matched 1:1 on holdings-weight rank. rows.name: RUT/IWM implied-vol premium in recon windows (RVX vs realised)

overlaps.note: The unconditional RVX VRP vs IWM: implied 24.9 vs realised 22.2 vol pts, p 0.0945. This candidate conditions it on the recon window.

data: FTSE Russell June recon dates (rule calendar, to compile; free)
rows.missing_data: Only the June recon-date list, compiled from FTSE Russell press releases and checked against the last-Friday rule (2010-2026 is all that RVX covers). RUT option volume and put/call history (Cboe's 1.71 vs 1.84) is not archived, so it is left out.

registration.claim: Over 2009-09 to 2026-09, define the 21-session variance gap as (RVX at day t's close / 100)^2 minus the annualised realised variance of IWM daily log returns over sessions t+1..t+21. Its mean on entry days whose window contains a June Russell recon day differs from the same year's other entry days. The 95% CI of the mean per-year difference must exclude zero, and both halves must agree in sign. The test is two-sided and the sign is reported either way.
registration.statistic: d_y = mean gap over treated entry days in year y minus mean gap over that year's untreated entry days. The statistic is the mean of d_y over the 17 years 2010-2026, with a studentized bootstrap over years. A secondary opex-matched contrast compares treated days with untreated entry days whose window contains the third Friday of March, September or December.
registration.procedure: RVX daily closes (Cboe close stamp 21:30 UTC) and IWM adjclose. Every trading day is an entry, with no grid phase (rule 10). RV = 252/21 x the sum of squared log returns over t+1..t+21. Treated = the window contains that year's published June recon date. Untreated = all other entry days of the same year whose window contains no recon date. Inference: studentized bootstrap over the 17 d_y values (10,000 draws). The alternative, a circular block bootstrap with 42-day blocks of the daily treated-minus-untreated contrast, must agree (rule 11). Halves are 2010-2017 and 2018-2026.
registration.data: cboe-RVX-history, daily-history-IWM, FTSE Russell recon-date list
registration.pass: 95% CI of mean d_y excludes 0, both halves' means share its sign, the opex-matched contrast has the same sign, and the block-bootstrap alternative agrees.
registration.controls: No thresholds, no grid. RVX is RUT index IV applied to IWM, as in T-65. June quad witching is isolated by the opex-matched contrast. T-65's unconditional gap is the baseline. A positive result only licenses a later model-priced recon-window IWM short-straddle registration (T-57 style), with nothing traded until chain captures cover several recon windows.
