rows.name: Downward migrants (Russell 1000 to 2000): run-up from Rank Day to recon close
rows.source_notes: Opened CHL (NBER w19290, Aug/Oct 2013; RFS 2015) as full text via pdftotext. Its R1000 cutoff sample is 1996-2012. With the optimal bandwidth of 100 the June effect for additions to the R2000 is 'on the order of 5.6% with a t-statistic of 2.65'. The paper says there are 'no effects in subsequent months (e.g. July, August,...)', and banding cut switching from about 10% to about 3%. Opened Dimensional: the authors are Roberts and Dai, and the piece is dated 15 May 2025, not 2024. Over 2014-2023 'R2 Migrating Additions' earned +1.2% vs the R2000 in the 20 days before recon and -0.95% after. Each year uses groups of 20 stocks, and volume is about 10x on recon day. Opened Chinco-Sammon (May 2023 draft): one-day recon-day returns to buying additions 'steadily converged to nearly zero' over 2000-2021. FTSE Russell's 2026 key-facts note says the past short-term impact 'hasn't reliably followed such a pattern'. Pavlova-Sikorskaya's +112 bp passive buying is confirmed. Calendar facts: Rank Day was 31 May until 2015, then 2016-05-27, 2017-05-12 and 2018-05-11 (P-S appendix), and 2026-04-30 for June 2026 (FTSE June 2026 summary). The December 2026 schedule is confirmed from the FTSE press release: Rank Day 2026-10-30, preliminary list after the close on 2026-11-13, effective after the close on 2026-12-11.
rows.replication_concerns: 1) Decay: CHL measured about 5.6% for June, Dimensional about 1.2% over 20 days (2014-2023), and Chinco-Sammon near zero on recon day itself, although that is a different, one-day window. 2) CHL's June return starts at Rank Day, so part of the RD effect falls between Rank Day and the list's publication, which a list-entry trade cannot earn. 3) An RD effect against just-missed stocks is not a tradable return against IWM. Downward migrants are past losers, so momentum works against the long, and the IWM hedge leaves size and momentum exposure. 4) The original row's 2007-2026 sample includes CHL's own 2007-2012, which is in-sample. Out-of-sample is 2013-2026, only 14 June events, each a cross-section of 20-40 names, so even Dimensional's +1.2% gross is near the detection limit after 30 bp of round-trip stock costs.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IWM is archived (2000-05-26..2026-10-14). sec-companyfacts and sec-submissions exist but cover only a subset of issuers: 36 of 44 CIK buckets (b003, b008-b013 and b019 are absent), and about 145 CIKs in b025. dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding only starts in 2009-2011, with 12 rows in 2009 and 244 in 2011 in b025, so a Rank-Day market-cap engine is infeasible before about 2012 and needs a full-universe SEC fetch. Nothing in the archive gives Russell membership: no FTSE Russell lists and no iShares IWB/IWM holdings history (only ssga-spy-holdings and the iShares IBIT files exist). T-393 found at most about 620 stocks per date with both a price and a point-in-time cap, so most names near rank 1000, delisted ones especially, are unpriced.
rows.lookahead_risks: Using ex-post (final, or holdings-diff) membership as the signal picks up the price moves that caused membership, the same mechanism as the Madhavan inflation and the closedTime landmine. Dropping names removed between the list and recon (for example acquired names) is survivorship. Rank Day differs by year: 31 May up to 2015, early or mid May in 2016-2022, 30 April in 2024-2026. Lists are published after the US close, so entry is the next session's close. SEC dei shares become available at filing acceptance plus 1 day, not at the period-end date. The recon-day exit assumes an MOC fill at the official close (the Yahoo close equals the closing auction; feasible on Alpaca). Yahoo daily bars carry observed_at at the open and available_at at +24h; the harness must not shift fills by a day because of that stamp.
rows.missing_data: FTSE Russell preliminary and final R1000/R2000 addition/deletion lists 2013-2026 with publication timestamps (the depth of the lseg.com PDF archive is unverified). Prior-recon R1000 membership (prior final lists, or iShares IWB holdings by asOfDate, depth unverified). Daily prices for every listed migrant, including later-delisted names (Yahoo has survivors; DoltHub or Stooq coverage is unverified). A per-year Rank Day and list-date calendar with source URLs. For the Rank-Day variant only: full-universe SEC dei shares and closes.

final.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2013-2026 (out of CHL's 1996-2012 sample), take the stocks on FTSE Russell's preliminary Russell 2000 additions list that were Russell 1000 members at the prior reconstitution. The statistic is the mean over events, with a t over events and a studentized bootstrap over events (10,000 draws); a stock bootstrap clustered by event must agree. final.procedure: A list's available_at is its publication time (after the US close), so entry is the next session's close by MOC order. Prior membership comes from the previous final list, or IWB holdings dated before Rank Day. Rank-Day variant (2013+ only, a separate trial): rank by total market cap, which is SEC dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding (all classes, latest accepted before Rank Day, available_at = acceptance + 1 day) x the Rank-Day close. December 2026 is a separate forward observation, never pooled with June: list 2026-11-13, entry at the 2026-11-16 close (Rank-Day variant: 2026-11-02), exit at the 2026-12-11 close.

final.controls: Benchmark is IWM. Secondary, Rank-Day variant only: the difference against prior-R1000 band stayers matched on Rank-Day total-cap rank must share the sign. The match is on total cap, not on float-adjusted index weight, because Wei-Young show weight-based ranks carry selection bias. One window, no grid. Ex-post membership is forbidden as a signal. rows.name: Migrant reversal in the 20 sessions after recon
rows.source_notes: Dimensional (opened; 2014-2023): about +2% rebound for upward migrants and -0.95% for downward migrants over the 20 days after recon. Madhavan (FAJ 2003; opened via pdftotext): the R3000 spread was -4.97% in July and negative in 5 of 7 years 1996-2002. For the R2000, 'six of the seven years' returns on the spread portfolio turned negative' in July, and the June R2000 spread was +10.78%. In Madhavan's sample, membership took effect on 1 July. CHL (opened) contradicts: 'no significant reversals' at the 1000 cutoff, 1996-2012. Shankar-Miller's abstract (opened): S&P 600 effects 'are fully reversed within 60 days'.
rows.replication_concerns: Contested: CHL find no July reversal. Dimensional's figures are in-sample for 2014-2023 and gross. The pre-recon moves of the migrants are opposite to the post-recon trade (upward migrants fell 1.1% and downward ones rose 1.2% in the prior 20 days), so a generic one-month short-term reversal can produce the spread without any index mechanism. The original row's controls do not separate the two. T-334's S&P analogue has the right sign (-0.605% net) but is not significant and only 82.6% priced.
rows.data_notes: Only daily-history-IWM and the 901 archived symbols (a survivor list) are available. No final migrant lists, no iShares holdings history and no prices for most migrants. French ST-reversal factor history is not archived; only ff3, ff5, momentum, 49 industries, accruals and net issuance are.
rows.lookahead_risks: The final list is public before recon day, so entering at the recon close is point-in-time. A holdings diff built after the fact is acceptable only because the same membership was published before entry, and it must use holdings dated the session before and the session after recon, so that non-recon corporate-action changes are not mixed in. A recon-close entry assumes an MOC fill at the official close; the next-open variant guards against that. Delisted or acquired names inside the window must be credited at their last close or the deal proceeds. Survivor-only pricing biases both legs.
rows.missing_data: FTSE Russell final migrant lists 2007-2026, or IWB/IWM holdings straddling each recon date. Delisting-aware daily open and close for migrants not in the 901-symbol archive. The French short-term-reversal daily factor (free; to fetch).

It is entered at the recon-day official close and closed at the close 20 NYSE sessions later. It earns a positive mean net spread per event after 15 bp per leg per side and 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg.
final.statistic: Mean over events of the net long-minus-short spread. Studentized bootstrap over events, with a stock bootstrap clustered by event that must agree. Required control: per event, the spread minus the French short-term-reversal factor's return over the same 20 sessions; its mean must also be > 0. Results at +5 and +60 sessions are reported for shape only.
final.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Placebo: the same stocks entered 60 sessions after recon and held 20 sessions. Its CI must cover 0.
final.procedure: Migrants come from the final published list, or IWB/IWM holdings dated the session before and after recon. Only ranking-driven moves count; corporate-action deletions are excluded. Entry at the recon-day Yahoo close (closing auction). Variant: entry at the next session's Yahoo open; it is a separate trial in the 6-trial migrant family. Delisted names exit at their last close or the deal proceeds. Report the share priced: an event with < 90% priced is excluded and reported, and < 90% overall is inconclusive. Halves are 2007-2016 and 2017-2026. A December arm (2026-12-11 close to 20 sessions later, spanning the turn of the year) is registered as a forward record only, never pooled with June.

The original design cannot separate an index unwind from generic short-term reversal, because the migrants' pre-recon moves are opposite to the trade. The fix adds an ST-reversal control, uses the post-Madhavan 2007-2026 sample and keeps the next-open variant in the family.

rows.name: Passive demand in days of volume (benchmarking-intensity change) as a continuous predictor
rows.source_notes: Opened the Pavlova-Sikorskaya 2 April 2021 draft via pdftotext. The sample is 1998-2018 across 34 indices. 'A stock in the top quartile has a 80bps higher return in June relative to an average stock in that year, while a stock in the bottom quartile has a 110bps lower return.' 'the average index effect of 2.3%' implies an elasticity of '-3.03 in 1998-2018'. Opened Chinco-Sammon: 'The typical index addition/deletion sees 9.5x its normal volume', and R2000 additions see '14.2 days' worth' of volume. Wei-Young (opened): weight-based ranking around the cutoff gives selection bias; 'with an unbiased approach, there is no significant discontinuity in institutional ownership'.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2018 replication. P-S themselves note optimized sampling and weaker cutoff incentives after 2007. The out-of-sample window (2019-2026) has about 8 events, and N-PORT AUM is only a lower bound on benchmarked money. The predictor is nested in the binary migrant flag, so it adds nothing unless the binary effect exists first.
rows.data_notes: Nothing needed is archived. There are no ETF shares-outstanding or NAV histories, the same AUM gap that blocks T-658. finra-regsho-cnms covers only about 590-620 symbols per month, so it cannot supply volume for names near rank 1000 or 3000. Membership, float and prices for non-archived names are missing.
rows.lookahead_risks: N-PORT: only the third month of each fiscal quarter is public, about 60 days after quarter end, so AUM at an April-30 Rank Day must come from the latest public filing, not the month-end NAV. SEC EntityPublicFloat is reported once a year on the 10-K cover (as of the prior Q2), so the float proxy is stale and must be taken as of filing acceptance. Predicted weights must use Rank-Day total cap, not later published index weights.
rows.missing_data: N-PORT tracker AUM for IWB, IWM, IWV, VTWO and the Russell Midcap trackers (2019+). The membership engine or FTSE Russell lists. SEC public float. Daily price and volume for every predicted change.

final.claim: Gated secondary, judged only if russell-downward-migrant-runup or russell-upward-migrant-short passes. For the June Russell reconstitutions 2019-2026 (out of P-S's 1998-2018 sample), predicted passive demand in days of volume has a positive mean cross-sectional Spearman IC with the excess return vs IWM from the first close after the preliminary list to the recon close, with t > 2 over events. D_i = sum over b in {R1000, R2000, R3000, Russell Midcap} of AUM_b x (w_new - w_old), divided by the 20-session median dollar volume before Rank Day. D must add IC beyond the binary migrant flag.
final.statistic: Per-event Spearman IC between D_i and the window excess return over all published ranking-driven changes (migrants and 3000-cutoff movers), averaged over events, with a t over events. Also the per-event IC of D_i after removing a direction-signed migrant dummy. The top-minus-bottom tercile portfolio at 15 bp per leg per side is reported.
final.procedure: AUM_b is the summed N-PORT net assets of each benchmark's trackers in the latest public filing accepted before Rank Day; this is a lower bound. Weights = Rank-Day total cap x the SEC public-float ratio (latest accepted before Rank Day), normalised within the predicted index. Changes come from the published preliminary lists, and entry is the first close after publication. Halves are 2019-2022 and 2023-2026. The 2026-10-30 D values are computed and frozen before 2026-11-13 as a forward observation.
final.data: New: N-PORT tracker AUM, FTSE Russell lists, SEC public float (sec-companyfacts after a full-universe fetch), daily price and volume for changed names.
final.pass: Only if the gate opened: mean IC > 0 with t > 2 over events, both halves' mean IC > 0, and the residual IC (beyond the migrant dummy) > 0. Below 7 events, only a decisive negative mean counts (rule 5).
final.controls: One window, no grid. The binary migrant flag is the nested baseline. The gating keeps the family's error rate unchanged when the base effect fails. Costs enter only the reported tercile portfolio.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but this is a continuous refinement of an effect Mandel has not yet shown, it needs the most data in the cluster and it has about 8 out-of-sample events. The fix registers it as a gated secondary on 2019-2026 that must beat the binary flag, so it costs nothing in deflation unless the migrant tests pass.

rows.name: Long-run benchmarking-intensity discount: just-moved-up R2000 stocks beat just-moved-down stocks for 12 months
rows.source_notes: From the P-S 2021 draft (pdftotext): 'In the 1998-2006 sample period, addition to the Russell 2000 results in around 60bps lower return per month in the next five years while deletion from it leads to a 48bps higher return per month. After 2007, ... around 26bps lower ... deletion leads to a 28bps higher return.' Two details the original row misses. Returns are measured as 'an average monthly excess return from September in year t', not from the recon close. Post-2007 the addition effect is 'even insignificant in some specifications' and 'lasts for 24 months only'. The draft also says that after banding, additions to the R1000 sit around rank 800 while R1000 members range up to rank 1300. Wei-Young (opened) show that ranking on Russell's June index weights produces selection bias.
rows.replication_concerns: The effect halves in the paper itself after 2007. The cutoff design is contested (Wei-Young; Appel-Gormley-Keim), and many papers reuse the same natural experiment (Heath et al.). The row's 'within 150 ranks of the cutoff' screen would discard most migrants, because under banding they sit near ranks 800 and 1300. Its 'holdings-weight rank' is exactly the method Wei-Young show is biased. Starting at the recon close double-counts the 20-session reversal trial. Migrants are momentum-sorted by construction, with upward migrants as winners and downward migrants as losers.
rows.data_notes: french-ff5-daily (1963-07-01..2026-08-31) and french-momentum-daily (1926-11..2026-08-31) are archived, which is enough for cohorts formed through August 2025. daily-history-IWM is archived. Migrant lists and delisting-aware 12-month prices are not.
rows.lookahead_risks: The French library is revised monthly, so the archived vintage is not point-in-time (a minor factor-construction look-ahead; state it). Delisting returns are unknown and must not be filled with survivor prices. Weight-based ranks embed float and institutional ownership, the Wei-Young selection bias. Cohort membership must come from published lists dated before formation.
rows.missing_data: Published ranking-driven migrant lists 2019-2025 (FTSE Russell or iShares holdings diffs). 12-month delisting-aware prices and merger proceeds for about 60-80 names a year.

final.claim: For annual cohorts of ranking-driven Russell migrants at the June recons 2019-2025 (out of P-S's 1998-2018 sample), the portfolio is formed at the close of the last trading day of August after each recon (P-S's September start, which also avoids overlap with the 20-session reversal trial). It is equal-weighted, long all names that moved from the Russell 2000 to the Russell 1000 and short all names that moved the other way, and held 12 months. It earns positive calendar-time FF5+UMD alpha after 10 bp per leg per side at formation and exit and 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg.
final.statistic: Monthly calendar-time return of the overlapping annual cohorts (2019-09..2026-08, 84 months), regressed on FF5 + UMD with Newey-West t (lag 12). Also the raw cohort-mean spread, with a bootstrap over cohorts.
final.procedure: Cohorts come from published lists only. There is no rank window, because banded migrants sit near ranks 800 and 1300. Variant (reported): each side against its own band stayers, matched on Rank-Day total-cap rank, never on index weight. Factors are compounded from french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily, using the archived vintage. Delisted names take merger proceeds where found; otherwise a performance delisting takes -30% (stated, with a -50% sensitivity). Halves are calendar months 2019-09..2023-02 and 2023-03..2026-08. Verdict: alpha > 0 with NW t > 2 is supported. A point estimate <= 0 is not_supported. Anything else is inconclusive.
final.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, daily-history-IWM. New: migrant lists, delisting-aware prices and proceeds.
final.pass: Alpha > 0 with NW t > 2, both halves' alphas > 0, >= 90% of names priced, and family DSR > 0.95 in the long-horizon index family (with russell2000-deletions-minus-additions-12m).
final.controls: One horizon (12 months from the end of August), no grid. Costs and borrow as stated. UMD absorbs the momentum sort. The Wei-Young bias is avoided by using lists and total-cap ranks only. The share of delistings is reported.

rows.reason: P-S's figures are verified, but the original design had three faults: a rank screen that excludes banded migrants, weight-based matching (the Wei-Young bias), and a start date that overlaps the reversal test. Only 2019-2025 cohorts are out of sample (84 months), so it is underpowered by construction, with an explicit inconclusive rule.

rows.name: Lower cutoff (rank about 3000): Microcap graduates into the R2000 and R2000 drop-outs
rows.source_notes: Madhavan (opened): R2000 adds-minus-deletes earned 10.78% in June with all 7 Junes positive and 29.04% for March-June. Broker predictions were 90-95% accurate by the end of May, and market cap as of 31 May set membership. CHL (opened) limits its 3000-cutoff analysis to 2005-2012, and the row's t-stats of 1.25-1.45 are consistent with 'not significant'; CHL confirms there is no band at the 3000 cutoff. From the FTSE Russell June 2026 summary (opened): 244 R2000 additions, of which 83 came up from Microcap and 105 from outside the Russell universe (newly eligible on voting rights or nationality, or IPOs). Of 160 departures, 84 went to Microcap and 34 left the universe. The smallest member was $146.4M, with 'no band applied at the bottom of the Russell 2000 Index'.

Costs and closing-auction impact in microcaps dominate. Many additions are not ranking-driven (105 of 244 in 2026 were newly eligible), and 34 departures were corporate exits, so pooling all additions and deletions mixes in non-flow events.

Ranks 2700-3300 are entirely outside the price archive (T-393), so the Rank-Day variant is infeasible and is dropped from the family. No Microcap membership (IWC holdings) is archived.

Microcap closing auctions may not fill at the official close in size.

final.claim: For the June Russell reconstitutions 2013-2026 (out of CHL's 2005-2012 sample at this cutoff), take the stocks FTSE Russell's preliminary list moves from the Russell Microcap into the Russell 2000. Newly eligible companies, IPOs and spin-offs are excluded. An equal-weighted portfolio of them, bought at the first close after publication and sold at the recon-day official close, earns a positive mean net excess return over IWM per event after the larger of 40 bp or the Corwin-Schultz half-spread estimate per leg per side.

Deletion arm (R2000 members the list moves to the Microcap) as a separate trial: shorted where FINRA days-to-cover is below that date's median (borrow 2%/yr), otherwise scored as an avoid-signal against IWM. Holm over the 2 arms.
final.null: Mean net excess <= 0 (additions); >= 0 for the deletion arm's return vs IWM. Placebo: the same names over a same-length window starting 63 sessions after recon. Its CI must cover 0.
final.procedure: Lists are point-in-time by publication timestamp, with entry at the next close. Only list rows whose source (additions) or destination (deletions) is the Russell Microcap count. Names removed before recon stay in, exiting at their last close or the deal proceeds. The Corwin-Schultz estimate comes from the 20 sessions before entry (stated assumption). FINRA rows enter at the first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement. For 2013-2017 deletions, which have no archived FINRA data, the arm is avoid-only. Report the share priced: < 90% is inconclusive. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026.
final.data: finra-short-interest, daily-history-IWM. New: FTSE Russell lists with source/destination, IWC holdings, delisting-aware microcap prices.
final.pass: Addition arm: net mean > 0 with a one-sided event-level 95% lower bound > 0, both halves > 0, the placebo CI covering 0, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 over 2 arms, and >= 500 stock-events.

The fix restricts the test to Microcap movers on the out-of-sample 2013-2026 window, with spread-calibrated costs.

rows.name: R2000 deletions beat additions over the next year (index-turnover drag)
rows.source_notes: Cai-Houge (FAJ 2008) abstract, opened via RePEc: 'A buy-and-hold index portfolio outperformed the annually rebalanced index in the 1979-2004 period by an average of 2.22 percent over one year and 17.29 percent over five years'. 'index deletions were found to provide significantly higher factor-adjusted returns than index additions'. 'The strongest performing funds enhanced their factor-adjusted returns by an average of 1.45 percent per year'. The Petajisto 38-77 bp figure was not opened (it is also cited in Mandel's underlying library).
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2004 replication was found. Greenwood-Sammon (opened) show S&P 500 deletion effects falling to insignificant by the late 2010s, which leaves less depression to recover. The deletion arm sits where free data are worst: delisted microcaps. The short-addition arm carries IPO and small-growth exposures, which FF5 only partly absorbs.
rows.data_notes: french-ff5-daily and french-momentum-daily run to 2026-08-31, enough for cohorts formed through June 2025 held 12 months (to June 2026). daily-history-IWM is archived. Lists and delisting-aware 12-month microcap prices and proceeds are not.
rows.lookahead_risks: Cohorts must come from lists published before formation. Corporate-action deletions (pending acquisition) carry deal returns and are excluded. Delisting returns must be explicit assumptions, not survivor prices. The French factor vintage is revised (stated).
rows.missing_data: Published R2000 addition and deletion lists 2005-2025 with source/destination and IPO flags. 12-month delisting-aware prices and delisting proceeds for microcaps; CRSP equivalents are not free, and DoltHub/Stooq coverage is unverified.

final.claim: For annual cohorts formed at each June recon close 2005-2025 (out of Cai-Houge's 1979-2004 sample), an equal-weighted buy-and-hold portfolio is held 12 months. It is long Russell 2000 deletions that moved to the Russell Microcap or left the Russell 3000E on rank or eligibility (pending acquisitions excluded), and short Russell 2000 additions that came from the Microcap or from outside the index and are neither migrants, IPOs nor spin-offs. It earns positive calendar-time FF5+UMD alpha after 40 bp per leg per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg.
final.statistic: Monthly calendar-time alpha on FF5 + UMD (Newey-West, lag 12), plus the cohort-mean 12-month spread with a bootstrap over cohorts.
final.procedure: Published lists only. Equal-weighted at formation, buy-and-hold. Delisting proceeds are credited where found. Otherwise a performance delisting takes -30% and a merger takes its last close (stated, with a -50% sensitivity). Report the share of names priced: < 80% is inconclusive. Halves are cohorts 2005-2014 and 2015-2025.
final.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, daily-history-IWM. New: lists, delisting-aware prices and proceeds.
final.pass: Alpha > 0 with NW t > 2, both halves' alphas > 0, family DSR > 0.95 (long-horizon index family with russell-migrant-bmi-12m-spread), and >= 80% of names priced.
final.controls: One horizon, no grid. Costs and borrow as stated. IPOs and spin-offs are excluded. UMD absorbs momentum. Pending-acquisition deletions are excluded. The delisting share and the sensitivity are reported.

rows.reason: The abstract is verified, but the effect is unreplicated since 2004 and depends on delisted-microcap data Mandel lacks. The fix keeps it registered on the out-of-sample 2005-2025 cohorts with explicit delisting rules and excludes corporate-action deletions. Keep it parked behind the list build.

rows.name: Short interest and short volume condition the recon effect
rows.source_notes: The Akhigbe-Martin-Newman-de Souza abstract (QREF 84, DOI 10.1016/j.qref.2020.10.009; RePEc dates it 2022, the author page 2020) gives no sample or magnitudes. It reports an 'inverse relationship in the reconstitution period' for additions and a direct one after. The co-author summary page found by search says this is about short interest RISING during the window going with lower returns, i.e. a contemporaneous co-movement of short-interest changes and returns. It is not a pre-window days-to-cover level predicting later returns. The candidate's registration claims the opposite sign (a positive slope for additions pre-recon) on a different variable, so the source does not support the claim as registered.
rows.replication_concerns: Single study with no magnitudes and an unclear variable definition. It reports contemporaneous co-movement, which is not tradable, because short interest within the window is published about 8 business days after each settlement. Ahn-Patatoukas finds effects only in hard-to-borrow microcaps. About 9 events. It conditions on base effects Mandel has not shown.
rows.data_notes: finra-short-interest covers the full universe from 2017-12. finra-regsho-cnms covers only about 590-620 symbols per month, so the RegSHO secondary cannot be computed for Russell changes. No change lists or prices for the changed names.
rows.lookahead_risks: Using within-window short-interest changes, which the paper's relation needs, is look-ahead, because FINRA publishes with about an 8-business-day lag. Any predictive version must use pre-entry days-to-cover only.
rows.missing_data: Change lists and prices for the changed names (shared with the migrant and cutoff tests). Full-universe RegSHO short volume (only about 600 symbols are archived).

final.claim: Not registered. Revive only if russell-downward-migrant-runup, russell-upward-migrant-short or russell-3000-cutoff-microcap-movers passes and the paper's variable definitions have been read. The claim would be: for Russell 2000 additions at the June recons 2018-2026, the within-event slope of excess return vs IWM (first close after the preliminary list to the recon close) on pre-entry FINRA days-to-cover is negative, averaged over events with t > 2.
final.statistic: Fama-MacBeth: per-event OLS slope of excess return on z-scored pre-entry days-to-cover, controlling for log market cap and the 20-session prior return. Mean over events with a t over events.
final.procedure: Days-to-cover is the latest FINRA row published (first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement) before entry. Within-window short-interest changes are never used as predictors. Published lists only.
final.data: finra-short-interest. New: change lists, prices.
final.pass: Mean slope < 0 with t < -2 over >= 8 events.
final.controls: One signal, no grid. Size and prior-return controls. Gated behind a passing base test.

rows.reason: Dropped: the cited study shows contemporaneous co-movement of short-interest changes and returns, which is not a pre-entry predictor, and the candidate registered the opposite sign. The study is a single paper with no magnitudes, the RegSHO bundle covers only about 600 symbols, and about 9 events cannot settle it.

rows.name: Recon-day closing-auction pressure and overnight reversal
rows.source_notes: LSEG key-facts (opened): on 27 June 2025, 'a record $102.5bn was traded on the Nasdaq and $114.7bn on the NYSE', with 2.5bn shares in the Nasdaq closing cross. The row's $219.6bn total is not in the article; the two figures sum to $217.2bn. The same article says recon's short-term price impact 'hasn't reliably followed such a pattern'. Chinco-Sammon (opened, Figure 10): recon-day abnormal returns to additions and deletions 'steadily converged to nearly zero' over 2000-2021, explained by prearranged upstairs trades at the close. Bogousslavsky-Muravyev's 3.1% to 7.5% auction share is confirmed via search. The 8.1 bp deviation and its overnight reversion were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Chinco-Sammon measure near-zero recon-day pressure, so there is little closing overshoot to revert. Mandel's T-428 found no overnight reversal of liquid closing pressure. The generic closing-auction-deviation reversal is already registered as T-664. The IWM-only arm has no signed mechanism, because the net index imbalance at the recon close is ambiguous in sign.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IWM and hourly-IWM (2023-11..2026-10, only 3 recons) are archived. Stock-level lists and the opens and closes of listed names are not. No auction imbalance history is archived (NOII and NYSE imbalance feeds are paid).
rows.lookahead_risks: Yahoo's first-print open is not the opening auction price for every name. MOC fills are assumed at the official close. Survivorship of delisted additions and deletions.
rows.missing_data: Published addition, deletion and migrant lists 2005-2026, and the listed names' official close and next open.

final.claim: Not registered as its own trial. The migrant version is the next-open entry variant inside russell-migrant-post-recon-reversal (close entry vs next-open entry gives the overnight leg). The generic mechanism is T-664 (closing-auction deviation vs next close-to-open). If revived: for the June recons 2013-2026, published Russell 2000 deletions minus additions (each vs IWM's own close-to-open) earn a positive close-to-next-open spread net of 5-15 bp per leg per side.
final.statistic: Mean over events of the equal-weighted deletion-minus-addition close-to-open spread net of costs, with an event bootstrap.
final.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Placebo: the same names on the four preceding Fridays.
final.procedure: Published lists. Yahoo official close and next open. Fills are assumed at the official close. Survivorship reported, with < 90% priced inconclusive. The pre-registered expectation is a null.
final.data: daily-history-IWM. New: lists and the names' daily open and close.
final.pass: Net spread > 0 with a one-sided 95% lower bound > 0 in both halves, and the placebo CI covering 0.
final.controls: One overnight window, size-tiered costs, the same-weekday IWM baseline (T-549 drift).

rows.reason: Dropped: the mechanism is measured as near zero (Chinco-Sammon) and Mandel's own T-428 failed. The generic auction-reversal claim is already T-664, and the migrant overnight leg is nested in the reversal test's next-open variant. Another trial would only add deflation.

rows.name: Russell 2000 vs S&P 600 (IWM vs IJR) around the recon windows
rows.source_notes: The S&P DJI Indexology posts (2015 'A Tale of Two Benchmarks: Reconstitution Effect' and 2020 'Recalled to Life') returned 403 to WebFetch, curl and the archive. Two independent search-index summaries of the posts agree: '+0.68% for the month of July vs. the Russell 2000, with a statistically significant t-stat of 2.54', 1994-2014. The 2020 update gives 0.64% in July (t 2.92), with the S&P 600 ahead in 19 of 27 Julys, attributed to Russell additions mean-reverting after entry. The mechanism is independently verified in opened sources: Madhavan's July reversal (R2000 spread negative in 6 of 7 Julys 1996-2002) and Dimensional's post-recon reversals 2014-2023. T-385 is confirmed in the registry: +0.22%/yr unconditional, +0.32%/yr with June excluded, family DSR 0.001 over 34 trials.
rows.replication_concerns: A commercial claim from a competing index provider, measured on calendar July (which starts 1-6 sessions after recon) and in-sample for 1993-2019, which overlaps most of the test period. Only 2015-2026 (12 events) is out of sample relative to the first publication. Index effects decay (Greenwood-Sammon, Chinco-Sammon), and Mandel's small-cap calendar spreads have failed through second-half decay (T-351, T-444). The S&P 600 profitability screen loads RMW (T-385: +0.18, t 4.7), so earnings-season months could carry a quality drift. The null must be drawn from the same year's other earnings months. Pre-2004 Russell recon dates differ from the fourth-Friday rule: in Madhavan's sample membership 'takes effect 1 July'.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IJR and daily-history-IWM are archived, 6,635 rows each, 2000-05-26..2026-10-14, with adjclose. daily-history--RUT runs 1987-09-10..2026-10-14 for a cross-check. All 27 June recons from 2000 to 2026 have a complete +20-session window. The recon-date list must be compiled. For 2004-2026 the rule is the fourth Friday of June, identical to 'the last Friday unless it is the 29th or 30th', and Chinco-Sammon say the same. 2000-2003 dates must be sourced, because recon was effective 1 July then.
rows.lookahead_risks: The recon calendar is announced months ahead, so it is point-in-time; but the date list must come from FTSE Russell's published schedule, never from looking for the volume spike in the data. The permutation null must exclude windows that overlap any recon pre-window (recon-20..recon+20 sessions) and the S&P quarterly rebalance weeks (third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec +/-5 sessions). Otherwise null draws starting in late May or late February carry the pre-recon or rebalance effect and bias p downward. Closes as fills assume MOC at the official close, which is fine for both ETFs. The Yahoo daily stamp (available_at = bar + 24h) must not shift entries by a day. Do not compute the spread before registration: the June/July returns have not been looked at, and must not be.
rows.missing_data: Only the June recon-date list with source URLs: FTSE Russell press releases, with 2000-2003 dates from contemporaneous Russell notices. A year whose date cannot be sourced is excluded and reported.

final.claim: Over the June Russell reconstitutions 2000-2026 (FTSE Russell's published recon dates), a dollar-neutral long IJR / short IWM position is entered at the recon-day close and closed at the close 20 NYSE sessions later. It earns a positive mean net return per event after 5 bp per leg per side (20 bp round trip) and 0.3%/yr IWM borrow pro rata. The one-sided within-year permutation p must be < 0.05, and both the pre-publication half (2000-2014) and the post-publication half (2015-2026, after S&P DJI's March 2015 post) must have a positive net mean.
final.statistic: Per event: (IJR adjclose[recon+20]/IJR adjclose[recon] - 1) - (IWM adjclose[recon+20]/IWM adjclose[recon] - 1) - 0.0020 - 0.003 x 20/252. The statistic is the mean over events. Inference: a one-sided within-year permutation p-value, plus a studentized bootstrap 95% CI over events. Descriptive only, not part of the verdict: recon-20 to recon (expected < 0) and the calendar July spread.
final.null: Mean net spread <= 0. Permutation: each draw takes, for every event year, one 20-session window starting at a uniformly random session whose whole span avoids recon-20..recon+20 sessions, the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec +/-5 sessions, and any session after 2026-10-14. 10,000 draws; p is the share of draw means >= the observed mean.
final.procedure: One sourced recon date per year (fourth Friday of June from 2004; sourced dates for 2000-2003, unsourceable years excluded). Entry and exit at Yahoo closes (the official closing auctions). Adjclose makes the short leg pay dividends. Placebo: the identical rule anchored on the last Friday of January, April and October of each year; the pooled placebo mean's 95% CI must include 0. The December 2026 recon (2026-12-11) is a separate forward arm, never pooled. The trial joins T-385's IJR-IWM family and its DSR is reported. It shares the recon-date file with rvx-vrp-russell-recon-window.
final.data: daily-history-IJR, daily-history-IWM (2000-05-26..2026-10-14), daily-history--RUT (cross-check), FTSE Russell June recon-date list
final.pass: Primary-window net mean > 0 with one-sided permutation p < 0.05, both halves' net means > 0 (2000-2014 and 2015-2026), and the placebo CI covering 0.
final.controls: One window (20 sessions), no grid, no thresholds; costs and borrow charged. The same-year permutation absorbs T-385's unconditional drift and earnings-season quality drift. Null windows exclude the recon pre-window and the S&P rebalance weeks. The post-2015 half is the out-of-sample check on the published claim. The July 4 pre-holiday session affects both legs.

rows.reason: The only migrant-free, testable-now claim in the cluster, and cheap. The fix restricts the null windows to remove a bias from overlapping recon and rebalance periods, requires the post-publication 2015-2026 half to be positive, sources the pre-2004 dates, and removes the 'Holm over 3, not deciding' contradiction. The S&P figures could only be confirmed through search summaries, so source_verified is false, although Madhavan and Dimensional independently verify the mechanism.

rows.name: Nasdaq-100 December reconstitution: predicted additions and deletions
rows.source_notes: QuanterLab (opened): 18 December windows 2007-2024, each held one year, buy-and-hold equal weight, 10 bp costs. Deletions beat QQQ by 18.7 points a window before 2016 and trailed by 16.3 after; the verdict is 'a large early effect faded to roughly a coin flip'. QuanterLab did NOT test the candidate's windows (ranking to effective, or effective to +20 sessions). Biktimirov-Xu abstract (opened): first-time additions 'experience permanent price gains', repeat additions and new deletions show 'temporary stock price changes'; no sample or magnitudes. 2026 rules (Nasdaq FAQ via search, the 'May' FAQ URL gives 404): fast entry for large IPOs effective 1 May 2026; the 10 bp rule is replaced by quarterly reviews removing names ranked outside the top 125; ranking uses total (listed + unlisted) shares; modified cap is capped at 3x float from the 22 June review.
rows.replication_concerns: There is no quantitative source for either proposed window; QuanterLab's decay finding concerns one-year holds. Nasdaq-100 changes are heavily anticipated by large desks. The 2026 rule changes (total shares, top-125 quarterly removals) make pre-2026 history only partly representative. The December effective date coincides with quad witching and the S&P quarterly rebalance.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-QQQ (1999-03-10..2026-10-14) is archived. Many Nasdaq-100 names are in the 901-symbol daily archive, but that list is today's universe, so deleted and acquired names are often missing. sec-companyfacts is a subset; dei cover data are missing for foreign filers (ADRs are frequent in NDX). There is no change list with announcement timestamps; wikipedia-sp500-changes covers only the S&P 500.
rows.lookahead_risks: Predictions must use Oct-last-session closes and shares accepted before the ranking date. Using Nasdaq's announced list as the 'prediction' for arm A is look-ahead. First-time vs repeat status must come from change history dated before the event. Deletion prices drawn from today's survivor archive bias arm B upward. The 2026 total-shares rule must not be back-applied to earlier years.
rows.missing_data: Nasdaq-100 annual change lists 2007-2025 with announcement timestamps and effective dates (Nasdaq/GlobeNewswire releases; Wikipedia yearly sections). Prices for non-archived and delisted deletions. Market caps for foreign filers. The membership history to tag first-time additions.

final.claim: For the Nasdaq-100 annual December reconstitutions, with the verdict on 2016-2025 (2007-2015 reported), two arms are tested. (A) Predicted first-time additions are bought at the first close after the ranking date (last trading day of October) and sold at the effective-date close (after the third Friday of December). Predictions apply Nasdaq's eligibility and the top-100 / 101-125-retention rule in force that year to Oct-last-session market caps (shares accepted before the ranking date x close). (B) Actual deletions are bought at the effective-date close and held 20 sessions. Each arm earns a positive mean net excess return over QQQ after 10 bp per leg per side.
final.statistic: Event-clustered mean net excess return vs QQQ per arm, with a studentized bootstrap over December events and a stock bootstrap clustered by event that must agree. Holm over the 2 arms.
final.null: Mean net excess <= 0. Placebo: the same names over same-length windows in the following March-April. Its CI must cover 0.
final.procedure: Arm A predictions are frozen from information dated on or before the ranking date, and accuracy against the announced list is reported. Unpredicted actual additions are excluded and mispredictions are kept. Arm B uses the announcement (available_at = press-release timestamp) and enters only at the effective close. Exits at Yahoo closes. Survivorship is reported: < 90% priced is inconclusive. First-time vs repeat additions are reported separately. December 2026 (ranking 2026-10-30, effective after 2026-12-18) is a forward observation under the 2026 rules, never pooled.
final.data: daily-history-QQQ, archived daily-history names. New: Nasdaq-100 change lists with timestamps, non-archived and delisted prices, foreign-filer caps.
final.pass: For at least one arm in 2016-2025: a one-sided event-clustered 95% lower bound > 0 after Holm over 2, with the placebo CI covering 0, and >= 30 stock-events in that arm.
final.controls: One window per arm, no grid. 10 bp per leg per side. Equal-weight QQQE is a secondary benchmark where available. The 2026 regime change is a stated limitation, with no pooling across regimes. The quad-witching and S&P-rebalance overlap affects the QQQ benchmark too.

rows.reason: The sources are verified, but none quantifies the proposed windows; QuanterLab's 'died around 2016' is about one-year holds, and the 2026 rule changes reduce the history's relevance. The fix freezes predictions at the ranking date, forbids using the announced list in arm A, and puts the verdict on the 2016-2025 half. Low prior.

rows.name: S&P MidCap 400 / SmallCap 600 changes: direct entrants vs migrations, with 60-day reversal
rows.source_notes: Shankar-Miller abstract (opened): 'Firms that newly enter (exit) the S&P universe experience a larger price increase (decrease) than firms that move between S&P indexes', and 'the price and volume effects are temporary and are fully reversed within 60 days'. Greenwood-Sammon (NBER w30748, December 2022; opened via pdftotext): migrations rose 'from about 40% of additions to over 80%'. 'In the mid-1990s, migration and non-migration additions had average returns of 6.7% and 6.4%... By the late 2010s, however, direct additions had returns of 2.2%, while migrations had returns of -2.3%.' These figures concern S&P 500 additions, not 400 or 600 changes. G-S do not themselves measure other index families; they cite Chinco-Sammon for the Russell decline, so the row's 'similar decline in other index families' overstates them. Mandel's A12 note quotes a different version (+5.4% / +1.8%). The NBER WP figures quoted in the candidate are correct for that version.
rows.replication_concerns: The S&P 400/600 effect has not been measured since Shankar-Miller. T-334 found +0.00% announcement-to-effective run-up for S&P 500 additions on 210 events. Spin-off additions and additions caused by M&A have no tradable pre-addition window, and the original design did not exclude them. Testing 2 arms x 2 indices x direct/migration (8 trials) dilutes power.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IJH (2000-05-26..2026-10-14), daily-history-IJR (same span) and daily-history-MDY (1995-05-04..) are archived. wikipedia-sp500-changes (412 rows, with announcement refs) can flag 400-to-500 moves only. There is no 400/600 change list with announcement timestamps; spglobal.com blocks plain fetches (T-213 note). Small and mid-cap prices outside the archive are missing.
rows.lookahead_risks: The press-release timestamp (usually after 17:15 ET) is available_at, so entry is at the next close. Using Wikipedia effective dates as entry dates is look-ahead for the announcement arm. Deleted names missing from Yahoo bias the reversal arm. Spin-offs enter the index before they trade regular-way.
rows.missing_data: S&P 400 and 600 change lists 2010-2026 with announcement timestamps and effective dates (S&P DJI releases via PR Newswire mirrors). Direct-vs-migration tags across the S&P 1500. Delisting-aware prices.

final.claim: For direct additions to the S&P MidCap 400 and SmallCap 600 announced 2010-2026 (entrants from outside the S&P 1500; spin-offs and additions caused by M&A share issuance excluded), pooled with each index's own ETF as benchmark (IJH for the 400, IJR for the 600), two arms are tested. Arm 1: the mean net abnormal return from the first close after the S&P DJI announcement to the effective-date close is positive. Arm 2: the mean net abnormal return from the effective-date close to +60 sessions is negative. Costs are 15 bp per leg per side for the 400 and 30 bp for the 600. Holm over the 2 arms.
final.statistic: Mean net abnormal return per arm, with a bootstrap over events clustered by effective date. Migrations (400 to/from 500 or 600) and per-index splits are reported, not judged.
final.null: Arm 1 mean <= 0; arm 2 mean >= 0. Placebo: the same stocks over equal-length windows 120-250 sessions after inclusion. Its CI must cover 0.
final.procedure: available_at is the press-release timestamp, with entry at the next close. Effective dates come from the release. Direct/migration tags are fixed from the S&P 1500 change lists before any return is computed. Reuse T-334's harness and survivorship accounting: report the share priced, with < 90% inconclusive. Halves are 2010-2017 and 2018-2026.
final.data: daily-history-IJH, daily-history-IJR, daily-history-MDY, wikipedia-sp500-changes. New: 400/600 change lists with announcement timestamps, delisting-aware prices.
final.pass: Each arm's 95% bound excludes zero in the predicted direction after Holm over 2, both halves share the sign, and the placebo CI covers 0.
final.controls: One window per arm, no grid. Index-specific costs. Spin-off and M&A additions are excluded. The migration split is fixed before measurement. The build also supplies announcement dates for T-340 and T-453.

rows.reason: The sources are verified, but the original 8-trial grid and the inclusion of spin-off and M&A additions would dilute or contaminate the test. The fix keeps the cleaner direct-addition case on the out-of-sample 2010-2026 window with Holm over 2. Building the timestamped list also unblocks T-340 and T-453.

rows.name: Membership-driven shifts in realised volatility, turnover and index beta for migrants (options angle)
rows.source_notes: NBER Digest of Ben-David, Franzoni and Moussawi (opened): 'A one-standard-deviation increase in ETF ownership raises daily volatility and turnover by about 16 percent', 2000-2012, identified from Russell 1000/2000 switchers. 'The price impact of ETF arbitrage appears to decay after a few days.' The CHL full text has a correlation section: deletion correlation effects are larger than addition effects, and correlation with the R2000 is significantly higher in August and September for just-added stocks. Wei-Young (opened) is the methods critique: ranking on Russell's June index weights produces selection bias.
rows.replication_concerns: Not tested since 2012. The original matched stayers on holdings-weight rank, the Wei-Young bias. Migrants' cap changes and past returns mechanically shift volatility through the size and leverage effects, so the difference-in-differences needs return and cap-change covariates. This is not a return edge; it only feeds variance forecasting and an IV-lag test that can only run forward.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IWM and daily-history-SPY (1993+) are archived. sec-companyfacts is a subset with dei only from about 2011, which bounds the turnover denominator to 2012+. options-chain-IWM exists only for 2026-10-14/15, so the options leg is forward-only. No migrant lists or stayer prices.
rows.lookahead_risks: Shares outstanding must be the latest dei value accepted before each day. Stayers must be chosen on Rank-Day total-cap rank from information dated by Rank Day, not on later index weights. The post window must start after recon so the pressure window is excluded. Forward IV must be recorded at the preliminary list, before any realised outcome.
rows.missing_data: Published migrant lists (FTSE Russell or iShares holdings). A Rank-Day total-cap ranking for matched stayers (SEC dei after a full-universe fetch, plus closes). Daily OHLCV for migrants and stayers outside the archive. Single-stock chains for the December 2026 predicted migrants on the capture box.

final.claim: For ranking-driven Russell 1000/2000 migrants at the June recons 2013-2026 (out of BFM's 2000-2012 sample), compared against band stayers on the same side matched 1:1 on Rank-Day total-market-cap rank, two difference-in-differences are tested from the 60 sessions ending at Rank Day to the 60 sessions starting the session after recon. Log 21-day realised volatility and log share turnover rise for downward migrants and fall for upward migrants. Each needs event-clustered t > 2, with both halves agreeing in sign.
final.statistic: Difference-in-differences of migrants vs matched stayers for log mean 21-day RV and log turnover, with covariates for the trailing 12-month return and the log total-cap change between consecutive Rank Days. Standard errors are clustered by event. Beta to IWM controlling for SPY (60-session regression) is reported in the same Holm family of 6 (3 outcomes x 2 directions).
final.null: DiD = 0 for each outcome and direction.
final.procedure: Turnover = Yahoo volume / SEC dei shares (latest accepted before each day). Stayers are R1000 members inside the lower band and R2000 members inside the upper band, matched on Rank-Day total-cap rank (never on index weight). The pre-window is the 60 sessions ending at Rank Day; the post-window is the 60 sessions starting the session after recon. Halves are 2013-2019 and 2020-2026. Options leg, descriptive and forward-only: for the December 2026 predicted migrants and stayers, record 30-day ATM IV at 2026-11-16 and realised vol over the 30 sessions after 2026-12-11; no verdict until >= 3 events.
final.data: daily-history-IWM, daily-history-SPY, sec-companyfacts and sec-submissions (after a full-universe fetch). New: lists, migrant and stayer prices, chain captures.
final.pass: Realised vol and turnover DiD > 0 for downward migrants and < 0 for upward migrants, each with event-clustered |t| > 2 after Holm over 6, both halves of the same sign, and >= 250 migrant-events per direction.
final.controls: Fixed windows, no grid. Matched stayers absorb market-wide changes; the covariates absorb the size and leverage effects. The Wei-Young bias is avoided by matching on total cap. The pressure window is excluded.

rows.reason: A high-prior structural fact with a verified source, but the original's weight-based matching reproduces the Wei-Young selection bias, and it ignored mechanical size and leverage effects on volatility. The fix matches on Rank-Day total cap, adds covariates and uses the out-of-sample 2013-2026 window. It shares the list build with the reversal test.

rows.name: Russell quarterly IPO additions
rows.source_notes: Micheli-Neuman abstract (arXiv 2006.07456, opened): 1989-2019, 'index portfolios following the Russell 3000 index and rebalanced on an annual basis are overall more crowded than those following the index on a quarterly basis', and 'transaction costs of indexing strategies could be significantly reduced by buying new IPOs additions in proximity to quarterly rebalance dates'. It states no return effect for quarterly IPO additions. If anything it implies less pressure at quarterly adds, the opposite of arm 1's premise. The other cited source (Lapalme-Jelusic) is known only from a search summary. No source supports the claimed pressure and reversal with magnitudes.
rows.replication_concerns: No study with magnitudes exists. IPO long-run underperformance and lockup expiries confound both arms. Each quarterly event is small, and IPO price histories carry their own survivorship (acquired IPOs vanish from Yahoo).
rows.data_notes: sec-submissions (S-1/424B filing dates) exists for a subset of CIKs. No FTSE Russell quarterly IPO lists are archived and no IPO-era prices for non-archived names. T-523 is blocked on the same corporate-event calendar.
rows.lookahead_risks: A lockup date taken from the default 180 days is an assumption. IPO lists need publication timestamps. Survivor-only IPO prices.
rows.missing_data: FTSE Russell quarterly IPO addition lists with publication dates (2015-2026), IPO prices including acquired names, and lockup terms.

final.claim: Not registered. If revived with a source that states a magnitude: for Russell quarterly IPO additions 2019-2026, an equal-weighted portfolio bought at the first close after the IPO list's publication and sold at the effective-date close earns a positive mean net excess return over IWM after 30 bp per leg per side.
final.statistic: Event-clustered mean net excess return vs IWM.
final.null: Mean <= 0. Placebo: the same names 60 sessions later.
final.procedure: available_at = list publication. Names within 10 sessions of the estimated lockup expiry (424B4 acceptance + 180 days) are reported separately. Survivorship is reported, with < 90% priced inconclusive.
final.data: sec-submissions. New: FTSE Russell IPO lists, IPO prices.
final.pass: One-sided 95% lower bound > 0 over 2019-2026 with the placebo CI covering 0.
final.controls: One window, no grid, 30 bp per leg per side, lockup proximity split out.

rows.reason: Dropped: the only cited study does not claim a tradable pressure or reversal for quarterly IPO additions; it implies they are less crowded than annual ones. No source quantifies the effect, and the data (IPO lists, lockups, IPO-era prices) are blocked like T-523.

rows.name: First December recon x year-end flows (forward-only)
rows.source_notes: FTSE Russell's December 2026 press release (opened) confirms Rank Day Friday 30 October, preliminary additions and deletions after the US close on Friday 13 November, lockdown from 30 November, and changes effective after the close on Friday 11 December, trading from Monday 14 December. It is 'the first December reconstitution in over 30 years'. New style probabilities apply to additions, including IPOs, and to R1000/R2000 movers; stayers keep their June 2026 style. The November 2025 parallel-run claims were not opened. Mandel's T-351 and T-444 are confirmed not_supported (Russell minus S&P over the turn of the year +0.87 pp, halves +1.91 / -0.13; IWM-SPY +0.09 pp).
rows.replication_concerns: No evidence that the effect exists. The January rebound literature has decayed in Mandel's own tests (T-351, T-440, T-444). A single event a year means no verdict before about 2031. The December 2026 windows also contain the 2026-12-18 Nasdaq-100 effective date, quad witching, the S&P quarterly rebalance and a mid-December FOMC.
rows.data_notes: daily-history-IWM, finra-short-interest (to 2026-09-30) and sec-companyfacts are archived. The December list and forward prices do not exist yet. Every name is listed at Rank Day, so survivorship does not arise at formation.
rows.lookahead_risks: The recording rule (tercile split, windows, list source) must be frozen before 2026-10-30. YTD returns use closes through the Rank Day close. FINRA days-to-cover is attached at its publication date. The forward record must log names that later delist instead of dropping them.
rows.missing_data: The December 2026 preliminary list (2026-11-13) and forward daily prices through about 2027-01-15.

final.claim: Forward record, report-only; no verdict before 5 December recons. It serves as the December arm of the migrant family (russell-downward-migrant-runup, russell-migrant-post-recon-reversal) and of russell-3000-cutoff-microcap-movers. From December 2026, the preliminary-list downward migrants and the Russell 2000 deletions to the Microcap are split by Rank-Day year-to-date return; the bottom tercile within each group is flagged as tax-loss candidates. Excess returns vs IWM are logged over three windows: (a) first close after the list to the recon close, (b) recon close to the last December close, (c) last December close to the 10th January session close. Candidates are compared with non-candidates and with the June cohort's same-length windows.
final.statistic: Per-window mean excess return vs IWM by group (candidates vs the rest), logged per event. No inference until 5 December events.
final.null: No difference between tax-loss candidates and the rest, and no difference from June's windows.
final.procedure: The rule is frozen before 2026-10-30: YTD = the 2026-10-30 close / the 2025-12-31 close - 1, with terciles cut within each group at Rank Day. Lists come from the 2026-11-13 publication; entry is at the 2026-11-16 close. Names delisting inside a window exit at their last close and stay logged. FINRA days-to-cover is attached at publication (first close after the end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement). Overlaps are flagged per name: Nasdaq-100 changes effective 2026-12-18, quad witching and the S&P rebalance on 2026-12-18, FOMC. December pre-holiday sessions are netted through IWM.
final.data: daily-history-IWM, sec-companyfacts, finra-short-interest. Forward: the FTSE Russell December list, forward daily prices.
final.pass: None until >= 5 December events. Then it graduates to a newly ledgered trial using the June migrant and reversal pass rules (net mean > 0, one-sided 95% lower bound > 0, both halves positive).
final.controls: Three fixed windows, one tercile split, no grid. Never pooled with June. Overlapping December events are flagged per name.

rows.reason: A time-critical, cheap, verified forward record with a very low prior (T-351, T-444). The fix fixes the YTD rule before Rank Day, makes it the single December arm shared by the migrant and cutoff registrations so December is not registered twice, and keeps delisting names in the log.

rows.name: RUT/IWM implied-vol premium in recon windows (RVX vs realised)
rows.source_notes: Cboe Insights (opened; Rick Rosenthal, 3 June 2022): 'Since 2015, RVX is generally lower during Russell Reconstitution (May - June) compared to the annual RVX average', 'with the exceptions of 2019 and 2020'. RVX minus RUT 30-day historical volatility averaged about '3.65%' (stated in percent, not points) over 'the past seven years'. The RUT put/call ratio was 1.71 during recon vs a 1.84 average. The article gives no statistics or strategy returns, and it is educational marketing ('potential opportunities' for option writing). T-65 is confirmed not_supported (implied 24.9 vs realised 22.2, p 0.0945). T-216 is confirmed supported (opex-Friday short straddle +9.14 bp, CI +1.81..+16.31).
rows.replication_concerns: The source makes a level statement about RVX, not about the implied-minus-realised gap, so the conditional-VRP claim is new rather than a replication. The mechanism's sign is ambiguous, and a two-sided test with 'report the sign either way' is a fishing design. With only 17 treated years, single June shocks dominate: the Brexit result arrived on 2016-06-24, the recon day itself, and June 2020 is another. June recon windows almost always contain June quad witching and the June FOMC, so the untreated same-year baseline is confounded.
rows.data_notes: cboe-RVX-history: 4,291 rows, 2009-09-16..2026-10-14, close stamped 21:15 UTC and available at 21:30 UTC. daily-history-IWM covers 2000-05-26..2026-10-14 with adjclose. The 2010-2026 June recons (17) all have complete 21-session windows. The recon dates need compiling (fourth Friday of June) and are shared with ijr-minus-iwm-post-russell-recon.
rows.lookahead_risks: RVX closes at 16:15 ET, 15 minutes after IWM's close, a small look-ahead if read as a tradable entry IV; state it. The window t+1..t+21 excludes day t's return. The treatment uses the published recon calendar, never data-detected dates. Treated entry days overlap heavily (the same realised window), so inference must be per year, not per day.
rows.missing_data: Only the 2010-2026 June recon-date list with source URLs.

final.claim: Over 2010-2026, define the 21-session variance gap g_t = (RVX_t/100)^2 - (252/21) x the sum of squared IWM daily log returns over sessions t+1..t+21. It is larger on entry days whose window contains that year's June Russell recon day than on the same year's other entry days whose window contains no recon day, i.e. vol sellers earn more in recon windows. The test is one-sided: mean over years of d_y > 0.
final.statistic: d_y = mean g over treated entry days in year y minus mean g over that year's untreated entry days. The statistic is the mean of d_y over the 17 years, with a studentized bootstrap over years (10,000 draws). Required secondary contrast: treated days minus untreated days of the same year whose window contains the third Friday of March, September or December (quad witching, and in practice the quarter's FOMC) and no recon. Its mean must also be > 0. Alternative inference: a circular block bootstrap with 42-day blocks of the daily treated-minus-untreated contrast must agree (rule 11).
final.procedure: Use RVX daily closes and IWM adjclose log returns. Every trading day is an entry, with no grid phase (rule 10); windows ending after 2026-10-14 are dropped. Treated = the window contains the sourced June recon date (fourth Friday of June). Untreated = the same year's entry days whose window contains no recon date. Halves are 2010-2017 and 2018-2026. A leave-one-year-out range is reported (2016 Brexit, 2020). This is a statistic, not a trade: no costs, and any straddle claim must be model-priced first (T-57 style) until chain captures cover several recon windows.
final.data: cboe-RVX-history (2009-09-16..2026-10-14), daily-history-IWM, FTSE Russell recon-date list
final.pass: One-sided 95% lower bound of mean d_y > 0, both halves' means > 0, the opex-matched contrast's mean > 0, and the block-bootstrap alternative agreeing.
final.controls: No thresholds, no grid. RVX (RUT index IV) is applied to IWM, as in T-65, which is the unconditional baseline. The opex-matched contrast isolates June quad witching and FOMC from the recon itself. Per-year inference handles overlapping windows. A significantly negative d is reported but never re-tested as an inverse claim without a new registration.

rows.reason: Testable now on verified archived data, but the original two-sided, report-either-sign design was a fishing test, and its same-year baseline is confounded by June quad witching and FOMC. The fix makes it one-sided in the direction of the trade it would license, makes the opex-matched contrast a required condition, and states the leave-one-year-out sensitivity.

knowledge.title: Russell 1000/2000 reconstitution and other rule-based index migrations: migrant flows, cutoff effects, post-recon reversal and how far they have decayed (literature survey)
knowledge.markdown:
# Russell 1000/2000 reconstitution and other rule-based index migrations: migrant flows, cutoff effects, post-recon reversal and how far they have decayed (literature survey)

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey of 16 candidate strategies on index-membership flows beyond S&P 500 additions, each source-checked and re-registered by a verifier (13 fixed, 3 dropped). Core papers: Chang, Hong & Liskovich (RFS 2015, "CHL"); Madhavan (FAJ 2003); Pavlova & Sikorskaya (RFS 2023, "P-S"); Chinco & Sammon (JFE 2024); Greenwood & Sammon (JF 2025); Ben-David, Franzoni & Moussawi (JF 2018, "BFM"); Cai & Houge (FAJ 2008); Shankar & Miller (2006); critiques by Wei & Young (CFR 2024) and Appel, Gormley & Keim. Practitioner: Dimensional, FTSE Russell/LSEG, Cboe, S&P DJI, QuanterLab.
- **Links:** https://www.nber.org/papers/w19290 · https://www.dimensional.com/us-en/insights/even-migrating-stocks-face-index-reconstitution-costs · https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f147357/f147357.pdf · https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/ftse-russell/2026/ftse-russell-announces-december-2026-russell-us-indexes-reconstitution-schedule
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.55 (fraction of the sources actually read and verified: 18 of 33, six only as abstracts or digests).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-21. **How much was read:** full text of CHL, Madhavan, the P-S 2021 draft, Chinco-Sammon, Greenwood-Sammon and Wei-Young; the Dimensional, LSEG, Cboe and QuanterLab articles; FTSE Russell's June 2026 summary and December 2026 schedule; abstracts of Shankar-Miller, Cai-Houge, Akhigbe et al., Biktimirov-Xu, Micheli-Neuman and the BFM digest. Not opened: S&P DJI's Indexology posts (403; figures from search summaries), Nasdaq's 2026 FAQ (404), Petajisto, Appel-Gormley-Keim.
- **Selected because:** market cap, shares outstanding, volume, dollar volume, short interest and calendars are inputs of the user's program, and index membership (index addition and deletion) is the adjacent variable that turns them into a scheduled, inelastic demand shock. Mandel's S&P 500 versions are inconclusive or blocked (T-334, T-340, T-453), and the first December Russell reconstitution in over 30 years is a clean forward event if registered before Rank Day (2026-10-30).

## What it says

- **Downward migrants (R1000 to R2000).** Both indices are value-weighted, so a migrant's weight jumps about 10-15x and R2000-benchmarked money must buy (P-S: passive funds buy an extra 112 bp of shares). CHL (1996-2012, regression discontinuity): +5.6% in June against just-missed stocks (t 2.65), nothing in July or August. Dimensional (2014-2023): +1.2% vs the R2000 over the 20 days before recon, -0.95% over the 20 after. Decayed: Chinco-Sammon find recon-day returns converged to nearly zero over 2000-2021, and FTSE Russell (2026) says short-term effects have not reliably followed the pattern.
- **Upward migrants (R2000 to R1000).** The mirror: R2000 trackers sell and active R2000 funds cut ownership by 46 bp. CHL: -5.4% in June (t 3.0); Dimensional: -1.1% before recon, about +2% after. June 2026 had 42 upward and 39 downward migrants: small cross-sections.
- **Post-recon reversal.** Madhavan (1996-2002): the R2000 additions-minus-deletions spread was negative in July in 6 of 7 years. CHL find no significant reversal at the 1000 cutoff. Contested; migrants' pre-recon moves oppose the trade, so generic short-term reversal can mimic it.
- **Benchmarking intensity and passive demand in days of volume.** P-S (1998-2018, 34 indices): the top quartile of benchmarking-intensity change earns +80 bp in June relative to the average stock, the bottom quartile -110 bp; demand elasticity -3.03. Chinco-Sammon: changed names trade 9.5x normal volume on recon day. No post-2018 replication.
- **Long-run benchmarking discount.** P-S: R2000 addition lowers returns about 60 bp a month for five years (1998-2006) and deletion raises them 48 bp; after 2007 about -26/+28 bp, the addition effect sometimes insignificant. Wei-Young find weight-based ranks at the cutoff introduce selection bias.
- **Lower cutoff (rank about 3000).** No band at the bottom of the R2000. Madhavan: additions minus deletions +10.78% in June, all 7 Junes positive, but his March-May figures are inflated by forming portfolios on actual membership. CHL (2005-2012): t 1.25-1.45, not significant.
- **Deletions beat additions over 12 months.** Cai-Houge (1979-2004): buy-and-hold beat the rebalanced R2000 by 2.22% at one year. Unreplicated since 2004; the deletion leg lives in delisted microcaps.
- **IJR minus IWM after recon.** S&P DJI, seen only through search summaries: a seasonal July spread, the S&P 600 beating the R2000 by +0.68% in July 1994-2014 (t 2.54).
- **Nasdaq-100 December.** Biktimirov-Xu: first-time additions keep their gains, repeat additions and deletions revert (no magnitudes). QuanterLab (one-year holds): deletions beat QQQ by 18.7 points per window before 2016 and trailed by 16.3 after.
- **S&P 400/600.** Shankar-Miller: direct entrants react more than inter-index migrations, fully reversed within 60 days. Greenwood-Sammon (S&P 500, NBER 2022 version): index effect 7.6% to 0.8%; late-2010s direct additions +2.2%, migrations -2.3%.
- **Volatility, turnover and beta.** BFM (2000-2012, Russell switchers): one SD more ETF ownership raises daily volatility and turnover about 16%. CHL: co-movement with the new index rises.
- **Closing auction.** LSEG: $102.5bn on Nasdaq and $114.7bn on NYSE traded at the 27 June 2025 close. Chinco-Sammon: recon-day price pressure is near zero.
- **RVX in recon windows.** Cboe (2022): RVX mostly sat below its annual average in May-June since 2015. No statistics.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: mainstream-educational.** The academic core is rigorous (discontinuity and IV designs at the Russell cutoff, RFS/JFE/JF), but its identification is contested, most samples end by 2012-2018, and the out-of-sample evidence is practitioner work, gross of costs, showing effects decayed about fivefold, or to zero. The IJR and RVX claims are commercial and untested.

## What Mandel adopts

- **Two testable-now trials, pre-registered before measurement.** `ijr-minus-iwm-post-russell-recon` (recon close to +20 sessions; within-year permutation null avoiding recon and S&P rebalance weeks; post-2015 half positive) joins T-385's family, whose unconditional spread failed (+0.22%/yr, DSR 0.001). `rvx-vrp-russell-recon-window` is a one-sided conditional successor to T-65 (RVX variance risk premium, not_supported, p 0.0945) with a required opex-matched contrast, because June recon windows also hold quad witching and the FOMC, and T-216 (supported) shows expiries move the variance gap.
- **A 6-trial migrant family under Holm:** downward run-up, upward short (each with a Rank-Day variant) and the 20-session reversal at the close and next open, with a short-term-reversal control. Out-of-sample 2013-2026, entered only after the preliminary list is published, keeping names later removed.
- **Lower-cutoff Microcap movers** with spread-based costs, excluding newly eligible names, IPOs and spin-offs.
- **Gated or long-horizon arms:** passive demand in days of volume only if a migrant test passes; the 12-month benchmarking spread and deletions-minus-additions in one DSR family.
- **Nasdaq-100 December arms** (predictions frozen at the ranking date) and **S&P 400/600 direct additions**, whose timestamped change list also unblocks T-340 and T-453.
- **Migrants' volatility and turnover shift** against total-cap-matched stayers; the implied volatility leg is forward-only on chain captures.
- **A December 2026 forward record**, frozen before Rank Day, never pooled with June.
- The children agree: their `closedTime` landmine (an anchor that conditions on the outcome) is the trap of signalling on ex-post membership; Hurst killed small-cap post-earnings drift when a placebo entry beat the real one, so every trial has a placebo; T-334 priced only 82.6% of its additions, so survivorship is reported per event.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Effect size.** CHL's 5.6% has decayed to Dimensional's 1.2% gross and Chinco-Sammon's near zero; at 30 bp round trip and 14 out-of-sample Junes the migrant trade sits at the detection limit. A discontinuity against just-missed stocks is not a tradable return against IWM, and migrants are momentum-sorted against the trade.
- **Closing-auction overnight reversal: dropped.** Chinco-Sammon measure no pressure, T-428 is not_supported, and the generic claim is T-664.
- **Short interest conditioning: dropped.** Akhigbe et al. report contemporaneous co-movement, not a pre-entry days-to-cover predictor, with the opposite sign to the candidate; RegSHO short volume covers about 600 symbols; T-393 and T-375 are inconclusive.
- **Quarterly IPO additions: dropped.** Micheli-Neuman imply less crowding; data blocked as for T-523.
- **December tax-loss stacking** is anecdotal: T-351, T-444 and T-440 are not_supported. Madhavan's March-May returns are look-ahead. Weight-based matching and practitioner screens (passive buying over 5x ADV, float under 40%) are rejected. Pre-2026 Nasdaq-100 history may not represent the new rules.
- Every trade uses Alpaca stocks, ETFs and options or CME RTY futures; nothing needs an offshore venue.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Data to add:** FTSE Russell preliminary and final lists with publication timestamps and source/destination index; iShares IWB/IWM/IWC holdings history; delisting-aware prices; a sourced Rank Day/list/recon calendar (31 May until 2015, early or mid May 2016-2022, 30 April 2024-2026); a full-universe SEC shares outstanding fetch (36 of 44 CIK buckets archived); N-PORT tracker AUM; S&P 400/600 and Nasdaq-100 change lists; the French short-term-reversal factor.
- **Harness:** extend T-334's event study with `russell_membership(rank_day, caps, prior_members, band=0.025)` with list-accuracy, FINRA publication-lag and survivorship reports.
- **Features for T-577/T-578:** sessions to Rank Day and recon, a recon-window flag for IWM/IJR, predicted migrant flag, distance from the band edge, predicted passive demand over 20-day median dollar volume, days to cover at publication.
- **Forward:** freeze December predictions before 2026-11-13 and capture chains for predicted migrants.

## Cross-links

- A6 (opex: the 2026-12-11 recon falls a week before quad witching), A7 (short interest, borrow fees), A10 (volume, ETF flows), A11 (implied volatility, VRP), A12 (S&P 500 index inclusion), A13 (closing auction, overnight), A14 (turn of year). 12, 13, 14: recon-window features belong there.
- Theories: T-334, T-340, T-453, T-385, T-65, T-216, T-57, T-351, T-444, T-440, T-428, T-664, T-549, T-393, T-375, T-523, T-577, T-578.

## Sources used

- CHL https://www.nber.org/papers/w19290
- Dimensional https://www.dimensional.com/us-en/insights/even-migrating-stocks-face-index-reconstitution-costs
- Chinco-Sammon https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/double-what-you-think-it-is%20may%2023_3c1ae213-5aec-407d-b656-13e3822f0b8b.pdf
- P-S https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f147357/f147357.pdf
- Madhavan https://www.hillsdaleinv.com/uploads/The_Russell_Reconstitution_Effect,_Ananth_Madhaven,_Financial_Analysts_Journal,_JulyAugust_2003,_Pages_51-64.pdf
- Greenwood-Sammon https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w30748/w30748.pdf
- Wei-Young https://cfr.ivo-welch.info/published/papers/wei2020selection.pdf
- Appel-Gormley-Keim (not opened) https://cfr.ivo-welch.info/published/papers/appel2020identification.pdf
- BFM https://www.nber.org/digest/sep14/do-etfs-increase-stock-volatility
- Shankar-Miller https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/finrev/v41y2006i3p339-360.html
- Cai-Houge https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/ufajxx/v64y2008i4p76-91.html
- Akhigbe et al. https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/quaeco/v84y2022icp577-588.html
- Micheli-Neuman https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07456
- Biktimirov-Xu https://ideas.repec.org/a/pal/assmgt/v20y2019i2d10.1057_s41260-019-00108-6.html
- QuanterLab https://quanterlab.com/research/nasdaq-100-additions-versus-deletions-eighteen-decembers-an-effect-that-died-aro
- S&P DJI (403) https://www.indexologyblog.com/2015/03/25/a-tale-of-two-benchmarks-reconstitution-effect/
- LSEG https://www.lseg.com/en/insights/ftse-russell/more-key-facts-ahead-of-the-2026-russell-us-indexes-reconstitution
