candidates.name: Aggregate short interest index as a market-timing signal (Rapach-Ringgenberg-Zhou SII)
candidates.summary: The equal-weighted average short interest ratio across US stocks, detrended and standardised (SII), predicts lower S&P 500 excess returns at 1-12 month horizons. In the original paper it was one of the strongest known aggregate predictors. Later updates find it much weaker: in US data it rests mostly on 2008, though it holds up internationally. DUPLICATES T-454 (blocked: FINRA SI not ingested, EDGAR shares unreachable). Both blockers are now partly gone: the finra-short-interest bundle exists, and sec-companyfacts has the shares. An aggregate signal also escapes the delisted-price problem that left T-393/T-375 inconclusive, because it needs only the FINRA rows (which include later-delisted names) and SPY returns.
candidates.mechanism: Short sellers are informed about aggregate cash flows (the authors' VAR decomposition puts the predictive power mainly in the cash-flow channel). When they lean bearish across the board, expected market returns are lower. On the other side are long-only investors who do not use positioning data. A competing reading is that SI rises into downturns as margin tightens (Gorbenko), so the signal may be a crisis indicator rather than steady information.
adjacent_variables: aggregate days to cover (SI/ADV averaged across stocks)
candidates.assets: US equity index: SPY / ES futures (CME) vs T-bills
candidates.claimed_effect: RRZ (JFE 2016, 1973-2014): annual R2 12.89% in-sample and 13.24% out-of-sample, with utility gains above 300 bp/yr for a mean-variance investor. CXO summary of the 2012 draft: a 1 SD rise in SII goes with about 6% lower annualised excess return, and gross certainty-equivalent gains were 3.5% (1m) to 4.6% (6m), concentrated in the late 1990s and 2008-09. Gross of costs.
candidates.replication: Contested and decayed in the US. Gorbenko (RAPS 2023, Markit lending data, 2006-2016, 32 countries): SI predicts negatively in 24 of 32 countries. For the US alone, OOS R2 is 5.5/11.8/18.0% at 4/8/12 weeks, but none of these is significant; the pooled figures are significant. Dwars (Erasmus bachelor thesis 2024, 1973-2021, Goyal's SII data): in-sample R2 is 0.67% monthly and 5.65% annual. Excluding the GFC, predictive power disappears (R2 0.13%). OOS R2 is 1.17% monthly, and SII is beaten by inflation, technical and consumption predictors at the annual horizon. No post-2014 US peer-reviewed replication was found.

sources.title: Rapach, Ringgenberg, Zhou - Short Interest and Aggregate Stock Returns (SSRN; JFE 121(1) 2016)
Gorbenko - Short Interest and Aggregate Stock Returns: International Evidence (RAPS 13(4))
Dwars - Short interest and aggregate stock return: a new post COVID perspective (Erasmus bachelor thesis)
CXO Advisory - Aggregate Short Interest and Future Stock Market Returns

candidates.proposed_test: Re-scope T-454 to the data Mandel holds. Signal: at each FINRA release, take the equal-weighted mean of log(SI / SEC point-in-time shares) over stocks with price >= $5 (variant without shares: mean log DTC from the FINRA row itself). Detrend with an expanding linear fit and z-score it. The signal is available at the bundle's available_at (about 8 business days after settlement); enter at the first SPY close after that. Target: SPY excess return to the next release, and over 1 and 3 months. Statistic: Clark-West OOS R2, expanding window from 36 months, plus a timing rule (hold SPY unless z > +1, else bills) at 2 bp per switch, against buy-and-hold Sharpe. Sample: 2017-12..2026-09 (about 210 releases, about 105 months), so power is low; pre-register 'parked: underpowered' if the OOS R2 CI spans zero. Second, independent check: rerun on Goyal's published SII for 2015-2021. Deflate over the 2 constructions x 3 horizons.

candidates.name: Aggregate daily shorting flow predicts the next 10 days of market returns (negative)
candidates.summary: Daily shorting flows co-move across stocks, and their market-wide aggregate predicts lower market excess returns over the next two weeks. This is the high-frequency counterpart of the SII. Mandel's finra-regsho-cnms bundle (2018-08..2026-10) can build it, but only from off-exchange (FINRA facility) short volume, which practitioners argue mostly records market makers selling short to fill buyers (see the DIX candidate, which claims the opposite sign).
candidates.mechanism: Short sellers hold superior short-term market-wide information (aggregate earnings and macro news, sentiment) and trade on it together. The authors find modest evidence that shorts anticipate aggregate earnings and macro news.
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES)
candidates.claimed_effect: Lynch, Nikolic, Yan, Yu (J. Financial Markets 2014): a one-SD increase in aggregate daily shorting goes with market excess returns up to 36 bp lower over the next 10 trading days (about 9% annualised). The abstract I read does not state the sample period or costs.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020) show that stock-level shorting flows still predicted returns in 2010-2015, but they do not test the aggregate. The sign is disputed for off-exchange data by SqueezeMetrics (next candidate).

sources.title: Lynch, Nikolic, Yan, Yu - Aggregate short selling, commonality, and stock market returns (JFM 17)
Wang, Yan, Zheng - Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency (JFE 135)

candidates.proposed_test: Build the aggregate short-volume ratio from finra-regsho-cnms each file day: sum of short volume divided by sum of total volume over point-in-time S&P 500 members (equal- and dollar-weighted), available at the end of day t. Remove the slow drift in off-exchange share with a 60-file-day z-score. Target: SPY open(t+1) to open(t+11) minus bills. Primary statistic: slope of the 10-day return on z with Newey-West (10 lags), plus non-overlapping 10-day blocks and halves 2018-2022 / 2023-2026. Pre-register a two-sided test with this candidate's negative sign and the DIX candidate's positive sign as rival hypotheses. Deflate jointly with the DIX test (same data). Trading rule cost 1-2 bp per switch on SPY. Feed the same z (level and 5-day change) to T-578's daily swing learner as an ablation feature family; features.py currently uses FINRA SI only from 2025-26, and no CNMS short volume at all.

candidates.name: Dark-pool short volume as a buying proxy (SqueezeMetrics DIX) predicts S&P 500 gains
candidates.summary: A practitioner claim that off-exchange short sales mostly record market makers selling short to investors who are buying. A high dollar-weighted off-exchange short-volume ratio across S&P 500 members (the 'Dark Index', DIX) therefore signals accumulation and predicts higher 60-day index returns. This is the opposite sign to the academic 'shorts are informed' view. Mandel's own T-394 found that stock-level spikes in off-exchange SVR did NOT predict negative 5-day returns (+0.7 bp gross), which is consistent with this reading. Everything after the March 2018 publication is out of sample, and that is exactly the CNMS bundle's span.
candidates.mechanism: Market makers and wholesalers hold no inventory, so they fill buy orders by selling short and cover later. Off-exchange 'short' prints are therefore investor buys. Persistent buying into weakness (dip accumulation) precedes recoveries. On the other side are sellers who sell into dips.
adjacent_variables: retail order flow / payment for order flow
candidates.assets: US equity index (SPY / ES)
candidates.claimed_effect: SqueezeMetrics 'Short is Long' (Mar 2018): DIX >= 45% goes with a mean 60-market-day S&P 500 return of 5.3% vs 2.8% for all days (2011-2018, overlapping windows, in-sample, no costs). Their stock-level chart is a CONTEMPORANEOUS relation (same-day open-to-close return of -0.059% when SVR < 50% vs +0.118% when >= 50%, 2010-2018, 11,254 securities), which is not a predictor. Using it as one would be look-ahead.
candidates.replication: No academic replication. A Slope of Hope check reports an average 1-month return near zero conditional on DIX (anecdotal). Industry notes (OTC Markets, ORTEX, Keubiko) agree on the mechanism, that daily short volume is mostly market making, which undercuts the 'bearish bet' reading but does not show predictive power. The figures are in-sample, and the post-2018 record is untested.

sources.title: SqueezeMetrics - Short is Long: Using dark pool short sales as a proxy for buying activity
jensolson/Dark-Pool-Buying - open DIX estimate from NYSE, Nasdaq and ORF files
Keubiko - Misunderstood and Misused: Daily Short Volume
Slope of Hope - Measuring DIX

candidates.proposed_test: Construct DIX each file day: sum of short volume x close divided by sum of total volume x close over point-in-time S&P 500 members from finra-regsho-cnms (2018-08..2026-10), excluding short-exempt volume, known at the end of day t. Entry at the SPY open on t+1. Pre-registered claim: SPY excess return over 60 sessions after days with DIX in the top quintile of its expanding history (at least 250 days of history) exceeds the unconditional 60-day mean. Statistic: difference in means on non-overlapping 60-day blocks, with a stationary block bootstrap and a Clark-West OOS R2 of a 60-day regression on DIX z. Secondary: a 20-day horizon. Report 2020 (retail boom, structural rise in off-exchange share) with and without. Cost 1-2 bp per entry. Deflate jointly with the aggregate-shorting-flow candidate. A pass would also mean T-394-style stock shorts on high SVR should be avoided.

candidates.name: Days-to-cover long-short (DTC beats the short ratio)
candidates.summary: Days to cover (short ratio divided by daily turnover) predicts low returns better than short interest over shares. Long the lowest-DTC decile and short the highest earned about 1.2% a month gross in 1988-2012. DUPLICATES T-393 (inconclusive) and T-375 (inconclusive): both failed for want of delisted-stock prices, and their survivor-only diagnostics were null to negative (T-393 net -0.05% per period 2018-2026; T-375 EW spread +0.36%/month net, under its 0.83% bar). The web evidence adds that the short leg is mostly a borrow-fee effect. That argues for testing the long leg only (next candidate) rather than spending more effort on the L/S.
candidates.mechanism: Arbitrageurs short until the marginal cost of shorting equals perceived overvaluation. Turnover proxies that cost, so DTC measures how much shorts are willing to pay to be short. The other side is overoptimistic longs who face short-sale constraints.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); short leg needs borrow
candidates.claimed_effect: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman, Yan (NBER w21166, 2015), 1988-2012, gross: EW 1.19%/month (SR-based 0.71%), VW 0.67% (SR 0.29%); EW gross Sharpe about 1.3 vs 0.5; DTC positive in 23 of 25 years. After 2000 the short ratio is insignificant while DTC stays significant. DTC shorts lost heavily in the 2008 shorting ban. Akbas et al. SI-ratio deciles (Quantpedia): 1.51%/month raw, 4-factor alpha 1.72% (t 8.14), 1988-2005.
candidates.replication: Decayed or contested. Quantpedia's own out-of-sample backtest of the SI-ratio decile strategy is slightly negative. Chen-Zimmermann rate ShortInterest (Dechow et al. 2001) as '2_likely' with replication quality '2_fair'. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (2023/2025, 162 Chen-Zimmermann anomalies, Markit fees, 2006-2020): the average L/S is 0.15%/month gross and -0.02% after borrow fees, and is unprofitable even gross once the 12% of high-fee stock-dates are dropped. High-SI/DTC stocks are exactly those high-fee names. Mandel's survivor-only runs (2018-2026) show no net spread.

candidates.proposed_test: Do not re-run T-393 on the same unpriceable universe. Re-scope to point-in-time S&P 500 members (93.4% priced in T-394; report the bound for the rest). At each FINRA release, take DTC deciles from the FINRA row's daysToCoverQuantity, entering at the first close after available_at and holding to the next release. Charge 10 bp per side, plus borrow on the short leg of 0.3%/yr general collateral for deciles 1-9 and a stress grid of 1/5/10%/yr for decile 10. Statistic: mean net VW and EW L/S per release with a CBB CI (6-release blocks) and FF5+UMD alpha; must survive excluding Jan-Mar 2021. Report the long leg vs the EW member average separately; that is the long-only candidate, and it decides tradability for a small account. DSR with trials = 2 weights x 3 borrow assumptions.

candidates.name: Good news in low short interest (long-only, no borrow)
candidates.summary: Heavily traded stocks with LOW short interest earn significant positive abnormal returns, often larger in absolute value than the negative returns of heavily shorted stocks. With daily shorting flows, Wang-Yan-Zheng likewise find the high-minus-low spread driven by the outperformance of the low-shorting quintile. The long leg needs no borrow and survives the Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet fee critique, so this is the executable half of the short-interest anomaly for an Alpaca account. Not in the registry: T-393/T-375 test L/S spreads only.
candidates.mechanism: Absence of informed shorting in a liquid, easily shortable stock is positive information (the shorts looked and passed), and public SI data is incorporated slowly. On the other side are investors who ignore positioning data.
candidates.assets: US large-cap single stocks, long only (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: weeks to months (one FINRA release period, about 2 weeks, to 1 month)
candidates.claimed_effect: Boehmer, Huszar, Jordan (JFE 2010): significant positive abnormal returns for heavily traded low-SI stocks; the abstract I read gives no figures. Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020, FINRA daily files 2010-2015), lowest 5-day shorting-flow quintile held days 2-21: 4-factor alpha 5.2 bp/day EW (t 6.38) and 2.2 bp/day VW (t 4.92). The high-shorting quintile's alpha is insignificant, so the spread is long-leg driven. Gross.
candidates.replication: Corroborated in a later, out-of-sample period (2010-2015) by WYZ with a different data source, which also finds weaker effects in large stocks: high-minus-low 2.2 bp/day EW and 1.3 bp/day VW for large caps. No 2016-2026 test of the SI-level long leg was found.

sources.title: Boehmer, Huszar, Jordan - The good news in short interest (JFE 96(1))
Wang, Yan, Zheng - Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency (JFE 135)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members in the top half by 60-day dollar volume. At each FINRA release (2017-12..2026-09, about 210), form at the first close after available_at: the bottom quintile of SI/shares (SEC point-in-time shares; DTC as a pre-registered alternative), equal- and value-weighted, held to the next release. Benchmark: the EW and VW averages of the same liquid half, so the test isolates the SI tilt rather than size or the EW premium. Cost 10 bp per side on turnover. Statistic: mean excess return over the benchmark per release, with a CBB CI and FF5+UMD alpha t; both halves (2018-2021, 2022-2026) the same sign; exclude Jan-Mar 2021 as a robustness check. DSR with trials = 2 signals x 2 weights. Delisted members follow T-394's survivorship accounting.

candidates.name: Persistent shorting flow (20-60 day short-volume ratio) cross-section
candidates.summary: Stocks with a high short-volume ratio over the past week or month underperform lightly shorted stocks over the next month. The predictability decays slowly over a year with no reversal. In 2010-2015 data, LONG-window flows were more informative than short-window ones, and ABNORMAL short-term flows did not predict. Mandel's T-394 (z > 2 spikes, 5-day hold) found nothing, which matches that finding; it is not a test of the persistent-level signal. The web adds a distinct, untested specification.
candidates.mechanism: Short sellers trade on long-lived public information (anomaly characteristics) that is incorporated slowly. Daily disclosure did not destabilise prices. The other side is slow-updating longs. Caveat: FINRA's off-exchange SVR also contains market-maker short sales against retail buys (see the DIX candidate), so the off-exchange-only signal may be diluted or sign-flipped.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca); long-only or L/S
candidates.horizon: weeks to months (20 days to 1 month)
candidates.claimed_effect: Boehmer-Jones-Zhang (JF 2008, NYSE system order data 2000-2004): heavily shorted stocks underperform lightly shorted ones by a risk-adjusted 1.16% over 20 trading days (15.6% annualised); institutional nonprogram shorts 1.43% in the next month. Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020, FINRA daily files 2010-2015, quintiles on the prior 5-day ratio, skip 1 day, hold 20 days): 4-factor alpha -12.6%/yr EW (t 6.0) and -6.0%/yr VW (t 4.03); large stocks -2.2 bp/day EW (t 4.95) and -1.3 bp/day VW (t 2.17). Rebalanced daily, gross. Diether-Lee-Werner (RFS 2009, Reg SHO 2005): shorts are contrarian and predict negative abnormal returns.
candidates.replication: WYZ is an out-of-sample replication of BJZ/DLW on public real-time data; it finds the effect alive in 2010-2015 but much shorter-lived in 2005-2007. Kelley-Tetlock (RFS 2017) find retail short selling also predicts (about 9%/yr), using proprietary data. No post-2015 test found. Mandel's T-394 null applies only to abnormal spikes.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members (T-394's survivorship accounting). Signal: mean off-exchange SVR over the prior 20 and 60 CNMS file days, cross-sectionally ranked and residualised on log market cap. Formed at month-end (not daily, so that costs do not dominate), skip one session, hold 21 sessions. Portfolios: VW and EW quintiles; report the low-SVR long leg vs the EW member average and the L/S. Costs: 10 bp per side plus 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg. Statistic: mean monthly net return, CBB CI, FF5+UMD alpha t, both halves (2018-08..2022, 2023..2026-10) the same sign, with no reversal tested over months 2-12. Pre-register the sign as negative (high SVR underperforms) and report the opposite sign as the DIX alternative. DSR trials = 2 windows x 2 weights.

candidates.name: Short interest surprise (standardised unexpected short interest, change in SI)
candidates.summary: A stock's short interest ratio relative to its own trailing 12-month mean and standard deviation (SUSI) predicts returns: big surprises underperform, and the effect is stronger around earnings announcements. Notably, it is NOT related to shorting costs, so unlike the level anomaly it might survive the borrow-fee critique. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: New shorting relative to a stock's normal level reveals fresh negative information, while the level partly reflects static hedging and constraints. The market under-reacts to the published change. The other side is longs who read the level, not the surprise.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Hanauer, Lesnevski, Smajlbegovic (2020 paper, via CXO), 1980-2013, price >= $5, excluding the bottom 5% of NYSE size: EW decile L/S (long low surprise, short high) 0.43%/month gross, VW 0.35%. Since 1995, using announcement dates: top 30% of surprises -0.25% over the next 30 days vs +0.27% for the bottom 30%. Factor alphas are similar to raw returns. Stronger around earnings and in illiquid, volatile, high-dispersion stocks.
candidates.replication: No independent replication found. The data end in 2013; the 12-month lookback may be data-snooped (the authors report other windows qualitatively similar). Untested on 2015-2026 data.

sources.title: CXO Advisory - Surprise in Short Interest as Stock Return Predictor (Hanauer, Lesnevski, Smajlbegovic)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members (plus a liquid-half variant). SUSI_t = (SI/shares_t - mean of the prior 24 FINRA releases) / SD of those 24 (12 months at twice-monthly frequency), so the first formation falls in 2019-01 (about 185 releases). Entry at the first close after available_at, held to the next release. Portfolios: VW and EW deciles. Cost: 10 bp per side plus 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg; report the long-only bottom decile vs the EW member average. Statistic: mean net L/S per release, CBB CI, FF5+UMD alpha t; interaction with releases whose holding window contains an earnings date (10-Q/10-K acceptance in sec-submissions as the proxy). Variant pre-registered and deflated: FINRA changePercent. DSR trials = 2 signals x 2 weights.

candidates.name: Borrow-fee level and fee risk (loan-fee anomaly, cheap-minus-expensive, short-selling risk): fee-adjusted
candidates.summary: Equity loan fees are the strongest single cross-sectional predictor in the anomaly literature: high-fee stocks badly underperform, and the anomaly zoo lives inside the roughly 12-20% of high-fee stocks. The decisive later finding is that after paying the fee, the short side earns about nothing, and there is no lending-market risk premium. For Mandel the only executable angles are (a) to BE the lender (fully-paid lending), which is T-375, or (b) to use high fees or implied borrow as an EXCLUSION filter on long books. DUPLICATES T-375 (inconclusive: unpriced delisted names) and T-193 (blocked: options-implied borrow capture began 2026-10-14).
candidates.mechanism: Fees ration scarce lendable supply. Prices stay too high until the borrower's fee is paid, so the underperformance is largely the fee transferred to lenders. Short-selling risk (fee spikes, recalls) is a further limit to arbitrage in the Engelberg-Reed-Ringgenberg view, but Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet find it is not priced as a premium.
candidates.assets: US single stocks; lender side via broker fully-paid lending; options parity for implied fee
candidates.claimed_effect: Engelberg, Evans, Leonard, Reed, Ringgenberg (Management Science 2025): loan-fee L/S 4.01%/month, monthly Sharpe 0.66, best of 103 anomalies; strong persistence; 42% of it not explained by other anomalies. An earlier version, per Counterpoint, gave 1.17%/month and Sharpe 0.40. Drechsler and Drechsler (NBER w20282, about 2004-2012): cheap-minus-expensive-to-short 1.43%/month gross, 0.91% net of fees, 1.53% 4-factor alpha; anomalies vanish in the 80% of low-fee stocks. Engelberg-Reed-Ringgenberg (JF 2018): more short-selling risk means lower returns; the second-hand Swedroe figures are 0.58% vs -0.49%/month. Hendrix-Crabb (2020, DFA lending data, 14 markets): persistently high-fee small caps -0.09%/yr vs +8.7% low-fee, gross, daily rebalanced.
candidates.replication: The gross effect is robust, but the net-of-fee effect is gone. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (JF 2025; 2023 draft): 162 anomalies, 0.15%/month gross becomes -0.02% after borrow fees, and the anomalies are unprofitable even gross without the 12% high-fee stock-dates. MPP (JF 2022): the lending-market risk premium is small, and fee risk does not predict fee-adjusted returns. The same authors' 'Why does options market information predict stock returns?' (from memory, not reopened) attributes put-call-parity predictors to borrow fees.

Muravyev, Pearson, Pollet - Anomalies and Their Short-Sale Costs (NBER conference draft; JF 2025)
Muravyev, Pearson, Pollet - Is There a Risk Premium in the Stock Lending Market? (JF 77(3))
Engelberg, Reed, Ringgenberg - Short Selling Risk (working paper; JF 73(2) 2018)

candidates.proposed_test: Two pre-registrations. (1) Forward record (no history exists for free): capture IBKR's daily shortable-stock file (fee rate, available shares) from the Linode box, alongside the capture box's options-implied borrow (T-193). After 12 months, sort point-in-time S&P 500 plus Russell-1000-like liquid names monthly on fee. Statistic: next-month return of the top-fee decile minus its own accrued fee (fee-adjusted short return) and the lender's capture (50% of fee) vs a 0.83%/month bar (T-375's bar). Expected result: fee-adjusted short return about 0 (the MPP replication). (2) Testable now as a long-book exclusion filter: in any Mandel long-only equity rule (e.g. the low-SI long leg above), drop names in the top FINRA-DTC decile as a fee proxy; the statistic is the paired difference in net returns. Deflate with the parent rule's trials.

candidates.name: ETF short interest as hedging demand (contrarian bullish for the index)
candidates.summary: Unlike single stocks, heavily shorted ETFs do not underperform, and heavy shorting of broad-market index ETFs has been followed by positive index returns. The reading is that ETF shorts are mostly hedges of long stock books and operational shorts by authorised participants, not directional bets. FINRA's bundle includes ETFs with days to cover (SPY 2.02, QQQ 1.95, IWM 3.74, XLF 3.36, XRT 6.15, EWZ 1.96 on 2026-09-30). ETFs in the 901-symbol list are rarely delisted, so this sidesteps the survivorship wall that left T-393/T-375 inconclusive. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: High ETF short interest means investors have bought protection (hedged long books), so positioning is defensive and forced selling risk is low. When hedges are lifted, the index rallies. AP operational shorting rises with investor BUY imbalance. The other side is the hedgers, who pay for insurance.
candidates.assets: US equity ETFs: SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, sector SPDRs, iShares country ETFs (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: weeks to months (1 release period to 1 month)
candidates.claimed_effect: Hughen and Ma (2012, via CXO), 21 iShares country ETFs, 2002-2011 (3,419 fund-months): the lowest-SI decile beats MSCI World by 0.71% the next month and the HIGHEST decile also beats it by 0.58%. The largest SI increases beat it by 0.50%, so high SI does not predict underperformance. Gross, and the 8-day publication lag was ignored. Chichernea, Petkevich, Wang (J. Financial Research, 2026 early access): heavy shorting of broad US index ETFs is followed by positive index returns, a hedging interpretation (second-hand summary; abstract not retrieved).
candidates.replication: Mixed sign. A London-listed ETF study (Applied Economics 2016) also finds over-performance after large SI increases. Chen (SSRN 4527115) reports the opposite: ETF shorting predicts negative ETF returns, especially around macro news (abstract via search only). Evans et al. separate operational from directional ETF shorting. No 2017-2026 US test found.

sources.title: CXO Advisory - ETF Short Interest and Future Returns (Hughen and Ma)
Chichernea, Petkevich, Wang - Short selling ETFs and market performance (J. Financial Research, record)
Chen - ETF Shorting Activity, Return Predictability and Information Efficiency of Underlying Securities (SSRN)

candidates.proposed_test: (a) Time series: at each FINRA release 2017-12..2026-09, aggregate index-ETF short positioning = sum of short shares x close for SPY+QQQ+IWM+DIA, divided by the sum of their 20-day dollar volume (an aggregate DTC with no shares-outstanding history needed), z-scored over the prior 24 releases and known at available_at. Target: SPY excess return from the first close after available_at to the next release, and over 1 month. Pre-registered sign: positive (hedging). Statistic: OOS R2 (Clark-West) plus a top-quintile-minus-rest mean with block bootstrap; cost 1-2 bp. (b) Cross-section: 11 sector SPDRs and about 20 iShares country ETFs from the 901 list, ranked on DTC z (own 24-release history), top-minus-bottom tercile held to the next release, 3 bp per side. Pre-register two-sided (Hughen-Ma predicts no negative spread; Chen predicts negative). Deflate over 2 designs x 2 horizons.

candidates.name: ETF-implied (synthetic) shorting of constituent stocks
candidates.summary: Investors can short a stock synthetically by shorting the ETFs that hold it. Stocks with heavy short exposure through their holding ETFs underperform lightly ETF-shorted stocks, even controlling for the stock's own short interest. This predicts the OPPOSITE sign at the constituent level from the ETF-hedging candidate at the ETF level. Not in the registry, and blocked on holdings history.
candidates.mechanism: When a stock is hard to borrow, or a view is sector-wide, informed shorts use ETFs. The ETF short is then passed through to constituents via AP arbitrage, and the stocks most exposed to ETF shorting carry hidden negative information. The other side is direct holders who do not see ETF-level positioning.
adjacent_variables: ETF ownership share of each stock
candidates.assets: US single stocks and sector ETFs
candidates.claimed_effect: SMU working paper 'Short selling ETFs' (search summary; the PDF did not render for me, and I believe it is Li and Zhu's 'Synthetic Shorting with ETFs' under a later title, which is unverified): stocks heavily shorted via their holding ETFs underperform lightly shorted ones by 94 bp/month, and an ETF-based short ratio forecasts returns beyond stock-level shorting.
candidates.replication: None found. The sample period was not retrieved. The sign conflicts with ETF-level hedging findings; both can hold if ETF shorts are bullish for the ETF but bearish for specific constituents relative to their peers.

sources.title: Short selling ETFs (SMU Lee Kong Chian School of Business research collection)
Li and Zhu - Synthetic Shorting with ETFs

candidates.proposed_test: Blocked on point-in-time ETF holdings (Mandel has a single SPY holdings day). Unblock with SEC Form N-PORT quarterly holdings, which become public about 60 days after quarter end, so the signal uses holdings no newer than their public date. Signal per S&P 500 member: sum over equity ETFs (sector SPDRs, SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, and the 901-list iShares) of ETF short shares x ETF holding weight x ETF price / stock market cap, z-scored; formed at each FINRA release's available_at and held to the next release. Statistic: residual (stock-own-SI-controlled) Fama-MacBeth slope with NW t, plus a VW quintile L/S net of 10 bp per side and 0.3%/yr borrow. A cheap proxy is testable now: assign each stock its GICS sector SPDR's DTC z and test whether high-ETF-short sectors' members underperform their sector ETF. Expected to be weak; pre-register two-sided.

candidates.name: Failures-to-deliver and ETF operational shorting
candidates.summary: Most US fails-to-deliver now come from ETFs (78% in 2016), driven by authorised participants who sell ETF shares to meet buy imbalances and delay creation ('operational shorting'), not by naked bearish shorting. For stocks, the SEC staff found GME's FTD spikes cleared within days and note that FTDs arise from long sales too. As a return signal FTDs look weak, but SEC FTD data is free back to 2004 and could proxy ETF creation demand. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: Operational shorting rises when investors buy the ETF faster than the AP creates shares. An FTD spike is therefore a lagged footprint of buying demand, which provides liquidity (lower spreads and volatility, per Evans et al.). For stocks, persistent FTDs can mark hard-to-borrow names, in which case the borrow-fee mechanism applies.
candidates.assets: US ETFs and single stocks
candidates.claimed_effect: Evans, Moussawi, Pagano, Sedunov (2018 draft): ETFs are 10% of US equity market cap but over 20% of short interest and 78% of FTDs. Operational shorting is linked to better liquidity and to commonality across ETFs sharing an AP. Discussant slides and a search summary say it has no relation with future underlying returns (not verified in the pages I read). A JFE 2026 version ('Operational shorting and ETF liquidity provision') reportedly finds operational shorting negatively predicts ETF price returns (search summary only; page 403). Diether-Lee-Werner WP (search summary): Reg SHO threshold-list stocks under $5 had lower future returns, with no effect for stocks at $5 or more.
candidates.replication: No return-predictability replication found. The SEC staff report (2021) cautions that FTDs are an imperfect measure of naked shorting.

candidates.proposed_test: Fetch SEC FTD files (free) into a bundle. Set available_at conservatively to the half-month end + 20 days, since the SEC does not guarantee posting dates (first half posts at month end, second half around the 15th). (a) ETFs from the 901 list: FTD shares summed over the half-month / FINRA averageDailyVolumeQuantity, z over the prior 24 half-months. Target: ETF return minus SPY from the first close after available_at over 20 sessions; cost 3 bp per side. (b) Point-in-time S&P 500 stocks: the same ratio's top decile vs the rest, 20-session return. Pre-register two-sided with null expected; the statistic is the date-clustered mean difference with bootstrap. A null closes the FTD branch for the signal map; a pass goes to independent refutation.

candidates.name: Crowded shorts plus retail attention: squeeze tail risk (risk filter for short legs)
candidates.summary: Stocks with extreme short interest or days to cover carry right-tail jump risk when attention arrives. GME's short interest exceeded 100% of shares (109.26% on 2020-12-31). The SEC staff found that buying to cover was a small fraction of total buy volume, that sentiment, not covering, sustained the rise, and found no gamma squeeze. DTC short books also suffered large losses in the 2008 ban. This is a risk pattern for any Mandel short leg, including Hurst's live memecoin bounce-short (T-556) on Kalshi perps, where the analogue of crowding is negative funding with rising open interest. Not in the registry.
candidates.mechanism: When a crowded short meets a demand shock (retail coordination, a news catalyst, a borrow recall or a ban), shorts' losses force covering, and attention-driven buyers keep the price elevated. The losers are the shorts; the winners are holders and lenders, through fee spikes.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (risk filter); crypto perps on Kalshi/Coinbase Derivatives
candidates.claimed_effect: Descriptive: GME SI around 100% through 2020 (peak 109.26%); for large non-financial stocks SI is usually below 2.5%, for small ones below 13%. Before 2021, SI above 90% had been seen only a few times (2007-2008), and 12 stocks had SI above 50% on a single date in 2008. Customer GME options volume rose from $58.5m (Jan 21) to $2.4bn (Jan 27), mostly put buying; market makers were buying, not writing, calls. Qian-Shi-Yang 'Short-Selling Hedge Funds' (2024, 11,054 funds, 2010-2022) study short funds through the meme episode; results paywalled.
candidates.replication: The episode is well documented, but squeeze prediction has no systematic out-of-sample evidence that I found. Treat this as a risk-control pattern, not an alpha claim.

candidates.proposed_test: Stocks: the 901-list names (includes GME, AMC, BBBY) and point-in-time S&P 500. Event = FINRA DTC in the top decile at the latest available_at AND StockTwits message intensity z > 3 (own 60-day history) on day t; controls are top-decile-DTC days without an attention spike, matched on size and month. Outcome: P(next 5- and 20-session return > +30%) and the mean. Statistic: risk ratio with a date-clustered bootstrap; also left as a filter: does excluding such names improve the low-SI long rule or any short rule? Crypto: in T-556's DOGE/SHIB entries, condition on Deribit/Kalshi-perp funding < 0 and the 3-day OI change > 0 at entry, and test whether such entries have a fatter adverse tail (stop-hit rate) than the rest, as a paired comparison within the supported rule. candidates.name: Abnormal shorting before earnings announcements
candidates.summary: The older literature (Christophe, Ferri and Angel 2004, cited from memory, Nasdaq 2000-2001) reported abnormal short selling in the days before earnings that predicted negative announcement returns. In 2010-2015 public daily data, Wang-Yan-Zheng find NO abnormally high shorting in the five days before negative earnings surprises, analyst downgrades or large insider sales. They also find abnormal short-term flows do not predict returns, which suggests shorts moved from short-lived private information to long-lived public information. SUSI is reported stronger around earnings. This uses the days-until-earnings variable. Not in the registry (T-204/T-209/T-226 are options-based earnings claims).
candidates.mechanism: Shorts with private information about an upcoming print trade ahead of it; after Reg FD and real-time disclosure, this channel should be weak. On the other side are longs holding through the announcement.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Christophe-Ferri-Angel (JF 2004): pre-announcement abnormal shorting is negatively related to announcement returns (from memory; source not reopened, no figures given). Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020, 2010-2015): no evidence of abnormally high shorting before negative news, and abnormal short-term shorting flows have little predictive power.
candidates.replication: Contested and likely gone: the 2010-2015 public-data replication finds no pre-news shorting. Mandel's T-394 null on SVR spikes points the same way.

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500, 2018-08..2026-10. Announcement proxy: 10-Q/10-K acceptance timestamps in sec-submissions; the bundle has no 8-K item codes, so either flag 8-Ks filed 0-5 days before a 10-Q as the earnings release or add Item 2.02 parsing. Signal: mean CNMS SVR over days -5..-1 minus the mean over -60..-11, known at the close of day -1. Target: CAR(-1 close, +1 close) minus SPY. Statistic: Fama-MacBeth slope with NW t, plus top-minus-bottom quintile CAR net of 10 bp per side and 0.3%/yr borrow over 2 days; both halves the same sign. Pre-register the sign negative with expected null. A null retires the 'shorts front-run earnings' node; a pass goes to refutation with an 8-K-dated rerun.

candidates.name: Informed-trading composite (INFO factor: short interest + insider net buying + option-to-stock volume)
candidates.summary: A 2025 paper combines three footprints of skilled traders into one score: net insider purchases (long side), short interest (short side) and option-to-stock volume (short side), ranked 1-100 and averaged. It forms equal-weighted decile L/S portfolios monthly, with costs set to half the effective spread. Combining short interest with other informed-flow variables may hold up better than SI alone. Partly blocked: Mandel lacks historical option volume, and insider transactions are tracked under T-391 (blocked).
candidates.mechanism: Each channel is noisy, but insiders, short sellers and options traders tend to trade on overlapping private or long-lived information, so the average is a better information proxy. On the other side are uninformed liquidity traders.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Ma, Martin, Ringgenberg, Zhou, 'An Information Factor: What Are Skilled Investors Buying and Selling?' (June 2025 revision), 1996-2019, with costs at half the effective bid-ask spread. The return figures are paywalled in the summary I opened, so no number is claimed here.
candidates.replication: None yet. The sample ends in 2019, so 2020-2026 would be out of sample.

candidates.proposed_test: A two-component version is testable once Form 4 transactions are ingested (T-391's blocker). Point-in-time S&P 500: percentile ranks of (i) net insider purchases over the prior 90 days by Form 4 acceptance time and (ii) minus SI/shares at the latest FINRA available_at. Average them, take monthly EW and VW deciles, hold 1 month. Cost: 10 bp per side plus 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg; report the long leg separately. Statistic: net L/S and FF5+UMD alpha t on 2020-2026 (out of sample for the paper) and on 2018-2019 for continuity. Add the option-to-stock volume leg only after 12+ months of forward capture from the chain box (option volume per underlying), as a separate pre-registration. DSR trials = 2 weights x 2 composites.

candidates.name: Short interest relative to institutional ownership (utilisation proxy)
candidates.summary: Short-sale constraints bind when shorting demand (short interest) is high relative to lendable supply, which institutional ownership proxies. Stocks with high SI and low IO underperform in equal-weighted portfolios, but not value-weighted ones, and the result depends on the sub-period. This is the free-data analogue of a lending-market utilisation signal. Not in the registry (T-392's 13F cloning is a different claim, but it shares the 13F ingestion blocker).
candidates.mechanism: Utilisation = shares on loan / lendable shares. Near full utilisation, borrowing is expensive and recall-prone (the fee mechanism), so pessimists are kept out and prices stay too high (Miller 1977). Low IO means little supply. The other side is the optimistic longs in constrained stocks.
candidates.assets: US single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Asquith, Pathak, Ritter (NBER w10434 2004; JFE 2005): with NYSE-Amex and Nasdaq stocks over a long sample, many earlier SI patterns do not hold. EW portfolios of high-SI stocks generally underperform, VW ones do not. Sub-periods mislead: high-SI stocks underperformed sharply in 1988-1994, while high-SI Nasdaq stocks did not in 1995-2002. Chen-Zimmermann's IO_ShortInterest: 'strong port sort but no long-short' in the original, rated 2_likely with replication quality 1_good. Nagel (2005) RIO-interaction signals are rated 1_clear (t 2.5-4.9 in the original, 1980-2003).
candidates.replication: Replicated in Chen-Zimmermann's open-source set, but EW and small-cap driven, and fragile across sub-periods by the authors' own account. After 2006 it falls under Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet's fee critique (high SI/low IO means high fee).

registration.claim: From 2017-12 to 2026-09, an aggregate short-interest index built from FINRA alone predicts the SPY log excess return over DTB3 negatively, with a positive Clark-West out-of-sample R^2 against the prevailing mean over at least 120 out-of-sample releases. The index is the equal-weighted mean of log(1 + daysToCoverQuantity) over exchange-listed common stocks with averageDailyVolumeQuantity >= 100,000 shares, linearly detrended and z-scored on an expanding window ending at release r, and known at release r's available_at (end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement). The return runs from the first SPY close after available_at to the next release's entry close.
registration.statistic: Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (Newey-West, 2 lags) of the recursive one-variable predictive regression against the expanding prevailing mean. Also: the OOS R^2 with a studentized circular block bootstrap CI (6-release blocks, reported), and the slope sign in each half.
registration.procedure: Universe: per release, keep finra-short-interest rows in the listed market classes whose issueName does not match a pre-declared fund/ETF/trust/warrant/unit/right/preferred/note regex and whose ADV >= 100,000 shares. Signal: x_r = mean log(1 + DTC). Revised rows: rows with revisionFlag set were revised after first dissemination and the bundle holds current values; the primary keeps them and a rerun without them is reported. Detrending: fit a linear time trend on releases 1..r only and z-score the residual by the residual sd up to r. Timing: decision at release r; entry at the first NYSE close after available_at (FINRA enters at publication, never at settlement); y_r = log SPY adjclose return from entry r to entry r+1, minus continuous DTB3 accrued (rule 7). Forecast: fit y_j on z_j using only pairs whose y is realised by entry r; first forecast after 72 releases (36 months); no tuned parameter. Reported only, carrying no verdict: the 1- and 3-month horizons; the SI / SEC cover-shares construction over point-in-time S&P 500 members (dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding at filing acceptance, coverage reported); and a timing rule (hold SPY unless z > +1, else bills, 2 bp per switch) Sharpe on excess returns vs buy-and-hold.
registration.data: finra-short-interest, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3; reported variant: sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, fja-sp500-components
registration.pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over >= 120 out-of-sample releases, AND the recursive slope negative in both halves of the out-of-sample window (2021-01..2023-10 and 2023-11..2026-09).
registration.controls: Benchmark: the expanding prevailing mean. Design: one construction, one horizon, one threshold. T-454's 12-cell grid is superseded and reported cells are labelled exploratory. Point-in-time: available_at only. Universe: rebuilt each release from FINRA rows, delisted names included, no price needed. Composition drift: names per release and the share first seen in the last 24 releases are reported, with a rerun excluding new listings (the SPAC wave). Crisis dependence: reported excluding 2020-02..2020-06, because Dwars and Gorbenko find US predictability rests on crises. Costs: 2 bp per switch on the timing rule.

rows.notes: Cheap and clean: every input for the DTC construction is in hand and point-in-time, with no survivorship. Power is the problem: about 139 OOS releases, and the literature puts the US effect mostly in 2008, which is outside the sample. Expect a null or 'undecided'. registration.claim: From 2018-08 to 2026-10, the z-score (trailing 60 CNMS file days, t included) of the equal-weighted mean off-exchange short-volume ratio (short_volume / total_volume) across point-in-time S&P 500 members, known at the end of file day t, predicts the SPY open(t+1)-to-open(t+11) return minus DTB3 negatively: pooled over every file day, the slope is below zero.
registration.statistic: OLS slope of the 10-session forward SPY excess return on z_t, pooled over all daily starts (rule 10), with a studentized circular block bootstrap (20-session blocks, at least twice the hold). The same slope with the trailing 10-session SPY return as a control. Clark-West OOS R^2 (expanding from 250 file days) reported.
registration.procedure: Membership: fja-sp500-components members as of day t at 09:30 ET. Signal: SVR_i = short_volume / total_volume for members with total_volume > 0 (short_volume as FINRA reports it, exempt volume included); x_t = mean_i SVR_i; z_t over the trailing 60 file days including t. Timing: entry at the SPY open on t+1, exit at the open on t+11, minus continuous DTB3 for the same days. Backfill: the primary uses the backfilled pre-2021-10 files; a rerun on 2021-10.. alone is reported. Family: this is one of four cells in a joint CNMS family (EW and dollar weights x 10 and 60 sessions). The dollar-weighted 60-session cell is registered as dix-dollar-weighted-svr-spy-60d; the other two cells are reported. ML export, no verdict: z_t and its 5-day change go to T-578 as an ablation feature family.

registration.statistic: Stop-hit risk ratio (crowded vs other entries) with an exact or bootstrap CI clustered by month, and the paired change in mean net return per trade from excluding crowded entries.
registration.null: Risk ratio <= 1, or excluding crowded entries lowers the mean.
registration.procedure: For every T-556 signal (the rule exactly as supported: next-open entry, later-bar exits), Hurst journals the funding rate and OI at the signal candle's close, from the Kalshi perp recorder, available before the next open. registration.pass: Over >= 40 journaled entries, the risk ratio's 95% lower bound > 1, AND the mean net return per trade without crowded entries >= the full rule's mean (paired, by month).
registration.controls: Rule: T-556 is the parent and is not changed. This is a filter test, and the parent's verdict stands either way. One crowding definition, no grid. Funding paid is charged, as in T-556. T-564's lesson applies: a filter that lowers the mean is rejected even if it trims the tail.

rows.notes: The only consumer of this filter is the live T-556 rule; Mandel has no supported stock short rule to protect. Forward accrual is slow, because T-556 fires about 20 times a year across both coins, so 40 entries takes about 2 years. Ask Hurst to log funding and OI at every signal now, which costs nothing. The stock DTC-only tail-ratio variant is testable now on S&P 500 members but has no consumer, so priority 5 if run alone.

rows.name: Abnormal shorting before earnings announcements

overlaps.note: Abnormal off-exchange SVR spikes carry no 5-day return information (FM slope NW t -0.08), which argues against shorts front-running news.
Earnings-event timing from SEC acceptance.
Earnings-announcement event study.
Options-based pre-earnings claim.

learnings.finding: Abnormal short-volume spikes are null at 5 days, survivor subset.
No abnormal shorting before negative surprises in 2010-2015 public data.
It keeps XBRL filings (form, acceptance) without 8-K item codes, so the earnings-release date (Item 2.02) cannot be told apart from other 8-Ks. 10-Q acceptance trails announcements by weeks.

rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance timestamps. They are free from data.sec.gov submissions JSON, which carries an 'items' column, but the archived bundle dropped it, so a re-fetch is needed. Delisted-member prices are handled by the absent-name bound.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2018-11 to 2026-10, abnormal pre-announcement off-exchange shorting predicts the announcement CAR negatively (Fama-MacBeth slope < 0). Abnormal shorting is the mean SVR over file days -5..-1 before an earnings release (8-K Item 2.02 acceptance) minus its mean over days -60..-11. The CAR runs from the day -1 close to the day +1 close, minus SPY.
registration.statistic: Fama-MacBeth slope across announcement weeks (NW t), plus the top-minus-bottom quintile CAR net of 10 bp per side and 0.3%/yr borrow over 2 days, with a date-clustered bootstrap.
registration.procedure: Event day 0: the session of an 8-K acceptance with Item 2.02 if accepted before 09:30 ET; the next session if accepted after 16:00 ET. The signal uses file days strictly before day 0's return window and is known at the day -1 close. Absent-name imputation as in dtc-long-short-sp500-pit.
registration.data: finra-regsho-cnms, new re-fetch of sec-submissions with 8-K items, fja-sp500-components, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY
registration.pass: Over >= 5,000 announcements, the slope < 0 with NW t <= -2, AND the quintile spread's upper 95% bound < 0 net, AND both halves (2018-11..2022-10, 2022-11..2026-10) negative.
registration.controls: Baseline window: -60..-11. Benchmark: SPY. Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow. One window definition, no grid. Expected null; a null retires the 'shorts front-run earnings' node.

rows.notes: Two independent lines (WYZ and T-394) already argue against it. Re-fetching 8-K items is worth doing anyway, because it also gives true earnings dates to SUSI, PEAD (T-452) and the earnings-announcement premium (T-339). That re-fetch is the main reason to keep this row alive.

rows.name: Informed-trading composite (INFO factor: short interest + insider net buying + option-to-stock volume)

overlaps.note: Form 4 ingestion is the shared blocker. Its small-cap delisted-price wall is milder for S&P 500 members.
An informed-investor cloning claim (13F).
The SI component on its own.

learnings.finding: Informed traders are a pointer to a source, not a signal to follow. Copying the best-CLV wallets loses the fee at any delay.
The SI component alone is null to weak in 2018-2026 survivor diagnostics.
Option volume per underlying exists for 2 capture days only. The option-to-stock leg needs about 12 months of forward capture.

rows.missing_data: Form 4 insider transactions: the free SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (quarterly from 2006-Q1) are not ingested (T-391). Historical option volume per underlying: capture began 2026-10-14. The paper's return figures are paywalled and unverified.

registration.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2020-01 to 2026-09 (out of sample for Ma-Martin-Ringgenberg-Zhou's 1996-2019 data), the equal-weighted top-minus-bottom decile of the average percentile rank of two components earns a positive mean monthly return after 10 bp per side and 0.3%/yr borrow on the short leg. The components are (i) net insider open-market purchases over the prior 90 days by Form 4 acceptance time and (ii) minus SI/shares at the latest FINRA available_at. Portfolios are formed at month-end and held one month.

registration.procedure: Insider component: from Form 4 non-derivative open-market P and S codes by acceptance time; 10b5-1 plan trades flagged and kept. SI component: as in low-short-interest-long-sp500. Ranks are within the month's members, with a missing component set to the median rank. The option-to-stock volume leg is a separate later registration after 12 or more months of chain capture. Absent-name imputation as in dtc-long-short-sp500-pit.
registration.data: new bundle sec-insider-transactions (T-391 ingest), finra-short-interest, sec-companyfacts, fja-sp500-components, daily-history-<members>, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily

registration.controls: Component baselines: SI-only and insider-only reported, so the composite must beat its parts. Factors: FF5+UMD. Costs: 10 bp per side plus borrow. Fixed equal weights, no fitted weights.

The fee and utilisation mechanism via DTC proxy, below its bar.

Borrow costs absorb short-side edges, so the high-utilisation short leg pays the fee.

Portfolios are formed at each FINRA available_at and held to the next release.

registration.data: new bundle sec-13f (to fetch), finra-short-interest, sec-companyfacts, fja-sp500-components, daily-history-<members>

rows.notes: The literature says it lives in small caps and EW portfolios, which Mandel cannot price free of survivorship. Run it only if 13F gets ingested for T-392, as an extra filter on the low-SI long book.

rows.name: Aggregate short interest index as a market-timing signal (Rapach-Ringgenberg-Zhou SII)
rows.source_notes: RRZ JFE 121(1) 2016 abstract (IDEAS): 'arguably the strongest known predictor', annual R2 12.89% in-sample and 13.24% OOS, >300 bp/yr utility gain, cash-flow channel. Confirmed. SSRN page returned 403. Gorbenko RAPS 13(4) 2023: Jul 2006-Dec 2016, Markit lending data, 32 countries, expected sign in 29, significant in 24, stronger around downturns. Confirmed; I did not read the US-only R2 figures (5.5/11.8/18.0%). Dwars (Erasmus 2024), from the PDF: 1973-2021 SII in-sample R2 0.67% monthly and 5.65% annual, beaten by output gap (17.46%); R2 falls to 0.13% excluding the crises; OOS R2 1.17% monthly. Goyal's site hosts a recursively detrended SII to 2021. RRZ's EWSI is SI/CRSP shares, with price < $5 and below-NYSE-5th-percentile caps excluded. Confirmed. Web-search budget was exhausted, so the Goyal-Welch-Zafirov 2024 reassessment was not checked.
rows.replication_concerns: US predictability rests on 2008 (Dwars: R2 0.13% without crises). The 2017-12..2026-09 FINRA window contains no GFC and puts the COVID crash in the training span, so the OOS window (2020-12..2026-09) is crisis-light. Mandel's two aggregate timing predictors (T-398, T-458) failed OOS. The FINRA-only construction is a NEW variant scaled by volume, not RRZ's SI/shares, so a null does not refute RRZ, and a pass could reflect volume rather than shorting.
rows.data_notes: finra-short-interest: 211 releases 2017-12-29..2026-09-30, no gap over 20 days. The schema holds currentShortPositionQuantity, averageDailyVolumeQuantity, daysToCoverQuantity and revisionFlag (1-7 revised rows per release). Listed classes only. Rows grow from 8,326 to 13,098, so composition drifts (SPACs, ETFs). The FINDING that changes the design: daysToCoverQuantity is FLOORED at 1.00. Raw SI/ADV < 1 on 2,929 of 8,326 rows (2017-12-29) and 5,661 of 13,098 (2026-09-30), and every one is reported as exactly 1. Among common stocks with ADV >= 100k the floored share is 13-34% and moves with volume (34% on 2021-02-12). The mean log1p(DTC) is biased up by 0.06-0.15 by the floor. daily-history-SPY and fred-DTB3 (to 2026-10-13) exist.
rows.lookahead_risks: available_at = end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement (one day more conservative than FINRA's schedule); entry at the next close. revisionFlag rows hold revised, not first-disseminated, values. A full-sample detrend (as in RRZ's in-sample work) leaks; detrend recursively only. ADV in a row covers the period ending at settlement, so it is known at publication. No survivorship: FINRA rows include later-delisted names and the target is SPY.
rows.missing_data: None for the primary. The SI/shares variant needs ticker-to-CIK maps for delisted names (sec-company-tickers is current-only), so coverage is partial and the variant is reported only. Goyal's published recursive SII (to 2021) is not archived; fetch it for a reported overlap check.

final.claim: From 2017-12 to 2026-09, an aggregate short-interest index built from FINRA rows alone predicts the SPY log excess return over DTB3 negatively and adds to its own volume denominator: positive Clark-West OOS R^2 against the prevailing mean over at least 120 OOS releases. The index is the equal-weighted mean over exchange-listed common stocks of log(1 + currentShortPositionQuantity / averageDailyVolumeQuantity), computed from the raw fields and never from the floored daysToCoverQuantity, recursively linearly detrended and z-scored, and known at each release's available_at. The return runs from the first SPY close after available_at to the next release's entry close.
final.statistic: Clark-West MSPE-adjusted t (Newey-West, 2 lags) of the recursive one-variable forecast vs the expanding prevailing mean; second Clark-West t of the two-variable forecast (index + volume placebo) vs the volume-placebo-only forecast. OOS R^2 with a studentized circular block bootstrap CI (6-release blocks) and the recursive slope sign per half are reported.
final.null: OOS R^2 <= 0 against the prevailing mean, or no MSPE gain over the volume-placebo forecast.
final.procedure: Universe per release: rows in the listed market classes with averageDailyVolumeQuantity >= 100,000 shares. Exclude issueName matching one pre-declared regex covering ETF, fund, ETN, trust, ACQUISITION (SPACs), ADR or DEPOSITARY, warrant, unit, right, preferred and note. Signal x_r = mean log(1 + SI/ADV) from the raw fields. Volume placebo v_r = mean log ADV of the same names. Each is detrended by an OLS line on releases 1..r and z-scored by the residual sd up to r. Timing: decision at release r's available_at; entry at the next SPY close; y_r = log adjclose return from entry r to entry r+1 minus DTB3 accrued over the same days. Fit only on pairs whose y is realised by entry r; the first forecast comes after 72 releases (about 2020-12), giving about 139 OOS releases. revisionFlag rows are kept, with a rerun without them reported. Reported only, no verdict: the 1- and 3-month horizons; SI over split-adjusted SEC cover shares for mapped names (coverage reported); a timing rule (bills when z > +1, else SPY) at 2 bp per switch vs buy-and-hold; names per release and the share first seen in the last 24 releases; a run excluding 2020-02..2020-06; and the correlation with Goyal's recursive SII on 2017-12..2021-12 if fetched.
final.data: finra-short-interest, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3 (reported variant: sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, daily-events, fja-sp500-components)
final.pass: Over >= 120 OOS releases, all of the following: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 vs the prevailing mean; Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 vs the volume-placebo forecast; and the recursive slope negative in both halves of the OOS window (2020-12..2023-10 and 2023-11..2026-09).
final.controls: Benchmark: the prevailing mean. Volume placebo: aggregate DTC falls mechanically when turnover spikes, so the index must beat its own denominator. Composition: the SPAC/ADR/fund regex is fixed in advance, and names per release are reported. Point-in-time: available_at only; no survivorship. One construction, one horizon, no threshold; it supersedes T-454's 12-cell grid. Crisis dependence is reported. Run in one harness with the ETF-short-interest diagnostic. Expected result: underpowered null.

rows.reason: T-454's blocker is gone and the FINRA-only design differs materially, so re-scope it rather than drop it. FINRA's daysToCoverQuantity is floored at 1.00 on 13-34% of common-stock rows, so the index must use raw SI/ADV and beat a volume-only placebo.

rows.name: Aggregate daily shorting flow predicts the next 10 days of market returns (negative)
rows.source_notes: Lynch, Nikolic, Yan, Yu, JFM 17 (2014), pp. 199-229 (IDEAS abstract): a 1-SD rise in daily aggregate shorting lowers the market excess return by up to 36 bp over the next 10 trading days (9% annualised), with commonality in daily shorting flows. Confirmed. The abstract does not give the sample period or data source. I believe it is the 2005-07 Reg SHO tick data (exchange plus TRF), but that is unverified. Wang-Yan-Zheng (JFE 2020), from the PDF: their data are FINRA's daily short-sale volume files, the same off-exchange facility source as CNMS, 2010-2015, stock-level only.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent replication of the aggregate result. The CNMS series is off-exchange only, while LNYY used all short sales. Aggregate off-exchange SVR rises into dips (SqueezeMetrics: DIX 'tends to rise into corrections'), so it may be a lagged price proxy. Mandel's T-394 stock-level null, T-398 and T-458 argue for a low prior.
rows.data_notes: finra-regsho-cnms: 99 monthly bundles 2018-08..2026-10 (2026-10 partial, 11 days), 2,063 file days, rows for the 690 point-in-time S&P 500 symbols since 2018-08, about 620 per day. 715 file days are flagged backfilled: all of 2018-08..2021-04, most of 2021-05, and scattered days to 2026-02. The cross-checker's '2021-10' boundary is wrong: live files start mid-2021-05. The EW mean SVR rose from 0.42 (2018-08) to 0.52 (2026), with a level shift in early 2022, so only a short-window z is usable. fja-sp500-components ends 2026-08-18; later membership comes from wikipedia-sp500-changes. daily-history-SPY and fred-DTB3 exist.
rows.lookahead_risks: Files are written about 17:20 ET; available_at = 23:59 UTC of the trade day; entry at the next open (clean). Backfilled files are FINRA restatements (sums of per-facility files), not the values published live. Wikipedia membership edits must use effective dates. The z includes day t, which is fine because t is known at the end of t. Overlapping 10-day targets need block inference.
rows.missing_data: None. Exchange (lit) short volume is not archived, so the signal is off-exchange only.

final.claim: From 2018-08 to 2026-10, the trailing-60-file-day z-score (t included) of the equal-weighted mean off-exchange short-volume ratio across point-in-time S&P 500 members, known at the end of file day t, predicts the SPY open(t+1)-to-open(t+11) return minus DTB3 negatively: the pooled slope is below zero.
final.statistic: OLS slope of the 10-session forward SPY excess return on z_t, pooled over every daily start, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (20-session blocks); the same slope with the trailing 10-session SPY return (close t-10 to close t) as a control. Clark-West OOS R^2 (expanding from 250 file days) reported.
final.procedure: Membership: fja-sp500-components as of day t 09:30 ET through 2026-08-18, then wikipedia-sp500-changes by effective date. SVR_i = short_volume / total_volume for members with total_volume > 0 (short-exempt included, as FINRA reports it). x_t = mean_i SVR_i; a day with fewer than 450 members in the file is skipped and counted. z_t is computed over the trailing 60 file days. Entry at the SPY open on t+1, exit at the open on t+11, minus continuous DTB3. The primary uses all file days; a rerun on non-backfilled days only (about 1,348, from mid-2021-05) is reported. Family: one of four CNMS cells (EW and dollar weights x 10 and 60 sessions), deflated jointly. The dollar-weighted 60-session cell is registered as dix-dollar-weighted-svr-spy-60d; the other two cells are reported. ML export, no verdict: z_t and its 5-day change go to T-578 as an ablation feature family.
final.data: finra-regsho-cnms, fja-sp500-components, wikipedia-sp500-changes, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Over >= 1,500 file days: slope < 0 with one-sided p < 0.0125 (0.05 Bonferroni over the 4 CNMS cells) both with and without the trailing-return control, AND negative in both halves (2018-08..2022-09 and 2022-10..2026-10).
final.controls: Baseline: the unconditional mean. Price-only control: the trailing 10-session SPY return, because off-exchange SVR rises mechanically when wholesalers short into retail dip-buying. Drift: the 60-day z only, never the level (the EW level rose 0.42 to 0.52). Regimes: reported excluding 2020-02..2020-06 and 2021-01..2021-03. Costs: a timing rule (bills when z > +1, else SPY) at 1 bp per side, reported. One threshold. The rival sign is the DIX row's.

rows.reason: A clean, point-in-time, survivorship-free test that has never been registered (an unregistered T-394 variant). The fixes are the backfill boundary (mid-2021-05, not 2021-10), the membership source after 2026-08-18 and a member-count floor.

rows.name: Dark-pool short volume as a buying proxy (SqueezeMetrics DIX) predicts S&P 500 gains
rows.source_notes: The SqueezeMetrics 'Short is Long' PDF, dated March 2018, read in full. Dollar-weighted dark-pool short volume across S&P 500 components since 2011. DIX >= 45% goes with a mean 60-market-day return of 5.3% vs 2.8% for the whole dataset (in-sample, no costs, no test statistic). 'DIX tends to rise into corrections.' The stock-level result is a same-day open-to-close return of -0.0593% (SVR < 50%) vs +0.1184% (>= 50%) on 11,254 securities, 2010-2018: contemporaneous, not predictive. They use the NYSE and Nasdaq TRF files and ignore short-exempt volume. The jensolson repo computes an estimate from NYSE, Nasdaq and ORF data but makes no predictive claim. The Slope of Hope check was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: No academic replication. The paper's own text says DIX rises into corrections, so it may be a dip-buying proxy; the price-only dip control is essential. Only about 30 non-overlapping 60-session blocks exist, and the 2018-2026 sample is a bull market.
rows.data_notes: CNMS as in the aggregate-flow row (2,063 file days, 715 backfilled). DESIGN FLAW in the cross-check registration: the EW off-exchange SVR trends from 0.42 (2018) to 0.52 (2026), with a level shift in 2022. An expanding-history top quintile would therefore fall almost entirely in 2022-2026 and act as a calendar dummy, and 'expanding quintiles' does not control drift, it creates it. A trailing-252-day rank is needed. Dollar weights need member closes: only 582 of the 690 member symbols have an archived daily-history bundle. The rest are renamed, acquired or removed-but-still-listed names that are absent from the 901-symbol archive. The shortfall affects the signal's weights, not the SPY target.
rows.lookahead_risks: Breakpoints must use file days before t only. The 901-symbol daily-history set is today's universe, so dollar weights over-represent survivors. SqueezeMetrics' published DIX history may be revised; use it as a cross-check, never as an input. The same-day stock-level chart must never be used as a predictor. Overlapping 60-session targets need long blocks.
rows.missing_data: Closes for about 108 former or renamed member symbols. Fetch the ones Yahoo still serves before the run, and report the dropped share of off-exchange volume per day. SqueezeMetrics' DIX CSV is not archived (needed for a reported correlation only).

final.claim: From 2019-08 to 2026-10 (out of sample for SqueezeMetrics' March 2018 paper): on file days when the dollar-weighted off-exchange short-volume ratio of point-in-time S&P 500 members is at or above the 80th percentile of its own trailing 252 file days, the SPY open(t+1)-to-open(t+61) return minus DTB3 exceeds both the all-eligible-day mean and the mean after price-only dip days, net of 1 bp per side. The ratio is sum short_volume x close / sum total_volume x close, known at the end of day t.
final.statistic: Difference in mean 60-session excess return, signal days minus all eligible days and signal days minus dip days, pooled over every daily start, with a studentized circular block bootstrap (120-session blocks). The 20-session horizon and the Clark-West OOS R^2 of the 60-session return on the trailing-rank z are reported.
final.procedure: close_i = split-adjusted daily-history close on day t. Members without an archived close are dropped from both sums; their share of off-exchange volume is reported per day. Before the run, fetch the missing members Yahoo still serves. Rank: DIX_t against DIX over file days t-252..t-1, so a day needs 252 prior file days. Dip days: SPY close(t)/close(t-5) in the bottom quintile of its own trailing 252 sessions. Entry at the SPY open on t+1. Reported only: the correlation with SqueezeMetrics' published DIX if fetched; the EW 60-session cell; 2020 with and without; the literal 45% level rule (not transferable, because CNMS adds ORF/ADF and keeps exempt volume).
final.data: finra-regsho-cnms, fja-sp500-components, wikipedia-sp500-changes, daily-history-<members>, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Over >= 1,500 eligible file days: both differences > 0 with one-sided p < 0.0125 (joint 4-cell CNMS Bonferroni), AND positive in both halves by entry date (2019-08..2022-12 and 2023-01..2026-08), AND positive excluding 2020-02..2020-06, AND the EW 60-session cell has the same sign (reported, not tested).
final.controls: Baselines: the unconditional mean and the price-only dip baseline (DIX must beat buying the dip). Trend: the trailing-252 rank removes the 0.42-to-0.52 drift that an expanding quintile would turn into a calendar dummy. Costs: 1 bp per side. One threshold. Deflation: joint with the EW 10-day cell.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the data are point-in-time, but the cross-check's expanding-history quintile on a series that drifted from 0.42 to 0.52 would turn the signal into a 2022-26 dummy. The fix is a trailing-252-day rank, plus a pre-run fetch of member prices for the dollar weights.

rows.name: Days-to-cover long-short (DTC beats the short ratio)
rows.source_notes: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman, Yan, NBER w21166 (May 2015): DTC predicts poor returns better than the short ratio; L/S 1.2%/month. CXO: 1988-2012, EW 1.19% vs SR 0.71%, VW 0.67% vs 0.29%, gross Sharpe 1.3 vs 0.5, DTC positive in 23 of 25 years, SR insignificant after 2000, DTC shorts lost in the 2008 ban. All confirmed. Quantpedia (Akbas et al. 1988-2005) gives 1.51%/month and alpha 1.72% (t 8.14), and states its OOS backtest 'shows slightly negative performance'. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (May 2023 draft, Jul 2006-Dec 2020, Markit), Appendix Table 1 row 'Short Interest (Dechow et al. 2001)': decile-1 average fee 4.20%, 36.6% of names high-fee, abnormal return -0.41%/month, -0.06% excluding fee > 1% names, -0.10% fee-adjusted. Chen-Zimmermann ShortInterest: 2_likely / 2_fair, 1976-1993, t about 1.0. All confirmed.
rows.replication_concerns: MPP shows the SI short leg is a fee transfer: -0.41% becomes -0.06% once high-fee names are excluded. Mandel's survivor diagnostics are null (T-393 net -0.05%/period, T-375 +0.36%/month vs a 0.83% bar). FINRA's DTC field is floored at 1.00 and rounded to 2 decimals, so the bottom decile of S&P 500 members contains ties at exactly 1.00 (1-5% of members per release, up to half the bottom decile in 2022).
rows.data_notes: FINRA and S&P 500 membership as above: 501-503 members with a FINRA row per release (BF/B, BRK/B need a symbol map). Only 582 of 690 member symbols have archived prices, and absences include names that left the index while still listed, not only delistings.
rows.lookahead_risks: Floored DTC creates ties; use raw SI/ADV. SEC shares by acceptance. The 901-symbol price archive is today's universe, so the losers removed from the index are missing; this biases the short leg up and the L/S down. FF factors are revised monthly and end 2026-08-31.
rows.missing_data: Delisted and former-member prices; real borrow fees (paid data, or a forward IBKR capture).

final.claim: Reported only, no verdict: among point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2018-01..2026-09, the EW bottom-minus-top decile of raw SI/ADV per release, net of 10 bp per side and short-leg borrow (0.3%/yr; 1/5/10%/yr grid on decile 10). Emitted from the low-short-interest-long-sp500 formations as a by-product attached to T-393's record.
final.statistic: Mean net L/S per release with a studentized CBB CI (6-release blocks); FF5+UMD alpha NW t.
final.procedure: Same formations, prices, absent-name handling and costs as low-short-interest-long-sp500. Raw SI/ADV, never the floored field.
final.data: finra-short-interest, fja-sp500-components, wikipedia-sp500-changes, daily-history-<members>, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3
final.pass: None: a reported diagnostic attached to T-393; it cannot change T-393's verdict without its own ledgered re-scope.
final.controls: As in low-short-interest-long-sp500; borrow grid reported; Jan-Mar 2021 excluded as a robustness check.

rows.name: Good news in low short interest (long-only, no borrow)
rows.source_notes: Boehmer-Huszar-Jordan JFE 96(1) 2010 abstract (IDEAS): heavily traded low-SI stocks earn significant positive abnormal returns, often larger in absolute value than the negative returns of high-SI stocks, and slowly incorporated; no numbers in the abstract. Confirmed. Wang-Yan-Zheng JFE 135 (2020), Table 2 Panel B from the PDF: the lowest prior-5-day-SVR quintile, held days 2-21, has a 4-factor alpha of 0.052%/day EW (t 6.38) and 0.022%/day VW (t 4.92). The high quintile is insignificant, and the text says the spread is 'primarily driven by the outperformance of low-shorting quintile'. Confirmed. Note that WYZ's long leg is a shorting-FLOW sort, not SI level.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2015 test of the SI-level long leg. In large caps the effect is weaker (WYZ: 2.2 bp/day EW, 1.3 VW). Low-SI large caps load on quality and low volatility, which are dead after publication in Mandel's record (T-383, T-384). Survivor diagnostics: T-393's large-cap spread +0.175% gross, net negative.
rows.data_notes: finra-short-interest (211 releases) has rows for 501-503 members per release. sec-companyfacts (36 buckets, dei cover shares by filed date) and sec-submissions exist. daily-events (splits) covers 837 symbols. A TRAP found: SI moves at a split immediately, but dei cover shares update only at the next filing, so a forward split between filing and settlement inflates SI/shares N-fold (NVDA's 10:1 in 2024, for example).

final.claim: Among point-in-time S&P 500 members in the top half by trailing 60-session median dollar volume, 2018-01 to 2026-09, the equal-weighted bottom quintile of short interest over split-adjusted SEC cover shares beats the equal-weighted average of the same eligible half by a positive mean per release, net of 10 bp per side on turnover. rows.name: Persistent shorting flow (20-60 day short-volume ratio) cross-section
rows.source_notes: Boehmer-Jones-Zhang JF 63(2) 2008 (IDEAS): NYSE system order data 2000-2004; heavily shorted stocks underperform by a risk-adjusted 1.16% over 20 days (15.6% annualised); institutional nonprogram shorts 1.43% next month. The candidate calls this 4-factor; it is three-factor. Large stocks 2.2 bp/day EW (t 4.95) and 1.3 VW (t 2.17). Table 5 long-term windows (days -25..-6 and -65..-6) give larger spreads: -65..-6 FF3 is 6.2 bp/day EW (t 5.55) and 3.5 VW (t 3.9). rows.name: Short interest surprise (standardised unexpected short interest, change in SI)
rows.source_notes: CXO (Dec 18, 2020) on Hanauer, Lesnevski, Smajlbegovic, SSRN Nov 2020: US common stocks 1980-03..2013-12, price >= $5, bottom 5% of NYSE caps excluded. SUSI = (SIR - 12-month mean)/12-month sd, monthly. EW decile L/S 0.43%/month gross, VW 0.35%. Since 1995, top 30% of surprises -0.25% vs bottom 30% +0.27% over 30 days. Portfolios are formed at the first close after that release's available_at and held to the next month-end release's entry close.
