knowledge.title: Short interest, short volume, securities lending and squeezes: what the positioning literature predicts, and what survives borrow fees
knowledge.markdown:
# Short interest, short volume, securities lending and squeezes: what the positioning literature predicts, and what survives borrow fees

- **Authors / kind:** literature survey. Journal papers: Rapach-Ringgenberg-Zhou (RRZ, JFE 2016), Boehmer-Jones-Zhang (BJZ, JF 2008), Boehmer-Huszar-Jordan (BHJ, JFE 2010), Lynch-Nikolic-Yan-Yu (LNYY, JFM 2014), Wang-Yan-Zheng (WYZ, JFE 2020), Engelberg et al. (Mgmt Sci 2025), Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (MPP, JF 2025), Asquith-Pathak-Ritter (APR, JFE 2005). Working papers: Hong et al., Drechsler-Drechsler, Evans et al., Hanauer et al. Practitioner sources (SqueezeMetrics, CXO, Quantpedia), the SEC staff report on early 2021, and Chen-Zimmermann's replication.
- **Links:** https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/Short_Final_Version.pdf · https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f184100/f184100.pdf · https://squeezemetrics.com/monitor/download/pdf/short_is_long.pdf · https://www.sec.gov/files/staff-report-equity-options-market-struction-conditions-early-2021.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.58 (about 24 of 41 cited sources opened and checked, 8 of them read in full or to table level; for 3 of the 15 candidates no source could be read).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** SqueezeMetrics, WYZ (Tables 2, 5, 7), MPP's Appendix Table 1, Evans et al., the SEC report, Dwars and the Chen-Zimmermann rows were read in full or to table level. The others were read only as abstracts or CXO summaries. SSRN returned 403 and four other sources would not open. Several cited works were not reopened (MPP 2022, Christophe-Ferri-Angel, Diether-Lee-Werner, Kelley-Tetlock). Every data claim was checked against Mandel's finra-short-interest (211 releases) and finra-regsho-cnms (2,063 file days) bundles.
- **Selected because:** short interest, days to cover and short volume are inputs to the learning program, and Mandel holds the free FINRA files for 2017-2026. Three registered theories (T-454, T-393, T-375) stalled on data that is now partly in hand.

## What it says

- **Aggregate short interest (SII).** The detrended equal-weighted SI ratio is claimed as a leading indicator of lower S&P 500 excess returns at 1-12 months, through cash flows. RRZ (1973-2014): annual R² of 12.89% in sample and 13.24% out of sample. **Decayed in the US:** excluding crises leaves R² at 0.13% (Dwars, 1973-2021), so the result rests on 2008. Internationally the sign holds in 29 of 32 countries (Gorbenko, 2006-2016).
- **Aggregate daily shorting flow.** A 1-SD rise goes with market returns up to 36 bp lower over 10 days (LNYY). No replication was found.
- **DIX ("short is long").** SqueezeMetrics read off-exchange short volume as market makers filling buyers. They report a 60-day S&P 500 return of 5.3% after DIX ≥ 45% vs 2.8% unconditional (2011-2018, in sample, no costs). Their own text says DIX "tends to rise into corrections". Their stock-level chart is a same-day relation, so using it as a predictor would be look-ahead.
- **Persistent shorting flow.** BJZ (2000-2004): heavily shorted stocks underperform by a risk-adjusted 1.16% over 20 days. WYZ (FINRA daily files 2010-2015, the CNMS source) find an FF3 alpha of −12.6%/yr EW (t 6.0). Their long window (−65..−6) gives a spread of 6.2 bp/day EW. Abnormal short-term flows do not predict, and there is no reversal.
- **Good news in low short interest.** Heavily traded low-SI stocks earn positive abnormal returns (BHJ). In WYZ the spread comes from the low-shorting quintile (5.2 bp/day EW, t 6.38; weaker in large caps). This half needs no borrow.
- **Days to cover.** Hong et al. (1988-2012): EW L/S 1.19%/month gross. **Contested:** Quantpedia's out-of-sample backtest is slightly negative, and Chen-Zimmermann's short-interest row has t ≈ 1.0.
- **SI surprise (SUSI).** SI against its own 12-month mean and sd: EW decile L/S 0.43%/month gross (Hanauer et al., 1980-2013). Stronger around earnings and unrelated to shorting costs. No replication was found.
- **Borrow fees.** The loan-fee L/S earns 4.01%/month gross (Engelberg et al.), and anomalies vanish in the 80% of low-fee stocks (Drechsler-Drechsler, about 2004-2012). **MPP's replication (2006-2020) is decisive:** 162 anomalies go from 0.15%/month gross to −0.02% after the borrow fee. The short-interest row goes from −0.41% to −0.06% without high-fee names. The short leg is a fee transfer to lenders.
- **SI over institutional ownership.** High-SI EW portfolios underperform; VW ones do not, and the result is fragile across sub-periods (APR). The published signal lives in the top 1% of SI.
- **FTDs and operational shorting.** ETFs accounted for 78% of FTDs in 2016, and operational shorting "is not a significant predictor of future ETF returns" (Evans et al.).
- **Shorting before earnings.** None was found before negative news in 2010-2015 (WYZ).
- **Short squeezes.** GME short interest peaked at 109.26% of shares. Covering was a small share of buying, and the SEC found no gamma squeeze. This is a tail-risk pattern with no out-of-sample prediction record.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** The core is peer-reviewed, risk-adjusted and independently replicated (WYZ of BJZ, MPP, Chen-Zimmermann), but what that work mostly establishes is decay: short legs are fee transfers, the US SII rests on 2008, and modern public data show no shorting before news. DIX and the squeeze material are practitioner tier. The ETF-hedging, ETF-synthetic and INFO-composite claims could not be verified.

## What Mandel adopts

- **`aggregate-short-interest-finra-rawdtc`**, a re-scope of T-454. The signal is log(1 + SI/ADV) from raw fields, recursively detrended. It must beat a volume-only placebo, because FINRA floors `daysToCoverQuantity` at 1.00 on 13-34% of common-stock rows. Expected result: an underpowered null (about 139 OOS releases, no GFC), matching T-398 and T-458, two aggregate timing predictors that failed out of sample.
- **Rival CNMS signs, deflated jointly (4-cell Bonferroni):** `aggregate-offexchange-svr-spy-10d` (pre-registered negative) and `dix-dollar-weighted-svr-spy-60d` (pre-registered positive). The ratio drifted from 0.42 to 0.52, so only trailing windows are used (a 60-day z, and a 252-day rank for DIX); an expanding history would act as a 2022-26 dummy. Both tests include a price-only dip control, because short volume rises into dips. T-394's spike null (+0.7 bp gross) fits the market-maker reading.
- **`low-short-interest-long-sp500`.** This is the executable, borrow-free half, and MPP's fee critique does not touch it. Controls: FF5+UMD+BAB, since low-SI large caps load on quality and low volatility, both dead in T-383 and T-384. Shares outstanding are split-adjusted, and survivorship is handled with a tipping-point bound.
- **`persistent-offexchange-svr-xs-monthly`** (WYZ's window, formed at month-end, residualised on dollar volume) and **`short-interest-surprise-susi-sp500-monthly`** (monthly, split-restated). Both are distinct from T-394.
- **`crowded-short-funding-oi-filter-t556-forward`** journals Kalshi perp funding rate and open interest at each T-556 short. It is a risk filter, and per T-564 a filter that lowers the mean is rejected.
- **By-products with no verdict:** the DTC L/S attached to T-393, an ETF short-interest diagnostic, and IBKR fee capture as an amendment to T-375 and T-193.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **SI/DTC long-short and loan fees as alpha.** Both are fee transfers, and Mandel's survivor-only runs are null (T-393 net −0.05% per release; T-375 +0.36%/month against a 0.83% bar). Borrow consumed the short edges in T-185 and T-325.
- **SII's headline R²:** crisis-dependent and decayed.
- **ETF short interest as bullish hedging (or a lagged ETF flows proxy), and ETF-implied constituent shorting (94 bp/month).** The sources are unverified, and the verified ones (Evans; Hughen-Ma) show no relation.
- **Parked:** FTD signals (Evans's null), pre-earnings shorting (needs 8-K Item 2.02 dates), INFO (paywalled; a two-component version would be a forking path; needs T-391's Form 4 insider filings) and SI/IO (about 5 S&P names; needs 13F, as T-392 does).
- **Squeeze-chasing.** There is no out-of-sample evidence, and no GME/AMC StockTwits history. Crypto crowding is traded only on US-legal venues (Kalshi perps, Coinbase Derivatives), and offshore funding feeds are never routed around geoblocks.
- **Children (EDGE_VERDICT Result 18, reference-price learnings).** Informed footprints point to a source; they are not signals to copy. Positioning every desk reads is a consensus, not a leading reference, so the prior is low.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Fix `mandel/ml/features.py`.** `si_dtc` reads the floored `daysToCoverQuantity`, and only from 2025-26. Use raw log1p(SI/ADV) from 2017-12 instead. Add `si_susi`, short-volume-ratio features (the 60-day z, its 5-day change, the residualised −65..−6 mean), and market-level SII and DIX percentile features, run as an ablation family in T-578 (306 cells, 0 pass so far).
- **Two shared harnesses.**
  - FINRA-release harness: available_at = end of the 8th NYSE business day after settlement; revisionFlag rerun; split adjustment.
  - CNMS harness: membership by effective date, a 450-member floor, a backfill flag before mid-2021-05, and trailing z-scores only.
- **Data to add:** prices for about 108 former members, Goyal's SII, the DIX CSV (as a cross-check only), a daily IBKR shortable-stock capture, and 8-K Item 2.02 dates (also for T-339 and T-452). Later: N-PORT, 13F and the Kalshi open-interest journal.
- **Metrics:** Clark-West OOS R² with block-bootstrap CIs, net returns per release, FF5+UMD(+BAB) alpha, DSR at declared trials, and the tipping-point bound.

## Cross-links

- A4: squeezes are fat-tail jumps; size stops by the jump tail. A5: slow incorporation of public SI is an information-decay question.
- 12, 13, 14: positioning features belong in those pipelines only with point-in-time stamps and a placebo.
- UNDERLYING-STRATEGIES.md; OPTIONS-STRATEGIES.md (implied borrow via put-call parity); SOCIAL-SOURCES.md; venues/US-LEVERAGE-VENUES-2026-10-20.md.
- T-454, T-393, T-375, T-394, T-193, T-183, T-185, T-325, T-556, T-564, T-303, T-423, T-398, T-458, T-391, T-392, T-399, T-339, T-452, T-383, T-384, T-578.

## Sources used

- RRZ (abstract read on IDEAS): https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Papers.cfm?abstract_id=2474930 · Gorbenko: https://academic.oup.com/raps/article/13/4/691/7127046 · Dwars: https://thesis.eur.nl/pub/73709/Thesis_Final_Draft.pdf
- LNYY: https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finmar/v17y2014icp199-229.html · WYZ: https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/Short_Final_Version.pdf
- SqueezeMetrics: https://squeezemetrics.com/monitor/download/pdf/short_is_long.pdf
- BJZ: https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/jfinan/v63y2008i2p491-527.html · BHJ: https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v96y2010i1p80-97.html
- Hong et al.: https://nber.org/papers/w21166 · Quantpedia: https://quantpedia.com/strategies/short-interest-effect-long-short-version/
- SUSI (CXO): https://www.cxoadvisory.com/short-selling/surprise-in-short-interest-as-stock-return-predictor/
- Engelberg et al.: https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ormnsc/v71y2025i7p5529-5551.html · Drechsler-Drechsler: https://www.nber.org/papers/w20282 · MPP: https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f184100/f184100.pdf
- APR: https://www.nber.org/papers/w10434 · Chen-Zimmermann: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/master/SignalDoc.csv
- Evans et al.: https://jacobslevycenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/ETF-Short-Interest-and-Failures-to-Deliver.pdf · SEC: https://www.sec.gov/files/staff-report-equity-options-market-struction-conditions-early-2021.pdf

candidates.name: Volatility-managed market exposure (Moreira-Muir), judged in real time and after costs
candidates.summary: Scale equity-market exposure by the inverse of recent realised variance (or VIX^2). Spanning-regression alphas replicate. Implementable real-time gains are contested, and after costs the market is the one factor where the effect survives. Mandel has never tested the plain monthly market version: T-562 scaled only the overnight slot, T-310 scaled only trend.
candidates.mechanism: Volatility is persistent, but expected returns do not rise in proportion to it in the short run. Cutting exposure after high-variance months therefore removes more risk than return. Leverage effect: high volatility follows declines, so the scaling adds a mild momentum overlay. On the other side are constant-notional holders and sentiment-driven investors who under-react to volatility: Barroso-Detzel find the managed market wins only in high-sentiment periods.
variables: implied volatility level (VIX as alternative scaler)
candidates.assets: US equity index: SPY / ES or MES futures; FF Mkt-RF for long history
candidates.claimed_effect: Moreira-Muir (JF 2017): large alphas and higher Sharpe ratios for the market, value, momentum, profitability, ROE, investment and FX carry. The abstract gives no numbers; from memory the market alpha is roughly 4-5%/yr over 1926-2015. Cederburg et al. (JFE 2020): over 103 equity strategies, real-time combination strategies do not systematically beat the unmanaged ones (50 of 103 outperform, as reported in Wang-Yan 2021). Barroso-Detzel (JFE 2021): after costs, volatility management of factors other than the market earns zero abnormal returns and lowers Sharpe ratios; the managed market's alpha survives costs. Harvey et al. (JPM 2018, to 2017): US equity Sharpe 0.40 unscaled vs 0.48-0.51 scaled.
candidates.replication: Contested. In-sample spanning alphas replicate (Cederburg et al.; Wang-Yan). Real-time out-of-sample gains fail for most factors because the regression weights are unstable. The market factor survives costs (Barroso-Detzel). Bongaerts-Kang-van Dijk (FAJ 2020): plain volatility targeting did not reliably help in global equity markets and could deepen drawdowns. No dedicated 2015-2026 decay study was found.

sources.title: Moreira & Muir, Volatility Managed Portfolios (NBER w22208; JF 2017)
Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang, Yan, On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios (JFE 2020)
Barroso & Detzel, Do limits to arbitrage explain the benefits of volatility-managed portfolios? (JFE 2021)
Bongaerts, Kang, van Dijk, Conditional Volatility Targeting (FAJ 2020)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY total return 1994-2026 as the tradable series and FF Mkt-RF daily 1927-2026 as a long-history check. The primary window is 2000-2026; 2015-2026 is a confirmation subsample. Signal at each month-end close: realised variance of the prior 21 daily excess returns. A pre-registered second arm uses VIX^2 at that close. Weight w = 0.15/sigma_hat (15% annual target, fixed ex ante, so there is no full-sample constant), capped at 1.5x. Fill at the next session's close; the rest sits in DTB3, and leverage above 1x pays DTB3 + 50 bp. Costs are 2 bp per unit of turnover. Statistics: (a) managed minus buy-and-hold Sharpe, with a studentized block-bootstrap CI (12-month blocks); (b) Cederburg's real-time combination test, with expanding-window OLS weights on managed and unmanaged; (c) DSR counting every variant (RV vs VIX, cap 1.0/1.5/2.0, monthly vs weekly). Pass: the lower 95% bound of the Sharpe difference is above 0 over 2000-2026, the 2015-2026 point estimate is positive, and DSR > 0.95. Report the high- vs low-sentiment split as a diagnostic only.

candidates.name: Downside-volatility-managed factors (Wang-Yan): scale by bad volatility, not total volatility
candidates.summary: Replacing total realised variance with downside semivariance (squared negative daily returns) as the scaler improves spanning alphas, direct Sharpe comparisons and real-time combination strategies. The gain comes from return timing: high downside volatility predicts lower future returns. This was the strongest repair of the Moreira-Muir critique that I found.
candidates.mechanism: Bad volatility (negative semivariance) carries the leverage-effect information, and it forecasts both future volatility (Patton-Sheppard) and lower future returns. Downside scaling therefore times risk and return together. The other side is constant-exposure holders who keep full exposure through high-downside-risk spells.
adjacent_variables: factor returns (FF5, UMD, BAB) as targets
candidates.assets: Equity factors (FF Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, UMD, AQR BAB); tradable arm SPY/QQQ/IWM and factor ETFs
candidates.claimed_effect: Wang-Yan (JBF 2021), sample to Dec 2018: downside-managed spanning alphas are positive and significant for all 9 factors, against 7 under total-volatility scaling. 89 of 94 anomalies have positive alphas, against 62 under total scaling. Downside-managed Sharpe beats unmanaged in 93 of 103 strategies, against 63 for total. The real-time combination beats unmanaged in 70 of 103, against 50 for total. Fixed 50/50 weights raise this to 80-81 of 103, against 64-68 for total. Return timing is positive for 8 of 9 factors and 71 of 94 anomalies under downside scaling, but for only 2 of 9 and 42 of 94 under total scaling.
candidates.replication: The paper is by part of the Cederburg et al. team, and Qiao et al. (2020) report a similar mean-variance expansion. I found no independent post-2018 out-of-sample check. The paper includes a trading-cost analysis whose numbers I did not read. Anomaly portfolios exclude price < $5 and NYSE bottom-decile stocks.

sources.title: Wang & Yan, Downside risk and the performance of volatility-managed portfolios (JBF 2021, author PDF)
IDEAS listing, JBF 131:106198
Patton & Sheppard, Good volatility, bad volatility: signed jumps and the persistence of volatility

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: archived FF daily Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, UMD and AQR BAB, 1963-2026. The decisive window is 2019-01 to 2026-09, which falls after the paper's sample. A tradable arm uses SPY, QQQ and IWM (2 bp per unit of turnover) and, from 2013, MTUM/QUAL/USMV/VLUE. Signal at month-end: downside RV = 2 x sum of squared negative daily returns over the prior 21 sessions, against total RV. Managed return = (k / RV_down) x f, with k chosen from data up to t only so that the expanding-window volatility matches the unmanaged series. Hold one month. Factor-level costs: Barroso-Detzel-style sensitivity at 10 and 30 bp per unit of turnover. Statistic: the paired Sharpe difference (downside-managed minus total-managed) and the 50/50 fixed-weight combination minus unmanaged, studentized block bootstrap, Holm across 7 factors, DSR over 7 factors x 2 scalers x 2 cost levels. Pass: the pooled difference is above 0 with the CI excluding 0 in 2019-2026. Caveat: the French library is revised over time, so these are not point-in-time factor returns. Report this as a limitation.

candidates.name: Volatility-scaled stock momentum (Barroso-Santa-Clara; Daniel-Moskowitz) as a crash repair for dead UMD
candidates.summary: Momentum's own volatility is predictable and its crashes come in high-volatility bear rebounds. Scaling UMD to constant volatility was reported to nearly double its Sharpe and remove the crashes. Mandel found raw UMD has a positive mean before 2009 but about zero after (T-446), and the bear-plus-high-volatility filter T-311 was inconclusive. The open question is whether scaling, not the signal, is what survives after 2009.
candidates.mechanism: Momentum loads on option-like crash risk after market declines: the loser leg rebounds sharply when volatility is high. Scaling cuts exposure exactly then. The other side is short-term reversal traders and distressed-loser rebounds. The return premium itself may have decayed (McLean-Pontiff-style decay; T-446: +11.3%/yr 1993-2008, +0.1%/yr 2009-2026).
variables: cross-asset leader: market return and volatility state
candidates.assets: US stocks (FF UMD factor; executable as a long/short decile book on Alpaca, or MTUM vs SPY as a crude proxy)
candidates.claimed_effect: Barroso-Santa-Clara (JFE 2015, 1927-2011): scaling by 6-month realised variance virtually eliminates crashes and nearly doubles the Sharpe ratio. From memory: about 0.53 to about 0.97. Hanauer-Windmuller (2022, 49 countries): scaling reduces crashes and raises Sharpe (search snippet; not opened). Fan-Li-Liu (55 futures): constant scaling is the most efficient approach (snippet). Daniel-Moskowitz: dynamic scaling improves further.
candidates.replication: Replicated internationally (49 countries) and in futures. Barroso-Detzel show that cost-adjusted volatility management of factors other than the market generally loses its alpha, which includes momentum. Cederburg et al. found MOM among the few factors whose real-time managed version held up (per the Alpha Architect summary). Mandel's T-446 shows the underlying UMD premium is about zero since 2009.

sources.title: Barroso & Santa-Clara, Momentum has its moments (working-paper PDF)
Volatility scaling in momentum (QUB working paper)
Alpha Architect summary of Cederburg et al. (real-time: MOM, ROE and BAB the exceptions)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: FF UMD daily 1927-2026. The pre-registered decisive window is 2009-01 to 2026-09, the period where T-446 found no premium. The executable arm is a top-minus-bottom decile 12-1 momentum book on the 901-symbol daily-history stocks, value-weighted, 2005-2026, with a survivorship flag because delisted firms are missing. Signal at month-end t: the strategy's realised variance over the prior 126 daily returns. Weight = 0.12/sigma_hat, capped at 2x. Hold one month. Costs: 20 bp per side per unit of incremental notional changed by scaling, plus 50 bp/yr borrow on shorts; sensitivity at 10 and 30 bp. Statistics: Sharpe of scaled minus unscaled UMD (studentized block bootstrap, 12-month blocks), worst 3-month return of each, and DSR with T-311's filter variants counted as trials. Pass: Sharpe difference CI above 0 in 2009-2026 AND scaled mean > 0. Expect a failure on the second clause if the premium is gone, which would be worth recording.

candidates.name: Conditional multifactor volatility management (DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera, Uppal)
candidates.summary: Rather than scaling each factor by its own volatility, let the weight on each factor in a mean-variance multifactor portfolio depend on MARKET volatility. Optimise with transaction costs, netting trades across factors. This is the answer to the Cederburg and Barroso-Detzel critiques that I found: it reportedly beats its unconditional counterpart out of sample and net of costs.
candidates.mechanism: Factor risk prices generally fall as market volatility rises, so a conditional portfolio de-risks the factors whose premia shrink in turbulent markets. It keeps or raises exposure to value, momentum and BAB. Trading diversification lowers the effective cost of volatility timing. The other side is constant-weight factor investors.
variables: implied volatility level (VIX as alternative state)
adjacent_variables: factor returns (MKT, SMB, HML, MOM, RMW, CMA, ROE, IA, BAB)
candidates.assets: US equity factor portfolios; tradable approximation via factor ETFs (SPY, IWM, VLUE, MTUM, QUAL, USMV) from 2013
candidates.claimed_effect: DeMiguel et al. (JF 2024): out-of-sample, net-of-costs Sharpe 13% higher than the unconditional mean-variance multifactor portfolio, significant at the 1% level. Ignoring trading diversification, 4 of 9 individually managed factors have negative net mean returns; with it, all nine are positive. The paper says it did particularly well in the early-2000s recession and the GFC.
candidates.replication: Recent (2024), open-access, with a MATLAB replication package on Mendeley. The authors note their replicated tables are not always identical to the paper. I found no independent replication.

sources.title: DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera, Uppal, A Multifactor Perspective on Volatility-Managed Portfolios (JF 2024, open access)
Replication package (Mendeley Data)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: archived FF5 + UMD daily, AQR BAB, and HXZ q-factors ROE/IA if fetched (free at global-q.org from memory, not verified). Use 1967-2026, expanding window, with out-of-sample evaluation from 2000 and a decisive holdout 2015-2026. Each month-end: estimate the conditional mean-variance weights w_t = a + b x RV_mkt,t per factor on data up to t, with a turnover-penalised objective (L1 penalty at the assumed cost). Compare against the unconditional mean-variance portfolio and Moreira-Muir per-factor scaling. Costs: 10 and 30 bp per unit of factor turnover, with netting across factors. Statistic: net Sharpe difference conditional minus unconditional (studentized block bootstrap), DSR over 2 cost levels x 2 state variables (RV vs VIX) x 2 penalty choices. ETF arm 2013-2026 on factor ETFs at 2 bp. Pass: CI above 0 in 2015-2026 and DSR > 0.95.

candidates.name: Volatility targeting pays only where the leverage effect lives (equities and credit, not bonds, FX or commodities)
candidates.summary: Man AHL's 60-asset study found volatility targeting raises Sharpe ratios for risk assets (equities, credit) and leaves them flat for bonds, currencies and commodities. In every asset it thins the left tail and lowers the volatility of volatility. That gives a cross-asset, pre-registerable prediction: the Sharpe gain should line up with each asset's leverage effect.
candidates.mechanism: Leverage effect: in risk assets, falling prices raise future volatility, so a volatility-targeted position cuts exposure during declines, which acts like time-series momentum. Assets without a negative return-volatility correlation gain nothing in Sharpe, only tail reduction. The other side is constant-notional and buy-the-dip holders.
variables: implied volatility (VIX, VXN, RVX, GVZ, OVX, VXTLT as alternative scalers)
candidates.assets: ETFs: SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM (equity); HYG, LQD (credit); TLT, IEF, AGG (bonds); GLD, SLV, USO, DBC, DBA, UNG (commodities); FX spot pairs (OANDA)
candidates.horizon: days to months (daily volatility estimate, daily or weekly rebalance)
candidates.claimed_effect: Harvey et al. (JPM 2018), 60+ assets, daily data back to 1926, to 2017: Sharpe rises for equities and credit (US equities 0.40 to 0.48-0.51, not very sensitive to the volatility estimator), and the effect on bonds, FX and commodities is negligible. Left-tail events are less severe in all asset classes.
candidates.replication: Practitioner research by Man AHL, published in a practitioner journal. It is consistent with Moreira-Muir on equities. Bongaerts et al. (FAJ 2020) dispute the reliability in global equities, and Mandel's T-310 found volatility scaling did not improve trend-following more than buy-and-hold. I found no 2018-2026 replication.

sources.title: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison, Van Hemert, The Impact of Volatility Targeting (JPM 2018)
Alpha Architect: Volatility targeting improves risk-adjusted returns (summary with US equity Sharpe figures)
Bongaerts, Kang, van Dijk, Conditional Volatility Targeting

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: the ETFs listed, 2007-07 to 2026-09 (from HYG's start), plus G10 FX spot with 3-month carry from the archived rates. The decisive window is 2018-01 to 2026-09, after the paper. Signal: EWMA volatility (half-life 20 days) at close t, position = 0.10/sigma_hat capped at 2x, traded at close t+1, 2 bp per unit of turnover for ETFs and 1 bp for FX. Primary statistic, pre-registered as a difference-in-differences: mean Sharpe gain (scaled minus unscaled) over the risk-asset group minus the same over the non-risk group > 0, with an asset-block bootstrap. Secondary: the cross-asset Spearman correlation between each asset's leverage-effect coefficient (estimated before 2018) and its 2018-2026 Sharpe gain > 0. Also report the change in 5% CVaR. Pass: the DiD lower 95% bound is above 0 in 2018-2026.

candidates.name: Economic value of better volatility forecasts: HAR with semivariances or implied vol versus EWMA in volatility targeting
candidates.summary: HAR-RV (Corsi) and its extensions with negative semivariance (Patton-Sheppard) or implied volatility forecast volatility better than EWMA. Bollerslev-Hood-Huss-Pedersen report utility gains from better risk models across 50+ futures. Man AHL report Sharpe is insensitive to the estimator. Mandel has QLIKE horse races (T-569 MSM > HMM, T-572) but no test of whether the forecast gain becomes money after costs.
candidates.mechanism: A volatility-targeted position's risk is only as stable as the forecast. Better forecasts (bad volatility persists longer; implied volatility adds forward information) reduce realised-risk overshoots and turnover from noise. The edge is risk control, not alpha, and the other side is nobody. It pays only if the reduced estimation error outweighs extra turnover.
variables: implied volatility level (VIX, VXN, RVX, GVZ, OVX, VXTLT)
volume in units (as an optional HAR regressor)
candidates.assets: SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD, USO (ETFs) and ES/NQ/GC/CL futures proxies
candidates.horizon: days (1-day and 21-day variance forecasts; daily/weekly rebalance)
candidates.claimed_effect: Bollerslev, Hood, Huss, Pedersen (RFS 2018): panel-based realised-volatility models on 50+ commodities, currencies, equity indices and bonds over 20+ years give better out-of-sample risk forecasts and significant utility gains; the paper studies transaction costs and trading speed (numbers not read). Patton-Sheppard (REStat 2015): negative jumps and negative semivariance lead to longer-lasting increases in volatility. Harvey et al. 2018: equity Sharpe after targeting is not very sensitive to the estimator.
candidates.replication: HAR forecasting gains are among the most replicated results in volatility econometrics, but the economic value net of costs is contested, and Man AHL found little sensitivity. Mandel's QLIKE wins (T-569, T-572) show forecast gains exist on SPY/QQQ/IWM but say nothing about money.

sources.title: Bollerslev, Hood, Huss, Pedersen, Risk Everywhere: Modeling and Managing Volatility (RFS 2018)
Patton & Sheppard, Good Volatility, Bad Volatility (REStat 2015, WP)
Harvey et al., The Impact of Volatility Targeting

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD, USO daily OHLC 2004-2026. The realised-variance proxy is Garman-Klass from daily OHLC, with a 60-minute-bar RV cross-check for 2024-2026. Forecasters, refit monthly on an expanding window: EWMA(0.94), HAR(1,5,22), SHAR (HAR with positive/negative semivariances from daily returns), and HAR-IV (adds the matching Cboe implied-vol index). Stage 1: QLIKE loss vs EWMA for 1-day and 21-day horizons, Diebold-Mariano with Holm across 6 assets x 2 horizons. Stage 2, run only for forecasters that pass stage 1: a 10%-volatility-target strategy per forecaster, signal at close t, trade at close t+1, 2 bp per unit of turnover. Statistics: net Sharpe difference vs EWMA, and the RMSE of realised vs target volatility (studentized block bootstrap), with DSR across the forecasters. Pass: stage 2 net Sharpe difference > 0 with CI excluding 0 on at least the pooled panel, holdout 2015-2026.

candidates.name: Statistical jump model regime switching (persistence-penalised) versus HMM for equity de-risking
candidates.summary: Shu-Yu-Mulvey fit a two-state statistical jump model, which adds a penalty for every state change, to exponentially weighted downside-deviation and Sortino features. They de-risk to T-bills in the bad state with a one-day delay and 10 bp costs, and report higher Sharpe and about half the drawdown of buy-and-hold on the S&P 500, DAX and Nikkei, beating an HMM on all three. This is the successor to Mandel's HMM tests T-561 and T-562, which failed.
candidates.mechanism: Volatility regimes are persistent and bad regimes carry low or negative risk-adjusted returns. The jump penalty suppresses the flip-flopping that makes HMM strategies pay too much in costs and whipsaw. The other side is buy-and-hold investors who ride drawdowns. It overlaps volatility timing, and the gain is mostly drawdown avoidance.
variables: implied volatility level and term structure (VIX, VIX/VIX3M) in a price-free variant
adjacent_variables: Kritzman-Li turbulence (Mahalanobis distance of cross-asset returns)
candidates.assets: SPY / ES (also QQQ, IWM; DAX/Nikkei not US-tradable except via EWG/EWJ)
candidates.horizon: days to months (daily signal, regimes last weeks to months)
candidates.claimed_effect: Shu, Yu, Mulvey (J. Asset Management 2024; arXiv 2402.05272), out-of-sample 1990-2023 with 12-year training and 8-year validation windows, 10 bp per one-way trade, signal applied with a one-day delay. Sharpe and maximum drawdown for jump model / HMM / buy-and-hold: S&P 500 0.68/-26.6%, 0.54/-28.9%, 0.48/-55.2%; DAX 0.44, 0.35, 0.30; Nikkei 0.31, 0.19, 0.12. The S&P HMM's CAGR (8.5%) is below buy-and-hold (10.2%). With a 5-day delay the HMM underperforms the market on the DAX and Nikkei.
candidates.replication: Single research group. Earlier regime-allocation work (Kritzman-Page-Turkington FAJ 2012; Nystrup et al.) is supportive, while a 2024 master's thesis found regime strategies struggle against static allocation. Mandel's own record: T-561 (HMM PUT-index filter) not supported, though it cut drawdown; T-562 HMM scaling raised QQQ overnight Sharpe +0.21 but not IWM's. Kelly child guidance: state models help where the state is measured directly.

sources.title: Shu, Yu, Mulvey, Downside Risk Reduction Using Regime-Switching Signals: A Statistical Jump Model Approach
Kritzman, Page, Turkington, Regime Shifts: Implications for Dynamic Strategies (FAJ 2012)
Nystrup et al., Regime-Based Asset Allocation: Do Profitable Strategies Exist? (DTU)

candidates.proposed_test: This partly duplicates T-561 and T-562 (HMM); it is kept because the web evidence says the persistence penalty, not the state model, is what matters. Universe: ^GSPC/SPY total return 1970/1993-2026 (training from 1978); QQQ and IWM as extra series. Arm A replicates the paper exactly: features EWM downside deviation (half-life 10) and Sortino (half-lives 20, 60); jump penalty chosen monthly by the best Sharpe over a rolling 8-year validation window; signal at close t applied on t+2; 10 bp per one-way trade; T-bills in the bad state. Arm B is the price-free variant: features EWM downside deviation, VIX z-score and VIX/VIX3M only. Comparators: buy-and-hold and T-561's frozen HMM rule. Statistics: Sharpe difference JM minus buy-and-hold and JM minus HMM (studentized block bootstrap, 63-day blocks), maximum-drawdown ratio, and DSR counting every JM variant and T-561/T-562. Windows: replication 1990-2023, decisive 2015-2026 (and 2024-2026 post-publication, reported only). Pass: the JM minus buy-and-hold Sharpe CI lower bound is above 0 in 1990-2026, the 2015-2026 point estimate is positive, and DSR > 0.95.

candidates.name: Cross-sectional skewness dispersion (and average skewness) predicts the stock market, concentrated in FOMC months
candidates.summary: The cross-sectional dispersion of firm-level realised skewness, the 75-25 percentile gap, negatively predicts next-month to 12-month S&P 500 excess returns in and out of sample. The predictability sits almost entirely in FOMC months. Jondeau-Zhang-Zhu's average skewness, the earlier measure, loses significance against it out of sample. Neither input is the target asset's price.
candidates.mechanism: The authors argue for gradual incorporation of macro and monetary news: when firm-level asymmetries are widely dispersed ahead of policy announcements, market risk premia adjust slowly. Average skewness was originally read as aggregate lottery demand or tail-risk exposure. The other side is investors slow to price policy news. This is a working paper, and the mechanism is the authors' interpretation.
variables: realised volatility / higher moments (realised skewness of stocks)
candidates.assets: S&P 500 (SPY / ES) as target; inputs from the US stock cross-section
candidates.claimed_effect: Babiak, Barunik, Kurka (arXiv 2604.07870, April 2026), 5-minute data on 6,770 US stocks, Dec 2000 to Dec 2022. The 1-month slope is -0.099 (NW t -2.95, adjusted R^2 4.09%); 3-month t -4.04, R^2 9.19%. Out-of-sample R^2 from Dec 2005 is 2.91% (1 month), 6.12% (3 months) and 7.85% (6 months), all significant by Clark-West. Jondeau-Zhang-Zhu average skewness scores -0.56% at 1 month and 0.53% at 3 months. FOMC months: coefficient -0.133 (t -3.28, R^2 7.08%); non-FOMC months: -0.018 (t -0.31). A mean-variance investor (gamma 3) earns CER 8.36% vs 2.40%, Sharpe 0.89 vs 0.57. Jondeau-Zhang-Zhu (JFE 2019): average monthly firm skewness predicts market returns and beats other predictors; I did not verify their out-of-sample numbers.
candidates.replication: New (April 2026) and not replicated. It reports a 50-predictor horse race but is not peer reviewed. Its own out-of-sample test finds the older average-skewness measure weak out of sample. Mandel's option-based tail measures failed: CBOE SKEW did not predict crashes (T-52, T-227). This is a different input (cross-sectional realised skewness).

sources.title: Babiak, Barunik, Kurka, Skewness Dispersion and Stock Market Returns (arXiv 2604.07870)
Jondeau, Zhang, Zhu, Average Skewness Matters (JFE 2019)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe for inputs: the 901-symbol daily-history stocks, flagged for survivorship; target SPY excess return over DTB3. Proxy signal, because Mandel lacks 5-minute data for the cross-section: each day, compute each stock's skewness from its prior 21 daily returns; the month-end value is the 75th-25th percentile spread averaged over the month's last 5 sessions, known at that close. A second signal is the equal-weighted average skewness (JZZ). Intraday check: the same spread from 60-minute bars on the ~60 single stocks with intraday history, 2024-2026, reported only. Statistics: expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 from 2005 with Clark-West; a pre-registered FOMC split (coefficient in months containing an FOMC decision < 0 and larger in magnitude than in other months, using the archived FOMC calendar); and the decisive post-paper window 2023-01 to 2026-09, reported with its low power (~45 months). Trading arm: SPY weight in [0, 1.5] from the mean-variance rule with gamma 3, rebalanced at month-end close t+1, 2 bp, Sharpe difference vs buy-and-hold with DSR over the two signals x 3 horizons. Pass: out-of-sample R^2 > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05 over 2005-2026 and the FOMC-month coefficient < 0.

candidates.name: Cross-sectional tail risk (Kelly-Jiang) as a market-return predictor
candidates.summary: Kelly and Jiang estimate a time-varying tail exponent each month from the pooled extreme daily returns of all stocks (a Hill estimator). High common tail risk forecasts higher market excess returns over the next year, and high tail-beta stocks earn higher alphas. The inputs are cross-sectional crash frequencies, not the target's price, and Mandel has the 901-stock daily panel to build it.
candidates.mechanism: This is a rare-disaster risk premium: when the cross-section signals fatter left tails, investors demand higher compensation, so expected returns rise. The other side is investors who insure against crashes and accept lower subsequent returns. The measure correlates with option-implied tail risk, but its history is much longer.
variables: realised volatility / tail frequency of stock returns
adjacent_variables: Hill tail exponent of the pooled cross-section
option-implied left-tail risk (CBOE SKEW as a weak proxy)
candidates.assets: S&P 500 (SPY / ES); cross-sectional tail-beta stock portfolios
candidates.claimed_effect: Kelly-Jiang (RFS 2014; NBER w19375): a one-standard-deviation increase in tail risk forecasts an increase in excess market returns of 4.5% over the following year. Stocks with high past tail-risk loadings earn an annual three-factor alpha 5.4 percentage points higher than low-loading stocks. The sample period is from memory roughly 1963-2010 and was not verified this session. The related Bollerslev-Todorov-Xu work (JFE 2015) attributes most variance-risk-premium predictability to the left-jump-tail component (options-based).
candidates.replication: Not checked. The shared web-search budget ran out before I could search for replications or post-2010 decay. Treat as unreplicated in this sweep. Mandel's option-based tail tests (T-52, T-227) were not supported, and T-228 found SKEW-implied tail probabilities far above realised ones.

sources.title: Kelly & Jiang, Tail Risk and Asset Prices (NBER w19375; RFS 2014)
Bollerslev, Todorov, Xu, Tail Risk Premia and Return Predictability

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: daily adjusted returns of the 901-symbol list, plus SPY as the target. Signal at month-end t: pool all stock-day returns in month t below the cross-sectional 5th percentile and compute the Hill estimator, with a pre-registered 3-month smoothing as in the original (from memory). Statistics: predictive regressions of SPY excess return over the next 1, 3 and 12 months on the standardised exponent, with Hodrick (1992) standard errors for overlap; expanding out-of-sample R^2 from 2000 with Clark-West; decisive window 2011-2026. Trading arm: SPY weight 1 + 0.5 x z_t, clipped to [0.5, 1.5], monthly, 2 bp, financing at DTB3 + 50 bp; Sharpe difference vs buy-and-hold with DSR over 3 horizons. Caveats to pre-register: survivorship (delisted crashers missing) biases the tail estimate downward, and the 12-month horizon has only about 15 independent observations post-2011. Report power before reading the result.

candidates.name: Variance risk premium as an equity-return predictor (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou), tested for its post-2010 decline
candidates.summary: Implied minus realised variance (VIX^2 minus trailing RV) predicts S&P 500 returns, best at 3-6 month horizons. A 2025 Chicago Fed paper finds index-option alphas have been indistinguishable from zero for about 15 years, with a break around 2010. That implies the premium, and possibly its predictive power, has shrunk. Mandel has tested the VRP's existence (T-48, T-540 supported) but never its use as a timing signal for SPY.
candidates.mechanism: A high VRP means investors pay a lot for variance insurance, so aggregate risk aversion or uncertainty is high and subsequent equity returns are higher. The other side is hedgers buying puts and variance. Intermediary-based explanation: option-dealer constraints set the premium (Dew-Becker and Giglio).
candidates.assets: S&P 500 (SPY / ES)
candidates.claimed_effect: Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou (RFS 2009): the VRP predicts returns, strongest at quarterly horizons. Bollerslev-Marrone-Xu-Zhou (2014): survives finite-sample bias and appears in several non-US markets (snippet). A 2001-2014 study reports the VRP was the only moment-based variable with a monthly out-of-sample R^2 above 6% (snippet, not opened). Dew-Becker and Giglio (Chicago Fed WP 2025-17): over the past 15 years equity-index option alphas are indistinguishable from zero; synthetic options never had negative alpha over 100 years.
candidates.replication: Replicated internationally pre-2014. Pyun (2016 WP) calls the original out-of-sample performance comparatively weak. The robust-estimation paper (arXiv 1612.05072) finds the predictive power survives, with the Lehman period most influential. I found no direct post-2010 predictive-regression decay test. The Dew-Becker-Giglio break suggests decay. Mandel: T-159 (VRP by term-structure regime) and T-235 (HAR-scaled short variance) not supported.

sources.title: Bollerslev, Tauchen, Zhou, Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia (RFS 2009)
Dew-Becker & Giglio, The Decline of the Variance Risk Premium: Evidence from Traded and Synthetic Options (Chicago Fed WP 2025-17)
Predictability Hidden by Anomalous Observations (robust re-estimation)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: monthly 1990-2026 from archived VIX and SPY or ^GSPC daily data. Signal at month-end t: VRP_t = (VIX_t/100)^2/12 - sum of squared daily log returns over the prior 21 sessions (BTZ used 5-minute RV; daily squares are the archived proxy). Statistics: regress SPY excess return over the next 1 and 3 months, with Newey-West or Hodrick SEs; expanding out-of-sample R^2 from 2000 with Clark-West. Pre-registered decay claim: the slope in 2010-2026 is above 0 with out-of-sample R^2 > 0. Also report the paired difference between 1990-2009 and 2010-2026 slopes. Trading arm: SPY weight 0.5/1.0/1.5 by VRP tercile, with cut-points from expanding data only, monthly, 2 bp, financing DTB3 + 50 bp; Sharpe difference vs buy-and-hold with DSR over 2 horizons x 2 RV estimators. Expect a not-supported result if Dew-Becker-Giglio's break carries over. The value is in recording which half the predictability lives in.

candidates.name: Realised skewness and relative signed jump variation in the cross-section (Amaya et al.; Bollerslev-Li-Zhao)
candidates.summary: Weekly realised skewness from intraday returns predicts next week's stock returns negatively. Relative signed jump variation, (good semivariance minus bad semivariance) / RV, gives large return spreads and is argued to drive the realised volatility, skewness and kurtosis anomalies. Lottery-like stocks with big recent upside jumps underperform.
candidates.mechanism: Investors with a preference for positive skewness (lottery demand) overpay for stocks with recent positive skewness or upside jumps. Stocks with recent negative jumps are shunned and carry a premium. The other side is retail lottery buyers. Limits to arbitrage are probably part of it, because daily-skewness versions fail with NYSE breakpoints (Hou-Xue-Zhang).
variables: realised volatility and higher moments (realised skewness, kurtosis)
candidates.assets: US single stocks (liquid large and mid caps); a sector-ETF aggregate version for SPY timing
candidates.claimed_effect: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs, Vasquez (JFE 2015): buying the lowest weekly realised-skewness decile and selling the highest earns 19 bp the following week (t 3.70); the working papers report 24 bp (t 3.65). Kurtosis is positive but not always significant; volatility shows no strong relation. Bollerslev-Li-Zhao (JFQA 2020): sorting on normalised good-minus-bad volatility gives economically large, highly significant spreads after controls; the 2014 working paper reports RSJ spreads as large as 23% a year.
candidates.replication: Partially contested. Hou-Xue-Zhang's 'Replicating Anomalies' places total and idiosyncratic skewness from daily returns among the friction anomalies that fail to replicate under NYSE breakpoints and value weighting. The high-frequency versions were not in that test. I found no post-2015 replication of the intraday measures. Expect McLean-Pontiff-style decay (about 58% average post-publication).

sources.title: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs, Vasquez, Does Realized Skewness Predict the Cross-Section of Equity Returns? (CREATES WP 2013-41; JFE 2015)
Bollerslev, Li, Zhao, Good Volatility, Bad Volatility, and the Cross Section of Stock Returns (JFQA 2020)
Bollerslev, Li, Zhao 2014 working paper (RSJ, 23% spread)
Hou, Xue, Zhang, Replicating Anomalies

candidates.proposed_test: Testable now (aggregate arm): build each sector SPDR's weekly RSJ from the archived 60-minute bars, 2024-2026, and the value-weighted aggregate ARSJ (Bollerslev-Li-Zhao's 9-ETF construct). Test whether ARSJ predicts next-week SPY excess return; this is low power and reported only. Decisive arm (blocked on data): minute bars for S&P 500 plus S&P 400 constituents 2018-2026 (Alpaca IEX feed; free history is from memory and must be verified). Weekly RSK and RSJ from 5-minute returns, Wednesday close to Wednesday close; skip one session; long the bottom decile, short the top decile, value-weighted, hold 1 week. Costs 10 bp per side large caps, 20 bp mid caps, borrow 50 bp/yr. Statistics: mean weekly net return (Newey-West t), FF5+UMD alpha, and DSR over RSK/RSJ/RKT x 2 weightings. Pass: net mean > 0 with t > 2 and DSR > 0.95 over 2018-2026. Pre-register that a daily-return-skewness proxy on the 901 stocks is a separate claim, expected to fail per Hou-Xue-Zhang.

candidates.name: Volatility-of-volatility (uncertainty about risk) predicts lower returns: Baltussen et al., testable on Cboe vol indices now and on captured chains later
candidates.summary: Stocks whose implied volatility is itself volatile (high vol-of-vol) underperform low vol-of-vol stocks by about 8% a year. The effect is distinct from 20+ known predictors, holds in Europe, and lasts up to 24 months. The input is option-implied, not price. At the index level, VIX and VVIX are only weakly related, and both negatively predict delta-hedged option payoffs.
candidates.mechanism: Preference-based (ambiguity or uncertainty aversion, limited participation): investors averse to uncertainty about risk stay out of high vol-of-vol stocks. Those stocks are then held by optimists and priced high, so subsequent returns are low. The other side is optimistic or uncertainty-tolerant holders. Trading activity falls after vol-of-vol rises.
variables: implied volatility level (and its own volatility)
adjacent_variables: vol-of-vol (std of daily IV changes / mean IV)
candidates.assets: US optionable stocks and ETFs; now: QQQ, IWM, DIA, EEM, TLT, GLD, USO, AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, SPY via their Cboe vol indices
candidates.horizon: months (1-month hold; effect persists up to 24 months)
candidates.claimed_effect: Baltussen, van Bekkum, van der Grient (JFQA 2018), 1996-2014: the highest vol-of-vol quintile underperforms the lowest by 0.69%/month value-weighted (0.50% equal-weighted), about 8% (6%) a year. Four-factor alpha is -0.60% (-0.44%) per month. The sample tilts to larger, more liquid stocks. The effect persists up to 24 months; Europe shows a high-minus-low of nearly -6%/yr. Huang, Schlag, Shaliastovich, Thimme (JFQA 2019): volatility and vol-of-vol risks are jointly priced with negative prices of risk, and both negatively predict delta-hedged S&P and VIX option payoffs.
candidates.replication: Out-of-sample within the paper (Europe). I found no independent post-2014 US replication; the search budget ran out before a targeted search. Mandel: the VVIX premium vs realised VIX volatility was not supported (T-243, T-536); that is a different claim from this cross-sectional one.

Statistic: monthly Spearman rank IC with the next month's excess return of the underlying (sign pre-registered negative), averaged over months with a block bootstrap; plus a long-bottom-third / short-top-third book at 5 bp per side. candidates.name: Commodity term-structure carry (roll yield / basis) on energy and metals, using EIA's free contract 1-4 curves
candidates.summary: A commodity's futures basis (annualised log F1/F2) predicts its excess return. Basis sorts give spot premia of 5-14%/yr and term premia of 1-3%/yr. This duplicates the blocked T-381-family theory T-371: it was blocked because Mandel has no curves. EIA publishes free daily contract 1-4 prices for WTI, RBOB, heating oil and Henry Hub up to 2024-04-05, which unblocks a time-series energy version.
candidates.mechanism: Theory of storage and hedging pressure: backwardation signals scarce inventory and hedgers paying speculators for insurance, so longs earn the roll yield. In contango, longs pay storage and financing. The other side is commercial hedgers and index funds rolling mechanically (USO/UNG roll losses).
adjacent_variables: futures basis / roll yield (F1 vs F2)
candidates.assets: CME energy and metals futures (CL, HO, RB, NG, GC, SI, HG) or ETFs (USO, BNO, UGA, UNG, GLD, SLV, CPER, DBC)
candidates.claimed_effect: Szymanowska, de Roon, Nijman, van den Goorbergh (JF 2014): sorting on basis, momentum, volatility, inflation, hedging pressure and liquidity gives spot premia of about 5-14%/yr and term premia of 1-3%/yr; one basis high-minus-low factor explains the spot premia. Practitioner: The Hedge Fund Journal reports spot moves offset about 60% of carry in commodities and equity indices; Macrosynergy reports relative commodity carry Sharpe 0.34-0.72, weaker since 2024 (search snippets; the Macrosynergy page returned 403 when opened). Koijen-Moskowitz-Pedersen-Vrugt (JFE 2018) commodity carry: from memory a Sharpe around 0.6 to about 2012, not verified.
candidates.replication: The cross-sectional basis premium is widely replicated (Gorton-Rouwenhorst, Erb-Harvey, Koijen et al.). Post-2015 performance is reported weaker by practitioners, and no academic decay estimate was found. Mandel: T-371 blocked (no curves); T-381 cross-asset carry composite not supported; T-370 metals implied financing ~ bills.

Data: EIA daily contracts 1-4 for WTI (1983-2024-04-05), heating oil, RBOB (2005-) and Henry Hub (1994-) plus Mandel's continuous GC/SI/HG fronts, for which a curve source is still needed. Signal at each month-end: annualised log(F1/F2). Time-series rule per commodity: long the front-month roll strategy when backwardated, flat (arm A) or short (arm B) when in contango. Hold one month. Returns are computed on the rolled futures series, not spot, rolling 5 business days before expiry. Costs: 1 tick per side per roll plus $2.50/contract in fees, or 5 bp per side for the ETF arm (USO/UGA/UNG/BNO). Statistic: pooled mean monthly excess return of the rule minus always-long, commodity-clustered block bootstrap, 1994-2024 with a decisive 2012-2024 window; DSR across arms. A cross-sectional version waits for 15+ curves. A going-forward data source (CME settlements or per-contract Yahoo tickers) must be verified before any live claim.

candidates.name: Basis-momentum in futures curves (Boons-Prado)
candidates.summary: Basis-momentum is the 12-month return of a first-nearby rolling futures strategy minus that of a second-nearby one. It captures curve slope changes and curvature, and is reported as the strongest predictor of commodity spot and term premia, beating basis and momentum in time series and cross-section. It also works in currencies and stock indexes and is not explained by COT hedging pressure. Mandel has a futures curve in hand now (Cboe VX futures, 2013-), and EIA supplies energy curves.
candidates.mechanism: Maturity-specific price pressure: when volatility rises and speculators' capacity to clear the market falls, demand imbalances at particular maturities move the curve, and the pressure persists. The other side is index and hedging flows concentrated at the front or at specific maturities. The authors read the premium largely as compensation for volatility and liquidity risk.
candidates.assets: CME energy futures (CL, HO, RB, NG); Cboe VX futures (M1/M2); ETF proxies; possibly CME BTC futures
candidates.claimed_effect: Boons and Porras Prado (JF 2019; working-paper PDF), 21 commodities since 1959: the high-minus-low basis-momentum portfolio earns 18.38%/yr (t 6.73) in nearby returns and 4.08%/yr (t 6.43) in spreading returns. A one-SD increase predicts +0.85% (+0.20%) per month in nearby (spreading) returns in pooled regressions. Returns survive transaction-cost estimates and hold in a 32-commodity cross-section; similar effects appear in 48 currencies and 12 stock indexes; COT hedging-pressure controls do not drive it out.
candidates.replication: Kwon-Kang-Yun (FRL 2021) find the 12-month ranking window's subperiods differ substantially in predictive power, a fragility warning. I found no post-2015 out-of-sample decay study. The published version reframes the mechanism (imbalances when speculators' and intermediaries' clearing ability is impaired) relative to the working paper (volatility risk).

candidates.proposed_test: Arm A (energy, EIA curves 1994-2024-04): for CL, HO, RB, NG, build rolled first-nearby and second-nearby excess-return series (roll 5 business days before expiry). At each month-end, BM = 12-month cumulative return of nearby minus that of second-nearby. Time-series rule: long nearby if BM > 0, short if BM < 0; a spreading arm goes long C1 / short C2 by the sign of BM. Hold one month; costs 1 tick per leg per trade plus fees. Statistics: pooled regression slope of the next-month nearby return on standardised BM, with commodity fixed effects and month-clustered SEs (pre-registered sign positive), and the net Sharpe of the rule vs always-long; decisive window 2012-2024. Arm B (archived Cboe VX futures, 2013-2026): the same BM on VX M1/M2 rolled series, predicting the next-month VX M1 excess return, monthly, $2/contract/leg. Pre-register it as a separate claim, because T-160/T-379/T-435 VIX carry rules failed. DSR over arms. Caveat: the 4 energy contracts are highly correlated, so the effective sample is small. Report it.

candidates.name: COT hedging pressure and hedgers' short-term liquidity provision in commodity futures
candidates.summary: Two COT effects. (1) Level: commodities where hedgers are net short (speculators net long) earn a risk premium, and long-short hedging-pressure sorts beat long-only commodities. (2) Flow: speculators trade momentum and impatiently, hedgers trade as contrarians, and prices predictably rise after hedgers buy and fall after speculators buy. Mandel has COT only for gold, silver and Bitcoin, and its gold-only tests are parked or blocked (T-405, T-456).
candidates.mechanism: Level: Keynes-Hicks normal backwardation, where hedgers pay speculators for price insurance. Flow: speculators demand immediacy, hedgers supply it, and the price impact reverses. Kang-Rouwenhorst-Tang show the two premia push in opposite directions, and the liquidity gains of commercials largely offset the insurance premium they pay. The other side for the flow trade is impatient trend-following speculators (CTAs).

candidates.assets: CME/ICE US commodity futures (CL, NG, HO, RB, GC, SI, HG, ZC, ZW, ZS, ZM, ZL, KC, SB, CC, CT, LE, HE) or ETF proxies (USO, UNG, GLD, SLV, CPER, CORN, WEAT, SOYB, DBA)
candidates.claimed_effect: Basu-Miffre (JBF 2013): single and double sorts on hedgers' and speculators' open interest give positive, significant commodity futures premia with Sharpe ratios above long-only portfolios, and the premia rise with lagged commodity volatility. Kang-Rouwenhorst-Tang (2013 WP; JF 2020): a typical speculator purchase is followed by a 16 bp price reversal the next week. A long-short strategy buying the top half (quintile) of commodities most heavily bought by hedgers earns 43 bp (67 bp) over the 20 days after the position change. Short-term position changes are driven by speculators' liquidity demand, long-term variation by hedging demand.
candidates.replication: Hedging-pressure premia were extended to currency, equity and fixed-income futures by later Miffre-team work, which I could not open; the search budget was exhausted before I could check 'Hedging pressure everywhere'. Maréchal (JFM 2023) revisits KRT on 1994-2017 with pre/post-financialisation splits; I did not retrieve its findings. Timing caution: COT positions are as of Tuesday and released Friday. Whether KRT's 'week following the trade' starts at the as-of date (which a trader could not use) was not verified. Mandel's T-405 gold managed-money extremes are parked as not_supported in the point-in-time run.

candidates.name: ML predictors that survive costs: price-free features, longer horizons, no microcaps, cost-aware objective
candidates.summary: The machine-learning asset-pricing literature agrees that gross predictability is real (Gu-Kelly-Xiu: trees and neural networks capture nonlinear interactions). Net returns are much smaller: they concentrate in microcaps and distressed stocks and in high-turnover 1-month horizons. What survives in recent work is longer prediction horizons, liquid stocks and cost-aware portfolio construction. That points directly at why T-577 (0/276 cells) and T-578 (0/306) failed, and how to design their successor.
candidates.mechanism: Short-horizon ML signals load on fleeting, high-turnover characteristics in illiquid names, where costs and arbitrage limits eat the alpha. Slower signals (quality, value, issuance, short interest) have lower turnover, and their premia are compensation for risk or behavioural mispricing that persists. The other side is slow-moving and constrained investors. Post-publication decay applies to the anomaly inputs themselves.
variables: short interest (days to cover, short volume)
candidates.assets: US stocks (large/mid caps, Alpaca), equity ETFs
candidates.horizon: months (3-12 month prediction horizon; monthly rebalance with overlapping tranches)
candidates.claimed_effect: Avramov-Cheng-Metzker (Mgmt Sci 2023): deep-learning profits come mainly from hard-to-arbitrage stocks and high limits-to-arbitrage periods; excluding microcaps cut the payoff about 62% (press summary); reasonable costs make it worse because of turnover and extreme positions. Blitz-Hanauer-Hoogteijling-Howard (Robeco 2023): 1-month ML strategies were mainly profitable before 2004, while 3/6/12-month horizons gave better net returns over 2004-2021 (described by Azevedo et al. as robust to 25 bp-per-trade costs). Azevedo-Hoegner-Velikov (AFA paper): net out-of-sample returns up to 1.42%/month and an LSTM net six-factor alpha of 1.20% (t 3.46), after costs, post-publication decay and decimalisation. Chen-Velikov (JFQA 2023, as summarised by Azevedo et al.): the strongest single anomalies net about 10 bp/month. Jensen-Kelly-Malamud-Pedersen: learning portfolio weights directly against a net-of-cost objective ('implementable efficient frontier').
candidates.replication: Gross ML predictability replicates widely, including in Europe and emerging markets. Net, large-cap profitability is contested (Avramov et al. vs Azevedo et al.). The Robeco evidence is practitioner research. Mandel's own record: T-577 0 of 276 intraday cells and T-578 0 of 306 swing cells pass. T-578's best cell was equity_etf 20-day F0 GBM, DSR 0.54, and its price-free F0 family had mean IC +0.011. T-579 (IC scan) and T-580 (implied family) are pending.

candidates.proposed_test: Register a T-578 successor (T-581-style) before fitting. Universe: the 901-symbol stock list restricted at each month-end to names above the NYSE 20th market-cap percentile, with cap = SEC companyfacts shares outstanding known at t times the close at t-1. Price-free features only, each stamped with its publication time: FINRA short interest and days to cover (as of the FINRA release date), RegSHO short-volume ratio (20-day), 12-month change in shares outstanding (net issuance), days until next earnings from SEC 10-Q/10-K filing cadence, realised volatility, downside semivariance and skewness from daily returns, dollar volume, and sector. Exclude past-return momentum features to keep price isolated. Targets: excess return over the next 3 and 6 months. Models: ridge vs gradient boosting, refit annually on an expanding window. Portfolio: value-weighted top-minus-bottom quintile in 3 (or 6) overlapping monthly tranches (Jegadeesh-Titman) to cut turnover. Costs: 10 bp per side above the NYSE median cap, 25 bp below; borrow 50 bp/yr. Statistics: development 2012-2025-09 with DSR counting every T-577/T-578/T-580 cell plus these, and the lockbox 2025-10 onward (or Mandel's sealed 2026-10 lockbox) mean net return > 0. Report the F0 feature-importance ranking by net contribution as in JKMP. Pass: development DSR >= 0.95 and positive lockbox mean.

registration.claim: On SPY total return 2000-01 to 2026-09, holding w_t = min(1.5, 0.15 / sigma_t) of SPY, where sigma_t is the annualised realised volatility of the 21 daily SPY excess returns ending at the last close of month t, decided at that close and filled at the next session's close, with the remainder in 3-month bills, leverage above 1x financed at DTB3 + 50 bp and 2 bp per unit of turnover, earns a higher annualised Sharpe ratio of monthly excess returns than buy-and-hold SPY, with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the Sharpe difference above zero.
registration.statistic: Annualised Sharpe(managed monthly excess) minus Sharpe(buy-and-hold monthly excess); paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks. Secondary (reported): Cederburg et al.'s real-time combination, the out-of-sample Sharpe of the expanding-window mean-variance mix of managed and unmanaged, minus unmanaged.
registration.procedure: SPY adjclose daily from 1993-02, with excess returns over DTB3 accrued daily at the prior print. sigma_t uses closed bars through the decision close only, annualised by sqrt(252). The 15% target and the 1.5x cap are fixed ex ante, with no full-sample normalising constant (the Cederburg critique). Each month-end decision executes at the next session's close. Drift is tracked between rebalances; turnover = |w_target - w_drifted|, charged at 2 bp per unit. Leverage financing is DTB3 + 50 bp on (w - 1) when w > 1. A pre-registered VIX arm uses (VIX_close/100) at the same decision; the Cboe close is 16:15 ET, archived available_at 21:30 UTC, so it too fills at the next close. Declared trials for the DSR: {RV21, VIX} x cap {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} x {monthly, weekly} = 12, primary RV21 / 1.5 / monthly. The family adds T-310's 20 and T-562's 2. Reported only: the frozen rule on FF Mkt-RF+RF daily 1927-1999 (long-history check), a UMCSENT high/low split, and the 2008, 2020 and 2022 regimes.
registration.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history--GSPC, french-ff3-daily, fred-DTB3, cboe-VIX-history, alfred-UMCSENT
registration.pass: Primary arm: lower 95% bound of the 2000-01..2026-09 Sharpe difference > 0, AND the 2015-01..2026-09 point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the 34 counted trials.
registration.controls: Buy-and-hold SPY on the same fills; a constant-weight SPY at the managed series' mean weight, which separates timing from average exposure; look-ahead: target and cap fixed ex ante, sigma from closed bars; costs on all scaling turnover and financing above 1x; mean excess return and volatility of both legs reported, so a gain that comes only from lower variance is stated as such; one primary threshold, the other variants count as trials.

rows.notes: Cheapest and most direct test in the cluster: it reuses the T-310/T-562 harness code, and T-310's pooled B&H gain is a non-judged hint in its favour. Expect a modest point gain (literature 0.05-0.10 Sharpe for the US market) and wide CIs. The likely failure is power, not sign. Monthly RV targeting de-risked after the March 2020 crash and missed the April-May rebound, so the 2015-2026 clause is at real risk. Executable on Alpaca (SPY) or CME MES; avoid perps for the leverage leg.

registration.statistic: Pooled (equal-weight mean over 7 factors) annualised Sharpe of downside-managed minus total-managed; secondary: pooled Sharpe of the fixed 50/50 combination of downside-managed and unmanaged minus unmanaged; paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks, resampling all factors jointly.
registration.procedure: Daily factor returns in percent (French/AQR). At each month-end close t: RVdown_t and RVtotal_t from the prior 21 sessions; c_t estimated on data up to t only, an expanding window from 1963-07 (BAB from its archive start). The weight applies to the next month's daily returns, with a one-month hold. Turnover = |weight_t - weight_{t-1}| per unit of factor notional; costs 10 bp per unit, sensitivity at 30 bp reported. An in-sample 1963-07..2018-12 replication is reported against the paper. Per-factor differences are Holm-adjusted across 7 and reported. DSR over 7 factors x 2 scalers x 2 cost levels = 28 trials plus the T-388/T-389 trials. Reported tradable arm: SPY/QQQ/IWM at 2 bp per unit, 2019-2026. The minimum detectable pooled Sharpe difference at 92 months is reported before the result is read.
registration.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, aqr-bab-daily, fred-DTB3, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM
registration.pass: Pooled downside-minus-total Sharpe difference lower 95% bound > 0 over 2019-01..2026-08, AND pooled 50/50-combination-minus-unmanaged point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
registration.controls: Unmanaged factors; total-RV-managed factors; an upside-semivariance-managed placebo (expected no better than total); c_t from past data only (no full-sample constant); costs at two levels; factor returns are pre-cost paper portfolios, so only scaling turnover is charged (stated).

rows.notes: The design is sound and cheap, since it reuses the T-388 factor loaders, but power is low (92 months) and most factor premia are near zero in Mandel's own post-publication tests. The market-factor slice is the informative part and overlaps the Moreira-Muir row: run both in one harness and count the trials jointly. Wang-Yan's own replication is by part of the Cederburg team, so it is not independent.

rows.name: Volatility-scaled stock momentum (Barroso-Santa-Clara; Daniel-Moskowitz) as a crash repair for dead UMD

overlaps.note: The same factor and window split: UMD 2009-2026 +0.12%/yr. This row asks whether scaling survives where the raw premium did not.
Bear-and-high-vol filter on sector-SPDR momentum: worst 3-month -18.4% vs -32.5%, better than 92.6% of random filters, only 3 episodes (inconclusive).
Vol scaling did not help trend more than buy-and-hold (DiD -0.082).
The executable 12-1 stock decile book is blocked on a point-in-time universe.
Factor momentum rotation fails vs static.

learnings.finding: The UMD premium is +11.33%/yr 1993-2008 vs +0.12%/yr 2009-2026. The 2009-Q2 momentum crash (about -40%) sits inside the decisive window. Scaling cut exposure then, because UMD's 126-day volatility was extreme in early 2009, so any gain may be one episode.
Crash protection on momentum gave the right sign and a large worst-case improvement but too few episodes. That is consistent with the mechanism but not with a verdict.
Cross-sectional stock books on the 901-symbol archive are survivor-only: about 91% of the FINRA universe has no archived price. The executable decile arm can only be a NOT-JUDGED diagnostic.
Vol-scaled UMD was already listed as a T-446 variant but never run.
BSC's sample ends in 2011, so 2009-2026 is mostly post-sample.

rows.missing_data: The paper-factor arm needs nothing more. A tradable momentum book needs a survivorship-free point-in-time US stock universe (CRSP-equivalent; no free full source). MTUM (free on Yahoo, from 2013) is a crude long-only proxy, not archived.

registration.claim: Over 2009-01 to 2026-08, FF UMD scaled each month by min(2, 0.12 / sigma_t), where sigma_t is the annualised realised volatility of the 126 daily UMD returns ending at month-end t, earns a higher annualised Sharpe ratio than unscaled UMD after 20 bp per unit of scaling-induced turnover, with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the Sharpe difference above zero and a positive scaled mean.
registration.statistic: Annualised Sharpe(scaled UMD monthly) minus Sharpe(unscaled UMD monthly), paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks; secondary: scaled annualised mean, and the worst 3-month return of each.
registration.procedure: Daily UMD (French, percent). The weight is decided at the last close of month t from the 126 daily returns through t, and applied to month t+1's compounded return. Turnover = |w_t - w_{t-1}| per unit of long-short notional, charged at 20 bp, with 10 and 30 bp reported. The factor's own rebalancing turnover is uncosted in both legs (paper factor; stated). The 1927-2008 replication is reported against BSC. Pre-registered decomposition: the same statistic over 2010-01..2026-08 (ex the 2009 crash) is reported. If that difference is <= 0, the record states that the gain is one episode. The executable diagnostic (value-weighted 12-1 top-minus-bottom decile on the 901-symbol survivor panel, 2005-2026) is reported as NOT JUDGED under rule 9. DSR counts T-311's 24 trials, T-446's family and this row's 4 variants: lookback {21, 126} x cap {1, 2}.
registration.data: french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 2009-01..2026-08 Sharpe difference > 0, AND scaled annualised mean > 0, AND DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: Unscaled UMD; a constant-weight UMD at the scaled series' mean weight; the Daniel-Moskowitz bear indicator (24-month market return < 0) reported as the comparator crash filter; costs on scaling turnover; no full-sample constant (target 12% fixed ex ante).

rows.notes: The most likely of the factor-scaling rows to pass the Sharpe clause, because one dated crash inside the window carries it; the ex-2009 decomposition is what to read. A pass would be a paper-factor result. Implementing it needs a long-short stock book with about 100%+ annual turnover per leg plus borrow, which FF UMD does not charge, so treat a pass as a reason to build a point-in-time universe, not as a trade. The map concept 'k:fat_tails' is the multifractal / fat-tails node (k:multifractal).

rows.name: Conditional multifactor volatility management (DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera, Uppal)

overlaps.note: Timed factor portfolio 1.04 vs static 1.08 Sharpe (1964-2026).
60-month reversal tilt: -0.03 Sharpe vs static.
UMD about 0 since 2009.
HML post-publication not significant.
Tradable BAB ETF spread +0.71%/yr with a wide CI.
Volatility-conditioned exposure on trend.

learnings.finding: Every factor-timing overlay Mandel tested on FF5+UMD+BAB lost to the static equal-risk portfolio (Sharpe about 1.08 pre-cost). A conditional mean-variance overlay estimates more parameters than those rules.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: in-house models usually lose to the price
learnings.finding: Estimated mean-variance weights are the textbook case of estimation error. The paper's 13% net gain is a ratio on a portfolio whose premia have shrunk.
The 2015-2026 decisive window falls where most factor premia are about zero, leaving little for a conditional portfolio to time.

rows.missing_data: HXZ q-factors (ROE, IA) are not archived; they are free at global-q.org (to verify) and can be added as a separately counted run. The French library is not point-in-time (revisions). The authors' replication code is MATLAB (Mendeley) and is not needed.

registration.claim: Over 2015-01 to 2026-08, a monthly mean-variance portfolio of FF Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, UMD and AQR BAB whose factor weights are linear in the month-end market realised variance (w_t = a + b x RV_mkt,t, with a and b estimated each month on an expanding window from 1967 under an L1 turnover penalty at 10 bp per unit and trades netted across factors) earns a higher annualised net Sharpe ratio than the unconditional mean-variance portfolio estimated the same way, with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero.
registration.statistic: Annualised net Sharpe(conditional) minus net Sharpe(unconditional), monthly, paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks.
registration.procedure: Monthly factor returns compounded from daily. RV_mkt,t = sum of squared daily Mkt-RF over month t, known at the month-end close. At each month-end, (a, b) maximise expanding-window net mean-variance utility, with risk aversion fixed ex ante at 5 and the turnover penalty on netted factor trades. Weights apply to month t+1. Out-of-sample evaluation from 2000-01 is reported; the decisive window is 2015-01..2026-08. Comparators: the unconditional MV portfolio; Moreira-Muir per-factor scaling; T-388's static equal-risk portfolio. DSR over cost {10, 30 bp} x state {RV, VIX^2 from 1990} x penalty {on, off} = 8 trials, plus T-388's 5 and T-389's 5. The ETF arm 2013-2026 (SPY, IWM, QUAL, USMV at 2 bp; MTUM/VLUE if fetched) is reported.
registration.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, aqr-bab-daily, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 2015-01..2026-08 net Sharpe difference > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
registration.controls: Unconditional MV estimated the same way; static equal-risk; per-factor MM scaling; expanding windows only; turnover and gross-vs-net reported; paper factors are pre-cost, so the factor-level cost assumption is stated.

rows.notes: Testable now for the FF5+UMD+BAB version, with light compute (a monthly small convex program). It has the lowest prior of the factor rows: Mandel's own record says factor timing loses to static, and the window is short (140 months). Run it only after the Moreira-Muir and Wang-Yan rows, sharing their harness; do not fund the HXZ fetch unless those pass.

rows.name: Volatility targeting pays only where the leverage effect lives (equities and credit, not bonds, FX or commodities)

overlaps.note: The same scaled-vs-unscaled machinery on 8 assets. Per-asset DiD (TSMOM vs B&H): GLD +0.06, SLV +0.10, SPY -0.07, QQQ -0.09. Not the per-asset B&H gains this row needs.
Equity vol scaling helped QQQ (+0.21) but not IWM: within-equity heterogeneity.
Inverse-vol metals TSMOM, no gain over the historical mean.
Vol-scaled carry sleeves; the trailing-vol weighting blew up sleeves that sat in cash (weights 3.3-5.5).
VRPs differ by asset (T-50 gold and T-64 bonds supported; T-51 Nasdaq and T-65 Russell not), so implied-vol scalers behave differently across groups.

learnings.finding: Pooled vol-scaled B&H Sharpe 0.810 vs 0.632. Part of that is risk-parity diversification across sleeves, not timing, so asset-level B&H gains must be computed per asset.
A trailing-vol weight on a series with quiet spells gives extreme leverage. The cap must be fixed ex ante and binding.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: PnL from hundreds of observations cannot settle an edge
learnings.finding: A cross-asset DiD over 8.75 years with about 16 correlated assets has few effective independent units. Report power first.

rows.missing_data: None. FX carry accrual uses monthly OECD 3-month rates (lagged one month, as in T-368), not daily deposit rates. OANDA financing differs and is stated.

registration.claim: Over 2018-01 to 2026-09, the mean Sharpe gain from volatility targeting (position 0.10 / sigma_t from an EWMA of daily returns with a 20-day half-life at close t, capped at 2x, traded at close t+1, 2 bp per unit of turnover for ETFs and 1 bp for FX) across the risk-asset group SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM, HYG and LQD exceeds the mean gain across the non-risk group TLT, IEF, AGG, GLD, SLV, USO, DBC, DBA, UNG and the G10 USD pairs, with the asset-and-time block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of this difference-in-differences above zero.
registration.statistic: DiD = mean over risk assets of [Sharpe(scaled) - Sharpe(unscaled)] minus the same mean over non-risk assets, annualised excess-return Sharpe from daily returns; secondary: Spearman correlation between each asset's leverage-effect coefficient corr(r_t, RV_{t+1..t+21}), estimated 2007-07..2017-12, and its 2018-2026 Sharpe gain; change in 5% CVaR reported.
registration.procedure: Group membership fixed ex ante as listed (credit counted as risk, as in Harvey et al.). Daily adjclose excess over DTB3; FX return = spot change + interest differential accrued daily from the one-month-lagged OECD 3-month rates. sigma_t uses closed bars through t; trade at the close of t+1; turnover costed; financing above 1x at DTB3 + 50 bp (ETFs) or the rate differential (FX). Bootstrap: stationary 21-day time blocks drawn jointly for all assets, combined with resampling assets within each group, 5,000 draws. One primary specification; the paper-period 2007-07..2017-12 DiD is reported and must share the sign. Per-asset gains reported.
registration.data: daily-history-{SPY,QQQ,IWM,EFA,EEM,HYG,LQD,TLT,IEF,AGG,GLD,SLV,USO,DBC,DBA,UNG}, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3
