registration.controls: Unscaled positions on identical fills; constant-weight versions at each scaled series' mean weight; 2x cap fixed ex ante; costs on all turnover; vol-of-vol reduction and 5% CVaR reported for every asset (Harvey et al. predict tail reduction everywhere, which is not the claim).

rows.notes: A cheap extension of the Moreira-Muir harness, giving a falsifiable cross-asset prediction rather than another 'vol targeting helps' claim. Low power is the main risk. A pass is still only a risk-management finding (where to apply a vol overlay), not a return edge, which matches Mandel's lesson that structural features are worth more than price prediction.

rows.name: Economic value of better volatility forecasts: HAR with semivariances or implied vol versus EWMA in volatility targeting

overlaps.note: MSM beats HMM on QLIKE for SPY/QQQ/IWM, a forecast gain with no money attached.
Daily HMM refit beats yearly on QLIKE.
Using HAR forecasts to size short variance gave no significant Sharpe gain (p 0.292, PBO 0.343).
A better state forecaster (HMM) monetised on QQQ only.
Swapping EWMA, RV21, RV126 and Yang-Zhang changed the result by less than 0.05 Sharpe.
StockTwits adds nothing to a pooled HAR.
VPIN over HAR for BTC.

learnings.finding: QLIKE gains between forecasters are real and significant on these ETFs, so Stage 1 will likely pass.
Mandel has twice found the estimator choice economically irrelevant once costs and the target are fixed. That matches Harvey et al.'s insensitivity and predicts a Stage 2 failure.
The MSM's forecast edge over GARCH grows from 1 to 50 days, so the 21-day horizon is where a forecaster difference could matter. Include MSM as a reported forecaster.

rows.missing_data: None for daily. Yahoo ETF opens can be stale, so Garman-Klass needs a check against close-to-close squared returns. The 60-minute RV cross-check is limited to 2024-2026 (local ml_data bars).

registration.claim: For SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD and USO over 2015-01 to 2026-09, a 10%-volatility-target position (position at close t, traded at close t+1, cap 2x, 2 bp per unit of turnover) sized on a monthly-refitted HAR-family forecaster (HAR, SHAR with daily semivariances, or HAR-IV adding the matched Cboe implied-vol index) that first beats EWMA(0.94) on QLIKE earns a higher pooled net Sharpe ratio than the same position sized on EWMA(0.94), with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the pooled Sharpe difference above zero.
registration.statistic: Stage 1: mean QLIKE(forecaster) - QLIKE(EWMA) for 1-day and 21-day horizons, Diebold-Mariano, Holm across 6 assets x 2 horizons. Stage 2 (only forecasters passing Stage 1 on the pooled panel): pooled net Sharpe(forecaster-sized) - Sharpe(EWMA-sized), plus RMSE of realised vs target volatility.
registration.procedure: Realised-variance target proxy: Garman-Klass from daily OHLC, checked against squared close-to-close returns. Forecasters are refit monthly on an expanding window from 2004 (VXTLT/GVZ/OVX arms from their first archived prints plus 250 days). Implied indices enter at the Cboe 21:30 UTC available_at, so the decision at close t uses the prior session's implied print when t's is not yet out. Positions are computed at close t and executed at close t+1. Studentized circular block bootstrap with 63-day blocks, resampling all assets jointly. DSR across the forecasters entering Stage 2. Reported only: MSM (T-569) as an extra forecaster, and the 60-minute RV cross-check 2024-2026.
registration.data: daily-history-{SPY,QQQ,IWM,TLT,GLD,USO}, cboe-{VIX,VXN,RVX,VXTLT,GVZ,OVX}-history, fred-DTB3, mandel/ml_data/bars/60m
registration.pass: At least one forecaster with a Stage 1 pooled 21-day Holm p < 0.05, AND its Stage 2 pooled net Sharpe-difference lower 95% bound > 0 over 2015-01..2026-09, AND DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: EWMA baseline; constant weight at the same mean exposure; turnover per forecaster reported (a better forecast that trades more can lose net); all fits expanding-window.

rows.notes: Worth running only as an add-on to the Moreira-Muir / leverage-effect harness, because Mandel's record already predicts the answer (forecast gains do not become money). Its value is to close the open loop on T-569/T-572: they are supported forecasting results with no economic test.

rows.name: Statistical jump model regime switching (persistence-penalised) versus HMM for equity de-risking

overlaps.note: HMM month-end filter on PUT: MDD 10.4% vs 34.6% (-70%, null p 0.0002), Sharpe +0.731 vs +0.515 (diff +0.216, CI -0.184..+0.752). Drawdown yes, Sharpe CI no.
HMM vol scaling overnight: QQQ passes, IWM fails.
Frozen-HMM PUT forward shadow.
Frozen-HMM QQQM forward shadow.
10-month SMA timing on SPY: MDD 24.3% vs 52.9% (p 0.0081) and Sharpe +0.69 vs +0.57, but it failed Holm over 96 variants. Drawdown timing gains do not survive multiplicity.
MSM is the better volatility-state forecaster.
VIX/VIX3M regime does not separate the VRP.

learnings.finding: State models help where the state is measured directly. T-561's volatility state cut drawdowns 70%, while return-state chains (T-563, T-564) added nothing. The JM's features are volatility measures.

Both regime filters cut drawdowns significantly and raised point Sharpe by 0.1-0.2, but neither cleared a Sharpe CI or multiplicity. A JM pass on the Sharpe clause needs a larger effect than either produced.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: PnL cannot settle edges; decay
learnings.finding: The JM result comes from a single research group, and the 2024-2026 post-publication window is about 2 years. Only the pre-registered decisive window counts.

rows.missing_data: None for arm A. Arm B (VIX/VIX3M features) can only start in 2010, because the archived VIX3M begins 2009-09-18. The jump-model fit (k-means-like coordinate descent with a switch penalty) needs a small implementation or the open-source 'jumpmodels' package. The compute is light but must not run while the LightGBM job holds the CPUs.

registration.claim: On SPY total return 1994-01 to 2026-09, holding SPY only while a two-state statistical jump model (features: EWM downside deviation with half-life 10 and EWM Sortino ratios with half-lives 20 and 60 of daily excess returns; trained on the 12 years before an 8-year validation window, with the jump penalty chosen each month as the value with the best validation Sharpe) estimated at close t puts day t in the good state, and 3-month bills otherwise, with the switch applied at close t+2 and 10 bp per one-way trade, earns a higher annualised excess-return Sharpe ratio than buy-and-hold SPY, with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero.
registration.statistic: Annualised Sharpe(JM-timed excess) - Sharpe(buy-and-hold excess), daily, paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 63-day blocks; secondary: JM minus T-561's frozen HMM rule applied to SPY with the same lag, and the maximum-drawdown ratio.
registration.procedure: Feature history from ^GSPC price returns and FF Mkt-RF from 1978, so the first 20-year train-plus-validation window ends before 1994. Live series: SPY adjclose from 1994-01, cash at DTB3 accrued daily. Each month the model is refit on training data ending at the validation start, and the penalty is selected on validation data ending at t. State inference at close t uses features through t only (online inference, never the smoothed path). The trade lands at the t+2 close and costs 10 bp per switch. Replication window 1990-2023 on ^GSPC price + DTB3 cash, reported against the paper. Arm B (EWM downside deviation, VIX z-score, VIX/VIX3M; 2010-2026) is a separately counted trial. A 1- and 5-day delay sensitivity is reported. DSR counts arms A/B, the three delays, T-561 and T-562. The spell-preserving random-timing MDD null (as T-301/T-561) is reported.
registration.data: daily-history-SPY, daily-history--GSPC, french-ff3-daily, fred-DTB3, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history
registration.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 1994-01..2026-09 Sharpe difference > 0, AND the 2015-01..2026-09 point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: Buy-and-hold; T-561's frozen HMM rule; T-301's 10-month SMA; the matched random-timing null for drawdown; switches per year and time in market reported; no smoothed (look-ahead) state paths; the penalty grid is declared before running and is part of the method.

rows.notes: The natural successor to T-561/T-562, and the web evidence (persistence penalty > state model) fits Mandel's own finding that volatility-state filters cut drawdowns. Expect the drawdown result to replicate and the Sharpe CI to be the binding clause. A drawdown-only pass would be recorded like T-561: useful as a risk overlay, not an edge.

rows.name: Cross-sectional skewness dispersion (and average skewness) predicts the stock market, concentrated in FOMC months

overlaps.note: CBOE SKEW does not predict crashes (wrong sign).
SKEW-conditioned tail frequency is not higher.
No FOMC-day SPY premium.
No macro-announcement-day premium.
No post-FOMC monetary momentum.
No FOMC-cycle even-week effect.
An aggregate fund-flow market predictor fails, with halves flipping sign.
Sentiment predictor: OOS R^2 -8.58%.

learnings.source: Mandel FOMC family (T-215, T-341, T-342, T-343, T-361)
learnings.finding: Every FOMC-calendar effect on SPY tested 1994-2026 failed. A predictor whose power lives only in FOMC months contradicts that record.
Aggregate predictors of the equity premium fail out of sample in Mandel's tests (Goyal-Welch pattern).

The 901-stock daily panel is survivor-only: about 480 names reach back to 2000, nearly all of them current survivors. A firm-skewness cross-section built from it is biased against crash-prone names, so the stock-level arm is a NOT-JUDGED diagnostic. The survivorship-free proxy is the FF 49 industries.
Return asymmetry measured from realised returns did carry information in 2009-2026, where option-implied skew failed.

rows.missing_data: The paper's construct needs firm-level 5-minute returns for about 6,770 stocks (no free source) or at least a survivorship-free daily stock cross-section (CRSP-equivalent, not free). Registered here is the survivorship-free industry proxy (FF49 daily, archived), with the 901-stock survivor panel and the 60-minute bars on about 60 stocks as reported-only diagnostics.

registration.claim: Over 2005-01 to 2026-08, the month-end cross-sectional 75th-minus-25th percentile spread of realised skewness across the 49 Fama-French industry portfolios (each industry's skewness from its prior 21 daily returns, averaged over the month's last 5 sessions) negatively predicts the next-month SPY excess return out of sample, with an expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 above zero against the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05) and a negative slope in months containing a scheduled FOMC decision.
registration.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 of the next-month SPY excess return (expanding OLS) vs the expanding historical mean, Clark-West one-sided test; FOMC-split slope (interaction with a scheduled-decision-month dummy from fomc-meetings); 3-month horizon with Hodrick SEs reported.
registration.null: OOS R^2 <= 0 (Clark-West), or the FOMC-month slope >= 0.
registration.procedure: The signal is known at the month-end close (FF49 daily returns through that close); the target is SPY total return from that close to the next month-end close, less DTB3. Training starts 1970 on FF Mkt-RF+RF as the target before SPY exists; the first OOS forecast is 2005-01. FOMC months are scheduled decisions only (available_at = meeting start). The second signal, the equal-weighted average industry skewness (JZZ-style), is counted as a trial. DSR over 2 signals x 3 horizons for the reported trading arm (SPY weight in [0, 1.5] from the gamma-3 mean-variance rule, monthly, 2 bp, financing DTB3 + 50 bp). The post-paper window 2023-01..2026-08 (44 months) is reported with its power. Survivor-stock and 60-minute versions are reported only (rule 9).
registration.data: french-industry49-daily, french-ff3-daily, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3, fomc-meetings
registration.pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over 2005-01..2026-08, AND the FOMC-month slope < 0.
registration.controls: Historical-mean benchmark; JZZ average skewness; a placebo with the signal shifted 12 months; the correlation between the industry and survivor-stock signals reported, to show what the proxy captures; industry portfolios diversify idiosyncratic skew, so a failure here does not refute the firm-level claim (stated).

rows.notes: The source is a new working paper (April 2026), unreplicated, whose own out-of-sample test finds the older average-skewness measure weak. Mandel's FOMC and aggregate-predictor records both argue against it. The testable proxy changes the construct (industry, not firm, skewness), so treat it as cheap triage, not a refutation. The firm-level test stays blocked until a point-in-time stock universe exists.

rows.name: Cross-sectional tail risk (Kelly-Jiang) as a market-return predictor

overlaps.note: Option-implied tail measure (SKEW) does not forecast drops.
SKEW-conditioned tail frequency not higher.
SKEW-implied tail probability 8.54% vs realised 1.05%: tail insurance is overpriced, which fits a tail-risk premium.
Aggregate market-return predictor fails out of sample.
Sentiment market predictor OOS R^2 -8.58%.
Aggregate short interest as a market predictor, also blocked on cross-sectional coverage.

learnings.finding: Tail insurance is priced well above realised tail frequency, consistent with a tail-risk premium existing, though it says nothing about time-varying predictability.

A survivor-only panel drops exactly the delisted crashers that drive the left-tail Hill exponent, worst in the early years. The signal would be biased in a time-varying way, so the archive cannot test this claim.
Aggregate predictors fail out of sample, and a 12-month horizon over 2011-2026 has only about 15 independent observations.

rows.missing_data: A survivorship-free daily return cross-section of all US common stocks, including delisted names (CRSP or equivalent; no free full source; partial free sources such as Stooq lack reliable delisting coverage). Without it the Hill exponent is mismeasured where it matters.

registration.claim: Over 2000-01 to 2026-08, the month-end Kelly-Jiang tail exponent (the Hill estimator on all US common-stock daily returns in month t below that month's cross-sectional 5th percentile, smoothed over 3 months) positively predicts the SPY excess return over the next 12 months, with an expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 above zero against the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05) and a positive Hodrick-t slope over 2011-2026.
registration.statistic: Predictive slope of the next 1-, 3- and 12-month SPY excess return on the standardised exponent, Hodrick (1992) SEs for overlap; Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2 from 2000 with Clark-West.
registration.procedure: Pooled stock-day returns in month t below the cross-sectional 5th percentile; Hill exponent with a threshold at the 5th percentile; 3-month moving average. Known at the last close of t; the target starts at that close. Expanding OLS from 1965 if a CRSP-equivalent panel is obtained. Power (independent 12-month observations after 2011) is reported before reading. The trading arm (SPY weight 1 + 0.5 z clipped to [0.5, 1.5], monthly, 2 bp, financing DTB3 + 50 bp) is reported with DSR over 3 horizons. The 901-symbol survivor version is a rule-9 diagnostic only.
registration.data: a survivorship-free US stock daily panel (not archived); daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3
registration.pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over 2000-01..2026-08, AND the 2011-2026 Hodrick slope > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05.
registration.controls: Historical mean; VIX level and realised market kurtosis as competing predictors; the survivorship direction stated (biases the exponent toward thinner tails); a 12-month-shift placebo.

rows.notes: Blocked: the archive's stock panel is survivor-only, and the measure is built from the very names survivorship deletes. Replication and decay were unchecked by the web sweep. Mandel's aggregate-predictor record is negative. Lowest priority; keep it registered as blocked so a future point-in-time universe unlocks it.

rows.name: Variance risk premium as an equity-return predictor (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou), tested for its post-2010 decline

overlaps.note: The VRP exists: implied 21.0 vs realised 18.6 vol pts, positive on 84% of days, 1993-2026.
BTZ anchor: mean (VIX^2 - RV21)/12 = +12.5 %^2/month 1990-2007 close-to-close (BTZ about 18 with intraday RV).
Top tercile of VIX - RV21 raises short-straddle P&L by +10.8 pts of premium (CI +2.6..+20.7): the VRP level carries information about subsequent variance outcomes.
VRP conditioning by the VIX/VIX3M regime fails.
HAR-based VRP z-scaling of short variance: no significant Sharpe gain.
A forward VRP exists at 1-3 months (also T-510).

learnings.finding: The level VRP is robust in Mandel's data at 1- and 3-month tenors, so the predictor is well measured from archived VIX and ^GSPC closes.
VRP-conditioning helped option-selling P&L out of sample (CI above 0), but the claim's full interval test was inconclusive. VRP timing has at least a positive option-side footprint.
Two VRP-conditioned rules failed. Conditioning on the VRP does not reliably earn money once trials and costs are counted.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: structural premia (VRP) are among the edges that exist
learnings.finding: The VRP is one of the structural premia Mandel's lessons rank above price-only signals. That supports testing it as a timing input, while the Dew-Becker-Giglio decline predicts a post-2010 failure.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: Deribit candle look-ahead landmine
learnings.finding: VIX closes at 16:15 ET and SPY at 16:00 ET. The signal must trade at the next session's close, or the 15-minute gap leaks.

rows.missing_data: None. BTZ's 5-minute RV is not archived before 2023-11; daily squared returns (and a Parkinson range variant) are the archived proxies, which make the VRP smaller and noisier than BTZ's, as stated in T-123.

registration.claim: Over 2010-01 to 2026-09, the month-end variance risk premium VRP_t = (VIX_t/100)^2/12 minus the sum of squared daily ^GSPC log returns over the 21 sessions ending at t positively predicts the SPY excess return over the next 3 months, measured from the next session's close, with a one-sided Hodrick (1992) p < 0.05 on the slope and an expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 above zero against the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05).
registration.statistic: Slope of the 3-month SPY excess return on standardised VRP_t, Hodrick SEs; Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2 with Clark-West, OOS forecasts over 2010-01..2026-09; reported: the paired difference between the 1990-2009 and 2010-2026 slopes.
registration.procedure: VIX close at the last session of month t (Cboe 16:15 ET, available_at 21:30 UTC) and ^GSPC closes for RV. The target is SPY adjclose from the next session's close over 63 sessions, less DTB3. Expanding OLS from 1990-02, with the first OOS forecast after 120 months of training. Declared trials: horizon {1, 3 months} x RV estimator {daily squared returns, Parkinson range} = 4, DSR over them. Reported trading arm: SPY weight 0.5/1.0/1.5 by expanding-window VRP terciles (cut-points from data through t), monthly, 2 bp, financing DTB3 + 50 bp; Sharpe difference vs buy-and-hold. Sensitivity excluding 2020-03..2020-06 reported.
registration.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: 2010-01..2026-09: slope > 0 with Hodrick one-sided p < 0.05, AND OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05, AND DSR > 0.95 over the 4 trials.
registration.controls: VIX^2 level alone and RV alone as competing predictors (the VRP must beat both components); the historical-mean benchmark; a placebo with the signal shifted one year; one-day execution delay; the 1990-2009 window reported so the record says which half the predictability lives in.

rows.notes: Cheap (archived series only) and informative whichever way it goes: Mandel has established the VRP's existence but never its timing value. A failure in 2010-2026 alongside a 1990-2009 pass would confirm the Dew-Becker-Giglio decline in Mandel's own ledger. Keep the trading arm reported only, because the predictive regression is the claim.

rows.name: Realised skewness and relative signed jump variation in the cross-section (Amaya et al.; Bollerslev-Li-Zhao)

overlaps.note: Volume-based cross-sectional anomaly on ETFs/crypto failed.
Crypto high-volume premium failed.
Retail order imbalance (the 'other side' of lottery demand) is blocked on data.
Retail attention vs abs return.
Reported: realised-skewness differences are informative in 2009-2026 at the index level.

learnings.finding: Any cross-sectional stock test on the archive is survivor-only and gets NOT JUDGED. The decisive arm needs point-in-time constituents.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: published anomalies decay; Hou-Xue-Zhang
learnings.finding: Daily-skewness versions fail with NYSE breakpoints and value weighting. The intraday versions are untested after 2015 and should be expected to decay.
Intraday ML on 5-60 minute bars found 0 of 276 cells passing, with weekly-horizon costs dominating. A 1-week hold at 10-20 bp per side needs a gross spread above about 40 bp a week.

rows.missing_data: 5-minute (or 1-minute) bars for point-in-time S&P 500 + S&P 400 constituents 2018-2026. Alpaca's free tier is believed to serve historical minute bars from about 2016 (IEX vs SIP coverage to verify). Point-in-time constituent lists are also needed (the S&P adds fetch in batch 6c may help). Local intraday bars cover about 60 single stocks for 60 days at 5 minutes and 2 years at 60 minutes, which is too few names and too short.

registration.claim: Over 2018-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 and S&P 400 constituents, the value-weighted portfolio long the bottom decile and short the top decile of weekly relative signed jump variation RSJ = (RV+ - RV-)/RV from 5-minute returns (Wednesday close to Wednesday close, one session skipped, held one week) earns a positive mean weekly return net of 10 bp per side for large caps, 20 bp for mid caps and 50 bp a year borrow, with Newey-West t > 2.
registration.statistic: Mean weekly net long-short return, Newey-West t (4 lags); FF5+UMD alpha reported; DSR over {RSK, RSJ, RKT} x {value, equal weight} = 6 trials.
registration.procedure: Constituent membership as of each formation date. 5-minute returns within regular hours; overnight returns are excluded from RV+ and RV- and reported separately. The signal is known at the Wednesday close; positions are opened at the Thursday close (one session skipped) and held to the next Thursday close. Costs per side by cap bucket plus borrow on shorts. Pilot (testable now, reported only, not the claim): weekly value-weighted aggregate ARSJ of the 9 original sector SPDRs from 60-minute bars 2024-2026 predicting next-week SPY excess return. A daily-return-skewness version on the 901-symbol survivor panel is a separate claim, expected to fail per Hou-Xue-Zhang.
registration.data: constituent minute bars (not archived), point-in-time S&P 500/400 membership (not archived), fred-DTB3; pilot: mandel/ml_data/bars/60m
registration.pass: Net mean weekly return > 0 with Newey-West t > 2 over 2018-01..2026-09, AND DSR > 0.95 over the 6 trials.
registration.controls: Gross vs net reported; short-term reversal (1-week return) as a control regressor, since RSJ correlates with the past week's return; value-weighted primary; cap-bucket costs; survivorship-free membership required.

rows.notes: Blocked on intraday constituent data. The aggregate 60-minute pilot is testable now but has about 100 weekly observations, so it is triage only. A 1-week single-stock long-short faces about 40-60 bp of round-trip cost a week against published gross spreads of 19-24 bp, and that was before post-publication decay, so the net prior is low even before data.

rows.name: Volatility-of-volatility (uncertainty about risk) predicts lower returns: Baltussen et al., testable on Cboe vol indices now and on captured chains later

overlaps.note: The VVIX premium over realised VIX vol is negative: VVIX prices VIX futures, not spot. A different claim.
VVIX - realised spot-VIX vol is -22.4 pts.
F3 includes log VVIX and per-asset implied-vol features. Its IC scan will touch the same inputs but not the vol-of-vol construct.
The low-volatility anomaly (USMV vs SPY) does not survive post-ETF.
The same low-vol claim, re-run.

learnings.finding: A volatility-sorted anomaly that was strong pre-publication failed in Mandel's post-2011 data. Uncertainty-based anomalies are in the same family.

Index vol-of-vol behaves unlike spot. Cboe vol indices are option-implied variance levels, so their daily log changes are smoother than chain ATM IV changes, and the pilot's input differs from the paper's.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: PnL from hundreds of bets cannot settle an edge
learnings.finding: 11 underlyings x about 180 months give a cross-section too narrow for a monthly rank IC to have power. Stage A is a pilot; Stage B (forward chains) is the real test and needs 24+ months.

rows.missing_data: Stage A needs nothing more. Stage B needs a daily single-stock option-chain history: archived chains are only 2026-10-14/15, the capture box records forward, so 24 months come no earlier than 2028-10. A point-in-time optionable universe is also needed.

registration.claim: Over 2011-07 to 2026-09, across the 11 underlyings with Cboe implied-volatility indices (SPY/VIX, QQQ/VXN, IWM/RVX, DIA/VXD, EEM/VXEEM, TLT/VXTLT, GLD/GVZ, USO/OVX, AAPL/VXAPL, GOOGL/VXGOG, AMZN/VXAZN), the month-end vol-of-vol (the standard deviation of daily log changes of the index over the prior 21 sessions divided by the index's mean level, standardised against its own expanding history) has a negative mean monthly Spearman rank correlation with the next month's excess return of the underlying, with a block-bootstrap one-sided p < 0.05.
registration.statistic: Mean over months of the cross-sectional Spearman IC between standardised vol-of-vol at month-end t and the underlying's excess return from the next close to the following month-end; circular block bootstrap over months (6-month blocks); secondary (reported): bottom-third minus top-third equal-weight book at 5 bp per side.
registration.procedure: Cboe closes enter at available_at 21:30 UTC, so returns start at the next session's close. Each underlying's vol-of-vol is z-scored on its own expanding history (from 252 days after its index's first print), so that asset-class level differences do not drive the ranks. Underlyings enter as their index history allows (at least 8 in every month from 2011-07). Both halves reported. Stage B is pre-registered now as a separate forward claim: 30-day ATM IV from the capture box's daily chains for every optionable US stock with open interest above a floor; vol-of-vol as in Baltussen et al.; value-weighted quintiles; 1-month hold; 10 bp per side; FF5+UMD alpha; read when 24 months exist.
registration.data: cboe-{VIX,VXN,RVX,VXD,VXEEM,VXTLT,GVZ,OVX,VXAPL,VXGOG,VXAZN}-history, daily-history-{SPY,QQQ,IWM,DIA,EEM,TLT,GLD,USO,AAPL,GOOGL,AMZN}, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Mean IC < 0 with block-bootstrap one-sided p < 0.05, AND the IC negative in both halves (2011-07..2018-12 and 2019-01..2026-09).
registration.controls: The same IC on the implied-vol level (to separate vol-of-vol from the low-vol effect); a placebo with vol-of-vol shifted 12 months; own-history standardisation fixed ex ante; one threshold, no grid.

rows.notes: Stage A is cheap and testable now but is a pilot. It is cross-asset rather than the paper's cross-section of stocks, and 11 names give little power. Its main value is to pre-register Stage B before the capture box accumulates chains, so that the forward test is clean. A Stage A pass should go to the T-579/T-580 IC family as a confirmed-sign input, not to trading.

rows.name: Commodity term-structure carry (roll yield / basis) on energy and metals, using EIA's free contract 1-4 curves

overlaps.note: Cross-sectional roll-yield sort over at least 15 commodities, blocked on curves. This row is a time-series version on 4 energy contracts that EIA's free curves unblock.
Cross-asset carry composite Sharpe -0.199. It contained no commodity sleeve.
Metals implied financing equals bills, so metals carry is about zero, which fits the candidate's focus on energy.
Commodity ETF momentum fails 2012-2026.
Brent-WTI spread reversion fails.
The oil VRP exists, a structural premium in the same complex.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md / Mandel lessons: structural premia (carry) are among the edges that exist
learnings.finding: Carry is the right class of edge by Mandel's own triage. Energy backwardation is a hedging-pressure premium with an identified other side (mechanical index and ETF rollers).
Every carry sleeve Mandel could build over 2013-2026 (FX, bonds, country equity) failed. Post-2013 carry has been weak across asset classes.

Dotsis-Psychoyios attribute USO's underperformance to prolonged post-2009 contango, supporting the roll-drag side. The library also lists a testable-now proxy: UNG/USO return minus FRED spot on prior-month contango.
Futures-plus-bills minus ETF gaps exist in gold (+1.07%/yr) but are financing effects, not carry. Keep energy carry separate from ETF wrapper drag.

rows.missing_data: EIA daily NYMEX contract 1-4 settlements for WTI (1983-), heating oil, RBOB (2005-) and Henry Hub (1994-). They are free from EIA (dnav CSVs / API v2) but end 2024-04-05 and are not archived. A going-forward curve source is also needed for anything live: CME settlements (DataMine is paid) or per-contract Yahoo tickers (free but only for listed contracts). Metals curves are not covered by EIA.

registration.claim: Over 2012-01 to 2024-03, for WTI crude, heating oil, RBOB gasoline and Henry Hub natural gas, holding the rolled front-month future long in months after a month-end at which the annualised log(F1/F2) from EIA's contract 1 and 2 settlements is positive (backwardation), and flat otherwise, earns a higher pooled mean monthly excess return than always holding the rolled front month, net of one tick per side per roll and $2.50 per contract, with the commodity-clustered block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero.
registration.statistic: Pooled (equal-weight across 4 commodities) mean monthly excess return of the carry rule minus always-long; block bootstrap over months (6-month blocks) drawn jointly across commodities.
registration.procedure: Rolled excess-return series from EIA contract 1/2 settlements, rolling from contract 1 to contract 2 five business days before contract 1's last trade, with returns on the held contract, never spot. The signal is the month-end basis annualised by the days between contract 1 and 2 expiries, known at the settlement (14:30 ET for CL) and acted on at the next settlement. Arm A is long/flat (primary); arm B is long/short (counted trial). Costs as stated. A 1994-2011 window is reported. DSR over 2 arms x 2 roll offsets {5, 10 days}. A cross-sectional version waits for 15+ curves (T-371). The reported ETF arm: USO/UGA/UNG/BNO at 5 bp per side by the same signal.
registration.data: EIA contract 1-4 settlements (to fetch), fred-DTB3, daily-history-{USO,UGA,UNG,BNO} for the reported ETF arm
registration.pass: Pooled mean-difference lower 95% bound > 0 over 2012-01..2024-03, AND the difference positive in at least 3 of 4 commodities, AND DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: Always-long rolled front; a placebo with the signal lagged 12 months; roll-date sensitivity; the 4 contracts are highly correlated, so the effective sample is reported; a curve source that runs past 2024-04 must be verified before any live claim.

rows.notes: High-value unblock: one free fetch (EIA) turns a blocked family (T-371) into testable time-series and basis-momentum claims, and carry is a class Mandel's lessons favour. The risk is that energy carry is mostly a 2014-2016 and 2020 contango story with 4 correlated series. Executable on CME micro futures (MCL, MNG) under US rules; no geoblock issue.

rows.name: Basis-momentum in futures curves (Boons-Prado)

overlaps.note: The library already lists basis-momentum as a T-371 variant; blocked on curves.
Gated VX M1-M2 calendar: $3.9/day, CI [-9.8, 16.8].
Contango-gated short VIX ETP fails.
SVXY contango filter: Sharpe diff -0.18.
VIX falls more from backwardation than from contango, so the VX curve has forecastable dynamics.
Spot VIX ends below the forward-implied level 79% of contango months, so the VX curve carries a term premium.

learnings.finding: Three VX curve-carry rules failed after costs in 2013-2026 even though the term premium exists (T-534). VX curve signals have not survived trading costs in Mandel.
VX curve dynamics are forecastable on average, so a maturity-specific pressure signal is not implausible on VX.
Basis-momentum's 12-month ranking window is fragile across subperiods. Pre-register one lookback.

rows.missing_data: Arm A needs EIA contract 1-4 settlements (free, not archived, ending 2024-04-05), as in the EIA carry row. Arm B (VX M1/M2) is testable now from cboe-vx-futures (2013-05 onward).

registration.claim: Over 2012-01 to 2024-03, for WTI crude, heating oil, RBOB gasoline and Henry Hub natural gas, the month-end basis-momentum (the 12-month cumulative return of the rolled first-nearby future minus that of the rolled second-nearby, from EIA contract 1 and 2 settlements) positively predicts the next month's rolled first-nearby excess return in a pooled regression with commodity fixed effects and month-clustered errors (one-sided p < 0.05), and the sign rule (long if positive, short if negative) earns a higher net Sharpe ratio than always-long after one tick per leg per trade plus fees.
registration.statistic: Pooled slope of the next-month nearby excess return on standardised BM with commodity fixed effects, month-clustered SEs; secondary: the net Sharpe of the sign rule minus always-long (paired block bootstrap, 6-month blocks).
registration.procedure: Rolled nearby and second-nearby series built as in the EIA carry row (roll 5 business days before expiry, returns on held contracts). BM uses the 12 months through month-end t only, known at that settlement; the position applies from the next settlement. A spreading arm (long C1 / short C2 by sign of BM) is reported. Arm B, pre-registered as a separate claim: the same BM on Cboe VX M1/M2 rolled series 2013-05..2026-09 predicting the next-month VX M1 excess return, monthly, $2/contract/leg, counted with the T-160/T-379/T-435 family in its DSR. DSR over arms. The effective sample of the 4 correlated energy contracts is reported.
registration.data: EIA contract 1-2 settlements (to fetch), cboe-vx-futures, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Arm A: pooled slope > 0 with month-clustered one-sided p < 0.05 over 2012-01..2024-03, AND the sign rule's net Sharpe minus always-long > 0, AND DSR > 0.95.
registration.controls: Basis (F1/F2 level) and 12-month nearby momentum as competing regressors (BM must add to both); one lookback (12 months), no grid; a placebo shift; costs per leg.

rows.notes: Arm A shares the EIA fetch with the carry row and should be run in the same harness. Arm B is testable now on VX, but Mandel's three VX carry failures make its prior lower (about 0.06). Register both arms before either is read, and keep the VX arm in the VX family's trial count.

rows.name: COT hedging pressure and hedgers' short-term liquidity provision in commodity futures

overlaps.note: Gold managed-money z-score extremes, point in time: tail difference +0.04% (CI -2.90%..+2.70%), slope NW t +0.55. Parked for too few extremes, with no effect visible.
Gold managed-money above the trailing-3-year 90th percentile.
Positioning or sentiment from BTC funding does not predict returns.
Commodity carry, whose premium hedging pressure is meant to explain.

learnings.finding: Mandel's point-in-time COT handling is already built (release-time available_at, backcast weeks dropped, superseded reports), and on gold the positioning signal showed nothing (slope t +0.55).
Reports released late (2013 and 2022 shutdowns) carry Socrata bulk-load stamps. The point-in-time rules must use release time, not the as-of Tuesday, or the KRT 1-week effect is unusable look-ahead.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: reference-price edges lead the book
learnings.finding: COT data is published with a 3-day lag to everyone. A flow effect that lives inside the Tuesday-to-Friday gap cannot be traded, so the diagnostic rerun from the as-of date measures how much of the published effect is lost.

rows.missing_data: CFTC Socrata legacy and disaggregated futures-only reports for the other ~16 contracts (free, same recipe as the archived gold and silver bundles). Rolled front-month return series for NG, HO, RB, ZC, ZW, ZS, ZM, ZL, KC, SB, CC, CT, LE and HE: Yahoo =F continuous series are free but not archived, have undocumented roll days (T-555's caveat) and need roll-gap removal. ETF proxies (CORN, WEAT, SOYB, DBA, UNG, USO) are partly archived.

registration.claim: Over 2015-01 to 2026-09, across 18 US commodity futures, a weekly portfolio long the top quintile and short the bottom quintile of the 1-week change in commercial net long / open interest from the CFTC legacy futures-only report, entered at the first close after the report's Friday 15:30 ET release and held 4 weeks in overlapping weekly cohorts, earns a positive mean net return per 4-week hold after one tick plus $2.50 per contract per side, with the block-bootstrap 95% lower bound above zero.
registration.statistic: Mean net 4-week long-short return over overlapping weekly cohorts (each cohort 1/4 of capital), circular block bootstrap with 8-week blocks; secondary: the Basu-Miffre level signal (52-week average commercial net short / OI) as a counted trial.
registration.procedure: available_at = the actual release time per report (the Friday 15:30 ET schedule, later for shutdown delays; Socrata stamps kept when later, as in T-405). Entry at the first settlement or close after available_at; rolled front-month returns with roll gaps removed (5 business days before first notice), or ETF proxies at 5 bp per side where futures are unavailable. Equal weight within quintiles. A diagnostic reruns from the Tuesday as-of date (not tradable) to measure the release-lag loss. DSR over 2 signals x 2 holds {1, 4 weeks} x 2 entry timings {Friday close, Monday close} = 8. Decisive window 2015-01..2026-09; 2006-2014 reported.
registration.data: CFTC legacy and disaggregated reports for 18 contracts (fetch), Yahoo continuous futures (fetch), daily-history-{CL-F,GC-F,SI-F,HG-F,USO,UNG,DBA}, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: Mean net 4-week return lower 95% bound > 0 over 2015-01..2026-09 (overlapping weekly cohorts), AND DSR > 0.95 over the 8 trials.
registration.controls: Equal-weight long-all-commodities baseline; a 1-week return reversal control (KRT's flow effect partly mirrors price reversal); release-time point-in-time stamps; costs per contract.

rows.notes: The fetch is cheap because the CFTC recipe exists, but Mandel's one point-in-time COT test (gold) saw no effect, and the KRT flow effect may sit inside the publication lag. Worth fetching mainly because the same COT and rolled-futures data also feed the EIA carry and basis-momentum rows and give hedging-pressure controls.

rows.name: ML predictors that survive costs: price-free features, longer horizons, no microcaps, cost-aware objective

overlaps.note: 306 daily cells, 0 pass. Best DSR 0.54 (equity_etf 20-day F0 GBM, +129 bp per hold); F0 mean IC +0.011. The 20-day stock and ETF region is strongest but rests on 9 non-overlapping periods.
276 intraday cells, 0 pass.
The IC scan with BH discovery and confirmation (inverse relationships included).
Implied-variable family F3.
Days-to-cover decile spread net -0.048%/period; NOT JUDGED because the universe is survivor-only.
DTC vs borrow-fee threshold: NOT JUDGED (90.9% of the FINRA universe unpriced).
Net share issuance spread +0.30%/month, CI spans 0, post-publication.
An MLP no better than logit on market features.

learnings.finding: Longer holds were Mandel's strongest ML region (20-day cells beat always-long), which agrees with the Robeco term-structure-of-ML-alpha result. But the development window is 9 months, so DSR over 306 trials cannot reach 0.95 without implausible Sharpe.

The archived stock universe is survivor-only and covers about 9% of the FINRA universe, with about 568 names holding point-in-time SEC shares. A cross-sectional ML book on it is NOT JUDGED by house rules.

learnings.source: child CLAUDE.md: in-house models usually lose to the price; calibrated is not profitable
learnings.finding: The children's Elo/Markov models carried no information the price lacked. Gross ML predictability (IC about 0.01-0.04) is the same order as Mandel's F0 IC and is eaten by costs.
The slow price-free anomaly inputs the candidate relies on (issuance, quality, investment) have near-zero post-publication premia in Mandel's data.
FINRA short interest starts 2017-12 and RegSHO 2018-08, so the development window cannot begin in 2012 as proposed. It is about 2018-07..2025-09, roughly 85 monthly decisions.

rows.missing_data: Four gaps: (1) a survivorship-free point-in-time US stock universe with prices for delisted names (no free full source); (2) NYSE market-cap breakpoints (free from the French library's ME_Breakpoints, not archived); (3) FINRA and RegSHO history before 2017-12/2018-08 (does not exist free); (4) time, because a 3-month target's lockbox from 2026-10 needs at least 6-12 months to accumulate reads. Analyst revisions and insider filings named as adjacent inputs are blocked (T-396) or partly archived (SEC Form 4 is in sec-submissions only as filing metadata).

registration.claim: On US stocks above the NYSE 20th market-cap percentile at each month-end, with a 2018-07 to 2025-09 development walk-forward and the sealed lockbox from 2026-10, a ridge or gradient-boosting model refit annually on price-free features each stamped at publication (FINRA short interest and days to cover at the FINRA release date, the 20-day RegSHO short-volume ratio, the 12-month change in SEC shares outstanding at filing acceptance, days to the next expected 10-Q/10-K, realised volatility, downside semivariance, skewness, dollar volume and sector), predicting the 3-month excess return and traded as a value-weighted top-minus-bottom quintile book in 3 overlapping monthly tranches net of 10 bp per side above the NYSE median cap, 25 bp below and 50 bp a year borrow, has a development DSR of at least 0.95 counting every T-577, T-578 and T-580 cell plus these, and a positive lockbox mean net return.
registration.statistic: Per cell (model x horizon {3, 6 months}): development net Sharpe of the tranche book, DSR over all ML-program cells; lockbox mean net monthly return; reported: feature importance by net contribution (Jensen-Kelly-Malamud-Pedersen style).
registration.null: No cell passes both the development DSR and the lockbox.
registration.procedure: Universe at each month-end t: names with a point-in-time price at t-1 and SEC cover shares filed before t, cap = shares x close(t-1), above the NYSE 20th-percentile breakpoint for t. Features use only values whose available_at <= t: FINRA SI at its publication date (not settlement), RegSHO at end of the trade day, SEC facts at filing acceptance, earnings proximity from the 10-Q/10-K filing cadence. No past-return momentum features, which keeps price isolated as the target. Target: excess return from the close after t over 63 (126) sessions. Annual refit on an expanding window, with rows purged unless their target window ends before the fit date. Jegadeesh-Titman tranches; costs and borrow as stated. The lockbox opens only after development is final. Rule 9: if the universe coverage check fails (a point-in-time universe missing), every return criterion is NOT JUDGED.
registration.data: finra-short-interest, finra-regsho-cnms, sec-companyfacts, sec-submissions, daily-history-*, fred-DTB3, NYSE ME breakpoints (to fetch), a survivorship-free price panel (missing)
registration.pass: Some cell with development DSR >= 0.95 (N = all ML-program cells) AND a positive lockbox mean net return over at least 12 lockbox months; a survivor goes to a separately pre-registered forward paper record, never directly live.
registration.controls: Baselines: always-long the universe and a single-feature days-to-cover sort (T-393's rule) on the same tranches; family ablation (drop short-interest features, drop issuance); costs by cap bucket; turnover reported; the universe-coverage check is a gate, not a footnote.

rows.notes: The design lessons are right and should shape the T-578 successor: longer horizons, liquid names, price-free inputs stamped at publication, a cost-aware objective and overlapping tranches. As a test, though, it is blocked by the survivor-only universe (rule 9 would mark it NOT JUDGED, as with T-393/T-375) and by FINRA history starting in 2017-12. A feasible near-term variant extends T-578's ETF classes to 63-day holds on the same features (survivorship-free) with the trial count carried over. Prior stays low because every Mandel ML and slow-anomaly result so far is negative.

rows.name: Volatility-managed market exposure (Moreira-Muir), judged in real time and after costs
rows.source_notes: Opened: NBER w22208 page (Moreira & Muir 2016 WP, JF 2017). The abstract confirms 'large alphas' and higher factor Sharpe ratios but gives no numbers, so the 4-5%/yr market alpha is unverified. Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan, JFE 138(1) 2020, confirmed via IDEAS: managed portfolios do not systematically beat unmanaged ones in direct comparisons; spanning alphas are not implementable in real time; the cause is structural instability. The '50 of 103' count is unverified because the author PDF returned HTTP 500. Barroso & Detzel, JFE 140(3) 2021, confirmed: the managed market's abnormal return survives costs, other factors do not, and the managed market wins only in high sentiment (also confirmed in DeMiguel et al. fn 3). Harvey et al. PDF opened: US equities 1927-2017, Sharpe 0.40 unscaled vs 0.48-0.51 scaled (net 0.4766), costs included. Design note: Moreira-Muir scale by inverse VARIANCE, while the proposed rule is inverse-vol targeting (Harvey). Both are now counted as trials. The web-search budget was exhausted, so no new replication or decay search was possible.
rows.replication_concerns: In-sample spanning alphas replicate. Real-time gains are contested (Cederburg), and the benefit is sentiment-dependent (Barroso-Detzel). Power is low: managed and unmanaged returns are highly correlated, and over about 321 months the SE of the annual Sharpe difference is about 0.10, against an expected gain of 0.05-0.10 (Harvey). In Mandel, T-310 has a pooled B&H Sharpe gain (0.81 vs 0.63) that was never judged alone, and its per-asset DiD on SPY and QQQ was negative. Monthly RV targeting cut exposure after March 2020 and missed the rebound, so the 2015-2026 clause is at risk.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed spans: daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..2026-10-14 (available_at = bar + 24 h); fred-DTB3 1954-01-04..2026-10-13; cboe-VIX-history 1990-01-02..2026-10-14 (available_at 21:30 UTC); french-ff3-daily 1926-07-01..2026-08-31 (revised monthly, not point-in-time); alfred-UMCSENT 1952-11..2026-08 with vintages. The primary window 2000-01..2026-09 has 321 months.
rows.lookahead_risks: A full-sample normalising constant (the Cederburg critique) is avoided by fixing the target and cap ex ante. Decisions use closes through t and fill at the t+1 close, consistent with available_at. VIX settles at 16:15 ET, after SPY's 16:00 close, so the VIX trial must also fill at t+1. DTB3 is a discount yield and must be converted to bond-equivalent (house rule 7) and accrued from the prior print. The French long-history check uses a revised series and is reported only.
rows.missing_data: None for the judged arm. Baker-Wurgler sentiment is not archived and is built by full-sample PCA, so it is not point-in-time; first-release UMCSENT vintages are the reported stand-in.

final.claim: On SPY total return from 2000-01 to 2026-09, holding w_t = min(1.5, 0.15 / sigma_t) of SPY, where sigma_t is the annualised standard deviation of the 21 daily SPY excess returns ending at the last close of month t (decided at that close, filled at the next session's close), with the remainder in 3-month bills, leverage above 1x financed at the bill rate + 50 bp and 2 bp per unit of turnover, earns a higher annualised Sharpe ratio of monthly excess returns than buy-and-hold SPY on the same fills, with the paired studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the Sharpe difference above zero.
final.statistic: Annualised Sharpe(managed monthly excess) minus Sharpe(buy-and-hold monthly excess), 2000-01..2026-09, paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks and 10,000 draws. Secondary (reported): Cederburg et al.'s real-time combination (expanding-window mean-variance mix of managed and unmanaged) minus unmanaged; the mean excess return and volatility of each leg; the constant-weight control.
final.procedure: SPY adjclose daily. Daily excess return = SPY return minus the bill accrual from the prior DTB3 print, converted from discount to bond-equivalent yield (house rule 7, as in T-373). sigma_t uses only sessions closed by the decision close, and the decision executes at the next session's close. The 15% target and 1.5x cap are fixed ex ante, with no full-sample constant. Drift is tracked between rebalances; turnover = |w_target - w_drifted|, charged at 2 bp per unit; financing on (w - 1) at bill + 50 bp when w > 1. Before the result is read, the minimum detectable Sharpe difference at 80% power is reported from the bootstrap SE. Declared trials, counted in the DSR: scaler {inverse vol RV21 (primary), Moreira-Muir inverse variance c_t/RV21 with c_t from data through t, VIX close filled at the next close} x cap {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} x rebalance {monthly, weekly} = 18, plus T-310's 20 and T-562's 2 = 40. Reported only: the frozen primary rule on FF Mkt-RF + RF daily 1927-1999; a high/low split on first-release UMCSENT vintages; the 2008, 2020 and 2022 regimes.
final.data: daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3, cboe-VIX-history (VIX trial), french-ff3-daily (reported long-history check, to 2026-08-31), alfred-UMCSENT (reported split)
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 2000-01..2026-09 Sharpe difference > 0, AND the 2015-01..2026-09 point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the 40 counted trials.
final.controls: Buy-and-hold SPY on identical fills. A constant-weight SPY at the managed series' mean weight: the 15% target sits below SPY's average volatility, so the mean weight is < 1, and this control separates timing from lower exposure. Target and cap are ex ante; sigma comes from closed bars; all scaling turnover and leverage financing are costed. Both legs' means and volatilities are reported, so a gain that comes only from lower variance is labelled as such. Power is reported before the result.

rows.reason: The source is real and the market is the one factor where volatility management survives costs (Barroso-Detzel), so this is worth a cheap judged test on the T-310 harness. Fixes: DTB3 bond-equivalent conversion, the Moreira-Muir inverse-variance scaler counted as a trial (the original design was really Harvey-style vol targeting), and a power report before reading.

rows.name: Downside-volatility-managed factors (Wang-Yan): scale by bad volatility, not total volatility
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Feifei Wang & Xuemin Sterling Yan, 'Downside risk and the performance of volatility-managed portfolios', JBF vol 131 (2021) 106198. The abstract confirms that downside scaling beats total scaling in spanning regressions, direct Sharpe comparisons and real-time strategies, that the gain comes from return timing, and that the sample covers 9 factors and 94 anomalies. The specific counts (93/103, 70/103, 80-81/103, 8 of 9 return timing) could NOT be verified: the author PDF returned HTTP 500 and the web-search budget was exhausted.
rows.replication_concerns: The authors overlap with Cederburg et al., so the replication is not independent, and no post-2018 check was found. In Mandel's post-publication data, 5 of the 7 factor premia are near zero (T-382, T-386, T-446, T-447) and factor timing lost to static (T-388 -0.04, T-389 -0.03), so any gain must come from Mkt-RF and BAB. Estimator swaps moved T-310 by < 0.05 Sharpe. Downside RV from about 10 negative days in 21 is noisy and can produce extreme weights without a cap. The 91-month decisive window has low power.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed spans: french-ff5-daily 1963-07-01..2026-08-31; french-momentum-daily 1926-11-03..2026-08-31; aqr-bab-daily 1930-12-01..2026-07-31, so the window must end 2026-07, not 2026-08; fred-DTB3. The ETF arm uses SPY/QQQ/IWM (archived); MTUM and VLUE are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The French and AQR histories are rebuilt at every update, so they are not point-in-time (a stated limitation, as in T-382/T-446). c_t must come from data through t only. Factor returns are pre-cost paper portfolios. A unit change in a long-short factor weight trades both legs, so it must be costed as such.
rows.missing_data: None for the factor arm. MTUM and VLUE (for the reported ETF arm) are free on Yahoo but not archived.

final.claim: Over 2019-01 to 2026-07 (after Wang-Yan's sample), scaling each of FF Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, UMD and AQR BAB each month by min(3, c_t / RVdown_t), where RVdown_t is the sum of squared negative daily factor returns over the 21 sessions ending at month-end t and c_t is set from data through t so that the managed series' expanding-window volatility equals the unmanaged one's, earns a higher pooled annualised Sharpe ratio than the identical rule using total realised variance, net of 10 bp per unit change in factor weight, with the studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the pooled difference above zero.
final.statistic: Pooled (equal-weight mean over the 7 factors) annualised monthly Sharpe of downside-managed minus total-managed; paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks, all factors resampled jointly. Secondary: the pooled Sharpe of the fixed 50/50 mix of downside-managed and unmanaged minus unmanaged; per-factor differences Holm-adjusted across 7 (reported).
final.procedure: Daily factor returns (French in percent, AQR in decimals). At each month-end close t, RVdown_t and RVtot_t are taken from the prior 21 sessions. c_t comes from an expanding window starting 1963-07 (BAB from its archive start), using data through t only. Weights are capped at 3 for both scalers, ex ante, so that low-variance months cannot create extreme leverage (the T-381 failure). Each weight applies to month t+1's compounded daily returns. Cost: 10 bp per unit of |w_t - w_{t-1}| (one unit trades both legs); 30 bp reported. The window ends 2026-07 because aqr-bab-daily ends 2026-07-31. Reported: the in-sample replication 1963-07..2018-12 against the paper, and an upside-semivariance placebo. DSR over 7 factors x 2 scalers x 2 cost levels = 28 trials, plus T-388's 5 and T-389's 5. The minimum detectable pooled difference at 91 months is reported before the result.
final.data: french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, aqr-bab-daily, fred-DTB3; reported ETF arm: daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the pooled downside-minus-total Sharpe difference > 0 over 2019-01..2026-07, AND the pooled 50/50-mix-minus-unmanaged point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
final.controls: Unmanaged factors; total-RV-managed factors with the same cap; the upside-semivariance placebo; c_t from past data only; two cost levels. Paper factors are pre-cost, so only scaling turnover is charged (stated). The factor histories are not point-in-time (stated limitation).

rows.reason: The source is verified at abstract level and the claim is cheap to test on archived factors. It needs a weight cap, the correct end date (BAB ends 2026-07) and two-leg costing. Expect a fail, because most of the factor premia it scales are near zero post-publication in Mandel's own tests.

rows.name: Volatility-scaled stock momentum (Barroso-Santa-Clara; Daniel-Moskowitz) as a crash repair for dead UMD
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Barroso & Santa-Clara, 'Momentum has its moments', JFE 116(1) 111-120 (2015). The abstract says risk management 'nearly eliminates crashes and nearly doubles the Sharpe ratio'. The 0.53 -> 0.97 figures and the 1927-2011 sample could not be checked: the working-paper PDF sits behind a bot check and the search budget was exhausted. Daniel-Moskowitz, Hanauer-Windmuller and Fan-Li-Liu were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: BSC's sample runs to 2011, so the proposed decisive window 2009-01..2026-08 is partly IN-sample. It also contains the March-May 2009 momentum crash, which the scaling avoided because UMD's 126-day volatility was extreme, so a pass could rest on one in-sample episode. The truly post-sample window starts 2012-01. Barroso-Detzel find that cost-adjusted volatility management of non-market factors, including momentum, loses its alpha. T-446 puts raw UMD at +0.12%/yr over 2009-2026, so a positive Sharpe difference on a zero-mean factor is not a usable edge without a positive scaled mean.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed spans: french-momentum-daily 1926-11-03..2026-08-31; french-ff3-daily to 2026-08-31; fred-DTB3. The executable decile book on the 901-symbol panel is survivor-only (rule 9, NOT JUDGED); MTUM is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: French UMD is revised, so it is not point-in-time. Scaling must use the 126 returns through month-end t, and the target must be fixed ex ante (no full-sample constant). The factor's own rebalancing costs are not in the paper series. The survivor-only stock panel would bias any executable diagnostic.
rows.missing_data: A survivorship-free point-in-time stock universe is needed for an executable long-short book (T-307 blocked).

final.claim: Over 2012-01 to 2026-08 (after Barroso and Santa-Clara's 1927-2011 sample), FF UMD scaled each month by min(2, 0.12 / sigma_t), where sigma_t is the annualised realised volatility of the 126 daily UMD returns ending at month-end t, earns a higher annualised Sharpe ratio than unscaled UMD net of 20 bp per unit change in weight, with the paired studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the Sharpe difference above zero and a positive scaled annualised net mean.
final.statistic: Annualised monthly Sharpe(scaled UMD, net) minus Sharpe(unscaled UMD); paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks. Secondary: the scaled annualised net mean, and the worst 3-month return of each series.
final.null: Sharpe difference <= 0, or scaled net mean <= 0.
final.procedure: French daily Mom in percent. The weight is decided at the last close of month t from the 126 daily returns through t and applied to month t+1's compounded return. Turnover = |w_t - w_{t-1}| per unit of long-short notional, charged at 20 bp; 10, 30 and 50 bp are reported (50 bp approximates Barroso-Detzel stock-level costs). The factor's own rebalancing is uncosted in both legs (paper factor; stated). Reported only: the 1927-2011 replication (BSC's in-sample period); 2009-01..2011-12 on its own, because the 2009 crash lies inside BSC's sample and is not evidence here; and the Daniel-Moskowitz bear indicator (24-month market return < 0) as a comparator crash filter. DSR counts T-311's 24 trials, T-446's 34-trial family and this row's 4 variants (lookback {21, 126} x cap {1, 2}).
final.data: french-momentum-daily, french-ff3-daily (market state, reported), fred-DTB3
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 2012-01..2026-08 Sharpe difference > 0, AND the scaled annualised net mean > 0, AND DSR > 0.95.
final.controls: Unscaled UMD; a constant-weight UMD at the scaled series' mean weight; the bear-indicator comparator; the 12% target fixed ex ante; costs on scaling turnover. A pass is a paper-factor result: executing it needs a point-in-time long-short stock book with borrow, so it would justify that data unlock, not a trade.

rows.reason: The claim is verified and cheap to test, but the proposed decisive window overlaps BSC's own sample, and its 2009 crash would carry the result. Moving the window to 2012-01 onward makes it a genuine out-of-sample test.

rows.name: Conditional multifactor volatility management (DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera, Uppal)
rows.source_notes: Opened the JF 2024 open-access PDF (DOI 10.1111/jofi.13395). Confirmed: the out-of-sample net Sharpe is 13% higher than the unconditional multifactor portfolio's, significant at 1%. Ignoring trading diversification, 4 of 9 managed factors have negative net means. The sample is 1967-2020, with expanding-window OOS from 1977-01 (first window 120 months). The nine factors include HXZ ROE and IA. The authors REBUILD all nine factors from CRSP/Compustat stocks in order to compute stock-level transaction costs, and 'trading diversification' (netting stock trades across factors) is named as the first driver of the result.
rows.replication_concerns: The mechanism behind the net-of-cost gain is netting of individual-stock trades across factor portfolios. That cannot be reproduced on French and AQR paper factor returns, which carry no holdings, so a flat bp-per-factor-turnover cost tests a different claim. The paper's sample ends 2020, so the proposed 2015-2026 'decisive' window is mostly in-sample; the post-publication span (2021-01..2026-07) is about 67 months, with no power for a Sharpe-ratio difference. HXZ ROE and IA are not archived. Mandel's factor-timing record contradicts it (T-388 -0.04, T-389 -0.03 Sharpe vs static), and most factor premia are about zero post-publication.
rows.data_notes: The archived FF5, UMD and BAB series exist (FF to 2026-08-31, BAB to 2026-07-31), but the claim needs stock-level factor holdings with cost estimates (CRSP/Compustat-equivalent, not archived, no free full source) and HXZ ROE/IA (not archived).
rows.lookahead_risks: Paper factors are revised and not point-in-time. The cost model would be misspecified on paper factors. Treating 2015-2020 as out-of-sample would be wrong, because it lies inside the published sample.
rows.missing_data: A survivorship-free point-in-time US stock panel with factor-construction inputs and effective-spread estimates; HXZ ROE/IA factors.

final.claim: From 2021-01 onward (after DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera and Uppal's 1967-2020 sample), a monthly conditional mean-variance portfolio of nine factors (MKT, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, UMD, ROE, IA, BAB) rebuilt from point-in-time US stock holdings, whose factor weights are linear in the month-end market realised variance, estimated on an expanding window and optimised net of stock-level trading costs with stock trades netted across factors, earns a higher net Sharpe ratio than the unconditional mean-variance portfolio built the same way, with the block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero.
final.statistic: Annualised monthly net Sharpe(conditional) minus net Sharpe(unconditional), paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 12-month blocks.
final.procedure: Factors rebuilt monthly from point-in-time holdings. Stock-level costs from effective-spread estimates. Trades netted across factors at the stock level. Risk aversion fixed ex ante at 5. Expanding estimation from 1967. Weights apply to month t+1. Comparators: unconditional MV, per-factor Moreira-Muir scaling, and T-388's static equal-risk portfolio. The paper-factor gross version is reported only, as a diagnostic inside the downside-semivariance harness.
final.data: A survivorship-free stock panel with holdings and cost estimates (not archived); HXZ q-factors (not archived); fred-DTB3
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 2021-01-onward net Sharpe difference > 0 over at least 60 months, AND DSR > 0.95 counting T-388/T-389.
final.controls: Unconditional MV estimated identically; static equal-risk; per-factor scaling; expanding windows only; gross versus net reported.

rows.reason: Drop for now: the paper's net-of-cost result depends on stock-level trade netting, which Mandel's paper-factor data cannot reproduce. The testable proxy is therefore a different and weaker claim, the post-publication window is about 67 months, and Mandel's factor-timing failures (T-388/T-389) already cover the gross idea. Report the paper-factor conditional MV as a diagnostic in the semivariance harness instead.

rows.name: Volatility targeting pays only where the leverage effect lives (equities and credit, not bonds, FX or commodities)
rows.source_notes: Opened the Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison & Van Hemert PDF (JPM 2018). It covers 60 futures/assets (19 commodities, 9 currencies, 10 equity indexes, 9 bonds, plus credit) with US equities from 1927. US equities 1927-2017: Sharpe 0.40 unscaled vs 0.48-0.51 scaled, not sensitive to the estimator, and robust to costs (0.4831 gross / 0.4766 net). The paper states that the leverage effect is confined to risk assets (equities and credit). For US bonds 1963-2017, volatility scaling lowered the Sharpe ratio. Left tails thin in all classes. The paper already plots the Sharpe improvement against the leverage-effect correlation across assets. Bongaerts et al. were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Practitioner study on futures. ETFs such as USO, UNG and DBC carry roll drag, which changes Sharpe levels but matters less for scaled-minus-unscaled differences. A key design flaw in the proposed registration: a common 10% target with a 2x cap pins low-volatility bond ETFs (AGG ~4%, IEF ~6%) at 2x permanently and charges them bill + 50 bp financing. That mechanically lowers the non-risk group's scaled Sharpe and inflates the DiD. LQD is mostly Treasury duration, not credit, so it is a poor 'risk asset'. Nine FX pairs would dominate an asset-weighted non-risk mean. In Mandel, T-310's per-asset DiD gave SPY -0.07, GLD +0.06 and SLV +0.10, and T-562 found heterogeneity within equities. Few effective independent units means low power.
rows.lookahead_risks: FX spot is FRED's noon New York buying rate, not a 16:00 close, so FX positions must trade at the next noon print after the signal. OECD 3-month rates are monthly averages and must be lagged one month (as in T-368). The EWMA must use closed bars only, and leverage-effect coefficients must be estimated on 2007-2017 only.
rows.missing_data: None. OANDA financing differs from the OECD rate differentials (stated).

final.claim: Over 2018-01 to 2026-09, the mean Sharpe gain from volatility targeting (position min(2, sigmaLR_t / sigma_t), with sigma_t an EWMA of daily returns with a 20-day half-life at close t and sigmaLR_t the asset's expanding-window realised volatility through t, traded at close t+1, 2 bp per unit of turnover for ETFs and 1 bp for FX, leverage financed at the bill rate) across the risk group SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM and HYG exceeds the mean gain across the non-risk group TLT, IEF, AGG, GLD, SLV, USO, DBC, DBA, UNG and one equal-weighted G10-vs-USD FX unit, with the joint asset-and-time block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of this difference-in-differences above zero.
final.statistic: DiD = mean over risk assets of [Sharpe(scaled) - Sharpe(unscaled)] minus the same mean over non-risk units, using annualised daily excess-return Sharpe ratios. Secondary: the Spearman correlation between each asset's leverage-effect coefficient corr(r_t, RV_{t+1..t+21}), estimated 2007-07..2017-12, and its 2018-2026 Sharpe gain; the change in 5% CVaR and vol-of-vol for every asset.
final.procedure: Groups are fixed ex ante following Harvey et al. (equities and credit are risk). LQD is reported but not grouped, because unhedged duration dominates its returns. The nine FX pairs form one unit, so FX does not dominate the non-risk mean. Each asset targets its own expanding-window volatility, which keeps the mean weight near 1 in both groups; a common fixed target would pin bond ETFs at the cap and bias the DiD. ETF returns are daily adjclose excess over DTB3 (bond-equivalent, prior print). FX return = spot change between noon prints plus the interest differential accrued daily from one-month-lagged OECD 3-month rates; FX trades at the next noon print after the signal. sigma_t uses closed bars through t. Bootstrap: stationary 21-day time blocks drawn jointly for all assets, combined with resampling assets within each group, 5,000 draws. The frozen rule's 2007-07..2017-12 DiD must share the sign. Reported only: the fixed-10%-target variant, the bill + 50 bp financing variant, and per-asset gains.
final.data: daily-history-{SPY,QQQ,IWM,EFA,EEM,HYG,LQD,TLT,IEF,AGG,GLD,SLV,USO,DBC,DBA,UNG}, fx-spot-g10, fx-rates-3m, fred-DTB3
final.controls: Unscaled positions on identical fills; constant-weight versions at each scaled series' mean weight; own-volatility target and 2x cap fixed ex ante; bill-rate financing in the primary, so leverage cost cannot drive the DiD; costs on all turnover. Tail and vol-of-vol changes are reported for every asset: Harvey et al. predict tail reduction everywhere, which is not the claim.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the cross-asset prediction is falsifiable and cheap. The registration as proposed would have produced a spurious pass: a fixed 10% target with a 2x cap and +50 bp financing mechanically penalises low-volatility bond ETFs. Fixed with own-volatility targets, bill financing, LQD excluded and FX as one unit.

rows.name: Economic value of better volatility forecasts: HAR with semivariances or implied vol versus EWMA in volatility targeting
rows.source_notes: Opened the Bollerslev, Hood, Huss & Pedersen PDF (RFS 2018): more than 50 commodities, currencies, equity indices and fixed-income instruments over more than two decades of high-frequency data. Economic value is measured with a utility framework that rewards hitting a constant risk target and penalises vol-of-vol. HExpGl is worth about 48 bp/yr over the best static risk model, 19 bp/yr over a simple daily-data model and 8 bp/yr over a 21-day rolling RV, and the benefits remain after realistic transaction costs. Harvey et al. (opened) confirm that equity Sharpe after targeting is insensitive to the estimator. Patton-Sheppard was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The proposed Stage 2 statistic (a net Sharpe difference) is the wrong instrument. The paper's value is risk-tracking accuracy, worth 8-19 bp/yr over simple models, which no Sharpe-difference CI over 6 assets and 11 years can detect. Mandel twice found the estimator choice economically irrelevant for Sharpe (T-310, T-235). Stage 1 QLIKE gains are likely (T-569, T-572). Garman-Klass from Yahoo OHLC omits the overnight gap that the position actually bears, and Yahoo ETF opens can be stale.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: daily-history SPY 1993-, QQQ 1999-03-, IWM 2000-05-, TLT 2002-07-, GLD 2004-11-, USO 2006-04-. Cboe archives: VIX 1990-, VXTLT 2004-01-, but VXN 2009-09-14-, RVX 2009-09-16-, GVZ and OVX 2009-09-18- (not 2001), so HAR-IV for QQQ, IWM, GLD and USO starts around 2010-09. The local 60m bars cover the ML universe for 2 years.
rows.lookahead_risks: Use the implied index close for day t only for trades at the t+1 close (available_at 21:30 UTC). Forecasters are refit at month-ends on expanding windows only. The realised-variance target must include overnight returns. Yahoo daily bars are usable the next day.
rows.missing_data: None for daily data. Intraday RV is limited to 2024-2026 (local 60m bars) and is reported only.

final.claim: For SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD and USO over 2015-01 to 2026-09, a 10%-volatility-target position (decided at close t, traded at close t+1, cap 2x, 2 bp per unit of turnover) sized on a monthly-refitted SHAR forecaster (HAR with positive and negative daily semivariances) tracks its target more closely than the same position sized on EWMA(0.94): the pooled mean squared log ratio of realised 21-session position volatility to the 10% target is lower, with the paired studentized block-bootstrap 95% upper bound of (SHAR minus EWMA) below zero, and the pooled net Sharpe ratio is not lower.
final.statistic: Primary: pooled mean, over assets and non-overlapping 21-session windows, of [ln(realised volatility of the position's daily returns / 0.10)]^2, SHAR minus EWMA; paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 63-day blocks, assets resampled jointly. Gate: pooled 21-day QLIKE of SHAR below EWMA's, Diebold-Mariano one-sided p < 0.05. Secondary: pooled net Sharpe difference; turnover; the Bollerslev et al. quadratic-utility gain in bp per year.
final.procedure: The variance proxy for both QLIKE and tracking is squared close-to-close log returns, since the position bears overnight risk. Garman-Klass is reported only, after a stale-open check on Yahoo OHLC. Forecasters are refit at each month-end on an expanding window from 2004 (each asset from its first bar + 500 days). Trials: SHAR (primary), HAR and HAR-IV, with Holm across the three on the tracking-loss p-values. HAR-IV adds the matched Cboe index (VIX; VXN and RVX from 2009-09; VXTLT from 2004; GVZ and OVX from 2009-09), each entering 250 sessions after its first archived print, using day t's close for the trade at close t+1. MSM (T-569) is reported. 2015-01..2026-09 is judged; 2005-2014 is reported. Costs enter the net Sharpe secondary.
final.data: daily-history-{SPY,QQQ,IWM,TLT,GLD,USO}, cboe-{VIX,VXN,RVX,VXTLT,GVZ,OVX}-history, fred-DTB3; reported cross-check: mandel/ml_data/bars/60m (2024-2026)
final.pass: SHAR's pooled 21-day QLIKE is below EWMA's with one-sided DM p < 0.05, AND the upper 95% bound of the pooled tracking-loss difference (SHAR - EWMA) is < 0 over 2015-01..2026-09, AND the pooled net Sharpe difference point estimate is >= 0.
final.controls: EWMA baseline; constant weight at the same mean exposure; turnover per forecaster reported (a better forecast that trades more can lose net); expanding fits only; the result is labelled risk control, not alpha.

rows.reason: The forecasting gain is plausible (T-569, T-572), but the proposed Sharpe-difference test cannot detect the 8-19 bp/yr utility gains the source reports. The fix tests the paper's actual economic claim, risk-target tracking accuracy, with Sharpe as a no-worse check.

rows.name: Statistical jump model regime switching (persistence-penalised) versus HMM for equity de-risking
rows.source_notes: Opened arXiv 2402.05272v3 (Shu, Yu, Mulvey; DOI 10.1057/s41260-024-00376-x, J. Asset Management 2024). Table 4 is confirmed exactly for 1990-2023: S&P 500 JM 0.68 / -26.6% / CAGR 11.2%, HMM 0.54 / -28.9% / 8.5%, B&H 0.48 / -55.2% / 10.2%; DAX 0.44 / 0.35 / 0.30; Nikkei 0.31 / 0.19 / 0.12. Design details confirmed: 3,000-day (~12-year) training, 8-year validation, the penalty chosen monthly by validation Sharpe, the JM refit every SIX months (not monthly), 10 bp per one-way trade, a signal at end of day t applied from t+2, and online (filtered) inference.
rows.replication_concerns: Single research group. The proposed judged window 1994-2023 overlaps the paper's own test period, so it is a replication window, not out-of-sample; only 2024-01..2026-09 is post-publication. Mandel's regime filters cut drawdowns but never cleared a Sharpe CI or multiplicity (T-561 diff +0.216, CI -0.184..+0.752; T-301 failed Holm). Arm B is infeasible as specified: VIX3M starts 2009-09-18, so a 12-year training plus 8-year validation window cannot begin before about 2029.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed spans: daily-history--GSPC 1927-12-30..2026-10-14 (price index, no dividends); daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..; fred-DTB3 1954-..; cboe-VIX-history 1990-..; cboe-VIX3M-history 2009-09-18-.. (too short for the method's windows). french-ff3-daily ends 2026-08-31, so it cannot supply features through 2026-09.
rows.lookahead_risks: Smoothed (Viterbi or forward-backward) state paths leak future data, so online inference from closes through t is required. The penalty must be selected on validation data ending at t. Features from ^GSPC price returns omit dividends (minor, stated). Execution at the t+1 close matches the paper's t+2 application.
rows.missing_data: None for the price arm. The price-free VIX/VIX3M arm cannot run under the paper's window lengths. The jump-model fit needs a small implementation; the compute is light but must wait for free CPUs.

final.claim: On SPY total return from 1994-01 to 2026-09, holding SPY while a two-state statistical jump model puts day t in the good state, and 3-month bills otherwise, earns a higher annualised excess-return Sharpe ratio than buy-and-hold SPY, with the paired studentized block-bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero. The model uses EWM downside deviation (half-life 10) and EWM Sortino ratios (half-lives 20 and 60) of daily ^GSPC excess returns; it is trained on the prior 3,000 sessions and refit every six months; its jump penalty is re-chosen each month as the value with the best Sharpe over the preceding 8-year validation window; and its state is inferred online through close t. Trades are made at the close of t+1, with 10 bp per one-way switch.
final.statistic: Annualised daily excess-return Sharpe(JM-timed) minus Sharpe(buy-and-hold); paired studentized circular block bootstrap with 63-day blocks. Secondary: JM minus T-561's frozen HMM rule applied to SPY with the same lag; maximum-drawdown ratio; switches per year; time in market.
final.procedure: Features come from ^GSPC price returns minus the DTB3 accrual (bond-equivalent, prior print) from 1970, so the first 3,000-session training plus 8-year validation ends before 1994. Dividends are omitted from the features only (stated). Live P&L uses SPY adjclose with cash at DTB3. The penalty grid is declared before running and is part of the method. The state at t comes from a forward pass over the trailing 3,000 sessions ending at t, never the smoothed path. 1994-2023 overlaps the paper's test period and is labelled a replication window; 2015-01..2026-09 and 2024-01..2026-09 (post-publication) are reported separately. Delay {t+1 (primary), t+5} is counted in the DSR together with T-561, T-562 and T-301's 96 variants. The VIX/VIX3M arm is dropped (VIX3M starts 2009-09). The spell-preserving random-timing MDD null (as T-301/T-561) is reported.
final.data: daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Lower 95% bound of the 1994-01..2026-09 Sharpe difference > 0, AND the 2015-01..2026-09 point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
final.controls: Buy-and-hold; T-561's frozen HMM; T-301's 10-month SMA; the random-timing drawdown null; no smoothed states; penalty grid fixed ex ante; 10 bp per switch. A drawdown-only result is recorded as a risk overlay, not an edge (as T-561).

rows.reason: The source is verified exactly and the test is the natural successor to T-561/T-562. Fixes: the paper's 6-month refit, honest labelling of 1994-2023 as a replication window, and dropping the VIX3M arm, which cannot satisfy the 20-year train-plus-validation requirement.

rows.name: Cross-sectional skewness dispersion (and average skewness) predicts the stock market, concentrated in FOMC months
