rows.source_notes: Opened arXiv 2604.07870 (Babiak, Barunik, Kurka, 9 April 2026). Confirmed: in-sample Dec 2000 to Dec 2022; OOS expanding from Dec 2005; 6,770 stocks from Kibot. Skewness is computed from 5-minute returns (78 per day) as a DAILY realised skewness, and the monthly predictor averages daily dispersion over the last 5 sessions. 1-month slope -0.099 (NW t -2.95, adj R^2 4.09%); 3-month t -4.04, R^2 9.19%; OOS R^2 2.91 / 6.12 / 7.85% (CW significant); JZZ equal-weighted skewness -0.56 / 0.53%. FOMC months -0.133 (t -3.28, R^2 7.08%), pre-FOMC -0.108 (t -2.97), post-FOMC -0.080 (t -1.95), non-FOMC -0.018 (t -0.31). Mean-variance weights are constrained to [-0.5, 1.5], not [0, 1.5]: CER 8.36% vs 2.40%, Sharpe 0.89 vs 0.57. The paper reports no daily-return skewness version.
rows.replication_concerns: New and unreplicated working paper. The testable proxy (21-day daily-return skewness of FF49 industry portfolios) is a different and far noisier construct: the skewness SE with n=21 is about 0.5, and industry portfolios diversify away the firm-level asymmetry that is the claimed signal. A fail would not refute the paper, and a pass would be a new unpublished claim. Eight scheduled FOMC meetings a year make about 2/3 of months 'FOMC months', with pre- and post-FOMC months mostly significant too, so the FOMC concentration is weak evidence. The post-paper window 2023-01..2026-08 is 44 months. Mandel's FOMC family failed after 2016 (T-341 2016-2026 -5.3 bps; T-342, T-343, T-361), and aggregate predictors fail out of sample (T-398).
rows.data_notes: french-industry49-daily (1926..2026-08-31) and fomc-meetings (from 1994-02 only, so an FOMC interaction cannot be estimated before 1994) exist. The real input, firm-level 5-minute bars for every US stock including delisted names, does not: local 5m bars cover about 123 symbols for 60 days, and the 60m bars give 7 returns a day, too few for daily realised skewness.
rows.lookahead_risks: Kibot's survivorship handling is unknown. Bars stamped by open time must not be read as closes. The FOMC-month definition (meeting month vs the month after) must be fixed ex ante. The 901-symbol panel is survivor-only.
rows.missing_data: 5-minute bars for all point-in-time US common stocks 2000-2026, including delisted names (no free source); a forward record would need many years to judge a monthly market-timing predictor.

final.claim: For month-end decisions from 2023-01 onward (after Babiak, Barunik and Kurka's 2000-2022 sample), the 75th-minus-25th percentile spread of daily realised skewness computed from 5-minute returns across all point-in-time US common stocks, averaged over the month's last 5 sessions, negatively predicts the next-month S&P 500 excess return, with an expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 above zero against the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05).
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2 of the next-month SPY excess return with Clark-West; the FOMC-month slope reported.
final.procedure: Firm-level daily realised skewness from 78 five-minute returns; cross-sectional 75-25 spread each day; mean over the last 5 sessions of month t, known at that close; target SPY from the next close; expanding OLS.
final.data: Firm-level 5-minute bars for every point-in-time US common stock, including delisted names (not archived); daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3; fomc-meetings
final.pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over at least 120 post-2022 decisions.
final.controls: Historical-mean benchmark; JZZ average skewness; a 12-month-shifted placebo.

rows.reason: Drop: the only archived proxy (industry-portfolio daily-return skewness) is a different, much noisier construct whose result would neither confirm nor refute the paper. The real firm-level 5-minute input has no free source, and a forward record of a monthly market-timing predictor would take a decade to judge.

rows.name: Cross-sectional tail risk (Kelly-Jiang) as a market-return predictor
rows.source_notes: The NBER w19375 page confirms Kelly & Jiang, 'Tail Risk and Asset Prices' (WP 2013; RFS 2014, 27(10)): a one-SD increase in tail risk forecasts +4.5% excess market return over the next year, and high tail-loading stocks earn a three-factor alpha 5.4% higher. The page does not state the sample period. Replication and decay could not be searched (web-search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: No replication check was possible. The measure is built from the extreme left tail of the full CRSP cross-section, which is exactly the set of crash-and-delist names a survivor-only panel removes, so the bias is time-varying. With a 12-month horizon, 2011-2026 holds about 15 independent observations. Aggregate predictors fail out of sample in Mandel (T-398), and option-based tail measures failed (T-52, T-227).
rows.data_notes: Only the survivor-only 901-symbol panel exists. About 480 names reach 2000 and nearly all are survivors (T-393/T-375, rule 9). No survivorship-free daily stock panel is archived or freely available.
rows.lookahead_risks: Survivorship bias pushes the Hill exponent toward thinner tails, worst in early years. Overlapping 12-month returns need Hodrick SEs.
rows.missing_data: A survivorship-free daily return panel of all US common stocks including delisted names (CRSP-equivalent).

final.claim: Over month-end decisions from 2000-01 to 2025-08, the Kelly-Jiang tail exponent (Hill estimator on all US common-stock daily returns in month t below that month's cross-sectional 5th percentile, smoothed over 3 months) positively predicts the SPY excess return over the next 12 months, with an expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 above zero against the historical mean (Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05).
final.statistic: Predictive slope with Hodrick (1992) SEs; Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2 with Clark-West.
final.procedure: Pooled stock-day returns below the monthly 5th percentile; Hill exponent; 3-month moving average known at the last close of t; target SPY from that close; expanding OLS from 1965; power reported before reading.
final.data: A survivorship-free US stock daily panel (not archived); daily-history-SPY; fred-DTB3
final.pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 over 2000-01..2025-08.
final.controls: Historical mean; VIX level and realised market kurtosis as competing predictors; a 12-month-shift placebo.

rows.reason: Drop: the archive's stock panel is survivor-only, which deletes exactly the crash names the Hill estimator is built from. No free survivorship-free source exists, and replication was unchecked. The 12-month horizon would have about 15 independent post-2011 observations even with data.

rows.name: Variance risk premium as an equity-return predictor (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou), tested for its post-2010 decline
rows.source_notes: Opened the BTZ PDF (RFS 2009): sample 1990-01..2007-12, VRP = model-free implied variance minus past-month realised variance. Quarterly slope t 2.86, R^2 6.82%; monthly R^2 about 1.07%. Their robustness check matters here: with VIX and DAILY-return RV, the quarterly t falls to 2.34 and R^2 to 4.45%; with Black-Scholes IV and daily RV, t 1.72 and R^2 2.16%. Opened Dew-Becker & Giglio (Chicago Fed WP 2025-17, Sept 2025): index-option alphas have been indistinguishable from zero for the past 15 years, and synthetic options never had negative alpha over 100 years. Note that option alphas are not the same as the VIX-minus-RV gap, which Mandel finds still positive in both halves (T-48, T-510).
rows.replication_concerns: BTZ say their result depends on 5-minute RV; the archived daily-squares proxy roughly halves the R^2 even in their own sample. Lehman (2008-10) and March 2020 are highly influential observations (strongly negative VRP before rebounds). No post-2010 predictive-regression decay test was found, and a search was not possible. Mandel: VRP-conditioned rules failed (T-159, T-235; T-179 CNDR slope HAC t 1.00), while T-101 had a positive option-side footprint.
rows.data_notes: Confirmed: cboe-VIX-history 1990-01-02..2026-10-14 (observed 21:15, available 21:30 UTC); daily-history--GSPC 1927..2026-10-14; daily-history-SPY 1993-01-29..; fred-DTB3. A 63-session target from the 2026-06 month-end ends in 2026-09, so decisions run 2010-01..2026-06 (198 months).
rows.lookahead_risks: VIX settles at 16:15 ET, 15 minutes after the SPY close, so the target must start at the next session's close. Overlapping 3-month targets need Hodrick SEs and HAC Clark-West. VIX^2/12 and the sum of squared daily log returns must be in the same monthly %^2 units. Parkinson RV from early ^GSPC highs and lows is unreliable and is reported only.
rows.missing_data: None. 5-minute RV is unavailable before the local bar window, which biases the test toward failure (stated).

final.claim: For month-end decisions from 2010-01 to 2026-06, the variance risk premium VRP_t = (VIX_t/100)^2/12 minus the sum of squared daily ^GSPC log returns over the 21 sessions ending at month-end t positively predicts the SPY excess return over the next 63 sessions measured from the next session's close: the predictive slope is positive with a one-sided Hodrick (1992) p < 0.05, and the expanding-window out-of-sample R^2 against the historical mean is positive with a one-sided Clark-West p < 0.05.
final.statistic: Slope of the 63-session SPY excess log return on standardised VRP_t over the 2010-01..2026-06 decisions, with Hodrick SEs; Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2 for those decisions from expanding OLS fitted from 1990-02, with HAC Clark-West. Reported: the 1990-2009 slope, the paired slope difference, and the 21-session horizon.
final.procedure: Inputs: the VIX close of the last session of month t and ^GSPC closes through t, both in monthly %^2 units. Target: SPY adjclose from the next session's close over 63 sessions, minus the DTB3 accrual (bond-equivalent, prior print). One primary specification (63 sessions, daily-return RV). Reported only: the 21-session horizon; Parkinson RV; VIX^2 and RV alone as competing predictors; a 12-month-shifted placebo; the sensitivity excluding 2020-03..2020-06; a trading arm (SPY weight 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 by expanding VRP tercile, monthly, 2 bp, financing bill + 50 bp). Before reading, the record states that BTZ's daily-RV version was weaker (quarterly t 2.34, R^2 4.45%).
final.data: cboe-VIX-history, daily-history--GSPC, daily-history-SPY, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Over the 2010-01..2026-06 decisions: slope > 0 with Hodrick one-sided p < 0.05, AND OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05.
final.controls: VIX^2 and RV alone as competing predictors (reported; the VRP should beat each); historical-mean benchmark; placebo shift; next-close execution; the 1990-2009 half reported, so the ledger records which half carries the predictability (Dew-Becker-Giglio predict a post-2010 fail).

rows.reason: The source is verified, the test is cheap and informative either way, and Mandel has never tested the VRP as a timing input. Fixes: decisions end 2026-06 so targets complete, the DSR clause is replaced by a single primary specification (the claim is a regression), and the daily-RV handicap BTZ documented is stated before reading.

rows.name: Realised skewness and relative signed jump variation in the cross-section (Amaya et al.; Bollerslev-Li-Zhao)
rows.source_notes: Opened CREATES RP 2013-41 (Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs, Vasquez): TAQ, every listed stock, 1993-01..2008-09. The lowest-minus-highest weekly realised-skewness decile earns 24 bp/week value-weighted (t 3.65) and 43-44 bp equal-weighted; kurtosis gives 14 bp (t 2.12). Bollerslev-Li-Zhao and Hou-Xue-Zhang were not opened (search budget exhausted).
rows.replication_concerns: A cost argument kills the trade before any data: a weekly-rebalanced decile long-short has turnover near 100% per week on both legs, and at 10-20 bp per side that costs 40-80 bp a week, against a published GROSS spread of 19-24 bp/week from a 1993-2008 sample, before post-publication decay. Daily-skewness versions fail Hou-Xue-Zhang's replication. The aggregate 60m-bar ARSJ pilot has about 100 weekly observations and 7 bars a day, which is not a test.
rows.data_notes: Constituent minute bars for 2018-2026 and point-in-time S&P 500/400 membership are not archived. Local intraday bars cover about 60 single stocks (5m for 60 days, 60m for 2 years), which is too few and too short.
rows.lookahead_risks: Intraday bars are stamped by open time. Survivor-only universes. One session must be skipped to avoid bid-ask bounce.
rows.missing_data: Point-in-time constituent minute bars 2018-2026 including delisted names; point-in-time index membership.

final.claim: Over 2018-01 to 2026-09, among point-in-time S&P 500 and S&P 400 constituents, the value-weighted portfolio long the bottom decile and short the top decile of weekly relative signed jump variation RSJ = (RV+ - RV-)/RV from 5-minute returns (Wednesday close to Wednesday close, one session skipped, held one week) earns a positive mean weekly return net of 10 bp per side for large caps, 20 bp for mid caps and 50 bp a year borrow, with Newey-West t > 2.
final.statistic: Mean weekly net long-short return, Newey-West t (4 lags); FF5+UMD alpha reported.
final.procedure: Point-in-time membership; 5-minute regular-hours returns; signal at the Wednesday close, positions from the Thursday close; costs by cap bucket plus borrow.
final.data: Constituent minute bars and point-in-time membership (not archived); fred-DTB3
final.pass: Net mean weekly return > 0 with Newey-West t > 2 over 2018-01..2026-09.
final.controls: Gross vs net reported; 1-week reversal control; value-weighted primary; survivorship-free membership required.

rows.reason: Drop: even the published gross spread (24 bp/week, 1993-2008) is below the 40-80 bp a week that a weekly decile long-short costs, and the decisive data (point-in-time constituent minute bars) are not available. Mandel's 'costs always charged' rule rejects it a priori.

rows.name: Volatility-of-volatility (uncertainty about risk) predicts lower returns: Baltussen et al., testable on Cboe vol indices now and on captured chains later
rows.source_notes: Opened the Baltussen, van Bekkum & van der Grient PDF (JFQA 2018, DOI 10.1017/S0022109018000480). Sample 1996-01..2014-10 (OptionMetrics). Vol-of-vol is the past month's volatility of implied volatility standardised by average IV. High minus low quintile: -0.69%/month value-weighted and -0.50% equal-weighted (t -3.97); 4-factor alpha -0.60% (t -2.62); persists up to 24 months; strong in Europe. Huang et al. (JFQA 2019) was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent post-2014 US replication was found (search budget exhausted). The proposed Stage A is a different construct: a cross-asset rank over 11 heterogeneous Cboe indices (4 equity-index ETFs, 3 mega-caps, gold, oil, bonds, EM) with own-history z-scores, not a stock cross-section, and has little power. The proposed Stage B is infeasible as written: the capture box records only 14 chains (AAPL, ETHA, GLD, IBIT, IWM, NVDA, QQQ, SLV, SPX, SPY, TLT, TSLA, USO, VIX), not every optionable stock. New unlock found: DoltHub's free post-no-preference/options volatility_history table holds iv_current for 625 symbols on 2021-06-15 and 1,540 on 2024-06-14, and includes since-delisted names (TWTR and ATVI present in 2021). That gives a point-in-time optionable universe; Mandel's fetcher exists but has pulled only 16 symbols. Low-volatility anomalies failed post-ETF in Mandel (T-384, T-448). Power over about 70-75 months is modest (expected t about -1.8 value-weighted before any decay).
rows.data_notes: Archived: cboe implied-vol index histories (VXAPL/VXGOG/VXAZN from 2011-01, VXEEM 2011-03, others 2009-09, VXTLT 2004) and dolt-volhistory for 16 ETFs 2019-02..2026-10 (about 1,290 snapshots, so roughly 1 session in 3 is missing). Verified live via the DoltHub API: about 625 symbols in 2021 and about 1,540 in 2024; no rows on 2019-03-01. Stock prices are archived only for the survivor-only 901 list; prices for delisted names must come from a fetch, and Yahoo often lacks them.
rows.lookahead_risks: Use DoltHub quote_date (not snapshot_date) and dolt commit time as available_at; drop rows flagged stale. Snapshots are irregular, so each IV change must be scaled by the square root of the sessions it spans. Missing returns for delisted names bias the result, so the rule-9 coverage gate must decide whether the claim is judged. Cboe index closes are available at 21:30 UTC.
rows.missing_data: A DoltHub volatility_history fetch for all symbols 2020-2026; daily prices for those symbols, including delisted names, with a coverage check; NYSE market-cap breakpoints (French ME_Breakpoints, free, not archived).

final.claim: Over holding months from the first month-end with at least 300 eligible names through 2026-09, among US-listed common stocks present in DoltHub's options volatility_history at each month-end (point-in-time membership) with market cap above the NYSE 20th percentile, the value-weighted top quintile of vol-of-vol underperforms the bottom quintile over the next month, net of 10 bp per side, with a Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05 on the mean high-minus-low return. Vol-of-vol is the standard deviation of log changes in iv_current over the month's snapshots, each change scaled by the square root of the sessions it spans, divided by the month's mean iv_current, with at least 12 snapshots required.
final.statistic: Mean monthly value-weighted high-minus-low quintile return, net; Newey-West t (3 lags). Reported: equal-weighted spread; FF5+UMD alpha; the same IC computed on the IV level, which separates vol-of-vol from the low-volatility effect.
final.procedure: Universe at month-end t: symbols with a non-stale DoltHub row in month t, common-stock flag from SEC submissions, cap = SEC cover shares filed before t x close(t-1), above the French NYSE 20th-percentile breakpoint. Quintiles at the t close; positions from the next session's close, held one month; 10 bp per side. Rule-9 gate: the month is judged only if names covering at least 90% of the value-weighted universe have a return through the holding month (delisting returns from the last trade); otherwise the claim is NOT JUDGED. The start month is fixed by the 300-name rule before any return is read. Reported only: the archived cross-asset Cboe-index pilot (Stage A), and a forward continuation of the same rule from 2026-10.
final.data: DoltHub post-no-preference/options volatility_history, all symbols (fetch via mandel.data.dolt_options.fetch_dolt_volhistory); daily prices for those symbols (fetch); sec-companyfacts; sec-submissions; French ME_Breakpoints (fetch); french-ff5-daily; french-momentum-daily; fred-DTB3
final.pass: Mean high-minus-low net return < 0 with Newey-West one-sided p < 0.05 over the judged months, AND the rule-9 coverage gate passes in every judged month.
final.controls: The IV-level sort as the competing low-volatility explanation; a placebo with vol-of-vol lagged 12 months; equal-weighted version reported; coverage gate; one breakpoint and one hold (no grid).

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the proposed Stage A tests a different construct and Stage B relied on chains the capture box does not record. DoltHub's free point-in-time volatility history (about 625-1,540 optionable names a day) makes a real stock-level test feasible after a fetch, gated by rule-9 coverage.

rows.name: Commodity term-structure carry (roll yield / basis) on energy and metals, using EIA's free contract 1-4 curves
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Szymanowska, de Roon, Nijman & van den Goorbergh, JF 69(1) 2014: spot premia about 5-14%/yr, term premia about 1-3%/yr; a single basis high-minus-low factor explains spot premia. The EIA pages, opened, confirm NYMEX daily contracts 1-4 for WTI (1983/85-2024), RBOB (2005-2024), No. 2 heating oil (1980/94-2024) and Henry Hub natural gas (1993/94-2024), with the explicit note 'Futures prices after April 5, 2024, are not available.' The Hedge Fund Journal, Macrosynergy and Koijen et al. claims were not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The cross-sectional basis premium is widely replicated, but post-2015 weakness is reported only by practitioners. Four highly correlated energy contracts give a small effective sample. Backwardation correlates with past price rises, so a backwardation timer may just be time-series momentum, which failed in Mandel (T-313). Every carry sleeve Mandel built for 2013-2026 failed (T-381, T-368, T-431, T-433). There is no free going-forward curve after 2024-04, so any pass is historical only.
rows.data_notes: The EIA series exist with the spans above (verified on eia.gov) but are not archived; one free fetch is needed. The archived ETF arm covers USO 2006-04-, UGA 2008-02-, UNG 2007-04-, BNO 2010-06-. CL-F (Yahoo continuous) has undocumented roll gaps (T-555 caveat) and is not used for returns.
rows.lookahead_risks: EIA 'contract 1' changes identity at each expiry, so rolled returns must be built from exchange expiry rules (CL: 3 business days before the 25th of the prior month; NG: 3 business days before the first day of the delivery month; HO and RB: the last business day of the prior month), with returns taken on the contract actually held. The signal is the month-end settlement (14:30 ET for CL) and is acted on at the next settlement. Days-to-expiry annualisation must use the two contracts' actual expiries.
rows.missing_data: EIA daily contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (free, ends 2024-04-05). A going-forward curve source is needed for any live claim (CME settlements are paid; Yahoo per-contract tickers are free only for listed months). Heating oil and RBOB have no micro contracts, so a small account would trade them through UGA (gasoline) or not at all.

final.claim: Over 2012-01 to 2024-03, for WTI crude, NY Harbor heating oil, RBOB gasoline and Henry Hub natural gas, holding the rolled front-month future long in months after a month-end at which the annualised log(F1/F2) from EIA's contract 1 and 2 settlements is positive, and holding bills otherwise, earns a higher pooled mean monthly excess return than always holding the rolled front month, net of one tick plus $2.50 per contract per side, with the month-block bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above zero.
final.statistic: Pooled (equal weight across the 4 commodities) mean monthly excess return of the carry rule minus always-long; circular block bootstrap over months (6-month blocks), drawn jointly across commodities. Secondary: the carry rule minus a 12-1 TSMOM long/flat rule on the same rolled series.
final.procedure: Rolled excess-return series are built from EIA contract 1 and 2 settlements, rolling from the nearby to the next contract 5 business days before the nearby's last trade (dates from the exchange rules), with returns on the held contract and never on spot. Signal: month-end log(F1/F2) x 365 / (days between the two contracts' expiries), acted on at the next settlement. Arm A, long/flat, is primary. Arm B (long/short) and the roll offset {5, 10 days} are counted with the basis-momentum row in one DSR. The 1994-2011 window is reported. A reported ETF arm applies the same signal to USO, UGA and UNG at 5 bp per side. A cross-sectional version waits for 15+ curves (T-371).
final.data: EIA NYMEX daily contract 1-4 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (to fetch; end 2024-04-05); fred-DTB3; daily-history-{USO,UGA,UNG} for the reported ETF arm
final.pass: Pooled mean-difference lower 95% bound > 0 over 2012-01..2024-03, AND the difference positive in at least 3 of the 4 commodities, AND the carry-minus-TSMOM point estimate > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
final.controls: Always-long rolled front; a 12-1 TSMOM timer as the competing explanation; a placebo with the signal lagged 12 months; roll-date sensitivity; the effective sample of the 4 correlated contracts reported; a going-forward curve source must be verified before any live claim.

rows.reason: Fix as a time-series variant of the blocked T-371: the EIA curves are confirmed free, though they end 2024-04-05, and carry is a class Mandel's lessons favour. Added a TSMOM competitor (backwardation proxies momentum) and exact expiry-based rolls, and noted that no live curve exists after 2024.

rows.name: Basis-momentum in futures curves (Boons-Prado)
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Boons & Porras Prado, JF 74(1) 239-279 (2019). Opened the working-paper PDF: 21 commodities from 1959-07 to 2014-02; the High4-minus-Low4 basis-momentum portfolio earns 18.38%/yr (t 6.73) in nearby returns and 4.08%/yr (t 6.43) in spreading returns; the 18.38% is almost entirely the average roll return of 21.53%; results hold for 32 commodities and survive cost estimates (about 211 bp/yr). BM is defined as the momentum of the first-nearby strategy minus that of the second-nearby. Kwon-Kang-Yun (FRL 2021, ranking-window fragility) was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: The headline result is cross-sectional (21-32 commodities); a time-series test on 4 correlated energy contracts is far weaker. BM on VX futures is outside the paper's sample (commodities, currencies, stock indexes), so it is a new claim, and Mandel's three VX curve rules failed after costs (T-160, T-379, T-435). The 12-month lookback is reportedly fragile across subperiods. The last decade is post-sample, with no decay study found.
rows.data_notes: EIA curves are verified on eia.gov but not archived (CL, HO, RB, NG contracts 1-4 to 2024-04-05). cboe-vx-futures is archived 2013-01-02..2026-10-14 with settle = 0 rows in early 2013 (T-160: first real settlement 2013-05-20), so VX BM can only start around 2014-06.
rows.lookahead_risks: Same expiry-rule roll construction as the EIA carry row. VX settle = 0 rows must be dropped. BM uses only the 12 months through month-end t and is acted on at the next settlement.
rows.missing_data: EIA contract 1-2 settlements (free, to fetch). The VX arm is testable now but is a separate claim in the VX family.

final.claim: Over 2012-01 to 2024-03, for WTI crude, heating oil, RBOB gasoline and Henry Hub natural gas, month-end basis-momentum (the 12-month cumulative return of the rolled first-nearby future minus that of the rolled second-nearby, from EIA contract 1 and 2 settlements) positively predicts the next month's rolled first-nearby excess return in a pooled regression with commodity fixed effects that also controls for the basis (annualised log F1/F2) and 12-month nearby momentum (month-clustered one-sided p < 0.05), and the sign rule (long if BM > 0, short if BM < 0) earns a higher net Sharpe ratio than always-long after one tick plus $2.50 per contract per side.
final.statistic: Pooled coefficient on standardised BM in a regression of the next-month nearby excess return on BM, basis and 12-month nearby momentum with commodity fixed effects and month-clustered SEs. Secondary: the net Sharpe of the sign rule minus always-long (paired block bootstrap, 6-month blocks).
final.procedure: Rolled nearby and second-nearby series are built as in the EIA carry row (expiry-rule rolls 5 business days before the last trade, returns on held contracts). BM uses months through t only and is applied from the next settlement. One lookback (12 months), no grid. The spreading arm (long C1 / short C2 by BM sign) is reported. The VX M1/M2 version (2014-06..2026-09, $2 per contract per leg) is registered separately in the VX family with T-160/T-379/T-435 counted in its DSR. Arms are counted with the EIA carry row in one DSR. The effective sample of the 4 correlated contracts is reported.
final.data: EIA NYMEX contract 1-2 settlements for CL, HO, RB and NG (to fetch); fred-DTB3; cboe-vx-futures (separate VX claim)
final.pass: BM coefficient > 0 with month-clustered one-sided p < 0.05 over 2012-01..2024-03, AND the sign rule's net Sharpe minus always-long > 0, AND DSR > 0.95 over the counted trials.
final.controls: Basis and 12-month momentum inside the regression (BM must add to both); a placebo shift; costs per leg; a single lookback.

rows.reason: The source is verified with numbers. The fix puts basis and momentum inside the primary regression (the paper's claim is that BM beats them), shares the EIA fetch and DSR with the carry row, and splits the VX arm into its own claim because VX lies outside the paper's sample.

rows.name: COT hedging pressure and hedgers' short-term liquidity provision in commodity futures
rows.source_notes: IDEAS confirms Kang, Rouwenhorst & Tang, JF 75(1) 2020, and Basu & Miffre, JBF 37(7) 2013 (abstract only, no numbers). Opened the KRT NBER working paper: 26 commodities on NYMEX/NYBOT/CBOT/CME, 1994-01..2012-06. Ranking is on the TUESDAY as-of date: the top-half-by-hedger-buying minus bottom-half spread earns 0.431% over 20 days (t 4.16), and 'about half of the 20 day excess return accrues during the days that precede the release' (days 1-4, before Friday's report). A typical speculator purchase reverses 16 bp the next week; quintiles give 67 bp. Maréchal (JFM 2023) was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: Only about half of the published flow effect (roughly 21 bp over 16 days) is tradable after the Friday release. That is thin against costs on 18 contracts, and many of those (cattle, cocoa, coffee, cotton) have no micro contract, so a small account cannot trade them. Yahoo continuous =F series have undocumented roll gaps whose sign correlates with the basis, which would contaminate returns. Mandel's one point-in-time COT test (gold) saw nothing (T-405 slope t +0.55). KRT's sample ends 2012-06, so 2013 onward is post-sample.
rows.data_notes: Archived COT covers only gold (088691) and silver (084691) legacy/disaggregated, plus a BTC TFF. The other contracts need the same Socrata recipe (CL 067651, NG 023651, RB 111659, HG 085692, ZC 002602, ZW 001602, ZS 005602, SB 080732). ETF proxies archived: USO, UNG, UGA, GLD, SLV, CORN (2010-06), WEAT and SOYB (2011-09); CPER is in the 901 list. CANE was not found in the archive (fetch).
rows.lookahead_risks: Positions are as of Tuesday and released Friday 15:30 ET, later during the 2013 and 2018-19 government shutdowns, so release time (with Socrata stamps when later) must be used as available_at, as in T-405. The Tuesday-dated version is not tradable and is diagnostic only. The Friday 16:00 close is too close to a 15:30 release for a closing order, so entry is at the next session's close.
rows.missing_data: CFTC legacy futures-only reports for CL, NG, RB, HG, ZC, ZW, ZS and SB (free Socrata); CANE prices (free Yahoo). Clean rolled futures returns for contracts without ETF proxies are not freely available, so they are excluded.

final.claim: Over 2013-01 to 2026-09, across ten commodities with US-listed ETF proxies (CL/USO, NG/UNG, RB/UGA, GC/GLD, SI/SLV, HG/CPER, ZC/CORN, ZW/WEAT, ZS/SOYB, SB/CANE), a weekly portfolio long the five and short the five ETFs with the largest and smallest 1-week change in commercial net long / open interest in the CFTC legacy futures-only report, entered at the close of the first session after the report's release and held 15 sessions in overlapping weekly cohorts, earns a positive mean net return per hold after 5 bp per side and 50 bp a year borrow on shorts, with the block-bootstrap 95% lower bound above zero.
final.statistic: Mean net 15-session long-short return over overlapping weekly cohorts (each cohort 1/3 of capital); circular block bootstrap with 8-week blocks.
final.procedure: available_at = the actual release time of each report: Friday 15:30 ET by schedule, later for shutdown delays, keeping the Socrata stamp when it is later (as in T-405). Entry at the close of the first session after available_at; exit 15 sessions later. Signal = (commercial long - commercial short) / open interest, change from the prior report. Equal weight within halves; 5 bp per side; borrow on shorts; cash at DTB3. Diagnostics (not tradable, reported): the same ranking measured from the Tuesday as-of date, to size the release-lag loss, and KRT's 1994-2012 window. Reported trial: the Basu-Miffre level signal (52-week mean commercial net short / OI). Each instrument enters when its ETF has 52 weeks of history.
final.data: CFTC legacy futures-only reports for the ten contracts (gold and silver archived; eight to fetch); daily-history-{USO,UNG,UGA,GLD,SLV,CPER,CORN,WEAT,SOYB} plus CANE (fetch); fred-DTB3
final.pass: Mean net return per 15-session hold, lower 95% bound > 0 over 2013-01..2026-09.
final.controls: An equal-weight long-all baseline; a 1-week return-reversal control (KRT's flow effect partly mirrors reversal); release-time point-in-time stamps; ETF proxies avoid continuous-futures roll gaps; the Tuesday-dated diagnostic quantifies how much of the published effect is unusable.

rows.reason: The source is verified, and opening it showed that half of KRT's 43 bp is earned before the COT report is public. The fix tests only the post-release, tradable window, after KRT's sample, on ETF proxies with clean returns, rather than on Yahoo continuous futures with roll gaps.

rows.name: ML predictors that survive costs: price-free features, longer horizons, no microcaps, cost-aware objective
rows.source_notes: Opened the Robeco page (Blitz, Hanauer, Hoogteijling, Howard 2023): 1-month ML strategies were profitable mainly before 2004 and close to zero net afterwards; 3/6/12-month horizons gave better net returns over 2004-2021 thanks to lower turnover and slower signals. Opened Azevedo, Hoegner & Velikov: net OOS returns up to 1.42%/month, LSTM net six-factor alpha 1.20% (t 3.46). They also find that 'prevalent cost-mitigation techniques reduce turnover and costs, [but] do not improve net anomaly performance', which partly contradicts the candidate's cost-aware-construction premise. Avramov-Cheng-Metzker returned SSRN 403 and is unverified; JKMP was not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: These papers use CRSP-wide universes with 100+ anomaly characteristics; Mandel's price-free inputs (FINRA SI, RegSHO, SEC shares, realised moments) are a much narrower set. The proposed stock-level design is blocked by rule 9: the archive is survivor-only, and FINRA starts 2017-12, so development would be about 2018-2025. The ML program now has 764 cells and 0 passes: T-577 326 (including crypto), T-578 306, and T-580's swing_dev_f3 132 cells already run (best DSR 0.37), not 'pending'. T-578's strongest region (20-day equity ETFs) informed this design, so its 2026-01..09 development window must not be reused as evidence.
rows.data_notes: Local daily bars cover 123 symbols for about 10 years (mandel/ml_data/bars/1d), including about 26 non-leveraged equity ETFs, 7 bond ETFs and 5 commodity ETFs. FINRA short interest covers ETFs (SPY, XLK, TLT and GLD present from 2017-12-29; 8,326-10,837 symbols per date). finra-regsho-cnms 2018-08..2026-10; fomc-meetings; Cboe implied-vol indices. The stock-level arm is survivor-only (rule 9).
rows.lookahead_risks: FINRA short interest is published about 8 business days after settlement, so features use the publication date. RegSHO is usable at the end of the trade day. The target starts at the next open. Rows must be purged unless their target window ends before the fit date. The ETF list was chosen in 2026 (mild survivor bias for large ETFs; T-420 precedent). Design choices informed by T-578's 2026 development results mean 2026-01..09 must be excluded from the new development window.
rows.missing_data: The stock-level version needs a survivorship-free point-in-time universe and French NYSE breakpoints; it stays a separate blocked follow-up.

final.claim: On the ML program's non-leveraged US-listed ETFs (local daily bars; TQQQ, SQQQ, IBIT and ETHA excluded), a ridge or gradient-boosting model refit each January on an expanding window, using only price-free features stamped at publication, predicts the 63-session excess return. Traded as an equal-weight top-fifth minus bottom-fifth book in 3 overlapping monthly tranches, net of T-577's per-side costs and 50 bp a year borrow, at least one model has a 2019-01..2025-09 development DSR of at least 0.95 counting every ML-program cell, and that model has a positive mean net return over the first 12 lockbox decisions from 2026-10. The features are FINRA short interest and days to cover at the FINRA publication date, the 20-day RegSHO short-volume ratio, volume and dollar-volume z-scores, realised volatility, downside semivariance and skewness of daily returns, the matched Cboe implied-vol index where one exists, and days to the next FOMC decision and CPI release.
final.statistic: Per model: development net Sharpe of the tranche book on monthly decisions 2019-01..2025-09 and its DSR over N = all ML-program cells (764 so far plus these 2); lockbox mean net return per decision over 2026-10..2027-09. Reported: feature importance by net contribution; the minimum annual Sharpe needed for DSR 0.95 at this N and length, stated before reading.
final.null: No model passes both the development DSR and the lockbox.
final.procedure: At each month-end t, the universe is the ETFs with at least 252 sessions of history by t. Features use only values with available_at <= t. Past-return levels (momentum) are excluded so that price stays the target. Target: log return from the open after t over 63 sessions, minus the DTB3 accrual. Annual refit on an expanding window from the first year with FINRA data, with rows purged unless their target ends before the fit date. Jegadeesh-Titman tranches, both legs costed. The T-578 development window (2026-01..09) is excluded because it informed this design; the 2026-10 lockbox stays sealed until development is final. Baselines: always-long the ETF set; a single-feature days-to-cover sort; family ablations (drop the short-interest features, drop the implied-vol features).
final.data: mandel/ml_data/bars/1d (local), finra-short-interest-*, finra-regsho-cnms-*, cboe implied-vol index histories, fomc-meetings, macro-release-cpi, fred-DTB3
final.pass: Some model with development DSR >= 0.95 (N = all ML-program cells) AND a positive lockbox mean net return over 12 lockbox decisions. A survivor goes to a separately pre-registered forward paper record, never directly live.
final.controls: Always-long and single-feature baselines on the same tranches; family ablations; costs per side and borrow; turnover reported; the T-578 window excluded from the evidence; the stock-level version stays blocked until a point-in-time universe exists (rule 9).

rows.reason: The design lessons (longer horizons, liquid instruments, publication-stamped price-free inputs) are supported by the opened sources. The proposed stock-level test, however, would be NOT JUDGED under rule 9, and FINRA history starts 2017-12. Re-scoped to a survivorship-light ETF version that is testable now on local bars, deflated over all 764+ ML cells, with the T-578 window excluded to avoid a forking path.

knowledge.title: Volatility management, variance risk, futures curves and positioning: which published predictors survive costs and publication (literature survey)
knowledge.markdown:
# Volatility management, variance risk, futures curves and positioning: which published predictors survive costs and publication (literature survey)

- **Authors / kind:** survey of 15 strategy claims, mostly from peer-reviewed journals, plus two working papers, practitioner research and EIA data. Lead papers: Moreira-Muir with its critics Cederburg et al. and Barroso-Detzel; Harvey et al.; Shu-Yu-Mulvey; Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou; Boons-Porras Prado; Kang-Rouwenhorst-Tang.
- **Links:** https://www.nber.org/papers/w22208 · https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P135_The_impact_of.pdf · https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05272v3 · https://public.econ.duke.edu/~boller/Published_Papers/rfs_09.pdf · https://www.chicagofed.org/-/media/publications/working-papers/2025/wp2025-17.pdf
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.40 (fraction of the sources actually read and verified: 14 opened in full, 8 at abstract level, about 25 cited replications not opened).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** full text of the 14 unmarked entries under Sources used (Shu-Yu-Mulvey's Table 4 checked exactly), abstracts of the 8 marked ones. The search allowance ran out before replication searches on tail risk, vol-of-vol and hedging pressure.
- **Selected because:** they use the learning program's non-price inputs (realised and implied volatility, variance risk premium, futures term structure, COT positioning, short interest, shares outstanding, dollar volume) and bear on why T-577/T-578/T-580 found nothing in 764 cells.

## What it says

- **Volatility-managed market (Moreira-Muir).** Scale equity exposure by inverse realised variance: volatility persists but expected returns do not rise with it. In-sample alphas replicate; real-time gains fail for most factors (Cederburg et al.); after transaction costs only the managed market keeps its alpha, in high-sentiment periods (Barroso-Detzel). Harvey et al.: US equities 1927-2017 Sharpe 0.40 unscaled vs 0.48-0.51 scaled, robust to costs. No 2015-2026 decay study found.
- **Downside semivariance scaling (Wang-Yan, to 2018).** Scaling by bad volatility beats total-variance scaling because high downside volatility also predicts lower returns. Shares authors with Cederburg et al.; no post-2018 check.
- **Volatility-scaled momentum (Barroso-Santa-Clara, 1927-2011).** Scaling UMD by its 6-month realised volatility "nearly eliminates crashes and nearly doubles the Sharpe ratio". The premium underneath has decayed: +11.3%/yr 1993-2008, +0.1%/yr 2009-2026 (T-446).
- **Conditional multifactor timing (DeMiguel et al., 1967-2020).** Factor weights linear in market volatility, optimised net of stock-level costs with trades netted across factors: out-of-sample net Sharpe 13% above the unconditional portfolio. The gain rests on the netting.
- **Where volatility targeting pays (Harvey et al., 60 assets).** Sharpe rises only in equities and credit, where the leverage effect lives; bonds, FX and commodities gain nothing, though left tails thin everywhere. Not replicated after 2017.
- **Better volatility forecasts (HAR-RV with semivariances or implied volatility).** Bollerslev et al. 2018: realised-volatility models track a risk target better, worth 8-19 bp/yr over simple models after costs; Sharpe is insensitive to the estimator (Harvey et al.). Risk control, not alpha.
- **Jump-model regime switching (Shu-Yu-Mulvey).** Two states on EWM downside deviation and Sortino ratios, a penalty per switch, applied from day t+2 at 10 bp a trade: S&P 500 1990-2023 Sharpe 0.68 vs a hidden Markov model 0.54 vs buy-and-hold 0.48, maximum drawdown -26.6% vs -55.2% for buy-and-hold. One research group; only 2024 onward is post-publication.
- **Skewness dispersion (Babiak et al., 2000-2022).** The cross-sectional spread of daily realised skewness from 5-minute returns predicts the S&P 500 (out-of-sample R^2 2.9% at 1 month), concentrated in FOMC months. Unreplicated; two-thirds of months contain a meeting.
- **Tail risk (Kelly-Jiang).** A monthly Hill exponent from pooled extreme stock returns: +1 SD forecasts +4.5% market excess return over a year. Replication unchecked.
- **Variance risk premium as a predictor (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou, 1990-2007).** VIX^2 minus realised variance predicts quarterly returns (t 2.86); with daily-return RV their own check gives t 2.34. Dew-Becker-Giglio: index-option alphas indistinguishable from zero for 15 years (a break near 2010): probably decayed.
- **Realised skewness in the cross-section (Amaya et al., 1993-2008).** Lowest-minus-highest weekly decile: 19-24 bp/week gross (t 3.65-3.70). Daily-return versions fail Hou-Xue-Zhang's replication (unopened).
- **Vol-of-vol (Baltussen et al., 1996-2014).** Stocks whose implied volatility is itself volatile underperform by 0.69%/month value-weighted, for up to 24 months and in Europe. No post-2014 US replication found.
- **Commodity carry (Szymanowska et al.).** Basis (roll yield) sorts earn spot premia of 5-14%/yr: backwardation pays longs through storage and hedging pressure. Practitioners report post-2015 decay (snippets). EIA's free contract 1-4 curves (WTI, heating oil, RBOB, Henry Hub) end 2024-04-05.
- **Basis-momentum (Boons-Prado, 21 commodities 1959-2014).** Nearby minus second-nearby 12-month return: 18.38%/yr (t 6.73), nearly all roll return, beating basis and momentum.
- **COT hedging pressure and flow (Basu-Miffre; Kang-Rouwenhorst-Tang, 1994-2012).** Hedger net short earns a premium; hedger buying predicts +43 bp over 20 days. KRT sort on the Tuesday as-of date, and about half the return accrues before the Friday release.
- **Machine learning after costs (Robeco; Azevedo et al.).** 1-month ML strategies paid mainly before 2004; 3-12 month horizons net better over 2004-2021 through lower turnover. Azevedo et al. report a net LSTM alpha of 1.20%/month (t 3.46) but find cost-mitigation does not raise net anomaly returns. Avramov et al. (unverified) put the profits in microcaps.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** Most claims come from top journals with out-of-sample tests and costs; several were checked to the table. But method is not implementability: real-time, after-cost and post-publication evidence is contested (Cederburg, Barroso-Detzel, Dew-Becker-Giglio), two sources are unreplicated working papers, and Man AHL and Robeco are practitioners.

## What Mandel adopts

- **vol-target-spy-monthly-realtime:** the volatility-managed market, the one case Barroso-Detzel find survives costs. Target fixed ex ante, 40 trials in the DSR (with T-310's and T-562's), paired block bootstrap, power reported first: the Sharpe-difference SE (~0.10) is as large as the expected gain. T-310's pooled buy-and-hold gain (0.81 vs 0.63) was never judged alone.
- **vol-target-gain-by-leverage-effect:** Harvey's cross-asset prediction as a difference-in-differences, with own-volatility targets (a common 10% target pins bond ETFs at the cap and fakes a pass).
- **jump-model-derisk-spy:** the regime-switching successor to T-561/T-562, matching Mandel's guidance to the Kelly child that state models help where the state is measured directly (T-561 cut drawdown). 1994-2023 is labelled replication.
- **har-forecaster-risk-targeting-value:** HAR-RV forecasters judged on tracking error, not Sharpe, building on the QLIKE wins T-569 and T-572.
- **vrp-predicts-spy-3m-post-2010:** Mandel's first VRP timing test for SPY, with the decay prediction recorded before reading.
- **downside-semivariance-vs-total-scaling-factors** (2019-2026, weight cap 3) and **vol-scaled-umd-post-bsc** (from 2012, so the in-sample 2009 crash cannot carry it).
- **eia-energy-backwardation-timing** and **energy-basis-momentum-ts:** a time-series route around blocked T-371, momentum as competitor, one shared DSR.
- **cot-hedger-flow-post-release-etf:** the post-release half only, with point-in-time release stamps as in T-405.
- **vol-of-vol-stock-dolthub** (after a DoltHub fetch, rule-9 coverage gate) and **ml-price-free-etf-quarterly-v1:** 63-session horizon, publication-stamped short interest, days to cover, RegSHO short volume, dollar volume, realised and implied volatility and days to FOMC/CPI; DSR over every ML cell; T-578's 2026 window excluded.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- Factor timing beyond the market: post-publication premia are near zero (T-382, T-386, T-447, T-446) and timing lost to static (T-388; T-389 -0.03). DeMiguel et al. is dropped: its netting needs stock-level holdings.
- Volatility targeting as alpha: in T-310 scaling helped trend no more than buy-and-hold (DiD -0.082); above 1x, Mandel's leverage review for the small-account desk child found financing exceeds the edges.
- Skewness dispersion, Kelly-Jiang tail risk, weekly realised skewness: dropped. The archive has survivorship bias, the 5-minute cross-section has no free source, and a weekly decile book costs 40-80 bp/week against 19-24 bp gross. Option tail measures already failed (T-52, T-227).
- VRP timing: the gap exists (T-48, T-540) but VRP-conditioned rules failed (T-159, T-235, T-179).
- Carry and curves: every recent carry sleeve failed (T-381, T-368, T-431, T-433), as did commodity momentum (T-313) and VX curve rules (T-160, T-379, T-435); EIA curves stop in 2024, so a pass is historical. Offshore funding carry (Hyperliquid) is not US-legal, and on US venues the desk child killed it.
- COT: half of KRT's effect is unusable; gold COT showed nothing (T-405).
- Vol-of-vol: the VVIX premium (T-243, T-536) and low-volatility tilts (T-384, T-448), related claims, failed. FOMC concentration: Mandel's FOMC drift faded after 2016 (T-341).

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- Features, each point-in-time at its available_at: EWMA, HAR-RV and SHAR forecasts; downside semivariance; VRP = (VIX/100)^2/12 - RV21; vol-of-vol of Cboe implied-volatility indices; VIX/VIX3M term structure; online jump-model state (never smoothed); basis and basis-momentum; weekly COT change at release; short interest at FINRA publication; net share issuance from shares outstanding.
- Data to add: EIA contracts 1-4 (CL, HO, RB, NG); CFTC Socrata reports for eight more contracts; DoltHub volatility_history for all symbols plus delisted-name prices; French NYSE breakpoints; CANE, MTUM, VLUE.
- A shared volatility-targeting sizing layer in the ML harness, so prediction and sizing are judged apart; drawdown-only results count as risk overlays (T-561); survivors go to a forward paper record, never live.

## Cross-links

- A4 (MSM, T-569): MSM is a reported forecaster in the HAR test.
- 13 (HMM regime model): the jump model is its successor (T-561, T-562).
- 12, 14 (Claude trading workflows): add volatility sizing and cost-aware ML.
- Theories: T-310, T-311, T-371, T-405, T-446, T-561, T-562, T-569, T-572, T-577, T-578, T-580.

## Sources used

- Moreira & Muir (abstract): https://www.nber.org/papers/w22208
- Cederburg et al. (abstract): https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/COWY.pdf
- Barroso & Detzel (abstract): https://ciencia.ucp.pt/en/publications/do-limits-to-arbitrage-explain-the-benefits-of-volatility-managed/
- Wang & Yan (abstract): https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jbfina/v131y2021ics0378426621001576.html
- Barroso & Santa-Clara (abstract): https://run.unl.pt/bitstream/10362/11836/1/Barroso_2012.pdf
- DeMiguel et al.: https://lbsresearch.london.edu/id/eprint/3716/1/The%20Journal%20of%20Finance%20-%202024%20-%20DeMIGUEL%20-%20A%20Multifactor%20Perspective%20on%20Volatility%E2%80%90Managed%20Portfolios.pdf
- Harvey et al.: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P135_The_impact_of.pdf

candidates.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks (STMOM, turnover-conditioned 1-month return)
candidates.summary: Double-sort on last month's return and last month's share turnover. Among high-turnover stocks, last month's winners keep beating last month's losers. Among low-turnover stocks the usual one-month reversal holds. The paper's sample ends in 2018, so 2019-2026 is clean post-publication data. Not a duplicate: T-420 (low-turnover-conditioned momentum) and T-462 (weekly reversal) were ETF-only and both not_supported. T-307 (12-1 stock momentum) is blocked on universe, not on result.
candidates.mechanism: High turnover means a lot of trading went into last month's price move. That marks the move as carrying fundamental information, which some traders underweight, so the price underreacts and drifts on. Low-turnover moves are temporary price pressure from liquidity demanders, and that reverts. The other side is investors anchored on the old price; in the reversal leg, impatient liquidity demanders. The authors argue against the Llorente et al. information-asymmetry story, because STMOM is strongest in mega-caps.
variables: own past 1-month return as conditioner (not the target)
candidates.assets: US equities (large caps; executable on Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: monthly rebalance; the paper reports drift persisting about 12 months
candidates.claimed_effect: 1963-2018 US, value-weighted conditional deciles with NYSE breakpoints. STMOM +1.37%/month (t 4.74). STREV* (low-turnover reversal) -1.41%/month (t -7.13). Net of CRSP half-spreads STMOM earns 1.00%/month (t 3.47); the strategy turns over about 90% a month and costs about 0.37%/month. Largest-500 2x2 version +0.42%/month (t 4.91). Megacap quintile +0.53%/month (t 2.53). The 1991-2018 subsample is stronger (+2.03%/month, t 4.80), while STREV* weakens across subsamples (-3.96% to -1.15%). International (22 markets, 1993-2018): STMOM 1.39%/month.
candidates.replication: In-paper international replication across 22 developed markets. A later study finds no short-term momentum in China, though reversal and the turnover effect do exist there. A CXO review notes STREV* has not worked since the mid-2000s, even gross. I found no independent US out-of-sample study for 2019-2026. That makes Mandel's test a genuine post-publication test. McLean-Pontiff's 58% average post-publication decline is the prior to expect.

sources.title: Short-term Momentum (Medhat and Schmeling, RFS 35(3) 2022)
