candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with Yahoo daily-history (the T-473 fja05680 membership join). Delisted names are absent, so this is an upper bound; say so. Turnover TO(m) = sum of daily volume in month m / shares outstanding. Shares outstanding is the latest sec-companyfacts dei value whose filing date is on or before the month-end. At each month-end, form independent halves on r(m) and TO(m), as in the paper's largest-500 2x2. Also run conditional deciles as a secondary cell. Long high-TO winners, short high-TO losers, value-weighted, filled at the next session's close. Also run the paper's implementation-lag variant (form on days 1..T-3). Hold one month and add 3-month overlapping cohorts. Charge 10 bps per side on traded weight plus 0.5%/yr borrow on the short leg. Statistic: mean monthly net long-short return with HAC t, and FF5+UMD alpha from Mandel's Fama-French archive. Pre-registered pass: 2010-2026 net mean > 0 with p < 0.05, a 2019-2026 post-publication mean > 0, both halves positive, and DSR >= 0.95 over the declared cells (2x2 or deciles; lag or no lag; 1 or 3-month hold). Run plain STREV and plain 12-1 momentum as baseline trials. Also add r(1m) x TO(1m) as an interaction feature to T-578's swing models. F0 currently holds relative volume only (mean IC about +0.01); the literature says volume's information sits in its interaction with returns, not in its level.

candidates.name: High-volume return premium in single stocks, split into visibility versus attention-buying shocks
candidates.summary: Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin: stocks with an unusually high-volume day or week, without a large price move, rise over the following month (visibility). Barber-Odean / Barber et al.: attention-grabbing days that retail investors herd into are followed by negative abnormal returns. Mandel has tested the visibility version only on ETFs and crypto: T-419 not_supported (ETF +6.9 bp, BTC/ETH +378 bp over 10 days); T-546 not_supported on altcoins, which instead showed -1.80% net. Single US stocks, the original setting, are untested. The two signs can be reconciled by conditioning on the price move and on attention.
candidates.mechanism: Visibility (Merton investor-recognition): a volume shock with no news raises the stock's investor base, lowers its required return and lifts its price. Attention: on high-attention days retail investors are net buyers (Barber-Odean), push prices above value, and the price then reverts. Institutions and short sellers take the other side.
candidates.assets: US equities (mid and large caps; Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: The GKM abstract reports direction only (high-volume stocks rise, low-volume stocks fall over the following month); I did not recover a magnitude. Kaniel-Ozoguz-Starks find the premium in 41 countries, and say it is not explained by risk or liquidity. Barber et al. 2022: the top stocks bought each day by Robinhood users have mean 20-day abnormal returns of -4.7%.
candidates.replication: Replicated internationally (Kaniel-Ozoguz-Starks 2012). Contested in Korea: Chae-Kang (2019) find a low-volume premium, and a 2025 preprint (Kang) recovers HVRP only for institutional-intensity shocks. Mandel's T-419 found little in liquid ETFs, a large crypto-major effect that failed deflation, and the opposite sign in altcoins. That is consistent with the attention channel dominating in retail-heavy assets. I found no 2015-2026 US single-stock replication.

sources.title: The High-Volume Return Premium (Gervais, Kaniel, Mingelgrin, JF 2001)
The high volume return premium: Cross-country evidence (Kaniel, Ozoguz, Starks, JFE 2012)
Attention-Induced Trading and Returns: Evidence from Robinhood Users (JF 2022)
Sources and Nonlinearity of High Volume Return Premium (Kang, arXiv 2512.14134)

candidates.proposed_test: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 plus the other US stocks in the 901-symbol daily-history archive, 2008-2026. Weekly volume surprise = log(weekly volume) minus its trailing 49-week mean, residualised on the market's surprise. That is T-419's idiosyncratic design, so market-wide volume weeks do not inflate counts. Two pre-registered buckets with opposite signs. (a) Visibility: top-decile surprise with |weekly return| < 1 trailing sigma; claim positive. (b) Attention: top-decile surprise with weekly return > +2 sigma, plus top-decile StockTwits intensity where Mandel has it; claim negative. Enter at the next Monday open and hold 20 sessions. Use beta-adjusted returns versus SPY, with 10 bps round trip (plus 0.5%/yr borrow for the short bucket). Statistics: event mean with date-clustered bootstrap CIs, T-419's block-shift placebo (2,000 shifts), a calendar-time portfolio with HAC t, halves 2008-2016 / 2017-2026, and DSR over the declared cells (two buckets, three size terciles, 10/20-session holds). Pass if bucket (a) > +50 bps or bucket (b) < -50 bps with placebo p < 0.01 in the size tercile the theory names (small/mid for visibility).

candidates.name: Aggregate Amihud illiquidity as a market-timing signal (time-series illiquidity premium)
candidates.summary: Amihud (2002) showed that expected market illiquidity (average |return| / dollar volume) predicts higher future market excess returns, while unexpected illiquidity coincides with lower contemporaneous returns. The cross-sectional version is T-455, blocked on survivorship. The time-series version uses aggregates, so it is far less sensitive to missing delisted names. It is not registered. Related but different: T-421 (Corwin-Schultz spread shock on SPY), not_supported.
candidates.mechanism: Investors demand compensation for expected trading costs and liquidity risk. When the market is expected to be illiquid, prices are set lower and expected returns rise. An illiquidity shock forces sales and depresses prices. Holders who must sell in illiquid states are on the other side.
candidates.assets: US equity index ETFs (SPY, IWM, MDY; Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Amihud 2002, 1964-1997 NYSE: expected illiquidity positively predicts excess market returns and unexpected illiquidity is contemporaneously negative. OSAP lists the cross-sectional Illiquidity predictor at t = 6.6 (equal-weighted). Amihud-Noh 2021 report the ILLIQ premium stays significant after mispricing, sentiment and seasonality controls, and that market ILLIQ beats market IDVOL in time series. For the adjacent Pastor-Stambaugh traded liquidity factor, the 4-factor alpha rose from 0.37%/month (t 2.14, 1968-1999) to 0.68%/month (t 2.31, 2000-2015) in Li et al.'s out-of-sample check, as reported by Pastor-Stambaugh 2019.
candidates.replication: Contested and largely decayed. Harris-Amato (CFR 2019) reproduce Amihud on current CRSP, but 1998-2015 shows a much weaker relation, and illiquidity levels there are about a tenth of earlier ones. Drienko, Smith and von Reibnitz (CFR 2019) find the out-of-sample time-series results lose significance and monotonicity, which they link to decimalisation. Ben-Rephael-Kadan-Wohl (JFQA 2015) document a diminishing liquidity premium. Hou-Xue-Zhang find 96% of trading-friction anomalies fail with NYSE breakpoints and value weights. Expect a fail. Run it because it is cheap and it settles a well-known claim.

sources.title: Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects (Amihud, JFM 2002)
Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects: A Replication (Harris and Amato, CFR 2019)
A review of the return-illiquidity relationship (Drienko, Smith, von Reibnitz, CFR 2019)
Liquidity Risk After 20 Years (Pastor and Stambaugh)

candidates.proposed_test: Build monthly aggregate ILLIQ from the 901-symbol daily-history archive (common stocks only, price > $5). Take each stock's mean of |r_d| / (close x volume) over the month, then the cross-sectional mean, scaled by the market-cap growth ratio as Amihud does so the series is stationary. Split expected from unexpected illiquidity with an AR(1) fitted on trailing data only. Predict next-month SPY and IWM excess returns over DTB3, and IWM minus SPY. Statistic: out-of-sample R^2 against the historical mean, expanding window, first forecast 2005-01, Clark-West test. Secondary: a timing rule that overweights IWM versus bills when expected ILLIQ is in its trailing top tercile, charged 5 bps per switch, Sharpe against buy-and-hold with a block bootstrap. Pass: OOS R^2 > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05, the same sign in 2005-2015 and 2016-2026, and the timing rule beating buy-and-hold net. Report the minimum detectable R^2, because about 260 monthly observations give low power.

candidates.name: Aggregate share turnover as a sentiment / overpricing signal (Baker-Stein, Jones)
candidates.summary: High market-wide liquidity, especially high share turnover, predicts lower subsequent market returns at one-year horizons. Jones (2002): over a century, high spreads predict high returns and high turnover predicts low returns, beating the dividend yield. Not a duplicate: T-398 (mutual-fund flows) and T-449 (net issuance) were not_supported, but turnover itself is untested.
candidates.mechanism: With short-sale constraints, unusually high liquidity and turnover means irrational, overconfident investors who underreact to order flow dominate trading. Prices are then inflated, so expected returns are low. Firms issue equity into such markets. The other side is long-horizon holders and issuers.
candidates.assets: US equity index ETFs (SPY, RSP, IWM; Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Jones (2002, Dow stocks 1900-2000): high turnover predicts low returns one year or more ahead and dominates the dividend yield; no number in the abstract. Baker-Stein (JFM 2004): aggregate turnover and equity issuance each predict lower equal-weighted market returns; no magnitude in the abstract.
candidates.replication: I found no post-2004 replication. Turnover trended up structurally after decimalisation and HFT, so any test must detrend it, and the old level-based evidence may not carry over. With about 20 independent annual observations since 2005, power is low and the result is likely inconclusive.

sources.title: Market liquidity as a sentiment indicator (Baker and Stein, JFM 2004)
A Century of Stock Market Liquidity and Trading Costs (Jones)
The Diminishing Liquidity Premium (Ben-Rephael, Kadan, Wohl, JFQA 2015)

candidates.proposed_test: Monthly aggregate turnover = sum of volume over the 901-symbol stock archive / sum of point-in-time shares outstanding (sec-companyfacts by filing date). Detrend as log(TO / trailing 60-month mean TO), so only information published by month-end enters. Predict the next-12-month excess return of SPY and of an equal-weighted proxy (RSP from 2003, or the archive's equal-weighted mean). Statistic: slope with Hodrick (1992) standard errors on overlapping data, plus non-overlapping annual regressions. Also an out-of-sample R^2 with an expanding window from 2005 and a Clark-West test. Also run a monthly risk-off rule: hold bills instead of RSP when detrended turnover is in its trailing top decile, charged 5 bps per switch. Pass: negative slope with p < 0.05, OOS R^2 > 0, the same sign excluding 2008-2009 and 2020, and a reported MDE. Deflate jointly with T-398 and T-449 as one sentiment family.

candidates.name: Volatility of liquidity: stocks with volatile turnover / dollar volume earn lower returns (Chordia-Subrahmanyam-Anshuman)
candidates.summary: The level of trading activity is priced negatively (the illiquidity premium), and so, surprisingly, is its variability. Stocks whose turnover or dollar volume swings more have lower future returns. OSAP lists std_turn and VolSD as clear predictors. Not registered in Mandel.
candidates.mechanism: There is no settled risk story, which makes it a puzzle. Candidates: an option value of liquidity (investors pay for stocks whose liquidity can spike, per Pereira-Zhang); attention or clientele effects; and mispricing among hard-to-arbitrage, volatile-volume names. Arbitrage is limited because these names are costly to short.
candidates.assets: US equities (Alpaca; a short leg needs borrow)
candidates.claimed_effect: Original NYSE/AMEX 1966-1995 sample: std of turnover t = 3.74 and std of dollar volume t = 3.56 (equal-weighted, OSAP SignalDoc). The abstract carries no magnitude.
candidates.replication: OSAP reproduces both as clear predictors on CRSP (equal-weighted). Hou-Xue-Zhang (RFS 2020): with microcaps mitigated (NYSE breakpoints, value weights), 96% of trading-friction anomalies fail |t| > 1.96. McLean-Pontiff: predictor returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication. Expect the value-weighted large-cap version to be near zero. OSAP's published long-short series let Mandel measure the 2015-2024 decay without CRSP.

sources.title: Trading activity and expected stock returns (Chordia, Subrahmanyam, Anshuman, JFE 2001)
Replicating Anomalies (Hou, Xue, Zhang, RFS 2020)
Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability? (McLean and Pontiff, JF 2016)
Open Source Asset Pricing data (std_turn, VolSD, DolVol, Illiquidity portfolios)

candidates.proposed_test: Two steps. (1) Offline decay check, no trading: read OSAP's published monthly long-short returns for std_turn, VolSD, DolVol, Illiquidity, ShareVol and zerotrade. Report mean, t, and the post-2015 mean against the original-sample mean, as an evidence row and not a verdict on tradability. (2) Mandel test on point-in-time S&P 500 plus the 901-symbol archive, 2008-2026. At each month-end, take the coefficient of variation of monthly turnover over the prior 36 months (CSA's window, scaled to strip the level). Sort into quintiles, long low CV and short high CV, value-weighted and equal-weighted as separate declared cells. Control by double-sorting on turnover level and size. Fill at the next close, hold one month, charge 10 bps per side plus 1%/yr borrow on the short. Statistic: net monthly mean with HAC t and FF5+UMD alpha. Pass only if the value-weighted cell is positive net with p < 0.05 in both 2008-2016 and 2017-2026. The equal-weighted cell is informative only, because of survivorship and microcap issues.

candidates.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) predicts negative returns
candidates.summary: Stocks with high option volume relative to share volume underperform the following week. The proposed reason: informed traders with bad news prefer options when shorting is costly, and the embedded leverage draws in informed call trading. Derivative volume is a non-price input. Not registered in Mandel. Blocked on data: Mandel has no per-symbol option-volume history (chains only from 2026-10-14 plus the capture box).
candidates.mechanism: Short-sale costs push negative private information into the options market, so relative option volume rises before bad news (Johnson-So). Ge-Lin-Pearson show the leverage channel dominates: opening call purchases are the strongest predictor. Market makers who sell those options and hedge are on the other side, along with uninformed stock holders.
candidates.assets: US optionable single stocks (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Johnson-So (JFE 2012, 1996-2010): the lowest O/S decile beats the highest by 0.34% per week (about 19% annualised), stronger when short-sale costs are high or option leverage is low, and O/S forecasts earnings news. A Quantpedia summary reports a 1.47%/month risk-adjusted spread over 1996-2008. OSAP lists OptionVolume1 at t = 3.45 (equal-weighted).
candidates.replication: Ge-Lin-Pearson (JFE 2016) confirm the effect with signed volume. Blau et al. (2014) find O/S predicts at daily, weekly and monthly horizons, per the 2024 JDQS review. A 2024 Korean study finds the opposite sign. I found no US evidence for 2015-2026. The retail options boom since 2020 (0DTE, call buying) could strengthen the effect or turn it into noise; this is untested.

sources.title: The option to stock volume ratio and future returns (Johnson and So, JFE 2012)
Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns? (Ge, Lin, Pearson, JFE 2016)
Whose option ratios contain information about future stock prices? (JDQS 2024)

candidates.proposed_test: Forward test from the capture box, plus a backfill if OCC per-symbol daily volume history can be pulled. Universe: the roughly 200 most option-active US names inside point-in-time S&P 500. Daily O/S = total option contracts traded across the chain / shares traded that day; the weekly O/S is the week's sums. Each Friday close, sort into deciles; long the lowest-O/S decile, short the highest, equal-weighted. Enter at Monday's open and exit at the next Monday's open. Charge 10 bps per side plus FINRA-based borrow (high days-to-cover names at 3%/yr). Pre-registered conditional cell: the spread is larger in the top tercile of FINRA days-to-cover (the short-cost channel). Statistic: mean weekly long-short net with HAC t. Need at least 104 weeks for the forward version; backfill 2016-2026 if OCC history exists. Report the call-only O/S variant (Ge-Lin-Pearson) as a declared second cell, and run DSR over the 4 cells.

candidates.name: Earnings-announcement premium conditioned on past announcement-period volume
candidates.summary: Stocks expected to announce earnings earn a premium in the announcement month. The premium is largest for stocks whose volume historically surges around announcements, which points to attention-driven retail buying. Duplicates T-339 (earnings-announcement-premium, blocked), but adds the volume conditioning, a point-in-time expected-date rule from SEC filings, and evidence that the US premium disappeared after 2004.
candidates.mechanism: Announcements grab attention, small investors buy what catches their attention, and they push prices up temporarily. A systematic-risk explanation also exists (Savor-Wilson). Attention-driven buyers are on the other side.
candidates.assets: US equities (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Frazzini-Lamont (NBER w13090, CRSP/Compustat 1972-2004): long expected announcers and short non-announcers earns over 60 bps per month. The premium lasts about four weeks, is especially large in large caps, and is largest for stocks with high past announcement volume; the NBER digest gives no numeric volume spread. Heitz, Narayanamoorthy and Zekhnini: average weekly announcement excess returns fell by about 40 bps after 2004 (figure from the search summary of their working paper; paper not opened). They link the decline to the 2004 8-K rule changes, and report the premium persists internationally.
candidates.replication: Barber et al. find a global premium. In the US it is contested and likely gone: Heitz et al. call it disappearing after 2004. A notification study finds the premium falls 0.44% for firms that start sending announcement notifications. Mandel tests from 2010, which is inside the decayed period. A fail would confirm decay, and a pass would contradict it.

sources.title: The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume (Frazzini and Lamont, NBER w13090)
Stocks Rise Around Earnings Announcements (NBER Digest)
Filings of Material Information and the Disappearing Earnings Announcement Premium (Heitz, Narayanamoorthy, Zekhnini)

candidates.proposed_test: Take earnings dates from sec-submissions: 8-K filings with Item 2.02 (acceptance timestamp), with 10-Q/10-K dates as a fallback. Set each stock's expected announcement month to the same month one year earlier. This uses only past filings and avoids the look-ahead of using realised dates. Past announcement volume ratio = mean volume over [-1, +1] of the prior 4 announcements / mean volume on all other days in that year. Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 plus the 901-symbol archive, 2010-2026. Each month-end: long expected announcers in the top tercile of the volume ratio, short non-announcers, equal-weighted, filled at the next close and held one month. Charge 10 bps per side. Weekly variant: hold from 5 sessions before the expected week through 2 sessions after. Statistic: net monthly mean with HAC t, and the difference between top and bottom volume-ratio terciles. Pass: net > 50 bps/month (T-339's bar) with p < 0.05, both halves positive, and the top-tercile spread > 0. Record the decay prior up front.

candidates.name: Volume-confirmed 52-week high/low breakouts
candidates.summary: Volume jumps when a stock's price crosses its 52-week high or low, more so the longer since the last extreme and the smaller the firm. Returns after either crossing are reliably positive, with elevated small-investor buying. This is the academic version of the trader's volume-confirmed breakout. Mandel's T-309 (52-week-high nearness, ETFs) and T-304 (Donchian breakout) were not_supported, but neither conditioned on volume nor used stocks.
candidates.mechanism: Investors anchor on past extremes (bounded rationality). A cross of the range limit triggers trading by investors who use it as a reference point, and the market underreacts to the information in the breakout, so prices drift. Anchored sellers are on the other side: they sell at the old high or capitulate at the low.
variables: volume in units (abnormal volume at the crossing)
candidates.assets: US equities (Alpaca); ETF version is already T-309
candidates.claimed_effect: Huddart-Lang-Yetman (Management Science 2009): volume is strikingly higher when price crosses either range limit, and returns after either event are reliably positive. The abstract gives no magnitudes.
candidates.replication: The related George-Hwang 52-week-high momentum effect is widely replicated, but Mandel's ETF test failed. I found no independent replication of the volume-conditioned version. Sullivan-Timmermann-White (JF 1999) is the data-snooping warning. From memory, its 7,846-rule universe includes on-balance-volume rules, and no rule survives the Reality Check out of sample. Treat the OBV / volume-breakout family as presumptively overfit.

sources.title: Volume and Price Patterns Around a Stock's 52-Week Highs and Lows: Theory and Evidence (Management Science 2009)
Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap (Sullivan, Timmermann, White, JF 1999)

candidates.proposed_test: Events on point-in-time S&P 500 plus the 901-symbol archive, 2005-2026. An event is a close above the trailing 252-session high (or below the low) with no prior crossing in the last 60 sessions. Abnormal volume AV = event-day volume / trailing 50-day median; confirmed = top tercile, unconfirmed = bottom tercile. Enter at the next open and hold 20 sessions. Use market-adjusted returns (beta vs SPY from trailing 252 days) and charge 10 bps round trip. Pre-registered claim: confirmed-high events earn a positive mean and beat unconfirmed-high events by at least 50 bps. Report lows separately, since HLY say returns are positive after lows too. Statistics: date-clustered bootstrap CIs; a placebo of random dates matched on trailing volatility and distance to the high; halves 2005-2015 / 2016-2026; DSR over the declared cells (5/20/60-session horizons, high/low, 2 AV cutoffs). Adding AV x 52-week-high distance as an ML interaction feature in T-578 is a cheap second check.

candidates.name: Dynamic volume-return relation (volume-price divergence): high-volume moves reverse or continue depending on who is trading
candidates.summary: Price changes on high volume reverse more at the index and large-stock level (Campbell-Grossman-Wang), but continue where informed trading dominates (Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang). Lee-Swaminathan add that past volume shapes momentum. This is the academic content behind OBV and volume-price divergence. Partially overlaps T-419 (volume without a price move); the return x volume interaction itself is untested and is not among the ML features.
candidates.mechanism: Volume from hedging or liquidity needs moves prices away from value; liquidity providers absorb it and the move reverts, so they earn the reversal. Volume from private information moves prices toward value, and the move continues as the information diffuses. The sign of the r(t) x V(t) coefficient therefore tracks information asymmetry.
variables: market cap / spread as information-asymmetry proxies
candidates.assets: US equities and ETFs (Alpaca); crypto via Coinbase as a second market
candidates.claimed_effect: From memory, not re-verified (abstracts give no numbers): CGW (QJE 1993) find daily index-return autocorrelation falls as volume rises. LMSW (RFS 2002) find the interaction coefficient is positive (continuation) for small, high-spread stocks and negative for large ones. Neither reports net-of-cost trading returns. Lee-Swaminathan (JF 2000): OSAP's MomVol (momentum in high-volume stocks) has t = 5.78 over 1965-1995.
candidates.replication: Contested. Medhat-Schmeling (2022) find monthly continuation strongest among the largest stocks, which contradicts LMSW's size pattern at monthly horizons. Bianchi et al. (2022) find a significant lagged-return x volume interaction in crypto. Mandel's ETF tests of turnover-conditioned momentum and reversal (T-420, T-462) failed.

sources.title: Dynamic Volume-Return Relation of Individual Stocks (Llorente, Michaely, Saar, Wang, RFS 2002)
Trading Volume and Serial Correlation in Stock Returns (Campbell, Grossman, Wang, QJE 1993)
Price Momentum and Trading Volume (Lee and Swaminathan, JF 2000)

candidates.proposed_test: Use daily Fama-MacBeth regressions on point-in-time S&P 500 plus the 901-symbol archive, 2005-2026. Regress r(t+1..t+5) (open t+1 to open t+6) on r(t), r(t) x AV(t) and AV(t). AV is log volume minus its trailing 60-day mean, residualised on the market's AV. Controls: size and trailing volatility. Estimate separately by size tercile. Pre-registered signs: interaction < 0 in the top size tercile (CGW), > 0 in the bottom tercile (LMSW). Use Newey-West t with 5 lags; pass at |t| > 2.8 to allow for the search (Harvey-Liu-Zhu style hurdle). Trading translation, only if the slope passes: in the top size tercile, fade the top and bottom deciles of r(t) when AV(t) is in the top tercile. Weekly rebalance, dollar-neutral, 10 bps per side, net Sharpe with HAC. Repeat on the point-in-time top-50 Coinbase USD products as an independent market at 50 bps round trip. Feed r x AV into T-578 as a declared F0xF2 interaction feature.

candidates.name: Market intraday momentum conditioned on volume and short-gamma / leveraged-ETF hedging demand
candidates.summary: The return from the previous close to the first half-hour (or to 15:30) predicts the last half-hour's return. The effect is stronger on high-volume and high-volatility days, and is linked to option-dealer and leveraged-ETF gamma hedging. Duplicates T-427 (intraday-half-hour-momentum, not_supported unconditionally on SPY 2023-2026). The new element is the volume / gamma conditioning that the primary papers name ahead of time, so it is not a post-hoc fork. T-217 (positive-GEX 0DTE condor) is blocked on the same gamma data.
candidates.mechanism: Short-gamma hedgers (option market makers, leveraged-ETF sponsors rebalancing to constant leverage) must buy late in up days and sell late in down days. Infrequent rebalancers and late-informed traders add to it. The price pressure is mechanical and reverts over the following days. Hedgers pay; liquidity providers who fade it lose until the close.
adjacent_variables: leveraged-ETF AUM x L(L-1) rebalancing demand
candidates.assets: SPY, QQQ, IWM (Alpaca); ES/NQ futures (CME)
candidates.horizon: intraday (last 30 minutes), reversal over the next days
candidates.claimed_effect: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou (JFE 2018), SPY 1993-2013: first-half-hour return predicts last-half-hour return; stronger on volatile days, high-volume days, recession days and macro-news days; also present in 10 other ETFs. From memory, the predictive R^2 is about 1.6%; not re-verified. Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021): over 60+ futures, 1974-2020, the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes everywhere, reverts over the next days, and is tied to gamma hedging. Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon (practitioner, SSRN 2024): a SPY intraday-momentum rule with VWAP-based dynamic trailing stops, 2007 to early 2024, earned 19.6%/yr net with Sharpe 1.33.
candidates.replication: Replicated across asset classes by Baltussen et al. through 2020. Mandel's own unconditional SPY test (T-427, 720 sessions, 2023-2026) failed. The Zarattini result is unreplicated practitioner work with many design choices; treat it as a candidate, not evidence.

sources.title: Market Intraday Momentum (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou, JFE 2018)
Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens, JFE 2021)
Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY) (Zarattini, Aziz, Barbon)

candidates.proposed_test: SPY, QQQ and IWM. Use Mandel's 60-minute bars (2 years) for a first-hour / last-hour version now. For the half-hour design, use 2016-2026 minute bars from Alpaca. Measure relative volume within the same feed: the IEX feed is a small share of consolidated volume. Conditioning variables, pre-registered in this order: (1) RVOL30 = 09:30-10:00 volume / trailing 20-session median of the same window; (2) negative dealer-gamma days from capture-box chains (forward only); (3) leveraged-ETF rebalancing demand = sum over TQQQ/SQQQ/UPRO/SPXU/TNA/TZA of NAV x shares outstanding x L(L-1) x r(prev close -> 15:30), captured daily forward. Rule: hold from 15:30 to the official close in the sign of r(prev close -> 15:30), only on top-tercile RVOL30 days; 2 bps round trip. Statistic: mean net per trade on conditioned days, and the conditioned-minus-unconditioned difference. Use a block bootstrap by week, halves, and a placebo of random-tercile days. Deflate together with T-427's earlier trial. Pass: conditioned mean net > 0 with p < 0.05 and greater than on low-RVOL days. Report the next-day reversal Baltussen predicts as a falsification check.

candidates.name: Opening-range breakout on 'Stocks in Play' selected by relative volume
candidates.summary: A 5-minute opening-range breakout traded only on the stocks with the highest relative volume at the open (usually news-driven) beat an index ORB and passive exposure over 2016-2023 on 7,000+ US stocks. Related to T-426 (opening-range-breakout on QQQ only, blocked). The cross-sectional relative-volume selection is new.
candidates.mechanism: Unusual opening volume flags a stock being repriced on fresh information. Order splitting by institutions and slow information diffusion make the opening direction persist into the close. Late or slow liquidity providers and stale limit orders are on the other side.
candidates.assets: US equities (Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz (SSRN 2024), more than 7,000 US stocks, 2016-2023: limiting the 5-minute ORB to Stocks in Play helps even after transaction costs. A top-20 Stocks-in-Play portfolio returned over 1,600% net in total, with Sharpe 2.81 and 36% annualised alpha, against 198% for passive S&P 500 exposure.
candidates.replication: I found no independent replication. The figures come from an authors' backtest with free parameters: top-N, RVOL cutoff, stop as an ATR fraction. Shannon's maker-fill learnings warn that stop-entry fills at breakouts are adverse-selection-prone, and that paper fills overstate.

sources.title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market (Zarattini, Barbon, Aziz)

candidates.proposed_test: This needs a full-universe 5-minute history. Mandel has only 60 days of 5-minute bars on 123 symbols, so use those as a smoke test only. Primary: a forward paper test on Alpaca from capture start. Universe: the archive's US stocks with price > $5 and 14-day ADV > 1M shares. At 09:35 ET, rank on RVOL5 = first 5-minute volume / trailing 14-session mean of the same bar (same-feed volume only). Take the top 20 with RVOL5 > 1 and a non-doji first bar. Place a stop entry at the first bar's high (if green) or low (if red), a stop-loss at 10% of 14-day ATR, and exit at the close. Equal risk per name. Costs: $0.0035/share plus one tick of slippage on entry and exit. Statistic: mean daily net portfolio return and Sharpe with HAC over at least 250 sessions, against a placebo of the same rule on 20 random eligible names each day. Pass: Stocks-in-Play minus placebo > 0 with p < 0.05, and an absolute net Sharpe > 1. Decide the parameters now, not after viewing results.

candidates.name: Intraday return periodicity and volume-profile (VWAP) execution timing
candidates.summary: A stock's return in a given half-hour continues at the same half-hour on following days for at least 40 days. Volume, order imbalance and spreads show the same daily periodicity. Timing trades to the cheap half-hours cuts execution cost by about the effective spread. This matters most as an execution input for Mandel's existing daily rules (for example the T-559 calendar sleeve and closing-auction fills). Not registered.
candidates.mechanism: Institutions execute large orders on recurring daily schedules (VWAP and volume-profile algorithms, infrequent rebalancing per Bogousslavsky). That creates predictable same-time-of-day order flow and price pressure. The other side is liquidity providers and traders who ignore the clock.
candidates.assets: US equities and ETFs (Alpaca)
candidates.horizon: intraday (hourly / half-hourly), lasting up to 40 days
candidates.claimed_effect: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (JF 2010): striking return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 trading days. Volume, imbalance, volatility and spread periodicities do not explain it. Short-term reversal comes from liquidity imbalances lasting under an hour and bid-ask bounce. Timing trades can save about the effective spread. The abstract gives no strategy return.
candidates.replication: Bogousslavsky (JF 2016) gives the theory. I found no 2015-2026 US replication. Mandel's T-577 intraday ML program (276 cells, 0 pass) suggests generic intraday features carry little net of costs. The cost-saving use is the more promising one.

sources.title: Intraday Patterns in the Cross-section of Stock Returns (Heston, Korajczyk, Sadka, JF 2010)
Infrequent Rebalancing, Return Autocorrelation, and Seasonality (Bogousslavsky, JF 2016)

candidates.proposed_test: (a) Alpha check on Mandel's 30-minute bars (93 symbols) and 60-minute bars (91 symbols, 2 years). For each half-hour slot h, run cross-sectional Fama-MacBeth of r(i,h,d) on the mean of r(i,h,d-k) for k = 1..20 (same slot), against the mean over other slots. Pre-registered claim: the same-slot coefficient is positive with NW t > 2 in both years. Trading cell: each slot, long the top quintile and short the bottom on the 20-day same-slot mean, hold one slot, 2 bps per side for ETFs and 5 bps for stocks; net mean with a block bootstrap by day. Expect gross > 0 and net <= 0. (b) Execution study (no claim of alpha): for each of Mandel's live daily rules, compare simulated fills at the official close, at the hour with the lowest historical same-slot spread/impact, and at an interval VWAP built from the 5-minute volume profile. Measure the mean shortfall against the decision price. Adopt a timing rule only if it lowers shortfall with p < 0.05 out of sample.

candidates.name: ETF primary-market flows (creations/redemptions) as non-fundamental demand: short high-flow, long low-flow ETFs
candidates.summary: Authorized participants create or redeem shares when ETF prices drift from NAV, so ETF flows reveal non-fundamental demand shocks that later reverse. Short high-flow and long low-flow ETFs earned 1.1-2.0% per month. Not registered. Consistent with Mandel's T-404 (GLD holdings change predicts next-week return positively: not_supported), which tested the momentum sign. The literature predicts the reverse sign, cross-sectionally.
candidates.mechanism: Non-fundamental demand (retail or thematic chasing, hedging flows) pushes the ETF and its basket away from fundamental value. APs arbitrage the ETF back to NAV, but the basket stays mispriced. Prices revert as the demand fades. Flow-chasing investors pay.
candidates.assets: US-listed ETFs (Alpaca); gold and bitcoin trusts
candidates.claimed_effect: Brown-Davies-Ringgenberg (Review of Finance 2021): a portfolio short high-flow ETFs and long low-flow ETFs earns 1.1-2.0% per month in excess returns, and non-fundamental demand imposes costs on investors. The sample period is not stated in the abstract.
candidates.replication: I found no independent replication or post-publication test. Mandel's adjacent tests (T-404 GLD flows positive sign, T-398 Fed Z.1 fund flows) were not_supported in the momentum direction, which neither contradicts nor confirms the reversal.

sources.title: ETF Arbitrage, Non-Fundamental Demand, and Return Predictability (Brown, Davies, Ringgenberg, Review of Finance 2021)
ETF Arbitrage and Return Predictability (SSRN version)

candidates.proposed_test: The data is the binding constraint. Historical daily ETF shares outstanding is not in Mandel's bundles except gold trust ounces (spdr-gld/gldm archives) and IBIT snapshots. So: (1) Retrospective pilot on the trusts with full histories: GLD, GLDM and the Sprott trusts, plus IBIT from the premium/discount bundle, and any issuer histories obtainable. Weekly flow = change in log shares (or ounces), z-scored on 52 weeks. Claim: top-tercile flow weeks are followed by negative 4-week returns relative to the asset's own benchmark (gold spot via GC=F, BTC via Coinbase). (2) Forward cross-section: capture daily shares outstanding for the 68 declared ETFs (T-420/T-462 list) from issuer pages starting now. Monthly: within asset-class buckets (US sector, country, bond), long the bottom flow quintile and short the top, by the trailing 1-month flow / AUM. Hold one month, 5 bps per side plus ETF borrow, net mean with HAC t. Declare at least 36 forward months as min_n, and treat it as inconclusive before then. Cross-check with SEC N-PORT quarterly holdings (point-in-time at filing) as a slow backfill of shares outstanding for 2019-2026.

candidates.name: ETF / trust premium-discount to NAV mean reversion (beyond IBIT)
candidates.summary: ETF prices deviate from NAV within a band of about 200 bps (about 100 bps after correcting stale NAVs), more for international and illiquid holdings. Strategies trading those deviations earned substantial abnormal returns before costs. Duplicates T-328 (btc-etf-premium-discount, parked / not_supported for IBIT against Coinbase). The new element is applying it where deviations are larger and more persistent: closed-end physical trusts (Sprott) and bond / international ETFs.
candidates.mechanism: AP arbitrage is limited by creation costs, basket illiquidity and stale NAVs. For closed-end trusts there is no creation mechanism at all, only occasional issuance. Deviations are temporary demand pressure that reverts. Impatient traders on the wrong side of the premium pay.
adjacent_variables: NAV strike time vs close (stale pricing)
candidates.assets: US-listed ETFs and physical metal trusts (PHYS, PSLV, SPPP, CEF vs GLD/SLV/PPLT; Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Petajisto (FAJ 2017): deviations are typically within about 200 bps, about 100 bps after controlling for stale pricing, larger for international and illiquid holdings. Active strategies exploiting this earn substantial abnormal returns before transaction costs. The abstract gives no figure.
candidates.replication: Mandel's IBIT test failed after realistic costs (T-328). I found no 2015-2026 replication. Petajisto's returns are stated before costs, and liquid US equity ETFs have deviations inside the spread. Any edge is likely confined to trusts and illiquid-basket ETFs.

sources.title: Inefficiencies in the Pricing of Exchange-Traded Funds (Petajisto, FAJ 2017)

candidates.proposed_test: Use Mandel's archived Sprott NAV bundles (sprott-phys/pslv/sppp/cef-nav, daily share price, NAV, premium) and SPDR GLD/GLDM premium archives. Signal: z of the trust's premium against its trailing 120-day mean and sd, known at the close. Trade: when z < -2, buy the trust and short the matching ETF (PHYS vs GLD, PSLV vs SLV, SPPP vs PPLT/PALL split by NAV weights). Size the hedge so metal exposure matches by NAV. Exit at z >= 0 or after 20 sessions; mirror the rule for z > +2. Costs: 5 bps per leg per side plus 1%/yr ETF borrow. Statistic: mean net return per trade, with date-clustered bootstrap CIs, halves, and a random-entry placebo matched on holding period. Pass: mean net > 0 with p < 0.05 across the four trusts pooled, and positive in at least 3 of 4. Note the NAV is struck at a fixed time and may be stale relative to the 16:00 close, so test both the reported premium and a premium recomputed from synchronous 16:00 metal prices.

candidates.name: Crypto liquidity provision: volume-conditioned short-term reversal, plus an out-of-sample short of altcoin volume shocks
candidates.summary: In crypto, reversal returns (the pay to liquidity providers) are concentrated in low-activity, small, volatile pairs, and lagged return x volume significantly predicts returns. Separately, Mandel's T-546 found that top-decile idiosyncratic volume days in altcoins were followed by -1.80% net over 10 days, 2019-2026, the opposite of the high-volume premium claim it tested. Any short version must be tested on data T-546 did not touch. Related: T-320 (BTC daily reversal does not beat one taker round trip, supported) and T-314 (crypto weekly momentum, not_supported).
candidates.mechanism: Reversal: liquidity providers bear inventory risk and adverse selection in thin pairs and are paid by impatient takers. Attention shock: volume spikes in alts mark attention, coordinated pumps or listing events. Late retail buyers pay as the price decays, which matches the Robinhood attention result in equities.
candidates.assets: Crypto spot on Coinbase (long side); shorts only via US-legal instruments (Coinbase Derivatives futures where listed, Kalshi perps)
candidates.claimed_effect: Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson (JBF 2022), USD pairs on multiple centralised exchanges, 2017-03 to 2022-03: liquidity-provision (reversal) returns are mainly in pairs with lower market activity, and the lagged return x volume interaction significantly predicts returns. The abstract gives no magnitudes. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (JF 2022): ten crypto characteristics form significant long-short strategies, all explained by a market, size and momentum 3-factor model. Liu-Tsyvinski (RFS 2021): attention proxies strongly forecast crypto returns. Mandel T-546: -1.80% net 10-day over 9,699 altcoin events.
candidates.replication: Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu show volume-type characteristics are spanned by size and momentum. T-546's negative drift is an in-sample observation; it supports registering a test, not trading. Shannon/Brier learnings on thin venues: the measured reversal premium is mostly the spread and fee a taker pays, so maker-only execution decides whether any of it is capturable.

sources.title: Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets (Bianchi, Babiak, Dickerson, JBF 2022)
Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency (Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu, JF 2022)
Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency (Liu and Tsyvinski, RFS 2021)

candidates.proposed_test: (a) Retrospective reversal test. Universe: T-546's point-in-time top 50 Coinbase USD products (same exclusions), 2019-2026, weekly at the Sunday 00:00 UTC close. Double sort on prior-week return (quintiles) x prior-week volume relative to its 30-day mean (terciles). Claim: low-activity losers minus low-activity winners has a positive next-week return, and it exceeds the high-activity spread. Long-only implementation: low-activity losers minus the equal-weighted universe, 50 bps round trip. Date-clustered CI, halves, DSR over the declared cells. (b) Short of volume shocks, untouched data only. Either forward from 2026-10-21, or on Kraken-only USD alts that were never in T-546's Coinbase universe. Same event definition as T-546; short at the next UTC close for 10 days, only where a US-legal short exists (Coinbase Derivatives listed futures, Kalshi perps). Cost 100 bps round trip plus funding/basis. Pass: mean net > 0 with a CI excluding 0 and placebo p < 0.05. Require at least 300 events before any verdict.

candidates.name: Commodity futures open-interest growth predicts commodity (and bond) returns
candidates.summary: Growth in commodity futures open interest is procyclical. It predicts commodity returns, bond returns and short-rate moves after controlling for known predictors, and predicts currency and stock returns less strongly. OI is a derivative-market non-price input, and Mandel can build it from free CFTC COT data. Not registered. The only COT theories are the gold positioning tests (T-405 not_supported, T-456 blocked), which use trader-class positioning, not aggregate OI growth.
candidates.mechanism: Hedging demand and the limited risk-absorption capacity of speculators: when hedgers demand more futures exposure, OI rises, and speculators must be paid a higher risk premium to take the other side. OI therefore carries information that prices miss. Hedgers pay the premium.
candidates.assets: CME/ICE US commodity futures (CME direct) or commodity ETFs (DBC, GSG, USO, UNG, DBA, GLD, SLV, CPER; Alpaca)
candidates.claimed_effect: Hong-Yogo (JFE 2012; NBER w16712): commodity-market OI movements predict commodity returns, bond returns and the short rate even with standard controls. The abstract gives no magnitudes. From memory, the sample is about 1965-2008 and the signal is 12-month growth of aggregate dollar OI; not re-verified.
candidates.replication: I found no independent replication or post-2008 test. Commodity financialisation after 2004 (index investors) may have changed what OI means.

sources.title: What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices? (Hong and Yogo, JFE 2012)
NBER Working Paper 16712 (Hong and Yogo)

candidates.proposed_test: Fetch CFTC legacy futures-only COT (Socrata 6dca-aqww, free, weekly) for about 20 liquid US commodity contracts: CL, NG, HO, RB, GC, SI, HG, PL, ZC, ZS, ZW, ZL, ZM, KC, SB, CT, CC, LE, HE, OJ. Use 2006-2026, with each report's release-time available_at (Friday 15:30 ET) as in Mandel's gold bundles. Dollar OI = contracts x multiplier x the settlement price on the as-of date; aggregate it and take 12-month log growth. Time series: predict the next-month equal-weighted commodity return (front futures from Yahoo =F continuous or DBC) and the TLT excess return. Expanding-window OOS R^2 from 2012 with Clark-West, plus a long/flat DBC rule (5 bps per switch). Cross-section: monthly long top-tercile and short bottom-tercile OI-growth contracts, via futures (CME) or single-commodity ETFs, with roll and 5 bps costs. Statistic: net mean with HAC t. Pass: OOS R^2 > 0 at p < 0.05, or a cross-sectional net mean > 0 at p < 0.05 with both halves positive, with deflation across the two cells.

registration.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived Yahoo prices and SEC cover shares, 2010-01 to 2026-09. At each month-end, form value-weighted portfolios from independent median splits on the month's total return r(m) and its share turnover TO(m) = sum of daily volume / split-adjusted shares outstanding. Long high-TO winners, short high-TO losers, filled at the next session's close and held one month. Claim: the portfolio earns a positive mean monthly return net of 10 bps per side on traded weight and 0.5%/yr borrow on the short leg, and the mean is positive in 2019-2026, after publication.
registration.statistic: Mean monthly net long-short return. Newey-West t (lag 6) plus a studentized circular block bootstrap (12-month blocks, 5,000 draws). Secondary: FF5+UMD alpha (NW t), and DSR over the declared trials.
registration.procedure: Membership comes from fja-sp500-components as of each month-end (available 09:30 ET on the effective date). Returns use Yahoo adjclose, volume uses Yahoo split-adjusted volume. Shares outstanding: the latest dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding (fallback us-gaap CommonStockSharesOutstanding) whose available_at (min of acceptance, filing date 22:00 ET) is before the month-end close. Multiply it by the split factors in daily-events between the cover date and month-end so it is on Yahoo's volume basis. Drop it if older than 15 months. Multi-class issuers follow T-393's rule. Market cap = close x shares. Independent halves at the cross-sectional median of r(m) and TO(m). Value weights from the month-end cap, filled at the next close. Declared cells, 8 in all: 2x2 vs conditional deciles (top-TO decile, winner minus loser deciles); no lag vs the paper's lag variant (formed on sessions 1..T-3 of the month, filled at the month-end close); 1-month hold vs 3-month overlapping cohorts. Baseline trials: plain STREV (low minus high r(m)) and plain 12-1 momentum on the same universe, so DSR covers 10 trials. Halves 2010-2017 / 2018-2026; post-publication window 2019-01..2026-09. Coverage audit: per month, the share of members without price or shares, plus a T-394-style bound (the mean return the absent names would need to flip the sign). The verdict is judged on the declared universe and labelled survivor-only. Side check, not part of this verdict: add r1m x TO1m (and r1m x lv_rel20) to T-578 as a declared interaction cell.

registration.pass: At least 180 months. The 2x2 value-weighted net mean > 0 with one-sided NW p < 0.05 and a studentized CBB 95% lower bound > 0. Mean > 0 in 2019-01..2026-09. Both halves positive. DSR >= 0.95 over the 10 declared trials. FF5+UMD alpha > 0.
registration.controls: Look-ahead: membership as of t; SEC shares only after acceptance and split-adjusted to Yahoo's basis; fills at the next close. Survivorship: the universe is defined as priced members and the bias sign is unknown, so report the absent share and the flip bound. One breakpoint (the median), no threshold grid. Costs: 10 bps per side on drift-adjusted turnover plus 0.5%/yr borrow; costs also reported at 20 bps. Baselines: STREV and 12-1 momentum. Regimes: 2020-03..2020-12 and 2022 reported. Multiple testing: DSR over 10 trials.

rows.notes: Worth testing: it is the strongest recent peer-reviewed claim in the cluster (RFS 2022, sample ends 2018), it has a clean post-publication window, and every input is archived. Expect a fail: UMD has been ~0 since 2009 (T-446), every post-publication factor test in Mandel failed, and 10 bps per side at ~90% monthly turnover takes most of the paper's largest-500 +0.42%/month gross. Main risk is a rule-9 inconclusive, so the claim defines its universe as the priced members, as T-473 did. The r x TO interaction for T-578 is a cheap second check of the literature's point that volume's information sits in its interaction with returns, not in its level (F0 IC ~+0.01).

rows.name: High-volume return premium in single stocks, split into visibility versus attention-buying shocks

overlaps.note: Same event design (idiosyncratic volume surprise, no 2-sigma move) on 22 ETFs plus BTC/ETH. Mean +21.1 bp against a +50 bp bar: ETF +6.9 bp, crypto +378 bp. Placebo p 0.0205 against a 0.01 bar, DSR 0.033.
Altcoins: -1.80% net over 10 days on 9,699 events, opposite sign. But the placebo null mean is -1.32%, so only ~-0.5% is specific to the shock.
Retail-attention herding reversal from mention spikes; blocked until 250 forward events exist.
Assets newly on trending lists underperform; blocked.
Same S&P 500 survivor-coverage template: 93.4% of events priced 2019-2026, plus a bound on what the absent names would need.
PEAD. High-volume, large-return weeks in large caps are often earnings weeks, where drift continues; this confounds the attention bucket.

learnings.finding: In liquid ETFs the visibility premium is +6.9 bp over 10 days, a seventh of the claimed bar; the large crypto-major effect did not survive deflation.
In retail-heavy alts, volume shocks are followed by negative drift (consistent with the attention channel), though mostly as a universe-wide drift (placebo -1.32%).
Volume ratio predicts the next bar's RANGE (t +4 to +43), not its return, on every coin. Volume carries volatility information, not direction.
Abnormal StockTwits intensity does not add to next-day realised vol beyond lagged RV and IV. Attention proxies have been weak in Mandel.
StockTwits intensity covers only 21 symbols from 2025-W43, so it cannot condition a single-stock event study over 2008-2026.

data: sec-submissions-b* (10-Q/10-K acceptance as an earnings-week flag)
rows.missing_data: There are no StockTwits or Reddit histories for single stocks before late 2025, so the attention bucket must use the price-based definition. Delisted names are absent. This is conservative for the negative attention claim (crashers missing) and optimistic for the visibility claim. The universe holds few true small caps, so the 'small' tercile is S&P 500 mid-caps.

registration.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, 2008-01 to 2026-09. Event: a week whose idiosyncratic volume surprise (log weekly volume minus its trailing 49-week mean, residualised on the members' mean surprise) is in that week's top decile. (a) Visibility events, with |weekly return| < 1 trailing weekly sigma, are followed by a positive 20-session beta-adjusted return from the next Monday open, net of 10 bps round trip. (b) Attention events, with weekly return > +2 sigma, are followed by a negative one, net of 10 bps plus 0.5%/yr borrow. Each claim is judged in the bottom size tercile.
registration.statistic: Mean 20-session beta-adjusted (vs SPY, trailing 252-session beta) net event return with date-clustered bootstrap CI; block-shift placebo (2,000 within-name shifts, as T-419); calendar-time portfolio mean with HAC t.
registration.procedure: Weekly bars from daily-history (Monday open to Friday close). Volume surprise is computed on trailing data only and residualised on the cross-sectional mean surprise, so market-wide volume weeks do not inflate counts. Sigma is the trailing 52-week sd of weekly returns. Size terciles come from point-in-time market cap (SEC cover shares after acceptance, split-adjusted). Entry at the next Monday open; exit 20 sessions later (10 sessions declared as the second hold). A secondary cell drops event weeks that contain a 10-Q/10-K acceptance (PEAD confound). Declared cells: 2 buckets x 3 size terciles x 10/20-session holds = 12; DSR over 12; Holm over the two bucket claims. Halves 2008-2016 / 2017-2026. Coverage audit and flip bound as T-394.
registration.data: daily-history-<SYM>, daily-history-SPY, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*
registration.pass: Bucket (a): at least 800 events, bottom-tercile mean net >= +50 bps with date-clustered 95% lower bound > 0, block-shift placebo p < 0.01, calendar-time HAC t >= 2, both halves positive. Bucket (b): the mirror, with mean <= -50 bps. Holm over the two buckets. DSR >= 0.95 over the 12 cells.
registration.controls: Look-ahead: trailing windows only; entry at the next open; SEC shares after acceptance. Market-wide weeks removed by residualising. Earnings-week confound cell. One decile threshold, no grid. Costs: 10 bps round trip plus 0.5%/yr borrow on (b). Survivorship bias sign stated per bucket. Regimes: VIX > 30 weeks and 2020-21 reported.

rows.notes: Worth one deflated test because single stocks, the setting GKM originally studied, are untested in Mandel, and data and harness pieces exist (T-419's placebo, T-394's coverage audit). Prior is low. T-419 found +6.9 bp in liquid ETFs, Hurst finds that volume predicts range rather than return, and the S&P 500 universe has few of the small, low-visibility firms where GKM's premium sits. The attention bucket is likely contaminated by earnings weeks (positive drift), so it is declared with an earnings-week exclusion cell. The pass rule makes this two claims with Holm, not one claim with two chances.

rows.name: Aggregate Amihud illiquidity as a market-timing signal (time-series illiquidity premium)

overlaps.note: Cross-sectional Amihud premium, blocked on a survivorship-free universe (CRSP). The time-series aggregate is less sensitive to absent names.
A Corwin-Schultz spread shock on SPY predicts a 20-day forward return of +0.13 points (CI -0.70..+0.88). Liquidity shocks have not timed the index in Mandel.
Same predictive-regression harness (Campbell-Thompson OOS R^2, Clark-West): consumer sentiment R^2_OS -8.6%.
Aggregate short interest timing. Its block (FINRA + SEC shares) is now resolved by archived bundles; a sibling time-series liquidity/positioning test.

learnings.finding: Every aggregate market-timing predictor Mandel has run failed out of sample (fund flows, sentiment, stablecoin supply, funding).

learnings.finding: The time-series illiquidity relation weakened sharply after decimalisation; illiquidity levels fell about tenfold.
Edges that exist are reference-price edges or structural premia. A liquidity-risk premium is a structural premium in principle, so the claim is not price-only.
Structural flows (month-end rebalancing) do show up in SPY in Mandel's data. Flow and liquidity mechanisms are not dead per se.

registration.claim: From 2005-01 to 2026-09, expected aggregate illiquidity predicts next-month IWM excess return over DTB3 with out-of-sample R^2 > 0 against the expanding historical mean (Clark-West p < 0.05). Expected illiquidity is the AR(1) forecast of log monthly Amihud ILLIQ across point-in-time S&P 500 members with prices, fitted on trailing data only.
registration.statistic: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 and Clark-West one-sided HAC test. Secondary: net Sharpe of the timing rule minus buy-and-hold, stationary block bootstrap (mean block 6 months).
registration.procedure: ILLIQ_i,m = mean over valid days of |r_d| / (close_d x volume_d) in $ millions, for members of month m (fja, as of each day) with at least 15 valid days, price > $5, ETFs excluded. Aggregate = cross-sectional mean x (^GSPC level at the first month / ^GSPC level at m-1), Amihud's scaling with the index level as the cap proxy, logged. Expected = AR(1) forecast from an expanding window of past months; unexpected = residual. Targets: IWM excess (primary), SPY excess and IWM-SPY (secondary; Holm over 3). Expanding regressions from 1997 data, first forecast 2005-01. Timing rule: IWM when expected ILLIQ is in its trailing top tercile, bills otherwise, 5 bps per switch. Report the minimum detectable R^2, member counts per month, a VIX-controlled version (VIX month-end close, Cboe stamp), halves 2005-2015 / 2016-2026, and joint deflation with T-421.

registration.pass: At least 240 out-of-sample months. IWM R^2_OS > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05 after Holm over 3 targets. Slope > 0 in both 2005-2015 and 2016-2026. The timing rule's net Sharpe beats buy-and-hold with block-bootstrap p < 0.05.
registration.controls: Look-ahead: membership and prices up to month-end only, AR fitted on past months only. Survivorship: aggregate over priced members, counts reported. One tercile threshold. registration.claim: On point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, 2005-2026, daily Fama-MacBeth regressions of the open(t+1)-to-open(t+6) return on r(t), r(t) x AV(t) and AV(t) give an interaction coefficient that is negative in the top size tercile (Campbell-Grossman-Wang) and positive in the bottom tercile (Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang), each with |NW t| > 2.8. AV = log volume minus its trailing 60-day mean, residualised on the members' mean AV; size = trailing 60-day median dollar volume.
registration.statistic: Time-series mean of daily FM coefficients with Newey-West t (5 lags) per size tercile. Trading translation, only if the top-tercile slope passes: weekly dollar-neutral fade of the top and bottom r(t) deciles on top-tercile-AV days, net Sharpe with HAC and a stationary bootstrap.
registration.procedure: Daily r(t) = close-to-close total return; AV computed on trailing data only and residualised cross-sectionally. Controls in each regression: log trailing dollar volume and trailing 20-day vol. Terciles re-formed daily on trailing data. Hurdle |t| > 2.8 (Harvey-Liu-Zhu style) for the search. The trading translation runs only after the slope verdict, with costs of 10 bps per side, and is a separate claim with its own DSR over 4 cells (decile/quintile x 1/5-day hold). Second market: point-in-time top 50 Coinbase USD products (T-546 exclusions), same regression with UTC closes, trading cell at 50 bps round trip. registration.data: daily-history-<SYM>, fja-sp500-components, coinbase-daily-<PID>, coinbase-products-<day>, cmc-historical-listings
registration.pass: At least 4,000 regression days. Top-tercile interaction < 0 with NW t < -2.8 AND bottom-tercile interaction > 0 with t > 2.8, same signs in 2005-2015 and 2016-2026. The trading translation passes separately only if net mean > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05, both halves positive and DSR >= 0.95.
registration.controls: Look-ahead: AV and terciles from trailing data; returns start at the next open. Cross-sectional residualising removes market volume days. Survivorship: declared priced universe. Costs apply only to the trading translation. Multiple testing: the t hurdle plus DSR on the trade.

rows.notes: This row was missing from the task's framing list but is in the candidate JSON. Worth running mainly as a measurement: it answers directly whether volume's information sits in its interaction with returns, which is the design question behind adding interaction features to T-578. The slope may well pass in the top tercile, since CGW-type reversal is robust at the index level (T-332). The bottom-tercile LMSW sign is unlikely inside the S&P 500, because even its smallest members have low information asymmetry. The trading translation will very likely hit the cost wall seen in T-473, T-319 and T-462, which is why it is registered as a separate claim.

A reference must lead the market. Aggregate OI growth is a slow positioning measure, not a sharper price for the same event, so it falls outside the class of edges Mandel has seen pay.
