Free: Socrata 6dca-aqww (futures-only) / jun7-fc8e, with the fetcher recipe already in mandel. Yahoo continuous front futures for NG, HO, RB, ZC, ZS, ZW, ZL, ZM, KC, SB, CT, CC, LE, HE, OJ (free). Expired-contract histories for a clean cross-sectional roll (T-371's block); ETFs serve as the tradable proxy.

registration.claim: From 2012-01 to 2026-09, the 12-month log growth of aggregate dollar open interest across about 20 US commodity futures predicts next-month DBC excess return over DTB3 positively, with out-of-sample R^2 > 0 against the expanding mean (Clark-West p < 0.05). Each CFTC legacy futures-only report enters at its Friday 15:30 ET release.
registration.statistic: Campbell-Thompson R^2_OS with a Clark-West HAC test. Secondary: the TLT excess-return regression (expected negative) and a cross-sectional top-minus-bottom tercile OI-growth portfolio, net mean with NW t.
registration.procedure: Dollar OI = contracts x the fixed multiplier x the front settlement on the report's as-of date. Aggregate over the declared contracts, then take the 12-month log growth, using only reports released by month-end. Backcast and superseded rows are handled as in T-405. Expanding regressions from 2006 data, first forecast 2012-01. Long/flat DBC rule at 5 bps per switch, reported. Cross-section: monthly long top / short bottom tercile by contract OI growth via front futures (CME) or single-commodity ETFs where they exist, with rolls at fixed days and 5 bps costs. Holm over the 2 primary cells (time series, cross-section). Halves 2012-2018 / 2019-2026. April 2020 WTI excluded from CL.
registration.data: CFTC Socrata legacy futures-only (to fetch for ~20 contracts), Yahoo =F continuous fronts (to fetch for the missing roots), daily-history-DBC/TLT, fred-DTB3
registration.pass: At least 150 out-of-sample months. R^2_OS > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05, OR cross-sectional net mean > 0 with NW p < 0.05 and both halves positive; Holm over the two cells.
registration.controls: Look-ahead: release-time availability, backcasts dropped. Fixed contract list. Roll handling fixed ex ante. Costs: 5 bps per switch or leg. Regimes: 2008, 2014-16, 2020-04, 2022. Index-investor financialisation era noted.

rows.notes: The data is free and the fetcher exists, so extending the COT bundles to about 20 contracts is a small job that also gives T-456 and T-371-style work a positioning layer. The claim has no post-2008 replication, and financialisation may have changed what OI means. Hong-Yogo's commodity-return sign is positive and the bond-return sign negative; both signs are declared above. Expect low power over 2012-2026.

rows.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks (STMOM, turnover-conditioned 1-month return)
rows.source_notes: I opened the City open-access manuscript (MS_short_term_mom_v27.pdf) and extracted its text. Medhat and Schmeling, RFS 35(3) 2022. The sample is July 1963 to December 2018. STMOM in the top-turnover decile earns +1.37%/month (t 4.74). STREV* earns -1.41% (t -7.13). Net of half-spreads the strategy earns 1.00%/month (t 3.47) on a cost of 0.37%/month. The largest-500 2x2 (independent splits at rank 250) earns +0.42%/month (t 4.91), and megacaps +0.53%/month (t 2.53). The 1991/07-2018/12 subsample earns 2.03%/month (t 4.80). The implementation-lag variant (sort on days 1..d-3) earns 1.83%/month (t 5.52), and about 0.60%/month net for large caps and megacaps. CXO's review gives the sample as through 2016 (an earlier draft) and says STREV* has not worked since the mid-2000s. Every claimed number matches the paper. I could not run new replication searches because the session's web-search budget was used up.
rows.replication_concerns: No independent US study for 2019-2026 was found, and I could not search again. Implied monthly sd of the largest-500 2x2 is about 2.2% (0.42 x sqrt(666) / 4.91). Over about 200 months the SE is about 0.16%, so the minimum detectable effect (one-sided 5%, 80% power) is about 0.39%/month: the paper's whole gross effect. After the McLean-Pontiff decay prior (about 0.18% gross) and about 0.2-0.35%/month of costs, a fail is expected and is likely to be a low-power fail, so the MDE must be reported. UMD has been about 0 since 2009 (T-446), and every post-publication factor test in Mandel has failed.
rows.data_notes: These bundles exist: fja-sp500-components (2,720 change rows from 1996-01-02, last date 2026-08-18, so membership is carried forward after that), fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history (901 symbols), daily-events, sec-companyfacts and sec-submissions (36 bundles each, b000..b043), french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily and fred-DTB3. CHECKED TRAP: Yahoo close and volume are split-adjusted to the fetch-date basis. NVDA shows no volume jump at its 2021-07-20 4:1 or 2024-06-10 10:1 split. The cross-checker split-adjusted SEC shares only 'between the cover date and month-end'. That leaves shares on the month-end basis, so turnover and market cap are wrong by every later split factor (NVDA in 2015 by 40x), which corrupts both the TO sort and the value weights. Fixed in the final.
rows.lookahead_risks: SEC shares must be taken at acceptance time (sec-submissions joined by accn), not at the period end. The split basis must be the fetch date (above). Use the split-adjusted close, not adjclose, for market cap. fja membership is as of each date. Fills are at the next close. Survivorship: about 18.5% of member-days since 2010 have no Yahoo price, and reused tickers need T-473's spell checks. The post-2018 window is post-sample, not post-publication (SSRN first version March 2018).
rows.missing_data: A survivorship-free universe (CRSP, paid). NYSE breakpoints (medians are taken within the S&P 500 instead). SEC shares are thin before about 2010, so months with less than 80% shares coverage are excluded.

final.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived Yahoo prices and point-in-time SEC shares, 2010-01 to 2026-09. At each month-end, form independent median splits on the month's total return r(m) and its share turnover TO(m), where TO(m) = the month's split-adjusted volume / shares outstanding on the same split basis. Hold value-weighted, long high-TO winners and short high-TO losers, filled at the next session's close and held to the next formation. Claim: this portfolio earns a positive mean monthly return net of 10 bps per side on traded weight and 0.5%/yr borrow on the short leg, and the mean is also positive over 2019-01..2026-09, after the paper's sample.
final.statistic: Mean monthly net long-short return. Newey-West t (6 lags) and a studentized circular block bootstrap (12-month blocks, 5,000 draws). Secondary: FF5+UMD alpha (NW t), DSR over the 4 declared trials, and the minimum detectable effect at 80% power.
final.procedure: Membership: fja-sp500-components as of each month-end, with T-473's ticker-spell and reused-ticker checks. Returns come from adjclose. Turnover and caps use the split-adjusted close and volume, which are on Yahoo's fetch-date share basis. Shares: the latest dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding (fallback us-gaap CommonStockSharesOutstanding) whose acceptance time is before the month-end close, multiplied by every split ratio in daily-events with an ex-date after that value's as-of date up to the fetch date. Drop share values older than 15 months; multi-class issuers follow T-393's rule. Cap = split-adjusted close x adjusted shares. A month is eligible only if at least 80% of members have both a price and shares. Declared trials (4): (1) primary, no lag; (2) the paper's implementation-lag variant, sorted on sessions 1..d-3 and filled at the month-end close; (3) plain STREV baseline (low minus high r(m)); (4) plain 12-1 momentum baseline. Halves 2010-01..2017-12 / 2018-01..2026-09. Report monthly the share of members without price or shares, a T-394-style flip bound, costs at 20 bps, and regimes 2020 and 2022. Side check outside this verdict: r1m x TO1m as a declared T-578 interaction cell.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<SYM>, daily-events-<SYM>, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, sec-company-tickers, sec-cik-lookup, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3
final.pass: At least 180 eligible months. Primary net mean > 0 with one-sided NW p < 0.05 and CBB 95% lower bound > 0. Mean > 0 over 2019-01..2026-09. Both halves positive. FF5+UMD alpha > 0. DSR >= 0.95 over the 4 trials. The MDE is reported with the verdict.
final.controls: Look-ahead: acceptance-time shares on the fetch-date split basis, membership as of t, next-close fills. Survivorship: the universe is declared as priced members, with the absent share and flip bound reported. One breakpoint (the median), no grid. Costs: 10 bps per side plus borrow, stressed at 20 bps. Baselines STREV and 12-1. Multiple testing: DSR over 4.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the test is cheap and post-sample. The cross-checker's split adjustment would corrupt turnover and value weights for any name that split after the cover date. The 8-cell grid is cut to the paper's largest-500 2x2 plus its lag variant and two baselines.

rows.name: High-volume return premium in single stocks, split into visibility versus attention-buying shocks
rows.source_notes: Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin, JF 56(3) 2001, abstract (RePEc): stocks with unusually high (low) volume over a day or a week appreciate (depreciate) over the following month. The premium is not explained by return autocorrelation, announcements, market risk or liquidity. Kaniel-Ozoguz-Starks, JFE 2012: found in 41 countries and not caused by risk or liquidity. Both confirmed. I did not open Barber et al. (Robinhood, -4.7%) or Kang (arXiv); the attention bucket is dropped, so they are not load-bearing. No new replication search was possible because the web-search budget was used up.
rows.replication_concerns: T-419 found +6.9 bp in liquid ETFs (DSR 0.033), and Hurst finds volume predicts range, not direction. S&P 500 'small' names are $5-20B caps, far from GKM's low-visibility firms. The attention bucket (b) is unmeasurable: StockTwits covers 21 symbols from 2025-W43, and the price-only proxy (short high-volume +2-sigma weeks) is the exact opposite of row 1's high-turnover-winner leg on the same universe. Large-cap high-volume up weeks are mostly earnings weeks, which drift positively. Registering (b) would put two contradictory claims on one dataset.
rows.data_notes: daily-history (split-adjusted volume, adjclose), daily-history-SPY, fja components and spells, and sec-submissions all exist. The cross-checker's earnings confound cell ('weeks containing a 10-Q/10-K acceptance') is mis-specified: a 10-Q is filed 1-4 weeks after the earnings release. The sec-submissions bundle has no 8-K item codes, and 8-Ks are sparse before 2019 (b000 has 1-33 a year 2005-2015). Size terciles are replaced by trailing median dollar volume, so the primary needs no SEC shares and can start in 2008.
rows.lookahead_risks: Volume surprise and sigma from trailing windows only. The cross-sectional mean surprise uses the same week's members, which is known at the Friday close. Entry is the next week's first open. Overlapping events of one name within 20 sessions: keep the first. Survivorship: delisted names are absent, which flatters a positive visibility drift.
rows.missing_data: Historical single-stock retail-attention data (needed for the attention bucket; not registered). 8-K Item 2.02 dates for a true earnings-week exclusion. Delisted members.

final.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, 2008-01 to 2026-09. Event: a week whose idiosyncratic volume surprise is in that week's cross-sectional top decile and whose return lies within +/-1 trailing weekly sigma (a visibility shock). Volume surprise = log weekly volume minus its trailing 49-week mean, minus the same week's cross-sectional mean surprise. Claim: such weeks are followed by a mean 20-session beta-adjusted return of at least +50 bps from the next week's first open, net of a 10 bp round trip.
final.statistic: Event mean of the 20-session net beta-adjusted return (vs SPY, trailing 252-session beta), with date-clustered bootstrap CI. Block-shift placebo (2,000 within-name shifts, as T-419). Calendar-time portfolio mean with HAC t.
final.procedure: Weekly bars (first open to last close of each week) from daily-history: split-adjusted volume, adjclose returns. Sigma = trailing 52-week sd of weekly returns. Entry at the next week's first open; exit at the open 20 sessions later. If one name has repeat events within 20 sessions, keep the first. Reported only, not judged: terciles by trailing 60-day median dollar volume; GKM's bottom-decile low-volume bucket (predicted negative); the share of events 5-35 days before a 10-Q/10-K acceptance (a rough earnings-window flag); VIX > 30 weeks; 2020-21. Halves 2008-2016 / 2017-2026. Coverage audit and flip bound as T-394. Deflation counts T-419's 36 cells. The attention/short bucket is not part of this claim.
final.data: daily-history-<SYM>, daily-history-SPY, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, sec-submissions-b*
final.pass: At least 800 events. Mean net >= +50 bps with date-clustered 95% lower bound > 0. Block-shift placebo p < 0.01. Calendar-time HAC t >= 2. Both halves positive. DSR >= 0.95 counting T-419's 36 cells plus this one.
final.controls: Look-ahead: trailing windows, next-week open entry. Market-wide volume weeks removed by cross-sectional residualising. One decile cut and one hold. Costs: 10 bp round trip. Survivorship stated as favouring the claim. Earnings-window diagnostic reported.

rows.reason: Single-stock HVRP is untested in Mandel and the source is confirmed. The attention bucket is dropped: it has no point-in-time data and its price proxy contradicts row 1 on the same data. The earnings-week cell used the wrong filing, so it is replaced by a diagnostic.

rows.name: Aggregate Amihud illiquidity as a market-timing signal (time-series illiquidity premium)
rows.source_notes: RePEc confirms Amihud, JFM 5(1) 2002, pp. 31-56, but has no abstract. ScienceDirect and the replication pages (Harris-Amato CFR 2019 on nowpublishers, Drienko et al.) returned 403, and a mirror PDF returned 503. OSAP SignalDoc (scratchpad) confirms the cross-sectional Illiquidity predictor: t 6.6, equal-weighted, 1964-1997. I could not confirm the time-series claim (expected illiquidity raises ex-ante excess returns; unexpected illiquidity lowers contemporaneous returns) from a fetched page, although it matches the paper as widely cited. No new replication search was possible (web-search budget used up).
rows.replication_concerns: Decay after decimalisation is documented in the candidate's sources, none of which I could open. In Mandel, every aggregate timing predictor (T-398, T-458, T-402, T-423) and the SPY spread shock (T-421) failed. Monthly R^2 of 0.5-1% over about 260 out-of-sample months gives low Clark-West power. This signal is nearly the mirror of row 4's aggregate turnover (ILLIQ ~ |r| / dollar volume; turnover ~ dollar volume / cap), so the two must be deflated as one family.
rows.data_notes: fja-sp500-components, daily-history (including IWM from 2000, SPY, ^GSPC with 24,814 rows), cboe-VIX-history and fred-DTB3 all exist. Trap: dollar volume must be the split-adjusted close x split-adjusted volume. That product is split-invariant and equals raw dollar volume. Using adjclose would shrink early dollar volume by the dividend back-adjustment and add a spurious upward trend to early ILLIQ. Priced-member coverage before 2008 is thinner (survivors only), so member counts must be reported.
rows.lookahead_risks: Fit the AR(1) on past months only. Membership as of each day. The VIX control uses the month-end close. Only the expected component is a trading signal: the unexpected component is contemporaneous and not tradable.
rows.missing_data: An NYSE-wide or CRSP aggregate, and delisted members. Market cap for Amihud's scaling is proxied by the ^GSPC level.

final.claim: From 2005-01 to 2026-09, expected aggregate illiquidity predicts next-month IWM excess return over DTB3 with a positive slope and out-of-sample R^2 > 0 against the expanding historical mean (Clark-West p < 0.05). Expected illiquidity is the expanding-window AR(1) forecast of log monthly Amihud ILLIQ across point-in-time S&P 500 common-stock members with prices. A rule that holds IWM when expected ILLIQ is in its trailing top tercile, and bills otherwise, beats buy-and-hold IWM net of 5 bps per switch.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson R^2_OS with a Clark-West HAC test. Net Sharpe of the timing rule minus buy-and-hold, with a stationary block bootstrap (mean block 6 months). MDE R^2 reported.
final.procedure: ILLIQ_i,m = mean over valid days of |r_d| / (close_d x volume_d / 1e6). r_d comes from adjclose; dollar volume from the split-adjusted close x split-adjusted volume, never adjclose. Require at least 15 valid days and price > $5; exclude ETFs and tickers not matched to fja spells. Aggregate = cross-sectional mean x (^GSPC level in the first month / ^GSPC level at m-1), logged. AR(1) and predictive regressions on expanding windows from 1997 data, first forecast 2005-01. Targets: IWM excess (primary), SPY excess and IWM minus SPY (Holm over 3). Report monthly member counts, a VIX-controlled slope, halves 2005-2015 / 2016-2026, and exclusion of 2008-09 and 2020. Family Holm with the aggregate-turnover claim and T-421.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<SYM>, daily-history-IWM, daily-history-SPY, daily-history--GSPC, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3
final.pass: At least 240 out-of-sample months. IWM R^2_OS > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05 after Holm over the 3 targets and the liquidity family. Slope > 0 in both halves. Timing-rule net Sharpe beats buy-and-hold with block-bootstrap p < 0.05.
final.controls: Look-ahead: month-end data only, AR fitted on the past. Split-invariant dollar volume. Survivorship: priced members only, counts reported. One tercile threshold. Costs: 5 bps per switch. MDE reported for power.

rows.reason: It is cheap and settles a famous claim, but the time-series abstract could not be opened. The dollar-volume construction is fixed to be split- and dividend-invariant, and the run is deflated jointly with its mirror (aggregate turnover).

rows.name: Aggregate share turnover as a sentiment / overpricing signal (Baker-Stein, Jones)
rows.source_notes: Baker and Stein, JFM 7(3) 2004, abstract (RePEc): high liquidity, including higher turnover, predicts lower subsequent returns in firm-level and aggregate data. Turnover has incremental predictive power for future EQUAL-WEIGHTED market returns, alongside equity issuance. Confirmed. I did not open Jones (2002). No new replication search was possible (budget used up).
rows.replication_concerns: There is no post-2004 replication, and three sentiment-family predictors failed in Mandel (T-398, T-449, T-458). About 21 independent annual observations since 2005 give very low power. This is the same market-liquidity-level signal as the Amihud aggregate row with the sign reversed, so the two cannot count as independent evidence. The cross-checker made SPY its primary target, but the verified claim is for equal-weighted returns.
rows.data_notes: fja, daily-history, ^GSPC, SPY, sec-companyfacts and DTB3 exist; RSP is not archived (checked). The cross-checker's proxy, the summed dollar volume of priced members divided by the ^GSPC level, is biased upward because the number of priced members rises over time (thin survivor coverage before 2008). Replaced with a per-name detrended share-volume aggregate, which needs neither shares nor the index divisor.
rows.lookahead_risks: Each name is detrended on its own trailing 60 months only. Overlapping 12-month targets need Hodrick SEs. Members enter only after 60 months of history.
rows.missing_data: Point-in-time shares before about 2010 (not needed for the fixed signal). An NYSE group volume series. RSP history (the equal-weighted member mean is used instead).

final.claim: From 2005-01 to 2026-09, detrended aggregate turnover predicts the next-12-month equal-weighted return of point-in-time S&P 500 members, in excess of DTB3, with a negative slope and out-of-sample R^2 > 0 (Clark-West p < 0.05). Detrended aggregate turnover is the cross-sectional mean, over members with prices, of log monthly split-adjusted share volume minus that name's own trailing 60-month mean of log volume, known at month-end.
final.statistic: Slope with Hodrick (1992) 1B standard errors on overlapping monthly data. Non-overlapping annual regressions for each of the 12 start months. Expanding-window R^2_OS with Clark-West. MDE reported.
final.procedure: Signal from members as of each month (fja) with at least 60 months of their own volume history. From 2010, check the correlation with SEC-shares turnover (acceptance-time shares on the fetch-date split basis). Targets: the members' equal-weighted mean total return (primary, Baker-Stein's verified target) and SPY excess (secondary). Expanding regressions, first forecast 2005-01. A risk-off rule (bills instead of the equal-weighted portfolio when the signal is in its trailing top decile, 5 bps per switch) is reported only. Sensitivities exclude 2008-09 and 2020. Family Holm with the aggregate Amihud claim, T-398, T-449 and T-458.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<SYM>, daily-history-SPY, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, fred-DTB3
final.pass: At least 200 out-of-sample monthly forecasts. Slope < 0 with Hodrick p < 0.05. R^2_OS > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05 after family Holm. Same sign excluding 2008-09 and excluding 2020.
final.controls: Look-ahead: per-name trailing detrending, month-end data. Structural trend and member-count drift removed by per-name detrending. Overlap handled by Hodrick SEs and non-overlapping fits. One reported threshold. Costs: 5 bps per switch. Multiple testing: family Holm.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the cross-checker targeted the wrong return series (the paper is about equal-weighted returns) and used a turnover proxy biased by member-count drift. Both are fixed, and the claim is tied to the Amihud row's family because it is the same liquidity-level signal.

rows.name: Volatility of liquidity: stocks with volatile turnover / dollar volume earn lower returns (Chordia-Subrahmanyam-Anshuman)
rows.source_notes: RePEc confirms CSA, JFE 59(1) 2001, but has no abstract. OSAP SignalDoc (scratchpad) confirms std_turn (36-month sd of turnover, t 3.74) and VolSD (36-month rolling sd of monthly SHARE volume vol, at least 24 obs, NYSE only, t 3.56). Both have Sign -1, are equal-weighted multivariate regressions, and cover 1966-1995. Neither OSAP definition is dollar volume. The OSAP long-short return download failed: dl_czret/lsret.csv is a Google Drive quota page, so the decay check has no data. No new replication search was possible.
rows.replication_concerns: The original evidence is an equal-weighted Fama-MacBeth regression with no value-weighted long-short. Hou-Xue-Zhang report 96% of trading-friction anomalies fail with NYSE breakpoints and value weights, and every post-publication factor test in Mandel failed. Expect about zero in value-weighted S&P 500. The cross-checker's CV of DOLLAR volume is mechanically driven by the 36-month price path (a name that doubled has high dollar-volume CV), so it partly re-tests long-term reversal and momentum and matches neither OSAP signal.
rows.data_notes: fja, daily-history (split-adjusted volume), sec-companyfacts (value weights from 2010 on the fetch-date split basis, as in row 1), and the French factors exist. OSAP portfolio returns are not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: Use the trailing 36 months only. Caps from acceptance-time SEC shares, split-adjusted to the fetch date. Next-close fills. Survivorship: priced members only.
rows.missing_data: OSAP long-short portfolio CSV (fetch failed on quota) for the decay evidence row. Delisted members. NYSE breakpoints.

final.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices and SEC shares, 2010-01 to 2026-09. Signal: the coefficient of variation of monthly split-adjusted share volume over the prior 36 months (at least 24 months required). Portfolio: value-weighted quintiles, long the lowest CV and short the highest, formed at month-end, filled at the next close and held one month. Claim: the portfolio earns a positive mean monthly return net of 10 bps per side and 1%/yr borrow on the short leg.
final.statistic: Mean monthly net long-short return with NW t (6 lags). FF5+UMD alpha. Spread within sequential terciles of 36-month mean share volume.
final.procedure: Monthly share volume = sum of split-adjusted daily volume. CV = sd / mean over months t-36..t-1. Quintiles within members as of t. Value weights from the split-adjusted close x acceptance-time SEC shares on the fetch-date split basis; members without shares are excluded and their share is reported. Report the equal-weighted cell only. Controls: sequential sorts on volume-level terciles and on cap terciles. Halves 2010-2017 / 2018-2026. Once the OSAP long-short file is fetched, record std_turn, VolSD, DolVol, Illiquidity, ShareVol and zerotrade (original sample vs post-2015) as a decay evidence row, not as a verdict.
final.data: fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells, daily-history-<SYM>, daily-events-<SYM>, sec-companyfacts-b*, sec-submissions-b*, french-ff5-daily, french-momentum-daily, fred-DTB3; OSAP portfolio CSV (to fetch)
final.pass: At least 180 months. Value-weighted net mean > 0 with one-sided NW p < 0.05. Both halves positive. FF5+UMD alpha > 0. Spread positive in at least 2 of 3 volume-level terciles.
final.controls: Look-ahead: trailing windows, next-close fills, acceptance-time shares. Price-path contamination removed by using share volume. Microcaps excluded by construction. One quintile cut. Costs: 10 bps per side plus 1%/yr borrow. Level and size by sequential sort. Counted in the volume-cluster deflation family.

rows.reason: The signal now matches the literature's share-volume and turnover variability, not dollar volume, which mostly encodes the past price path. The pass rule changes from 'p < 0.05 in each half', which has almost no power, to full-sample significance with both halves positive.

rows.name: Option-to-stock volume ratio (O/S) predicts negative returns
rows.source_notes: Johnson-So, JFE 106(2) 2012, abstract (RePEc): low-O/S firms beat high-O/S by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualised). The effect is stronger with high short-sale costs or low option leverage, and O/S predicts earnings news. Ge-Lin-Pearson, JFE 120(3) 2016: opening call purchases predict most strongly, and the leverage channel dominates. OSAP SignalDoc: OptionVolume1 t 3.45, equal-weighted, 1996-2010, Sign -1. All confirmed.
rows.replication_concerns: Nothing tested after 2010. The 2020+ retail call and 0DTE boom could flip or swamp the signal, and the candidate cites an opposite-sign Korean result. Flow signals have failed after costs in Mandel's children (T-411, T-463).
rows.data_notes: There is no per-symbol option-volume history. options-chain bundles cover 14 roots on 2 days (2026-10-14/15). scratchpad dl_occ_test.csv (145,888 rows, 2025-10-15) shows TRAP: OCC reports each cleared trade once per side by account type (e.g. 5250 BHC as both C and M; 4000 FRSH as C and F). Total contracts traded = sum over account types / 2, and the customer-only variant uses the C rows. OCC history depth is unverified.
rows.lookahead_risks: OCC daily volume is published in the evening, so a Friday decision uses data through Friday and trades at Monday's open. Sort-universe re-ranking uses trailing option volume. FINRA DTC enters only after its publication date. The earnings-week split needs 8-K dates, not 10-Q dates.
rows.missing_data: Per-symbol daily OCC volume history (probe how far back the volume query reaches). Otherwise forward capture of at least 104 weeks.

final.claim: Universe: the 200 most option-active point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2016-2026, on an OCC per-symbol daily volume backfill (or forward from capture start if none exists). Weekly O/S = the week's option contracts traded x 100 / the week's shares traded. Claim: an equal-weighted portfolio long the lowest and short the highest O/S decile, formed at the Friday close and held from Monday's open to the next Monday's open, earns a positive mean weekly return net of 10 bps per side and borrow (3%/yr for top-tercile FINRA days-to-cover names, 0.5%/yr otherwise).
final.statistic: Mean weekly net long-short return, NW t (4 lags) and a studentized CBB (8-week blocks). The DTC-conditional spread is reported.
final.procedure: OCC contracts by underlying: sum quantity over account types and divide by 2, because each trade is listed once per side. A declared second cell uses customer-account (C) call volume only (Ge-Lin-Pearson). Map underlyings to tickers point in time. Data enter after OCC's evening publication. Shares traded from Yahoo split-adjusted volume. Re-rank the universe each quarter on trailing 3-month option volume among members as of t. FINRA DTC enters at its publication. Halves 2016-2020 / 2021-2026. Weeks with an earnings release are reported only once 8-K Item 2.02 dates exist.
final.data: OCC volume query (to fetch; scratchpad dl_occ_test.csv proves the format), daily-history-<SYM>, fja-sp500-components, finra-short-interest-<date>
final.pass: At least 400 weeks on a backfill (or 104 forward weeks for a forward-only read). Net mean > 0 with one-sided NW p < 0.05 and CBB lower bound > 0. Both halves positive. DSR >= 0.95 over the 2 declared cells.
final.controls: Look-ahead: publication-time OCC data, next-open entry. Double counting removed. Survivorship: priced members, flip bound reported. One decile cut. Costs: 10 bps per side plus tiered borrow. Regime split at 2021.

rows.reason: The source is verified and the mechanism has the 'leading source' shape, but the test is blocked until OCC's history depth is probed. The final fixes a double-count in OCC's per-side account-type rows, which would otherwise double O/S unevenly across names.

rows.name: Earnings-announcement premium conditioned on past announcement-period volume
rows.source_notes: Frazzini-Lamont, NBER w13090 (2007), abstract confirmed: the premium is large and robust, strongly related to volume surges, largest for stocks with high past announcement volume, and consistent with small-investor attention buying. The abstract gives no monthly figure. Heitz et al. (SSRN 3296537) returned 403, so the post-2004 decay figure is unverified.
rows.replication_concerns: The test window lies inside the documented post-2004 decay. Mandel's scheduled-event premia also decayed (T-341, T-343).
rows.data_notes: Checked sec-submissions b000: the filing schema is {cik, accn, form, filing_date, report_date, acceptance_json, is_xbrl, is_inline_xbrl, primary_document}, with no 8-K items field. 8-K counts are 1-33 a year 2005-2015, 505 in 2016, 5 in 2018 and over 2,000 a year from 2020. Item 2.02 dates cannot be built, and 10-Q dates lag releases by 1-4 weeks.
rows.lookahead_risks: Expected months must come from filings at least 11 months old. Using realised announcement dates would be look-ahead.
rows.missing_data: Refetch data.sec.gov submissions keeping every 8-K with its 'items' field. That also unblocks T-338, T-452 and T-578's earnings-date features. Delisted names remain absent.

final.claim: Amendment cell for T-339, registered before T-339 is measured. Among point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2011-01 to 2026-09, expected announcers (an Item 2.02 8-K accepted in the same calendar month a year earlier) in the top tercile of past announcement-window volume ratio outperform non-announcers by more than 50 bps per month net of 10 bps per side. The portfolio is equal-weighted and runs from the month-end close to the next month-end close.
final.statistic: Mean monthly spread with NW (lag 3) t and a studentized block bootstrap (6-month blocks). Top-minus-bottom volume-tercile difference.
final.procedure: Item 2.02 acceptance times from a refetched submissions bundle. Expected month = the acceptance month 12 months earlier, using only filings at least 11 months old. Volume ratio = mean split-adjusted volume over [-1,+1] of the prior 4 announcements / mean volume on the other days of the trailing year. Halves 2011-2018 / 2019-2026. Survivor coverage audit and flip bound as T-394. 2020 sensitivity. Counted among T-339's trials.
final.data: sec-submissions (refetch with 8-K items), daily-history-<SYM>, fja-sp500-components
final.pass: At least 150 months. Spread > 50 bps/month with NW p < 0.05. Both halves positive. Top-minus-bottom tercile spread > 0 with p < 0.05. Deflated within T-339's trial count.
final.controls: Look-ahead: only old filings set expectations. Survivorship: priced universe with flip bound. Costs: 10 bps per side at about 100% turnover. One tercile cut.

rows.reason: In substance this is T-339 (blocked) plus a conditioning cell. Add the cell to T-339 before it is measured instead of registering a new theory. The useful action is the free 8-K items refetch, which unblocks T-339, T-338, T-452 and T-578's earnings features.

rows.name: Volume-confirmed 52-week high/low breakouts
rows.source_notes: Huddart-Lang-Yetman, Management Science 55(1) 2009, abstract (RePEc): volume is strikingly higher when price crosses the upper or lower bound of its past range, and more so the longer since the last extreme, for smaller firms, for stocks with more individual-investor interest and for those with more valuation ambiguity. Returns after either crossing are reliably positive, and small-investor buyer-initiated trades rise. Confirmed. The abstract does not claim that volume-confirmed crossings beat unconfirmed ones; that part is a trader's extension.
rows.replication_concerns: There is no replication of the volume-conditioned version. In Mandel, T-309 (52-week-high nearness), T-304 (Donchian) and T-318 (88-rule SPA) all failed. 'Positive returns after lows' is the half most exposed to survivorship.
rows.data_notes: daily-history, SPY, fja and sec-submissions exist. TRAPS: (1) highs computed on adjclose are mechanically lower in the past for dividend payers, so they manufacture crossings; use the split-adjusted close. (2) The cross-checker's earnings flag (10-Q/10-K acceptance within +/-3 sessions) is the wrong event, because the release precedes the 10-Q by 1-4 weeks. Replaced by a same-day news proxy.
rows.lookahead_risks: AV tercile breakpoints must come from prior events only. Beta from the trailing 252 sessions. Next-open entry. The 60-session no-crossing filter uses past data only.
rows.missing_data: 8-K Item 2.02 dates for a real earnings flag. Delisted names (which inflate the lows). Small-investor signed trades.

final.claim: Universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, 2005-01 to 2026-09. Event: a split-adjusted (not dividend-adjusted) close above the trailing 252-session high, with no such crossing in the prior 60 sessions. Confirmed events have event-day volume / trailing 50-session median volume in the top tercile of that ratio across prior events. Claim: confirmed events earn a positive mean 20-session beta-adjusted return from the next open, net of a 10 bp round trip, and beat bottom-tercile (unconfirmed) events by at least 50 bps.
final.statistic: Event means with date-clustered bootstrap CIs. Confirmed-minus-unconfirmed difference. Matched-placebo p.
final.null: Confirmed mean <= 0, or confirmed minus unconfirmed < 50 bps.
final.procedure: Highs on the split-adjusted close; returns on adjclose. AV tercile breakpoints come from an expanding set of prior events, so no full-sample breakpoints. Beta vs SPY from the trailing 252 sessions. Placebo: random dates of the same name matched on trailing 60-day vol and distance to the 252-day high (0.25-sd bands), 2,000 draws. Reported only: lows, 5- and 60-session horizons, the top-decile AV cut, and events with an event-day |return| > 3 trailing sigma (news proxy). Halves 2005-2015 / 2016-2026. Coverage audit as T-394. Side check outside the verdict: AV x distance-to-high as a T-578 interaction cell.
final.data: daily-history-<SYM>, daily-history-SPY, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells
final.pass: At least 500 confirmed-high events. Confirmed mean net > 0 with date-clustered 95% lower bound > 0. Confirmed minus unconfirmed >= 50 bps with lower bound > 0. Placebo p < 0.05. Both halves positive. DSR >= 0.95 counting T-309's and T-304's trials plus this one.
final.controls: Look-ahead: trailing windows and prior-event breakpoints, next-open entry. No dividend-manufactured crossings. Survivorship: lows flagged and not judged. One AV cutoff, one horizon. Costs: 10 bp round trip. Prior breakout trials counted.

rows.reason: It is testable and cheap, but the cross-checker's 12-cell grid, dividend-adjusted highs and misdated earnings flag would inflate or confound it. One primary cell on highs is kept, with the prior breakout trials counted in the deflation.

rows.name: Dynamic volume-return relation (volume-price divergence): high-volume moves reverse or continue depending on who is trading
rows.source_notes: Campbell-Grossman-Wang, QJE 108(4) 1993, abstract (RePEc): the first-order daily return autocorrelation declines with volume, for indexes and for large individual stocks. Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang, RFS 15(4) 2002: hedging trades generate reversal and speculative trades continuation, and the cross-section of the volume-autocorrelation relation tracks informed trading. The abstract does not state a size pattern; it is from memory and is consistent with the theory. Medhat-Schmeling (opened) report monthly r x TO continuation strongest in megacaps, against LMSW's size prediction at monthly horizons.
rows.replication_concerns: The bottom-tercile LMSW sign is unlikely inside the S&P 500, where even the smallest members have low information asymmetry. Large-cap short-horizon reversal has hit the cost wall in Mandel (T-473, T-319, T-462), so a passing slope does not make a trade.
rows.data_notes: daily-history, fja and spells exist. Size from trailing median dollar volume, so no SEC shares are needed. The Coinbase second market (coinbase-daily bundles) exists but is moved to a separate later claim to keep one claim per registration.
rows.lookahead_risks: AV and terciles from trailing data. The cross-sectional AV demeaning uses day-t members only. The dependent return starts at open t+1, so bid-ask bounce in close t does not enter mechanically.
rows.missing_data: Analyst coverage and institutional ownership as true asymmetry proxies; not archived.

final.claim: On point-in-time S&P 500 members with archived prices, 2005-01 to 2026-09, run daily cross-sectional regressions of the open(t+1)-to-open(t+2) return on r(t), r(t) x AV(t) and AV(t), with controls. r(t) is the close-to-close return. AV(t) is log volume minus its trailing 60-day mean, demeaned across that day's members. Claim: the mean interaction coefficient is negative in the top size tercile (Campbell-Grossman-Wang) and positive in the bottom tercile (Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang), each with |NW t| > 2.8. Size is trailing 60-day median dollar volume.
final.statistic: Time-series mean of daily Fama-MacBeth coefficients per size tercile, with Newey-West t (5 lags).
final.procedure: Daily regressions within each size tercile, re-formed daily on trailing data. Controls: log trailing dollar volume and trailing 20-day volatility. Returns from adjclose for r(t), and from split-adjusted opens (dividend-adjusted on ex-dates) for the dependent return. Halves 2005-2015 / 2016-2026. The trading translation (weekly fade of extreme-r deciles on high-AV days) and the Coinbase replication are registered only after this verdict, as separate claims with costs. ML side check outside the verdict: r1 x lv_rel20 as a declared T-578 cell.
final.data: daily-history-<SYM>, fja-sp500-components, fja-sp500-ticker-spells
final.pass: At least 4,000 regression days. Top-tercile mean interaction < 0 with NW t < -2.8, AND bottom-tercile mean interaction > 0 with t > 2.8. Same signs in both halves.
final.controls: Look-ahead: trailing AV and terciles, next-open returns. Market volume days removed by demeaning. Survivorship: priced members. Search: a hurdle of |t| > 2.8. A correlation is not a trade: costs enter only in the separate trading claim.

rows.reason: This is a useful measurement of whether volume's information sits in its interaction with returns, which settles the T-578 feature-design question. The trading translation and the crypto replication are split out so that one registration holds one claim.

rows.name: Market intraday momentum conditioned on volume and short-gamma / leveraged-ETF hedging demand
rows.source_notes: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou, JFE 129(2) 2018 (RePEc, plus the scratchpad pdfs/gao.txt): SPY 1993-2013, predictive R^2 1.6%, stronger on volatile, high-volume, recession and macro-news days. In the paper, high-volume days are formed by sorting days YEAR-BY-YEAR into terciles of first-half-hour volume, which uses the whole year and is look-ahead; the registration uses a trailing tercile. Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens, JFE 142(1) 2021: more than 60 futures, 1974-2020; the return from the prior close through the rest of the day predicts the last 30 minutes, reverts over the following days, and is tied to gamma hedging by option dealers and leveraged ETFs. Confirmed. I did not open Zarattini et al. (practitioner).
rows.replication_concerns: T-427 found the unconditional rule at -0.09 bp gross over the same 720 sessions, with slope t -0.22, so the condition has to create the whole effect. T-428 shows no next-day reversal. RVOL in the first hour is largely a proxy for first-hour volatility. The archived window is seen data, so the 2016-2023 replication is the informative test.
rows.data_notes: hourly-SPY/QQQ/IWM bundles (5,080 rows each, stamped at bar start) and local 60m bars (2023-11-21..2026-10-20) exist. TRAP: the local bars end each day with a zero-volume 16:00 bar (o=h=l=c, v=0; SPY 2026-10-20 20:00 UTC), which is the closing print, not a slot. Drop it, and take the exit from the daily official close. Yahoo intraday volume is a partial feed, so RVOL compares within the same feed only.
rows.lookahead_risks: Bars are stamped at their start: the 09:30 hourly bar is known at 10:30, and the 15:30 bar's open is the entry print. The tercile cut must be trailing (Gao's year-by-year sort is look-ahead). Exit at the official close, not the 15:30 bar's last trade.
rows.missing_data: Alpaca SIP minute bars 2016-01..2023-10 (the required unseen replication). Dealer-gamma history and leveraged-ETF shares outstanding/NAV, both forward capture only, for the mechanism legs.

final.claim: On SPY, 2023-11-15 to 2026-10, using archived 60-minute bars with QQQ and IWM as replications. Rule: hold from the 15:30 bar's open to the official daily close, in the sign of the return from the previous official close to that 15:30 open. Claim: on high-RVOL sessions the rule earns a positive mean net return after a 2 bp round trip, and more than on low-RVOL sessions. High-RVOL sessions are those where the 09:30-10:30 bar's volume / the median of the same bar over the prior 20 sessions is above the 67th percentile of that ratio over the prior 60 sessions; low-RVOL sessions are below the 33rd percentile.
final.statistic: Mean net return per trade on high-RVOL sessions, and the high-minus-low difference. Weekly block bootstrap. Within-week random-tercile placebo (2,000 draws).
final.null: High-RVOL mean net <= 0, or high minus low <= 0.
final.procedure: Bar-start stamps converted to known-at times; the zero-volume 16:00 bar is dropped. Early closes and sessions missing the 09:30 or 15:30 bar are excluded, as in T-427. Exit price is the daily official close. FOMC and CPI days reported. Falsification check (reported): the next close-to-open return on high-RVOL sessions against T-428's regression. Deflation counts T-427's 60 cells. Required before any forward paper: the same rule on 2016-01..2023-10 Alpaca minute bars, using the half-hour version (09:30-10:00 volume). Dealer-gamma and leveraged-ETF rebalancing legs are separate later claims on forward capture.
final.data: local mandel/ml_data/bars/60m (SPY, QQQ, IWM), hourly-SPY, hourly-QQQ, hourly-IWM, daily-history-SPY, daily-history-QQQ, daily-history-IWM, fomc and CPI calendars
final.pass: At least 200 high-RVOL SPY sessions. Mean net > 0 with one-sided block-bootstrap p < 0.05. High minus low > 0 with p < 0.05. Placebo p < 0.05. Same sign on QQQ and IWM. Deflated p < 0.05 counting T-427's 60 cells.
final.controls: Look-ahead: completed bars only, trailing tercile. Seen window disclosed and deflated with T-427, with the unseen 2016-2023 replication required. One tercile cut. Costs: 2 bp round trip. The 16:00 print bar removed.

rows.reason: It is testable now and the conditioning is named ex ante by verified papers. But Gao's own tercile sort is look-ahead, and the archived window is T-427's. The final uses trailing terciles, drops the 16:00 print bar, and makes the unseen 2016-2023 replication a precondition for anything further.

rows.name: Opening-range breakout on 'Stocks in Play' selected by relative volume
rows.source_notes: SSRN 4729284 (Zarattini, Barbon, Aziz 2024) returned HTTP 403 and no other copy was reachable. The claimed +1,600% total return, Sharpe 2.81 and 36% annualised alpha could not be confirmed. No search for replications was possible (web-search budget used up).
rows.replication_concerns: An unreplicated practitioner backtest with free parameters (top-N, RVOL cutoff, ATR stop fraction) and an extraordinary Sharpe. The child repo's rule is that a result that good against a liquid market is a leak until the leak is found. Stop-entry fills at breakouts are adversely selected (Shannon/Kelly maker and touch learnings), and the intraday rules in T-577, T-427 and T-333 all failed.
rows.data_notes: Local 5-minute bars cover 123 symbols for about 60 days only (a smoke test at most). There is no full-universe minute history and no delisted names.
rows.lookahead_risks: RVOL5 must use completed bars at 09:35. Stop-entry fills must not be assumed at the trigger price. The universe must include inactive assets.
rows.missing_data: Alpaca SIP minute bars 2016-2026 for the full US stock universe, including inactive assets.

final.claim: Not registered. If the Alpaca minute backfill is built for T-426, the rule can be declared as a cell of T-426 with frozen parameters. Rule: the 20 names ranked highest on RVOL5 at 09:35 ET (price > $5, 14-day ADV > 1M shares, RVOL5 > 1, non-doji first bar); a 5-minute ORB stop entry; a stop at 10% of the 14-day ATR; exit at the close.
final.statistic: Mean daily net portfolio return and Sharpe (HAC), minus the same rule on 20 random eligible names (day-block bootstrap).
final.null: Mean net <= 0, or Stocks-in-Play minus placebo <= 0.
final.procedure: Only as a T-426 cell on an Alpaca SIP backfill that includes inactive assets. Stops fill at the next bar's open or worse. Costs: $0.0035/share plus one tick per fill, stressed at two ticks. Deflation counts T-426's 72 cells.
final.data: Alpaca SIP minute bars (not available), daily-history-<SYM>
final.pass: At least 250 sessions. Stocks-in-Play minus placebo > 0 with p < 0.05. Net Sharpe > 1 with 95% lower bound > 0. Both halves positive. Deflated p < 0.05 including T-426's cells.
final.controls: Frozen parameters, inactive assets included, no fills at the trigger price, news days reported.

rows.reason: The source is unverifiable from here (403), the claim has no independent replication and an implausible Sharpe, and it is untestable without a full-universe minute backfill. It can ride on T-426 at near-zero cost if that backfill is ever built.

rows.name: Intraday return periodicity and volume-profile (VWAP) execution timing
rows.source_notes: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka, JF 65(4) 2010, abstract (RePEc): return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 trading days; timing trades can cut execution costs by the equivalent of the effective spread. Confirmed. Bogousslavsky (2016) not opened.
rows.replication_concerns: No 2015-2026 US replication was found or searchable. T-577 (276 intraday cells, 0 pass) suggests the trading version fails net. The sample of about 53 names over about 3 years is small for cross-sectional periodicity.
rows.data_notes: Local 60m bars: 91 symbols, 2023-11-21..2026-10-20. Of these, about 28 are US single stocks and about 25 unlevered US equity ETFs. TQQQ/SQQQ are excluded as levered or inverse. Bonds, futures, FX and crypto are excluded as other sessions. The trailing zero-volume 16:00 bar must be dropped. The 30m and 5m bars span only about 60 days.
rows.lookahead_risks: Bar-start stamps: slot h's return is known at its end. Same-slot lookbacks exclude day d. The 16:00 bar is a closing print, not a slot.
rows.missing_data: Half-hour history longer than 60 days (Alpaca backfill). Quote data for an execution study (forward Alpaca paper fills only).

final.claim: Across the US single stocks and unlevered US equity ETFs in Mandel's local 60-minute bars (about 53 names, 2023-11 to 2026-10). Run cross-sectional Fama-MacBeth regressions per slot-day of a name's return in hourly slot h on day d on its mean return in the same slot over the previous 20 sessions. Claim: the same-slot slope exceeds the slope on the mean of the other slots over the same 20 sessions, with NW t > 2 in each half of the sample.
final.statistic: Time-series mean of the per slot-day FM slope differences (same-slot minus other-slot) with NW t. A top-minus-bottom quintile slot portfolio is reported net of 2 bps per side for ETFs and 5 bps for stocks.
final.procedure: Slots are the 6 full hourly bars plus the 15:30 half-hour bar, all bar-start stamped; the zero-volume 16:00 print bar is dropped. Names are restricted to US single stocks and unlevered equity ETFs trading RTH. Lookback k = 1..20 days for the same slot, excluding day d; the control is the other slots' mean over the same days. Halves 2023-11..2025-04 / 2025-05..2026-10. The slot portfolio (day-block bootstrap) is reported and expected to fail net. An execution-shortfall study for T-559/T-576 runs separately as forward Alpaca paper measurement, not as part of this claim.
final.data: local mandel/ml_data/bars/60m, hourly-<SYM>, daily-history-<SYM>
final.pass: At least 450 trading days. Mean same-slot minus other-slot slope > 0 with NW t > 2 in both halves.
final.controls: Look-ahead: known-at conversion, today excluded from lookbacks. Session mixing removed by asset-class restriction. The print bar removed. One lookback. Costs charged in the reported portfolio.

rows.reason: The source is verified and it is cheap on archived bars. The fix narrows it to one measurable claim on a clean equity-only slot set, without the 16:00 print bar. Execution timing is a forward measurement and alpha is not expected.

rows.name: ETF primary-market flows (creations/redemptions) as non-fundamental demand: short high-flow, long low-flow ETFs
rows.source_notes: Brown-Davies-Ringgenberg, Review of Finance 25(4) 2021, abstract (RePEc): creation and redemption activity reveals non-fundamental demand shocks, and a portfolio short high-flow ETFs and long low-flow ETFs earns 1.1-2.0% per month in excess returns. Confirmed. The sample period is not in the abstract.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-publication test was found. T-404 (GLD holdings changes) found no prediction in either sign at 1 week, and Granger tests show flows follow price. The GLD/GLDM pilot is therefore close to a duplicate of T-404 and is removed.
rows.data_notes: Daily shares outstanding are archived only for GLD and GLDM (spdr-gld-archive, spdr-gldm-archive). IBIT has one snapshot, and the Sprott bundles carry no units. The 68-ETF cross-section needs forward capture. N-PORT filings carry net assets rather than a clean daily shares series, so they are not a reliable backfill.
rows.lookahead_risks: Issuer shares-outstanding pages update after the close and sometimes with a lag, so available_at = capture time and trades start the next session. The declared ETF list is survivor-drawn at the start.
rows.missing_data: A daily shares-outstanding and NAV capture for the 68 declared ETFs, to start now. It would also serve the leveraged-ETF leg of the intraday-momentum row.

final.claim: Over at least 36 forward months from capture start, take the 68 declared ETFs within asset-class buckets (US sector, country, bond, commodity). Claim: an equal-weighted portfolio long the bottom and short the top quintile of trailing 21-session flow / AUM, formed at month-end and held one month, earns a positive mean monthly return after 5 bps per side and ETF borrow. Flow = change in log shares outstanding captured daily from issuer pages.
final.statistic: Mean monthly net long-short return with NW t (lag 3). Per-bucket spreads reported.
final.procedure: Capture daily shares outstanding and NAV for the 68 ETFs, with available_at = capture time. Flow / AUM over the trailing 21 sessions. Quintiles within buckets, or top and bottom names where a bucket has fewer than 10. Fill at the next close after month-end. Halves by date. The GLD/GLDM pilot is not run (T-404 duplicate).
final.data: issuer shares-outstanding capture (to start), daily-history-<ETF>
final.pass: At least 36 forward months. Net mean > 0 with one-sided NW p < 0.05. Both halves positive.
final.controls: Look-ahead: capture-time availability, next-close fills. Survivorship: the list is fixed at the start. One quintile cut. Costs: 5 bps per side plus borrow. Inconclusive before 36 months.

rows.reason: The source is verified, but the data exist only as forward capture. The GLD pilot is removed because it repeats T-404's design and data. Starting the capture is cheap and shared with the leveraged-ETF leg of the intraday row.

rows.name: ETF / trust premium-discount to NAV mean reversion (beyond IBIT)
rows.source_notes: Petajisto, FAJ 73(1) 2017, abstract (RePEc): deviations usually lie within about 200 bps, about 100 bps after a stale-price correction, and are larger for international and illiquid holdings. Active strategies earn substantial abnormal returns before transaction costs. Confirmed. The returns are gross.
rows.replication_concerns: T-472 (PHYS/GLD: 27 trades, net +0.059%, lower bound -0.198%; z < -2 variant +0.016%; PSLV/SLV -0.156%), T-328 (IBIT) and T-324 (SPY/IVV) all sat inside the cost band.
rows.data_notes: sprott-sppp-nav (2012-12-18..2026-10-15, 3,507 rows) and sprott-cef-nav (2018-01-16..2026-10-15, 2,209 rows) exist. There is no daily-history for SPPP or CEF (checked), so US NYSE prices are unverified, and Sprott's share_price may include TSX-only sessions. Synchronous 16:00 metal spot is not archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: The NAV is struck after the close (next-morning availability). Share prices may be TSX prints. T-472's PHYS/PSLV results were seen.
rows.missing_data: Verified NYSE daily prices for SPPP and CEF, and synchronous 16:00 metal spot.

final.claim: Not registered now. Re-register only as a T-472 extension restricted to the unseen trusts (SPPP vs PPLT+PALL, CEF vs GLD+SLV at NAV weights), and only once NYSE prices are archived. Rule: long the trust and short the matched ETF at the next NYSE close when the premium z (trailing 120-day) is below -2, and the mirror above +2. Exit at z = 0 or after 20 sessions. Claim: positive mean net return per trade after 5 bps per leg per side and 1%/yr borrow.
final.statistic: Mean net return per trade with a month-clustered studentized bootstrap; block-shift null.
final.procedure: Next-morning NAV availability, next-close fills, NYSE sessions only, deflated jointly with T-472's 5 trials and T-328's 6 variants.
final.data: sprott-sppp-nav, sprott-cef-nav, NYSE prices for SPPP/CEF (to fetch), daily-history-PPLT/PALL/GLD/SLV
final.pass: At least 60 trades. Month-clustered one-sided 95% lower bound > 0. Block-shift p < 0.05. Positive in both trusts. Deflated with T-472 and T-328.
final.controls: Look-ahead: next-morning NAV. Seen PHYS/PSLV results excluded. Costs stressed at 10 bps per leg.

rows.reason: In substance this is T-472 (not_supported), and it pools trusts T-472 already measured. The two new trusts lack verified US price series. Extending a failed rule to thinner assets is a forking search.

rows.name: Crypto liquidity provision: volume-conditioned short-term reversal, plus an out-of-sample short of altcoin volume shocks
rows.source_notes: Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson, JBF 142 (2022), abstract (RePEc): USD pairs on multiple centralised exchanges, 2017-03-01 to 2022-03-01. Liquidity-provision (reversal) returns are concentrated in pairs with lower market activity, and are larger in smaller, more volatile, less liquid pairs. The lagged return x volume interaction significantly predicts returns. Confirmed. I did not open Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu.
rows.replication_concerns: Crypto reversal sits below costs at BTC (T-320, T-469) and on Kalshi perps (Hurst). Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu span volume characteristics by size and momentum. The low-activity alts where the premium sits are where 50 bp underestimates the real spread. Part (b) is already answered: T-546's placebo null is -1.32%, so only about -0.5% is shock-specific, and Hurst's H-hype-fade forward test (read 2027-01-12) covers it. Part (b) is not registered.
rows.data_notes: coinbase-daily bundles exist (about 493 products, 2015-07-20..2026-10-14, including delisted products; days without trades absent), along with coinbase-products (current status snapshots 2026-10-15/16) and cmc-daily-listings 2017-2026. Membership must come from trailing daily dollar volume, not the current product list. The 2019-2026 data were seen by T-546 under a different conditional (disclosed).
rows.lookahead_risks: TRAP: in the cross-checker's design, the signal's last close is also the entry price ('entry at that close'). That captures bid-ask bounce in a reversal sort. Fix: skip one day and enter at the next daily close. UTC bar alignment: a daily candle's close is known at the next 00:00 UTC. Use trailing 30-day dollar volume for membership.
rows.missing_data: Intraday spreads for thin alts (cost is only stressed, not measured). Kraken alt histories for an untouched replication.

final.claim: Universe: the point-in-time top 50 Coinbase USD products by trailing 30-day dollar volume (T-546's exclusions), 2019-01 to 2026-09, weekly. Signals come from daily bars through Saturday's UTC bar. Entry is at the close of Sunday's bar (a one-day skip), with a 7-day hold. Claim: the equal-weighted low-activity-loser portfolio beats the equal-weighted universe after a 50 bp round trip on traded weight. Low-activity losers are the bottom quintile of prior-week return within the bottom tercile of prior-week volume relative to its trailing 30-day mean. In addition, the low-activity loser-minus-winner spread exceeds the high-activity spread.
final.statistic: Weekly mean net long-only excess return (portfolio minus universe) with a studentized CBB (8-week blocks). Difference between the low- and high-activity loser-minus-winner spreads.
final.null: Long-only excess net <= 0, or the low-activity spread minus the high-activity spread <= 0.
final.procedure: Membership from coinbase-daily, dead products included; stablecoin, wrapped and staked bases excluded as in T-546. Prior-week return and relative volume from bars closed by Sunday 00:00 UTC. Entry at the Sunday bar's close (Monday 00:00 UTC), exit 7 days later. Costs: 50 bp round trip on traded weight, stressed at 100 bp. Halves split at 2022-11-17. Regimes 2022 (Terra, FTX) reported. Long-short spreads are reported only, because US-legal shorts cover few alts. Part (b) is read from Hurst's H-hype-fade on 2027-01-12, not registered here.
final.data: coinbase-daily-<PID>, coinbase-products-<day>, cmc-daily-listings
final.pass: At least 300 weeks. Long-only excess net > 0 with CBB 95% lower bound > 0. Both halves positive. Low-activity minus high-activity spread > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05. Holds at the 100 bp stress. DSR >= 0.95 counting T-314's and T-546's trials.
final.controls: Look-ahead: a one-day skip between signal and entry, UTC alignment, trailing membership. Survivorship: dead products included. One quintile/tercile scheme. Costs stressed. Seen-data disclosure for T-546.

rows.reason: The source is verified and part (a) is testable on point-in-time data. The cross-checker's same-close entry would book bid-ask bounce as reversal profit, so a one-day skip is added. Part (b) is left to Hurst's existing forward test.

rows.name: Commodity futures open-interest growth predicts commodity (and bond) returns
rows.source_notes: Hong-Yogo, JFE 105(3) 2012 (RePEc and NBER w16712): open interest is strongly pro-cyclical. Movements in commodity open interest predict commodity returns, bond returns and short-rate movements after controls, and predict currency and stock returns less strongly. Confirmed. Neither abstract states the SIGN or the sample. The declared positive commodity sign (negative for bonds) is from memory and the hedging-pressure mechanism, so it is unverified.
rows.replication_concerns: No post-2008 replication was found or searchable. Financialisation after 2004 (index investors) may change what open interest measures. About 177 out-of-sample months give low power.
rows.data_notes: CFTC COT bundles exist only for gold (088691) and silver (084691), legacy, disaggregated and TFF BTC (133741), checked. The other about 18 contracts need a Socrata fetch (6dca-aqww), using the existing recipe. TRAP: Yahoo '=F' continuous fronts splice contracts without back-adjustment, so =F returns jump at every roll (worst for NG, CL and livestock). Use =F settles only to weight OI in dollars, never as return targets or cross-sectional legs. Use roll-inclusive tradable ETFs instead: DBC, USO, UNG, DBA, CPER, GLD, SLV, PPLT and PALL are archived.
rows.lookahead_risks: A COT report (Tuesday as-of) is usable only after its Friday 15:30 ET release. Backcast or revised rows are dropped as in T-405. A month-end signal uses only reports released by then.
rows.missing_data: CFTC legacy futures-only rows for about 18 more contracts (free Socrata fetch). Yahoo =F settles for the missing roots (dollar weights only). Expired-contract histories for a clean futures cross-section (T-371's block); ETFs are used instead.

final.claim: From 2012-01 to 2026-09, the 12-month log growth of aggregate dollar open interest predicts next-month DBC excess return over DTB3 with a positive slope and out-of-sample R^2 > 0 against the expanding historical mean (Clark-West p < 0.05). Open interest covers about 20 US commodity futures in the CFTC legacy futures-only reports, each report entered at its Friday 15:30 ET release.
final.statistic: Campbell-Thompson R^2_OS with a Clark-West HAC test. Reported: the TLT excess-return regression (expected negative) and a long/flat DBC rule net of 5 bps per switch.
final.procedure: Fixed contract list: CL, NG, HO, RB, GC, SI, HG, PL, ZC, ZS, ZW, ZL, ZM, KC, SB, CT, CC, LE, HE, OJ. Dollar OI = contracts x the fixed multiplier x the =F settle on the report's as-of date (a level, used only for weighting). Aggregate and take 12-month log growth from reports released by month-end. Expanding regressions from 2006 data, first forecast 2012-01. Targets only roll-inclusive tradable series: DBC (primary) and TLT (reported). A cross-sectional tercile portfolio across single-commodity ETFs (USO, UNG, DBA, CPER, GLD, SLV, PPLT, PALL) is reported only, never on =F returns. Halves 2012-2018 / 2019-2026. April 2020 WTI flagged.
final.data: CFTC Socrata legacy futures-only (to fetch for about 18 contracts; gold and silver archived), Yahoo =F settles (to fetch for missing roots), daily-history-DBC, daily-history-TLT, commodity ETF daily-history, fred-DTB3
final.pass: At least 150 out-of-sample months. DBC R^2_OS > 0 with Clark-West p < 0.05. Slope > 0 in both halves. The long/flat rule is reported net.
final.controls: Look-ahead: release-time availability, backcasts dropped. Fixed contract list. No =F returns anywhere. Costs: 5 bps per switch. The sign is declared ex ante from the hedging-pressure mechanism and flagged unverified. Regimes 2008, 2014-16, 2020-04 and 2022 reported.

rows.reason: The data are free and the fetcher exists. The cross-checker's design would have taken returns from unadjusted =F continuous fronts, whose roll jumps would swamp any signal, so the targets are limited to roll-inclusive ETFs. The predicted sign could not be verified from the abstracts.

knowledge.title: Trading volume, turnover and liquidity as return signals: the academic record, its decay, and Mandel's tests
knowledge.markdown:
# Trading volume, turnover and liquidity as return signals: the academic record, its decay, and Mandel's tests

- **Authors / kind:** Literature survey (web sweep and verification pass) of 16 strategies and patterns built on volume, dollar volume, share turnover, liquidity and one-step-adjacent flows (option volume, open interest, ETF flows). Mostly peer-reviewed (JF, RFS, JFE, QJE and others, 1993-2022), plus replication and decay studies and two practitioner backtests.
- **Links:** https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/31278/ · https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/jfinan/v56y2001i3p877-919.html · https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finmar/v5y2002i1p31-56.html · https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v106y2012i2p262-286.html
- **Coverage confidence:** 0.45 (about 20 of the 44 cited sources opened and checked against the claims, mostly at abstract level).
- **Date researched:** 2026-10-20. **How much was read:** two papers in full text (the Medhat-Schmeling manuscript, every number checked; Gao et al.); RePEc/NBER abstracts for most others; OSAP SignalDoc for std_turn, VolSD, Illiquidity and OptionVolume1. Unreachable (403 or quota): Harris-Amato, Drienko et al., Heitz et al., Zarattini et al., OSAP long-short returns. Figures marked "from memory" are unverified.
- **Selected because:** volume, dollar volume and turnover are the F0 inputs of the learning program (T-577, T-578), where relative volume alone has a mean IC near +0.01. The literature puts volume's information in its interaction with returns and in volatility, not in its level, so this cluster decides how F0 is redesigned and which classic claims archived data can settle.

## What it says

- **Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks (Medhat-Schmeling, RFS 2022).** Sort on last month's return and turnover (volume / shares outstanding). High-turnover winners beat losers: +1.37%/month (t 4.74), 1.00% net of half-spreads, largest-500 2x2 +0.42% (t 4.91), US 1963-2018; 22 markets agree. The low-turnover reversal leg has not worked since the mid-2000s (CXO). No independent US test after 2018.
- **High-volume return premium (Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin, JF 2001).** A high-volume week without a large price move precedes higher returns over the next month (visibility); found in 41 countries. Contested in Korea; no recent US single-stock replication.
- **Aggregate illiquidity (Amihud 2002).** Expected market illiquidity (mean |return| / dollar volume) predicts higher excess returns. The time-series abstract was unreachable; OSAP confirms the cross-sectional predictor (t 6.6, equal-weighted, 1964-1997). Replications (not opened) report decay after decimalisation.
- **Aggregate turnover as sentiment (Baker-Stein 2004).** High turnover predicts lower equal-weighted market returns. No post-2004 replication; turnover trends up, so it must be detrended.
- **Volatility of liquidity (Chordia-Subrahmanyam-Anshuman 2001).** Stocks whose turnover or share volume varies more earn less (std_turn t 3.74, VolSD t 3.56, equal-weighted, 1966-1995); no settled mechanism.
- **Option-to-stock volume ratio (Johnson-So 2012).** Low-minus-high O/S decile +0.34%/week, 1996-2010, stronger when short-sale costs (borrow fee, short interest) are high; Ge-Lin-Pearson trace it to opening call buys. No US test after 2010, before the 0DTE boom.
- **Earnings-announcement premium (Frazzini-Lamont).** Largest where past announcement volume surged (attention buying); reported gone in the US after 2004 (Heitz et al., unverified).
- **Volume at 52-week highs (Huddart-Lang-Yetman 2009).** Volume jumps when price crosses its 52-week range, and returns afterwards are positive. "Confirmed beats unconfirmed" is a trader's extension, not the paper's claim.
- **Dynamic volume-return relation (Campbell-Grossman-Wang 1993; Llorente et al. 2002).** Return autocorrelation falls with volume for indexes and large stocks (hedging volume reverts); informed volume continues. The size pattern is from memory and Medhat-Schmeling's megacap result contradicts it monthly.
- **Market intraday momentum (Gao et al. 2018; Baltussen et al. 2021).** The first half-hour predicts the last half-hour (SPY 1993-2013, R² 1.6%), more on high-volume and macro-news days; across 60+ futures (1974-2020) the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes, reverts over the next days, and is tied to short-gamma dealer and leveraged-ETF rebalancing. Gao's year-by-year volume terciles are look-ahead.
- **Intraday periodicity (Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka 2010).** A half-hour slot's return recurs at the same slot for 40+ days (VWAP schedules); timing trades saves about the effective spread.
- **ETF flows (Brown-Davies-Ringgenberg 2021).** Short high-flow, long low-flow ETFs: 1.1-2.0%/month; no post-publication test. **Premium/discount (Petajisto 2017):** abnormal returns reported before costs only.
- **Crypto liquidity provision (Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson 2022).** Reversal pay concentrates in low-activity, small, volatile pairs; Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu find volume characteristics spanned by size and momentum.
- **Commodity open interest (Hong-Yogo 2012).** Open-interest growth predicts commodity and bond returns (hedging pressure); sign not in the abstract, post-financialisation untested.

## Evidence quality

**Rating: rigorous.** Peer-reviewed, with cross-country replications for STMOM, the volume premium and intraday momentum, and OSAP reproductions on CRSP. Rigorous method is not a current edge: samples end 1995-2018, effects are strongest equal-weighted in small names, liquidity premia are documented as decayed (Ben-Rephael-Kadan-Wohl; Hou-Xue-Zhang: 96% of trading-friction anomalies fail value-weighted; McLean-Pontiff: 58% post-publication fall), and the practitioner items are unreplicated.

## What Mandel adopts

- **STMOM post-sample** (`stmom-high-turnover-2x2-sp500`, with STREV and 12-1 baselines). Expect a low-power fail: the MDE (~0.39%/month) about equals the paper's largest-500 effect and UMD is ~0 since 2009 (T-446). T-420/T-462 failed on ETFs only.
- **Single-stock visibility premium** (`hvrp-visibility-weeks-sp500`), deflated with T-419's 36 cells (ETF events +6.9 bp, DSR 0.033).
- **Return x volume interaction as a measurement** (`return-volume-interaction-daily-by-size`, |NW t| > 2.8); trading translations only after.
- **Market liquidity as one family:** `aggregate-amihud-expected-illiq-iwm` and `aggregate-turnover-sentiment-ew-12m` are mirror images, Holm-corrected with T-421 and the failed sentiment predictors T-398, T-449, T-458.
- **Volume variability** (`volume-variability-cv-sp500-vw`) on share volume, value-weighted; dollar volume would encode the price path.
- **Volume-confirmed 52-week highs** (`volume-confirmed-52w-high-sp500`), counting T-309 and T-304.
- **Intraday momentum on high opening relative volume** (`intraday-momentum-rvol-tercile-spy`), trailing terciles, deflated with T-427's 60 cells (T-427: -2.09 bp/day net); the unseen 2016-2023 replication is a precondition.
- **Same-slot continuation** (`intraday-same-slot-continuation-hourly`), expected to fail net (T-577: 0 of 276 non-crypto cells), useful for execution timing (T-559, T-576).
- **Crypto low-activity loser reversal** (`crypto-low-activity-loser-reversal-weekly`), long-only on Coinbase, one-day skip; T-320 sets the cost bar.
- **Registered blocked:** `option-stock-volume-ratio-weekly-occ`, `etf-flow-reversal-xs-forward`, `commodity-oi-growth-dbc-timing`. The Frazzini-Lamont volume cell joins T-339 before it is measured.

## What Mandel holds loosely or rejects

- **Volume predicts the size of the next move, not its sign.** Hurst: volume ratio predicts next-bar range (t +4 to +43), not return; T-415: StockTwits intensity fails to add to HAR volatility forecasts; T-12 (higher-volume markets better calibrated) not_supported; the children's settle rates sit within ~1c of mid in every volume bucket.
- **Final volume is look-ahead:** the children's Result 9 "+6% favourite" cell was a final-volume artefact. Only volume published by decision time enters.
- **Stocks-in-Play opening-range breakout** (Zarattini et al.): source unreachable, Sharpe 2.81 implausible, stop entries adversely selected (Shannon/Kelly maker-fill learnings). At most a frozen T-426 cell.
- **Trust/ETF premium reversion:** duplicates T-472 (27 trades, net +0.059%, lower bound -0.198%), T-328 and T-324. Dropped.
- **Attention-buying short:** no point-in-time retail-attention data, and its price proxy contradicts the STMOM leg. Dropped.
- **Altcoin volume-shock short:** T-546's -1.80% sits over a placebo null of -1.32%, on seen data; left to Hurst's H-hype-fade (read 2027-01-12). Shorts only via Coinbase Derivatives or Kalshi perps, never offshore venues.
- **Decayed or contested:** time-series Amihud; low-turnover reversal; the earnings premium after 2004; ETF flow momentum (T-404: flows follow price). OBV and volume-breakout rules are presumed overfit (T-318's 88-rule SPA failed). Hong-Yogo's sign is unverified.

## Design implications for the RSI predictive substrate

- **Features (T-578):** r(1m) x TO(1m), r1 x lv_rel20 and abnormal volume x 52-week-high distance as declared F0xF2 interaction cells; route volume features to the realised volatility (HAR-RV) target too.
- **Construction traps:** shares outstanding from sec-companyfacts at acceptance time, split-adjusted to Yahoo's fetch-date basis (else NVDA's 2015 turnover is off 40x); dollar volume = split-adjusted close x volume, never adjclose; 52-week highs on the split-adjusted close; relative volume within one feed; drop the zero-volume 16:00 bar.
- **Data to add:** SEC submissions with 8-K items (unblocks T-339, T-338, T-452); OCC per-symbol volume (each trade listed once per side: halve it); CFTC COT for ~18 contracts (=F settles as weights only); daily ETF shares outstanding; Alpaca SIP minute bars 2016-2023; OSAP long-short returns.
- **Gate:** MDE with every verdict; prior trials counted; survivorship (~18.5% of member-days since 2010 unpriced) stated as an upper bound.

## Cross-links

- A4 (multifractal model): volume is the observable of trading time; subordination predicts Hurst's finding that volume forecasts volatility, not direction.
- 12, 13, 14 (Claude trading videos): their relative-volume and VWAP filters are F0 features to test as interactions.
- A5 (Halawi): turnover-conditioned drift is a claim about how fast information enters price.
- UNDERLYING-STRATEGIES.md, OPTIONS-STRATEGIES.md (O/S, dealer gamma), VENUES.md.
- Theories: T-12, T-304, T-307, T-309, T-318, T-320, T-328, T-339, T-393 and T-394 (days to cover, short volume), T-398, T-404, T-415, T-419, T-420, T-421, T-426, T-427, T-446, T-449, T-455, T-458, T-462, T-472, T-546, T-577, T-578.

## Sources used

- Medhat & Schmeling 2022, RFS: https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhab055 (manuscript https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/31278/)
